- Root: ر-ج-ح (r-j-ḥ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To outweigh, to preponderate; a scale tipping toward one side.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Preponderance of evidence in juridical-theological reasoning (tarjīḥ), establishing one proof over another.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal in weighing; metaphorical in scholarly preference — tarjīḥ as the act of declaring one report superior.
- Root: ع-ل-ق (ʿ-l-q) — [Note: Root ع is excluded per instruction; using alternative anchor]
- Root: ش-ذ-ذ (sh-dh-dh)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To stand apart, to deviate from the majority; singularity.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In ḥadīth terminology, shādhdh is a report whose transmitter contradicts one more reliable — a technical defect.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal physical separation; metaphorical as anomalous narration.
- Root: ع-ل-ل (ʿ-l-l) — [Excluded; using alternative]
- Root: م-ز-ج (m-z-j) — [Not needed]
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clauses with Implied Apodosis (Sharṭ maʿa ḥadhf al-jawāb) — In phrases like "لو أن أهل الحديث يكتبون مائتي سنة... فمدارهم على هذا المسند," the protasis is followed by a resumptive clause, requiring the reader to supply the logical consequence.
chapters.translation:
I say: Abū ʿAlī al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī al-Naysābūrī, the ḥāfiẓ and teacher of al-Ḥākim Abū ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Bayyiʿ, stated that the book of Muslim is the most authentic. Some scholars of the Maghrib concurred with him. However, the correct position is the first one — namely, the preponderance of al-Bukhārī. The Imām, ḥāfiẓ, jurist, and dialectical theologian Abū Bakr al-Ismāʿīlī — may Allāh have mercy on him — established in his book *al-Madkhal* the preponderance of al-Bukhārī's book. We have also related from the Imām Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Nasāʾī — may Allāh have mercy on him — that he said: "There is nothing in all these books more excellent than the book of al-Bukhārī."

I say: Among the most concise grounds for preponderance is the consensus of the scholars that al-Bukhārī is greater than Muslim and more knowledgeable in the craft of ḥadīth. He selected from his knowledge and distilled what he approved in this book. He spent sixteen years in its refinement and selection, compiling it from thousands of authentic reports. I have already mentioned the evidences for all of this at the beginning of my commentary on Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī.

Among the grounds that give preponderance to al-Bukhārī's book is that Muslim — may Allāh have mercy on him — held the doctrine — nay, he transmitted consensus at the beginning of his Ṣaḥīḥ — that the chain of transmission using ʿanʿanah (the particle "on the authority of") has the ruling of an explicitly heard (musalsal bi-samiʿ) chain, merely by virtue of the fact that the one transmitting with ʿanʿanah and the one transmitted from were contemporaries, even if their actual meeting is not established. Al-Bukhārī, however, does not deem such a chain connected until their meeting is verified. This doctrine gives preponderance to al-Bukhārī's book — although we do not pass judgment against Muslim for acting on this doctrine in his Ṣaḥīḥ, because he gathered many chains, making it difficult for this ruling he permitted to be absent. And Allāh knows best.

Muslim was uniquely distinguished by a beneficial feature: his book is easier to access, in that he assigned to every ḥadīth a single fitting place, gathering therein the chains he approved and chose to mention, and presenting its multiple chains and variant wordings. This makes it easy for the student to examine its aspects and derive benefit, and he attains confidence in all the chains Muslim cited. This contrasts with al-Bukhārī, who mentions those variant aspects in scattered, distant chapters — and many of them he mentions in a chapter other than the one that first comes to mind as most appropriate. This is due to a subtlety that al-Bukhārī perceives, which the student misses, making it difficult for him to gather the chains and attain confidence in all the versions al-Bukhārī cited for a given ḥadīth. I have seen a group of later ḥuffāẓ err in such matters, denying that al-Bukhārī narrated reports that are in fact present in his Ṣaḥīḥ, albeit not in the places that first come to mind. And Allāh knows best.

Among what has reached us concerning the virtue of Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim is what we related from Makkī ibn ʿAbdān, one of the ḥuffāẓ of Naysābūr, who said: I heard Muslim ibn al-Ḥajjāj — may Allāh be pleased with him — say: "If the people of ḥadīth were to write ḥadīth for two hundred years, their pivot would be this musnad" — meaning his Ṣaḥīḥ. He said: And I heard Muslim say: "I presented this book of mine to Abū Zurʿah al-Rāzī. Whatever he indicated had a defect, I abandoned; and whatever he said was authentic and had no defect, I included." Someone else mentioned what the ḥāfiẓ Abū Bakr al-Khaṭīb al-Baghdādī related with his chain from Muslim — may Allāh have mercy on him — that he said: "I compiled this authentic musnad from three hundred thousand heard reports."

---

**CHAPTER**

The Shaykh, the Imām Abū ʿAmr ibn al-Ṣalāḥ — may Allāh have mercy on him — said: The condition of Muslim — may Allāh the Exalted have mercy on him — in his Ṣaḥīḥ is that the ḥadīth have a connected chain, transmitted by trustworthy narrators from trustworthy narrators from its beginning to its end, being free from shādhdh (anomaly) and ʿillah (hidden defect). He said: This is the definition of authenticity. Every ḥadīth in which these conditions are combined is authentic, without disagreement among the people of ḥadīth. Whatever they disagreed about concerning its authenticity, the cause of their disagreement may be the absence of one of these conditions, with a difference among them regarding whether it is required — as when one of the narrators is concealed (mastūr) or the ḥadīth is interrupted (mursal). Or the cause of their disagreement may be whether these conditions are in fact combined or some are absent — and this is the more frequent cause — as when a ḥadīth has among its narrators someone concerning whom there is disagreement as to whether he meets the condition of authenticity. Thus, if all the narrators of a ḥadīth are trustworthy, except that among them is, for example, Abū al-Zubayr al-Makkī, or Suhayl ibn Abī Ṣāliḥ, or al-ʿAlāʾ ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, or Ḥammād ibn Salamah, they say: "This ḥadīth is authentic according to the condition of Muslim, but not authentic according to the condition of al-Bukhārī" — because these narrators, in Muslim's view, are among those in whom the considered conditions are combined, whereas this was not established in al-Bukhārī's view. Likewise is the case of al-Bukhārī regarding what he included from the ḥadīth of ʿIkrimah, the freed slave of Ibn ʿAbbās, and Isḥāq ibn Muḥammad al-Farwī, and ʿAmr ibn Marzūq, and others whom al-Bukhārī cited as proof but Muslim did not.

Al-Ḥākim Abū ʿAbd Allāh, the ḥāfiẓ of Naysābūr, said in his book *al-Madkhal ilā Maʿrifat al-Mustadrak*: The number of shaykhs for whom al-Bukhārī included narrations in *al-Jāmiʿ al-Ṣaḥīḥ* but Muslim did not include for them is four hundred and thirty-four. And the number of those whom Muslim cited as proof in *al-Musnad al-Ṣaḥīḥ* but al-Bukhārī did not cite as proof in *al-Jāmiʿ al-Ṣaḥīḥ* is six hundred and twenty-five shaykhs. And Allāh knows best.

As for the statement of Muslim — may Allāh have mercy on him — in his Ṣaḥīḥ, in the chapter on the description of the prayer of the Messenger of Allāh — may Allāh bless him and grant him peace: "Not everything authentic in my view have I placed here" — meaning in this authentic book of his — "rather, I placed here only what they have agreed upon" — this is problematic. For he placed therein many ḥadīths concerning whose authenticity there is disagreement, because they are from the narrators we mentioned and others we did not mention, concerning whose ḥadīth's authenticity there is disagreement.

The Shaykh said: The answer to this is from two aspects. One: his meaning is that he did not place therein anything except what, in his view, had the conditions of authenticity agreed upon — even if the combination of these conditions is not apparent in some ḥadīths to some scholars. The second: he meant that he did not place therein anything concerning which the trustworthy narrators disagreed regarding the ḥadīth itself, whether in text or chain; he did not mean cases where their disagreement was only concerning the reliability of some of its narrators. This is the apparent meaning of his words — for he said this when he was asked about the ḥadīth of Abū Hurayrah: "When he recites, then be silent" — whether it is authentic. He said: "It is authentic in my view." It was said to him: "Why did you not place it here?" So he answered with this statement.

chapters.title_en: The Issue of Interrupted Chains (Taʿlīq) in the Two Ṣaḥīḥs — A Scholarly Vindication of Their Authenticity
chapters.arabic_text: المذكور ومع هذا فقد اشتمل كتابه على أحاديث اختلفوا في اسنادها أو متنها لصحتها عنده وفي ذلك ذهول منه عن هذا الشرط أو سبب آخر وقد استدركت وعللت هذا آخر كلام الشيخ رحمه الله | | فصل # ) # قال الشيخ الإمام أبو عمرو بن الصلاح رحمه الله ما وقع في صحيحي البخاري ومسلم مما صورته صورة المنقطع ليس ملتحقا بالمنقطع في خروجه من حيز الصحيح إلى حيز الضعيف ويسمى هذا النوع تعليقا سماه به الامام أبو الحسن الدارقطني ويذكره الحميدي في الجمع بين الصحيحين وكذا غيره من المغاربة وهو في كتاب البخاري كثير جدا وفي كتاب مسلم قليل جدا قال فاذا كان التعليق منهما بلفظ فيه جزم بأن من بينهما وبينه الانقطاع قد قال ذلك أو رواه واتصل الاسناد منه على الشرط مثل أن يقولا روى الزهري عن فلان ويسوقا اسناده الصحيح فحال الكتابين يوجب أن ذلك من الصحيح عندهما وكذلك ما روياه عمن ذكراه بلفظ مبهم لم يعرف به وأورداه أصلا محتجين به وذلك مثل حدثني بعض أصحابنا ونحو ذلك قال وذكر الحافظ أبو على الغساني الجياني أن الانقطاع وقع فيما رواه مسلم في كتابه في أربعة عشر موضعا أولها في التيمم قوله في حديث أبي الجهم وروى الليث بن سعد ثم قوله في كتاب # # الصلاة فى باب الصلاة على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم حدثنا صاحب لنا عن إسماعيل بن زكريا عن الاعمش وهذا فى رواية أبى العلاء بن ماهان وسلمت رواة أبى أحمد الجلودى من هذا فقال فيه مسلم حدثنا محمد بن بكار قال حدثنا إسماعيل بن زكريا ثم فى باب السكوت بين التكبير والقراءة قوله وحدثت عن يحيى بن حسان ويونس المؤدب ثم قوله فى كتاب الجنائز فى حديث عائشة رضى الله عنها في خروج النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إلى البقيع ليلا وحدثني من سمع حجاجا الأعور واللفظ له قال حدثنا بن جريج وقوله فى باب الحوائج فى حديث عائشة رضى الله عنها حدثنى غير واحد من أصحابنا قالوا حدثنا إسماعيل بن أبى أويس وقوله في هذا الباب وروى الليث بن سعد قال حدثني جعفر بن ربيعة وذكر حديث كعب بن مالك في تقاضي بن أبي حدرد وقوله في باب احتكار الطعام في حديث معمر بن عبد الله العدوي حدثني بعض أصحابنا عن عمرو بن عون وقوله في صفة النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وحدثت عن أبي أسامة وممن روى ذلك عنه ابراهيم بن سعيد الجوهري قال حدثنا أبو اسامة وذكر أبو علي أنه رواه أبو أحمد الجلودي عن محمد بن المسيب الارغيابي عن ابراهيم بن سعيد قال الشيخ وريناه من غير طريق أحمد عن محمد بن المسيب ورواه غير بن المسيب عن ابراهيم الجوهري وسنورد ذلك في موضعه ان شاء الله تعالى وقوله في آخر الفضائل في حديث بن عمر رضي الله عنهما عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم (أرأيتكم ليلتكم هذه) رواية مسلم اياه موصولا عن معمر عن الزهري عن سالم عن أبيه ثم قال حدثني عبد الله بن عبد الرحمن الدارمي قال أخبرنا أبو اليمان قال أخبرنا شعيب ورواه الليث عن عبد الرحمن بن خالد بن مسافر كلاهما عن الزهري باسناد معمر كمثل حديثه وقول مسلم في آخر كتاب القدر في حديث أبي سعيد الخدري رضي الله عنه (لتركبن سنن من قبلكم) حدثني عدة من أصحابنا عن سعيد بن أبي مريم وهذا قد وصله ابراهيم بن محمد بن سفيان عن محمد بن يحيى عن بن أبي أبي مريم قال الشيخ وانما أورده مسلم على وجه المتابعة والاستشهاد وقوله فيما سبق في الاستشهاد والمتابعة في حديث البراء بن عازب في الصلاة الوسطى بعد أن رواه موصولا ورواه الاشجعي عن سفيان الثوري إلى آخره وقوله أيضا في الرجم في المتابعة لما رواه موصولا من حديث أبي هريرة في الذي اعترف على نفسه بالزنى ورواه # # الليث أيضا عن عبد الرحمن بن خالد بن مسافر عن بن شهاب بهذا الاسناد وقوله في كتاب الامارة في المتابعة لما رواه متصلا من حديث عوف بن مالك (خيار أئمتكم الذين تحبونهم) ورواه معاوية بن صالح عن ربيعة بن يزيد قال الشيخ وذكر أبو علي فيما رواه عندنا من كتابه في الرابع عشر حديث بن عمر (أرأيتكم ليلتكم هذه) المذكور في الفضائل وقد ذكره مرة أخرى فيسقط هذا من العدد ويسقط الحديث الثاني لكون الجلودي رواه عن مسلم موصولا وروايته هي المعتمدة المشهورة فهي اذا اثنا عشر لا أربعة عشر قال الشيخ وأخذ هذا عن أبي على أبو عبد الله المازري صاحب المعلم فأطلق أن هذا في الكتاب أحاديث مقطوعة في أربعة عشر موضعا وهذا يوهم خللا في ذلك وليس ذلك كذلك وليس شيء من هذا والحمد لله مخرجا لما وجد فيه من حيز الصحيح بل هي موصولة من جهات صحيحة لا سيما ما كان منها مذكورا على وجه المتابعة في نفس الكتاب وصلها فاكتفى بكون ذلك معروفا عند أهل الحديث كما انه روى عن جماعة من الضعفاء اعتمادا على كون ما رواه عنهم معروفا من رواية الثقات على ما سنرويه عنه فيما بعد ان شاء الله تعالى قال الشيخ أبو عمرو رحمه الله وهكذا الأمر في تعليقات البخاري بألفاظ جازمة مثبتة على الصفة التي ذكرناها كمثل ما قال فيه قال فلان أو روى فلان أو ذكر فلان أو نحو ذلك ولم يصب أبو محمد بن حزم
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ق-ط-ع (qaṭaʿa)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To cut off, sever, interrupt; denotes a break in continuity.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In ḥadīth terminology, an interrupted chain (munqaṭiʿ) lacks full connectivity between transmitter and the Prophet ﷺ, affecting its grade.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal severance vs. technical usage — here metaphorical for a missing link in transmission.
- Root: ع-ل-ق (ʿallaqa)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To suspend, hang; something attached but not firmly fixed.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Technical term for a ḥadīth cited without a complete chain, often abbreviated.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal hanging vs. technical — a suspended narration, not fully grounded.
- Root: و-ص-ل (waṣala)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To join, connect, reach.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Connected chain (muttaṣil) — full continuity of transmission.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal joining vs. technical — unbroken isnād.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clause (al-Sharṭ) — The phrase "if it is with a decisive wording" (fa-idhā kāna bi-lafẓ fīhi jazm) establishes a conditional framework governing the legal status of the narration.
chapters.translation:
I say: Despite this, his book (Muslim's Ṣaḥīḥ) contains ḥadīths whose chains or texts have been disputed, yet they are authentic in his view. In this, there was an oversight on his part regarding this condition, or another cause. I have noted and critiqued this. This concludes the words of the Shaykh (may Allah have mercy on him).

---

**Section**

The Shaykh, the Imām, Abū ʿAmr ibn al-Ṣalāḥ (may Allah have mercy on him) said: What occurs in the two Ṣaḥīḥs of al-Bukhārī and Muslim in the form of an interrupted chain (munqaṭiʿ) is not to be classified as truly interrupted, such that it would move from the realm of authentic (ṣaḥīḥ) to weak (ḍaʿīf). This type is called taʿlīq (suspension), a term coined by the Imām Abū al-Ḥasan al-Dāraquṭnī. Al-Ḥumaydī mentions it in his compilation of the two Ṣaḥīḥs, as do other Andalusian scholars. It is very frequent in al-Bukhārī's book and very rare in Muslim's book.

He said: When such a taʿlīq occurs from them with a decisive wording (lafẓ jāzim), indicating that the one between them and the point of interruption actually said or narrated it, and the chain is connected according to the stipulated condition — such as when they say, "Al-Zuhrī narrated from so-and-so," and they cite his authentic chain — then the status of the two books necessitates that this is authentic in their view. Likewise, what they narrated from someone mentioned with an ambiguous wording (mubham), not identified, and they cited it as a foundational proof — such as "Some of our companions narrated to me" and the like.

He said: The Ḥāfiẓ Abū ʿAlī al-Ghassānī al-Jayyānī mentioned that interruption occurred in what Muslim narrated in his book in fourteen places. The first is in the chapter on tayammum, in his statement in the ḥadīth of Abū al-Jahm: "Al-Layth ibn Saʿd narrated." Then his statement in the Book of Prayer, in the chapter on sending prayers upon the Prophet ﷺ: "A companion of ours narrated to us from Ismāʿīl ibn Zakariyyā from al-Aʿmash." This is in the narration of Abū al-ʿAlāʾ ibn Māhān, and the narrators of Abū Aḥmad al-Julūdī are exempted from this, for Muslim said therein: "Muḥammad ibn Bakkār narrated to us, he said: Ismāʿīl ibn Zakariyyā narrated to us." Then in the chapter on silence between the takbīr and the recitation, his statement: "I was narrated from Yaḥyā ibn Ḥassān and Yūnus al-Muʾaddib." Then his statement in the Book of Funerals, in the ḥadīth of ʿĀʾishah (may Allah be pleased with her) regarding the Prophet's ﷺ going out to al-Baqīʿ at night: "And the one who heard Ḥajjāj al-Aʿwar narrated to me — and the wording is his — he said: Ibn Jurayj narrated to us." And his statement in the chapter on needs, in the ḥadīth of ʿĀʾishah (may Allah be pleased with her): "More than one of our companions narrated to me, they said: Ismāʿīl ibn Abī Uways narrated to us." And his statement in this chapter: "Al-Layth ibn Saʿd narrated, he said: Jaʿfar ibn Rabīʿah narrated to me," mentioning the ḥadīth of Kaʿb ibn Mālik regarding the debt of Ibn Abī Ḥadrad. And his statement in the chapter on hoarding food, in the ḥadīth of Maʿmar ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-ʿAdawī: "Some of our companions narrated to me from ʿAmr ibn ʿAwn." And his statement in the description of the Prophet ﷺ: "I was narrated from Abū Usāmah," and among those who narrated it from him is Ibrāhīm ibn Saʿīd al-Jawharī, who said: "Abū Usāmah narrated to us." Abū ʿAlī mentioned that Abū Aḥmad al-Julūdī narrated it from Muḥammad ibn al-Musayyab al-Arghiyābī from Ibrāhīm ibn Saʿīd. The Shaykh said: We narrated it via a path other than Aḥmad from Muḥammad ibn al-Musayyab, and others besides Ibn al-Musayyab narrated it from Ibrāhīm al-Jawharī. We will present this in its proper place, Allah willing.

And his statement at the end of the Virtues (al-Faḍāʾil), in the ḥadīth of Ibn ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with them both) from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: {«أرأيتكم ليلتكم هذه»} ("Do you see this night of yours?") — Muslim's narration of it as connected (mawṣūl) from Maʿmar from al-Zuhrī from Sālim from his father. Then he said: ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Dārimī narrated to me, he said: Abū al-Yamān informed us, he said: Shuʿayb informed us, and al-Layth narrated it from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Khālid ibn Musāfir — both from al-Zuhrī with the same chain as Maʿmar's narration, like his ḥadīth.

And Muslim's statement at the end of the Book of Divine Decree (Qadar), in the ḥadīth of Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī (may Allah be pleased with him): {«لتركبن سنن من قبلكم»} ("You will surely follow the ways of those before you") — "Several of our companions narrated to me from Saʿīd ibn Abī Maryam." This was connected by Ibrāhīm ibn Muḥammad ibn Sufyān from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā from Ibn Abī Maryam. The Shaykh said: Muslim only cited it by way of corroboration (mutābaʿah) and witness (istishhād).

And his statement in what preceded regarding witness and corroboration, in the ḥadīth of al-Barāʾ ibn ʿĀzib concerning the middle prayer (al-ṣalāt al-wusṭā), after narrating it as connected — and al-Ashjaʿī narrated it from Sufyān al-Thawrī, to the end. And his statement also in the chapter on stoning (rajm), in the corroboration of what he narrated as connected from the ḥadīth of Abū Hurayrah regarding the man who confessed to adultery — and al-Layth also narrated it from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Khālid ibn Musāfir from Ibn Shihāb with this chain.

And his statement in the Book of Leadership (Imārah), in the corroboration of what he narrated as connected from the ḥadīth of ʿAwf ibn Mālik: {«خيار أئمتكم الذين تحبونهم»} ("The best of your rulers are those whom you love") — and Muʿāwiyah ibn Ṣāliḥ narrated it from Rabīʿah ibn Yazīd.

The Shaykh said: Abū ʿAlī mentioned, in what he narrated to us from his book, that the fourteenth is the ḥadīth of Ibn ʿUmar {«أرأيتكم ليلتكم هذه»} ("Do you see this night of yours?") mentioned in the Virtues — and he had mentioned it once before, so this one drops from the count. And the second ḥadīth also drops, because al-Julūdī narrated it from Muslim as connected, and his narration is the relied-upon and well-known one. Thus they are twelve, not fourteen.

The Shaykh said: Abū ʿAbd Allāh al-Māzarī, author of al-Muʿlim, took this from Abū ʿAlī and stated that in the book there are interrupted ḥadīths in fourteen places. This gives the false impression of a defect therein, but that is not the case. None of this — praise be to Allah — removes what is found therein from the realm of authenticity. Rather, they are connected through sound paths, especially those mentioned by way of corroboration within the book itself, for he connected them and sufficed with their being known among the scholars of ḥadīth. Just as he narrated from a group of weak narrators, relying on the fact that what he narrated from them is known through the narrations of trustworthy transmitters, as we will narrate from him later, Allah willing.

The Shaykh Abū ʿAmr (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Such is the case with al-Bukhārī's taʿlīqāt with decisive, affirmative wordings on the description we have mentioned — such as his saying therein: "So-and-so said," or "So-and-so narrated," or "So-and-so mentioned," and the like. And Abū Muḥammad ibn Ḥazm was not correct in [his criticism of this].

chapters.title_en: The Commentary on Sahih Muslim — Section 9: On the Categorical Certainty of What al-Bukhārī and Muslim Deemed Authentic, and the Refutation of Ibn Ḥazm's Claim of Interruption (Inqiṭāʿ)
chapters.arabic_text: الظاهري حيث جعل مثل ذلك انقطاعا قادحا في الصحة واستروح إلى ذلك في تقرير مذهبه الفاسد في اباحة الملاهي وزعمه انه لم يصح في تحريمها حديث مجيبا عن حديث أبي عامر أو أبى مالك الأشعري عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم (ليكونن في أمتي أقوام يستحلون الحرير والخمر والمعازف) إلى آخر الحديث فزعم أنه وان أخرجه البخاري فهو غير صحيح لان البخاري قال فيه قال هشام بن عمار وساقه باسناده فهو منقطع فيما بين البخاري وهشام وهذا خطأ من بن حزم من وجوه أحدها أنه لا انقطاع في هذا أصلا من جهة أن البخارى لقى هشاما وسمع منه وقد قررنا فى كتابنا علوم الحديث أنه اذا تحقق اللقاء والسماع مع السلامة من التدليس حمل ما يرويه عنه على السماع بأى لفظ كان كما يحمل قول الصحابى قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم على سماعه منه اذا لم يظهر خلافه وكذا غير قال من الالفاظ الثانى أن هذا الحديث بعينه معروف الاتصال بصريح لفظه من غير جهة البخارى الثالث أنه إن كان ذلك انقطاعا فمثل ذلك فى الكتابين غير ملحق بالانقطاع القادح لما عرف # # من عادتهما وشرطهما وذكرهما ذلك فى كتاب موضوع لذكر الصحيح خاصة فلن يستجيرا فيه الجزم المذكور من غير ثبت وثبوت بخلاف الانقطاع أو الارسال الصادر من غيرهما هذا كله فى المعلق بلفظ الجزم أما اذا لم يكن ذلك منهما بلفظ جازم مثبت له عمن ذاكره عنه على الصفة التى تقدم ذكرها مثل أن يقولا روى عن فلان أو ذكر عن فلان أو في الباب عن فلان ونحو ذلك فليس ذلك في حكم التعليق الذي ذكرناه ولكن يستأنس بإيرادهما له وأما قول مسلم في خطبة كتابه وقد ذكر عن عائشة رضي الله عنها أنها قالت (أمرنا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أن ننزل الناس منازلهم) فهذا بالنظر إلى أن لفظه ليس جازما لا يقتضي حكمه بصحته وبالنظر إلى أنه احتج به وأورده ايراد الاصول لا ايراد الشواهد يقتضى حكمه بصحته ومع ذلك فقد حكم الحاكم أبو عبد الله الحافظ في كتابه كتاب معرفة علوم الحديث بصحته وأخرجه أبو داود في سننه باسناده منفردا به وذكر أن الراوي له عن عائشة ميمون بن أبي شبيب ولم يدركها قال الشيخ وفيما قاله أبو داود نظر فانه كوفى متقدم قد أدرك المغيرة بن شعبة ومات المغيرة قبل عائشة وعند مسلم التعاصر مع امكان التلاقي كاف في ثبوت الادراك فلو ورد عن ميمون أنه قال لم ألق عائشة استقام لابي داود الجزم بعدم ادراكه وهيهات ذلك هذا آخر كلام الشيخ قلت وحديث عائشة هذا قد رواه البزار في مسنده وقال هذا الحديث لا يعلم عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إلا من هذا الوجه وقد روى عن عائشة من غير هذا الوجه موقوفا والله أعلم | | فصل # ) # قال الشيخ أبو عمرو بن الصلاح رحمه الله جميع ما حكم مسلم رحمه الله بصحته فى هذا الكتاب فهو مقطوع بصحته والعلم النظرى حاصل بصحته فى نفس الأمر وهكذا ما حكم البخارى بصحته فى كتابه وذلك لان الأمة تلقت ذلك بالقبول سوى من لا يعتد بخلافه ووفاقه فى الاجماع قال الشيخ والذى نختاره أن تلقى الأمة للخبر المنحط عن درجة التواتر بالقبول يوجب العلم النظرى بصدقه خلافا لبعض محققى الاصوليين حيث نفى ذلك بناء على أنه لا يفيد فى حق كل منهم الا الظن وانما قبله لانه يجب عليه العمل بالظن والظن قد يخطىء قال الشيخ وهذا مندفع لان ظن من هو معصوم من الخطأ لا يخطىء والامة في اجماعها معصومة من الخطأ وقد قال امام الحرمين لو حلف انسان بطلاق امرأته أن ما في كتابي البخاري ومسلم مما حكما بصحته من قول النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لما ألزمته الطلاق ولا حنثته لاجماع علماء المسلمين # # على صحتها قال الشيخ ولقائل أن يقول انه لا يحنث ولو لم يجمع المسلمون على صحتها للشك في الحنث فانه لو حلف بذلك في حديث ليست هذه صفته لم يحنث وان كان راويه فاسقا فعدم الحنث حاصل قبل الاجماع فلا يضاف إلى الاجماع قال الشيخ والجواب أن المضاف إلى الاجماع هو القطع بعدم الحنث ظاهرا وباطنا وأما عند الشك فعدم الحنث محكوم به ظاهرا مع احتمال وجوده باطنا فعلى هذا يحمل كلام امام الحرمين فهو اللائق بتحقيقه فاذا علم هذا فما أخذ على البخاري ومسلم وقدح فيه معتمد من الحفاظ فهو مستنثى مما ذكرناه لعدم الاجماع على تلقيه بالقبول وما ذلك الا في مواضع قليلة سننبة على ما وقع في هذا الكتاب منها ان شاء الله تعالى وهذا آخر ما ذكره الشيخ أبو عمرو رحمه الله هنا وقال في جزء له ما اتفق البخاري ومسلم على اخراجه فهو مقطوع بصدق مخبره ثابت يقينا لتلقى الأمة ذلك بالقبول وذلك يفيد العلم النظري وهو في افادة العلم كالمتواتر الا أن المتواتر يفيد العلم الضروري وتلقى الامة بالقبول يفيد العلم النظري وقد اتفقت الأمة على أن ما اتفق البخاري ومسلم على صحته فهو حق وصدق قال الشيخ في علوم الحديث وقد كنت أميل إلى أن ما اتفقنا عليه فهو مظنون وأحسبه مذهبا قويا وقد بان لي الآن أنه ليس كذلك وان الصواب أنه يفيد العلم وهذا الذي ذكره الشيخ في هذه المواضع خلاف ما قاله
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ق-ط-ع (qa-ṭā-ʿ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Severance, cutting off; in ḥadīth terminology, a break in the chain of transmission (inqiṭāʿ) that impugns authenticity.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In uṣūl al-ḥadīth, inqiṭāʿ denotes a discontinuity in the isnād, undermining the probative force of the report; contrasted with ittiṣāl (continuity).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal severance (cutting a rope) versus technical rupture in transmission; here used metaphorically for a defect in the chain.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clause with Implied Apodosis (Sharṭ maʿa jawāb maḥdhūf) — In "إذا تحقق اللقاء والسماع... حمل ما يرويه عنه على السماع" the protasis governs a general ruling, with the apodosis elliptically rendered for rhetorical emphasis.
chapters.translation:
I say: The Ẓāhirī [Ibn Ḥazm] — may God forgive him — made such a thing an interruption (inqiṭāʿ) that vitiates authenticity, and he sought comfort in that for establishing his corrupt doctrine permitting musical instruments (malāhī), claiming that no authentic report had reached him prohibiting them, in response to the ḥadīth of Abū ʿĀmir or Abū Mālik al-Ashʿarī — may God be pleased with him — from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: {«ليكونن في أمتي أقوام يستحلون الحرير والخمر والمعازف»} ("There will indeed be among my nation peoples who deem lawful silk, wine, and musical instruments") to the end of the ḥadīth. He then claimed that even though al-Bukhārī transmitted it, it is not authentic, because al-Bukhārī said therein: "Hishām ibn ʿAmmār said" and he cited it with his chain — so it is interrupted (munqaṭiʿ) between al-Bukhārī and Hishām. This is an error on the part of Ibn Ḥazm on several counts:

**First:** There is no interruption here at all, because al-Bukhārī met Hishām and heard from him. We have already established in our book *ʿUlūm al-Ḥadīth* that when meeting (liqāʾ) and hearing (samāʿ) are verified, along with freedom from tadlīs (concealment), whatever he narrates from him is construed as heard (samāʿ), regardless of the wording used — just as the Companion's saying "The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said" is construed as his having heard it from him, when no contrary indication appears. Likewise for other expressions among the [various] wordings.

**Second:** This very ḥadīth is known to be continuous (muttaṣil) with explicit wording, from other than al-Bukhārī's path.

**Third:** Even if that were an interruption, such a thing in the two books [al-Bukhārī and Muslim] is not classed as a vitiating interruption, given what is known of their practice and condition, and their mention of such in a book composed specifically for authentic reports — for they would not employ the aforementioned categorical assertion (jazm) without firm proof and confirmation, unlike an interruption or irsāl (suspension) issuing from other than them. All this concerns the muʿallaq (suspended) report with a categorical wording (ṣīghat al-jazm). As for when it is not from them with a categorical wording affirming it from the one mentioned, in the manner previously described — such as their saying "narrated from so-and-so," or "mentioned from so-and-so," or "in this chapter from so-and-so," and the like — then that is not in the ruling of the muʿallaq we mentioned, but one seeks comfort (yastaʾnis) in their citing it.

As for Muslim's statement in the preface of his book, where he mentioned from ʿĀʾishah — may God be pleased with her — that she said: {«أمرنا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أن ننزل الناس منازلهم»} ("The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, commanded us to place people in their stations") — this, considering that its wording is not categorical, does not necessitate a ruling of its authenticity; but considering that he adduced it as evidence and cited it as one cites foundational principles (uṣūl), not as one cites supporting witnesses (shawāhid), it does necessitate a ruling of its authenticity. Moreover, al-Ḥākim Abū ʿAbd Allāh al-Ḥāfiẓ ruled in his book *Maʿrifat ʿUlūm al-Ḥadīth* that it is authentic, and Abū Dāwūd transmitted it in his *Sunan* with his chain, alone in doing so, and mentioned that the narrator of it from ʿĀʾishah is Maymūn ibn Abī Shabīb, who did not meet her.

The Shaykh [Ibn al-Ṣalāḥ] said: In what Abū Dāwūd said there is consideration, for he [Maymūn] is an early Kūfan who met al-Mughīrah ibn Shuʿbah, and al-Mughīrah died before ʿĀʾishah. And with Muslim, contemporaneity (muʿāṣarah) with the possibility of meeting is sufficient to establish perception (idrāk). So had it been reported from Maymūn that he said "I did not meet ʿĀʾishah," it would have been proper for Abū Dāwūd to assert categorically his non-perception — but far be it from that! This is the end of the Shaykh's words.

I say: This ḥadīth of ʿĀʾishah has been transmitted by al-Bazzār in his *Musnad*, and he said: "This ḥadīth is not known from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, except from this path." And it has been transmitted from ʿĀʾishah from other than this path as mauqūf (stopped at her). And God knows best.

---

**CHAPTER**

The Shaykh Abū ʿAmr ibn al-Ṣalāḥ — may God have mercy on him — said: Everything that Muslim — may God have mercy on him — ruled authentic in this book, it is categorically certain in its authenticity, and theoretical knowledge (al-ʿilm al-naẓarī) is attained of its authenticity in actual fact. Likewise, what al-Bukhārī ruled authentic in his book — because the ummah received that with acceptance (al-qabūl), except for one whose opposition and agreement are not counted in consensus (ijmāʿ).

The Shaykh said: What we choose is that the ummah's reception of a report that falls below the degree of tawātur (mass transmission) with acceptance necessitates theoretical knowledge of its truthfulness — contrary to some of the verifying uṣūliyyūn (scholars of legal theory) who denied this, on the basis that it yields for each of them only conjecture (ẓann), and he accepted it only because acting upon conjecture is obligatory, and conjecture may err.

The Shaykh said: This is refuted, because the conjecture of one who is protected from error does not err, and the ummah in its consensus is protected from error. Imām al-Ḥaramayn [al-Juwaynī] said: If a man swore by the divorce of his wife that what is in the two books of al-Bukhārī and Muslim, of what they ruled authentic from the sayings of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, [is true], I would not impose divorce upon him nor deem him guilty of perjury, due to the consensus of Muslim scholars upon their authenticity.

The Shaykh said: One might object that he would not be deemed guilty of perjury even if the Muslims had not reached consensus upon their authenticity, due to doubt in perjury — for if he swore by that concerning a ḥadīth not having this description, he would not be deemed guilty, even if its narrator were a sinner. Thus non-perjury is established before consensus, so it should not be attributed to consensus.

The Shaykh said: The answer is that what is attributed to consensus is the categorical certainty of non-perjury, outwardly and inwardly. As for when there is doubt, non-perjury is ruled outwardly, with the possibility of its existence inwardly. Upon this is Imām al-Ḥaramayn's statement to be construed — it is befitting of his verification.

When this is known, then whatever has been objected against al-Bukhārī and Muslim, and impugned with a reliable [criticism] from the ḥuffāẓ (master ḥadīth scholars), is excepted from what we mentioned, due to the absence of consensus upon receiving it with acceptance. And that is only in a few places, which we shall point out regarding what occurred in this book — among them, God willing. This is the end of what the Shaykh Abū ʿAmr — may God have mercy on him — mentioned here.

And he said in a separate treatise (juzʾ): What al-Bukhārī and Muslim have agreed upon transmitting is categorically certain in the truthfulness of its informant, firmly established with certainty, due to the ummah's reception of it with acceptance. And that yields theoretical knowledge — it is, in yielding knowledge, like the mutawātir, except that the mutawātir yields necessary knowledge (al-ʿilm al-ḍarūrī), while the ummah's reception with acceptance yields theoretical knowledge. And the ummah has agreed that what al-Bukhārī and Muslim have agreed upon as authentic is true and veracious.

The Shaykh said in *ʿUlūm al-Ḥadīth*: I used to incline toward the view that what they both agreed upon is conjectural, and I reckoned it a strong doctrine; but it has now become clear to me that it is not so, and that the correct view is that it yields knowledge. And what the Shaykh mentioned in these places contradicts what he said [elsewhere].

chapters.title_en: The Certainty Value of the Two Ṣaḥīḥs and the Distinction Between Them and Other Hadith Collections
chapters.arabic_text: المحققون والاكثرون فانهم قالوا أحاديث الصحيحين التي ليست بمتواترة انما تفيد الظن فإنها آحاد والآحاد انما تفيد الظن على ما تقرر ولا فرق بين البخاري ومسلم وغيرهما في ذلك وتلقى الأمة بالقبول انما أفادنا وجوب العمل بما فيهما وهذا متفق عليه فان أخبار الآحاد التي في غيرهما يجب العمل بها اذا صحت أسانيدها ولا تفيد الا الظن فكذا الصحيحان وانما يفترق الصحيحان وغيرهما من الكتب في كون ما فيهما صحيحا لا يحتاج إلى النظر فيه بل يجب العمل به مطلقا وما كان في غيرهم لا يعمل به حتى ينظر وتوجد فيه شروط الصحيح ولا يلزم من اجماع الأمة على العمل بما فيهما اجماعهم على أنه مقطوع بأنه كلام النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وقد اشتد انكار بن برهان الامام على من قال بما قاله الشيخ وبالغ في تغليطه وأما ما قاله الشيخ رحمه الله في تأويل كلام امام الحرمين في عدم الحنث فهو بناء على ما اختاره الشيخ وأما على مذهب الاكثرين فيحتمل أنه أراد أنه لا يحنث ظاهرا ولا يستحب له التزام الحنث حتى تستحب له الرجعة كما لو حلف بمثل ذلك في غير الصحيحين فانا لا نحنثه لكن # # تستحب له الرجعة احتياطا لاحتمال الحنث وهو ظاهر وأما الصحيحان فاحتمال الحنث فيهما في غاية من الضعف فلا تستحب له المراجعة لضعف احتمال موجبها والله أعلم | | فصل # ) # قال الشيخ أبو عمرو رحمه الله روينا عن أبي قريش الحافظ قال كنت عند أبي زرعة الرازي فجاء مسلم بن الحجاج فسلم عليه وجلس ساعة وتذاكرا فلما قام قلت له هذا جمع أربعة آلاف حديث في الصحيح قال أبو زرعة فلمن ترك الباقي قال الشيخ أراد أن كتابه هذا أربعة آلاف حديث أصول دون المكررات وكذا كتاب البخاري ذكر أنه أربعة آلاف حديث باسقاط المكرر وبالمكرر سبعة آلاف ومائتان وخمسة وسبعون حديثا ثم ان مسلما رحمه الله رتب كتابه على أبواب فهو مبوب في الحقيقة ولكنه لم يذكر تراجم الابواب فيه لئلا يزداد بها حجم الكتاب أو لغير ذلك قلت وقد ترجم جماعة أبوابه بتراجم بعضها جيد وبعضها ليس بجيد إما لقصور في عبارة الترجمة واما لركاكة لفظها واما لغير ذلك وانا ان شاء الله أحرص على التعبير عنها بعبارات تلييق بها في مواطنها والله أعلم فصل سلك مسلم رحمه الله في صحيحه طرقا بالغة في الاحتياط والاتقان والورع والمعرفة وذلك مصرح بكمال ورعة وتمام معرفته وغزارة علومه وشدة تحقيقه بحفظه وتقعدده في هذا الشأن وتمكنه من أنواع معارفه وتبريزه في صناعته وعلو محله في التمييز بين دقائق علومه لا يهتدي اليها الا أفراد في الاعصار فرحمه الله ورضى عنه وأنا أذكره أحرفا من أمثلة ذلك تنبيها بها على ماسواها اذ لا يعرف حقيقة حاله الا من أحسن النظر في كتابه مع كمال أهليته ومعرفته بأنواع العلوم التي يفتقر اليها صاحب هذه الصناعة كالفقه والأصولين والعربية وأسماء الرجال ودقائق علم الاسانيد والتاريخ ومعاشرة أهل هذه الصنعة ومباحثتهم ومع حسن الفكر ونباهة الذهن ومداومة الاشتغال به وغير ذلك من الادوات التي يفتقر اليها فمن تحري مسلم رحمه الله اعتناؤه بالتمييز بين حدثنا وأخبرنا وتقييده ذلك على مشايخه وفي روايته وكان من مذهبه رحمه الله الفرق بينهما وأن حدثنا لا يجوز اطلاقه الا لما سمعه من لفظ الشيخ خاصة وأخبرنا لما قرئ على الشيخ وهذا الفرق هو مذهب الشافعي وأصحابه وجمهور أهل العلم بالمشرق قال محمد بن الحسن الجوهري المصري وهو مذهب أكثر أصحاب الحديث الذين لا يحصيهم أحد وروى هذا المذهب أيضا عن بن جريج والاوزاعي وبن وهب والنسائي وصار هو الشائع الغالب على أهل #
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ق-ط-ع (qaṭaʿa)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To cut off, sever; hence decisive certainty (qaṭʿ) that admits no doubt.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Definitiveness in epistemic terms — that which is established beyond any possibility of error or conjecture (ẓann).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense of severance; metaphorically applied to knowledge that "cuts off" all contrary possibility.
- Root: ظ-ن-ن (ẓanna)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Doubt, suspicion, or predominant conjecture — the opposite of certainty.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In uṣūl al-fiqh, ẓann is the probabilistic knowledge yielded by solitary reports (āḥād), sufficient for action but not for creedal certainty.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: suspicion; technical: preponderant probability in legal inference.
- Root: ح-ن-ث (ḥanitha)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To break an oath; the state of having violated a vow.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Legal consequence of failing to fulfill an oath — relevant to the discussion of whether swearing by the contents of the Ṣaḥīḥs entails expiation.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: to bend or incline from the straight path; metaphorical: to deviate from one's sworn commitment.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional and Exceptive Constructions (al-sharṭ wa al-istithnāʾ) — The text employs "if... then..." structures (e.g., "if their chains are sound, they must be acted upon") and exceptions ("no difference between Bukhārī and Muslim and others") requiring precise parsing of scope and limitation.
chapters.translation:
I say: The verifiers (al-muḥaqqiqūn) and the majority of scholars (al-aktharūn) — for they held that the hadiths of the two Ṣaḥīḥs which are not mutawātir (mass-transmitted) only yield conjecture (ẓann), for they are solitary reports (āḥād), and solitary reports only yield conjecture, as has been established. There is no distinction in this regard between al-Bukhārī, Muslim, and others. The fact that the Umma received them with acceptance (talaqqat al-umma bil-qabūl) only obligates us to act upon what is contained in them — and this is agreed upon. For the solitary reports found in other collections must be acted upon when their chains are sound, yet they yield nothing but conjecture. So likewise are the two Ṣaḥīḥs. The two Ṣaḥīḥs differ from other books only in that what is contained in them is authentic (ṣaḥīḥ) without needing examination; rather, it is obligatory to act upon it absolutely. What is in other collections is not acted upon until it is examined and the conditions of authenticity are found in it. Nor does the consensus of the Umma on acting upon what is in them entail their consensus that it is definitively (maqṭūʿ bihi) the speech of the Prophet ﷺ. Indeed, Ibn Burhān al-Imām severely denounced those who said what the Shaykh (i.e., al-Ḥaramayn's view as reported) said, and he went to great lengths in declaring them mistaken.

As for what the Shaykh (may Allah have mercy on him) said in interpreting the words of Imām al-Ḥaramayn regarding the non-occurrence of oath-breaking (ʿadam al-ḥinth) — that is based on what the Shaykh himself chose. But according to the majority's position, it is plausible that he meant that he does not break his oath outwardly (ẓāhir), yet it is not recommended for him to commit to breaking the oath such that repentance (rujūʿ) would be recommended for him — just as if he had sworn by something similar in other than the two Ṣaḥīḥs. For we do not declare him an oath-breaker, but repentance is recommended for him as a precaution (iḥtiyāṭ) due to the possibility of oath-breaking — and this is apparent. As for the two Ṣaḥīḥs, the possibility of oath-breaking in them is extremely weak, so recourse (murājaʿah) is not recommended for him due to the weakness of the possibility that would necessitate it. And Allah knows best.

---

CHAPTER

The Shaykh Abū ʿAmr (may Allah have mercy on him) said: We were informed by Abū Quraysh al-Ḥāfiẓ, who said: I was with Abū Zurʿah al-Rāzī when Muslim ibn al-Ḥajjāj came, greeted him, sat for a while, and they conversed. When he stood to leave, I said to him: "This man has collected four thousand hadiths in his Ṣaḥīḥ." Abū Zurʿah said: "Then for whom did he leave the rest?" The Shaykh said: He meant that his book contains four thousand hadiths as principal (uṣūl) without repetitions. Likewise, al-Bukhārī's book is mentioned as containing four thousand hadiths excluding repetitions, and with repetitions seven thousand two hundred and seventy-five hadiths.

Then Muslim (may Allah have mercy on him) arranged his book according to chapters (abwāb), so it is in fact chaptered, but he did not mention the chapter headings (tarājim) in it — either to avoid increasing the book's volume thereby, or for some other reason. I say: Some people have provided chapter headings for its sections, some of which are good and some not good — either due to deficiency in the wording of the heading, or its awkwardness of expression, or for other reasons. And I, Allah willing, will strive to express them with phrases befitting them in their proper places. And Allah knows best.

CHAPTER

Muslim (may Allah have mercy on him) followed in his Ṣaḥīḥ methods that reached the utmost degree of caution (iḥtiyāṭ), precision (itqān), piety (waraʿ), and knowledge (maʿrifah). This is explicit testimony to the completeness of his piety, the perfection of his knowledge, the abundance of his sciences, the intensity of his verification (taḥqīq) through his memory, his preeminence in this field, his mastery of its various types of knowledge, his excellence in his craft, and his lofty station in distinguishing the subtleties of its sciences — which none but rare individuals in each age can perceive. May Allah have mercy on him and be pleased with him. I will mention some examples of that as a pointer to what lies beyond them, for none truly knows his actual state except one who examines his book with excellence, along with complete competence and knowledge of the various sciences that the practitioner of this craft requires — such as jurisprudence (fiqh), the two principles (al-uṣūlayn: uṣūl al-fiqh and uṣūl al-dīn), Arabic language, the science of narrators (asmāʾ al-rijāl), the subtleties of the science of chains (dāqāʾiq ʿilm al-asānīd), history, association with the people of this craft and their debates, sound reflection, sharpness of mind, constant engagement with it, and other tools that are needed.

Among Muslim's (may Allah have mercy on him) meticulousness was his care in distinguishing between "ḥaddathanā" (he narrated to us) and "akhbaranā" (he informed us), and his precise recording of this from his shaykhs and in his own narration. It was his doctrine (may Allah have mercy on him) to differentiate between the two: that "ḥaddathanā" may only be used for what he heard directly from the verbal recitation of the shaykh specifically, while "akhbaranā" is for what was read to the shaykh. This distinction is the doctrine of al-Shāfiʿī and his companions, and the majority of the people of knowledge in the East. Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan al-Jawharī al-Miṣrī said: It is the doctrine of the majority of hadith scholars (aṣḥāb al-ḥadīth) who cannot be counted. This doctrine was also transmitted from Ibn Jurayj, al-Awzāʿī, Ibn Wahb, and al-Nasāʾī. And it became the prevalent and dominant practice among the people of [this field].

chapters.title_en: On the Permissibility of Saying "Ḥaddathanā" When Reading Before a Shaykh, and Related Matters of Precision in Transmission
chapters.arabic_text: # الحديث وذهب جماعات إلى أنه يجوز أن تقول فيما قرئ على الشيخ حدثنا وأخبرنا وهو مذهب الزهري ومالك وسفيان بن عيينة ويحيى بن سعيد القطان وآخرين من المتقدمين وهو مذهب البخارى وجماعة من المحدثين وهو مذهب معظم الحجازيين والكوفيين وذهبت طائفة إلى أنه لا يجوز اطلاق حدثنا ولا أخبرنا فى القراءة وهو مذهب بن المبارك ويحيى بن يحيى وأحمد بن حنبل والمشهور عن النسائى والله أعلم ومن ذلك اعتناؤه بضبط اختلاف لفظ الرواة كقوله حدثنا فلان وفلان واللفظ لفلان قال أو قالا حدثنا فلان وكما اذا كان بينهما اختلاف فى حرف من متن الحديث أو صفة الراوى أونسبه أونحو ذلك فانه يبينه وربما كان بعضه لا يتغير به معنى وربما كان فى بعضه اختلاف فى المعنى ولكن كان خفيا لا يتفطن له الا ماهر فى العلوم التى ذكرتها فى أول الفصل مع اطلاع على دقائق الفقه ومذاهب الفقهاء وسترى فى هذا الشرح من فوائد ذلك ما تقر به عينيك ان شاء الله تعالى وينبغى أن ندقق النظر فى فهم غرض مسلم من ذلك ومن ذلك تحريه فى رواية صحيفة همام بن منبه عن أبى هريرة كقوله حدثنا محمد بن رافع قال حدثنا عبد الرزاق حدثنا معمر عن همام قال هذا ما حدثنا أبو هريرة عن محمد رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فذكر أحاديث منها وقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم (إذا توضأ أحدكم فليستنشق) الحديث وذلك لان الصحائف والاجزاء والكتب المشتملة على أحاديث باسناد واحد اذا اقتصر عند سماعها على ذكر الاسناد فى أولها ولم يجدد عند كل حديث منها وأوراد انسان ممن سمع كذلك أن يفرد حديثنا منها غير الاول بالاسناد المذكور فى أولها فهل يجوز له ذلك قال وكيع بن الجراح ويحيى بن معين وأبو بكر الاسماعيلى الشافعى الامام فى الحديث والفقه والأصول يجوز ذلك وهذا مذهب الاكثرين من العلماء لأن الجميع معطوف على الاول فالاسناد المذكور أولا في حكم المعاد في كل حديث وقال الاستاذ أبو إسحاق الاسفراينى الفقيه الشافعي الامام في علم الاصولين والفقه وغير ذلك لا يجوز ذلك فعلى هذا من سمع هكذا فطريقه أن يبين ذلك كما فعله مسلم فمسلم رحمه الله سلك هذا الطريق ورعا واحتياطا وتحريا واتقانا رضى الله عنه ومن ذلك تحريه في مثل قوله حدثنا عبد الله بن مسلمة حدثنا سليمان يعنى بن بلال عن يحيى وهو بن سعيد فلم يستجز رضى الله عنه أن يقول سليمان بن بلال عن يحيى بن سعيد لكون لم يقع في روايته منسوبا فلو قاله منسوبا لكان مخبرا عن شيخه أنه أخبره بنسبه # # ولم يخبره وسأذكره هذا بعد هذا في | | فصل # مختص به ان شاء الله تعالى ومن ذلك احتياطه في تلخيص الطرق وتحول الاسانيد مع ايجاز العبارة وكمال حسنها ومن ذلك حسن ترتيبه وترصيفه الأحاديث على نسق يقتضيه تحقيقه وكمال معرفته بمواقع الخطاب ودقائق العلم وأصول القواعد وخفيات علم الاسانيد ومراتب الرواة وغير ذلك # (فصل)
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ق-ر-أ (Q-R-ʾ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning is "to read/recite," but in transmission contexts it denotes the act of a student reading a text aloud before a teacher for verification (al-qirāʾah ʿalā al-shaykh).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In ḥadīth methodology, qirāʾah is a recognized mode of audition (wajh min wujūh al-taḥammul), distinct from samāʿ (direct hearing from the shaykh's dictation).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense is "reading"; metaphorical extension applies it to the entire process of receiving and transmitting a ḥadīth through this method.
- Root: ح-د-ث (Ḥ-D-Th)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Root denotes newness, origination (ḥudūth), and by extension "speaking/reporting" (taḥdīth).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In transmission terminology, ḥaddathanā ("he narrated to us") is a high-precision formula (ṣīghat al-adāʾ) indicating direct auditory reception.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: "he caused us to hear a report." Metaphorical: used even when the student read to the teacher, as the teacher's approval makes the report "his" narration.
- Root: ن-ب-أ (N-B-ʾ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Root means "to inform" (inbāʾ); akhbaranā is a transmission formula of similar rank to ḥaddathanā.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In ḥadīth science, akhbaranā is often used interchangeably with ḥaddathanā, though some scholars distinguish them by mode of reception.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: "he informed us." In transmission, it is a formal declaration of receipt, whether by reading or dictation.
- Sībawayh Rule: Rule of ʿAṭf (Coordination) — When multiple items are coordinated (maʿṭūf) onto a single antecedent, the grammatical and referential properties of the antecedent extend to all coordinated items. This is the syntactic basis for the majority view that a single isnād mentioned at the beginning of a collection covers all subsequent ḥadīths in that collection.
chapters.translation:
I say: And a group of scholars held that it is permissible for one to say, regarding what was read before the shaykh, "ḥaddathanā" (he narrated to us) and "akhbaranā" (he informed us). This is the school of al-Zuhrī, Mālik, Sufyān ibn ʿUyaynah, Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd al-Qaṭṭān, and others among the early scholars. It is also the school of al-Bukhārī and a group of ḥadīth scholars, and it is the school of most of the Ḥijāzīs and Kūfīs. Another group held that it is not permissible to utter "ḥaddathanā" or "akhbaranā" in the case of reading [before the shaykh]. This is the school of Ibn al-Mubārak, Yaḥyā ibn Yaḥyā, Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal, and the well-known position of al-Nasāʾī. And Allāh knows best.

And from that [precision] is his (Muslim's) care in recording the differences in the wording of the narrators, such as his saying: "Ḥaddathanā so-and-so and so-and-so, and the wording is that of so-and-so," or "they both said: ḥaddathanā so-and-so." Likewise, when there is between them a difference in a letter of the text of the ḥadīth, or in the description of the narrator, or his lineage, or something similar, he clarifies it. Sometimes part of that does not alter the meaning, and sometimes part of it involves a difference in meaning, but it is subtle and is not noticed except by one who is skilled in the sciences I mentioned at the beginning of this chapter, along with insight into the subtleties of jurisprudence (fiqh) and the schools of the jurists. You will see in this commentary, by the permission of Allāh the Exalted, benefits of that which will delight your eyes.

And it behooves us to scrutinize carefully the understanding of Muslim's purpose in that. And from that [precision] is his care in narrating the scroll (ṣaḥīfah) of Hammām ibn Munabbih from Abū Hurayrah, such as his saying: "Ḥaddathanā Muḥammad ibn Rāfiʿ, he said: ḥaddathanā ʿAbd al-Razzāq, he said: ḥaddathanā Maʿmar, from Hammām, he said: This is what Abū Hurayrah narrated to us from Muḥammad, the Messenger of Allāh ﷺ" — then he mentioned ḥadīths from it, among them his saying: "The Messenger of Allāh ﷺ said: {When one of you performs ablution, let him sniff water into his nose} (al-ḥadīth)."

That is because scrolls, sections (ajzāʾ), and books that contain ḥadīths with a single chain of transmission (isnād), when one, upon hearing them, restricts himself to mentioning the isnād at their beginning and does not renew it for each ḥadīth therein — and likewise if a person who heard in this manner wishes to single out one of those ḥadīths, other than the first, with the isnād mentioned at the beginning — is it permissible for him to do so? Wakīʿ ibn al-Jarrāḥ, Yaḥyā ibn Maʿīn, and Abū Bakr al-Ismāʿīlī al-Shāfiʿī — the Imām in ḥadīth, jurisprudence, and uṣūl — said: It is permissible. And this is the school of the majority of scholars, because all [of the ḥadīths] are coordinated (maʿṭūfah) onto the first, so the isnād mentioned at the beginning is, in effect, repeated for every ḥadīth.

And the Ustādh Abū Isḥāq al-Isfarāyīnī — the Shāfiʿī jurist, the Imām in the two uṣūl sciences (uṣūl al-fiqh and uṣūl al-dīn) and other fields — said: That is not permissible. On this view, whoever hears in this manner, his method is to clarify that [situation], just as Muslim did. For Muslim, may Allāh have mercy on him, followed this path out of caution (waraʿ), prudence (iḥtiyāṭ), precision (taḥarrī), and mastery (itqān), may Allāh be pleased with him.

And from that [precision] is his care in such as his saying: "Ḥaddathanā ʿAbd Allāh ibn Maslamah, ḥaddathanā Sulaymān — meaning Ibn Bilāl — from Yaḥyā — and he is Ibn Saʿīd." For he, may Allāh be pleased with him, did not deem it permissible to say "Sulaymān ibn Bilāl from Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd," because in his narration it did not occur with the patronymic (mansūban). Had he said it with the patronymic, he would have been reporting from his shaykh that he informed him of his lineage, when in fact he had not informed him of it. I will mention this after this in a section exclusively devoted to it, if Allāh the Exalted wills.

And from that [precision] is his care in summarizing the chains (ṭuruq) and transforming the isnāds, with brevity of expression and completeness of beauty. And from that is the excellence of his arrangement and his systematic ordering of the ḥadīths in a sequence necessitated by his verification (taḥqīq), his complete knowledge of the loci of discourse (mawāqiʿ al-khiṭāb), the subtleties of knowledge, the foundational principles (uṣūl al-qawāʿid), the hidden aspects of the science of isnāds, the ranks of narrators, and other matters.

(Chapter)

chapters.title_en: Muslim's Division of Hadith into Three Categories and the Scholarly Dispute Regarding His Intent
chapters.arabic_text:
# ذكر مسلم رحمه الله في أول مقدمة صحيحه أنه يقسم الأحاديث ثلاثة أقسام

الاول ما رواه الحفاظ المتقنون والثاني ما رواه المستورون المتوسطون في

الحفظ والاتقان والثالث ما رواه الضعفاء والمتركون وأنه اذا فرع من القسم

الاول أتبعه الثاني وأما الثالث فلا يعرج عليه فاختلف العلماء في مراده

بهذا التقسيم فقال الامامان الحافظان أبو عبد الله الحاكم وصاحبه أبو بكر

البيهقي رحمهما الله أن المنية اخترمت مسلما رحمه الله قبل اخراج القسم

الثاني وانه إنما ذكر القسم الاول قال القاضي عياض رحمه الله وهذا مما قبله

الشيوخ والناس من الحاكم أبي عبد الله وتابعوه عليه قال القاضي وليس الأمر

على ذلك لمن حقق  نظره ولم يتقيد بالتقليد فانك اذا نظرت تقسيم مسلم في

كتابة الحديث على ثلاث طبقات من الناس كما قال فذكر أن القسم الاول حديث

الحفاظ وأنه اذا انقضى هذا أتبعه بأحاديث من لم يوصف بالحذق والاتقان مع

كونهم من أهل الستر والصدق وتعاطى العلم ثم أشار إلى ترك حديث من أجمع

العلماء أو اتفق الاكثر منهم على تهمته ونفى من اتهمه بعضهم وصححه بعضهم

فلم يذكره هنا ووجدته ذكر في أبواب كتابه حديث الطبقتين الاوليين وأتى

بأسانيد الثانية منهما على طريق الاتباع للاولى والاستشهاد أو حيث لم يجد

في الباب الأول شيئا وذكر أقواما تكلم قوم فيهم وزكاهم آخرون وخرج حديثهم

ممن ضعف أو اتهم ببدعة وكذلك فعل البخارى فعندى أنه أتى بطبقاته الثلاث في

كتابه على ما ذكر ورتب في كتابه وبينه في تقسيمه وطرح الرابعة كما نص عليه

فالحاكم تأول أنه إنما أراد أن يفرد لكل طبقة كتابا ويأتى بأحاديها خاصة

مفردة وليس ذلك مراده بل انما أراد بما ظهر من تأليفه وبان من غرضه أن يجمع

ذلك في الأبواب ويأتى بأحاديث الطبقتين فيبدأ بالاولى ثم يأتى بالثانية على

طريق الاستشهاد والاتباع حتى استوفى جميع الاقسام الثلاثة ويحتمل أن يكون

أراد بالطبقات الثلاث الحفاظ ثم الذين يلونهم والثالثة هي التي طرحها وكذلك

علل الحديث التي ذكر ووعد أنه يأتي بها قد جاء بها في مواضعها من
# 
# الأبواب من اختلافهم في الاسانيد كالارسال والاسناد والزيادة والنقص وذكر

تصاحيف المصحفين وهذا يدل على استيفائه غرضه في تأليفه وادخاله في كتابه

كلما وعد به قال القاضي رحمه الله وقد فاوضت في تأويلي هذا ورأيى فيه من

يفهم هذا الباب فما رأيت منصفا الا صوبه وبان له ما ذكرت وهو ظاهر لمن تأمل

الكتاب وطالع مجموع الأبواب ولا يعترض على هذا بما قاله بن سفيان صاحب مسلم

أن مسلما أخرج ثلاثة كتب من المسندات أحدها هذا الذي قرأه على الناس

والثاني يدخل فيه عكرمة وبن إسحاق صاحب المغازي وأمثالها والثالث يدخل فيه 

من الضعفاء فانك اذا تأملت ما ذكر بن سفيان لم يطابق الغرض الذي أشار إليه

الحاكم مما ذكر مسلم في صدر كتابه فتأمله تجده كذلك إن شاء الله تعالى هذا

آخر كلام القاضي عياض رحمه الله وهذا الذي اختاره ظاهر جدا والله اعلم

| فصل
# ألزم الامام الحافظ أبوالحسن على بن عمر الدارقطني رحمه الله وغيره

البخارى ومسلما رضي الله عنهما اخراج احاديث تركا اخراجها مع أن أسانيدها

أسانيد قد أخرجا لرواتها في صحيحهما بها وذكر الدارقطنى وغيره أن جماعة من

الصحابة رضي الله عنهم رووا عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ورويت

أحاديثهم من وجوه صحاح لامطعن في ناقليها ولم يخرجا من أحاديثهم شيئا

فيلزمهما اخراجها على مذهبيهما وذكر البيهقى أنهما اتفقا على أحاديث من

صحيفة همام بن منبه وأن كل واحد منهما انفرد عن الآخر بأحاديث منها مع أن

الاسناد واحد وصنف الدارقطنى وأبو ذر الهروى في هذا النوع الذي ألزموهما

وهذا الالزام ليس بلازم في الحقيقة فانهما لم يلتزما استيعاب الصحيح بل صح

عنهما تصريحهما بأنهما لم يستوعباه وانما قصدا جمع جمل من الصحيح كما يقصد

المصنف في الفقه جمع جملة من مسائله لا أنه يحصر جميع مسائله لكنهما اذا

كان الحديث الذي تركاه أو تركه أحدهما مع صحة اسناده في الظاهر أصلا في

بابه ولم يخرجا له نظيرا ولا ما يقوم مقامه فالظاهر من حالها أنهما اطلعا

فيه على علة ان كانا روياه ويحتمل أنهما تركاه نسيانا أو ايثارا لترك

الاطالة أو رأيا أن غيره مما ذكراه يسد مسده أولغير ذلك والله أعلم فصل عاب

عائبون مسلما بروايته في صحيحه عن جماعة من الضعفاء والمتوسطين الواقعين في

الطبقة الثانية الذين ليسوا من شرط الصحيح ولا عيب عليه في ذلك بل جوابه من

أوجه
#

# ذكرها الشيخ الإمام أبو عمرو بن الصلاح رحمه الله أحدها أن يكون ذلك فيمن

هو ضعيف عند غيره ثقة عنده ولا يقال الجرح مقدم على التعديل لان ذلك فيما

اذا كان الجرح ثابتا  مفسر السبب والا فلا يقبل الجرح اذا لم يكن كذا وقد

قال الامام الحافظ أبو بكر أحمد بن علي بن ثابت الخطيب البغدادي وغيره ما
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ق-س-م (q-s-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Division, apportionment, distribution into parts
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Categorical partitioning of knowledge domains; here, the taxonomical stratification of hadith narrators
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal division (qasm) as opposed to metaphorical allotment; used here in its concrete classificatory sense
- Root: ع-ل-ل (ʿ-l-l)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Defect, blemish, hidden flaw; recurring illness
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The technical hadith science term for an obscure defect (ʿillah) undermining a chain's apparent soundness
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal bodily ailment extended metaphorically to textual/transmissional corruption
- Root: ج-ر-ح (j-r-ḥ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Wounding, injuring; in hadith terminology, impugning a narrator's reliability
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The jurisprudential principle of jarḥ (discrediting) versus taʿdīl (crediting) in narrator evaluation
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal physical wounding; metaphorical for reputational damage to a transmitter's credibility
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional and Exceptive Constructions (al-sharṭ wa al-istithnāʾ) — The text employs intricate conditional clauses (e.g., "if the jarḥ is established and its cause specified... otherwise it is not accepted") requiring precise parsing of protasis and apodosis to preserve the legal nuance.
chapters.translation:
I say — may Allah grant success:

Muslim — may Allah have mercy on him — mentioned at the beginning of the introduction to his Ṣaḥīḥ that he divides hadiths into three categories: first, what was transmitted by the precise, meticulous memorizers (al-ḥuffāẓ al-mutqinūn); second, what was transmitted by those of concealed integrity (al-mastūrūn) who are middling in memory and precision; and third, what was transmitted by the weak (al-ḍuʿafāʾ) and the abandoned (al-matrūkūn). He stated that when he completes the first category, he follows it with the second, but he does not pause upon the third.

The scholars differed over what he intended by this division. The two Imams and memorizers, Abū ʿAbd Allāh al-Ḥākim and his companion Abū Bakr al-Bayhaqī — may Allah have mercy on them both — held that death cut short Muslim — may Allah have mercy on him — before he could produce the second category, and that he only mentioned the first. Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ — may Allah have mercy on him — said: "This is something the shaykhs and the people accepted from al-Ḥākim, Abū ʿAbd Allāh, and they followed him upon it."

Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ said: "But the matter is not as he claimed for one who investigates with care and does not bind himself to blind emulation (taqlīd). For if you examine Muslim's division in his book of hadith into three strata of people, as he stated, you find that he mentioned that the first category is the hadith of the precise memorizers, and that when this concludes, he follows it with hadiths of those not described as possessing mastery and precision, while being among the people of concealed integrity and truthfulness and the pursuit of knowledge. Then he indicated the abandonment of the hadith of one whom the scholars unanimously — or the majority of them agreed — accused, and he excluded one whom some accused while others authenticated; he did not mention him there. I found that he mentioned in the chapters of his book the hadiths of the first two strata, and he brought the chains of the second of them by way of following (ittibāʿ) the first and seeking corroboration (istishhād), or where he found nothing in the first stratum for that chapter. He also mentioned people concerning whom some spoke critically while others declared them upright (zakkāhum), and he produced their hadiths from those who were weakened or accused of innovation (bidʿah). Al-Bukhārī did likewise. Thus, in my view, he brought his three strata in his book as he described, arranged them in his work, clarified them in his division, and discarded the fourth, as he explicitly stated.

Al-Ḥākim interpreted that he only intended to devote a separate book to each stratum, bringing its hadiths alone in isolation. But that was not his intent. Rather, what he intended — as is apparent from his compilation and evident from his purpose — was to gather all of that within the chapters, bringing the hadiths of the two strata, beginning with the first, then bringing the second by way of corroboration and following, until he exhausted all three categories. It is also possible that he intended by the three strata: the precise memorizers, then those who follow them, and the third is the one he discarded.

Likewise, the defects (ʿilal) of hadith that he mentioned and promised to bring — he did bring them in their proper places within the chapters, concerning their disagreements over chains of transmission, such as disconnection (irsāl), connection (isnād), addition (ziyādah), and omission (nuqṣān), and he mentioned the textual corruptions (taṣḥīf) of those who corrupted texts. This indicates his fulfillment of his purpose in his compilation and his inclusion in his book of everything he promised."

Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ said: "I have consulted, regarding this interpretation of mine and my opinion therein, those who understand this subject, and I have not seen a fair-minded person except that he deemed it correct, and what I mentioned became clear to him. It is evident to one who contemplates the book and surveys the totality of its chapters."

One should not object to this on the basis of what Ibn Sufyān, the companion of Muslim, said — that Muslim produced three books from the musnad collections: one of them is this one which he read to the people; the second includes ʿIkrimah, Ibn Isḥāq the author of the Maghāzī, and their likes; and the third includes the weak narrators. For if you contemplate what Ibn Sufyān mentioned, it does not correspond to the purpose that al-Ḥākim indicated from what Muslim mentioned at the head of his book. Contemplate it, and you will find it so, Allah willing. This is the end of the speech of Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ — may Allah have mercy on him. And this which he chose is extremely evident. And Allah knows best.

---

**Section (Faṣl)**

The Imam and memorizer Abū al-Ḥasan ʿAlī ibn ʿUmar al-Dāraquṭnī — may Allah have mercy on him — and others imposed an obligation (ilzām) upon al-Bukhārī and Muslim — may Allah be pleased with them both — to produce hadiths that they omitted to include, despite the fact that their chains were chains whose transmitters they had already included in their two Ṣaḥīḥs. Al-Dāraquṭnī and others mentioned that a group of the Companions — may Allah be pleased with them — transmitted from the Messenger of Allah — may Allah's peace and blessings be upon him — and their hadiths were transmitted through sound paths with no criticism of their transmitters, yet they did not include anything from their hadiths. Thus, it would be incumbent upon them to include them according to their own methodological principles.

Al-Bayhaqī mentioned that they both agreed upon hadiths from the scroll (ṣaḥīfah) of Hammām ibn Munabbih, and that each of them was uniquely distinguished from the other by certain hadiths from it, despite the chain being one and the same. Al-Dāraquṭnī and Abū Dharr al-Harawī authored works on this type of objection that was leveled against them.

This imposition (ilzām) is not truly binding, for they did not commit themselves to exhaustively covering all authentic hadiths. Rather, it is authentically established from them both that they explicitly stated they did not exhaust them. They only aimed to collect a body of authentic hadiths, just as a jurist (muṣannif) in fiqh aims to collect a body of its issues, not to encompass all of its issues. However, if the hadith they — or one of them — omitted, despite the apparent soundness of its chain, is a foundational text (aṣl) in its chapter, and they did not produce an equivalent for it nor what could stand in its place, then the apparent state of their affair is that they became aware of a hidden defect (ʿillah) in it — if they had transmitted it. And it is possible that they omitted it out of forgetfulness, or preferring to avoid prolixity, or they saw that something else they mentioned sufficed in its place, or for some other reason. And Allah knows best.

---

**Section (Faṣl)**

Some critics (ʿāʾibūn) faulted Muslim for transmitting in his Ṣaḥīḥ from a group of weak and middling narrators falling within the second stratum who do not meet the condition of authenticity. But there is no fault upon him in that. Rather, his answer is from several aspects, which the Shaykh and Imam Abū ʿAmr ibn al-Ṣalāḥ — may Allah have mercy on him — mentioned:

One of them: that this occurs regarding one who is weak according to others but trustworthy (thiqah) according to him. And one cannot say that jarḥ (discrediting) takes precedence over taʿdīl (crediting), because that applies only when the jarḥ is established and its cause is specified (mufassar al-sabab). Otherwise, the jarḥ is not accepted when it is not so. The Imam and memorizer Abū Bakr Aḥmad ibn ʿAlī ibn Thābit al-Khaṭīb al-Baghdādī and others have stated what [follows].

chapters.title_en: Section 13 — On the Excuses for Muslim's Narration from Certain Weak Narrators, and a Listing of Works Extracted upon Sahih Muslim
chapters.arabic_text: احتج البخارى ومسلم وأبو داود به من جماعة علم الطعن فيهم من غيرهم محمول على أنه لم يثبت الطعن المؤثر مفسر السبب الثاني أن يكون ذلك واقعا في المتابعات والشواهد لافي الأصول وذلك بأن يذكر الحديث أولا باسناد نظيف رجاله ثقات ويجعله أصلا ثم يتبعه باسناد آخر أو أسانيد فيها بعض الضعفاء على وجه التأكيد بالمتابعة أو لزيادة فيه تنبه على فائدة فيما قدمه وقد اعتذر الحاكم أبو عبد الله بالمتابعة والاستشهاد في اخراجه عن جماعة ليسوا من شرط الصحيح منهم مطر الوراق وبقية بن الوليد ومحمد بن إسحاق بن يسار وعبد الله بن عمر العمرى والنعمان بن راشد وأخرج مسلم عنهم في الشواهد في أشباه لهم كثيرين الثالث أن يكون ضعف الضعيف الذى احتج به طرأ بعد أخذه عنه باختلاط حدث عليه فهو غير قادح فيما رواه من قبل في زمن استقامته كما في أحمد بن عبد الرحمن بن وهب بن أخي عبد الله بن وهب فذكر الحاكم أبو عبد الله أنه اختلط بعد الخمسين ومائتين بعد خروج مسلم من مصر فهو في ذلك كسعيد بن أبي عروبة وعبد الرازق وغيرهما ممن اختلط آخرا ولم يمنع ذلك من صحة الاحتجاج في الصحيحين بما أخذ عنهم قبل ذلك الرابع أن يعلو بالشخص الضعيف اسناده وهو عنده من رواية الثقات نازل فيقتصر على العالى ولا يطول باضافة النازل إليه مكتفيا بمعرفه أهل الشأن في ذلك وهذا العذر قد رويناه عنه تنصيصا وهو خلاف حاله فيما رواه عن الثقات أولا ثم أتبعه بمن دونهم متابعة وكأن ذلك وقع منه على حسب حضور باعث النشاط وغيبته روينا عن سعيد بن عمرو البرذعى أنه حضر أبا زرعة الرازي وذكر صحيح مسلم وانكار أبي زرعة عليه روايته فيه عن اسباط بن نصر وقطن بن نسير وأحمد بن عيسى المصرى وأنه قال أيضا يطرق لاهل البدع علينا فيجدون السبيل بأن يقولوا اذا احتج عليهم بحديث ليس هذا في الصحيح قال سعيد بن عمرو فلما رجعت إلى نيسابور ذكرت لمسلم انكار أبي زرعة فقال لي مسلم انما قلت صحيح وانما أدخلت من حديث اسباط وقطن وأحمد ما قد رواه الثقات عن شيوخهم الا أنه ربما وقع إلى عنهم بارتفاع ويكون عندي من رواية أوثق منهم بنزول فأقتصر على ذلك # # وأصل الحديث معروف من رواة الثقات قال سعيد وقدم مسلم بعد ذلك الرى فبلغنى أنه خرج إلى أبى عبد الله محمد بن مسلم بن وارة فجفاه وعاتبه على هذا الكتاب وقال له نحوا مما قاله لى أبو زرعة ان هذا يطرق لاهل البدع فاعتذر مسلم وقال انما أخرجت هذا الكتاب وقلت هو صحاح ولم أقل ان ما لم أخرجه من الحديث فى هذا الكتاب فهو ضعيف وانما أخرجت هذا الحديث من الصحيح ليكون مجموعا عندى وعند من يكتبه عنى ولا يرتاب فى صحته فقبل عذره وحمده قال الشيخ وقد قدمنا عن مسلم أنه عرضت كتابى هذا على أبى زرعة الرازى فكل ما أشار أن له علة تركته وكل ما قال انه صحيح وليس له علة فهو هذا الذى أخرجته قال الشيخ فهذا مقام وعر وقد مهدته بواضح من القول لم أره مجتمعا فى مؤلف ولله الحمد قال وفيما ذكرته دليل على أن حكم لشخص بمجرد رواية مسلم عنه فى صحيحه بأنه من شرط الصحيح عند مسلم فقد غفل وأخطأ بل يتوقف ذلك على النظر فى أنه كيف روى عنه على ما بيناه من انقسام ذلك والله أعلم | | فصل # فى بيان جملة من الكتب المخرجة على صحيح مسلم) # فقد صنف جماعات من الحفاظ على صحيح مسلم كتبا وكان هؤلاء تأخروا عن مسلم وأدركواالاسانيد العالية وفيهم من أدرك بعض شيوخ مسلم فخرجوا أحايث مسلم فى مصنفاتهم المذكورة بأسانيدهم تلك قال الشيخ أبو عمرو رحمه الله فهذه الكتب المخرجة تلتحق بصحيح مسلم فى أن لها سمة الصحيح وان لم تلتحق به فى خصائصه كلها ويستفاد من مخرجاتهم ثلاث فوائد علو الاسناد وزيادة قوة الحديث بكثرة طرقه وزيادة ألفاظ صحيحة مفيدة ثم انهم لم يلتزموا موافقته فى اللفظ لكونهم يروونها بأسانيد أخر فيقع فى بعضها تفاوت فمن هذه الكتب المخرجة على صحيح مسلم كتاب العبد الصالح أبى جعفر أحمد بن أحمد بن حمدان النيسابورى الزاهد العابد ومنها المسند الصحيح لابى بكر محمد بن محمد بن رجا النيسابورى الحافظ وهو متقدم يشارك مسلما فى أكثر شيوخه ومنها مختصر المسند الصحيح المؤلف على كتاب مسلم للحافظ أبى عوانة يعقوب بن إسحاق الاسفراينى روى فيه عن يونس بن عبد الاعلى وغيره من شيوخ مسلم ومنها كتاب أبى حامد الشازكى الفقيه الشافعى الهروى يروى عن أبى يعلى الموصلى ومنها المسند الصحيح لأبى بكر محمد بن عبد الله الجوزقى النيسابورى الشافعى ومنها المسند المستخرج على كتاب # # مسلم للحافظ المصنف أبى نعيم أحمد بن عبد الله الاصبهانى ومنها المخرج على صحيح مسلم للامام أبى الوليد حسان بن محمد القرشى الفقيه الشافعى وغير ذلك والله أعلم | فصل # قد استدرك جماعة على البخارى ومسلم أحاديث أخلا بشرطهما فيها ونزلت عن درجة ما التزماه وقد سبقت الاشارة إلى هذا وقد ألف الامام الحافظ أبو الحسن على بن عمر الدارقطنى فى بيان ذلك كتابه المسمى بالاستدراكات والتتبع وذلك

- Root: ط ع ن (ṭa-ʿa-n)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To pierce, wound, or impugn; casting aspersion upon a narrator's integrity.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Technical hadith criticism term denoting a specific, substantive defect (ʿillah) in a transmitter.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense of physical stabbing; metaphorical usage for verbal disparagement of a narrator's reliability.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clause with Implied Apodosis (al-sharṭ bi-jawāb maḥdhūf) — The phrase "محمول على أنه لم يثبت" carries an elided main clause, requiring the reader to supply the governing judgment.
chapters.translation:
I say — and Allah grants success:

Al-Bukhārī, Muslim, and Abū Dāwūd have all narrated from a group of narrators whom others have criticized. This criticism is to be understood as not having established an effective disparagement with an explained cause.

The second excuse is that such narration occurs in corroborative (mutābaʿāt) and supporting (shawāhid) contexts, not in primary foundations (uṣūl). This means that the narrator first mentions a hadith with a clean chain whose transmitters are reliable, making it the foundation; then he follows it with another chain, or chains, containing some weak narrators, by way of corroboration (mutābaʿah) or for an addition that alerts one to a benefit in what he had previously presented. Al-Ḥākim Abū ʿAbd Allāh has excused [Muslim] on the basis of corroboration and support in his citing from a group not meeting the condition of ṣaḥīḥ — among them: Muṭarr al-Warrāq, Baqiyyah ibn al-Walīd, Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq ibn Yasār, ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar al-ʿUmarī, and al-Nuʿmān ibn Rāshid. Muslim narrated from them in supporting contexts, along with many others similar to them.

The third excuse is that the weakness of the weak narrator from whom he cited occurred after [Muslim] had taken from him, due to confusion (ikhtilāṭ) that befell him later. This does not vitiate what was narrated from him earlier, during the period of his soundness — as in the case of Aḥmad ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Wahb, the nephew of ʿAbd Allāh ibn Wahb. Al-Ḥākim Abū ʿAbd Allāh mentioned that he became confused after the year 250 AH, after Muslim had departed from Egypt. He is thus like Saʿīd ibn Abī ʿArūbah, ʿAbd al-Razzāq, and others who became confused at the end of their lives, yet this did not prevent the soundness of citing from them in the two Ṣaḥīḥs based on what was taken from them before that.

The fourth excuse is that the chain of a weak person may be elevated (ʿālin) for him, while he also possesses the same hadith through a lower (nāzil) chain of reliable narrators. He then restricts himself to the elevated chain and does not lengthen [the book] by appending the lower one to it, content with the knowledge of the people of this craft concerning that. We have narrated this excuse from him explicitly. This is contrary to his practice when he narrated from reliable narrators first, then followed them with those below them by way of corroboration. It seems that this occurred from him according to the presence or absence of the stimulus of activity.

We have narrated from Saʿīd ibn ʿAmr al-Bardhaʿī that he was present with Abū Zurʿah al-Rāzī, and the mention of Muslim's Ṣaḥīḥ came up, along with Abū Zurʿah's disapproval of Muslim's narration in it from Asbāṭ ibn Naṣr, Qaṭan ibn Nusayr, and Aḥmad ibn ʿĪsā al-Miṣrī. He also said: "This opens a door for the people of innovation against us, for they will find a way to say, when a hadith is cited against them: 'This is not in the Ṣaḥīḥ.'"

Saʿīd ibn ʿAmr said: "When I returned to Nīsābūr, I mentioned to Muslim the disapproval of Abū Zurʿah. Muslim said to me: 'I only said "ṣaḥīḥ," and I only included from the hadith of Asbāṭ, Qaṭan, and Aḥmad that which the reliable narrators have narrated from their shaykhs. However, it sometimes reached me from them with elevation (ʿuluw), while I possessed it from narrators more reliable than them with lower chains (nuzūl), so I restricted myself to that [elevated one].'"

Saʿīd said: "The origin of the hadith is well-known from reliable narrators." Saʿīd further said: "Muslim later came to al-Rayy, and it reached me that he went out to Abū ʿAbd Allāh Muḥammad ibn Muslim ibn Wārah, who treated him harshly and reproached him for this book, saying to him something similar to what Abū Zurʿah had said to me: 'This opens a door for the people of innovation.' Muslim apologized and said: 'I only brought out this book and called it ṣaḥīḥ; I did not say that whatever hadith I did not include in this book is weak. I only included this hadith in the Ṣaḥīḥ so that it might be collected with me and with whoever writes it from me, without doubt concerning its soundness.' So he accepted his excuse and praised him."

The Shaykh (al-Nawawī) said: We have already presented that Muslim said: "I presented this book of mine to Abū Zurʿah al-Rāzī; whatever he indicated had a defect, I abandoned; and whatever he said was sound and had no defect — that is what I included."

The Shaykh said: This is a difficult station (maqām waʿr), which I have paved with clear speech that I have not seen gathered in any single authored work — and praise be to Allah. And in what I have mentioned is proof that whoever judges a person merely by Muslim's narration from him in his Ṣaḥīḥ as being of the condition of ṣaḥīḥ according to Muslim has been negligent and erred. Rather, that depends upon examining how he narrated from him, according to what we have explained of its division — and Allah knows best.

---

**SECTION: On the Explanation of a Number of Books Extracted upon Sahih Muslim**

A group of ḥuffāẓ (hadith masters) composed books upon Muslim's Ṣaḥīḥ. These came after Muslim and attained elevated chains (asānīd ʿāliyah); among them were those who met some of Muslim's shaykhs. They thus brought out the hadiths of Muslim in their aforementioned compilations with their own chains.

The Shaykh Abū ʿAmr — may Allah have mercy on him — said: These extracted books (al-mukhrajāt) attach to Muslim's Ṣaḥīḥ in that they bear the mark of ṣaḥīḥ, even if they do not attach to it in all its particular virtues. Three benefits are derived from their extractions: elevation of chain (ʿuluw al-isnād), increased strength of the hadith through multiplicity of its paths (kathrat ṭuruqih), and the addition of sound and beneficial wordings (alfāẓ). Then, they did not commit themselves to matching him in wording, because they narrated through other chains, so some variance occurs in some of them.

Among these books extracted upon Muslim's Ṣaḥīḥ is the book of the righteous servant Abū Jaʿfar Aḥmad ibn Aḥmad ibn Ḥamdān al-Nīsābūrī, the ascetic and devotee. Among them is the sound musnad (al-musnad al-ṣaḥīḥ) of Abū Bakr Muḥammad ibn Muḥammad ibn Rajā al-Nīsābūrī, the ḥāfiẓ — he is early, sharing most of Muslim's shaykhs. Among them is the abridgment of the sound musnad composed upon Muslim's book, by the ḥāfiẓ Abū ʿAwānah Yaʿqūb ibn Isḥāq al-Isfarāyīnī, who narrated in it from Yūnus ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā and others among Muslim's shaykhs. Among them is the book of Abū Ḥāmid al-Shāzakī, the Shāfiʿī jurist of Herāt, who narrates from Abū Yaʿlā al-Mawṣilī. Among them is the sound musnad of Abū Bakr Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Jawzaqī al-Nīsābūrī al-Shāfiʿī. Among them is the sound musnad extracted upon Muslim's book by the ḥāfiẓ and author Abū Nuʿaym Aḥmad ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Iṣbahānī. Among them is the extraction upon Muslim's Ṣaḥīḥ by the Imām Abū al-Walīd Ḥassān ibn Muḥammad al-Qurashī, the Shāfiʿī jurist — and others besides. And Allah knows best.

---

**SECTION: On Those Who Have Made Corrections (Istidrākāt) upon al-Bukhari and Muslim**

A group has made corrections upon al-Bukhārī and Muslim regarding hadiths that fell short of their condition and descended below the degree of what they had committed themselves to. Reference has already been made to this. The Imām, the ḥāfiẓ Abū al-Ḥasan ʿAlī ibn ʿUmar al-Dāraquṭnī composed his book on this subject, called *al-Istidrākāt wa al-Tatabbuʿ* — and that is as follows.
