بالفرائض لا يسمى مؤمنا بالإطلاق وإن كان في كلام العرب يسمى مؤمنا

بالتصديق فذلك غير مستحق في كلام الله تعالى لقوله عز وجل إنما المؤمنون

الذين إذا ذكر الله وجلت قلوبهم وإذا تليت عليهم آياته زادتهم إيمانا وعلى

ربهم يتوكلون الذين يقيمون الصلاة ومما رزقناهم ينفقون أولئك هم المؤمنون

حقا فأخبرنا سبحانه وتعالى أن المؤمن من كانت هذه صفته وقال بن بطال في باب

من قال الإيمان هو العمل فإن قيل قد قدمتم أن الإيمان هو التصديق قيل

التصديق هو أول منازل الإيمان ويوجب للمصدق الدخول فيه ولا يوجب له استكمال

منازله ولا يسمى مؤمنا مطلقا هذا مذهب جماعة أهل السنة أن الإيمان قول وعمل

قال أبو عبيد وهو قول مالك والثوري والأوزاعي ومن بعدهم من أرباب العلم

والسنة الذين كانوا مصابيح الهدى وأئمة الدين من أهل الحجاز والعراق والشام

وغيرهم قال بن بطال وهذا المعنى أراد البخاري رحمه الله إثباته في كتاب

الإيمان وعليه بوب أبوابه كلها فقال باب أمور الإيمان وباب الصلاة من

الإيمان وباب الزكاة من الإيمان وباب الجهاد من الإيمان وسائر أبوابه وإنما

أراد الرد على المرجئة في قولهم إن الإيمان قول بلا عمل وتبيين غلطهم وسوء

اعتقادهم ومخالفتهم للكتاب والسنة ومذاهب الأئمة ثم قال بن بطال في باب آخر

قال المهلب الإسلام على الحقيقة هو الإيمان الذي هو عقد القلب المصدق

لإقرار اللسان الذي لا ينفع عند الله تعالى غيره وقالت الكرامية وبعض

المرجئة الإيمان هو الإقرار باللسان دون عقد القلب ومن أقوى ما يرد به

عليهم إجماع الأمة على إكفار المنافقين وإن كانوا قد أظهروا الشهادتين قال

الله تعالى ولا تصل على أحد منهم مات أبدا ولا تقم على قبره إنهم كفروا
chapters.anchors:
- Root: د-ي-ن (d-y-n)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning of "religion" (dīn) as obedience, recompense, and the comprehensive system of belief and practice owed to God.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Dīn as the divinely ordained path (sharīʿah) encompassing inward conviction and outward submission (islām).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense of "debt/obligation" (jazāʾ) extended metaphorically to the entire religious law binding the servant.
- Root: أ-م-ن (a-m-n)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Root meaning of security (amn) and safety from fear; taṣdīq (affirmation) as the intellectual act of certifying truth.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Īmān as taṣdīq bi-l-qalb (heartfelt affirmation) — the theological technical sense distinguishing it from mere linguistic usage.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal taṣdīq (assent) vs. metaphorical complete īmān (faith comprising works); the shift from ḥaqīqah to sharʿī convention.
- Root: ع-م-ل (ʿ-m-l)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Action, deed, labor — the outward manifestation of inner conviction.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): ʿAmal as the necessary complement to taṣdīq in the sharʿī definition of īmān; works are the fruit of faith.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal physical action; metaphorically extended to all acts of obedience (ṭāʿāt) that perfect faith.
- Sībawayh Rule: Rule of ʿAṭf al-Bayān (Appositional Clarification) — The phrase "qawl wa ʿamal" (speech and action) functions as a single composite predicate, where each element is syntactically coordinated to define the indivisible reality of īmān, requiring the reader to parse the whole as one semantic unit.
chapters.translation:
I say: God — glorified and exalted be He — has informed us that the religion which He is pleased with and accepts from His servants is Islam (islām). And religion does not attain a station of acceptance and divine pleasure except through the conjunction of affirmation (taṣdīq) with action (ʿamal). This is the statement of al-Baghawī.

And the Imām, Abū ʿAbd Allāh Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl ibn Muḥammad ibn al-Faḍl al-Tamīmī al-Aṣbahānī al-Shāfiʿī — may God have mercy on him — said in his book al-Taḥrīr fī Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim: "Īmān (faith) in the language (lughah) is affirmation (taṣdīq). If it is meant in this sense, then it neither increases nor decreases, because affirmation is not a divisible thing such that its perfection could be conceived at one time and its deficiency at another. And īmān in the tongue of the Sacred Law (lisān al-sharʿ) is affirmation by the heart and action by the limbs (al-ʿamal bi-l-arkān). When it is interpreted in this manner, increase and decrease apply to it — and this is the doctrine (madhhab) of the People of the Sunnah (ahl al-sunnah)."

He said: "So the disagreement in this matter, upon precise investigation, is only this: when a person who affirms with his heart does not join to his affirmation the action required by the obligations of faith (mawājib al-īmān), is he called a believer (muʾmin) absolutely (muṭlaqan) or not? And the chosen position with us is that he is not called by that name." The Messenger of God — may God bless him and grant him peace — said: {«لَا يَزْنِي الزَّانِي حِينَ يَزْنِي وَهُوَ مُؤْمِنٌ»} "The fornicator does not fornicate while he is a believer" — because he did not act upon the obligations of faith, and thus he does not deserve this absolute designation. This is the end of the statement of the author of al-Taḥrīr.

And the Imām, Abū al-Ḥasan ʿAlī ibn Khalaf ibn Baṭṭāl al-Mālikī al-Maghribī said in his commentary on Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī: "The doctrine of the group of the People of the Sunnah, from the predecessors (salaf) of this community and its successors (khalaf), is that īmān is speech (qawl) and action (ʿamal); it increases and decreases. The proof for its increase and decrease is what al-Bukhārī cited from the verses — meaning the saying of God — exalted be He: {«لِيَزْدَادُوا إِيمَانًا مَعَ إِيمَانِهِمْ»} "That they may increase in faith along with their faith" (al-Fatḥ 48:4); and His saying — exalted be He: {«وَزِدْنَاهُمْ هُدًى»} "And We increased them in guidance" (al-Kahf 18:13); and His saying — exalted be He: {«وَيَزِيدُ اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ اهْتَدَوْا هُدًى»} "And God increases those who are guided in guidance" (Maryam 19:76); and His saying — exalted be He: {«وَالَّذِينَ اهْتَدَوْا زَادَهُمْ هُدًى»} "And those who are guided — He increases them in guidance" (Muḥammad 47:17); and His saying — exalted be He: {«وَيَزْدَادَ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا إِيمَانًا»} "And that those who believe may increase in faith" (al-Muddaththir 74:31); and His saying — exalted be He: {«أَيُّكُمْ زَادَتْهُ هَذِهِ إِيمَانًا فَأَمَّا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا فَزَادَتْهُمْ إِيمَانًا»} "Which of you has this increased in faith? As for those who believe, it has increased them in faith" (al-Tawbah 9:124); and His saying — exalted be He: {«فَاخْشَوْهُمْ فَزَادَهُمْ إِيمَانًا»} "So fear them, and it increased them in faith" (Āl ʿImrān 3:173); and His saying — exalted be He: {«وَمَا زَادَهُمْ إِلَّا إِيمَانًا وَتَسْلِيمًا»} "And it increased them not except in faith and submission" (al-Aḥzāb 33:22)."

Ibn Baṭṭāl said: "So the faith of one who has not attained this increase is deficient (nāqiṣ)."

He said: "If it is said: 'Īmān in the language is affirmation (taṣdīq),' then the answer is that affirmation is perfected (yakmul) by all acts of obedience. So whatever additional righteous deeds (aʿmāl al-birr) the believer performs, his faith becomes more complete. By this totality, faith increases, and by its deficiency, it decreases. Whenever deeds of righteousness diminish, the perfection (kamāl) of faith diminishes; and whenever they increase, faith increases in perfection. This is the moderate position (tawassuṭ) concerning faith."

"As for affirmation of God — exalted be He — and His Messenger — may God bless him and grant him peace — it does not decrease. For this reason, Mālik — may God have mercy on him — hesitated in some narrations from explicitly stating decrease, since the decrease of affirmation is not permissible; because if it decreased, it would become doubt (shakk) and would exit from the very name of faith."

And some said: "Mālik only hesitated from stating the decrease of faith out of fear that it would be interpreted against him as agreement with the Khawārij, who declare the sinners among the believers to be disbelievers (takfīr) on account of their sins. Yet Mālik did state the decrease of faith, just like the statement of the group of the People of the Sunnah."

ʿAbd al-Razzāq said: "I heard those of my teachers and companions whom I encountered — Sufyān al-Thawrī, Mālik ibn Anas, ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿUmar, al-Awzāʿī, Maʿmar ibn Rāshid, Ibn Jurayj, and Sufyān ibn ʿUyaynah — all saying: 'Īmān is speech and action; it increases and decreases.' And this is the statement of Ibn Masʿūd, Ḥudhayfah, al-Nakhaʿī, al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī, ʿAṭāʾ, Ṭāwūs, Mujāhid, and ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Mubārak."

So the meaning by which a servant deserves praise (madḥ) and alliance (wilāyah) from the believers is his performance of these three things: affirmation by the heart (al-taṣdīq bi-l-qalb), utterance by the tongue (al-iqrār bi-l-lisān), and action by the limbs (al-ʿamal bi-l-jawāriḥ). This is because there is no disagreement among all parties that if one utters and acts without knowledge and cognizance of his Lord, he does not deserve the name of believer. And if he knows Him and acts but denies with his tongue and belies what he knows of divine unity (tawḥīd), he does not deserve the name of believer. Likewise, if he affirms God — exalted be He — and His messengers — may God's blessings and peace be upon them all — but does not perform the obligatory duties (farāʾiḍ), he is not called a believer absolutely (bi-l-iṭlāq), even though in the speech of the Arabs he might be called a believer by virtue of affirmation. But that [linguistic usage] is not what is merited in the speech of God — exalted be He — for His saying — exalted be He: {«إِنَّمَا الْمُؤْمِنُونَ الَّذِينَ إِذَا ذُكِرَ اللَّهُ وَجِلَتْ قُلُوبُهُمْ وَإِذَا تُلِيَتْ عَلَيْهِمْ آيَاتُهُ زَادَتْهُمْ إِيمَانًا وَعَلَى رَبِّهِمْ يَتَوَكَّلُونَ * الَّذِينَ يُقِيمُونَ الصَّلَاةَ وَمِمَّا رَزَقْنَاهُمْ يُنْفِقُونَ * أُولَئِكَ هُمُ الْمُؤْمِنُونَ حَقًّا»} "The believers are only those who, when God is mentioned, their hearts tremble; and when His verses are recited to them, it increases them in faith; and upon their Lord they rely — those who establish prayer and spend from what We have provided them — those are the believers in truth" (al-Anfāl 8:2-4). So He — glorified and exalted be He — has informed us that the believer is one whose attribute is this.

And Ibn Baṭṭāl said in the chapter of "Whoever Said Īmān is Action": "If it is said: 'You have previously stated that īmān is affirmation (taṣdīq),' then the answer is: affirmation is the first of the stations (manāzil) of faith. It obligates for the one who affirms entry into it, but it does not obligate for him the completion of its stations, nor is he called a believer absolutely (muṭlaqan). This is the doctrine of the group of the People of the Sunnah: that īmān is speech and action."

Abū ʿUbayd said: "And this is the statement of Mālik, al-Thawrī, al-Awzāʿī, and those after them among the people of knowledge and the Sunnah — those who were the lamps of guidance (maṣābīḥ al-hudā) and the imāms of religion from the people of the Hijāz, Iraq, Syria, and others."

Ibn Baṭṭāl said: "And this is the meaning that al-Bukhārī — may God have mercy on him — intended to establish in his Book of Faith (Kitāb al-Īmān), and upon it he titled all his chapters. Thus he said: 'Chapter: The Matters of Faith (Bāb Umūr al-Īmān),' 'Chapter: Prayer is from Faith (Bāb al-Ṣalāh min al-Īmān),' 'Chapter: Zakāh is from Faith (Bāb al-Zakāh min al-Īmān),' 'Chapter: Jihād is from Faith (Bāb al-Jihād min al-Īmān),' and the rest of his chapters. He only intended thereby to refute the Murjiʾah in their statement that faith is speech without action, and to clarify their error, the corruption of their belief, and their opposition to the Book, the Sunnah, and the doctrines of the imāms."

Then Ibn Baṭṭāl said in another chapter: "Al-Muhallab said: 'Islām in reality is īmān, which is the contract of the heart (ʿaqd al-qalb) that affirms the utterance of the tongue — that which avails nothing before God — exalted be He — other than it.'"

And the Karāmiyyah and some of the Murjiʾah said: "Īmān is the utterance of the tongue (al-iqrār bi-l-lisān) without the contract of the heart." Among the strongest things by which they are refuted is the consensus (ijmāʿ) of the community upon declaring the hypocrites (munāfiqūn) to be disbelievers, even though they had outwardly manifested the two testimonies (al-shahādatayn). God — exalted be He — said: {«وَلَا تُصَلِّ عَلَى أَحَدٍ مِنْهُمْ مَاتَ أَبَدًا وَلَا تَقُمْ عَلَى قَبْرِهِ إِنَّهُمْ كَفَرُوا»} "And do not pray over any of them who dies, ever, and do not stand at his grave. Indeed, they disbelieved" (al-Tawbah 9:84).

chapters.title_en: Section 56 — On the Relationship Between Faith (Īmān) and Submission (Islām), and the Increase and Decrease of Faith
chapters.arabic_text:
بالله ورسوله إلى قوله تعالى وتزهق أنفسهم  وهم كافرون هذا آخر كلام بن بطال

وقال الشيخ الإمام أبو عمرو بن الصلاح رحمه الله قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم

الاسلام أن تشهد أن لااله إلا الله وأن محمدا رسول الله وتقيم الصلاة وتؤتي

الزكاة وتصوم رمضان وتحج البيت إن استطعت إليه سبيلا
# 
# والإيمان أن تؤمن بالله وملائكته وكتبه ورسله واليوم الآخر وتؤمن بالقدر

خيره وشره قال هذا بيان لأصل الإيمان وهو التصديق الباطن وبيان لأصل

الإسلام وهو الاستسلام والانقياد الظاهر وحكم الإسلام في الظاهر ثبت

بالشهادتين وإنما أضاف إليهما الصلاة والزكاة والحج والصوم لكونها أظهر

شعائر الإسلام وأعظمها وبقيامه بها يتم استسلامه وتركه لها يشعر بانحلال

قيد انقياده أو اختلاله ثم إن اسم الإيمان يتناول ما فسر به الإسلام في هذا

الحديث وسائر الطاعات لكونها ثمرات للتصديق الباطن الذي هو أصل الإيمان

ومقويات ومتممات وحافظات له ولهذا فسر صلى الله عليه وسلم الإيمان في حديث

وفد عبد القيس بالشهادتين والصلاة والزكاة وصوم رمضان وإعطاء الخمس من

المغنم ولهذا لا يقع اسم المؤمن المطلق على من ارتكب كبيرة أو بدل فريضة

لأن اسم الشيء مطلقا يقع على الكامل منه ولا يستعمل في الناقص ظاهرا إلا

بقيد ولذلك جاز إطلاق نفيه عنه في قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم لا يسرق السارق

حين يسرق وهو مؤمن واسم الإسلام يتناول أيضا ما هو أصل الإيمان وهو التصديق

الباطن ويتناول أصل الطاعات فإن ذلك كله استسلام قال فخرج مما ذكرناه

وحققنا أن الإيمان والإسلام يجتمعان ويفترقان وأن كل مؤمن مسلم وليس كل

مسلم مؤمنا قال وهذا تحقيق وافر بالتوفيق بين متفرقات نصوص الكتاب والسنة

الواردة في الإيمان والإسلام التي طالما غلط فيها الخائضون وما حققناه من

ذلك موافق لجماهير العلماء من أهل الحديث وغيرهم هذا آخر كلام الشيخ أبي

عمرو بن الصلاح فإذا تقرر ما ذكرناه من مذاهب السلف وأئمة الخلف فهي

متظاهرة متطابقة على كون الإيمان يزيد وينقص وهذا مذهب السلف والمحدثين

وجماعة من المتكلمين وأنكر أكثر المتكلمين زيادته ونقصانه وقالوا متى  قبل

الزيادة كان شكا وكفرا قال المحققون من أصحابنا المتكلمين نفس التصديق لا

يزيد ولا ينقص والإيمان الشرعي يزيد وينقص بزيادة ثمراته وهي الأعمال

ونقصانها قالوا وفي هذا توفيق بين ظواهر النصوص التي جاءت بالزيادة وأقاويل

السلف وبين أصل وضعه في اللغة وما عليه المتكلمون وهذا الذي قاله هؤلاء وإن

كان ظاهرا حسنا فالأظهر والله أعلم أن نفس التصديق يزيد بكثرة النظر وتظاهر

الأدلة ولهذا يكون إيمان الصديقين أقوى من إيمان غيرهم بحيث لا تعتريهم

الشبه ولا يتزلزل إيمانهم بعارض بل لا تزال قلوبهم منشرحة نيرة وإن اختلفت

عليهم
# 
# الأحوال وأما غيرهم من المؤلفة ومن قاربهم ونحوهم فليسوا كذلك فهذا مما

لا يمكن إنكاره ولا يتشكك عاقل في أن نفس تصديق أبي بكر الصديق رضي الله

عنه لا يساويه تصديق آحاد الناس ولهذا قال البخارى فى صحيحه قال بن أبي

مليكة أدركت ثلاثين من أصحاب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كلهم يخاف النفاق

على نفسه ما منهم أحد يقول إنه على إيمان جبريل وميكائيل والله أعلم وأما

إطلاق اسم الإيمان على الأعمال فمتفق عليه عند أهل الحق ودلائله في الكتاب

والسنة أكثر من أن تحصر وأشهر من أن تشهر قال الله تعالى وما كان الله

ليضيع ايمانكم أجمعوا على أن المراد صلاتكم وأما الأحاديث فستمر بك في هذا

الكتاب منها جمل مستكثرات والله أعلم واتفق أهل السنة من المحدثين والفقهاء

والمتكلمين على أن المؤمن الذي يحكم بأنه من أهل القبلة ولا يخلد في النار

لا يكون إلا من اعتقد بقلبه دين الإسلام اعتقادا جازما خاليا من الشكوك

ونطق بالشهادتين فإن اقتصر على إحداهما لم يكن من أهل القبلة أصلا إلا إذا

عجز عن النطق لخلل في لسانه أو لعدم التمكن منه لمعاجلة المنية أو لغير ذلك

فإنه يكون مؤمنا أما إذا أتى بالشهادتين فلا يشترط معهما أن يقول وأنا بريء

من كل دين خالف الإسلام إلا إذا كان من الكفار الذين يعتقدون اختصاص رسالة

نبينا صلى الله عليه وسلم إلى  العرب فإنه لا يحكم بإسلامه إلا بأن يتبرأ

ومن أصحابنا أصحاب الشافعي رحمه الله من شرط أن يتبرأ مطلقا وليس بشيء أما

إذا اقتصر على قوله لا إله إلا الله ولم يقل محمد رسول الله فالمشهور من

مذهبنا ومذاهب العلماء أنه لايكون مسلما ومن أصحابنا من قال يكون مسلما

ويطالب بالشهادة الأخرى فإن أبى جعل مرتدا ويحتج لهذا القول بقوله صلى الله

عليه وسلم أمرت أن أقاتل الناس حتى يقولوا لا إله إلا الله فإذا قالوا ذلك

عصموا مني دماءهم وأموالهم وهذا محمول عند الجماهير على قول الشهادتين

واستغنى بذكر إحداهما عن الأخرى لارتباطهما وشهرتهما والله أعلم أما إذا

أقر بوجوب الصلاة أو الصوم أو غيرهما من أركان الإسلام وهو على خلاف ملته

التي كان عليها فهل يجعل بذلك مسلما فيه وجهان لأصحابنا فمن جعله مسلما قال
chapters.anchors:
- Root: أ-م-ن (ʾ-m-n)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Security, safety from fear; trustworthiness; the heart's tranquil assent.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Taṣdīq (inner verification) as the core of īmān; the theological act of affirming divine truths.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense is inner conviction; metaphorical extension to outward acts as fruits of that conviction.
- Root: س-ل-م (s-l-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Soundness, freedom from defect; surrender, submission.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Islām as outward compliance (inqiyād) and self-surrender to God's command.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal is outward submission; metaphorical when applied to inner faith, as both converge in total surrender.
- Root: ز-ي-د (z-y-d)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Increase, growth, augmentation.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Increment of faith via multiplication of evidences and acts; theological debate on its nature.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal quantitative increase; metaphorical qualitative strengthening of certitude.
- Sībawayh Rule: Rule of Taḍmīn (ضمن) — [A verb or noun implicitly incorporates the meaning of another, allowing a single term to carry both literal and extended senses, as īmān encompasses both inner taṣdīq and outward works.]
chapters.translation:
I say: Up to His saying, the Exalted, {«وَتَزْهَقَ أَنْفُسُهُمْ وَهُمْ كَافِرُونَ»} (and their souls depart while they are disbelievers) — this is the end of Ibn Baṭṭāl's discourse.

And the Shaykh, the Imām, Abū ʿAmr ibn al-Ṣalāḥ — may God have mercy on him — said: His saying, peace be upon him: "Islām is that you bear witness that there is no god but God and that Muḥammad is the Messenger of God, and establish prayer, and give alms, and fast Ramaḍān, and perform the pilgrimage to the House if you are able to find a way to it." And: "Īmān is that you believe in God, His angels, His books, His messengers, the Last Day, and believe in divine decree, its good and its evil." He said: This is an elucidation of the foundation of īmān, which is inner verification (al-taṣdīq al-bāṭin), and an elucidation of the foundation of Islām, which is submission and outward compliance (al-istislām wa-l-inqiyād al-ẓāhir). The legal ruling of Islām in the outward sense is established by the two testimonies; prayer, alms, pilgrimage, and fasting are only appended to them because they are the most manifest rites of Islām and the greatest of them, and by his performance of them his submission is perfected, while his abandonment of them signals the dissolution of the bond of his compliance or its corruption. Then, the name of īmān encompasses what Islām was interpreted to mean in this ḥadīth, and all other acts of obedience, because they are fruits of the inner verification that is the root of īmān, and strengtheners, completers, and preservers of it. For this reason, the Prophet, peace be upon him, interpreted īmān in the ḥadīth of the delegation of ʿAbd al-Qays as the two testimonies, prayer, alms, fasting Ramaḍān, and giving the fifth of the spoils. And for this reason, the unqualified name of believer (muʾmin) does not apply to one who commits a grave sin or abandons an obligatory duty, because the unqualified name of a thing applies to its complete form, and it is not used for the deficient one in an apparent sense except with a qualification. Therefore, it is permissible to negate it of him in his saying, peace be upon him: "The thief does not steal while he is a believer" — at the moment of his stealing. And the name of Islām also encompasses what is the root of īmān, namely inner verification, and encompasses the root of acts of obedience, for all of that is submission. He said: So it follows from what we have mentioned and verified that īmān and Islām converge and diverge, and that every believer is a Muslim, but not every Muslim is a believer. He said: This is a sufficient verification, reconciling the scattered texts of the Book and the Sunnah concerning īmān and Islām, in which those who wade in have long erred. And what we have verified therein accords with the majority of scholars among the people of ḥadīth and others. This is the end of the discourse of Shaykh Abū ʿAmr ibn al-Ṣalāḥ.

Now, when what we have mentioned of the doctrines of the Salaf and the leading Imāms of the successors is established, they are mutually corroborative and concordant upon the fact that īmān increases and decreases. This is the doctrine of the Salaf, the muḥaddithūn, and a group of the theologians (mutakallimūn). But most of the theologians denied its increase and decrease, saying: Whenever increase is admitted, it would entail doubt and unbelief. The verifying scholars among our companions, the theologians, said: The very act of verification (nafs al-taṣdīq) does not increase or decrease, while legal īmān (al-īmān al-sharʿī) increases and decreases with the increase of its fruits, namely the works, and their decrease. They said: In this there is a reconciliation between the apparent meanings of the texts that came with increase, and the sayings of the Salaf, and between its original lexical sense and what the theologians hold. And this which these have said — though it is apparently good — yet the more apparent view, and God knows best, is that the very act of verification increases with the multiplicity of reflection (naẓar) and the convergence of evidences. For this reason, the faith of the ṣiddīqūn (the most veracious) is stronger than the faith of others, such that doubts do not assail them, nor does their faith tremble at any occurrence; rather, their hearts remain expanded and luminous, even if circumstances vary over them. As for others — the newly reconciled (al-muʾallafa qulūbuhum) and those near to them and the like — they are not so. This is something that cannot be denied, and no rational person doubts that the very verification of Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq — may God be pleased with him — is not equaled by the verification of ordinary individuals. For this reason, al-Bukhārī said in his Ṣaḥīḥ: Ibn Abī Mulayka said: "I encountered thirty of the companions of the Prophet, peace be upon him, all of them fearing hypocrisy for themselves; not one of them said that he was upon the faith of Gabriel and Michael." And God knows best.

As for the application of the name of īmān to works, it is agreed upon by the people of truth, and its evidences in the Book and the Sunnah are too numerous to be enumerated and too famous to be proclaimed. God the Exalted said: {«وَمَا كَانَ اللَّهُ لِيُضِيعَ إِيمَانَكُمْ»} (And God would never cause your faith to be lost) — they unanimously agreed that what is meant is "your prayer." As for the ḥadīths, they will come to you in this book, among them a copious collection. And God knows best.

The people of the Sunnah — from the muḥaddithūn, jurists, and theologians — have agreed that the believer who is judged to be among the people of the Qibla and who will not abide eternally in the Fire is only one who has believed in his heart the religion of Islām with a firm conviction (iʿtiqād jāzim) free of doubts, and uttered the two testimonies. If he confines himself to one of them, he is not among the people of the Qibla at all — except if he is unable to utter it due to a defect in his tongue, or the lack of ability to do so due to the sudden onset of death, or for some other reason; then he is a believer. As for when he utters the two testimonies, it is not required alongside them that he say: "I am free of every religion contrary to Islām" — except if he is among the disbelievers who hold that the message of our Prophet, peace be upon him, is specific to the Arabs; for then he is not judged to have entered Islām unless he disavows that. Among our companions, the followers of al-Shāfiʿī — may God have mercy on him — there are those who stipulated that he disavow absolutely, but that is nothing. As for when he confines himself to saying "There is no god but God" and does not say "Muḥammad is the Messenger of God," the well-known view of our school and the schools of the scholars is that he is not a Muslim. Among our companions there are those who said: He is a Muslim, and is required to utter the second testimony; if he refuses, he is deemed an apostate. This view is argued by his saying, peace be upon him: "I have been commanded to fight people until they say: There is no god but God; when they say it, they protect from me their blood and their wealth." But this is interpreted by the majority as meaning the utterance of the two testimonies, and the mention of one of them suffices over the other due to their interconnection and their fame. And God knows best.

As for when he acknowledges the obligation of prayer, or fasting, or other pillars of Islām, while he is upon a religion contrary to his former one — is he thereby judged a Muslim? There are two views among our companions. Those who judge him a Muslim said: ...

chapters.title_en: The Rulings on Faith (Al-Īmān): Declarations, Exceptions, and the Status of the Unbeliever
chapters.arabic_text:
كل ما يكفر المسلم بإنكاره يصير الكافر بالإقرار به مسلما أما إذا أقر

بالشهادتين بالعجمية وهو يحسن العربية فهل يجعل بذلك مسلما فيه وجهان

لأصحابنا الصحيح منهما أنه يصير مسلما لوجود الإقرار وهذا الوجه هو الحق

ولا يظهر للآخر وجه وقد بينت ذلك مستقصى في شرح المهذب والله أعلم واختلفا
# 
# العلماء من السلف وغيرهم في إطلاق الإنسان قوله أنا مؤمن فقالت طائفة لا

يقول أنا مؤمن مقتصرا عليه بل يقول أنا مؤمن إن شاء الله وحكى هذا المذهب

بعض أصحابنا عن أكثر أصحابنا المتكلمين وذهب آخرون إلى جواز الاطلاق وأنه

لايقول إن شاء الله وهذا هو المختار وقول أهل التحقيق وذهب الأوزاعي وغيره

إلى جواز الأمرين والكل صحيح باعتبارات مختلفة فمن أطلق نظر إلى الحال

وأحكام الإيمان جارية عليه في الحال ومن قال إن شاء الله فقالوا فيه هو إما

للتبرك وإما لاعتبار العاقبة وما قدر الله تعالى فلا يدري أيثبت على

الإيمان أم يصرف عنه والقول بالتخيير حسن صحيح نظرا إلى مأخذ القولين

الأولين ورفعا لحقيقة الخلاف وأما الكافر ففيه خلاف غريب لأصحابنا منهم من

قال يقال هو كافر ولا يقول إن  شاء الله ومنهم من قال هو في التقييد كالمسلم

على ما تقدم فيقال على قول التقييد هو كافر إن شاء الله نظرا إلى الخاتمة

وأنها مجهولة وهذا القول اختاره بعض المحققين والله أعلم واعلم أن مذهب أهل

الحق أنه لا يكفر أحد من أهل القبلة بذنب ولا يكفر أهل الأهواء والبدع وأن

من جحد ما يعلم من دين الإسلام ضرورة حكم بردته وكفره إلا أن يكون قريب عهد

بالإسلام أو نشأ ببادية بعيدة ونحوه ممن يخفى عليه فيعرف ذلك فإن استمر حكم

بكفره وكذا حكم من استحل الزنى أو الخمر أو القتل أو غير ذلك من المحرمات

التي يعلم تحريمها ضرورة فهذه جمل من المسائل المتعلقة بالإيمان قدمتها في

صدر الكتاب تمهيدا لكونها مما يكثر الاحتياج إليه ولكثرة تكررها وتردادها

في الأحاديث فقدمتها لأحيل عليها اذا مررت بما يحرج عليها والله أعلم

بالصواب وله الحمد والنعمة وبه التوفيق والعصمة قال الإمام أبو الحسين مسلم

بن الحجاج رضي الله عنه
# [8] (حدثني أبو خيثمة زهير بن حرب ثنا وكيع عن كهمس عن عبد الله بن بريدة

عن يحيى بن
# 
# يعمر ح وثنا عبيد الله بن معاذ العنبري وهذا حديثه ثنا أبى ثنا كهمس عن

بن بريدة عن يحيى بن يعمر قال كان أول من قال في القدر بالبصرة معبد الجهني

إلى آخر الحديث) اعلم أن مسلما رحمه الله سلك في هذا الكتاب طريقة في

الإتقان والاحتياط والتدقيق والتحقيق مع الاختصار البليغ والإيجاز التام في

نهاية من الحسن مصرحة بغزارة علومه ودقة نظره وحذقه وذلك يظهر في الإسناد

تارة وفي المتن تارة وفيهما تارة فينبغي للناظر في كتابه أن يتنبه لما

ذكرته فإنه يجد عجائب من النفائس والدقائق تقر بآحاد أفرادها عينه وينشرح

لها صدره وتنشطه للاشتغال بهذا العلم واعلم أنه لا يعرف أحد شارك مسلما في

هذه النفائس التي يشير إليها من دقائق علم الإسناد وكتاب البخاري وإن كان

أصح وأجل وأكثر فوائد في الأحكام والمعاني فكتاب مسلم يمتاز بزوائد من صنعة

الإسناد وسترى مما أنبه عليه من ذلك ما ينشرح له صدرك ويزداد به الكتاب

ومصنفه في قلبك جلالة إن شاء الله تعالى فإذا تقرر ما قلته ففي هذه الأحرف

التي ذكرها من الإسناد أنواع مما ذكرته فمن ذلك أنه قال أولا حدثني أبو

خيثمة ثم قال في الطريق الآخر وحدثنا عبيد الله بن معاذ ففرق بين حدثني

وحدثنا وهذا تنبيه على القاعدة المعروفة عند أهل الصنعة وهي أنه يقول فيما

سمعه وحده من لفظ الشيخ حدثني وفيما سمعه مع غيره من لفظ الشيخ حدثنا وفيما

قرأه وحده على الشيخ أخبرني وفيما قرئ بحضرته في جماعة على الشيخ أخبرنا

وهذا اصطلاح معروف عندهم وهو مستحب عندهم ولو تركه وأبدل حرفا من ذلك بآخر

صح السماع ولكن ترك الأولى والله أعلم ومن ذلك أنه قال في الطريق الأول

حدثنا وكيع عن كهمس عن عبد الله بن بريدة عن يحيى بن يعمر ثم في الطريق

الثانى أعاد الرواية عن كهمس عن بن بريدة عن يحيى فقد يقال هذا تطويل لا

يليق بإتقان مسلم واختصاره فكان ينبغي أن يقف بالطريق الأول على وكيع

ويجتمع معاذ ووكيع في الرواية عن كهمس عن بن بريدة وهذا الاعتراض فاسد لا

يصدر إلا من شديد الجهالة بهذا الفن فإن مسلما رحمه الله يسلك الاختصار لكن

بحيث لا يحصل خلل ولا يفوت به مقصود وهذا الموضع يحصل في الاختصار فيه خلل

ويفوت به مقصود وذلك لأن وكيعا قال عن كهمس ومعاذ قال حدثنا
# 
# كهمس وقد علم بما قدمناه في باب المعنعن أن العلماء اختلفوا فى الاحتجاج

بالمعنعن ولم يختلفوا فى المتصل بحدثنا فأتى مسلم بالروايتين كما سمعتا

ليعرف المتفق عليه من المختلف فيه وليكون راويا باللفظ الذي سمعه ولهذا

نظائر في مسلم ستراها مع التنبيه عليها إن شاء الله تعالى وإن كان مثل هذا

ظاهرا لمن له أدنى اعتناء بهذا الفن إلا أني أنبه عليه لغيرهم ولبعضهم ممن
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Covering, concealing; ingratitude; disbelief as veiling the truth.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Kufr as the rejection of divine unity (tawḥīd) and revealed mandates; its opposite is īmān (faith).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) in theological usage for denial of what is known necessarily; metaphorical (majāz) for minor ingratitude.
- Root: أ-م-ن (a-m-n)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Security, safety; to trust, to believe; īmān as inward assent and outward submission.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Īmān is the assent of the heart (taṣdīq) coupled with works; its perfection varies by degree.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for conviction; metaphorical for mere verbal profession without inner verification.
- Root: ش-ه-د (sh-h-d)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To witness, testify, bear witness; shahāda as the declaration of faith.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Testimony that establishes legal rulings in this world, even if inner state is known only to God.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for oral utterance; metaphorical for living testimony through deeds.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional and Exceptive Syntax (al-sharṭ wa al-istithnāʾ) — The phrase "in shāʾ Allāh" (إن شاء الله) functions as a suspended clause (taʿlīq) affecting the predicate's temporal scope, not its essential truth.
chapters.translation:
I say: Everything by the denial of which a Muslim becomes an unbeliever, by the affirmation of it the unbeliever becomes a Muslim. However, if he affirms the two testimonies (al-shahādatayn) in a non-Arab tongue while he is proficient in Arabic, is he thereby rendered a Muslim? There are two faces (wajhān) among our companions. The sounder of the two is that he becomes a Muslim, due to the existence of the affirmation (al-iqrār); and this face is the truth. No sound basis appears for the other. I have explained this exhaustively in my commentary on al-Muhadhdhab. And God knows best.

The scholars among the Salaf and others have differed concerning a person's unrestricted utterance of his saying, "I am a believer" (anā muʾmin). A group said: He should not say "I am a believer" confining himself to it, but rather say, "I am a believer, if God wills" (anā muʾmin in shāʾ Allāh). Some of our companions related this school from the majority of our theological companions (al-mutakallimīn). Others held the permissibility of the unrestricted form, and that he should not say "if God wills." This is the chosen view (al-mukhtār) and the saying of the people of verification (ahl al-taḥqīq). Al-Awzāʿī and others held the permissibility of both matters. All are sound according to different considerations. For whoever uses the unrestricted form looks to the present state, and the rulings of faith are operative upon him in the present. As for those who say "if God wills," they said concerning it: It is either for seeking blessing (tabarruk) or for considering the final outcome (al-ʿāqiba), for what God—exalted is He—has decreed, a person does not know whether he will remain steadfast upon faith or be turned away from it. The view of choosing either is good and sound, considering the bases of the first two views and lifting the reality of the disagreement.

As for the unbeliever, there is a curious disagreement among our companions. Some of them said: It is said of him, "He is an unbeliever," and he does not say "if God wills." Others said: He is, in the restriction, like the Muslim, as previously mentioned. Thus on the view of restriction, it is said: "He is an unbeliever, if God wills," considering the final end and that it is unknown. This view was chosen by some of the verifiers. And God knows best.

Know that the school of the people of truth (ahl al-ḥaqq) is that no one among the people of the qibla is rendered an unbeliever by a sin, nor are the people of passions (ahl al-ahwāʾ) and innovations (ahl al-bidaʿ) rendered unbelievers. And that whoever denies what is known of the religion of Islam by necessity (ḍarūra), the ruling of apostasy (ridda) and unbelief is passed upon him—unless he be of recent acquaintance with Islam, or raised in a remote desert, or the like of one for whom it is hidden, so he is to be taught it. If he persists, the ruling of unbelief is passed upon him. Likewise is the ruling for one who deems lawful (istaḥalla) fornication, wine, murder, or other forbidden things whose prohibition is known by necessity. These are summaries of matters pertaining to faith which I have presented at the outset of this book as a preamble, because of the frequent need for them and their repeated occurrence in the ḥadīths. So I have presented them to refer back to them whenever I pass by something that requires them. And God knows best what is correct; to Him belongs praise and grace, and from Him is success and protection.

Imam Abū al-Ḥusayn Muslim ibn al-Ḥajjāj—may God be pleased with him—said:

[8] (He narrated to me Abū Khaythama Zuhayr ibn Ḥarb; he narrated to us Wakīʿ, from Kahmas, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Burayda, from Yaḥyā ibn Yaʿmar. And he narrated to us ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Muʿādh al-ʿAnbarī—and this is his ḥadīth—he narrated to us my father, he narrated to us Kahmas, from Ibn Burayda, from Yaḥyā ibn Yaʿmar. He said: The first to speak about qadar (divine decree) in Basra was Maʿbad al-Juhanī... to the end of the ḥadīth.)

Know that Muslim—may God have mercy on him—followed in this book a method of precision (itqān), caution (iḥtiyāṭ), exactness (tadqīq), and verification (taḥqīq), combined with eloquent brevity and complete conciseness, in the utmost degree of excellence, plainly declaring the abundance of his sciences, the subtlety of his view, and his mastery. This appears sometimes in the chain of transmission (al-isnād), sometimes in the text (al-matn), and sometimes in both. It behooves the examiner of his book to pay attention to what I have mentioned, for he will find wonders of precious subtleties and fine points at which his eye will rejoice in their individual instances, his breast will expand with them, and they will rouse him to devote himself to this science.

Know that no one is known to have shared with Muslim in these precious subtleties to which he points, from the fine points of the science of transmission. The book of al-Bukhārī, although it is more sound, more exalted, and more abundant in benefits regarding rulings and meanings, the book of Muslim is distinguished by additional merits in the craft of transmission (ṣināʿat al-isnād). You will see, from what I point out of that, what will expand your breast and increase in your heart the veneration of the book and its author, if God—exalted is He—wills.

Now that what I have said is established, in these letters he mentioned from the chain of transmission there are types of what I have mentioned. Among them: He said first, "He narrated to me Abū Khaythama" (ḥaddathanī), then he said in the other path, "And he narrated to us ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Muʿādh" (ḥaddathanā). Thus he distinguished between ḥaddathanī and ḥaddathanā. This is an indication of the well-known rule among the people of this craft: that one says ḥaddathanī for what he heard alone from the mouth of the shaykh, and ḥaddathanā for what he heard with others from the mouth of the shaykh; and akhbaranī for what he read alone to the shaykh, and akhbaranā for what was read in his presence in a group to the shaykh. This is a known convention among them, and it is recommended (mustaḥabb) among them. Even if he abandoned it and substituted one letter for another, the hearing (samāʿ) would still be sound, but abandoning the preferable is [not ideal]. And God knows best.

Among them: He said in the first path, "He narrated to us Wakīʿ, from Kahmas, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Burayda, from Yaḥyā ibn Yaʿmar." Then in the second path, he repeated the narration from Kahmas, from Ibn Burayda, from Yaḥyā. It might be said: This is a prolongation unbefitting Muslim's precision and conciseness; he should have stopped the first path at Wakīʿ, and Muʿādh and Wakīʿ would have met in narrating from Kahmas, from Ibn Burayda, from Yaḥyā. But this objection is corrupt, and issues only from one of extreme ignorance of this art. For Muslim—may God have mercy on him—follows conciseness, but in such a way that no defect occurs and no purpose is lost. In this place, conciseness would produce a defect and lose a purpose. That is because Wakīʿ said "from Kahmas" (ʿan), while Muʿādh said "he narrated to us Kahmas" (ḥaddathanā). And it is known, from what we have previously presented in the chapter on the ʿanʿana (the use of "from" in transmission), that the scholars differed concerning argumentation by the ʿanʿana, but they did not differ concerning the connected transmission by ḥaddathanā. So Muslim brought both narrations as they were heard, to make known the agreed-upon from the disputed, and to be a transmitter with the very wording he heard. There are parallels to this in Muslim which you will see, with attention drawn to them, if God—exalted is He—wills. Even if such a thing is apparent to anyone with the least concern for this art, I still point it out for others, and for some of them who...
