The venerable Imam Abū Muḥammad ʿAbdullāh ibn Abī Zayd, the Imam of the Mālikīs in the Maghrib in his time, said: "The sum of the etiquettes of goodness branches from four hadiths: The Prophet's saying, peace and blessings be upon him, 'Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him speak good or remain silent' {«مَنْ كَانَ يُؤْمِنُ بِاللَّهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ فَلْيَقُلْ خَيْرًا أَوْ لِيَصْمُتْ»}; his saying, peace and blessings be upon him, 'From the excellence of a person's Islam is his leaving what does not concern him' {«مِنْ حُسْنِ إِسْلَامِ الْمَرْءِ تَرْكُهُ مَا لَا يَعْنِيهِ»}; his saying, peace and blessings be upon him, to the one to whom he abbreviated the counsel, 'Do not become angry' {«لَا تَغْضَبْ»}; and his saying, peace and blessings be upon him, 'None of you believes until he loves for his brother what he loves for himself' {«لَا يُؤْمِنُ أَحَدُكُمْ حَتَّى يُحِبَّ لِأَخِيهِ مَا يُحِبُّ لِنَفْسِهِ»}." And Allah knows best.

We have related from the master Abū al-Qāsim al-Qushayrī, may Allah have mercy on him, that he said: "Silence with safety is the principle, and keeping quiet at its proper time is a trait of men, just as speaking in its proper place is among the noblest of qualities." He said: "I heard Abū ʿAlī al-Daqqāq say: 'Whoever remains silent about the truth is a mute devil (shayṭān akhras).'" He said: "As for the preference of the people of spiritual striving (ahl al-mujāhadah) for silence, it is because they know the afflictions in speech — then what is in it of the soul's share, the display of praiseworthy traits, the inclination to distinguish oneself among one's peers by eloquence, and other such afflictions. That is the description of the masters of discipline (arbāb al-riyāḍah), and it is one of their pillars in the station of spiritual combat (al-munāzalah) and the refinement of character."

We have related from al-Fuḍayl ibn ʿIyāḍ, may Allah have mercy on him, that he said: "Whoever counts his speech as part of his deeds, his speech about what does not concern him becomes little." And from Dhū al-Nūn, may Allah have mercy on him: "The most protective of people of his own soul is the most restrained of them of his tongue." And Allah knows best.

As for his saying, peace and blessings be upon him, "Let him not harm his neighbor" {«فَلَا يُؤْذِي جَارَهُ»}, thus it occurs in the sources with the yāʾ at its end (yuʾdhī). We have related in other than Muslim: "lā yuʾdhi" with its omission. Both are correct: its omission is for the imperative (nahy), and its inclusion is as a declarative (khabar) by which the imperative is intended, making it more emphatic. From this is the saying of the Exalted: {«لَا تُضَارَّ وَالِدَةٌ بِوَلَدِهَا»} ("Let not a mother be harmed by her child") on the reading of those who raise (rafʿ), and from this is his saying, peace and blessings be upon him: "Let none of you sell over the sale of his brother" {«لَا يَبِيعُ أَحَدُكُمْ عَلَى بَيْعِ أَخِيهِ»}, and similar examples are many. And Allah knows best.

As for the chains of transmission (asānīd) of this chapter, Muslim, may Allah have mercy on him, said: "Abū Bakr ibn Abī Shaybah narrated to us, from Abū al-Aḥwaṣ, from Abū Ḥuṣayn, from Abū Ṣāliḥ, from Abū Hurayrah." This chain is entirely Kūfan and Meccan, except for Abū Hurayrah, for he is Medinan. The explanation of all their names has preceded in their places. "Ḥuṣayn" is with the fatḥah on the ḥāʾ. As for his saying in the other chain, "from Abū Shurayḥ al-Khuzāʿī," we have already presented at the end of the commentary on the introduction of the book the disagreement over his name: it is said his name is Khulayd ibn ʿAmr, and it is said ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, and it is said ʿAmr ibn Khulayd, and it is said Hāniʾ ibn ʿAmr, and it is said Kaʿb. And it is said he is called al-Khuzāʿī, al-ʿAdawī, and al-Kaʿbī. And Allah knows best.

| (Chapter: The Explanation that Forbidding Evil is Part of Faith, and that Faith Increases and Decreases, and that Enjoining Good and Forbidding Evil are Both Obligatory) |

[49] His saying: "The first to begin with the sermon on the day of the Festival before the prayer was Marwān." Al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ, may Allah have mercy on him, said: "There is disagreement on this. What occurs here is what we see. It is said the first to begin with the sermon before the prayer was ʿUthmān, may Allah be pleased with him, and it is said ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, may Allah be pleased with him, when he saw the people..."

chapters.title_en: Section 99 — On the Prayer Before the Sermon, the Obligation of Enjoining Good and Forbidding Evil, and Its Conditions
chapters.arabic_text:
يذهبون عند تمام الصلاة ولا ينتظرون الخطبة وقيل بل ليدرك الصلاة من تأخر

وبعد منزله وقيل أول من فعله معاوية وقيل فعله بن الزبير رضي الله عنه

والذي ثبت عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وأبي بكر وعمر وعثمان وعلي رضي الله

عنهم تقديم الصلاة وعليه جماعة فقهاء الأمصار وقد عده بعضهم إجماعا يعني

والله أعلم بعد الخلاف أولم يلتفت إلى خلاف بني أمية بعد إجماع الخلفاء

والصدر الأول وفي قوله بعد هذا أما هذا فقد قضى ما عليه بمحضر من ذلك الجمع

العظيم دليل على استقرار السنة عندهم على خلاف ما فعله مروان وبينه أيضا

احتجاجه بقوله سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول من رأى منكم منكرا

فليغيره ولا يسمى منكرا لو اعتقده ومن حضر أوسبق به عمل أو مضت به سنة وفي

هذا دليل على أنه لم يعمل به خليفة قبل مروان وأن ما حكي عن عمر وعثمان

ومعاوية لا يصح والله أعلم قوله (فقام إليه رجل فقال الصلاة قبل الخطبة

فقال قد ترك ما هنالك فقال أبو سعيد أما هذا)
# 
# فقد قضى ما عليه سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول من رأى منكم

منكرا فليغيره بيده الحديث) قد يقال كيف تأخر أبو سعيد رضي الله عنه عن

إنكار هذا المنكر حتى سبقه إليه هذا الرجل وجوابه أنه يحتمل أن أبا سعيد لم

يكن حاضرا أول ما شرع مروان في أسباب تقديم الخطبة فأنكر عليه الرجل ثم دخل

أبو سعيد وهما في الكلام ويحتمل أن أبا سعيد كان حاضرا من الأول ولكنه خاف

على نفسه أو غيره حصول فتنة بسبب إنكاره فسقط عنه الإنكار ولم يخف ذلك

الرجل شيئا لاعتضاده بظهور عشيرته أو غير ذلك أو أنه خاف وخاطر بنفسه وذلك

جائز في  مثل هذا بل مستحب ويحتمل أن أبا سعيد هم بالإنكار فبدره الرجل

فعضده أبو سعيد والله أعلم ثم أنه جاء في الحديث الآخر الذي اتفق البخاري

ومسلم رضي الله عنهما على إخراجه في باب صلاة العيد أن أبا سعيد هو الذي

جذب بيد مروان حين رآه يصعد المنبر وكانا جاءا معا فرد عليه مروان بمثل ما

رد هنا على الرجل فيحتمل أنهما قضيتان إحداهما لأبي سعيد والأخرى للرجل

بحضرة أبي سعيد والله أعلم وأما قوله فقد قضى ما عليه ففيه تصريح بالإنكار

أيضا من أبي سعيد وأما قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم فليغيره فهو أمر إيجاب

بإجماع الأمة وقد تطابق على وجوب الأمر بالمعروف والنهي عن المنكر الكتاب

والسنة وإجماع الأمة وهو أيضا من النصيحة التي هي الدين ولم يخالف في ذلك

إلا بعض الرافضة ولا يعتد بخلافهم كما قال الإمام أبو المعالي إمام الحرمين

لا يكترث بخلافهم في هذا فقد أجمع المسلمون عليه قبل أن ينبغ هؤلاء ووجوبه

بالشرع لا بالعقل خلافا للمعتزلة وأما قول الله عز وجل عليكم أنفسكم لا

يضركم من ضل إذا اهتديتم فليس مخالفا لما ذكرناه لأن المذهب الصحيح عند

المحققين في معنى الآية أنكم إذا فعلتم ما كلفتم به فلا يضركم تقصير غيركم

مثل قوله تعالى ولا تزر وازرة وزر أخرى وإذا كان كذلك فمما كلف به الأمر

بالمعروف والنهي عن المنكر فإذا فعله ولم يمتثل المخاطب فلا عتب بعد ذلك

على الفاعل لكونه أدى ما عليه فإنما
# 
# عليه الأمر والنهي لا القبول والله أعلم ثم إن الأمر بالمعروف والنهي عن

المنكر فرض كفاية إذا قام به بعض الناس سقط الحرج عن الباقين وإذا تركه

الجميع أثم كل من تمكن منه بلا عذر ولا خوف ثم إنه قد يتعين كما إذا كان في

موضع لا يعلم به الا هو أولا يتمكن من إزالته إلا هو وكمن يرى زوجته أو

ولده أو غلامه على منكر أو تقصير في المعروف قال العلماء رضي الله عنهم ولا

يسقط عن المكلف الأمر بالمعروف والنهي عن المنكر لكونه لا يفيد في ظنه بل

يجب عليه فعله فإن الذكرى تنفع المؤمنين وقد قدمنا أن الذي عليه الأمر

والنهي لا القبول وكما قال الله عز وجل ما على الرسول إلا البلاغ ومثل

العلماء هذا بمن يرى إنسانا في الحمام أو غيره مكشوف بعض العورة ونحو ذلك

والله أعلم قال العلماء ولا يشترط في الآمر والناهي أن يكون كامل الحال

ممتثلا ما يأمر به مجتنبا ما ينهى عنه بل عليه الأمر وإن كان مخلا بما يأمر

به والنهي وإن كان متلبسا بما ينهى عنه فإنه يجب عليه شيئان أن يأمر نفسه

وينهاها ويأمر غيره وينهاه فإذا أخل بأحدهما كيف يباح له الإخلال بالآخر

قال العلماء ولا يختص الأمر بالمعروف والنهي عن المنكر بأصحاب الولايات بل

ذلك جائز لآحاد المسلمين قال إمام الحرمين والدليل عليه إجماع المسلمين فإن

غير الولاة في الصدر الأول والعصر الذي يليه كانوا يأمرون الولاة بالمعروف

وينهونهم عن المنكر مع تقرير المسلمين إياهم وترك توبيخهم على التشاغل

بالأمر بالمعروف والنهي عن المنكر من غير ولاية والله أعلم ثم إنه إنما

يأمر وينهى من كان عالما بما يأمر به وينهى عنه وذلك يختلف باختلاف الشيء

فإن كان من الواجبات الظاهرة والمحرمات المشهورة كالصلاة والصيام والزنا

والخمر ونحوها فكل المسلمين علماء بها وإن كان من دقائق الأفعال والأقوال

ومما يتعلق بالاجتهاد لم يكن للعوام مدخل فيه ولا لهم إنكاره بل ذلك
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ق-ض-ي (qaḍā)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To accomplish, fulfill, or discharge a duty; to settle a matter decisively.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The completion of an obligation (taklīf) such that nothing remains due; used of God's decree and of human fulfillment of commands.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal in reference to judicial settlement and fulfillment; metaphorical here in the sense of "he has discharged his duty."
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional-Responsive Construction (al-Sharṭ wa al-Jawāb) — The phrase "من رأى منكم منكرا فليغيره" employs an imperative as the response to a conditional clause, indicating universal applicability.
chapters.translation:
They depart upon completion of the prayer and do not wait for the sermon. And it was said: rather, [the delay] was so that those who arrived late could catch the prayer. And it was said: the first to do this was Muʿāwiyah. And it was said: Ibn al-Zubayr (may Allah be pleased with him) did it. What is authentically established from the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him), Abū Bakr, ʿUmar, ʿUthmān, and ʿAlī (may Allah be pleased with them) is the advancement of the prayer [before the sermon], and upon this are the majority of the jurists of the regions. Some have counted it as consensus (ijmāʿ) — meaning, and Allah knows best — after the disagreement, or they did not pay attention to the disagreement of the Umayyads after the consensus of the Rightly-Guided Caliphs and the early generation. And in his statement after this — "As for this one, he has discharged what was upon him" — in the presence of that great gathering, there is evidence that the established practice (sunnah) among them was contrary to what Marwān did. This is also clarified by his argument when he said: "I heard the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) say: 'Whoever among you sees an evil, let him change it.'" And a thing is not called an evil (munkar) if one believes it to be permissible, nor if one attends it, nor if a practice has preceded it, nor if a sunnah has passed regarding it. In this there is evidence that no caliph before Marwān acted upon this [i.e., advancing the sermon], and that what was narrated from ʿUmar, ʿUthmān, and Muʿāwiyah is not authentic. And Allah knows best.

His statement (a man stood up to him and said: "The prayer before the sermon!" He [Marwān] replied: "That has been abandoned." Then Abū Saʿīd said: "As for this one, he has discharged what was upon him. I heard the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) say: 'Whoever among you sees an evil, let him change it with his hand'") — the hadith. It may be asked: how did Abū Saʿīd (may Allah be pleased with him) delay in denouncing this evil until the man preceded him in it? The answer is that it is possible Abū Saʿīd was not present at the very beginning when Marwān commenced the measures of advancing the sermon, so the man denounced him, then Abū Saʿīd entered while they were speaking. And it is possible Abū Saʿīd was present from the beginning, but he feared for himself or for others the occurrence of tribulation (fitnah) due to his denunciation, so the obligation of denunciation fell from him — whereas that man feared nothing, being strengthened by the prominence of his clan or otherwise. Or [it is possible] he feared and risked himself, and that is permissible in such a matter — rather, it is recommended (mustaḥabb). And it is possible Abū Saʿīd intended to denounce, but the man preceded him, so Abū Saʿīd supported him. And Allah knows best.

Then, in the other hadith which al-Bukhārī and Muslim (may Allah be pleased with them) agreed upon in the chapter on the ʿĪd prayer, it is reported that Abū Saʿīd was the one who pulled Marwān's hand when he saw him ascending the pulpit, and the two had come together. Marwān replied to him with the same reply he gave here to the man. So it is possible these were two incidents — one involving Abū Saʿīd and the other involving the man in the presence of Abū Saʿīd. And Allah knows best.

As for his statement "he has discharged what was upon him," it contains an explicit denunciation from Abū Saʿīd as well. As for his statement (peace and blessings be upon him) "let him change it," it is a command of obligation (amr ījāb) by consensus of the ummah. The Book, the Sunnah, and the consensus of the ummah have concurred upon the obligation of enjoining good and forbidding evil. It is also part of the sincere counsel (naṣīḥah) which is the religion. None opposed this except some of the Rāfiḍah, and their opposition is not to be counted, as Imām Abū al-Maʿālī, Imām al-Ḥaramayn, said: "No heed is paid to their opposition in this, for the Muslims have agreed upon it before these emerged." Its obligation is by the Sacred Law (sharʿ), not by reason — contrary to the Muʿtazilah.

As for the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: {«عَلَيْكُمْ أَنفُسَكُمْ ۖ لَا يَضُرُّكُم مَّن ضَلَّ إِذَا اهْتَدَيْتُمْ»} ("Upon you are your own selves; those who go astray will not harm you when you are guided") — this does not contradict what we have mentioned, because the sound position (al-madhhab al-ṣaḥīḥ) among the verifiers regarding the meaning of the verse is: when you do what you have been charged with, the shortcoming of others does not harm you — like His saying, Exalted is He: {«وَلَا تَزِرُ وَازِرَةٌ وِزْرَ أُخْرَىٰ»} ("And no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another"). If this is so, then among what one is charged with is enjoining good and forbidding evil. So if he does it and the addressed person does not comply, there is no blame thereafter upon the doer, because he has discharged what was upon him — for upon him is only the enjoining and the forbidding, not the acceptance. And Allah knows best.

Then, enjoining good and forbidding evil is a communal obligation (farḍ kifāyah): if some people undertake it, the burden falls from the rest; and if all abandon it, every one who is able to do it without excuse or fear sins. Then it may become individually obligatory (mutʿayyan) — as when one is in a place where none knows of it except him, or none can remove it except him; and like one who sees his wife, his child, or his servant upon an evil or a shortcoming in good. The scholars (may Allah be pleased with them) said: the obligation of enjoining good and forbidding evil does not fall from the accountable person (mukallaf) because he thinks it will not be effective; rather, he must do it, for the reminder benefits the believers. We have already stated that upon him is the enjoining and the forbidding, not the acceptance — as Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: {«مَا عَلَى الرَّسُولِ إِلَّا الْبَلَاغُ»} ("Upon the Messenger is only the conveyance"). The scholars likened this to one who sees a person in the bathhouse or elsewhere with part of his ʿawrah exposed, and the like. And Allah knows best.

The scholars said: it is not a condition for the one who enjoins and forbids that he be perfect in his own state — complying with what he commands and avoiding what he forbids. Rather, he must enjoin even if he is deficient in what he commands, and forbid even if he is engaged in what he forbids. For two things are obligatory upon him: to command himself and forbid himself, and to command others and forbid others. So if he is deficient in one of them, how could it be permissible for him to be deficient in the other?

The scholars said: enjoining good and forbidding evil is not restricted to those in positions of authority; rather, it is permissible for individual Muslims. Imām al-Ḥaramayn said: the evidence for this is the consensus of the Muslims — for in the early generation and the era following it, those who were not rulers used to command the rulers to good and forbid them from evil, with the Muslims affirming them and not rebuking them for occupying themselves with enjoining good and forbidding evil without holding authority. And Allah knows best.

Then, one only enjoins and forbids if he is knowledgeable of what he enjoins and forbids. This varies according to the matter: if it is among the manifest obligations and well-known prohibitions — like prayer, fasting, fornication, wine, and the like — then all Muslims are knowledgeable of them. But if it is among the subtle matters of actions and sayings, and what pertains to independent reasoning (ijtihād), then the common people have no entry into it, nor do they have the right to denounce it. Rather, that is...

chapters.title_en: The Obligation of Enjoining Good and Forbidding Evil: Its Ranks, Conditions, and the Limits of Disagreement
chapters.arabic_text:
للعلماء ثم العلماء إنما ينكرون ما أجمع عليه أما المختلف فيه فلا إنكار

فيه لأن على أحد المذهبين كل مجتهد مصيب وهذا هو المختار عند كثيرين من

المحققين أو أكثرهم وعلى المذهب الآخر المصيب واحد والمخطىء غير متعين لنا

والإثم مرفوع عنه لكن إن ندبه على جهة النصيحة إلى الخروج من الخلاف فهو

حسن محبوب مندوب إلى فعله برفق فإن العلماء متفقون على الحث على الخروج من

الخلاف إذا لم يلزم منه إخلال بسنة أو وقوع في خلاف آخر وذكر  أقضى القضاة

أبو الحسن الماوردي البصري الشافعي في كتابه الأحكام السلطانية خلافا بين

العلماء في أن من قلده
# 
# السلطان الحسبة هل له أن يحمل الناس على مذهبه فيما اختلف فيه الفقهاء

إذا كان المحتسب من أهل الاجتهاد أم لا يغير ما كان على مذهب غيره والأصح

أنه لا يغير لما ذكرناه ولم يزل الخلاف في الفروع بين الصحابة والتابعين

فمن بعدهم رضي الله عنهم أجمعين ولا ينكر محتسب ولا غيره على غيره وكذلك

قالوا ليس للمفتي ولا للقاضي أن يعترض على من خالفه إذا لم يخالف نصا أو

اجماعا أوقياسا جليا والله أعلم واعلم أن هذا الباب أعني باب الأمر

بالمعروف والنهي عن المنكر قد ضيع أكثره من أزمان متطاولة ولم يبق منه في

هذه الأزمان إلا رسوم قليلة جدا وهو باب عظيم به قوام الأمر وملاكه واذا

كثر الخبث عم العقاب الصالح والطالح وإذا لم يأخذوا على يد الظالم أوشك أن

يعمهم الله تعالى بعقابه فليحذر الذين يخالفون عن أمره أن تصيبهم فتنة أو

يصيبهم عذاب أليم فينبغي لطالب الآخرة والساعي في تحصيل رضا الله عز وجل أن

يعتني بهذا الباب فإن نفعه عظيم لا سيما وقد ذهب معظمه ويخلص نيته ولا

يهابن من ينكر عليه لارتفاع مرتبته فإن الله تعالى قال ولينصرن الله من

ينصره وقال تعالى ومن يعتصم بالله فقد هدي إلى صراط مستقيم وقال تعالى

والذين جاهدوا فينا لنهدينهم سبلنا وقال تعالى أحسب الناس أن يتركوا أن

يقولوا آمنا وهم لا يفتنون ولقد فتنا الذين من قبلهم فليعلمن الله الذين

صدقوا وليعلمن الكاذبين واعلم أن الأجر على قدر النصب ولا يتاركه أيضا

لصداقته ومودته ومداهنته وطلب الوجاهة عنده ودوام المنزلة لديه فإن صداقته

ومودته توجب له حرمة وحقا ومن حقه أن ينصحه ويهديه إلى مصالح آخرته وينقذه

من مضارها وصديق الإنسان ومحبه هو من سعى في عمارة آخرته وإن أدى ذلك إلى

نقص في دنياه وعدوه من يسعى في ذهاب أو نقص آخرته وإن حصل بسبب  ذلك صورة

نفع في دنياه وإنما كان إبليس عدوا لنا لهذا وكانت الأنبياء صلوات الله

وسلامه عليهم أجمعين أولياء للمؤمنين لسعيهم في مصالح آخرتهم وهدايتهم

إليها ونسأل الله الكريم توفيقنا وأحبابنا وسائر المسلمين لمرضاته وأن

يعمنا بجوده ورحمته والله أعلم وينبغي للآمر بالمعروف والناهي عن المنكر أن

يرفق ليكون أقرب إلى تحصيل المطلوب فقد قال الإمام الشافعي رضي الله عنه من

وعظ أخاه سرا فقد نصحه وزانه ومن وعظه علانية فقد فضحه وشانه ومما يتساهل

أكثر الناس فيه من هذا الباب ما إذا رأى إنسانا يبيع متاعا معيبا أو نحوه

فإنهم لا ينكرون ذلك ولا يعرفون المشتري بعيبه وهذا خطأ ظاهر وقد
# 
# نص العلماء على أنه يجب على من علم ذلك أن ينكر على البائع وأن يعلم

المشتري به والله أعلم وأما صفة النهي ومراتبه فقد قال النبي صلى الله عليه

وسلم في هذا الحديث الصحيح فليغيره بيده فإن لم يستطع فبلسانه فإن لم يستطع

فبقلبه فقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم فبقلبه معناه فليكرهه بقلبه وليس ذلك

بإزالة وتغيير منه للمنكر ولكنه هو الذي في وسعه وقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم

(وذلك أضعف الإيمان) معناه والله أعلم أقله ثمرة قال القاضي عياض رحمه الله

هذا الحديث أصل في صفة التغيير فحق المغير أن يغيره بكل وجه أمكنه زواله به

قولا كان أو فعلا فيكسر آلات الباطل ويريق المسكر بنفسه أو يأمر من يفعله

وينزع الغصوب ويردها إلى أصحابها بنفسه أو بأمره إذا أمكنه ويرفق في

التغيير جهده بالجاهل وبذي العزة الظالم المخوف شره إذ ذلك أدعى إلى قبول

قوله كما يستحب أن يكون متولي ذلك من أهل الصلاح والفضل لهذا المعنى ويغلظ

على المتمادي في غيه والمسرف في بطالته إذا أمن أن يؤثر إغلاظه منكرا أشد

مما غيره لكون جانبه محميا عن سطوة الظالم فإن غلب على ظنه أن تغييره بيده

يسبب منكرا أشد منه من قتله أو قتل غيره بسبب كف يده واقتصر على القول

باللسان والوعظ والتخويف فإن  خاف أن يسبب قوله مثل ذلك غير بقلبه وكان في

سعة وهذا هو المراد بالحديث إن شاء الله تعالى وإن وجد من يستعين به على

ذلك استعان ما لم يؤد ذلك إلى إظهار سلاح وحرب وليرفع ذلك إلى من له الأمر

إن كان المنكر من غيره أو يقتصر على تغييره بقلبه هذا هو فقه المسألة وصواب

العمل فيها عند العلماء والمحققين خلافا لمن رأى الإنكار بالتصريح بكل حال

وإن قتل ونيل منه كل أذى هذا آخر كلام القاضي رحمه الله قال إمام الحرمين

رحمه الله ويسوغ لآحاد الرعية أن يصد مرتكب الكبيرة ان لم يندفع عنها بقوله
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ن-ك-ر (n-k-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To recognize, to disavow; the known versus the unknown (al-nakīr = the disavowed act).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Al-munkar is that which the sound intellect and divine law (Sharʿ) deem repugnant; its negation is al-inkār, the heart's and limb's repudiation.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: to change a physical object of wrong. Metaphorical: verbal rebuke or inward detestation when physical change is impossible.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional-Responsive Construction (al-sharṭ wa al-jawāb) — "If he cannot, then by tongue; if he cannot, then by heart" (fa-in lam yastaṭiʿ fa-bi-lisānihi...), where each protasis governs an elliptical apodosis, marking graded obligation (taklīf bi-ḥasab al-wusʿ).
chapters.translation:
I say: The scholars — then the scholars — only disapprove (yunkirūn) that upon which there is consensus (ijmāʿ). As for that in which there is disagreement (ikhtilāf), there is no disapproval therein, because upon one of the two schools (madhhabayn), every mujtahid is correct (muṣīb) — and this is the chosen position (al-mukhtār) according to many of the verifiers (muḥaqqiqīn), or most of them. Upon the other school, the correct one is single (al-muṣīb wāḥid), and the mistaken one is not specified to us (ghayr mutaʿayyin lanā), and sin (ithm) is lifted from him. However, if one urges him (nadabahu) by way of sincere counsel (naṣīḥah) to exit from the disagreement (al-khurūj min al-khilāf), that is excellent (ḥasan), beloved (maḥbūb), and recommended (mandūb) to do with gentleness (rifq). For the scholars are agreed upon urging the exit from disagreement when it does not entail neglecting a Sunnah or falling into another disagreement.

And the Chief Judge (Aqḍā al-Quḍāh) Abū al-Ḥasan al-Māwardī al-Baṣrī al-Shāfiʿī — may Allah have mercy on him — mentioned in his book *al-Aḥkām al-Sulṭāniyyah* a disagreement among the scholars concerning one whom the Sultan has appointed to the ḥisbah (market inspection): Is he permitted to compel the people to follow his own school (madhhab) in matters where the jurists (fuqahāʾ) disagreed, if the muḥtasib is among the people of ijtihād? Or does he not change what is upon the school of another? The more correct (al-aṣaḥḥ) is that he does not change it, for what we have mentioned. And disagreement in subsidiary matters (furūʿ) has never ceased between the Companions (al-Ṣaḥābah) and the Followers (al-Tābiʿīn) and those after them — may Allah be pleased with them all — and no muḥtasib or anyone else disapproves upon another. Likewise, they said: It is not for the muftī (one who issues legal rulings) nor for the judge (al-qāḍī) to object to (yaʿtariḍ) one who opposes him, when that one has not opposed a text (naṣṣ), a consensus (ijmāʿ), or a clear analogy (qiyās jalī). And Allah knows best.

Know that this chapter — I mean the chapter of enjoining good and forbidding evil — most of it has been neglected (ḍuyyiʿa) for long ages, and nothing remains of it in these times except very few vestiges (rusūm). And it is a mighty chapter; by it the very foundation of the affair (qiwām al-amr) and its mainstay (mālākuhu) subsist. When wickedness (khabuth) multiplies, the punishment (ʿiqāb) encompasses the righteous and the wicked alike. And if they do not seize the hand of the wrongdoer (al-ẓālim), it is near that Allah — exalted be He — will encompass them all with His punishment. So let those who oppose His command beware lest a trial (fitnah) strike them or a painful torment (ʿadhāb alīm) strike them. {«فليحذر الذين يخالفون عن أمره أن تصيبهم فتنة أو يصيبهم عذاب أليم»} (Q. 24:63).

It behooves the seeker of the Hereafter (ṭālib al-ākhirah) and the striver for the attainment of Allah's good pleasure — mighty and majestic is He — to attend to this chapter, for its benefit is immense, especially since most of it has vanished. And he should purify his intention (yukhliṣ niyyatahu), and not fear (lā yahābu) the one upon whom he enjoins disapproval due to the loftiness of that person's rank. For Allah — exalted be He — said: {«ولينصرن الله من ينصره»} (Q. 22:40) — "And Allah will surely aid those who aid Him." And He said — exalted be He: {«ومن يعتصم بالله فقد هدي إلى صراط مستقيم»} (Q. 3:101) — "And whoever holds fast to Allah has been guided to a straight path." And He said — exalted be He: {«والذين جاهدوا فينا لنهدينهم سبلنا»} (Q. 29:69) — "And those who strive in Us, We will surely guide them to Our ways." And He said — exalted be He: {«أحسب الناس أن يتركوا أن يقولوا آمنا وهم لا يفتنون * ولقد فتنا الذين من قبلهم فليعلمن الله الذين صدقوا وليعلمن الكاذبين»} (Q. 29:2-3) — "Do the people think they will be left to say, 'We believe,' while they will not be tried? And We have certainly tried those before them, so Allah will surely make evident those who are truthful and make evident the liars."

Know that the reward (al-ajr) is proportionate to the hardship (al-naṣab). And he should not abandon it either for the sake of friendship (ṣadāqah), affection (mawaddah), flattery (mudāhanah), seeking prestige (al-wajāhah) with him, or preserving his standing (al-manzilah) with him. For his friendship and affection entail for him a sanctity (ḥurmah) and a right (ḥaqq); and from his rights is that he counsel him sincerely (yanṣaḥahu) and guide him to the interests of his Hereafter (maṣāliḥ ākhiratihi) and rescue him from its harms (maḍārrihā). A person's true friend and beloved is the one who strives in building his Hereafter, even if that leads to a deficiency in his worldly life. And his enemy is the one who strives in the destruction or deficiency of his Hereafter, even if a semblance of worldly benefit (ṣūrat nafʿ) results from that. It was for this very reason that Iblīs was an enemy to us, and it was for this reason that the Prophets — may Allah's prayers and peace be upon them all — were the friends (awliyāʾ) of the believers, due to their striving in the interests of their Hereafter and their guidance to it. And we ask Allah the Generous (al-Karīm) to grant us, our beloved ones, and all Muslims success (tawfīq) to His good pleasure, and to encompass us with His bounty (jūd) and mercy (raḥmah). And Allah knows best.

It behooves the one who enjoins good and forbids evil to be gentle (yarfuq), for that is more conducive to attaining the sought goal (taḥṣīl al-maṭlūb). For Imām al-Shāfiʿī — may Allah be pleased with him — said: "Whoever admonishes his brother in secret has sincerely counseled him and adorned him (zānahu); and whoever admonishes him publicly has disgraced him (faḍaḥahu) and sullied him (shānahu)."

Among the matters in which most people are negligent (yatasāhalūna) in this chapter is when a person sees someone selling defective merchandise (matāʿ maʿīban) or the like — they do not disapprove of it, nor do they inform the buyer of its defect. This is a manifest error (khaṭaʾ ẓāhir). The scholars have explicitly stated (naṣṣū) that it is obligatory upon the one who knows of this to disapprove upon the seller and to inform the buyer of the defect. And Allah knows best.

As for the description of the prohibition (ṣifat al-nahy) and its ranks (marātibuhu), the Prophet — peace and blessings be upon him — said in this authentic ḥadīth: "Let him change it with his hand; if he cannot, then with his tongue; if he cannot, then with his heart." His saying — peace and blessings be upon him — "then with his heart" means: let him detest it (yukrihuhu) with his heart. That is not a removal (izālah) nor a change (taghyīr) of the wrong by him, but it is what lies within his capacity (wusʿihi). And his saying — peace and blessings be upon him — {«وذلك أضعف الإيمان»} — "And that is the weakest of faith" — means, and Allah knows best: the least in fruitfulness (aqalluhu thamarah).

Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ — may Allah have mercy on him — said: This ḥadīth is a foundational principle (aṣl) in the description of change (ṣifat al-taghyīr). The right of the one who changes is to change it by every means by which its removal is possible for him, whether by word (qawl) or deed (fiʿl). So he breaks the instruments of falsehood (ālāt al-bāṭil), spills the intoxicant (al-muskir) himself or commands one to do it, seizes back usurped property (al-ghuṣūb) and returns it to its owners himself or by his command, when possible. And he should be gentle (yarfuq) in his changing, to the utmost of his effort, with the ignorant one (al-jāhil) and with the powerful oppressor (dhū al-ʿizzah al-ẓālim) whose evil is feared — for that is more conducive to the acceptance of his words. Likewise, it is recommended (yustaḥabb) that the one undertaking this be among the people of righteousness (al-ṣalāḥ) and virtue (al-faḍl), for this very reason. And he should be stern (yughalliẓ) with the one who persists in his error (al-mutamāddī fī ghayyihi) and is excessive in his falsehood (al-musrif fī biṭālatihi), when he is secure that his sternness will not cause a wrong more severe than the one he is changing — because his side is protected (maḥmī) from the oppression of the tyrant. If he strongly suspects (ghalaba ʿalā ẓannihi) that his changing by hand will cause a more severe wrong — such as his own killing or the killing of another due to it — then he withholds his hand and confines himself to speech with the tongue, admonition (waʿẓ), and intimidation (takhwīf). If he fears that his speech would cause the like of that, then he changes with his heart, and he is within ample scope (fī saʿah). This is what is meant by the ḥadīth, Allah willing. And if he finds someone to assist him in that, he seeks assistance (istaʿāna), as long as that does not lead to the display of weapons (silāḥ) and warfare (ḥarb). And he should refer the matter (yarfaʿu) to those in authority (man lahu al-amr) if the wrong is from someone else, or confine himself to changing it with his heart. This is the jurisprudence of the matter (fiqh al-masʾalah) and the correct practice therein according to the scholars and the verifiers — contrary to those who held the view of disapproval by explicit declaration (al-inkār bi-l-taṣrīḥ) in every case, even if one is killed or subjected to every harm. This is the end of the speech of Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ — may Allah have mercy on him.

Imām al-Ḥaramayn — may Allah have mercy on him — said: It is permissible (yasūghu) for individual subjects (āḥād al-rāʿiyyah) to repel (yaṣudda) the perpetrator of a major sin (kabīrah) if he is not deterred from it by his speech.

chapters.title_en: On the Limits of Enjoining Good and Forbidding Evil, and the Conditions for Deposing a Tyrannical Ruler
chapters.arabic_text:
ما لم ينته الأمر إلى نصب قتال وشهر سلاح فإن انتهى الأمر إلى ذلك ربط

الأمر بالسلطان قال وإذا جار والي الوقت وظهر ظلمه وغشمه ولم ينزجر حين زجر

عن سوء صنيعه بالقول فلأهل الحل والعقد التواطؤ على خلعه ولو بشهر الأسلحة

ونصب الحروب هذا كلام إمام الحرمين وهذا الذي ذكره من خلعه غريب ومع هذا

فهو محمول
# 
# على ما إذا لم يخف منه إثارة مفسدة أعظم منه قال وليس للآمر بالمعروف

البحث والتنقير والتجسس واقتحام الدور بالظنون بل إن عثر على منكر غيره

جهده هذا كلام إمام الحرمين وقال أقضى القضاة الماوردي ليس للمحتسب أن يبحث

عما لم يظهر من المحرمات فإن غلب على الظن استسرار قوم بها لأمارة وآثار

ظهرت فذلك ضربان أحدهما أن يكون ذلك في انتهاك حرمة يفوت استدراكها مثل أن

يخبره من يثق بصدقه أن رجلا خلا برجل ليقتله أو بامرأة ليزني بها فيجوز له

في مثل هذا الحال أن يتجسس ويقدم على الكشف والبحث حذرا من فوات مالا

يستدرك وكذا لوعرف ذلك غير المحتسب من المتطوعة جازلهم الإقدام على الكشف

والإنكار الضرب الثاني ما قصر عن هذه الرتبة فلا يجوز التجسس عليه ولا كشف

الأستار عنه فإن سمع أصوات الملاهي المنكرة من دار أنكرها خارج الدار لم

يهجم عليها بالدخول لأن المنكر ظاهر وليس عليه أن يكشف  عن الباطن وقد ذكر

الماوردي في آخر الأحكام السلطانية بابا حسنا في الحسبة مشتملا على جمل من

قواعد الأمر بالمعروف والنهي عن المنكر وقد أشرنا هنا إلى مقاصدها وبسطت

الكلام في هذا الباب لعظم فائدته وكثرة الحاجة إليه وكونه من أعظم قواعد

الإسلام والله أعلم قوله (وحدثنا أبو كريب حدثنا أبو معاوية حدثنا الأعمش

عن إسماعيل بن رجاء عن أبيه عن أبي سعيد وعن قيس بن مسلم عن طارق بن شهاب

عن أبي سعيد) فقوله وعن قيس معطوف على إسماعيل معناه رواه الأعمش عن

إسماعيل عن قيس والله أعلم
# [50] قوله (عن صالح بن كيسان عن الحرث عن جعفر بن عبد الله بن الحكم عن
# 
# عبد الرحمن بن المسور عن أبي رافع عن عبد الله بن مسعود رضي الله عنه أن

رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال ما من نبي بعثه الله في أمة قبلي إلا كان

له من أمته حواريون وأصحاب يأخذون بسنته ويقتدون بأمره ثم إنها تخلف من

بعدهم خلوف يقولون ما لا يفعلون ويفعلون ما لا يؤمرون فمن جاهدهم بيده فهو

مؤمن ومن جاهدهم بلسانه فهو مؤمن ومن جاهدهم بقلبه فهو مؤمن وليس وراء ذلك

من الإيمان حبة خردل قال أبورافع فحدثت عبد الله بن عمر رضي الله عنهما

فانكره علي فقدم بن مسعود رضي الله عنه فنزل بقناة فاستتبعني إليه عبد الله

بن عمر رضي الله عنهما يعوده فانطلقت معه فلما جلسنا سألت بن مسعود عن هذا

الحديث فحدثنيه كما حدثته بن عمر قال صالح وقد تحدث بنحو ذلك عن أبى رافع)

أما الحرث فهو بن فضيل الأنصاري الخطمي أبو عبد الله المدني روى عن عبد

الرحمن بن أبي قراد الصحابي قال يحيى بن معين هو ثقة وأما أبو رافع فهو

مولى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم والأصح أن اسمه أسلم وقيل إبراهيم وقيل

هرمز وقيل ثابت وقيل يزيد وهو غريب حكاه بن الجوزى فى كتابه جامع المسانيد
# 
# وفى هذاالاسناد طريفة وهو أنه اجتمع فيه  أربعة تابعيون يروي بعضهم عن بعض

صالح والحرث وجعفر وعبد الرحمن وقد تقدم نظير هذا وقد جمعت فيه بحمد الله

تعالى جزءا مشتملا على أحاديث رباعيات منها أربعة صحابيون بعضهم عن بعض

وأربعة تابعيون بعضهم عن بعض وأما قوله قال صالح وقد تحدث بنحو ذلك عن أبي

رافع فهو بضم التاء والحاء قال القاضي عياض رحمه الله معنى هذا أن صالح بن

كيسان قال إن هذا الحديث روي عن أبي رافع عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم من

غير ذكر بن مسعود فيه وقد ذكره البخاري كذلك في تاريخه مختصرا عن أبي رافع

عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وقد قال أبوعلى الجياني عن أحمد بن حنبل رحمه

الله قال هذا الحديث غير محفوظ قال وهذا الكلام لا يشبه كلام بن مسعود وبن

مسعود يقول اصبروا حتى تلقوني هذا كلام القاضي رحمه الله وقال الشيخ أبو

عمرو وهذا الحديث قد أنكره أحمد بن حنبل رحمه الله وقد روى عن الحرث هذا

جماعة من الثقات ولم نجد له ذكرا في كتب الضعفاء وفى كتاب بن أبي حاتم عن

يحيى بن معين أنه ثقة ثم أن الحرث لم ينفرد به بل توبع عليه على ما أشعر به

كلام صالح بن كيسان المذكور وذكر الإمام الدارقطني رحمه الله في كتاب العلل

أن هذا الحديث قد روي من وجوه أخر منها عن أبي واقد الليثى عن بن مسعود عن

النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وأما قوله اصبروا حتى تلقوني فذلك حيث يلزم من

ذلك سفك الدماء أو إثارة الفتن أو نحو ذلك وما ورد في هذا الحديث من الحث

على جهاد المبطلين باليد واللسان فذلك حيث لا يلزم منه إثارة فتنة على أن

هذا الحديث مسوق فيمن سبق من الأمم وليس في لفظه ذكر لهذه الأمة هذا آخر

كلام الشيخ أبي عمرو وهو ظاهر كما قال وقدح الإمام أحمد رحمه الله في هذا

بهذا عجب والله أعلم وأما الحواريون المذكورون فاختلف فيهم فقال الأزهري
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ن-ص-ب (na-ṣa-ba)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To erect, set up, establish; the act of raising something into a fixed position, whether physical (a banner, a weapon) or abstract (a struggle, a war).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological discourse, it denotes the formal initiation of a confrontation or the establishment of a normative command; here, the "erection of combat" (naṣb qitāl) marks the threshold where verbal admonition ceases and coercive force begins.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) for physical erection (e.g., a spear); metaphorical (majāz) for the commencement of hostilities, where the physical act symbolizes the transition from persuasion to compulsion.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clause with Temporal Limit (Sharṭ bi-ghāyah) — The phrase "until the matter reaches..." (mā lam yantahī...) establishes a boundary condition; the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is suspended until the protasis is fulfilled, governing the legal ruling (ḥukm) that follows.
chapters.translation:
I say: [The obligation of forbidding evil by hand] applies so long as the matter does not escalate to the erection of combat and the brandishing of weapons. But if the matter reaches that point, then the affair is bound to the authority of the ruler (al-sulṭān).

He (al-Imām al-Ḥaramayn) said: And when the governor of the time acts unjustly, his oppression and tyranny become manifest, and he is not deterred when admonished verbally concerning the evil of his conduct, then it is permissible for the people of loosening and binding (ahl al-ḥall wa-l-ʿaqd) to conspire together to depose him, even by the brandishing of weapons and the erection of wars. This is the speech of al-Imām al-Ḥaramayn. And what he mentioned regarding his deposition is anomalous (gharīb), and despite this, it is interpreted as applying to the case where no greater corruption (mafsadah) is feared to arise from him than [the corruption of his continued rule].

He said: And it is not for the one commanding good to investigate, to pry, or to spy, nor to break into houses based on suspicions. Rather, if he comes upon a wrong action (munkar) openly, he changes it with his utmost effort. This is the speech of al-Imām al-Ḥaramayn.

And the Chief Judge al-Māwardī said: It is not for the muḥtasib (the official censor of morals) to investigate what has not become manifest of forbidden things. But if it becomes overwhelmingly probable (ghalaba ʿalā al-ẓann) that a group is secretly engaging in them, due to an indication (amārah) and traces that have appeared, then this falls into two categories:

The first: That the matter involves the violation of a sanctity (ḥurmah) whose recovery would be lost [if delayed], such as when one whom he trusts for his truthfulness informs him that a man has secluded himself with another man to kill him, or with a woman to commit fornication with her. In such a case, it is permissible for him to spy, to proceed with uncovering and investigation, out of caution against the loss of what cannot be recovered. Likewise, if this is known by volunteers (al-mutaṭawwiʿah) other than the muḥtasib, it is permissible for them to proceed with uncovering and forbidding.

The second category: What falls short of this rank — then it is not permissible to spy upon it, nor to uncover veils concerning it. If he hears the sounds of forbidden musical instruments (malāhī) from a house, he forbids it from outside the house, but he does not storm it by entering, because the wrong action is manifest [in its sound], and he is not obliged to uncover what is hidden.

Al-Māwardī has mentioned at the end of al-Aḥkām al-Sulṭāniyyah a fine chapter on the ḥisbah (the office of enjoining good and forbidding evil), comprising a summary of the principles of commanding good and forbidding evil. I have here indicated its objectives, and I have expanded the discussion in this chapter due to its great benefit, the abundance of need for it, and its being among the greatest principles of Islam. And God knows best.

His saying (i.e., the narrator's): "And ʿAmr narrated to us..." — [Regarding the chain:] "Abū Kurayb narrated to us, Abū Muʿāwiyah narrated to us, al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from Ismāʿīl ibn Rajāʾ, from his father, from Abū Saʿīd; and from Qays ibn Muslim, from Ṭāriq ibn Shihāb, from Abū Saʿīd." His saying "and from Qays" is conjoined (maʿṭūf) upon Ismāʿīl, meaning: al-Aʿmash narrated it from Ismāʿīl and from Qays. And God knows best.

[50] His saying: "From Ṣāliḥ ibn Kaysān, from al-Ḥārith, from Jaʿfar ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ḥakam, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Miswar, from Abū Rāfiʿ, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, may God be pleased with him, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: 'There was no prophet whom God sent to a nation before me but that he had from his nation disciples (ḥawāriyyūn) and companions who adhered to his sunnah and followed his command. Then after them came successors (khalaf) who say what they do not do, and do what they are not commanded. Whoever strives against them with his hand is a believer; whoever strives against them with his tongue is a believer; and whoever strives against them with his heart is a believer. And beyond that there is not a mustard-seed's weight of faith.'"

Abū Rāfiʿ said: I narrated this to ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar, may God be pleased with them both, and he rejected it against me. Then Ibn Masʿūd arrived and lodged at Qanāh. ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar, may God be pleased with them both, sent for me to accompany him to visit him (Ibn Masʿūd). So I went with him. When we sat down, I asked Ibn Masʿūd about this ḥadīth, and he narrated it to me just as I had narrated it to Ibn ʿUmar. Ṣāliḥ said: And he (Ibn Masʿūd) had spoken something similar to that from Abū Rāfiʿ.

As for al-Ḥārith, he is Ibn Fuḍayl al-Anṣārī al-Khaṭmī, Abū ʿAbd Allāh al-Madanī. He narrated from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Qirād, the Companion. Yaḥyā ibn Maʿīn said: He is trustworthy (thiqah). As for Abū Rāfiʿ, he is the freed slave (mawlā) of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. The most correct opinion is that his name was Aslam; it was also said Ibrāhīm; it was said Hurmuz; it was said Thābit; and it was said Yazīd — and this last is anomalous (gharīb), related by Ibn al-Jawzī in his book Jāmiʿ al-Masānīd.

In this chain of transmission there is a remarkable feature (ṭarīfah): four Successors (tābiʿūn) are gathered in it, each narrating from the other — Ṣāliḥ, al-Ḥārith, Jaʿfar, and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān. A similar case has preceded [in this commentary]. And I have, by the praise of God the Exalted, collected in this regard a volume comprising ḥadīths of fourfold chains (rubāʿiyyāt), among them four Companions narrating one from another, and four Successors narrating one from another.

As for his saying — Ṣāliḥ said: "And he had spoken something similar to that from Abū Rāfiʿ" — it is with ḍammah on the tāʾ and the ḥāʾ (tahaddatha, "he had narrated"). Judge ʿIyāḍ, may God have mercy on him, said: The meaning of this is that Ṣāliḥ ibn Kaysān said that this ḥadīth was narrated from Abū Rāfiʿ from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, without the mention of Ibn Masʿūd in it. Al-Bukhārī has mentioned it likewise in his Tārīkh, abbreviated, from Abū Rāfiʿ from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace.

Abū ʿAlī al-Jayyānī said, from Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal, may God have mercy on him, that he said: This ḥadīth is not preserved (ghayr maḥfūẓ). And he (al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ) said: And this speech does not resemble the speech of Ibn Masʿūd, for Ibn Masʿūd says: "Be patient until you meet me." This is the speech of al-Qāḍī, may God have mercy on him.

And Shaykh Abū ʿAmr said: This ḥadīth was indeed rejected by Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal, may God have mercy on him. Yet a group of trustworthy narrators have narrated it from al-Ḥārith, and we have found no mention of him in the books of weak narrators. In the book of Ibn Abī Ḥātim, from Yaḥyā ibn Maʿīn, that he is trustworthy. Moreover, al-Ḥārith did not single himself out with it, but rather he was followed (tūbiʿa) upon it, as is indicated by the aforementioned speech of Ṣāliḥ ibn Kaysān. And Imām al-Dāraquṭnī, may God have mercy on him, mentioned in his book al-ʿIlal that this ḥadīth has been narrated from other paths, among them from Abū Wāqid al-Laythī, from Ibn Masʿūd, from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace.

As for his saying "Be patient until you meet me" — that applies where bloodshed or the stirring of tribulation (fitan) or the like would necessarily result [from resistance]. And what is mentioned in this ḥadīth of urging the striving against the people of falsehood (mubṭilīn) with the hand and the tongue — that applies where no tribulation would necessarily result from it. Moreover, this ḥadīth is directed at those who preceded from among the [earlier] nations, and there is no mention in its wording of this ummah. This is the end of the speech of Shaykh Abū ʿAmr, and it is evident as he said. And the criticism (qadḥ) of Imām Aḥmad, may God have mercy on him, against this [ḥadīth] is astonishing. And God knows best.

As for the disciples (ḥawāriyyūn) mentioned [in the ḥadīth], there is disagreement concerning them. Al-Azharī said...

chapters.title_en: Section 102 — On the Excellence of the People of Faith and the Preeminence of the People of Yemen therein
chapters.arabic_text:
وغيره هم خلصان الأنبياء وأصفياؤهم والخلصان الذين نقوا من كل عيب وقال

غيرهم أنصارهم وقيل المجاهدون وقيل الذين يصلحون للخلافة بعدهم قوله صلى

الله عليه وسلم ثم إنها تخلف من بعدهم خلوف الضمير في إنها هو الذي يسميه

النحويون ضمير القصة والشأن ومعنى تخلف تحدث وهو بضم اللام وأما الخلوف

فبضم الخاء وهو جمع خلف باسكان اللام وهوالخالف بشر وأما بفتح اللام فهو

الخالف بخير هذا هو الأشهر وقال جماعة وجماعات من أهل اللغة منهم أبو زيد

يقال كل واحد منهما بالفتح والإسكان ومنهم من جوز الفتح في الشر ولم يجوز

الإسكان في الخير والله أعلم قوله فنزل بقناة
# 
# هكذا هو في بعض الأصول المحققة بقناة بالقاف المفتوحة وآخره تاء التأنيث

وهو غير مصروف للعلمية والتأنيث وهكذا ذكره أبو عبد الله الحميدي في الجمع

بين الصحيحين ووقع في أكثر الأصول ولمعظم رواة كتاب مسلم بفنائه بالفاء

المكسورة وبالمد وآخره هاء الضمير قبلها همزة والفناء ما بين أيدي المنازل

والدور وكذا رواه أبو عوانة الاسفراينى قال القاضي عياض رحمه الله في رواية

السمرقندي بقناة وهو الصواب وقناة واد من أودية المدينة عليه مال من

أموالها قال ورواية الجمهور بفنائه وهو خطأ وتصحيف قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم

(يهتدون بهديه) هو بفتح الهاء وإسكان الدال أي بطريقته وسمته قول مسلم رحمه

الله (ولم يذكر قدوم بن مسعود واجتماع بن عمر معه) هذا مما أنكره الحريري

في كتابه درة الغواص فقال لا يقال اجتمع فلان مع فلان وإنما يقال اجتمع

فلان وفلان وقد خالفه الجوهري فقال في صحاحه جامعه على كذا أي اجتمع معه

| (باب تفاضل أهل الإيمان فيه ورجحان أهل اليمن فيه
# [51] في
# هذا الباب (أشار النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بيده نحو اليمن فقال الا أن

الإيمان ها هنا وان القسوة)
# 
# وغلظ القلوب في الفدادين عند أصول أذناب الإبل حيث يطلع قرنا الشيطان في

ربيعة ومضر وفي رواية جاء أهل اليمن هم أرق أفئدة الإيمان يمان والفقه يمان

والحكمة يمانية وفي  رواية أتاكم أهل اليمن هم أضعف قلوبا وأرق أفئدة الفقه

يمان والحكمة يمانية وفي رواية رأس الكفر نحو المشرق والفخر والخيلاء في

أهل الخيل والإبل الفدادين أهل الوبر والسكينة في أهل الغنم
# 
# وفي رواية الإيمان يمان والكفر قبل المشرق والسكينة في أهل الغنم والفخر

والرياء في الفدادين أهل الخيل والوبر وفي رواية أتاكم أهل اليمن هم ألين

قلوبا وأرق أفئدة الايمان يمان
# 
# والحكمة يمانية ورأس الكفر قبل المشرق وفي رواية غلظ القلوب والجفاء في

المشرق والإيمان في أهل الحجاز) قد اختلف فى مواضع من هذا الحديث وقد جمعها

القاضي عياض رحمه الله ونقحها مختصرة بعده الشيخ أبو عمرو بن الصلاح رحمه

الله وأنا أحكي ما ذكره قال أما ما ذكر من نسبة الإيمان إلى أهل اليمن فقد

صرفوه عن ظاهره من حيث إن مبدأ الإيمان من مكة ثم من المدينة حرسهما الله

تعالى فحكى أبو عبيد إمام الغرب ثم من بعده في ذلك أقوالا أحدها أنه أراد

بذلك مكة فإنه يقال إن مكة من تهامة وتهامة من أرض اليمن والثاني أن المراد

مكة والمدينة فإنه يروى في الحديث أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال هذا

الكلام وهو بتبوك ومكة والمدينة حينئذ بينه وبين اليمن فأشار إلى ناحية

اليمن وهو يريد مكة والمدينة فقال الإيمان يمان ونسبهما إلى اليمن لكونهما

حينئذ من ناحية اليمن كما قالوا الركن اليماني وهو بمكة لكونه إلى ناحية

اليمن والثالث ما ذهب إليه كثير من الناس وهو أحسنها عند أبي عبيد أن

المراد بذلك الأنصار لأنهم يمانون في الأصل فنسب الإيمان إليهم لكونهم

أنصاره قال الشيخ أبو عمرو رحمه الله ولو جمع أبو عبيد ومن سلك سبيله طرق

الحديث بألفاظه كما جمعها مسلم وغيره وتأملوها لصاروا إلى غير ما ذكروه

ولما تركوا الظاهر ولقضوا بأن المراد اليمن وأهل اليمن على ما هو المفهوم

من إطلاق ذلك إذ من ألفاظه أتاكم أهل اليمن والانصار
# 
# من جملة المخاطبين بذلك فهم إذن غيرهم وكذلك قوله صلى الله عليه  وسلم جاء

أهل اليمن وإنما جاء حينئذ غير الأنصار ثم إنه صلى الله عليه وسلم وصفهم

بما يقضي بكمال إيمانهم ورتب عليه الإيمان يمان فكان ذلك إشارة للإيمان إلى

من أتاه من أهل اليمن لا إلى مكة والمدينة ولا مانع من إجراء الكلام على

ظاهره وحمله على أهل اليمن حقيقة لأن من اتصف بشيء وقوي قيامه به وتأكد

اطلاعه منه ينسب ذلك الشيء إليه إشعارا بتميزه به وكمال حاله فيه وهكذا كان

حال أهل اليمن حينئذ في الإيمان وحال الوافدين منه في حياة رسول الله صلى

الله عليه وسلم وفي أعقاب موته كأويس القرني وأبي مسلم الخولاني رضي الله

عنهما وشبههما ممن سلم قلبه وقوي إيمانه فكانت نسبة الإيمان إليهم لذلك

إشعارا بكمال إيمانهم من غير أن يكون في ذلك نفي له عن غيرهم فلا منافاة

بينه وبين قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم الإيمان في أهل الحجاز ثم المراد بذلك

الموجودون منهم حينئذ لا كل أهل اليمن في كل زمان فإن اللفظ لا يقتضيه هذا
chapters.anchors:
- Root: خ-ل-ف (kh-l-f)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Succession, that which comes after; a "khalaf" (خلف) is one who comes later, whether good or bad depending on vocalization.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Temporal succession (takhlīf) implying replacement of one generation by another; theological nuance of moral decline or excellence in successors.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) for physical succession; metaphorical (majāz) when applied to moral character — "khalūf" (خَلُوف) with ḍammah on lām denotes the wicked successor, "khalaf" (خَلَف) with fatḥah denotes the righteous one.
- Sībawayh Rule: Ḍamīr al-qaṣṣah (ضمير القصة) — The impersonal pronoun "innahā" (إنها) functioning as a sentential subject introducing a whole narrative clause, not referring to a specific antecedent.

- Root: ق-ن-و (q-n-w)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Qanāh (قناة) — a channel, watercourse, or valley; also a spear-shaft.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradats): A natural land formation; here a proper noun for a valley in Madīnah.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal toponym; the variant "fināʾihī" (فنائه) is a scribal corruption (taṣḥīf) — "fināʾ" being the open space before dwellings.
- Sībawayh Rule: ʿAlam muʾannath (العلم المؤنث) — Proper feminine noun ending in tāʾ marbūṭah, rendered non-diptotic (ghayr munṣarif) due to definiteness and feminine gender.

- Root: ي-م-ن (y-m-n)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Right side, blessing, auspiciousness; Yemen as the southern land.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Theological association of īmān (faith) with Yemen — a metonymic attribution indicating perfection and strength of faith in its people.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal geographical reference vs. metaphorical extension to Makkah and Madīnah; the Prophet's gesture (īshārah) toward Yemen is literal, but the attribution of faith is majāz indicating excellence.
- Sībawayh Rule: Isnād al-fiʿl ilā al-sabab (إسناد الفعل إلى السبب) — Attributing an action to its cause or locus of manifestation, as in "al-īmān yamān" (faith is Yemeni), where the predicate is a relative attribution.
chapters.translation:
And others — they are the sincere devotees of the prophets and their chosen ones, the purified ones who have been cleansed of every defect. And others said: they are their supporters (anṣār). And it was said: they are the mujāhidūn (strivers). And it was said: they are those who are fit for the caliphate after them.

His saying, peace and blessings be upon him: "Then there will succeed after them successors (khulūf)" — the pronoun in "innahā" (verily it) is what grammarians call the pronoun of the story and affair (ḍamīr al-qaṣṣah wa al-shaʾn). And the meaning of "takhalluf" (تَخَلُّف) is "it will come to be" (taḥduth), and it is with ḍammah on the lām. As for "al-khulūf" (الخُلُوف), it is with ḍammah on the khāʾ, and it is a plural of "khalaf" (خَلَف) with sukūn on the lām, and it means the one who comes after with evil. As for with fatḥah on the lām (khalaf), it is the one who comes after with good. This is the most well-known (opinion). And a group — indeed, many groups — of the people of language, among them Abū Zayd, said: each of the two is said with both fatḥah and sukūn. And among them are those who permitted fatḥah for evil but did not permit sukūn for good. And Allah knows best.

His saying, peace and blessings be upon him: "So he encamped at Qanāh (بقناة)" — thus it is in some of the verified manuscripts: "bi-Qanāh" with fatḥah on the qāf and at its end tāʾ of femininity, and it is non-diptotic (ghayr munṣarif) due to proper-noun status and femininity. Thus did Abū ʿAbd Allāh al-Ḥumaydī mention it in "al-Jamʿ bayn al-Ṣaḥīḥayn." And it occurs in most manuscripts and in the majority of the transmitters of the book of Muslim as "bi-fināʾihi" (بفنائه) with kasrah on the fāʾ and with madd (elongation), and at its end hāʾ of the pronoun preceded by a hamzah. And "al-fināʾ" is the open space before dwellings and houses. Thus also did Abū ʿAwānah al-Isfarāʾīnī transmit it. Al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ, may Allah have mercy on him, said: in the transmission of al-Samarqandī it is "bi-Qanāh," and it is the correct version. And Qanāh is a valley among the valleys of Madīnah upon which there is property (māl) from its wealth. He said: and the transmission of the majority is "bi-fināʾihi," and it is an error and a scribal corruption (taṣḥīf).

His saying, peace and blessings be upon him: "They will be guided by his guidance (yah'tadūna bi-hadyihi)" — it is with fatḥah on the hāʾ and sukūn on the dāl, meaning: by his path (ṭarīqatihi) and his way (samtihi).

The saying of Muslim, may Allah have mercy on him: "And he did not mention the arrival of Ibn Masʿūd and the gathering of Ibn ʿUmar with him" — this is among the things that al-Ḥarīrī criticized in his book "Durrat al-Ghawwāṣ," for he said: one does not say "so-and-so gathered with so-and-so" (ijtamaʿa fulān maʿa fulān); rather, one says "so-and-so and so-and-so gathered" (ijtamaʿa fulān wa fulān). And al-Jawharī opposed him, for he said in his "Ṣiḥāḥ": "jāmaʿahu ʿalā kadhā" (he gathered with him upon such-and-such), i.e., he assembled with him.

[Chapter: On the Excellence of the People of Faith therein and the Preeminence of the People of Yemen therein]

[51] In this chapter: (The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, pointed with his hand toward Yemen and said: "Verily, faith is here, and verily harshness and hardness of hearts are among the camel-herding Bedouins (al-faddādīn) at the roots of the tails of camels, where the two horns of Satan will appear, in Rabīʿah and Muḍar.")

And in another transmission: "The people of Yemen have come to you; they are the most tender of hearts. Faith is Yemeni, and jurisprudence (fiqh) is Yemeni, and wisdom (ḥikmah) is Yemeni."

And in another transmission: "The people of Yemen have come to you; they are the weakest of hearts and the most tender of feelings. Jurisprudence is Yemeni, and wisdom is Yemeni."

And in another transmission: "The head of disbelief is toward the East, and pride and vainglory are among the people of horses and camels — the Bedouin herders (al-faddādīn), the people of wool-tents (ahl al-wabar). And tranquility (sakīnah) is among the people of sheep."

And in another transmission: "Faith is Yemeni, and disbelief is before the East, and tranquility is among the people of sheep, and pride and ostentation (riyāʾ) are among the Bedouin herders, the people of horses and wool-tents."

And in another transmission: "The people of Yemen have come to you; they are the softest of hearts and the most tender of feelings. Faith is Yemeni, and wisdom is Yemeni, and the head of disbelief is before the East."

And in another transmission: "Hardness of hearts and coarseness (jafāʾ) are in the East, and faith is among the people of the Ḥijāz."

There has been disagreement concerning certain places in this ḥadīth, and al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ, may Allah have mercy on him, has collected them and refined them, and after him the Shaykh Abū ʿAmr ibn al-Ṣalāḥ, may Allah have mercy on him, summarized them. And I shall relate what he mentioned.

He said: As for what was mentioned concerning the attribution of faith to the people of Yemen, they have diverted it from its apparent meaning (ẓāhir), on the grounds that the origin of faith was from Makkah, then from Madīnah — may Allah the Exalted protect them both. Thus Abū ʿUbayd, the Imām of the West, and those after him, related concerning this several opinions:

**First:** That he meant thereby Makkah, for it is said that Makkah is from Tihāmah, and Tihāmah is from the land of Yemen.

**Second:** That the intended meaning is Makkah and Madīnah, for it is transmitted in the ḥadīth that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said this statement while he was at Tabūk, and Makkah and Madīnah at that time were between him and Yemen. So he pointed toward the direction of Yemen while intending Makkah and Madīnah, and said: "Faith is Yemeni," attributing them to Yemen because they were at that time in the direction of Yemen — just as they said "al-Rukn al-Yamānī" (the Yemeni Corner), which is in Makkah, because it faces the direction of Yemen.

**Third:** What many people adopted, and which is the best of them according to Abū ʿUbayd: that the intended meaning is the Anṣār (Helpers), for they are Yemenite in origin. So faith was attributed to them because they were its supporters (anṣāruhu).

The Shaykh Abū ʿAmr, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Had Abū ʿUbayd and those who followed his path collected the versions of the ḥadīth with their exact wordings, just as Muslim and others collected them, and had they reflected upon them, they would have arrived at something other than what they mentioned, and they would not have abandoned the apparent meaning (ẓāhir). And they would have ruled that the intended meaning is Yemen and the people of Yemen, according to what is understood from the unrestricted usage of that term — for among its wordings is: "The people of Yemen have come to you" (atākum ahl al-Yaman), and the Anṣār are among those addressed by that statement. They are therefore other than them. Likewise, his saying, peace and blessings be upon him: "The people of Yemen have come" (jāʾa ahl al-Yaman) — and at that time, only other than the Anṣār had come. Then he, peace and blessings be upon him, described them with what necessitates the perfection of their faith, and upon that he based the statement "Faith is Yemeni." So that was an indication of faith toward those who came to him from the people of Yemen — not toward Makkah and Madīnah.

Nor is there any impediment to running the speech upon its apparent meaning and carrying it upon the people of Yemen literally (ḥaqīqatan), because whoever is characterized by a thing, and his standing in it is strong, and his share of it is firmly established, that thing is attributed to him as an indication of his distinction therein and the perfection of his state in it. And such was the state of the people of Yemen at that time in faith, and the state of those who came from it during the lifetime of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, and in the aftermath of his death — like Uways al-Qaranī and Abū Muslim al-Khawlānī, may Allah be pleased with them both, and those similar to them among those whose hearts were sound and whose faith was strong. So the attribution of faith to them was for that reason an indication of the perfection of their faith, without that entailing any negation of it from others. Thus there is no contradiction between it and his saying, peace and blessings be upon him: "Faith is among the people of the Ḥijāz." Then the intended meaning thereby is those who existed among them at that time — not all the people of Yemen in every age, for the wording does not necessitate that.

chapters.title_en: Section 103 — On the Meaning of Fiqh and Wisdom, the Yemeni Attribution, the Description of the Hearts of the Yemenites, the Meaning of "Faddādīn," the Two Horns of Satan, and the Chains of Transmission
chapters.arabic_text:
هو الحق في ذلك ونشكر الله تعالى على هدايتنا له والله أعلم قال وأما ما

ذكر من الفقه والحكمة فالفقه هنا عبارة عن الفهم في الدين واصطلح بعد ذلك

الفقهاء وأصحاب الأصول على تخصيص الفقه بإدراك الأحكام الشرعية العملية

بالاستدلال على أعيانها وأما الحكمة ففيها أقوال كثيرة مضطربة قد اقتصر كل

من قائليها على بعض صفات الحكمة وقد صفا لنا منها أن الحكمة عبارة عن العلم

المتصف بالأحكام المشتمل على المعرفة بالله تبارك وتعالى المصحوب بنفاذ

البصيرة وتهذيب النفس وتحقيق الحق والعمل به والصد عن اتباع الهوى والباطل

والحكيم من له ذلك وقال أبو بكر بن دريد كل كلمة وعظتك وزجرتك أودعتك إلى

مكرمة أو نهتك عن قبيح فهي حكمة وحكم ومنه قول النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إن

من الشعر حكمة وفي بعض الروايات حكما والله أعلم قال الشيخ وقوله صلى الله

عليه وسلم يمان ويمانية هو بتخفيف الياء عند جماهير أهل العربية لأن  الألف

المزيدة فيه عوض من ياء النسب المشددة فلا يجمع بينهما وقال بن السيد في

كتابه الاقتضاب حكى المبرد وغيره أن التشديد لغة قال الشيخ وهذا غريب قلت

وقد حكى الجوهري وصاحب المطالع وغيرهما من العلماء عن سيبويه أنه حكى عن

بعض العرب أنهم يقولون اليماني بالياء المشددة وأنشد لأمية بن خلف ...

يمانيا يظل يشب كيرا ... وينفخ دائما لهب الشواظ ...

| (والله أعلم قال الشيخ وقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم 
# ألين قلوبا وأرق أفئدة المشهور أن)
# 
# الفؤاد هو القلب فعلى هذا يكون كرر لفظ القلوب بلفظين وهو أولى من تكريره

بلفظ واحد وقيل الفؤاد غير القلب وهو عين القلب وقيل باطن القلب وقيل غشاء

القلب وأما وصفها باللين والرفة والضعف فمعناه أنها ذات خشية واستكانة

سريعة الاستجابة والتأثر بقوارع التذكير سالمة من الغلظ والشدة والقسوة

التي وصف بها قلوب الآخرين قال وقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم في الفدادين فزعم

أبو عمرو الشيباني أنه بتخفيف الدال وهو جمع فداد بتشديد الدال وهو عبارة

عن البقر التي يحرث عليها حكاه عنه أبو عبيد وأنكره عليه وعلى هذا المراد

بذلك أصحابها فحذف المضاف والصواب في الفدادين بتشديد الدال جمع فداد

بدالين أولاهما مشددة وهذا قول أهل الحديث والأصمعي وجمهور أهل اللغة وهو

من الفديد وهو الصوت الشديد فهم الذين تعلو أصواتهم في إبلهم وخيلهم

وحروثهم ونحو ذلك وقال أبو عبيدة معمر بن المثنى هم المكثرون من الإبل

الذين يملك أحدهم المائتين منها إلى الالف وقوله ان القسو في الفدادين عند

أصول أذناب الإبل معناه الذين لهم جلبة وصياح عند سوقهم لها وقوله صلى الله

عليه وسلم حيث يطلع فرنا الشيطان في ربيعة ومضر قوله ربيعة ومضر بدل من

الفدادين وأما قرنا الشيطان فجانبا رأسه وقيل هما جمعاه اللذان يغريهما

بإضلال الناس وقيل شيعتاه من الكفار والمراد بذلك اختصاص المشرق بمزيد من

تسلط الشيطان ومن الكفر كما قال في الحديث الآخر رأس الكفر نحو المشرق وكان

ذلك في عهده صلى الله عليه وسلم حين قال  ذلك ويكون حين يخرج الدجال من

المشرق وهو فيما بين ذلك منشأ الفتن العظيمة ومثار الكفرة الترك الغاشمة

العاتية الشديدة البأس وأما قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم الفخر والخيلاء فالفخر

هو الافتخار وعد المآثر القديمة تعظيما والخيلاء الكبر واحتقار الناس وأما

قوله في أهل الخيل والإبل الفدادين أهل الوبر فالوبر وإن كان من الإبل دون

الخيل فلا يمتنع أن يكون قد وصفهم بكونهم جامعين بين الخيل والابل والوبر

وأما قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم والسكينة فى أهل الغنم فالسكينة الطمأنينة

والسكون على خلاف ما ذكره من صفة الفدادين هذا آخر ما ذكره الشيخ أبو عمرو

رحمه الله وفيه كفاية فلا نطول بزيادة عليه والله أعلم وأما أسانيد الباب

فقال مسلم رحمه الله حدثنا أبو بكر بن أبي شيبة حدثنا أبو أسامة قال وحدثنا

بن نمير حدثنا أبي قال وحدثنا أبو كريب حدثنا بن إدريس كلهم عن إسماعيل بن

أبي خالد قال وحدثنا يحيى بن حبيب حدثنا
# 
# معتمر عن إسماعيل قال سمعت قيسا يروي عن أبى مسعود هؤلاء الرجال كلهم

كوفيون إلا يحيى بن حبيب ومعتمرا فانهما بصريان وقد تقدم أن اسم بن أبي

شيبة عبد الله بن محمد بن إبراهيم بن أبي شيبة وأن أبا أسامة حماد بن اسامة

وبن نمير محمد بن عبد الله بن نمير وأبو كريب محمد بن العلاء وبن إدريس عبد

الله وأبو خالد هرمز وقيل سعد وقيل كثير وأبو مسعود عقبة بن عمرو الأنصاري

البدري رضي الله عنهم وفي الإسناد الآخر الدارمي وقد تقدم في مقدمة الكتاب

أنه منسوب إلى جد للقبيلة اسمه دارم وفيه أبو اليمان واسمه الحكم بن نافع

وبعده أبو معاوية محمد بن خازم بالخاء المعجمة والأعمش سليمان بن مهران

وأبو صالح ذكوان وبن جريج عبد الملك بن عبد العزيز بن جريج وأبو الزبير

محمد بن مسلم بن تدرس وكل هذا وإن كان ظاهرا وقد تقدم فإنما أقصد بتكريره

وذكره الإيضاح لمن لا يكون من أهل هذا الشأن فربما وقف على هذا  الباب وأراد
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ف-ق-ه (f-q-h)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning is deep comprehension (al-fahm) and discernment of a thing's reality.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In the Qur'an, it denotes penetrating understanding of religious matters, often contrasted with mere surface knowledge.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense is "understanding"; the technical restriction to legal rulings is a later convention (iṣṭilāḥ), not a lexical shift.
- Root: ح-ك-م (ḥ-k-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Root denotes preventing, restraining, and judging; ḥikmah is that which prevents one from error and base action.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Ḥikmah is knowledge of realities combined with sound action; it is the perfection of the rational soul.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Used literally for wisdom as a divine gift; metaphorically for any speech that restrains from folly.
- Root: ي-م-ن (y-m-n)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Derived from barakah (blessing) and the right hand (yumn); the Yemeni attribution is to the land of Yemen.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The nisbah (relative adjective) form is normally yamānī with a single yā', the doubled form being a rare dialectal variant.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): The added alif in yamānī compensates for the doubled yā' of the nisbah; thus the default is takhfīf (lightening).
- Root: ف-د-د (f-d-d)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Fadīd is a loud, intense sound; faddād (with shaddah) is a plural of faddād meaning a camel-herder or one who raises his voice.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Not a Qur'anic term; used in ḥadīth for those who are loud and boastful among the desert dwellers.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): The reading with tashdīd on the dāl is the established one; the lightened form is a rejected variant meaning "oxen for plowing."
- Root: ق-ر-ن (q-r-n)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Qarn means horn, and also a side or extremity; the two horns of Satan are his two sides or his two hosts.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological usage, it denotes power and influence; Satan's "horns" are his means of misguidance.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for the horn of an animal; metaphorical here for the two flanks or the two armies of Satan.
- Sībawayh Rule: Badal (Substitution) — In the phrase "Rabīʿah wa Muḍar" following "al-Faddādīn," the former is a substitute (badal) clarifying the latter, a standard appositional construction in nominal sentences.
chapters.translation:
I say: He is the Truth in that, and we thank Allah the Exalted for His guiding us to it. And Allah knows best.

He said: As for what was mentioned of fiqh and wisdom — fiqh here is an expression for understanding in religion. Afterward, the jurists and the scholars of uṣūl agreed upon restricting fiqh to the apprehension of the practical sharʿī rulings through inference upon their specific instances. As for wisdom (ḥikmah), there are many conflicting statements concerning it; each of its proponents has confined himself to some of the attributes of wisdom. What has become clear to us from it is that wisdom is an expression for knowledge characterized by rulings, encompassing cognizance of Allah, Blessed and Exalted, accompanied by penetrating insight (nafādh al-baṣīrah), refinement of the soul, actualization of the truth and acting upon it, and turning away from following caprice and falsehood. The wise one (ḥakīm) is he who possesses that. Abū Bakr ibn Durayd said: Every word that admonishes you, restrains you, impels you to a noble deed, or deters you from a vile one — that is wisdom (ḥikmah) and judgment (ḥukm). From this is the saying of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him: {«Indeed, among poetry there is wisdom»} — and in some narrations, {«judgments»}. And Allah knows best.

The Shaykh said: His saying, peace and blessings be upon him, "Yamānūn" (Yemenites) and "Yamāniyyah" (Yemenite) — it is with lightening of the yā' according to the majority of the Arabic scholars, because the added alif therein is a substitute for the doubled yā' of the relative nisbah, so the two are not combined. Ibn al-Sayyid said in his book al-Iqtiḍāb: Al-Mubarrad and others related that the tashdīd (doubling) is a dialect. The Shaykh said: This is strange. I say: Al-Jawharī, the author of al-Maṭāliʿ, and others of the scholars have related from Sībawayh that he related from some of the Arabs that they say "al-Yamānī" with the doubled yā', and he cited as evidence the verse of Umayyah ibn Khalaf:

... A Yemenite who keeps a forge blazing, and ever blows the flame of the firebrand ...

And Allah knows best.

The Shaykh said: His saying, peace and blessings be upon him, {«Softer in hearts and more tender in livers (af'idah)»} — the well-known view is that the fu'ād is the heart (qalb). On this basis, he repeated the word "hearts" with two expressions, which is preferable to repeating it with a single expression. It was also said: The fu'ād is other than the qalb — it is the core of the heart. And it was said: It is the inner part of the heart. And it was said: It is the membrane covering the heart. As for their description with softness, tenderness, and weakness, its meaning is that they possess fearfulness and humility, quick in response and impressionable to the striking admonitions, free from the harshness, severity, and hardness with which the hearts of others were described.

He said: His saying, peace and blessings be upon him, concerning "al-Faddādīn" — Abū ʿAmr al-Shaybānī claimed that it is with lightening of the dāl, being a plural of faddād (with tashdīd on the dāl), which is an expression for the oxen upon which one plows. Abū ʿUbayd related this from him and rejected it against him. On this view, the intended meaning is their owners, so the muḍāf (possessed noun) was elided. The correct view regarding "al-Faddādīn" is with tashdīd on the dāl, a plural of faddād with two dāls, the first of which is doubled. This is the saying of the people of ḥadīth, of al-Aṣmaʿī, and of the majority of the lexicographers. It is derived from fadīd, which is the intense voice — thus they are those whose voices rise high over their camels, horses, and fields, and the like. Abū ʿUbaydah Maʿmar ibn al-Muthannā said: They are those who possess many camels, one of them owning from two hundred to a thousand of them. His saying, "Verily, hardness is in the Faddādīn at the roots of the tails of camels" — its meaning is those who have clamor and shouting when driving them.

His saying, peace and blessings be upon him, "where the two horns of Satan rise, in Rabīʿah and Muḍar" — his saying "Rabīʿah and Muḍar" is a substitute (badal) for "al-Faddādīn." As for "the two horns of Satan," they are the two sides of his head. And it was said: They are his two hosts with which he incites to the misguidance of people. And it was said: They are his two factions from among the disbelievers. The intended meaning of that is the particular distinction of the East with an increase of Satan's dominion and of disbelief, just as he said in the other ḥadīth: {«The head of disbelief is toward the East»}. And that was in his era, peace and blessings be upon him, when he said that — and it will be when the Dajjāl emerges from the East. And in the period between that, it is the place of origin of great tribulations and the rising place of the Turkish disbelievers — the oppressive, rebellious, fiercely mighty ones.

As for his saying, peace and blessings be upon him, "pride (al-fakhr) and vainglory (al-khaylā')" — al-fakhr is boasting and enumerating ancient merits for self-aggrandizement, and al-khaylā' is arrogance and contempt for people.

As for his saying concerning the people of horses and camels, "the Faddādīn, the people of the tent-hair (al-wabar)" — even though al-wabar is from camels rather than horses, there is no impediment to his having described them as combining horses, camels, and tent-hair.

As for his saying, peace and blessings be upon him, "and tranquility (al-sakīnah) is in the people of sheep" — al-sakīnah is serenity and stillness, in contrast to what he mentioned of the description of the Faddādīn. This is the end of what the Shaykh Abū ʿAmr, may Allah have mercy on him, mentioned. In it is sufficiency, so we shall not lengthen by adding beyond it. And Allah knows best.

As for the chains of transmission (asānīd) of this chapter: Muslim, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Abū Bakr ibn Abī Shaybah narrated to us, from Abū Usāmah; he said: And Ibn Numayr narrated to us, from his father; he said: And Abū Kurayb narrated to us, from Ibn Idrīs — all of them from Ismāʿīl ibn Abī Khālid. He said: And Yaḥyā ibn Ḥabīb narrated to us, from Muʿtamir, from Ismāʿīl, who said: I heard Qays narrating from Abū Masʿūd. All of these men are Kūfans except Yaḥyā ibn Ḥabīb and Muʿtamir, for they are Baṣrans. It has already been mentioned that the name of Ibn Abī Shaybah is ʿAbdullāh ibn Muḥammad ibn Ibrāhīm ibn Abī Shaybah, that Abū Usāmah is Ḥammād ibn Usāmah, that Ibn Numayr is Muḥammad ibn ʿAbdullāh ibn Numayr, that Abū Kurayb is Muḥammad ibn al-ʿAlā', that Ibn Idrīs is ʿAbdullāh, that Abū Khālid is Hurmuz — and it was said: Saʿd, and it was said: Kathīr — and that Abū Masʿūd is ʿUqbah ibn ʿAmr al-Anṣārī al-Badrī, may Allah be pleased with them all. In the other chain there is al-Dārimī, and it has already been mentioned in the introduction to the book that he is attributed to a grandfather of the tribe whose name was Dārim. In it is Abū al-Yamān, whose name is al-Ḥakam ibn Nāfiʿ; after him Abū Muʿāwiyah, Muḥammad ibn Khāzim, with the khā' with a dot; al-Aʿmash, Sulaymān ibn Mihrān; Abū Ṣāliḥ, Dhakwān; Ibn Jurayj, ʿAbd al-Malik ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn Jurayj; and Abū al-Zubayr, Muḥammad ibn Muslim ibn Tadrus. All of this, though it is apparent and has already been mentioned, my purpose in repeating and mentioning it is only to clarify for those who are not of this craft — for perhaps one may come upon this chapter and desire [to understand it].

chapters.title_en: Section 104 — Clarifying that None Enter Paradise Except the Believers, that Mutual Love is Part of Faith, and that Spreading Salām is a Means to Attain It; and Clarifying that Religion is Sincere Counsel (Naṣīḥah)
chapters.arabic_text:
معرفة اسم بعض هؤلاء ليتوصل به إلى مطالعة ترجمته ومعرفة حاله أوغير ذلك من

الأغراض فسهلت عليه الطريق بعبارة مختصرة والله أعلم بالصواب

| (باب بيان أنه لا يدخل الجنة الا المؤمنون (وأن محبة
# المؤمنين من الايمان وأن افشاء السلام سبب لحصولها)
# [54] قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (لا تدخلون الجنة حتى تؤمنوا ولا تؤمنوا

حتى تحابوا أولا أدلكم)
# 
# على شيء إذا فعلتموه تحاببتم أفشوا السلام بينكم وفي الرواية الأخرى

والذي نفسي بيده لا تدخلون الجنة حتى تؤمنوا) هكذا هو في جميع الأصول

والروايات ولا تؤمنوا بحذف النون من آخره وهي لغة معروفة صحيحة وأما معنى

الحديث فقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم ولا تؤمنوا حتى تحابوا معناه لا يكمل

إيمانكم ولا يصلح حالكم في الإيمان إلا بالتحاب وأما قوله صلى الله عليه

وسلم لاتدخلون الجنة حتى تؤمنوا فهو على ظاهره وإطلاقه فلا يدخل الجنة إلا

من مات مؤمنا وإن لم يكن كامل الإيمان فهذا هو الظاهر من الحديث وقال الشيخ

أبو عمرو رحمه الله معنى الحديث لا يكمل إيمانكم إلا بالتحاب ولا تدخلون

الجنة عند دخول أهلها إذا لم تكونوا كذلك وهذا الذي قاله محتمل والله أعلم

وأما قوله أفشوا السلام بينكم فهو بقط الهمزة المفتوحة وفيه الحث العظيم

على إفشاء السلام وبذله للمسلمين كلهم من عرفت ومن لم تعرف كما تقدم في

الحديث الآخر والسلام أول أسباب التألف ومفتاح استجلاب المودة وفي إفشائه

تمكن ألفة المسلمين بعضهم لبعض وإظهار شعارهم المميز لهم من غيرهم من أهل

الملل مع ما فيه من رياضة النفس ولزوم التواضع وإعظام حرمات المسلمين وقد

ذكر البخاري رحمه الله في صحيحه عن عمار بن ياسر رضي الله عنه أنه قال ثلاث

من جمعهن فقد جمع الإيمان الإنصاف من نفسك وبذل السلام للعالم والإنفاق من

الاقتار وروى غير البخاري هذا الكلام مرفوعا إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

وبذل السلام للعالم والسلام على من عرفت ومن لم تعرف وإفشاء السلام كلها

بمعنى واحد وفيها لطيفة أخرى  وهي أنها تتضمن رفع التقاطع والتهاجر والشحناء

وفساد ذات البين التي هي الحالقة وأن سلامه لله لا يتبع فيه هواه ولا يخص

أصحابه وأحبابه به والله سبحانه وتعالى أعلم بالصواب
#

| (باب بيان أن الدين النصيحة
# [55] فيه (عن تميم الداري رضي
# الله عنه أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال الدين النصيحة قلنا لمن قال

لله ولكتابه ولرسوله ولأئمة المسلمين عامتهم) هذا حديث عظيم الشأن وعليه

مدار الإسلام كما سنذكره من شرحه وأما ما قاله جماعات من العلماء أن أحد

أرباع الإسلام أي أحد الأحاديث الأربعة التي تجمع أمور الإسلام فليس كما

قالوه بل المدار على هذا وحده وهذا الحديث من أفراد مسلم وليس لتميم الداري

في صحيح البخاري عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم شيء ولا له في مسلم عنه غير

هذا الحديث وقد تقدم في آخر مقدمة الكتاب بيان الاختلاف في نسبة تميم وأنه

دارى أوديرى وأما شرح هذا الحديث فقال الإمام أبو سليمان الخطابي رحمه الله

النصيحة كلمة جامعة معناها حيازة الحظ للمنصوح له قال ويقال هو من وجيز

الأسماء ومختصر الكلام وليس في كلام العرب كلمة مفردة يستوفى بها العبارة

عن المعنى هذه الكلمة كما قالوا في الفلاح ليس في كلام العرب كلمة أجمع

لخير الدنيا والآخرة منه قال وقيل النصيحة مأخوذة من نصح الرجل ثوبه إذا

خاطه فشبهوا فعل الناصح فيما يتحراه من صلاح المنصوح له بما يسده من خلل

الثوب قال وقيل إنها مأخوذة من نصحت العسل إذا صفيته من الشمع شبهوا تخليص

القول من الغش بتخليص العسل من الخلط قال ومعنى الحديث عماد الدين وقوامه

النصحية كقوله الحج عرفة أي عماده ومعظمه عرفة وأما تفسير النصيحة)
# 
# وأنواعها فقد ذكر الخطابي وغيره من العلماء فيها كلاما نفيسا أنا أضم

بعضه إلى بعض مختصرا قالوا أما النصيحة لله تعالى فمعناها منصرف إلى

الإيمان به ونفي الشريك عنه وترك الإلحاد في صفاته ووصفه بصفات الكمال

والجلال كلها وتنزيهه سبحانه وتعالى من جميع النقائص والقيام بطاعته

واجتناب معصيته  والحب فيه والبغض فيه وموالاة من أطاعه ومعادة من عصاه

وجهاد من كفر به والاعتراف بنعمته وشكره عليها والإخلاص في جميع الأمور

والدعاء إلى جميع الأوصاف المذكورة والحث عليها والتلطف في جميع الناس أو

من أمكن منهم عليها قال الخطابي رحمه الله وحقيقة هذه الإضافة راجعة إلى

العبد في نصحه نفسه فالله تعالى غني عن نصح الناصح وأما النصيحة لكتابه

سبحانه وتعالى فالإيمان بأن كلام الله تعالى وتنزيله لا يشبهه شيء من كلام

الخلق ولا يقدر على مثله أحد من الخلق ثم تعظيمه وتلاوته حق تلاوته

وتحسينها والخشوع عندها وإقامة حروفه في التلاوة والذب عنه لتأويل المحرفين

وتعرض الطاعنين والتصديق بما فيه والوقوف مع أحكامه وتفهم علومه وأمثاله

والاعتبار بمواعظه والتفكر في عجائبه والعمل بمحكمه والتسليم لمتشابهه

والبحث عن عمومه وخصوصه وناسخه ومنسوخه ونشر علومه والدعاء إليه والى ما
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ن-ص-ح (n-ṣ-ḥ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning is sincerity, purity, and free counsel; also used for sewing a garment (repairing its tear) and clarifying honey (straining out wax).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Naṣīḥah in theological terms is the sincere pursuit of the well-being of the one counseled, whether toward God (in faith and obedience) or toward creation.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage denotes the act of sincere advising; metaphorical (majāz) usage extends to the repair of a garment or purification of honey, signifying the removal of defect and impurity.
- Root: أ-ل-ف (a-l-f)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Root denotes familiarity, harmony, and the joining of hearts; from it derives 'ulfah (intimacy) and ta'alluf (mutual accord).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In the Qur'anic and theological frame, it signifies the divinely-created bond of social cohesion among believers.
