يكون في حياته فنهاهم عنه بعد مماته وقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (استنصت

الناس) معناه مرهم بالإنصات ليسمعوا هذه الأمور المهمة والقواعد التي

سأقررها لكم وأحملكموها وقوله في حجة الوداع سميت بذلك لأن النبي صلى الله

عليه وسلم ودع الناس فيها وعلمهم في خطبته فيها أمر دينهم وأوصاهم بتبليغ

الشرع فيها إلى من غاب عنها فقال صلى الله عليه وسلم ليبلغ الشاهد منكم

الغائب والمعروف في الرواية حجة الوداع بفتح الحاء وقال الهروي وغيره من

أهل اللغة المسموع من العرب في واحدة الحجج حجة بكسر الحاء قالوا والقياس

فتحها لكونها اسما للمرة الواحدة وليست عبارة عن الهيئة حتى تكسر قالوا

فيجوز الكسر بالسماع والفتح بالقياس وقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (ويحكم أو

قال ويلكم) قال القاضي هما كلمتان استعملتهما العرب بمعنى التعجب والتوجع

قال سيبويه ويل كلمة لمن وقع في هلكة وويح ترحم وحكي عنه ويح زجر لمن أشرف

على الهلكة قال غيره ولا يراد بهما الدعاء بإيقاع الهلكة ولكن الترحم
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ر-ء-ي (rā'-hamza-yā') — for "الراء" (the letter rā')
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: The letter rā'; a distinct phonetic unit in Arabic orthography.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Used here purely as a linguistic marker for textual transmission (riwāyah).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal reference to the letter, not metaphorical.
- Root: س-ب-ب (sīn-bā'-bā') — for "سباب" (reviling)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To insult, vilify, or speak against one's honor; derived from cutting or severing (qaṭʿ).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological terms, reviling a Muslim violates the sanctity of brotherhood in faith (ukhuwwah īmāniyyah).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) in the text; no metaphorical extension.
- Root: ف-س-ق (fā'-sīn-qāf) — for "فسوق" (disobedience)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To emerge or exit (khurūj) from something.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In Sharīʿah, exiting from obedience to Allah's commands; a technical term for grave sin without outright unbelief.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal root meaning "exit"; legally applied as a technical term (naql sharʿī).
- Root: ك-ف-ر (kāf-fā'-rā') — for "كفر" (unbelief)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To cover, conceal; ingratitude for a benefit.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Theological: denial of divine truth (juhūd) or ingratitude (kufr al-niʿmah); distinguishes major unbelief (kufr al-millah) from minor (kufr al-niʿmah).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: covering; metaphorical: rejection of faith or gratitude.
- Root: ق-ت-ل (qāf-tā'-lām) — for "قتال" (fighting)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To kill or engage in combat.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In legal discourse, armed aggression against a Muslim.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: physical combat; possible metaphorical: verbal strife (mushārah) per Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ.
- Root: ض-ر-ب (ḍād-rā'-bā') — for "يضرب" (striking)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To strike, hit, or beat.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Physical violence against another's neck (raqabah).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: striking; here, killing in mutual combat.
- Sībawayh Rule: Naṣb of "كفارا" as ḥāl (circumstantial accusative) — "Do not return [while being] disbelievers"; and the rafʿ of "يضرب" as a new sentence (isti'nāf) or jāz (apocopate) on a suppressed conditional (in tarjiʿū yaḍrib).
chapters.translation:
I say: Regarding the letter rā' and the kāf — in it is Abū ʿUthmān, who is al-Nahdī, with the fatḥah on the nūn, and his name is ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Mill, with the fatḥah, kasrah, and ḍammah on the mīm, along with the tashdīd of the lām. It is also said: Mill', with the kasrah on the mīm, the sukūn on the lām, and a hamzah after it. Its clarification has already preceded in the commentary at the end of the Introduction. As for Abū Bakrah, his name is Nufayʿ ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Kaladah, with the fatḥah on the kāf and lām. His mother and the mother of his brother Ziyād was Sumayyah, a slave-woman of al-Ḥārith ibn Kaladah. He was called Abū Bakrah because he lowered himself down to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, from the fortress of al-Ṭā'if by means of a pulley (bakrah). He died in Baṣrah in the year fifty-one, or it is said fifty-two, may Allah be pleased with him. And Allah, Glorified and Exalted, knows best.

| (Chapter: Clarification of the Prophet's saying, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: "Reviling a Muslim is disobedience, and fighting him is unbelief.")

In the language, reviling (sibāb) means insulting and speaking about a person's honor with what disparages him. Disobedience (fisq) in the language means exiting, and what is meant by it in the Sacred Law is exiting from obedience. As for the meaning of the ḥadīth: reviling a Muslim without right is forbidden by the consensus of the Community (ijmāʿ al-ummah), and its perpetrator is a disobedient sinner (fāsiq), just as the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, informed. As for fighting him without right, it does not render one an unbeliever in the view of the People of Truth (ahl al-ḥaqq) — unbelief that removes one from the religion (millah) — as we have already stated in many places, unless he deems it lawful (istaḥallahu). When this is established, it is said regarding the interpretation of the ḥadīth there are several sayings: One of them is that it concerns the one who deems it lawful. The second is that what is meant is unbelief of ingratitude for the favor and the brotherhood of Islam, not unbelief of denial (juhūd). The third is that it leads to unbelief by its ill-omen. The fourth is that it is an act like the acts of the disbelievers. And Allah knows best. Then, the apparent meaning of "fighting him" is the well-known combat. Al-Qāḍī said: It is permissible that what is meant is verbal contention and repulsion. And Allah knows best.

As for what pertains to the chain of transmission (isnād): In it is Muḥammad ibn Bakkār ibn al-Rayyān, with the fatḥah on the rā' and the tashdīd of the dotted tā' (i.e., the tā' with two dots, meaning the tā' marbūṭah or the tā' of "thā'" — here, the tā' with two dots above, i.e., the letter "tā'" as in "thā'"? Actually, "المثناة تحت" means the letter with two dots below, i.e., "yā'" — so it is "al-muthannāh taḥt," meaning the letter yā' with two dots beneath, so it is "al-Rayyān" with tashdīd on the yā'). In it is Zubayd, with the ḍammah on the zāy and with the single bā', then the dotted tā' (i.e., the tā' with two dots above, meaning "thā'"? No — "المثناة" here refers to the letter with two dots, which is "yā'" when below, or "tā'" when above; here it says "ثم المثناة" meaning then the letter with two dots, i.e., the "tā'" — so it is Zubayd ibn al-Ḥārith al-Yāmī, and it is also said al-Ayāmī. There is no other [Zubayd] in the two Ṣaḥīḥs. In the Muwaṭṭa', there is Zubayd ibn al-Ṣalt, with the repetition of the dotted letter (i.e., the tā' with two dots) and with the ḍammah and kasrah on the zāy. Its clarification has already preceded at the end of the Chapters. In it is Abū Wā'il, Shaqīq ibn Salamah.

As for Muslim's saying at the beginning of the chain: {[64] "Muḥammad ibn Bakkār and ʿAwn narrated to us; they said: Muḥammad ibn Ṭalḥah narrated to us; ḥ — and Muḥammad ibn al-Muthannā narrated to us; ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Mahdī narrated to us; Sufyān narrated to us; and Muḥammad ibn al-Muthannā narrated to us; Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us; Shuʿbah narrated to us; all of them on the authority of Zubayd"} — thus we have recorded it, and likewise it occurred in our original copy and in some copies. And in the copies upon which Shaykh Abū ʿAmr ibn al-Ṣalāḥ, may Allah have mercy on him, relied, it occurred with the two paths of Muḥammad ibn Ṭalḥah and Shuʿbah, and the path of Muḥammad ibn al-Muthannā from Ibn Mahdī from Sufyān did not occur in them. The Shaykh disapproved of his saying "all of them" (kulluhum), since they are only two — Muḥammad ibn Ṭalḥah and Shuʿbah. His disapproval is correct according to what is in his copies. But according to what we have, there is no disapproval, for Sufyān is the third of them. And Allah knows best.

| (Chapter: Clarification of the meaning of {[65] the Prophet's saying, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: "Do not return after me as disbelievers, striking the necks of one another."})

His saying, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: "Do not return after me as disbelievers, striking the necks of one another" — it is said regarding its meaning there are seven sayings: One of them is that this unbelief applies to the one who deems it lawful without right. The second is that what is meant is unbelief of ingratitude for the favor and the right of Islam. The third is that it approaches unbelief and leads to it. The fourth is that it is an act like the acts of the disbelievers. The fifth is that what is meant is literal unbelief, and its meaning is: do not become disbelievers, but rather remain Muslims. The sixth is related by al-Khaṭṭābī and others: that what is meant by "disbelievers" is those who are covered with weapons (al-mutakaffirūn bil-silāḥ). It is said: a man is "covered" (takaffara) with his weapon when he puts it on. Al-Azharī said in his book Tahdhīb al-Lughah: It is said of the wearer of weapons: "kāfir" (one who is covered). The seventh is stated by al-Khaṭṭābī: its meaning is — do not let some of you declare others disbelievers, so that you deem it lawful to fight one another. The most apparent of the sayings is the fourth, and it is the choice of Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ, may Allah have mercy on him.

Then, regarding the narration "yaḍribu" (striking) — with the rafʿ (ḍammah) on the bā' — thus is it correct, and likewise the earlier and later scholars narrated it, and by it the intended meaning here is sound. Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ, may Allah have mercy on him, transmitted that some scholars recorded it with the sukūn on the bā'. Al-Qāḍī said: That corrupts the meaning, and the correct is the ḍammah. I say: Likewise, Abū al-Baqā' al-ʿUkbarī said that it is permissible to make the bā' jāzim (sukūn) on the basis of a suppressed conditional, i.e., "if you return, they will strike." And Allah knows best.

As for his saying, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: "Do not return after me as disbelievers" — al-Qāḍī said: al-Ṣabrī said: Its meaning is "after my departure from this station of mine," and this was on the Day of Sacrifice (yawm al-naḥr) at Minā during the Farewell Pilgrimage. Or it means "after me," i.e., "after my time," meaning: do not succeed me regarding yourselves with other than what I commanded you. Or it means that he, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was certain that this would not occur during his lifetime, so he forbade them from it after his death.

His saying, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: "He silenced the people" (istanṣata al-nās) — its meaning is: he commanded them to be silent so that they might hear these important matters and the principles that I will establish for you and convey to you.

His saying "in the Farewell Pilgrimage" (ḥajjat al-wadāʿ) — it was so named because the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, took leave of (waddaʿa) the people in it, and taught them in his sermon therein the matters of their religion, and enjoined them to convey the Sacred Law therein to those who were absent from it. He said, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: "Let the one present convey to the one absent." The well-known form in the narration is "ḥajjat al-wadāʿ" with the fatḥah on the ḥā'. Al-Harawī and others of the linguists said: What is heard from the Arabs for the singular of "ḥajaj" (pilgrimages) is "ḥijjah" with the kasrah on the ḥā'. They said: The analogical form is the fatḥah, because it is a noun for a single instance (ism al-marrah), and it is not an expression of a mode (hay'ah) so as to be broken (i.e., with kasrah). They said: So the kasrah is permissible by audition (samāʿ) and the fatḥah by analogy (qiyās).

His saying, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: "Woe to you (wayḥakum), or he said: woe to you (waylakum)" — al-Qāḍī said: They are two words that the Arabs used to express astonishment and grief. Sībawayh said: "Wayl" is a word for one who has fallen into destruction, and "wayḥ" is an expression of mercy. It is related from him: "Wayḥ" is a rebuke for one who is on the brink of destruction. Someone else said: Neither of them is intended as a supplication for the occurrence of destruction, but rather as an expression of mercy.

chapters.title_en: Section 111 — On the Utterance of Wonder, the Naming of Slander of Lineage and Wailing as Disbelief, the Naming of the Fugitive Slave as Disbeliever, and the Disbelief of One Who Attributes Rain to the Stars
chapters.arabic_text:
والتعجب وروي عن عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه قال ويح كلمة
# 
# رحمة وقال الهروي ويح لمن وقع في هلكة لا يستحقها فيترحم عليه ويرثى له

وويل للذي  يستحقها ولا يترحم عليه والله أعلم وأما أسانيد الباب ففيه علي

بن مدرك بضم الميم وإسكان الدال وكسر الراء وفيه أبو زرعة بن عمرو بن جرير

وفي اسمه خلاف مشهور قد قدمناه في أول الكتاب وهو كتاب الإيمان قيل اسمه

هرم وقيل عمرو وقيل عبد الرحمن وقيل عبيد وفيه واقد بن محمد بالقاف وقد

قدمنا أنه ليس فى الصحيحين وافد والله أعلم بالصواب

| (باب إطلاق اسم الكفر على الطعن في النسب والنياحة
# [67] قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (اثنتان في الناس هما بهم كفر الطعن في

النسب والنياحة على الميت) وفيه أقوال أصحها أن معناه هما من أعمال الكفار

وأخلاق الجاهلية والثاني أنه يؤدي إلى الكفر والثالث أنه كفر النعمة

والإحسان والرابع أن ذلك في المستحل وفي هذا الحديث تغليظ تحريم الطعن في

النسب والنياحة وقد جاء في كل واحد منهما نصوص معروفة والله أعلم)

# باب تسمية العبد الآبق كافرا
# [68] قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (أيما عبد أبق من مواليه فقد كفر حتى يرجع

إليهم) وفي الرواية
# 
# الأخرى فقد برئت منه الذمة وفي الأخرى إذا أبق العبد لم تقبل له صلاة أما

تسميته كافرا ففيه الأوجه التي في الباب قبله وأما
# [69] قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (فقد برئت منه الذمة) فمعناه لا ذمة له قال

الشيخ أبو عمرو رحمه الله الذمة هنا يجوز أن تكون هي الذمة المفسرة بالذمام

وهي الحرمة ويجوز أن يكون من قبيل ما جاء في قوله له ذمة الله تعالى وذمة

رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أي ضمانه وأمانته ورعايته ومن ذلك أن الآبق

كان مصونا عن عقوبة السيد له وحبسه فزال ذلك بإباقه والله أعلم
# [70] وأما قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (إذا أبق العبد لم تقبل له صلاة) فقد

أوله الإمام المازري وتابعه القاضي عياض رحمهما الله على أن ذلك محمول على

المستحل للإباق فيكفر ولا تقبل له صلاة لا غيرها ونبه بالصلاة على غيرها

وأنكر الشيخ أبوعمرو هذا وقال بل ذلك جار في غير  المستحل ولا يلزم من عدم

القبول عدم الصحة فصلاة الآبق صحيحة غير مقبولة فعدم قبولها لهذا الحديث

وذلك لاقترانها بمعصية وأما صحتها فلوجود شروطها وأركانها المستلزمة صحتها

ولا تناقض في ذلك ويظهر أثر عدم القبول في سقوط الثواب وأثر الصحة في سقوط

القضاء وفي أنه لا يعاقب عقوبة تارك الصلاة هذا آخر كلام الشيخ أبي عمرو

رحمه الله وهو ظاهر لاشك في حسنه وقد قال جماهير أصحابنا إن الصلاة في

الدار المغصوبة صحيحة لا ثواب فيها ورأيت في فتاوى أبي نصر بن الصباغ من

أصحابنا التى نقلها عنه بن أخيه القاضي أبومنصور قال المحفوظ من كلام

أصحابنا بالعراق أن الصلاة فى الدار المغصوبة صحيحة يسقط بها الفرض ولا

ثواب فيها قال أبو منصور ورأيت أصحابنا بخراسان اختلفوا فمنهم من قال لا

تصح الصلاة قال وذكر شيخنا في الكامل أنه ينبغي أن تصح ويحصل الثواب على

الفعل فيكون مثابا على فعله عاصيا بالمقام في المغصوب فإذا لم نمنع
# 
# من صحتها لم نمنع من حصول الثواب قال أبو منصور وهذا هو القياس على طريق

من صححها والله أعلم ويقال أبق العبد وأبق بفتح الباء وكسرها لغتان

مشهورتان الفتح أفصح وبه جاء القرآن إذ أبق إلى الفلك المشحون وأما قوله عن

منصور بن عبد الرحمن عن الشعبي عن جرير أنه سمعه يقول أيما عبد أبق من

مواليه فقد كفر حتى يرجع إليهم قال منصور قد والله روي عن النبي صلى الله

عليه وسلم ولكنى أكره أن يروى عنى ها هنا بالبصرة فمعناه أن منصورا روى هذا

الحديث عن الشعبي عن جرير موقوفا عليه ثم قال منصور بعد روايته إياه موقوفا

والله إنه مرفوع إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فاعلموه أيها الخواص

الحاضرون فإني أكره أن أصرح برفعه في لفظ روايتي فيشيع عنى فى البصرة التى

هي مملؤة من المعتزلة والخوارج الذين يقولون بتخليد أهل المعاصي في النار

والخوارج يزيدون على التخليد فيحكمون بكفره ولهم شبهة في التعلق بظاهر هذا

الحديث وقد قدمنا  تأويله وبطلان مذاهبهم بالدلائل القاطعة الواضحة التي

ذكرناها في مواضع من هذا الكتاب والله أعلم وأما منصور بن عبد الرحمن هذا

فهو الأشل الغداني البصري وثقه أحمد بن حنبل ويحيى بن معين ووضعفه أبو حاتم

الرازي وفي الرواة خمسة يقال لكل واحد منهم منصور بن عبد الرحمن هذا أحدهم

والله اعلم

| (باب بيان كفر من قال مطرنا بالنوء
# [71] قوله (صلى بنا
# رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم صلاة الصبح بالحديبية على إثر سماء كانت من

الليل فلما انصرف قال هل تدرون ماذا قال ربكم قالوا الله ورسوله أعلم قال

قال أصبح من عبادي)
# 
# مؤمن بي وكافر فأما من قال مطرنا بفضل الله ورحمته فذلك مؤمن بي كافر

بالكوكب وأما من قال مطرنا بنوء كذا وكذا فذلك كافر بي مؤمن بالكوكب) أما

الحديبية ففيها لغتان تخفيف الياء وتشديدها والتخفيف هو الصحيح المشهور
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ع ج ب (ʿ-j-b)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Astonishment, wonder, the state of being struck by something extraordinary
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The soul's agitation upon encountering that which is unfamiliar or beyond expectation
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense of marveling; here applied to the rhetorical exclamation "Wayḥ" as a word of mercy
- Root: ك ف ر (k-f-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To cover, conceal; ingratitude; denial of beneficence
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In Sharīʿah discourse, the covering of truth; graded meanings from minor ingratitude to outright unbelief
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal covering (satr); metaphorical application to disbelief as the veiling of truth
- Root: أ ب ق (ʾ-b-q)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: The fleeing of a slave from his master; escape from servitude
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): A specific legal category of slave flight entailing loss of protective covenant
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal act of running away; metaphorical extension to severance of obligation
- Root: ن و ء (n-w-ʾ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: A star's setting; the mansions of the moon; rain attributed to stellar influence
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In pre-Islamic usage, the celestial station from which rain was superstitiously believed to descend
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal astronomical setting; metaphorical attribution of divine acts to created causes
- Sībawayh Rule: Taqdīr al-Maḥdhūf (Ellipsis Restoration) — Where the nominal predicate is omitted, the implied copula or governing verb is restored from context, as in "هما بهم كفر" where the intended meaning requires supplying the connective force of "min aʿmāl" (from the deeds of).
chapters.translation:
I say: Regarding the expression of wonder, it is related from ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, may God be pleased with him, that he said: "Wayḥ" is a word of mercy. And al-Harawī said: "Wayḥ" is said of one who has fallen into a destruction he does not deserve, so mercy is invoked for him and he is pitied. As for "Wayl," it is for one who deserves it and is not pitied. And God knows best.

As for the chains of transmission in this chapter, among them is ʿAlī ibn Mudrik — with ḍammah on the mīm, sukūn on the dāl, and kasrah on the rāʾ — and among them is Abū Zurʿah ibn ʿAmr ibn Jarīr. Concerning his name there is a well-known disagreement which we have already mentioned at the beginning of the book, namely the Book of Faith (Kitāb al-Īmān). It is said his name was Hirm, and it is said ʿAmr, and it is said ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, and it is said ʿUbayd. And among them is Wāqid ibn Muḥammad — with the qāf — and we have already stated that there is no "Wāfid" in the two Ṣaḥīḥs. And God knows best what is correct.

CHAPTER: On the Application of the Name "Disbelief" to Slander of Lineage and Wailing

[67] His saying, peace and blessings be upon him: "Two qualities among people are acts of disbelief in them: slander of lineage and wailing over the dead." Concerning this there are several opinions. The soundest of them is that its meaning is: they are among the deeds of the disbelievers and the traits of the Age of Ignorance (Jāhiliyyah). The second is that it leads to disbelief. The third is that it is disbelief in the beneficence (kufr al-niʿmah) and goodness. The fourth is that it applies to the one who deems it lawful (mustaḥill). In this ḥadīth there is a severe emphasis on the prohibition of slander of lineage and wailing, and well-known texts have come down concerning each of the two. And God knows best.

CHAPTER: On Naming the Fugitive Slave a Disbeliever

[68] His saying, peace and blessings be upon him: "Any slave who flees from his masters has committed disbelief until he returns to them." And in the other narration: "The covenant of protection (dhimmah) has been absolved from him." And in yet another: "When a slave flees, no prayer is accepted from him." As for his being named a disbeliever, the same considerations apply as in the preceding chapter. And as for —

[69] His saying, peace and blessings be upon him: "The covenant of protection has been absolved from him" — its meaning is that he has no covenant. Shaykh Abū ʿAmr, may God have mercy on him, said: The dhimmah here may be the dhimmah explained as dhimām, namely inviolability (ḥurmah); and it may be of the type occurring in his saying: "He has the covenant of God Most High and the covenant of His Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him," meaning His guarantee, His security, and His protection. From this it follows that the fugitive slave was previously shielded from the master's punishment and imprisonment, and that shielding lapsed by virtue of his flight. And God knows best.

[70] As for his saying, peace and blessings be upon him: "When a slave flees, no prayer is accepted from him" — Imām al-Māzarī interpreted it, and Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ followed him, may God have mercy on them both, as being carried upon the one who deems flight lawful (mustaḥill), who thereby disbelieves, and no prayer is accepted from him, nor anything else; and prayer is mentioned to draw attention to all other acts. But Shaykh Abū ʿAmr rejected this and said: Rather, it applies to one who does not deem it lawful; and the absence of acceptance does not necessitate the absence of validity (ṣiḥḥah). Thus the prayer of a fugitive slave is valid but not accepted. Its non-acceptance is due to this ḥadīth, because it is conjoined with disobedience; and its validity is due to the presence of its conditions and pillars, which necessitate its validity. There is no contradiction in this. The effect of non-acceptance appears in the forfeiture of reward (thawāb), and the effect of validity appears in the dropping of the obligation to make it up (qaḍāʾ) and in that he is not punished with the punishment of one who abandons prayer. This is the end of Shaykh Abū ʿAmr's statement, may God have mercy on him, and it is manifest, with no doubt as to its excellence.

The majority of our companions (aṣḥāb) have said that prayer in a usurped dwelling (al-dār al-maghṣūbah) is valid with no reward in it. And I saw in the legal opinions (fatāwā) of Abū Naṣr ibn al-Ṣabbāgh, one of our companions, which his nephew, the judge Abū Manṣūr, transmitted from him, that he said: The preserved statement from our companions in Iraq is that prayer in a usurped dwelling is valid, by which the obligation is discharged, and there is no reward in it. Abū Manṣūr said: And I saw our companions in Khurāsān differ; among them was one who said the prayer is not valid. He said: And our teacher mentioned in al-Kāmil that it ought to be valid, and reward is attained upon the act, so that one is rewarded for his act while being disobedient by remaining in the usurped property. Thus, since we do not prevent its validity, we do not prevent the attainment of reward. Abū Manṣūr said: And this is the analogical inference (qiyās) upon the path of those who deem it valid. And God knows best.

It is said "abaqa al-ʿabdu" and "abiqa" — with fatḥah on the bāʾ and kasrah on it — two well-known dialects; the fatḥah is the more eloquent, and upon it the Qurʾān came: {«إِذْ أَبَقَ إِلَى الْفُلْكِ الْمَشْحُونِ»} (When he fled to the laden ship) (Q 37:140).

As for his statement concerning Manṣūr ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from al-Shaʿbī, from Jarīr, that he heard him say: "Any slave who flees from his masters has committed disbelief until he returns to them" — Manṣūr said: By God, it has indeed been related from the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, but I dislike that it be related from me here in Baṣrah. Its meaning is that Manṣūr related this ḥadīth from al-Shaʿbī, from Jarīr, as stopped (mawqūf) upon him; then Manṣūr said after relating it as stopped: By God, it is raised (marfūʿ) to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him — so take note of it, you select ones present, for I dislike to declare its raising explicitly in the wording of my narration, lest it become widely known from me in Baṣrah, which is filled with the Muʿtazilah and the Khawārij, who hold that the perpetrators of sins abide eternally in the Fire. And the Khawārij go beyond eternal abiding, for they rule that such a one is a disbeliever, and they have a specious argument in clinging to the apparent meaning of this ḥadīth. We have already presented its interpretation and the nullity of their doctrines by the decisive and clear proofs which we have mentioned in various places of this book. And God knows best.

As for this Manṣūr ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, he is al-Ashall al-Ghudānī al-Baṣrī. Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal and Yaḥyā ibn Maʿīn declared him trustworthy (thiqah), while Abū Ḥātim al-Rāzī weakened him. And among the narrators there are five, each of whom is called Manṣūr ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān; this one is one of them. And God knows best.

CHAPTER: On Explaining the Disbelief of One Who Says "We Were Rained Upon by the Rising of Such-and-Such a Star"

[71] His saying — he, peace and blessings be upon him, led us in the dawn prayer (ṣalāt al-ṣubḥ) at al-Ḥudaybiyyah following a rain (samāʾ) that had fallen during the night. When he turned away, he said: "Do you know what your Lord said?" They said: "God and His Messenger know best." He said: "He said: 'This morning, among My servants there became a believer in Me and a disbeliever. As for the one who said, "We were rained upon by the bounty of God and His mercy," that one is a believer in Me, a disbeliever in the star. And as for the one who said, "We were rained upon by the rising of such-and-such a star," that one is a disbeliever in Me, a believer in the star.'"

As for al-Ḥudaybiyyah, there are two dialects in it: the lightening of the yāʾ and its doubling. The lightening is the correct and well-known one.

chapters.title_en: The Preferred Reading of "Ji'rānah," the Meaning of "Naw'" (Lunar Mansion), and the Interpretation of the Rain-Related Hadith
chapters.arabic_text:
المختار وهو قول الشافعي وأهل اللغة وبعض المحدثين والتشديد قول الكسائي

وبن وهب وجماهير المحدثين واختلافهم في الجعرانة كذلك في تشديد الراء

وتخفيفها والمختار فيها أيضا التخفيف وقوله على إثر سماء هو بكسر الهمزة

وإسكان الثاء وبفتحهما جميعا لغتان مشهورتان والسماء المطر وأما معنى

الحديث فاختلف العلماء في كفر من قال مطرنا بنوء كذا على قولين أحدهما هو

كفر بالله سبحانه وتعالى سالب لأصل الإيمان مخرج من ملة الإسلام قالوا وهذا

فيمن قال ذلك معتقدا أن الكوكب فاعل مدبر منشىء للمطر كما كان بعض أهل

الجاهلية يزعم ومن اعتقد هذا فلا شك في كفره وهذا القول هو الذي ذهب إليه

جماهير العلماء والشافعي منهم وهو ظاهر الحديث قالوا وعلى هذا لو قال مطرنا

بنوء كذا معتقدا أنه من الله تعالى
# 
# وبرحمته وأن النوء ميقات له وعلامة اعتبارا بالعادة فكأنه قال مطرنا في

وقت كذا فهذا لا يكفر واختلفوا في كراهته والأظهر كراهته لكنها كراهة تنزيه

لا إثم فيها وسبب الكراهة أنها كلمة مترددة بين الكفر وغيره فيساء الظن

بصاحبها ولأنها شعار الجاهلية ومن سلك مسلكهم والقول الثاني في أصل  تأويل

الحديث أن المراد كفر نعمة الله تعالى لاقتصاره على إضافة الغيث إلى الكوكب

وهذا فيمن لا يعتقد تدبير الكوكب ويؤيد هذا التأويل الرواية الأخيرة في

الباب أصبح من الناس شاكر وكافر وفي الرواية الأخرى ما أنعمت على عبادي من

نعمة إلا أصبح فريق منهم بها كافرين وفي الرواية الأخرى ما أنزل الله تعالى

من السماء من بركة إلا أصبح فريق من الناس بها كافرين فقوله بها يدل على

أنه كفر بالنعمة والله أعلم وأما النوء ففيه كلام طويل قد لخصه الشيخ أبو

عمرو بن الصلاح رحمه الله فقال النوء في أصله ليس هو نفس الكوكب فإنه مصدر

ناء النجم ينوء نوءا أي سقط وغاب وقيل أي نهض وطلع وبيان ذلك أن ثمانية

وعشرين نجما معروفة المطالع في أزمنة السنة كلها وهي المعروفة بمنازل القمر

الثمانية والعشرين يسقط فى كل ثلاثة عشرة ليلة منها نجم في المغرب مع طلوع

الفجر ويطلع آخر يقابله في المشرق من ساعته وكان أهل الجاهلية إذا كان عند

ذلك مطر ينسبونه إلى الساقط الغارب منهما وقال الأصمعي إلى الطالع منهما

قال أبو عبيد ولم أسمع أحدا ينسب النوء للسقوط إلا في هذا الموضع ثم إن

النجم نفسه قد يسمى نوءا تسمية للفاعل بالمصدر قال أبو إسحاق الزجاج في بعض

أماليه الساقطة في الغرب هي الأنواء والطالعة فى المشرق هي البوارح والله

اعلم
# [73] وأما قوله فى رواية بن عباس رضي الله عنهما (مطر الناس على عهد رسول

الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
# 
# فقال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أصبح من الناس شاكر ومنهم كافر قالوا هذه

رحمة الله وقال بعضهم لقد صدق نوء كذا وكذا قال فنزلت هذه الآية فلا أقسم

بمواقع النجوم حتى بلغ وتجعلون رزقكم أنكم تكذبون) فقال الشيخ أبو عمرو

رحمه الله ليس مراده أن جميع هذا نزل في قولهم في الأنواء فإن الأمر في ذلك

وتفسيره يأبى ذلك وإنما النازل في ذلك قوله تعالى وتجعلون رزقكم أنكم

تكذبون والباقي نزل في غير  ذلك ولكن اجتمعا في وقت النزول فذكر الجميع من

أجل ذلك قال الشيخ أبوعمرو رحمه الله ومما يدل على هذا أن فى بعض الروايات

عن بن عباس رضى الله عنهما في ذلك الاقتصار على هذا القدر اليسير فحسب هذا

آخر كلام الشيخ رحمه الله وأما تفسير الآية فقيل تجعلون زرقكم أى شكركم كذا

قاله بن عباس والأكثرون وقيل تجعلون شكر رزقكم قاله الأزهري وأبو علي

الفارسي وقال الحسن أي تجعلون حظكم وأما مواقع النجوم فقال الأكثرون المراد

نجوم السماء ومواقعها مغاربها وقيل مطالعها وقيل انكدارها وقيل انتثارها

يوم القيامة وقيل النجوم نجوم القرآن وهي أوقات نزوله وقال مجاهد مواقع

النجوم محكم القرآن والله أعلم وأما ما يتعلق بالأسانيد ففيه عمرو بن سواد

بتشديد الواو آخره دال وفيه أبو يونس مولى أبي هريرة واسمه سليم بن جبير

بضم أولهما وفيه عباس بن عبد العظيم العنبري هو بالسين المهملة والعنبري

بالعين المهملة والنون بعدها موحدة قال القاضي وضبطه العذري الغبري بالغين

المعجمة وهو تصحيف بلا شك وفيه أبو زميل بضم الزاي وفتح الميم واسمه سماك

بن الوليد الحنفى اليمامى قال بن عبد البر أجمعوا على أنه ثقة والله أعلم

وأما قول مسلم رحمه الله حدثني محمد بن سلمة المرادي حدثنا عبد الله بن وهب

عن عمرو بن الحارث قال مسلم رحمه الله وحدثني عمرو بن سواد أخبرنا عبد الله

بن وهب أخبرنا عمرو بن الحارث أن أبا يونس مولى أبي هريرة حدثه عن أبي

هريرة فهذا الإسناد كله بصريون إلا أبا
# 
# هريرة فمدني وإنما أتى مسلم بعبد الله بن وهب وعمرو بن الحارث أولا ثم

أعادهما ولم يقتصر على قوله حدثنا محمد وعمرو بن سواد لاختلاف لفظ الروايات

كما ترى وقد نبهنا على مثل هذا التدقيق والاحتياط لمسلم رحمه الله في مواضع

والله اعلم بالصواب
chapters.anchors:
- Root: خ-ي-ر (kh-y-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: The core meaning is "to choose" or "to prefer"; al-khiyārah denotes selection of the better of two matters.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological usage, al-mukhtār (the chosen/preferred) often contrasts with al-marjūḥ (the preponderant) in juristic preference (tarjīḥ), indicating a considered scholarly choice.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense is "selection"; metaphorically, it denotes the outcome of deliberation where one option is deemed superior.
- Sībawayh Rule: [Verbal Noun Derivation (Maṣdar)] (The maṣdar pattern faʿala-yafʿalu yields naw' as a verbal noun, governing the syntactic behavior of the verb nā'a in its transitive/intransitive uses.)

- Root: ن-و-ء (n-w-')
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: The root denotes rising, appearing, or, conversely, falling and setting; al-naw' refers to a star's setting or rising, and by extension, a lunar mansion.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In Quranic and theological context, naw' is tied to cosmic order (niẓām al-kawn) and the attribution of rain to celestial bodies—a key locus of tawḥīd versus jāhilīyyah belief.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: the star's setting (sugūṭ) or rising (ṭulūʿ); metaphorical: the time-period associated with that event, used idiomatically in "muṭirnā bi-naw' kadhā" (we were rained upon by such-and-such a mansion).
- Sībawayh Rule: [Prepositional Phrase Attachment (Taʿalluq al-Jār wa-l-Majrūr)] (The phrase "bi-naw'" attaches to the verb "muṭirnā" as a circumstantial qualifier (ḥāl) or causal adjunct, affecting the theological interpretation of agency.)

- Root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning is "to cover" (satara); kufr is the covering of truth or gratitude.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Distinguishes kufr al-niʿmah (ingratitude for blessings) from kufr al-millah (disbelief that exits one from the faith), a critical distinction in this hadith's interpretation.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: covering; metaphorical: rejection of divine agency, whether in belief (iʿtiqād) or in speech (qawl) without belief.
- Sībawayh Rule: [Predicate of Inna/Kāna] (The sentence "aṣbaḥa min al-nāsi shākirun wa-kāfir" requires the predicate to be a prepositional phrase or nominal, parsed as "among the people became a thankful one and a disbelieving one.")
chapters.translation:
I say: The preferred reading (al-mukhtār) is with lightening (takhfīf) of the rā' in "al-Ji'rānah"—and this is the position of al-Shāfiʿī, the people of language (ahl al-lughah), and some of the hadith scholars. The reading with doubling (tashdīd) is the position of al-Kisāʾī, Ibn Wahb, and the majority of hadith scholars. Their disagreement concerning "al-Ji'rānah" is likewise [found] in the doubling of the rā' and its lightening, and the preferred reading therein is also lightening.

His statement "on the heels of rain (ʿalā ithri samāʾ)"—"ithr" is with kasrah of the hamzah and sukūn of the thā', and with fathah of both, two well-known dialects (lughatān mashhūratān). And "samāʾ" here means rain (al-maṭar).

As for the meaning of the hadith, the scholars have differed concerning the kufr of one who says "We were rained upon by such-and-such a naw'"—on two positions (qawlān):

The first: It is kufr against Allah, may He be glorified and exalted, that negates the very foundation of faith (aṣl al-īmān) and expels one from the religion of Islam (millat al-Islām). They said: This applies to one who says this while believing that the celestial body (al-kawkab) is the agent (fāʿil), the manager (mudabbir), and the originator (munshiʾ) of the rain—just as some of the people of the Jāhiliyyah used to claim. Whoever believes this, there is no doubt concerning his kufr. This is the position adopted by the majority of scholars (jamāhīr al-ʿulamāʾ), and al-Shāfiʿī is among them, and it is the apparent meaning (ẓāhir) of the hadith. They said: On this basis, if one says "We were rained upon by such-and-such a naw'" while believing that it is from Allah, may He be exalted, and from His mercy, and that the naw' is merely a time-marker (mīqāt) for it and a sign (ʿalāmah) by way of customary observation (iʿtibāran bi-l-ʿādah)—as if he said "We were rained upon at such-and-such a time"—then this person does not commit kufr. They differed concerning its disapproval (karāhah); the more apparent (al-aẓhar) is its disapproval, but it is a disapproval of tanzīh (propriety), entailing no sin (ithm). The reason for the disapproval is that it is an expression wavering between kufr and other than it, so ill suspicion (sūʾ al-ẓann) falls upon its speaker, and because it is a slogan (shiʿār) of the Jāhiliyyah and of those who tread their path.

The second position concerning the fundamental interpretation (taʾwīl) of the hadith: The intended meaning is kufr of the blessing of Allah (kufr niʿmat Allāh), due to his restricting himself to attributing the rain to the celestial body. This applies to one who does not believe in the celestial body's management (tadbīr). This interpretation is supported by the final narration in this chapter: "Among the people, there became a thankful one and a disbelieving one (aṣbaḥa min al-nāsi shākirun wa-kāfir)." And in the other narration: "I have not bestowed upon My servants any blessing (niʿmah) except that a group of them became, by it, disbelievers (kāfirīn)." And in yet another narration: "Allah has not sent down from the sky any blessing (barakah) except that a group of people became, by it, disbelievers." So his statement "by it (bihā)" indicates that it is kufr of the blessing. And Allah knows best.

As for the naw' (lunar mansion), there is lengthy discussion concerning it, which Shaykh Abū ʿAmr ibn al-Ṣalāḥ, may Allah have mercy on him, summarized. He said: The naw' in its origin is not itself the celestial body, for it is a verbal noun (maṣdar): "nā'a al-najmu yanū'u naw'an," i.e., it fell and set (sagaṭa wa-ghāba). And it was said: i.e., it rose and appeared (nahada wa-ṭalaʿa). The clarification of this is that there are twenty-eight well-known stars whose rising-places (maṭāliʿ) occur in all the seasons of the year—these being the well-known twenty-eight lunar mansions (manāzil al-qamar). Every thirteen nights, one of them sets in the west (al-maghrib) at the appearance of dawn (ṭulūʿ al-fajr), and another, opposite it, rises in the east (al-mashriq) at that very hour. The people of the Jāhiliyyah, when rain occurred at that time, attributed it to the setting one (al-sāqiṭ al-ghārib) of the two—and al-Aṣmaʿī said: to the rising one (al-ṭāliʿ) of the two. Abū ʿUbayd said: I have not heard anyone attribute the naw' to the setting except in this place. Then, the star itself may be called a naw'—naming the agent by the verbal noun (tasmīyat al-fāʿil bi-l-maṣdar). Abū Isḥāq al-Zajjāj said in some of his dictations (amālī): The setting ones in the west are the anwāʾ, and the rising ones in the east are the bawāriḥ. And Allah knows best.

[73] As for his statement in the narration of Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with them both: "The people were rained upon during the era of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: 'Among the people, there became a thankful one and among them a disbelieving one.' They said: 'This is a mercy of Allah.' And some of them said: 'Indeed, such-and-such a naw' has proven true (ṣadaqa).' He said: 'Then this verse was revealed: {«So I swear by the positions of the stars—and indeed, it is a mighty oath, if you only knew—that this is a noble Quran»} (al-Wāqiʿah 56:75-77) until His statement: {«And you make your provision that you should deny»} (al-Wāqiʿah 56:82)."

Shaykh Abū ʿAmr, may Allah have mercy on him, said: It is not his intent that all of this was revealed concerning their statement about the anwāʾ, for the matter and its interpretation (tafsīr) preclude that. Rather, what was revealed concerning that is His statement, exalted: {«And you make your provision that you should deny»} (al-Wāqiʿah 56:82). The rest was revealed concerning other than that, but they coincided in the time of revelation (waqt al-nuzūl), so the entirety was mentioned for that reason. Shaykh Abū ʿAmr, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Among the evidence for this is that in some narrations from Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with them both, concerning that, there is restriction to this small amount only. This is the end of the Shaykh's speech, may Allah have mercy on him.

As for the interpretation of the verse: It was said: "You make your provision (rizq)" i.e., your gratitude (shukr)—thus said Ibn ʿAbbās and the majority (al-aktharūn). And it was said: "You make the gratitude for your provision"—said by al-Azharī and Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī. And al-Ḥasan said: i.e., you make your share (ḥaẓẓ).

As for "the positions of the stars (mawāqiʿ al-nujūm)": The majority said the intended meaning is the stars of the sky and their positions, i.e., their setting-places (maghārib). And it was said: their rising-places (maṭāliʿ). And it was said: their falling (inkidār). And it was said: their scattering (intithār) on the Day of Resurrection. And it was said: the stars are the stars of the Quran, i.e., the times of its revelation. And Mujāhid said: "The positions of the stars" is the muhkam (decisive) of the Quran. And Allah knows best.

As for what pertains to the chains of transmission (asānīd): In it is ʿAmr ibn Sawād—with tashdīd of the wāw, its final letter being a dāl. And in it is Abū Yūnus, the freed slave (mawlā) of Abū Hurayrah, whose name is Sulaym ibn Jubayr—with ḍammah on the first letter of both. And in it is ʿAbbās ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAẓīm al-ʿAnbarī—it is with the unpointed sīn (sīnh), and al-ʿAnbarī with the unpointed ʿayn, followed by nūn and then a single bā'. Al-Qāḍī said: Al-ʿUdhrī recorded it as al-Ghubarī with the pointed ghayn—and this is a corruption (taṣḥīf) without doubt. And in it is Abū Zumayl—with ḍammah of the zāy and fathah of the mīm—whose name is Simāk ibn al-Walīd al-Ḥanafī al-Yamāmī. Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr said: They are unanimous that he is trustworthy (thiqah). And Allah knows best.

As for the statement of Muslim, may Allah have mercy on him: "Muḥammad ibn Salamah al-Murādī narrated to me; ʿAbd Allāh ibn Wahb narrated to us; from ʿAmr ibn al-Ḥārith." Muslim, may Allah have mercy on him, said: "And ʿAmr ibn Sawād narrated to me; ʿAbd Allāh ibn Wahb informed us; ʿAmr ibn al-Ḥārith informed us; that Abū Yūnus, the freed slave of Abū Hurayrah, narrated to him; from Abū Hurayrah." This entire chain (isnād) consists of Baṣrans (Baṣriyyūn), except for Abū Hurayrah, who is a Medinan (Madanī). Muslim only brought ʿAbd Allāh ibn Wahb and ʿAmr ibn al-Ḥārith first, then repeated them, and did not restrict himself to his statement "Muḥammad and ʿAmr ibn Sawād narrated to us," due to the difference in the wording (lafẓ) of the narrations, as you see. And we have drawn attention to this kind of precision (tadqīq) and caution (iḥtiyāṭ) on the part of Muslim, may Allah have mercy on him, in other places. And Allah knows best what is correct.

chapters.title_en: Section 113 — The Evidence that Love for the Anṣār and for ʿAlī (may Allah be pleased with them) is a Sign of Faith, and Hatred of Them is a Sign of Hypocrisy; and the Chapter on the Diminution of Faith by Diminution of Acts of Obedience, and the Application of the Term "Disbelief" (kufr) to Other than Disbelief in Allah, such as Ingratitude for Kindness and Rights
chapters.arabic_text:
| باب الدليل على أن حب الانصار وعلى رضى الله عنهم
# (من الايمان وعلاماته وبعضهم من علامات النفاق)
# [74] قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (آية المنافق بغض الأنصار وآية  المؤمن حب

الأنصار وفي الرواية الأخرى حب الأنصار آية الإيمان وبغضهم آية النفاق وفي

الأخرى لا يحبهم إلا مؤمن ولا يبغضهم إلا منافق من أحبهم أحبه الله ومن

أبغضهم أبغضه الله وفي الأخرى)
# 
# لا يبغض الأنصار رجل يؤمن بالله واليوم الآخر وفي حديث علي رضي الله عنه

والذي فلق الحبة وبرأ النسمة إنه لعهد النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إلي أن لا

يحبني إلا مؤمن ولا يبغضني إلا منافق) قد تقدم أن الآية هي العلامة ومعنى

هذه الأحاديث أن من عرف مرتبة الأنصار وما كان منهم في نصرة دين الإسلام

والسعي في إظهاره وإيواء المسلمين وقيامهم في مهمات دين الإسلام حق القيام

وحبهم النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وحبه إياهم وبذلهم أموالهم وأنفسهم بين

يديه وقتالهم ومعاداتهم سائر الناس إيثارا للإسلام وعرف من علي بن أبي طالب

رضي الله عنه قربه من رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وحب النبي صلى الله

عليه وسلم له وما كان منه في نصرة الإسلام وسوابقه فيه ثم أحب الأنصار

وعليا لهذا كان ذلك من دلائل صحة إيمانه وصدقه في إسلامه لسروره بظهور

الإسلام والقيام بما يرضي الله سبحانه وتعالى ورسوله صلى الله عليه وسلم

ومن أبغضهم كان بضد ذلك واستدل به على نفاقه وفساد سريرته والله أعلم وأما

قوله فلق الحبة فمعناه شقها بالنبات وقوله وبرأ النسمة هو بالهمزة أي خلق
# 
# النسمة وهي بفتح النون والسين وهي الإنسان وقيل النفس وحكى الأزهري أن

النسمة هي النفس وأن كل دابة في جوفها روح فهي نسمة والله أعلم وأما ما

يتعلق بأسانيد الباب ففيه عبد الله بن عبد الله بن جبر فعبد مكبر في اسمه

واسم أبيه وجبر بفتح الجيم وإسكان الباء ويقال فيه أيضا جابر وفيه البراء

بن عازب وهو معروف بالمد هذا هو المشهور عند أهل العلم من المحدثين وأهل

اللغة والأخبار وأصحاب الفنون كلها قال الشيخ أبوعمرو بن الصلاح رحمه الله

وحفظت فيه عن بعض أهل اللغة القصر والمد وفيه يعقوب بن  عبد الرحمن القارىء

بتشديد الياء منسوب إلى القارة قبيلة معروفة وفيه زر بكسر الزاي وتشديد

الراء وهو زر بن حبيش وهو من المعمرين أدرك الجاهلية ومات سنة اثنتين

وثمانين وهو بن مائة وعشرين سنة وقيل بن مائة واثنتين وعشرين سنة وقيل مائة

وسبعة وعشرين وهو أسدي كوفي وأما قول مسلم رحمه الله حدثنا محمد بن المثنى

حدثنا عبد الرحمن بن مهدي عن شعبة عن عبد الله بن عبد الله بن جبر قال سمعت

أنسا يقول ثم قال مسلم حدثنا يحيى بن حبيب الحارثي حدثنا خالد يعنى بن

الحرث حدثنا شعبة عن عبد الله بن عبد الله عن أنس فهذان الإسنادان رجالهما

كلهم بصريون الا بن جبر فإنه أنصاري مدني وقد قدمنا أن شعبة وإن كان واسطيا

فقد استوطن البصرة والله اعلم

| باب بيان نقصان الايمان بنقص الطاعات وبيان اطلاق
# لفظ (الكفر على غير الكفر بالله ككفر النعمة والحقوق) قوله صلى الله عليه

وسلم (يا معشر النساء تصدقن وأكثرن الاستغفار فإني رأيتكن أكثر أهل)
# 
# النار فقالت امرأة منهن جزلة وما لنا يا رسول الله أكثر أهل النار قال

تكثرن اللعن وتكفرن العشير ما رأيت من ناقصات عقل ودين أغلب لذي لب منكن

قالت يا رسول الله وما نقصان العقل والدين قال أما نقصان العقل فشهادة

امرأتين تعدل شهادة رجل واحد فهذا نقصان العقل وتمكث الليالي ما تصلي وتفطر

في رمضان فهذا نقصان الدين) قال أهل اللغة المعشر هم الجماعة الذين أمرهم

واحد أي مشتركون وهو اسم يتناولهم كالإنس معشر والجن معشر والأنبياء معشر

والنساء معشر ونحو ذلك وجمعه معاشر وقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم رأيتكن أكثر

اهل النار هو بنصب أكثر إما على أن هذه الرؤية تتعدى إلى مفعولين وإما على

الحال على مذهب بن السراج وأبي علي الفارسي وغيرهما ممن قال إن أفعل لا

يتعرف بالإضافة وقيل هو بدل من الكاف في رأيتكن وأما قولها ومالنا أكثر أهل

النار فمنصوب إما على الحكاية وإما على الحال وقوله جزلة بفتح الجيم  وإسكان

الزاي أي ذات عقل ورأي قال بن دريد الجزالة العقل والوقار وأما العشير

فبفتح العين وكسرالشين وهو في الأصل المعاشر مطلقا والمراد هنا الزوج وأما

اللب فهو العقل والمراد كمال العقل وقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم فهذا نقصان

العقل أي علامة نقصانه وقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم وتمكث الليالي ما تصلي أي

تمكث ليالي وأياما لا تصلي بسبب الحيض وتفطر أياما من رمضان بسبب الحيض

والله أعلم وأما أحكام الحديث ففيه جمل من العلوم منها الحث على الصدقة

وأفعال البر والإكثار من الاستغفار وسائر الطاعات وفيه أن الحسنات يذهبن

السيئات كما قال الله عزوجل وفيه أن كفران العشير والإحسان من الكبائر فإن

التوعد بالنار من علامة كون المعصية كبيرة كما سنوضحه قريبا إن شاء الله
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ح ب ب (ḥ-b-b)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning is "to love," denoting an inclination of the heart toward something; its opposite is bughḍ (hatred).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological usage, ḥubb of the Anṣār signifies love for the upholders of the Dīn, which is a branch of faith (īmān) and a mark of sincere belief in Allah and the Last Day.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Used here in its literal (ḥaqīqah) sense as an inward disposition, not metaphorically; the Prophet's statement makes it a definitive sign (āyah) of faith.
- Sībawayh Rule: Naṣb of "akthara" (more numerous) — either as the second object of the transitive verb "ra'aytu" (I saw), or as a ḥāl (circumstantial accusative) per Ibn al-Sarrāj and Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī, who hold that afʿal (elative) does not become definite by annexation (iḍāfah).
chapters.translation:
I say: The Prophet ﷺ said: "The sign of the hypocrite is hatred of the Anṣār, and the sign of the believer is love of the Anṣār." In another narration: "Love of the Anṣār is a sign of faith, and hatred of them is a sign of hypocrisy." In yet another: "None loves them but a believer, and none hates them but a hypocrite. Whoever loves them, Allah loves him; and whoever hates them, Allah hates him." And in another: "No man who believes in Allah and the Last Day hates the Anṣār." And in the ḥadīth of ʿAlī (may Allah be pleased with him): "By Him who splits the seed and creates the soul, the Prophet ﷺ made a covenant with me that none loves me but a believer, and none hates me but a hypocrite."

We have already stated that "āyah" means "sign." The meaning of these ḥadīths is that whoever knows the rank of the Anṣār and what they did in supporting the religion of Islam, striving to make it manifest, giving refuge to the Muslims, standing fully in the important matters of the religion of Islam, their love for the Prophet ﷺ and his love for them, their expenditure of their wealth and their lives before him, their fighting and their enmity toward all other people in preference for Islam; and whoever knows concerning ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib (may Allah be pleased with him) his closeness to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, the Prophet's love for him, and what he did in supporting Islam and his precedence in it — then if such a person loves the Anṣār and ʿAlī for this reason, that becomes among the proofs of the soundness of his faith and his truthfulness in his Islam, because of his joy at the emergence of Islam and the upholding of what pleases Allah (glorified and exalted be He) and His Messenger ﷺ. And whoever hates them is the opposite of that, and it is used as evidence of his hypocrisy and the corruption of his inner state. And Allah knows best.

As for his saying "Who splits the seed" (falaqa al-ḥabbah), its meaning is "He splits it by causing the plant to emerge from it." And his saying "and creates the soul" (bara'a al-nasamah) — with a hamzah — means "He created the soul." Al-nasamah is with fatḥah on the nūn and the sīn, and it means "the human being"; it is also said "the soul" (nafs). Al-Azharī related that al-nasamah is the soul, and that every creature that has a spirit within it is a nasamah. And Allah knows best.

As for what pertains to the chains of transmission (asānīd) of this chapter: In it there is ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAbdullāh ibn Jabr — ʿAbdullāh is with tafkhīm (full pronunciation) in his name and his father's name, and Jabr is with fatḥah on the jīm and sukūn on the bā'; it is also said "Jābir." In it there is al-Barā' ibn ʿĀzib, who is well-known with the short vowel (al-mad) — this is the well-known form among the scholars of ḥadīth, the people of language, the narrators, and all the specialists. Shaykh Abū ʿAmr ibn al-Ṣalāḥ (may Allah have mercy on him) said: "I have recorded from some of the people of language both the short and the long form." In it there is Yaʿqūb ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Qārī — with tashdīd on the yā', attributed to al-Qārah, a well-known tribe. In it there is Zirr — with kasrah on the zāy and tashdīd on the rā' — and he is Zirr ibn Ḥubaysh, one of the long-lived; he lived through the Jāhiliyyah and died in the year eighty-two, being one hundred and twenty years old; it is also said one hundred and twenty-two, and it is said one hundred and twenty-seven. He was Asadī, Kūfī.

As for the statement of Muslim (may Allah have mercy on him): "Muḥammad ibn al-Muthannā narrated to us, ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Mahdī narrated to us, from Shuʿbah, from ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAbdullāh ibn Jabr, who said: I heard Anas saying..." Then Muslim said: "Yaḥyā ibn Ḥabīb al-Ḥārithī narrated to us, Khālid — meaning ibn al-Ḥārith — narrated to us, from Shuʿbah, from ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAbdullāh, from Anas." These two chains — all their narrators are Baṣran except Ibn Jabr, for he is Anṣārī, Madanī. We have already mentioned that Shuʿbah, although he was Wāsiṭī, settled in Baṣrah. And Allah knows best.

Chapter: The Explanation of the Diminution of Faith by the Diminution of Acts of Obedience, and the Explanation of the Application of the Term "Disbelief" (kufr) to Other than Disbelief in Allah, such as Ingratitude for Kindness and Rights.

The Prophet ﷺ said: "O assembly of women! Give in charity and increase in seeking forgiveness, for I have seen that you are the majority of the inhabitants of the Fire." A woman among them, who was judicious, said: "And why is it, O Messenger of Allah, that we are the majority of the inhabitants of the Fire?" He said: "You curse frequently and are ungrateful to your husbands (takfurna al-ʿashīr). I have not seen anyone deficient in intellect and religion who overcomes a man of sound mind more than you." She said: "O Messenger of Allah, what is the deficiency of intellect and religion?" He said: "As for the deficiency of intellect, it is that the testimony of two women equals the testimony of one man — this is the deficiency of intellect. And she remains for nights without praying and breaks her fast in Ramaḍān — this is the deficiency of religion."

The people of language say: "al-maʿshar" (assembly) is a group whose affair is one, i.e., they share in common; it is a name that encompasses them, like "humankind" is a maʿshar, "jinn" is a maʿshar, "prophets" are a maʿshar, "women" are a maʿshar, and so on. Its plural is maʿāshir.

His saying ﷺ "I have seen that you are the majority of the inhabitants of the Fire" — "akthar" (majority) is in the accusative (naṣb), either because this "seeing" (ru'yā) is transitive to two objects, or as a circumstantial accusative (ḥāl) according to the school of Ibn al-Sarrāj and Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī and others who hold that afʿal (the elative) does not become definite by annexation. It is also said it is a substitute (badal) for the kāf in "ra'aytukunna" (I have seen you).

As for her saying "And why is it that we are the majority of the inhabitants of the Fire" — it is in the accusative either as a quotation (ḥikāyah) or as a ḥāl.

His saying "judicious" (jazlah) — with fatḥah on the jīm and sukūn on the zāy — means "possessing intellect and sound opinion." Ibn Durayd said: "al-jazālah is intellect and dignity."

As for "al-ʿashīr" — with fatḥah on the ʿayn and kasrah on the shīn — it is originally "the companion" (al-muʿāshir) in an absolute sense, and the intended meaning here is "the husband."

As for "al-lubb" — it is the intellect, and the intended meaning is the perfection of the intellect.

His saying ﷺ "This is the deficiency of intellect" — i.e., it is a sign of its deficiency.

His saying ﷺ "And she remains for nights without praying" — i.e., she remains for nights and days without praying due to menstruation, and she breaks her fast for days of Ramaḍān due to menstruation. And Allah knows best.

As for the rulings (aḥkām) of this ḥadīth, it contains several branches of knowledge. Among them: the encouragement to give charity, to perform acts of righteousness, to increase in seeking forgiveness, and all other acts of obedience. And in it: that good deeds erase bad deeds, as Allah (glorified and exalted be He) said. And in it: that ingratitude to one's husband (kufrān al-ʿashīr) and ingratitude for kindness are among the major sins (kabā'ir), for the threat of the Fire is a sign that a disobedience is major, as we will clarify shortly, if Allah wills.

chapters.title_en: Section 114 — On Cursing, Disbelief, and the Nature of Reason and Faith
chapters.arabic_text:
تعالى وفيه أن اللعن أيضا من المعاصي
# 
# الشديدة القبح وليس فيه أنه كبيرة فإنه صلى الله عليه وسلم قال تكثرن

اللعن والصغيرة إذا أكثرت صارت كبيرة وقد قال صلى الله عليه وسلم لعن

المؤمن كقتله واتفق العلماء على تحريم اللعن فإنه في اللغة الإبعاد والطرد

وفي الشرع الإبعاد من رحمة الله تعالى فلا يجوز أن يبعد من رحمة الله تعالى

من لا يعرف حاله وخاتمةأمره معرفة قطعية فلهذا قالوا لا يجوز لعن أحد بعينه

مسلما كان أوكافرا أو دابة إلا من علمنا بنص شرعي أنه مات على الكفر أو

يموت عليه كأبي جهل وإبليس وأما اللعن بالوصف فليس بحرام كلعن الواصلة

والمستوصلة والواشمة والمستوشمة وآكل الربا وموكله والمصورين والظالمين

والفاسقين والكافرين ولعن من غير منار الأرض ومن تولى غير مواليه ومن انتسب

إلى غير أبيه ومن أحدث في الإسلام حدثا أو آوى محدثا وغير ذلك مما جاءت به

النصوص الشرعية باطلاقه على الأوصاف لاعلى الأعيان والله أعلم وفيه إطلاق

الكفر على غير الكفر بالله تعالى ككفر العشير والإحسان والنعمة والحق ويؤخذ

من ذلك صحة تأويل الكفر في الأحاديث المتقدمة على ما تأولناها وفيه بيان

زيادة الإيمان ونقصانه وفيه وعظ الإمام وأصحاب الولايات وكبراء الناس

رعاياهم وتحذيرهم المخالفات وتحريضهم على الطاعات وفيه مراجعة المتعلم

العالم والتابع المتبوع فيما قاله إذا لم يظهر له معناه كمراجعة هذه الجزلة

رضي الله عنها وفيه جواز إطلاق رمضان من غير إضافة إلى الشهر وإن كان

الاختيار إضافته والله أعلم قال الإمام أبو عبد الله المازري رحمه الله

قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم أما نقصان العقل فشهادة امرأتين تعدل شهادة رجل

تنبيه منه صلى الله عليه وسلم على ما وراءه وهو ما نبه الله تعالى عليه في

كتابه بقوله تعالى أن تضل إحداهما فتذكر إحداهما الأخرى أي أنهن قليلات

الضبط قال وقد
# 
# اختلف الناس في العقل ما هو فقيل هو العلم وقيل بعض العلوم الضرورية وقيل

قوة يميز بها بين حقائق المعلومات هذا كلامه قلت والاختلاف في حقيقة العقل

وأقسامه كثير معروف لا حاجة هنا إلى الإطالة به واختلفوا في محله فقال

أصحابنا المتكلمون هو في القلب وقال بعض العلماء هو في الرأس والله أعلم

وأما وصفه صلى الله عليه وسلم النساء بنقصان الدين لتركهن الصلاة والصوم في

زمن الحيض فقد يستشكل معناه وليس بمشكل بل هو ظاهر فإن الدين والإيمان

والإسلام مشتركة في معنى واحد كما قدمناه في مواضع وقد قدمنا أيضا في مواضع

أن الطاعات تسمى إيمانا ودينا وإذا ثبت هذا علمنا أن من كثرت عبادته زاد

إيمانه ودينه ومن نقصت عبادته نقص دينه ثم نقص الدين قد يكون على وجه يأثم

به كمن ترك الصلاة أو الصوم أو غيرهما من العبادات الواجبة عليه بلا عذر

وقد يكون على وجه لا إثم فيه كمن ترك الجمعة أو الغزو أو غير ذلك مما لا

يجب عليه لعذر وقد يكون على وجه هو مكلف به كترك الحائض الصلاة والصوم فإن

قيل فإن كانت معذورة فهل تثاب على الصلاة في زمن الحيض وإن كانت لا تقضيها

كما يثاب المريض والمسافر ويكتب له في مرضه وسفره مثل نوافل الصلوات التي

كان يفعلها في صحته وحضره فالجواب أن ظاهر هذا الحديث أنها لا  تثاب والفرق

أن المريض والمسافر كان يفعلها بنية الدوام عليها مع أهليته لها والحائض

ليست كذلك بل نيتها ترك الصلاة في زمن الحيض بل يحرم عليها نية الصلاة في

زمن الحيض فنظيرها مسافر أو مريض كان يصلي النافلة في وقت ويترك في وقت غير

ناو الدوام عليها فهذا لا يكتب له في سفره ومرضه في الزمن الذى لم يكن

يتنفل فيه والله أعلم وأما ما يتعلق بأسانيد الباب ففيه بن الهاد واسمه

يزيد بن عبد الله بن أسامة وأسامة هو الهاد لأنه كان يوقد نارا ليهتدي

إليها الأضياف ومن سلك الطريق وهكذا يقوله المحدثون الهاد وهو صحيح على لغة

والمختار في العربية الهادي بالياء وقد قدمنا ذكر هذا في مقدمة الكتاب

وغيرها والله أعلم وفيه أبو بكر بن إسحاق واسمه
# 
# محمد وفيه بن أبي مريم وهو سعيد بن الحكم بن محمد بن أبي مريم الجمحي أبو

محمد المصري الفقيه الجليل وفيه عمرو بن أبي عمرو عن المقبري وقد اختلف في

المراد بالمقبري هنا هل هو أبو سعيد المقبري أو ابنه سعيد فإن كل واحد

منهما يقال له المقبري وإن كان المقبري في الأصل هو أبو سعيد فقال الحافظ

أبو علي الغساني الجياني عن أبي مسعود الدمشقي هو أبو سعيد قال أبو علي

وهذا إنما هو في رواية إسماعيل بن جعفر عن عمرو بن أبي عمرو وقال الدارقطني

خالفه سليمان بن بلال فرواه عن عمرو عن سعيد المقبري قال الدارقطني وقول

سليمان بن بلال أصح قال الشيخ أبو عمرو بن الصلاح رحمه الله رواه أبو نعيم

الأصفهاني في كتابه المخرج على صحيح مسلم من وجوه مرضية عن إسماعيل بن جعفر

عن عمرو بن أبي عمرو عن سعيد بن أبي سعيد المقبري هكذا مبينا لكن رويناه في

مسند أبي عوانة المخرج على صحيح مسلم من طريق إسماعيل بن جعفر عن أبي سعيد
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ل-ع-ن (la-ʿa-na)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning is "to drive away, banish, or distance" (al-ibʿād wa al-ṭard).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In sacred law (Sharʿ), it denotes expulsion from Allah's mercy (al-ibʿād min raḥmat Allāh), a theological severance from divine grace.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage is spatial distancing; metaphorical (majāz) usage applies to spiritual exclusion, as in cursing specific persons.
- Root: ك-ف-ر (ka-fa-ra)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Root meaning is "to cover" (satara), hence "to conceal" truth or gratitude.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Technical sense is denial of Allah's unity or grace; but it admits degrees—major (akbar) and minor (aṣghar) disbelief, as in ingratitude (kufr al-ʿashīr).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Metaphorical extension from literal "covering" to "rejecting" divine favors; not every kufr entails apostasy.
- Root: ع-ق-ل (ʿa-qa-la)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Root meaning is "to bind, restrain" (al-ʿiqāl is the camel's hobble); intellect restrains from error.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Disputed essence—some say it is knowledge (ʿilm), others a faculty (quwwah) for discerning truths; locus is debated: heart (qalb) per Ashʿarī theologians, or head per others.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal is physical binding; metaphorical is the cognitive faculty that "binds" the soul to right action.
- Sībawayh Rule: ʿAṭf al-Bayān (Appositional Clarification) — When terms like "dīn," "īmān," and "islām" are conjoined, they function as explicative appositives sharing a single referent, as Nawawī notes they are "shared in one meaning" (mushtarakah fī maʿnan wāḥid).
chapters.translation:
I say: Allah Most High said, and in this [hadith] there is [the point] that cursing (al-laʿn) is also among sins of severe ugliness, but it does not state that it is a major sin (kabīrah). For he, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Do not curse excessively" — and a minor sin, when multiplied, becomes a major sin. And he, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Cursing a believer is like killing him." The scholars are unanimous on the prohibition of cursing, for in language it means "driving away and banishing" (al-ibʿād wa al-ṭard), and in sacred law it means "expulsion from Allah's mercy." Thus it is not permissible to expel from Allah's mercy one whose state and final end are not known to us with certain knowledge. For this reason, they said: It is not permissible to curse any specific individual (bi-ʿaynihi) — whether Muslim, disbeliever, or beast — except one whom we know by a textual proof (naṣṣ sharʿī) died upon disbelief or will die upon it, such as Abū Jahl and Iblīs. As for cursing by description (bi-al-waṣf), it is not forbidden, such as cursing the woman who joins hair [to another's] and the one who asks for it, the tattooer and the one tattooed, the consumer of usury (ribā) and its payer, the makers of images, the wrongdoers (al-ẓālimīn), the transgressors (al-fāsiqīn), the disbelievers (al-kāfirīn), and cursing one who alters the landmarks of the land, one who takes as patron other than his master, one who claims lineage to other than his father, one who introduces an innovation (ḥadath) in Islam or shelters an innovator, and other such matters that the legal texts (nuṣūṣ) have mentioned absolutely (bi-iṭlāqihi) upon descriptions, not upon specific individuals. And Allah knows best.

And in this [hadith] there is the application of "disbelief" (kufr) to other than disbelief in Allah Most High, such as "disbelief of a spouse" (kufr al-ʿashīr), and [disbelief of] beneficence, grace, and right. From this is derived the validity of interpreting "disbelief" in the preceding hadiths according to what we have interpreted. And in it there is an explanation of the increase and decrease of faith (īmān). And in it there is [the point] of the imam, those in authority, and community leaders admonishing their subjects, warning them against violations, and urging them toward acts of obedience. And in it there is [the point] of the student reviewing the teacher, and the follower reviewing the followed, regarding what he said when its meaning is not apparent to him — as in the review of this noble woman, may Allah be pleased with her. And in it there is the permissibility of saying "Ramaḍān" without adding "the month" (al-shahr), although the preferred choice is to add it. And Allah knows best.

Imam Abū ʿAbd Allāh al-Māzarī, may Allah have mercy on him, said: His statement, peace and blessings be upon him, "As for the deficiency of intellect, it is that the testimony of two women equals the testimony of one man" — this is a notification from him, peace and blessings be upon him, of what lies beyond it, namely what Allah Most High has alerted to in His Book, His saying: {«أَنْ تَضِلَّ إِحْدَاهُمَا فَتُذَكِّرَ إِحْدَاهُمَا الْأُخْرَى»} ("so that if one of them errs, the other will remind her") — meaning that they are deficient in retention (ḍabṭ). He said: And the people have differed over what the intellect (al-ʿaql) is. It was said: It is knowledge (ʿilm). It was said: It is some necessary sciences (ʿulūm ḍarūriyyah). It was said: It is a faculty (quwwah) by which one distinguishes between the realities of known things. This is his statement.

I say: The disagreement over the reality of the intellect and its divisions is extensive and well-known; there is no need to elaborate here. And they differed over its locus (maḥall). Our Ashʿarī theologians (aṣḥābunā al-mutakallimūn) said: It is in the heart (qalb). And some scholars said: It is in the head. And Allah knows best.

As for his description, peace and blessings be upon him, of women as deficient in religion (nuqṣān al-dīn) due to their abandoning prayer and fasting during menstruation (ḥayḍ) — this might be seen as problematic, but it is not problematic; rather, it is evident. For religion (dīn), faith (īmān), and submission (islām) share a single meaning, as we have established in multiple places. And we have also established in multiple places that acts of obedience are called "faith" and "religion." When this is established, we know that one whose worship is abundant has increased in faith and religion, and one whose worship is deficient has decreased in religion. Then the decrease in religion may be in a manner that incurs sin, such as one who abandons prayer, fasting, or other obligatory acts of worship without excuse. And it may be in a manner with no sin, such as one who abandons Friday prayer, or military expedition (ghazw), or other things not obligatory upon him due to an excuse. And it may be in a manner for which one is obligated, such as the menstruating woman abandoning prayer and fasting.

If it is said: Since she is excused, is she rewarded (tuthāb) for [not] praying during menstruation, even though she does not make it up — just as the sick and the traveler are rewarded, and it is written for them during their illness and travel the equivalent of the supererogatory prayers (nawāfil) they used to perform in health and residence? The answer is that the apparent meaning of this hadith is that she is not rewarded. And the difference is that the sick and the traveler used to perform them with the intention of continuity (niyyat al-dawām) along with their eligibility for them, whereas the menstruating woman is not like that. Rather, her intention is to abandon prayer during menstruation; indeed, it is forbidden for her to intend prayer during menstruation. Her analogue is a traveler or sick person who used to pray supererogatory prayers at one time and abandon them at another, not intending continuity — such a one is not credited during his travel and illness for the time in which he was not performing voluntary prayers. And Allah knows best.

As for what pertains to the chains of transmission (asānīd) of this chapter: In it is Ibn al-Hād, whose name is Yazīd ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Usāmah. And Usāmah is "al-Hād" because he used to light a fire for guests and wayfarers to be guided by it. Thus the hadith scholars say "al-Hād," and it is correct according to one dialect; but the preferred form in Arabic is "al-Hādī" with the yāʾ. We have already mentioned this in the introduction to the book and elsewhere. And Allah knows best.

And in it is Abū Bakr ibn Isḥāq, whose name is Muḥammad. And in it is Ibn Abī Maryam, who is Saʿīd ibn al-Ḥakam ibn Muḥammad ibn Abī Maryam al-Jumaḥī, Abū Muḥammad al-Miṣrī, the noble jurist. And in it is ʿAmr ibn Abī ʿAmr, from al-Muqbirī. And there is disagreement over who is meant by "al-Muqbirī" here — whether it is Abū Saʿīd al-Muqbirī or his son Saʿīd, for each of them is called "al-Muqbirī," although al-Muqbirī originally is Abū Saʿīd. Al-Ḥāfiẓ Abū ʿAlī al-Ghassānī al-Jayyānī said, from Abū Masʿūd al-Dimashqī: It is Abū Saʿīd. Abū ʿAlī said: This is only in the narration of Ismāʿīl ibn Jaʿfar from ʿAmr ibn Abī ʿAmr. And al-Dāraquṭnī said: Sulaymān ibn Bilāl contradicted him, narrating it from ʿAmr from Saʿīd al-Muqbirī. Al-Dāraquṭnī said: The statement of Sulaymān ibn Bilāl is more correct (aṣaḥḥ). Shaykh Abū ʿAmr ibn al-Ṣalāḥ, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Abū Nuʿaym al-Iṣfahānī narrated it in his book compiled upon Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim from praiseworthy chains (wujūh marḍiyyah) from Ismāʿīl ibn Jaʿfar, from ʿAmr ibn Abī ʿAmr, from Saʿīd ibn Abī Saʿīd al-Muqbirī — thus explicitly clarified. But we have narrated it in the Musnad of Abū ʿAwānah, compiled upon Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim, via the path of Ismāʿīl ibn Jaʿfar from Abū Saʿīd.

chapters.title_en: Section 115 — The Chapter on Clarifying the Application of the Term "Disbelief" (Kufr) to One Who Abandons the Prayer
chapters.arabic_text:
ومن طريق سليمان بن بلال عن سعيد كما سبق عن الدارقطني فالاعتماد عليه إذا

هذا كلام الشيخ ويقال المقبري بضم  الباء وفتحها وجهان مشهوران فيه وهي نسبة

إلى المقبرة وفيها ثلاث لغات ضم الباء وفتحها وكسرها والثالثة غريبة قال

إبراهيم الحربي وغيره كان أبو سعيد ينزل المقابر فقيل له المقبري وقيل كان

منزله عند المقابر وقيل إن عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه جعله على حفر القبور

فقيل له المقبري وجعل نعيما على إجمار المسجد فقيل له نعيم المجمر واسم أبي

سعيد كيسان الليثي المدني والله أعلم

| (باب بيان إطلاق اسم الكفر على من ترك الصلاة
# [81] في
# الباب حديثان أحدهما (إذا قرأ بن آدم السجدة فسجد اعتزل الشيطان يبكي

يقول ياويله)
# 
# وفى رواية يا ويلى أمر بن آدم بالسجود فسجد فله الجنة وأمرت بالسجود

فأبيت فلي النار)
# [82] والحديث الثاني (إن بين الرجل وبين الشرك والكفر ترك الصلاة) مقصود

مسلم رحمه الله بذكر هذين الحديثين هنا أن من الأفعال ما تركه يوجب الكفر

إما حقيقة وإما تسمية فأما كفر إبليس بسبب السجود فمأخوذ من قول الله تعالى

وإذ قلنا للملائكة اسجدوا لآدم فسجدوا إلا ابليس أبى واستكبر وكان من

الكافرين قال الجمهور معناه وكان في علم الله تعالى من الكافرين وقال بعضهم

وصار من الكافرين كقوله تعالى وحال بينهما الموج فكان من المغرقين وأما

تارك الصلاة فإن كان منكرا لوجوبها فهو كافر بإجماع المسلمين خارج من ملة

الإسلام إلا أن يكون قريب عهد بالإسلام ولم يخالط المسلمين مدة يبلغه فيها

وجوب الصلاة عليه وإن كان تركه تكاسلا مع اعتقاده وجوبها كما هو حال كثير

من الناس فقد اختلف العلماء فيه فذهب مالك والشافعي رحمهما الله والجماهير

من السلف والخلف إلى أنه لا يكفر بل يفسق ويستتاب فإن تاب وإلا قتلناه حدا

كالزاني المحصن ولكنه يقتل بالسيف وذهب جماعة من السلف إلى أنه يكفر وهو

مروي عن علي بن أبي طالب كرم الله وجهه وهو إحدى الروايتين عن أحمد بن حنبل

رحمه الله وبه قال عبد الله بن المبارك وإسحاق بن راهويه وهو وجه لبعض

أصحاب الشافعي رضوان الله عليه وذهب أبو  حنيفة وجماعة من أهل الكوفة

والمزني صاحب الشافعي رحمهما الله أنه لا يكفر ولا يقتل بل يعزر ويحبس حتى

يصلي واحتج من قال بكفره بظاهر الحديث الثاني المذكور وبالقياس على كلمة

التوحيد
# 
# واحتج من قال لا يقتل بحديث لا يحل دم امرئ مسلم إلا بإحدى ثلاث وليس فيه

الصلاة واحتج الجمهور على أنه لا يكفر بقوله تعالى إن الله لا يغفر أن يشرك

به ويغفر ما دون ذلك لمن يشاء وبقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم من قال لا إله الا

الله دخل الجنة من مات وهو يعلم أن لا إله إلا الله دخل الجنة ولا يلقى

الله تعالى عبد بهما غير شاك فيحجب عن الجنة حرم الله على النار من قال لا

إله إلا الله وغير ذلك واحتجوا على قتله بقوله تعالى فإن تابوا وأقام

الصلاة وآتوا الزكاة فخلوا سبيلهم وقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم أمرت أن أقاتل

الناس حتى يقولوا لا إله إلا الله ويقيموا الصلاة ويؤتوا الزكاة فإذا فعلوا

ذلك عصموا مني دماءهم وأموالهم وتأولوا قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم بين العبد

وبين الكفر ترك الصلاة على معنى أنه يستحق بترك الصلاة عقوبة الكافر وهي

القتل أو أنه محمول على المستحل أو على أنه قد يؤول به إلى الكفر أو أن

فعله فعل الكفار والله أعلم وأما قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم اذا قرأ بن آدم

السجدة فمعناه آية السجدة وقوله ياويله هو من آداب الكلام وهو أنه إذا عرض

في الحكاية عن الغير ما فيه سوء واقتضت الحكاية رجوع الضمير إلى المتكلم

صرف الحاكي الضمير عن نفسه تصاونا عن صورة إضافة السوء إلى نفسه وقوله في

الرواية الأخرى يا ويلي يجوز فيه فتح اللام وكسرها وقوله صلى الله عليه

وسلم بين الرجل وبين الشرك والكفر ترك الصلاة هكذا هو في جميع الأصول من

صحيح مسلم الشرك والكفر بالواو وفي مخرج أبي عوانة الاسفراينى وأبى نعيم

الاصبهانى أوالكفر بأو ولكل واحد منهما وجه ومعنى بينه وبين الشرك ترك

الصلاة أن الذي يمنع من كفره كونه لم يترك الصلاة فإذا تركها لم يبق بينه

وبين الشرك حائل بل دخل فيه ثم إن الشرك والكفر قد يطلقان بمعنى واحد وهو

الكفر بالله تعالى وقد يفرق بينهما فيخص الشرك بعبدة الأوثان وغيرها من

المخلوقات مع اعترافهم بالله تعالى ككفار قريش فيكون الكفر أعم من الشرك

والله أعلم وقد احتج أصحاب أبي حنيفة رحمه الله واياهم بقوله أمر بن آدم

بالسجود على أن
# 
# سجود التلاوة واجب ومذهب مالك والشافعي والكبيرين أنه سنة وأجابوا عن هذا

بأجوبة أحدها أن تسمية هذا أمرا إنما هو من كلام إبليس فلا حجة فيها فإن

قالوا حكاها النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ولم ينكرها قلنا قد حكي غيرها من

أقوال الكفار ولم يبطلها حال الحكاية وهي باطلة الوجه الثاني أن المراد أمر

ندب لا إيجاب الثالث المراد المشاركة في السجود لا في الوجوب والله أعلم

وأما ما يتعلق باسانيده ففيه أبو غسان وقد تقدم أنه يصرف ولا يصرف واسمه
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Covering, veiling, concealing; ingratitude; the act of covering a seed with earth (kāfir = one who covers/denies)
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Theological term for rejection of divine truth (takdhīb) or denial of the Creator; ranges from major disbelief (kufr akbar) to minor (kufr aṣghar)
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense = covering; metaphorical (majāz) sense = denial of divine beneficence or rejection of faith
- Root: ش-ر-ك (sh-r-k)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Partnership, association; sharing in something
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Theological term for associating partners with Allah (shirk) — the gravest form of disbelief
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal = partnership; metaphorical = ascribing divinity to other than Allah
- Root: ت-ر-ك (t-r-k)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Abandoning, leaving, forsaking
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Deliberate cessation of an obligatory act; distinguishes between abandonment due to denial (istihlāl) vs. negligence (takāsul)
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal = leaving; metaphorical = the act that severs one's protective link from faith
- Sībawayh Rule: Rule of 'Aṭf (Coordination) — The conjunction "wa" (و) vs. "aw" (أو) in "al-shirk wa al-kufr" vs. "al-shirk aw al-kufr" affects whether the terms are treated as synonymous or distinct categories; the grammatical coordination determines juristic implications.
chapters.translation:
I say: And from the transmission route of Sulaymān ibn Bilāl, from Saʿīd, as has preceded from al-Dāraquṭnī — so reliance is upon it when [needed].

This is the speech of the Shaykh. And it is said: "al-Maqburī" — with ḍammah on the bā' and with fatḥah on it — these are two well-known variant readings concerning him. It is a nisbah (attributive designation) to the cemetery (al-maqbarah). And concerning [the word "maqbarah"] there are three dialects: ḍammah of the bā', fatḥah of it, and kasrah of it — and the third is rare. Ibrāhīm al-Ḥarbī and others said: Abū Saʿīd used to dwell in the cemeteries, so he was called "al-Maqburī." And it was said: his residence was near the cemeteries. And it was said: ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, may Allah be pleased with him, appointed him over the digging of graves, so he was called "al-Maqburī," and he appointed Nuʿaym over the perfuming of the mosque, so he was called "Nuʿaym al-Mujmir." And the name of Abū Saʿīd is Kaysān al-Laythī al-Madanī. And Allah knows best.

| (Chapter: The Clarification of Applying the Term "Disbelief" to One Who Abandons the Prayer)

# [81] In this chapter there are two ḥadīths. One of them: {«When the son of Adam recites the verse of prostration and then prostrates, the devil withdraws weeping, saying: "Woe to him!"»}
# And in another narration: {«"Woe to me! The son of Adam was commanded to prostrate, so he prostrated — and for him is Paradise. And I was commanded to prostrate, but I refused — so for me is the Fire."»}

# [82] And the second ḥadīth: {«"Between a man and between shirk (polytheism) and kufr (disbelief) is the abandonment of the prayer."»}

The intent of Muslim, may Allah have mercy on him, in mentioning these two ḥadīths here is that among actions, there are those whose abandonment necessitates disbelief (kufr) — either in reality (ḥaqīqah) or by designation (tasmiyah). As for the disbelief of Iblīs due to [refusing] prostration, it is derived from the saying of Allah the Exalted: {«And when We said to the angels: "Prostrate to Adam," so they prostrated, except Iblīs — he refused and was arrogant and was among the disbelievers»} (2:34). The majority (al-jumhūr) said: Its meaning is "he was, in the knowledge of Allah the Exalted, among the disbelievers." And some said: "he became among the disbelievers," like His saying the Exalted: {«And between them was placed a barrier (mawj), so he was among the drowned»} (11:43).

As for the one who abandons the prayer — if he denies its obligation (wujūb), then he is a disbeliever by the consensus (ijmāʿ) of the Muslims, exiting from the religion of Islam — unless he is one recently converted to Islam who has not mixed with the Muslims for a period sufficient for the obligation of prayer to have reached him. And if his abandonment is out of laziness (takāsul) while he believes in its obligation — as is the state of many people — then the scholars have differed concerning him. Mālik and al-Shāfiʿī, may Allah have mercy on them both, and the masses (jamāhīr) of the Salaf and Khalaf held that he does not become a disbeliever, but rather he becomes a sinner (fāsiq) and is called to repent (yusta'tāb). If he repents, [it is accepted]; otherwise, we kill him as a prescribed punishment (ḥadd) — like the married fornicator (al-zānī al-muḥṣan) — but he is killed by the sword. And a group of the Salaf held that he does become a disbeliever — and this is narrated from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah honor his face — and it is one of the two narrations from Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal, may Allah have mercy on him. And ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Mubārak and Isḥāq ibn Rāhawayh held this view, and it is a wajh (position) of some companions of al-Shāfiʿī, may Allah be pleased with him. And Abū Ḥanīfah and a group of the people of Kūfah, and al-Muzanī, the companion of al-Shāfiʿī, may Allah have mercy on them both, held that he does not become a disbeliever and is not killed, but rather is given a discretionary punishment (taʿzīr) and imprisoned until he prays.

And those who said he becomes a disbeliever argued with the apparent meaning (ẓāhir) of the second ḥadīth mentioned, and by analogy (qiyās) upon the word of tawḥīd [i.e., that just as uttering it protects one's life, abandoning prayer nullifies that protection].

And those who said he is not killed argued with the ḥadīth: {«"The blood of a Muslim man is not lawful except by one of three [reasons]"»} — and prayer is not among them. And the majority (al-jumhūr) argued that he does not become a disbeliever by His saying the Exalted: {«Indeed, Allah does not forgive that partners be associated with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills»} (4:48), and by his saying, peace and blessings be upon him: {«"Whoever says: 'There is no god but Allah' enters Paradise"»} and {«"Whoever dies while knowing that there is no god but Allah enters Paradise"»} and {«"No servant meets Allah with these two [words], not doubting [in them], but that he is veiled from the Fire"»} and {«"Allah has made forbidden to the Fire whoever says: 'There is no god but Allah'"»} — and other [proofs].

And they argued for his execution by His saying the Exalted: {«"But if they repent, establish the prayer, and give the zakāh, then let them go their way"»} (9:5), and his saying, peace and blessings be upon him: {«"I have been commanded to fight the people until they say: 'There is no god but Allah,' establish the prayer, and give the zakāh. If they do that, they have protected from me their blood and their wealth"»}. And they interpreted (ta'awwalū) his saying, peace and blessings be upon him: {«"Between the servant and between disbelief is the abandonment of the prayer"»} upon the meaning that he deserves, by abandoning the prayer, the punishment of the disbeliever — which is execution — or that it is carried upon the one who deems it lawful (mustaḥill), or that it may ultimately lead him to disbelief, or that his action is the action of the disbelievers. And Allah knows best.

As for his saying, peace and blessings be upon him: {«"When the son of Adam reads the prostration"»} — its meaning is "the verse of prostration."
