في ذلك وإن كان غير معتقد ذلك بقلبه فهو كاذب في الصورة لكونه عظمه بالحلف

به  وإذا علم أنه لا ينفك عن كونه كاذبا حمل التقييد بكاذبا على أنه بيان

لصورة الحالف ويكون التقييد خرج على سبب فلا يكون له مفهوم ويكون من باب

قول الله تعالى ويقتلون الانبياء بغير حق وقوله تعالى ولا تقتلوا أولادكم

من إملاق وقوله تعالى وربائبكم اللاتى فى حجوركم وقوله تعالى فإن خفتم ألا

يقيما حدود الله فلا جناح عليهما فيما افتدت به وقوله تعالى فليس عليكم

جناح أن تقصروا من الصلاة ان خفتم وقوله تعالى ولا تكرهوا فتياتكم على

البغاء إن أردن تحصنا ونظائره كثيرة ثم إن كان الحالف به معظما لما حلف به

مجلاله كان كافرا وإن لم يكن معظما بل كان قلبه مطمئنا بالإيمان فهو كاذب

في حلفه بما لا يحلف به ومعاملته إياه معاملة ما يحلف به ولا يكون كافرا

خارجا عن ملة الإسلام ويجوز أن يطلق عليه اسم الكفر ويراد به كفر الإحسان

وكفر نعمة الله تعالى فإنها تقتضي أن لا يحلف هذا الحلف القبيح وقد قال

الإمام أبو عبد الرحمن عبد الله بن المبارك رضي الله عنه فيما ورد من مثل

هذا مما ظاهره تكفير أصحاب المعاصي إن ذلك على جهة التغليظ والزجر عنه وهذا

معنى مليح ولكن ينبغي أن يضم إليه ما ذكرناه من كونه كافر النعم وأما قوله

صلى الله عليه وسلم من ادعى دعوى كاذبة ليتكثر بها لم يزده الله إلا قلة

فقال القاضي عياض هو عام في كل دعوى يتشبع بها المرء بما لم يعط من مال

يختال في التجمل به من غيره أو نسب ينتمي إليه أو علم يتحلى به وليس هو من

حملته أو دين يظهره وليس هو من أهله فقد أعلم صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه غير
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ث د ي (th-d-y)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: The breast or teat; the protruding fleshy part of the chest. Ibn Fāris specifies it for women, while al-Jawharī extends it to men.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Denotes a physical bodily member; in prophetic speech, its application to a man is a metaphorical extension (istiʿārah) when context requires.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) for the female breast; metaphorical (majāz) when predicated of a male, as in this ḥadīth.
- Root: ر ق أ (r-q-ʾ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To cease, subside, or stop flowing — said of blood and tears.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Cessation of a physical flux; used literally for blood, with no theological extension.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Purely literal; no metaphorical usage attested.
- Root: ن ك أ (n-k-ʾ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To scrape, tear open, or puncture a wound or sore.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Physical lancing of an abscess; a concrete action with no abstract sense.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal action verb; hamzated (mahmūz) in all forms.
- Root: ك ن ن (k-n-n)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To cover, shield, or conceal something.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The quiver (kinānah) is so named because it conceals arrows; the covering is the governing semantic feature.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal derivation from the verb "to cover"; no metaphorical shift.
- Sībawayh Rule: Restrictive Qualification (al-Taqyīd bi-al-Ḥāl) — When a qualifier like "kādhiban" (lying) is inseparable from the subject's state, it functions as an explanatory clause (khārij ʿalā al-sabab) rather than a restrictive condition, thus carrying no concept of exclusivity (lā mafhūm lahu).
chapters.translation:
He mentions it according to the eloquent language (al-lughah al-faṣīḥah) upon which al-Farrāʾ, Thaʿlab, and others restricted themselves; and Ibn Fāris, al-Jawharī, and others narrated regarding it both the masculine and the feminine [usage]. Ibn Fāris said: "The breast (al-thady) is for the woman," and it is said of that place on a man: "thanduwah" and "thanduʾah" — with the opening (fatḥ) of the initial letter and without hamzah, and with the ḍammah together with the hamzah. Al-Jawharī said: "The breast (al-thady) is for the woman and for the man." So according to the statement of Ibn Fāris, in this ḥadīth the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) has metaphorically applied the breast to the man. The plural of "thady" is "athdun," "thudy," and "thudy" — with the ḍammah of the thāʾ and its kasrah.

[113] His statement (peace and blessings be upon him): "A man was afflicted with a sore (qarḥah) that pained him, so he drew an arrow from his quiver (kinānah) and lanced it (fankaʾahā), but the blood did not stop (lam yarqaʾ) until he died." In the other narration: "A boil (khurāj) came out on him." "Al-qarḥah" — with the fatḥah of the qāf and the sukūn of the rāʾ — is the singular of "qurūḥ," which are pustules that appear on a person's body. "Al-kinānah" — with the kasrah of the kāf — is the quiver of arrows (jaʿbah al-nushshāb), with the fatḥah of the jīm; it is called "kinānah" because it conceals (takunnu) the arrows, i.e., shields them. The meaning of "nakaʾahā" is: he scraped it, tore it, and opened it — and it is hamzated. The meaning of "lam yarqaʾ al-dam" is: it did not cease — and it is hamzated. One says: "raqaʾa al-dam wa-al-damʿu yarqaʾu ruqūʾan" — like "rakaʿa yarkaʿu rukūʿan" — when it subsides and stops. "Al-khurāj" — with the ḍammah of the khāʾ (with its dot) and the tashdīd-less rāʾ — is the sore.

His statement (peace and blessings be upon him): "We have not forgotten, nor do we fear that he lied" is a type of emphasis and strengthening of the speech in the soul, or an informing of its verification and the negation of any defect reaching it. And God knows best.

As for the rulings of the ḥadīth and their meanings: In them is an exposition of the severity of the prohibition of killing oneself, and of the perjurious oath (al-yamīn al-fājirah) by which one seizes another's wealth, and of swearing by a religion other than Islam — such as one saying: "He is a Jew or a Christian if such-and-such occurs," or "By al-Lāt and al-ʿUzzā," and the like. In them [also] is that a vow (nadhr) is not valid regarding what one does not possess, and nothing is incumbent by such a vow. In them is the severity of the prohibition of cursing a Muslim — and there is no disagreement on this. Imām Abū Ḥāmid al-Ghazālī and others said: It is not permissible to curse any of the Muslims, nor animals, and there is no difference between the sinner and others. It is not permissible to curse specific individuals among the disbelievers, whether living or dead, except those whom we know by textual proof (naṣṣ) died as disbelievers — such as Abū Lahab, Abū Jahl, and their like. It is permissible to curse their group collectively, as when one says: "May God curse the disbelievers," and "May God curse the Jews and the Christians."

As for his statement (peace and blessings be upon him): "Cursing a believer is like killing him" — the apparent [meaning] is that the intent is that the two are equal in the fundamental prohibition, even though killing is more severe. This is what Imām Abū ʿAbd Allāh al-Māzarī chose; and another [view] was said, which is not apparent.

As for his statement (peace and blessings be upon him): "He is in the fire of Hell, remaining eternally (khālidan mukhalladan) therein forever" — several statements were made about it. The first: It is carried upon one who does that deeming it lawful (mustaḥillan) while knowing its prohibition — for such a one is a disbeliever, and this is his punishment. The second: The intent by "eternity" (al-khulūd) is the length of duration and prolonged abiding, not the reality of perpetuity — just as one says: "May God eternize (khallada) the kingdom of the Sultan." The third: This is his recompense, but He — glorified and exalted be He — has graciously informed that no one who dies a Muslim will remain eternally in the Fire.

Al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ (may God have mercy on him) said regarding his statement (peace and blessings be upon him): "Whoever kills himself with an iron instrument, his iron instrument will be in his hand, thrusting (yatawajjaʾu) with it into his belly" — in it is evidence that retaliation (al-qiṣāṣ) from the killer is by that with which he killed, whether it be pointed or otherwise, in emulation of God's punishment of the self-killer. But the inference (al-istidlāl) by this for that is weak.

As for his statement (peace and blessings be upon him): "Whoever swears an oath by a religion other than Islam, lying (kādhiban)" — it is as he said. In the other narration: "lying deliberately (kādhiban mutaʿammidan)" — in it is an exposition of the severity of the prohibition of this oath. His statement (peace and blessings be upon him) "lying" — the intent is not restriction and caution against swearing by it truthfully, because the one swearing by it cannot be free of being a liar. That is because he must necessarily be magnifying that by which he swears: if he believes in its greatness in his heart, then he is a liar in that; and if he does not believe that in his heart, then he is a liar in form, because he magnified it by swearing by it. And when it is known that he cannot be free of being a liar, the restriction by "lying" is carried upon being an exposition of the state of the swearer, and the restriction is issued upon a cause (kharaja ʿalā sabab), so it has no concept of exclusivity (lā mafhūm lahu). It falls under the category of God's statement: {«وَيَقْتُلُونَ الْأَنبِيَاءَ بِغَيْرِ حَقٍّ»} ("And they kill the prophets without right"), and His statement: {«وَلَا تَقْتُلُوا أَوْلَادَكُم مِّنْ إِمْلَاقٍ»} ("And do not kill your children out of poverty"), and His statement: {«وَرَبَائِبُكُمُ اللَّاتِي فِي حُجُورِكُمْ»} ("And your step-daughters in your care"), and His statement: {«فَإِنْ خِفْتُمْ أَلَّا يُقِيمَا حُدُودَ اللَّهِ فَلَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيْهِمَا فِيمَا افْتَدَتْ بِهِ»} ("Then if you fear that they will not maintain the limits of God, there is no blame upon them in what she ransoms herself with"), and His statement: {«فَلَيْسَ عَلَيْكُمْ جُنَاحٌ أَن تَقْصُرُوا مِنَ الصَّلَاةِ إِنْ خِفْتُمْ»} ("Then there is no blame upon you to shorten the prayer if you fear"), and His statement: {«وَلَا تُكْرِهُوا فَتَيَاتِكُمْ عَلَى الْبِغَاءِ إِنْ أَرَدْنَ تَحَصُّنًا»} ("And do not compel your slave-girls to prostitution if they desire chastity") — and their like are many.

Then, if the swearer by it magnifies that by which he swears and venerates it, he is a disbeliever. And if he does not magnify it, rather his heart is at rest with faith, then he is a liar in his oath by that which one does not swear by, and his treating it as something sworn by — and he is not a disbeliever, nor outside the religion of Islam. It is permissible to apply to him the name of "disbelief" (kufr), intending thereby the disbelief of ingratitude (kufr al-iḥsān) and the disbelief of denying God's blessing (kufr niʿmat Allāh) — for that necessitates that he not swear this ugly oath. Imām Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Mubārak (may God be pleased with him) said regarding what has been narrated of this kind — whose apparent [sense] is the takfīr of the people of sins — that it is by way of severity (taghlīẓ) and deterrence (zajr) from it. This is a fine meaning, but one should append to it what we have mentioned of his being a disbeliever of blessings (kāfir al-niʿam).

As for his statement (peace and blessings be upon him): "Whoever makes a false claim (daʿwā kādhibah) to seek increase thereby, God will not increase him except in decrease" — al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ said: It is general for every claim by which a man seeks to adorn himself (yatashabbaʿu) with what he has not been given — of wealth he flaunts to beautify himself with from others, or lineage he affiliates himself to, or knowledge he adorns himself with that he does not carry, or religion he displays that he is not of its people. He (peace and blessings be upon him) has informed that he is not...

chapters.title_en: Section 134 — On the Severity of the Prohibition of Ghulūl (Embezzlement from War-Booty) and that None Enters Paradise except the Believers
chapters.arabic_text:
مبارك له في دعواه ولا زاك ما اكتسبه بها ومثله الحديث الآخر اليمين

الفاجرة منفقة للسلعة ممحقة للكسب وأما قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم إن الرجل

ليعمل عمل أهل الجنة فيما يبدو للناس وهو من أهل النار وإن الرجل ليعمل عمل

أهل النار وهو من أهل الجنة ففيه التحذير من الاغترار بالأعمال وأنه ينبغي

للعبد أن لا يتكل عليها ولا يركن إليها مخافة من انقلاب الحال للقدر السابق

وكذا ينبغي للعاصي أن لا يقنط ولغيره
# 
# أن لا يقنطه من رحمة الله تعالى ومعنى قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم إن الرجل

ليعمل عمل أهل الجنة وإنه من أهل النار وكذا عكسه أن هذا قد يقع وأما قوله

صلى الله عليه وسلم إن رجلا ممن كان قبلكم خرجت به قرحة فلما آذته انتزع

سهما من كنانته فنكأها فلم يرقأ الدم حتى مات قال ربكم قد حرمت عليه الجنة

فقال القاضي رحمه الله فيه يحتمل أنه كان مستحلا أو يحرمها حين يدخلها

السابقون والأبرار أو يطيل حسابه أو يحبس في الأعراف هذا كلام القاضي قلت

ويحتمل أن شرع أهل ذلك العصر تكفير أصحاب الكبائر ثم إن هذا محمول على أنه

نكأها استعجالا للموت أو لغير مصلحة فإنه لو كان على طريق المداواة التي

يغلب على الظن نفعها لم يكن حراما والله أعلم

| (باب غلظ تحريم الغلول وأنه لا يدخل الجنة إلا 
# المؤمنون
# [114] فيه عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه قال (لما كان يوم خيبر أقبل نفر من

صحابة النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقالوا فلان شهيد فلان شهيد حتى مروا على

رجل فقالوا فلان شهيد فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كلا إني رأيته في

النار في بردة غلها أو عباءة ثم قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يا بن

الخطاب اذهب فناد في الناس أنه لا يدخل الجنة إلا المؤمنون قال فخرجت

فناديت)
# 
# ألا إنه لا يدخل الجنة إلا المؤمنون) وفيه حديث أبي هريرة من نحو معناه

في الإسناد أبو زميل بضم الزاي وتخفيف الميم المفتوحة وتقدم وقوله لما كان

يوم خيبر هو بالخاء المعجمة وآخره راء فهكذا وقع في مسلم وهو الصواب وذكر

القاضي عياض رحمه الله أن أكثر رواة الموطأ رووه هكذا وأنه الصواب قال

ورواه بعضهم حنين بالحاء  المهملة والنون والله أعلم وقوله صلى الله عليه

وسلم كلا زجر ورد لقولهم في هذا الرجل إنه شهيد محكوم له بالجنة أول وهلة

بل هو في النار بسبب غلوله
# [115] وقوله (ثور بن زيد الديلي) هو هنا بكسر الدال وإسكان الياء هكذا هو

في أكثر الأصول الموجودة ببلادنا وفي بعضها الدؤلي بضم الدال وبالهمزة

بعدها التي تكتب صورتها واوا وذكر القاضي عياض رحمه الله أنه ضبطه هنا عن

أبي بحر دولي بضم الدال وبواو ساكنة قال وضبطناه عن غيره بكسر الدال وإسكان

الياء قال وكذا ذكره مالك في الموطأ والبخاري في التاريخ وغيرهما قلت وقد

ذكر أبو علي الغساني أن ثورا هذا من رهط أبي الأسود فعلى هذا يكون فيه

الخلاف الذي قدمناه قريبا في أبي الأسود وقوله (عن سالم أبى الغيث مولى بن

مطيع) هذا صحيح وفيه التصريح بأن أبا الغيث هذا يسمى سالما وأما قول أبي

عمر بن عبد البر في أول كتابه التمهيد لا يوقف على اسمه صحيحا فليس بمعارض

لهذا الاثبات الصحيح واسم بن مطيع عبد الله بن مطيع بن الأسود القرشي والله

أعلم قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم إني رأيته في النار في بردة غلها أو عباءة

أما البردة بضم الباء فكساء مخطط وهي الشملة والنمرة وقال أبو عبيد هو كساء

أسود فيه صور وجمعها برد بفتح الراء وأما العباءة فمعروفة وهي ممدودة ويقال

فيها أيضا عباية بالياء قاله بن السكيت وغيره وقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم في

بردة أي من أجلها وبسببها وأما الغلول فقال أبو عبيد هو الخيانة
# 
# في الغنيمة خاصة وقال غيره هي الخيانة في كل شيء ويقال منه غل يغل بضم

الغين وقوله (رجل من بني الضبيب) هو بضم الضاد المعجمة وبعدها باء موحدة

مفتوحة ثم ياء مثناة من تحت ساكنة ثم باء موحدة قوله (يحل رحله) هو بالحاء

المهملة وهو مركب الرجل على البعير وقوله (فكان فيه حتفه) هو بفتح الحاء

المهملة وإسكان المثناة فوق أي موته وجمعه حتوف ومات حتف  أنفه أي من غير

قتل ولا ضرب قوله (فجاء رجل بشراك أو شراكين فقال يا رسول الله أصبت يوم

خيبر) كذا هو في الأصول وهو صحيح وفيه حذف المفعول أي أصبت هذا والشراك

بكسر الشين المعجمة وهو السير المعروف الذي يكون في النعل على ظهر القدم

قال القاضي عياض رحمه الله قوله النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم (إن الشملة

لتلتهب عليه نارا) وقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (شراك أو شراكان من نار) تنبيه

على المعاقبة عليهما وقد تكون المعاقبة بهما أنفسهما فيعذب بهما وهما من

نار وقد يكون ذلك على أنهما سبب لعذاب النار والله أعلم وأما قوله (ومع

النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم عبد له) فاسمه مدعم بكسر الميم وإسكان الدال وفتح

العين المهملتين كذا جاء مصرحا به في الموطأ في هذا الحديث بعينه قال

القاضي عياض رحمه الله وقيل إنه غير مدعم قال وورد في حديث مثل هذا اسمه
chapters.anchors:
- Root: غ-ل-ل (gh-l-l)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning is "to insert something into something else" and, derivatively, "to betray secretly" — specifically, the clandestine concealment of war-booty (ghanīmah) prior to its lawful distribution.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological usage, ghulūl is a species of treachery (khiyānah) that nullifies the moral integrity of the acquisition, rendering it "unblessed" (lā zāka) and "profitless" (mumḥiqah) — a sin whose gravity is underscored by its linkage to exclusion from Paradise.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): The literal sense is physical insertion (e.g., a hand slipped into a garment); the metaphorical (majāz) extension applies it to any covert act of betrayal, especially the unlawful taking of spoils — the rhetorical force being the hidden, internalized nature of the offense.
- Sībawayh Rule: Rule of Taʿlīq (Suspension of the Object) — In the phrase "أصبت يوم خيبر" (I acquired on the Day of Khaybar), the direct object is elided (ḥadhf al-mafʿūl), the omission being recoverable from context (i.e., "I acquired this [item]"). This is a standard ellipsis permissible when the referent is pragmatically evident.
chapters.translation:
I say: And the like of this is the other hadith: "The false oath is a means of exhausting the merchandise and erasing the blessing from the gain." As for his saying, may God's peace and blessings be upon him: "Verily, a man performs the deeds of the people of Paradise, as it appears to people, while he is of the people of the Fire; and verily, a man performs the deeds of the people of the Fire, while he is of the people of Paradise" — in this is a warning against being deluded by deeds, and that it behooves the servant not to rely upon them nor to lean toward them, out of fear of the reversal of one's state due to the prior decree (al-qadar al-sābiq). Likewise, it behooves the disobedient one not to despair, and it behooves others not to cause him to despair of the mercy of God, the Exalted. The meaning of his saying, may God's peace and blessings be upon him: "Verily, a man performs the deeds of the people of Paradise, while he is of the people of the Fire," and likewise its converse, is that this may indeed occur. As for his saying, may God's peace and blessings be upon him: "Verily, a man among those before you was afflicted with a sore; when it pained him, he drew an arrow from his quiver and lanced it, but the blood did not stop until he died. Your Lord said: 'I have forbidden Paradise to him'" — al-Qāḍī, may God have mercy on him, said concerning this: It is possible that he deemed it lawful (mustaḥill), or that Paradise is forbidden to him at the time when the forerunners and the righteous enter it, or that his reckoning is prolonged, or that he is detained in al-Aʿrāf. This is the speech of al-Qāḍī. I say: It is also possible that the law (sharʿ) of the people of that era deemed the expiation of major sins to be [required] for its perpetrators. Then, this [hadith] is to be interpreted as [referring to] his lancing the sore out of haste for death or for no benefit; for had it been by way of medical treatment whose benefit is overwhelmingly probable, it would not have been forbidden. And God knows best.

[Chapter: The Severity of the Prohibition of Ghulūl, and that None Enters Paradise except the Believers]

[114] In it [is the hadith] of ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, may God be pleased with him, who said: "When the Day of Khaybar came, a group of the companions of the Prophet, may God's peace and blessings be upon him, approached and said: 'So-and-so is a martyr, so-and-so is a martyr,' until they passed by a man and said: 'So-and-so is a martyr.' The Messenger of God, may God's peace and blessings be upon him, said: 'No indeed! I have seen him in the Fire, [punished] for a cloak (burdah) or an ʿabā'ah which he had embezzled (ghallahā).' Then the Messenger of God, may God's peace and blessings be upon him, said: 'O son of al-Khaṭṭāb, go and call out among the people: None enters Paradise except the believers.' He said: 'So I went out and called out: "Indeed, none enters Paradise except the believers."'"

In it also is the hadith of Abū Hurayrah of similar meaning. Regarding the chain of transmission: Abū Zumayl — with a ḍammah on the zāy and a lightened, opened mīm — and this has been mentioned previously. His saying, "When the Day of Khaybar came" — it is with the khā' (kh) and ending with rā'; thus it occurs in Muslim, and it is correct. Al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ, may God have mercy on him, mentioned that the majority of the transmitters of al-Muwaṭṭa' narrated it thus, and that it is correct. He said: Some narrated it as "Ḥunayn" with the unpointed ḥā' and nūn. And God knows best. His saying, may God's peace and blessings be upon him, "No indeed!" (kallā) is a rebuke and a rejection of their statement concerning this man that he is a martyr, judged to be in Paradise at first glance — rather, he is in the Fire due to his ghulūl.

[115] His saying: "Thawr ibn Zayd al-Daylī" — here it is with a kasrah on the dāl and a sukūn on the yā'; thus it is in most of the manuscripts found in our lands. In some of them it is "al-Du'alī" with a ḍammah on the dāl and a hamzah after it, whose written form is a wāw. Al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ, may God have mercy on him, mentioned that he recorded it here from Abū Baḥr as "Dawlī" with a ḍammah on the dāl and a silent wāw. He said: And we recorded it from others with a kasrah on the dāl and a sukūn on the yā'. He said: Likewise, Mālik mentioned him in al-Muwaṭṭa' and al-Bukhārī in al-Tārīkh and others. I say: Abū ʿAlī al-Ghassānī mentioned that this Thawr was of the clan (rahṭ) of Abū al-Aswad; on this basis, the disagreement which we mentioned earlier concerning Abū al-Aswad applies here as well. His saying: "From Sālim, Abū al-Ghayth, the freed slave (mawlā) of Ibn Muṭīʿ" — this is sound, and in it is the explicit statement that this Abū al-Ghayth is named Sālim. As for the statement of Abū ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-Barr at the beginning of his book al-Tamhīd, "His name cannot be authentically ascertained," this does not contradict this sound affirmation. The name of Ibn Muṭīʿ is ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muṭīʿ ibn al-Aswad al-Qurashī. And God knows best.

His saying, may God's peace and blessings be upon him: "I have seen him in the Fire, [punished] for a cloak (burdah) or an ʿabā'ah which he had embezzled." As for al-burdah — with a ḍammah on the bā' — it is a striped garment; it is the shamlāh and the namirah. Abū ʿUbayd said: It is a black garment containing images; its plural is burd, with a fatḥah on the rā'. As for al-ʿabā'ah, it is well-known, and it is pronounced with elongation (mamdūdah); it is also said as ʿabāyah with a yā', as stated by Ibn al-Sikkīt and others. His saying, may God's peace and blessings be upon him, "in a burdah" — i.e., "because of it" and "by reason of it." As for al-ghulūl, Abū ʿUbayd said: It is treachery (khiyānah) specifically regarding the war-booty (ghanīmah). Others said: It is treachery in everything. From it is derived: ghalla, yaghillu, with a ḍammah on the ghayn. His saying: "A man of Banī al-Ḍubayb" — it is with a ḍammah on the pointed ḍād, followed by an opened unpointed bā', then a silent yā', then an unpointed bā'. His saying: "He untied his saddle (yaḥillu raḥlahu)" — it is with the unpointed ḥā', and it is the man's riding apparatus on the camel. His saying: "And therein was his death (ḥatfuhu)" — it is with a fatḥah on the unpointed ḥā' and a sukūn on the tā', i.e., his demise; its plural is ḥutūf. And one says: "He died the death of his nose (māta ḥatfa anfihi)," i.e., without being killed or struck. His saying: "A man came with a sandal-strap (shirāk) or two straps and said: 'O Messenger of God, I acquired (aṣabtu) on the Day of Khaybar'" — thus it is in the manuscripts, and it is sound. In it, the object is elided, i.e., "I acquired this." Al-shirāk — with a kasrah on the pointed shīn — is the well-known strap which is on the upper part of the foot in the sandal. Al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ, may God have mercy on him, said: His saying, may God's peace and blessings be upon him, "Verily, the shamlāh will blaze upon him as fire," and his saying, "A strap or two straps of fire" — is an indication of the punishment for them. The punishment may be by them themselves, so that he is tormented by them while they are of fire; or it may be that they are a cause for the punishment of the Fire. And God knows best. As for his saying: "And with the Prophet, may God's peace and blessings be upon him, there was a slave of his" — his name is Midʿam, with a kasrah on the mīm, a sukūn on the dāl, and a fatḥah on the unpointed ʿayn; thus it is explicitly stated in al-Muwaṭṭa' in this very hadith. Al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ, may God have mercy on him, said: It is said that he was not Midʿam. He said: And in a hadith of similar nature, his name is mentioned as...

chapters.title_en: Section 135 — On the Severity of Ghulūl (Embezzlement from War-Booty), the Ruling on the Suicide, and the Wind Before the Hour
chapters.arabic_text:
كركرة ذكره البخاري هذا كلام القاضي وكركرة بفتح الكاف الأولى وكسرها وأما
# 
# الثانية فمكسورة فيهما والله أعلم وأما أحكام الحديثين فمنها غلظ تحريم

الغلول ومنها أنه لا فرق بين قليله وكثيره حتى الشراك ومنها أن الغلول يمنع

من إطلاق اسم الشهادة على من غل إذا قتل وسيأتي بسط هذا إن شاء الله تعالى

ومنها أنه لا يدخل الجنة أحد ممن مات على الكفر وهذا بإجماع المسلمين ومنها

جواز الحلف بالله تعالى من غير ضرورة لقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم والذي نفس

محمد بيده ومنها أن من غل شيئا من الغنيمة يجب عليه رده وأنه إذا رده يقبل

منه ولا يحرق متاعه سواء رده أو لم يرده فإنه صلى الله عليه وسلم لم يحرق

متاع صاحب الشملة وصاحب الشراك ولو كان واجبا لفعله ولو فعله لنقل وأما

الحديث من غل فاحرقوا متاعه واضربوه وفي رواية واضربوا عنقه فضعيف بين بن

عبد البر وغيره ضعفه قال الطحاوي رحمه الله ولو كان صحيحا لكان منسوخا

ويكون هذا حين كانت العقوبات في الأموال  والله أعلم

| (باب الدليل على أن قاتل نفسه لا يكفر
# [116] فيه حديث جابر
# رضي الله عنه (أن الطفيل بن عمرو الدوسي هاجر إلى رسول الله صلى الله

عليه وسلم إلى المدينة وهاجر معه رجل من قومه فاجتووا المدينة فمرض فجزع

فأخذ مشاقص)
# 
# فقطع بها براجمه فشخبت يداه حتى مات فرآه الطفيل في منامه وهيئته حسنة

ورآه مغطيا يديه فقال له ما صنع بك ربك فقال غفر لي بهجرتي إلى نبيه صلى

الله عليه وسلم فقال مالي أراك مغطيا يديك قال قيل لي لن نصلح منك ما أفسدت

فقصها الطفيل على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال رسول الله صلى الله

عليه وسلم اللهم وليديه فاغفر) قوله فاجتووا المدينة هو بضم الواو الثانية

ضمير جمع وهو ضمير يعود على الطفيل والرجل المذكور ومن يتعلق بهما ومعناه

كرهوا المقام بها لضجر ونوع من سقم قال أبو عبيد والجوهري وغيرهما اجتويت

البلد إذا كرهت المقام به وإن كنت في نعمة قال الخطابي وأصله من الجوى وهو

داء يصيب الجوف وقوله فأخذ مشاقص هي بفتح الميم وبالشين المعجمة وبالقاف

والصاد المهملة وهي جمع مشقص بكسر الميم وفتح القاف قال الخليل وبن فارس

وغيرهما هو سهم فيه نصل عريض وقال آخرون سهم طويل ليس بالعريض وقال الجوهري

المشقص ما طال وعرض وهذا هو الظاهر هنا لقوله قطع بها براجمه ولا يحصل ذلك

إلا بالعريض وأما البراجم بفتح الباء الموحدة وبالجيم فهي مفاصل الأصابع

واحدتها برجمة وقوله فشخبت يداه هو بفتح الشين والخاء المعجمتين أي سال

دمهما وقيل سال بقوة وقوله هل لك في حصن حصين ومنعة هي بفتح الميم وبفتح

النون وإسكانها لغتان ذكرهما بن السكيت والجوهري وغيرهما الفتح أفصح وهي

العز والامتناع ممن يريده وقيل المنعة جمع مانع كظالم وظلمة أي جماعة

يمنعونك ممن يقصدك بمكروه أما أحكام الحديث ففيه حجة لقاعدة عظيمة
# 
# لأهل السنة أن من قتل نفسه أو ارتكب معصية غيرها ومات من غير توبة فليس

بكافر ولا يقطع له بالنار  بل هو في حكم المشيئة وقد تقدم بيان القاعدة

وتقريرها وهذا الحديث شرح للأحاديث التي قبله الموهم ظاهرها تخليد قاتل

النفس وغيره من أصحاب الكبائر في النار وفيه إثبات عقوبة بعض أصحاب المعاصي

فإن هذا عوقب في يديه ففيه رد على المرجئة القائلين بأن المعاصي لا تضر

والله أعلم

| (باب في الريح التي تكون قرب القيامة تقبض (من في 
# قلبه شيء من الإيمان)
# [117] فيه قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (إن الله تعالى يبعث ريحا من اليمن

ألين من الحرير فلا تدع أحدا في قلبه مثقال حبة من إيمان إلا قبضته) أما

إسناده ففيه أحمد بن عبدة بإسكان الباء وأبو علقمة الفروي بفتح الفاء

وإسكان الراء واسمه عبد الله بن محمد بن عبد الله بن أبي فروة المدني مولى

آل عثمان بن عفان رضي الله عنه وأما معنى الحديث فقد جاءت في هذا النوع

أحاديث منها لا تقوم الساعة حتى لا يقال في الأرض الله الله ومنها لا تقوم

على أحد يقول الله الله ومنها لا تقوم إلا على شرار الخلق وهذه كلها وما في

معناها على ظاهرها وأما الحديث الآخر لاتزال طائفة من أمتي ظاهرين على الحق

إلى يوم القيامة فليس مخالفا لهذه الأحاديث لأن معنى هذا أنهم لا يزالون

على الحق حتى تقبضهم هذه الريح اللينة قرب القيامة وعند تظاهر أشراطها

فأطلق في هذا الحديث بقاءهم إلى قيام الساعة على أشراطها ودنوها المتناهي

في القرب والله أعلم وأما قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم مثقال حبة أو مثقال ذرة

من إيمان ففيه بيان للمذهب الصحيح)
# 
# أن الإيمان يزيد وينقص وأما قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم ريحا ألين من الحرير

ففيه والله أعلم إشارة إلى الرفق بهم والا كرام لهم والله أعلم وجاء في هذا

الحديث يبعث الله تعالى ريحا من اليمن وفي حديث آخر ذكره مسلم في آخر

الكتاب عقب أحاديث الدجال ريحا من قبل الشام ويجاب عن هذا بوجهين أحدهما

يحتمل أنهما ريحان شامية ويمانية ويحتمل أن مبدأها من  أحد الإقليمين ثم تصل

الآخر وتنتشر عنده والله أعلم
chapters.anchors:
- Root: غ-ل-ل (gh-l-l)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning is "to insert something into something else" (idkhāl al-shayʾ fī al-shayʾ); from this derives ghulūl as the secretive taking of war-booty before its distribution, i.e., treachery (khiyānah).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological usage, ghulūl is a species of treachery (khiyānah) specifically tied to the violation of trust in sacred matters (amānah), particularly the spoils of war; it is a major sin (kabīrah) that bars one from the absolute designation of martyrdom.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) is the physical insertion/concealment; metaphorical (majāz) extends to any act of hidden betrayal of communal trust, including the embezzlement of any public or sacred property.
- Sībawayh Rule: Rule of ʿAṭf al-Bayān (Appositional Clarification) — The phrase "حتى الشراك" (even the sandal-strap) functions as an inclusive appositive clarifying the scope of "قليله وكثيره" (its little and its much), establishing that the ruling applies to the minutest quantity without exception.

- Root: ج-ز-ع (j-z-ʿ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning is "to be restless, impatient, and unable to bear affliction" (ʿadam al-ṣabr ʿalā al-muṣībah); jazaʿ is the antithesis of ṣabr.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In ethical-theological terms, jazaʿ denotes a failure of trust in divine decree (tark al-riḍā bi-al-qaḍāʾ), which is blameworthy but does not remove one from the fold of faith (īmān).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: physical agitation; metaphorical: the soul's internal turmoil manifesting in despair (yaʾs) or self-destructive action.
- Sībawayh Rule: Rule of Ḥāl (Circumstantial Clause) — In "فجزع فأخذ مشاقص" (he grew restless, so he took arrowheads), the verb "جزع" establishes the circumstantial state (ḥāl) that explains the subsequent action, showing the causal nexus between psychological distress and the act of self-harm.

- Root: ق-ب-ض (q-b-ḍ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning is "to take, seize, or grasp" (akhdh); also "to contract" as opposed to "to expand" (bast).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In eschatological context, qabḍ refers to the divine act of seizing the souls of the believers — a gentle taking (qabḍ latīf) that occurs at the end of time, distinct from the violent seizure at death.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: physical grasping; metaphorical: the complete removal of a thing from its place, here used for the extraction of the soul (qabḍ al-rūḥ) with gentleness.
- Sībawayh Rule: Rule of Taʿlīq al-Sharṭ (Conditional Suspension) — In "فلا تدع أحدا في قلبه مثقال حبة من إيمان إلا قبضته" (it will not leave anyone in whose heart is the weight of a grain of faith except that it seizes him), the particle "إلا" after a negated general statement functions as an exception that renders the statement exhaustive (istighrāq), confirming that the wind takes all who possess even the minimum of faith.
chapters.translation:
I say: Concerning the word "Karkarah" (كركرة) — al-Bukhārī mentioned it. This is the statement of al-Qāḍī. And "Karkarah" is with the fatḥah (a-vowel) on the first Kāf, and it is also related with kasrah (i-vowel) on it. As for the second letter, it is with kasrah in both variant readings. And Allāh knows best.

As for the legal rulings (aḥkām) of the two ḥadīths [concerning ghulūl], among them is the extreme severity of the prohibition of ghulūl (embezzlement from war-booty). And among them is that there is no distinction between its little and its much, even [down to] the sandal-strap (al-shirāk). And among them is that ghulūl prevents the unrestricted application of the name "martyrdom" (shahādah) upon the one who commits ghulūl if he is killed [in battle]. And the detailed exposition of this will come later, if Allāh the Exalted wills.

And among them is that no one enters Paradise who dies upon disbelief (kufr) — and this is by the unanimous consensus of the Muslims (ijmāʿ al-Muslimīn). And among them is the permissibility of swearing by Allāh the Exalted without necessity, due to his statement, peace and blessings be upon him: {«والذي نفس محمد بيده»} ("By Him in Whose Hand is the soul of Muḥammad").

And among them is that whoever embezzles something from the war-booty (ghanīmah) is obligated to return it, and that if he returns it, it is accepted from him, and his goods are not burned — whether he returns it or does not return it. For he, peace and blessings be upon him, did not burn the goods of the owner of the cloak (ṣāḥib al-shamlah) nor the owner of the sandal-strap. And had it been obligatory [to burn], he would have done it; and had he done it, it would have been transmitted [to us].

As for the ḥadīth: "Whoever commits ghulūl, burn his goods and beat him" — and in another narration: "and strike his neck" — it is weak (ḍaʿīf). Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr and others have explicitly declared its weakness. Al-Ṭaḥāwī, may Allāh have mercy on him, said: "Even if it were authentic (ṣaḥīḥ), it would be abrogated (mansūkh), and this [ruling] would have been [applicable] at the time when corporal punishments were [carried out] upon wealth." And Allāh knows best.

---

**[Chapter: The Evidence that the Killer of Himself Does Not Disbelieve]**

[116] In it is the ḥadīth of Jābir, may Allāh be pleased with him: (That al-Ṭufayl ibn ʿAmr al-Dawsī migrated to the Messenger of Allāh, peace and blessings be upon him, in Madīnah, and a man from his people migrated with him. They found Madīnah disagreeable (fajtawū al-madīnah), and he fell ill. He grew restless (jazaʿa), so he took arrowheads (mashāqiṣ) and severed with them his finger-joints (barājim). His hands gushed with blood (fashakhabat yadāhu) until he died. Al-Ṭufayl saw him in a dream, and his state was good, and he saw him with his hands covered. He said to him: "What did your Lord do with you?" He said: "He forgave me due to my migration to His Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him." He said: "Why do I see you covering your hands?" He said: "It was said to me: 'We will not repair for you what you have corrupted.'" So al-Ṭufayl narrated this to the Messenger of Allāh, peace and blessings be upon him, and the Messenger of Allāh, peace and blessings be upon him, said: {«اللهم وليديه فاغفر»} ("O Allāh, and forgive his hands."))

His statement "fajtawū al-madīnah" (they found Madīnah disagreeable) — the second Wāw is with ḍammah (u-vowel), and it is a plural pronoun referring back to al-Ṭufayl, the aforementioned man, and whoever is connected to them. Its meaning is: they disliked residing therein due to vexation and a type of sickness. Abū ʿUbayd, al-Jawharī, and others said: "Ijtawayta al-balad" (you found the land disagreeable) means you disliked residing in it, even if you were in comfort. Al-Khaṭṭābī said: "Its origin is from al-jawā (الجوى), which is a disease that afflicts the interior (al-jawf)."

His statement "fa-akhadha mashāqiṣ" (so he took arrowheads) — it is with fatḥah on the Mīm, with the dotted Shīn, with Qāf, and with the undotted Ṣād. It is the plural of "mishqaṣ" (مشقص), with kasrah on the Mīm and fatḥah on the Qāf. Al-Khalīl, Ibn Fāris, and others said: "It is an arrow in which there is a broad arrowhead." Others said: "It is a long arrow that is not broad." Al-Jawharī said: "Al-mishqaṣ is that which is long and broad." And this is the apparent [meaning] here, due to his statement "he severed with them his finger-joints" — and this is not achieved except with the broad [arrowhead].

As for "al-barājim" (the finger-joints) — it is with fatḥah on the unified Bāʾ and with Jīm — they are the joints of the fingers, and their singular is "barjamah" (برجمة).

His statement "fashakhabat yadāhu" (his hands gushed with blood) — it is with fatḥah on the Shīn and the Khāʾ, both dotted, meaning: their blood flowed. And it is said: it flowed with force.

His statement "hal laka fī ḥiṣn ḥaṣīn wa manʿah" (Do you have [interest] in a fortified fortress and protection?) — "manʿah" is with fatḥah on the Mīm and with fatḥah on the Nūn, and its sukūn (quiescence) is a second variant — both are mentioned by Ibn al-Sikkīt, al-Jawharī, and others. The fatḥah is the more eloquent (afṣaḥ). It means might (ʿizz) and protection from whoever seeks to harm one. And it is said: "al-manʿah" is a plural of "māniʿ" (protector), like "ẓālim" and "ẓalamah" — i.e., a group that protects you from whoever intends you harm.

As for the legal rulings (aḥkām) of this ḥadīth: In it is a proof for a great principle (qāʿidah ʿaẓīmah) of the People of the Sunnah (Ahl al-Sunnah): that whoever kills himself, or commits any other act of disobedience (maʿṣiyah), and dies without repentance — he is not a disbeliever (kāfir), nor is it decreed for him that he is [doomed] to the Fire. Rather, he is under the ruling of the Divine Will (mashīʾah). And the exposition and establishment of this principle has already preceded.

And this ḥadīth is an explanation of the ḥadīths before it, whose apparent meaning suggests the eternal abiding (takhālud) in the Fire of the killer of himself and others among the perpetrators of major sins (aṣḥāb al-kabāʾir). And in it is the affirmation of punishment for some of the perpetrators of sins — for this one was punished in his hands. Thus in it is a refutation of the Murjiʾah (المرجئة), who claim that sins do not cause harm. And Allāh knows best.

---

**[Chapter: Concerning the Wind that Will Be Near the Hour, Which Will Seize (Everyone in Whose Heart is Something of Faith)]**

[117] In it is his statement, peace and blessings be upon him: {«إن الله تعالى يبعث ريحا من اليمن ألين من الحرير فلا تدع أحدا في قلبه مثقال حبة من إيمان إلا قبضته»} ("Indeed, Allāh the Exalted will send a wind from Yemen, softer than silk. It will not leave anyone in whose heart is the weight of a grain of faith except that it seizes him.")

As for its chain of transmission (isnād): In it is Aḥmad ibn ʿAbdah — with sukūn on the Bāʾ — and Abū ʿAlqamah al-Farawī — with fatḥah on the Fāʾ and sukūn on the Rāʾ — and his name is ʿAbdullāh ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAbdullāh ibn Abī Farwah al-Madanī, the freed slave (mawlā) of the family of ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān, may Allāh be pleased with him.

As for the meaning of the ḥadīth: There have come in this type [of narration] ḥadīths, including: "The Hour will not be established until 'Allāh, Allāh' is not said upon the earth." And including: "It will not be established upon anyone who says 'Allāh, Allāh.'" And including: "It will not be established except upon the most evil of creation." And all of these, and whatever is in their meaning, are upon their apparent [sense] (ẓāhirihā).

As for the other ḥadīth: "A group of my Ummah will not cease to be manifest upon the truth until the Day of Resurrection" — it is not contradictory to these ḥadīths, because the meaning of this is that they will not cease to be upon the truth until this soft wind seizes them near the Hour, and at the time of the manifestation of its portents (ashrāṭ). Thus in this ḥadīth, their remaining until the establishment of the Hour is mentioned with respect to its portents and its extreme proximity (al-dunūw al-mutanāhī fī al-qurb). And Allāh knows best.

As for his statement, peace and blessings be upon him: "the weight of a grain (mithqāl ḥabbah) or the weight of a particle (mithqāl dharrāh) of faith" — in it is an elucidation of the correct doctrine (al-madhhab al-ṣaḥīḥ) that faith (īmān) increases and decreases.

As for his statement, peace and blessings be upon him: "a wind softer than silk" — in it, and Allāh knows best, is an indication of gentleness (al-rifq) toward them and honor (al-ikrām) for them. And Allāh knows best.

And there has come in this ḥadīth: "Allāh the Exalted will send a wind from Yemen," while in another ḥadīth — which Muslim mentioned at the end of the book, following the ḥadīths of the Dajjāl — [it is]: "a wind from the direction of al-Shām (Syria)." And this is answered by two aspects: One of them — it is possible that they are two winds, one Shāmī (Syrian) and one Yamanī (Yemeni). And it is possible that its origin is from one of the two regions, then it reaches the other and spreads in its vicinity. And Allāh knows best.

chapters.title_en: The Urging to Hasten to Righteous Deeds Before the Onset of Trials, and the Fear of the Believer that His Deeds May Be Nullified
chapters.arabic_text:
| (باب الحث على المبادرة بالأعمال قبل تظاهر الفتن
# [118] فيه قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم بادروا بالأعمال فتنا كقطع الليل

المظلم يصبح الرجل مؤمنا ويمسي كافرا أو يمسي مؤمنا ويصبح كافرا يبيع دينه

بعرض من الدنيا) معنى الحديث الحث على المبادرة إلى الأعمال الصالحة قبل

تعذرها والاشتغال عنها بما يحدث من الفتن الشاغلة المتكاثرة المتراكمة

كتراكم ظلام الليل المظلم لا المقمر ووصف صلى الله عليه وسلم نوعا من شدائد

تلك الفتن وهو أنه يمسي مؤمنا ثم يصبح كافرا أو عكسه شك الراوي وهذا لعظم

الفتن ينقلب الإنسان في اليوم الواحد هذا الانقلاب والله أعلم)

# باب مخافة المؤمن أن يحبط عمله
# [119] فيه قصة ثابت بن قيس بن الشماس رضي الله عنه وخوفه حين نزلت لا

ترفعوا أصواتكم فوق
# 
# صوت النبى الآية وكان ثابت رضي الله عنه جهير الصوت وكان يرفع صوته وكان

خطيب الأنصار ولذلك اشتد حذره أكثر من غيره وفي هذا الحديث منقبة عظيمة

لثابت بن قيس رضي الله عنه وهي أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أخبر أنه من

أهل الجنة وفيه أنه ينبغي للعالم وكبير القوم أن يتفقد أصحابه ويسأل عمن

غاب منهم وقول مسلم رحمه الله (حدثنا قطن بن نسير قال حدثنا جعفر بن سليمان

حدثنا ثابت عن أنس) فيه لطيفة وهو أنه اسناد كله بصريون وقطن بفتح القاف

والطاء المهملة وبالنون ونسير بنون مضمومة ثم سين مهملة مفتوحة ثم مثناة من

تحت ساكنة ثم راء وقد قدمنا أنه ليس في الصحيحين نسير غيره وقد قدمنا في

الفصول المذكورة في مقدمة هذا الشرح إنكار من أنكر على مسلم روايته عنه

وجوابه وفي
# 
# الإسناد الآخر حبان هو بفتح الحاء المهملة والباء الموحدة وهو بن هلال

وكل هذا الإسناد أيضا بصريون إلا أحمد بن سعيد الدارمي في أوله فإنه

نيسابوري وقول مسلم (حدثنا هريم بن عبد الأعلى حدثنا المعتمر بن سليمان قال

سمعت أبي يذكر عن ثابت عن أنس) هذا الاسناد  أيضا كله بصريون حقيقة وهريم

بضم الهاء وفتح الراء وإسكان الياء وقوله (فكنا نراه يمشي بين أظهرنا رجلا

من أهل الجنة) هكذا هو في بعض الأصول رجلا وفي بعضها رجل وهو الأكثر

وكلاهما صحيح الأول على البدل من الهاء في نراه والثاني على الاستئناف

| (باب هل يؤاخذ بأعمال الجاهلية
# [120] قال مسلم (حدثنا عثمان
# بن أبي شيبة حدثنا جرير عن منصور عن أبي وائل عن عبد الله قال قال أناس

يا رسول الله أنؤاخذ بما عملنا في الجاهلية قال أما من أحسن منكم في

الإسلام فلا يؤاخذ بها ومن أساء أخذ بعمله في الجاهلية والإسلام) قال مسلم

(حدثنا محمد بن)
# 
# عبد الله بن نمير قال حدثنا أبي ووكيع قال وحدثنا أبو بكر بن أبي شيبة

واللفظ له قال حدثنا وكيع عن الأعمش عن أبي وائل عن عبد الله رضي الله عنه

قال قلنا يا رسول الله أنؤاخذ بما عملنا في الجاهلية فذكره) قال مسلم

(حدثنا منجاب أخبرنا بن مسهر عن الأعمش بهذا الإسناد) هذه الأسانيد الثلاثة

كلهم كوفيون وهذا من أطرف النفائس لكونها أسانيد متلاصقة مسلسلة بالكوفيين

وعبد الله هو بن مسعود ومنجاب بكسر الميم وأما معنى الحديث فالصحيح فيه ما

قاله جماعة من المحققين أن المراد بالإحسان هنا الدخول في الإسلام بالظاهر

والباطن جميعا وأن يكون مسلما حقيقيا فهذا يغفر له ما سلف في الكفر بنص

القرآن العزيز والحديث الصحيح الإسلام يهدم ما قبله وبإجماع المسلمين

والمراد بالإساءة عدم الدخول في الإسلام بقلبه بل يكون منقادا فى الظاهر

مظهرا للشهادتين غير معتقد للإسلام بقلبه فهذا منافق باق على كفره بإجماع

المسلمين فيؤاخذ بما عمل في الجاهلية قبل إظهار صورة الإسلام وبما عمل بعد

إظهارها لأنه مستمر على كفره وهذا معروف في استعمال الشرع يقولون حسن إسلام

فلان إذا دخل فيه حقيقة بإخلاص وساء إسلامه أو لم يحسن إسلامه إذا لم يكن

كذلك والله أعلم

| (باب كون الإسلام يهدم ما قبله وكذا الحج والهجرة
# [121] فيه حديث عمرو بن العاصي رضي الله  عنه وقصة وفاته وفيه حديث بن

عباس رضي الله عنهما)
# 
# في سبب نزول قول الله تعالى والذين لا يدعون مع الله إلها آخر وقوله

تعالى يا عبادي الذين أسرفوا على أنفسهم فأما حديث عمرو فنتكلم في إسناده

ومتنه ثم نعود إلى حديث بن عباس رضي الله عنهما أما إسناده ففيه محمد بن

مثنى العنزى بفتح العين والنون وأبو معن الرقاشي بفتح الراء وتخفيف القاف

اسمه زيد بن يزيد وأبو عاصم هو النبيل واسمه الضحاك بن مخلد وبن شماسة

المهري وشماسة بالشين المعجمة في أوله بفتحها وضمها ذكرهما صاحب المطالع

والميم مخففة وآخره سين مهملة ثم هاء واسمه عبد الرحمن بن شماسة بن ذئب أبو

عمرو وقيل أبو عبد الله والمهرى بفتح الميم وإسكان الهاء وبالراء وأما

ألفاظ متنه فقوله (في سياقة الموت) هو بكسر السين أى حال حضور الموت وقوله

(أفضل ما نعد) هو بضم النون وقوله (كنت على أطباق ثلاث) أي على أحوال قال

الله تعالى لتركبن طبقا عن طبق فلهذا أنث ثلاثا إرادة لمعنى أطباق قوله صلى
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ب-د-ر (b-d-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To hasten, to be foremost, to rush toward something with urgency; derived from the early morning rush to water (al-badr).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In the theological sense, it denotes the eager acceleration toward acts of obedience (ṭāʿah) before impediments arise, reflecting the Quranic imperative of competing in good works.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage refers to physical haste; here it is metaphorical (majāz) for spiritual vigilance and moral urgency in the face of temporal decay.
- Root: ف-ت-ن (f-t-n)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Trial, tribulation, affliction; originally from the smelting of gold in fire to test its purity (fatana al-dhahab).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In Kalām, it signifies divinely ordained tests that distinguish the sincere from the hypocrite, often manifesting as social and political chaos.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: burning or refining; metaphorical: the moral and spiritual confusion that overwhelms the community like darkness.
- Root: ح-ب-ط (ḥ-b-ṭ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To nullify, to render void; originally, the swelling of an animal's belly from eating poisonous plants, leading to death—hence, the corruption of a thing's essence.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological discourse, it refers to the invalidation of one's good deeds due to disbelief (kufr) or hypocrisy (nifāq), as in the Quranic verse {«وَقَدِمْنَا إِلَىٰ مَا عَمِلُوا مِنْ عَمَلٍ فَجَعَلْنَاهُ هَبَاءً مَّنثُورًا»} (We shall turn to whatever deeds they did and make them scattered dust).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: bodily corruption; metaphorical: the spiritual annihilation of merit before God.
- Sībawayh Rule: Rule of Badal (Substitution) and Isti'nāf (Resumption) — In the phrase "فكنا نراه يمشي بين أظهرنا رجلا من أهل الجنة" (We would see him walking among us, a man of Paradise), the accusative "رجلا" is parsed as a badal (substitute) of the object pronoun "الهاء" in "نراه," while the nominative "رجل" is parsed as an isti'nāf (new sentence beginning), both being grammatically sound.
chapters.translation:
I say — and Allah knows best — the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Hasten to deeds before trials come like pieces of dark night. A man wakes up a believer and becomes a disbeliever by evening, or becomes a believer by evening and wakes up a disbeliever by morning, selling his religion for a portion of worldly goods." The meaning of this hadith is the urging to hasten toward righteous deeds before they become unattainable and before one is distracted from them by the trials that arise—distracting, multiplying, and piling upon one another like the accumulation of the darkness of a dark night, not a moonlit one. The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, described a type of the severities of those trials: that a man becomes a believer in the evening, then wakes up a disbeliever in the morning, or the reverse—the narrator being uncertain. This is due to the magnitude of the trials: a person is overturned in a single day with this overturning. And Allah knows best.

Chapter: The Fear of the Believer that His Deeds May Be Nullified

[119] In this chapter is the story of Thābit ibn Qays ibn al-Shammās, may Allah be pleased with him, and his fear when the verse was revealed: {«لَا تَرْفَعُوا أَصْوَاتَكُمْ فَوْقَ صَوْتِ النَّبِيِّ»} (Raise not your voices above the voice of the Prophet). Thābit, may Allah be pleased with him, had a loud voice and would raise it, and he was the orator of the Ansār. For this reason, his caution was more intense than that of others. In this hadith is a great virtue for Thābit ibn Qays, may Allah be pleased with him—namely, that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, informed that he is among the people of Paradise. It also contains the point that it is befitting for the scholar and the leader of a people to check on his companions and to ask about those who are absent from them.

Muslim, may Allah have mercy on him, said: "Qaṭan ibn Nusayr narrated to us; he said: Jaʿfar ibn Sulaymān narrated to us; Thābit narrated to us, from Anas." In this is a subtlety: it is an isnād whose narrators are all Baṣran. "Qaṭan" is with a fatḥa on the qāf and the ṭā' (the unpointed one) and a nūn. "Nusayr" is with a ḍamma on the nūn, then a fatḥa on the sīn (the unpointed one), then a sukūn on the tā' (the dotted one from below), then a rā'. We have already mentioned that in the two Ṣaḥīḥs there is no other Nusayr besides him. We have also already mentioned in the chapters presented in the introduction to this commentary the rejection of those who criticized Muslim for narrating from him, and the answer to that.

In the other isnād, "Ḥabbān" is with a fatḥa on the unpointed ḥā' and the dotted bā', and he is Ibn Hilāl. All of this isnād is also Baṣran, except Aḥmad ibn Saʿīd al-Dārimī at its beginning, for he is Naysābūrī.

Muslim's saying: "Huraym ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā narrated to us; al-Muʿtamir ibn Sulaymān narrated to us; he said: I heard my father mention, from Thābit, from Anas." This isnād is also entirely Baṣran in reality. "Huraym" is with a ḍamma on the hā', a fatḥa on the rā', and a sukūn on the yā'.

His saying: "We would see him walking among us, a man of Paradise" — thus it is in some manuscripts: "rajulan" (accusative), and in others: "rajulun" (nominative), which is the more frequent. Both are correct: the first is on the basis of badal (substitution) from the hā' in "narāhu" (we see him), and the second is on the basis of isti'nāf (a new sentence).

Chapter: Whether One is Held Accountable for Deeds of the Pre-Islamic Era (Jāhiliyyah)

[120] Muslim said: "ʿUthmān ibn Abī Shaybah narrated to us; Jarīr narrated to us, from Manṣūr, from Abū Wā'il, from ʿAbd Allāh; he said: People said: O Messenger of Allah, will we be held accountable for what we did in the Jāhiliyyah? He said: As for the one among you who does well in Islam, he will not be held accountable for it; and the one who does ill will be held accountable for his deeds in both the Jāhiliyyah and Islam."

Muslim said: "Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Numayr narrated to us; he said: My father and Wakīʿ narrated to us; and he said: Abū Bakr ibn Abī Shaybah narrated to us—and the wording is his—he said: Wakīʿ narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash, from Abū Wā'il, from ʿAbd Allāh, may Allah be pleased with him; he said: We said: O Messenger of Allah, will we be held accountable for what we did in the Jāhiliyyah? And he mentioned it."

Muslim said: "Minjāb narrated to us; Ibn Mushir informed us, from al-Aʿmash, with this isnād." These three isnāds are all Kūfan. This is among the rarest of precious things, for they are contiguous isnāds, sequentially linked by Kūfans. "ʿAbd Allāh" is Ibn Masʿūd. "Minjāb" is with a kasra on the mīm.

As for the meaning of the hadith, the correct view is what a group of the verifying scholars (muḥaqqiqūn) have stated: that the intended meaning of "doing well" (iḥsān) here is entering into Islam with both the outward and the inward, and that one becomes a true Muslim. Such a person is forgiven for what preceded in disbelief, by the text of the Noble Quran, the authentic hadith—"Islam demolishes what preceded it"—and by the consensus of the Muslims. The intended meaning of "doing ill" (isā'ah) is the failure to enter into Islam with one's heart, but rather being outwardly submissive, manifesting the two testimonies of faith while not believing in Islam with his heart. Such a person is a hypocrite (munāfiq), remaining upon his disbelief by the consensus of the Muslims. He is therefore held accountable for what he did in the Jāhiliyyah before manifesting the form of Islam, and for what he did after manifesting it, because he is persistent upon his disbelief. This is well-known in the usage of the Sacred Law: they say "his Islam is good" (ḥasuna islāmuhu) when one enters into it truly with sincerity, and "his Islam is bad" (sā'a islāmuhu) or "he did not do well in his Islam" when he is not like that. And Allah knows best.

Chapter: That Islam Demolishes What Preceded It, and Likewise Pilgrimage (Ḥajj) and Emigration (Hijrah)

[121] In this chapter is the hadith of ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ, may Allah be pleased with him, and the story of his death. Also in it is the hadith of Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with them both, concerning the occasion of the revelation of the saying of Allah the Exalted: {«وَالَّذِينَ لَا يَدْعُونَ مَعَ اللَّهِ إِلَٰهًا آخَرَ»} (And those who do not invoke with Allah another deity), and His saying the Exalted: {«يَا عِبَادِيَ الَّذِينَ أَسْرَفُوا عَلَىٰ أَنفُسِهِمْ»} (O My servants who have transgressed against themselves).

As for the hadith of ʿAmr, we will discuss its isnād and its text, then we will return to the hadith of Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with them both. As for its isnād, it contains Muḥammad ibn Muthannā al-ʿAnazī—with a fatḥa on the ʿayn and the nūn—and Abū Maʿn al-Raqāshī—with a fatḥa on the rā' and a takhfīf (lightening) of the qāf; his name is Zayd ibn Yazīd. And Abū ʿĀṣim is al-Nabīl; his name is al-Ḍaḥḥāk ibn Makhlad. And Ibn Shamāsah al-Mahrī—"Shamāsah" is with the dotted shīn at its beginning, with a fatḥa and a ḍamma on it, both mentioned by the author of al-Maṭāliʿ; the mīm is lightened (mukhaffafah), and its end is an unpointed sīn followed by a hā'. His name is ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Shamāsah ibn Dhi'b, Abū ʿAmr—and it is said Abū ʿAbd Allāh. "Al-Mahrī" is with a fatḥa on the mīm, a sukūn on the hā', and a rā'.

As for the wording of its text, his saying: "in the throes of death" (fī siyāqat al-mawt) — "siyāqah" is with a kasra on the sīn, meaning the state of the presence of death. His saying: "the best of what we count" (afḍal mā naʿuddu) — "naʿuddu" is with a ḍamma on the nūn. His saying: "I was upon three layers" (kuntu ʿalā aṭbāq thalāth) — meaning upon three states. Allah the Exalted said: {«لَتَرْكَبُنَّ طَبَقًا عَن طَبَقٍ»} (You shall surely ride layer upon layer). For this reason, "three" is in the feminine, intending the meaning of "aṭbāq" (layers). His saying, peace be upon him...

chapters.title_en: Section 137 — The Chapter on the Explanation of the Ruling on the Deeds of an Unbeliever Who Embraces Islam Afterwards
chapters.arabic_text:
الله عليه وسلم
# 
# (تشترط بماذا) هكذا ضبطناه بما بإثبات الباء فيجوز أن تكون زائدة للتوكيد

كما في نظائرها ويجوز أن تكون دخلت على معنى تشترط وهو تحتاط أي تحتاط

بماذا وقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (الإسلام يهدم ما كان قبله) أي يسقطه ويمحو

أثره قوله (وما كنت أطيق أن أملأ عيني) هو بتشديد الياء من عيني على

التثنية قوله (فإذا دفنتموني فسنوا علي التراب سنا) ضبطناه بالسين المهملة

وبالمعجمة وكذا قال القاضي إنه بالمعجمة والمهملة قال وهو الصب وقيل

بالمهملة الصب فى سهولة وبالمعجمة التفريق وقوله (قدر ما ينحر جزور) هي

بفتح الجيم وهي من الإبل أما أحكامه ففيه عظم موقع الإسلام والهجرة والحج

وأن كل واحد منها يهدم ما كان قبله من المعاصي وفيه استحباب تنبيه المحتضر

على إحسان ظنه بالله سبحانه وتعالى وذكر آيات الرجاء وأحاديث العفو عنده

وتبشيره بما أعده الله تعالى للمسلمين وذكر حسن أعماله عنده ليحسن  ظنه

بالله تعالى ويموت عليه وهذا الأدب مستحب بالاتفاق وموضع الدلالة له من هذا

الحديث قول بن عمرو لأبيه أما بشرك رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بكذا وفيه

ما كانت الصحابة رضي الله عنهم عليه من توقير رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

وإجلاله وفي قوله فلا تصحبني نائحة ولا نار امتثال لنهي النبي صلى الله

عليه وسلم عن ذلك وقد كره العلماء ذلك فأما النياحة فحرام وأما اتباع الميت

بالنار فمكروه للحديث ثم قيل سبب الكراهة كونه
# 
# من شعار الجاهلية وقال بن حبيب المالكي كره تفاؤلا بالنار وفي قوله فشنوا

علي التراب استحباب صب التراب في القبر وأنه لا يقعد على القبر بخلاف ما

يعمل في بعض البلاد وقوله ثم أقيموا حول قبري قدر ما ينحر جزور ويقسم لحمها

حتى أستأنس بكم وأنظر ماذا أراجع به رسل ربي فيه فوائد منها إثبات فتنة

القبر وسؤال الملكين وهو مذهب أهل الحق ومنها استحباب المكث عند القبر بعد

الدفن لحظة نحو ما ذكر لما ذكر وفيه أن الميت يسمع حينئذ من حول القبر وقد

يستدل به لجواز قسمة اللحم المشترك ونحوه من الأشياء الرطبة كالعنب وفي هذا

خلاف لأصحابنا معروف قالوا إن قلنا بأحد القولين أن القسمة تمييز حق ليست

ببيع جاز وإن قلنا بيع فوجهان أصحهما لا يجوز للجهل بتماثله في حال الكمال

فيؤدي إلى الربا والثاني يجوز لتساويهما في الحال فإذا قلنا لا يجوز

فطريقها أن يجعل اللحم وشبهه قسمين ثم يبيع أحدهما صاحبه نصيبه من أحد

القسمين بدرهم مثلا ثم يبيع الآخر نصيبه من القسم الآخر لصاحبه بذلك الدرهم

الذي له عليه فيحصل لكل واحد منهما قسم بكماله ولها طرق غير هذا لا حاجة

إلى الإطالة بها هنا والله أعلم
# [122] وأما حديث بن عباس رضي الله عنهما فمراد مسلم رحمه الله منه أن

القرآن العزيز جاء بما جاءت به السنة من كون الإسلام يهدم ما قبله وقوله

فيه (ولو تخبرنا بأن لما عملنا كفارة فنزل والذين لا  يدعون مع الله إلها

آخر الآية) فيه محذوف وهو جواب لو أي لو تخبرنا
# 
# لأسلمنا وحذفها كثير في القرآن العزيز وكلام العرب كقوله تعالى ولو ترى

إذ الظالمون وأشباهه وأما قوله تعالى يلق أثاما فقيل معناه عقوبة وقيل هو

واد في جهنم وقيل بئر فيها وقيل جزاء إثمه

| (باب بيان حكم عمل الكافر إذا أسلم بعده
# [123] فيه حديث
# حكيم بن حزام رضي الله عنه أنه قال لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم (أرأيت

أمورا كنت أتحنث بها في الجاهلية هل لي فيها من شيء فقال له رسول الله صلى

الله عليه وسلم أسلمت على ما أسلفت من خير) أما التحنث فهو التعبد كما فسره

في الحديث وفسره في الرواية الأخرى بالتبرر وهو فعل البر وهو الطاعة قال

أهل اللغة أصل التحنث أن يفعل فعلا يخرج به من الحنث وهو الإثم وكذا تأثم

وتحرج وتهجد أي فعل فعلا يخرج به عن الإثم والحرج والهجود وأما قوله صلى

الله عليه وسلم أسلمت على ما أسلفت من خير فاختلف في معناه فقال الإمام أبو

عبد الله المازري رحمه الله ظاهره خلاف ما تقتضيه الأصول لأن الكافر لا يصح

منه التقرب فلا يثاب على طاعته ويصح أن يكون مطيعا غير متقرب كنظيره في

الإيمان فإنه مطيع فيه من حيث كان موافقا للأمر والطاعة عندنا موافقة الأمر

ولكنه لا يكون متقربا لأن من شرط المتقرب أن يكون عارفا بالمتقرب إليه وهو

في حين نظره لم يحصل له العلم بالله تعالى بعد فإذا تقرر هذا علم أن الحديث

متأول وهو يحتمل وجوها أحدها أن يكون معناه اكتسبت طباعا جميلة وأنت تنتفع

بتلك الطباع في الإسلام وتكون تلك العادة تمهيدا لك ومعونة على فعل الخير

والثاني معناه اكتسبت بذلك)
# 
# ثناء جميلا فهو باق عليك في الإسلام والثالث أنه لا يبعد أن يزاد في

حسناته التي يفعلها في الإسلام ويكثر أجره لما تقدم له من الأفعال الجميلة

وقد قالوا في الكافر إذا كان يفعل الخير فإنه يخفف عنه  به فلا يبعد أن يزاد

هذا في الأجور هذا آخر كلام المازري رحمه الله قال القاضي عياض رحمه الله

وقيل معناه ببركة ما سبق لك من خير هداك الله تعالى إلى الإسلام وأن من ظهر
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ش ر ط (sh-r-ṭ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To stipulate, condition, or make a prerequisite; a mark or sign by which something is known.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): A stipulated condition (sharṭ) that renders an act valid or contingent upon its fulfillment; here, the Prophet's query probes the basis of the companion's precautionary practice.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) — a binding condition; metaphorical (majāz) — the sense of "being cautious" (iḥtiyāṭ), as the preposition "bi" enters upon the meaning of "to be wary of."
- Root: ه د م (h-d-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To demolish, raze, or obliterate a structure; to efface a trace.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological terms, the abrogation and nullification of prior sins by a subsequent act of faith — a divine grace that erases the effect of disobedience.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — physical destruction; metaphorical — the complete removal of moral culpability, as the verb "yahdimu" is used figuratively for "to cancel and wipe away."
- Root: س ن و (s-n-w)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To pour out, scatter, or spread (earth, water); to flow gently.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The act of pouring soil over a grave — a ritual act of burial with specific mannerisms.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — pouring; metaphorical — the distinction between "sanna" (easy pouring) and "shanna" (scattering/separating), as noted by the Qāḍī.
- Root: ج ز ر (j-z-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To slaughter a camel; a "jazūr" is a mature camel prepared for sacrifice.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The measure of time for slaughtering and dividing the meat — a temporal benchmark in ritual practice.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — the animal; metaphorical — the duration of a specific act, extended to the waiting period at the grave.
- Sībawayh Rule: The Rule of Ziyādah (Redundancy) — The preposition "bi" in "bimādhā" may be augmentative (zāʾidah) for emphasis, as in parallel constructions, or it may govern the verbal sense of "iḥtiyāṭ" (caution), where the preposition is integral to the transitive verb's meaning.
chapters.translation:
I say: As for his statement (upon him be peace) — "By what do you stipulate?" — we have recorded it thus with the "bāʾ" affirmed, so it is permissible that it be augmentative for emphasis, as in its parallels, and it is permissible that it entered upon the meaning of "you stipulate," which is "you are cautious," i.e., "by what are you cautious?" And his statement (upon him be peace): "Islam demolishes what was before it" — i.e., it cancels it and wipes away its trace. His statement: "And I was not able to fill my eyes" — it is with the shaddah on the "yāʾ" of "ʿaynayya" (my two eyes), upon the dual form. His statement: "So when you have buried me, then pour upon me earth in a pouring" — we have recorded it with the unpointed "sīn" and with the pointed letter (shīn); likewise the Qāḍī said it is with the pointed and the unpointed. He said: "It is the pouring," and it was said: with the unpointed letter it is the pouring with ease, and with the pointed letter it is the scattering. And his statement: "To the measure of what a camel is slaughtered" — it is with the fatḥah on the "jīm," and it is among camels.

As for its rulings: In it is the great significance of Islam, the emigration (hijrah), and the pilgrimage (ḥajj), and that each one of them demolishes what preceded it of sins. And in it is the recommendation (istiḥbāb) of alerting the dying person to the excellence of his good opinion of Allah (Glory be to Him and Exalted), and the mention of the verses of hope and the hadiths of pardon in his presence, and giving him glad tidings of what Allah (Exalted) has prepared for the Muslims, and the mention of his good deeds in his presence, so that his opinion of Allah (Exalted) may be good and he may die upon that. This etiquette is recommended by consensus. The point of indication for it in this hadith is the statement of Ibn ʿAmr to his father: "Shall I not give you glad tidings that the Messenger of Allah (upon him be peace) mentioned you with such-and-such?" And in it is what the Companions (may Allah be pleased with them) were upon of reverence for the Messenger of Allah (upon him be peace) and veneration of him. And in his statement: "So let no wailing woman accompany me, nor fire" — there is compliance with the Prophet's (upon him be peace) prohibition of that. The scholars have deemed that disliked (makrūh). As for wailing (niyāḥah), it is forbidden (ḥarām); and as for following the deceased with fire, it is disliked, due to the hadith. Then it was said: the reason for its dislike is that it is from the insignia of the pre-Islamic era (jāhiliyyah). And Ibn Ḥabīb al-Mālikī said: it was disliked as an ill omen with fire.

And in his statement: "So scatter upon me earth" — there is the recommendation of pouring earth into the grave, and that one does not sit upon the grave, contrary to what is done in some lands. And his statement: "Then stand around my grave to the measure of what a camel is slaughtered and its meat is divided, until I am comforted by you and I see with what I shall answer the messengers of my Lord" — in it are benefits: among them, the affirmation of the trial of the grave (fitnat al-qabr) and the questioning of the two angels, which is the doctrine of the people of truth (ahl al-ḥaqq). And among them, the recommendation of tarrying at the grave after burial for a moment, approximately what was mentioned, for what was mentioned. And in it is that the deceased hears at that time those around the grave. And it may be adduced as evidence for the permissibility of dividing shared meat and the like of moist things, such as grapes. In this there is a known disagreement among our companions (al-Shāfiʿiyyah). They said: if we hold one of the two opinions — that division is a distinguishing of rights and not a sale — it is permissible; and if we hold it is a sale, then there are two aspects: the more correct of them is that it is not permissible due to ignorance of its equivalence in the state of completeness, leading to usury (ribā); and the second is that it is permissible due to their equality in the present state. So if we say it is not permissible, then its method is that the meat and its like be made into two portions, then one sells to his companion his share of one of the two portions for a dirham, for example, then the other sells his share of the other portion to his companion for that same dirham which he owes him; thus each of them obtains a complete portion. And there are other methods besides this, with no need to elaborate here. And Allah knows best.

[122] As for the hadith of Ibn ʿAbbās (may Allah be pleased with them both), the intent of Muslim (may Allah have mercy on him) from it is that the Noble Qurʾān came with what the Sunnah came with — that Islam demolishes what precedes it. And his statement in it: "And if you had told us that what we had done was an expiation, then it was revealed: {«And those who do not invoke with Allah another deity»} to the end of the verse" — in it there is an omitted element, which is the answer to "law" (if): i.e., "if you had told us, we would have embraced Islam." And its omission is frequent in the Noble Qurʾān and the speech of the Arabs, like His statement (Exalted): {«And if you could see when the wrongdoers»} and its like. As for His statement (Exalted): "He will meet with athām" — it was said its meaning is punishment; and it was said it is a valley in Hell; and it was said a well therein; and it was said the recompense of his sin.

| (Chapter: The Explanation of the Ruling on the Deeds of an Unbeliever When He Embraces Islam Afterwards)

[123] In it is the hadith of Ḥakīm ibn Ḥizām (may Allah be pleased with him) that he said to the Messenger of Allah (upon him be peace): "Do you see these matters which I used to perform taḥannuth with in the pre-Islamic era — is there anything for me in them?" So the Messenger of Allah (upon him be peace) said to him: "You have embraced Islam upon what you have forwarded of good."

As for taḥannuth, it is devotion (taʿabbud), as he interpreted it in the hadith, and he interpreted it in the other narration as tabarrur — i.e., the doing of piety (birr), which is obedience. The people of language said: the origin of taḥannuth is that one performs an act by which he exits from ḥanath, which is sin. Likewise taʾaththum, taḥarruj, and tahajjud — i.e., he performs an act by which he exits from sin, constraint, and sleeplessness (hujūd).

As for his statement (upon him be peace): "You have embraced Islam upon what you have forwarded of good" — there is disagreement over its meaning. The Imām Abū ʿAbdullāh al-Māzarī (may Allah have mercy on him) said: its apparent meaning contradicts what the principles (uṣūl) require, because the unbeliever's act of drawing near (taqarrub) is not valid, so he is not rewarded for his obedience; yet it is valid that he be obedient without drawing near, like its parallel in faith — for he is obedient therein insofar as it conforms to the command, and obedience for us is conformity to the command. But he is not one who draws near, because among the conditions of the one who draws near is that he be cognizant of the One to whom he draws near, and he, at the time of his consideration, had not yet attained knowledge of Allah (Exalted). So when this is established, it is known that the hadith requires interpretation (taʾwīl), and it admits several aspects: One of them — that its meaning is: you acquired noble dispositions, and you benefit from those dispositions in Islam, and that habit becomes a preparation for you and an aid upon the doing of good. The second — its meaning: you acquired by that a beautiful praise, and it remains upon you in Islam. The third — that it is not far that there be added to his good deeds which he performs in Islam, and his reward be multiplied, due to what preceded him of beautiful acts. And they have said concerning the unbeliever who does good: it lightens (punishment) for him thereby, so it is not far that this be added to the rewards. This is the end of the speech of al-Māzarī (may Allah have mercy on him).

Al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ (may Allah have mercy on him) said: And it was said its meaning is: by the blessing of what preceded you of good, Allah (Exalted) guided you to Islam, and that whoever manifests...

chapters.title_en: Section 138 — On the Reward of the Disbeliever's Good Deeds After Embracing Islam, and the Chapter on the Truthfulness of Faith and Its Sincerity
chapters.arabic_text:
منه خير في أول أمره فهو دليل على سعادة آخره وحسن عاقبته هذا كلام القاضي

وذهب بن بطال وغيره من المحققين إلى أن الحديث على ظاهره وأنه إذا أسلم

الكافر ومات على الإسلام يثاب على ما فعله من الخير في حال الكفر واستدلوا

بحديث أبي سعيد الخدري رضي الله عنه قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

إذا أسلم الكافر فحسن إسلامه كتب الله تعالى له كل حسنة زلفها ومحا عنه كل

سيئة زلفها وكان عمله بعد الحسنة بعشر أمثالها إلى سبعمائة ضعف والسيئة

بمثلها إلا أن يتجاوز الله سبحانه وتعالى ذكره الدارقطني في غريب حديث مالك

ورواه عنه من تسع طرق وثبت فيها كلها أن الكافر إذا حسن إسلامه يكتب له في

الإسلام كل حسنة عملها فى الشرك قال بن بطال رحمه الله تعالى
# 
# بعد ذكره الحديث ولله تعالى أن يتفضل على عباده بما يشاء لا اعتراض لأحد

عليه قال وهو كقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم لحكيم بن حزام رضي الله عنه أسلمت

على ما أسلفت من خير والله أعلم وأما قول الفقهاء لا يصح من الكافر عبادة

ولو أسلم لم يعتد بها فمرادهم أنه لا يعتد له بها في أحكام الدنيا وليس فيه

تعرض لثواب الآخرة فإن أقدم قائل على التصريح بأنه إذا أسلم لا يثاب عليها

في الآخرة رد قوله بهذه السنة الصحيحة وقد يعتد ببعض أفعال الكفار في أحكام

الدنيا فقد قال الفقهاء إذا وجب على الكافر كفارة ظهار أو غيرها فكفر في

حال كفره أجزأه ذلك وإذا أسلم لم تجب عليه إعادتها واختلف أصحاب الشافعي

رحمه الله فيما إذا أجنب واغتسل في حال كفره ثم أسلم هل تجب عليه إعادة

الغسل أم لا وبالغ بعض أصحابنا فقال يصح من  كل كافر كل طهارة من غسل ووضوء

وتيمم وإذا أسلم صلى بها والله أعلم وأما ما يتعلق بلفظ الباب فقوله (أعتق

مائة رقبة وحمل على مائة بعير) معناه تصدق بها وفيه صالح عن بن شهاب عن

عروة وهؤلاء ثلاثة تابعيون روى بعضهم عن بعض وقد قدمنا أمثال ذلك وفيه حكيم

بن حزام الصحابي رضي الله عنه ومن مناقبه أنه ولد في الكعبة قال بعض

العلماء ولا يعرف أحد شاركه في هذا قال العلماء ومن طرف أخباره أنه عاش

ستين سنة في الجاهلية وستين في الإسلام وأسلم عام الفتح ومات بالمدينة سنة

أربع وخمسين فيكون المراد بالإسلام من حين ظهوره وانتشاره والله أعلم
#

| (باب صدق الإيمان وإخلاصه
# [124] فيه قول عبد الله بن مسعود
# رضي الله عنه (لما نزلت الذين آمنوا ولم يلبسوا إيمانهم بظلم شق ذلك على

أصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وقالوا أينا لا يظلم نفسه فقال رسول

الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ليس هو كما تظنون إنما هو كما قال لقمان لابنه يا

بني لا تشرك بالله ان الشرك لظلم عظيم) هكذا وقع الحديث هنا في صحيح مسلم

ووقع في صحيح البخاري لما نزلت الآية قال أصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه

وسلم أينا لم يظلم نفسه فأنزل الله تعالى ان الشرك لظلم عظيم فهاتان

الروايتان إحداهما تبين الأخرى فيكون لما شق عليهم أنزل الله تعالى إن

الشرك لظلم عظيم وأعلم النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أن الظلم المطلق هناك

المراد به هذا المقيد وهو الشرك فقال لهم النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بعد ذلك

ليس الظلم على إطلاقه وعمومه كما ظننتم إنما هو الشرك كما قال لقمان لابنه

فالصحابة رضي الله عنهم حملوا الظلم على عمومه والمتبادر إلى الأفهام منه

وهو وضع الشيء في غير موضعه وهو مخالفة الشرع فشق عليهم إلى أن أعلمهم

النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بالمراد بهذا الظلم قال الخطابي إنما شق عليهم

لأن ظاهر الظلم الافتيات بحقوق الناس وما ظلموا به  أنفسهم من ارتكاب

المعاصي فظنوا أن المراد معناه الظاهر وأصل الظلم وضع الشيء في غير موضعه

ومن جعل العبادة لغير الله تعالى فهو أظلم الظالمين وفي هذا الحديث جمل من

العلم منها أن المعاصي لا تكون كفرا والله أعلم وأما ما يتعلق بالإسناد

فقول مسلم رحمه الله (حدثنا أبو بكر بن أبي شيبة حدثنا عبد الله بن إدريس

وأبو معاوية ووكيع عن الأعمش عن إبراهيم عن علقمة عن عبد الله)
# 
# هذا إسناد رجاله كوفيون كلهم وحفاظ متقنون في نهاية الجلالة وفيهم ثلاثة

أئمة جلة فقهاء تابعيون بعضهم عن بعض سليمان الأعمش وإبراهيم النخعي وعلقمة

بن قيس وقل اجتماع مثل هذا الذي اجتمع في هذا الإسناد والله أعلم وفيه علي

بن خشرم بفتح الخاء وإسكان الشين المعجمتين وفتح الراء وقد تقدم بيانه في

المقدمة وفيه منجاب بكسر الميم وإسكان النون وبالجيم وآخره باء موحدة وفيه

(قال بن إدريس حدثنيه أولا أبي عن أبان بن تغلب عن الأعمش ثم سمعته منه)

هذا تنبيه منه على علو إسناده هنا فإنه نقص عنه رجلان وسمعه من الأعمش وقد

تقدم مثل هذا في باب الدين النصيحة وتقدم الخلاف في صرف أبان في مقدمة

الكتاب وأن المختار عند المحققين صرفه وتغلب بكسر اللام غير مصروف وفيه

لقمان الحكيم واختلف العلماء في نبوته قال الإمام أبو إسحاق الثعلبي اتفق

العلماء على أنه كان حكيما ولم يكن نبيا إلا عكرمة فإنه قال كان نبيا وتفرد
chapters.anchors:
- Root: خ-ي-ر (khayr)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Goodness, excellence, that which is chosen as preferable; the opposite of evil (sharr).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological usage, denotes what brings benefit in the Hereafter; often contrasted with worldly benefit (nafʿ).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense is intrinsic goodness; metaphorically applied to acts that lead to salvation (najāh).
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clause (al-Sharṭ wa al-Jawāb) — The protasis (in-sharṭ) governs the apodosis, requiring careful parsing of "idhā aslama" to distinguish temporal from conditional nuance.
chapters.translation:
I say: The statement that goodness at the beginning of one's affair is evidence of felicity at its end and excellence of its final outcome — this is the speech of al-Qāḍī (ʿIyāḍ).

Ibn Baṭṭāl and other investigators among the scholars, however, held that the ḥadīth is to be taken upon its apparent meaning (ẓāhir): that when a disbeliever embraces Islam and dies upon Islam, he is rewarded for the good he performed during the state of disbelief. They adduced as evidence the ḥadīth of Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: {«إذا أسلم الكافر فحسن إسلامه كتب الله تعالى له كل حسنة زلفها ومحا عنه كل سيئة زلفها وكان عمله بعد الحسنة بعشر أمثالها إلى سبعمائة ضعف والسيئة بمثلها إلا أن يتجاوز الله سبحانه وتعالى»} — "When a disbeliever embraces Islam and perfects his Islam, Allah the Exalted writes for him every good deed he previously performed and erases from him every evil deed he previously committed; thereafter his good deed is rewarded tenfold up to seven hundredfold, and his evil deed is recorded as its like, unless Allah the Exalted pardons." Al-Dāraquṭnī mentioned this in his Gharāʾib Ḥadīth Mālik, and it was transmitted from him through nine chains, all of which confirmed that when a disbeliever perfects his Islam, every good deed he performed during polytheism (shirk) is written for him in Islam.

Ibn Baṭṭāl, may Allah the Exalted have mercy on him, said after mentioning the ḥadīth: Allah the Exalted has the right to bestow His favor upon His servants as He wills; no one has any objection against Him. He said: This is like his saying, peace and blessings be upon him, to Ḥakīm ibn Ḥizām, may Allah be pleased with him: {«أسلمت على ما أسلفت من خير»} — "You have embraced Islam upon the good you previously sent forth." And Allah knows best.

As for the statement of the jurists (fuqahāʾ) that no act of worship is valid from a disbeliever, and that if he embraces Islam it is not reckoned for him — their intent is that it is not reckoned for him regarding the rulings of this world (aḥkām al-dunyā), and there is nothing in this touching upon the reward of the Hereafter. For if anyone were so bold as to explicitly declare that if he embraces Islam he is not rewarded for it in the Hereafter, his statement would be refuted by this authentic Sunnah.

Indeed, some actions of disbelievers may be reckoned in the rulings of this world. For the jurists have said: When an expiation (kaffārah) for ẓihār or other matters becomes obligatory upon a disbeliever, and he performs the expiation during his state of disbelief, that suffices for him; and if he embraces Islam, he is not required to repeat it. The companions of al-Shāfiʿī, may Allah have mercy on him, differed concerning the case of one who becomes ritually impure (junub) and performs the major ablution (ghusl) during his state of disbelief, then embraces Islam — is he required to repeat the ghusl or not? Some of our companions went to the extreme and said: Every ablution — whether major (ghusl), minor (wuḍūʾ), or dry ablution (tayammum) — is valid from every disbeliever, and when he embraces Islam he may pray with it. And Allah knows best.

As for what pertains to the wording of the chapter heading — his saying (may Allah be pleased with him): "He freed one hundred slaves and carried one hundred camels" — its meaning is that he gave them in charity (ṣadaqah). In this chain there is Ṣāliḥ, from Ibn Shihāb, from ʿUrwah — these three are Successors (tābiʿūn), each transmitting from the other, and we have already mentioned similar examples. In it also is Ḥakīm ibn Ḥizām, the Companion, may Allah be pleased with him. Among his merits is that he was born inside the Kaʿbah. Some scholars said: No one is known to have shared this distinction with him. The scholars said: Among the remarkable reports concerning him is that he lived sixty years in the Jāhiliyyah and sixty years in Islam; he embraced Islam in the Year of the Conquest (of Mecca), and died in Medina in the year fifty-four (AH). Thus the intent of "Islam" here is from the time of its emergence and spread. And Allah knows best.

---

| (Chapter: The Truthfulness of Faith and Its Sincerity)

[124] In it is the saying of ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd, may Allah be pleased with him: "When the verse {«الذين آمنوا ولم يلبسوا إيمانهم بظلم»} — 'Those who believe and do not mix their faith with wrongdoing' — was revealed, this weighed heavily upon the companions of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, and they said: 'Which of us does not wrong himself?' So the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: 'It is not as you suppose. Rather, it is as Luqmān said to his son: {«يا بني لا تشرك بالله ان الشرك لظلم عظيم»} — "O my son, do not associate partners with Allah; indeed, polytheism is a great wrongdoing."'" Thus it occurred in this place in Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim.
