And in Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī it occurred: "When the verse was revealed, the companions of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: 'Which of us has not wronged himself?' Then Allah the Exalted revealed: {«ان الشرك لظلم عظيم»} — 'Indeed, polytheism is a great wrongdoing.'" These two narrations — each clarifies the other. Thus, when it weighed heavily upon them, Allah the Exalted revealed that polytheism is a great wrongdoing, and the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, informed them that the absolute wrongdoing (al-ẓulm al-muṭlaq) mentioned there intended this restricted meaning (al-muqayyad), namely polytheism. So the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said to them afterward: The wrongdoing is not upon its absoluteness and generality as you supposed; rather, it is polytheism, as Luqmān said to his son.

Thus the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, had interpreted wrongdoing according to its generality and what immediately springs to the mind from it — namely, placing a thing in other than its proper place, which is contravening the Sacred Law (mukhālafat al-sharʿ) — and this weighed heavily upon them until the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, informed them of the intended meaning of this wrongdoing. Al-Khaṭṭābī said: It weighed heavily upon them only because the apparent sense of wrongdoing is encroaching upon the rights of people, and what they had wronged themselves with was committing acts of disobedience — so they supposed that the intended meaning was its apparent sense. The origin of wrongdoing (ẓulm) is placing a thing in other than its proper place; and whoever directs worship to other than Allah the Exalted is the most unjust of the wrongdoers (aẓlam al-ẓālimīn).

In this ḥadīth there are several bodies of knowledge. Among them: acts of disobedience (maʿāṣī) do not constitute disbelief (kufr). And Allah knows best.

As for what pertains to the chain of transmission — the saying of Muslim, may Allah have mercy on him: "Abū Bakr ibn Abī Shaybah narrated to us: ʿAbdullāh ibn Idrīs, Abū Muʿāwiyah, and Wakīʿ narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash, from Ibrāhīm, from ʿAlqamah, from ʿAbdullāh" — this is a chain whose narrators are all Kūfans, all precise memorizers (ḥuffāẓ) of the utmost dignity. Among them are three eminent imams, jurists among the Successors, each transmitting from the other: Sulaymān al-Aʿmash, Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī, and ʿAlqamah ibn Qays. Rare is the gathering of such a constellation as assembled in this chain. And Allah knows best.

In it also is ʿAlī ibn Khashram — with fatḥah on the khāʾ, sukūn on the shīn, both unpointed letters, and fatḥah on the rāʾ — and its clarification has already preceded in the Introduction. In it is also Minjāb — with kasrah on the mīm, sukūn on the nūn, then jīm, and its final letter is an unpointed bāʾ. In it is his saying: "Ibn Idrīs said: 'My father narrated it to me at first, from Abān ibn Taghlib, from al-Aʿmash; then I heard it from him (al-Aʿmash) directly.'" This is an indication from him of the elevation (ʿulūw) of his chain here, for he omitted two narrators from it and heard it directly from al-Aʿmash. Similar to this has already preceded in the Chapter of Religion is Sincerity (Bāb al-Dīn al-Naṣīḥah). The disagreement concerning the declension of Abān has already preceded in the Introduction of the Book — namely, that the preferred view among the investigators is its declension. Taghlib — with kasrah on the lām — is non-declinable (ghayr munṣarif).

In it also is Luqmān the Wise. The scholars differed concerning his prophethood. Imam Abū Isḥāq al-Thaʿlabī said: The scholars agreed that he was a wise man (ḥakīm) and was not a prophet — except ʿIkrimah, for he said he was a prophet, and he was alone in this view.

chapters.title_en: Section 139 — The Explanation of Allah's Pardon for Whisperings of the Soul and Passing Thoughts, and the Clarification that He Only Charges a Soul with What It Can Bear
chapters.arabic_text:
بهذا القول وأما بن لقمان الذي قال له لا تشرك بالله فقيل اسمه أنعم ويقال

مشكم والله أعلم

| (باب بيان تجاوز الله تعالى عن حديث النفس (والخواطر 
# بالقلب إذا لم تستقر وبيان أنه سبحانه وتعالى لم يكلف إلا ما يطاق)

(وبيان حكم الهم بالحسنة وبالسيئة)
# [127] أما أسانيد الباب ولغاته ففيه أمية بن بسطام العيشي فبسطام بكسر

الباء على المشهور وحكى صاحب المطالع أيضا فتحها والعيشي بالشين المعجمة

وقد قدمت ضبط هذا كله مع بيان)
# 
# الخلاف في صرف بسطام وفيه قوله (عن أبي هريرة  قال لما نزلت على رسول الله

صلى الله عليه وسلم لله ما في السماوات وما في الأرض وإن تبدوا ما في

أنفسكم أو تخفوه يحاسبكم به الله فيغفر لمن يشاء ويعذب من يشاء والله على

كل شيء قدير قال فاشتد ذلك) إنما أعاد لفظة قال لطول الكلام فإن أصل الكلام

لما نزلت اشتد فلما طال حسن إعادة لفظة قال وقد تقدم مثل هذا في موضعين من

هذا الكتاب وذكرت ذلك مبينا وأنه جاء مثله في القرآن العزيز في قوله تعالى

أيعدكم أنكم إذا متم وكنتم ترابا وعظاما أنكم مخرجون فأعاد أنكم وقوله ولما

جاءهم كتاب من عند الله مصدق لما معهم إلى قوله فلما جاءهم والله أعلم وفيه

قوله تعالى لا نفرق بين أحد من رسله لا نفرق بينهم في الإيمان فنؤمن ببعضهم

ونكفر ببعض كما فعله أهل الكتابين بل نؤمن بجميعهم وأحد في هذا الموضع

بمعنى الجمع ولهذا دخلت فيه بين ومثله قوله تعالى فما منكم من أحد عنه

حاجزين وفيه قوله (فأنزل الله تعالى في إثرها) هو بفتح الهمزة والثاء وبكسر

الهمزة مع إسكان الثاء لغتان
# 
# وفيه محمد بن عبيد الغبري بضم الغين المعجمة وفتح الباء الموحدة منسوب

إلى بني غبر وقد قدمنا
# 
# بيانه فى المقدمة وفيه أبوعوانة واسمه الوضاح بن عبد الله
# [127] وفيه قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (إن الله تجاوز لأمتى ماحدثت به

أنفسها) ضبط العلماء أنفسها بالنصب والرفع وهما ظاهران إلا أن النصب أظهر

وأشهر قال القاضي عياض أنفسها بالنصب ويدل عليه قوله إن أحدنا يحدث نفسه

قال قال الطحاوي وأهل اللغة يقولون أنفسها بالرفع يريدون بغير اختيارها كما

قال الله تعالى ونعلم ماتوسوس به نفسه والله اعلم وفيه أبو الزناد عن

الأعرج أما أبو الزناد فاسمه عبد الله بن ذكوان كنيته أبو عبد الرحمن وأما

أبو الزناد فلقب غلب عليه وكان يغضب منه وأما الأعرج فعبد الرحمن بن هرمز

وهذان وإن كانا مشهورين وقد تقدم بيانهما إلا أنه
# 
# قد تخفى أسماؤهما على بعض الناظرين  في الكتاب وقوله سبحانه وتعالى (إنما

تركها من جراي) هو بفتح الجيم وتشديد الراء وبالمد والقصر لغتان معناه من

أجلي وقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (إذا أحسن أحدكم إسلامه فكل حسنة يعملها

تكتب بعشر أمثالها وكل سيئة يعملها تكتب بمثلها) معنى أحسن إسلامه أسلم

إسلاما حقيقيا وليس كإسلام المنافقين وقد تقدم بيان هذا وفيه
# 
# أبو خالد الأحمر هو سليمان بن حيان بالمثناة تقدم بيانه وفيه شيبان بن

فروخ بفتح الفاء وبالخاء المعجمة وهو غير مصروف لكونه عجميا علما وقد تقدم

بيانه وفيه أبو رجاء العطاردي اسمه عمران بن تيم وقيل بن ملحان وقيل بن عبد

الله أدرك زمن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ولم يره وأسلم عام الفتح وعاش مائة

وعشرين سنة وقيل مائة وثمانيا وعشرين سنة وقيل مائة وثلاثين سنة وأما فقه

أحاديث الباب ومعانيها فكثيرة وأنا أختصر مقاصدها إن شاء الله تعالى فقوله

لما نزلت لله ما في السماوات وما في الأرض وإن تبدوا ما في أنفسكم أو تخفوه

يحاسبكم به الله فاشتد ذلك على الصحابة رضي الله عنهم وقالوا لا نطيقها قال

الإمام أبو عبد الله المازري رحمه الله يحتمل أن يكون اشفاقهم وقولهم لا

نطيقها لكونها اعتقدوا أنهم يؤاخذون بما لا قدرة لهم على دفعه من الخواطر

التي لا تكتسب فلهذا رأوه من قبل ما لا يطاق وعندنا أن تكليف ما لا يطاق

جائز عقلا واختلف هل وقع التعبد به في الشريعة أم لا والله أعلم وأما قوله

فلما فعلوا ذلك نسخها الله تعالى فأنزل الله تعالى لا يكلف الله نفسا إلا

وسعها فقال المازري رحمه الله في تسمية هذا نسخا نظر لأنه إنما يكون نسخا

إذا تعذر البناء ولم يمكن رد إحدى الآيتين إلى الأخرى وقوله تعالى وإن

تبدوا ما فى أنفسكم أو تخفوه عموم يصح أن يشتمل على ما يملك من الخواطر دون

ما لا يملك فتكون الآية الأخرى مخصصة إلا أن يكون قد فهمت الصحابة بقرينة

الحال أنه تقرر تعبدهم بما لا يملك  من الخواطر فيكون حينئذ لنه رفع ثابت

مستقر هذا كلام المازري قال القاضي عياض لا وجه لإبعاد النسخ في هذه القضية

فان روايها قد روى فيها النسخ ونص عليه لفظا ومعنى بأمر النبي صلى الله

عليه وسلم لهم بالإيمان والسمع والطاعة لما أعلمهم الله
# 
# تعالى من مؤاخذته إياهم فلما فعلوا ذلك وألقى الله تعالى الايمان فى

قلبوبهم وذلت بالاستسلام لذلك ألسنتهم كما نص في هذا الحديث رفع الحرج عنهم

ونسخ هذا التكليف وطريق علم النسخ إنما هو بالخبر عنه أو بالتاريخ وهما
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ح د ث (ḥ-d-th)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Origination, occurrence; a novel event; speech that arises anew.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Ḥadīth al-nafs denotes the passing thought that originates in the soul without deliberate acquisition (iktisāb).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense is "that which the soul newly conceives"; metaphorically extended to involuntary whisperings (waswās) that do not settle.
- Sībawayh Rule: Naṣb vs. Rafʿ in circumstantial complements (ḥāl) — the accusative (naṣb) of "anfusahā" is preferred as the object of "ḥaddathat," while the nominative (rafʿ) treats it as an agentive phrase meaning "without its choice."
chapters.translation:
I say: With this statement [the preceding discussion concludes]. As for Ibn Luqmān to whom it was said, "Do not associate partners with Allah," it is said his name was Anʿam, and it is also said Mushkam — and Allah knows best.

| (Chapter: The Explanation of Allah's Transcendent Pardon for the Whisperings of the Soul and Passing Thoughts within the Heart When They Do Not Settle, and the Explanation that He, Glorified and Exalted, Has Only Charged a Soul with What It Can Bear)

(And the Explanation of the Ruling Concerning the Intention toward a Good Deed and toward an Evil Deed)

[127] As for the chains of transmission (asānīd) of this chapter and its lexical points: Among them is Umayyah ibn Bisṭām al-ʿAyshī. Bisṭām is with kasrah on the bāʾ according to the well-known pronunciation, and the author of al-Maṭāliʿ also reported its fatḥah. Al-ʿAyshī is with the unpointed shīn (muʿjamah). I have already presented the precise voweling of all this along with the explanation of the disagreement concerning the diptotic status (ṣarf) of Bisṭām.

Also in it is his statement (from Abū Hurayrah, who said): "When there was revealed upon the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, {«To Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth. And whether you disclose what is in yourselves or conceal it, Allah will call you to account for it. Then He forgives whom He wills and punishes whom He wills, and Allah is over all things competent»} — he said: 'This was severe upon them.'" He (the narrator) only repeated the word "qāla" (he said) due to the length of the discourse. For the original form of the speech was: "When it was revealed, it became severe." When the speech became lengthy, it was deemed good to repeat the word "qāla." This has already occurred in two places in this book, and I have mentioned it with clarification — and that the like of it occurs in the Mighty Qurʾān in His statement, the Exalted: {«Does he promise you that when you have died and become dust and bones that you will be brought forth?»} — so He repeated "that you" (annakum); and His statement: {«And when there came to them a Book from Allah confirming what was with them»} up to His statement {«then when there came to them»}. And Allah knows best.

Also in it is His statement, the Exalted: {«We do not differentiate between any of His messengers»} — i.e., we do not differentiate between them in faith, so that we believe in some and disbelieve in others, as the People of the Two Books did. Rather, we believe in all of them. And "aḥad" (any one) in this place carries the meaning of the plural, and for this reason "bayna" (between) entered upon it. The like of it is His statement, the Exalted: {«So there is not among you any one who could shield him»} (ḥājizīn).

Also in it is his statement: "So Allah, the Exalted, revealed in its wake (fi ithrihā)" — this is with fatḥah on the hamzah and the thāʾ, and with kasrah on the hamzah with sukūn on the thāʾ — two dialects.

Also in it is Muḥammad ibn ʿUbayd al-Ghubrī — with ḍammah on the unpointed ghayn and fatḥah on the pointed bāʾ, attributed to the Banū Ghubr. I have already presented its explanation in the Introduction.

Also in it is Abū ʿAwānah, whose name is al-Waḍḍāḥ ibn ʿAbdillāh.

[127] Also in it is his statement, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: "Verily Allah has pardoned for my community what their souls whisper to them (mā ḥaddathat bihi anfusuhā)." The scholars have vowelled "anfusuhā" with naṣb (accusative) and with rafʿ (nominative), and both are evident — except that the naṣb is more evident and more famous. Al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ said: "Anfusahā" is with naṣb, and evidence for it is his statement: "Verily one of us speaks to his soul (yuḥaddithu nafsahu)." He said: Al-Ṭaḥāwī and the people of language say "anfusuhā" with rafʿ, meaning "without its choice," just as Allah, the Exalted, said: {«And We know what his soul whispers to him»} (tuwāsawisu bihi nafsuhu). And Allah knows best.

Also in it is Abū al-Zinād from al-Aʿraj. As for Abū al-Zinād, his name is ʿAbdullāh ibn Dhakwān, and his kunyah is Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān. As for "Abū al-Zinād," it is a nickname that overcame him, and he used to be angered by it. As for al-Aʿraj, he is ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Hurmuz. And these two, although they are well-known and their explanation has already been presented, yet their names may remain hidden to some of those who look into the book.

And his statement, Glorified and Exalted be He: "I only left it for my sake (min jarāy)" — it is with fatḥah on the jīm and tashdīd on the rāʾ, and with madd and qaṣr — two dialects — meaning "for my sake (min ajlī)."

And his statement, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: "When one of you perfects his Islam (aḥsana islāmahu), then every good deed he performs is written for him as ten times its like, and every evil deed he performs is written for him as its like" — the meaning of "perfects his Islam" is that he submits with a genuine submission (islāman ḥaqīqiyyan), not like the submission of the hypocrites. The explanation of this has already been presented.

Also in it is Abū Khālid al-Aḥmar — he is Sulaymān ibn Ḥayyān, with the mathnāh (tāʾ); his explanation has been presented. Also in it is Shaybān ibn Farrukh — with fatḥah on the fāʾ and with the unpointed khāʾ — and he is diptotic (ghayr maṣrūf) because he is a non-Arab proper name; his explanation has been presented. Also in it is Abū Rajāʾ al-ʿAṭāridī — his name is ʿImrān ibn Taym, and it is said Ibn Milḥān, and it is said Ibn ʿAbdillāh. He reached the time of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, but did not see him; he embraced Islam in the Year of the Conquest, and lived one hundred and twenty years — and it is said one hundred and twenty-eight years, and it is said one hundred and thirty years.

As for the jurisprudence (fiqh) of the ḥadīths of this chapter and their meanings, they are many, and I shall summarize their objectives, Allah the Exalted willing. His statement: "When there was revealed {«To Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth. And whether you disclose what is in yourselves or conceal it, Allah will call you to account for it»} — this was severe upon the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, and they said: 'We cannot bear it.'"

The Imām Abū ʿAbdillāh al-Māzarī, may Allah have mercy on him, said: It is possible that their apprehension and their statement "We cannot bear it" was because they believed they would be held to account for what they had no power to repel — namely, the passing thoughts (khawāṭir) that are not acquired (lā tuktasab). For this reason they saw it as belonging to the category of what cannot be borne. And in our view, the charging of what cannot be borne (taklīf mā lā yuṭāq) is intellectually permissible (jāʾiz ʿaqlan), and there is disagreement as to whether worship was actually obligated by it in the Sacred Law or not. And Allah knows best.

As for his statement: "Then when they did that, Allah abrogated it (nasakhahā), and Allah, the Exalted, revealed: {«Allah does not charge a soul except with its capacity»}" — al-Māzarī, may Allah have mercy on him, said: There is consideration (naẓar) in calling this "abrogation" (naskh), because abrogation only occurs when construction upon [the earlier verse] becomes impossible and one of the two verses cannot be reconciled with the other. And His statement, the Exalted: {«And whether you disclose what is in yourselves or conceal it»} is a general statement (ʿumūm) that may properly encompass what one possesses of passing thoughts, excluding what one does not possess — so the other verse would be a specification (takhṣīṣ) of it. Unless it be that the Companions understood, by the indication of the situation (qarīnat al-ḥāl), that they were definitively obligated regarding what they do not possess of passing thoughts — in which case it would be the lifting of an established and settled obligation. This is the speech of al-Māzarī.

Al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ said: There is no basis for dismissing abrogation in this matter, for its narrator has narrated the abrogation in it and explicitly stated it, in wording and in meaning, by the command of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, to them to believe and to hear and obey when Allah, the Exalted, informed them of His taking them to account. Then when they did that, and Allah, the Exalted, cast faith into their hearts, and their tongues were humbled by submission to that — as explicitly stated in this ḥadīth — the burden was lifted from them, and this obligation was abrogated. And the path to knowing abrogation is only through report concerning it (al-khabar ʿanhu) or through historical dating (al-tārīkh) — and both are [present here].

chapters.title_en: The Question of Abrogation (Naskh) in the Verse of Inner Concealment, and the Recording of Inner Resolves (Hamam) and Intentions (ʿAzm)
chapters.arabic_text:
مجتمعان في هذه الآية قال القاضي وقول المازري إنما يكون نسخا إذا تعذر

البناء كلام صحيح فيما لم يرد فيه النص بالنسخ فإن ورد وقفنا عنده لكن

اختلف أصحاب الأصول في قول الصحابي رضي الله عنه نسخ كذا بكذا هل يكون حجة

يثبت بها النسخ أم لا يثبت بمجرد قوله وهو قول القاضي أبي بكر والمحققين

منهم لأنه قد يكون قوله هذا عن اجتهاده وتأويله فلا يكون نسخا حتى ينقل ذلك

عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وقد اختلف الناس في هذه الآية فأكثر المفسرين

من الصحابة ومن بعدهم على ما تقدم فيها من النسخ وأنكره بعض المتأخرين قال

لأنه خبر ولا يدخل النسخ الأخبار وليس كما قال هذا المتأخر فإنه وإن كان

خبرا فهو خبر عن تكليف ومؤاخذة بما تكن النفوس والتعبد بما أمرهم النبي صلى

الله عليه وسلم في الحديث بذلك وأن يقولوا سمعنا وأطعنا وهذه أقوال وأعمال

اللسان والقلب ثم نسخ ذلك عنهم برفع الحرج والمؤاخذة وروي عن بعض المفسرين

أن معنى النسخ هنا إزالة ما وقع في قلوبهم من الشدة والفرق من هذا الأمر

فأزيل عنهم بالآية الأخرى واطمأنت نفوسهم وهذا القائل يرى أنهم لم يلزموا

مالا يطيقون لكن ما يشق عليهم من التحفظ من خواطر النفس وإخلاص الباطن

فأشفقوا أن يكلفوا من ذلك مالا يطيقون فأزيل عنهم الإشفاق وبين أنهم لم

يكلفوا الا وسعهم وعلى هذا لاحجة فيه لجواز تكليف ما لا يطاق  إذ ليس فيه نص

على تكليفه واحتج بعضهم باستعاذتهم منه بقوله تعالى
# 
# ولا تحملنا مالا طاقة لنا به ولا يستعيذون إلا مما يجوز التكليف به وأجاب

عن ذلك بعضهم بأن معنى ذلك مالا نطيقه إلا بمشقة وذهب بعضهم إلى أن الآية

محكمة في إخفاء اليقين والشك للمؤمنين والكافرين فيغفر للمؤمنين ويعذب

الكافرين هذا آخر كلام القاضي عياض رحمه الله وذكر الإمام الواحدي رحمه

الله الاختلاف في نسخ الآية ثم قال والمحققون يختارون أن تكون الآية محكمة

غير منسوخة والله أعلم وأما قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (إن الله تجاوز لأمتي

ما حدثت به أنفسها ما لم يتكلموا أو يعملوا به)
# [128] وفي الحديث الآخر (إذا هم عبدي بسيئة فلا تكتبوا عليه فإن عملها

فاكتبوها سيئة وإذا هم بحسنة فلم يعملها فاكتبوها حسنة فإن عملها فاكتبوها

عشرا) وفي الحديث الآخر (في الحسنة إلى سبعمائة ضعف) وفي الآخر (في السيئة

إنما تركها من جراي) فقال الإمام المازري رحمه الله مذهب القاضي أبي بكر بن

الطيب أن من عزم على المعصية بقلبه ووطن نفسه عليها أثم في اعتقاده وعزمه

ويحمل ما وقع في هذه الأحاديث وأمثالها على أن ذلك فيمن لم يوطن نفسه على

المعصية وإنما مر ذلك بفكره من غير استقرار ويسمى هذا هما ويفرق بين الهم

والعزم هذا مذهب القاضي أبي بكر وخالفه كثير من الفقهاء والمحدثين وأخذوا

بظاهر الحديث قال القاضي عياض رحمه الله عامة السلف وأهل العلم من الفقهاء

والمحدثين على ما ذهب إليه القاضي أبو بكر للأحاديث الدالة على المؤاخذة

بأعمال القلوب لكنهم قالوا إن هذا العزم يكتب سيئة وليست السيئة التي هم

بها لكونه لم يعملها وقطعه عنها قاطع غير خوف الله تعالى والإنابة لكن نفس

الإصرار والعزم معصية فتكتب معصية فإذا عملها كتبت معصية ثانية فإن تركها

خشية لله تعالى كتبت حسنة كما في الحديث إنما تركها من جراي فصار تركه لها

لخوف الله تعالى ومجاهدته نفسه الأمارة بالسوء فى ذلك وعصيانه هواه فأما

الهم الذي لا  يكتب فهي الخواطر التي لا توطن النفس عليها ولا يصحبها عقد

ولا نية وعزم وذكر بعض المتكلمين خلافا فيما إذا تركها لغير خوف الله تعالى

بل لخوف الناس هل تكتب حسنة قال لا لأنه إنما حمله على تركها الحياء وهذا

ضعيف لا وجه له هذا آخر كلام القاضي وهو ظاهر حسن لا مزيد عليه وقد تظاهرت

نصوص الشرع بالمؤاخذة بعزم القلب المستقر ومن ذلك قوله تعالى إن الذين

يحبون أن تشيع الفاحشة في الذين آمنوا لهم عذاب أليم الآية وقوله تعالى

اجتنبوا كثيرا من الظن إن بعض الظن إثم
# 
# والآيات في هذا كثيرة وقد تظاهرت نصوص الشرع وإجماع العلماء على تحريم

الحسد واحتقار المسلمين وإرادة المكروه بهم وغير ذلك من أعمال القلوب

وعزمها والله أعلم وأما قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (ولن يهلك على الله إلا

هالك) فقال القاضي عياض رحمه الله معناه من حتم هلاكه وسدت عليه أبواب

الهدى مع سعة رحمة الله تعالى وكرمه وجعله السيئة حسنة إذا لم يعملها وإذا

عملها واحدة والحسنة إذا لم يعملها واحدة وإذا عملها عشرا إلى سبعمائة ضعف

إلى أضعاف كثيرة فمن حرم هذه السعة وفاته هذا الفضل وكثرت سيئاته حتى غلبت

مع أنها أفراد حسناته مع أنها متضاعفة فهو الهالك المحروم والله أعلم قال

الإمام أبو جعفر الطحاوي رحمه الله في هذه الأحاديث دليل على أن الحفظة

يكتبون أعمال القلوب وعقدها خلافا لمن قال إنها لا تكتب إلا الأعمال

الظاهرة والله أعلم وأما قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم إلى سبعمائة ضعف إلى

أضعاف كثيرة ففيه تصريح بالمذهب الصحيح المختار عند العلماء أن التضعيف لا
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ن-س-خ (n-s-kh)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Erasure, cancellation, replacement; the removal of one ruling by another.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Technical abrogation of a divine command by a later revelation, contingent on textual evidence.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal in legal contexts; metaphorical when applied to the removal of hardship or fear.
- Root: ه-م-م (h-m-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Inner inclination, fleeting thought, or resolve that does not settle.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): A passing notion in the heart, distinct from settled intention (ʿazm).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for transient thought; metaphorical for firm resolve when accompanied by determination.
- Root: ع-ز-م (ʿ-z-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Firm determination, binding resolution.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Settled intention of the heart that incurs moral accountability.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for decisive will; contrasted with mere passing thought.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional and Exceptive Constructions (al-sharṭ wa al-istithnāʾ) — Parsing of "if... then..." clauses and exceptions (e.g., "unless they speak or act") to distinguish legal scope.
chapters.translation:
I say: The scholars are in agreement regarding this verse, as the Qāḍī (ʿIyāḍ) noted. The statement of al-Māzarī — that abrogation (naskh) only occurs when reconciliation is impossible — is sound speech concerning that for which no explicit text of abrogation has been reported. But if such a text is reported, we halt at it. However, the scholars of uṣūl (legal theory) differed concerning the saying of a Companion (may God be pleased with him), "Such-and-such was abrogated by such-and-such": is it an authoritative proof (ḥujjah) by which abrogation is established, or is it not established by his mere statement? The latter is the view of Qāḍī Abū Bakr (al-Bāqillānī) and the verifying scholars among them, because his statement may stem from his own juristic reasoning (ijtihād) and interpretation, and thus it is not abrogation unless it is transmitted from the Prophet (peace be upon him).

The people have differed concerning this verse. The majority of the exegetes (mufassirūn) among the Companions and those after them held the aforementioned view of its abrogation. But some later scholars denied this, saying: "It is a report (khabar), and abrogation does not enter into reports." This later scholar is not correct, for although it is a report, it is a report concerning obligation (taklīf) and accountability for what the souls conceal, and concerning the devotion to what the Prophet (peace be upon him) commanded them in the hadith — namely, that they should say, "We hear and we obey" — and these are statements and actions of the tongue and the heart. Then that was abrogated for them by the removal of hardship and accountability.

It is narrated from some exegetes that the meaning of "abrogation" here is the removal of what had fallen into their hearts of severity and fear concerning this matter, which was removed from them by the other verse, and their souls became tranquil. This proponent holds that they were not obligated with what they could not bear, but rather with what was burdensome upon them — namely, guarding against the promptings of the soul and sincerity of the inner self. They feared that they might be charged with more than they could bear, so the fear was removed from them, and it was made clear that they were not charged except with their capacity. On this basis, there is no proof in it for the permissibility of charging one with what cannot be borne, since there is no explicit text therein for such charging.

Some of them adduced as proof their seeking refuge from it in His saying (Exalted is He): {«وَلَا تُحَمِّلْنَا مَا لَا طَاقَةَ لَنَا بِهِ»} ("And do not burden us with what we have no capacity to bear") — and they do not seek refuge except from what is permissible to be charged with. Another group answered this by saying that its meaning is "what we cannot bear except with hardship." Yet another group held that the verse is un-abrogated (muḥkamah) concerning the concealment of certainty and doubt for believers and disbelievers: the believers are forgiven, and the disbelievers are punished.

This is the end of the speech of Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ (may God have mercy on him). Imām al-Wāḥidī (may God have mercy on him) mentioned the disagreement concerning the abrogation of the verse, then said: "The verifying scholars choose that the verse is un-abrogated and not abrogated." And God knows best.

As for his saying (peace be upon him): "Indeed God has pardoned my community for what their souls whisper to them, as long as they do not speak or act upon it" — and in the other hadith: "When My servant intends (hamma) a sin, do not record it against him; if he commits it, record it as one sin. And when he intends a good deed and does not perform it, record it as one good deed; if he performs it, record it as ten" — and in the other hadith: "For a good deed, up to seven hundredfold" — and in the other: "Concerning a sin, he only abandoned it for My sake" — Imām al-Māzarī (may God have mercy on him) said: The doctrine of Qāḍī Abū Bakr ibn al-Ṭayyib is that whoever resolves upon disobedience with his heart and settles his soul upon it is sinful in his conviction and resolve. He interprets what occurs in these hadiths and their like as applying to one who has not settled his soul upon disobedience, but rather it merely passed through his thought without stability. This is called "intention" (hamm), and a distinction is made between hamm and ʿazm (firm resolve). This is the doctrine of Qāḍī Abū Bakr.

Many jurists (fuqahāʾ) and hadith scholars opposed him, taking the apparent meaning of the hadith. Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ (may God have mercy on him) said: The generality of the Salaf and the people of knowledge among the jurists and hadith scholars are upon what Qāḍī Abū Bakr held, due to the hadiths indicating accountability for the actions of the hearts. However, they said: This resolve (ʿazm) is recorded as a sin, but it is not the sin he intended, because he did not commit it, and what cut him off from it was not the fear of God or repentance, but rather the very persistence and resolve itself is a disobedience, so it is recorded as a disobedience. If he commits it, a second disobedience is recorded. If he abandons it out of fear of God (Exalted is He), a good deed is recorded, as in the hadith: "He only abandoned it for My sake." Thus his abandonment of it became for the fear of God and his striving against his soul that commands evil, and his disobeying his caprice.

As for the hamm that is not recorded, it is the passing thoughts (khaṭarāt) upon which the soul does not settle, and which are not accompanied by a binding covenant, intention, or resolve. Some theologians mentioned a disagreement concerning one who abandons a sin for other than the fear of God — rather, for fear of people — whether it is recorded as a good deed. He said: No, because what drove him to abandon it was shame (ḥayāʾ). This is weak and has no basis.

This is the end of the Qāḍī's speech, and it is apparent, sound, and nothing further can be added to it. The texts of the Sacred Law have concurred upon accountability for the settled resolve of the heart. Among that is His saying (Exalted is He): {«إِنَّ الَّذِينَ يُحِبُّونَ أَنْ تَشِيعَ الْفَاحِشَةُ فِي الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لَهُمْ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ»} ("Indeed, those who love that immorality should spread among those who believe — for them is a painful punishment") — and His saying (Exalted is He): {«اجْتَنِبُوا كَثِيرًا مِنَ الظَّنِّ إِنَّ بَعْضَ الظَّنِّ إِثْمٌ»} ("Avoid much suspicion; indeed, some suspicion is sin"). The verses concerning this are numerous. The texts of the Sacred Law and the consensus of the scholars have concurred upon the prohibition of envy (ḥasad), holding Muslims in contempt, desiring harm for them, and other such actions of the hearts and their resolves. And God knows best.

As for his saying (peace be upon him): "And none will perish before God except a perisher" — Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ (may God have mercy on him) said: Its meaning is: one whose perdition is decreed and for whom the doors of guidance are sealed, despite the vastness of God's mercy and generosity, and His making a sin — if not committed — as nothing, and if committed, as one; and a good deed — if not performed — as one, and if performed, as ten up to seven hundredfold, up to many multiples. Whoever is deprived of this vastness, and this bounty eludes him, and his sins multiply until they overcome — even though his good deeds are individual while being multiplied — he is the perished, the deprived. And God knows best.

Imām Abū Jaʿfar al-Ṭaḥāwī (may God have mercy on him) said concerning these hadiths: They are proof that the recording angels (ḥafażah) write down the actions of the hearts and their firm resolves, contrary to those who said that only outward actions are recorded. And God knows best.

As for his saying (peace be upon him): "Up to seven hundredfold, up to many multiples" — therein is an explicit statement of the sound and chosen doctrine among the scholars that the multiplication (taḍʿīf) is not...

chapters.title_en: The Multiplicity of Rewards, Divine Lightening of Burdens, and the Reality of Whisperings (Waswāsah) in Faith
chapters.arabic_text:
يقف على سبعمائة ضعف وحكى أبو الحسن أقضى القضاة الماوردي عن بعض العلماء

أن التضعيف لا يتجاوز سبعمائة ضعف وهو غلط لهذا الحديث والله أعلم وفي

أحاديث الباب بيان ما أكرم الله تعالى به هذه الأمة زادها الله شرفا وخففه

عنهم مما كان على غيرهم من الإصر وهو الثقل والمشاق وبيان ما كانت الصحابة

رضي الله عنهم  عليه من المسارعة إلى الانقياد لأحكام الشرع قال أبو إسحاق

الزجاج هذا الدعاء الذي في قوله تعالى ربنا لا تؤاخذنا ان نسينا أو أخطأنا

إلى آخر السورة أخبر الله تعالى به عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم والمؤمنين

وجعله في كتابه ليكون دعاء من يأتي بعد النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم والصحابة

رضي الله عنهم فهو من الدعاء الذين ينبغي أن يحفظ ويدعى به كثيرا قال

الزجاج وقوله تعالى فانصرنا على القوم الكافرين أي أظهرنا عليهم في الحجة

والحرب وإظهار الدين وسيأتي في كتاب الصلاة من هذا الكتاب الصحيح أن رسول

الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال من قرأ الآيتين من آخر سورة البقرة في ليلة

كفتاه قيل كفتاه
# 
# من قيام تلك الليلة وقيل كفتاه المكروه فيها والله أعلم

| (باب بيان الوسوسة في الإيمان وما يقوله من وجدها
# [132] فيه أبو هريرة رضي الله عنه (قال جاء ناس من أصحاب النبي صلى الله

عليه وسلم فسألوه إنا نجد في أنفسنا ما يتعاظم أحدنا أن يتكلم به قال وقد

وجدتموه قالوا نعم قال ذاك صريح الإيمان) وفي الرواية الأخرى
# [133] (سئل النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم عن الوسوسة فقال تلك محض الإيمان)
# [134] وفى الحديث الآخر (لا يزال الناس يتساءلون حتى يقال هذا خلق الله

الخلق فمن خلق الله فمن وجد من ذلك شيئا فليقل آمنت بالله) وفي)
# 
# الرواية الأخرى (فليقل آمنت بالله ورسله) وفي الرواية الأخرى (يأتي

الشيطان أحدكم فيقول من خلق كذا وكذا حتى يقول له من خلق ربك فإذا بلغ ذلك

فليستعذ بالله ولينته) أما معاني الأحاديث وفقهها فقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم

ذلك صريح الإيمان ومحض الإيمان معناه استعظامكم الكلام به هو صريح الإيمان

فإن استعظام هذا وشدة الخوف منه ومن النطق به فضلا عن اعتقاده إنما يكون

لمن استكمل الإيمان استكمالا محققا وانتفت عنه الريبة والشكوك واعلم أن

الرواية الثانية وإن لم يكن فيها ذكر الاستعظام فهو مراد وهي مختصرة من

الرواية الأولى ولهذا قدم مسلم رحمه الله الرواية  الأولى وقيل معناه أن

الشيطان إنما يوسوس لمن أيس من إغوائه فينكد عليه بالوسوسة لعجزه عن إغوائه

وأما الكافر فإنه يأتيه من حيث شاء ولا يقتصر في حقه على الوسوسة بل يتلاعب

به كيف أراد فعلى هذا معنى الحديث سبب الوسوسة محض الإيمان أو الوسوسة

علامة محض الإيمان وهذا القول اختيار القاضي عياض وأما قوله
# 
# ص فمن وجد ذلك فليقل آمنت بالله وفي الرواية الأخرى فليستعذ بالله ولينته

فمعناه الإعراض عن هذا الخاطر الباطل والالتجاء إلى الله تعالى في إذهابه

قال الإمام المازري رحمه الله ظاهر الحديث أنه صلى الله عليه وسلم أمرهم أن

يدفعوا الخواطر بالإعراض عنها والرد لها من غير استدلال ولا نظر في إبطالها

قال والذي يقال في هذا المعنى أن الخواطر على قسمين فأما التي ليست بمستقرة

ولا اجتلبتها شبهة طرأت فهي التي تدفع بالإعراض عنها وعلى هذا يحمل الحديث

وعلى مثلها ينطلق اسم الوسوسة فكأنه لما كان أمرا طارئا بغير أصل دفع بغير

نظر فى دليل اذلا أصل له ينظر فيه وأما الخواطر المستقرة التي أوجبتها

الشبهة فإنها لا تدفع إلا بالاستدلال والنظر في إبطالها والله أعلم وأما

قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم فليستعذ بالله ولينته فمعناه إذا عرض له هذا

الوسواس فليلجأ إلى الله تعالى في دفع شره عنه وليعرض عن الفكر في ذلك

وليعلم أن هذا الخاطر من وسوسة الشيطان وهو إنما يسعى بالفساد والإغواء

فليعرض
# 
# عن الإصغاء إلى وسوسته وليبادر إلى قطعها بالاشتغال بغيرها والله أعلم

وأما أسانيد الباب ففيه محمد بن عمرو بن جبلة هو محمد بن عمرو بن عباد بن

جبلة وفيه أبو الجواب عن عمار بن رزيق أما أبو الجواب فبفتح الجيم وتشديد

الواو وآخره باء موحدة واسمه الأحوص بن جواب وأما رزيق فبتقدم الراء على

الزاى وفيه قال مسلم حدثنا يوسف بن يعقوب الصفار حدثني علي بن عثام عن سعير

بن الخمس عن مغيرة عن إبراهيم عن علقمة عن عبد الله هو بن مسعود رضي الله

عنه وهذا  الإسناد كله كوفيون وعثام بالثاء المثلثة وسعير هو بضم السين

المهملة وآخره راء والخمس بكسر الخاء المعجمة وإسكان الميم وبالسين المهملة

وسعير وأبوه لا يعرف لهما نظير ومغيرة وإبراهيم وعلقمة تابعيون وقد اعترض

على هذا الإسناد وفيه أبو النضر عن أبي سعيد المؤدب هو أبو النضر هاشم بن

القاسم واسم أبي سعيد المؤدب محمد بن مسلم بن أبي الوضاح واسم أبي الوضاح

المثنى وكان يؤدب المهدي وغيره من الخلفاء وفيه بن أخى بن شهاب
# 
# وهو محمد بن عبد الله بن مسلم بن عبيد الله بن عبد الله بن شهاب أبو عبد
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ض-ع-ف (ḍa-ʿa-fa)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Doubling, multiplication; weakness in one sense, but here denotes increase in magnitude and recompense.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological context, the multiplication of reward (taḍʿīf al-ḥasanāt) is a divine grace (faḍl) exceeding mere arithmetic equivalence, signifying God's unbounded generosity.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) doubling of quantity; metaphorical (majāz) here indicates an immense, incalculable increase—the number "seven hundred" being a rhetorical hyperbole (mubālaghah) for divine abundance, not a fixed limit.
- Root: و-س-و-س (wa-s-wa-sa)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: The faint, subtle sound; the quiet, insinuating voice; from the same root as the "whisperer" (waswās) who speaks covertly.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In Quranic and theological usage, it is the satanic insinuation (khaṭir) that intrudes upon the heart without volition—distinct from deliberate thought or belief.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: a low, indistinct sound; metaphorical: the internal dialogue of doubt or intrusive thought that has no external reality—its "sound" is purely psychological.
- Root: أ-ص-ر (a-ṣa-ra)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Binding, constricting; a heavy burden that confines and restricts movement.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The "iṣr" in Quranic terms is the severe religious obligation or punishment imposed on prior nations—a weight of law that God lifted from this community.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: a physical fetter or load; metaphorical: the oppressive strictures of earlier dispensations (e.g., excessive penances) that were abrogated by divine mercy.
- Sībawayh Rule: Rule of Taqdīr (Ellipsis/Supposition) — In the phrase "ذلك صريح الإيمان" (that is the purest faith), the demonstrative "dhālika" refers not to the waswāsah itself but to the implied subject: the believers' profound distress (istiʿẓām) at such thoughts. The predicate requires the elided element (muqaddar) to complete the semantic sense, as the outward referent (the whisper) is not the intended meaning but its psychological effect.
chapters.translation:
I say: It stands at seven hundredfold. Abū al-Ḥasan al-Māwardī, the Chief Judge, narrated from some scholars that the multiplication does not exceed seven hundredfold—and this is an error on their part, contradicted by this hadith. And God knows best.

In the hadiths of this chapter there is an exposition of what God—may He be exalted—has honored this community with (may God increase it in honor), and how He lightened for them what had been upon others of the "iṣr"—that is, the heaviness and hardship—and an exposition of what the Companions (may God be pleased with them) were upon of hastening to submit to the rulings of the Sacred Law.

Abū Isḥāq al-Zajjāj said: This supplication contained in the saying of God—may He be exalted—{«رَبَّنَا لَا تُؤَاخِذْنَا إِن نَّسِينَا أَوْ أَخْطَأْنَا»} (Our Lord, do not seize us if we forget or err) to the end of the sūrah—God—may He be exalted—informed of it on behalf of the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) and the believers, and placed it in His Book so that it might be a supplication for those who come after the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) and the Companions (may God be pleased with them). Thus it is among the supplications that ought to be memorized and frequently invoked.

Al-Zajjāj said: And His saying—may He be exalted—{«فَانصُرْنَا عَلَى الْقَوْمِ الْكَافِرِينَ»} (so grant us victory over the disbelieving people) means: make us manifest over them in argument and in war, and in the establishment of the religion.

It will come in the Book of Prayer from this authentic collection that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Whoever recites the two verses from the end of Sūrat al-Baqarah in a night, they will suffice him." It was said: "suffice him" from the night prayer of that night; and it was said: "suffice him" against the disliked matters therein. And God knows best.

---

CHAPTER: The Exposition of Whispering (Waswāsah) in Faith and What One Who Encounters It Should Say

[132] In it: Abū Hurayrah (may God be pleased with him) said: "People from among the Companions of the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) came and asked him: 'We find within ourselves something that one of us deems too grave to even utter.' He said: 'And have you indeed found it?' They said: 'Yes.' He said: 'That is the purest faith (ṣarīḥ al-īmān).'"

[133] In the other narration: "The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) was asked about the waswāsah, and he said: 'That is the very essence of faith (maḥḍ al-īmān).'"

[134] And in the other hadith: "People will continue to ask one another until it is said: 'God created the creation—so who created God?' So whoever finds anything of that, let him say: 'I believe in God.'" And in the other narration: "Let him say: 'I believe in God and His messengers.'" And in the other narration: "Satan comes to one of you and says: 'Who created such-and-such?' until he says to him: 'Who created your Lord?' So when he reaches that point, let him seek refuge in God and desist."

As for the meanings of these hadiths and their jurisprudence: His saying (peace and blessings be upon him) "That is the purest faith" and "the very essence of faith" means: your deeming it too grave to utter such speech is itself the purest faith. For the deeming of this as grave, and the intense fear of it and of uttering it—let alone believing it—only occurs for one who has perfected faith with true completion, and from whom doubt and skepticism have been removed.

Know that the second narration, even though it does not mention the deeming-it-grave, that is its intended meaning, and it is an abridgment of the first narration. For this reason, Muslim (may God have mercy on him) presented the first narration first.

And it was said: Its meaning is that Satan only whispers to one whom he has despaired of leading astray, so he vexes him with waswāsah due to his inability to misguide him. As for the disbeliever, he comes to him from wherever he wishes and does not restrict himself to waswāsah in his case, but rather toys with him however he desires. So on this interpretation, the meaning of the hadith is: the cause of waswāsah is the very essence of faith, or waswāsah is a sign of the very essence of faith. And this is the position chosen by Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ.

As for his saying (peace and blessings be upon him) "So whoever finds that, let him say: 'I believe in God'"—and in the other narration "let him seek refuge in God and desist"—its meaning is: turning away from this false intrusive thought (khaṭir) and seeking refuge in God—may He be exalted—for its removal.

Imām al-Māzarī (may God have mercy on him) said: The apparent meaning of the hadith is that he (peace and blessings be upon him) commanded them to repel these thoughts by turning away from them and rejecting them, without recourse to demonstration (istidlāl) or reflection (naẓar) upon their refutation.

He said: And what is said regarding this meaning is that thoughts (khaṭawāt) are of two kinds: As for those that are not settled and are not attracted by a doubt that has newly arisen—these are repelled by turning away from them, and upon this the hadith is interpreted, and upon their like the name "waswāsah" is applied. For since it is a matter that is transient without any foundation, it is repelled without reflection upon evidence, because it has no foundation to be examined. As for the settled thoughts that are necessitated by doubts, these are not repelled except by demonstration and reflection upon their refutation. And God knows best.

As for his saying (peace and blessings be upon him) "Let him seek refuge in God and desist"—its meaning is: when this waswāsah presents itself to him, let him flee to God—may He be exalted—for the repulsion of its evil from him, and let him turn away from thought about it, and let him know that this thought is from the whisperings of Satan, and that he only strives for corruption and misguidance. So let him turn away from lending ear to his whispering, and hasten to cut it off by occupying himself with something else. And God knows best.

---

As for the chains of transmission (asānīd) of this chapter: In it is Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr ibn Jabalah—he is Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr ibn ʿAbbād ibn Jabalah. And in it is Abū al-Jawwāb, from ʿAmmār ibn Ruzayq. As for Abū al-Jawwāb, it is with the fatḥah on the jīm and the tashdīd on the wāw, and its final letter is a single bāʾ—and his name is al-Aḥwaṣ ibn Jawwāb. As for Ruzayq, the rāʾ precedes the zāy.

And in it: Muslim said: "We were narrated by Yūsuf ibn Yaʿqūb al-Ṣaffār, who said: ʿAlī ibn ʿAththām narrated to me, from Suʿayr ibn al-Khims, from Mughīrah, from Ibrāhīm, from ʿAlqamah, from ʿAbd Allāh—he is Ibn Masʿūd (may God be pleased with him)." And this entire chain is Kūfan. ʿAththām is with the thāʾ (three-dotted). Suʿayr is with ḍammah on the sīn (unpointed), and its final letter is rāʾ. Al-Khims is with kasrah on the khāʾ (pointed) and sukūn on the mīm, and with the unpointed sīn. Suʿayr and his father—no parallel is known for them. Mughīrah, Ibrāhīm, and ʿAlqamah are Followers (tābiʿūn). And objection has been raised against this chain.

And in it: Abū al-Naḍr, from Abū Saʿīd al-Muʾaddib—he is Abū al-Naḍr Hāshim ibn al-Qāsim. The name of Abū Saʿīd al-Muʾaddib is Muḥammad ibn Muslim ibn Abī al-Waḍḍāḥ, and the name of Abū al-Waḍḍāḥ is al-Muthannā. He used to tutor al-Mahdī and others among the caliphs.

And in it: Ibn akhī Ibn Shihāb—he is Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muslim ibn ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Shihāb, Abū ʿAbd Allāh...

chapters.title_en: Section 142 — The Chapter on the Severe Threat Against One Who Usurps a Muslim's Right by a False Oath, and the Clarification of Certain Chains and Linguistic Points
chapters.arabic_text:
الله وفيه يعقوب الدورقي تقدم بيانه في شرح المقدمة وفيه عبد الله بن

الرومي هو عبد الله بن محمد وقيل بن عمر بغدادي وفيه جعفر بن برقان بضم

الموحدة وبالقاف تقدم بيانه في المقدمة والله أعلم وفي ألفاظ المتن حتى

يقولوا الله خلق كل شيء هكذا هو في بعض الأصول يقولوا بغير نون وفي بعضها

يقولون بالنون وكلاهما صحيح وإثبات النون مع الناصب لغة قليلة ذكرها جماعة

من محققي النحويين وجاءت متكررة في الأحاديث الصحيحة كما ستراها في مواضعها

إن شاء الله تعالى والله أعلم

| (باب وعيد من اقتطع حق مسلم بيمين فاجرة بالنار
# [137] فيه
# قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (من اقتطع حق امرئ مسلم بيمينه فقد أوجب الله

تعالى له النار وحرم عليه الجنة فقال له رجل وإن كان شيئا يسيرا يا رسول

الله قال وإن قضيب من أراك))
# 
# [138] وفي الرواية الأخرى (من حلف على يمين صبر يقتطع بها مال امرئ مسلم

هو فيها فاجر لقي الله تعالى وهو عليه غضبان) وفي الرواية الأخرى (عن

الأشعث بن قيس كانت بيني وبين رجل أرض باليمن فخاصمته إلى النبي صلى الله

عليه وسلم فقال هل لك بينة فقلت لا قال فيمينه قلت إذن يحلف فقال لي رسول

الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عند ذلك من حلف على يمين صبر يقتطع بها مال امرئ
# 
# مسلم هو فيها فاجر لقي الله تعالى  وهو عليه غضبان)
# [139] وفي الرواية الأخرى (جاء رجل من حضرموت ورجل من كندة إلى النبي صلى

الله عليه وسلم فقال الحضرمي يا رسول الله إن هذا غلبني على أرض لي كانت

لأبي فقال الكندي هي أرضي في يدي أزرعها ليس له فيها حق فقال النبي صلى

الله عليه وسلم للحضرمي ألك بينة قال لا قال فلك يمينه قال يا رسول الله إن

الرجل فاجر لا يبالي على ما حلف عليه وليس يتورع من شيء فقال ليس لك منه

إلا ذلك فانطلق ليحلف فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لما أدبر أما لئن

حلف على ماله ليأكله ظلما ليلقين الله تعالى وهو عنه معرض) أما أسماء الباب

ولغاته ففيه مولى الحرقة بضم الحاء وفتح الراء وهي بطن من جهينة تقدم بيانه

مرات وفيه معبد بن كعب السلمي بفتح السين واللام منسوب إلى بني سلمة بكسر

اللام من الأنصار وفي النسب بفتح اللام على المشهور عند أهل العربية وغيرهم

وقيل يجوز كسر اللام في النسب أيضا وفيه عبد الله بن كعب بن أبي أمامة

الحارثي وفي الرواية
# 
# الأخرى سمعت عبد الله بن كعب يحدث أن أبا أمامة الحارثي حدثه اعلم أن أبا

أمامة هذا ليس هو أبا أمامة الباهلي صدي بن عجلان المشهور بل هذا غيره واسم

هذا إياس بن ثعلبة الأنصاري الحارثى من بنى الحرث بن الخزرج وقيل إنه بلوي

وهو حليف بني حارثة وهو بن أخت أبي بردة بن نيار هذا هو المشهور في اسمه

وقال أبو حاتم الرازي اسمه عبد الله بن ثعلبة ويقال ثعلبة بن عبد الله ثم

اعلم أن هنا دقيقة لابد من التنبيه عليها وهي أن الذين صنفوا في أسماء

الصحابة رضي الله عنهم ذكر كثير منهم أن أبا أمامة هذا الحارثي رضي الله

عنه توفي عند انصراف النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم من أحد فصلى عليه ومقتضى هذا

التاريخ أن يكون هذا الحديث الذي رواه مسلم منقطعا فإن عبد الله بن كعب

تابعي فكيف  يسمع من توفي عام أحد في السنة الثالثة من الهجرة ولكن هذا

النقل في وفاة أبي أمامة ليس بصحيح فإنه صح عن عبد الله بن كعب أنه قال

حدثني أبو أمامة كما ذكره مسلم في الرواية الثانية فهذا تصريح بسماع عبد

الله بن كعب التابعي منه فبطل ما قيل في وفاته ولو كان ما قيل في وفاته

صحيحا لم يخرج مسلم حديثه ولقد أحسن الإمام أبو البركات الجزري المعروف

بابن الأثير حيث أنكر في كتابه معرفة الصحابة رضي الله عنهم هذا القول في

وفاته والله أعلم وفيه وإن قضيب من أراك هكذا هو في بعض الأصول أو أكثرها

وفي كثير منها وإن قضيبا على أنه خبر كان المحذوفة أو أنه مفعول لفعل محذوف

تقديره وإن اقتطع قضيبا وفيه من حلف على يمين صبر هو بإضافة يمين إلى صبر

ويمين الصبر هي التي يحبس الحالف نفسه عليها وقد تقدم بيانها في باب غلظ

تحريم قتل الانسان نفسه وفيه قول صلى الله عليه وسلم من حلف على يمين صبر

هو فيها فاجر أي متعمد الكذب وتسمى هذه اليمين الغموس وفيه قوله إذن يحلف

يجوز بنصب الفاء ورفعها وذكر الإمام أبو الحسن بن خروف في شرح الجمل أن

الرواية فيه برفع الفاء وفيه قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم شاهداك أو يمينه

معناه لك ما يشهد به شاهداك أو يمينه وفيه حضرموت بفتح الحاء المهملة

وإسكان الضاد المعجمة وفتح الراء والميم وفيه قول مسلم (حدثني زهير
# 
# بن حرب وإسحاق بن إبراهيم جميعا عن أبي الوليد قال زهير حدثنا هشام بن

عبد الملك) هشام هو أبو الوليد وفيه قوله (انتزى على أرضي في الجاهلية)

معناه غلب عليها واستولى والجاهلية ما قبل النبوة لكثرة جهلهم وفيه (امرؤ

القيس بن عابس وربيعة بن عيدان) وأما عابس فبالموحدة والسين المهملة وأما

عيدان فقد ذكر مسلم أن زهيرا وإسحاق اختلفا في ضبطه وذكر القاضي عياض
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ق-ط-ع (q-ṭ-ʿ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To cut off, sever, detach; to take away something wholly from another's possession.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Usurpation (ikhtilās) of another's right by cutting it off from its rightful owner through aggression or deceit.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) in the sense of physical severance; metaphorical (majāz) here for appropriating property by false oath.
- Sībawayh Rule: Nominal Sentence with Omitted Predicate (al-ḥadhf) — In "وإن قضيب من أراك" (even if it be a twig of an arāk tree), the predicate of the omitted kāna or the object of an omitted verb is understood, requiring naṣb (accusative) in one reading.
chapters.translation:
I say: In this chain there is Yaʿqūb al-Dawraqī — his clarification has already preceded in the commentary on the Introduction. In it there is also ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Rūmī, who is ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muḥammad, and it is said: ibn ʿUmar, a Baghdādī. In it there is also Jaʿfar ibn Burqān — with ḍammah on the bāʾ (i.e., "Burqān") and with a qāf — his clarification has already preceded in the Introduction. And Allāh knows best.

Regarding the wording of the text: "until they say (yaqūlū) 'Allāh created everything'" — thus it appears in some manuscripts without the nūn (i.e., yaqūlū), and in others with the nūn (yaqūlūna). Both are correct. The affirmation of the nūn with the naṣib particle (an) is a rare dialect (lughah qalīlah) mentioned by a group of the verifying grammarians, and it has occurred repeatedly in the authentic ḥadīths, as you will see in their proper places, if Allāh the Exalted wills. And Allāh knows best.

| (Chapter: The Threat Against One Who Usurps a Muslim's Right by a False Oath — with Fire)

# [137] In it:
His saying, peace and blessings be upon him: "Whoever usurps the right of a Muslim by his oath, Allāh the Exalted has made the Fire obligatory for him and forbidden Paradise to him." A man said to him: "Even if it be something insignificant, O Messenger of Allāh?" He said: "Even if it be a twig of an arāk tree."

# [138] In the other narration: "Whoever swears an oath of ṣabr (i.e., an oath by which one detains his own self, compelling it to swear) by which he usurps the property of a Muslim, being in it a fājir (wicked liar), he will meet Allāh the Exalted while He is angry with him." In the other narration, on the authority of al-Ashʿath ibn Qays: "There was between me and a man a piece of land in Yemen, and I disputed with him before the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him. He said: 'Do you have a proof?' I said: 'No.' He said: 'Then his oath.' I said: 'Then he will swear.' The Messenger of Allāh, peace and blessings be upon him, said to me at that point: 'Whoever swears an oath of ṣabr by which he usurps the property of a Muslim, being in it a fājir, will meet Allāh the Exalted while He is angry with him.'"

# [139] In the other narration: "A man from Ḥaḍramawt and a man from Kindah came to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him. The Ḥaḍramī said: 'O Messenger of Allāh, this man has overcome me regarding land of mine that belonged to my father.' The Kindī said: 'It is my land in my hand; I cultivate it; he has no right in it.' The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said to the Ḥaḍramī: 'Do you have a proof?' He said: 'No.' He said: 'Then you have his oath.' He said: 'O Messenger of Allāh, the man is a fājir; he does not care what he swears upon, and he does not refrain from anything.' He said: 'You have nothing from him except that.' So he went off to swear. The Messenger of Allāh, peace and blessings be upon him, said when he turned away: 'Indeed, if he swears upon his property to consume it unjustly, he will surely meet Allāh the Exalted while He is turning away from him.'"

As for the names and linguistic points of the chapter: In it there is Mawlā al-Ḥurqah — with ḍammah on the ḥāʾ and fatḥah on the rāʾ — and it is a sub-tribe of Juhaynah; its clarification has preceded multiple times. In it there is Maʿbad ibn Kaʿb al-Sulamī — with fatḥah on the sīn and the lām — attributed to Banū Salamah (with kasrah on the lām) of the Anṣār; in the nisbah (attribution) it is with fatḥah on the lām according to the well-known view of the people of Arabic and others, and it is said that kasrah on the lām in the nisbah is also permissible. In it there is ʿAbd Allāh ibn Kaʿb ibn Abī Umāmah al-Ḥārithī. In the other narration: "I heard ʿAbd Allāh ibn Kaʿb narrating that Abū Umāmah al-Ḥārithī narrated to him."

Know that this Abū Umāmah is not the well-known Abū Umāmah al-Bāhilī, Ṣudayy ibn ʿAjlān. Rather, this one is someone else. His name is Iyās ibn Thaʿlabah al-Anṣārī al-Ḥārithī, from Banū al-Ḥārith ibn al-Khazraj. It is said he was from Balī, and he was an ally (ḥalīf) of Banū Ḥārithah, and he was the son of the sister of Abū Burdah ibn Niyār. This is the well-known view regarding his name. Abū Ḥātim al-Rāzī said: His name is ʿAbd Allāh ibn Thaʿlabah, and it is said: Thaʿlabah ibn ʿAbd Allāh.

Then know that here there is a subtle point (daqīqah) that must be noted: Those who composed works on the names of the Companions, may Allāh be pleased with them — many of them mentioned that this Abū Umāmah al-Ḥārithī, may Allāh be pleased with him, died at the time of the Prophet's, peace and blessings be upon him, return from Uḥud, and he (the Prophet) prayed over him. The implication of this dating would be that this ḥadīth narrated by Muslim is interrupted (munqaṭiʿ), for ʿAbd Allāh ibn Kaʿb is a Tābiʿī (successor) — how could he hear from one who died in the year of Uḥud, which is the third year of the Hijrah? However, this report concerning the death of Abū Umāmah is not sound, for it is authentically established on the authority of ʿAbd Allāh ibn Kaʿb that he said: "Abū Umāmah narrated to me," as Muslim mentioned in the second narration. This is an explicit statement of ʿAbd Allāh ibn Kaʿb the Tābiʿī hearing from him, and thus what was said about his death is refuted. Had what was said about his death been sound, Muslim would not have included his ḥadīth. And excellent is what the Imām Abū al-Barakāt al-Jazarī, known as Ibn al-Athīr, did when he rejected in his book Maʿrifat al-Ṣaḥābah (Knowledge of the Companions), may Allāh be pleased with them, this statement concerning his death. And Allāh knows best.

In it there is also: "Even if it be a twig of an arāk tree" — thus it appears in some manuscripts or most of them. In many of them: "wa-in qaḍīban" (with accusative), either as the predicate of an omitted kāna, or as the object of an omitted verb, the estimation being: "even if he usurped a twig." In it there is: "Whoever swears an oath of ṣabr" — this is with the idāfah (construct) of yamīn to ṣabr. The oath of ṣabr is that by which the swearer detains his own self upon it. Its clarification has already preceded in the chapter on the severity of the prohibition of a person killing himself. In it there is his saying, peace and blessings be upon him: "Whoever swears an oath of ṣabr, being in it a fājir" — meaning: deliberately lying. This oath is called al-ghamūs (the plunging oath, i.e., one that plunges its swearer into sin). In it there is his saying: "If so, he will swear (idhan yaḥlifu)" — it is permissible to read the fāʾ with naṣb (i.e., idhan yaḥlifa) or with rafʿ (idhan yaḥlifu). The Imām Abū al-Ḥasan ibn Kharūf mentioned in his commentary on al-Jumal that the narration therein is with rafʿ of the fāʾ. In it there is his saying, peace and blessings be upon him: "Your two witnesses or his oath" — its meaning is: you have what your two witnesses testify to, or his oath. In it there is Ḥaḍramawt — with fatḥah on the unpointed ḥāʾ, sukūn on the pointed ḍād, and fatḥah on the rāʾ and the mīm. In it there is Muslim's saying: "Zuḥayr ibn Ḥarb and Isḥāq ibn Ibrāhīm narrated to me, both from Abū al-Walīd; Zuḥayr said: Hishām ibn ʿAbd al-Malik narrated to us" — Hishām is Abū al-Walīd. In it there is his saying: "He overpowered (intazā) my land in the Jāhiliyyah" — its meaning is: he overcame and dominated it. Al-Jāhiliyyah is the period before prophethood, due to the abundance of their ignorance (jahl). In it there is: "Imruʾ al-Qays ibn ʿĀbis and Rabīʿah ibn ʿĪdān" — as for ʿĀbis, it is with the unpointed bāʾ and the unpointed sīn; as for ʿĪdān, Muslim mentioned that Zuḥayr and Isḥāq differed in its precise vocalization, and al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ mentioned...

chapters.title_en: Section 143 — On the Severity of Usurping a Muslim's Right by False Oath, and the Martyrdom of One Killed Defending His Property
chapters.arabic_text:
الأقوال فيه واختلاف الرواة فقال هو بفتح العين وبياء مثناة من تحت هذا

صوابه  وكذا هو في رواية إسحاق وأما رواية زهير فعبدان بكسر العين وبباء

موحدة قال القاضي كذا ضبطناه في الحرفين عن شيوخنا قال ووقع عند بن الحذاء

عكس ما ضبطناه فقال في رواية زهير بالفتح والمثناة وفي رواية إسحاق بالكسر

والموحدة قال الجياني وكذا هو في الأصل عن الجلودي قال القاضي والذي صوبناه

أولا هو قول الدارقطني وعبد الغني بن سعيد وأبي نصر بن ماكولا وكذا قاله بن

يونس في التاريخ هذا كلام القاضي وضبطه جماعة من الحفاظ منهم الحافظ أبو

القاسم بن عساكر الدمشقي عبدان بكسر العين والموحدة وتشديد الدال والله

أعلم وأما أحكام الباب فقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم من اقتطع حق امرئ مسلم

بيمينه إلى آخره فيه لطيفة وهي أن قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم حق امرئ يدخل

فيه من حلف على غير مال كجلد الميتة والسرجين وغير ذلك من النجاسات التي

ينتفع بها وكذا سائر الحقوق التي ليست بمال كحد القذف ونصيب الزوجة في

القسم وغير ذلك وأما قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقد أوجب الله تعالى له النار

وحرم عليه الجنة ففيه الجوابان المتقدمان المتكرران في نظائره أحدهما أنه

محمول على المستحل لذلك إذا مات على ذلك فإنه يكفر ويخلد في النار والثاني

معناه فقد
# 
# استحق النار ويجوز العفو عنه وقد حرم عليه دخول الجنة أول وهلة مع

الفائزين وأما تقييده صلى الله عليه وسلم بالمسلم فليس يدل على عدم تحريم

حق الذمي بل معناه أن هذا الوعيد الشديد وهو أنه يلقى الله تعالى وهو عليه

غضبان لمن اقتطع حق المسلم وأما الذمي فاقتطاع حقه حرام لكن ليس يلزم أن

تكون فيه هذه العقوبة العظيمة هذا كله على مذهب من يقول بالمفهوم وأما من

لا يقول به فلا يحتاج إلى تأويل وقال القاضي عياض رحمه الله تخصيص المسلم

لكونهم المخاطبين وعامة المتعاملين في الشريعة لا أن غير المسلم بخلافه بل

حكمه حكمه في ذلك والله أعلم ثم إن هذه العقوبة لمن اقتطع حق المسلم ومات

قبل  التوبة أما من تاب فندم على فعله ورد الحق إلى صاحبه وتحلل منه وعزم

على أن لا يعود فقد سقط عنه الإثم والله أعلم وفي هذا الحديث دلالة لمذهب

مالك والشافعي وأحمد والجماهير أن حكم الحاكم لا يبيح للإنسان ما لم يكن له

خلافا لأبي حنيفة رحمه الله تعالى وفيه بيان غلظ تحريم حقوق المسلمين وأنه

لا فرق بين قليل الحق وكثيره لقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم وإن قضيب من أراك

وأما قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم من حلف على يمين هو فيها فاجر ليقتطع

فالتقييد بكونه فاجرا لا بد منه ومعناه هو آثم ولا يكون آثما إلا إذا كان

متعمدا عالما بأنه غير محق وأما قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم لقي الله تعالى

وهو عليه غضبان وفي الرواية الأخرى وهو عنه معرض فقال العلماء الإعراض

والغضب والسخط من الله تعالى هو إرادته إبعاد ذلك المغضوب عليه من رحمته

وتعذيبه وانكار فعله وذمه والله أعلم وأما حديث الحضرمى والكندى ففيه أنواع

من العلوم ففيه أن صاحب اليد أولى من أجنبي يدعي عليه وفيه أن المدعى عليه

يلزمه اليمين إذا لم يقر وفيه أن البينة تقدم على اليد ويقضى لصاحبها بغير

يمين وفيه أن يمين الفاجر المدعى عليه تقبل كيمين العدل وتسقط عنه المطالبة

بها وفيه أن أحد الخصمين إذا قال لصاحبه إنه ظالم أو فاجر أو نحوه في حال
# 
# الخصومة يحتمل ذلك منه وفيه أن الوارث إذا ادعى شيئا لمورثه وعلم الحاكم

أن مورثه مات ولا وارث له سوى هذا المدعي جاز له الحكم به ولم يكلفه حال

الدعوى بينة على ذلك وموضع الدلالة أنه قال غلبني على أرض لي كانت لأبي فقد

أقر بأنها كانت لأبيه فلولا علم النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بأنه ورثها وحده

لطالبه بينة على كونه وارثا ثم ببينة أخرى على كونه محقا في دعواه على خصمه

فإن قال قائل قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم شاهداك معناه شاهداك على ما تستحق به

انتزاعها وإنما يكون  ذلك بأن يشهدا بكونه وارثا وحده وأنه ورث الدار

فالجواب أن هذا خلاف الظاهر ويجوز أن يكون مرادا والله أعلم

| (باب دليل على أن من قصد أخذ مال غيره بغير حق (كان 
# القاصد مهدر الدم حقه وإن قتل كان في النار) (وأن من قتل دون ماله فهو

شهيد)
# [140] فيه (أن رجلا جاء إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال يا رسول

الله أرأيت ان جاء رجل يريد أخذ مالى فلا تعطه مالك قال أرأيت إن قاتلني

قال قاتله قال أرأيت إن قتلني قال فأنت شهيد قال أرأيت إن قتلته قال هو في

النار) أما ألفاظ الباب فالشهيد قال النضر بن شميل سمي بذلك لأنه حي لأن

أرواحهم شهدت دار السلام وأرواح غيرهم لا تشهدها إلا يوم القيامة وقال)
# 
# بن الأنباري لأن الله تعالى وملائكته عليهم السلام يشهدوم له بالجنة

فمعنى شهيد مشهود له وقيل سمي شهيدا لأنه يشهد عند خروج روحه ماله من

الثواب والكرامة وقيل لأن ملائكة الرحمة يشهدون فيأخذون روحه وقيل لأنه شهد

له بالإيمان وخاتمة الخير بظاهر حاله وقيل لأن عليه شاهدا يشهد بكونه شهيدا
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ق-ط-ع (q-ṭ-ʿ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To cut off, sever, detach; hence 'iqtataʿa' — to take away or appropriate something wholly, severing it from its owner.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In legal-theological context, denotes wrongful appropriation of another's due right (ḥaqq), implying transgression against divine ordinance.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) — physical severance; metaphorical (majāz) — usurpation of a legal claim or entitlement.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional-Protasis Construction (al-sharṭ wa-l-jawāb) — The phrase "man iqtaṭaʿa" (whoever severs) introduces a general conditional clause; the apodosis carries the legal consequence, requiring careful parsing of the subject's moral state (e.g., mustaḥill vs. non-mustaḥill).
chapters.translation:
I say: The statements concerning it and the divergence of the transmitters — he said: It is with fatḥah on the ʿayn and a yāʾ (the second letter from below, i.e., tāʾ marbūṭah form) — this is its correct form, and likewise it is in the narration of Isḥāq. As for the narration of Zuhayr, it is ʿAbdān with kasrah on the ʿayn and a single bāʾ. Al-Qāḍī said: Thus we have recorded it in both letters from our shaykhs. He said: And it occurred with Ibn al-Ḥadhāʾ reversed from what we recorded, for he said in Zuhayr's narration (it is) with fatḥah and the tāʾ marbūṭah, and in Isḥāq's narration with kasrah and the bāʾ. Al-Jayyānī said: And likewise it is in the original from al-Julūdī. Al-Qāḍī said: And what we first corrected is the statement of al-Dāraquṭnī, ʿAbd al-Ghanī ibn Saʿīd, and Abū Naṣr ibn Mākūlā; and likewise Ibn Yūnus said it in the Tārīkh. This is the speech of al-Qāḍī. And a group of ḥuffāẓ have recorded it, among them the ḥāfiẓ Abū al-Qāsim ibn ʿAsākir al-Dimashqī: ʿAbdān with kasrah on the ʿayn, the bāʾ, and tashdīd on the dāl. And Allāh knows best.

As for the legal rulings of the chapter — his saying, peace and blessings be upon him: "Whoever severs the right of a Muslim man by his oath" — to its end — therein is a subtlety, namely that his saying, peace and blessings be upon him, "right of a man" includes one who swears concerning something other than property, such as the skin of a dead animal, dung, and other impure things from which benefit is derived; and likewise all rights that are not property, such as the prescribed punishment for slander (ḥadd al-qadhf) and the wife's share in division of nights, and other such matters.

As for his saying, peace and blessings be upon him: "Allāh has made the Fire obligatory for him and forbidden Paradise to him" — therein are the two answers previously mentioned and repeatedly applied in similar instances. One of them: It is interpreted as referring to one who deems it lawful (mustaḥill) and dies upon that; for then he disbelieves and is eternally in the Fire. The second: Its meaning is that he has rendered himself deserving of the Fire, and pardon is permissible for him; and Paradise's entry has been forbidden to him at the first instance, along with the triumphant ones.

As for his restricting it, peace and blessings be upon him, to the Muslim — this does not indicate that the right of the dhimmī is not forbidden; rather, its meaning is that this severe threat — that he meets Allāh while He is angry with him — applies to one who severs the right of a Muslim. As for the dhimmī, severing his right is unlawful, but it is not necessary that this great punishment be incurred therein. All of this is according to the school of those who affirm the concept of exception (al-mafhūm). As for one who does not affirm it, he has no need for such interpretation. Al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ, may Allāh have mercy on him, said: The specification of the Muslim is because they are the addressees and the general transactors in the Sacred Law, not that the non-Muslim is otherwise; rather, his ruling is his ruling in that matter. And Allāh knows best.

Then, this punishment applies to one who severs the right of a Muslim and dies before repentance. As for one who repents — regretting his deed, returning the right to its owner, seeking release from it, and resolving not to return to it — the sin has fallen away from him. And Allāh knows best.

In this ḥadīth is evidence for the school of Mālik, al-Shāfiʿī, Aḥmad, and the majority (al-jamāhīr) that the judge's ruling does not render lawful for a person what was not his, contrary to Abū Ḥanīfah, may Allāh the Exalted have mercy on him. And therein is a clarification of the gravity of the prohibition of Muslims' rights, and that there is no difference between a small right and a great one, due to his saying, peace and blessings be upon him: "Even if it be a twig of an arāk tree."

As for his saying, peace and blessings be upon him: "Whoever swears an oath in which he is wicked (fājir) to sever [property]" — the restriction to his being wicked is indispensable. Its meaning: He is sinful; and he is not sinful unless he is deliberate, knowing that he is not in the right.

As for his saying, peace and blessings be upon him: "He meets Allāh the Exalted while He is angry with him," and in the other narration: "While He is turning away from him" — the scholars said: Turning away (iʿrāḍ), anger (ghaḍab), and displeasure (sakhaṭ) from Allāh the Exalted are His willing the exclusion of that one against whom wrath is incurred from His mercy, His punishing him, and His disapproval and condemnation of his deed. And Allāh knows best.

As for the ḥadīth of al-Ḥaḍramī and al-Kindī — therein are various types of knowledge. In it: The possessor of the object in hand (ṣāḥib al-yad) has priority over a stranger who makes a claim against him. In it: The defendant is obligated to take the oath if he does not admit [the claim]. In it: Evidence (bayyinah) takes precedence over the hand, and judgment is given for its possessor without an oath. In it: The oath of a wicked defendant is accepted like the oath of an upright one, and the claim against him is dropped thereby. In it: One of the two litigants, if he says to his opponent that he is an oppressor, or wicked, or similar, during the course of the dispute, it is tolerated from him. In it: If an heir claims something for his deceased predecessor, and the judge knows that his predecessor died with no heir other than this claimant, it is permissible for him to judge in his favor, and he is not required at the time of the claim to produce evidence of that. The locus of indication is that he said: "He overcame me regarding land of mine that belonged to my father" — for he admitted that it belonged to his father. Had the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, not known that he had inherited it alone, he would have demanded evidence of his being an heir, and then further evidence of his being in the right in his claim against his opponent.

If someone says: His saying, peace and blessings be upon him, "Your two witnesses" means: Your two witnesses to what entitles you to its seizure; and that only occurs by their testifying that he is the sole heir and that he inherited the abode — then the answer is that this contradicts the apparent meaning, though it is possible that it is intended. And Allāh knows best.

[Chapter: Evidence that one who intends to take another's property without right — the one intending it has his blood rendered permissible (mahdūr al-dam), and if he is killed, he is in the Fire; and that one killed defending his property is a martyr.]

[140] In it: That a man came to the Messenger of Allāh, peace and blessings be upon him, and said: "O Messenger of Allāh, what do you think if a man comes intending to take my property?" He said: "Do not give him your property." He said: "What if he fights me?" He said: "Fight him." He said: "What if he kills me?" He said: "Then you are a martyr." He said: "What if I kill him?" He said: "He is in the Fire."

As for the wording of the chapter — al-shahīd (the martyr): al-Naḍr ibn Shumayl said: He is so named because he is alive, for their souls have witnessed the Abode of Peace (Dār al-Salām), whereas the souls of others do not witness it except on the Day of Resurrection. Ibn al-Anbārī said: Because Allāh the Exalted and His angels, peace be upon them, bear witness for him with Paradise; so the meaning of shahīd is "one for whom witness is borne." It was said: He is named shahīd because he witnesses, at the departure of his soul, what he has of reward and honor. It was said: Because the angels of mercy bear witness and take his soul. It was said: Because he bore witness to faith and a good end by his apparent state. It was said: Because upon him is a witness who testifies that he is a martyr.
