His statement, peace and blessings be upon him, "fearing that Allah would cast him (yakubbahu) into the Fire" — yakubbahu is with the opening of the yā'. One says "akabba al-rajul" (the man fell on his face) and "kabbahu Allāh" (Allah cast him down). This construction is strange, for the customary pattern is that the intransitive verb is without hamzah and is made transitive by the hamzah; here it is the reverse. The pronoun in "yakubbahu" refers to the giver, i.e., "I seek to win over his heart by giving, fearing his disbelief if he is not given." His statement "He gave to a group (rahṭan)" — i.e., a company; its root meaning is a group of fewer than ten. His statement "while he was the most beloved of them to me" — i.e., the most virtuous and most righteous in my belief. His statement "Indeed, I see him (la-arāhu) as a believer" — the hamzah is opened (i.e., "la-arāhu" meaning "I know him to be"), and it is not permissible to close it (i.e., "la-urāhu" meaning "I think him to be"). For he said: "What I know of him overcame me," and because he returned to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, three times; had he not been certain of his belief, he would not have repeated the return. His statement, from Ṣāliḥ, from Ibn Shihāb: "ʿĀmir ibn Saʿd narrated to me" — these are three Successors (tābiʿūn), each narrating from the other, and this is an instance of the narration of the elder from the younger (riwāyat al-akābir ʿan al-aṣāghir), for Ṣāliḥ is older than al-Zuhrī.

As for its jurisprudence (fiqh) and meanings: In it is the distinction between Islam (islām) and faith (īmān). On this question there is disagreement and lengthy discussion, and the clarification of this question and the exposition of its explanation have already preceded at the beginning of the Book of Faith (Kitāb al-Īmān). In it is an indication of the doctrine of the people of truth (ahl al-ḥaqq) in their statement that verbal affirmation (al-iqrār bi al-lisān) avails nothing unless accompanied by belief in the heart (al-iʿtiqād bi al-qalb), contrary to the Karrāmiyyah and the extreme Murjiʾah in their statement that affirmation alone suffices. This is a manifest error, as is seen by the consensus of the Muslims and the texts declaring the hypocrites (munāfiqūn) to be disbelievers, and this is their description. In it is the permissibility of intercession (shafāʿah) with those in authority (wulāt al-umūr) in matters that are not prohibited. In it is the permissibility of the one asked to be revisited on a single matter (murājaʿat al-masʾūl fī al-amr al-wāḥid). In it is the notification by the inferior (al-mafdūl) to the superior (al-fāḍil) of what he sees as beneficial. In it is that the superior does not accept what is suggested to him absolutely, but rather deliberates over it; if its benefit does not become apparent, he does not act upon it. In it is the command to exercise caution (al-tathabbut) and to refrain from decisive judgment (al-qaṭʿ) regarding what one does not know with certainty. In it is that the Imam may disburse wealth according to the interests of the Muslims, prioritizing the most important (al-ahamm fa-al-ahamm). In it is that one does not decisively affirm Paradise (al-jannah) for anyone by specific designation except one for whom a text (naṣṣ) is established, such as the Ten (al-ʿasharah) and those like them; this is a matter of consensus (mujmaʿ ʿalayhi) among the Ahl al-Sunnah.

As for his statement, peace and blessings be upon him, "or a Muslim" — it does not contain a denial that he was a believer; rather, its meaning is the prohibition of decisive judgment on faith, and that the term "Islam" is more appropriate for him. For Islam is known by the outward ruling (ḥukm al-ẓāhir), whereas faith is inward, known only to Allah Most High. The author of al-Taḥrīr has claimed that in this hadith there is an indication that the man was not a believer. It is not as he claimed; rather, in it there is an indication of his faith. For the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said in response to Saʿd: "Indeed, I give to a man while another is more beloved to me than him" — meaning: I give to one whom I fear, due to the weakness of his faith, might disbelieve, and I refrain from giving to another who is more beloved to me than him, because of what I know of the tranquility of his heart and the firmness of his faith.

As for Muslim's statement, may Allah have mercy on him, at the beginning of the chapter: "Ibn Abī ʿUmar narrated to us, he said: Sufyān narrated to us, from al-Zuhrī, from ʿĀmir" — Abū ʿAlī al-Ghassānī said: al-Ḥāfiẓ Abū Masʿūd al-Dimashqī said: "This hadith is only narrated by Sufyān ibn ʿUyaynah from Maʿmar, from al-Zuhrī, with his chain of transmission, and this is the preserved version (al-maḥfūẓ) from Sufyān." Likewise, Abū al-Ḥasan al-Dāraquṭnī said in his book al-Istidrākāt. I say: This statement that these scholars have made regarding this chain of transmission — it may be said that one ought not to concur with them on it, because it is possible that Sufyān heard it from al-Zuhrī on one occasion, and heard it from Maʿmar, from al-Zuhrī, on another, and thus narrated it in both ways; so neither one detracts from the other. However, certain matters have combined to necessitate what they mentioned, among them: that Sufyān was a mudallis (one who obscures his sources), and he said "from" (ʿan); and that most of his students narrated it from Maʿmar. This may be answered by what we have already presented: that Muslim, may Allah have mercy on him, does not narrate from a mudallis who says "from" unless it is established that he heard it from the one from whom he narrates with ʿanʿanah. However that may be, this discussion concerning the chain of transmission does not affect the text (al-matn), for it is authentic (ṣaḥīḥ) in every estimation and continuous (muttaṣil). And Allah knows best.

Chapter: On the Increase of the Heart's Tranquility Through the Multiplicity of Evidences (Bāb Ziyādat Ṭumaʾnīnat al-Qalb bi-Taẓāhur al-Adillah). In it is his statement, peace and blessings be upon him: "We are more deserving of doubt than Abraham, peace be upon him, when he said..."

chapters.title_en: Section 150 — On the Saying of the Prophet ﷺ: "We Are More Deserving of Doubt than Abraham" and the Question of Abraham's Request to See the Revivification of the Dead
chapters.arabic_text:
رب أرني كيف تحيي الموتى قال أو لم تؤمن قال بلى ولكن ليطمئن قلبى قال

ويرحم الله لوطا لقد كان يأوي إلى ركن شديد ولو لبثت في السجن طول لبث يوسف

لأجبت الداعى) اختلف العلماء في معنى نحن أحق بالشك من إبراهيم على أقوال

كثيرة أحسنها وأصحها ما قاله الإمام أبو إبراهيم المزني صاحب الشافعي

وجماعات  من العلماء معناه أن الشك مستحيل في حق إبراهيم فإن الشك في إحياء

الموتى لو كان متطرقا إلى الأنبياء لكنت أنا أحق به من إبراهيم وقد علمتم

أني لم أشك فاعلموا أن إبراهيم عليه السلام لم يشك وإنما خص إبراهيم صلى

الله عليه وسلم لكون الآية قد يسبق إلى بعض الأذهان الفاسدة منها احتمال

الشك وانما رجح إبراهيم على نفسه صلى الله عليه وسلم تواضعا وأدبا أو قبل

أن يعلم صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه خير ولد آدم قال صاحب التحرير قال جماعة من

العلماء لما نزل قول الله تعالى أولم تؤمن قالت طائفة شك إبراهيم ولم يشك

نبينا فقال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم نحن أحق بالشك منه فذكر نحو ما قدمته

ثم قال ويقع لي فيه معنيان أحدهما أنه خرج مخرج العادة في الخطاب فإن من

أراد المدافعة عن إنسان قال للمتكلم فيه ما كنت قائلا لفلان أو فاعلا معه

من مكروه فقله لي وافعله معي ومقصوده لا تقل ذلك فيه والثاني أن معناه أن

هذا الذي تظنونه شكا أنا أولى به فإنه ليس بشك وإنما هو طلب لمزيد اليقين

وقيل غير هذا من الاقوال)
# 
# فنقتصر على هذه لكونها أصحها وأوضحها والله أعلم وأما سؤال إبراهيم صلى

الله عليه وسلم فذكر العلماء في سببه أوجها أظهرها أنه أراد الطمأنينة بعلم

كيفية الإحياء مشاهدة بعد العلم بها استدلالا فإن علم الاستدلال قد تتطرق

إليه الشكوك في الجملة بخلاف علم المعاينة فإنه ضروري وهذا مذهب الإمام أبي

منصور الأزهري وغيره والثاني أراد اختبار منزلته عند ربه في إجابة دعائه

وعلى هذا قالوا معنى قوله تعالى أولم تؤمن أي تصدق بعظم منزلتك عندي

واصطفائك وخلتك والثالث سأل زيادة يقين وإن لم يكن الأول شكا فسأل الترقي

من علم اليقين إلى عين اليقين فإن بين العلمين تفاوتا قال سهل بن عبد الله

التستري رضي الله عنه سأل كشف غطاء العيان ليزداد بنور اليقين تمكنا الرابع

أنه لما احتج على المشركين بأن ربه  سبحانه وتعالى يحيي ويميت طلب ذلك منه

سبحانه وتعالى ليظهر دليله عيانا وقيل أقوال أخر كثيرة ليست بظاهرة قال

الإمام أبو الحسن الواحدي رحمه الله اختلفوا في سبب سؤاله فالأكثرون على

أنه رأى جيفة بساحل البحر يتناولها السباع والطير ودواب البحر فتفكر كيف

يجتمع ما تفرق من تلك الجيفة وتطلعت نفسه إلى مشاهدة ميت يحييه ربه ولم يكن

شاكا في إحياء الموتى ولكن أحب رؤية ذلك كما أن المؤمنين يحبون أن يروا

النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم والجنة ويحبون رؤية الله تعالى مع الإيمان بكل

ذلك وزوال الشكوك عنه قال العلماء والهمزة فى قوله تعالى أولم تؤمن همزة

إثبات كقول جرير ألستم خير من ركب المطايا والله أعلم وأما قول النبي صلى

الله عليه وسلم ويرحم الله لوطا لقد كان يأوي إلى ركن شديد فالمراد بالركن

الشديد هو الله سبحانه وتعالى
# 
# فإنه أشد الأركان وأقواها وأمنعها ومعنى الحديث والله أعلم أن لوطا صلى

الله عليه وسلم لما خاف على أضيافه ولم يكن له عشيرة تمنعهم من الظالمين

ضاق ذرعه واشتد حزنه عليهم فغلب ذلك عليه فقال في ذلك الحال لو أن لي بكم

قوة فى الدفع بنفسى أو آوى إلى عشيرة تمنع لمنعتكم وقصد لوط صلى الله عليه

وسلم إظهار العذر عند أضيافه وأنه لو استطاع دفع المكروه عنهم بطريق ما

لفعله وأنه بذل وسعه في إكرامهم والمدافعة عنهم ولم يكن ذلك إعراضا منه صلى

الله عليه وسلم عن الاعتماد على الله تعالى وإنما كان لما ذكرناه من تطيب

قلوب الأضياف ويجوز أن يكون نسي الالتجاء إلى الله تعالى في حمايتهم ويجوز

أن يكون التجأ فيما بينه وبين الله تعالى وأظهر للأضياف التألم وضيق الصدر

والله أعلم وأما قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (ولو لبثت في السجن طول لبث يوسف

لأجبت الداعى) فهو ثناء على يوسف عليه السلام وبيان لصبره وتأنيه والمراد

بالداعي رسول الملك الذي أخبر الله سبحانه وتعالى أنه قال ائتوني به فلما

جاءه الرسول قال ارجع إلى  ربك فاسأله ما بال النسوة اللاتي قطعن أيديهن فلم

يخرج يوسف صلى الله عليه وسلم مبادرا إلى الراحة ومفارقة السجن الطويل بل

تثبت وتوقر وراسل الملك في كشف أمره الذي سجن بسببه ولتظهر براءته عند

الملك وغيره ويلقاه مع اعتقاده براءته مما نسب إليه ولا خجل من يوسف ولا

غيره فبين نبينا صلى الله عليه وسلم فضيلة يوسف فى هذا وقوة نفسه فىالخير

وكمال صبره وحسن نظره وقال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم عن نفسه ما قاله

تواضعا وإيثارا للإبلاغ في بيان كمال فضيلة يوسف صلى الله عليه وسلم والله

أعلم وأما ما يتعلق بأسانيد الباب ففيه مما تقدم بيانه المسيب والد سعيد

وهو بفتح الياء على المشهور الذي قاله الجمهور ومنهم من يكسرها وهو قول أهل
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ش-ك-ك (sh-k-k)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Penetration of uncertainty into the heart; oscillation between two matters without preponderance; the opposite of certainty (yaqīn).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological discourse, shakk denotes a state of epistemic deficiency incompatible with prophetic infallibility (ʿiṣmah); its attribution to a prophet is categorically impossible.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal usage denotes genuine doubt; here it is employed metaphorically (majāz) to mean "the mere possibility of doubt's intrusion," not its actual occurrence.
- Root: ر-أ-ي (r-'-y)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Visual perception (ruʾyah); also intellectual discernment (raʾy).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Distinguishes ʿilm al-yaqīn (knowledge by inference) from ʿayn al-yaqīn (knowledge by direct vision); the latter is necessary (ḍarūrī) and immune to doubt.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): The request "show me" (arinī) is literal — a petition for ocular witnessing, not a metaphorical expression of doubt.
- Root: ر-ك-ن (r-k-n)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: A strong pillar or support; that which one leans upon for protection.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In the prophetic saying, "a strong pillar" (rukn shadīd) refers allegorically to God Himself — the mightiest of all supports.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Metaphorical extension from physical pillar to divine protection; the literal sense is impossible here.
- Sībawayh Rule: Rule of Hamzah Istifhām vs. Hamzah Ithbāt (The Interrogative vs. Assertive Hamzah) — In {«أَوَلَمْ تُؤْمِن»}, the hamzah is assertive (hamzat ithbāt), not interrogative, as confirmed by Jarīr's verse "أَلَسْتُمْ خَيْرَ مَنْ رَكِبَ الْمَطَايَا" where the hamzah affirms rather than questions.
chapters.translation:
I say: The Prophet ﷺ said: "My Lord, show me how You give life to the dead." He said: "Do you not believe?" He said: "Yes, but that my heart may be at rest." He said: "And may God have mercy on Lot — he indeed sought refuge in a mighty pillar. And had I remained in prison as long as Joseph remained, I would have answered the caller."

The scholars have differed concerning the meaning of the Prophet's saying "We are more deserving of doubt than Abraham" — may God bless him and grant him peace — according to numerous opinions. The best and most sound of them is what was stated by Imam Abū Ibrāhīm al-Muzanī, the companion of al-Shāfiʿī, and groups of scholars. Its meaning is that doubt is impossible in the case of Abraham, for had doubt concerning the revivification of the dead been capable of reaching the prophets, then I would have been more deserving of it than Abraham. And you have known that I did not doubt. So know that Abraham — peace be upon him — did not doubt. Rather, Abraham — may God bless him and grant him peace — was singled out because the verse might suggest to some corrupt minds the possibility of doubt. And the Prophet — may God bless him and grant him peace — only preferred Abraham over himself out of humility and courtesy, or before he knew — may God bless him and grant him peace — that he was the best of the children of Adam.

The author of al-Taḥrīr said: A group of scholars stated: When the saying of God Most High {«أَوَلَمْ تُؤْمِن»} was revealed, a faction said: "Abraham doubted, and our Prophet did not doubt." So the Prophet ﷺ said: "We are more deserving of doubt than him" — and he mentioned something similar to what I have already presented. Then he said: Two meanings occur to me concerning it. The first: that it issued in the manner of customary address, for when one intends to defend a person, he says to the one speaking against him: "Whatever you would say against so-and-so, or whatever harm you would do to him, say it to me and do it to me" — his intent being: do not say that about him. The second: that its meaning is: this thing which you suppose to be doubt — I am more deserving of it, for it is not doubt; rather, it is a request for additional certainty. And other opinions besides these have been mentioned.

We restrict ourselves to these because they are the most sound and the clearest. And God knows best.

As for the question of Abraham — peace be upon him — the scholars have mentioned concerning its cause several aspects. The most apparent of them is that he intended tranquility through knowledge of the manner of revivification by direct vision, after having known it by inference. For inferential knowledge may be subject to doubts in general, unlike the knowledge of direct vision, for it is necessary (ḍarūrī). This is the doctrine of Imam Abū Manṣūr al-Azharī and others.

The second: he intended to test his station with his Lord regarding the answering of his supplication. On this basis they said: the meaning of His saying {«أَوَلَمْ تُؤْمِن»} is: "Do you not affirm the greatness of your station with Me, and My selection of you, and My taking you as a close friend (khullah)?"

The third: he asked for an increase of certainty, even though the first was not doubt; he asked to ascend from knowledge of certainty (ʿilm al-yaqīn) to the very eye of certainty (ʿayn al-yaqīn), for between the two knowledges there is a distinction. Sahl ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Tustarī — may God be pleased with him — said: "He asked for the unveiling of the cover of ocular vision so that he might increase, by the light of certainty, in firmness."

The fourth: when he argued against the polytheists that his Lord — glorified and exalted is He — gives life and causes death, he requested that from Him — glorified and exalted is He — so that his proof might appear as ocular evidence.

And other numerous opinions have been mentioned which are not apparent.

Imam Abū al-Ḥasan al-Wāḥidī — may God have mercy on him — said: They differed concerning the cause of his question. The majority held that he saw a carcass on the seashore, with beasts, birds, and sea creatures devouring it, and he reflected upon how what had been scattered of that carcass would be gathered together. His soul yearned to witness a dead thing being revived by his Lord. He was not in doubt concerning the revivification of the dead, but he loved to see that — just as the believers love to see the Prophet ﷺ and Paradise, and love to see God Most High, while believing in all of that and with doubt removed from them.

The scholars said: The hamzah in His saying {«أَوَلَمْ تُؤْمِن»} is a hamzah of affirmation (hamzat ithbāt), like the saying of Jarīr: "Are you not the best of those who ride mounts?" (أَلَسْتُمْ خَيْرَ مَنْ رَكِبَ الْمَطَايَا). And God knows best.

As for the saying of the Prophet ﷺ: "And may God have mercy on Lot — he indeed sought refuge in a mighty pillar" — the intended meaning of "the mighty pillar" is God — glorified and exalted is He — for He is the mightiest of pillars, the strongest of them, and the most protective.

The meaning of the hadith — and God knows best — is that Lot — peace be upon him — when he feared for his guests and had no clan to protect them from the wrongdoers, his breast became constricted and his grief over them intensified, and that overcame him. So he said in that state: "If only I had strength against you in repelling by myself, or I could betake myself to a clan that would protect — I would have protected you." Lot — peace be upon him — intended to show an excuse before his guests, and that had he been able to repel harm from them by any means, he would have done so, and that he had exerted his utmost in honoring them and defending against them. That was not an aversion on his part — peace be upon him — from reliance upon God Most High; rather, it was for what we have mentioned of comforting the hearts of the guests. And it is permissible that he forgot the recourse to God Most High in their protection. And it is permissible that he did have recourse to Him privately between himself and God Most High, while he showed to the guests his distress and constriction of breast. And God knows best.

As for his saying ﷺ: "And had I remained in prison as long as Joseph remained, I would have answered the caller" — it is praise of Joseph — peace be upon him — and an exposition of his patience and deliberation. The intended meaning of "the caller" is the messenger of the king, of whom God — glorified and exalted is He — reported that he said: "Bring him to me." When the messenger came to him, he said: "Return to your master and ask him what was the matter of the women who cut their hands." Joseph — peace be upon him — did not come out hastily seeking comfort and departure from the long imprisonment; rather, he showed firmness and dignity, and corresponded with the king concerning the uncovering of his affair for which he had been imprisoned, so that his innocence might appear before the king and others, and he would meet him while holding his innocence of what had been attributed to him — and there is no shame upon Joseph or anyone else. Thus our Prophet ﷺ made clear the virtue of Joseph in this, and the strength of his soul in goodness, and the perfection of his patience, and the excellence of his discernment. And the Prophet ﷺ said concerning himself what he said out of humility and preference for conveying fully the perfection of Joseph's virtue — peace be upon him. And God knows best.

As for what pertains to the chains of transmission (asānīd) of this chapter, among what has already been explained is al-Musayyab, the father of Saʿīd — and it is with the opening of the yāʾ (Musayyab) according to the well-known opinion which the majority stated, and among them are those who break it (Musayyib) — and it is the saying of the people of [Medina].

chapters.title_en: Section 151 — On the Names of Certain Narrators, the Meaning of "Jāzahā" and "Anjazahā," and the Obligation of Faith in the Prophethood of Muhammad (Peace Be Upon Him) to All Mankind, and the Abrogation of All Religions by His Religion
chapters.arabic_text:
المدينة وفيه أبو سلمة بن عبد الرحمن بن عوف واسمه عبد الله على المشهور

وقيل اسمه إسماعيل وقيل لا يعرف اسمه وفيه قول مسلم رحمه الله وحدثني به إن

شاء الله تعالى عبد الله بن أسماء هذا مما قد ينكره على مسلم من لا علم

عنده ولا خبرة لديه لكون مسلم رحمه الله قال وحدثني به إن شاء الله تعالى

فيقول كيف يحتج بشيء يشك فيه وهذا خيال باطل من قائله فإن مسلما رحمه الله

لم يحتج بهذا الإسناد وإنما ذكره متابعة واستشهادا وقد قدمنا أنهم يحتملون

فى المتابعات والشواهد مالا يحتملون في الأصول والله
# 
# تعالى أعلم وفيه أبو عبيد عن أبي هريرة واسم أبي عبيد هذا سعد بن عبيد

المدني مولى عبد الرحمن بن أزهر ويقال مولى عبد الرحمن بن عوف وفيه أبو

أويس واسمه عبد الله بن عبد الله بن أويس بن مالك بن أبي عامر الأصبحي

المدني ومن ألفاظ الباب قوله قرأ الآية حتى جازها وفي الرواية الأخرى

أنجزها معنى جازها فرغ منها ومعنى أنجزها أتمها وفيه يوسف وفيه ست لغات ضم

السين وكسرها وفتحها مع الهمز فيهن وتركه والله أعلم

| (باب وجوب الإيمان برسالة نبينا محمد صلى الله عليه  
# وسلم (إلى جميع الناس ونسخ الملل بملته)
# [152] فيه قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (ما من نبي من الأنبياء إلا قد أعطي

من الآيات ما مثله آمن عليه البشر وإنما كان الذي أوتيته وحيا أوحى الله

إلي فأرجو أن أكون أكثرهم تابعا يوم القيامة)
# [153] وفي الرواية الأخرى (والذي نفس محمد بيده لا يسمع بي أحد من هذه

الأمة يهودي ولا نصراني ثم يموت ولم يؤمن بالذي أرسلت به إلا كان من أصحاب

النار) وفيه حديث (ثلاثة يؤتون أجرهم مرتين) أما ألفاظ الباب فقوله صلى

الله عليه وسلم ما مثله آمن عليه البشر)
# 
# آمن بالمد وفتح الميم ومثله مرفوع وفيه قول مسلم حدثنى يونس قال حدثنا بن

وهب قال وأخبرني عمرو أن أبا يونس حدثه فقوله وأخبرنى عمرو هو بالواو في

أول وأخبرني وهي واو حسنة فيها دقيقة نفيسة وفائدة لطيفة وذلك أن يونس سمع

من بن وهب أحاديث من جملتها هذا الحديث وليس هو أولها فقال بن وهب في

روايته الحديث الأول أخبرني عمرو بكذا ثم قال وأخبرني عمرو بكذا وأخبرني

عمرو بكذا إلى آخر تلك الأحاديث فإذا روى يونس عن بن وهب غير الحديث الأول

فينبغي أن يقول قال بن وهب وأخبرني عمرو فيأتي بالواو لأنه سمعه هكذا ولو

حذفها لجاز ولكن الأولى الإتيان بها ليكون راويا كما سمع والله أعلم وأما

أبو يونس فاسمه سليم بن جبير
# [154] وفيه (هشيم عن صالح بن صالح الهمداني عن الشعبي قال رأيت رجلا من

أهل خراسان سألى الشعبي فقال يا أبا عمرو) أما هشيم فبضم الهاء وهو مدلس

وقد قال عن صالح وقد قدمنا أن مثل هذا إذا كان الصحيح محمول على أن هشيما

ثبت سماعه لهذا الحديث من صالح وأما صالح فهو صالح بن صالح بن مسلم بن حيان

ولقب حيان حي قاله أبو علي الغساني وغيره وأما الهمداني فبإسكان الميم

وبالدال المهملة وأما الشعبي بفتح الشين فاسمه عامر وفي هذا الإسناد لطيفة

يتكرر مثلها وقد تقدم بيانها وهو أنه قال عن  صالح عن الشعبي قال رأيت رجلا

سأل الشعبي وهذا الكلام ليس منتظما في الظاهر ولكن تقديره حدثنا صالح عن

الشعبي قال رأيت رجلا سأل الشعبي بحديث وقصة طويلة قال فيها صالح رأيت رجلا

سأل الشعبي والله أعلم وفيه أبو بردة
# 
# عن أبي موسى اسم أبي بردة عامر وقيل الحرث واسم أبي موسى عبد الله بن قيس

وفيه قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (فغذاها فأحسن غذاءها) أما الأول فبتخفيف

الذال وأما الثانى فبالمد أما معانى الحديث فالحديث الأول اختلف فيه على

أقوال أحدها أن كل نبي أعطي من المعجزات ما كان مثله لمن كان قبله من

الأنبياء فآمن به البشر وأما معجزتي العظيمة الظاهرة فهي القرآن الذي لم

يعط أحد مثله فلهذا قال أنا أكثرهم تابعا والثاني معناه أن الذي أوتيته لا

يتطرق إليه تخييل بسحر وشبهة بخلاف معجزة غيري فإنه قد يخيل الساحر بشيء

مما يقارب صورتها كما خيلت السحرة في صورة عصا موسى صلى الله عليه وسلم

والخيال قد يروج على بعض العوام والفرق بين المعجزة والسحر والتخييل يحتاج

إلى فكر ونظر وقد يخطىء الناظر فيعتقدهما سواء والثالث معناه أن معجزات

الأنبياء انقرضت بانقراض أعصارهم ولم يشاهدها إلا من حضرها بحضرتهم ومعجزة

نبينا صلى الله عليه وسلم القرآن المستمر إلى يوم القيامة مع خرق العادة في

أسلوبه وبلاغته وإخباره بالمغيبات وعجز الجن والإنس عن أن يأتوا بسورة من

مثله مجتمعين أومتفرقين فى جميع الأعصار مع اعتنائهم بمعارضته فلم يقدروا

وهم أفصح القرون مع غير ذلك من وجوه إعجازه المعروفة والله أعلم وقوله صلى

الله عليه وسلم فأرجو أن أكون أكثرهم تابعا علم من أعلام النبوة فإنه أخبر

عليه السلام بهذا في زمن قلة المسلمين ثم من الله تعالى وفتح على المسلمين

البلاد وبارك فيهم حتى انتهى الأمر واتسع الإسلام في المسلمين إلى هذه

الغاية المعروفة ولله الحمد على هذه النعمة وسائر نعمه التي لا تحصى والله
chapters.anchors:
- Root: م-ث-ل (mathala)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Likeness, similitude, equivalent; something standing in place of another.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological discourse, denotes the miraculous sign (āyah) granted to prophets as proof of veracity, paralleling but distinct in kind.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for physical resemblance; metaphorical here for equivalence in evidential force.
- Root: ج-و-ز (jawaza)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To pass over, traverse, cross beyond a boundary.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Completion of an act, passing from one state to another; in Quranic recitation, finishing a passage.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for spatial crossing; metaphorical for completing a task.
- Root: ن-ج-ز (najaza)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To fulfill, accomplish, bring to completion.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Fulfillment of a promise or command; perfection of an action.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for finishing; no metaphorical extension beyond completion.
- Root: ت-ب-ع (tabi'a)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To follow, pursue, walk behind another.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In eschatology, followers (tābi'ūn) of a prophet in faith and obedience.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for physical following; metaphorical for adherence in belief.
- Sībawayh Rule: Al-ʿAṭf bi-al-Wāw (The Conjunctive Wāw) — The wāw of conjunction (wāw al-ʿaṭf) links a narrated report to a preceding chain, preserving the exact order of audition; its omission is permissible but its retention is preferred for fidelity to the heard transmission.
chapters.translation:
I say: Regarding al-Madīnah, and in it [the chain] is Abū Salamah ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf, whose name is ʿAbd Allāh according to the well-known [view]. And it is said his name is Ismāʿīl, and it is said his name is not known. And in it [there is] the statement of Muslim, may Allah have mercy on him: "And ʿAbd Allāh ibn Asmā' narrated to me, if Allah the Exalted wills." This is something that one who has no knowledge and no expertise might censure Muslim for, because Muslim, may Allah have mercy on him, said: "And he narrated to me, if Allah the Exalted wills." So he says: How can one adduce as proof something about which there is doubt? But this is a false fancy on the part of its proponent. For Muslim, may Allah have mercy on him, did not adduce this chain as proof; rather, he mentioned it as corroboration (mutābaʿah) and as supporting witness (shāhid). And we have already stated that they tolerate in corroborative reports (mutābiʿāt) and supporting witnesses (shawāhid) what they do not tolerate in primary chains (uṣūl). And Allah the Exalted knows best.

And in it [there is] Abū ʿUbayd, from Abū Hurayrah; the name of this Abū ʿUbayd is Saʿd ibn ʿUbayd, the Madanī, the freed slave (mawlā) of ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Azhar. And it is said: the freed slave of ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf. And in it [there is] Abū Uways, whose name is ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Uways ibn Mālik ibn Abī ʿĀmir al-Aṣbaḥī, the Madanī.

And among the expressions of this section is his saying, peace be upon him: "He recited the verse until he passed it (jāzahā)." And in the other narration: "he completed it (anjazahā)." The meaning of "jāzahā" is: he finished it; and the meaning of "anjazahā" is: he perfected it. And in it [there is the name] Yūsuf, and it has six pronunciations: ḍamm of the sīn, kasr of it, and fatḥ of it, with hamzah in all of them, and its omission. And Allah knows best.

| (Chapter: The Obligation of Faith in the Messengership of Our Prophet Muḥammad, Peace Be Upon Him, to All Mankind, and the Abrogation of All Religions by His Religion)

[152] In it [is] his saying, peace be upon him: "There is no prophet among the prophets except that he was given of the signs (āyāt) that which, its like, mankind believed upon. And indeed what I was given was a revelation (waḥy) that Allah revealed to me. So I hope to be the most followed of them on the Day of Resurrection."

[153] And in the other narration: "By Him in whose hand is the soul of Muḥammad, there is no one of this nation who hears of me — neither Jew nor Christian — then dies without believing in that with which I was sent, except that he will be among the companions of the Fire." And in it [is] the ḥadīth: "Three will be given their reward twice."

As for the expressions of the chapter, his saying, peace be upon him: "that which, its like, mankind believed upon" — "āmana" is with madd (prolongation) and fatḥ of the mīm, and "mithluhu" (its like) is raised (marfūʿ).

And in it [is] the saying of Muslim: "Yūnus narrated to me; he said: Ibn Wahb narrated to us; he said: And ʿAmr informed me that Abū Yūnus narrated to him." So his saying: "And ʿAmr informed me" — the wāw is at the beginning of "wa-akhbaranī" (and informed me). It is a good wāw containing a subtle point and a fine benefit. That is because Yūnus heard from Ibn Wahb ḥadīths, among which was this ḥadīth, and it was not the first of them. So Ibn Wahb said in his narration of the first ḥadīth: "ʿAmr informed me of such-and-such," then he said: "And ʿAmr informed me of such-and-such, and ʿAmr informed me of such-and-such," until the end of those ḥadīths. So when Yūnus narrates from Ibn Wahb other than the first ḥadīth, he should say: "Ibn Wahb said: And ʿAmr informed me," bringing the wāw because he heard it thus. And if he omitted it, it would be permissible, but the preferable [course] is to bring it, so that he narrates as he heard. And Allah knows best.

As for Abū Yūnus, his name is Sulaym ibn Jubayr.

[154] And in it [there is]: "Hushaym, from Ṣāliḥ ibn Ṣāliḥ al-Hamdānī, from al-Shaʿbī, who said: I saw a man from the people of Khurāsān ask al-Shaʿbī, and he said: O Abā ʿAmr." As for Hushaym, it is with ḍamm of the hā', and he was a mudallis (one who conceals gaps in transmission), and he said "from Ṣāliḥ." And we have already stated that such [a case], when [the report] is sound, is carried on the basis that Hushaym's hearing of this ḥadīth from Ṣāliḥ is confirmed. As for Ṣāliḥ, he is Ṣāliḥ ibn Ṣāliḥ ibn Muslim ibn Ḥayyān, and the nickname of Ḥayyān is Ḥayy; Abū ʿAlī al-Ghassānī and others said this. As for al-Hamdānī, it is with sukūn of the mīm and with the unpointed dāl. As for al-Shaʿbī, with fatḥ of the shīn, his name is ʿĀmir.

And in this chain there is a subtlety whose like recurs, and its explanation has already been given: namely, that he said: "from Ṣāliḥ, from al-Shaʿbī, who said: I saw a man ask al-Shaʿbī." And this speech is not, on the surface, well-ordered. But its estimation (taqdīr) is: "Ṣāliḥ narrated to us, from al-Shaʿbī, who said: I saw a man ask al-Shaʿbī" — with a ḥadīth and a long story in which Ṣāliḥ said: "I saw a man ask al-Shaʿbī." And Allah knows best.

And in it [there is] Abū Burdah, from Abū Mūsā. The name of Abū Burdah is ʿĀmir, and it is said: al-Ḥārith. And the name of Abū Mūsā is ʿAbd Allāh ibn Qays.

And in it [is] his saying, peace be upon him: "So he fed her and excelled in her feeding (fa-ghadhāhā fa-aḥsana ghidhā'ahā)." As for the first [word], it is with takhfīf (unvocalized lightening) of the dhāl; and as for the second, it is with madd (prolongation).

As for the meanings of the ḥadīth: The first ḥadīth has been differed over concerning it on several views. One of them: that every prophet was given of the miracles (muʿjizāt) that which was the like of what was given to those before him among the prophets, and mankind believed upon it. As for my great, manifest miracle, it is the Qurʾān, the like of which no one was given. For this reason he said: "I am the most followed of them." The second [view]: its meaning is that what I was given is not susceptible to the illusion of sorcery or doubt, unlike the miracle of another, for the sorcerer may conjure an illusion of something approximating its form, just as the sorcerers conjured an illusion in the form of the staff of Mūsā, peace be upon him. And illusion may deceive some of the common folk, and the distinction between miracle (muʿjizah), sorcery (siḥr), and illusion (takhyīl) requires thought and reflection, and the observer may err and deem them the same. The third [view]: its meaning is that the miracles of the prophets expired with the expiration of their eras, and none witnessed them except those present in their presence. As for the miracle of our Prophet, peace be upon him — the Qurʾān — it continues until the Day of Resurrection, with the breaking of custom (kharq al-ʿādah) in its style and eloquence, and its informing of unseen things, and the incapacity of jinn and mankind to produce a single sūrah like it, whether collectively or individually, in all eras, despite their earnest endeavor to oppose it — and they could not, though they were the most eloquent of centuries — along with other aspects of its miraculousness (iʿjāz) that are well known. And Allah knows best.

And his saying, peace be upon him: "So I hope to be the most followed of them" — this is a sign of prophethood (ʿalam min aʿlām al-nubuwwah). For he, peace be upon him, informed of this at a time when the Muslims were few. Then Allah the Exalted bestowed [favor] and opened the lands for the Muslims and blessed them, until the matter reached its end and Islam spread among the Muslims to this well-known extent. And to Allah belongs praise for this blessing and for the rest of His blessings that cannot be counted. And Allah knows best.

chapters.title_en: Section 152 — On the Abrogation of All Previous Laws by the Message of Our Prophet ﷺ, the Excuse of One Not Reached by the Call, the Virtue of the Believing People of the Book, and the Descent of Jesus Son of Mary as a Judge by Our Sacred Law
chapters.arabic_text:
أعلم وأما الحديث الثاني ففيه نسخ المللم كلها برسالة نبينا صلى الله عليه

وسلم وفي مفهومه دلالة على أن من لم تبلغه دعوة الإسلام فهو معذور وهذا جار

على ما تقدم في الأصول أنه لا حكم قبل ورود الشرع على الصحيح والله أعلم

وقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم لا يسمع بي أحد من هذه الأمة أي من هو موجود في

زمني وبعدي إلى يوم القيامة فكلهم يجب عليهم الدخول في طاعته وإنما ذكر

اليهودي والنصراني تنبيها على من سواهما وذلك لأن اليهود النصارى لهم كتاب

فإذا كان هذا شأنهم مع أن لهم كتابا فغيرهم ممن لا كتاب له أولى والله أعلم

وأما الحديث الثالث ففيه فضيلة من آمن من أهل الكتاب
# 
# بنبينا صلى الله عليه وسلم وأن له أجرين لايمانه بنبيه قبل النسخ والثانى

لا يمانه بنبينا صلى الله عليه وسلم وفيه فضيلة العبد المملوك القائم بحقوق

الله تعالى وحقوق سيده وفضيلة من أعتق مملوكته وتزوجها وليس هذا من الرجوع

في الصدقة في شيء بل هو إحسان إليها بعد إحسان وقول الشعبي (خذ هذا الحديث

بغير شيء فقد كان الرجل يرحل فيما دون هذا إلى المدينة) ففيه جواز قول

العالم مثل هذا تحريضا للسامع على حفظ ما قاله وفيه بيان ما كان السلف

رحمهم الله عليه من الرحلة إلى البلدان البعيدة في حديث واحد أو مسألة

واحدة والله أعلم

| (باب بيان نزول عيسى بن مريم حاكما (بشريعة نبينا 
# محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم) (وإكرام الله تعالى هذه الأمة زادها الله شرفا

وبيان الدليل على أن هذه الملة لا تنسخ) (وانه لا تزال طائفة منها ظاهرين

على الحق إلى يوم القيامة)
# [155] فيه الأحاديث المشهورة فنذكر ألفاظها ومعانيها وأحكامها على

ترتيبها فقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (ليوشكن أن ينزل فيكم عيسى بن مريم صلى

الله عليه وسلم حكما مقسطا فيكسر)
# 
# الصليب ويقتل الخنزير ويضع الجزية ويفيض المال حتى لا يقبله أحد) أما

ليوشكن فهو بضم الياء وكسر الشين ومعناه ليقربن وقوله فيكم أي في هذه الأمة

وإن كان خطابا لبعضها ممن لا يدرك نزوله وقوله  صلى الله عليه وسلم (حكما)

أي ينزل حاكما بهذه الشريعة لا ينزل نبيا برسالة مستقلة وشريعة ناسخة بل هو

حاكم من حكام هذه الأمة والمقسط العادل يقال أقسط يقسط إقساطا فهو مقسط إذا

عدل والقسط بكسر القاف العدل وقسط يقسط قسطا بفتح القاف فهو قاسط إذا جار

وقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (فيكسر الصليب) معناه يكسره حقيقة ويبطل ما يزعمه

النصارى من تعظيمه وفيه دليل على تغيير المنكرات وآلات الباطل وقتل الخنزير

من هذا القبيل وفيه دليل للمختار من مذهبنا ومذهب الجمهور أنا اذا وجدنا

الخنزير فى دار الكفر أوغيرها وتمكنا من قتله قتلناه وإبطال لقول من شذ من

أصحابنا وغيرهم فقال يترك إذا لم يكن فيه ضراوة وأما قوله صلى الله عليه

وسلم (ويضع الجزية) فالصواب في معناه أنه لا يقبلها ولا يقبل من الكفار إلا

الإسلام ومن بذل منهم الجزية لم يكف عنه بها بل لا يقبل إلا الإسلام أو

القتل هكذا قاله الإمام أبو سليمان الخطابي وغيره من العلماء رحمهم الله

تعالى وحكى القاضي عياض رحمه الله عن بعض العلماء معنى هذا ثم قال وقد يكون

فيض المال هنا من وضع الجزية وهو ضربها على جميع الكفرة فإنه لا يقاتله أحد

فتضع الحرب أوزارها وانقياد جميع الناس له إما بالإسلام وإما بإلقاء يد

فيضع عليه الجزية ويضربها وهذا كلام القاضي وليس بمقبول والصواب ما قدمناه

وهو أنه لا يقبل منه إلا الإسلام فعلى هذا قد يقال هذا خلاف حكم الشرع

اليوم فإن الكتابي إذا بذل الجزية وجب قبولها ولم يجز قتله ولا إكراهه على

الإسلام وجوابه أن هذا الحكم ليس بمستمر إلى يوم القيامة بل هو مقيد بما

قبل عيسى عليه السلام وقد أخبرنا النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في هذه الأحاديث

الصحيحة بنسخه وليس عيسى عليه السلام هو الناسخ بل نبينا صلى الله عليه

وسلم هو المبين للنسخ فإن عيسى يحكم بشرعنا فدل على أن الامتناع من قبول

الجزية في ذلك الوقت هو شرع نبينا محمد  صلى الله عليه وسلم وأما قوله صلى

الله عليه وسلم (ويفيض المال) فهو بفتح الياء ومعناه يكثر وتنزل البركات

وتكثر الخيرات بسبب العدل
# 
# وعدم التظالم وتقيء الأرض أفلاذ كبدها كما جاء في الحديث الآخر وتقل أيضا

الرغبات لقصر الآمال وعلمهم بقرب الساعة فإن عيسى صلى الله عليه وسلم علم

من أعلام الساعة والله أعلم وأما قوله في الرواية الأخرى (حتى تكون السجدة

الواحدة خيرا من الدنيا وما فيها) فمعناه والله أعلم أن الناس تكثر رغبتهم

في الصلاة وسائر الطاعات لقصر آمالهم وعلمهم بقرب القيامة وقلة رغبتهم في

الدنيا لعدم الحاجة إليها وهذا هو الظاهر من معنى الحديث وقال القاضي عياض

رحمه الله معناه أن أجرها خير لمصليها من صدقته بالدنيا وما فيها لفيض

المال حينئذ وهوانه وقلة الشح وقلة الحاجة إليه للنفقة في الجهاد قال

والسجدة هي السجدة بعينها أو تكون عبارة عن الصلاة والله أعلم وأما قوله

(ثم يقول أبو هريرة اقرؤوا إن شئتم وإن من أهل الكتاب إلا ليؤمنن به قبل
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ن-س-خ (n-s-kh)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Erasure, transcription, replacement; to remove and substitute one thing for another.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Technical legal abrogation (naskh) — the supersession of a prior divine ruling by a later one.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal in scribal copying; metaphorical in jurisprudence — the "erasure" of a ruling's applicability.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clause (al-Sharṭ wa al-Jawāb) — the protasis "if one has not been reached" governs the apodosis of excusal, requiring careful temporal parsing.
chapters.translation:
Know that as for the second hadith, it contains the abrogation (naskh) of all previous laws (milal) by the message of our Prophet ﷺ. And in its implication (mafhūm) there is an indication that whoever has not been reached by the call of Islam is excused. This runs in accordance with what has preceded in the principles of theology (uṣūl) — that there is no ruling (ḥukm) before the advent of revelation (sharʿ), according to the soundest position (al-ṣaḥīḥ). And Allah knows best.

And his saying ﷺ: "There is no one of this nation who hears of me" — meaning whoever exists in my time and after me until the Day of Resurrection — all of them are obligated to enter into obedience to him. He only mentioned the Jew and the Christian as a notification (tanbīh) regarding those other than them. This is because the Jews and Christians possess a scripture (kitāb). If such is their case despite having a scripture, then those who have no scripture are even more deserving [of the obligation]. And Allah knows best.

As for the third hadith, it contains the virtue of one from the People of the Book who believes in our Prophet ﷺ — that he has two rewards: one for his faith in his own prophet before the abrogation, and the second for his faith in our Prophet ﷺ. It also contains the virtue of the enslaved servant who fulfills the rights of Allah the Exalted and the rights of his master, and the virtue of one who frees his female slave and then marries her. This is not in any way a return (rujūʿ) in charity (ṣadaqah); rather, it is an act of beneficence (iḥsān) toward her after a prior beneficence.

And the saying of al-Shaʿbī: "Take this hadith for nothing, for a man would once travel to Medina for something less than this" — in this is the permissibility of a scholar saying such a thing as an incitement (taḥrīḍ) for the listener to preserve what he has said. And in it is an exposition of what the Salaf — may Allah have mercy on them — were upon: traveling to distant lands for a single hadith or a single issue. And Allah knows best.

[Chapter: The Explanation of the Descent of Jesus Son of Mary as a Judge by the Sacred Law of Our Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, and Allah's Honoring of This Nation — may Allah increase it in honor — and the Exposition of the Proof that This Religion (millah) Shall Not Be Abrogated, and that a Group of It Shall Remain Victorious upon the Truth Until the Day of Resurrection]

[155] In it are the well-known hadiths; we shall mention their wordings, meanings, and rulings in their order.

His saying ﷺ: "Soon (layūshikanna) there will descend among you Jesus Son of Mary ﷺ as a just judge (ḥakaman muqsiṭan); he will break the cross, kill the swine, impose the jizyah, and wealth will overflow until no one accepts it."

As for "layūshikanna" — it is with a ḍammah on the yāʾ and a kasrah on the shīn — its meaning is "it will surely draw near." His saying "among you" (fīkum) means "in this nation," even though the address is to some of them — those who will not witness his descent.

His saying ﷺ: "as a judge" (ḥakaman) — meaning he descends as a judge by this sacred law (sharīʿah); he does not descend as a prophet with an independent message and an abrogating law. Rather, he is a judge from among the judges of this nation. And "al-muqsiṭ" is the just one. It is said: "aqsaṭa yuqsiṭu iqsāṭan, fa-huwa muqsiṭ" — when he is just. And "al-qisṭ" (with kasrah on the qāf) is justice. And "qasaṭa yaqsiṭu qasṭan" (with fatḥah on the qāf) — "fa-huwa qāsiṭ" — when he is unjust.

His saying ﷺ: "he will break the cross" — its meaning is that he will literally break it and nullify what the Christians claim of its veneration. In this is a proof for the changing of evil deeds (munkarāt) and the instruments of falsehood (ālāt al-bāṭil). The killing of the swine is of this category. And in this is a proof for the chosen position (al-mukhtār) of our school (madhhab) and the position of the majority (jumhūr) — that when we find a swine in the abode of unbelief (dār al-kufr) or elsewhere and are able to kill it, we kill it. And it nullifies the position of those who deviated from our companions and others who said: "It should be left alone if there is no harm (ḍarāwah) in it."

As for his saying ﷺ: "and he will impose the jizyah" — the correct meaning is that he will not accept it, and will not accept from the unbelievers anything except Islam. Whoever offers the jizyah from them will not be spared by it; rather, nothing will be accepted except Islam or death. This is what Imam Abū Sulaymān al-Khaṭṭābī and other scholars — may Allah the Exalted have mercy on them — said. And Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ — may Allah have mercy on him — related from some scholars a meaning of this. Then he said: "And it may be that the overflowing of wealth here is from the imposition of the jizyah — namely, its being levied upon all the unbelievers, for no one will fight him. Thus war will lay down its burdens, and all people will submit to him — either by Islam or by casting down their hands. So he will impose the jizyah upon them and levy it." This is the speech of Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ, and it is not acceptable. The correct view is what we have presented — that nothing will be accepted from him except Islam.

On this basis, it may be said: This contradicts the ruling of the sacred law today, for if a scriptuary (kitābī) offers the jizyah, it is obligatory to accept it, and it is not permissible to kill him nor to coerce him to Islam. The answer is that this ruling is not continuous until the Day of Resurrection; rather, it is restricted to the period before Jesus — peace be upon him. The Prophet ﷺ has informed us in these authentic hadiths of its abrogation. And Jesus — peace be upon him — is not the abrogator; rather, our Prophet ﷺ is the one who clarified the abrogation. For Jesus judges by our sacred law, which indicates that the refusal to accept the jizyah at that time is the sacred law of our Prophet Muhammad ﷺ.

As for his saying ﷺ: "and wealth will overflow" (yafīḍ al-māl) — it is with a fatḥah on the yāʾ, and its meaning is that it will become abundant, blessings will descend, and good things will multiply due to justice and the absence of mutual wrongdoing. The earth will vomit forth the pieces of its liver (aflādh kabidihā), as has come in the other hadith. Desires (raghabāt) will also diminish due to the shortening of hopes and their knowledge of the nearness of the Hour — for Jesus ﷺ is one of the signs of the Hour. And Allah knows best.

As for his saying in the other narration: "until a single prostration (sajdah) will be better than the world and all that is in it" — its meaning, and Allah knows best, is that people's desire for prayer and all acts of obedience will increase due to the shortening of their hopes and their knowledge of the nearness of the Resurrection, and their desire for the world will diminish due to the absence of need for it. This is the apparent meaning of the hadith.

And Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ — may Allah have mercy on him — said: "Its meaning is that its reward is better for the one who performs it than his giving charity with the world and all that is in it, due to the overflowing of wealth at that time, its lowliness, the absence of miserliness, and the lack of need for it for spending in jihad." He said: "And the prostration is the prostration itself, or it may be an expression for the prayer." And Allah knows best.

As for his saying: "Then Abū Hurayrah says: 'Recite, if you wish: {«And there is none of the People of the Book but will surely believe in him before his death»}'" — [the verse continues]...

chapters.title_en: Section 153 — On the Interpretation of "His Death" in the Verse, the Hadith of the She-Camels, the Acceptance of Faith at the Rising of the Sun from the West, and the Beginning of Revelation
chapters.arabic_text:
موته) ففيه دلالة ظاهرة على أن مذهب أبي هريرة في الآية أن الضمير في موته

يعود على عيسى عليه السلام ومعناها وما من أهل الكتاب يكون في زمن عيسى

عليه السلام إلا من آمن به وعلم أنه عبد الله وبن أمته وهذا مذهب جماعة من

المفسرين وذهب كثيرون أو الأكثرون إلى أن الضمير يعود على الكتابي ومعناها

وما من أهل الكتاب أحد يحضره الموت إلا آمن عند الموت قبل خروج روحه بعيسى

صلى الله عليه وسلم وانه عبد
# 
# الله وبن أمته ولكن لا ينفعه هذا الإيمان لأنه في حضرة الموت وحالة النزع

وتلك الحالة لا حكم لما يفعل أو يقال فيها فلا يصح فيها إسلام ولا كفر ولا

وصية ولا بيع ولا عتق ولا غير ذلك من الأقوال لقول الله تعالى وليست التوبة

للذين يعملون السيئات حتى إذا حضر أحدهم الموت قال انى تبت الآن وهذا

المذهب أظهر فإن الأول يخص الكتابي وظاهر القرآن عمومه لكل كتابي  في زمن

عيسى وقبل نزله ويؤيد هذا قراءة من قرأ قبل موتهم وقيل إن الهاء في به يعود

على نبينا محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم والهاء في موته تعود على الكتابي والله

أعلم قوله في الإسناد (عن عطاء بن ميناء) هو بكسر الميم بعدها ياء مثناة من

تحت ساكنة ثم نون ثم ألف ممدودة هذا هو المشهور وقال صاحب المطالع يمد

ويقصر والله أعلم وأما قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (وليتركن القلاص فلا يسعى

عليها) فالقلاص بكسر القاف جمع قلوص بفتحها وهي من الإبل كالفتاة من النساء

والحدث من الرجال ومعناه أن يزهد فيها ولا يرغب في اقتنائها لكثرة الأموال

وقلة الآمال وعدم الحاجة والعلم بقرب القيامة وإنما ذكرت القلاص لكونها

أشرف الإبل التي هي أنفس الأموال عند العرب وهو شبيه بمعنى قول الله عز وجل

واذا العشار عطلت ومعنى لا يسعى عليها لا يعتنى بها أي يتساهل أهلها فيها

ولا يعتنون بها هذا هو الظاهر وقال القاضي عياض وصاحب المطالع رحمهما الله

معنى لا يسعى عليها أي لا تطلب زكاتها إذ لا يوجد من يقبلها وهذا تأويل

باطل من وجوه كثيرة تفهم من هذا الحديث وغيره بل الصواب ما قدمناه والله

أعلم وأما قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (ولتذهبن الشحناء) فالمراد به العداوة

وقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (وليدعون إلى المال فلا يقبله أحد) هو بضم العين
# 
# وفتح الواو وتشديد النون وإنما لا يقبله أحد لما ذكرنا من كثرة الأموال

وقصر الآمال وعدم الحاجة وقلة الرغبة للعلم بقرب الساعة
# [156] وأما قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (لا تزال طائفة من أمتي يقاتلون على

الحق ظاهرين إلى يوم القيامة) فقد قدمنا بيانه والجمع بينه وبين حديث
# 
# لا تقوم الساعة على أحد يقول الله الله وقوله (تكرمة الله هذه الأمة) هو

بنصب تكرمة على المصدر أو على أنه مفعول له والله أعلم

| (باب بيان الزمن الذي لا يقبل فيه الإيمان
# [157] فيه قوله
# صلى الله عليه وسلم (لاتقوم الساعة حتى تطلع الشمس من  مغربها فإذا طلعت

من مغربها آمن الناس كلهم أجمعون فيومئذ لا ينفع نفسا إيمانها لم تكن آمنت

من قبل أو كسبت)
# 
# فى ايمانها خيرا)
# [158] وفى الرواية الاخرى (ثلاث إذا خرجن لا ينفع نفسا إيمانها لم تكن

آمنت من قبل أو كسبت في إيمانها خيرا طلوع الشمس من مغربها والدجال ودابة

الأرض) قال القاضي عياض رحمه الله هذا الحديث على ظاهره عند أهل الحديث

والفقه والمتكلمين من أهل السنة خلافا لما تأولته الباطنية وأما قوله صلى

الله عليه وسلم
# [159] في الحديث الآخر في الشمس (مستقرها تحت العرش فتخر ساجدة) فهذا مما

اختلف المفسرون فيه فقال جماعة
# 
# بظاهر الحديث قال الواحدي وعلى هذا القول إذا غربت كل يوم استقرت تحت

العرش إلى أن تطلع من مغربها وقال قتادة ومقاتل معناه تجري إلى وقت لها

وأجل لا تتعداه قال الواحدي وعلى هذا مستقرها انتهاء سيرها عند انقضاء

الدنيا وهذا اختيار الزجاج وقال الكلبي تسير في
# 
# منازلها حتى تنتهي إلى آخر مستقرها الذي لا تجاوزه ثم ترجع إلى أول

منازلها واختار بن قتيبة هذا القول والله أعلم وأما سجود الشمس فهو بتمييز

وادراك بخلق الله تعالى فيها وفي الإسناد عبد الحميد بن بيان الواسطي هو

بباء موحدة ثم ياء مثناة من تحت وفي هذا الحديث بقايا تأتي في آخر الكتاب

إن شاء الله تعالى حيث ذكره مسلم رحمه الله تعالى والله سبحانه وتعالى أعلم

بالصواب

| (باب بدء الوحى إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
# [160] فيه الأحاديث المشهورة فنذكرها إن شاء الله تعالى على ترتيب

ألفاظها ومعانيها فقوله في الإسناد (أبو الطاهر بن السرح) هو بالسين والحاء

المهملتين والسين مفتوحة وقوله (أن عائشة رضي الله عنها قالت كان أول ما

بدىء به رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم من الوحي الرؤيا الصادقة) هذا الحديث

من مراسيل الصحابة رضي الله عنهم فإن عائشة رضي الله عنها لم تدرك هذه

القضية فتكون قد سمعتها من النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أو من الصحابي وقد

قدمنا في  الفصول أن مرسل الصحابي حجة عند جميع العلماء إلا ما انفرد به

- Root: م-و-ت (m-w-t)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Death; the departure of the soul; cessation of vital functions.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological discourse, the moment of death (ḥaḍrat al-mawt) is a state of duress (iḍṭirār) wherein acts and utterances carry no legal or salvific weight.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage denotes physical death; metaphorical (majāz) usage may denote the "death" of a faculty or era, but here it is literal.
- Sībawayh Rule: Pronoun Resolution (Marjiʿ al-Ḍamīr) — The antecedent of a pronoun is determined by syntactic context and semantic plausibility; ambiguity is resolved by textual evidence (qarīnah).

- Root: ق-ل-ص (q-l-ṣ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: A young, swift she-camel (qalūṣ); plural qilāṣ.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Symbolizes prized wealth; in eschatological contexts, its neglect signals the nearness of the Hour.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal reference to camels; metaphorically, the abandonment of worldly treasures.
- Sībawayh Rule: Collective Noun Agreement — The plural (qilāṣ) with a singular predicate (lā yusʿā) indicates distributive neglect.

- Root: ش-ح-ن (sh-ḥ-n)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To fill; shiḥnāʾ (enmity) as a filling of the heart with rancor.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In eschatological contexts, the removal of shiḥnāʾ signifies the purification of hearts from mutual hatred.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: filling a vessel; metaphorical: the heart filled with hostility.
- Sībawayh Rule: Masdar Usage — The verbal noun (shiḥnāʾ) functions as a concrete state, not an action.

- Root: س-ج-د (s-j-d)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Prostration; humble submission.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): For inanimate beings, prostration is an act of divinely-instilled cognition (tamyīz) and obedience, not voluntary worship.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for humans; metaphorical (majāz) for celestial bodies, denoting their subservience to divine command.
- Sībawayh Rule: Causative Construction — The verb (takhirru sājidah) implies an inherent faculty granted by God.
chapters.translation:
I say: Regarding his statement "his death" (mawtihi), therein is an evident indication that the doctrine of Abū Hurayrah concerning the verse is that the pronoun in "his death" refers to Jesus (ʿalayhi al-salām), and its meaning is: "There is none of the People of the Book but will surely believe in him before his death" — that is, none of the People of the Book who exists during the time of Jesus (ʿalayhi al-salām) except that he will believe in him and know that he is the servant of God and the son of His handmaiden. This is the doctrine of a group of the exegetes (mufassirūn). However, many — or the majority — have held that the pronoun refers to the scriptural person (kitābī), and its meaning is: "There is none of the People of the Book but that when death approaches him, he will believe at the moment of death, before his soul departs, in Jesus (ṣallā Allāhu ʿalayhi wa-sallam) and that he is the servant of God and the son of His handmaiden." Yet this faith will not benefit him, because it occurs in the presence of death and the throes of agony (ḥālat al-nazaʿ). In that state, no weight is given to any deed or utterance; neither Islam nor disbelief is valid therein, nor a bequest, nor a sale, nor a manumission, nor any other speech, due to the saying of God the Exalted: {«وَلَيْسَتِ التَّوْبَةُ لِلَّذِينَ يَعْمَلُونَ السَّيِّئَاتِ حَتَّىٰ إِذَا حَضَرَ أَحَدَهُمُ الْمَوْتُ قَالَ إِنِّي تُبْتُ الْآنَ»} ("And repentance is not for those who commit evil deeds until when death approaches one of them, he says, 'Indeed, I repent now'"). This latter doctrine is the more apparent (aẓhar), for the first one restricts the verse to the scriptural person of Jesus' time, whereas the apparent wording of the Qur'an is general for every scriptural person in the time of Jesus and before his descent. This is supported by the reading of those who recited "before their death" (qabla mawtihim). It has also been said that the pronoun in "in him" (bihi) refers to our Prophet Muḥammad (ṣallā Allāhu ʿalayhi wa-sallam), and the pronoun in "his death" refers to the scriptural person. And God knows best.

Regarding his statement in the chain of transmission (isnād): "from ʿAṭāʾ ibn Maynāʾ" — it is with a kasrah on the mīm, followed by a yāʾ (the dual-form letter from below) that is quiescent, then a nūn, then an elongated alif. This is the well-known pronunciation. The author of al-Maṭāliʿ said it may be elongated or shortened. And God knows best.

As for his statement (ṣallā Allāhu ʿalayhi wa-sallam): "And the swift she-camels (al-qilāṣ) will be left, and none will strive after them" — al-qilāṣ, with a kasrah on the qāf, is the plural of qalūṣ, with a fatḥah on the qāf, which is a young she-camel, akin to a young woman among women and a youth among men. Its meaning is that people will become ascetic regarding them and will not desire their acquisition due to the abundance of wealth, the shortness of hopes, the lack of need, and the knowledge of the nearness of the Hour. The she-camels are mentioned specifically because they are the noblest of camels, which are the most precious of possessions among the Arabs. This resembles the meaning of the saying of God the Exalted: {«وَإِذَا الْعِشَارُ عُطِّلَتْ»} ("And when the pregnant she-camels are neglected"). The meaning of "none will strive after them" (lā yusʿā ʿalayhā) is that no one will care for them — that is, their owners will be negligent regarding them and will not attend to them. This is the apparent interpretation. However, Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ and the author of al-Maṭāliʿ (may God have mercy on them) said: The meaning of "none will strive after them" is that their zakāh will not be sought, for no one will be found to accept it. This interpretation is false on many counts, as can be understood from this hadith and others. Rather, the correct view is what we have presented. And God knows best.

As for his statement (ṣallā Allāhu ʿalayhi wa-sallam): "And enmity (al-shiḥnāʾ) will depart" — what is meant by it is hostility (al-ʿadāwah).

As for his statement (ṣallā Allāhu ʿalayhi wa-sallam): "And they will be called to wealth, but no one will accept it" — it is with a ḍammah on the ʿayn, a fatḥah on the wāw, and a shaddah on the nūn. No one will accept it only for what we have mentioned: the abundance of wealth, the shortness of hopes, the lack of need, and the diminished desire due to the knowledge of the nearness of the Hour.

[156] As for his statement (ṣallā Allāhu ʿalayhi wa-sallam): "A group of my community will not cease fighting upon the truth, victorious, until the Day of Resurrection" — we have already explained it and the reconciliation between it and the hadith "The Hour will not be established upon anyone who says 'God, God.'" As for his statement: "as an honor (takrimah) from God for this community" — takrimah is in the accusative (naṣb), either as a verbal noun (maṣdar) or as an object of purpose (mafʿūl lahu). And God knows best.

| (Chapter: The Explanation of the Time in Which Faith is Not Accepted)

[157] In it is his statement (ṣallā Allāhu ʿalayhi wa-sallam): "The Hour will not be established until the sun rises from its place of setting. When it rises from its place of setting, all people will believe, all of them together. And on that day, faith will not benefit a soul that had not believed before, or had not earned good through its faith."

[158] In the other narration: "Three things, when they appear, faith will not benefit a soul that had not believed before, or had not earned good through its faith: the rising of the sun from its place of setting, the Dajjāl, and the Beast of the Earth." Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ (may God have mercy on him) said: This hadith is upon its apparent meaning (ẓāhir) according to the people of hadith, jurisprudence, and the theologians (mutakallimūn) of the Ahl al-Sunnah, contrary to what the Bāṭiniyyah have interpreted.

As for his statement (ṣallā Allāhu ʿalayhi wa-sallam) in the other hadith concerning the sun: "Its resting place (mustaqarr) is beneath the Throne, and it falls prostrate" — this is among the matters over which the exegetes have differed. A group held the apparent meaning of the hadith. Al-Wāḥidī said: According to this view, when it sets each day, it settles beneath the Throne until it rises from its place of setting. Qatādah and Muqātil said: Its meaning is that it runs to a time appointed for it and a term it does not exceed. Al-Wāḥidī said: According to this, "its resting place" is the end of its course at the conclusion of this world. This is the choice of al-Zajjāj. Al-Kalbī said: It travels through its stations until it reaches the final resting place it does not surpass, then it returns to the beginning of its stations. Ibn Qutaybah chose this latter view. And God knows best.

As for the sun's prostration, it is through a discernment (tamyīz) and perception (idrāk) created by God the Exalted within it. In the chain of transmission is ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd ibn Bayān al-Wāsiṭī — it is with a single bāʾ, then a yāʾ (the dual-form letter from below). In this hadith there are remaining points that will come at the end of the book, God willing, where Muslim (may God have mercy on him) mentions it. And God, Glorified and Exalted, knows best what is correct.

| (Chapter: The Beginning of Revelation to the Messenger of God, ṣallā Allāhu ʿalayhi wa-sallam)

[160] In it are the well-known hadiths; we will mention them, God willing, in the order of their wordings and meanings. His statement in the chain of transmission: "Abū al-Ṭāhir ibn al-Sarraḥ" — it is with the unpointed sīn and ḥāʾ, and the sīn is fatḥah. His statement: "That ʿĀʾishah (raḍiya Allāhu ʿanhā) said: 'The first thing with which the Messenger of God (ṣallā Allāhu ʿalayhi wa-sallam) was commenced of revelation was the true vision (al-ruʾyā al-ṣādiqah)'" — this hadith is among the mursal reports of the Companions (raḍiya Allāhu ʿanhum), for ʿĀʾishah (raḍiya Allāhu ʿanhā) did not witness this event, so she must have heard it from the Prophet (ṣallā Allāhu ʿalayhi wa-sallam) or from a Companion. We have already stated in the chapters that the mursal of a Companion is an authoritative proof (ḥujjah) according to all scholars, except for what is uniquely held by...

chapters.title_en: Section 154 — On the Beginning of Revelation and the First Descent of the Qur'an
chapters.arabic_text:
الأستاذ أبو إسحاق الإسفرايني والله أعلم وقولها رضي الله عنها (الرؤيا

الصادقة) وفي رواية البخاري رحمه الله الرؤيا الصالحة وهما بمعنى واحد وفى

من هنا قولان أحدهما أنها لبيان الجنس والثانى للتبعيض ذكرهما القاضي

وقولها (فكان لا يرى رؤيا إلا جاءت مثل فلق الصبح) قال أهل اللغة فلق الصبح

وفرق الصبح بفتح الفاء واللام والراء هو ضياؤه وإنما يقال هذا في الشيء

الواضح البين قال القاضي رحمه الله وغيره من)
# 
# العلماء انما ابتدىء صلى الله عليه وسلم بالرؤيا لئلا يفجأه الملك ويأتيه

صريح النبوة بغتة فلا يحتملها قوى البشرية فبدىء بأول خصال النبوة وتباشير

الكرامة من صدق الرؤيا وما جاء في الحديث الآخر من رؤية الضوء وسماع الصوت

وسلام الحجر والشجر عليه بالنبوة قولها (ثم حبب إليه الخلاء فكان يخلو بغار

حراء يتحنث فيه وهو التعبد الليالي أولات العدد قبل أن يرجع إلى أهله

ويتزود ثم يرجع إلى خديجة رضى الله عنها فيتزود لمثلها حتى فجئه الحق) أما

الخلاء فممدود وهو الخلوة وهي شأن الصالحين وعباد الله العارفين قال أبو

سليمان الخطابي رحمه الله حببت العزلة إليه صلى الله عليه وسلم لأن معها

فراغ القلب وهي معينة على التفكر وبها ينقطع عن مألوفات البشر ويتخشع قلبه

والله أعلم وأما الغار فهو الكهف والنقب في الجبل وجمعه غيران والمغار

والمغارة بمعنى الغار وتصغير الغار غوير وأما حراء فبكسر الحاء المهملة

وتخفيف الراء وبالمد وهو مصروف ومذكر هذا هو الصحيح وقال القاضي فيه لغتان

التذكير والتأنيث والتذكير أكثر فمن ذكره صرفه ومن أنثه لم يصرفه أراد

البقعة أو الجهة التي فيها الجبل قال القاضي وقال بعضهم فيه حرى بفتح الحاء

والقصر وهذا ليس بشيء قال أبو عمر الزاهد صاحب ثعلب وأبو سليمان الخطابي

وغيرهما أصحاب الحديث والعوام يخطئون في حراء في ثلاثة مواضع يفتحون الحاء

وهي مكسورة ويكسرون الراء وهي مفتوحة ويقصرون الألف وهي ممدودة وحراء جبل

بينه وبين مكة  نحو ثلاثة أميال عن يسار الذاهب من مكة إلى منى والله أعلم

وأما التحنث بالحاء المهملة والنون والثاء المثلثة فقد فسره بالتعبد وهو

تفسير صحيح وأصل الحنث الإثم فمعنى يتحنث يتجنب الحنث فكأنه بعبادته يمنع

نفسه من الحنث ومثل يتحنث يتحرح ويتأثم أي يتجنب الحرج والإثم وأما قولها

الليالى أولات العدد فمتعلق يتحنث لا بالتعبد ومعناه يتحنث الليالي ولو جعل

متعلقا بالتعبد فسد المعنى فإن التحنث لا يشترط فيه الليالي بل يطلق على

القليل والكثير وهذا التفسير اعترض بين كلام
# 
# عائشة رضي الله عنها وأما كلامها فيتحنث فيه الليالي أولات العدد والله

أعلم وقولها فجئه الحق أي جاءه الوحي بغتة فإنه صلى الله عليه وسلم لم يكن

متوقعا للوحي ويقال فجئه بكسر الجيم وبعدها همزة مفتوحة ويقال فجأه بفتح

الجيم والهمزة لغتان مشهورتان حكاهما الجوهري وغيره قوله صلى الله عليه

وسلم (ما أنا بقارىء) معناه لا أحسن القراءة فما نافية هذا هو الصواب وحكى

القاضي عياض رحمه الله فيها خلافا بين العلماء منهم من جعلها نافية ومنهم

من جعلها استفهامية وضعفوه بإدخال الباء في الخبر قال القاضي ويصحح قول من

قال استفهامية رواية من روى ما أقرأ ويصح أن تكون ما في هذه الرواية أيضا

نافية والله أعلم قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (فغطني حتى بلغ مني الجهد ثم

أرسلني) أما غطني فبالغين المعجمة والطاء المهملة ومعناه عصرني وضمني يقال

غطه وغته وضغطه وعصره وخنقه وغمزه كله بمعنى واحد وأما الجهد فيجوز فتح

الجيم وضمها لغتان وهو الغاية والمشقة ويجوز نصب الدال ورفعها فعلى النصب

بلغ جبريل مني الجهد وعلى الرفع بلغ الجهد مني مبلغه وغايته وممن ذكر

الوجهين في نصب الدال ورفعها صاحب التحرير وغيره وأما أرسلني فمعناه أطلقني

قال العلماء والحكمة في الغط شغله من الالتفات والمبالغة في أمره بإحضار

قلبه لما يقوله له وكرره ثلاثا مبالغة فى التنبيه ففيه أنه ينبغي للمعلم أن

يحتاط في تنبيه المتعلم وأمره بإحضار قلبه والله أعلم قوله صلى الله عليه

وسلم  (ثم أرسلني فقال اقرأ باسم ربك الذى خلق) هذا دليل صريح في أن أول ما

نزل من القرآن اقرأ وهذا هو الصواب الذي عليه الجماهير من السلف والخلف

وقيل أوله يا أيها المدثر وليس بشيء وسنذكره بعد هذا في
# 
# موضعه من هذا الباب إن شاء الله تعالى واستدل بهذا الحديث بعض من يقول إن

بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم ليست من القرآن في أوائل السور لكونها لم تذكر هنا

وجواب المثبتين لها أنها لم تنزل أولا بل نزلت البسملة في وقت آخر كما نزل

باقي السورة في وقت آخر قولها (ترجف بوادره) بفتح الباء الموحدة ومعنى ترجف

ترعد وتضطرب وأصله شدة الحركة قال أبو عبيد وسائر أهل اللغة والغريب وهي

اللحمة التي بين المنكب والعنق تضطرب عند فزع الإنسان قوله صلى الله عليه

وسلم (زملوني زملوني) هكذا هو في الروايات مكرر مرتين ومعنى زملوني غطوني

بالثياب ولفوني بها وقولها فزملوه حتى ذهب عنه الروع هو بفتح الراء وهو
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ر-ء-ي (ra-ʾa-yā)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Perception by sight or vision; in dream-context, the faculty of inner sight (ruʾyā) as distinct from ocular vision.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Ruʾyā (vision) in prophetic idiom denotes truthful inner perception granted by God, a precursor to revelation (waḥy).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) for physical sight; metaphorical (majāz) for dream-vision as a form of divine communication.
- Root: خ-ل-و (kh-l-w)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Emptiness, solitude; khilwah (seclusion) as withdrawal from company.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In spiritual praxis, seclusion (khalwah) is a means to purify the heart for contemplation (tafakkur).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: being alone; metaphorical: heart's detachment from worldly attachments.
- Root: ح-ن-ث (ḥ-n-th)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Sin, transgression; taḥannuth (the fifth form) means to avoid sin.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Taḥannuth as devotional practice—abstaining from sin through worship.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: sin; metaphorical: the act of shunning sin as worship.
- Root: ف-ج-أ (f-j-ʾ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To come upon suddenly, unexpectedly.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In revelation context, the sudden arrival of divine truth (ḥaqq) without prior expectation.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: sudden assault; metaphorical: the abrupt onset of prophetic inspiration.
- Sībawayh Rule: Rule of Taʿlīq (Suspension) — The particle "mā" (ما) in "mā anā bi-qāriʾ" is analyzed as nāfiyah (negative) governing the predicate via the preposition "bi-", per the standard construction of laysa-like negation; the alternative istifhāmiyyah (interrogative) reading is syntactically weakened by the presence of "bi-" in the khabar.
chapters.translation:
The teacher Abū Isḥāq al-Isfarāyīnī — and God knows best. Her saying, may God be pleased with her, "the truthful vision (al-ruʾyā al-ṣādiqah)" — and in the narration of al-Bukhārī, may God have mercy on him, "the righteous vision (al-ruʾyā al-ṣāliḥah)" — and the two are of one meaning. Concerning the "min" (from) here, there are two sayings: one, that it is for the clarification of the genus (li-bayān al-jins); the second, that it is for partiality (al-tabʿīḍ). Al-Qāḍī mentioned both.

And her saying, "He did not see a vision but that it came like the splitting of dawn (falaq al-ṣubḥ)" — the people of language said: falaq al-ṣubḥ and faraq al-ṣubḥ, with the fatḥah on the fāʾ, lām, and rāʾ, is its light. This expression is only used for something clear and manifest. Al-Qāḍī, may God have mercy on him, and others among the scholars said: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, was only initiated with visions so that the angel would not come upon him suddenly and bring him the explicit prophecy (nuṣūṣ al-nubuwwah) all at once, which the strength of human nature could not bear. Thus he was begun with the first of the traits of prophethood and the harbingers of honor (tabāshīr al-karāmah), from the truthfulness of visions — and what is mentioned in the other ḥadīth of seeing light, hearing a voice, and the greeting of stone and tree to him with prophethood.

Her saying, "Then solitude (al-khalāʾ) was made beloved to him, so he would seclude himself in the cave of Ḥirāʾ, engaging in taḥannuth therein — that is, devotion (taʿabbud) — for nights of a number (layālī ūlāt al-ʿadad) before returning to his family, and he would take provisions, then return to Khadījah, may God be pleased with her, and take provisions for the like of it, until the truth (al-ḥaqq) came upon him suddenly (fajaʾahu)."

As for al-khalāʾ, it is with madd (prolongation), and it is seclusion (khilwah), which is the concern of the righteous and the worshipful servants of God, the knowers. Abū Sulaymān al-Khaṭṭābī, may God have mercy on him, said: Seclusion was made beloved to him, peace and blessings be upon him, because with it comes the heart's emptiness, and it aids in reflection (tafakkur), and through it one is cut off from the familiar habits of humans, and his heart becomes humble — and God knows best.

As for al-ghār (the cave), it is the cavern and the hollow in the mountain; its plural is ghīrān, and al-maghār and al-maghārah are synonymous with al-ghār. The diminutive of al-ghār is ghuyayr.

As for Ḥirāʾ, it is with kasrah on the unpointed ḥāʾ, with takhfīf (lightening) of the rāʾ, and with madd (prolongation of the alif). It is declinable (maṣrūf) and masculine — this is the correct view. Al-Qāḍī said: There are two dialects in it: masculine and feminine, with masculine being more frequent. Whoever treats it as masculine declines it; whoever treats it as feminine does not decline it, intending the locale or the direction in which the mountain lies. Al-Qāḍī said: Some said "ḥarāʾ" with fatḥah on the ḥāʾ and qaṣr (shortening), and this is nothing. Abū ʿUmar al-Zāhid, the companion of Thaʿlab, and Abū Sulaymān al-Khaṭṭābī, and others among the ḥadīth scholars said: The common people err in Ḥirāʾ in three places: they open the ḥāʾ, whereas it is kasrah; they break the rāʾ, whereas it is fatḥah; and they shorten the alif, whereas it is madd. Ḥirāʾ is a mountain, between it and Mecca about three miles, on the left of one going from Mecca to Minā — and God knows best.

As for al-taḥannuth, with the unpointed ḥāʾ, the nūn, and the thāʾ with three dots — he (the narrator) has interpreted it as devotion (taʿabbud), and this is a sound interpretation. The root of al-ḥanath is sin (ithm); thus the meaning of "yataḥannath" is: he avoids sin (yatajannab al-ḥanath), as if through his worship he prevents himself from sin. Similar to yataḥannath is yataḥarraj and yaʾtham, i.e., he avoids constraint (ḥaraj) and sin (ithm).

As for her saying "nights of a number (layālī ūlāt al-ʿadad)," it is attached (mutaʿalliq) to yataḥannath, not to taʿabbud. Its meaning is: he would engage in taḥannuth during the nights. If one made it attached to taʿabbud, the meaning would be corrupted, for taḥannuth is not conditioned upon nights; rather, it is applied to little and much. This interpretation was interposed between the speech of ʿĀʾishah, may God be pleased with her — and as for her speech, it is "yataḥannathu fīhi al-layālī ūlāt al-ʿadad" — and God knows best.

And her saying "fajaʾahu al-ḥaqq" (the truth came upon him suddenly) — i.e., the revelation (waḥy) came to him unexpectedly, for he, peace and blessings be upon him, was not anticipating revelation. It is said "fajiʾahu" with kasrah on the jīm followed by a fatḥah hamzah, and it is said "fajaʾahu" with fatḥah on the jīm and the hamzah — two well-known dialects, reported by al-Jawharī and others.

His saying, peace and blessings be upon him, "I am not one who reads (mā anā bi-qāriʾ)" — its meaning is: I do not know how to read. So "mā" is negative (nāfiyah); this is the correct view. Al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ, may God have mercy on him, reported concerning it a disagreement among the scholars: some made it negative, and some made it interrogative (istifhāmiyyah), and they weakened this by the entry of the "bāʾ" into the predicate (khabar). Al-Qāḍī said: The view of those who said interrogative is supported by the narration of one who narrated "mā aqraʾ" (what do I read?). And it is also valid that "mā" in this narration be negative — and God knows best.

His saying, peace and blessings be upon him, "Then he covered me (fa-ghaṭṭanī) until the exertion (al-juhd) reached its limit in me, then he released me (arsalanī)" — as for ghaṭṭanī, it is with the pointed ghayn and the unpointed ṭāʾ, and its meaning is: he pressed me and embraced me. It is said: ghaṭṭahu, ghattahu, ḍaghaṭahu, ʿaṣarahu, khanaqahu, and ghamazahu — all of one meaning. As for al-juhd, it is permissible to open the jīm or to double it (ḍammah) — two dialects — and it is the utmost limit and hardship. It is permissible to give naṣb (accusative) to the dāl or rafʿ (nominative). On the naṣb: "Jibrīl reached the utmost exertion from me (balagha Jibrīlu minnī al-juhda)"; on the rafʿ: "the exertion reached its limit and end from me (balagha al-juhdu minnī mablaghahu wa-ghāyatahu)." Among those who mentioned the two aspects of naṣb and rafʿ on the dāl is the author of al-Taḥrīr and others. As for arsalanī, its meaning is: he released me (aṭlaqanī).

The scholars said: The wisdom in the covering (al-ghaṭṭ) was to occupy him from looking away, and to emphasize the matter of summoning his heart to what was being said to him; and he repeated it three times as an emphasis in the warning. In this there is the point that the teacher ought to be cautious in alerting the student and commanding him to summon his heart — and God knows best.

His saying, peace and blessings be upon him, "Then he released me and said: Recite in the name of your Lord who created {«اقْرَأْ بِاسْمِ رَبِّكَ الَّذِي خَلَقَ»}" — this is an explicit proof that the first of what descended of the Qur'an was "Iqraʾ" (Recite). This is the correct view, upon which are the masses (al-jamāhīr) of the predecessors (salaf) and successors (khalaf). It was said: its first was "O you wrapped in a garment {«يَا أَيُّهَا الْمُدَّثِّرُ»}" — and this is nothing. We shall mention it after this in its place from this chapter, God willing.

Some of those who say that "Bismillāh al-Raḥmān al-Raḥīm" is not part of the Qur'an at the beginnings of the sūrahs used this ḥadīth as evidence, because it was not mentioned here. The response of those who affirm it is that it did not descend first; rather, the basmalah descended at another time, just as the rest of the sūrah descended at another time.

Her saying, "His collar bones trembled (tarjafu bawādiruhu)" — with fatḥah on the unpointed bāʾ. The meaning of tarjafu is: it quakes and trembles, and its origin is intense movement. Abū ʿUbayd and the rest of the people of language and strange speech (al-gharīb) said: It is the flesh between the shoulder and the neck, which trembles at a person's fright.

His saying, peace and blessings be upon him, "Cover me, cover me (zammilūnī zammilūnī)" — thus it is in the narrations, repeated twice. The meaning of zammilūnī is: cover me with garments and wrap me in them.

And her saying, "So they covered him until the fright (al-rawʿ) left him" — it is with fatḥah on the rāʾ, and it is...

chapters.title_en: Section 155 — On the Prophet's Fear, Khadījah's Reassurance, and the Meanings of Her Words
chapters.arabic_text:
الفزع قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (لقد خشيت على نفسي) قال القاضي عياض رحمه

الله ليس هو بمعنى الشك فيما أتاه من الله تعالى لكنه ربما خشي أن لا يقوى

على مقاومة هذا الأمر ولا يقدر على حمل أعباء الوحي فتزهق نفسه أو يكون هذا

لأول ما رأى التباشير في النوم واليقظة وسمع الصوت قبل لقاء الملك وتحققه

رسالة ربه فيكون خاف أن يكون من الشيطان الرجيم فأما منذ جاءه الملك برسالة

ربه سبحانه وتعالى فلا يجوز عليه الشك فيه ولا يخشى من تسلط الشيطان عليه

وعلى هذا الطريق يحمل جميع ما ورد من مثل هذا في حديث البعث هذا كلام

القاضي رحمه الله في شرح صحيح مسلم وذكر أيضا في كتابه الشفاء هذين

الاحتمالين في كلام مبسوط وهذا الاحتمال الثاني ضعيف لأنه خلاف تصريح

الحديث لأن هذا كان بعد غط الملك وإتيانه باقرأ باسم ربك الذي خلق والله

أعلم قولها (قالت له خديجة كلا أبشر فوالله لا يخزيك الله أبدا والله إنك

لتصل الرحم وتصدق الحديث وتحمل الكل وتكسب المعدوم
# 
# وتقري الضيف وتعين على نوائب الحق) أما قولها كلا فهي هنا كلمة نفي

وإبعاد وهذا أحد معانيها وقد تأتي كلا بمعنى حقا وبمعنى ألا التي للتنبيه

يستفتح بها الكلام وقد جاءت في القرآن العزيز على أقسام وقد جمع الإمام أبو

بكر بن الأنباري أقسامها ومواضعها في باب من كتابه الوقف والابتداء وأما

قولها لا يخزيك فهو بضم الياء وبالخاء المعجمة كذا هو في رواية يونس وعقيل

وقال معمر فى روايته يحزنك بالحاء المهملة والنون ويجوز فتح الياء في أوله

وضمها وكلاهما صحيح والخزي الفضيحة والهوان وأما صلة الرحم فهي الإحسان إلى

الأقارب على حسب حال الواصل والموصول فتارة تكون بالمال وتارة بالخدمة

وتارة بالزيارة والسلام وغير ذلك وأما الكل فهو بفتح الكاف وأصله الثقل

ومنه قوله تعالى وهو كل على مولاه ويدخل في حمل الكل الإنفاق على الضعيف

واليتيم والعيال وغير ذلك وهو من الكلال وهو الإعياء وأما قولها وتكسب

المعدوم فهو بفتح التاء هذا هو الصحيح المشهور ونقله القاضي عياض عن رواية

الأكثرين قال ورواه بعضهم بضمها قال أبو العباس ثعلب وأبو سليمان الخطابي

وجماعات من أهل اللغة يقال كسبت الرجل مالا وأكسبته مالا لغتان أفصحهما

باتفاقهم كسبته بحذف الألف وأما معنى تكسب المعدوم فمن رواه بالضم فمعناه

تكسب غيرك المال المعدوم أي تعطيه إياه تبرعا فحذف أحد المفعولين وقيل

معناه تعطى الناس مالايجدونه عند غيرك من نفائس الفوائد ومكارم الأخلاق

وأما رواية الفتح فقيل معناها كمعنى الضم وقيل معناها تكسب المال المعدوم

وتصيب منه ما يعجز غيرك عن تحصيله وكانت العرب تتمادح بكسب المال المعدوم

لا سيما قريش وكان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم محظوظا في تجارته وهذا القول

حكاه القاضي عن ثابت صاحب الدلائل وهو ضعيف أو غلط وأي معنى لهذا القول في

هذا الموطن إلا أنه يمكن تصحيحه بأن يضم إليه زيادة فيكون معناه تكسب المال

العظيم الذي يعجز عنه غيرك ثم تجود به في وجوه الخير وأبواب  المكارم كما

ذكرت من حمل الكل وصلة الرحم وقرى الضيف والإعانة على نوائب الحق فهذا هو
# 
# الصواب في هذا الحرف وأما صاحب التحرير فجعل المعدوم عبارة عن الرجل

المحتاج المعدم العاجز عن الكسب وسماه معدوما لكونه كالمعدوم الميت حيث لم

يتصرف في المعيشة كتصرف غيره قال وذكر الخطابي أن صوابه المعدم بحذف الواو

قال وليس كما قال الخطابي بل ما رواه الرواة صواب قال وقيل معنى تكسب

المعدوم أي تسعى في طلب عاجز تنعشه والكسب هو الاستفادة وهذا الذي قاله

صاحب التحرير وإن كان له بعض الاتجاه كما حررت لفظه فالصحيح المختار ما

قدمته والله أعلم وأما قولها وتقري الضيف فهو بفتح التاء قال أهل اللغة

يقال قريت الضيف أقريه قرى بكسر القاف مقصور وقراء بفتح القاف والمد ويقال

للطعام الذي يضيفه به قرى بكسر القاف مقصور ويقال لفاعله قار مثل قضى فهو

قاض وأما قولها وتعين على نوائب الحق فالنوائب جمع نائبة وهى الحادثة وانما

قالت نوائب الحق لأن النائبة قد تكون في الخير وقد تكون في الشر قال لبيد

... نوائب من خير وشر كلاهما ... فلا الخير ممدود ولا الشر لازب ...

| (قال العلماء رضي الله عنهم معنى كلام خديجة رضي 
# الله عنها إنك لا يصيبك مكروه لما جعل الله فيك من مكارم الأخلاق وكرم

الشمائل وذكرت ضروبا من ذلك وفي هذا دلالة على أن مكارم الأخلاق وخصال

الخير سبب السلامة من مصارع السوء وفيه مدح الإنسان في وجهه في بعض الأحوال

لمصلحة نظر أو فيه تأنيس من حصلت له مخافة من أمر وتبشيره وذكر أسباب

السلامة له وفيه أعظم دليل وأبلغ حجة على كمال خديجة رضي الله عنها وجزالة

رأيها وقوة نفسها وثبات قلبها وعظم فقهها والله أعلم قولها (وكان امرأ تنصر

في الجاهلية) معناه صار نصرانيا والجاهلية ما قبل رسالته صلى الله عليه

وسلم سموا بذلك لما كانوا عليه من فاحش الجهالة والله أعلم قولها (وكان

يكتب الكتاب العربي ويكتب من الإنجيل بالعربية ما شاء الله تعالى أن  يكتب)
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ف-ز-ع (f-z-ʿ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning of alarm, fright, or sudden terror that seizes one.
