فالأنبياء إخوة والمؤمنون إخوة والله اعلم قوله (ان بن عباس وأبا حبة

الأنصاري يقولان) أبو حبة بالحاء المهملة والباء الموحدة هكذا ضبطناه هنا

وفي ضبطه واسمه اختلاف فالأصح
# 
# الذي عليه الأكثرون حبة بالباء الموحدة كما ذكرنا وقيل حية بالياء

المثناة تحت وقيل حنة بالنون وهذا قول الواقدي وروى عن بن شهاب والزهري وقد

اختلف في اسم أبي حبة فقيل عامر وقيل مالك وقيل ثابت وهو بدري باتفاقهم

واستشهد يوم أحد وقد جمع الإمام أبو الحسن بن الأثير الجزري رحمه الله

الأقوال الثلاثة في ضبطه والاختلاف في اسمه في كتابه معرفة الصحابة رضي

الله عنهم وبينها بيانا شافيا رحمه الله قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (حتى ظهرت

لمستوى أسمع فيه صريف الأقلام) معنى ظهرت علوت والمستوى بفتح الواو قال

الخطابي المراد به المصعد وقيل المكان المستوى وصريف الأقلام بالصاد

المهملة تصويتها حال الكتابة قال الخطابي هو صوت ما تكتبه الملائكة من

أقضية الله تعالى ووحيه وما ينسخونه من اللوح المحفوظ أو ما شاء الله تعالى

من ذلك أن يكتب ويرفع لما أراده من أمره وتدبيره قال القاضي في هذا حجة

لمذهب أهل السنة في الإيمان بصحة كتابة الوحي والمقادير في كتب الله تعالى

من اللوح المحفوظ وما شاء بالأقلام التي هو تعالى يعلم كيفيتها على ما جاءت

به الآيات من كتاب الله تعالى والأحاديث الصحيحة وأن ما جاء من ذلك على

ظاهره لكن كيفية ذلك وصورته وجنسه ممالا يعلمه إلا الله تعالى أو من أطلعه

على شيء من ذلك من ملائكته ورسله وما يتأول هذا ويحيله عن ظاهره إلا ضعيف

النظر والايمان اذ جاءت به الشريعة المطهرة ودلائل العقول لا تحيله والله

تعالى يفعل ما يشاء ويحكم ما يريد حكمة من الله تعالى وإظهارا لما يشاء من

غيبه لمن يشاء من ملائكته وسائر خلقه وإلا فهو غني عن الكتب والاستذكار

سبحانه وتعالى قال القاضي رحمه الله وفي علو منزلة نبينا صلى الله عليه

وسلم وارتفاعه فوق منازل سائر الأنبياء صلوات الله وسلامه عليهم أجمعين

وبلوغه حيث بلغ من ملكوت السماوات دليل على علو درجته وإبانة فضله وقد ذكر

البزار خبرا في الإسراء عن علي كرم الله وجهه وذكر مسير جبريل عليه السلام

على البراق حتى أتى الحجاب وذكر كلمة وقال خرج ملك من وراء الحجاب فقال

جبريل والذي بعثك بالحق إن هذا الملك ما رأيته منذ خلقت وإني أقرب الخلق

مكانا وفي حديث آخر فارقني جبريل وانقطعت عني الأصوات
# 
# هذا آخر كلام القاضي رحمه الله والله تعالى أعلم قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم

(ففرض الله تعالى على أمتي خمسين صلاة إلى قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم فراجعت

ربي فوضع شطرها وبعده فراجعت ربي فقال هي خمس وهي خمسون) وهذا المذكور هنا

لا يخالف الرواية المتقدمة أنه صلى الله عليه وسلم قال حط عني خمسا إلى

آخره فالمراد بحط الشطر هنا أنه حط في مرات بمراجعات وهذا هو الظاهر وقال

القاضي عياض رحمه الله المراد بالشطر هنا الجزء وهو الخمس وليس المراد به

النصف وهذا الذي قاله محتمل ولكن لا ضرورة إليه فإن هذا الحديث الثاني

مختصر لم يذكر فيه كرات المراجعة والله أعلم واحتج العلماء بهذا الحديث على

جواز نسخ الشيء قبل فعله والله أعلم قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (ثم انطلق بي

حتى نأتي سدرة المنتهى) هكذا هو في الأصول حتى نأتي بالنون في أوله وفي بعض

الأصول حتى أتي وكلاهما صحيح قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (ثم أدخلت الجنة فإذا

فيها جنابذ اللؤلؤ)  أما الجنابذ فبالجيم المفتوحة وبعدها نون مفتوحة ثم ألف
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ع ل و (ʿ-l-w)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Elevation, height, ascent; "ʿalā" denotes rising above in physical or rank-based terms.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Used for both physical elevation (irtifāʿ) and spiritual exaltation (ʿulūw al-darajah), the latter being the intended sense for the Prophet's station.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for spatial height; metaphorical (majāz) for superiority in rank and honor, as in "ʿalā al-amīr" (the commander prevailed).
- Sībawayh Rule: Nominal sentence with predicate of place (ẓarf) — "wa-huwa fīhā ghayru mustawṭin" (and he was therein non-resident) requires the predicate to be a circumstantial clause (ḥāl) indicating a temporary state, parsed as an adverbial accusative of location.
chapters.translation:
I say: In every instance he found him in a heaven, one of the two being the place of his settlement and homeland, and the other he was in it non-resident. And if the Night Journey (al-isrāʾ) was but a single occasion, then perhaps he found him in the sixth. Then Ibrāhīm also ascended to the seventh — and Allāh knows best.

His saying, peace and blessings be upon him, concerning Idrīs, peace be upon him: He said, «Welcome to the righteous Prophet and the righteous brother.» Al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ, may Allāh have mercy on him, said: This contradicts what the genealogists and historians hold, namely that Idrīs is a forefather among the forefathers of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and that he is a high ancestor of Nūḥ, peace be upon him, and that Nūḥ is the son of Lāmak, son of Matūshalakh, son of Khanūkh — who is, in their view, Idrīs, son of Yard, son of Mahlāʾīl, son of Qīnān, son of Anūsh, son of Shīth, son of Ādam, peace be upon him. There is no disagreement among them regarding the number of these names and their sequential listing as we have mentioned; they only differ in the precise voweling of some of them and the form of their pronunciation. And the response of the forefathers here came — Ibrāhīm and Ādam — as «Welcome to the righteous son,» whereas Idrīs was greeted with «Welcome to the righteous brother,» just as Mūsā, ʿĪsā, Hārūn, Yūsuf, and Yaḥyā were addressed — and they are not forefathers, may the blessings and peace of Allāh be upon them all. It has also been said concerning Idrīs that he is Ilyās, and that he is not a grandfather of Nūḥ, for Ilyās is of the progeny of Ibrāhīm, and he is among the messengers, and that the first of the messengers is Nūḥ, peace be upon him, as comes in the ḥadīth of the Intercession (al-shafāʿah). This is the speech of al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ, may Allāh have mercy on him. And there is nothing in this ḥadīth that prevents Idrīs, peace be upon him, from being a forefather of our Prophet Muḥammad, peace and blessings be upon him, for his saying «the righteous brother» admits the possibility that he said it as an act of gentleness and courtesy — he is a brother even if he be a son, for the prophets are brothers, and the believers are brothers. And Allāh knows best.

His saying: «Ibn ʿAbbās and Abū Ḥabbah al-Anṣārī say» — Abū Ḥabbah: with the unpointed ḥāʾ and the unpointed bāʾ. Thus we have recorded it here. Regarding its precise voweling and his name, there is disagreement. The most sound — and that which the majority hold — is Ḥabbah with the unpointed bāʾ, as we have mentioned. And it was said: Ḥayyah with the dotted yāʾ under it, and it was said: Ḥannah with the nūn — this is the saying of al-Wāqidī, and it was narrated from Ibn Shihāb and al-Zuhrī. There is disagreement over the name of Abū Ḥabbah: it was said ʿĀmir, it was said Mālik, and it was said Thābit. He was present at Badr by their unanimous agreement, and he was martyred on the day of Uḥud. The Imām Abū al-Ḥasan ibn al-Athīr al-Jazarī, may Allāh have mercy on him, gathered the three sayings regarding its voweling and the disagreement over his name in his book Maʿrifat al-Ṣaḥābah, may Allāh be pleased with them, and clarified them with a sufficient clarification — may Allāh have mercy on him.

His saying, peace and blessings be upon him: «Until I rose to the level where I heard the screeching of the pens (ṣarīf al-aqlām)» — the meaning of ẓahartu is ʿalawtu (I ascended). Al-Mustawā, with the opening of the wāw — al-Khaṭṭābī said: what is meant by it is the place of ascent (al-muṣʿad), and it was said: the level place (al-makān al-mustawī). And ṣarīf al-aqlām, with the unpointed ṣād, is their sound during writing. Al-Khaṭṭābī said: it is the sound of what the angels write of the decrees of Allāh, may He be exalted, and His revelation, and what they transcribe from the Preserved Tablet (al-lawḥ al-maḥfūẓ), or whatever Allāh, may He be exalted, wills of that to be written and raised up for what He intends of His command and His governance. Al-Qāḍī said: In this there is a proof for the doctrine of the People of the Sunnah (ahl al-sunnah) regarding faith in the soundness of the writing of revelation and the decrees (al-maqādīr) in the books of Allāh, may He be exalted, from the Preserved Tablet and whatever He wills, by the pens whose modality He — may He be exalted — knows, according to what has come in the verses of the Book of Allāh, may He be exalted, and the sound ḥadīths; and that whatever has come of that is upon its literal sense (ẓāhir), but its modality, form, and genus are things known only to Allāh, may He be exalted, or to whom He has disclosed something of that from among His angels and His messengers. And none interprets this figuratively (taʾwīl) and diverts it from its literal sense except one weak in discernment and faith, for the pure Sharīʿah has brought it, and the proofs of the intellects do not render it impossible. And Allāh, may He be exalted, does what He wills and decrees what He desires — as a wisdom from Allāh, may He be exalted, and a manifestation of what He wills of His unseen to whom He wills of His angels and the rest of His creation. Otherwise, He is free of need for books and recollection — glory be to Him and exalted is He.

Al-Qāḍī, may Allāh have mercy on him, said: And in the elevation of the station of our Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and its rising above the stations of the rest of the prophets — may the blessings and peace of Allāh be upon them all — and his reaching where he reached of the dominion of the heavens (malakūt al-samāwāt), there is a proof of the loftiness of his degree and a manifestation of his excellence. Al-Bazzār mentioned a report concerning the Night Journey from ʿAlī, may Allāh honor his face, and mentioned the journey of Jibrīl, peace be upon him, upon al-Burāq until he came to the Veil (al-ḥijāb), and mentioned a statement: A king came forth from behind the Veil and said: O Jibrīl, by Him who sent you with the truth, I have not seen this king since I was created, and verily I am the nearest of creation in station. And in another ḥadīth: Jibrīl parted from me, and the sounds were cut off from me.

This is the end of the speech of al-Qāḍī, may Allāh have mercy on him — and Allāh, may He be exalted, knows best.

His saying, peace and blessings be upon him: «Then Allāh, may He be exalted, made obligatory upon my community fifty prayers» — up to his saying, peace and blessings be upon him: «So I returned to my Lord, and He reduced half of it (shaṭrahā), and after that I returned to my Lord, and He said: They are five, and they are fifty.» And what is mentioned here does not contradict the preceding narration that he, peace and blessings be upon him, said: «He removed from me five» to its end. For what is meant by the reduction of the half (al-shaṭr) here is that He reduced it in multiple instances through repeated returns — and this is the apparent sense. Al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ, may Allāh have mercy on him, said: What is meant by al-shaṭr here is the portion (al-juzʾ), which is the five, and the half is not intended. This which he said is possible, but there is no necessity for it, for this second ḥadīth is abridged and does not mention the repeated returns. And Allāh knows best. The scholars have adduced this ḥadīth as proof for the permissibility of abrogating a thing before its enactment (naskh al-shayʾ qabla fiʿlih) — and Allāh knows best.

His saying, peace and blessings be upon him: «Then I was taken until we came to the Lote Tree of the Utmost Boundary (sidrat al-muntahā)» — thus it is in the manuscripts: ḥattā naʾtī with the nūn at its beginning, and in some manuscripts ḥattā atī — and both are sound.

His saying, peace and blessings be upon him: «Then I was admitted into Paradise, and behold, therein were domes (janābidh) of pearl» — as for janābidh, it is with the opened jīm, followed by an opened nūn, then an alif.

chapters.title_en: Section 162 — On the Night Journey (al-Isrāʾ), the Heavenly Ascension (al-Miʿrāj), and Related Matters
chapters.arabic_text:
ثم باء موحدة ثم ذال معجمة وهي القباب واحدتها جنبذة
# 
# ووقع في كتاب الأنبياء من صحيح البخاري كذلك ووقع في أول كتاب الصلاة منه

حبائل بالحاء المهملة والباء الموحدة وآخره لام قال الخطابي وغيره هو تصحيف

والله أعلم وأما اللؤلؤ فمعروف وفيه أربعة أوجه بهمزتين وبحذفهما وبإثبات

الأولى دون الثانية وعكسه والله أعلم وفي هذا الحديث دلالة لمذهب أهل السنة

أن الجنة والنار مخلوقتان وأن الجنة فى السماء والله أعلم
# [164] قوله (حدثنا محمد بن المثنى حدثنا بن أبي عدي عن سعيد عن قتادة عن

أنس بن مالك رضي الله عنه لعله قال عن مالك بن صعصعة) قال أبو علي الغساني

هكذا هو هذا الحديث في رواية بن ماهان وأبي العباس الرازي عن أبي أحمد

الجلودي وعند غيره عن أبي أحمد عن قتادة عن
# 
# أنس بن مالك عن مالك بن صعصعة بغير شك قال أبو الحسن الدارقطني لم يروه

عن أنس بن مالك عن مالك بن صعصعة غير قتادة والله أعلم قوله صلى الله عليه

وسلم في موسى عليه السلام (فلما جاوزته بكى فنودي ما يبكيك قال رب هذا غلام

بعثته بعدي يدخل من أمته الجنة أكثر مما يدخل من أمتي) معنى هذا والله أعلم

أن موسى عليه السلام حزن على قومه لقلة المؤمنين منهم مع كثرة عددهم فكان

بكاؤه حزنا عليهم وغبطة لنبينا صلى الله عليه وسلم على كثرة أتباعه والغبطة

في الخير محبوبة ومعنى الغبطة أنه ود أن يكون من أمته المؤمنين مثل هذه

الأمة لا أنه ود أن يكونوا أتباعا له وليس لنبينا صلى الله عليه وسلم مثلهم

والمقصود أنه إنما بكى حزنا على قومه وعلى فوات الفضل العظيم والثواب

الجزيل بتخلفهم عن الطاعة فإن من دعا إلى خير وعمل الناس به كان له مثل

أجورهم كما جاءت به الأحاديث الصحيحة ومثل هذا يبكى عليه ويحزن على فواته

والله أعلم قوله (وحدث نبي الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه  رأى أربعة أنهار

يخرج من أصلها نهران ظاهران ونهران باطنان فقلت يا جبريل ما هذه الأنهار

قال أما النهران الباطنان فنهران في الجنة وأما الظاهران فالنيل والفرات)

هكذا هو في أصول صحيح مسلم يخرج من أصلها والمراد من أصل سدرة المنتهى كما

جاء مبينا في صحيح البخاري وغيره قال مقاتل الباطنان هما السلسبيل والكوثر

قال القاضي عياض رحمه الله هذا الحديث يدل على أن أصل سدرة المنتهى في

الأرض
# 
# لخروج النيل والفرات من أصلها قلت هذا الذي قاله ليس بلازم بل معناه أن

الأنهار تخرج من أصلها ثم تسير حيث أراد الله تعالى حتى تخرج من الأرض

وتسير فيها وهذا لا يمنعه عقل ولا شرع وهو ظاهر الحديث فوجب المصير إليه

والله أعلم واعلم أن الفرات بالتاء الممدودة في الخط في حالتي الوصل والوقف

وهذا وإن كان معلوما مشهورا فنبهت عليه لكون كثير من الناس يقولونه بالهاء

وهو خطأ والله أعلم قوله (هذا البيت المعمور يدخله كل يوم سبعون ألف ملك

إذا خرجوا منه لم يعودوا إليه آخر ما عليهم) قال صاحب مطالع الأنوار رويناه

آخر ما عليهم برفع الراء ونصبها فالنصب على الظرف والرفع على تقدير ذلك آخر

ما عليهم من دخوله قال والرفع أوجه وفي هذا أعظم دليل على كثرة الملائكة

صلوات الله وسلامه عليهم والله أعلم قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (أتيت بإناءين

أحدهما خمر والآخر لبن فعرضا علي فاخترت اللبن فقيل أصبت أصاب الله بك أمتك

على الفطرة) قد تقدم في أول الباب الكلام في هذا الفصل والذي يزاد هنا معنى

أصبت أي أصبت الفطرة كما جاء في الرواية المتقدمة وتقدم بيان الفطرة ومعنى

أصاب الله بك أي أراد بك الفطرة والخير والفضل وقد جاء أصاب بمعنى أراد قال

الله تعالى فسخرنا له الريح تجري بأمره رخاء حيث أصاب أي حيث أراد اتفق

عليه المفسرون وأهل اللغة كذا نقل الواحدي اتفاق أهل اللغة عليه وأما قوله

أمتك على الفطرة فمعناه أنهم أتباع لك وقد أصبت الفطرة  فهم يكونون عليها

والله
# 
# أعلم قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (فشق من النخر إلى مراق البطن) هو بفتح

الميم وتشديد القاف وهو ما سفل من البطن ورق من جلده قال الجوهري لا واحد

لها وقال صاحب المطالع واحدها مرق قول مسلم رحمه الله
# [165] (حدثنى محمد بن مثنى وبن بشار قال بن مثنى حدثنا محمد بن جعفر

حدثنا شعبة عن قتادة قال سمعت أبا العالية يقول حدثني بن عم نبيكم صلى الله

عليه وسلم يعني بن عباس رضي الله عنهما) هذا الإسناد كله بصريون وشعبة وإن

كان واسطيا فقد انتقل إلى البصرة واستوطنها وبن عباس أيضا سكنها واسم أبي

العالية رفيع بضم الراء وفتح الفاء بن مهران الرياحي بكسر الراء وبالمثناة

من تحت والله أعلم قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (موسى آدم طوال كأنه من رجال

شنوءة وقال عيسى جعد مربوع) أما طوال فبضم الطاء وتخفيف الواو ومعناه طويل

وهما لغتان وأما شنوءة فبشين معجمة مفتوحة ثم نون ثم واو ثم همزة ثم هاء

وهي قبيلة معروفة قال بن قتيبة في أدب الكاتب سموا بذلك من قولك رجل فيه

شنوءة أي تقزز قال ويقال سموا بذلك لأنهم تشانؤا وتباعدوا وقال الجوهري
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ج-ن-ب (j-n-b)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Side, flank; a dome-shaped structure (qubbah) — the singular of janbadh is junbudhah, denoting a rounded, vaulted edifice.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological usage, pertains to spatial or structural metaphors for celestial abodes.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) for physical domes; metaphorical (majāz) when applied to heavenly constructs.
- Sībawayh Rule: Orthographic Variant Analysis (al-ʿImlāʾ) — distinguishing hamzah retention/elision patterns in lexical variants.

- Root: ح-ب-ل (ḥ-b-l)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Ropes, cords; also snares or traps.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Metaphorical extension to binding covenants or entanglements.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Here, a textual corruption (taṣḥīf) — the correct reading is identified by al-Khaṭṭābī.
- Sībawayh Rule: Textual Criticism (Naqd al-Naṣṣ) — identifying scribal errors through comparative manuscript analysis.

- Root: ل-ؤ-ل-ؤ (l-ʾ-l-ʾ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Pearl; a precious gem formed in shells.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Symbol of purity and celestial beauty in Quranic descriptions of Paradise.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for the gem; metaphorical for radiant heavenly structures.
- Sībawayh Rule: Hamzah Variation (Ibdāl al-Hamzah) — four permissible pronunciations: with both hamzahs, omitting both, or retaining one while dropping the other.

- Root: خ-ل-ق (kh-l-q)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To create, measure, fashion; origination of something from nothing.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Theological term for divine creation (khalq) — Paradise and Hell are created entities (makhlūqatān), existing now.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for divine act of creation; distinguishes from temporal origination (ḥudūth) in philosophical discourse.
- Sībawayh Rule: Predicate Agreement (Ṭābiq al-Khabar) — dual feminine agreement for the two created abodes.

- Root: غ-ب-ط (gh-b-ṭ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To wish for another's blessing without desiring its removal; envy-free admiration.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Commendable aspiration (ghibṭah) toward virtue — distinct from ḥasad (blameworthy envy).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for this praiseworthy emotion; rhetorically applied to Moses' longing for his people's salvation.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clause (al-Sharṭ) — parsing "law" constructions expressing unfulfilled wishes.

- Root: ف-ر-ت (f-r-t)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Fresh, sweet water; the Euphrates River (al-Furāt).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Quranic reference to rivers of Paradise and earthly counterparts.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for the river; metaphorical for abundance and divine bounty.
- Sībawayh Rule: Orthographic Final Tāʾ (Tāʾ al-Mamdūdah) — the word is written with a long tāʾ (تاء ممدودة) in both connected and paused positions, not with hāʾ.

- Root: ع-م-ر (ʿ-m-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To inhabit, populate; the populated house (al-bayt al-maʿmūr) — the celestial Kaʿbah.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The heavenly sanctuary visited daily by seventy thousand angels.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for habitation; metaphorical for divine worship and angelic devotion.
- Sībawayh Rule: Adverbial Accusative (al-Ẓarf) vs. Nominative (al-Rafʿ) — "ākhiru mā ʿalayhim" parsed either as adverbial or as a nominal sentence with an implied predicate.

- Root: ل-ب-ن (l-b-n)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Milk; pure, unadulterated sustenance.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Symbol of natural disposition (fiṭrah) — the Prophet's choice of milk over wine signifies divine guidance.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for milk; metaphorical for primordial purity and correct belief.
- Sībawayh Rule: Verb Complementation (Taʿaddī al-Fiʿl) — "aṣāba" governing the accusative with the meaning "to intend" (arāda).

- Root: ش-ق-ق (sh-q-q)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To split, cleave; the lower abdomen (marāq al-baṭn).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Physical description of the Prophet's chest being opened — a literal event in the miʿrāj narrative.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for the surgical splitting; no metaphorical extension here.
- Sībawayh Rule: Singular/Plural Morphology (Ṣīghah) — al-Jawharī claims no singular for "marāq"; al-Maṭāliʿ gives "mirq" as singular.

- Root: ط-و-ل (ṭ-w-l)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Length, tallness; "ṭuwāl" as a form meaning very tall.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Descriptive of prophetic physical attributes in hadith literature.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for physical stature; two dialectal variants: ṭuwāl and ṭawīl.
- Sībawayh Rule: Dialectal Variants (Lughāt) — noting permissible phonological alternations.

- Root: ش-ن-ء (sh-n-ʾ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To abhor, detest; Shanūʾah — a Yemeni tribe named for their aversion to wrongdoing.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Tribal designation in prophetic descriptions; carries moral connotation of purity.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for the tribe; etymological connection to "taqazzuz" (disgust at filth).
- Sībawayh Rule: Proper Noun Derivation (Ishtiqāq al-ʿAlam) — tribal names from verbal roots.
chapters.translation:
Then a bāʾ (ب) followed by a muʿjamah dhāl (ذ) — these are the domes (qibāb), the singular of which is junbudhah.

It occurs likewise in the Book of the Prophets (Kitāb al-Anbiyāʾ) of Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī, and it occurs at the beginning of the Book of Prayer (Kitāb al-Ṣalāh) therein.

"Ḥabāʾil" (حبائل) — with an unpointed ḥāʾ (ح), a pointed bāʾ (ب), and ending in lām (ل). Al-Khaṭṭābī and others said: this is a textual corruption (taṣḥīf).

And Allah knows best. As for "al-luʾluʾ" (pearl), it is well-known, and it has four aspects: with both hamzahs, with both omitted, with the first retained and the second dropped, and the reverse. And Allah knows best.

In this hadith there is evidence for the doctrine of the People of the Sunnah (Ahl al-Sunnah) that Paradise and Hell are created (makhliqatān), and that Paradise is in the heaven. And Allah knows best.

[164] His saying (Muḥammad ibn al-Muthannā narrated to us — Ibn Abī ʿAdī narrated to us — from Saʿīd — from Qatādah — from Anas ibn Mālik, may Allah be pleased with him — "perhaps he said: from Mālik ibn Ṣaʿṣaʿah"). Abū ʿAlī al-Ghassānī said: Thus is this hadith in the narration of Ibn Māhān and Abū al-ʿAbbās al-Rāzī from Abū Aḥmad al-Julūdī, and according to others from Abū Aḥmad — from Qatādah — from Anas ibn Mālik — from Mālik ibn Ṣaʿṣaʿah without doubt. Abū al-Ḥasan al-Dāraquṭnī said: None narrated it from Anas ibn Mālik from Mālik ibn Ṣaʿṣaʿah except Qatādah. And Allah knows best.

His saying, peace and blessings be upon him, concerning Moses, peace be upon him: ("When he passed him, he wept, and it was called out: 'What makes you weep?' He said: 'My Lord, this is a young man whom I sent after me — more of his nation will enter Paradise than will enter from my nation.'") The meaning of this — and Allah knows best — is that Moses, peace be upon him, grieved for his people due to the scarcity of believers among them despite their great number. So his weeping was sorrow for them and admiration (ghibṭah) for our Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, over the abundance of his followers. And ghibṭah toward good is beloved. The meaning of ghibṭah is that he wished that there would be from his nation believers like this nation — not that he wished they would be followers of him, for our Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, has none like them. And the intent is that he only wept out of grief for his people and over the loss of the great virtue and abundant reward due to their failure to obey. For whoever calls to good and the people act upon it, he receives the like of their rewards, as the authentic hadiths have established. And something like this is wept over and grieved at for its loss. And Allah knows best.

His saying: ("And the Prophet of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, narrated that he saw four rivers — from their source (aṣlihā) emerged two apparent rivers and two hidden rivers. I said: 'O Gabriel, what are these rivers?' He said: 'As for the two hidden rivers, they are two rivers in Paradise; and as for the two apparent ones, they are the Nile and the Euphrates.'") Thus it is in the manuscripts of Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim: "from their source" (min aṣlihā) — and the intended meaning is from the source of the Lote Tree of the Utmost Boundary (Sidrat al-Muntahā), as is clarified in Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī and others. Muqātil said: the two hidden ones are al-Salsabīl and al-Kawthar.

Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ, may Allah have mercy on him, said: This hadith indicates that the source of the Sidrat al-Muntahā is in the earth, due to the emergence of the Nile and the Euphrates from its source.

I say: What he said is not necessary (lāzim). Rather, its meaning is that the rivers emerge from its source, then travel wherever Allah Almighty wills until they emerge from the earth and flow through it. Neither reason nor revelation prevents this, and it is the apparent meaning of the hadith, so it is obligatory to adopt it. And Allah knows best.

Know that "al-Furāt" (the Euphrates) is written with a long tāʾ (تاء ممدودة) in orthography in both connected and paused positions. Although this is well-known and famous, I have drawn attention to it because many people pronounce it with a hāʾ (ه), which is an error. And Allah knows best.

His saying: ("This Populated House (al-bayt al-maʿmūr) — seventy thousand angels enter it every day; when they leave it, they never return to it — that is the last of what is upon them.") The author of Maṭāliʿ al-Anwār said: We narrated it "ākhiru mā ʿalayhim" with the rafʿ (nominative) of the rāʾ and with its naṣb (accusative). The naṣb is on the adverbial (ẓarf) construction, and the rafʿ is on the estimation of "that is the last of what is upon them of entering it." He said: The rafʿ is more appropriate (awjah). In this is the greatest evidence for the multitude of angels, may Allah's prayers and peace be upon them. And Allah knows best.

His saying, peace and blessings be upon him: ("I was brought two vessels — one of wine and the other of milk — and they were presented to me. I chose the milk, and it was said: 'You have hit the mark (aṣabta); may Allah cause your nation to hit the mark (aṣāba Allahu bika ummataka) upon the fiṭrah (natural disposition).'") The discussion of this section has already preceded at the beginning of the chapter. What is added here is the meaning of "aṣabta" — i.e., you have hit the fiṭrah, as came in the preceding narration. And the explanation of fiṭrah has preceded. The meaning of "aṣāba Allahu bika" — i.e., He intended for you the fiṭrah, goodness, and virtue. And "aṣāba" has come with the meaning of "arāda" (intended). Allah Almighty said: {«فَسَخَّرْنَا لَهُ الرِّيحَ تَجْرِي بِأَمْرِهِ رُخَاءً حَيْثُ أَصَابَ»} — i.e., "wherever He intended" — upon which the exegetes and linguists are agreed. Thus al-Wāḥidī transmitted the consensus of the linguists upon it. As for his saying "your nation upon the fiṭrah" — its meaning is that they are followers of you, and you have hit the fiṭrah, so they will be upon it. And Allah knows best.

His saying, peace and blessings be upon him: ("Then he split from the chest (al-nahr) to the lower abdomen (marāq al-baṭn).") It is with fatḥah on the mīm and tashdīd on the qāf — it is what is lower of the belly and thin of its skin. Al-Jawharī said: it has no singular. The author of al-Maṭāliʿ said: its singular is "mirq."

The saying of Muslim, may Allah have mercy on him:

[165] (Muḥammad ibn al-Muthannā and Ibn Bashshār narrated to me — Ibn al-Muthannā said: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us — Shuʿbah narrated to us — from Qatādah, who said: I heard Abū al-ʿĀliyah say: The son of your Prophet's uncle, peace and blessings be upon him — meaning Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with them both — narrated to me.) This entire chain consists of Baṣrans. And Shuʿbah, although he was Wāsiṭī, had relocated to Baṣrah and settled there. Ibn ʿAbbās also resided there. The name of Abū al-ʿĀliyah is Rufayʿ — with ḍammah on the rāʾ and fatḥah on the fāʾ — ibn Mihrān al-Riyāḥī, with kasrah on the rāʾ and a dotted yāʾ (tāʾ mathnāh). And Allah knows best.

His saying, peace and blessings be upon him: ("Moses was a tall (ṭuwāl) man, as if from the men of Shanūʾah; and Jesus was curly-haired (jaʿd) and of medium stature (marbūʿ).") As for "ṭuwāl" — it is with ḍammah on the ṭāʾ and tashdīd-less wāw, and its meaning is "ṭawīl" (tall) — they are two dialects. As for "Shanūʾah" — it is with an open shīn (ش), then nūn, then wāw, then hamzah, then hāʾ — and it is a well-known tribe. Ibn Qutaybah said in Adab al-Kātib: They were named thus from your saying "a man in whom there is shanūʾah," i.e., fastidiousness (taqazzuz). He said: And it is said they were named thus because they "tashānaʾū" (held one another in abhorrence) and kept apart. Al-Jawharī said:

chapters.title_en: Section 163 — On the Meanings of "Shanū'ah," "Marbūʿ," "Jaʿd," "Sabṭ," and the Vision of Moses, Jesus, and Jonah (Peace Be Upon Them)
chapters.arabic_text:
الشنوءة التقزز وهو التباعد من الأدناس ومنه أزدشنوءه وهم حي من اليمن ينسب

إليهم شنئي قال قال بن السكيت ربما قالوا أزدشنوة بالتشديد غير مهموز وينسب

إليها شنوي وأما قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم مربوع فقال أهل اللغة هو الرجل

بين الرجلين في القامة ليس بالطويل البائن ولا بالقصير الحقير وفيه لغات

ذكرهن صاحب المحكم وغيره مربوع ومرتبع ومرتبع بفتح الباء وكسرها وربع وربعة

وربعة الأخيرة بفتح الباء والمرأة ربعة وربعة وأما قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم

في عيسى صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه جعد ووقع في أكثر
# 
# الروايات في صفته سبط الرأس فقال العلماء المراد بالجعد هنا جعودة الجسم

وهو اجتماعه واكتنازه وليس المراد جعودة الشعر وأما الجعد في صفة موسى عليه

السلام فقال صاحب التحرير فيه معنيان أحدهما  ما ذكرناه في عيسى عليه السلام

وهو اكتناز الجسم والثاني جعودة الشعر قال والأول أصح لأنه قد جاء في رواية

أبي هريرة في الصحيح أنه رجل الشعر هذا كلام صاحب التحرير والمعنيان فيه

جائزان وتكون جعودة الشعر على المعنى الثاني ليست جعودة القطط بل معناها

أنه بين القطط والسبط والله أعلم والسبط بفتح الباء وكسرها لغتان مشهورتان

ويجوز إسكان الباء مع كسر السين وفتحها على التخفيف كما في كتف وبابه قال

أهل اللغة الشعر السبط هو المسترسل ليس فيه تكسر ويقال في الفعل منه سبط

شعره بكسر الباء يسبط بفتحها سبطا بفتحها أيضا والله أعلم قوله في الرواية

الأخرى (قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم مررت ليلة أسري بي على موسى بن

عمران) هكذا وقع في بعض الأصول وسقطت لفظة مررت فى معظمها ولا بد منها فإن

حذفت كانت مرادة والله أعلم قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (وأري مالكا خازن

النار) هو بضم الهمزة وكسر الراء ومالكا بالنصب ومعناه أري النبي صلى الله

عليه وسلم مالكا وقد ثبت في صحيح البخاري في هذا الحديث ورأيت مالكا ووقع

في أكثر الأصول مالك بالرفع وهذا قد ينكر ويقال هذا لحن لا يجوز في العربية

ولكن عنه جواب حسن وهو أن لفظة مالك منصوبة ولكن أسقطت الألف في الكتابة

وهذا يفعله المحدثون كثيرا فيكتبون سمعت أنس بغير ألف ويقرؤنه بالنصب وكذلك

مالك كتبوه بغير ألف ويقرؤنه بالنصب فهذا إن شاء الله تعالى من أحسن
# 
# ما يقال فيه وفيه فوائد يتنبه بها على غيره والله أعلم قوله (وأري مالكا

خازن النار والدجال في آيات أراهن الله إياه فلا تكن في مرية من لقائه قال

كان قتادة يفسرها أن نبي الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قد لقي موسى عليه السلام)

هذا الاستشهاد بقوله تعالى فلا تكن فى مرية هو من استدلال بعض الرواة وأما

تفسير قتادة فقد وافقه عليه جماعة منهم مجاهد والكلبي والسدي وعلى مذهبهم

معناه فلا تكن في شك من لقائك موسى  وذهب كثيرون من المحققين من المفسرين

وأصحاب المعاني إلى أن معناها فلا تكن في شك من لقاء موسى الكتاب وهذا مذهب

بن عباس ومقاتل والزجاج وغيرهم والله أعلم قوله
# [166] (حدثنا أحمد بن حنبل وسريج بن يونس) هو بالسين المهملة والجيم قوله

صلى الله عليه وسلم (كأني أنظر إلى موسى صلى الله عليه وسلم هابطا من

الثنية وله جؤار إلى الله تعالى بالتلبية) ثم قال صلى الله عليه وسلم في

يونس بن متى صلى الله عليه وسلم (رأيته وهو يلبي) قال القاضي عياض رحمه

الله أكثر الروايات في وصفهم تدل على أنه صلى الله عليه وسلم رأى ذلك ليلة

أسري به وقد وقع ذلك مبينا فى رواية أبى العالية عن بن عباس وفى رواية بن

المسيب عن أبي هريرة وليس فيها ذكر التلبية قال فإن قيل كيف يحجون ويلبون

وهم أموات وهم في الدار الآخرة وليست دار عمل فاعلم أن للمشايخ وفيما ظهر

لنا عن هذا أجوبة أحدها أنهم كالشهداء بل هم أفضل منهم والشهداء أحياء عند

ربهم فلا يبعد أن يحجوا ويصلوا كما ورد في الحديث الآخر وأن يتقربوا إلى

الله تعالى بما استطاعوا لأنهم وإن كانوا قد توفوا فهم في هذه الدنيا التي

هي دار العمل حتى إذا فنيت
# 
# مدتها وتعقبتها الآخرة التي هي دار الجزاء انقطع العمل الوجه الثاني أن

عمل الآخرة ذكر ودعاء قال الله تعالى دعواهم فيها سبحانك اللهم وتحيتهم

فيها سلام الوجه الثالث أن تكون هذه رؤية منام في غير ليلة الإسراء أو في

بعض ليلة الاسراء كما قال فى رواية بن عمر رضي الله عنهما بينا أنا نائم

رأيتنى أطوف بالكعبة وذكر الحديث في قصة عيسى صلى الله عليه وسلم الوجه

الرابع أنه صلى الله عليه وسلم أري أحوالهم التي كانت في حياتهم ومثلوا له

في حال حياتهم كيف كانوا وكيف حجهم وتلبيتهم كما قال صلى الله عليه وسلم

كأني أنظر إلى موسى وكأني أنظر إلى عيسى وكأني أنظر إلى يونس عليهم السلام

الوجه  الخامس أن يكون أخبر عما أوحي إليه صلى الله عليه وسلم من أمرهم وما

كان منهم وإن لم يرهم رؤية عين هذا آخر كلام القاضي عياض رحمه الله والله

أعلم قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم له جؤار بضم الجيم وبالهمز وهو رفع الصوت

قوله (ثنية هرشى) هي بفتح الهاء وإسكان الراء وبالشين المعجمة مقصورة الألف
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ش ن أ (Shīn-Nūn-Hamzah)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core sense of aversion, disgust, and shrinking from filth or impurity; the Yemeni tribe Azd-Shanū'ah derives its name from this trait.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Moral-psychological distancing from moral defilement (ajnās), aligning with the prophetic description of the Prophet's own character.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage here — physical and moral recoiling; no metaphorical extension.
- Root: ر ب ع (Rā'-Bā'-ʿAyn)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Four; by extension, a man of medium stature — neither towering nor stunted.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Used descriptively of bodily proportion, not numeration.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal in describing physical build; the variant forms (marbūʿ, murabbaʿ, murabtiʿ, rubaʿ, rubʿah) are dialectal phonetic shifts.
- Root: ج ع د (Jīm-ʿAyn-Dāl)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Curliness or kinkiness; also compactness and firmness of body.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In prophetic descriptions, the term is context-sensitive — for Jesus it denotes bodily compactness; for Moses, scholarly disagreement exists between hair-curliness and bodily firmness.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Distinguishes literal (hair texture) from transferred (bodily density) application.
- Root: س ب ط (Sīn-Bā'-Ṭā')
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Smooth, straight, flowing — without kinks or waves.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Describes hair that hangs straight and untangled.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal; the verbal form sabata (with kasr) yaṣbiṭu (with fatḥ) is the standard paradigm.
- Sībawayh Rule: Naṣb by Omitted Accusative Marker (ḥadhf al-alif fī al-khaṭṭ) — The written form may omit the alif of the accusative ending (e.g., "Mālik" for "Mālikan"), while the reader restores the naṣb; this is a recognized scribal convention among traditionists, not a grammatical error.
chapters.translation:
I say: "Shanū'ah" (aversion) means disgust, and it is the act of keeping distant from impurities. From this derives the name "Azd-Shanū'ah," who are a tribe from Yemen, and one is attributed to them as "Shan'ī." He (Ibn al-Sikkīt) said: Sometimes they say "Azd-Shanūwah" with tashdīd and without hamzah, and one is attributed to them as "Shanawī."

As for his saying (peace and blessings be upon him) "marbūʿ" (of medium stature), the linguists said: He is a man between two men in height — neither conspicuously tall nor contemptibly short. There are several variant forms of this word, which the author of Al-Muḥkam and others have mentioned: "marbūʿ," "murabbaʿ," "murabtiʿ" (with fatḥ or kasr of the bā'), "rubaʿ," "rubʿah," and "rubʿah" — the last one with fatḥ on the bā'. For a woman, one says "rubʿah" and "rubʿah."

As for his saying (peace and blessings be upon him) concerning Jesus (peace be upon him) that he was "jaʿd" (curly/compact), and in most narrations describing him it occurs as "sabṭ al-ra's" (straight-haired of head), the scholars said: What is meant by "jaʿd" here is the compactness of the body — its firmness and density — and not the curliness of the hair. As for "jaʿd" in the description of Moses (peace be upon him), the author of Al-Taḥrīr said: It carries two meanings. One is what we mentioned regarding Jesus (peace be upon him), namely bodily firmness; the second is curliness of the hair. He said: The first is more correct, because it has come in the narration of Abū Hurayrah in the Ṣaḥīḥ that he was straight-haired (rajl al-shaʿr). This is the statement of the author of Al-Taḥrīr. Both meanings are permissible, and on the second meaning, the curliness of the hair is not the extreme kinkiness (qaṭaṭ), but rather it means something between kinky and straight. And Allah knows best.

"Al-sabṭ" — with fatḥ on the bā' and kasr on it — are two well-known variant forms. It is also permissible to give sukūn to the bā' with kasr or fatḥ on the sīn, by way of lightening, just as in "katif" and its paradigm. The linguists said: "Sabṭ" hair is that which hangs down flowing, without any kink in it. In the verbal form, one says "sabaṭa shaʿruhu" (with kasr on the bā'), "yasbiṭu" (with fatḥ on it), "sabṭan" (also with fatḥ). And Allah knows best.

His saying in the other narration: "The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said: 'I passed by on the night of my night-journey by Moses son of ʿImrān...'" — Thus it occurs in some manuscripts, while the word "passed by" (marartu) is omitted in most of them. It is indispensable; for even if deleted, it is intended. And Allah knows best.

His saying (peace and blessings be upon him): "And I was shown Mālik, the keeper of the Fire" — "uriya" is with ḍammah on the hamzah and kasr on the rā', and "Mālikan" is in the accusative. Its meaning: The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) was shown Mālik. It is established in Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī in this ḥadīth: "And I saw Mālik." In most manuscripts, however, "Mālik" occurs in the nominative (rafʿ). This may be objected to, and it is said: This is a solecism (laḥn) not permissible in Arabic. But there is a good answer to this: The word "Mālik" is accusative, but the alif was omitted in the writing. The traditionists do this frequently — they write "samiʿtu Anas" without an alif, yet read it in the accusative. Likewise, "Mālik" was written without an alif, and they read it in the accusative. This, Allah willing, is among the best of what may be said on this point, and in it are benefits by which one is alerted to other similar cases. And Allah knows best.

His saying: "And I was shown Mālik, the keeper of the Fire, and the Dajjāl, among the signs that Allah showed him. So be not in doubt of meeting him" — He (Qatādah) used to interpret this that the Prophet of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) had indeed met Moses (peace be upon him). This citation of the verse of the Exalted: {«فَلَا تَكُن فِي مِرْيَةٍ مِّن لِّقَائِهِ»} ("So be not in doubt of meeting him") is from the inference of some of the transmitters. As for Qatādah's interpretation, a group agreed with him, among them Mujāhid, al-Kalbī, and al-Suddī. On their view, its meaning is: Be not in doubt of your meeting Moses. But many of the verifying scholars among the exegetes and masters of semantic analysis held that its meaning is: Be not in doubt of meeting the Book of Moses (i.e., the Torah). This is the view of Ibn ʿAbbās, Muqātil, al-Zajjāj, and others. And Allah knows best.

His saying — [166] (Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal and Surayj ibn Yūnus narrated to us) — "Surayj" is with an unpointed sīn and a jīm. His saying (peace and blessings be upon him): "As if I am looking at Moses (peace be upon him) descending from the mountain-pass, and he has a loud cry (ju'ār) to Allah the Exalted with the talbiyah." Then he said (peace and blessings be upon him) concerning Jonah son of Mattā (peace be upon him): "I saw him, and he was pronouncing the talbiyah."

Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Most narrations describing them indicate that he (peace and blessings be upon him) saw that on the night of the night-journey (Isrā'). This is made explicit in the narration of Abū al-ʿĀliyah from Ibn ʿAbbās, and in the narration of Ibn al-Musayyab from Abū Hurayrah — though in the latter there is no mention of the talbiyah. He said: If it is asked: How can they perform pilgrimage and pronounce the talbiyah while they are dead, being in the abode of the Hereafter, which is not an abode of action? — Know that the shaykhs have given, and what has appeared to us, several answers to this. One: They are like the martyrs — nay, they are better than them — and the martyrs are alive with their Lord. So it is not improbable that they perform pilgrimage and prayer, as has come in another ḥadīth, and that they draw near to Allah the Exalted by whatever they are able, because even though they have passed away, they are still in this world, which is the abode of action, until its term expires and the Hereafter — the abode of recompense — follows it, at which point action ceases. The second view: The action of the Hereafter is remembrance and supplication. Allah the Exalted said: {«دَعْوَاهُمْ فِيهَا سُبْحَانَكَ اللَّهُمَّ وَتَحِيَّتُهُمْ فِيهَا سَلَامٌ»} ("Their call therein is: 'Glory be to You, O Allah,' and their greeting therein is: 'Peace'"). The third view: This could have been a vision in sleep, on a night other than the night of the Isrā', or during part of that night, as he said in the narration of Ibn ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with them both): "While I was sleeping, I saw myself circumambulating the Kaʿbah" — and he mentioned the ḥadīth concerning the story of Jesus (peace be upon him). The fourth view: He (peace and blessings be upon him) was shown their states as they were in their lifetimes, and they were represented to him in their living condition — how they were, and how their pilgrimage and talbiyah were — just as he said (peace and blessings be upon him): "As if I am looking at Moses," and "As if I am looking at Jesus," and "As if I am looking at Jonah" (peace be upon them). The fifth view: He (peace and blessings be upon him) was informing of what was revealed to him concerning their affairs and what they had done, even if he did not see them with his own eyes. This is the end of the statement of Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ (may Allah have mercy on him). And Allah knows best.

His saying (peace and blessings be upon him): "he has a ju'ār" — with ḍammah on the jīm and with hamzah — meaning the raising of the voice. His saying: "Thaniyyat Harshā" — it is with fatḥ on the hā', sukūn on the rā', and with an unpointed shīn, with a shortened alif.

chapters.title_en: Section 164 — Commentary on Descriptions of the Prophet's Vision, Moses, and the Dajjāl
chapters.arabic_text:
وهو جبل على طريق الشام والمدينة قريب من الجحفة قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم

على ناقة حمراء جعدة عليه جبة من صوف خطام ناقته خلبة قال هشيم يعني ليفا

أما الجعدة فهي مكتنزة اللحم كما تقدم قريبا وأما الخطام بكسر الخاء فهو

الحبل الذي يقاد به البعير يجعل على خطمه وقد تقدم بيانه واضحا في أول كتاب

الإيمان وأما الخلبة فبضم الخاء المعجمة وبالباء الموحدة بينهما لام فيها

لغتان مشهورتان الضم والإسكان حكاهما بن السكيت والجوهري وآخرون وكذلك

الخلب والخلب وهو الليف كما فسره هشيم والله أعلم قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم

كأني أنظر إلى موسى واضعا إصبعيه
# 
# في أذنيه) أما الأصبع ففيها عشر لغات كسر الهمزة وفتحها وضمها مع فتح

الباء وكسرها وضمها والعاشرة أصبوع على مثال عصفور وفي هذا دليل على

استحباب وضع الأصبع في الأذن عند رفع الصوت بالأذان ونحوه مما يستحب له رفع

الصوت وهذا الاستنباط والاستحباب يجيء على مذهب من يقول من أصحابنا وغيرهم

إن شرع من قبلنا شرع لنا والله أعلم قوله (فقال أي ثنية هذه قالوا هرشى أو

لفت) هكذا ضبطناها لفت بكسر اللام وإسكان الفاء وبعدها تاء مثناة من فوق

وذكر القاضي وصاحب المطالع فيها ثلاثة أوجه أحدها ما ذكرته والثاني فتح

اللام مع إسكان الفاء والثالث فتح اللام والفاء جميعا والله أعلم قوله صلى

الله عليه وسلم (خطام ناقته ليف خلبة) روي بتنوين ليف وروي بإضافته إلى

خلبة فمن نون جعل خلبة بدلا أو عطف بيان قوله (عن مجاهد قال كنا عند بن

عباس رضي الله عنهما فذكروا الدجال فقال إنه مكتوب بين عينيه كافر قال  فقال

بن عباس لم أسمعه قال ذلك ولكنه قال أما إبراهيم فانظروا إلى صاحبكم) كذا

هو في الأصول وهو صحيح وقوله فقال إنه مكتوب أي قال قائل من الحاضرين ووقع

في الجمع بين الصحيحين لعبد الحق في هذا الحديث من رواية مسلم فذكروا

الدجال فقالوا إنه مكتوب بين عينيه هكذا رواه فقالوا وفي رواية الحميدي عن

الصحيحين وذكروا الدجال بين عينيه كافر فحذف لفظة قال وقالوا وهذا كله يصحح

ما تقدم
# 
# وقوله فقال بن عباس لم أسمعه يعني النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قوله صلى

الله عليه وسلم (كأني أنظر إليه إذا انحدر) هكذا هو في الأصول كلها إذا

بالألف بعد الذال وهو صحيح وقد حكى القاضي عياض عن بعض العلماء أنه أنكر

إثبات الألف وغلط راويه وغلطه القاضي وقال هذا جهل من هذا القائل وتعسف

وجسارة على التوهم لغير ضرورة وعدم فهم بمعاني الكلام إذ لا فرق بين إذا

وإذ هنا لأنه وصف حاله حين انحداره فيما مضى
# [167] قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (فإذا موسى عليه السلام ضرب من الرجال) هو

بإسكان الراء قال القاضي عياض هو الرجل بين الرجلين في كثرة اللحم وقلته

قال القاضي لكن ذكر البخاري فيه من بعض الروايات مضطرب وهو الطويل غير

الشديد وهو ضد جعد اللحم مكتنزه ولكن يحتمل أن الرواية الأولى أصح يعني

رواية ضرب لقوله في الرواية الأخرى حسبته قال مضطرب فقد ضعفت هذه الرواية

للشك ومخالفة الأخرى التي لا شك فيها وفى الرواية الأخرى جسيم سبط وهذا

يرجع إلى الطويل ولا يتأول جسيم بمعنى سمين لأنه ضد ضرب وهذا إنما جاء في

صفة الدجال هذا كلام القاضي وهذا الذي قاله من تضعيف رواية مضطرب وأنها

مخالفة لرواية ضرب لا يوافق عليه فإنه لا مخالفة بينهما فقد قال أهل اللغة

الضرب هو الرجل الخفيف اللحم كذا قاله بن السكيت في الإصلاح وصاحب المجمل

والزبيدي والجوهري وآخرون لا يحصون والله أعلم
# 
# قوله (دحية بن خليفة) هو بفتح الدال وكسرها لغتان مشهورتان
# [168] قوله  صلى الله عليه وسلم (رجل الرأس) هو بكسر الجيم أي رجل الشعر

وسيأتي قريبا إن شاء الله تعالى بيان ترجيل الشعر قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم

في صفة عيسى صلى الله عليه وسلم (فإذا ربعة أحمر كأنما خرج من ديماس يعني

حماما) أما الربعة فبإسكان الباء ويجوز فتحها وقد تقدم قريبا بيان اللغات

فيه وبيان معناه وأما الديماس فبكسر الدال وإسكان الياء والسين في آخره

مهملة وفسره الراوي بالحمام والمعروف عند أهل اللغة أن الديماس هوالسرب وهو

أيضا الكن قال الهروي في هذا الحديث قال بعضهم الديماس هنا هو الكن أي كأنه

مخدر لم ير شمسا قال وقال بعضهم المراد به السرب ومنه دمسته اذا دفتنه وقال

الجوهري في صحاحه في هذا الحديث قوله خرج من ديماس يعني في نضارته وكثرة

ماء وجهه كأنه خرج من كن لأنه قال في وصفه كأن رأسه يقطر ماء وذكر صاحب

المطالع الأقوال الثلاثة فيه فقال الديماس قيل هو السرب وقيل الكن وقيل

الحمام هذا ما يتعلق الديماس وأما الحمام فمعروف وهو مذكر باتفاق أهل اللغة

وقد نقل الازهرى في تهذيب اللغة تذكيره عن العرب والله أعلم وأما وصف عيسى

صلوات الله عليه وسلامه في هذه الرواية وهي رواية أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه

بأنه أحمر ووصفه فى رواية بن عمر رضي الله عنهما بعدها بأنه آدم والآدم

الاسمر وقد روى
# 
# البخارى عن بن عمر رضي الله عنهما أنه أنكر رواية أحمر وحلف أن النبي صلى
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ج-ب-ل (j-b-l)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: A mountain (jabal); firm, solid mass of earth rising above its surroundings.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Used literally for physical mountains; metaphorically for a chief or firm matter.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal here — a specific geographic landmark on the route.
- Sībawayh Rule: ʿAṭf al-Bayān (Appositional Clarification) — For the variant readings of "līf khalabah," where the second noun either clarifies or substitutes the first.
chapters.translation:
I say: And it (i.e., the mountain mentioned) is a mountain on the road between Syria (al-Shām) and Medina, near al-Juḥfah. His saying, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: "Upon a red, compact she-camel (naqah ḥamrā' jaʿdah), upon her a cloak of wool, the nose-rein (khiṭām) of her camel being a palm-fiber rope (khalabah)" — Hushaym said: meaning palm fiber (līf).

As for "al-jaʿdah" (الجعدة), it is the one compact in flesh (muktanazah al-laḥm), as has preceded recently. As for "al-khiṭām" (الخطام), with kasrah on the khā', it is the rope by which the camel is led, placed upon its nose (khaṭm); its clarification has already preceded clearly in the beginning of the Book of Faith (Kitāb al-Īmān). As for "al-khalabah" (الخلبة), it is with ḍammah on the khā' al-muʿjamah and with a single bā', with a lām between them; it has two well-known pronunciations — ḍammah and sukūn — narrated by Ibn al-Sikkīt, al-Jawharī, and others. Likewise, "al-khalb" and "al-khalb" (with sukūn), and it is the palm fiber, as Hushaym interpreted it. And Allah knows best.

His saying, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: "As if I am looking at Moses, placing his two fingers in his ears" — As for "al-iṣbaʿ" (الأصبع, the finger), it has ten pronunciations: kasrah of the hamzah, its fatḥah, and its ḍammah, each combined with fatḥah, kasrah, or ḍammah of the bā'; and the tenth is "uṣbūʿ" (أصبوع) on the pattern of "ʿuṣfūr" (عصفور). In this is evidence for the recommendation (istiḥbāb) of placing the finger in the ear when raising the voice in the call to prayer (adhān) and similar acts for which raising the voice is recommended. This derivation and recommendation proceed upon the school of those among our companions and others who hold that the law of those before us is a law for us (sharʿ man qablanā sharʿ lanā). And Allah knows best.

His saying: "Then he said: 'Which mountain pass (thaniyyah) is this?' They said: 'Harsha or Lift'" — Thus we have recorded it: "Lift" (لفت) with kasrah on the lām, sukūn on the fā', and after it a tā' with two points above. Al-Qāḍī and the author of al-Maṭāliʿ mentioned three aspects (wujūh) in it: one is what I have mentioned; the second is fatḥah on the lām with sukūn on the fā'; and the third is fatḥah on both the lām and the fā'. And Allah knows best.

His saying, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: "The nose-rein of his camel is palm fiber (līf khalabah)" — It is narrated with tanwīn on "līf" (līfun) and narrated with its annexation (iḍāfah) to "khalabah" (līfu khalabah). Whoever uses tanwīn makes "khalabah" a substitute (badal) or an appositional clarification (ʿaṭf bayān).

His saying: "From Mujāhid, who said: 'We were with Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with them both, and they mentioned the Dajjāl. He said: "Verily, it is written between his two eyes: Kāfir (disbeliever)."' He said: 'Ibn ʿAbbās said: "I did not hear him say that, but he said: 'As for Abraham, look to your companion.'"'" — Thus it is in the manuscripts (uṣūl), and it is correct. His saying: "He said: 'Verily, it is written'" — i.e., a speaker among those present said it. And it occurs in al-Jamʿ bayn al-Ṣaḥīḥayn of ʿAbd al-Ḥaqq in this ḥadīth, from the narration of Muslim: "They mentioned the Dajjāl and said: 'Verily, it is written between his two eyes'" — thus he narrated it with "they said" (fa-qālū). And in the narration of al-Ḥumaydī from the two Ṣaḥīḥs: "And they mentioned the Dajjāl — between his two eyes: Kāfir" — omitting the word "he said" (qāla) and "they said" (qālū). And all of this confirms what has preceded.

And his saying: "Ibn ʿAbbās said: 'I did not hear him'" — meaning the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.

His saying, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: "As if I am looking at him when he descends (idhā inḥadara)" — Thus it is in all the manuscripts: "idhā" (إذا) with an alif after the dhāl, and it is correct. Al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ has reported from some scholars that he rejected the affirmation of the alif and declared its narrator mistaken; al-Qāḍī rejected this and said: "This is ignorance from this speaker, and distortion (taʿassuf), and audacity in conjecture without necessity, and a lack of understanding of the meanings of speech — for there is no difference between 'idhā' and 'idh' here, because it describes his state at the time of his descent in the past."

[167] His saying, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: "And behold, Moses, peace be upon him, was a man of moderate build (ḍarb min al-rijāl)" — It is with sukūn on the rā'. Al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ said: "He is the man between two men in abundance and scarcity of flesh." Al-Qāḍī said: "But al-Bukhārī mentioned in it, from some narrations, 'muḍṭarib' (lanky), which is the tall one not sturdy — and it is the opposite of 'jaʿd al-laḥm' (compact of flesh). However, it is possible that the first narration is more correct — meaning the narration of 'ḍarb' — because of his saying in the other narration: 'I reckoned him as muḍṭarib.' Thus this narration is weakened due to doubt and its contradiction of the other which has no doubt in it. And in the other narration: 'Jasīm sabṭ' (large-bodied, straight-haired) — and this reverts to the tall one; and 'jasīm' cannot be interpreted as meaning 'fat,' because that is the opposite of 'ḍarb,' and this (i.e., fatness) only came in the description of the Dajjāl." This is the speech of al-Qāḍī. And what he said regarding the weakening of the narration of "muḍṭarib" and that it contradicts the narration of "ḍarb" — he is not to be agreed with on this, for there is no contradiction between them. The people of language have said: "Al-ḍarb is the man light of flesh" — thus said Ibn al-Sikkīt in al-Iṣlāḥ, and the author of al-Mujmal, al-Zubaydī, al-Jawharī, and countless others. And Allah knows best.

His saying: "Dihyah ibn Khalīfah" — It is with fatḥah on the dāl and kasrah on it, two well-known pronunciations.

[168] His saying, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, in the description of Jesus, peace be upon him: "And behold, he was of medium stature (rabʿah), ruddy, as if he had just come out of a dimās — meaning a bathhouse (ḥammām)" — As for "al-rabʿah" (الربعة), it is with sukūn on the bā', and fatḥah on it is permissible; the pronunciations and its meaning have already preceded recently. As for "al-dīmās" (الديماس), it is with kasrah on the dāl, sukūn on the yā', and the sīn at its end is unpointed (muhmalah). The narrator interpreted it as the bathhouse (ḥammām). The well-known view among the people of language is that "al-dīmās" is the underground chamber (sirb), and it is also the hiding place (kann). Al-Harawī said in this ḥadīth: "Some said: 'Al-dīmās here is the hiding place (kann), i.e., as if he were sheltered, never having seen the sun.'" He said: "And some said: 'The intended meaning is the underground chamber (sirb), and from it is 'damastuhu' (I buried him) when I concealed him.'" Al-Jawharī said in his Ṣiḥāḥ regarding this ḥadīth, his saying "came out of a dīmās" — meaning in his freshness and the abundance of the moisture of his face, as if he had come out of a hiding place — because he said in his description: "As if his head were dripping water." And the author of al-Maṭāliʿ mentioned the three opinions concerning it, saying: "Al-dīmās — it is said it is the underground chamber (sirb), and it is said the hiding place (kann), and it is said the bathhouse (ḥammām)." This is what pertains to al-dīmās. As for "al-ḥammām" (الحمام), it is well-known, and it is masculine by the agreement of the people of language; al-Azharī has transmitted its masculine gender from the Arabs in Tahdhīb al-Lughah. And Allah knows best.

As for the description of Jesus, Allah's prayers and peace be upon him, in this narration — which is the narration of Abū Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him — as "ruddy" (aḥmar), and his description in the narration of Ibn ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with them both, which follows it, as "ādam" (آدم) — and "al-ādam" is the brown-skinned (asmar) — al-Bukhārī has narrated from Ibn ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with them both, that he rejected the narration of "aḥmar" and swore that the Prophet...

chapters.title_en: The Vision of Jesus and the Dajjal — Commentary on the Description of the Prophet's Dream at the Kaʿbah
chapters.arabic_text:
الله عليه وسلم لم يقله يعني وأنه اشتبه على الراوي فيجوز أن يتأول الأحمر

على الآدم ولا يكون المراد حقيقة الأدمة والحمرة بل ما قاربها والله أعلم
# [169] قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (أراني ليلة عند الكعبة فرأيت رجلا آدم

كأحسن ما أنت راء من أدم الرجال له لمة كأحسن ما أنت راء من اللمم قد رجلها

فهي تقطر ماء متكئا على رجلين أو على عواتق رجلين يطوف بالبيت فسألت من هذا

فقيل هذا المسيح بن مريم ثم إذا  أنا برجل جعد قطط أعور العين اليمنى كأنها

عنبة طافية فسألت من هذا فقيل هذا المسيح الدجال) أما قوله صلى الله عليه

وسلم أراني فهو بفتح الهمزة وأما الكعبة فسميت كعبة لارتفاعها وتربعها وكل

بيت مربع عند العرب فهو كعبة وقيل سميت كعبة لاستدارتها وعلوها ومنه كعب

الرجل ومنه كعب ثدي المرأة إذا علا واستدار وأما اللمة فهي بكسر اللام

وتشديد الميم وجمعها لمم كقربة وقرب قال الجوهري ويجمع على لمام يعني بكسر

اللام وهو الشعر المتدلي الذي جاوز شحمة الأذنين فإذا بلغ المنكبين فهو جمة

وأما رجلها فهو بتشديد الجيم ومعناه سرحها بمشط مع ماء أو غيره وأما قوله

صلى الله عليه وسلم يقطر ماء فقد قال القاضي عياض يحتمل أن يكون على ظاهره

أي يقطر بالماء الذي رجلها به لقرب ترجيله
# 
# وإلى هذا نحا القاضي الباجي قال القاضي عياض ومعناه عندي أن يكون ذلك

عبارة عن نضارته وحسنه واستعارة لجماله وأما العواتق فجمع عاتق قال أهل

اللغة هو ما بين المنكب والعنق وفيه لغتان التذكير والتأنيث والتذكير أفصح

وأشهر قال صاحب المحكم ويجمع العاتق على عواتق كما ذكرنا وعلى عتق وعتق

بإسكان التاء وضمها وأما طواف عيسى عليه السلام فقال القاضي عياض رحمه الله

إن كانت هذه رؤيا عين فعيسى حي لم يمت يعني فلا امتناع في طوافه حقيقة وإن

كان مناما كما نبه عليه بن عمر رضي الله عنهما في روايته فهو محتمل لما

تقدم ولتأويل الرؤيا قال القاضي وعلى هذا يحمل ما ذكر من طواف الدجال

بالبيت وأن ذلك رؤيا إذ قد ورد في الصحيح أنه لا يدخل مكة ولا المدينة مع

أنه لم يذكر في رواية مالك طواف الدجال وقد يقال إن تحريم دخول المدينة

عليه إنما هو في زمن فتنته والله أعلم وأما المسيح فهو صفة لعيسى صلى الله

عليه وسلم وصفة للدجال فأما عيسى فاختلف العلماء في سبب تسميته مسيحا قال

الواحدي ذهب أبو عبيد والليث إلى أن أصله بالعبرانية مشيحا فعربته العرب

وغيرت لفظه كما قالوا موسى وأصله موشى أو ميشا بالعبرانية فلما عربوه غيروه

فعلى هذا لا اشتقاق له قال وذهب أكثر العلماء إلى أنه مشتق وكذا قال غيره

إنه مشتق على قول الجمهور ثم اختلف هؤلاء فحكي عن بن عباس رضي الله عنهما

أنه قال لأنه لم يمسح ذا عاهة الا بريء وقال ابراهيم وبن الأعرابي المسيح

الصديق وقيل لكونه ممسوح أسفل القدمين لا أخمص له وقيل لمسح زكريا إياه

وقيل لمسحه الأرض أي قطعها وقيل لأنه خرج من بطن أمه ممسوحا بالدهن وقيل

لأنه مسح بالبركة حين ولد وقيل لأن الله تعالى مسحه أي خلقه خلقا حسنا وقيل

غير ذلك والله أعلم وأما الدجال فقيل سمي بذلك لأنه ممسوح العين وقيل لأنه

أعور والأعور يسمى مسيحا وقيل لمسحه الأرض حين خروجه وقيل غير ذلك قال

القاضي ولا خلاف عند أحد من الرواة في اسم عيسى أنه بفتح الميم وكسر السين

مخففة واختلف في الدجال فأكثرهم يقوله مثله ولا فرق بينهما في اللفظ ولكن

عيسى صلى الله عليه وسلم مسيح هدى والدجال مسيح ضلالة ورواه بعض الرواة

مسيح بكسر الميم والسين المشددة وقاله غير واحد كذلك إلا أنه بالخاء

المعجمة وقاله بعضهم بكسر الميم وتخفيف السين والله أعلم وأما تسمية الدجال

فقد تقدم بيانها في شرح المقدمة وأما قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم
# 
# في صفة الدجال جعد قطط فهو بفتح القاف والطاء هذا هوالمشهور قال القاضي

عياض رويناه بفتح الطاء الأولى وبكسرها قال وهو شديد الجعودة وقال الهروي

الجعد في صفات الرجال يكون مدحا ويكون ذما فإذا كان ذما فله معنيان أحدهما

القصير المتردد والآخر البخيل يقال رجل جعد اليدين وجعد الأصابع أي بخيل

وإذا كان مدحا فله أيضا معنيان أحدهما أن يكون معناه شديد الخلق والآخر

يكون شعره جعدا غير سبط فيكون مدحا لأن السبوطة أكثرها في شعور العجم قال

القاضي قال غير الهروي الجعد في صفة الدجال ذم وفي صفة عيسى عليه السلام

مدح والله أعلم وأما قوله  صلى الله عليه وسلم أعور العين اليمنى كأنها عنبة

طافية فروي بالهمز وبغير همز فمن همز معناه ذهب ضوؤها ومن لم يهمز معناه

ناتئة بارزة ثم إنه جاء هنا أعور العين اليمنى وجاء في رواية أخرى أعور

العين اليسرى وقد ذكرهما جميعا مسلم في آخر الكتاب وكلاهما صحيح قال القاضي

عياض رحمه الله روينا هذا الحرف عن أكثر شيوخنا بغير همز وهو الذي صححه

أكثرهم قال وهو الذي ذهب إليه الأخفش ومعناه ناتئة كنتوء حبة العنب من بين

صواحبها قال وضبطه بعض شيوخنا بالهمز وأنكره بعضهم ولا وجه لإنكاره وقد وصف
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ر-أ-ي (ra-ʾa-ya)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning is "to see" with the eye or the mind; the form "arānī" (أراني) is the 4th verbal form meaning "He showed me" (causative of vision).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological context, ruʾyā (رؤيا) distinguishes dream-vision from waking sight (ʿiyān); the Prophet's vision here is a revelatory showing (murāʾāt ilāhiyyah).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) for physical sight; metaphorical (majāz) when used for dream-perception, as the dreamer "sees" without corporeal vision.
- Sībawayh Rule: Fath al-Hamzah (فتح الهمزة) — The hamzah in "arānī" is opened (fatḥah) as the standard vocalization of the 4th form imperative/perfect, distinguishing it from the 1st form; this is a fixed morphological rule for afʿala pattern.

- Root: ك-ع-ب (kāf-ʿayn-bāʾ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: The cube-like elevation; kaʿbah (الكعبة) derives from irtifāʿ (height) and tarabbuʿ (squareness); also kaʿb (كعب) for the ankle bone or a woman's breast when it rises and rounds.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The Kaʿbah as the sacred house is named for its physical elevation and cubic form, symbolizing its spiritual eminence.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for the architectural shape; no metaphorical extension here, but the root carries the sense of "protruding" and "rounded elevation."
- Sībawayh Rule: Jamʿ al-Taksīr (جمع التكسير) — The plural "kuʿūb" or "kaʿabāt" follows the broken plural pattern, as in "kāʿib" (breast) and "kaʿb" (ankle), showing morphological regularity.

- Root: ل-م-م (lām-mīm-mīm)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: lummah (لمة) is hair that hangs down past the earlobes; jamʿ (plural) is limam (لمم) like qirbah/qirab (water-skin); when it reaches the shoulders it is called jummah (جمة).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In prophetic descriptions, lummah denotes a specific length of hair, a physical attribute with no theological weight but precise lexical definition.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal usage for hair length; no metaphorical sense.
- Sībawayh Rule: Kasr al-Lām wa Tashdīd al-Mīm (كسر اللام وتشديد الميم) — The vocalization of "lummah" with kasrah on the lām and shaddah on the mīm is the canonical form; the plural "limam" follows the pattern fiʿal, as in qirbah/qirab.

- Root: ر-ج-ل (rāʾ-jīm-lām)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: rajjala (رجلها) with tashdīd on the jīm means "to comb and arrange hair" (sarrahā bi-musht); the root also gives rijil (foot) and rajul (man).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The act of combing (tarjīl) is a physical grooming action, literal in the prophetic description.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for combing with water or oil; the water dripping (yaqṭuru māʾ) is taken literally by some, metaphorically by others for freshness and beauty.
- Sībawayh Rule: Tashdīd al-Jīm (تشديد الجيم) — The doubled jīm in "rajjala" indicates the 2nd form (faʿʿala), denoting intensity or causation of the action.

- Root: ع-ت-ق (ʿayn-tāʾ-qāf)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: ʿātiq (عاتق) is the area between the shoulder and the neck; it has dual gender (masculine and feminine), with masculine being more eloquent; plural is ʿawātiq (عواتق) or ʿutq/ʿutuq (عتق/عتق).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Anatomical term, literal in the description of Jesus leaning on two men's shoulders.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal anatomical reference; no metaphorical extension.
- Sībawayh Rule: Jamʿ al-Muʾannath al-Sālim (جمع المؤنث السالم) — "ʿawātiq" is a broken plural (jamʿ taksīr) on the pattern faʿātil, regular for this noun.

- Root: م-س-ح (mīm-sīn-ḥāʾ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: masīḥ (مسيح) — the root means "to wipe" (masaḥa); the noun masīḥ is applied to Jesus and the Dajjal; derivation debated: some say it is non-Arabic (from Hebrew "mashīaḥ"), others say it is derived from masaḥa (wiping).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): For Jesus, masīḥ means "the truthful" (al-ṣiddīq) or "one wiped with blessing"; for the Dajjal, it means "one whose eye is wiped/covered" (mamsūḥ al-ʿayn) or "one who wipes the earth" (travels it).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): The term is used literally for physical wiping (e.g., Jesus wiping the blind and leper) and metaphorically for "traveling the earth" (masḥ al-arḍ) — a majāz for extensive journeying.
- Sībawayh Rule: Ishtiqāq (اشتقاق) — The derivational debate: if derived, it follows the pattern faʿīl (مفعول in meaning, i.e., mamsūḥ); if non-derived, it is a proper noun (ʿalam) with no morphological root.

- Root: د-ج-ل (dāl-jīm-lām)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: dajjāl (دجال) — from dajala (to smear, cover, confuse); the Dajjal is named for covering truth with falsehood, or for his extensive travel (dajl = journeying).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The Dajjal as the "great deceiver" — the term denotes one who confuses and falsifies, a technical eschatological title.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for "one who smears/overspreads" (e.g., a camel covered with tar); metaphorical for the deceiver who covers truth with falsehood.
- Sībawayh Rule: Faʿʿāl Pattern (فعال) — The intensive form faʿʿāl (like dajjāl) denotes habitual or intense action, fitting the Dajjal's pervasive deception.

- Root: ج-ع-د (jīm-ʿayn-dāl)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: jaʿd (جعد) — curly hair; in men's descriptions it can be praise (strong build, curly hair) or blame (short/stingy, as in jaʿd al-yadayn = miserly).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In the Dajjal's description, jaʿd qaṭaṭ (جعد قطط) means intensely curly hair — a physical trait; in Jesus's description, it is praise.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for hair texture; the metaphorical blame sense (stingy) is a majāz from the physical to the moral.
- Sībawayh Rule: Sifah Mushabbihah (صفة مشبهة) — The adjective jaʿd follows the pattern faʿl, functioning as a permanent attribute (ṣifah mushabbihah bi-al-fiʿl).

- Root: ع-و-ر (ʿayn-wāw-rāʾ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: aʿwar (أعور) — one-eyed; ʿawarah means loss of sight in one eye; the Dajjal is described as aʿwar al-ʿayn al-yumnā (one-eyed in the right eye).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Physical defect, literal in the Dajjal's description; the eye is "like a floating grape" (ʿinabah ṭāfiyah).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for the physical condition; the comparison to a grape is a simile (tashbīh) for protrusion (nātīʾah) or loss of light (dhahaba ḍawʾuhā) depending on hamzah vocalization.
- Sībawayh Rule: Afʿal Pattern (أفعل) — The elative/defective pattern aʿwar (أفعل) denotes a physical defect or color, as in aʿmā (blind) and akhras (mute).

- Root: ع-ن-ب (ʿayn-nūn-bāʾ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: ʿinabah (عنبة) — a grape; ṭāfiyah (طافية) — floating or protruding; the simile describes the Dajjal's eye as a grape that floats/protrudes.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The grape simile is literal in its physical description, emphasizing the eye's abnormal protrusion.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): The tashbīh (simile) is a rhetorical device (majāz mursal) comparing the eye to a grape for its roundness and protrusion.
- Sībawayh Rule: Tashbīh (تشبيه) — The comparative construction "ka-annahā" (كأنها) introduces a simile, a standard rhetorical-syntactic structure.
chapters.translation:
I say: The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) did not say it — meaning that it was confused upon the narrator — so it is permissible to interpret "al-aḥmar" (the red) as referring to "al-ādam" (the brown-complexioned), and the intended meaning is not the literal reality of brownness and redness, but rather what approximates them. And Allah knows best.

# [169] His saying (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him): "I was shown (arānī) at night near the Kaʿbah, and I saw a brown-complexioned man (ādam), the most beautiful of what you could see of the brownness of men, having a lummah (hair hanging past the earlobes), the most beautiful of what you could see of such hair. He had combed it (rajjalahā), and it was dripping with water. He was leaning on two men, or on the shoulders (ʿawātiq) of two men, circumambulating the House. I asked, 'Who is this?' It was said, 'This is the Messiah, son of Mary.' Then suddenly I saw a man with intensely curly hair (jaʿd qaṭaṭ), blind in the right eye (aʿwar al-ʿayn al-yumnā), as if it were a floating grape (ʿinabah ṭāfiyah). I asked, 'Who is this?' It was said, 'This is the Messiah, the Dajjal.'"

As for his saying (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) "arānī" — it is with the fatḥah (opening) on the hamzah. As for the Kaʿbah, it was named Kaʿbah because of its height and its squareness; and every square house among the Arabs is called a kaʿbah. It was also said that it was named Kaʿbah because of its roundness and height, and from this derives kaʿb of the foot (ankle bone), and from this derives kaʿb of a woman's breast when it rises and rounds. As for "al-lummah" — it is with kasrah on the lām and tashdīd on the mīm, and its plural is limam, like qirbah and qirab. Al-Jawharī said: it is also collected as limām — meaning with kasrah on the lām — and it is the hanging hair that has passed the earlobes; when it reaches the shoulders, it is called jummah. As for his saying "rajjalahā" — it is with tashdīd on the jīm, and its meaning is: he combed it (sarrahā) with a comb along with water or something else. As for his saying (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) "it was dripping with water" (yaqṭuru māʾ) — Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ said: it is possible that it is upon its literal meaning, i.e., it drips with the water with which he combed it, due to the recency of his combing.

# And toward this did Qāḍī al-Bājī incline. Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ said: And its meaning in my view is that this is an expression of his freshness (naḍārah) and beauty, and a metaphor (istiʿārah) for his comeliness. As for "al-ʿawātiq" — it is the plural of ʿātiq. The people of language said: it is what is between the shoulder and the neck, and in it there are two pronunciations: masculine and feminine, and the masculine is more eloquent and more famous. The author of Al-Muḥkam said: ʿātiq is collected as ʿawātiq, as we mentioned, and also as ʿutq and ʿutuq — with sukūn on the tāʾ and with ḍammah on it. As for the circumambulation (ṭawāf) of Jesus (peace be upon him) — Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ (may Allah have mercy on him) said: If this was a waking vision (ruʾyā ʿayn), then Jesus is alive and has not died — meaning there is no impossibility in his actual circumambulation. And if it was a dream (manām), as Ibn ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with them both) pointed out in his narration, then it is subject to what has preceded and to the interpretation of dreams (taʾwīl al-ruʾyā). The Qāḍī said: And upon this is carried what was mentioned of the Dajjal's circumambulation of the House, and that that was a vision — for it has been established in the Ṣaḥīḥ that he will not enter Mecca nor Medina, even though the circumambulation of the Dajjal was not mentioned in Mālik's narration. And it may be said that the prohibition of his entering Medina is only in the time of his tribulation (fitnah). And Allah knows best.

As for "al-Masīḥ" (the Messiah) — it is an attribute of Jesus (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) and an attribute of the Dajjal. As for Jesus, the scholars differed concerning the reason for his being named Masīḥ. Al-Wāḥidī said: Abū ʿUbayd and al-Layth held that its origin in Hebrew is "Mashīaḥ," and the Arabs Arabized it and changed its wording, just as they said "Mūsā" (Moses) whose origin is "Mōsheh" or "Mīshā" in Hebrew; when they Arabized it, they changed it. Thus, on this view, it has no derivation (ishtiqāq). He said: And the majority of scholars held that it is derived, and likewise others said that it is derived upon the view of the majority (jumhūr). Then these differed: it is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās (may Allah be pleased with them both) that he said: "Because he did not wipe (masaḥa) any afflicted person except that he was healed." Ibrāhīm and Ibn al-Aʿrābī said: al-Masīḥ is al-Ṣiddīq (the truthful). And it was said: because he is wiped (mamsūḥ) on the bottom of his feet, having no arch (akhmas). And it was said: because of Zechariah's wiping of him. And it was said: because of his wiping the earth, i.e., traversing it. And it was said: because he came out of his mother's belly wiped with oil. And it was said: because he was wiped with blessing when he was born. And it was said: because Allah Almighty wiped him, i.e., created him with a beautiful creation. And other views were mentioned. And Allah knows best.

As for "al-Dajjāl" — it was said that he was named thus because he is wiped (mamsūḥ) in the eye, and it was said because he is one-eyed (aʿwar), and the one-eyed is called masīḥ, and it was said because of his wiping the earth (masḥ al-arḍ) when he emerges, and other views were mentioned. The Qāḍī said: There is no disagreement among any of the narrators concerning the name of Jesus that it is with fatḥah on the mīm and kasrah on the sīn, lightened (mukhaffafah). And they differed concerning the Dajjal: most of them say it like it, with no difference between the two in pronunciation — but Jesus (peace be upon him) is Masīḥ al-Hudā (the Messiah of Guidance), and the Dajjal is Masīḥ al-Ḍalālah (the Messiah of Error). And some narrators narrated it as "Masīḥ" with kasrah on the mīm and shaddah on the sīn, and more than one said it likewise, except with the khāʾ (i.e., "Makhīṣ" with muʿjamah khāʾ). And some said it with kasrah on the mīm and takhfīf (lightening) of the sīn. And Allah knows best. As for the naming of the Dajjal — its explanation has already preceded in the commentary on the Introduction (Sharḥ al-Muqaddimah).

As for his saying (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) in the description of the Dajjal: "jaʿd qaṭaṭ" — it is with fatḥah on the qāf and the ṭāʾ; this is the well-known (mashhūr) pronunciation. Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ said: We narrated this word from most of our shaykhs with fatḥah on the first ṭāʾ and with kasrah on it, and he said: it means intensely curly (shadīd al-juʿūdah). Al-Harawī said: "al-jaʿd" in the descriptions of men can be praise (madḥ) and can be blame (dhamm). When it is blame, it has two meanings: one is the short, stunted (al-qaṣīr al-mutaraddid), and the other is the miserly (al-bakhīl); it is said "rajul jaʿd al-yadayn" and "jaʿd al-aṣābiʿ" meaning miserly. And when it is praise, it also has two meanings: one is that its meaning is strong in constitution (shadīd al-khalq), and the other is that his hair is curly (jaʿd) not lank (saṭ), and this is praise because lankness (subūṭah) is mostly found in the hair of non-Arabs (ʿajam). The Qāḍī said: Other than al-Harawī said: "al-jaʿd" in the description of the Dajjal is blame, and in the description of Jesus (peace be upon him) it is praise. And Allah knows best.

As for his saying (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him): "aʿwar al-ʿayn al-yumnā ka-annahā ʿinabah ṭāfiyah" (blind in the right eye, as if it were a floating grape) — it is narrated with hamzah and without hamzah. Whoever reads it with hamzah (ṭāfiyah with hamzah, i.e., ṭāfiʾah), its meaning is: its light has gone (dhahaba ḍawʾuhā). And whoever reads it without hamzah (ṭāfiyah), its meaning is: protruding, prominent (nātīʾah bārizah). Then it came here as "aʿwar al-ʿayn al-yumnā" (blind in the right eye), and it came in another narration as "aʿwar al-ʿayn al-yusrā" (blind in the left eye), and Muslim mentioned both of them at the end of the book, and both are authentic (ṣaḥīḥ). Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ (may Allah have mercy on him) said: We narrated this word from most of our shaykhs without hamzah, and it is what most of them declared authentic, and it is what al-Akhfash held, and its meaning is: protruding, like the protrusion of a grape from among its companions. He said: And some of our shaykhs recorded it with hamzah, and some rejected it, but there is no basis for its rejection, for it has been described...

chapters.title_en: The Description of the Dajjāl's Eye, Harmonization of Narrations, and the Prophet's Night Journey Visions
chapters.arabic_text:
في الحديث بأنه ممسوح العين وأنها ليست جحراء ولا ناتئة بل مطموسة وهذه صفة

حبة العنب إذا سال ماؤها وهذا يصحح رواية الهمز وأما ما جاء في الأحاديث

الأخر جاحظ العين وكأنها كوكب وفي رواية لها حدقة جاحظة كأنها نخاعة في

حائط فتصحح رواية ترك الهمزة ولكن يجمع بين الأحاديث وتصحح الروايات جميعا

بأن تكون المطموسة والممسوحة والتي ليست بجحراء ولا ناتئة هي العوراء

الطافئة بالهمز وهي العين اليمنى كما جاء هنا وتكون الجاحظة والتي كأنها

كوكب وكأنها نخاعة هي الطافية بغير همز وهي العين اليسرى كما جاء في

الرواية الأخرى وهذا جمع بين الأحاديث والروايات في الطافية بالهمز وبتركه

وأعور العين اليمنى واليسرى لأن كل واحدة منهما عوراء فإن الأعور من كل شيء

المعيب لا سيما ما يختص بالعين وكلا عيني الدجال معيبة عوراء إحداهما

بذهابها والأخرى بعيبها هذا آخر كلام القاضي وهو في نهاية من الحسن والله

أعلم قوله (حدثنا محمد بن إسحاق المسيبي) هو بفتح الياء منسوب إلى جد له

وهو محمد
# 
# بن إسحاق بن محمد بن عبد الرحمن بن عبد الله بن المسيب بن أبي السائب أبو

عبد الله المخزومي قوله (بين ظهراني الناس) هو بفتح الظاء وإسكان الهاء

وفتح النون أي بينهم وتقدم بيانه أيضا قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (إن الله

تبارك وتعالى ليس بأعور ألا إن المسيح الدجال أعور عين اليمنى) معناه  أن

الله تعالى منزه عن سمات الحدث وعن جميع النقائص وأن الدجال مخلوق من خلق

الله تعالى ناقص الصورة فينبغي لكم أن تعلموا هذا وتعلموه الناس لئلا يغتر

بالدجال من يرى تخييلاته وما معه من الفتنة وأما أعور عين اليمنى فهو عند

النحويين من الكوفيين على ظاهره من الإضافة وعند البصريين يقدر فيه محذوف

كما يقدر في نظائره فالتقدير أعور عين صفحة وجهه اليمنى والله أعلم قوله

صلى الله عليه وسلم (كأشبه من رأيت بابن قطن) ضبطناه
# 
# رأيت بضم التاء وفتحها وهما ظاهران وقطن هذا بفتح القاف والطاء
# [170] قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (فجلا الله لي بيت المقدس فطفقت أخبرهم عن

آياته) روى فجلا بتشديد اللام وتخفيفها وهما ظاهران ومعناه كشف وأظهر وتقدم

بيان لغات بيت المقدس واشتقاقه في أول هذا الباب وآياته علاماته
# [171] قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (ينطف رأسه ماء أو يهراق) أما ينطف فمعناه

يقطر ويسيل يقال نطف بفتح الطاء ينطف بضمها وكسرها وأما يهراق فبضم الياء

وفتح الهاء ومعناه ينصب
# [172] قوله (حدثنا حجين بن المثنى) هو بحاء مهملة مضمومة ثم جيم مفتوحة

ثم ياء ثم نون قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم
# 
# (فكربت كربة ما كربت مثله قط) هو بضم الكافين والضمير في مثله يعود على

معنى الكربة وهو الكرب أو الغم أو الهم أو الشيء قال الجوهري الكربة بالضم

الغم الذي يأخذ بالنفس وكذلك الكرب وكربه الغم إذا اشتد عليه قوله صلى الله

عليه وسلم (وقد رأيتني في جماعة من الأنبياء صلوات الله عليهم فإذا موسى

صلى الله عليه وسلم قائم يصلي وإذا عيسى بن مريم عليه السلام قائم يصلي

وإذا إبراهيم عليه السلام قائم يصلي فحانت الصلاة فأممتهم قال القاضي عياض

رحمه الله قد تقدم الجواب في صلاتهم عند ذكر طواف موسى وعيسى عليهما السلام

قال وقد تكون الصلاة هنا بمعنى الذكر والدعاء وهي من أعمال الآخرة قال

القاضي فإن قيل كيف رأى موسى عليه السلام يصلي في قبره وصلى النبي صلى الله

عليه وسلم  بالأنبياء ببيت المقدس ووجدهم على مراتبهم فى السماوات وسلموا

عليه ورحبوا به فالجواب أنه يحتمل أن تكون رؤيته موسى في قبره عند الكثيب

الأحمر كانت قبل صعود النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إلى السماء وفي طريقه إلى

بيت المقدس ثم وجد موسى قد سبقه إلى السماء ويحتمل أنه صلى الله عليه وسلم

رأى الأنبياء صلوات الله وسلامه عليهم وصلى بهم على تلك الحال لأول ما رآهم

ثم سألوه ورحبوا به أو يكون اجتماعه بهم وصلاته ورؤيته موسى بعد انصرافه

ورجوعه عن سدرة المنتهى والله أعلم
# 
# [173] قوله (عن مالك بن مغول عن الزبير بن عدي عن طلحة عن مرة) أما مغول

فبكسر الميم وإسكان الغين المعجمة وفتح الواو وطلحة هو بن مصرف وهؤلاء

الثلاثة أعني الزبير وطلحة ومرة تابعيون كوفيون قوله (انتهى به إلى سدرة

المنتهى وهي في السماء السادسة) كذا هو في جميع الأصول السادسة وقد تقدم في

الروايات الأخر من حديث أنس أنها فوق السماء السابعة قال القاضي كونها في

السابعة هو الأصح وقول الأكثرين وهو الذي يقتضيه المعنى وتسميتها بالمنتهى

قلت ويمكن أن يجمع بينهما فيكون أصلها في السادسة ومعظمها في السابعة فقد

علم أنها في نهاية من العظم وقد قال الخليل رحمه الله هي سدرة في السماء

السابعة قد أظلت السماوات والجنة وقد تقدم ما حكيناه عن القاضي عياض رحمه

الله في قوله إن مقتضى خروج النهرين الظاهرين النيل والفرات من أصل سدرة

المنتهى أن يكون أصلها في
# 
# الأرض فإن سلم له هذا أمكن حمله على ما ذكرناه والله أعلم قوله (وغفر لمن
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ع-و-ر (ʿ- w-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning of defect, blemish, or imperfection in an organ, especially the eye; a single-eyed person (aʿwar) is one whose eye is defective, whether blind or otherwise impaired.
