The traditions (āthār) have come, which collectively reach the level of tawātur (mass transmission), affirming the soundness of intercession in the Hereafter for the sinful believers. The Salaf (early generations) and the Khalaf (later generations), and those after them from the People of the Sunnah, have reached consensus (ijmāʿ) upon it. The Khawārij and some of the Muʿtazilah denied it, clinging to their doctrines of the eternal punishment of sinners in the Fire. They argued with His statement, Exalted be He: {«So the intercession of intercessors will not benefit them»} (al-Muddaththir 74:48), and His statement: {«The wrongdoers will have no friend nor any intercessor to be obeyed»} (Ghāfir 40:18). These verses concern the disbelievers. As for their interpretation of the intercession ḥadīths as being about the increase of ranks (ziyādat al-darajāt), it is false, and the very wording of the ḥadīths in this book and elsewhere is explicit in refuting their doctrine and in the exit of those who have merited the Fire.

Yet intercession is of five divisions: The first is exclusive to our Prophet — peace and blessings be upon him — and it is the relief from the terror of the Standing Place (al-mawqif) and the hastening of the Reckoning (al-ḥisāb), as will be explained shortly. The second is the admission of a people into Paradise without reckoning; this too has been reported for our Prophet — peace and blessings be upon him — and Muslim — may Allah have mercy on him — has mentioned it. The third is intercession for a people who have merited the Fire, so our Prophet — peace and blessings be upon him — and whomever Allah wills will intercede for them; we will draw attention to its place soon, Allah willing. The fourth concerns those who have entered the Fire among the sinners; these ḥadīths have come affirming their exit from the Fire through the intercession of our Prophet — peace and blessings be upon him — the angels, and their brethren among the believers. Then Allah, Exalted be He, will bring out everyone who said "There is no god but Allah" (lā ilāha illā Allāh), as came in the ḥadīth: "None will remain therein except the disbelievers." The fifth is the increase of ranks in Paradise for its people; this the Muʿtazilah do not deny, nor do they deny the intercession of the first gathering (shafāʿat al-ḥashr al-awwal).

The Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ said: It is known through widespread transmission (al-naql al-mustafīḍ) that the righteous Salaf — may Allah be pleased with them — asked for the intercession of our Prophet — peace and blessings be upon him — and desired it. On this basis, no attention is paid to the statement of one who says it is disliked (makrūh) for a person to ask Allah, Exalted be He, to grant him the intercession of Muḥammad — peace and blessings be upon him — on the grounds that it occurs only for sinners; for it may occur, as we have stated, for the alleviation of the Reckoning and the increase of ranks. Then every rational person who acknowledges his shortcoming, is in need of pardon, does not rely on his deeds, and fears that he might be among the perished — such a one is compelled to seek it. And this speaker would be obliged not to pray for forgiveness and mercy, because they are for those with sins. All of this contradicts what is known of the supplication of the Salaf and the Khalaf. This is the end of the Qāḍī's statement — may Allah have mercy on him — and Allah knows best.

[184] His statement — peace and blessings be upon him: "They will emerge from it as embers (ḥumaman) that have been scorched (imtaḥashū), then they will be cast into the River of Life (Nahr al-Ḥayāh) or al-Ḥayā, and they will sprout therein as the seed sprouts." As for "al-ḥumam," its explanation has preceded in the previous chapter; it is with ḍammah on the ḥāʾ and fatḥah on the mīm, ungeminated, and it means "charcoal" (faḥm). Therein has also preceded the explanation of "the seed" (al-ḥabbah), "the river," and the explanation of "imtaḥashū" — that it is with fatḥah on the tāʾ according to the preferred view, and it is said with ḍammah on it; its meaning is "they were burned." His statement "al-Ḥayāh or al-Ḥayā" — thus it occurs here, and in al-Bukhārī from the narration of Mālik; al-Bukhārī explicitly stated at the beginning of his Ṣaḥīḥ that this doubt is from Mālik, and the narrations of others have "al-Ḥayāh" with the tāʾ without doubt. Then, "al-Ḥayā" here is with qaṣr (shortened vowel), and it means "rain" (al-maṭar); it is called "ḥayā" because the earth comes to life (taḥyā) through it, and likewise this water brings life to these people.

chapters.title_en: The Burned Ones and Their Restoration to Freshness, and the Meaning of "Ghuthā'" and "Ḥamīlah" in the Hadith of Intercession
chapters.arabic_text:
المحترقون وتحدث فيهم النضارة كما يحدث ذلك المطر في الأرض والله أعلم قوله

(كما تنبت الغثاء) هو بضم الغين المعجمة وبالثاء المثلثة المخففة وبالمد

وآخره هاء وهو كل ما جاء به السيل وقيل المراد ما احتمله السيل من البذور

وجاء في غير مسلم كما تنبت الحبة في غثاء السيل بحذف الهاء من آخره وهو ما

احتمله السيل من الزبد والعيدان ونحوهما من الأقذاء والله أعلم قوله (وفي

حديث وهيب كما تنبت الحبة في حمئة أو حميلة السيل) أما الأول فهو حمئة بفتح

الحاء وكسر الميم وبعدها همزة وهي الطين الأسود الذي يكون في أطراف النهر

وأما الثاني فهو حميلة وهي واحدة الحميل المذكور في الروايات الأخر بمعنى

المحمول وهو الغثاء الذي يحتمله السيل والله أعلم
# [185] قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (أهل النار الذين هم أهلها فإنهم لا

يموتون فيها ولا يحيون ولكن ناس أصابتهم النار بذنوبهم أو قال بخطاياهم

فأماتهم إماتة حتى اذا كانوا فحما أذن بالشفاعة فجئ بهم ضبائر ضبائر فبثوا

على أنهار الجنة ثم قيل يا أهل الجنة أفيضوا عليهم فينبتون  نبات الحبة تكون

في حميل السيل) هكذا وقع في معظم النسخ أهل النار وفي بعضها أما أهل النار

بزيادة أما وهذا أوضح والأول صحيح وتكون الفاء في فإنهم زائدة وهو جائز

وقوله (فأماتهم) أي أماتهم إماتة وحذف للعلم به وفي بعض النسخ فأماتتهم
# 
# بتاءين أي أماتتهم النار وأما معنى الحديث فالظاهر والله أعلم من معنى

هذا الحديث أن الكفار الذين هم أهل النار والمستحقون للخلود لا يموتون فيها

ولا يحيون حياة ينتفعون بها ويستريحون معها كما قال الله تعالى لا يقضى

عليهم فيموتوا ولا يخفف عنهم من عذابها وكما قال تعالى ثم لا يموت فيها ولا

يحيى وهذا جار على مذهب أهل الحق أن نعيم أهل الجنة دائم وأن عذاب أهل

الخلود في النار دائم وأما قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم ولكن ناس أصابتهم النار

إلى آخره فمعناه أن المذنبين من المؤمنين يميتهم الله تعالى إماتة بعد أن

يعذبوا المدة التي أرادها الله تعالى وهذه الإماتة إماتة حقيقية يذهب معها

الإحساس ويكون عذابهم على قدر ذنوبهم ثم يميتهم ثم يكونون محبوسين في النار

من غير إحساس المدة التي قدرها الله تعالى ثم يخرجون من النار موتى قد

صاروا فحما فيحملون ضبائر كما تحمل الأمتعة ويلقون على أنهار الجنة فيصب

عليهم ماء الحياة فيحيون وينبتون نبات الحبة في حميل السيل في سرعة نباتها

وضعفها فتخرج لضعفها صفراء ملتوية ثم تشتد قوتهم بعد ذلك ويصيرون إلى

منازلهم وتكمل أحوالهم فهذا هو الظاهر من لفظ الحديث ومعناه وحكى القاضي

عياض رحمه الله فيه وجهين أحدهما أنها إماتة حقيقية والثاني ليس بموت حقيقي

ولكن تغيب عنهم إحساسهم بالآلام قال ويجوز أن تكون آلامهم أخف فهذا كلام

القاضي والمختار ما قدمناه والله أعلم وأما قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم ضبائر

ضبائر فكذا هو في الروايات والأصول ضبائر ضبائر مكرر مرتين وهو منصوب على

الحال وهو بفتح الضاد المعجمة وهو جمع ضبارة بفتح الضاد وكسرها لغتان

حكاهما القاضي عياض وصاحب المطالع وغيرهما أشهرهما الكسر ولم يذكر  الهروي

وغيره إلا الكسر ويقال فيها أيضا إضبارة بكسر الهمزة قال أهل اللغة الضبائر

جماعات في تفرقة وروى ضبارات ضبارات وأما قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (فبثوا)

فهو بالباء الموحدة المضمومة بعدها ثاء مثلثة ومعناه فرقوا والله أعلم قوله

(عن أبي مسلمة قال سمعت أبا نضرة عن أبى سعيد الخدرى) أما أبو سعيد فاسمعه

سعد بن مالك بن
# 
# سنان وأما أبو نضرة فاسمه المنذر بن مالك بن قطعة بكسر القاف وأما أبو

مسلمة فبفتح الميم وإسكان السين واسمه سعيد بن يزيد الأزدي البصري والله

أعلم
# [186] قوله (حدثنا عثمان بن أبي شيبة وإسحاق بن إبراهيم الحنظلي كليهما)

هكذا وقع في معظم الأصول كليهما بالياء ووقع في بعضها كلاهما بالألف مصلحا

وقد قدمت في الفصول التي في أول الكتاب بيان جوازه بالياء قوله (عن عبيدة)

هو بفتح العين وهو عبيدة السلماني قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (رجل يخرج من

النار حبوا) وفي الرواية الأخرى زحفا قال أهل اللغة الحبو المشي على اليدين

والرجلين وربما قالوا على اليدين والركبتين وربما قالوا على يديه ومقعدته

وأما الزحف فقال بن دريد وغيره هو المشي على الاست مع افراشه بصدره فحصل من

هذا أن الحبو والزحف متماثلان أو متقاربان ولو ثبت اختلافهما حمل على أنه

في حال يزحف وفي حال يحبو والله أعلم قوله (أتسخر بي أو أتضحك بي وأنت

الملك) هذا شك من الراوي هل قال أتسخر بي أو قال أتضحك بي فإن كان الواقع
# 
# في نفس الأمر أتضحك بي فمعناه أتسخر بي لأن الساخر في العادة يضحك ممن

يسخر به فوضع الضحك موضع السخرية مجازا وأما معنى أتسخر بي هنا ففيه أقوال

أحدها قاله المازري أنه خرج على المقابلة الموجودة في معنى الحديث دون لفظه

لأنه عاهد الله مرارا ألا يسأله غير ما سأل ثم غدر فحل غدره محل الاستهزاء
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ح ر ق (ḥ-r-q)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning of burning, scorching, or consuming by fire; "muḥtariqūn" (المحترقون) denotes those who have been burned or scorched.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological context, refers to the punishment of sinners in Hellfire—a literal burning that affects the body, distinct from the eternal torment of the disbelievers.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage here—actual burning by fire, not metaphorical; the "freshness" (naḍārah) that returns to them is a literal restoration of vitality.
- Root: غ ث و (gh-th-w)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: "Ghuthā'" (الغثاء) is what a flood carries—scum, foam, debris, or seeds borne by torrential water; derived from the verb "ghathā" meaning to come forth or be carried.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In the prophetic simile, it signifies the weak, fragile growth that emerges from flood-borne debris—a metaphor for the believers' emergence from Hellfire in a state of weakness.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal in reference to the flood's debris; metaphorical (majāz) in the hadith, likening the believers' rapid, weak growth to that of a seed in flood-carried soil.
- Root: ح م ل (ḥ-m-l)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: "Ḥamīlah" (حميلة) is that which is carried or borne; "ḥamīl" (حميل) is the carried thing, i.e., the debris transported by a flood.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In the hadith, it denotes the flood-borne material that nurtures the seed—symbolizing the means by which the saved sinners are revived.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense of carrying; the term is used in its concrete meaning here, not figuratively.
- Sībawayh Rule: Rule of Ḥāl (الحال) — The accusative noun "ḍabā'ira ḍabā'ira" (ضبائر ضبائر) is parsed as a circumstantial accusative (ḥāl) indicating the manner in which the people are brought, i.e., in groups, as established by the grammatical tradition.
chapters.translation:
I say: The burned ones—freshness occurs in them just as that rain causes [freshness] in the earth. And Allah knows best.

His saying (peace and blessings be upon him): {«كما تنبت الغثاء»} — "Ghuthā'" is with a ḍammah on the ghayn (غ), a lightened thā' (ث), a madd (lengthening), and a final hā' (ه). It is everything that the flood brings. It is also said that what is meant is the seeds that the flood carries. And in [a narration] other than Muslim, [it appears as]: {«كما تنبت الحبة في غثاء السيل»} — with the hā' omitted from its end—and it is what the flood carries of foam, twigs, and similar filth. And Allah knows best.

His saying (in the hadith of Wuhaib): {«كما تنبت الحبة في حمئة أو حميلة السيل»} — As for the first, it is "ḥam'ah" (حمئة), with a fatḥah on the ḥā' (ح) and kasrah on the mīm (م), followed by a hamzah (ء); it is the black mud that is at the edges of a river. As for the second, it is "ḥamīlah" (حميلة), which is the singular of "ḥamīl" (حميل) mentioned in the other narrations, meaning "that which is carried"—i.e., the debris that the flood carries. And Allah knows best.

[185] His saying (peace and blessings be upon him): {«أهل النار الذين هم أهلها فإنهم لا يموتون فيها ولا يحيون ولكن ناس أصابتهم النار بذنوبهم أو قال بخطاياهم فأماتهم إماتة حتى اذا كانوا فحما أذن بالشفاعة فجئ بهم ضبائر ضبائر فبثوا على أنهار الجنة ثم قيل يا أهل الجنة أفيضوا عليهم فينبتون نبات الحبة تكون في حميل السيل»} — "The people of the Fire, those who are its [true] inhabitants—they do not die therein nor live. But [there are] people whom the Fire afflicted due to their sins—or he said: their misdeeds—and it caused them to die a [complete] death, until when they became charcoal, permission was given for intercession. Then they were brought in clusters, cluster by cluster, and scattered upon the rivers of Paradise. Then it was said: 'O people of Paradise, pour [water] upon them.' So they sprout as a seed sprouts that is in the flood's debris." Thus it occurs in most copies: "Ahl al-Nār" (أهل النار). In some copies: "Amma ahl al-Nār" (أما أهل النار) with the addition of "ammā" (أما), and this is clearer. The first is also correct, and the "fā'" (ف) in "fa-innahum" (فإنهم) is redundant (zā'idah), which is permissible.

His saying: {«فأماتهم»} — i.e., He caused them to die a [complete] death, and the object is omitted because it is known. In some copies: {«فأماتتهم»} with two tā's—i.e., the Fire caused them to die.

As for the meaning of the hadith, the apparent [understanding]—and Allah knows best—of the meaning of this hadith is that the disbelievers who are the [true] inhabitants of the Fire and deserving of eternity [in it] do not die therein, nor do they live a life by which they benefit or find rest, as Allah the Exalted said: {«لا يقضى عليهم فيموتوا ولا يخفف عنهم من عذابها»} ("They will not be judged so they die, nor will its punishment be lightened for them") and as He said: {«ثم لا يموت فيها ولا يحيى»} ("Then he will not die therein nor live"). This runs according to the doctrine of the people of truth (ahl al-ḥaqq) that the bliss of the people of Paradise is eternal and that the punishment of those who are eternal in the Fire is eternal.

As for his saying (peace and blessings be upon him): {«ولكن ناس أصابتهم النار»} to the end, its meaning is that the sinful believers—Allah the Exalted causes them to die a [complete] death after they have been punished for the duration that Allah the Exalted willed. This death is a real death (imātah ḥaqīqiyyah) by which sensation departs, and their punishment is proportionate to their sins. Then He causes them to die, and they remain imprisoned in the Fire without sensation for the duration that Allah the Exalted decreed. Then they are brought out of the Fire dead, having become charcoal, and they are carried in clusters (ḍabā'ir) as loads are carried, and they are cast upon the rivers of Paradise. Then the water of life is poured upon them, and they come alive and sprout as a seed sprouts in the flood's debris—in the speed of its growth and its weakness—so it emerges, due to its weakness, yellow and twisted. Then their strength intensifies afterward, and they proceed to their stations, and their states are completed. This is the apparent [understanding] of the wording of the hadith and its meaning.

Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ (may Allah have mercy on him) reported two views regarding this: one is that it is a real death (imātah ḥaqīqiyyah), and the second is that it is not a real death, but rather their sensation of pains becomes absent from them. He said: "And it is possible that their pains become lighter." This is the statement of the Qāḍī. The chosen [view] is what we have presented. And Allah knows best.

As for his saying (peace and blessings be upon him): {«ضبائر ضبائر»} — thus it is in the narrations and the manuscripts: "ḍabā'ira ḍabā'ira," repeated twice. It is in the accusative as a circumstantial accusative (ḥāl), with a fatḥah on the ḍād (ض). It is the plural of "ḍibārah" (ضبارة) with fatḥah or kasrah on the ḍād—two dialects, both reported by Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ, the author of al-Maṭāliʿ, and others. The more famous of the two is the kasrah, and al-Harawī and others mentioned only the kasrah. It is also said therein "iḍbārah" (إضبارة) with kasrah on the hamzah. The linguists said: "Al-ḍabā'ir" are groups in dispersion. And it is narrated: "ḍibārāt ḍibārāt" (ضبارات ضبارات).

As for his saying (peace and blessings be upon him): {«فبثوا»} — it is with a ḍammah on the single bā' (ب), followed by a thā' (ث) with three dots, and its meaning is "they were scattered" (furriqū). And Allah knows best.

His saying: {«عن أبي مسلمة قال سمعت أبا نضرة عن أبي سعيد الخدري»} — As for Abū Saʿīd, his name is Saʿd ibn Mālik ibn Sinān. As for Abū Naḍrah, his name is al-Mundhir ibn Mālik ibn Qaṭʿah, with kasrah on the qāf (ق). As for Abū Maslamah, it is with fatḥah on the mīm (م) and sukūn on the sīn (س), and his name is Saʿīd ibn Yazīd al-Azdī al-Baṣrī. And Allah knows best.

[186] His saying: {«حدثنا عثمان بن أبي شيبة وإسحاق بن إبراهيم الحنظلي كليهما»} — Thus it occurs in most manuscripts: "kilayhimā" (كليهما) with a yā' (ي). In some copies, it occurs as "kilāhumā" (كلاهما) with an alif (ا), corrected [in the margin]. I have already presented in the chapters at the beginning of the book the permissibility of [using] the yā' [form].

His saying: {«عن عبيدة»} — it is with fatḥah on the ʿayn (ع), and he is ʿUbaydah al-Salmānī.

His saying (peace and blessings be upon him): {«رجل يخرج من النار حبوا»} — and in the other narration: {«زحفا»}. The linguists said: "Al-ḥabw" (الحبو) is walking on the hands and feet, and sometimes they say on the hands and knees, and sometimes they say on his hands and his buttocks. As for "al-zaḥf" (الزحف), Ibn Durayd and others said: it is walking on the buttocks with the chest spread [forward]. From this, it is established that "al-ḥabw" and "al-zaḥf" are similar or nearly so. If their difference were established, it would be interpreted as [meaning] that in one state he crawls (yazḥaf) and in another he creeps (yaḥbū). And Allah knows best.

His saying: {«أتسخر بي أو أتضحك بي وأنت الملك»} — This is a doubt from the narrator as to whether he said "Do you mock me?" or "Do you laugh at me?" If what actually occurred was "Do you laugh at me?" then its meaning is "Do you mock me?" because the mocker, by custom, laughs at the one he mocks, so laughter was placed in the position of mockery metaphorically (majāzan).

As for the meaning of "Do you mock me?" here, there are several sayings. One of them, stated by al-Māzarī, is that it emerged as a counterpoint (muqābalah) to what exists in the meaning of the hadith, not its wording, because he had covenanted with Allah repeatedly not to ask Him for anything other than what he had asked, then he broke [his covenant], so his breaking [of the covenant] took the place of mockery.

chapters.title_en: Section 179 — On the Mocking Utterance of the Man Entering Paradise, the Laughter of the Prophet ﷺ, and Related Matters
chapters.arabic_text:
والسخرية فقدر الرجل أن قول الله تعالى له ادخل الجنة وتردده إليها وتخييل

كونها مملوءة ضرب من الإطماع له والسخرية به جزاء لما تقدم  من غدره وعقوبة

له فسمي الجزاء على السخرية سخرية فقال أتسخر بي أي تعاقبني بالإطماع

والقول الثاني قاله أبو بكر الصوفي إن معناه نفي السخرية التي لا تجوز على

الله تعالى كأنه قال أعلم أنك لا تهزأ بي لأنك رب العالمين وما أعطيتني من

جزيل العطاء وأضعاف مثل الدنيا حق ولكن العجب أنك أعطيتني هذا وأنا غير أهل

له قال والهمزة في أتسخر بي همزة نفي قال وهذا كلام منبسط متدلل والقول

الثالث قاله القاضي عياض أن يكون هذا الكلام صدر من هذا الرجل وهو غير ضابط

لما قاله لما ناله من السرور ببلوغ مالم يخطر بباله فلم يضبط لسانه دهشا

وفرحا فقاله وهو لا يعتقد حقيقة معناه وجرى على عادته في الدنيا في مخاطبة

المخلوق وهذا كما قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في الرجل الآخر أنه لم يضبط

نفسه من الفرح فقال أنت عبدي وأنا ربك والله أعلم واعلم أنه وقع في

الروايات أتسخر بي وهو صحيح يقال سخرت منه وسخرت به والأول هو الأفصح

الأشهر وبه جاء القرآن والثاني فصيح أيضا وقد قال بعض العلماء أنه انما جاء

بالباء لإرادة معناه كأنه قال أتهزأ بي والله أعلم قوله (رأيت رسول الله

صلى الله عليه وسلم ضحك حتى بدت نواجذه) هو بالجيم والذال المعجمة قال أبو

العباس ثعلب وجماهير العلماء من أهل اللغة وغريب الحديث وغيرهم المراد

بالنواجذ هنا الأنياب وقيل المراد هنا الضواحك وقيل المراد بها الأضراس

وهذا هو الأشهر في إطلاق النواجذ في اللغة ولكن الصواب عند الجماهير ما

قدمناه وفي هذا جواز الضحك وأنه ليس بمكروه في بعض المواطن ولا بمسقط

للمروءة إذا لم يجاوز به الحد المعتاد من أمثاله في مثل
# 
# تلك الحال والله أعلم قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (فيقول الله تعالى له اذهب

فادخل الجنة فإن لك مثل الدنيا وعشرة أمثالها) وفي الرواية الأخرى (لك الذي

تمنيت وعشرة أضعاف الدنيا) هاتان الروايتان بمعنى واحد وإحداهما تفسير

الأخرى فالمراد بالأضعاف الأمثال فإن المختار  عند أهل اللغة أن الضعف المثل

وأما قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم في الأخرى في الكتاب (فيقول الله تعالى

أيرضيك أن أعطيك الدنيا ومثلها معها) وفي الرواية الأخرى (أترضى أن يكون لك

مثل ملك ملك من ملوك الدنيا فيقول رضيت رب فيقول لك ذلك ومثله ومثله ومثله

ومثله ومثله فقال في الخامسة رضيت رب فيقول هذا لك وعشرة أمثاله) فهاتان

الروايتان لا تخالفان الأوليين فإن المراد بالأولى من هاتين أن يقال له

أولا لك الدنيا ومثلها ثم يزاد إلى تمام عشرة أمثالها كما بينه في الرواية

الأخيرة وأما الأخيرة فالمراد بها أن أحد ملوك الدنيا لا ينتهي ملكه إلى

جميع الأرض بل يملك بعضا منها ثم منهم من يكثر البعض الذي يملكه ومنهم من

يقل بعضه فيعطى هذا الرجل مثل أحد ملوك الدنيا خمس مرات وذلك كله
# 
# قدر الدنيا كلها ثم يقال له لك عشرة أمثال هذا فيعود معنى هذه الرواية

إلى موافقة الروايات المتقدمة ولله الحمد وهو أعلم
# [187] قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (آخر من يدخل الجنة رجل فهو يمشي مرة

ويكبو مرة وتسفعه النار مرة) أما يكبو فمعناه يسقط على وجهه وأما تسفعه فهو

بفتح التاء وإسكان السين المهملة وفتح الفاء ومعناه تضرب وجهه وتسوده وتؤثر

فيه أثرا قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (لأنه يرى مالا صبر له عليه) كذا هو في

الأصول في المرتين الاولتين وأما الثالثة فوقع في أكثر الاصول مالا صبر له

عليها وفي بعضها عليه وكلاهما صحيح ومعنى عليها أي نعمة لا صبر له عليها أي

عنها قوله عز وجل يا بن آدم مايصرينى منك هو بفتح الياء وإسكان الصاد

المهملة ومعناه يقطع مسئلتك مني قال أهل اللغة الصري بفتح الصاد وإسكان

الراء هو القطع وروي في غير مسلم ما يصريك مني قال إبراهيم الحربي هو

الصواب وأنكر الرواية التي في صحيح مسلم وغيره ما يصريني منك وليس هو كما

قال بل كلاهما صحيح فإن السائل متى انقطع من المسؤل انقطع
# 
# المسؤل منه والمعنى  أى شئ يرضيك ويقطع السؤال بيني وبينك والله أعلم قوله

(قالوا مم تضحك يارسول الله قال من ضحك رب العالمين) قد قدمنا معنى الضحك

من الله تعالى وهو الرضى والرحمة وإرادة الخير لمن يشاء رحمته من عباده

والله أعلم
# [188] قوله (عن النعمان بن أبي عياش) هو بالشين المعجمة وهو أبو عياش

الزرقي الأنصاري الصحابي المعروف في اسمه خلاف مشهور قيل زيد بن الصامت

وقيل زيد بن النعمان وقيل عبيد وقيل عبد الرحمن قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم
# 
# (فتدخل عليه زوجتاه من الحور العين فتقولان الحمد لله الذي أحياك لنا

وأحيانا لك) هكذا ثبت في الروايات والأصول زوجتاه بالتاء تثنية زوجة بالهاء

وهي لغة صحيحة معروفة وفيها أبيات كثيرة من شعر العرب وذكرها بن السكيت

وجماعات من أهل اللغة وقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (فتقولان) هو بالتاء

المثناة من فوق وإنما ضبطت هذا وإن كان ظاهرا لكونه مما يغلط فيه بعض من لا
chapters.anchors:
- Root: س-خ-ر (s-kh-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To mock, deride, or treat with scorn; also to subject someone to a deceptive promise or vain hope (al-ṭamʿ).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Mockery (sukhriyyah) as a form of belittlement; in divine contexts, it denotes requital that carries the form of mockery without attributing a blameworthy trait to God.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage denotes actual derision; metaphorical (majāz) usage here applies to punitive requital that resembles mockery in its effect.
- Sībawayh Rule: Hamzah of Interrogation vs. Negation (hamzat al-istifhām wa-l-nafy) — The particle "a-" may function either as interrogative or as negating, distinguished by context and the verb's mood.
chapters.translation:
I say: And the mockery (sukhriyyah) — it is that God most high says to the man: "Enter Paradise," and His repeated bidding him to it, and the suggestion (takhyīl) that it is filled [with delights] — this is a kind of feeding his hope (iṭmāʿ) and mocking him, as requital for what preceded of his treachery and as punishment for him. Thus the requital for mockery was itself called mockery, so He said: "Do you mock at me (a-taskharu bī)?" — i.e., "Do you punish me by feeding my hope?"

The second saying — stated by Abū Bakr al-Ṣūfī — is that its meaning is the negation of mockery, which is not permissible to attribute to God most high. As if he said: "I know that you do not deride me, for You are the Lord of the worlds, and what You have given me of abundant gift and multiples like unto the world is a right [due to Your bounty]; but the wonder is that You have given me this while I am not worthy of it." He said: And the hamzah in "a-taskharu bī" is a hamzah of negation. He said: And this is speech of one expansive and emboldened [in intimacy].

The third saying — stated by Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ — is that this speech issued from this man while he was not in control of what he said, due to what had befallen him of joy at attaining what had never crossed his mind; so he did not restrain his tongue in bewilderment (dahash) and joy, and he uttered it while not believing the true meaning of it, and he followed his habitual way in the world of addressing created beings. This is like what the Prophet ﷺ said concerning the other man — that he did not restrain himself from joy, so he said: "You are my servant and I am Your Lord." And God knows best.

Know that in the narrations it occurs as "a-taskharu bī" (with the preposition bā'), and it is sound. It is said: "sakhirtu minhu" and "sakhirtu bihī." The first is the more eloquent and more famous, and with it the Qur'an came; the second is also eloquent. Some scholars have said that it came with the bā' to convey its meaning, as if he said: "Do you deride me (a-tahza'u bī)?" And God knows best.

His saying ﷺ: "I saw the Messenger of God ﷺ laugh until his molars (nawājidh) appeared" — it is with jīm and dhāl (i.e., "nawājidh"). Abū al-ʿAbbās Thaʿlab and the majority of scholars among the people of language and of strange ḥadīth and others said: The intended meaning of "nawājidh" here is the canine teeth (anyāb). It was also said: The intended meaning here is the lateral incisors (ḍawāḥik). And it was said: The intended meaning is the molars (aḍrās) — and this is the more famous usage of "nawājidh" in the language. But the correct view according to the majority is what we have stated. And in this [ḥadīth] is the permissibility of laughter, and that it is not disliked (makrūh) in certain situations, nor does it detract from manliness (murū'ah) when one does not exceed the customary limit of one's peers in such a state. And God knows best.

His saying ﷺ: "God most high will say to him: 'Go and enter Paradise, for you shall have the like of the world and ten times its like.'" And in the other narration: "You shall have what you wished for and tenfold the world." These two narrations are of one meaning, and each interprets the other; for the intended meaning of "aḍʿāf" (multiples) is "amthāl" (likes), since the chosen view among the people of language is that "al-ḍiʿf" means "al-mithl" (the like).

As for his saying ﷺ in the other [narration] in the Book: "God most high says: 'Would it please you that I give you the world and its like with it?'" And in the other narration: "Would you be pleased that you have the like of the kingdom of one of the kings of the world?" He says: "I am pleased, my Lord." He says: "You shall have that and its like and its like and its like and its like and its like." And when he said the fifth [time], he said: "I am pleased, my Lord." He says: "This is yours and ten times its like." These two narrations do not contradict the first two; for the intended meaning of the first of these two is that it is said to him first: "You shall have the world and its like," then it is increased until it completes ten times its like, as is clarified in the last narration. As for the last one, the intended meaning is that none of the kings of the world has a kingdom that extends to the entire earth; rather, he possesses a part of it. Then among them are those whose portion is great and among them are those whose portion is small. So this man is given the like of one of the kings of the world five times — and all of that is the measure of the entire world — then it is said to him: "You shall have ten times this." Thus the meaning of this narration returns to agreement with the preceding narrations. And to God belongs praise, and He knows best.

[187] His saying ﷺ: "The last of the people to enter Paradise is a man who walks at times and stumbles (yakbū) at times and the Fire scorches him (tasfaʿuhu) at times." As for "yakbū," its meaning is: he falls on his face. As for "tasfaʿuhu," it is with fatḥah on the tā', sukūn on the sīn (unpointed), and fatḥah on the fā'; its meaning is: it strikes his face, blackens it, and leaves a mark upon it.

His saying ﷺ: "Because he sees what he has no patience for (mā lā ṣabra lahu ʿalayhi)" — thus it is in the sources (uṣūl) in the first two instances. As for the third, it occurs in most sources as "mā lā ṣabra lahu ʿalayhā" and in some as "ʿalayhi" — and both are correct. The meaning of "ʿalayhā" is: a blessing (niʿmah) that he has no patience for — i.e., no endurance of it.

His saying, exalted is He: "O son of Adam, what would cut off your asking of Me (mā yuṣarrinīka minnī)" — it is with fatḥah on the yā' and sukūn on the ṣād (unpointed); its meaning is: what would sever your petition from me. The people of language said: "al-ṣarr" — with fatḥah on the ṣād and sukūn on the rā' — means cutting off. And it is narrated in other than Muslim: "mā yuṣrikka minnī." Ibrāhīm al-Ḥarbī said: That is the correct [reading], and he rejected the narration in Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim and elsewhere: "mā yuṣarrinīka minnī." But it is not as he said; rather, both are correct — for whenever the petitioner is cut off from the one petitioned, the one petitioned is cut off from him. And the meaning is: "What thing would please you and cut off the asking between me and you?" And God knows best.

His saying: "They said: 'At what do you laugh, O Messenger of God?' He said: 'At the laughter of the Lord of the worlds.'" We have already stated the meaning of laughter from God most high — and it is approval (riḍā), mercy (raḥmah), and the willing of good for whomsoever He wills of His servants' mercy. And God knows best.

[188] His saying: "On the authority of al-Nuʿmān ibn Abī ʿAyyāsh" — it is with shīn (pointed), and he is Abū ʿAyyāsh al-Zuraqī al-Anṣārī, the Companion, well-known; concerning his name there is a famous disagreement: it was said Zayd ibn al-Ṣāmit, and it was said Zayd ibn al-Nuʿmān, and it was said ʿUbayd, and it was said ʿAbd al-Raḥmān.

His saying ﷺ: "Then his two wives from the ḥūr al-ʿīn will enter upon him, and they will say: 'Praise be to God who has revived you for us and revived us for you.'" Thus it is confirmed in the narrations and the sources: "zawjatāhu" with tā' — the dual of "zawjah" with hā' — and it is a correct, well-known dialect; there are many verses of Arab poetry attesting it, and Ibn al-Sikkīt and groups of the people of language have mentioned it. And his saying ﷺ: "they will say (fa-taqūlāni)" is with tā' (the dotted one from above, i.e., tā' marbūṭah form). I have noted this despite its being apparent, because it is something in which some of those who lack [knowledge] err.

chapters.title_en: Section 180 — On the Narration of "A'dnā Ahl al-Jannah" (The Lowest Rank of the People of Paradise) and Related Linguistic Clarifications
chapters.arabic_text:
يميز فيقوله بالمثناة من تحت وذلك لحن لا شك فيه قال الله تعالى اذ همت

طائفتان منكم أن تفشلا وقال تعالى ووجد من دونهم امرأتين تذودان وقال الله

تعالى إن الله يمسك السماوات والارض أن تزولا وقال تعالى فيهما عينان

تجريان وأما قولهما الحمد لله الذي أحياك لنا وأحيانا لك فمعناه الذي خلقك

لنا وخلقنا لك وجمع بيننا في هذه الدار الدائمة السرور والله أعلم
# [189] قوله (حدثنا سعيد بن عمرو الأشعثي) هو بالثاء المثلثة بعد العين

المهملة منسوب إلى جده الأشعث وقد تقدم بيانه قوله (عن بن أبجر) هو بفتح

الهمزة وإسكان الباء الموحدة وفتح الجيم واسمه عبد الملك بن سعيد بن حيان

بن أبجر وهو تابعي سمع أبا الطفيل عامر بن واثلة وقد سماه مسلم في الطريق

الثاني فقال عبد الملك بن سعيد قوله (عن مطرف وبن أبجر عن الشعبي قال سمعت

المغيرة بن شعبة رواية إن شاء الله تعالى) وفي الرواية
# 
# الاخرى (سمعته على المنبر يرفعه إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم) وفي

الرواية الأخرى  (عن سفيان عن مطرف وبن أبجر عن الشعبي عن المغيرة قال سفيان

رفعه أحدهما أراه بن أبجر قال سأل موسى صلى الله عليه وسلم ربه سبحانه

وتعالى ما أدنى أهل الجنة منزلة) اعلم أنه قد تقدم في الفصول التي في أول

الكتاب أن قولهم رواية أو يرفعه أو ينميه أو يبلغ به كلها ألفاظ موضوعة عند

أهل العلم لإضافة الحديث إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لا خلاف في ذلك

بين أهل العلم فقوله رواية معناه قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وقد

بينه هنا في الرواية الثانية وأما قوله رواية إن شاء الله فلا يضره هذا

الشك والاستثناء لأنه جزم به في الروايات الباقية وأما قوله في الرواية

الأخيرة رفعه أحدهما فمعناه أن أحدهما رفعه وأضافه إلى رسول الله صلى الله

عليه وسلم والآخر وقفه على المغيرة فقال عن المغيرة قال سأل موسى صلى الله

عليه وسلم والضمير في أحدهما يعود على مطرف وبن أبجر شيخي سفيان فقال

أحدهما عن الشعبي عن المغيرة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال سأل موسى صلى

الله عليه وسلم وقال الآخر عن الشعبي عن المغيرة قال سأل موسى ثم إنه يحصل

من هذا أن الحديث روي مرفوعا وموقوفا وقد قدمنا في الفصول المتقدمة في أول

الكتاب أن المذهب الصحيح المختار الذي عليه الفقهاء وأصحاب الأصول

والمحققون من المحدثين أن الحديث إذا روي متصلا وروي مرسلا وروي مرفوعا

وروي موقوفا فالحكم للموصول والمرفوع لأنها زيادة ثقة وهي مقبولة عند

الجماهير من أصحاب فنون العلوم فلا يقدح اختلافهم ها هنا في رفع الحديث

ووقفه لاسيما وقد رواه الأكثرون مرفوعا والله أعلم وأما قول موسى صلى الله

عليه وسلم (ما أدنى أهل الجنة) كذا هو في الأصول ما أدنى
# 
# وهو صحيح ومعناه ما صفة أو ما علامة أدنى أهل الجنة وقد تقدم أن المغيرة

يقال بضم الميم وكسرها لغتان والضم أشهر والله أعلم قوله (كيف وقد نزل

الناس منازلهم وأخذوا أخذاتهم) هو  بفتح الهمزة والخاء قال القاضي هو ما

أخذوه من كرامة مولاهم وحصلوه أو يكون معناه قصدوا منازلهم قال وذكره ثعلب

بكسر الهمزة قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (فأعلاهم منزلة قال أولئك الذين أردت

غرست كرامتهم بيدي وختمت عليها فلم تر عين ولم تسمع أذن ولم يخطر على قلب

بشر قال ومصداقه في كتاب الله تعالى) أما أردت فبضم التاء ومعناه اخترت

واصطفيت وأما غرست كرامتهم بيدي إلى آخره فمعناه اصطفيتهم وتوليتهم فلا

يتطرق إلى كرامتهم تغيير وفي آخر الكلام حذف اختصر للعلم به تقديره ولم

يخطر على قلب بشر ما أكرمتهم به وأعددته لهم وقوله ومصداقه هو بكسر الميم

ومعناه دليله وما يصدقه والله أعلم قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (إن موسى صلى

الله عليه وسلم سأل الله تعالى عن أخس أهل الجنة) هكذا ضبطناه بالخاء

المعجمة وبعدها
# 
# السين المشددة وهكذا رواه جميع الرواة ومعناه أدناهم كما تقدم في الرواية

الأخرى
# [190] قوله (عن المعرور بن سويد) هو بالعين المهملة والراء المكررة
# [191] قوله (عن أبي الزبير أنه سمع جابر بن عبد الله رضي الله عنهما يسأل

عن الورود فقال نجئ نحن يوم القيامة عن كذا وكذا انظر أي ذلك فوق الناس قال

فتدعى الأمم بأوثانها إلى آخره) هكذا وقع هذا اللفظ في جميع الأصول من صحيح

مسلم واتفق المتقدمون والمتأخرون على أنه تصحيف وتغيير واختلاط في اللفظ

قال الحافظ عبد الحق
# 
# في كتابه الجمع بين الصحيحين هذا الذي وقع في كتاب مسلم تخليط من أحد

الناسخين أو كيف كان وقال القاضي عياض هذه صورة الحديث في جميع النسخ وفيه

تغيير كثير وتصحيف قال وصوابه نجئ يوم القيامة على كوم هكذا رواه بعض أهل

الحديث وفي كتاب بن أبي خيثمة من طريق كعب بن مالك يحشر الناس يوم القيامة

على تل وأمتي على تل وذكر الطبري في التفسير من حديث بن عمر فيرقى هو يعني

محمدا صلى الله عليه وسلم وأمته على كوم فوق الناس وذكر من حديث كعب بن

مالك يحشر  الناس يوم القيامة فأكون أنا وأمتي على تل قال القاضي فهذا كله
chapters.anchors:
- Root: م ي ز (m-y-z)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Separation, distinction, discrimination between things.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The act of discerning and setting apart one thing from another, often used for intellectual or linguistic distinction.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) for physical separation; metaphorical (majāz) for cognitive or grammatical discernment.
- Root: ر و ي (r-w-y)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To quench thirst (of water); to transmit or narrate (a report), as if giving drink to the listener's mind.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Technical term for hadith transmission, implying a chain of conveyance (isnād).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for watering; metaphorical for narrating, where the narrator "waters" the audience with knowledge.
- Root: ر ف ع (r-f-ʿ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To raise, elevate, lift up.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In hadith terminology, to attribute a statement or action to the Prophet (ﷺ) explicitly, elevating its chain.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for physical elevation; metaphorical for ascribing a report to a higher authority.
- Root: و ق ف (w-q-f)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To stand, halt, stop; to make something stand still.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In hadith science, to restrict a narration to a Companion (ṣaḥābī) without attributing it to the Prophet (ﷺ).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for standing; metaphorical for halting a chain at a specific narrator.
- Sībawayh Rule: Rule of Taqdīr (Ellipsis/Supposition) — When a phrase contains an omitted element (ḥadhf) for brevity, the understood completion (muqaddar) is supplied based on context, as in "lam yakhṭur ʿalā qalb bashar" where the object is implied.
chapters.translation:
I say: He distinguishes, saying it with the letter tā' (ت) with two dots beneath — and that is a solecism (laḥn) without doubt. Allah the Exalted said: {«إِذْ هَمَّتْ طَائِفَتَانِ مِنْكُمْ أَنْ تَفْشَلَا»} (When two parties among you were about to lose heart) [Āl ʿImrān 3:122], and He said: {«وَوَجَدَ مِنْ دُونِهِمُ امْرَأَتَيْنِ تَذُودَانِ»} (And he found, besides them, two women driving away [their flocks]) [Al-Qaṣaṣ 28:23], and Allah the Exalted said: {«إِنَّ اللَّهَ يُمْسِكُ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ أَنْ تَزُولَا»} (Indeed, Allah holds the heavens and the earth, lest they cease) [Fāṭir 35:41], and Allah the Exalted said: {«فِيهِمَا عَيْنَانِ تَجْرِيَانِ»} (In both of them are two springs flowing) [Al-Raḥmān 55:50].

As for their saying: "Praise be to Allah who gave you life for us and gave us life for you" — its meaning is: who created you for us and created us for you, and brought us together in this abode of everlasting joy. And Allah knows best.

[189] His saying (حدثنا سعيد بن عمرو الأشعثي) — it is with the letter thā' (ث) with three dots, after the unpointed ʿayn (ع), attributed to his grandfather al-Ashʿath; its explanation has already preceded. His saying (عن بن أبجر) — it is with the opening of the hamzah (أ), the stillness of the unpointed bā' (ب), and the opening of the jīm (ج); his name is ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Saʿīd ibn Ḥayyān ibn Abjar, and he is a Tābiʿī (follower) who heard from Abū al-Ṭufayl ʿĀmir ibn Wāthilah. Muslim named him in the second path (ṭarīq) and said: ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Saʿīd. His saying (عن مطرف وبن أبجر عن الشعبي قال سمعت المغيرة بن شعبة رواية إن شاء الله تعالى) — and in the other narration: (سمعته على المنبر يرفعه إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم). And in the other narration: (عن سفيان عن مطرف وبن أبجر عن الشعبي عن المغيرة قال سفيان رفعه أحدهما أراه بن أبجر قال سأل موسى صلى الله عليه وسلم ربه سبحانه وتعالى ما أدنى أهل الجنة منزلة).

Know that it has already preceded, in the chapters at the beginning of the book, that their saying "riwāyah" (narration), or "yarfaʿuhu" (he raises it), or "yanmīhi" (he attributes it), or "yuballighu bihi" (he conveys it) — all of these are technical terms (alfāẓ mawḍūʿah) among the people of knowledge for attributing the hadith to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). There is no disagreement among the people of knowledge regarding that. So his saying "riwāyah" means: he said, "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said." And he has clarified this here in the second narration. As for his saying "riwāyah in shā' Allāh" (narration, if Allah wills) — this doubt and exception does not harm it, because he affirmed it definitively in the remaining narrations. As for his saying in the last narration: "rafaʿahu aḥaduhumā" (one of the two raised it) — its meaning is that one of the two raised it and attributed it to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), while the other stopped it (waqafahu) at al-Mughīrah, saying: "al-Mughīrah said: Mūsā (ﷺ) asked." The pronoun in "aḥaduhumā" refers to Muṭarrif and Ibn Abjar, the two shaykhs of Sufyān. So one said: "al-Shaʿbī from al-Mughīrah from the Prophet (ﷺ), he said: Mūsā (ﷺ) asked." And the other said: "al-Shaʿbī from al-Mughīrah, he said: Mūsā asked." Then it results from this that the hadith was narrated both as marfūʿ (raised to the Prophet) and mawqūf (stopped at a Companion).

We have already presented in the preceding chapters at the beginning of the book that the correct and chosen doctrine (al-madhhab al-ṣaḥīḥ al-mukhtār), upon which are the jurists (fuqahā'), the scholars of uṣūl (principles), and the verifying scholars (muḥaqqiqūn) among the hadith specialists, is that when a hadith is narrated as connected (muttaṣil) and also as interrupted (mursal), and narrated as marfūʿ and also as mawqūf, then the ruling is for the connected and the raised (marfūʿ), because it is an addition by a trustworthy narrator (ziyādat thiqah), and that is accepted by the majority (jamāhīr) of the practitioners of the various sciences. So their disagreement here does not impugn the raising (rafʿ) or stopping (waqf) of the hadith — especially since the majority narrated it as marfūʿ. And Allah knows best.

As for the saying of Mūsā (ﷺ): "ما أدنى أهل الجنة" (What is the lowest of the people of Paradise) — thus it is in the sources (uṣūl): "mā adnā" — and it is correct. Its meaning is: what is the description (ṣifah) or what is the sign (ʿalāmah) of the lowest-ranked person among the people of Paradise. It has already preceded that "al-Mughīrah" is said with ḍammah of the mīm and kasrah of it — two dialects (lughatān), and the ḍammah is more famous. And Allah knows best.

His saying (كيف وقد نزل الناس منازلهم وأخذوا أخذاتهم) — it is with the opening of the hamzah and the khā' (خ). Al-Qāḍī said: It is what they took of the honor (karāmah) of their Lord and obtained it. Or its meaning could be: they headed toward their stations. He said: Thaʿlab mentioned it with kasrah of the hamzah.

His saying (ﷺ): (فأعلاهم منزلة قال أولئك الذين أردت غرست كرامتهم بيدي وختمت عليها فلم تر عين ولم تسمع أذن ولم يخطر على قلب بشر قال ومصداقه في كتاب الله تعالى) — As for "aradtu" (أردت), it is with ḍammah of the tā' (ت), and its meaning is: I chose (ikhtartu) and selected (iṣṭafaytu). As for "gharastu karāmatahum bi-yadayya" (I planted their honor with My own hands) to the end — its meaning is: I chose them and took direct charge of them (tawallaytuhum), so no change can reach their honor. And at the end of the speech there is an ellipsis (ḥadhf) abbreviated for the sake of what is known; its estimated completion (taqdīruhu) is: "nor has it occurred to the heart of any human what I have honored them with and prepared for them." And his saying "miṣdāquhu" (ومصداقه) — it is with kasrah of the mīm, and its meaning is: its proof (dalīluhu) and what confirms it (mā yuṣaddiquhu). And Allah knows best.

His saying (ﷺ): (إن موسى صلى الله عليه وسلم سأل الله تعالى عن أخس أهل الجنة) — Thus we have recorded it with the pointed khā' (خ) and after it the shaddah'd sīn (س). And thus all the narrators narrated it. Its meaning is: the lowest of them (adnāhum), as preceded in the other narration.

[190] His saying (عن المعرور بن سويد) — it is with the unpointed ʿayn (ع) and the doubled rā' (ر).

[191] His saying (عن أبي الزبير أنه سمع جابر بن عبد الله رضي الله عنهما يسأل عن الورود فقال نجئ نحن يوم القيامة عن كذا وكذا انظر أي ذلك فوق الناس قال فتدعى الأمم بأوثانها إلى آخره) — Thus this wording occurred in all the sources (uṣūl) of Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim. The earlier and later scholars (muttafaqūn) agreed that it is a corruption (taṣḥīf), alteration (taghyīr), and confusion (ikhtilāṭ) in the wording. Al-Ḥāfiẓ ʿAbd al-Ḥaqq said in his book "al-Jamʿ bayn al-Ṣaḥīḥayn": This which occurred in Muslim's book is a confusion from one of the copyists (nāsikhīn) or however it was. And Al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ said: This is the form of the hadith in all copies, and in it there is much alteration and corruption. He said: Its correct form is: "We will come on the Day of Resurrection upon a mound (kam)" — thus some of the hadith scholars narrated it. And in the book of Ibn Abī Khaythamah, via the path of Kaʿb ibn Mālik: "The people will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection upon a hill (tal), and my nation upon a hill." And al-Ṭabarī mentioned in the Tafsīr, from the hadith of Ibn ʿUmar: "Then he — meaning Muḥammad (ﷺ) — and his nation will ascend upon a mound (kam) above the people." And he mentioned from the hadith of Kaʿb ibn Mālik: "The people will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection, and I and my nation will be upon a hill." Al-Qāḍī said: So all of this...

chapters.title_en: Clarification of Altered Hadith Wording and the Meaning of "Vegetation of the Sesame" (Nabāt al-Simsim)
chapters.arabic_text:
يبين ما تغير من الحديث وأنه كان أظلم هذا الحرف على الراوي أو أمحي فعبر

عنه بكذا وكذا وفسره بقوله أي فوق الناس وكتب عليه انظر تنبيها فجمع النقلة

الكل ونسقوه على أنه من متن الحديث كما تراه هذا كلام القاضي وقد تابعه

عليه جماعة من المتأخرين والله أعلم قال القاضي ثم إن هذا الحديث جاء كله

من كلام جابر موقوفا عليه وليس هذا من شرط مسلم إذ ليس فيه ذكر النبي صلى

الله عليه وسلم وإنما ذكره مسلم وأدخله في المسند لأنه روي مسندا من غير

هذا الطريق فذكر بن أبي خيثمة عن بن جريج يرفعه بعد قوله يضحك قال سمعت

رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول فينطلق بهم وقد نبه على هذا مسلم بعد

هذا في حديث بن أبي شيبة وغيره في الشفاعة وإخراج من يخرج من النار وذكر

إسناده وسماعه من النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بمعنى بعض ما في هذا الحديث

والله أعلم وأما قوله (فيتجلى لهم يضحك فينطلق بهم ويتبعونه) فتقدم بيانهما

في أوائل الكتاب وكذلك تقدم قريبا معنى الضحك وأما التجلي فهو الظهور

وإزالة المانع من الرؤية ومعنى يتجلى يضحك أي يظهر وهو راض عنهم
# 
# قوله (ثم يطفأ نور المنافقين) روي بفتح الياء وضمها وهما صحيحان معناهما

ظاهر قوله (ثم ينجو المؤمنون) هكذا هو في كثير من الأصول وفي أكثرها

المؤمنين بالياء قوله (أول زمرة) أي جماعة قوله (حتى ينبتوا نبات الشئ في

السيل ويذهب حراقه ثم يسأل حتى تجعل له الدنيا وعشرة أمثالها) هكذا هو في

جميع الاصول ببلادنا نبات الشئ وكذا نقله القاضي عياض عن رواية الأكثرين

وعن بعض رواة مسلم نبات الدمن يعني بكسر الدال وإسكان الميم وهذه الرواية

هي الموجودة في الجمع بين الصحيحين لعبد الحق وكلاهما صحيح لكن الأول هو

المشهور الظاهر وهو بمعنى الروايات السابقة نبات الحبة في حميل السيل وأما

نبات الدمن فمعناها أيضا  كذلك فإن الدمن البعر والتقدير نبات ذي الدمن في

السيل أى كما ينبت الشئ الحاصل في البعر والغثاء الموجود في أطراف النهر

والمراد التشبيه به في السرعة والنضارة وقد أشار صاحب المطالع إلى تصحيح

هذه الرواية ولكن لم ينقح الكلام في تحقيقها بل قال عندي أنها رواية صحيحة

ومعناه سرعة نبات الدمن مع ضعف ما ينبت فيه وحسن منظره والله أعلم وأما

قوله (ويذهب حراقه) فهو بضم الحاء المهملة وتخفيف الراء والضمير في حراقه

يعود على المخرج من النار وعليه يعود الضمير في قوله
# 
# ثم يسأل ومعنى حراقه أثر النار والله أعلم قوله (حدثني يزيد الفقير) هو

يزيد بن صهيب الكوفي ثم المكي أبو عثمان قيل له الفقير لأنه أصيب في فقار

ظهره فكان يألم منه حتى ينحني له قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (إن قوما يخرجون

من النار يحترقون فيها إلا دارات وجوههم حتى يدخلون الجنة) هكذا هو في

الأصول حتى يدخلون بالنون وهو صحيح وهي لغة سبق بيانها وأما دارات الوجوه

فهي جمع دارة وهي ما يحيط بالوجه من جوانبه ومعناه أن النار لا تأكل دارة

الوجه لكونها محل السجود ووقع هنا إلا دارات الوجوه وسبق في الحديث الآخر

إلا مواضع السجود وسبق هناك الجمع بينهما والله أعلم قوله (كنت قد شغفني

رأي من رأي الخوارج) هكذا هو في الأصول والروايات شغفني بالغين المعجمة

وحكى القاضي عياض رحمه الله تعالى أنه روي بالعين المهملة وهما متقاربان

ومعناه لصق بشغاف قلبي وهو غلافه وأما رأي الخوارج فهو ما قدمناه مرات أنهم

يرون أن أصحاب الكبائر يخلدون في النار ولا يخرج منها من دخلها قوله

(فخرجنا في عصابة ذوي عدد نريد أن نحج ثم نخرج على الناس) معناه خرجنا من

بلادنا ونحن جماعة كثيرة
# 
# لنحج ثم نخرج على الناس مظهرين مذهب الخوارج وندعوا إليه ونحث عليه قوله

(غير أنه قد زعم أن قوما يخرجون من النار) زعم هنا بمعنى قال وقد تقدم في

أول الكتاب إيضاحها ونقل كلام الأئمة فيها  والله أعلم قوله (فيخرجون كأنهم

عيدان السماسم) هو بالسينين المهملتين الأولى مفتوحة والثانية مكسورة وهو

جمع سمسم وهو هذا السمسم المعروف الذي يستخرج منه الشيرج قال الإمام أبو

السعادات المبارك بن محمد بن عبد الكريم الجزري المعروف بابن الأثير رحمه

الله تعالى معناه والله أعلم أن السماسم جمع سمسم وعيدانه تراها إذا قلعت

وتركت في الشمس ليؤخذ حبها دقاقا سودا كأنها محترقة فشبه بها هؤلاء قال

وطالما طلبت هذه اللفظة وسألت عنها فلم أجد فيها شافيا قال وما أشبه أن

تكون اللفظة محرفة وربما كانت عيدان الساسم وهو خشب أسود كالآبنوس هذا كلام

أبي السعادات والساسم الذي ذكره هو بحذف الميم وفتح السين الثانية كذا قاله

الجوهري وغيره وأما القاضي عياض فقال لا يعرف معنى السماسم هنا قال ولعله

صوابه عيدان الساسم وهو أشبه وهو عود أسود وقيل هو الآبنوس وأما صاحب

المطالع فقال قال بعضهم السماسم كل نبت ضعيف كالسمسم والكزبرة وقال آخرون

لعله السأسم مهموز وهو الآبنوس شبههم به في سواده فهذا
# 
# مختصر ما قالوه فيه والمختار أنه السمسم كما قدمناه على ما بينه أبو
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ظ-ل-م (ẓ-l-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning of darkness, obscurity, or injustice; here denotes textual obscurity or corruption in transmission.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In Hadith criticism, refers to an error or ambiguity in a transmitted word requiring clarification.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense of "darkness" metaphorically applied to unclear or altered text.
- Root: ن-ب-ت (n-b-t)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To grow, sprout, or vegetate; refers to plant emergence from soil.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Used for growth, often metaphorically for rapid emergence or development.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for plant growth; metaphorical for swift appearance, as in the simile of vegetation in floodwater.
- Root: د-م-ن (d-m-n)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Dung, manure, or refuse; specifically animal droppings used as fertilizer.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Not a primary theological term; here denotes the medium in which vegetation grows.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for manure; metaphorical for the base substance from which something beautiful emerges.
- Sībawayh Rule: Taqdīr (Ellipsis Restoration) — The phrase "nabāt al-dimn" requires an implied genitive construction (i.e., "nabāt dhī al-dimn"), restoring the omitted qualifier for syntactic completeness.
chapters.translation:
I say: The Qāḍī (ʿIyāḍ) — may Allah have mercy on him — clarified what has been altered in the Hadith, noting that this letter had become obscure to the transmitter or was effaced, so he expressed it with such-and-such, and he interpreted it by his saying "i.e., above the people," and he wrote upon it "see the notice." Thus, the transmitters all gathered it and arranged it as being from the text of the Hadith, as you see it. This is the speech of the Qāḍī, and a group of later scholars have followed him upon it. And Allah knows best.

The Qāḍī said: Then this entire Hadith came as the speech of Jābir, stopped upon him (mawqūf), and this is not a condition of Muslim, since there is no mention of the Prophet ﷺ in it. Rather, Muslim mentioned it and included it in the Musnad because it was narrated as connected (musnad) via another path. Thus, Ibn Abī Khaythamah mentioned, from Ibn Jurayj, raising it (marfūʿan) after his saying "he laughs": "I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: 'Then he will set off with them.'" Muslim has alerted to this after this point in the Hadith of Ibn Abī Shaybah and others concerning the intercession and the extraction of those who come out of the Fire, and he mentioned its chain and his hearing it from the Prophet ﷺ with the meaning of part of what is in this Hadith. And Allah knows best.

As for his saying "Then He will manifest Himself to them, laughing, so He sets off with them, and they follow Him" — its explanation has already preceded at the beginning of the Book, and likewise the meaning of "laughing" (ḍaḥik) has recently preceded. As for "manifestation" (tajallī), it is the appearing and the removal of the barrier to vision. The meaning of "He manifests Himself laughing" is: He appears while being pleased with them.

His saying "Then the light of the hypocrites will be extinguished" — it is narrated with the fatḥa on the yāʾ (yutfāʾu) and with its ḍamma (yutfiʾu), and both are correct; their meaning is apparent.

His saying "Then the believers will be saved" — thus it is in many of the sources, and in most of them it is "the believers" (al-muʾminīn) with the yāʾ.

His saying "the first group" (awwal zumra) — i.e., a company.

His saying "until they grow like the growth of a thing in the torrent, and its black residue goes away, then he will be asked until he is given the world and ten times its like" — thus it is in all the sources in our lands: "the growth of a thing" (nabāt al-shayʾ). Likewise, al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ transmitted it from the narration of the majority. And from some of the narrators of Muslim: "the growth of dung" (nabāt al-dimn), meaning with kasra on the dāl and sukūn on the mīm. This narration is the one found in al-Jamʿ bayn al-Ṣaḥīḥayn of ʿAbd al-Ḥaqq. Both are correct, but the first is the well-known and apparent one, and it corresponds to the previous narrations: "the growth of the seed in the flood's debris" (nabāt al-ḥabba fī ḥamīl al-sayl). As for "the growth of dung," its meaning is likewise that, for "al-dimn" is dung, and the estimation (taqdīr) is "the growth of that which is in the dung" in the torrent, i.e., just as a thing grows that is found in dung and the scum present at the river's edges. The intent is the comparison to it in swiftness and freshness. The author of al-Maṭāliʿ has indicated the correction of this narration, but he did not refine the discussion in verifying it; rather, he said: "In my view, it is a sound narration, and its meaning is the swiftness of the growth of dung with the weakness of what grows in it and the beauty of its appearance." And Allah knows best.

As for his saying "and its black residue goes away" (wa-yadhhabu ḥurāquhu) — it is with ḍamma on the unpointed ḥāʾ and takhfīf of the rāʾ. The pronoun in "ḥurāquhu" refers back to the one brought out of the Fire, and upon him also returns the pronoun in his saying "then he will be asked." The meaning of "ḥurāq" is the trace of the Fire. And Allah knows best.

His saying "Yazīd al-Faqīr narrated to me" — he is Yazīd ibn Ṣuhayb al-Kūfī, then al-Makkī, Abū ʿUthmān. He was called "al-Faqīr" because he was afflicted in the vertebrae of his back (faqār ẓahrihī), so he would feel pain from it until he bent over for it.

His saying ﷺ "Indeed, a people will come out of the Fire, burned in it except the circles of their faces, until they enter Paradise" — thus it is in the sources: "until they enter" (ḥattā yadkhulūn) with the nūn, and it is correct, being a dialect whose explanation has preceded. As for "the circles of the faces" (dārāt al-wujūh), they are the plural of "dāra," which is what surrounds the face from its sides. Its meaning is that the Fire does not consume the circle of the face because it is the place of prostration. Here it occurs as "except the circles of the faces," and in the other Hadith it preceded as "except the places of prostration," and the reconciliation between them has preceded there. And Allah knows best.

His saying "I had been captivated (shughiftu) by an opinion of the opinions of the Khawārij" — thus it is in the sources and narrations: "shughiftu" with the pointed ghayn. Al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ — may Allah have mercy on him — reported that it is narrated with the unpointed ʿayn, and the two are close in meaning. Its meaning is: it clung to the pericardium (shighāf) of my heart, which is its covering. As for "the opinion of the Khawārij," it is what we have presented multiple times: that they hold that the committers of major sins abide eternally in the Fire, and none who enters it comes out of it.

His saying "So we set out in a band possessing number, intending to perform the pilgrimage, then to rise against the people" — its meaning is: we set out from our land while we were a large group, to perform the pilgrimage, then to rise against the people, manifesting the doctrine of the Khawārij, calling to it, and urging upon it.

His saying "except that he claimed (zaʿama) that a people will come out of the Fire" — "zaʿama" here carries the meaning of "he said," and its clarification has preceded at the beginning of the Book, along with the transmission of the scholars' speech concerning it. And Allah knows best.

His saying "so they come out as if they were the stalks of sesame (ʿīdān al-simsim)" — it is with two unpointed sīns, the first fatḥa and the second kasra, being the plural of "simsim," which is the well-known sesame from which sesame oil (shīraj) is extracted. Imam Abū al-Saʿādāt al-Mubārak ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Karīm al-Jazarī, known as Ibn al-Athīr — may Allah have mercy on him — said: Its meaning, and Allah knows best, is that "al-simāsim" is the plural of "simsim," and its stalks — you see them when uprooted and left in the sun so that their seeds are taken — as thin, black things as if burned. So these people were likened to them. He said: "I have long sought this word and asked about it, but I found no sufficient explanation for it." He said: "It is most likely that the word is corrupted, and perhaps it is 'the stalks of al-sāsam' (ʿīdān al-sāsam), which is a black wood like ebony." This is the speech of Abū al-Saʿādāt. And "al-sāsam" which he mentioned is with the elision of the mīm and fatḥa on the second sīn; thus al-Jawharī and others stated it. As for al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ, he said: "The meaning of 'al-simsim' here is not known." He said: "Perhaps its correct form is 'the stalks of al-sāsam,' and it is more fitting; it is a black wood, and it is said it is ebony." As for the author of al-Maṭāliʿ, he said: "Some said 'al-simsim' is every weak plant like sesame and coriander." And others said: "Perhaps it is 'al-sāsam' with hamza, which is ebony, likening them to it in its blackness." This is a summary of what they said concerning it. And the chosen view is that it is "sesame" (al-simsim) as we have presented, according to what Abū [al-Saʿādāt] clarified.

chapters.title_en: On the Felicities, the Variant Readings of Certain Words, and the Doctrine of Prophetic Infallibility (ʿIṣmah)
chapters.arabic_text:
السعادات والله أعلم واعلم أنه وقع في كثير من الأصول والكتب كأنها عيدان

السماسم بألف بعد الهاء والصحيح الموجود في معظم الأصول والكتب كأنهم بميم

بعد الهاء وللأول أيضا وجه وهو أن يكون الضمير في كأنها عائد على الصور أي

كأن صورهم عيدان السماسم والله أعلم قوله (فيخرجون كأنهم القراطيس)

القراطيس جمع قرطاس بكسر القاف وضمها لغتان وهو الصحيفة التي يكتب فيها

شبههم بالقراطيس لشدة بياضهم بعد اغتسالهم وزوال ما كان عليهم من السواد

والله أعلم قوله (فقلنا ويحكم أترون الشيخ يكذب على رسول الله صلى الله

عليه وسلم) يعني بالشيخ جابر بن عبد الله رضي الله عنه وهو استفهام إنكار

وجحد أي لا يظن به الكذب بلا شك قوله (فرجعنا فلا والله ماخرج منا غير رجل

واحد) معناه رجعنا من حجنا ولم نتعرض لرأي الخوارج بل كففنا عنه وتبنا منه

إلا رجلا  منا فإنه لم يوافقنا في الانكفاف عنه قوله (أو كما قال أبو نعيم)

المراد بأبي نعيم الفضل بن دكين بضم الدال المهملة المذكور في أول الإسناد

وهو شيخ شيخ مسلم وهذا الذي فعله أدب معروف من آداب الرواة وهو أنه ينبغي

للراوي إذا روى بالمعنى أن يقول عقب روايته أو كما قال احتياطا وخوفا من

تغيير حصل
# [192] قوله (حدثنا هداب بن خالد الأزدي حدثنا حماد بن سلمة عن أبي عمران

وثابت عن أنس رضي الله عنه) هذا الإسناد كله بصريون أما هداب فهو بفتح

الهاء وتشديد الدال المهملة وآخره باء موحدة ويقال فيه أيضا هدبة بضم الهاء

وإسكان الدال فأحدهما اسم والآخر لقب واختلف فيهما وقد قدمنا بيانه وأما

أبو عمران فهو الجوني واسمه عبد الملك بن حبيب وأما
# 
# ثابت فهو البناني
# [193] قوله في الإسناد (الجحدري) هو بفتح الجيم وبعدها حاء مهملة ساكنة

ثم دال مهملة مفتوحة منسوب إلى جد له اسمه جحدر وقد تقدم بيانه في أول

الكتاب قوله (محمد بن عبيد الغبري) هو بضم الغين المعجمة وفتح الباء

الموحدة منسوب إلى غبر جد القبيلة تقدم أيضا بيانه قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم

(يجمع الله الناس يوم القيامة فيهتمون لذلك وفي رواية فيلهمون معنى

اللفظتين متقارب فمعنى الأولى أنهم يعتنون بسؤال الشفاعة وزوال الكرب الذي

هم فيه ومعنى الثانية أن الله تعالى يلهمهم سؤال ذلك والإلهام أن يلقي الله

تعالى في النفس أمرا يحمل على فعل الشئ أو تركه والله أعلم قوله صلى الله

عليه وسلم في الناس أنهم يأتون آدم ونوحا وباقي الأنبياء صلوات الله وسلامه

عليهم فيطلبون شفاعتهم فيقولون لسنا هناكم ويذكرون خطاياهم إلى آخره اعلم

أن العلماء من أهل الفقه والأصول وغيرهم اختلفوا في جواز المعاصي على

الأنبياء صلوات الله وسلامه عليهم وقد لخص القاضي رحمه الله تعالى مقاصد

المسألة فقال لا خلاف أن الكفر عليهم بعد النبوة ليس بجائز بل هم معصومون

منه واختلفوا فيه قبل النبوة والصحيح أنه لا يجوز وأما المعاصي فلا خلاف

أنهم معصومون من كل كبيرة واختلف العلماء هل ذلك بطريق العقل أو الشرع فقال

الأستاذ أبو إسحاق ومن معه ذلك ممتنع من مقتضى دليل المعجزة وقال القاضي

أبو بكر ومن وافقه ذلك من طريق الإجماع وذهبت المعتزلة إلى أن ذلك من طريق

العقل وكذلك اتفقوا على أن كل ما كان طريقه الإبلاغ في القول فهم معصومون

فيه على كل حال وأما ما كان طريقه الإبلاغ في الفعل فذهب بعضهم إلى العصمة

فيه رأسا وأن السهو والنسيان لا يجوز عليهم فيه وتأولوا
# 
# أحاديث السهو في الصلاة وغيرها بما سنذكره في مواضعه وهذا مذهب الأستاذ

أبي المظفر الإسفرايني من أئمتنا الخراسانيين المتكلمين وغيره من المشايخ

المتصوفة وذهب معظم المحققين وجماهير العلماء إلى جواز ذلك ووقوعه منهم

وهذا هو الحق ثم لا بد من تنبيههم عليه وذكرهم إياه إما في الحين على قول

جمهور المتكلمين وإما قبل وفاتهم على قول بعضهم ليسنوا حكم ذلك ويبينوه قبل

انخرام مدتهم وليصح تبليغهم ما أنزل إليهم وكذلك لا خلاف أنهم معصومون من

الصغائر التي تزرى بفاعلها وتحط منزلته وتسقط مروأته واختلفوا في وقوع

غيرها من الصغائر منهم فذهب معظم الفقهاء والمحدثين والمتكلمين من السلف

والخلف إلى جواز وقوعها منهم وحجتهم ظواهر القرآن والأخبار وذهب جماعة من

أهل التحقيق والنظر من الفقهاء والمتكلمين من أئمتنا إلى عصمتهم من الصغائر

كعصمتهم من الكبائر وأن منصب النبوة يجل عن مواقعها وعن مخالفة الله تعالى

عمدا وتكلموا على الآيات والأحاديث الواردة في ذلك وتأولوها وأن ما ذكر

عنهم من ذلك إنما هو فيما كان منهم على تأويل أو سهو أو من إذن من الله

تعالى في أشياء أشفقوا من المؤاخذة بها وأشياء منهم قبل النبوة وهذا المذهب

هو الحق لما قدمناه ولأنه لو صح ذلك منهم لم يلزمنا الاقتداء بأفعالهم

وإقرارهم وكثير من أقوالهم ولا خلاف في الاقتداء بذلك وإنما اختلاف العلماء

هل ذلك على الوجوب أو على الندب أو الإباحة أو التفريق فيما كان من باب

القرب أو غيرها  قال القاضي وقد بسطنا القول في هذا الباب في كتابنا الشفاء
chapters.anchors:
- Root: س-ع-د (sa-ʿa-da)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Felicity, good fortune, prosperity; the state of being fortunate in both worldly and otherworldly affairs.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): True felicity (al-saʿādah) is the attainment of divine pleasure and proximity, contrasted with mere worldly happiness.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Used literally for enduring bliss; metaphorically for the ultimate success of the Hereafter.
- Sībawayh Rule: Rule of Pronominal Reference (Marjiʿ al-Ḍamīr) — The antecedent of a pronoun must be contextually determined; ambiguity is resolved by the nearest grammatically valid referent.

- Root: ع-ص-م (ʿa-ṣa-ma)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To protect, guard, defend; to hold back from error or sin.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Divine protection (ʿiṣmah) as a theological necessity for prophets, preventing them from committing sins or errors that would undermine their mission.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: physical protection; metaphorical: moral and spiritual immunity from transgression.
- Sībawayh Rule: Rule of Categorical Predication (Ḥaml al-Muṭlaq) — Distinguishing between universal negative claims (e.g., "no major sin") and particular affirmative claims (e.g., "some minor sins may occur").
chapters.translation:
I say: These are the felicities (al-saʿādāt), and God knows best. Know that in many manuscript copies and books, the phrase occurs as "like stalks of sesame" (ka-annahā ʿīdān al-simsim) with an alif after the hāʾ. However, the correct reading found in the majority of manuscripts and books is "as if they were" (ka-annahum) with a mīm after the hāʾ. The first reading also has a valid interpretation, namely that the pronoun in "as if they were" (ka-annahā) refers to the forms (al-ṣuwar), i.e., "as if their forms were stalks of sesame." And God knows best.

His saying (may God's peace and blessings be upon him): "They will emerge as if they were sheets of paper (al-qarāṭīs)." Al-qarāṭīs is the plural of qirṭās, with kasrah on the qāf and ḍammah on it as two variant readings; it is the sheet upon which one writes. They are likened to sheets of paper due to the intensity of their whiteness after their washing and the removal of the blackness that had been upon them. And God knows best.

His saying: "So we said, 'Woe to you! Do you see the Shaykh lying about the Messenger of God (may God's peace and blessings be upon him)?'" By "the Shaykh," he means Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh (may God be pleased with him). This is an interrogative of denial and rejection, i.e., it is not to be thought that he lies, without any doubt.

His saying: "So we returned, and by God, none of us left except one man." Its meaning: we returned from our pilgrimage and did not engage with the opinion of the Khawārij; rather, we refrained from it and repented of it, except for one man among us, for he did not agree with us in refraining from it.

His saying: "Or as Abū Nuʿaym said." By Abū Nuʿaym is meant al-Faḍl ibn Dukayn, with ḍammah on the unpointed dāl, mentioned at the beginning of the chain of transmission; he is the teacher of Muslim's teacher. This action he performed is a well-known etiquette among the etiquettes of hadith transmitters, namely that it is incumbent upon the transmitter, when narrating by meaning, to say after his narration "or as he said," as a precaution and out of fear of any alteration that may have occurred.

# [192] His saying: "Haddāb ibn Khālid al-Azdī narrated to us; Ḥammād ibn Salamah narrated to us, from Abū ʿImrān and Thābit, from Anas (may God be pleased with him)." This entire chain consists of Baṣrans. As for Haddāb, it is with fatḥah on the hāʾ and tashdīd on the unpointed dāl, and its final letter is an unpointed bāʾ. It is also said of him "Haddabah" with ḍammah on the hāʾ and sukūn on the dāl; one of the two is a name and the other a nickname, and there is disagreement concerning them, and we have already explained this. As for Abū ʿImrān, he is al-Jawnī, and his name is ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Ḥabīb. As for Thābit, he is al-Bunānī.

# [193] His saying in the chain: "al-Jaḥdarī" — it is with fatḥah on the jīm, followed by an unpointed ḥāʾ with sukūn, then an unpointed dāl with fatḥah, attributed to a grandfather of his named Jaḥdar. Its explanation has already preceded at the beginning of the book. His saying: "Muḥammad ibn ʿUbayd al-Ghubarī" — it is with ḍammah on the pointed ghayn and fatḥah on the unpointed bāʾ, attributed to Ghubar, the grandfather of the tribe. Its explanation has also already preceded.

His saying (may God's peace and blessings be upon him): "God will gather the people on the Day of Resurrection, and they will be concerned about that (fa-yahummūna li-dhālika), and in another narration, 'they will be inspired' (fa-yulhamūna)." The meaning of the two expressions is close. The meaning of the first is that they will be occupied with seeking intercession and the removal of the distress in which they find themselves. The meaning of the second is that God (Exalted is He) will inspire them to seek that. Inspiration (ilhām) is that God (Exalted is He) casts into the soul a matter that impels one to do a thing or to refrain from it. And God knows best.

His saying (may God's peace and blessings be upon him) concerning the people, that they will come to Adam, Noah, and the rest of the prophets (may God's peace and blessings be upon them all), seeking their intercession, and they will say, "We are not for this," and they will mention their sins, up to the end of the narration. Know that the scholars among the people of jurisprudence (fiqh), the people of principles (uṣūl), and others have differed concerning the permissibility of sins (maʿāṣī) upon the prophets (may God's peace and blessings be upon them). The Qāḍī (may God have mercy on him) has summarized the objectives of this question, saying: There is no disagreement that disbelief (kufr) upon them after prophethood is not permissible; rather, they are infallible (maʿṣūmūn) from it. They differed concerning it before prophethood, and the correct view is that it is not permissible. As for sins (maʿāṣī), there is no disagreement that they are infallible from every major sin (kabīrah). The scholars differed as to whether this is by way of reason (ʿaql) or by way of revelation (sharʿ). Al-Ustādh Abū Isḥāq and those with him said that this is impossible by virtue of the evidence of the miracle (muʿjizah). Al-Qāḍī Abū Bakr and those who agreed with him said that this is by way of consensus (ijmāʿ). The Muʿtazilah held that this is by way of reason. Likewise, they agreed that in everything whose mode is the conveyance of speech (tablīgh fī al-qawl), they are infallible in it in all circumstances. As for that whose mode is conveyance in action (tablīgh fī al-fiʿl), some held the view of infallibility in it absolutely, and that forgetfulness (sahw) and inadvertence (nisyān) are not permissible upon them in it, and they interpreted the hadiths of forgetfulness in prayer and other matters as we will mention in their proper places. This is the doctrine of al-Ustādh Abū al-Muẓaffar al-Isfarāyīnī, one of our Khurāsānī imams among the theologians (mutakallimūn), and others among the Sufi masters. The majority of the verifiers (muḥaqqiqūn) and the masses of scholars held the permissibility of that and its occurrence from them, and this is the truth. Then it is necessary that they be alerted to it and reminded of it — either immediately, according to the view of the majority of the theologians, or before their death, according to the view of some — so that they may establish the ruling of that matter and clarify it before the end of their term, and so that their conveyance of what was revealed to them may be sound.

Likewise, there is no disagreement that they are infallible from minor sins (ṣaghāʾir) that debase their perpetrator, lower his station, and destroy his moral integrity (murūʾah). They differed concerning the occurrence of other minor sins from them. The majority of jurists, hadith scholars, and theologians among the early generations (salaf) and later ones (khalaf) held the permissibility of their occurrence from them, and their proof is the apparent meanings (ẓawāhir) of the Qurʾān and the reports (akhbār). A group of the people of verification and reflection among the jurists and theologians of our imams held their infallibility from minor sins just as they are infallible from major sins, and that the station of prophethood is too exalted for the occurrence of such things and for deliberately disobeying God (Exalted is He). They discussed the verses and hadiths concerning that and interpreted them, and that what is mentioned of them concerning that is only what occurred from them by way of interpretation (taʾwīl), or forgetfulness (sahw), or from God's permission (idhn) in matters for which they feared being held accountable, and matters from them before prophethood. This doctrine is the truth, for what we have already presented, and because if that were sound from them, we would not be obligated to follow their actions, their approvals (iqrār), and many of their sayings. There is no disagreement concerning following them in that; rather, the scholars' disagreement is whether that is obligatory (wujūb), recommended (nadb), permissible (ibāḥah), or differentiated between what pertains to acts of devotion (qurb) and other matters. The Qāḍī said: We have expanded the discussion of this chapter in our book al-Shifāʾ.

chapters.title_en: Section 183 — On the Intercession of the Prophet (ﷺ), the Sins of the Prophets, and the Meaning of Khalīl
chapters.arabic_text:
وبلغنا فيه المبلغ الذي لا يوجد في غيره وتكلمنا على الظواهر في ذلك بما

فيه كفاية ولا يهولك أن نسب قوم هذا المذهب إلى الخوارج والمعتزلة وطوائف

من المبتدعة إذ منزعهم فيه منزع آخر من التكفير بالصغائر ونحن نتبرأ إلى

الله تعالى من هذا المذهب وانظر هذه الخطايا التي ذكرت للأنبياء من أكل آدم

عليه الصلاة والسلام من الشجرة ناسيا ومن دعوة نوح عليه السلام على قوم

كفار وقتل موسى صلى الله عليه وسلم لكافر لم يؤمر بقتله ومدافعة إبراهيم

صلى الله عليه وسلم الكفار بقوله
# 
# عرض به هو فيه من وجه صادق وهذه كلها في حق غيرهم ليست بذنوب لكنهم

أشفقوا منها إذ لم تكن عن أمر الله تعالى وعتب على بعضهم فيها لقدر منزلتهم

من معرفة الله تعالى هذا آخر كلام القاضي عياض رحمه الله تعالى والله أعلم

قوله (في آدم خلقك الله بيده ونفخ فيك من روحه) هو من باب إضافة التشريف

قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (لست هناكم) معناه لست أهلا لذلك قوله صلى الله

عليه وسلم (ولكن ائتوا نوحا أول رسول بعثه الله تعالى) قال الإمام أبو عبد

الله المازري قد ذكر المؤرخون أن إدريس جد نوح عليهما السلام فإن قام دليل

أن إدريس أرسل أيضا لم يصح قول النسابين أنه قبل نوح لإخبار النبي صلى الله

عليه وسلم عن آدم أن نوحا أول رسول بعث وإن لم يقم دليل جاز ما قالوه وصح

أن يحمل أن إدريس كان نبيا غير مرسل قال القاضي عياض وقد قيل إن إدريس هو

إلياس وأنه كان نبيا في بني إسرائيل كما جاء في بعض الأخبار مع يوشع بن نون

فإن كان هكذا سقط الاعتراض قال القاضي وبمثل هذا يسقط الاعتراض بآدم وشيث

ورسالتهما إلى من معهما وإن كانا رسولين فإن آدم إنما أرسل لبنيه ولم

يكونوا كفارا بل أمر بتعليمهم الإيمان وطاعة الله تعالى وكذلك خلفه شيث

بعده فيهم بخلاف رسالة نوح إلى كفار أهل الأرض قال القاضي وقد رأيت أبا

الحسن بن بطال ذهب إلى أن آدم ليس برسول ليسلم من هذا الاعتراض وحديث أبي

ذر الطويل ينص على أن آدم وإدريس رسولان هذا آخر كلام القاضي والله أعلم

قوله (ائتوا إبراهيم الذي اتخذه الله خليلا) قال القاضي عياض رحمه الله

تعالى أصل الخلة الاختصاص والاستصفاء وقيل
# 
# أصلها الانقطاع إلى من خاللت مأخوذ من الخلة وهي الحاجة فسمى ابراهيم صلى

الله عليه وسلم بذلك لأنه قصر حاجته على ربه سبحانه وتعالى وقيل الخلة صفاء

المودة التي توجب تخلل الأسرار وقيل معناها المحبة والإلطاف هذا كلام

القاضي وقال بن الأنباري الخليل معناه المحب الكامل المحبة والمحبوب الموفي

بحقيقة المحبة اللذان ليس في حبهما نقص ولا خلل قال الواحدي هذا القول هو

الاختيار لأن الله عز وجل خليل إبراهيم وإبراهيم خليل الله ولا يجوز أن

يقال الله تعالى خليل إبراهيم من الخلة التي هي الحاجة والله أعلم قوله صلى

الله عليه وسلم (إن كل واحد من الأنبياء صلوات الله وسلامه عليهم يقول لست

هناكم أو لست لها) قال القاضي عياض هذا يقولونه تواضعا واكبارا لما يسئلونه

قال وقد تكون إشارة من كل واحد منهم إلى أن هذه الشفاعة وهذا المقام ليس له

بل لغيره وكل واحد منهم يدل على الآخر حتى انتهى الأمر إلى صاحبه قال

ويحتمل أنهم علموا أن صاحبها محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم معينا وتكون إحالة كل

واحد منهم على الآخر على تدريج الشفاعة في ذلك إلى نبينا محمد صلى الله

عليه وسلم قال وفيه تقديم ذوي الأسنان والآباء على الأبناء في الأمور التي

لها بال قال وأما مبادرة النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لذلك واجابته لدعوتهم

فلتحققه صلى الله عليه وسلم أن هذه الكرامة والمقام له صلى الله عليه وسلم

خاصة هذا كلام القاضي والحكمة في أن الله تعالى ألهمهم سؤال آدم ومن بعده

صلوات الله وسلامه عليهم في الابتداء ولم يلهموا سؤال نبينا  محمد صلى الله

عليه وسلم هي والله أعلم إظهار فضيلة نبينا محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم فإنهم

لو سألوه ابتداء لكان يحتمل أن غيره يقدر على هذا ويحصله وأما إذا سألوا

غيره من رسل الله تعالى وأصفيائه فامتنعوا ثم سألوه فأجاب وحصل غرضهم فهو

النهاية في ارتفاع المنزلة وكمال القرب وعظيم الإدلال والأنس وفيه تفضيله

صلى الله عليه وسلم على جميع المخلوقين من الرسل والآدميين والملائكة فإن

هذا الأمر العظيم وهي الشفاعة العظمى لا يقدر على الإقدام عليه غيره صلى

الله عليه وسلم وعليهم أجمعين والله أعلم قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم في موسى

صلى الله عليه وسلم
# 
# (الذي كلمه الله تكليما) هذا بإجماع أهل السنة على ظاهره وأن الله تعالى

كلم موسى حقيقة كلاما سمعه بغير واسطة ولهذا أكد بالمصدر والكلام صفة ثابتة

لله تعالى لا يشبه كلام غيره قوله في عيسى (روح الله وكلمته) تقدم الكلام

في معناه في أوائل كتاب الإيمان قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (ائتوا محمدا صلى

الله عليه وسلم عبدا قد غفر الله له ما تقدم من ذنبه وما تأخر) هذا مما

اختلف العلماء في معناه قال القاضي قيل المتقدم ما كان قبل النبوة والمتأخر
chapters.anchors:
- Root: خ-ل-ل (kh-l-l)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning is "to penetrate, to interpose between," from which derives "intimacy that pierces the heart" and "need" (khillah).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological usage, khillah denotes exclusive, unmediated intimacy with God, signifying the highest degree of divine selection (iṣṭifāʾ).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) sense is "penetration" or "need"; metaphorical (majāz) sense is "perfect love" — the latter is the operative meaning for Ibrāhīm (ʿalayhi al-salām).
- Root: ش-ف-ع (sh-f-ʿ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: "To make even, to pair," hence "intercession" as joining one's plea to another's need.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Technical term for the Prophet's (ﷺ) unique mediatory role on the Day of Resurrection (al-shafāʿah al-ʿuẓmā).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: "to double" or "to pair"; metaphorical: the act of a noble intercessor pleading for a lesser party.
- Sībawayh Rule: Taʾkīd al-Maṣdar (Emphatic Cognate Accusative) — In {«كَلَّمَهُ تَكْلِيمًا»}, the verbal noun reinforces the verb, affirming the reality of divine speech without metaphor or negation.
chapters.translation:
And we have attained in it a level of thoroughness not found in any other work, and we have discoursed upon the apparent meanings (al-ẓawāhir) therein with what suffices. And let it not alarm you that some people attribute this school of thought to the Khawārij, the Muʿtazilah, and factions of the innovators (al-mubtadiʿah), for their point of departure in this matter is another path — namely, the declaring of unbelief (takfīr) over minor sins. And we dissociate ourselves unto Allah the Exalted from this school of thought. And consider these lapses (khaṭāyā) which have been mentioned regarding the prophets: the eating of Ādam (upon him peace and prayer) from the tree while forgetful; the supplication of Nūḥ (upon him peace) against his people who were disbelievers; the killing by Mūsā (upon him peace) of a disbeliever whom he was not commanded to kill; and the repelling by Ibrāhīm (upon him peace) of the disbelievers with his saying — wherein he was, in one respect, truthful. And all of these, in relation to others, are not sins; rather, they (the prophets) felt apprehension concerning them because they were not issued from the command of Allah the Exalted, and He reproached some of them therein, commensurate with their rank in knowledge of Allah the Exalted. This is the end of the discourse of Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ (may Allah have mercy on him). And Allah knows best.

His saying (upon him peace and prayer): "In Ādam, Allah created you with His Hand and breathed into you of His Spirit" — this is of the category of the genitive of honorification (iḍāfat al-tashrīf).

His saying (upon him peace and prayer): "I am not the one for that" — its meaning is: I am not worthy of that.

His saying (upon him peace and prayer): "But go to Nūḥ, the first messenger whom Allah sent" — Imām Abū ʿAbd Allāh al-Māzarī said: The historians have mentioned that Idrīs was the grandfather of Nūḥ (upon them both peace). If evidence is established that Idrīs was also sent (as a messenger), then the genealogists' claim that he was before Nūḥ is not sound, due to the Prophet's (upon him peace and prayer) informing about Ādam that Nūḥ was the first messenger sent. But if no evidence is established, then what they said is permissible, and it is sound to interpret that Idrīs was a prophet (nabī) not sent (as a messenger). Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ said: And it has been said that Idrīs is Ilyās, and that he was a prophet among the Children of Israel, as has come in some reports, along with Yūshaʿ ibn Nūn. If this is the case, the objection falls away.
