- Root: ر-ح-م (r-ḥ-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning of tenderness, compassion, and mercy; the womb (raḥim) as the seat of kinship-bond.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Raḥmah as divine mercy and prophetic compassion — an attribute of beneficence toward creation.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) for kinship-tie; metaphorical (majāz) for the Prophet's encompassing pity over his community.
- Sībawayh Rule: ʿAṭf al-Bayān (Appositional Clarification) — for parsing vocative constructions like "yā Fāṭimah" with optional tarkhīm (apocopation).
chapters.translation:
I say: The section on the supplication of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, for his community, and his weeping out of compassion for them.

His saying — "Yūnus ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā al-Ṣadafī narrated to me; Ibn Wahb narrated to us; he said: ʿAmr ibn al-Ḥārith informed me that Bakr ibn Sawādah narrated to him, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Jubayr, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ" — this entire chain consists of Baṣrans. We have already mentioned that in the name Yūnus there are six pronunciations: with ḍammah on the nūn, with fatḥah, and with kasrah, each with hamzah or without it. As for al-Ṣadafī, it is with fatḥah on the ṣād and the dāl, both unpointed, and with a fāʾ, being a relative adjective from al-Ṣadaf — with fatḥah on the ṣād and kasrah on the dāl — a well-known tribe. Abū Saʿīd ibn Yūnus said: I called upon them in al-Ṣadaf, and he was neither of their own lineage nor of their clients. Yūnus ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā died in the month of Rabīʿ al-Ākhir, in the year two hundred and sixty-four. His birth was in Dhū al-Ḥijjah, in the year one hundred and seventy. In this chain there is Muslim's narration from a shaykh who outlived him, for Muslim died in the year two hundred and sixty-one, as previously mentioned. As for Bakr ibn Sawādah, it is with fatḥah on the sīn and lightening of the wāw. And God knows best.

His saying — "from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, recited the saying of God the Exalted concerning Abraham, peace be upon him: {«Lord, indeed they have led astray many among mankind»} — the verse — and the saying of Jesus, peace be upon him: {«If You punish them, indeed they are Your servants»}" — thus it appears in the manuscripts: "and the saying of Jesus." Al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ said: Some scholars stated that his word "qāla" (he said) is a verbal noun, not a verb; one says "qāla qawlan" and "qīlan," as if he said: "and he recited the saying of Jesus." This is the speech of al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ.

His saying — "from the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, that he raised his hands and said: 'O God, my community, my community,' and wept. Then God, Mighty and Majestic, said: 'O Gabriel, go to Muhammad — and your Lord knows best — and ask him what makes him weep.' So Gabriel, peace be upon him, came to him and asked him, and the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, informed him of what he had said — and he knew best. Then God the Exalted said: 'O Gabriel, go to Muhammad and say: Indeed, We shall please you regarding your community and shall not grieve you.'"

This ḥadīth comprises various types of benefits. Among them: the demonstration of the perfection of the Prophet's, peace and blessings be upon him, compassion for his community, his care for their welfare, and his concern for their affairs. Among them: the recommendation (istiḥbāb) of raising the hands in supplication. Among them: the great glad tidings for this community — may God the Exalted increase it in honor — by what God the Exalted promised it in His saying: "We shall please you regarding your community and shall not grieve you." This is among the most hope-inspiring ḥadīths for this community, or the most hope-inspiring of them. Among them: the demonstration of the greatness of the Prophet's, peace and blessings be upon him, station before God the Exalted, and His immense gentleness toward him, peace and blessings be upon him. The wisdom in sending Gabriel to ask him, peace and blessings be upon him, is the manifestation of the Prophet's honor, peace and blessings be upon him, and that he occupies the highest station, so that he is sought to be pleased and honored with what satisfies him. And God knows best. This ḥadīth accords with the saying of God, Mighty and Majestic: {«And soon your Lord will give you, and you will be satisfied»}. As for His saying the Exalted: "and shall not grieve you," the author of al-Taḥrīr said: it is an emphasis of the meaning, i.e., "We shall not make you sorrowful," because satisfaction (irḍāʾ) may occur for some by pardoning them while the rest enter the Fire. So God the Exalted said: "We shall please you and shall not bring sorrow upon you, rather We shall save all." And God knows best.

The section on clarifying that one who dies upon disbelief is in the Fire, and that neither intercession reaches him nor does the kinship of the near ones benefit him.

His saying — "that a man said: 'O Messenger of God, where is my father?' He said: 'In the Fire.' When he turned away, he called him and said: 'Indeed, my father and your father are in the Fire.'" In this: that one who dies upon disbelief is in the Fire, and the kinship of the near ones does not benefit him. And in this: that one who dies in the interval period (fatrah) upon what the Arabs were upon — the worship of idols — is among the people of the Fire. This is not a punishment before the reaching of the call (daʿwah), for these people had been reached by the call of Abraham and other prophets, may God's prayers and peace be upon them. And his saying, peace and blessings be upon him, "Indeed, my father and your father are in the Fire" is from good companionship, to console by sharing in the calamity. The meaning of "qaffā" is: he turned his back, departing.

His saying, peace and blessings be upon him — "O Banī Kaʿb ibn Luʾayy" — the author of al-Maṭāliʿ said: Luʾayy is pronounced with hamzah and without it, and the hamzah is more frequent.

His saying, peace and blessings be upon him — "O Fāṭimah, save yourself" — thus it occurs in some manuscripts: "Fāṭimah," and in some — or most of them — "yā Fāṭim" with the elision of the hāʾ by way of tarkhīm (apocopation). On this basis, it is permissible to place ḍammah or fatḥah on the mīm, as is known in its parallels.

His saying, peace and blessings be upon him — "for indeed I do not possess for you anything from God" — its meaning: do not rely upon my kinship, for I am not able to repel any disliked thing that God the Exalted wills for you.

His saying, peace and blessings be upon him — "except that you have a tie of kinship which I shall water with its water" — we have recorded it with fatḥah on the second bāʾ and with kasrah, both being two well-known readings mentioned by groups of scholars. Al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ said: we narrated it with kasrah. He said: and I saw that al-Khaṭṭābī had it with fatḥah. The author of al-Maṭāliʿ said: we narrated it with kasrah on the bāʾ and fatḥah, from "balahu yabiluhu," and al-bilāl is water. The meaning of the ḥadīth: "I shall connect it" — he likened the severance of kinship to heat, and its connection to extinguishing heat with coolness. From this is the saying: "water your wombs (bulū arḥāmakum)," i.e., connect them.

His saying, peace and blessings be upon him — "O Fāṭimah daughter of Muḥammad, O Ṣafiyyah daughter of ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib, O ʿAbbās son of ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib" — it is permissible to put naṣb (accusative) on Fāṭimah, Ṣafiyyah, and ʿAbbās, and also ḍammah (nominative); the naṣb is more eloquent and more famous. As for "bint" and "ibn," they are naṣb only. And although this is apparent and well-known, there is no harm in drawing attention to it for one who does not memorize it. The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, singled out these individuals due to the intensity of their kinship.

His saying — "from Qabīṣah ibn al-Mukhāriq and Zuhayr ibn ʿAmr, may God be pleased with them both, who said: When {«And warn your nearest kindred»} was revealed, the Prophet of God, peace and blessings be upon him, went out to a rocky elevation of a mountain, climbed to its highest rock, then called out: 'O Banī ʿAbd Manāf, indeed I...'"

chapters.title_en: Section 190 — The Prophet's ﷺ Parable, the Abrogation of "And Warn Your Nearest Kinsmen," and the Intercession for Abū Ṭālib
chapters.arabic_text:
نذير إنما مثلي ومثلكم كمثل رجل رأى العدو فانطلق يربأ أهله فخشي أن يسبقوه

فجعل يهتف يا صباحاه) أما قوله أولا قال انطلق فمعناه قالا لان
# 
# المراد أن قبيصة وزهيرا قالا ولكن لما كانا متفقين وهما كالرجل الواحد

أفرد فعلهما ولو حذف لفظة قال كان الكلام واضحا منتظما ولكن لما حصل في

الكلام بعض الطول حسن إعادة قال للتأكيد ومثله في القرآن العزيز أيعدكم

أنكم إذا متم وكنتم ترابا وعظاما أنكم مخرجون فأعاد أنكم وله نظائر كثيرة

في القرآن العزيز والحديث وقد تقدم بيانه في مواضع من هذا الكتاب والله

أعلم وأما المخارق والد قبيصة فبضم الميم والخاء المعجمة وأما الرضمة فبفتح

الراء وإسكان الضاد المعجمة وبفتحها لغتان حكاهما صاحب المطالع وغيره

واقتصر صاحب العين والجوهري والهروي وغيرهم على الاسكان وبن فارس وبعضهم

على الفتح قالوا والرضمة واحدة الرضم والرضام وهي صخور عظام بعضها فوق بعض

وقيل هي دون الهضاب وقال صاحب العين الرضمة حجارة مجتمعة ليست بثابتة في

الأرض كأنها منثورة وأما يربأ فهو بفتح الياء وإسكان الراء وبعدها باء

موحدة ثم همزة على وزن يقرأ ومعناه يحفظهم ويتطلع لهم ويقال لفاعل ذلك ربئة

وهو العين والطليعة الذي ينظر للقوم لئلا يدهمهم العدو ولا يكون في الغالب

إلا على جبل أو شرف أو شئ مرتفع لينظر إلى بعد وأما يهتف فبفتح الياء وكسر

التاء ومعناه يصيح ويصرخ وقولهم ياصباحاه كلمة يعتادونها عند وقوع أمر عظيم

فيقولونها ليجتمعوا ويتأهبوا له والله أعلم قوله (عن بن عباس رضي الله عنه

قال لما نزلت هذه الآية وأنذر عشيرتك الأقربين ورهطك منهم المخلصين) هو

بفتح اللام فظاهر هذه العبارة أن قوله ورهطك منهم المخلصين كان قرآنا أنزل

ثم نسخت
# 
# تلاوته ولم تقع هذه الزيادة في روايات البخاري قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم

(أرأيتكم لو أخبرتكم أن خيلا بسفح هذا الجبل أكنتم مصدقي) أما سفح الجبل

فبفتح السين وهو أسفله وقيل عرضه وأما مصدقي فبتشديد الدال والياء قوله

(فنزلت هذه السورة  تبت يدا أبي لهب وقد تب كذا قرأ الأعمش إلى آخر السورة)

معناه أن الأعمش زاد لفظة قد بخلاف القراءة المشهورة وقوله إلى آخر السورة

يعني أتم القراءة إلى آخر السورة كما يقرؤها الناس وفي السورة لغتان الهمز

وتركه حكاهما بن قتيبة والمشهور بغير همز كسور البلد لارتفاعها ومن همزه

قال هي قطعة من القرآن كسؤر الطعام والشراب وهي البقية منه وفي أبي لهب

لغتان قرئ بهما فتح الهاء وإسكانها واسمه عبد العزى ومعنى تب خسر قال

القاضي عياض وقد استدل بهذه السورة على جواز تكنية الكافر وقد اختلف

العلماء في ذلك واختلفت الرواية عن مالك في جواز تكنية الكافر بالجواز

والكراهة وقال بعضهم إنما يجوز من ذلك ما كان على جهة التألف وإلا فلا إذ

في التكنية تعظيم وتكبير وأما تكنية الله تعالى لأبي لهب فليست من هذا ولا

حجة فيه إذا كان اسمه عبد العزى وهذه تسمية باطلة فلهذا كنى عنه وقيل لأنه

إنما كان يعرف بها وقيل إن أبا لهب لقب وليس بكنية وكنيته أبو عتبة وقيل

جاء ذكر أبي لهب
# 
# لمجانسة الكلام والله أعلم

| (باب شفاعة النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لابي طالب)
# (والتخفيف عنه بسببه)
# قوله (كان يحوطك) هو بفتح الياء وضم الحاء قال أهل اللغة يقال حاطه يحوطه

حوطا وحياطة إذا صانه وحفظه وذب عنه وتوفر على مصالحه قوله صلى الله عليه

وسلم (وجدته في غمرات من النار فأخرجته إلى ضحضاح) أما الضحضاح فهو بضادين

معجمتين مفتوحتين والضحضاح ما رق من الماء على وجه الأرض إلى نحو الكعبين

واستعير في النار وأما الغمرات فبفتح الغين والميم واحدتها غمرة بإسكان

الميم وهي المعظم من الشئ قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (ولولا أنا لكان في

الدرك الأسفل من النار) قال أهل اللغة في الدرك لغتان فصيحتان مشهورتان فتح

الراء وإسكانها وقرئ بهما في القراءات السبع قال الفراء هما لغتان جمعهما

أدراك وقال الزجاج اللغتان جميعا حكاهما أهل اللغة إلا أن الاختيار فتح

الراء لأنه أكثر في  الاستعمال وقال أبو حاتم جمع الدرك بالفتح أدراك كجمل

وأجمال وفرس وأفراس وجمع الدرك بالإسكان أدرك كفلس
# 
# وأفلس وأما معناه فقال جميع أهل اللغة والمعاني والغريب وجماهير المفسرين

الدرك الأسفل قعر جهنم وأقصى أسفلها قالوا ولجهنم أدراك فكل طبقة من

أطباقها تسمى دركا والله
# 
# أعلم قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (يوضع في أخمص قدميه) هو بفتح الهمزة وهو

المتجافي من الرجل عن الأرض قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (أهون أهل النار عذابا

من له نعلان وشراكان من نار يغلي منهما دماغه كما يغلي المرجل) أما الشراك

فبكسر الشين وهو أحد سيور النعل وهو الذي يكون على وجهها وعلى ظهر القدم

والغليان معروف وهو شدة اضطراب الماء ونحوه على النار لشدة اتقادها يقال

غلت القدر تغلي غليا وغليانا وأغليتها أنا وأما المرجل فبكسر الميم وفتح

الجيم وهو قدر معروف سواء كان من حديد أو نحاس أو حجارة أو خزف هذا هو
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ن ذ ر (nadhara)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To warn, to make known with fear; a warner (nadhīr) who alerts a people to impending danger.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological usage, a nadhīr is a prophet or messenger who warns of divine punishment—here, the Prophet ﷺ as the warner of his community.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) sense of physical warning; metaphorical (majāz) extension to the eschatological warning of Hellfire.
- Root: ر ب أ (raba'a)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To be on a lookout, to guard, to protect; the agent is a rabī'ah (scout) who ascends a height to watch for the enemy.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In prophetic discourse, the act of vigilant guardianship over one's people—spiritually, the Prophet's ﷺ role as protector of his ummah.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: physical surveillance from an elevated place; metaphorical: the Prophet's ﷺ proactive warning before calamity strikes.
- Root: ض ح ض ح (ḍaḥḍaḥa)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Shallow water reaching only to the ankles; a thin layer covering the ground.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In eschatological context, the minimal depth of Hellfire—a metaphor for the least severe punishment.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: shallow water; metaphorical (istiʿārah): the uppermost, least intense layer of Hellfire.
- Root: د ر ك (daraka)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To reach, to attain; a level or stage (darak) in a descending series.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The seven descending levels of Hellfire, each called a darak, contrasting with the ascending levels of Paradise (darajāt).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: a step or degree; metaphorical: the stratified depths of Jahannam.
- Sībawayh Rule: Rule of Redundancy for Emphasis (Takrār li-l-Tawkīd) — When a verb or pronoun is repeated in a sentence to reinforce clarity after a lengthy construction, as in the Qur'anic {«أَنَّكُمْ إِذَا مِتُّمْ وَكُنْتُمْ تُرَابًا وَعِظَامًا أَنَّكُمْ مُخْرَجُونَ»}, the repetition serves grammatical cohesion and rhetorical emphasis.
chapters.translation:
I say: The Prophet ﷺ said: "A warner (nadhīr). Indeed, my example and your example is like a man who saw the enemy, so he set out to guard his family, fearing that they would be overtaken. So he began to shout: 'O morning calamity!'"

As for his statement at the beginning: "he set out" (inṭalaqa), its meaning is that Qabīṣah and Zuhayr both said this. The intent is that Qabīṣah and Zuhayr both spoke, but since they were in agreement and were like a single man, the verb was rendered in the singular. Had the word "he said" (qāla) been omitted, the speech would have been clear and well-ordered. However, since the speech contained some length, repeating "he said" was deemed good for emphasis. A similar instance occurs in the Noble Qur'an: {«أَيَعِدُكُمْ أَنَّكُمْ إِذَا مِتُّمْ وَكُنْتُمْ تُرَابًا وَعِظَامًا أَنَّكُمْ مُخْرَجُونَ»} — "Does he promise you that when you have died and become dust and bones, that you will be brought forth?" — where "that you" (annakum) is repeated. This has many parallels in the Noble Qur'an and the Hadith, and its explanation has already preceded in several places of this book. And Allah knows best.

As for al-Makhāriq, the father of Qabīṣah, it is with a ḍammah on the mīm and a fatḥah on the khā' (al-mukhāriq). As for al-Raḍmah, it is with a fatḥah on the rā' and a sukūn on the ḍād, and with a fatḥah on it as well — two dialects, both narrated by the author of al-Maṭāliʿ and others. The author of al-ʿAyn, al-Jawharī, al-Harawī, and others restricted themselves to the sukūn, while Ibn Fāris and some others restricted themselves to the fatḥah. They said: al-raḍmah is the singular of riḍām and riḍāmah, which are great rocks piled one upon another. It was also said they are below hills (al-hiḍāb). The author of al-ʿAyn said: "al-raḍmah is stones gathered together, not firmly fixed in the earth, as if scattered."

As for "yarba'u" (he guards), it is with a fatḥah on the yā', a sukūn on the rā', followed by a bā' with a single point, then a hamzah, on the pattern of yaqra'u. Its meaning is: he protects them and watches out for them. The one who does this is called a rabī'ah — the eye and the scout who watches for the people lest the enemy descend upon them suddenly. This is generally only done from a mountain, a high place, or something elevated, so that he may see into the distance.

As for "yahitifu" (he shouts), it is with a fatḥah on the yā' and a kasrah on the tā'. Its meaning is: he calls out and cries loudly. Their saying "Yā ṣabāḥāh!" (O morning calamity!) is a phrase they customarily use when a great matter occurs; they say it so that people may gather and prepare themselves for it. And Allah knows best.

His statement (concerning Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with him): "He said: When this verse was revealed: {«وَأَنْذِرْ عَشِيرَتَكَ الْأَقْرَبِينَ»} — 'And warn your nearest kinsmen' — and 'and your clan from among them, the sincere ones' (wa-rahṭaka minhum al-mukhliṣīn) —" the lām is with a fatḥah. The apparent meaning of this expression is that the phrase "and your clan from among them, the sincere ones" was Qur'an that was revealed, then its recitation was abrogated (naskh al-tilāwah). This addition does not occur in the narrations of al-Bukhārī.

His statement ﷺ: "Do you see? If I told you that horsemen were at the base of this mountain, would you believe me?" — As for "safḥ" (base) of the mountain, it is with a fatḥah on the sīn, and it is its lowest part. It was also said: its breadth. As for "muṣaddiqī" (believing me), it is with a tashdīd on the dāl and the yā'.

His statement: "Then this sūrah was revealed: {«تَبَّتْ يَدَا أَبِي لَهَبٍ وَتَبَّ»} — 'May the hands of Abū Lahab be ruined, and ruined he is' — thus al-Aʿmash recited, to the end of the sūrah." Its meaning is that al-Aʿmash added the word "qad" (قَدْ), contrary to the well-known recitation. His statement "to the end of the sūrah" means he completed the recitation to the end of the sūrah, just as the people recite it.

In the word "al-sūrah" there are two dialects: with hamzah and without it, both narrated by Ibn Qutaybah. The well-known form is without hamzah, like "sūr al-balad" (the wall of the city), due to its height. Those who pronounce the hamzah say it is a portion (qiṭʿah) of the Qur'an, like the remnant (su'ār) of food and drink — i.e., the remainder of it.

In "Abī Lahab" there are two dialects, both recited: fatḥah on the hā' and its sukūn. His name was ʿAbd al-ʿUzzā. The meaning of "tabba" is "he perished" (khasira).

Al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ said: This sūrah has been used as evidence for the permissibility of giving a kunyah (teknonym) to a disbeliever. The scholars have differed on this matter, and the narration from Mālik differs regarding the permissibility of giving a kunyah to a disbeliever — between permissibility and disapproval. Some said: only that which is done for the purpose of drawing hearts (ta'alluf) is permissible; otherwise, it is not, for in the kunyah there is an element of honor and magnification. As for Allah's giving the kunyah of Abū Lahab to him, this is not of this category, nor is it an argument therein, for his name was ʿAbd al-ʿUzzā, and this is a false naming — therefore He referred to him by his kunyah. It was also said: because he was only known by it. And it was said: Abū Lahab is a nickname (laqab), not a kunyah, and his actual kunyah was Abū ʿUtbah. It was also said: the mention of Abū Lahab came for the sake of rhetorical harmony (mujānasah) of the speech. And Allah knows best.

---

(Chapter: The Intercession of the Prophet ﷺ for Abū Ṭālib, and the Lightening of His Punishment Because of Him)

His statement: "He used to protect you (yaḥūṭuka)" — it is with a fatḥah on the yā' and a ḍammah on the ḥā'. The linguists say: "ḥāṭahu yaḥūṭuhu ḥawṭan wa ḥiyāṭatan" — when he guards him, preserves him, defends him, and attends diligently to his interests.

His statement ﷺ: "I found him in the depths (ghamarāt) of the Fire, so I brought him out to a shallow surface (ḍaḥḍāḥ)." — As for al-ḍaḥḍāḥ, it is with two ḍāds, both with fatḥah. Al-ḍaḥḍāḥ is the shallow water on the surface of the earth, up to about the ankles. It is used metaphorically (mustaʿār) for the Fire. As for al-ghamarāt, it is with a fatḥah on the ghayn and the mīm; its singular is ghamrah, with a sukūn on the mīm, and it is the overwhelming majority of a thing.

His statement ﷺ: "Were it not for me, he would have been in the lowest depth (al-darak al-asfal) of the Fire." — The linguists say: in "al-darak" there are two eloquent, well-known dialects: fatḥah on the rā' and its sukūn, and both have been recited in the seven canonical readings. Al-Farrā' said: they are two dialects, and their plural is adrāk. Al-Zajjāj said: both dialects are narrated by the linguists, but the preferred choice is the fatḥah on the rā', because it is more frequent in usage. Abū Ḥātim said: the plural of al-darak (with fatḥah) is adrāk, like jamal and ajmāl, and faras and afrās; and the plural of al-dark (with sukūn) is adruk, like filas and aflus.

As for its meaning, all the linguists, the scholars of meanings and rare expressions, and the majority of the exegetes said: al-darak al-asfal is the bottom of Jahannam and its furthest depth. They said: Jahannam has adrāk (levels), and every layer of its layers is called a darak. And Allah knows best.

His statement ﷺ: "It is placed in the arch of his feet (akhmaṣ)" — it is with a fatḥah on the hamzah, and it is the part of the foot that is raised off the ground.

His statement ﷺ: "The one with the lightest punishment among the people of the Fire is a man who has two sandals and two straps (shirākān) of Fire, from which his brain boils as a cauldron (mirjal) boils." — As for al-shirāk, it is with a kasrah on the shīn, and it is one of the thongs of the sandal — the one that is on its surface and on the top of the foot. Boiling (al-ghalyān) is well-known: it is the intense agitation of water and the like over the fire due to its intense blazing. One says: "ghalat al-qidru taghlī ghalyan wa ghalayānan" (the pot boiled), and "aghlaytuhā" (I made it boil). As for al-mirjal, it is with a kasrah on the mīm and a fatḥah on the jīm, and it is a well-known cooking pot, whether made of iron, copper, stone, or earthenware. This is the case.

chapters.title_en: Section 191 — On the Disparity of Punishment for the Disbelievers, the Futility of Their Deeds, and Related Matters
chapters.arabic_text:
الأصح وقال صاحب المطالع وقيل هو القدر من النحاس يعني خاصة والأول أعرف

والميم فيه زائدة وفي هذا الحديث وما أشبهه تصريح بتفاوت عذاب أهل النار

كما أن نعيم أهل الجنة متفاوت والله أعلم

| (باب الدليل على أن من مات على الكفر لا ينفعه عمل)
# فيه حديث عائشة رضي الله عنها (قالت قلت يارسول الله بن جدعان كان في

الجاهلية يصل الرحم ويطعم المسكين فهل ذلك نافعه قال لا ينفعه إنه لم يقل

يوما رب اغفر لي خطيئتي يوم الدين
# 
# معنى هذا الحديث أن ما كان يفعله من الصلة والإطعام ووجوه المكارم لا

ينفعه في الآخرة لكونه كافرا وهو معنى قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم لم يقل رب

اغفر لي خطيئتي يوم الدين أي لم يكن مصدقا بالبعث ومن لم يصدق به كافر ولا

ينفعه عمل قال القاضي عياض رحمه الله تعالى وقد انعقد الإجماع على أن

الكفار لا تنفعهم أعمالهم ولا يثابون عليها بنعيم ولا تخفيف عذاب لكن بعضهم

أشد عذابا من بعض بحسب جرائمهم هذا آخر كلام القاضي  وذكر الإمام الحافظ

الفقيه أبو بكر البيهقي في كتابه البعث والنشور نحو هذا عن بعض أهل العلم

والنظر قال البيهقي وقد يجوز أن يكون حديث بن جدعان وما ورد من الآيات

والأخبار في بطلان خيرات الكافر إذا مات على الكفر ورد في أنه لا يكون لها

موقع التخلص من النار وإدخال الجنة ولكن يخفف عنه من عذابه الذي يستوجبه

على جنايات ارتكبها سوى الكفر بما فعل من الخيرات هذا كلام البيهقي قال

العلماء وكان بن جدعان كثير الإطعام وكان اتخذ للضيفان جفنة يرقى إليها

بسلم وكان من بني تميم بن مرة أقرباء عائشة رضي الله عنها وكان من رؤساء

قريش واسمه عبد الله وجدعان بضم الجيم وإسكان الدال المهملة وبالعين

المهملة وأما صلة الرحم فهي الإحسان إلى الأقارب وقد تقدم بيانها وأما

الجاهلية فما كان قبل النبوة سموا بذلك لكثرة جهالاتهم والله تعالى أعلم

| (باب موالاة المؤمنين ومقاطعة غيرهم والبراءة منهم)
# قوله (سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم جهارا غير سر يقول ألا إن آل

أبي يعني فلانا ليسوا لي بأولياء إنما وليي الله وصالح المؤمنين) هذه

الكناية بقوله يعني فلانا هي من بعض الرواة خشي أن يسميه فيترتب عليه مفسدة

وفتنة إما في حق نفسه وإما في حقه وحق غيره فكنى عنه
# 
# والغرض إنما هو قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم إنما وليي الله وصالح المؤمنين

ومعناه إنما وليي من كان صالحا وإن بعد نسبه مني وليس وليي من كان غير صالح

وان كان نسبه قريبا قال القاضي عياض رضي الله عنه قيل إن المكنى عنه ها هنا

هو الحكم بن أبي العاص والله أعلم وأما قوله جهارا فمعناه علانية لم يخفه

بل باح به وأظهره وأشاعه ففيه التبرؤ من المخالفين وموالاة الصالحين

والاعلان بذلك مالم يخف ترتب فتنة عليه والله أعلم

| (باب الدليل على دخول طوائف من المسلمين الجنة)
# (بغير حساب ولا عذاب)
# قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (يدخل من أمتي الجنة سبعون ألفا بغير حساب) فيه

عظم  ما أكرم الله سبحانه وتعالى به النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وأمته زادها

الله فضلا وشرفا وقد جاء في صحيح مسلم
# 
# سبعون ألفا مع كل واحد منهم سبعون ألفا قوله (عكاشة بن محصن) هو بضم

العين وتشديد الكاف وتخفيفها لغتان مشهورتان ذكرهما جماعات منهم ثعلب

والجوهري وآخرون قال الجوهري قال ثعلب هو مشدد وقد يخفف وقال صاحب المطالع

التشديد أكثر ولم يذكر القاضي عياض هنا غير التشديد وأما محصن فبكسر الميم

وفتح الصاد وأما قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم للرجل الثاني سبقك بها عكاشة فقال

القاضي عياض قيل إن الرجل الثاني لم يكن ممن يستحق تلك المنزلة ولا كان

بصفة أهلها بخلاف عكاشة وقيل بل كان منافقا فأجابه النبي صلى الله عليه

وسلم بكلام محتمل ولم ير صلى الله عليه وسلم التصريح له بأنك لست منهم لما

كان صلى الله عليه وسلم عليه من حسن العشرة وقيل قد يكون سبق عكاشة بوحي

أنه يجاب فيه ولم يحصل ذلك للآخر قلت وقد ذكر الخطيب البغدادي في كتابه في

الأسماء المبهمة أنه يقال إن هذا الرجل هو سعد بن عبادة رضي الله عنه فإن

صح هذا بطل قول من زعم أنه منافق والأظهر المختار هو القول الأخير والله

أعلم قوله (يرفع نمرة) النمرة كساء فيه خطوط بيض وسود وحمر كأنها أخذت من

جلد النمر لاشتراكهما في التلون وهي من مآزر العرب قوله (حدثني أبو يونس عن

أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه) واسم أبي يونس هذا سليم بن جبير بضم السين والجيم

المصري الدوسي مولى ابي هريرة رضي الله عنه قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (يدخل

الجنة من أمتي سبعون ألفا
# 
# زمرة واحدة منهم على صورة القمر) روي زمرة واحدة بالنصب والرفع والزمرة

الجماعة في تفرقة بعضها في إثر بعض قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (هم الذين لا

يكتوون ولا يسترقون وعلى ربهم يتوكلون) اختلف العلماء في معنى هذا الحديث

فقال الإمام أبو عبد الله المازري احتج بعض الناس بهذا الحديث على أن

التداوي مكروه ومعظم العلماء على خلاف ذلك واحتجوا بما وقع في أحاديث كثيرة
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ق-د-ر (q-d-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Measure, quantity, extent; the specific amount of a thing.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Divine decree and determination; the precise limit assigned to each thing by God.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense of measuring; metaphorically, the specific portion of copper (qadr min al-nuḥās) denotes a defined quantity, not an indefinite amount.
- Sībawayh Rule: Rule of Ziyādah (Augmentation) — The letter mīm in "mīm" (ميم) is deemed augmentative (zāʾidah) in the word under discussion, a recognized morphological feature where an extra letter does not alter the root meaning.
chapters.translation:
The most correct opinion is [the first one], and the author of al-Maṭāliʿ said: "It was also said that it is a specific measure of copper," meaning specifically [a defined quantity]. And the first [opinion] is more well-known.

And the mīm in it is augmentative. In this ḥadīth and what resembles it, there is an explicit declaration of the disparity in the punishment of the inhabitants of the Fire, just as the bliss of the inhabitants of Paradise is disparate. And God Most High knows best.

| (Chapter: The Evidence That Whoever Dies Upon Disbelief, His Deeds Do Not Benefit Him)

In it is the ḥadīth of ʿĀʾishah, may God be pleased with her, who said: "I said, 'O Messenger of God, Ibn Judʿān during the Jāhiliyyah used to maintain ties of kinship and feed the poor — will that benefit him?' He said: 'It will not benefit him, for he never said, "O Lord, forgive me my sin on the Day of Recompense."'"

The meaning of this ḥadīth is that what he used to do of maintaining ties, feeding [the poor], and other noble deeds does not benefit him in the Hereafter, because he was a disbeliever. And that is the meaning of his saying, may God's peace and blessings be upon him: "He never said, 'O Lord, forgive me my sin on the Day of Recompense'" — i.e., he was not a believer in the Resurrection. And whoever does not believe in it is a disbeliever, and no deed benefits him.

Al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ, may God Most High have mercy on him, said: "The consensus (ijmāʿ) has been established that the deeds of the disbelievers do not benefit them, nor are they rewarded for them with bliss, nor with a lightening of punishment. Rather, some of them are more severely punished than others, according to their crimes." This is the end of al-Qāḍī's statement.

And the Imām, the ḥāfiẓ, the jurist Abū Bakr al-Bayhaqī mentioned in his book al-Baʿth wa al-Nushūr something similar to this, transmitted from some of the people of knowledge and reflection. Al-Bayhaqī said: "It is possible that the ḥadīth of Ibn Judʿān, and what has come of the verses (āyāt) and reports (akhbār) concerning the nullification of the good deeds of the disbeliever when he dies upon disbelief, is [to be understood] as [meaning] that they have no effect in achieving deliverance from the Fire and entry into Paradise. However, [it is possible that] he is lightened [in punishment] from the chastisement he deserves for crimes he committed other than disbelief, by virtue of the good deeds he performed." This is the statement of al-Bayhaqī.

The scholars said: Ibn Judʿān was one who fed [people] abundantly. He had made for guests a large bowl (jafnah) that was climbed up to by a ladder. He was from the Banū Tamīm ibn Murrah, the relatives of ʿĀʾishah, may God be pleased with her. He was among the chiefs of Quraysh. His name was ʿAbd Allāh. "Judʿān" is with a ḍammah on the jīm, a sukūn on the dāl (unpointed), and with the unpointed ʿayn.

As for maintaining ties of kinship (ṣilat al-raḥim), it is beneficence toward relatives, and its explanation has already preceded. As for the Jāhiliyyah, it is what was before prophethood; they were called by that name due to the abundance of their ignorances (jahālāt). And God Most High knows best.

| (Chapter: Loyalty to the Believers, Severance from Others, and Disavowal of Them)

His saying — [the narrator] — "I heard the Messenger of God, may God's peace and blessings be upon him, openly (jihāran), not secretly, say: 'Indeed, the family of Abī — meaning so-and-so — are not my allies. My ally is only God and the righteous believers.'" This circumlocution (kināyah) in his saying "meaning so-and-so" is from some of the narrators, who feared that if he named him, some harm or tribulation (fitnah) would result — either regarding himself, or regarding him and others — so he used a circumlocution for him.

The purpose, however, is his saying, may God's peace and blessings be upon him: "My ally is only God and the righteous believers." Its meaning is: my ally is only whoever is righteous, even if his lineage from me is distant; and my ally is not whoever is not righteous, even if his lineage is near.

Al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ, may God be pleased with him, said: "It was said that the one referred to by circumlocution here is al-Ḥakam ibn Abī al-ʿĀṣ." And God knows best.

As for his saying "openly (jihāran)," its meaning is publicly, not concealing it; rather, he divulged it, manifested it, and spread it. In this is the disavowal (tabarruʾ) from the opponents and loyalty (muwālāh) to the righteous, and the public declaration of that, as long as no tribulation upon oneself is feared. And God knows best.

| (Chapter: The Evidence That Groups of Muslims Enter Paradise Without Reckoning and Without Punishment)

His saying, may God's peace and blessings be upon him: "Seventy thousand of my community will enter Paradise without reckoning" — in this is the greatness of what God, Glorified and Exalted is He, has honored the Prophet, may God's peace and blessings be upon him, and his community with — may God increase them in virtue and honor. And it has come in Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim: "Seventy thousand, with each one of them seventy thousand."

His saying: "ʿUkāshah ibn Miḥṣan" — it is with a ḍammah on the ʿayn, and a tashdīd on the kāf, and its lightening [without tashdīd] — two well-known pronunciations, mentioned by groups [of scholars], among them Thaʿlab, al-Jawharī, and others. Al-Jawharī said: "Thaʿlab said it is with tashdīd, and it may be lightened." The author of al-Maṭāliʿ said: "The tashdīd is more frequent." And al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ did not mention here other than the tashdīd. As for "Miḥṣan," it is with a kasrah on the mīm and a fatḥah on the ṣād.

As for his saying, may God's peace and blessings be upon him, to the second man: "ʿUkāshah has preceded you to it," al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ said: "It was said that the second man was not among those who deserved that station, nor was he of the description of its people, unlike ʿUkāshah. And it was said: rather, he was a hypocrite (munāfiq), so the Prophet, may God's peace and blessings be upon him, answered him with an ambiguous statement, and he did not see fit to declare plainly to him, 'You are not among them,' due to the excellence of companionship (ḥusn al-ʿishrah) that he, may God's peace and blessings be upon him, possessed. And it was said: perhaps ʿUkāshah's precedence was by revelation (waḥy) that he would be answered [with acceptance], and that was not attained for the other."

I say: Al-Khaṭīb al-Baghdādī mentioned in his book on ambiguous names (al-Asmāʾ al-Mubhamah) that it is said this man was Saʿd ibn ʿUbādah, may God be pleased with him. If this is authentic, then the claim of whoever alleged that he was a hypocrite is refuted. And the most apparent and chosen [opinion] is the last statement. And God knows best.

His saying: "raising a namirah" — the namirah is a garment (kisāʾ) in which there are white, black, and red stripes, as if taken from the skin of the leopard (nimr) due to their shared variegation. It is among the waist-wraps (maʾāzir) of the Arabs.

His saying: "Abū Yūnus narrated to me from Abū Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him" — the name of this Abū Yūnus is Sulaym ibn Jubayr, with a ḍammah on the sīn and the jīm, the Egyptian, al-Dawsī, the freed slave (mawlā) of Abū Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him.

His saying, may God's peace and blessings be upon him: "Seventy thousand of my community will enter Paradise as one group (zumrah wāḥidah), their faces upon the form of the moon" — it was narrated "zumrah wāḥidah" with naṣb (accusative) and rafʿ (nominative). And al-zumrah is a group, in a succession of some following after others.

His saying, may God's peace and blessings be upon him: "They are those who do not seek cauterization (lā yaktawūn), nor seek ruqyah (lā yastarqūn), and upon their Lord they rely (wa ʿalā Rabbihim yatawakkalūn)" — the scholars differed regarding the meaning of this ḥadīth. The Imām Abū ʿAbd Allāh al-Māzarī said: "Some people used this ḥadīth as evidence that seeking medical treatment is disliked (makrūh)." And the majority of scholars are contrary to that, and they adduced as evidence what has occurred in many ḥadīths...

chapters.title_en: Section 192 — On the Prophet's Mention of the Benefits of Medicines and Foods (Such as Black Seed and Qusṭ), His Own Treatment, ʿĀʾishah's Report of His Frequent Treatment, the Permissibility of Seeking Cure via His Ruqyah, and the Hadith of the Companions Taking Payment for Ruqyah — with a Detailed Discussion on True Tawakkul
chapters.arabic_text:
من ذكره صلى الله عليه وسلم لمنافع الأدوية والأطعمة كالحبة السوداء والقسط

والصبر وغير ذلك وبأنه صلى الله عليه وسلم تداوى وبإخبار عائشة رضي الله

عنها بكثرة تداويه وبما علم من الاستشفاء برقاه وبالحديث الذي فيه أن بعض

الصحابة أخذوا على الرقية أجرا فإذا ثبت هذا حمل ما في الحديث على قوم

يعتقدون أن الأدوية نافعة بطبعها ولا يفوضون الأمر إلى الله تعالى قال

القاضي عياض قد ذهب إلى هذا التأويل غير واحد ممن تكلم على الحديث ولا

يستقيم هذا التأويل وإنما أخبر صلى الله عليه وسلم أن هؤلاء لهم مزية

وفضيلة يدخلون الجنة بغير حساب وبان وجوههم تضئ إضاءة القمر ليلة البدر ولو

كان كما تأوله هؤلاء لما اختص هؤلاء بهذه الفضيلة لأن تلك هي عقيدة جميع

المؤمنين ومن اعتقد خلاف ذلك كفر وقد تكلم العلماء وأصحاب المعاني على هذا

فذهب أبو سليمان الخطابي وغيره إلى أن المراد من تركها توكلا على الله

تعالى ورضاء بقضائه وبلائه قال الخطابي وهذه من أرفع درجات المحققين

بالإيمان قال وإلى هذا ذهب جماعة سماهم قال القاضي وهذا ظاهر الحديث

ومقتضاه أنه لا فرق بين ما ذكر من الكي والرقى وسائر أنواع الطب وقال

الداودي المراد بالحديث الذي يفعلونه في الصحة فإنه يكره لمن ليست به علة

أن يتخذ التمائم ويستعمل الرقى وأما من يستعمل ذلك ممن
# 
# به مرض فهو جائز وذهب بعضهم إلى تخصيص الرقى والكي من بين أنواع الطب

لمعنى وأن الطب غير قادح في التوكل إذ تطبب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

والفضلاء من السلف وكل سبب مقطوع به كالأكل والشرب للغذاء والري لا يقدح في

التوكل عند المتكلمين في هذا الباب ولهذا لم ينف عنهم التطبب ولهذا لم

يجعلوا الاكتساب للقوت وعلى العيال قادحا في التوكل إذا لم يكن ثقته في

رزقه باكتسابه وكان مفوضا في ذلك كله إلى الله تعالى والكلام في الفرق بين

الطب والكي يطول وقد أباحهما النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وأثنى عليهما لكني

أذكر منه نكتة تكفي وهو أنه صلى الله عليه وسلم تطبب في نفسه وطبب غيره ولم

يكتو وكوى غيره ونهى في الصحيح أمته عن الكي وقال ما أحب أن أكتوي هذا آخر

كلام القاضي والله أعلم والظاهر من معنى الحديث ما اختاره الخطابي ومن

وافقه كما تقدم وحاصله أن هؤلاء كمل تفويضهم إلى الله عز وجل فلم يتسببوا

في دفع ما أوقعه بهم ولا شك في فضيلة هذه الحالة ورجحان صاحبها وأما تطبب

النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ففعله ليبين لنا الجواز والله أعلم قوله صلى الله

عليه وسلم وعلى ربهم يتوكلون اختلفت عبارات العلماء من السلف والخلف في

حقيقة التوكل فحكى الإمام أبو جعفر الطبري وغيره عن طائفة من السلف أنهم

قالوا لا يستحق اسم التوكل إلا من لم يخالط قلبه خوف غير الله تعالى من سبع

أو عدو حتى يترك السعي في طلب الرزق ثقة بضمان الله تعالى له رزقه واحتجوا

بما جاء في ذلك من الآثار وقالت طائفة حده الثقة بالله تعالى والايقان بأن

قضاءه نافذ واتباع سنة نبيه صلى الله عليه وسلم في السعي فيما لا بد منه من

المطعم والمشرب والتحرز من العدو كما فعله الأنبياء صلوات الله تعالى عليهم

أجمعين قال القاضي عياض وهذا المذهب هو اختيار الطبري وعامة الفقهاء والأول

مذهب بعض المتصوفة وأصحاب علم القلوب والإشارات وذهب المحققون منهم إلى نحو

مذهب الجمهور ولكن لا يصح عندهم اسم التوكل مع الالتفات والطمأنينة إلى

الأسباب بل فعل الأسباب سنة الله وحكمته والثقة بأنه لا يجلب نفعا ولا يدفع

ضرا والكل من الله تعالى وحده هذا كلام القاضي عياض قال الإمام الأستاذ أبو

القاسم القشيري رحمه الله تعالى اعلم أن التوكل محله القلب وأما الحركة

بالظاهر فلا تنافي التوكل بالقلب بعد ما تحقق العبد أن الثقة من قبل الله

تعالى فان تعسر شئ فبتقديره وإن تيسر فبتيسيره وقال سهل بن
# 
# عبد  الله التستري رضي الله عنه التوكل الاسترسال مع الله تعالى على ما

يريد وقال أبو عثمان الجبري التوكل الاكتفاء بالله تعالى مع الاعتماد عليه

وقيل التوكل أن يستوي الإكثار والتقلل والله أعلم قوله (حدثنا حاجب بن عمر

أبو خشينة) هو بضم الخاء وفتح الشين المعجمتين بعدهما مثناة من تحت ثم نون

ثم هاء وحاجب هذا هو أخو عيسى بن عمر النحوي الإمام المشهور قوله صلى الله

عليه وسلم (ليدخلن الجنة من أمتي سبعون ألفا متماسكون آخذ بعضهم بعضا لا

يدخل أولهم حتى يدخل آخرهم) هكذا هو في معظم الأصول متماسكون بالواو وآخذ

بالرفع ووقع في بعض الاصول متماسكين وآخذا بالياء والألف وكلاهما صحيح

ومعنى متماسكين ممسك بعضهم بيد بعض ويدخلون معترضين صفا واحدا بعضهم بجنب

بعض وهذا تصريح بعظم سعة باب الجنة نسأل الله الكريم رضاه والجنة لنا

ولأحبابنا ولسائر المسلمين قوله (أيكم رأى الكوكب الذي انقض البارحة) هو

بالقاف
# 
# والضاد المعجمة ومعناه سقط وأما البارحة فهي أقرب ليلة مضت قال أبو

العباس ثعلب يقال قبل الزوال رأيت الليلة وبعد الزوال رأيت البارحة وهكذا
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ك-ي (k-y)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Cauterization (al-kayy) — the act of branding with fire for medicinal purposes; from the core sense of "touching/burning a surface."
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological discourse, kayy is a physical means (sabab) whose efficacy is contingent upon divine decree; it is not inherently opposed to tawakkul.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) — actual cauterization; metaphorical (majāz) — any reliance on created means that displaces trust in Allah.
- Root: ر-ق-ي (r-q-y)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Ruqyah — a protective incantation or supplication recited over the sick; from "ascending" (ruqiyy), as the words ascend seeking divine aid.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): A licit spiritual remedy when free of shirk; its benefit is by Allah's permission, not intrinsic power.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — verbal recitation; metaphorical — any act of seeking cure through permissible means.
- Root: و-ك-ل (w-k-l)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Tawakkul — entrusting one's affair to another; from wakīl (trustee, guardian).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): True reliance (tawakkul) is the heart's firm confidence in Allah alone, while outwardly pursuing ordained means.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — delegation of one's matter; metaphorical — the believer's state of serene dependence on Allah's decree.
- Sībawayh Rule: Rule of ʿAṭf (Coordination) and Ḥāl (Circumstantial Clause) — In the phrase "متماسكون آخذ بعضهم ببعض" (holding one another, each grasping the other), the nominative forms indicate a circumstantial clause (ḥāl) describing the state of entry into Paradise, while the variant accusative forms (متماسكين وآخذا) function adverbially, both being syntactically valid per the canonical readings.
chapters.translation:
I say: Know that the Prophet ﷺ mentioned the benefits of medicines and foods — such as black seed (al-ḥabbah al-sawdāʾ), qusṭ (costus), al-ṣabr (aloes), and other similar remedies — and that he ﷺ himself sought medical treatment, and that ʿĀʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her, reported his frequent use of treatment, and that it is known that he sought cure through his own ruqyah (spiritual incantations), and by the hadith in which some of the Companions accepted payment for performing ruqyah. Now, once all this is established, the hadith (concerning those who enter Paradise without reckoning) is interpreted as referring to a people who believe that medicines are beneficial by their own nature and who do not delegate the matter entirely to Allah, the Exalted.

Al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ said: More than one scholar who commented on this hadith has adopted this interpretation. However, this interpretation is not sound. For the Prophet ﷺ informed us that these people possess a special merit and excellence — they enter Paradise without reckoning, and their faces shine with the radiance of the full moon on the night of the badr (full moon). Had the matter been as those scholars interpreted it, these people would not have been singled out for this excellence, because that very belief (that medicines are not efficacious by themselves but only by Allah's will) is the creed of all believers. Indeed, whoever believes otherwise commits unbelief (kufr).

The scholars and the masters of semantic analysis (aṣḥāb al-maʿānī) have spoken extensively on this matter. Abū Sulaymān al-Khaṭṭābī and others held that the intended meaning (of those who do not use such means) is one who abandons them out of tawakkul (reliance) upon Allah, the Exalted, and out of contentment with His decree and His trial (qaḍāʾihi wa-balāʾihi). Al-Khaṭṭābī said: "This is among the highest stations of those who are verifiers (muḥaqqiqīn) in faith." He said: "And a group of scholars, whom he named, adopted this view."

Al-Qāḍī said: This is the apparent meaning of the hadith, and its implication is that there is no distinction between what was mentioned of cauterization (kayy), ruqyah, and all other types of medicine. Al-Dāwūdī said: The hadith refers to what people do in a state of health — for it is disliked (makrūh) for one who has no ailment to wear amulets (tamāʾim) and to employ ruqyah. As for one who uses these due to illness, it is permissible.

Some scholars went further and specified ruqyah and cauterization from among the types of medicine, on the grounds that medicine does not detract from tawakkul, since the Messenger of Allah ﷺ himself sought medical treatment, as did the virtuous among the Salaf (predecessors). Every means that is definitively established — such as eating and drinking for nourishment and quenching thirst — does not detract from tawakkul according to those who speak on this subject. For this reason, the Prophet's seeking treatment was not negated from him, and for this reason, they did not consider earning a livelihood for one's dependents as detracting from tawakkul, so long as one's trust in one's provision is not placed in one's earning, and one delegates all of that to Allah, the Exalted.

The discussion on the distinction between medicine and cauterization is lengthy, and the Prophet ﷺ permitted both and praised both. However, I shall mention a subtle point (nukta) that suffices: he ﷺ sought medical treatment for himself and treated others, but he never cauterized himself, though he did cauterize others. In the Ṣaḥīḥ, he forbade his community from cauterization and said: "I do not love to be cauterized." This is the end of al-Qāḍī's statement. And Allah knows best.

The apparent meaning of the hadith is what al-Khaṭṭābī and those who agreed with him chose, as mentioned earlier. Its essence is that these people perfected their delegation (tafwīḍ) to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, such that they did not employ means to repel what He had brought upon them. There is no doubt about the excellence of this state and the superiority of its possessor. As for the Prophet's ﷺ seeking medical treatment, he did so to demonstrate to us the permissibility (jawāz) of such means. And Allah knows best.

His statement ﷺ: "And upon their Lord they rely" {«وَعَلَىٰ رَبِّهِمْ يَتَوَكَّلُونَ»} — The scholars, both early (Salaf) and later (Khalaf), have differed in their expressions concerning the reality of tawakkul. The Imām Abū Jaʿfar al-Ṭabarī and others reported from a group of the Salaf that they said: "The name of tawakkul is not deserved except by one whose heart is not mixed with fear of anything other than Allah, the Exalted — whether beast or enemy — to the point that he abandons striving in seeking provision, out of confidence in Allah's guarantee of his sustenance." They adduced the traditions (āthār) reported on this matter.

Another group said: Its definition is confidence (thiqah) in Allah, the Exalted, and certainty (īqān) that His decree is executed, along with following the Sunnah of His Prophet ﷺ in striving for what is indispensable — food, drink, and guarding against the enemy — just as the Prophets, may the blessings of Allah be upon them all, did.

Al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ said: This latter school is the choice of al-Ṭabarī and the generality of the jurists (fuqahāʾ). The first school is the view of some of the Sufis and the people of heart-knowledge (aṣḥāb ʿilm al-qulūb) and allusions (ishārāt). The verifiers (muḥaqqiqūn) among them inclined toward the view of the majority (jumhūr). However, according to them, the name of tawakkul is not valid with the heart's heedless attention (iltifāt) and complacency (ṭumaʾnīnah) toward means. Rather, employing means is the Sunnah of Allah and His wisdom, while the confidence is that means neither bring benefit nor repel harm — all is from Allah alone.

This is the statement of al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ.

The Imām, the teacher (al-Ustādh), Abū al-Qāsim al-Qushayrī, may Allah the Exalted have mercy on him, said: Know that the locus of tawakkul is the heart. As for outward movement (al-ḥarakah bi-al-ẓāhir), it does not contradict inward tawakkul, so long as the servant is certain that confidence (thiqah) comes from Allah, the Exalted. For if something is difficult, it is by His decree (taqdīr); and if it is easy, it is by His facilitation (taysīr).

Sahl ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Tustarī, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "Tawakkul is surrendering oneself (istirsāl) to Allah, the Exalted, in accordance with what He wills."

Abū ʿUthmān al-Jabarī said: "Tawakkul is being content with Allah, the Exalted, while relying upon Him."

And it was said: "Tawakkul is that abundance and scarcity become equal (in one's heart)." And Allah knows best.

His statement (regarding the narrator): "Ḥājib ibn ʿUmar Abū Khushaynah" — the khāʾ is vowelled with ḍammah (u) and the shīn with fatḥah (a), both being unpointed letters, followed by a tāʾ (with two dots below), then nūn, then hāʾ. This Ḥājib is the brother of ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar al-Naḥwī, the renowned grammarian.

His statement ﷺ: "Seventy thousand of my community will enter Paradise, holding one another, each grasping the other — the first of them will not enter until the last of them enters." Thus it appears in most manuscripts: "متماسكون" (with wāw) and "آخذ" (with rafʿ, nominative). In some manuscripts it appears as "متماسكين" and "آخذا" (with yāʾ and alif, accusative). Both are correct. The meaning of "holding one another" (mutamāsikīn) is that each holds the hand of the other, and they enter in a single row, side by side. This is an explicit statement of the vastness of the gate of Paradise. We ask Allah, the Generous, for His pleasure, and for Paradise for ourselves, our beloved ones, and all Muslims.

His statement: "Which of you saw the star that fell last night?" — it is with qāf and ḍād (unpointed), meaning "it fell" (saqaṭa). As for "al-bāriḥah" (last night), it refers to the most recent night that has passed. Abū al-ʿAbbās Thaʿlab said: "Before noon (zawāl), one says 'I saw it last night' (al-laylah); after noon, one says 'I saw it last night' (al-bāriḥah)." And so it is.

chapters.arabic_text:
قاله غير ثعلب قالوا وهي مشتقة من برح إذا زال وقد ثبت في صحيح مسلم في

كتاب الرؤيا أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان إذا صلى الصبح قال هل رأى أحد

منكم البارحة رؤيا قوله (أما إني لم أكن في صلاة ولكني لدغت) أراد أن ينفي

عن نفسه اتهام العبادة والسهر في الصلاة مع أنه لم يكن فيها وقوله لدغت هو

بالدال المهملة والغين المعجمة قال أهل اللغة يقال لدغته العقرب وذوات

السموم إذا أصابته بسمها وذلك بأن تأبره بشوكتها قوله (لا رقية إلا من عين

أو حمة) أما الحمة فهي بضم الحاء المهملة وتخفيف الميم وهي سم العقرب

وشبهها وقيل فوعة السم وهي حدته وحرارته والمراد أو ذي حمة كالعقرب وشبهها

أي لا رقية إلا من لدغ ذي حمة وأما العين فهي إصابة العائن غيره بعينه

والعين حق قال الخطابي ومعنى الحديث لا رقية  أشفى وأولى من رقية العين وذي

الحمة وقد رقى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وأمر بها فإذا كانت بالقرآن

وبأسماء الله تعالى فهي مباحة وإنما جاءت الكراهة منها لما كان بغير لسان

العرب فإنه ربما كان كفرا أو قولا يدخله الشرك قال ويحتمل أن يكون الذي كره

من الرقية ما كان منها على مذاهب الجاهلية في العوذ التي كانوا يتعاطونها

ويزعمون أنها تدفع عنهم الآفات ويعتقدون أنها من قبل الجن ومعونتهم هذا

كلام الخطابي رحمه الله تعالى والله أعلم قوله (بريدة بن حصيب) هو بضم

الحاء وفتح الصاد المهملتين قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (فرأيت النبي ومعه

الرهيط) هو بضم
# 
# الراء تصغير الرهط وهي الجماعة دون العشرة قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (فإذا

سواد عظيم فقيل لي هذه أمتك ومعهم سبعون ألفا يدخلون الجنة بغير حساب ولا

عذاب) معناه ومع هؤلاء سبعون ألفا من أمتك فكونهم من أمته صلى الله عليه

وسلم لا شك فيه وأما تقديره فيحتمل أن يكون معناه وسبعون ألفا من أمتك غير

هؤلاء وليسوا مع هؤلاء ويحتمل أن يكون معناه في جملتهم سبعون ألفا ويؤيد

هذا رواية البخاري في صحيحه هذه أمتك ويدخل الجنة من هؤلاء سبعون ألفا

والله أعلم قوله (فخاض الناس) هو بالخاء والضاد المعجمتين أي تكلموا

وتناظروا
# 
# وفي هذا إباحة المناظرة في العلم والمباحثة في نصوص الشرع على جهة

الاستفادة وإظهار الحق والله أعلم

| باب بيان كون هذه الامة نصف أهل الجنة
# قال مسلم (حدثنا هناد بن السري حدثنا أبو الأحوص عن أبي إسحاق عن عمرو بن

ميمون عن عبد الله) هذا الإسناد كله كوفيون واسم أبي الأحوص سلام بن سليم

وأبو إسحاق هو السبيعي واسمه عمرو بن عبد الله وعبد الله هو بن مسعود قوله

(كشعرة بيضاء في ثور أسود أو كشعرة سوداء في ثور أبيض) هذا شك من الراوي

قوله (حدثنا محمد بن عبد الله بن نمير حدثنا أبي حدثنا مالك وهو بن مغول عن

أبي إسحاق عن عمرو بن ميمون  عن عبد الله) هذا الإسناد كله كوفيون قوله (قال

لنا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أما ترضون أن تكونوا ربع أهل الجنة قال

فكبرنا ثم قال أما ترضون أن تكونوا ثلث أهل الجنة فكبرنا ثم قال إني لأرجو

أن تكونوا شطر أهل الجنة) أما تكبيرهم فلسرورهم بهذه البشارة العظيمة وأما

قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم ربع أهل الجنة ثم ثلث أهل الجنة ثم الشطر ولم يقل

أولا شطر أهل الجنة فلفائدة حسنة وفي أن ذلك أوقع في نفوسهم وأبلغ في

إكرامهم فإن إعطاء الإنسان مرة بعد أخرى دليل على الاعتناء به ودوام

ملاحظته وفيه فائدة أخرى هي تكريره البشارة مرة بعد أخرى وفيه أيضا حملهم

على تجديد شكر الله تعالى وتكبيره وحمده على كثرة نعمه والله أعلم ثم إنه

وقع في هذا الحديث شطر أهل الجنة وفي الرواية الأخرى نصف أهل الجنة وقد ثبت

في الحديث الآخر أن أهل الجنة عشرون ومائة صف هذه الأمة منها ثمانون صفا

فهذا دليل
# 
# على أنهم يكونون ثلثي أهل الجنة فيكون النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أخبر

أولا بحديث الشطر ثم تفضل الله سبحانه بالزيادة فأعلم بحديث الصفوف فأخبر

النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بعد ذلك ولهذا نظائر كثيرة في الحديث معروفة

كحديث الجماعة تفضل صلاة المنفرد بسبع وعشرين درجة وبخمس وعشرين درجة على

والله أعلم قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (لا يدخل الجنة إلا نفس مسلمة) هذا نص

بإجماع المسلمين قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (اللهم هل بلغت اللهم اشهد) معناه
#

chapters.anchors:
- Root: ب-ر-ح (barḥa)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: "To depart, to remove oneself from a place"; al-bāriḥah = "the night just past" (the night that has departed).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Temporal designation for the immediately preceding night; used in prophetic inquiry about visions.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense of "removal"; here a time-marker (ẓarf) for "last night," not metaphorical.
- Sībawayh Rule: ʿAṭf al-Bayān (Appositional Clarification) — "أو ذي حمة" clarifies the antecedent "حمة" as referring to the possessor of venom, not the venom itself.
chapters.translation:
I say: The one who said this other than Thaʿlab — they said: It (al-bāriḥah) is derived from "baraḥa" meaning "he departed." It has been established in Sahih Muslim, in the Book of Visions (Kitāb al-Ruʾyā), that the Prophet ﷺ, when he prayed the morning prayer, would say: "Has any one of you seen a vision last night?"

His saying (peace be upon him): "As for me, I was not in prayer, but I was stung" — he intended thereby to negate from himself any accusation of devotion and vigil in prayer, despite the fact that he was not engaged in it. His saying "ludightu" (I was stung) is with the unpointed dāl (د) and the pointed ghayn (غ). The people of language said: One says "ladaghat-hu al-ʿaqrab" (the scorpion stung him) and likewise creatures with venom, when it afflicts him with its poison — and that is by its piercing him with its stinger.

His saying (peace be upon him): "There is no ruqyah except from an evil eye or a ḥummah" — as for al-ḥummah, it is with a ḍammah on the unpointed ḥāʾ (ح) and a lightened mīm (م), and it is the venom of the scorpion and the like. It was also said: it is the potency of the poison, namely its sharpness and heat. The intended meaning is "or from one possessing ḥummah," such as the scorpion and its like — i.e., there is no ruqyah except from the sting of one possessing venom. As for al-ʿayn (the evil eye), it is the affliction by the envier (al-ʿāʾin) of another person with his eye. And the evil eye is real (ḥaqq).

Al-Khaṭṭābī said: The meaning of the hadith is: no ruqyah is more healing and more worthy than the ruqyah for the evil eye and the one possessing venom. The Prophet ﷺ himself performed ruqyah and commanded it. So when it is done with the Qurʾān and the names of Allah, it is permissible. The disapproval (karāhah) that came regarding it is only for what is in a language other than Arabic, for perhaps it is unbelief or a saying into which polytheism (shirk) enters. He said: And it is possible that what he disapproved of from ruqyah is that which was upon the ways of the pre-Islamic era (al-Jāhiliyyah) in the incantations (al-ʿuwadh) which they practiced, claiming that they repelled afflictions from them, and believing that they were from the jinn and their assistance. This is the speech of al-Khaṭṭābī — may Allah have mercy on him. And Allah knows best.

His saying (peace be upon him): "Buraydah ibn Ḥuṣayb" — it is with a ḍammah on the ḥāʾ and a fatḥah on the ṣād, both unpointed.

His saying (peace be upon him): "And I saw the Prophet, and with him was a small group (al-ruhayṭ)" — it is with a ḍammah on the rāʾ, the diminutive of "rahṭ" (a company), which is a group of fewer than ten.

His saying (peace be upon him): "Then suddenly there was a great black mass, and it was said to me: These are your nation, and with them are seventy thousand who will enter Paradise without reckoning and without punishment" — its meaning is: and with these are seventy thousand from your nation. That they are from his nation ﷺ is beyond doubt. As for its estimation (taqdīr), it is possible that the meaning is: "and seventy thousand from your nation other than these, not being among them." And it is possible that the meaning is: "within their total number are seventy thousand." This is supported by the narration of al-Bukhārī in his Sahih: "This is your nation, and there will enter Paradise from these seventy thousand." And Allah knows best.

His saying (peace be upon him): "Then the people plunged (fāḍa)" — it is with the pointed khāʾ (خ) and the pointed ḍād (ض), i.e., they spoke and debated with one another. And in this is the permissibility of scholarly debate (al-munāẓarah) and investigation into the texts of the Sacred Law, on the basis of seeking benefit and manifesting the truth. And Allah knows best.

| Chapter: The Explanation that This Nation is Half of the People of Paradise

Muslim said: (Narrated to us Hannād ibn al-Sarī; narrated to us Abū al-Aḥwaṣ, from Abū Isḥāq, from ʿAmr ibn Maymūn, from ʿAbd Allāh) — this entire chain is Kūfan. The name of Abū al-Aḥwaṣ is Sallām ibn Sulaym, and Abū Isḥāq is al-Sabīʿī, whose name is ʿAmr ibn ʿAbd Allāh, and ʿAbd Allāh is Ibn Masʿūd.

His saying (peace be upon him): "Like a white hair on a black bull, or like a black hair on a white bull" — this is a doubt from the narrator.

His saying: (Narrated to us Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Numayr; narrated to us my father; narrated to us Mālik — and he is Ibn Mighwal — from Abū Isḥāq, from ʿAmr ibn Maymūn, from ʿAbd Allāh) — this entire chain is Kūfan.

His saying (peace be upon him): "He said to us: Are you not pleased to be a quarter of the people of Paradise?" He said: "So we said 'Allāhu akbar.' Then he said: 'Are you not pleased to be a third of the people of Paradise?' So we said 'Allāhu akbar.' Then he said: 'Indeed I hope that you will be half of the people of Paradise.'"

As for their takbīr, it was out of joy at this great glad tiding. As for his saying ﷺ "a quarter of the people of Paradise," then "a third of the people of Paradise," then "half" — and he did not say from the outset "half of the people of Paradise" — it was for a fine benefit: that this is more impactful upon their souls and more profound in honoring them. For giving a person something time after time is evidence of care for him and continuous attention to him. And in it is another benefit: the repetition of the glad tiding time after time. And in it also is the urging of them to renew gratitude to Allah, His takbīr, and His praise for the abundance of His blessings. And Allah knows best.

Then it occurred in this hadith "half of the people of Paradise," and in the other narration "half of the people of Paradise." And it has been established in the other hadith that the people of Paradise are one hundred and twenty ranks, and this nation has eighty ranks from them. This is evidence that they will be two-thirds of the people of Paradise. So the Prophet ﷺ first informed of the hadith of "half," then Allah — glorified be He — bestowed the increase, and He made known through the hadith of the ranks, so the Prophet ﷺ informed of that afterward. And there are many known parallels to this in hadith, such as the hadith that congregational prayer excels the prayer of the individual by twenty-seven degrees, and by twenty-five degrees according to one of the interpretations therein — and its establishment will come in its place, if we reach it, Allah willing. And Allah knows best.

His saying (peace be upon him): "None shall enter Paradise except a Muslim soul" — this is an explicit text (naṣṣ) that whoever dies upon unbelief shall not enter Paradise at all. And this text is upon its generality by the consensus of the Muslims.

His saying (peace be upon him): "O Allah, have I conveyed? O Allah, bear witness" — its meaning is: conveyance (al-tablīgh) is obligatory upon me, and I have conveyed, so bear witness for me to it.

His saying: (Narrated to us ʿUthmān ibn Abī Shaybah al-ʿAbsī) — it is with the unpointed bāʾ (ب) and the unpointed sīn (س).

His saying (peace be upon him): "Here I am at Your service (labbayka) and at Your pleasure (saʿdayka), and all good is in Your hands" — the meaning of "in Your hands" is "with You" (ʿindaka). The explanation of "labbayka wa saʿdayka" has already preceded in the hadith of Muʿādh — may Allah be pleased with him.

His saying — glorified and exalted be He — to Adam ﷺ: "Bring forth the contingent of the Fire (baʿth al-nār)" — al-baʿth here is in the sense of "the one sent forth" (al-mabʿūth) directed to it. And its meaning is: distinguish the people of the Fire from others.

His saying (peace be upon him): "That is the time when the young child grows grey-haired, and every female carrying a burden..."
