حملها وترى الناس سكارى وما هم بسكارى ولكن عذاب الله شديد) معناه موافقة

الآية في قوله تعالى إن زلزلة الساعة شئ عظيم يوم ترونها تذهل كل مرضعة عما

أرضعت إلى آخرها وقوله تعالى فكيف تتقون إن كفرتم يوما يجعل الولدان شيبا

وقد اختلف العلماء في وقت وضع كل ذات حمل حملها وغيره من المذكور فقيل عند

زلزلة الساعة قبل خروجهم من الدنيا وقيل هو في القيامة فعلى الأول هو على

ظاهره وعلى الثاني يكون مجازا لأن القيامة ليس فيها حمل ولا ولادة وتقديره

ينتهي به الأهوال والشدائد إلى أنه لو تصورت الحوامل هناك لوضعن أحمالهن

كما تقول العرب أصابنا أمر يشيب منه الوليد يريدون شدته والله أعلم
# 
# قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (فإن من يأجوج ومأجوج ألف ومنكم رجل) هكذا هو في

الأصول والروايات ألف ورجل بالرفع فيهما وهو صحيح وتقديره أنه بالهاء التي

هي ضمير الشأن وحذفت الهاء وهو جائز معروف وأما ياجوج وماجوج فهما غير

مهموزين عند جمهور القراء وأهل اللغة وقرأ عاصم بالهمز فيهما وأصله من أجيج

النار وهو صوتها وشررها شبهوا به لكثرتهم وشدتهم واضطرابهم بعضهم في بعض

قال وهب بن منبه ومقاتل بن سليمان هم من ولد يافث بن نوح وقال الضحاك هم

جيل من الترك وقال كعب هم بادرة من ولد آدم من غير حواء قال وذلك أن آدم

صلى الله عليه وسلم احتلم فامتزجت نطفته بالتراب فخلق الله تعالى منها

يأجوج ومأجوج والله أعلم قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (كالرقمة في ذراع الحمار)

هي بفتح الراء وإسكان القاف قال أهل اللغة الرقمتان في الحمار هما الأثران

في باطن عضديه وقيل هي الدائرة في ذراعيه وقيل هي الهنة الناتئة في ذراع

الدابة من داخل والله  أعلم بالصواب
#

| (كتاب الطهارة)
# قال جمهور أهل اللغة يقال الوضوء والطهور بضم أولهما إذا أريد به الفعل

الذي هو المصدر ويقال الوضوء والطهور بفتح أولهما إذا أريد به الماء الذي

يتطهر به هكذا نقله بن الأنباري وجماعات من أهل اللغة وغيرهم عن أكثر أهل

اللغة وذهب الخليل والأصمعي وأبو حاتم السجستاني والأزهري وجماعة إلى أنه

بالفتح فيهما قال صاحب المطالع وحكي الضم فيهما جميعا وأصل الوضوء من

الوضاءة وهي الحسن والنظافة وسمي وضوء الصلاة وضوءا لأنه ينظف المتوضئ

ويحسنه وكذلك الطهارة أصلها النظافة والتنزه وأما الغسل فإذا أريد به الماء

فهو مضموم الغين وإذا أريد به المصدر فيجوز بضم الغين وفتحها لغتان

مشهورتان وبعضهم يقول إن كان مصدرا لغسلت فهو بالفتح كضربت ضربا وإن كان

بمعنى الاغتسال فهو بالضم كقولنا غسل الجمعة مسنون وكذلك الغسل من الجنابة

واجب وما أشبهه وأما ما ذكره بعض من صنف في لحن الفقهاء من أن قولهم غسل

الجنابة وغسل الجمعة وشبههما بالضم لحن فهو خطأ منه بل الذي قالوه صواب كما

ذكرناه وأما الغسل بكسر الغين فهو اسم لما يغسل به الرأس من خطمى وغيره

والله أعلم

| (باب فضل الوضوء)
# قال مسلم رحمه الله (حدثنا إسحاق بن منصور حدثنا حبان بن هلال حدثنا أبان

حدثنا يحيى أن زيدا حدثه أن أبا سلام حدثه عن أبي مالك الأشعري) هذا

الإسناد مما تكلم فيه الدارقطني وغيره فقالوا سقط فيه رجل بين أبي سلام

وأبي مالك والساقط عبد الرحمن بن غنم قالوا والدليل على
# 
# سقوطه أن معاوية بن سلام رواه عن أخيه زيد بن سلام عن جده أبي سلام عن

عبد الرحمن بن غنم عن أبي مالك الأشعري وهكذا أخرجه النسائي وبن ماجه

وغيرهما ويمكن أن يجاب لمسلم عن هذا بأن الظاهر من حال مسلم أنه علم سماع

أبي سلام لهذا الحديث من أبي مالك فيكون أبو سلام سمعه من أبي مالك وسمعه

أيضا من عبد الرحمن بن غنم عن أبي مالك فرواه مرة عنه ومرة عن  عبد الرحمن

وكيف كان فالمتن صحيح لا مطعن فيه والله أعلم وأما حبان بن هلال فبفتح

الحاء وبالباء الموحدة وأما أبان فقد تقدم ذكره في أول الكتاب وأنه يجوز

صرفه وترك صرفه وأن المختار صرفه وأما أبو سلام فاسمه ممطور الأعرج الحبشي

الدمشقي نسب إلى حي من حمير من اليمن لا إلى الحبشة وأما أبو مالك فاختلف

في اسمه فقيل الحارث وقيل عبيد وقيل كعب بن عاصم وقيل عمرو وهو معدود في

الشاميين قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (الطهور شطر الإيمان والحمد لله تملأ

الميزان وسبحان الله والحمد لله تملآن أو تملأ ما بين السماوات والأرض

والصلاة نور والصدقة برهان والصبر ضياء والقرآن حجة لك أو عليك كل الناس

يغدو فبائع نفسه فمعتقها أو موبقها) هذا حديث عظيم أصل من أصول الإسلام قد

اشتمل على مهمات من قواعد الإسلام فأما الطهور فالمراد به الفعل فهو مضموم

الطاء على المختار وقول الأكثرين ويجوز فتحها كما تقدم وأصل الشطر النصف

واختلف في معنى قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم الطهور شطر الإيمان فقيل معناه أن

الأجر فيه ينتهي تضعيفه إلى نصف أجر الإيمان وقيل معناه أن الإيمان يجب ما

قبله من الخطايا وكذلك الوضوء لأن الوضوء لا يصح إلا مع الإيمان فصار

لتوقفه على الإيمان في معنى الشطر وقيل المراد بالإيمان هنا الصلاة كما قال
chapters.anchors:
- Root: و ض أ (wa-ḍa-ʾa)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Root denotes cleanliness, brightness, and beauty; al-waḍāʾah is the quality of being fair and spotless.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In sacred law, waḍūʾ (ablution) is the ritual act of cleansing that precedes prayer, deriving its name from its effect of purifying and beautifying the believer.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): The literal sense is physical cleanliness; the religious sense is a transferred (majāz) application to ritual purification.
- Sībawayh Rule: Nominal vs. Verbal Derivation (al-maṣdar wa-ism al-ʿayn): The vocalic pattern distinguishes the verbal noun (action) from the noun of instrument/substance — a distinction governed by established Arabic usage, not by analogy to other verbs.
chapters.translation:
I say: His statement — the Exalted — {«...تُذهِلُ كُلَّ مُرضِعَةٍ عَمَّا أَرضَعَت...»} ("...will make every nursing mother forget what she nursed...") — its meaning accords with the verse in His saying — the Exalted — {«إِنَّ زَلزَلَةَ السَّاعَةِ شَيءٌ عَظيمٌ * يَومَ تَرَونَها تَذهَلُ كُلُّ مُرضِعَةٍ عَمّا أَرضَعَت»} ("Indeed, the earthquake of the Hour is a tremendous thing — on the Day you see it, every nursing mother will forget what she nursed...") — to its end; and His saying — the Exalted — {«فَكَيفَ تَتَّقونَ إِن كَفَرتُم يَومًا يَجعَلُ الوِلدانَ شيبًا»} ("Then how will you guard yourselves, if you disbelieve, against a Day that will make children gray-haired?").

The scholars have differed concerning the time of the casting down of every pregnant woman's burden and the other mentioned matters. It was said: it occurs at the earthquake of the Hour, before their departure from this world. And it was said: it occurs on the Day of Resurrection. On the first view, it is literal (ʿalā ẓāhirihi); on the second, it is metaphorical (majāz), because in the Hereafter there is neither pregnancy nor childbirth. Its estimated meaning is: the terrors and hardships will reach such a degree that if pregnant women were to be imagined there, they would cast down their burdens — just as the Arabs say, "We were struck by a matter that would make a newborn gray-haired," intending thereby its severity. And Allah knows best.

As for his saying — peace and blessings be upon him — (فَإِنَّ مِن يَأجوجَ وَمَأجوجَ أَلفًا وَمِنكُم رَجُلٌ) ("For from Gog and Magog there will be a thousand, and from you one man") — thus it appears in the codices and transmissions: "a thousand" (alfan) and "a man" (rajulun), both in the nominative (rafʿ). This is sound. Its estimated construction is with the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn), the pronoun being elided — and such elision is permissible and well-known. As for Yājūj and Mājūj, they are unhamzated according to the majority of the reciters and linguists. ʿĀṣim recited them with hamzah. Their origin is from the blazing of fire (ajīj al-nār) — its crackling sound and sparks — and they were likened to it due to their multitude, severity, and the turmoil of some of them among others.

Wahb ibn Munabbih and Muqātil ibn Sulaymān said: they are from the progeny of Yāfith (Japheth) son of Nūḥ. Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: they are a generation from the Turks. Kaʿb said: they are an outburst from the descendants of Ādam, not from Ḥawwāʾ. He said: that is because Ādam — peace be upon him — had a nocturnal emission, and his seminal fluid mixed with the earth, and Allah — the Exalted — created from it Gog and Magog. And Allah knows best.

As for his saying — peace and blessings be upon him — (كَالرَّقمَةِ في ذِراعِ الحِمارِ) ("like the weal on the forearm of the donkey") — it is with fatḥah on the rāʾ and sukūn on the qāf. The linguists said: the two weals (al-raqmatān) on the donkey are the two marks on the inner part of its upper forelegs. It was also said: they are the ring on its forearms. And it was said: they are the protruding lump on the inner side of the animal's forearm. And Allah knows best what is correct.

---

(Book of Purification — Kitāb al-Ṭahārah)

The majority of the linguists said: one says "al-wuḍūʾ" and "al-ṭuhūr" with ḍammah on their first letters when the act itself — which is the verbal noun (maṣdar) — is intended; and one says "al-waḍūʾ" and "al-ṭahūr" with fatḥah on their first letters when the water with which one performs purification is intended. Thus Ibn al-Anbārī and groups of linguists and others transmitted it from the majority of the linguists. Al-Khalīl, al-Aṣmaʿī, Abū Ḥātim al-Sijistānī, al-Azharī, and a group held that it is with fatḥah in both cases. The author of al-Maṭāliʿ said: ḍammah in both was also reported.

The origin of al-wuḍūʾ is from al-waḍāʾah, which is beauty and cleanliness. The ablution of prayer was named "wuḍūʾ" because it cleanses the one performing ablution and beautifies him. Likewise, al-ṭahārah — its origin is cleanliness and purity (al-naẓāfah wa-al-tanazzuh).

As for al-ghusl: if the water is intended, it is with ḍammah on the ghayn. If the verbal noun is intended, both ḍammah and fatḥah on the ghayn are permissible — two well-known dialects. Some say: if it is the verbal noun of "ghasaltu" (I washed), it is with fatḥah, like "ḍarabtu ḍarban" (I struck a striking); and if it means "al-ightisāl" (the act of bathing), it is with ḍammah, as we say "ghusl al-jumuʿah masnūn" (the Friday bath is Sunnah), and likewise "al-ghusl min al-janābah wājib" (the bath from major impurity is obligatory), and similar expressions.

As for what some of those who composed works on the solecisms of the jurists (laḥn al-fuqahāʾ) mentioned — that their saying "ghusl al-janābah" and "ghusl al-jumuʿah" and the like with ḍammah is an error — that is a mistake on his part. Rather, what they said is correct, as we have stated. As for "al-ghisl" with kasrah on the ghayn, it is the name for what is used to wash the head, such as marsh mallow and other things. And Allah knows best.

---

(Chapter on the Virtue of Ablution — Bāb Faḍl al-Wuḍūʾ)

Muslim — may Allah have mercy on him — said: (Ishāq ibn Manṣūr narrated to us: Ḥabbān ibn Hilāl narrated to us: Abān narrated to us: Yaḥyā narrated that Zayd narrated to him that Abū Salām narrated to him from Abū Mālik al-Ashʿarī). This chain of transmission (isnād) is among those concerning which al-Dāraquṭnī and others spoke, saying: a man has fallen out of it between Abū Salām and Abū Mālik — and the one omitted is ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ghanm. They said: the evidence for its omission is that Muʿāwiyah ibn Salām narrated it from his brother Zayd ibn Salām, from his grandfather Abū Salām, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ghanm, from Abū Mālik al-Ashʿarī — and thus al-Nasāʾī, Ibn Mājah, and others transmitted it.

It is possible to answer on behalf of Muslim by saying: the apparent state of Muslim's practice indicates that he knew that Abū Salām heard this ḥadīth directly from Abū Mālik. Thus Abū Salām heard it from Abū Mālik, and also heard it from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ghanm, from Abū Mālik — so he narrated it once directly from him, and once via ʿAbd al-Raḥmān. However the matter stands, the text (matn) is sound; there is no ground for criticism against it. And Allah knows best.

As for Ḥabbān ibn Hilāl — it is with fatḥah on the ḥāʾ and with an unpointed bāʾ. As for Abān, its mention has preceded at the beginning of the book — that its diptotic and triptotic declension are both permissible, and that the preferred choice is its triptotic declension. As for Abū Salām, his name is Mamṭūr al-Aʿraj al-Ḥabashī al-Dimashqī — he is attributed to a tribe of Ḥimyar from Yemen, not to Abyssinia. As for Abū Mālik, there is disagreement over his name: it was said al-Ḥārith; it was said ʿUbayd; it was said Kaʿb ibn ʿĀṣim; and it was said ʿAmr — and he is counted among the Syrians (al-Shāmiyyīn).

His saying — peace and blessings be upon him — (الطُّهورُ شَطرُ الإيمانِ وَالحَمدُ لِلَّهِ تَملَأُ الميزانَ وَسُبحانَ اللهِ وَالحَمدُ لِلَّهِ تَملَآنِ أَو تَملَأُ ما بَينَ السَّماواتِ وَالأَرضِ وَالصَّلاةُ نورٌ وَالصَّدَقَةُ بُرهانٌ وَالصَّبرُ ضِياءٌ وَالقُرآنُ حُجَّةٌ لَكَ أَو عَلَيكَ كُلُّ النّاسِ يَغدو فَبائِعٌ نَفسَهُ فَمُعتِقُها أَو موبِقُها) ("Purity is half of faith; 'Praise be to Allah' fills the Scale; 'Glory be to Allah' and 'Praise be to Allah' fill — or fill — what is between the heavens and the earth; prayer is light; charity is a proof; patience is illumination; and the Qurʾān is an argument for you or against you. Every person sets out in the morning, selling his soul — either freeing it or destroying it.") — this is a tremendous ḥadīth, a root from the roots of Islam, comprising important matters from the foundations of the religion.

As for al-ṭuhūr, what is intended by it is the act — thus it is with ḍammah on the ṭāʾ according to the preferred view and the position of the majority, and fatḥah is permissible as has preceded. The origin of al-shāṭr is the half. There is disagreement over the meaning of his saying — peace and blessings be upon him — "al-ṭuhūr shāṭr al-īmān" (purity is half of faith). It was said: its meaning is that its reward reaches, in its multiplication, half the reward of faith. And it was said: its meaning is that faith erases what preceded it of sins — and likewise ablution, because ablution is not valid except with faith; thus, due to its dependence on faith, it becomes in the sense of a half. And it was said: what is intended by "faith" here is prayer, as he said — as will be mentioned in what follows, Allah willing.

chapters.title_en: The Commentary on Sahih Muslim — Section 195: On the Obligation of Purification for Prayer and the Interpretation of the Prophet's Words on Faith, Praise, Prayer, Charity, Patience, and the Qur'an
chapters.arabic_text:
الله تعالى وما كان الله ليضيع ايمانكم والطهارة شرط في صحة الصلاة فصارت

كالشطر وليس يلزم في الشطر أن يكون نصفا حقيقيا وهذا القول أقرب الأقوال

ويحتمل أن يكون
# 
# معناه أن الإيمان تصديق بالقلب وانقياد بالظاهر وهما شطران للإيمان

والطهارة متضمنة الصلاة فهي انقياد في الظاهر والله أعلم وأما قوله صلى

الله عليه وسلم والحمد لله تملأ الميزان فمعناه عظم أجرها وأنه يملأ

الميزان وقد تظاهرت نصوص القرآن والسنة على وزن الأعمال وثقل الموازين

وخفتها وأما قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم وسبحان الله والحمد لله تملآن أو تملأ

ما بين السماوات والأرض فضبطناه بالتاء المثناة من فوق في  تملآن وتملأ وهو

صحيح فالأول ضمير مؤنثتين غائبتين والثاني ضمير هذه الجملة من الكلام وقال

صاحب التحرير يجوز تملآن بالتأنيث والتذكير جميعا فالتأنيث على ما ذكرناه

والتذكير على إرادة النوعين من الكلام أو الذكرين قال وأما تملأ فمذكر على

إرادة الذكر وأما معناه فيحتمل أن يقال لو قدر ثوابهما جسما لملأ ما بين

السماوات والأرض وسبب عظم فضلهما ما اشتملتا عليه من التنزيه لله تعالى

بقوله سبحان الله والتفويض والافتقار إلى الله تعالى بقوله الحمد لله والله

أعلم وأما قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم والصلاة نور فمعناه أنها تمنع من

المعاصي وتنهى عن الفحشاء والمنكر وتهدي إلى الصواب كما أن النور يستضاء به

وقيل معناه أنه يكون أجرها نورا لصاحبها يوم القيامة وقيل لأنها سبب لإشراق

أنوار المعارف وانشراح القلب ومكاشفات الحقائق لفراغ القلب فيها وإقباله

إلى الله تعالى بظاهره وباطنه وقد قال الله تعالى واستعينوا بالصبر والصلاة

وقيل معناه أنها تكون نورا ظاهرا على وجهه يوم القيامة ويكون في الدنيا

أيضا على وجهه البهاء بخلاف من لم يصل والله أعلم وأما قوله صلى الله عليه

وسلم والصدقة برهان فقال صاحب التحرير معناه يفزع إليها كما يفزع إلى

البراهين كأن العبد إذا سئل يوم القيامة عن مصرف ماله كانت صدقاته براهين

في جواب هذا السؤال فيقول تصدقت به قال ويجوز أن يوسم المتصدق بسيماء يعرف

بها فيكون برهانا له على حاله ولا يسأل عن مصرف ماله وقال غير صاحب التحرير

معناه الصدقة حجة على إيمان فاعلها فإن المنافق يمتنع منها لكونه لا

يعتقدها فمن تصدق استدل بصدقته على صدق إيمانه والله أعلم وأما قوله صلى

الله عليه وسلم والصبر ضياء فمعناه الصبر المحبوب في الشرع وهو الصبر على

طاعة الله تعالى والصبر عن معصيته والصبر أيضا على النائبات وأنواع المكاره

في الدنيا والمراد أن الصبر محمود ولا يزال صاحبه مستضيئا مهتديا مستمرا

على الصواب قال إبراهيم الخواص الصبر هو الثبات على
# 
# الكتاب والسنة وقال بن عطاء الصبر الوقوف مع البلاء  بحسن الأدب وقال

الأستاذ أبو علي الدقاق رحمه الله تعالى حقيقة الصبر أن لا يعترض على

المقدور فأما إظهار البلاء لا على وجه الشكوى فلا ينافي الصبر قال الله

تعالى في أيوب عليه السلام إنا وجدناه صابرا نعم العبد مع أنه قال إني مسني

الضر والله أعلم وأما قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم والقرآن حجة لك أو عليك

فمعناه ظاهر أي تنتفع به إن تلوته وعملت به وإلا فهو حجة عليك وأما قوله

صلى الله عليه وسلم كل الناس يغدو فبائع نفسه فمعتقها أو موبقها فمعناه كل

إنسان يسعى بنفسه فمنهم من يبيعها لله تعالى بطاعته فيعتقها من العذاب

ومنهم من يبيعها للشيطان والهوى باتباعهما فيوبقها أي يهلكها والله أعلم

| (باب وجوب الطهارة للصلاة)
# في إسناده (أبو كامل الجحدري) بفتح الجيم وإسكان الحاء المهملة وفتح

الدال واسمه الفضيل بن حسين منسوب إلى جد له اسمه جحدر وتقدم بيانه مرات

وفيه (أبو عوانة) واسمه الوضاح بن عبد الله قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (لا

يقبل الله صلاة بغير طهور ولا صدقة من غلول) هذا الحديث نص في وجوب الطهارة

للصلاة وقد أجمعت الأمة على أن الطهارة شرط في صحة الصلاة قال القاضي عياض

واختلفوا متى فرضت الطهارة للصلاة فذهب بن الجهم إلى أن الوضوء في أول

الإسلام كان سنة ثم نزل فرضه في آية التيمم قال الجمهور بل كان قبل ذلك

فرضا قال واختلفوا في أن الوضوء فرض على كل قائم إلى الصلاة أم على المحدث

خاصة
# 
# فذهب ذاهبون من السلف إلى أن الوضوء لكل صلاة فرض بدليل قوله تعالى إذا

قمتم إلى الصلاة الآية وذهب قوم إلى أن ذلك قد كان ثم نسخ وقيل الأمر به

لكل صلاة على الندب وقيل بل لم يشرع إلا لمن أحدث ولكن تجديده لكل صلاة

مستحب وعلى هذا أجمع أهل الفتوى بعد ذلك ولم يبق بينهم فيه خلاف ومعنى

الآية عندهم إذا كنتم محدثين هذا كلام القاضي رحمه الله تعالى واختلف

أصحابنا في الموجب  للوضوء على ثلاثة أوجه أحدها أنه يجب بالحدث وجوبا موسعا

والثاني لا يجب إلا عند القيام إلى الصلاة والثالث يجب بالأمرين وهو الراجح

عند أصحابنا وأجمعت الأمة على تحريم الصلاة بغير طهارة من ماء أو تراب ولا

فرق بين الصلاة المفروضة والنافلة وسجود التلاوة والشكر وصلاة الجنازة إلا
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ط-ه-ر (ṭ-h-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Purity, cleanliness; removal of filth (najāsah) and ritual impurity (ḥadath)
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Ritual purification (ṭahārah) as a prerequisite for the validity of worship, signifying both physical and spiritual cleanliness
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) — physical cleansing; metaphorical (majāz) — purity of the heart from sin
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clause (al-sharṭ wa al-jawāb) — The phrase "al-ṭahārah sharṭ fī ṣiḥḥat al-ṣalāh" establishes a necessary condition, where the predicate (sharṭ) is a nominal sentence indicating a permanent, essential requirement.
chapters.translation:
I say: Allah the Exalted said, {«وَمَا كَانَ اللَّهُ لِيُضِيعَ إِيمَانَكُمْ»} (And Allah would never cause your faith to be lost). Purification (al-ṭahārah) is a condition (sharṭ) for the validity of prayer (ṣalāh), and thus it becomes like a half (shāṭr) of it. It is not required, however, that a "half" be a literal half. This is the closest of the opinions (aqrab al-aqwāl).

And it is possible that its meaning is that faith (īmān) is affirmation by the heart (taṣdīq bi al-qalb) and submission by the outward limbs (inqiyād bi al-ẓāhir), and these two are the two halves of faith. Purification is subsumed within prayer, so it is an outward submission. And Allah knows best.

As for his saying, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, "And praise be to Allah (al-ḥamdu lillāh) fills the scale (al-mīzān)," its meaning is the greatness of its reward and that it fills the scale. The texts of the Qur'an and the Sunnah have concurred (taẓāharat) on the weighing of deeds (wazn al-aʿmāl), the heaviness of the scales (thiqal al-mawāzīn), and their lightness.

As for his saying, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, "And glory be to Allah (subḥān Allāh) and praise be to Allah (al-ḥamdu lillāh) fill (tamlā'āni) or fill (tamlā') what is between the heavens and the earth," we have recorded it with the tā' with two dots above (al-tā' al-muthannāh min fawq) in "tamlā'āni" and "tamlā'," and this is correct. The first is a pronoun referring to two feminine subjects (mu'annathatayn ghā'ibatayn), and the second is a pronoun referring to this entire statement (hādhihi al-jumlah min al-kalām).

The author of al-Taḥrīr said: It is permissible in "tamlā'āni" to use both the feminine (al-ta'nīth) and the masculine (al-tadhkīr). The feminine is as we have mentioned, and the masculine is on the intention of the two types of speech (al-nawʿayn min al-kalām) or the two mentions (al-dhikrayn). He said: As for "tamlā'," it is masculine on the intention of the mention (al-dhikr).

As for its meaning, it is possible to say: If their reward were estimated as a body, it would fill what is between the heavens and the earth. The cause of the greatness of their virtue is what they contain of the glorification of Allah the Exalted through his saying "Subḥān Allāh" and the delegation (al-tafwīḍ) and the neediness (al-iftiqār) toward Allah the Exalted through his saying "al-ḥamdu lillāh." And Allah knows best.

As for his saying, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, "And prayer is a light (nūr)," its meaning is that it prevents from sins (maʿāṣī) and forbids indecency (faḥshā') and wrongdoing (munkar), and guides to what is correct (ṣawāb), just as light is used for illumination. It is said its meaning is that its reward will be a light for its possessor on the Day of Resurrection. And it is said because it is a cause for the illumination of the lights of knowledge (anwār al-maʿārif), the expansion of the heart (inshirāḥ al-qalb), and the unveiling of realities (mukāshafāt al-ḥaqā'iq), due to the heart's emptiness in it and its turning toward Allah the Exalted with its outward and inward aspects. Allah the Exalted has said: {«وَاسْتَعِينُوا بِالصَّبْرِ وَالصَّلَاةِ»} (And seek help through patience and prayer).

And it is said its meaning is that it will be a visible light on his face on the Day of Resurrection, and in this world too, there will be radiance (bahā') on his face, unlike the one who does not pray. And Allah knows best.

As for his saying, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, "And charity (al-ṣadaqah) is a proof (burhān)," the author of al-Taḥrīr said: Its meaning is that one flees to it as one flees to proofs (barāhīn). It is as if the servant, when asked on the Day of Resurrection about the expenditure of his wealth, his charities would be proofs in answer to this question, and he would say, "I gave it in charity." He said: It is also permissible that the one who gives charity is marked with a distinguishing sign (sīmā') by which he is recognized, and thus it becomes a proof for him of his state, and he is not asked about the expenditure of his wealth.

Someone other than the author of al-Taḥrīr said: Its meaning is that charity is an argument (ḥujjah) for the faith of its doer, for the hypocrite (munāfiq) refrains from it because he does not believe in it. So whoever gives charity, his charity is used as evidence for the truthfulness of his faith. And Allah knows best.

As for his saying, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, "And patience (al-ṣabr) is a radiance (ḍiyā')," its meaning is the patience that is beloved in the Sacred Law (al-ṣabr al-maḥbūb fī al-sharʿ), which is patience upon obedience to Allah the Exalted, patience in refraining from His disobedience, and patience also upon calamities (nā'ibāt) and various kinds of hardships (makārih) in this world. The intent is that patience is praiseworthy, and its possessor remains illuminated (mustaḍī'an), guided (muhtadiyan), and steadfast upon what is correct.

Ibrāhīm al-Khawwāṣ said: Patience is steadfastness upon the Book and the Sunnah. Ibn ʿAṭā' said: Patience is standing with affliction (balā') with good manners (ḥusn al-adab). The master Abū ʿAlī al-Daqqāq, may Allah the Exalted have mercy on him, said: The reality of patience (ḥaqīqat al-ṣabr) is not to object to what is decreed (al-maqdūr). As for displaying affliction (iẓhār al-balā') not in the manner of complaint (shakwā), this does not contradict patience. Allah the Exalted said concerning Job (Ayyūb), peace be upon him: {«إِنَّا وَجَدْنَاهُ صَابِرًا ۚ نِعْمَ الْعَبْدُ»} (Indeed, We found him patient, an excellent servant), even though he said: {«إِنِّي مَسَّنِيَ الضُّرُّ»} (Indeed, adversity has touched me). And Allah knows best.

As for his saying, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, "And the Qur'an is an argument (ḥujjah) for you or against you," its meaning is apparent: you benefit from it if you recite it and act upon it; otherwise, it is an argument against you.

As for his saying, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, "Every person goes forth (yaghdū) and sells his soul, either freeing it (fa-muʿtiqahā) or destroying it (fa-mūbiqahā)," its meaning is that every person strives with his soul. Among them is one who sells it to Allah the Exalted through His obedience, and thus frees it from punishment (ʿadhāb). And among them is one who sells it to Satan (al-shayṭān) and desire (al-hawā) by following them, and thus destroys it (yūbiqahā), meaning he ruins it. And Allah knows best.

| (Chapter: The Obligation of Purification for Prayer)

In its chain of transmission (isnād) is Abū Kāmil al-Jaḥdarī — with the opening of the jīm, the stillness of the unpointed ḥā', and the opening of the dāl — and his name is al-Fuḍayl ibn Ḥusayn, attributed to a grandfather of his named Jaḥdar. Its explanation has been mentioned multiple times previously.

In it is also Abū ʿAwānah, whose name is al-Waḍḍāḥ ibn ʿAbd Allāh.

His saying, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: "Allah does not accept prayer without purification (ṭahūr), nor charity from ghulūl (war booty treachery)" — this hadith is an explicit text (naṣṣ) on the obligation of purification for prayer. The ummah has unanimously agreed (ajmaʿat al-ummah) that purification is a condition for the validity of prayer.

Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ said: They differed as to when purification for prayer was made obligatory (furḍat). Ibn al-Jahm held that ablution (wuḍū') at the beginning of Islam was a Sunnah, then its obligation was revealed in the verse of tayammum (dry ablution). The majority (al-jumhūr) held that it was obligatory before that.

He said: They also differed as to whether ablution is obligatory upon every person standing for prayer (kull qā'im ilā al-ṣalāh) or specifically upon the one in a state of minor ritual impurity (al-muḥdith).

A group of the Salaf held that ablution for every prayer is obligatory, based on the saying of the Exalted: {«إِذَا قُمْتُمْ إِلَى الصَّلَاةِ»} (When you stand for prayer) — the verse. Another group held that this was the case but was then abrogated (naskh). And it is said the command for it for every prayer is on the basis of recommendation (nadb). And it is said it was not legislated except for the one who has had an event (aḥdath), but renewing it for every prayer is recommended (mustaḥabb). Upon this, the people of legal opinion (ahl al-fatwā) have unanimously agreed thereafter, and no disagreement remains among them. The meaning of the verse according to them is: "If you are in a state of ḥadath." This is the statement of Qāḍī, may Allah the Exalted have mercy on him.

Our companions (aṣḥābunā) differed concerning what necessitates ablution (al-mūjib li al-wuḍū') on three aspects (awjuh): One: that it is obligatory due to ḥadath with an expanded obligation (wujūb mūsāʿ). The second: that it is not obligatory except upon standing for prayer. The third: that it is obligatory by both matters — and this is the preponderant view (al-rājiḥ) according to our companions.

The ummah has unanimously agreed upon the prohibition of prayer without purification, whether by water or by earth (turāb). There is no difference between the obligatory prayer (al-ṣalāh al-mafrūḍah) and the supererogatory prayer (al-nāfilah), the prostration of recitation (sujūd al-tilāwah), the prostration of thanks (sujūd al-shukr), and the funeral prayer (ṣalāt al-janāzah), except...

chapters.arabic_text:
ما حكي عن الشعبي ومحمد بن جرير الطبري من قولهما تجوز صلاة الجنازة بغير

طهارة وهذا مذهب باطل وأجمع العلماء على خلافه ولو صلى محدثا متعمدا بلا

عذر أثم ولا يكفر عندنا وعند الجماهير وحكي عن أبي حنيفة رحمه الله تعالى

أنه يكفر لتلاعبه ودليلنا أن الكفر للاعتقاد وهذا المصلي اعتقاده صحيح وهذا

كله إذا لم يكن للمصلي محدثا عذر أما المعذور كمن لم يجد ماء ولا ترابا

ففيه أربعة أقوال للشافعي رحمه الله تعالى وهي مذاهب للعلماء قال بكل واحد

منها قائلون أصحها عند أصحابنا يجب عليه أن يصلي على حاله ويجب أن يعيد إذا

تمكن من الطهارة والثاني يحرم عليه أن يصلي ويحب القضاء والثالث يستحب أن

يصلي ويجب القضاء والرابع يجب أن يصلي ولا يجب القضاء وهذا القول اختيار

المزني وهو أقوى الأقوال دليلا فأما وجوب الصلاة فلقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم

وإذا أمرتكم بأمر فافعلوا منه ما استطعتم وأما الإعادة فإنما تجب بأمر مجدد

والأصل عدمه وكذا يقول المزني كل صلاة أمر بفعلها في الوقت على نوع من

الخلل لا يجب قضاؤها والله أعلم وأما قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم في الحديث

الثاني لا يقبل الله صلاة أحدكم إذا أحدث حتى يتوضأ فمعناه حتى يتطهر بماء

أو تراب وإنما اقتصر صلى الله عليه وسلم على الوضوء لكونه الأصل والغالب

والله أعلم وأما قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم ولا صدقة من غلول فهو بضم الغين

والغلول الخيانة وأصله السرقة من مال الغنيمة قبل القسمة وأما قول بن عامر

ادع لى فقال بن عمر رضي الله عنهما سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول

لا يقبل الله صلاة بغير  طهور ولا صدقة من غلول وكنت على البصرة فمعناه أنك

لست بسالم من الغلول فقد كنت واليا على
# 
# البصرة وتعلقت بك تبعات من حقوق الله تعالى وحقوق العباد ولا يقبل الدعاء

لمن هذه صفته كما لا تقبل الصلاة والصدقة إلا من متصون والظاهر والله أعلم

أن بن عمر قصد زجر بن عامر وحثه على التوبة وتحريضه على الإقلاع عن

المخالفات ولم يرد القطع حقيقة بأن الدعاء للفساق لا ينفع فلم يزل النبي

صلى الله عليه وسلم والسلف والخلف يدعو للكفار وأصحاب المعاصي بالهداية

والتوبة والله أعلم قوله (حدثنا محمد بن مثنى وبن بشار قالا حدثنا محمد بن

جعفر حدثنا شعبة ح وحدثنا أبو بكر بن أبي شيبة حدثنا حسين بن علي عن زائدة

قال أبو بكر ووكيع حدثنا عن إسرائيل كلهم عن سماك بن حرب) أما قوله كلهم

فيعني به شعبة وزائدة وإسرائيل فأما قوله قال أبو بكر ووكيع حدثنا فمعناه

أن أبا بكر بن أبي شيبة رواه عن حسين بن علي عن زائدة ورواه أبو بكر أيضا

عن وكيع عن إسرائيل فقال أبو بكر ووكيع حدثنا وهو بمعنى قوله حدثنا وكيع

وسقط في بعض الأصول لفظة حدثنا وبقي قوله أبو بكر ووكيع عن إسرائيل وهو

صحيح أيضا ويكون معطوفا على قول أبي بكر أولا حدثنا حسين أي وحدثنا وكيع عن

إسرائيل ووقع في بعض الأصول هكذا قال أبو بكر وحدثنا وكيع وكله صحيح والله

أعلم
#

| (باب صفة الوضوء وكماله)
# فيه حرملة التجيبي هو بضم التاء وفتحها وقد تقدم بيانه في أول الكتاب في

مواضع والله أعلم قوله (عن بن شهاب أن عطاء بن يزيد أخبره أن حمران أخبره)

هؤلاء ثلاثة تابعيون بعضهم عن بعض وحمران أن بضم الحاء قوله (فغسل كفيه

ثلاث مرات) هذا دليل على أن غسلهما في أول الوضوء سنة وهو كذلك باتفاق

العلماء وقوله (ثم تمضمض واستنثر) قال جمهور أهل اللغة والفقهاء والمحدثون

الاستنثار هو إخراج الماء من الانف بعد الاستنشاق وقال بن الاعرابي وبن

قتيبة  الاستنثار الاستنشاق والصواب الأول ويدل عليه الرواية الأخرى استنشق

واستنثر فجمع بينهما قال أهل اللغة هو مأخوذ من النثرة وهي طرف الأنف وقال

الخطابي وغيره هي الأنف والمشهور الأول قال الأزهري روى سلمة عن الفراء أنه

يقال نثر الرجل وانتثر واستنثر إذا حرك النثرة في الطهارة والله أعلم وأما

حقيقة المضمضة فقال أصحابنا كمالها أن يجعل الماء في فمه ثم يديره فيه ثم

يمجه وأما أقلها فأن يجعل الماء في فيه ولا يشترط إدارته على المشهور الذي

قاله الجمهور وقال جماعة من أصحابنا يشترط وهو مثل الخلاف في مسح الرأس أنه

لو وضع يده المبتلة على رأسه ولم يمرها هل يحصل المسح والأصح الحصول كما

يكفي إيصال الماء إلى باقي الأعضاء من غير دلك وأما الاستنشاق فهو إيصال

الماء إلى داخل الأنف وجذبه بالنفس إلى أقصاه ويستحب المبالغة في المضمضة

والاستنشاق إلا أن يكون صائما فيكره ذلك لحديث لقيط أن النبي صلى الله عليه

وسلم قال وبالغ في الاستنشاق إلا أن تكون صائما وهو حديث صحيح رواه أبو

داود والترمذي وغيرهما بالأسانيد الصحيحة قال الترمذي هو حديث حسن صحيح قال

أصحابنا وعلى أي صفة وصل الماء إلى الفم والأنف حصلت المضمضة والاستنشاق

وفي الأفضل خمسة أوجه الأول يتمضمض ويستنشق بثلاث غرفات يتمضمض من كل
# 
# واحدة ثم يستنشق منها والوجه الثاني يجمع بينهما بغرفة واحدة يتمضمض منها

ثلاثا ثم يستنشق منها ثلاثا والوجه الثالث يجمع أيضا بغرفة ولكن يتمضمض
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ط-ه-ر (ṭ-h-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Purity, cleanliness, freedom from filth — both physical (ḥissī) and spiritual (maʿnawī)
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Ṭahārah as the ritual state prerequisite for valid worship (ṣalāh), encompassing both wuḍūʾ and tayammum
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Used literally for physical purification; metaphorically for moral/spiritual innocence (e.g., "pure of sin")
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clause (al-Sharṭ) — The phrase "if he prays intentionally without excuse" establishes a protasis whose apodosis (he sins) is contingent, not absolute

- Root: غ-ل-ل (gh-l-l)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Treachery, betrayal; specifically the misappropriation of war-booty (ghanīmah) before its division
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): A moral corruption (khiyānah) that invalidates the acceptance of charitable deeds
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal root meaning "to insert something into something else" (as in a hand inserted into armor); metaphorically extended to hidden treachery
- Sībawayh Rule: Genitive Construction (al-Idāfah) — "ṣadaqah min ghalūl" uses min to denote the causal source of invalidation

- Root: ن-ث-ر (n-th-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: The tip of the nose (al-nathrah); to scatter or disperse
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Istinthār as the technical act of expelling water from the nose after drawing it in
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — the nose's extremity; metaphorical — the act of expulsion itself
- Sībawayh Rule: Verbal Noun Derivation (al-Maṣdar) — istinthār follows the pattern of istifʿāl, indicating an act of drawing something out
chapters.translation:
I say: Concerning what has been narrated from al-Shaʿbī and Muḥammad ibn Jarīr al-Ṭabarī — their statement that the funeral prayer (ṣalāt al-janāzah) is permissible without purification — this is a false doctrine (madhhab bāṭil), and the scholars are unanimously agreed upon its contrary. If one prays while in a state of ritual impurity (ḥadath) deliberately, without excuse, he commits a sin, but he does not become an unbeliever (kāfir) in our view and in the view of the majority (al-jumhūr). It has been narrated from Abū Ḥanīfah — may Allah have mercy on him — that he becomes an unbeliever because of his mockery (talāʿub). Our evidence is that unbelief (kufr) pertains to conviction (iʿtiqād), and this praying person's conviction is sound.

All of this applies when the one praying in a state of impurity has no excuse. As for the excused person — such as one who finds neither water nor earth — there are four opinions (aqwāl) of al-Shāfiʿī — may Allah have mercy on him — and these are also doctrines of the scholars, each one having proponents among them:

The soundest of them in the view of our companions (aṣḥābunā) is that he must pray in his present state and must repeat (yuʿīd) when he becomes able to attain purification.

The second: it is forbidden (yaḥrum) for him to pray, and he must make up the prayer (al-qaḍāʾ).

The third: it is recommended (yustaḥabb) for him to pray, and the making up is obligatory.

The fourth: he must pray, and the making up is not obligatory. This latter opinion is the choice of al-Muzanī, and it is the strongest of the opinions in terms of evidence.

As for the obligation of the prayer, it is due to his saying — peace and blessings be upon him: {«وَإِذَا أَمَرْتُكُمْ بِأَمْرٍ فَافْعَلُوا مِنْهُ مَا اسْتَطَعْتُمْ»} ("And when I command you with a matter, do of it what you are able"). As for the repetition (iʿādah), it is only obligatory by a renewed command, and the original principle is its absence (al-aṣl ʿadamuhu). Likewise, al-Muzanī says: every prayer commanded to be performed in its time with some kind of defect (khalal) does not require making it up. And Allah knows best.

As for his saying — peace and blessings be upon him — in the second ḥadīth: {«لَا يَقْبَلُ اللهُ صَلَاةَ أَحَدِكُمْ إِذَا أَحْدَثَ حَتَّى يَتَوَضَّأَ»} ("Allah does not accept the prayer of any of you when he has had an event until he performs ablution") — its meaning is: until he purifies himself with water or earth. He — peace and blessings be upon him — mentioned only ablution (wuḍūʾ) because it is the original and the predominant means. And Allah knows best.

As for his saying — peace and blessings be upon him: {«وَلَا صَدَقَةَ مِنْ غُلُولٍ»} ("And no charity from ghulūl") — it is with ḍammah on the ghayn. Ghulūl is treachery (khiyānah), and its origin is the theft of wealth from the war-booty (ghanīmah) before its division.

As for the statement of Ibn ʿĀmir: "Supplicate for me," Ibn ʿUmar — may Allah be pleased with them both — said: "I heard the Messenger of Allah — peace and blessings be upon him — say: {«لَا يَقْبَلُ اللهُ صَلَاةً بِغَيْرِ طَهُورٍ وَلَا صَدَقَةً مِنْ غُلُولٍ»} ('Allah does not accept a prayer without purification, nor charity from ghulūl') — and you were the governor of Baṣrah." Its meaning is: you are not safe from ghulūl, for you were a governor over Baṣrah, and obligations attached to you from the rights of Allah — exalted is He — and the rights of the servants. Supplication is not accepted for one of this description, just as prayer and charity are not accepted except from one who is guarded (mutasawwin). And the apparent meaning — and Allah knows best — is that Ibn ʿUmar intended to rebuke Ibn ʿĀmir, urge him toward repentance (tawbah), and incite him to desist from violations — not to assert categorically that supplication for sinners is of no benefit. For the Prophet — peace and blessings be upon him — and the predecessors (salaf) and successors (khalaf) never ceased supplicating for the disbelievers and the people of sins, asking for guidance and repentance. And Allah knows best.

His saying: (Muḥammad ibn al-Muthannā and Ibn Bashshār narrated to us; they said: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us; Shuʿbah narrated to us — and by another chain: Abū Bakr ibn Abī Shaybah narrated to us; Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī narrated to us, from Zāʾidah; Abū Bakr said: and Wakīʿ narrated to us, from Isrāʾīl — all of them from Simāk ibn Ḥarb.)

As for his saying "all of them" (kulluhum), he means Shuʿbah, Zāʾidah, and Isrāʾīl. As for his saying "Abū Bakr and Wakīʿ narrated to us," its meaning is that Abū Bakr ibn Abī Shaybah narrated it from Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī, from Zāʾidah; and Abū Bakr also narrated it from Wakīʿ, from Isrāʾīl. So he said: "Abū Bakr and Wakīʿ narrated to us" — which is equivalent to his saying "Wakīʿ narrated to us." In some manuscripts, the word "narrated to us" (ḥaddathanā) has fallen out, leaving his saying "Abū Bakr and Wakīʿ, from Isrāʾīl" — and this is also correct, being coordinated (maʿṭūf) upon Abū Bakr's earlier statement "Ḥusayn narrated to us," i.e., "and Wakīʿ narrated to us, from Isrāʾīl." In some manuscripts it occurs thus: "Abū Bakr said: and Wakīʿ narrated to us" — and all of it is correct. And Allah knows best.

---

| (Chapter: The Description of Ablution and Its Completeness)

In it: Ḥarmalah al-Tujaybī — it is with ḍammah on the tāʾ and also with fatḥah upon it. Its explanation has already preceded at the beginning of the book in several places. And Allah knows best.

His saying: (from Ibn Shihāb that ʿAṭāʾ ibn Yazīd informed him that Ḥumrān informed him) — these are three Followers (tābiʿūn), one from the other. And Ḥumrān is with ḍammah on the ḥāʾ.

His saying: (then he washed his hands three times) — this is evidence that washing them at the beginning of ablution is a Sunnah (sunnah), and it is so by the consensus of the scholars.

His saying: (then he rinsed his mouth (tamaḍmaḍa) and expelled water from his nose (istanthara)) — the majority of the linguists, jurists, and ḥadīth scholars say: al-istinthār is the expulsion of water from the nose after al-istinshāq (drawing water into the nose). Ibn al-Aʿrābī and Ibn Qutaybah said: al-istinthār is al-istinshāq (the drawing in itself). The correct view is the first. Evidence for it is the other narration: "he drew water into his nose (istanshaqa) and expelled it (istanthara)" — combining both. The linguists say it is derived from al-nathrah, which is the tip of the nose. Al-Khaṭṭābī and others said: it is the nose itself. The well-known view is the first. Al-Azharī said: Salamah narrated from al-Farrāʾ that one says: nathara al-rajul, intathara, and istanthara — when he moves the tip of his nose (nathrah) during purification. And Allah knows best.

As for the reality of al-maḍmaḍah (mouth-rinsing), our companions say: its completeness (kamāluhā) is that one places water in his mouth, then swishes it around inside, then expels it. As for its minimum (aqalluhā), it is that one places water in his mouth, and its swishing is not a condition according to the well-known view held by the majority. A group of our companions say it is a condition — this being similar to the disagreement concerning wiping the head (masḥ al-raʾs): if one places his wet hand on his head without passing it over, does the wiping occur? The soundest view is that it does occur, just as the delivery of water to the remaining limbs suffices without rubbing (dalk). As for al-istinshāq, it is the delivery of water into the interior of the nose and drawing it by breath to its farthest depth.

It is recommended (yustaḥabb) to exaggerate (mubālaghah) in the mouth-rinsing and nose-drawing — except when one is fasting, in which case that is disliked (yukrah), due to the ḥadīth of Laqīṭ that the Prophet — peace and blessings be upon him — said: {«وَبَالِغْ فِي الِاسْتِنْشَاقِ إِلَّا أَنْ تَكُونَ صَائِمًا»} ("And exaggerate in the nose-drawing unless you are fasting"). This is a sound ḥadīth, narrated by Abū Dāwūd, al-Tirmidhī, and others with sound chains. Al-Tirmidhī said: it is a ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ ḥadīth.

Our companions say: in whatever manner the water reaches the mouth and nose, the mouth-rinsing and nose-drawing are achieved. Concerning what is most excellent (al-afḍal), there are five aspects:

The first: one rinses his mouth and draws water into his nose with three handfuls (gharafāt) — rinsing his mouth from each one, then drawing water into his nose from it.

The second aspect: one combines both with a single handful — rinsing his mouth from it three times, then drawing water into his nose from it three times.

The third aspect: one also combines with a single handful, but rinses his mouth...
