chapters.arabic_text:
صحيحه وقد قيل إن صاحب الأذان لا يعرف له غير
# 
# حديث الأذان والله أعلم قوله (فدعا بإناء فأكفأ منها على يديه) هكذا هو

في الأصول منها وهو صحيح أي من المطهرة أو الإداوة وقوله أكفأ هو بالهمز أي

أمال وصب وفيه استحباب تقديم غسل الكفين قبل غمسهما في الإناء قوله (فمضمض

واستنشق من كف واحدة ففعل ذلك ثلاثا) وفي الرواية التي بعدها فمضمض واستنشق

واستنثر من ثلاث غرفات في هذا الحديث دلالة ظاهرة للمذهب الصحيح المختار أن

السنة في المضمضة والاستنشاق أن يكون بثلاث غرفات يتمضمض ويستنشق من كل

واحدة منها وقد قدمنا إيضاح هذه المسألة والخلاف فيها في الباب الأول والله

أعلم وقوله في الرواية الثانية فمضمض واستنشق واستنثر فيه حجة للمذهب

المختار الذي عليه الجماهير من أهل اللغة وغيرهم أن الاستنثار غير

الاستنشاق خلافا لما قاله بن الاعرابي وبن قتيبة أنهما بمعنى واحد وقد تقدم

في الباب الاول ايضاحه والله أعلم قوله (ثم أدخل يده فاستخرجها فغسل وجهه

ثلاثا) هكذا وقع في صحيح مسلم أدخل يده بلفظ الإفراد وكذا في أكثر روايات

البخاري ووقع في رواية للبخاري في حديث عبد الله بن زيد هذا ثم أدخل يديه

فاغترف بهما فغسل وجهه ثلاثا وفي صحيح البخاري أيضا من رواية بن عباس ثم

أخذ غرفة فجعل بها هكذا أضافتها إلى يده الأخرى فغسل بها وجهه ثم قال هكذا

رأيت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يتوضأ وفي سنن أبي داود والبيهقي من

رواية علي رضي الله عنه في صفة وضوء رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ثم أدخل

يديه في الإناء جميعا فأخذ بهما حفنة من ماء فضرب بها على وجهه فهذه أحاديث

في بعضها يده وفي بعضها يديه وفي بعضها يده وضم إليها الأخرى فهي دالة على

جواز الأمور الثلاثة وأن الجميع سنة ويجمع بين الأحاديث بأنه صلى الله عليه

وسلم فعل ذلك في مرات وهي ثلاثة أوجه لأصحابنا ولكن الصحيح منها والمشهور

الذي قطع به الجمهور ونص عليه الشافعي رضي الله عنه في البويطي والمزني أن

المستحب أخذ الماء للوجه باليدين جميعا لكونه أسهل وأقرب إلى الإسباغ والله

أعلم قال أصحابنا ويستحب أن يبدأ في غسل وجهه بأعلاه لكونه أشرف ولأنه أقرب
# 
# إلى الاستيعاب والله أعلم قوله (فغسل وجهه ثلاثا ثم غسل يديه إلى

المرفقين مرتين مرتين) فيه دلالة على جواز مخالفة الأعضاء وغسل بعضها ثلاثا

وبعضها مرتين وبعضها مرة وهذا جائز والوضوء على هذه الصفة صحيح بلا شك ولكن

المستحب تطهير الأعضاء كلها ثلاثا ثلاثا كما قدمناه وإنما كانت مخالفتها من

النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في بعض الأوقات بيانا للجواز كما توضأ صلى الله

عليه وسلم مرة مرة  في بعض الأوقات بيانا للجواز وكان في ذلك الوقت أفضل في

حقه صلى الله عليه وسلم لأن البيان واجب عليه صلى الله عليه وسلم فإن قيل

البيان يحصل بالقول فالجواب أنه أوقع بالفعل في النفوس وأبعد من التأويل

والله أعلم قوله (فمسح برأسه فأقبل بيديه وأدبر) هذا مستحب باتفاق العلماء

فإنه طريق إلى استيعاب الرأس ووصول الماء إلى جميع شعره قال أصحابنا وهذا

الرد إنما يستحب لمن كان له شعر غير مضفور أما من لا شعر على رأسه وكان

شعره مضفورا فلا يستحب له الرد إذ لا فائدة فيه ولو رد في هذه الحالة لم

يحسب الرد مسحة ثانية لأن الماء
# 
# صار مستعملا بالنسبة إلى ما سوى تلك المسحة والله أعلم وليس في هذا

الحديث دلالة لوجوب استيعاب الرأس بالمسح لأن الحديث ورد في كمال الوضوء لا

فيما لا بد منه والله أعلم قوله (فمسح برأسه فأقبل به) أى بالمسح قوله

(حدثنا هارون بن معرف وحدثني هارون بن سعيد الأيلي وأبو الطاهر قالوا حدثنا

بن وهب قال أخبرني عمرو بن الحارث أن حبان بن واسع حدثه فذكر الحديث ثم قال

في آخره قال أبو الطاهر حدثنا بن وهب عن عمرو بن الحارث) هذا من احتياط

مسلم رحمه الله تعالى ووفور علمه وورعه ففرق بين روايته عن شيخيه الهارونين

فقال في الأول حدثنا وفي الثاني حدثني فإن روايته عن الأول كانت سماعا من

لفظ الشيخ له ولغيره وروايته عن الثاني كانت له خاصة من غير شريك له وقد

قدمنا أن المستحب في مثل الأول أن يقول حدثنا وفي الثاني وحدثني وهذا مستحب

بالاتفاق وليس بواجب فاستعمله مسلم رحمه الله تعالى وقد أكثر من التحري في

مثل هذا وقد قدمت له نظائر وسيأتي إن شاء الله تعالى التنبيه على نظائره

كثيرة والله أعلم وأما قوله قال أبو الطاهر حدثنا بن وهب عن عمرو بن الحارث

فهو أيضا من احتياط مسلم وورعه فإنه روى الحديث أولا عن شيوخه الثلاثة

الهارونين وأبي الطاهر عن  بن وهب قال أخبرني عمرو بن الحارث ولم يكن في

رواية أبي الطاهر أخبرني إنما كان فيها عن عمرو بن الحارث وقد تقرر أن لفظة

عن مختلف في حملها على الاتصال والقائلون إنها للاتصال وهم الجماهير

يوافقون على أنها دون أخبرنا فاحتاط مسلم رحمه الله تعالى وبين ذلك وكم في

كتابه من الدرر والنفائس المشابهة لهذا رحمه الله تعالى وجمع بيننا وبينه
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ك-ف-أ (k-f-ʾ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To tilt, incline, and pour out; to overturn a vessel so its contents flow forth.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Physical act of pouring with deliberate inclination, signifying controlled emission of water.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) here — actual tilting of the vessel; no metaphorical extension.
- Root: ن-ث-ر (n-th-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To scatter, disperse, or expel forcefully; in ritual context, expulsion of water from the nose.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Distinct ritual act (istinthār) separate from istinshāq — drawing water into the nose versus expelling it.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal distinction upheld by the majority of linguists; Ibn al-Aʿrābī and Ibn Qutaybah's equation of the two is rejected as a metaphorical conflation.
- Root: ر-د-د (r-d-d)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To return, bring back, or repeat; in ablution, the hand's return motion over the head.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Ritual repetition for thorough coverage (istiʿāb) of the head in wiping (masḥ).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal physical motion; not metaphorical. The return (radd) is a recommended (mustaḥabb) completion, not an obligatory second wipe.
- Sībawayh Rule: Rule of Distinction in Transmission (Farq bayn al-Ṣīghatayn) — The syntactic difference between "ḥaddathanā" (indicating public dictation to a group) and "ḥaddathanī" (indicating private dictation to the narrator alone) governs the narrator's choice of verb form, as applied by Muslim in his transmission from the two Hārūns.
chapters.translation:
I say: And it has been said that the Companion who reported the call to prayer (adhān) has no other hadith known from him besides the hadith of the adhān — and Allah knows best.

His saying (peace and blessings be upon him): "Then he called for a vessel and tilted it, pouring from it onto his hands" — thus it appears in the manuscripts: "from it" (minhā), and this is correct, meaning from the purification vessel (al-muṭahharah) or the small water-skin (al-idāwah). His saying "akfaʾa" is with hamzah, meaning he inclined and poured. In this is the recommendation (istiḥbāb) of washing the hands before immersing them in the vessel.

His saying: "Then he rinsed his mouth and drew water into his nose from one handful, and he did this three times" — and in the narration that follows: "Then he rinsed his mouth and drew water into his nose and expelled it from three handfuls." In this hadith is a clear indication for the correct and chosen school (al-madhhab al-ṣaḥīḥ al-mukhtār) that the Sunnah in rinsing the mouth (maḍmaḍah) and drawing water into the nose (istinshāq) is to use three handfuls, rinsing the mouth and drawing water into the nose from each one. We have already presented the clarification of this issue and the disagreement concerning it in the first chapter — and Allah knows best.

His saying in the second narration: "Then he rinsed his mouth, drew water into his nose, and expelled it" — in this is a proof for the chosen school, upon which the masses (al-jamāhīr) of linguists and others agree, that istinthār (expulsion from the nose) is other than istinshāq (drawing into the nose), contrary to what Ibn al-Aʿrābī and Ibn Qutaybah said — that they are of one meaning. This has already been clarified in the first chapter — and Allah knows best.

His saying: "Then he inserted his hand and withdrew it, and washed his face three times" — thus it occurred in Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim: "inserted his hand" (adkhala yadahu) in the singular form, and likewise in most narrations of al-Bukhārī. And in one narration of al-Bukhārī, in the hadith of ʿAbdullāh ibn Zayd, it occurred: "Then he inserted his two hands (yadayhi) and scooped with them, and washed his face three times." And in Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī also, from the narration of Ibn ʿAbbās: "Then he took a scoop and did thus with it" — adding to it his other hand — "and washed his face with it, then said: 'Thus I saw the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) perform ablution.'" And in the Sunan of Abū Dāwūd and al-Bayhaqī, from the narration of ʿAlī (may Allah be pleased with him) concerning the description of the ablution of the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him): "Then he inserted both his hands into the vessel together, and took with them a handful of water, and struck it upon his face." These are hadiths — in some of them "his hand," in some "his two hands," and in some "his hand" with the other joined to it. They indicate the permissibility of all three matters, and that all of them are Sunnah. One reconciles between the hadiths by noting that he (peace and blessings be upon him) did this on multiple occasions. These are three aspects (wujūh) among our companions, but the correct and well-known one — upon which the majority have decisively ruled and which al-Shāfiʿī (may Allah be pleased with him) explicitly stated in al-Buwayṭī and al-Muzanī — is that the recommended practice is to take water for the face with both hands together, because it is easier and closer to thorough coverage (isbāgh) — and Allah knows best.

Our companions said: And it is recommended to begin washing the face from its upper part, because it is nobler, and because it is closer to complete coverage — and Allah knows best.

His saying: "Then he washed his face three times, then washed his hands up to the elbows twice, twice" — in this is an indication of the permissibility of varying the limbs, washing some three times, some twice, and some once. This is permissible, and the ablution in this manner is valid without doubt. However, the recommended practice is to purify all the limbs three times, three times, as we have already stated. The Prophet's (peace and blessings be upon him) varying of them on some occasions was only a clarification (bayān) of permissibility, just as he performed ablution once, once on some occasions as a clarification of permissibility — and at that time it was more virtuous in his case (peace and blessings be upon him), because clarification was obligatory upon him (peace and blessings be upon him). If it is said: Clarification is achieved by speech — the answer is that he effected it by action, which is more impactful upon souls and further from interpretation (taʾwīl) — and Allah knows best.

His saying: "Then he wiped his head, bringing his hands forward and returning them" — this is recommended by the unanimous agreement of the scholars, for it is a means to the complete coverage (istiʿāb) of the head and the reaching of water to all of his hair. Our companions said: This return (radd) is only recommended for one who has hair that is not braided. As for one who has no hair on his head, or whose hair is braided, the return is not recommended for him, since there is no benefit in it. And if he were to return in this state, the return would not be counted as a second wipe, because the water has become used (mustaʿmal) with respect to other than that wipe — and Allah knows best. And there is no indication in this hadith of the obligation of complete coverage of the head in wiping, because the hadith concerns the perfection (kamāl) of ablution, not what is indispensable — and Allah knows best.

His saying: "Then he wiped his head, bringing it forward" — meaning, bringing the wiping forward.

His saying: "Hārūn ibn Maʿrūf narrated to us, and Hārūn ibn Saʿīd al-Aylī and Abū al-Ṭāhir narrated to me; they said: Ibn Wahb narrated to us; he said: ʿAmr ibn al-Ḥārith informed me that Ḥibbān ibn Wāsiʿ narrated to him" — then he mentioned the hadith, then said at its end: "Abū al-Ṭāhir said: Ibn Wahb narrated to us from ʿAmr ibn al-Ḥārith." This is from the caution (iḥtiyāṭ) of Muslim (may Allah have mercy upon him), the abundance of his knowledge, and his piety. He distinguished between his narration from his two shaykhs, both named Hārūn, saying in the first "ḥaddathanā" (narrated to us) and in the second "ḥaddathanī" (narrated to me). For his narration from the first was by hearing (samāʿ) from the shaykh's dictation to him and to others, while his narration from the second was for him alone, without a partner. We have already stated that the recommended practice in the first case is to say "ḥaddathanā," and in the second "ḥaddathanī." This is recommended by agreement, not obligatory. Muslim (may Allah have mercy upon him) employed it, and he was abundant in his meticulousness in such matters. I have already presented parallels for this, and there will come, Allah willing, the pointing out of many of its parallels — and Allah knows best.

As for his saying: "Abū al-Ṭāhir said: Ibn Wahb narrated to us from ʿAmr ibn al-Ḥārith" — this too is from the caution and piety of Muslim. For he first narrated the hadith from his three shaykhs — the two Hārūns and Abū al-Ṭāhir — from Ibn Wahb, who said: "ʿAmr ibn al-Ḥārith informed me (akhbaranī)." But in Abū al-Ṭāhir's narration there was no "akhbaranī"; rather, it contained only "from ʿAmr ibn al-Ḥārith" (ʿan). And it is established that the word "ʿan" is subject to disagreement regarding its being construed as indicating continuity (ittiṣāl). Those who hold that it indicates continuity — and they are the masses (al-jamāhīr) — agree that it is below "akhbaranā" in strength. So Muslim (may Allah have mercy upon him) exercised caution and clarified this. How many pearls and precious gems similar to this are in his book! May Allah have mercy upon him, and may He gather us with him.

chapters.title_en: Section 203 — On Odd-Numbered Istinjā' and Snuffing Water into the Nose; The Obligation of Washing the Feet Completely
chapters.arabic_text:
في دار كرامته والله أعلم
# 
# وحبان بفتح الحاء المهملة وبالموحدة والأيلي بفتح الهمزة وإسكان المثناة

والله أعلم قوله (ومسح برأسه بماء غير فضل يده) وفي بعض النسخ يديه معناه

أنه مسح الرأس بماء جديد لا ببقية ماء يديه ولا يستدل بهذا على أن الماء

المستعمل لا تصح الطهارة به لأن هذا إخبار عن الإتيان بماء جديد للرأس ولا

يلزم من ذلك اشتراطه والله أعلم

| (باب الإيتار في الاستنثار والاستجمار)
# فيه قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (إذا استجمر أحدكم فليستجمر وترا وإذا توضأ

أحدكم فليجعل في أنفه ماء ثم لينثر) أما الاستجمار فهو مسح محل البول

والغائط بالجمار وهي الأحجار الصغار قال العلماء يقال الاستطابة والاستجمار

والاستنجاء لتطهير محل البول والغائط فأما الاستجمار فمختص بالمسح بالأحجار

وأما الاستطابة والاستنجاء فيكونان بالماء ويكونان بالأحجار هذا الذي

ذكرناه من معنى الاستجمار هو الصحيح المشهور الذي قاله الجماهير من طوائف

العلماء من اللغويين والمحدثين والفقهاء وقال القاضي عياض رحمه الله تعالى

اختلف قول مالك وغيره في معنى الاستجمار المذكور في هذا الحديث فقيل هذا

وقيل المراد به في البخور أن يأخذ منه ثلاث قطع أو يأخذ منه ثلاث مرات

يستعمل واحدة بعد أخرى قال والأول أظهر والله أعلم والصحيح المعروف ما

قدمناه والمراد بالإيتار أن يكون عدد المسحات ثلاثا أو خمسا أو فوق
# 
# ذلك من الأوتار ومذهبنا أن الإيتار فيما زاد على الثلاث مستحب وحاصل

المذهب أن الإنقاء واجب واستيفاء ثلاث مسحات واجب فإن حصل الإنقاء بثلاث

فلا زيادة وإن لم يحصل وجب الزيادة ثم إن حصل بوتر فلا زيادة وإن حصل  بشفع

كأربع أو ست استحب الإيتار وقال بعض أصحابنا يجب الإيتار مطلقا لظاهر هذا

الحديث وحجة الجمهور الحديث الصحيح في السنن أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه

وسلم قال من استجمر فليوتر من فعل فقد أحسن ومن لا فلا حرج ويحملون حديث

الباب على الثلاث وعلى الندب فيما زاد والله أعلم وأما قوله صلى الله عليه

وسلم فليجعل في أنفه ماء ثم لينثر ففيه دلالة ظاهرة على أن الاستنثار غير

الاستنشاق وأن الانتثار هو إخراج الماء بعد الاستنشاق مع ما في الأنف من

مخاط وشبهه وقد تقدم ذكر هذا وفيه دلالة لمذهب من يقول الاستنشاق واجب

لمطلق الأمر ومن لم يوجبه حمل الأمر على الندب بدليل أن المأمور به حقيقة

وهو الانتثار ليس بواجب بالاتفاق فإن قالوا ففي الرواية الأخرى إذا توضأ

فليستنشق بمنخريه من الماء ثم لينثر فهذا فيه دلالة ظاهرة للوجوب ولكن حمله

على الندب محتمل ليجمع بينه وبين الأدلة الدالة على الاستحباب والله أعلم

قوله في حديث همام (فذكر أحاديث منها وقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم)

قد قدمنا مرات بيان الفائدة في هذه العبارة وإنما ننبه على تقدمها ليتعاهد

قوله (بمنخريه) هما بفتح الميم وكسر الخاء وبكسرهما جميعا لغتان معروفتان

قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم
# 
# (فليستنثر فإن الشيطان يبيت على خياشيمه) قال العلماء الخيشوم أعلى الأنف

وقيل هو الأنف كله وقيل هي عظام رقاق لينة في أقصى الأنف بينه وبين الدماغ

وقيل غير ذلك وهو اختلاف متقارب المعنى قال القاضي عياض رحمه الله تعالى

يحتمل أن يكون قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم فإن الشيطان يبيت على خياشيمه على

حقيقته فإن الأنف أحد منافذ الجسم التي يتوصل إلى القلب منها لا سيما وليس

من منافذ الجسم ماليس عليه غلق سواه وسوى الأذنين وفي الحديث إن الشيطان لا

يفتح غلقا وجاء في التثاؤب الأمر بكظمه من أجل دخول الشيطان حينئذ في الفم

قال ويحتمل أن يكون على الاستعارة فإن ما ينعقد من الغبار ورطوبة الخياشيم

قذارة توافق  الشيطان والله أعلم

| باب وجوب غسل الرجلين بكمالها
# في الباب قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (ويل للاعقاب من النار أسبغوا الوضوء)

ومراد مسلم
# 
# رحمه الله تعالى بإيراده هنا الاستدلال به على وجوب غسل الرجلين وأن

المسح لا يجزئ وهذه مسألة اختلف الناس فيها على مذاهب فذهب جمع من الفقهاء

من أهل الفتوى في الأعصار والأمصار إلى أن الواجب غسل القدمين مع الكعبين

ولا يجزئ مسحهما ولا يجب المسح مع الغسل ولم يثبت خلاف هذا عن أحد يعتد به

في الإجماع وقالت الشيعة الواجب مسحهما وقال محمد بن جرير والجبائي رأس

المعتزلة يتخير بين المسح والغسل وقال بعض أهل الظاهر يجب الجمع بين المسح

والغسل وتعلق هؤلاء المخالفون للجماهير بما لا تظهر فيه دلالة وقد أوضحت

دلائل المسألة من الكتاب والسنة وشواهدها وجواب ما تعلق به المخالفون بأبسط

العبارات المنقحات في شرح المهذب بحيث لم يبق للمخالف شبهة أصلا إلا وضح

جوابها من غير وجه والمقصود هنا شرح متون الأحاديث وألفاظها دون بسط الأدلة

وأجوبة المخالفين ومن أخصر ما نذكره أن جميع من وصف وضوء رسول الله صلى

الله عليه وسلم في مواطن مختلفة وعلى صفات متعددة متفقون على غسل الرجلين

وقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم ويل للأعقاب من النار فتواعدها بالنار لعدم
chapters.anchors:
- Root: و-ت-ر (watara)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: The single, the odd; that which is not paired; the act of making something odd in number.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In ritual law, denotes performing an act an odd number of times (3, 5, 7...) as a devotional form (ṣifat al-ʿibādah).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) in arithmetic counting; metaphorical (majāz) when applied to ritual acts, signifying the intended odd count.
- Root: ن-ث-ر (nathara)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To scatter, to expel forcibly; snuffing water into the nose then expelling it.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Istinthār is the expulsion of water from the nasal cavity after istinshāq (snuffing), a distinct ritual act.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for physical expulsion; in ḥadīth, a commanded act (amr) whose modality (wujūb vs. nadb) is debated.
- Root: ج-م-ر (jamara)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Small stones (al-jimār); the act of wiping with stones.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Istinjā' by stones for purification from filth; technical term for dry cleansing.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for stone-wiping; distinguished from istiṭābah (water cleansing) in juristic usage.
- Root: خ-ي-ش-م (khaysham)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: The upper part of the nose; the nasal bridge.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Anatomical term; in ḥadīth, locus of Shayṭān's nocturnal dwelling.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal anatomical reference; metaphorical (majāz) possibility per Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ, denoting filth attracting Shayṭān.
- Sībawayh Rule: ʿAṭf al-Bayān (Appositional Clarification) — For parsing "بمنخريه" (dual form with kasrah on khā'), noting the two valid vowellings (fatḥah on mīm + kasrah on khā', or kasrah on both), as dual nouns in genitive position governed by the preposition "ب".
chapters.translation:
I say: And Allah knows best.

As for his statement (regarding the narrator) "Ḥibbān" — it is with a fatḥah on the unpointed ḥā' and a bā' (i.e., Ḥibbān) — and "al-Aylī" — with a fatḥah on the hamzah and a sukūn on the tā' (i.e., al-Aylī).

And Allah knows best. His statement (in the ḥadīth): "And he wiped his head with water not from the remainder of his hand" — and in some copies "his hands" — its meaning is that he wiped his head with fresh water, not with the leftover water on his hands. This is not to be taken as evidence that water already used (al-mā' al-mustaʿmal) does not render purification valid, because this is merely an informative report (ikhbār) of his bringing fresh water for the head, and it does not necessarily imply that this is a stipulated condition. And Allah knows best.

| Chapter: On Performing Odd Numbers in Istinthār (Snuffing and Expelling) and Istinjā' (Cleansing)

In this chapter is his statement, peace and blessings be upon him: "When any of you performs istinjā' with stones, let him do so an odd number of times, and when any of you performs wuḍū', let him put water in his nose and then expel it." As for istinjā' (stone-cleansing), it is the wiping of the place of urine and feces with stones (al-jimār), which are small stones. The scholars said: One says istiṭābah, istinjār, and istinjā' for the purification of the place of urine and feces. As for istinjā', it is specifically the wiping with stones. As for istiṭābah and istinjā', they may be with water or with stones. What we have mentioned regarding the meaning of istinjā' is the correct and well-known view held by the majority of scholars from the various classes — the lexicographers, the ḥadīth scholars, and the jurists.

Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ, may Allah have mercy on him, said: There is a divergence in the statement of Mālik and others regarding the meaning of istinjā' mentioned in this ḥadīth. It was said: such-and-such. And it was said: the intended meaning is regarding incense (al-bakhūr), that one takes three pieces from it, or takes from it three times, using one after another. He said: And the first (view) is more apparent. And Allah knows best. The correct and well-known view is what we have already presented.

The intended meaning of "odd number" (ītār) is that the number of wipings be three, or five, or more than that from among the odd numbers. Our school (al-Shāfiʿī) holds that making it odd beyond three is recommended (mustaḥabb). The summary of the school is: complete cleansing (al-inqā') is obligatory, and completing three wipings is obligatory. If cleansing is achieved with three, then no increase. If it is not achieved, then an increase becomes obligatory. Then, if it is achieved with an odd number, no increase; and if it is achieved with an even number, such as four or six, then making it odd is recommended. Some of our companions said: Making it odd is obligatory absolutely, due to the apparent meaning of this ḥadīth. The proof of the majority is the authentic ḥadīth in the Sunan collections, that the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Whoever performs istinjā' with stones, let him do so odd. Whoever does so has done well, and whoever does not, there is no sin upon him." They interpret the ḥadīth of this chapter as referring to the three (obligatory wipings), and to recommendation (nadb) regarding what is beyond that. And Allah knows best.

As for his statement, peace and blessings be upon him: "Let him put water in his nose and then expel it" — in it is a clear indication that istinthār (expelling) is distinct from istinshāq (snuffing), and that istinthār is the expulsion of the water after snuffing, along with whatever is in the nose of mucus and the like. We have already mentioned this earlier. In it is also an indication for the school of those who say that istinshāq is obligatory, due to the absolute command (al-amr al-muṭlaq). Those who do not deem it obligatory interpret the command as indicating recommendation (nadb), on the evidence that the thing actually commanded — namely, the expulsion (istinthār) — is not obligatory by consensus. If they say: "But in the other narration: 'When he performs wuḍū', let him snuff water into his nostrils and then expel it' — this contains a clear indication of obligation," then we say: interpreting it as recommendation is plausible, in order to reconcile between it and the evidences indicating recommendation. And Allah knows best.

His statement in the ḥadīth of Hammām: "And he mentioned ḥadīths, among them, and the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said..." — We have already explained multiple times the benefit in this expression. We only draw attention to its prior mention so that one may revisit it.

His statement: "into his nostrils (biminkharayhi)" — the two nostrils: with a fatḥah on the mīm and kasrah on the khā', or with kasrah on both — these are two well-known dialects.

His statement, peace and blessings be upon him: "Let him expel (the water), for Shayṭān spends the night upon his nasal passages (khayāshīm)" — The scholars said: al-khayshūm is the upper part of the nose. It was also said: it is the entire nose. And it was said: they are thin, soft bones at the deepest part of the nose, between it and the brain. And other views were mentioned — and this is a divergence of closely related meanings. Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ, may Allah have mercy on him, said: It is possible that his statement, peace and blessings be upon him, "for Shayṭān spends the night upon his nasal passages" is on its literal meaning (ḥaqīqah), for the nose is one of the body's openings through which one reaches the heart — especially since there is no opening of the body that lacks a cover (ghalaq) except it and the two ears. And in the ḥadīth: "Shayṭān does not open a locked cover." And it has come in the ḥadīth of yawning the command to suppress it, because of Shayṭān's entry at that time through the mouth. He said: And it is possible that it is metaphorical (istiʿārah), for what accumulates of dust and moisture in the nasal passages is a filth that befits Shayṭān. And Allah knows best.

| Chapter: On the Obligation of Washing the Feet Completely

In this chapter is his statement, peace and blessings be upon him: "Woe to the heels from the Fire — perfect your wuḍū' (asbighū al-wuḍū')." The intent of Muslim, may Allah have mercy on him, in citing it here is to use it as evidence for the obligation of washing the feet, and that wiping (al-masḥ) does not suffice. This is a matter in which people have differed according to various schools. A group of jurists — those qualified for legal opinion (ahl al-fatwā) across the ages and regions — held that the obligatory act is washing the feet including the ankles (al-kaʿbayn), that wiping them does not suffice, and that wiping is not required alongside washing. No contrary view has been established from anyone whose opinion counts in consensus (ijmāʿ). The Shīʿah said: The obligatory act is wiping them. Muḥammad ibn Jarīr (al-Ṭabarī) and al-Jubbā'ī, the head of the Muʿtazilah, said: One may choose between wiping and washing. Some of the Ẓāhirīs said: One must combine both wiping and washing. These opponents of the majority clung to what contains no evident proof. I have already clarified the evidences of this matter from the Book and the Sunnah, along with their corroborations, and the refutation of what the opponents clung to, in the most expansive and refined expressions in my commentary on al-Muhadhdhab (Sharḥ al-Muhadhdhab), such that no doubt remains for any opponent except that its refutation is made clear from multiple angles. The purpose here is to explain the texts of the ḥadīths and their wordings, without expanding the evidences and the refutations of the opponents. Among the most concise of what we mention is that all those who described the wuḍū' of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, in various places and in multiple forms, are in agreement upon the washing of the feet. And his statement, peace and blessings be upon him: "Woe to the heels from the Fire" — he threatened them with the Fire for the neglect of (washing them).

chapters.title_en: The Purity of the Heels and the Comprehensive Naming of Sālim, the Freed Slave of Shaddād; The Obligation of Complete Coverage in Ablution
chapters.arabic_text:
طهارتها ولو كان المسح كافيا لما تواعد من ترك غسل عقبيه وقد صح من حديث

عمرو بن شعيب عن أبيه عن جده أن رجلا قال يارسول الله كيف الطهور فدعا بماء

فغسل كفيه ثلاثا إلى أن قال ثم غسل رجليه ثلاثا ثم قال هكذا الوضوء فمن زاد

على هذا أو نقص فقد أساء وظلم هذا حديث صحيح أخرجه أبو داود وغيره

بأسانيدهم الصحيحة والله أعلم قوله (عن سالم مولى شداد وفي الرواية الأخرى

أن أبا عبد الله مولى شداد بن الهاد وفي الثالثة سالم مولى المهري) هذه

كلها صفات له وهو شخص واحد يقال له سالم مولى شداد بن الهاد وسالم مولى

المهري وسالم بادوس وسالم مولى مالك  بن أوس بن الحدثان النصري بالنون

والصاد المهملة وسالم سبنان بفتح السين المهملة والباء الموحدة وسالم

البراد وسالم مولى البصريين وسالم أبو عبد الله المديني وسالم بن عبد الله

وأبو عبيد الله مولى شداد بن الهاد فهذه كلها تقال فيه قال أبو حاتم كان

سالم من خيار المسلمين وقال عطاء بن السائب حدثني سالم البراد وكان أوثق

عندي من نفسي وأما قوله (حدثني سلمة بن شبيب حدثنا الحسن بن أعين حدثنا

فليح حدثني نعيم بن عبد الله عن سالم مولى بن شداد) فكذا وقع في الاصول

مولى بن شداد قيل إنه خطأ والصواب حذف لفظة بن كما تقدم والظاهر أنه صحيح

فإن مولى شداد مولى لابنه وإذا أمكن
# 
# تأويل ما صحت به الرواية لم يجز إبطالها لا سيما في هذا الذي قد قيل فيه

هذه الأقوال والله أعلم قوله (حدثنا عكرمة بن عمار حدثنا يحي بن أبي كثير

قال حدثني أو حدثنا أبو سلمة بن عبد الرحمن حدثنا سالم مولى المهري) هذا

إسناد اجتمع فيه أربعة تابعيون يروي بعضهم عن بعض فسالم وأبو سلمة ويحي

تابعيون معروفون وعكرمة بن عمار أيضا تابعي سمع الهرماس بن زياد الباهلي

الصحابي رضي الله عنه وفي سنن أبي داود التصريح بسماعه منه والله أعلم

وقوله حدثني أو حدثنا فيه أحسن احتياط وقد تقدم التنبيه على مثل هذا قريبا

وسابقا والله أعلم قوله (حدثني محمد بن حاتم وأبو معن الرقاشي) اسم أبي معن

زيد بن يزيد وقد تقدم بيانه في أوائل كتاب الإيمان قوله (كنت أنا مع عائشة)

هكذا هو في الأصول المحققة التي ضبطها المتقنون أنا مع بالنون والميم

بينهما ألف ووقع في كثير من الأصول ولكثير من الرواة المشارقة والمغاربة

أبايع عائشة بالباء الموحدة والياء المثناة من المبايعة قال القاضي الصواب

هو الأول قلت وللثاني أيضا وجه قوله (عن هلال بن يساف عن أبي يحيى) أما

يساف ففيه ثلاث لغات فتح الياء وكسرها وإساف بكسر الهمزة قال صاحب المطالع

يقوله المحدثون بكسر الياء  قال وقال بعضهم هو بفتح الياء لأنه لم يأت في

كلام العرب كلمة أولها ياء مكسور إلا يسار لليد قلت والأشهر عند أهل اللغة

إساف بالهمزة وقد ذكره بن السكيت وبن قتيبة وغيرهما فيما يغيره الناس

ويلحنون فيه فقال هو هلال بن إساف وأما أبو يحيى فالأكثرون على أن اسمه

مصدع بكسر الميم وإسكان الصاد وفتح الدال وبالعين المهملات وقال يحيى بن

معين اسمه زياد الأعرج المعرقب الأنصاري والله أعلم قوله (فتوضؤا وهم عجال)

هو بكسر العين جمع عجلان وهو المستعجل كغضبان وغضاب قوله (حدثنا أبو عوانة

عن أبي بشر عن يوسف
# 
# بن ماهك) أما أبو عوانة فتقدم أن اسمه الوضاح بن عبد الله وأما أبو بشر

فهو جعفر بن أبي وحشية وأما ماهك فبفتح الهاء وهو غيره مصروف لأنه اسم عجمي

علم قوله (وقد حضرت صلاة العصر) أي جاء وقت فعلها ويقال حضرت بفتح الضاد

وكسرها لغتان الفتح أشهر قوله (يتوضؤن من المطهرة) قال العلماء المطهرة كل

إناء يتطهر به وهي بكسر الميم وفتحها لغتان مشهورتان وذكرهما بن السكيت من

كسر جعلها آلة ومن فتحها جعلها موضعا يفعل فيه قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم

(ويل للعراقيب من النار) العراقيب جمع عرقوب بضم العين في المفرد وفتحها في

الجمع وهوالعصبة التي فوق العقب ومعنى ويل لهم هلكة وخيبة

| (باب وجوب استيعاب جميع أجزاء محل الطهارة)
# فيه (أن رجلا توضأ فترك موضع ظفر على ظهر قدمه فأبصره النبي صلى الله

عليه وسلم فقال
# 
# ارجع فأحسن وضوءك فرجع ثم صلى) في هذا الحديث أن من ترك جزءا يسيرا مما

يجب تطهيره لا تصح طهارته وهذا متفق عليه واختلفوا في المتيمم يترك بعض

وجهه فمذهبنا ومذهب الجمهور أنه لا يصح كما لا يصح وضوءه وعن أبي حنيفة

ثلاث روايات إحداها إذا ترك أقل من النصف أجزأه والثانية إذا ترك أقل من

قدر الدرهم أجزأه والثالثة إذا ترك الربع فما دونه أجزأه وللجمهور أن

يحتجوا بالقياس والله أعلم وفي هذا الحديث دليل على أن  من ترك شيئا من

أعضاء طهارته جاهلا لم تصح طهارته وفيه تعليم الجاهل والرفق به وقد استدل

به جماعة على أن الواجب في الرجلين الغسل دون المسح واستدل القاضي عياض

رحمه الله تعالى وغيره بهذا الحديث على وجوب الموالاة في الوضوء لقوله صلى

الله عليه وسلم أحسن وضوءك ولم يقل اغسل الموضع الذي تركته وهذا الاستدلال

ضعيف أو باطل فإن قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم أحسن وضوءك محتمل للتتميم
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ط-ه-ر (ṭ-h-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning of cleanliness and purity, both physical and spiritual; the act of removing filth (najāsah) or ritual impurity (ḥadath).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In Sharīʿah, ṭahārah denotes the removal of ḥadath (ritual state requiring ablution) and khabath (physical impurity), a prerequisite for valid prayer.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Used literally (ḥaqīqah) for physical washing; metaphorically (majāz) for spiritual purification from sin.
- Root: ع-ر-ق-ب (ʿ-r-q-b)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: The strong sinew (ʿaṣabah) above the heel (ʿaqib); the plural is ʿarāqīb.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Anatomical term; in the prophetic warning, it signifies the specific bodily part that must be washed in ablution.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal anatomical reference; the threat of fire is a literal consequence for neglect, not metaphorical.
- Root: م-س-ح (m-s-ḥ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To wipe or pass the hand over something; distinct from washing (ghasl) in that it does not require water to flow.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In fiqh, masḥ is a specific legal act for wiping over leather socks (khuffayn) or the head, distinct from the obligatory washing of limbs.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal wiping; the prophetic command to wash the heels negates any metaphorical extension of masḥ to the feet.
- Root: و-ل-ي (w-l-y)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To be near, to be in charge, or to be a freed slave (mawlā) of someone; denotes a bond of patronage or clientage.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In biographical contexts, mawlā indicates a freed slave (ʿatīq) or client, a legal and social status in early Islamic society.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal patron-client relationship; used here to identify the narrator Sālim, not metaphorically.
- Sībawayh Rule: Rule of ʿAṭf al-Bayān (Appositional Clarification) — When multiple names or epithets are listed for a single person (e.g., Sālim Mawlā Shaddād, Sālim al-Mahrī), they function as appositives clarifying one referent, not as separate individuals. Also, the Rule of Taʿdīl (Correction of Transmission) — When a narrator expresses doubt (e.g., "ḥaddathanī aw ḥaddathanā"), the syntax allows for cautious ambiguity, preserving the integrity of the isnād.
chapters.translation:
I say: Its purity [is required], and if wiping (al-masḥ) had sufficed, there would have been no threat [of punishment] for one who neglects washing his heels (ʿaqibayh). This is confirmed by the authentic narration of ʿAmr ibn Shuʿayb, from his father, from his grandfather, that a man said: "O Messenger of Allah, how is the purification (al-ṭuhūr)?" So he called for water and washed his hands three times, until he said: "Then he washed his feet three times." Then he said: "Thus is the ablution (al-wuḍūʾ). Whoever adds to this or diminishes from it has done evil and wronged." This is an authentic ḥadīth, recorded by Abū Dāwūd and others with their authentic chains of transmission. And Allah knows best.

His statement (concerning Sālim, the freed slave of Shaddād — and in the other narration, that Abū ʿAbdullāh, the freed slave of Shaddād ibn al-Hād, and in the third, Sālim, the freed slave of al-Mahrī): All of these are attributes of him, and he is one person. He is called Sālim, the freed slave of Shaddād ibn al-Hād, and Sālim, the freed slave of al-Mahrī, and Sālim Bādūs, and Sālim, the freed slave of Mālik ibn Aws ibn al-Ḥadathān al-Naṣrī (with the nūn and unpointed ṣād), and Sālim Sabnān (with the fatḥah on the sīn and the unpointed bāʾ), and Sālim al-Barrād, and Sālim, the freed slave of the Baṣrans, and Sālim Abū ʿAbdullāh al-Madanī, and Sālim ibn ʿAbdullāh, and Abū ʿUbaydullāh, the freed slave of Shaddād ibn al-Hād. All of these are said of him. Abū Ḥātim said: "Sālim was among the best of the Muslims." And ʿAṭāʾ ibn al-Sāʾib said: "Sālim al-Barrād narrated to me, and he was more trustworthy to me than my own self."

As for his statement ("Salamah ibn Shabīb narrated to me; al-Ḥasan ibn Aʿyan narrated to us; Fulayḥ narrated to me; Nuʿaym ibn ʿAbdullāh narrated to me, from Sālim, the freed slave of ibn Shaddād") — thus it occurred in the manuscripts: "the freed slave of ibn Shaddād." It was said that this is an error, and the correct [reading] is to omit the word "ibn," as mentioned previously. However, the apparent [view] is that it is correct, for Sālim was the freed slave of Shaddād and also of his son. When a valid interpretation of what has been authentically transmitted is possible, it is not permissible to declare it invalid — especially in this case where these various statements have been made. And Allah knows best.

His statement ("ʿIkrimah ibn ʿAmmār narrated to us; Yaḥyā ibn Abī Kathīr narrated to us; he said: Abū Salamah ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to me or to us; Sālim, the freed slave of al-Mahrī, narrated to us"): This is a chain of transmission in which four Successors (tābiʿūn) are gathered, each narrating from the other. For Sālim, Abū Salamah, and Yaḥyā are well-known Successors, and ʿIkrimah ibn ʿAmmār is also a Successor who heard from al-Hirmās ibn Ziyād al-Bāhilī, the Companion, may Allah be pleased with him. In the Sunan of Abū Dāwūd, there is explicit confirmation of his hearing from him. And Allah knows best. His statement "narrated to me or narrated to us" contains the best precaution, and I have previously drawn attention to similar cases recently and before. And Allah knows best.

His statement ("Muḥammad ibn Ḥātim and Abū Maʿn al-Raqāshī narrated to me"): The name of Abū Maʿn is Zayd ibn Yazīd, and I have already explained this at the beginning of the Book of Faith (Kitāb al-Īmān).

His statement ("I was with ʿĀʾishah"): Thus it is in the verified manuscripts that the meticulous scholars have recorded: "anā maʿa" (I was with) — with the nūn and mīm and an alif between them. And it occurred in many manuscripts and with many narrators, both Eastern and Western, as "ubāyiʿu ʿĀʾishah" (I was pledging allegiance to ʿĀʾishah) — with the unpointed bāʾ and the dotted yāʾ, from the act of pledging allegiance (mubāyaʿah). Al-Qāḍī said: "The correct [reading] is the first." I say: And for the second, there is also a valid interpretation.

His statement ("from Hilāl ibn Yasāf, from Abū Yaḥyā"): As for Yasāf, there are three dialects: the fatḥah on the yāʾ, the kasrah on it, and Isāf with the kasrah on the hamzah. The author of al-Maṭāliʿ said: "The ḥadīth scholars pronounce it with the kasrah on the yāʾ." He said: "And some said it is with the fatḥah on the yāʾ, because there is no word in the speech of the Arabs beginning with a kasrah yāʾ except yasār, for the left hand." I say: And the most famous among the linguists is Isāf with the hamzah. Ibn al-Sikkīt, Ibn Qutaybah, and others have mentioned it among the words that people alter and in which they err, saying: "It is Hilāl ibn Isāf." As for Abū Yaḥyā, the majority hold that his name is Muṣaddiʿ — with the kasrah on the mīm, the sukūn on the ṣād, the fatḥah on the dāl, and all with unpointed letters. And Yaḥyā ibn Maʿīn said: "His name is Ziyād al-Aʿraj al-Muʿarqab al-Anṣārī." And Allah knows best.

His statement ("So they performed ablution while they were ʿijāl"): It is with the kasrah on the ʿayn, the plural of ʿajlān, meaning one who hastens, like ghaḍbān and ghiḍāb.

His statement ("Abū ʿAwānah narrated to us, from Abū Bishr, from Yūsuf ibn Māhak"): As for Abū ʿAwānah, I have already mentioned that his name is al-Waḍḍāḥ ibn ʿAbdullāh. As for Abū Bishr, he is Jaʿfar ibn Abī Waḥshiyyah. As for Māhak, it is with the fatḥah on the hāʾ, and it is not declinable (ghayr muṣraf) because it is a non-Arabic proper noun.

His statement ("And the ʿAṣr prayer had become present"): That is, its time for performance had arrived. It is said "ḥaḍarat" with the fatḥah on the ḍād and with the kasrah on it — two dialects, the fatḥah being more famous.

His statement ("They were performing ablution from al-muṭahharah"): The scholars said: al-muṭahharah is any vessel from which one performs purification. It is with the kasrah on the mīm and the fatḥah on it — two well-known dialects. Ibn al-Sikkīt mentioned both: whoever uses the kasrah treats it as an instrument (ālah), and whoever uses the fatḥah treats it as a place (mawḍiʿ) in which the act is done.

His statement, peace and blessings be upon him ("Woe to the ʿarāqīb from the Fire"): The ʿarāqīb is the plural of ʿurqūb — with the ḍammah on the ʿayn in the singular and the fatḥah on it in the plural — and it is the sinew (ʿaṣabah) that is above the heel (ʿaqib). The meaning of "woe to them" is destruction and loss.

| (Chapter: The Obligation of Complete Coverage of All Parts of the Place of Purification)

In it [is the ḥadīth] that a man performed ablution and left a spot the size of a fingernail on the top of his foot, and the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, saw him and said: "Go back and perfect your ablution." So he went back and then prayed.

In this ḥadīth [is the proof] that whoever leaves a small part of what must be purified, his purification is not valid. This is agreed upon [by consensus]. They differed concerning the one who performs dry ablution (mutayammim) and leaves part of his face: our school (madhhab) and the school of the majority is that it is not valid, just as his ablution would not be valid. From Abū Ḥanīfah there are three narrations: one, if he leaves less than half, it suffices him; the second, if he leaves less than the amount of a dirham, it suffices him; the third, if he leaves a quarter or less, it suffices him. The majority may argue by analogy (qiyās). And Allah knows best.

In this ḥadīth is also proof that whoever leaves something of the limbs of his purification out of ignorance, his purification is not valid. And in it is the teaching of the ignorant one and gentleness with him. A group has used it as evidence that the obligation regarding the two feet is washing (ghasl), not wiping (masḥ). And al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ, may Allah the Exalted have mercy on him, and others used this ḥadīth as evidence for the obligation of continuity (muwālāh) in ablution, due to his statement, peace and blessings be upon him: "Perfect your ablution," and he did not say: "Wash the spot you left." This inference is weak or false, for his statement, peace and blessings be upon him, "Perfect your ablution" is open to the interpretation of completing [the rest].
