chapters.arabic_text:
أنا لا أمتنع من سؤالي عما أنا محتاجة إليه وقيل معناه إن الله لا يأمر

بالحياء في الحق ولا يبيحه وإنما قالت هذا اعتذارا بين يدي سؤالها عما دعت

الحاجة إليه مما تستحي النساء في العادة من السؤال عنه وذكره بحضرة الرجال

ففيه أنه ينبغي لمن عرضت له مسألة أن يسأل عنها ولا يمتنع من السؤال حياء

من ذكرها فإن ذلك ليس بحياء حقيقي لأن الحياء خير كله والحياء لا يأتي إلا

بخير والإمساك عن السؤال في هذه الحال ليس بخير بل هو شر فكيف يكون حياء

وقد تقدم إيضاح هذه المسألة في أوائل كتاب الإيمان وقد قالت عائشة رضي الله

عنها نعم النساء نساء الأنصار لم يمنعهن الحياء أن يتفقهن في الدين والله

أعلم قال أهل العربية يقال استحيا بياء قبل الألف يستحي بياءين ويقال أيضا

يستحي بياء واحدة في المضارع والله أعلم قوله (قالت عائشة فقلت لها أف لك)

معناه استحقارا لها ولما تكلمت به وهي كلمة تستعمل في الاحتقار والاستقذار

والإنكار قال الباجي والمراد بها
# 
# هنا الإنكار وأصل الأف وسخ الأظفار وفي أف عشر لغات أف وأف وأف بضم

الهمزة مع كسر الفاء وفتحها وضمها بغير تنوين وبالتنوين فهذه الستة

والسابعة إف بكسر الهمزة وفتح الفاء والثامنة أف بضم الهمزة وإسكان الفاء

والتاسعة أفي بضم الهمزة وبالياء وأفه بالهاء وهذه اللغات مشهورات ذكرهن

كلهن بن الأنباري وجماعات من العلماء ودلائلها مشهورة ومن أخصرها ما ذكره

الزجاج وبن الأنباري واختصره أبو البقاء فقال من كسر بناه على الأصل ومن

فتح طلب التخفيف ومن ضم أتبع ومن نون أراد التنكير ومن لم ينون أراد

التعريف ومن خفف الفاء حذف أحد المثلين تخفيفا وقال الأخفش وبن الأنباري في

اللغة التاسعة بالياء كأنه إضافة إلى نفسه والله أعلم قوله (عن مسافع بن

عبد الله) هو بضم الميم وبالسين المهملة وبكسر الفاء قولها (تربت يداك

وألت) هو بضم الهمزة وفتح اللام المشددة وإسكان التاء هكذا الرواية فيه

ومعناه أصابتها الألة بفتح الهمزة وتشديد اللام وهي الحربة وأنكر بعض

الأئمة هذا اللفظ وزعم أن صوابه أللت بلامين الأولى مكسورة والثانية ساكنة

وبكسر التاء وهذا الإنكار فاسد بل ما صحت به الرواية صحيح وأصله أللت بكسر

اللام الأولى وفتح الثانية وإسكان التاء كردت أصله رددت ولا يجوز فك هذا

الإدغام إلا مع المخاطب وإنما وحد ألت مع تثنية يداك لوجهين أحدهما أنه

أراد الجنس والثاني صاحبة اليدين أي وأصابتك
# 
# الألة فيكون جمعا بين دعاءين والله أعلم

| (باب بيان صفة مني الرجل والمرأة وأن الولد مخلوق من 
# مائها)
# فيه حديث ثوبان رضي الله عنه في قصة الحبر اليهودي وقد تقدم في الباب

الذي قبله بيان صفة  المني وأما الحبر فهو بفتح الحاء وكسرها لغتان مشهورتان

وهو العالم قوله (حدثني أبو أسماء الرحبي) هو بفتح الراء والحاء واسمه عمرو

بن مرثد الشامي الدمشقي قال أبو سليمان بن زيد كان أبو أسماء الرحبي من

رحبة دمشق قرية من قراها بينها وبين دمشق ميل رأيتها عامرة والله أعلم قوله

(فنكت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بعود) هو بفتح النون والكاف وبالتاء

المثناة من فوق ومعناه يخط بالعود في الأرض ويؤثر به فيها وهذا يفعله

المفكر وفي هذا دليل على جواز فعل مثل هذا وأنه ليس مخلا بالمروءة والله

أعلم قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم
# 
# (هم في الظلمة دون الجسر) هو بفتح الجيم وكسرها لغتان مشهورتان والمراد

به هنا الصراط قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (فمن أول الناس إجازة) هو بكسر

الهمزة وبالزاي ومعناه جوازا وعبورا قوله (فما تحفتهم) هي بإسكان الحاء

وفتحها لغتان وهي ما يهدى إلى الرجل ويخص به ويلاطف وقال إبراهيم الحلبي هي

طرف الفاكهة والله أعلم قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (زيادة كبد النون) هو

النون بنونين الأولى مضمومة وهو الحوت وجمعه نينان وفي الرواية الأخرى

(زائدة كبد النون) والزيادة والزائدة شئ واحد وهو طرف الكبد وهو أطيبها

قوله (فما غذاؤهم) روي على وجهين أحدهما بكسر الغين وبالذال المعجمة

والثاني بفتح الغين وبالدال المهملة قال القاضي عياض هذا الثاني هو الصحيح

وهو رواية الأكثرين قال والأول ليس بشئ قلت وله وجه وتقديره ما غذاؤهم في

ذلك الوقت وليس المراد والسؤال عن غذائهم دائما والله أعلم قوله (على

إثرها) بكسر الهمزة مع إسكان الثاء وبفتحهما جميعا لغتان مشهورتان قوله صلى

الله عليه وسلم (من عين فيها تسمى سلسبيلا) قال جماعة من أهل اللغة

والمفسرين السلسبيل اسم للعين وقال مجاهد وغيره هي شديدة الجري وقيل هي

السلسة اللينة قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (أذكرا بإذن الله وآنثا بإذن الله)

معنى الأول
# 
# كان الولد ذكرا ومعنى الثاني كان أنثى وقوله آنثا بالمد في أوله وتخفيف

النون وقد روي  بالقصر وتشديد النون والله أعلم

| (باب صفة غسل الجنابة)
# قال أصحابنا كمال غسل الجنابة أن يبدأ المغتسل فيغسل كفيه ثلاثا قبل

إدخالهما في الإناء ثم يغسل ما على فرجه وسائر بدنه من الأذى ثم يتوضأ
chapters.anchors:
- Root: س-أ-ل (sa-ʾa-la)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To ask, to seek information or a request; the act of inquiry (suʾāl) rooted in need (ḥājah).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological discourse, suʾāl is the legitimate seeking of knowledge or clarification, untainted by blameworthy shyness (ḥayāʾ) when truth (ḥaqq) is at stake.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) — verbal inquiry; metaphorical (majāz) — the inner prompting of need that compels speech.
- Sībawayh Rule: ʿAṭf al-Bayān (Appositional Clarification) — The phrase "وقيل معناه" introduces an alternative parsing, where the predicate is re-anchored to a new subject, requiring careful tracking of the implicit pronoun (ḍamīr al-shaʾn).

- Root: أ-ف-ف (a-f-f)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning — dirt under the fingernails (wasakh al-azfār); extended to an expression of disgust or contempt.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In Quranic usage (e.g., {«فَلَا تَقُل لَّهُمَا أُفٍّ»}), it signifies the minimal utterance of annoyance, prohibited as a breach of filial piety; here, it denotes rhetorical rebuke (inkār).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — the physical filth; metaphorical — a verbal particle (ism fiʿl) conveying disdain, not literal speech.
- Sībawayh Rule: Bināʾ al-Ism ʿalā al-Fatḥ (Nominal Construction on Fatha) — The ten dialectal variants of "af" (af, uff, iff, etc.) are parsed as single-letter nouns (asmāʾ afʿāl) built on different vowels, each reflecting phonological principles of taṭwīl (lengthening), takhfīf (lightening), and itbāʿ (vowel harmony).

- Root: أ-ل-ل (a-l-l)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: The spear (al-alah, with fatha on hamza and tashdīd on lām); also, to strike with a spear.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Not a theological term; used here in its concrete, physical sense of affliction by a weapon.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — the spear; metaphorical — the verbal phrase "taribat yadāk wa-alat" as a dual invocation (duʿāʾ), combining a wish for poverty (tarab) and a curse of being struck (al-alah).
- Sībawayh Rule: Idghām and Fakk al-Idghām (Assimilation and Its Dissolution) — The verb "alat" derives from "alaltu" (root: ʾ-l-l), where the original doubled lām is assimilated; fakk (dissolution) is permissible only with the second-person masculine singular object, as in "radadtu" → "radadtu."
chapters.translation:
I say: She (ʿĀʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her) said, "I do not refrain from asking about what I am in need of." And it was said: Its meaning is that Allah does not command shyness in matters of truth, nor does He permit it. Rather, she said this as an apology before her question concerning what necessity had driven her to ask about — matters which women customarily feel shy to ask about and to mention in the presence of men.

In this [narration] there is [proof] that it is incumbent upon one to whom a question presents itself to ask about it, and not to refrain from asking out of shyness of mentioning it. For that is not true shyness (ḥayāʾ), because shyness is all good, and shyness does not bring anything but good. And refraining from asking in this situation is not good; rather, it is evil. So how could it be shyness? The clarification of this matter has already preceded in the opening of the Book of Faith (Kitāb al-Īmān). And ʿĀʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her, said: "Excellent are the women of the Anṣār — shyness did not prevent them from acquiring deep understanding in religion." And Allah knows best.

The scholars of Arabic said: One says "istaḥyā" with a yāʾ before the alif, and "yastaḥyī" with two yāʾs; and it is also said "yastaḥī" with a single yāʾ in the present tense. And Allah knows best.

His saying (she said — ʿĀʾishah said: "I said to her: Uff to you"): Its meaning is belittlement of her and of what she had spoken. It is a word used for contempt, disgust, and disapproval. Al-Bājī said: The intended meaning here is disapproval (inkār). The origin of "uff" is the dirt of the fingernails. In "uff" there are ten dialectal forms: "uff" (with ḍamma on the hamza and kasra on the fāʾ), "uff" (with fatḥa on the fāʾ), "uff" (with ḍamma on the fāʾ) — these three without tanwīn and with tanwīn, making six. The seventh is "if" (with kasra on the hamza and fatḥa on the fāʾ). The eighth is "uf" (with ḍamma on the hamza and sukūn on the fāʾ). The ninth is "ufī" (with ḍamma on the hamza and a yāʾ). And the tenth is "ufih" (with a hāʾ). These dialectal forms are well-known; Ibn al-Anbārī and groups of scholars have mentioned them all, and their evidences are famous. Among the most concise [treatments] is what al-Zajjāj and Ibn al-Anbārī mentioned, which Abū al-Baqāʾ summarized, saying: "Whoever uses kasra built it on the original [pattern]; whoever uses fatḥa sought lightness (takhfīf); whoever uses ḍamma followed [the vowel of the preceding word] (itbāʿ); whoever uses tanwīn intended indefiniteness (tankīr); whoever omits tanwīn intended definiteness (taʿrīf); and whoever lightens the fāʾ has deleted one of the two doubled letters for ease." Al-Akhfash and Ibn al-Anbārī said regarding the ninth form with the yāʾ: It is as if it is an attribution to oneself. And Allah knows best.

His saying (on the authority of Musāfiʿ ibn ʿAbdillāh): He is with ḍamma on the mīm, with an unpointed sīn, and with kasra on the fāʾ.

Her saying ("Taribat yadāk wa-alat"): It is with ḍamma on the hamza, fatḥa on the shaddah'd lām, and sukūn on the tāʾ — thus is the narration. Its meaning: "May the spear (al-alah, with fatḥa on the hamza and tashdīd on the lām) strike you" — and it is the spear (ḥarbah). Some imams rejected this wording and claimed that the correct form is "alalt" with two lāms, the first with kasra and the second with sukūn, and with kasra on the tāʾ. But this rejection is corrupt; rather, whatever is authenticated by narration is correct. Its origin is "alaltu" with kasra on the first lām, fatḥa on the second, and sukūn on the tāʾ — like "radadtu," whose origin is "radadtu." It is not permissible to dissolve this assimilation (fakk al-idghām) except with the second-person [masculine singular] addressee. And the verb "alat" is singular despite the dual "yadāk" (your two hands) for two reasons: First, that she intended the generic sense (jins); and second, [that she meant] "the possessor of the two hands," i.e., "may the spear strike you" — thus combining two invocations (duʿāʾayn). And Allah knows best.

| (Chapter: The Description of the Man's and Woman's Fluid (manī) and That the Child Is Created from Both Fluids)

In it is the ḥadīth of Thawbān, may Allah be pleased with him, concerning the story of the Jewish scholar (ḥibr). The description of the fluid (manī) has already preceded in the previous chapter. As for "ḥibr," it is with fatḥa on the ḥāʾ and kasra on it — two well-known dialectal forms — and it means the learned scholar.

His saying (Abū Asmāʾ al-Raḥabī narrated to me): It is with fatḥa on the rāʾ and the ḥāʾ, and his name is ʿAmr ibn Marthad al-Shāmī al-Dimashqī. Abū Sulaymān ibn Zayd said: Abū Asmāʾ al-Raḥabī was from Raḥbah of Damascus — one of its villages, between it and Damascus a mile [distant]; I saw it inhabited. And Allah knows best.

His saying (The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, drew lines (fanakata) with a stick): It is with fatḥa on the nūn and the kāf, and with a tāʾ with two dots above. Its meaning: He was tracing lines with the stick on the ground and making marks with it. This is what a person deep in thought does. In this is evidence for the permissibility of doing such a thing and that it does not detract from manliness (murūʾah). And Allah knows best.

His saying, may Allah bless him and grant him peace ("They are in the darkness beyond the bridge (al-jisr)"): It is with fatḥa on the jīm and kasra on it — two well-known dialectal forms. The intended meaning here is the Path (al-ṣirāṭ).

His saying, may Allah bless him and grant him peace ("So who is the first of the people to cross (ijāzah)"): It is with kasra on the hamza and with a zāy. Its meaning: passing and crossing over.

His saying ("So what is their gift (tuḥfatuhum)"): It is with sukūn on the ḥāʾ and fatḥa on it — two dialectal forms. It is what is presented to a man, with which he is singled out, and by which he is honored. Ibrāhīm al-Ḥalabī said: It is the choicest part of the fruit. And Allah knows best.

His saying, may Allah bless him and grant him peace ("An extra piece of the liver of the fish (nūn)"): It is "nūn" with two nūns, the first with ḍamma — and it is the fish (ḥūt); its plural is "nīnān." In the other narration: "zāʾidat kabad al-nūn" (an extra piece of the liver of the fish). "Al-ziyādah" and "al-zāʾidah" are one and the same thing — it is the tip of the liver, which is its most delicious part.

His saying ("So what is their nourishment (ghidhāʾuhum)"): It is narrated in two ways: One with kasra on the ghayn and with an unpointed dhāl; the second with fatḥa on the ghayn and with a pointed dāl. Al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ said: This second one is the correct [reading], and it is the narration of the majority. He said: And the first is nothing. I say: It has a valid interpretation — its estimation is "what is their nourishment at that time," and the intent is not a question about their nourishment perpetually. And Allah knows best.

His saying ("Upon its trace (atharihā)"): With kasra on the hamza and sukūn on the thāʾ, and with fatḥa on both — two well-known dialectal forms.

His saying, may Allah bless him and grant him peace ("From a spring therein called Salsabīl"): A group of linguists and exegetes said: Salsabīl is a name for the spring. Mujāhid and others said: It is the intensely flowing [spring]. And it was said: It is the smooth, gentle [spring].

His saying, may Allah bless him and grant him peace ("Male by Allah's permission, and female by Allah's permission"): The meaning of the first is "the child was male," and the meaning of the second is "it was female." And "ānathā" is with madd (prolongation) at its beginning and lightening (takhfīf) of the nūn; and it has been narrated with qaṣr (shortening) and tashdīd of the nūn. And Allah knows best.

| (Chapter: The Description of the Major Ritual Bath (ghusl) from Janābah)

Our companions (aṣḥābunā) said: The perfection of the major ritual bath from janābah is that the bather begins by washing his hands three times before inserting them into the vessel; then he washes off whatever filth is on his genitals and the rest of his body; then he performs the ablution (wuḍūʾ).

chapters.title_en: The Complete Description of the Major Ritual Ablution (Ṣifat al-Ghusl al-Kāmilah) and Its Rulings
chapters.arabic_text:
وضوءه للصلاة بكماله ثم يدخل أصابعه كلها في الماء فيغرف غرفة يخلل بها

أصول شعره من رأسه ولحيته ثم يحثي على رأسه ثلاث حثيات ويتعاهد معاطف بدنه

كالإبطين وداخل الأذنين والسرة وما بين الأليتين وأصابع الرجلين وعكن البطن

وغير ذلك فيوصل الماء إلى جميع ذلك ثم يفيض على رأسه ثلاث حثيات ثم يفيض

الماء على سائر جسده ثلاث مرات يدلك في كل مرة ما تصل إليه يداه من بدنه

وإن كان يغتسل في نهر أو بركة انغمس فيها ثلاث مرات ويوصل الماء إلى جميع

بشرته والشعور الكثيفة والخفيفة ويعم بالغسل ظاهر الشعر وباطنه وأصول

منابته والمستحب أن يبدأ بميامنه وأعالي بدنه وأن يكون مستقبل القبلة وأن

يقول بعد الفراغ أشهد أن لا إله
# 
# إلا الله وحده لا شريك له وأشهد أن محمدا عبده ورسوله وينوي الغسل من أول

شروعه فيما ذكرناه ويستصحب النية إلى أن يفرغ من غسله فهذا كمال الغسل

والواجب من هذا كله النية في أول ملاقاة أول جزء من البدن للماء وتعميم

البدن شعره وبشره بالماء ومن شرطه أن يكون البدن طاهرا من النجاسة وما زاد

على هذا مما ذكرناه سنة وينبغي لمن اغتسل من إناء كالإبريق ونحوه أن يتفطن

لدقيقة قد يغفل عنها وهي أنه إذا استنجى وطهر محل الاستنجاء بالماء فينبغي

أن يغسل محل الاستنجاء بعد ذلك بنية غسل الجنابة لأنه إذا لم يغسله الآن

ربما غفل عنه بعد ذلك فلا يصح غسله لترك ذلك وإن ذكره احتاج إلى مس فرجه

فينتقض وضوءه أو يحتاج إلى كلفة في لف خرقة على يده والله أعلم هذا مذهبنا

ومذهب كثيرين من الأئمة ولم يوجب أحد من العلماء الدلك في الغسل ولا في

الوضوء إلا مالك والمزني ومن سواهما يقول هو سنة لو  تركه صحت طهارته في

الوضوء والغسل ولم يوجب أيضا الوضوء في غسل الجنابة إلا داود الظاهري ومن

سواه يقولون هو سنة فلو أفاض الماء على جميع بدنه من غير وضوء صح غسله

واستباح به الصلاة وغيرها ولكن الأفضل أن يتوضأ كما ذكرنا وتحصل الفضيلة

بالوضوء قبل الغسل أو بعده وإذا توضأ أولا لا يأتي به ثانيا فقد اتفق

العلماء على أنه لا يستحب وضوءان والله أعلم فهذا مختصر ما يتعلق بصفة

الغسل وأحاديث الباب تدل على معظم ما ذكرناه وما بقي فله دلائل مشهورة

والله أعلم واعلم أنه جاء في روايات عائشة رضي الله عنها في صحيح البخاري

ومسلم أنه صلى الله عليه وسلم توضأ وضوءه للصلاة قبل إفاضة الماء عليه

فظاهر هذا أنه صلى الله عليه وسلم أكمل الوضوء بغسل الرجلين وقد جاء في

أكثر روايات ميمونة توضأ ثم أفاض الماء عليه ثم تنحى فغسل رجليه وفي رواية

من حديثها رواها البخاري توضأ وضوءه للصلاة غير قدميه ثم أفاض الماء عليه

ثم نحى قدميه فغسلهما وهذا تصريح بتأخير القدمين وللشافعي رضي الله عنه

قولان أصحهما وأشهرهما والمختار منهما أنه يكمل وضوءه بغسل القدمين والثاني

أنه يؤخر غسل القدمين فعلى القول الضعيف يتأول روايات عائشة وأكثر روايات

ميمونة على أن المراد بوضوء الصلاة أكثره وهو ما سوى الرجلين كما بينته

ميمونة في رواية البخاري فهذه الرواية صريحة وتلك الرواية محتملة للتأويل

فيجمع بينهما بما ذكرناه وأما على المشهور الصحيح فيعمل بظاهر الروايات

المشهورة المستفيضة عن عائشة وميمونة جميعا في تقديم وضوء
# 
# الصلاة فإن ظاهره كمال الوضوء فهذا كان الغالب والعادة المعروفة له صلى

الله عليه وسلم وكان يعيد غسل القدمين بعد الفراغ لإزالة الطين لا لأجل

الجنابة فتكون الرجل مغسولة مرتين وهذا هو الأكمل الأفضل فكان صلى الله

عليه وسلم يواظب عليه وأما رواية البخاري عن ميمونة فجرى ذلك مرة أو نحوها

بيانا للجواز وهذا كما ثبت أنه صلى الله عليه وسلم توضأ ثلاثا ثلاثا ومرة

مرة فكان الثلاث في  معظم الأوقات لكونه الأفضل والمرة في نادر من الأوقات

لبيان الجواز ونظائر هذا كثيرة والله أعلم وأما نية هذا الوضوء فينوي به

رفع الحدث الأصغر إلا أن يكون جنبا غير محدث فإنه ينوي به سنة الغسل والله

أعلم قوله فيدخل أصابعه في أصول الشعر إنما فعل ذلك ليلين الشعر ويرطبه

فيسهل مرور الماء عليه قوله (حتى إذا رأى أنه قد استبرأ حفن على
# 
# رأسه ثلاث حفنات) معنى استبرأ أي أوصل البلل إلى جميعه ومعنى حفن أخذ

الماء بيديه جميعا قولها (أدنيت لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم غسله من

الجنابة) هو بضم الغين وهو الماء الذي يغتسل به قولها (ثم ضرب بيده الأرض

فدلكها دلكا شديدا) فيه أنه يستحب للمستنجي بالماء إذا فرغ أن يغسل يده

بتراب أو أشنان أو يدلكها بالتراب أو بالحائط ليذهب الاستقذار منها قولها

(ثم أفرغ على رأسه ثلاث حفنات ملء كفه) هكذا هو في الأصول التي ببلادنا كفه

بلفظ الإفراد وكذا نقله القاضي عياض عن رواية الأكثرين وفي رواية الطبري

كفيه بالتثنية وهي مفسرة لرواية الأكثرين والحفنة ملء الكفين جميعا قولها

(ثم أتيته بالمنديل فرده) فيه استحباب ترك تنشيف الأعضاء وقد اختلف علماء

أصحابنا في تنشيف الأعضاء في الوضوء والغسل على خمسة أوجه أشهرها أن
chapters.anchors:
- Root: غ-س-ل (gh-s-l)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Washing with water; removing dirt or impurity by flowing water over a surface.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Ritual purification (ṭahārah) from major impurity (janābah); a legal obligation (farḍ) entailing intention (niyyah) and complete coverage of the body.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) — physical washing; metaphorical (majāz) — spiritual purification from sin.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clause (al-Sharṭ wa al-Jawāb) — The protasis (in-sharṭ) governs the apodosis, as in "if he neglects it, his ghusl is invalid."
chapters.translation:
I say: Know that the complete form of the major ablution (ghusl) is that one performs the minor ablution (wuḍūʾ) for prayer in its full perfection, then inserts all his fingers into the water and scoops a single handful, with which he thoroughly wets the roots of his hair — both of his head and his beard — then pours three handfuls over his head, and attends meticulously to the folds of his body, such as the armpits, the inner parts of the ears, the navel, the area between the buttocks, the toes, and the creases of the belly, and similar places, ensuring that the water reaches all of these. Then he pours three handfuls over his head, then pours water over the rest of his body three times, rubbing with each pour whatever parts of his body his hands can reach. If he is bathing in a river or a pool, he immerses himself in it three times, ensuring the water reaches all his skin — both the thick and the thin hair — and he includes in the washing the outer surface of the hair, its inner part, and the roots of its growth.

It is recommended (mustaḥabb) that he begin with his right side and the upper parts of his body, that he face the qiblah, and that he say after finishing: {«أشهد أن لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له وأشهد أن محمدا عبده ورسوله»} ("I bear witness that there is no god but Allah alone, with no partner, and I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and His Messenger"). He should intend the major ablution from the very beginning of what we have mentioned, and he should maintain the intention continuously until he completes his washing. This is the perfection of the ghusl.

The obligatory (wājib) elements of all this are: the intention at the first moment of the first part of the body meeting the water, and the complete coverage of the body — both hair and skin — with water. Among its conditions is that the body be pure from physical impurity (najāsah). Whatever exceeds this of what we have mentioned is Sunnah.

It behooves the one who bathes from a vessel — such as a ewer (ibrīq) and the like — to be attentive to a subtle point that one might overlook: namely, that if he has performed istinjāʾ (cleansing after relieving oneself) and purified the place of istinjāʾ with water, he should then wash that place afterward with the intention of the ghusl of janābah. For if he does not wash it now, he might forget it afterward, and his ghusl would be invalid due to omitting it. And if he remembers it, he would need to touch his private part, which would nullify his wuḍūʾ, or he would need the trouble of wrapping a cloth around his hand. And Allah knows best. This is our school (madhhab) and the school of many of the imams.

None of the scholars made rubbing (dalk) obligatory in the ghusl or in the wuḍūʾ except Mālik and al-Muzanī. All others say it is Sunnah — if one omits it, his purification remains valid in both wuḍūʾ and ghusl. Likewise, none made the wuḍūʾ obligatory in the ghusl of janābah except Dāwūd al-Ẓāhirī. All others say it is Sunnah — so if one pours water over his entire body without performing wuḍūʾ, his ghusl is valid, and he may thereby perform prayer and other acts. However, it is better to perform wuḍūʾ as we have mentioned. The virtue is attained whether the wuḍūʾ is performed before or after the ghusl. If one performs wuḍūʾ first, he does not repeat it afterward — for the scholars are unanimous that two wuḍūʾs are not recommended. And Allah knows best.

This is a summary of what pertains to the description of the ghusl. The hadiths of this chapter indicate most of what we have mentioned, and for the remainder there are well-known evidences. And Allah knows best.

Know that it has come in the narrations of ʿĀʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her, in Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī and Muslim, that the Prophet ﷺ performed the wuḍūʾ for prayer before pouring water over himself. The apparent meaning of this is that he ﷺ completed the wuḍūʾ including the washing of the feet. And it has come in most narrations of Maymūnah that he performed wuḍūʾ, then poured water over himself, then moved aside and washed his feet. In one narration from her, reported by al-Bukhārī: "He performed the wuḍūʾ for prayer except his feet, then poured water over himself, then moved his feet and washed them." This is an explicit statement of delaying the feet.

For al-Shāfiʿī, may Allah be pleased with him, there are two opinions. The more correct (aṣaḥḥ) and more famous (ashhar) of them, and the one chosen (mukhtār), is that he completes his wuḍūʾ by washing the feet. The second is that he delays the washing of the feet. According to the weaker opinion, the narrations of ʿĀʾishah and most narrations of Maymūnah are interpreted to mean that by "the wuḍūʾ for prayer" what is intended is most of it — namely, what is other than the feet — as Maymūnah clarified in al-Bukhārī's narration. Thus, that narration is explicit (ṣarīḥah), while the other is susceptible to interpretation (muʾawwal), and one reconciles between them by what we have mentioned.

As for the well-known and correct opinion, one acts upon the apparent meaning of the well-known and widely transmitted (mustafīḍah) narrations from both ʿĀʾishah and Maymūnah regarding the precedence of the wuḍūʾ for prayer — for its apparent meaning is the completion of the wuḍūʾ. This was the predominant and known custom of the Prophet ﷺ. He would repeat the washing of the feet after finishing to remove mud — not for the sake of janābah — so the foot would be washed twice. This is the most complete and most virtuous, and the Prophet ﷺ would persist upon it. As for al-Bukhārī's narration from Maymūnah, that occurred once or the like, as an indication of permissibility. This is analogous to what is established that the Prophet ﷺ performed wuḍūʾ three times (thulāthā) and once (marrah). The threefold was in most instances because it is superior, and the single was in rare instances to indicate permissibility. There are many parallels to this. And Allah knows best.

As for the intention of this wuḍūʾ: one intends by it the lifting of the minor impurity (ḥadath aṣghar), unless he is in a state of janābah without minor impurity — then he intends by it the Sunnah of the ghusl. And Allah knows best.

His saying — "then he inserted his fingers into the roots of the hair" — he did this only to soften the hair and moisten it, making it easier for the water to pass over it.

His saying — "until when he saw that he had thoroughly wetted it (istabrāʾ), he scooped three handfuls over his head" — the meaning of istabrāʾ is that he delivered the wetness to all of it. The meaning of ḥafana is that he took water with both hands together.

Her saying — "I brought near to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ his water for the ghusl of janābah" — the word ghisl (with ḍammah on the ghayn) is the water with which one performs the ghusl.

Her saying — "then he struck his hand on the ground and rubbed it vigorously" — in this is the recommendation that the one who performs istinjāʾ with water, when he finishes, should wash his hand with soil or cleansing ash (ushnān), or rub it with soil or against a wall, to remove the filth from it.

Her saying — "then he poured over his head three handfuls, the fill of his palm (kafihi)" — thus it is in the manuscripts of our lands: kafihi in the singular form. Al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ likewise transmitted it from the narration of the majority. In al-Ṭabarī's narration it is kafayhi in the dual form, which explains the narration of the majority. And the ḥafnah is the fill of both palms together.

Her saying — "then I brought him a towel and he refused it" — in this is the recommendation of refraining from drying the limbs. The scholars of our companions have differed regarding drying the limbs in wuḍūʾ and ghusl on five views, the most famous of which is...

chapters.title_en: Section 236 — On Drying the Limbs after Ablution, the Recommended Quantity of Water for Major Ritual Purification, and the Ruling on a Man Using the Leftover Water of a Woman
chapters.arabic_text:
المستحب تركه ولا يقال فعله مكروه والثاني أنه مكروه والثالث أنه مباح

يستوي فعله وتركه وهذا هو الذي نختاره فإن المنع والاستحباب يحتاج إلى دليل

ظاهر والرابع أنه مستحب لما فيه من الاحتراز عن الأوساخ والخامس يكره في

الصيف دون الشتاء هذا ما ذكره أصحابنا وقد اختلف الصحابة وغيرهم في التنشيف

على ثلاثة مذاهب أحدها أنه لا بأس به في الوضوء والغسل وهو قول أنس بن مالك

والثوري والثاني مكروه فيهما وهو قول بن عمر وبن أبي ليلى والثالث يكره في

الوضوء دون الغسل وهو قول بن عباس رضي الله عنهما وقد جاء في ترك التنشيف

هذا الحديث والحديث الآخر في الصحيح أنه
# 
# صلى الله عليه وسلم

| (اغتسل وخرج ورأسه  يقطر ماء وأما فعل التنشيف فقد 
# رواه جماعة من الصحابة رضي الله عنهم من أوجه لكن أسانيدها ضعيفة قال

الترمذي لا يصح في هذا الباب عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم شئ وقد احتج بعض

العلماء على إباحة التنشيف بقول ميمونة في هذا الحديث وجعل يقول بالماء

هكذا يعني ينفضه قال فإذا كان النفض مباحا كان التنشيف مثله أو أولى

لاشتراكهما في إزالة الماء والله أعلم وأما المنديل فبكسر الميم وهو معروف

وقال بن فارس لعله مأخوذ من الندل وهو النقل وقال غيره هو مأخوذ من الندل

وهو الوسخ لأنه يندل به ويقال تندلت بالمنديل قال الجوهري ويقال أيضا

تمندلت به وأنكرها الكسائي والله أعلم قولها (وجعل يقول بالماء هكذا يعني

ينفضه) فيه دليل على أن نفض اليد بعد الوضوء والغسل لا بأس به وقد اختلف

أصحابنا فيه على أوجه أشهرها أن المستحب تركه ولا يقال أنه مكروه والثاني

أنه مكروه والثالث أنه مباح يستوي فعله وتركه وهذا هو الأظهر المختار فقد

جاء هذا الحديث الصحيح في الإباحة ولم يثبت في النهي شئ أصلا والله أعلم

قوله (وحدثنا محمد بن المثنى العنزي) هو بفتح العين والنون وبالزاي)
# 
# قولها (دعا بشئ نحو الحلاب) هو بكسر الحاء وتخفيف اللام وآخره باء موحدة

وهو إناء يحلب فيه ويقال له المحلب أيضا بكسر الميم قال الخطابي هو إناء

يسع قدر حلبة ناقة وهذا هو المشهور الصحيح المعروف في الرواية وذكر الهروي

عن الأزهري أنه الجلاب بضم الجيم وتشديد اللام قال الأزهري وأراد به ماء

الورد وهو فارسي معرب وأنكر الهروي هذا وقال أراه الحلاب وذكر نحو ما

قدمناه والله أعلم
#

| (باب القدر المستحب من الماء في غسل الجنابة)
# (وغسل الرجل والمرأة في إناء واحد وغسل أحدهما بفضل الآخر) أجمع المسلمون

على أن الماء الذي يجزئ في الوضوء والغسل غير مقدر بل يكفي فيه القليل

والكثير إذا وجد شرط الغسل وهو جريان الماء على الأعضاء قال الشافعي رحمه

الله تعالى وقد يرفق بالقليل فيكفي ويخرق  بالكثير فلا يكفي قال العلماء

والمستحب ان لاينقص في الغسل عن صاع ولافي الوضوء عن مد والصاع خمسة أرطال

وثلث بالبغدادي والمد رطل وثلث ذلك معتبر على التقريب لاعلى التحديد وهذا

هو الصواب المشهور وذكر جماعة من أصحابنا وجها لبعض أصحابنا أن الصاع هنا

ثمانية أرطال والمد رطلان وأجمع العلماء على النهي عن الإسراف في الماء ولو

كان على شاطيء البحر والأظهر أنه مكروه كراهة تنزيه وقال بعض أصحابنا

الإسراف حرام والله أعلم وأما تطهير الرجل والمرأة من إناء واحد فهو جائز

بإجماع المسلمين لهذه الأحاديث التي في الباب وأما تطهير المرأة بفضل الرجل

فجائز بالإجماع أيضا وأما تطهير الرجل بفضلها فهو جائز عندنا وعند مالك

وأبي حنيفة وجماهير العلماء سواء خلت به أو لم تخل قال بعض أصحابنا ولا

كراهة في ذلك للأحاديث الصحيحة الواردة به وذهب أحمد بن حنبل وداود إلى

أنها إذا خلت بالماء واستعملته لا يجوز للرجل استعمال فضلها وروي هذاعن عبد

الله بن سرجس والحسن البصري وروي عن أحمد رحمه الله تعالى كمذهبنا وروي عن

الحسن
# 
# وسعيد بن المسيب كراهة فضلها مطلقا والمختار ما قاله الجماهير لهذه

الأحاديث الصحيحة في تطهيره صلى الله عليه وسلم مع أزواجه وكل واحد منهما

يستعمل فضل صاحبه ولا تأثير للخلوة وقد ثبت في الحديث الآخر أنه صلى الله

عليه وسلم اغتسل بفضل بعض أزواجه رواه أبو داود والترمذي والنسائي وأصحاب

السنن قال الترمذي هو حديث حسن صحيح وأما الحديث الذي جاء بالنهي وهو حديث

الحكم بن عمرو فأجاب العلماء عنه بأجوبة أحدها أنه ضعيف ضعفه أئمة الحديث

منهم البخاري وغيره الثاني أن المراد النهي عن فضل أعضائها وهو المتساقط

منها وذلك مستعمل الثالث أن النهي للاستحباب والأفضل والله أعلم قوله

(الفرق) قال سفيان هو ثلاثة آصع أما كونه ثلاثة آصع فكذا قاله الجماهير وهو

بفتح الفاء وفتح الراء وإسكانها لغتان حكاهما بن دريد وجماعة غيره والفتح

أفصح وأشهر وزعم الباجي أنه الصواب وليس كما قال بل هما لغتان وأما  قوله

ثلاثة آصع فصحيح فصيح وقد جهل من أنكر هذا وزعم أنه لا يجوز إلا أصوع وهذه

منه غفلة بينة أو جهالة ظاهرة فإنه يجوز أصوع وآصع فالأول هو الأصل والثاني
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ن-ش-ف (n-sh-f)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To dry, to absorb moisture; drying (tanashshuf) of the limbs after ablution.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Pertains to the removal of residual water from the body, a matter of ritual practice (fiʿl) rather than creedal import.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) — physical drying; no metaphorical extension here.
- Root: ف-ض-ل (f-ḍ-l)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Excess, surplus, leftover; the remaining portion of water after use.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In juristic context, surplus water (faḍl) carries rulings of purity (ṭahārah) and permissibility.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — leftover quantity; metaphorically extended to "merit" but not in this ritual context.
- Root: ص-ع (ṣ-ʿ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: A specific volumetric measure; a unit of capacity.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In fiqh, the ṣāʿ is a standard measure for ritual quantities, approximating five and one-third Baghdadi ratls.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — a defined measure; not metaphorical.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional and Exceptive Constructions (al-sharṭ wa al-istithnāʾ) — The text employs conditional clauses (e.g., "if the condition of washing is met") and exceptions ("no prohibition is established at all") requiring precise parsing to distinguish obligation, recommendation, and permissibility.
chapters.translation:
I say: Know that the scholars of our school (al-Shāfiʿiyyah) have differed concerning the drying of the limbs after ablution and major ritual purification (ghusl) on five well-known positions. The first is that it is recommended to leave it, yet it is not said that doing it is disliked (makrūh). The second is that it is disliked. The third is that it is permissible (mubāḥ), such that doing it and leaving it are equal — and this is the position we choose, for prohibition and recommendation both require an evident proof (dalīl ẓāhir). The fourth is that it is recommended, due to what it contains of guarding against filth. The fifth is that it is disliked in summer but not in winter. This is what our companions have mentioned.

The Companions (ṣaḥābah) and others have differed concerning drying on three schools: First, that there is no harm in it in both ablution (wuḍūʾ) and ghusl — this is the saying of Anas ibn Mālik and al-Thawrī. Second, that it is disliked in both — this is the saying of Ibn ʿUmar and Ibn Abī Laylā. Third, that it is disliked in ablution but not in ghusl — this is the saying of Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with them both. Concerning leaving off drying, this ḥadīth has come, and in the other ḥadīth in the Ṣaḥīḥ, that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, {«اغتسل وخرج ورأسه يقطر ماء»} (performed ghusl and came out with his head dripping with water). As for the act of drying, a group of the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, have narrated it through various chains, but their chains of transmission (asānīd) are weak. Al-Tirmidhī said: "Nothing is authentic in this chapter from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace." Some scholars have argued for the permissibility of drying by the saying of Maymūnah in this ḥadīth: "And he began to say with the water like this" — meaning he was shaking it off. He said: "If shaking off is permissible, then drying is like it or more fitting, since both share in the removal of water." And Allah knows best.

As for the word "al-mindīl" (towel), it is with a kasrah on the mīm, and it is well-known. Ibn Fāris said: "Perhaps it is derived from al-nadl, which means transferring." Another said: "It is derived from al-nadl, which means filth, because one removes filth with it." It is said: "tanaddaltu bi-al-mindīl" (I dried myself with the towel). Al-Jawharī said: "It is also said: tamandaltu bihī," but al-Kisāʾī rejected this. And Allah knows best.

Her saying: "And he began to say with the water like this" — meaning he was shaking it off — contains evidence that shaking the hand after ablution and ghusl is permissible. Our companions have differed on it in several aspects, the most famous being that it is recommended to leave it, and it is not said that it is disliked. The second is that it is disliked. The third is that it is permissible, with doing and leaving being equal — and this is the more apparent and chosen view, for this authentic ḥadīth has come regarding permissibility, and nothing at all has been established regarding prohibition. And Allah knows best.

His saying: "And narrated to us Muḥammad ibn al-Muthannā al-ʿAnazī" — it is with a fatḥah on the ʿayn and nūn, and with a zāy.

Her saying: "He called for something like a milking vessel (al-ḥilāb)" — it is with a kasrah on the ḥāʾ, a tashdīd-free lām, and its final letter is a single bāʾ. It is a vessel in which one milks, and it is also called al-miḥlab, with a kasrah on the mīm. Al-Khaṭṭābī said: "It is a vessel that holds the measure of one milking of a she-camel." This is the well-known, correct, and established version in the narration. Al-Harawī mentioned from al-Azharī that it is al-jullāb, with a ḍammah on the jīm and a shaddah on the lām. Al-Azharī said: "He meant rosewater, and it is an Arabized Persian word." Al-Harawī rejected this and said: "I consider it to be al-ḥilāb," mentioning something similar to what we have stated. And Allah knows best.

Chapter: The Recommended Quantity of Water in Ghusl for Major Impurity (Janābah), and the Washing of a Man and Woman from a Single Vessel, and the Washing of One with the Leftover of the Other.

The Muslims are in consensus (ijmāʿ) that the water sufficient for ablution and ghusl is not fixed by a specific measure; rather, a small or large amount suffices when the condition of washing is met, namely the flowing of water over the limbs. Al-Shāfiʿī, may Allah the Exalted have mercy on him, said: "Sometimes a small amount suffices, and sometimes a large amount fails to suffice." The scholars said: It is recommended that the ghusl not be less than a ṣāʿ, and the ablution not less than a mudd. The ṣāʿ is five and one-third Baghdadi ratls, and the mudd is one and one-third of that. This is considered approximately, not as a fixed limit — and this is the correct and well-known view. A group of our companions mentioned a position of some of our companions that the ṣāʿ here is eight ratls and the mudd is two ratls. The scholars are in consensus on the prohibition of extravagance (isrāf) in water, even if one is on the shore of the sea. The more apparent view is that it is disliked with a dislike of tanzīh (recommendation to avoid). Some of our companions said: "Extravagance is forbidden (ḥarām)." And Allah knows best.

As for the purification of a man and woman from a single vessel, it is permissible by the consensus of the Muslims, due to these ḥadīths in this chapter. As for the purification of a woman with the leftover of a man, it is permissible by consensus as well. As for the purification of a man with her leftover, it is permissible in our school, and with Mālik, Abū Ḥanīfah, and the majority of scholars — whether she was alone with it or not. Some of our companions said: "There is no dislike in that, due to the authentic ḥadīths narrated concerning it." Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal and Dāwūd held that if she was alone with the water and used it, it is not permissible for a man to use her leftover. This has been narrated from ʿAbdullāh ibn Sarjis and al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī. It has also been narrated from Aḥmad, may Allah the Exalted have mercy on him, in accordance with our school, and from al-Ḥasan and Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab a dislike of her leftover absolutely. The chosen view is what the majority have said, due to these authentic ḥadīths concerning the purification of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, with his wives, each one of them using the leftover of the other, and being alone with it has no effect. It has been established in the other ḥadīth that he, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, performed ghusl with the leftover of one of his wives — narrated by Abū Dāwūd, al-Tirmidhī, al-Nasāʾī, and the authors of the Sunan. Al-Tirmidhī said: "It is a ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ ḥadīth." As for the ḥadīth that came with prohibition — namely the ḥadīth of al-Ḥakam ibn ʿAmr — the scholars have answered it with several responses: First, that it is weak, and the imams of ḥadīth have declared it weak, among them al-Bukhārī and others. Second, that the intended meaning is the prohibition of the leftover of her limbs, which is what falls from her, and that is used water. Third, that the prohibition is one of recommendation and preference. And Allah knows best.

His saying: "al-faraq" — Sufyān said: "It is three āṣāʿ (plural of ṣāʿ)." As for it being three āṣāʿ, this is what the majority have said. It is with a fatḥah on the fāʾ and a fatḥah on the rāʾ, and its sukūn is a second permissible pronunciation — two dialects, as narrated by Ibn Durayd and a group of others. The fatḥah is more eloquent and more famous. Al-Bājī claimed that it is the correct one, but it is not as he said; rather, both are dialects. As for his saying "three āṣāʿ," it is correct and eloquent. Whoever denied this and claimed that only "aṣwuʿ" is permissible has committed a clear oversight or an apparent ignorance, for both "aṣwuʿ" and "āṣāʿ" are permissible — the first being the original form and the second being...
