chapters.arabic_text:
لسانه وشفتيه معناه كان كثيرا ما يفعل ذلك وقيل معناه هذا شأنه ودأبه قوله

عز وجل فإذا قرأناه أي قرأه جبريل عليه السلام ففيه إضافة ما يكون عن أمر

الله تعالى إليه قوله فيشتد عليه وفي الرواية الأخرى يعالج من التنزيل شدة

سبب الشدة هيبة الملك وما جاء به وثقل الوحي قال الله تعالى إنا سنلقي عليك

قولا ثقيلا والمعالجة المحاولة للشيء والمشقة في تحصيله قوله فكان ذلك يعرف

منه يعني يعرفه من رآه لما يظهر على وجهه وبدنه من أثره كما قالت عائشة رضي

الله عنها ولقد رأيته ينزل عليه في اليوم الشديد البرد فيفصم عنه وإن جبينه

ليتفصد عرقا قوله فاستمع له وأنصت الاستماع
# 
# الإصغاء له والإنصات السكوت فقد يستمع ولا ينصت فلهذا جمع بينهما كما قال

الله تعالى فاستمعوا له وأنصتوا قال الأزهري يقال أنصت ونصت وانتصت ثلاث

لغات أفصحهن أنصت وبها جاء القرآن العزيز

| (باب الجهر بالقراءة في الصبح والقراءة على الجن)
# قوله سوق عكاظ هو بضم العين وبالظاء المعجمة يصرف ولا يصرف والسوق تؤنث

وتذكر لغتان قيل سميت بذلك لقيام الناس فيها على سوقهم قوله عن بن عباس رضي

الله عنهما قال ما قرأ رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم على الجن وما رآهم

وذكر بعده حديث بن مسعود رضي الله عنه عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال

أتاني داعي الجن فذهبت معه فقرأت عليهم القرآن قال العلماء هما قضيتان

فحديث بن عباس في أول الأمر وأول النبوة حين أتوا فسمعوا قراءة قل أوحى

واختلف المفسرون هل علم النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم استماعهم حال استماعهم

بوحي أوحي إليه أم لم يعلم بهم إلا بعد ذلك واما حديث بن مسعود فقضية أخرى

جرت بعد ذلك بزمان الله أعلم بقدره وكان بعد اشتهار الإسلام قوله وقد حيل

بين الشياطين وبين خبر السماء  وأرسلت الشهب عليهم ظاهر هذا الكلام أن هذا

حدث بعد نبوة نبينا صلى الله عليه وسلم ولم يكن قبلها ولهذا أنكرته

الشياطين وارتاعت له وضربوا مشارق الأرض ومغاربها ليعرفوا خبره ولهذا كانت

الكهانة فاشية في العرب حتى قطع بين الشياطين وبين صعود السماء واستراق

السمع كما أخبر الله تعالى عنهم أنهم قالوا وأنا
# 
# لمسنا السماء فوجدناها ملئت حرسا شديدا وشهبا وأنا كنا نقعد منها مقاعد

للسمع فمن يستمع الآن يجد له شهابا رصدا وقد جاءت أشعار العرب باستغرابهم

رميها لكونهم لم يعهدوه قبل النبوة وكان رميها من دلائل النبوة وقال جماعة

من العلماء مازالت الشهب منذ كانت الدنيا وهو قول بن عباس والزهري وغيرهما

وقد جاء ذلك في أشعار العرب وروى فيه بن عباس رضي الله عنهما حديثا قيل

للزهري فقد قال الله تعالى فمن يستمع الآن يجدله شهابا رصدا فقال كانت

الشهب قليلة فغلظ أمرها وكثرت حين بعث نبينا صلى الله عليه وسلم وقال

المفسرون نحو هذا وذكروا أن الرمي بها وحراسة السماء كانت موجودة قبل

النبوة ومعلومة ولكن إنما كانت تقع عند حدوث أمر عظيم من عذاب ينزل بأهل

الأرض أو إرسال رسول إليهم وعليه تأولوا قوله تعالى وأنا لا ندري أشر أريد

بمن في الأرض أم أراد بهم ربهم رشدا وقيل كانت الشهب قبل مرئية ومعلومة لكن

رجم الشياطين واحراقهم لم يكن الابعد نبوة نبينا صلى الله عليه وسلم

واختلفوا في إعراب قوله تعالى رجوما وفي معناه فقيل هو مصدر فتكون الكواكب

هي الراجمة المحرقة بشهبها لا بأنفسها وقيل هو اسم فتكون هي بأنفسها التي

يرجم بها ويكون رجوم جمع رجم بفتح الراء والله أعلم قوله فاضربوا مشارق

الأرض ومغاربها معناه سيروا فيها كلها ومنه قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم لا

يخرج الرجلان يضربان الغائط كاشفين عن عوراتهما يتحدثان فإن الله
# 
# تعالى يمقت على ذلك قوله فمر النفر الذين أخذوا نحو تهامة وهو بنخل هكذا

وقع في مسلم بنخل بالخاء المعجمة وصوابه بنخلة بالهاء وهو موضع معروف  هناك

كذا جاء صوابه في صحيح البخاري ويحتمل أنه يقال فيه نخل ونخلة وأما تهامة

فبكسر التاء وهو اسم لكل ما نزل عن نجد من بلاد الحجاز ومكة من تهامة قال

بن فارس في المجمل سميت تهامة من التهم بفتح التاء والهاء وهو شدة الحر

وركود الريح وقال صاحب المطالع سميت بذلك لتغير هوائها يقال تهم الدهن إذا

تغير وذكر الحازمي أنه يقال في أرض تهامة تهائم قوله وهو يصلي بأصحابه صلاة

الصبح فلما سمعوا القرآن قالوا هذا الذي حال بيننا وبين السماء فيه الجهر

بالقراءة في الصبح وفيه إثبات صلاة الجماعة وأنها مشروعة في السفر وأنها

كانت مشروعة من أول النبوة قال الإمام أبو عبد الله المازري ظاهر الحديث

أنهم آمنوا عند سماع القرآن ولا بد لمن آمن عند سماعه أن يعلم حقيقة

الإعجاز وشروط المعجزة وبعد ذلك يقع له العلم بصدق الرسول فيكون الجن علموا

ذلك من كتب الرسل المتقدمين قبلهم على أنه هو النبي الصادق المبشر به واتفق

العلماء على أن الجن يعذبون في الآخرة على المعاصي قال الله تعالى لأملأن

جهنم من الجنة والناس أجمعين واختلفوا في أن مؤمنهم ومطيعهم هل يدخل الجنة
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ل-س-ن (l-s-n)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: The tongue; extended to speech and utterance.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The physical organ and, metaphorically, the faculty of articulated expression.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for the organ; majāz for "manner of speaking" (as in "his tongue and lips" = his habitual practice).
- Root: ع-ل-ج (ʿ-l-j)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To treat, handle, or grapple with something; to strive in managing a matter.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The exertion of effort against resistance; in revelation context, the Prophet's struggle to receive and retain the divine word.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for physical handling; majāz for enduring hardship in acquiring something.
- Root: ن-ص-ت (n-ṣ-t)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Silence; to be quiet and attentive.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The state of hushed stillness prerequisite to true listening.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Distinct from istimāʿ (listening); inṣāt is the silence that accompanies it — hence the pairing in the Quranic command.
- Root: ش-ه-ب (sh-h-b)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: A meteor or shooting star; a flame of fire with a white-hot core.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The celestial missiles hurled at eavesdropping devils; a sign of prophetic mission.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for the fiery body; majāz for the divine act of repulsion through it.
- Sībawayh Rule: Masdar vs. Ism (Verbal Noun vs. Noun) — In the parsing of {«رُجُومًا»}, the word may be a masdar (yielding "the stars are the agents that burn by their meteors") or a plural noun (yielding "the stars themselves are the projectiles"), each altering the grammatical agency of the subject.
chapters.translation:
I say: His statement "his tongue and his lips" means that he (peace and blessings be upon him) did this frequently. And it is said its meaning is: this was his constant habit and practice.

His statement — He, Glorified and Exalted, said: {«فَإِذَا قَرَأْنَاهُ»} — "And when We have recited it" — i.e., when Gabriel (peace be upon him) recited it. In this there is an attribution to God of that which occurs by His command.

His statement "it became severe upon him" — and in the other narration, "he would struggle (yuʿāliju) with the descent of revelation in severity" — the cause of the severity is the awe of the angel and what he brought, and the weight of revelation. God, Exalted, said: {«إِنَّا سَنُلْقِي عَلَيْكَ قَوْلًا ثَقِيلًا»} — "Indeed, We will cast upon you a heavy word." And al-muʿālajah is the striving for a thing and the hardship in its acquisition.

His statement "and that was known from him" — i.e., whoever saw him knew it, due to what appeared on his face and body of its trace, as ʿĀʾishah (may God be pleased with her) said: "Indeed, I saw him when revelation descended upon him on an intensely cold day, and it would cease from him while his forehead dripped with sweat."

His statement "so listen to it and be silent (fa-stamiʿ lahu wa-anṣit)" — al-istimāʿ is the inclining of the ear to it, and al-inṣāt is silence. For one may listen without being silent, and therefore both are combined, as God, Exalted, said: {«فَاسْتَمِعُوا لَهُ وَأَنْصِتُوا»} — "So listen to it and be silent." Al-Azharī said: One says anṣata, naṣata, and intaṣata — three dialects, the most eloquent of which is anṣata, and with it came the Mighty Quran.

(Chapter: On Audible Recitation in the Dawn Prayer and Recitation to the Jinn)

His statement "the market of ʿUkāẓ" — it is with ḍammah on the ʿayn and with the dotted ẓāʾ; it is declined and not declined. The market is feminine and masculine — two dialects. It is said it was so named because the people stood therein upon their wares.

His statement, on the authority of Ibn ʿAbbās (may God be pleased with them both): "The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) did not recite to the Jinn, nor did he see them." And he mentioned after it the hadith of Ibn Masʿūd (may God be pleased with him) from the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him), who said: "The caller of the Jinn came to me, so I went with him and recited the Quran to them."

The scholars said: These are two separate events. The hadith of Ibn ʿAbbās pertains to the beginning of the matter and the beginning of prophethood, when they came and heard the recitation of {«قُلْ أُوحِيَ»} — "Say: It has been revealed." And the commentators differed as to whether the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) knew of their listening at the time of their listening through revelation sent to him, or whether he did not know of them except afterward. As for the hadith of Ibn Masʿūd, it is another event that occurred after that by a period of time — God knows best its extent — and it was after the spread of Islam.

His statement "and a barrier was placed between the devils and the news of the heaven, and the shooting stars were sent against them" — the apparent meaning of this speech is that this occurred after the prophethood of our Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him), and it was not before it. For this reason the devils denied it and were alarmed by it, and they struck the easts and wests of the earth to learn of his affair. And for this reason soothsaying was widespread among the Arabs until the barrier was placed between the devils and the ascent to heaven and the eavesdropping, as God, Exalted, informed of them, that they said: {«وَأَنَّا لَمَسْنَا السَّمَاءَ فَوَجَدْنَاهَا مُلِئَتْ حَرَسًا شَدِيدًا وَشُهُبًا وَأَنَّا كُنَّا نَقْعُدُ مِنْهَا مَقَاعِدَ لِلسَّمْعِ فَمَنْ يَسْتَمِعِ الْآنَ يَجِدْ لَهُ شِهَابًا رَصَدًا»} — "And we touched the heaven and found it filled with mighty guards and meteors, and we used to sit therein in positions for listening. But whoever listens now finds for him a meteor in wait."

And the poems of the Arabs have come down expressing their astonishment at this pelting, because they had not witnessed it before prophethood. And its pelting was among the proofs of prophethood. And a group of scholars said: The shooting stars have never ceased since the world was — and this is the saying of Ibn ʿAbbās, al-Zuhrī, and others. And this has come in the poems of the Arabs. And Ibn ʿAbbās (may God be pleased with them both) narrated a hadith concerning it.

It was said to al-Zuhrī: But God, Exalted, said: {«فَمَنْ يَسْتَمِعِ الْآنَ يَجِدْ لَهُ شِهَابًا رَصَدًا»} — "But whoever listens now finds for him a meteor in wait." He said: The shooting stars were few, then their matter intensified and they multiplied when our Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) was sent. And the commentators said something similar, and they mentioned that the pelting with them and the guarding of the heaven existed before prophethood and was known — but it only occurred upon the advent of a great matter, whether a punishment descending upon the people of the earth or the sending of a messenger to them. And upon this they interpreted His statement, Exalted: {«وَأَنَّا لَا نَدْرِي أَشَرٌّ أُرِيدَ بِمَنْ فِي الْأَرْضِ أَمْ أَرَادَ بِهِمْ رَبُّهُمْ رَشَدًا»} — "And we do not know whether evil is intended for those on earth or whether their Lord intends for them right guidance."

And it was said: The shooting stars were previously visible and known, but the stoning of the devils and their burning did not occur except after the prophethood of our Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him).

And they differed concerning the parsing of His statement, Exalted: {«رُجُومًا»} — "as projectiles" — and its meaning. It is said it is a verbal noun (maṣdar), in which case the stars are the agents that burn by their meteors, not by themselves. And it is said it is a noun (ism), in which case they themselves are that with which one is pelted, and rujūm is the plural of rajmun with fatḥah on the rāʾ. And God knows best.

His statement "so they struck the easts of the earth and its wests" — its meaning is: they traveled throughout it entirely. And from it is his statement (peace and blessings be upon him): "Two men shall not go out to relieve themselves, exposing their private parts while conversing, for God, Exalted, abhors that."

His statement "and the group that headed toward Tihāmah passed by — and it was at Nakhl" — thus it occurred in Muslim as "Nakhl" with the dotted khāʾ, and the correct form is "Nakhlah" with the hāʾ, which is a well-known place there. Thus it came correctly in Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī. And it is possible that both "Nakhl" and "Nakhlah" are said of it. As for Tihāmah, it is with kasrah on the tāʾ, and it is a name for everything that descends from Najd of the lands of the Ḥijāz, and Makkah is of Tihāmah. Ibn Fāris said in al-Mujmal: "Tihāmah was named from al-tahm (with fatḥah on the tāʾ and hāʾ), which is the intensity of heat and the stillness of wind." And the author of al-Maṭāliʿ said: "It was so named for the change of its air; one says tahima al-duhn (the oil changed) when it alters." And al-Ḥāzimī mentioned that one says of the land of Tihāmah: tahāʾim.

His statement "while he was praying the dawn prayer with his companions, and when they heard the Quran they said: 'This is what has barred us from heaven'" — in this is the audibility of recitation in the dawn prayer, and in it is the affirmation of congregational prayer, that it is legislated in travel, and that it was legislated from the beginning of prophethood.

Imam Abū ʿAbd Allāh al-Māzarī said: The apparent meaning of the hadith is that they believed upon hearing the Quran. And it is necessary for one who believes upon hearing it to know the reality of the inimitability (iʿjāz) and the conditions of the miracle, and after that the knowledge of the truthfulness of the messenger occurs to him. Thus the Jinn knew that from the books of the previous messengers before them — that he is the truthful prophet announced to them. And the scholars are agreed that the Jinn are punished in the Hereafter for disobedience. God, Exalted, said: {«لَأَمْلَأَنَّ جَهَنَّمَ مِنَ الْجِنَّةِ وَالنَّاسِ أَجْمَعِينَ»} — "I will surely fill Hell with the Jinn and mankind together." And they differed as to whether their believers and obedient ones enter Paradise.

chapters.title_en: Section 282 — On the Fate of the People of the Interval (Ahl al-Fatrah), the Night of the Jinn, and the Recitation in the Ẓuhr and ʿAṣr Prayers
chapters.arabic_text:
وينعم بها ثوابا ومجازاة له على طاعته أم لا يدخلون بل يكون ثوابهم أن

ينجوا من النار ثم يقال كونوا ترابا كالبهائم وهذا مذهب بن أبي سليم وجماعة

والصحيح أنهم يدخلونها وينعمون فيها بالأكل والشرب وغيرهما وهذا قول الحسن

البصري والضحاك ومالك بن أنس وبن أبي ليلى وغيرهم وقوله (سألت بن مسعود هل

شهد أحد منكم مع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ليلة الجن قال لا) هذا صريح

في إبطال الحديث المروي في سنن أبي داود وغيره المذكور فيه الوضوء بالنبيذ

وحضور بن مسعود معه صلى الله عليه وسلم ليلة الجن فإن هذا الحديث صحيح

وحديث النبيذ ضعيف باتفاق المحدثين ومداره على زيد
# 
# مولى عمرو بن حريث وهو مجهول قوله (استطير أو اغتيل) معنى استطير طارت به

الجن ومعنى اغتيل قتل سرا  والغيلة بكسر الغين هي القتل في خفية قال

الدارقطني انتهى حديث بن مسعود عند قوله فأرانا آثارهم وآثار نيرانهم وما

بعده من قول الشعبي كذا رواه أصحاب داود الراوي عن الشعبي وبن علية وبن

زريع وبن أبي زائدة وبن إدريس وغيرهم هكذا قاله الدارقطني وغيره ومعنى قوله

إنه من كلام الشعبي أنه ليس مرويا عن بن مسعود بهذا الحديث وإلا فالشعبي لا

يقول هذا الكلام إلا بتوقيف عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم والله أعلم قوله

(لكم كل عظم ذكر اسم الله عليه) قال بعض العلماء هذا لمؤمنيهم وأما غيرهم

فجاء في حديث آخر أن طعامهم مالم يذكر اسم الله
# 
# عليه قوله (وددت أني كنت معه) فيه الحرص على مصاحبة أهل الفضل في أسفارهم

ومهماتهم ومشاهدهم ومجالسهم مطلقا والتأسف على فوات ذلك قوله (آذنت بهم

شجرة) هذا دليل على أن الله تعالى يجعل فيما يشاء من الجماد تمييزا ونظيره

قول الله تعالى وإن منها لما يهبط من خشية الله وقوله تعالى وان من شئ

الايسبح بحمده ولكن لا تفقهون تسبيحهم وقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم إني لأعرف

حجرا بمكة كان يسلم علي وحديث الشجرتين اللتين أتتاه صلى الله عليه وسلم

وقد ذكره مسلم في آخر الكتاب وحديث حنين الجذع وتسبيح الطعام وفرار حجر

موسى بثوبه ورجعان حراء وأحد والله أعلم

| (باب القراءة في الظهر والعصر)
# قوله في حديث أبي قتادة رضي الله عنه (أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان

يقرأ في الركعتين
# 
# الأوليين بفاتحة الكتاب وسورتين ويسمعنا الآية أحياناويقرأ في الركعتين

الأخريين بفاتحة الكتاب) وفي رواية أبي سعيد رضي الله عنه (كان يقرأ في كل

ركعة من الأوليين قدر ثلاثين آية وفي الأخريين قدر خمس عشرة آية أو قال نصف

ذلك وفي العصر في الركعتين الأوليين في
# 
# كل ركعة قدر قراءة خمس عشرة وفي الأخريين قدر نصف ذلك) وفي حديث سعد

(أركد في الأوليين وأحذف في الأخريين) وفي حديث أبي سعيد الآخر قال (لقد

كانت صلاة الظهر تقام فيذهب  الذاهب إلى البقيع فيقضي حاجته ثم يتوضأ ثم

يأتي ورسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في الركعة
# 
# الأولى مما يطولها) وفي أحاديث أخر في غير الباب وهي في الصحيحين أن

النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان أخف الناس صلاة في تمام وأنه صلى الله عليه

وسلم قال إني لأدخل في الصلاة أريد إطالتها فأسمع بكاء الصبي فأتجوز في

صلاتي مخافة أن تفتتن أمه قال العلماء كانت صلاة رسول الله صلى الله عليه

وسلم تختلف في الإطالة والتخفيف باختلاف الأحوال فإذا كان المأمومون يؤثرون

التطويل ولا شغل هناك له ولا لهم طول وإذا لم يكن كذلك خفف وقد يريد

الإطالة ثم يعرض ما يقتضي التخفيف كبكاء الصبي ونحوه وينضم إلى هذا أنه قد

يدخل في الصلاة في أثناء الوقت فيخفف وقيل إنما طول في بعض الأوقات وهو

الأقل وخفف في معظمها فالإطالة لبيان جوازها والتخفيف لأنه الأفضل وقد أمر

صلى الله عليه وسلم بالتخفيف وقال إن منكم منفرين فأيكم صلى بالناس فليخفف

فإن فيهم السقيم والضعيف وذا الحاجة وقيل طول في وقت وخفف في وقت ليبين أن

القراءة فيما زاد على الفاتحة لا تقدير فيها من حيث الاشتراط بل يجوز

قليلها وكثيرها وإنما المشترط الفاتحة ولهذا اتفقت الروايات عليها واختلف

فيما زاد وعلى الجملة السنة التخفيف كما أمر به النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

للعلة التي بينها وإنما طول في بعض الأوقات لتحققه انتفاء العلة فإن تحقق

أحد انتفاء العلة طول قوله وكان يقرأ بفاتحة الكتاب وسورتين فيه دليل لما

قاله أصحابنا وغيرهم أن قراءة سورة قصيرة بكمالها أفضل من قراءة قدرها من

طويلة لان المستحب للقارئ ان يبتدىء من أول الكلام المرتبط ويقف عند انتهاء

المرتبط وقد يخفى الارتباط على أكثر الناس أو كثير فندب منهم إلى إكمال

السورة ليحترز عن الوقوف دون الارتباط وأما اختلاف الرواية في السورة في

الأخريين فلعل سببه ما ذكرناه من اختلاف إطالة الصلاة وتخفيفها بحسب

الأحوال وقد اختلف العلماء في استحباب قراءة السورة في  الأخريين من

الرباعية والثالثة من المغرب فقيل بالاستحباب وبعدمه وهما قولان للشافعي

رحمه الله تعالى قال الشافعي ولو أدرك المسبوق الأخريين أتى بالسورة في
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ن-ع-م (n-ʿ-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning of softness, ease, and abundant provision; in the Hereafter, denotes perpetual felicity.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In Kalām, naʿīm is the ontological state of bliss granted by divine grace (faḍl), not by merited right.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) for sensory delights; metaphorical (majāz) when applied to spiritual contentment.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clause with Amr (Command) — "كونوا ترابا" is an imperative functioning as a declarative of divine decree, parsed as inshāʾ with the force of khabar.
chapters.translation:
I say: And He grants them bliss therein as a reward and recompense for their obedience — or do they not enter it, but rather their reward is that they are saved from the Fire, and then it is said to them: "Be dust, like the beasts." This is the school of Ibn Abī Sulaym and a group (of scholars).

The correct view is that they do enter it and are blessed therein with eating, drinking, and other delights. This is the saying of al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī, al-Ḍaḥḥāk, Mālik ibn Anas, Ibn Abī Laylā, and others.

His saying (I asked Ibn Masʿūd: "Did any of you witness with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ the night of the jinn?" He said: "No") — this is explicit in nullifying the ḥadīth reported in Sunan Abī Dāwūd and others, which mentions the ablution with nabīdh (date-infused water) and the presence of Ibn Masʿūd with him ﷺ on the night of the jinn. For this ḥadīth (of Ibn Masʿūd's denial) is authentic (ṣaḥīḥ), while the ḥadīth of nabīdh is weak (ḍaʿīf) by consensus of the ḥadīth scholars, and its chain revolves around Zayd, the freed slave of ʿAmr ibn Ḥurayth, who is unknown (majhūl).

His saying (ustuṭīra or ughtīla): The meaning of ustuṭīra is that the jinn carried him off flying; the meaning of ughtīla is that he was killed secretly. And al-ghīlah — with kasrah on the ghayn — is killing in concealment.

Al-Dāraquṭnī said: The ḥadīth of Ibn Masʿūd ends at his saying: "And he showed us their traces and the traces of their fires." What comes after that — namely, the saying of al-Shaʿbī — is thus narrated by the companions of Dāwūd, the narrator from al-Shaʿbī, and Ibn ʿUlayyah, Ibn Zurays, Ibn Abī Zāʾidah, Ibn Idrīs, and others. This is what al-Dāraquṭnī and others stated. The meaning of his saying that it is from the speech of al-Shaʿbī is that it is not transmitted from Ibn Masʿūd as part of this ḥadīth. Otherwise, al-Shaʿbī would not utter such a statement except upon authoritative instruction (tawqīf) from the Prophet ﷺ. And Allah knows best.

His saying (For you is every bone upon which the name of Allah has been mentioned): Some scholars said this pertains to their believers. As for others (the disbelieving jinn), it has come in another ḥadīth that their food is that upon which the name of Allah has not been mentioned.

His saying (I wish I had been with him): In this is the encouragement to accompany people of virtue in their travels, their important affairs, their battle-scenes, and their gatherings — absolutely — and regret over missing that.

His saying (A tree gave me notice of them): This is evidence that Allah Almighty grants discernment (tamyīz) to whatever He wills of inanimate objects. Its parallel is the saying of Allah Almighty: {«وَإِنَّ مِنْهَا لَمَا يَهْبِطُ مِنْ خَشْيَةِ اللَّهِ»} (And indeed, among them are stones that fall down from fear of Allah), and His saying: {«وَإِنْ مِنْ شَيْءٍ إِلَّا يُسَبِّحُ بِحَمْدِهِ وَلَكِنْ لَا تَفْقَهُونَ تَسْبِيحَهُمْ»} (And there is not a thing except that it glorifies His praise, but you do not understand their glorification), and his saying ﷺ: "Indeed, I know a stone in Mecca that used to greet me with salām," and the ḥadīth of the two trees that came to him ﷺ — which Muslim has mentioned at the end of the Book — and the ḥadīth of the moaning of the palm-trunk, the glorification of the food, the fleeing of Moses' stone with his garment, and the trembling of Ḥirāʾ and Uḥud. And Allah knows best.

---

(Chapter: On the Recitation in the Ẓuhr and ʿAṣr Prayers)

His saying in the ḥadīth of Abū Qatādah, may Allah be pleased with him (That the Prophet ﷺ used to recite in the first two rakʿahs the Opening of the Book and two sūrahs, and he would make us hear the verse sometimes, and he would recite in the last two rakʿahs the Opening of the Book): And in the narration of Abū Saʿīd, may Allah be pleased with him (He used to recite in every rakʿah of the first two the equivalent of thirty verses, and in the last two the equivalent of fifteen verses — or he said: half of that — and in the ʿAṣr prayer, in the first two rakʿahs, in every rakʿah the equivalent of the recitation of fifteen verses, and in the last two the equivalent of half of that). And in the ḥadīth of Saʿd (I would make the first two rakʿahs lengthy (urkidu) and shorten (aḥdhif) the last two). And in the other ḥadīth of Abū Saʿīd, he said (Indeed, the ẓuhr prayer would be established, and one going to al-Baqīʿ would go, relieve himself, then perform ablution, then come while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was still in the first rakʿah, due to its length). And in other aḥādīth outside this chapter — and they are in the two Ṣaḥīḥs — that the Prophet ﷺ was the lightest of people in prayer while being complete, and that he ﷺ said: "Indeed, I enter into prayer intending to lengthen it, then I hear the cry of an infant, so I shorten my prayer, fearing that his mother would be distressed."

The scholars said: The prayer of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ varied between lengthening and shortening according to the variation of circumstances. When the congregants preferred lengthening, and there was no occupation for him or for them, he would lengthen. When it was not so, he would shorten. And he might intend lengthening, then something would arise necessitating shortening, such as the cry of an infant and the like. Added to this is that he might enter the prayer in the middle of the time, so he would shorten.

And it was said: He only lengthened in some times — and that was the lesser portion — and he shortened in most of them. So the lengthening was to demonstrate its permissibility, and the shortening was because it is superior. And the Prophet ﷺ commanded shortening and said: "Indeed, among you are those who drive others away. So whoever prays with the people, let him shorten, for among them are the sick, the weak, and the one with a need."

And it was said: He lengthened at one time and shortened at another, to clarify that the recitation beyond the Fātiḥah has no fixed measure in terms of obligation; rather, both its little and its much are permissible. The only obligatory element is the Fātiḥah. For this reason, the narrations agree upon it, while they differ regarding what is beyond it.

In sum: The Sunnah is shortening, as the Prophet ﷺ commanded, for the reason he explained. He only lengthened in some times because he was certain of the absence of that reason. So if one is certain of the absence of the reason, he lengthens.

His saying (And he would recite the Opening of the Book and two sūrahs): In this is evidence for what our companions (the Shāfiʿīs) and others have said — that reciting a short sūrah in its entirety is superior to reciting its equivalent length from a long sūrah. For it is recommended for the reciter to begin from the start of connected speech and to stop at the end of the connected unit. And the connection may be obscure to most people or to many, so they were directed to complete the sūrah, to guard against stopping without completing the connected unit.

As for the variation in the narration regarding the sūrah in the last two rakʿahs, perhaps its cause is what we mentioned of the variation in lengthening and shortening the prayer according to circumstances.

The scholars have differed regarding the recommendation of reciting a sūrah in the last two rakʿahs of the four-rakʿah prayer and the third of the Maghrib. It was said: it is recommended; and it was said: it is not. These are two positions of al-Shāfiʿī, may Allah have mercy on him. Al-Shāfiʿī said: If a latecomer (masbūq) catches the last two rakʿahs, he should come with the sūrah in them.

chapters.title_en: The Length of Recitation in the Five Daily Prayers and Related Rulings on the Prophet's Practice
chapters.arabic_text:
الباقيتين عليه لئلا تخلو صلاته من سورة وأما اختلاف قدر القراءة في

الصلوات فهو عند العلماء على ظاهره قالوا فالسنة أن يقرأ في الصبح والظهر

بطوال المفصل وتكون الصبح أطول وفي العشاء والعصر بأوساطه وفي المغرب

بقصاره قالوا والحكمة في إطالة الصبح والظهر أنهما في وقت غفلة بالنوم آخر

الليل وفي القائلة فيطولهما ليدركهما المتأخر بغفلة ونحوها والعصر ليست

كذلك بل تفعل في وقت تعب أهل الأعمال فخففت عن ذلك والمغرب ضيقة الوقت
# 
# فاحتيج إلى زيادة تخفيفها لذلك ولحاجة الناس إلى عشاء صائمهم وضيفهم

والعشاء في وقت غلبة النوم والنعاس ولكن وقتها واسع فأشبهت العصر والله

أعلم وقوله وكان يطول الركعة الأولى ويقصر الثانية هذا مما اختلف العلماء

في العمل بظاهره وهما وجهان لأصحابنا أشهرهما عندهم لا يطول والحديث متأول

على أنه طول بدعاء الافتتاح والتعوذ أو لسماع دخول داخل في الصلاة ونحوه

لافي القراءة والثاني أنه يستحب تطويل القراءة في الأولى قصدا وهذا هو

الصحيح المختار الموافق لظاهر السنة ومن قال بقراءة السورة في الأخريين

اتفقوا على أنها أخف منها في الأوليين واختلف أصحابنا في تطويل الثالثة على

الرابعة إذا قلنا بتطويل الأولى على الثانية وفي هذه الأحاديث كلها دليل

على أنه لا بد من قراءة الفاتحة في جميع الركعات ولم يوجب أبو حنيفة رضي

الله عنه في الأخريين القراءة بل خيره بين القراءة والتسبيح والسكوت

والجمهور على وجوب القراءة وهو الصواب الموافق للسنن الصحيحة وقوله (وكان

يسمعنا الآية) أحيانا هذا محمول على أنه أراد به بيان جواز الجهر في

القراءة السرية وأن الإسرار ليس بشرط لصحة الصلاة بل هو سنة ويحتمل أن

الجهر بالآية كان يحصل بسبق اللسان للاستغراق في التدبر والله أعلم قوله

(أخبرنا هشيم عن منصور عن الوليد بن مسلم عن أبي الصديق عن أبي سعيد) أما

منصور فهو بن المعتمر وأما  الوليد بن مسلم فليس هو الوليد بن مسلم الدمشقي

أبا العباس الأموي مولاهم الإمام الجليل المشهور المتأخر صاحب الأوزاعي بل

هو الوليد بن مسلم العنبري البصري أبو بشر التابعي وأن اسم أبي الصديق بكر

بن عمرو وقيل بن قيس الناجي منسوب إلى ناجية قبيلة قوله (كنا نحزر قيامه)

هو بضم الزاي وكسرها لغتان قوله (والآوليين والآخريين) هو بيائين مثناتين

تحت قوله (فحزرنا قيامه قدر الم تنزيل السجدة) يجوز جر السجدة على البدل

ونصبها بأعني ورفعها خبر مبتدأ محذوف قوله (على قدر قيامه من الأخريين) كذا

هو في معظم الأصول من الأخريين وفي بعضها في الأخريين وهو معنى رواية من

قوله (إن أهل الكوفة شكوا سعدا) هو سعد بن أبي وقاص رضي الله عنه والكوفة

هي البلدة المعروفة ودار الفضل ومحل الفضلاء بناها عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله

عنه أعني أمر نوابه ببنائها هي والبصرة قيل سميت كوفة لاستدارتها تقول

العرب رأيت كوفا وكوفانا للرمل المستدير وقيل لاجتماع الناس فيها تقول

العرب تكوف الرمل إذا استدار وركب بعضه بعضا وقيل لأن ترابها خالطه
# 
# حصى وكل ما كان كذلك سمي كوفة قال الحافظ أبو بكر الحازمي وغيره ويقال

للكوفة أيضا كوفان بضم الكاف قوله (فذكروا من صلاته) أي أنه لا يحسن الصلاة

قوله (فأرسل إليه عمر رضي الله عنه) فيه أن الإمام إذا شكي إليه نائبه بعث

إليه واستفسره عن ذلك وأنه إذا خاف مفسدة باستمراره في ولايته ووقوع فتنة

عزله فلهذا عزله عمر رضي الله عنه مع أنه لم يكن فيه خلل ولم يثبت ما يقدح

في ولايته وأهليته وقد ثبت في صحيح البخاري في حديث مقتل عمر والشورى أن

عمر رضي الله عنه قال إن أصابت الإمارة سعدا فذاك وإلا فليستعن به أيكم ما

أمر فإني لم أعزله من عجز ولا خيانة قوله (لا أخرم عنها) هو بفتح الهمزة

وكسر الراء أي لا أنقص قوله (إني لأركد بهم في الأوليين) يعني أطولهما

وأديمهما وأمدهما كما قاله في الرواية الأخرى من  قولهم ركدت السفن والريح

والماء إذا سكن ومكث وقوله وأحذف في الأخريين يعني أقصرهما عن الأوليين لا

أنه يخله بالقراءة ويحذفها كلها قوله (ذاك الظن بك أبا إسحاق) فيه مدح

الرجل الجليل في وجهه إذا لم يخف عليه فتنة بإعجاب ونحوه والنهي عن ذلك

إنما هو لمن خيف عليه الفتنة وقد جاءت أحاديث كثيرة في الصحيح بالأمرين

وجمع العلماء بينهما بما ذكرته وقد أوضحتهما في كتاب الأذكار وفيه خطاب

الرجل الجليل بكنيته دون اسمه قوله (وما آلوا ما اقتديت به من صلاة رسول

الله صلى الله عليه وسلم) آلو بالمد في أوله وضم اللام أي لا أقصر في ذلك

ومنه قوله تعالى لا يألونكم خبالا أي لا يقصرون في إفسادكم قوله (حدثنا

الوليد) يعنى بن مسلم هو صاحب الأوزاعي قوله (عن قزعة) هو بفتح الزاي

وإسكانها قوله (وهو مكثور عليه) أي عنده ناس كثيرون للاستفادة منه قوله

(أسألك عن صلاة رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال مالك في ذلك من خير)

معناه إنك لا تستطيع الإتيان بمثلها لطولها وكمال خشوعها وإن تكلفت ذلك شق

عليك ولم تحصله فتكون قد علمت السنة وتركتها
#
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ط-و-ل (ṭ-w-l)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning of extension, elongation, and protraction in physical or temporal terms.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In ritual context, denotes deliberate prolongation of recitation to achieve greater devotional absorption (khushūʿ) and to accommodate latecomers.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Used literally here for actual temporal extension of prayer, not metaphorically.
- Sībawayh Rule: ʿAṭf al-Bayān (Appositional Clarification) — The phrase "الم تنزيل السجدة" permits grammatical variation (jarr, naṣb, rafʿ) as apposition, implied object, or predicate of an omitted subject, each syntactically valid.
chapters.translation:
I say: Regarding the two remaining [rakʿahs], [the recitation of a sūrah] is [recommended] so that his prayer is not devoid of a sūrah [after al-Fātiḥah]. As for the difference in the amount of recitation among the prayers, it is, in the view of the scholars, taken at its apparent meaning. They said: The Sunnah is to recite in the Dawn (Ṣubḥ) and Noon (Ẓuhr) prayers from the long section of the detailed (al-Mufaṣṣal) [sūrahs], with the Dawn being longer; in the Sunset (Maghrib) and Afternoon (ʿAṣr) prayers, from its middle section; and in the Evening (ʿIshāʾ) prayer, from its short section.

They said: The wisdom in prolonging the Dawn and Noon prayers is that they occur at times of heedlessness — the Dawn after sleep at the end of the night, and the Noon during the midday nap (al-Qāyilāh) — so they are lengthened so that the one who is delayed by sleep or similar causes may still catch them. The Afternoon prayer is not like that; rather, it is performed at a time when people of work are fatigued, so it was lightened accordingly. The Sunset prayer has a constricted time, so it required additional lightening for that reason, and because of people's need to attend to the evening meal of their faster and their guest. The Evening prayer occurs at a time when sleep and drowsiness prevail, but its time is expansive, so it resembles the Afternoon [in moderate length]. And Allah knows best.

His statement: "And he would lengthen the first rakʿah and shorten the second" — this is among the matters on which the scholars differed regarding acting upon its apparent meaning. There are two positions among our companions (the Shāfiʿīs). The more famous one among them is that he did not deliberately lengthen [the first], and the ḥadīth is interpreted as meaning that he lengthened due to the opening supplication (duʿāʾ al-iftitāḥ) and the seeking of refuge (al-taʿawwudh), or because he heard someone entering the prayer and similar reasons — not due to recitation. The second position is that it is recommended to deliberately lengthen the recitation in the first [rakʿah], and this is the correct and chosen view, consistent with the apparent meaning of the Sunnah.

As for those who held the recitation of a sūrah in the last two rakʿahs, they unanimously agreed that it is lighter than in the first two. Our companions differed regarding lengthening the third over the fourth if we adopt the view of lengthening the first over the second.

In all these ḥadīths there is evidence that reciting al-Fātiḥah is obligatory in all rakʿahs. Abū Ḥanīfah — may Allah be pleased with him — did not make recitation obligatory in the last two [rakʿahs]; rather, he gave the choice between recitation, glorification (tasbīḥ), and silence. The majority hold that recitation is obligatory, and this is the correct view, consistent with the authentic Sunnahs.

His statement: "And he would sometimes make us hear the verse" — this is interpreted as his intent to demonstrate the permissibility of audible recitation within silent recitation, and that keeping silent is not a condition for the validity of the prayer but rather a Sunnah. It is also possible that the audible recitation of the verse occurred due to the tongue's precedence [over control] from being fully absorbed in contemplation. And Allah knows best.

His statement: "Hushaym informed us, from Manṣūr, from al-Walīd ibn Muslim, from Abū al-Ṣiddīq, from Abū Saʿīd" — As for Manṣūr, he is Ibn al-Muʿtamir. As for al-Walīd ibn Muslim, he is not al-Walīd ibn Muslim al-Dimashqī, Abū al-ʿAbbās al-Umawī, their freed slave, the renowned, eminent, later [scholar], the companion of al-Awzāʿī. Rather, he is al-Walīd ibn Muslim al-ʿAnbarī al-Baṣrī, Abū Bishr, the Tābiʿī. The name of Abū al-Ṣiddīq is Bakr ibn ʿAmr — and it was said Ibn Qays — al-Nājī, attributed to Nājiyah, a tribe.

His statement: "We would estimate his standing" — it is with ḍammah on the zāy and kasrah, two [valid] dialects.

His statement: "the first two and the last two" — it is with two yāʾs, both with kasrah beneath.

His statement: "So we estimated his standing as the measure of 'Alif Lām Mīm, the Revelation of the Prostration' (al-Sajdah)" — it is permissible to put al-Sajdah in the genitive (jarr) as an apposition, in the accusative (naṣb) with the implied [verb] "I mean" (aʿnī), and in the nominative (rafʿ) as the predicate of an omitted subject.

His statement: "according to the measure of his standing in the last two" — thus it appears in most manuscripts: "from the last two" (min al-ākhiratayn), and in some of them: "in the last two" (fī al-ākhiratayn), which is the meaning of the narration.

His statement: "The people of Kūfah complained about Saʿd" — he is Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ, may Allah be pleased with him. Kūfah is the well-known city, the abode of virtue and the place of the virtuous. It was built by ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, may Allah be pleased with him — that is, he commanded his deputies to build it, along with Baṣrah. It was said that it was named Kūfah for its roundness; the Arabs say "I saw a kūf and kūfān" for round sand. It was also said [it was named] for the gathering of people therein; the Arabs say "takawwafa al-raml" when it becomes round and piles up in layers. And it was said [it was named] because its soil was mixed with gravel, and everything like that is called kūfah. The Ḥāfiẓ Abū Bakr al-Ḥāzimī and others said: Kūfah is also called Kūfān, with ḍammah on the kāf.

His statement: "So they mentioned about his prayer" — meaning that he does not perform the prayer well.

His statement: "So ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, sent to him" — in this [there is evidence] that when a governor's deputy is complained about to the Imām, he sends for him and investigates the matter with him, and that if he fears corruption from his continued tenure and the occurrence of discord, he removes him. For this reason, ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, removed him — even though there was no defect in him, and nothing was established that would impugn his governorship or his qualification. It is established in Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī, in the ḥadīth of ʿUmar's assassination and the consultation (al-Shūrā), that ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "If the leadership reaches Saʿd, then that is it; otherwise, let whichever of you is appointed seek his assistance. For I did not remove him due to incapacity or treachery."

His statement: "I do not fall short of it" (lā akhrimu ʿanhā) — it is with fatḥah on the hamzah and kasrah on the rāʾ, meaning: I do not diminish [anything] from it.

His statement: "Indeed, I make them stand long (arkudu) in the first two" — meaning: I lengthen them, prolong them, and extend them, as he stated in the other narration. This is from their saying: "The ships, the wind, and the water are rākidah" when they are still and settled. His statement: "And I shorten (aḥdhifu) in the last two" means: I make them shorter than the first two — not that he is negligent in recitation or omits it entirely.

His statement: "That is the expectation of you, Abū Isḥāq" — in this [there is evidence for] praising a venerable man to his face when no discord is feared from him, such as self-admiration and the like. The prohibition of that applies only to one from whom discord is feared. Many authentic ḥadīths have come in the Ṣaḥīḥ [collections] commanding both matters, and the scholars reconciled between them as I have mentioned. I have clarified both in the book al-Adhkār. In it [also] is addressing a venerable man by his kunyah rather than his name.

His statement: "And I did not fall short (mā ālū) in what I followed of the prayer of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him" — ālū is with madd on its first letter and ḍammah on the lām, meaning: I do not fall short in that. From it is the saying of the Exalted: {«لَا يَأْلُونَكُمْ خَبَالًا»} (They do not fall short in corrupting you) — meaning they do not spare any effort in ruining you.

His statement: "Al-Walīd narrated to us" — meaning Ibn Muslim, the companion of al-Awzāʿī.

His statement: "From Qazaʿah" — it is with fatḥah on the zāy and its sukūn [both valid].

His statement: "And he is much-frequented (makthūrun ʿalayhi)" — meaning he has many people around him for seeking benefit from him.

His statement: "I ask you about the prayer of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him" — and he said: "You have no good in that" — its meaning is: You will not be able to perform it like it, due to its length and the perfection of its humility. Even if you undertake that, it would be difficult for you and you would not achieve it. Thus you would have learned the Sunnah and abandoned it.
