Thus, its meaning is: nothing of the speech of people and their mutual conversations is fitting in it; rather, it is glorification and what is in its meaning of remembrance and supplication and their like, which the Sacred Law has brought.

In this is evidence that one who swears an oath not to speak, and then glorifies (subḥān Allāh), magnifies (Allāhu akbar), or recites the Qurʾān, does not break his oath. This is the correct and well-known view in our school.

In this also is evidence for the school of al-Shāfiʿī — may Allah have mercy on him — and the majority, that the opening takbīr (takbīrat al-iḥrām) is an obligatory pillar (farḍ) of the prayer and a part of it. Abū Ḥanīfah — may Allah be pleased with him — said: "It is not part of it; rather, it is a condition (sharṭ) external to it, preceding it."

In this hadith is also the prohibition of responding to a sneezer's praise of Allah (tashmīt) during prayer, and that it is among the speech of people which is forbidden in prayer and by which the prayer is corrupted if one performs it knowingly and deliberately. He said...

chapters.title_en: The Ruling on Responding to a Sneezer in Prayer, and the Prohibition of Consulting Soothsayers and Diviners
chapters.arabic_text:
أصحابنا إن قال يرحمك الله بكاف الخطاب بطلت صلاته وإن قال يرحمه الله أو

اللهم ارحمه أو رحم الله فلانا لم تبطل صلاته لأنه ليس بخطاب وأما العاطس

في الصلاة فيستحب له أن يحمد الله تعالى سرا هذا مذهبنا وبه قال مالك وغيره

وعن بن عمر والنخعي وأحمد رضي الله عنهم أنه يجهر به والأول أظهر لأنه ذكر

والسنة في الأذكار في الصلاة الإسرار إلا ما استثنى من القراءة في بعضها

ونحوها قوله إني حديث عهد بجاهلية
# 
# قال العلماء الجاهلية ما قبل ورود الشرع سموا جاهلية لكثرة جهالاتهم

وفحشهم قوله إن منا رجالا يأتون الكهان قال فلا تأتهم قال العلماء إنما نهي

عن إتيان الكهان لأنهم يتكلمون في مغيبات قد يصادف بعضها الإصابة فيخاف

الفتنة على الإنسان بسبب ذلك لأنهم يلبسون على الناس كثيرا من أمر الشرائع

وقد تظاهرت الأحاديث الصحيحة بالنهي عن إتيان الكهان وتصديقهم فيما يقولون

وتحريم ما يعطون من الحلوان وهو حرام بإجماع المسلمين وقد نقل الإجماع في

تحريمه جماعة منهم أبو محمد البغوي رحمهم الله تعالى قال البغوي اتفق أهل

العلم على تحريم حلوان الكاهن وهو ما أخذه المتكهن على كهانته لأن  فعل

الكهانة باطل لا يجوز أخذ الأجرة عليه وقال الماوردي رحمه الله تعالى في

الأحكام السلطانية ويمنع المحتسب الناس من التكسب بالكهانة واللهو ويؤدب

عليه الآخذ والمعطي وقال الخطابي رحمه الله تعالى حلوان الكاهن ما يأخذه

المتكهن على كهانته وهو محرم وفعله باطل قال وحلوان العراف حرام أيضا قال

والفرق بين العراف والكاهن أن الكاهن إنما يتعاطى الأخبار عن الكوائن في

المستقبل ويدعي معرفة الأسرار والعراف يتعاطى معرفة الشيء المسروق ومكان

الضالة ونحوهما وقال الخطابي أيضا في حديث من أتى كاهنا فصدقه بما يقول فقد

برئ مما أنزل الله على محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم قال كان في العرب كهنة

يدعون أنهم يعرفون كثيرا من الأمور فمنهم من يزعم أن له رئيا من الجن يلقي

إليه الأخبار ومنهم من يدعي استدراك ذلك بفهم أعطيه ومنهم من يسمى عرافا

وهو الذي يزعم معرفة الأمور بمقدمات أسباب استدل بها كمعرفة من سرق الشيء

الفلاني ومعرفة من يتهم به المرأة ونحو ذلك ومنهم من يسمي المنجم كاهنا قال

والحديث يشتمل على النهي عن إتيان هؤلاء كلهم والرجوع إلى قولهم وتصديقهم

فيما يدعونه هذا كلام الخطابي وهو نفيس قوله ومنا رجال يتطيرون قال ذلك شيء

يجدونه في صدورهم فلا يصدنهم وفي رواية فلا يصدنكم قال العلماء معناه أن

الطيرة شيء تجدونه في نفوسكم ضرورة
# 
# ولا عتب عليكم في ذلك فإنه غير مكتسب لكم فلا تكليف به ولكن لا تمتنعوا

بسببه من التصرف في أموركم فهذا هو الذي تقدرون عليه وهو مكتسب لكم فيقع به

التكليف فنهاهم صلى الله عليه وسلم عن العمل بالطيرة والامتناع من تصرفاتهم

بسببها وقد تظاهرت الأحاديث الصحيحة في النهي عن التطير والطيرة هي محمولة

على العمل بها لا على ما يوجد في النفس من غير عمل على مقتضاه عندهم وسيأتي

بسط الكلام فيها في موضعها إن شاء الله تعالى حيث ذكرها مسلم رحمه الله

تعالى قوله ومنا رجال يخطون قال كان نبي من الأنبياء عليهم السلام يخط فمن

وافق خطه  فذاك اختلف العلماء في معناه فالصحيح أن معناه من وافق خطه فهو

مباح له ولكن لا طريق لنا إلى العلم اليقيني بالموافقة فلا يباح والمقصود

أنه حرام لأنه لا يباح إلا بيقين الموافقة وليس لنا يقين بها وإنما قال

النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فيمن وافق خطه فذاك ولم يقل هو حرام بغير تعليق

على الموافقة لئلا يتوهم متوهم أن هذا النهي يدخل فيه ذاك النبي الذي كان

يخط فحافظ النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم على حرمة ذاك النبي مع بيان الحكم في

حقنا فالمعنى أن ذلك النبي لا منع في حقه وكذا لو علمتم موافقته ولكن لا

علم لكم بها وقال الخطابي هذا الحديث يحتمل النهي عن هذا الخط إذا كان علما

لنبوة ذاك النبي وقد انقطعت فنهينا عن تعاطي ذلك وقال القاضي عياض المختار

أن معناه أن من وافق خطه فذاك الذي يجدون إصابته فيما يقول لا أنه أباح ذلك

لفاعله قال ويحتمل أن هذا نسخ في شرعنا فحصل من مجموع كلام العلماء فيه

الاتفاق على النهي عنه الآن قوله وكانت لي جارية ترعى غنما لي قبل أحد

والجوانية هي بفتح الجيم وتشديد الواو وبعد الألف نون مكسورة ثم ياء مشددة

هكذا ضبطناه وكذا ذكر أبو عبيد البكري والمحققون وحكى القاضي عياض عن بعضهم

تخفيف الياء والمختار التشديد والجوانية بقرب أحد موضع في شمالي المدينة

وأما قول القاضي عياض إنها من عمل الفرع فليس بمقبول لأن الفرع بين مكة

والمدينة بعيد من المدينة وأحد في شام المدينة وقد
# 
# قال في الحديث قبل أحد والجوانية فكيف يكون عند الفرع وفيه دليل على جواز

استخدام السيد جاريته في الرعي وإن كانت تنفرد في المرعى وإنما حرم الشرع

مسافرة المرأة وحدها لأن السفر مظنة الطمع فيها وانقطاع ناصرها والذاب عنها

وبعدها منه بخلاف الراعية ومع هذا فإن خيف مفسدة من رعيها لريبة فيها أو
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ح-م-د (ḥ-m-d)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning is praise and commendation; al-ḥamdu denotes the act of extolling virtues.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In worship, taḥmīd is the verbal acknowledgment of divine beneficence, an act of devotion (dhikr).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) praise of God; in prayer, it is a licit form of remembrance, distinct from addressing creatures.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clause (al-sharṭ wa-l-jawāb) — The protasis "in qāla" governs the apodosis "baṭalat ṣalātuhu," with the condition being the direct address (khiṭāb) using the second-person pronoun.
chapters.translation:
I say: Our companions (the Shāfiʿīs) hold that if one says "May God have mercy on you" (yarḥamuka Allāh) with the second-person address (kāf al-khiṭāb), his prayer is invalidated. But if he says "May God have mercy on him" (yarḥamuhu Allāh), or "O God, have mercy on him" (Allāhumma irḥamhu), or "May God have mercy on so-and-so" (raḥima Allāhu fulānan), his prayer is not invalidated, because it is not an address [to a person]. As for the one who sneezes during prayer, it is recommended (mustaḥabb) for him to praise God (al-ḥamdu lillāh) silently. This is our school (madhhab), and it is also the view of Mālik and others. It is reported from Ibn ʿUmar, al-Nakhaʿī, and Aḥmad — may God be pleased with them — that he should do so aloud. But the first view is more apparent (aẓhar), because it is a remembrance (dhikr), and the Sunnah in the remembrances during prayer is to be silent, except for what is exempted, such as the recitation (qirāʾah) in certain parts of it.

His saying (peace be upon him): "I have recently come from a state of jāhiliyyah" — the scholars said: al-Jāhiliyyah is the period before the advent of the Sacred Law (sharʿ). They were called "people of ignorance" (jāhiliyyah) because of the abundance of their ignorances and their obscene conduct.

His saying: "Among us are men who go to soothsayers (kuhhān)" — he said: "Do not go to them." The scholars said: The prohibition against going to soothsayers is only because they speak about unseen matters (mughayyabāt), some of which may coincidentally hit the mark, and thus one fears tribulation (fitnah) for the person due to that, because they confound the people regarding many matters of the Sacred Law. The authentic hadiths have concurred (taẓāharat) in prohibiting going to soothsayers, believing them in what they say, and forbidding what they are given as a fee (ḥulwān). This is forbidden by the consensus (ijmāʿ) of the Muslims. A group has transmitted the consensus on its prohibition, among them Abū Muḥammad al-Baghawī — may God have mercy on them. Al-Baghawī said: The people of knowledge have agreed on the prohibition of the soothsayer's fee (ḥulwān al-kāhin), which is what the diviner takes for his soothsaying, because the act of soothsaying is null and void (bāṭil), and it is not permissible to take payment for it.

Al-Māwardī — may God have mercy on him — said in al-Aḥkām al-Sulṭāniyyah: The muḥtasib (market inspector) should prevent people from earning a living through soothsaying and frivolous amusement (lahw), and should discipline both the taker and the giver [of such fees].

Al-Khaṭṭābī — may God have mercy on him — said: The soothsayer's fee (ḥulwān al-kāhin) is what the diviner takes for his soothsaying; it is forbidden (muḥarram) and his act is null. He said: The fee of the augur (ʿarrāf) is also forbidden. He said: The difference between the augur (ʿarrāf) and the soothsayer (kāhin) is that the soothsayer only engages in reporting future events (kawāʾin) and claims knowledge of secrets, whereas the augur engages in knowing the stolen object, the location of a lost item, and similar things.

Al-Khaṭṭābī also said regarding the hadith: "Whoever goes to a soothsayer and believes him in what he says has disbelieved in what was revealed to Muḥammad (peace be upon him)": There were soothsayers among the Arabs who claimed to know many matters. Among them were those who claimed to have a familiar spirit (riʾy) from the jinn that would cast reports to them; among them were those who claimed to attain that through an understanding given to them; among them were those called ʿarrāf (augur), who claimed to know matters through preliminary causes (muqaddimāt asbāb) by which they inferred, such as knowing who stole such-and-such an object, or knowing the man with whom a woman is suspected, and similar things; and among them were those called astrologers (munajjim), also termed soothsayers. He said: The hadith encompasses the prohibition of going to all of these, referring back to their words, and believing them in what they claim. This is the speech of al-Khaṭṭābī, and it is precious (nafīs).

His saying: "Among us are men who practice augury from birds (taṭayyur)" — he said: "That is something they find in their breasts, so let it not deter them." In another narration: "So let it not deter you." The scholars said: Its meaning is that augury (ṭiyarah) is something one finds in one's soul by necessity (ḍarūrah). There is no blame upon you for that, for it is not acquired (muktasab) by you, so there is no obligation (taklīf) attached to it. But do not refrain, because of it, from proceeding in your affairs. This is what you are capable of, and it is acquired by you, so the obligation attaches to it. Thus he (peace be upon him) prohibited them from acting upon augury and refraining from their affairs because of it. The authentic hadiths have concurred in prohibiting taṭayyur (practicing augury). Al-ṭiyarah is to be understood as acting upon it, not as what occurs in the soul without acting in accordance with it, according to them. The full discussion of it will come in its proper place, God willing, where Muslim — may God have mercy on him — mentions it.

His saying: "Among us are men who draw lines (yakhuṭṭūn)" — he said: "There was a prophet among the prophets, peace be upon them, who used to draw lines; whoever's line matches his, then that is it." The scholars differed on its meaning. The correct view (al-ṣaḥīḥ) is that its meaning is: whoever's line matches his, it is permissible (mubāḥ) for him, but there is no way for us to attain certain knowledge (ʿilm yaqīnī) of the match, so it is not permitted. The point is that it is forbidden (ḥarām), because it is not permitted except with certainty of the match, and we have no certainty of it. The Prophet (peace be upon him) only said, regarding the one whose line matches his, "then that is it," and did not say "it is forbidden" unconditionally, lest someone imagine that this prohibition includes that prophet who used to draw lines. Thus the Prophet (peace be upon him) preserved the sanctity (ḥurmah) of that prophet while clarifying the ruling regarding us. So the meaning is: that prophet has no prohibition in his case, and likewise if you knew of the match — but you have no knowledge of it.

Al-Khaṭṭābī said: This hadith may imply the prohibition of this line-drawing if it was a sign of the prophethood of that prophet, and it has now ceased, so we are forbidden from engaging in it.

Al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ said: The chosen view (al-mukhtār) is that its meaning is: whoever's line matches his, that is the one whose accuracy they find in what he says — not that it is permitted for the doer. He said: It may be that this was abrogated (naskh) in our Sacred Law. Thus, from the totality of the scholars' speech, there is agreement (ittifāq) on its prohibition now.

His saying: "I had a slave-girl (jāriyah) who used to pasture sheep for me before Uḥud, at al-Jawwāniyyah." Al-Jawwāniyyah is with a fatḥah on the jīm, a shaddah on the wāw, and after the alif a kasrah on the nūn, then a shaddah on the yāʾ. This is how we have recorded it (ḍabaṭnāhu), and likewise Abū ʿUbayd al-Bakrī and the verifying scholars (al-muḥaqqiqūn) mentioned it. Al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ reported from some of them the lightening (takhfīf) of the yāʾ, but the chosen view is the shaddah. Al-Jawwāniyyah is a place near Uḥud, north of Medina.

As for the statement of al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ that it is from the district of al-Farʿ, it is not acceptable, because al-Farʿ is between Mecca and Medina, far from Medina, while Uḥud is in the north of Medina. He said in the hadith: "before Uḥud, at al-Jawwāniyyah" — so how could it be near al-Farʿ?

In this hadith there is evidence for the permissibility of a master employing his slave-girl in pasturing, even if she is alone in the pasture. The Sacred Law only forbade a woman traveling alone because travel is a place where covetousness (ṭamaʿ) for her is likely, and where her supporter and defender are cut off from her, and her distance from him — unlike the shepherdess. Nevertheless, if corruption (mafsadah) is feared from her pasturing due to suspicion (rībah) regarding her, or...

chapters.arabic_text:
لفساد من يكون في الناحية التي ترعى فيها أو نحو ذلك لم يسترعها ولم تمكن

الحرة ولا  الأمة من الرعي حينئذ لأنه حينئذ يصير في معنى السفر الذي حرم

الشرع على المرأة فإن كان معها محرم أو نحوه ممن تأمن معه على نفسها فلا

منع حينئذ كما لا يمنع من المسافرة في هذا الحال والله أعلم قوله آسف أي

أغضب وهو بفتح السين قوله صككتها أي لطمتها قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم أين

الله قالت في السماء قال من أنا قالت أنت رسول الله قال أعتقها فإنها مؤمنة

هذا الحديث من أحاديث الصفات وفيها مذهبان تقدم ذكرهما مرات في كتاب

الإيمان أحدهما الإيمان به من غير خوض في معناه مع اعتقاد أن الله تعالى

ليس كمثله شيء وتنزيهه عن سمات المخلوقات والثاني تأويله بما يليق به فمن

قال بهذا قال كان المراد امتحانها هل هي موحدة تقر بأن الخالق المدبر

الفعال هو الله وحده وهو الذي إذا دعاه الداعي استقبل السماء كما إذا صلى

المصلي استقبل الكعبة وليس ذلك لأنه منحصر في السماء كما أنه ليس منحصرا في

جهة الكعبة بل ذلك لأن السماء قبلة الداعين كما أن الكعبة قبلة المصلين أو

هي من عبدة الأوثان العابدين للأوثان التي بين أيديهم فلما قالت في السماء

علم أنها موحدة وليست عابدة للأوثان قال القاضي عياض لا خلاف بين المسلمين

قاطبة فقيههم ومحدثهم ومتكلمهم ونظارهم ومقلدهم أن الظواهر الواردة بذكر

الله تعالى في السماء كقوله تعالى أأمنتم من في السماء أن يخسف بكم الأرض

ونحوه ليست على ظاهرها بل متأولة عند جميعهم فمن قال بإثبات جهة فوق من غير

تحديد ولا تكييف من المحدثين والفقهاء والمتكلمين تأول في السماء
# 
# أي على السماء ومن قال من دهماء النظار والمتكلمين وأصحاب التنزيه بنفي

الحد واستحالة الجهة في حقه سبحانه وتعالى تأولوها تأويلات بحسب مقتضاها

وذكر نحو ما سبق قال ويا ليت شعري ما الذي جمع أهل السنة والحق كلهم على

وجوب الإمساك عن الفكر في الذات كما أمروا وسكتوا لحيرة العقل واتفقوا على

تحريم التكييف والتشكيل وأن ذلك من وقوفهم وإمساكهم  غير شاك في الوجود

والموجود وغير قادح في التوحيد بل هو حقيقته ثم تسامح بعضهم بإثبات الجهة

خاشيا من مثل هذا التسامح وهل بين التكييف وإثبات الجهات فرق لكن إطلاق ما

أطلقه الشرع من أنه القاهر فوق عباده وأنه استوى على العرش مع التمسك

بالآية الجامعة للتنزيه الكلي الذي لا يصح في المعقول غيره وهو قوله تعالى

ليس كمثله شيء عصمة لمن وفقه الله تعالى وهذا كلام القاضي رحمه الله تعالى

وفي هذا الحديث أن إعتاق المؤمن أفضل من إعتاق الكافر وأجمع العلماء على

جواز عتق الكافر في غير الكفارات وأجمعوا على أنه لا يجزئ الكافر في كفارة

القتل كما ورد به القرآن واختلفوا في كفارة الظهار واليمين والجماع في نهار

رمضان فقال الشافعي ومالك والجمهور لا يجزئه إلا مؤمنة حملا للمطلق على

المقيد في كفارة القتل وقال أبو حنيفة رضي الله عنه والكوفيون يجزئه الكافر

للإطلاق فإنها تسمى رقبة قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم أين الله قالت في السماء

قال من أنا قالت أنت رسول الله قال أعتقها فإنها مؤمنة فيه دليل على أن

الكافر لا يصير مؤمنا إلا بالإقرار بالله تعالى وبرسالة رسول الله صلى الله

عليه وسلم وفيه دليل على أن من أقر بالشهادتين واعتقد ذلك جزما كفاه ذلك في

صحة إيمانه وكونه من أهل القبلة والجنة ولا يكلف مع هذا إقامة الدليل

والبرهان على ذلك ولا يلزمه معرفة الدليل وهذا هو الصحيح الذي عليه الجمهور

وقد سبق بيان هذه المسألة في أول
#

# كتاب الإيمان مع ما يتعلق بها وبالله التوفيق
# [538] قوله في حديث بن مسعود كنا نسلم على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

وهو في الصلاة فيرد علينا فلما رجعنا من عند النجاشي سلمنا عليه فلم يرد

علينا فقلنا يا رسول الله كنا نسلم عليك في الصلاة فترد علينا فقال إن في

الصلاة شغلا
# [539] وفي حديث زيد بن أرقم رضي الله عنه كنا نتكلم في الصلاة يكلم الرجل

صاحبه وهو إلى جنبه في الصلاة حتى  نزلت وقوموا لله قانتين فأمرنا بالسكوت

ونهينا عن الكلام
# [540] وفي حديث جابر رضي الله عنه قال إن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

بعثني لحاجة ثم أدركته وهو يصلي فسلمت عليه فأشار
# 
# إلي فلما فرغ دعاني فقال إنك سلمت آنفا وأنا أصلي هذه الأحاديث فيها

فوائد منها تحريم الكلام في الصلاة سواء كان لمصلحتها أم لا وتحريم رد

السلام فيها باللفظ وأنه لا تضر الإشارة بل يستحب رد السلام بالإشارة وبهذه

الجملة قال الشافعي والأكثرون قال القاضي عياض قال جماعة من العلماء برد

السلام في الصلاة نطقا منهم أبو هريرة وجابر والحسن وسعيد بن المسيب وقتادة

وإسحاق وقيل يرد في نفسه وقال عطاء والنخعي والثوري يرد بعد السلام في

الصلاة وقال أبو حنيفة رضي الله عنه لا يرد بلفظ ولا إشارة بكل حال وقال

عمر بن عبد العزيز ومالك وأصحابه وجماعة يرد إشارة ولا يرد نطقا ومن قال

يرد نطقا كأنه لم يبلغه الأحاديث وأما ابتداء السلام على المصلي فمذهب
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ر-ع-ي (r-ʿ-y)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To pasture, tend, guard; hence, a shepherd's care over a flock.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The act of custodial supervision; here, the master's failure to restrain his livestock from grazing on another's land.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) in the context of herding; metaphorical (majāz) when applied to divine providence, which is not intended here.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clause (al-Sharṭ) — The protasis (law) with its apodosis (lam yastarʿihā) governs the legal consequence, as in "if he did not restrain her, then no liability."

- Root: س-ف-ر (s-f-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To uncover, travel; the root implies removing a veil, hence journeying (since one's face is exposed).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Travel as a legal category (safar) that alters rulings, such as prayer and fasting; here, the woman's movement without a guardian.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for physical travel; metaphorical for the unveiling of hidden matters, not applicable here.
- Sībawayh Rule: ʿAṭf al-Bayān (Appositional Clarification) — "or the like of him" (aw naḥwuhu) specifies the class of permissible companions.

- Root: ص-ك-ك (ṣ-k-k)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To strike, slap, or hit with force; the sound of impact.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Physical striking as a legal act; here, the Prophet's (peace be upon him) action of striking the slave-girl to test her.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for the physical blow; no metaphorical extension intended.
- Sībawayh Rule: Fiʿl Mutaʿaddī (Transitive Verb) — "I struck her" (ṣakaktu-hā) requires a direct object, indicating the completeness of the action.

- Root: أ-س-ف (ʾ-s-f)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Intense grief, anger, or sorrow; the state of being deeply vexed.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In Quranic usage, it denotes divine displeasure; here, it is human anger, as glossed by the commentator.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for human emotion; metaphorical for divine attributes, which are not to be anthropomorphized.
- Sībawayh Rule: Ism al-Fāʿil (Active Participle) — "Āsif" (angry) with the vowel fatḥah on the sīn, as specified in the text.

- Root: ع-ت-ق (ʿ-t-q)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To become free, old, or noble; the act of manumission.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Legal emancipation of a slave; a meritorious act, especially for a believing slave.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for freeing from bondage; metaphorical for spiritual liberation from sin.
- Sībawayh Rule: Amr (Imperative) — "Free her" (aʿtiq-hā) is a command indicating obligation or recommendation, depending on context.

- Root: س-م-و (s-m-w)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To be high, elevated; the root of "heaven" (samāʾ).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The divine attribute of al-Fawqiyyah (being above); a contested term in Kalām, requiring taʾwīl (interpretation).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for spatial elevation; metaphorical for divine transcendence and sovereignty, as in "the Most High" (al-ʿAlī).
- Sībawayh Rule: Jār wa-Majrūr (Prepositional Phrase) — "In the heaven" (fī al-samāʾ) functions as a predicate, but its syntactic surface is not its theological reality.

- Root: ق-ن-ت (q-n-t)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To stand in obedience, be submissive; devotion in prayer.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The Quranic command "and stand before Allah with devotion" (qānitīn) — a state of stillness and focus.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for physical standing; metaphorical for inner humility and silence.
- Sībawayh Rule: Ḥāl (Circumstantial Clause) — "While standing" (qānitīn) describes the state of the worshipper, prohibiting speech.
chapters.translation:
I say: And the Prophet (peace be upon him) did not restrain her, nor did he permit the free woman or the slave-girl to graze [there] at that time, because it would then become akin to the travel that the Sacred Law has prohibited for a woman. If she has a mahram (unmarriageable kin) or someone similar whom she trusts with her person, then there is no prohibition at that time, just as she is not prevented from traveling in such a circumstance. And Allah knows best.

His saying, "Āsif" — meaning "angry" — and it is with the fatḥah on the sīn. His saying, "I struck her" (ṣakaktu-hā) — meaning "I slapped her."

His saying, peace be upon him: "Where is Allah?" She said: "In the heaven." He said: "Who am I?" She said: "You are the Messenger of Allah." He said: "Free her, for she is a believer."

This hadith is among the ḥadīths of the Divine Attributes (ṣifāt). Regarding them, there are two schools of thought, which have been mentioned repeatedly in the Book of Faith (Kitāb al-Īmān). The first is to affirm them without delving into their meaning, while holding the conviction that Allah, the Exalted, is not like anything, and declaring His transcendence above the attributes of created beings. The second is to interpret them (taʾwīl) in a manner befitting Him. Those who adopt this latter view say: The intent was to test her — whether she is a monotheist who affirms that the Creator, the Disposer, the Doer is Allah alone, and that when a supplicant calls upon Him, he faces the heaven, just as when a worshipper prays, he faces the Kaʿbah. This is not because He is confined to the heaven, just as He is not confined to the direction of the Kaʿbah. Rather, it is because the heaven is the qiblah of those who supplicate, just as the Kaʿbah is the qiblah of those who pray. Or [the test was] whether she was among the idol-worshippers who worship the idols before them. So when she said "in the heaven," he knew she was a monotheist and not an idol-worshipper.

Al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ said: There is no disagreement among all Muslims — their jurists, their ḥadīth scholars, their theologians, their speculative thinkers, and their followers — that the apparent texts mentioning Allah, the Exalted, in the heaven, such as His saying, the Exalted: {«Do you feel secure that He who is in the heaven would not cause the earth to swallow you?»} (Q 67:16) and similar verses, are not to be taken at their apparent meaning. Rather, they are interpreted (mutāʾawwalah) by all of them. So whoever affirms a direction of "above" (fawq) without specifying modality (takyīf) or form (tashkīl) — from the ḥadīth scholars, jurists, and theologians — interprets "in the heaven" as meaning "upon the heaven." And whoever, from the common run of speculative thinkers, theologians, and the people of transcendence (ahl al-tanzīh), affirms the negation of limit (ḥadd) and deems direction (jihah) impossible for Him, Glorified and Exalted, they interpret it according to what its context demands, and he mentioned something similar to what preceded.

He said: Would that I knew what has gathered the people of the Sunnah and the Truth, all of them, upon the obligation of refraining from speculation about the Divine Essence (al-Dhāt), as they were commanded, and they remained silent due to the intellect's bewilderment. They unanimously agreed upon the prohibition of specifying modality (takyīf) and form (tashkīl), and that this is from their standing firm and their restraint — not doubting in existence and the Existent, nor casting aspersion on monotheism, but rather it is its very reality. Then some of them were lenient in affirming a direction, fearing [the consequences of] such leniency — and is there any difference between specifying modality and affirming directions? However, adhering to what the Sacred Law has affirmed — that He is the Subduer above His servants, and that He established Himself upon the Throne (istawā ʿalā al-ʿarsh) — while clinging to the verse that encompasses absolute transcendence, which nothing else is sound in the intellect, namely His saying, the Exalted: {«There is nothing like unto Him»} (Q 42:11), is a safeguard for whomever Allah grants success. And this is the speech of al-Qāḍī, may Allah have mercy on him.

In this ḥadīth [there is evidence] that freeing a believing slave is more virtuous than freeing a disbelieving one. The scholars are unanimous on the permissibility of freeing a disbelieving slave outside of expiations (kaffārāt). They are also unanimous that a disbelieving slave does not suffice for the expiation of killing, as the Quran has stated. They differed regarding the expiation of ẓihār (injurious comparison), oaths, and intercourse during the daytime of Ramaḍān. Al-Shāfiʿī, Mālik, and the majority said: Only a believing slave suffices, by carrying the absolute (muṭlaq) to the restricted (muqayyad) in the expiation of killing. Abū Ḥanīfah, may Allah be pleased with him, and the Kūfans said: A disbelieving slave suffices, due to the absolute wording, for it is called a "neck" (raqabah).

His saying, peace be upon him: "Where is Allah?" She said: "In the heaven." He said: "Who am I?" She said: "You are the Messenger of Allah." He said: "Free her, for she is a believer" — in this is evidence that a disbeliever does not become a believer except by affirming Allah, the Exalted, and the messengership of His Messenger, peace be upon him. And in it is evidence that whoever affirms the two testimonies (al-shahādatayn) and holds that conviction with certainty, that suffices for the soundness of his faith and his being among the people of the qiblah and Paradise. He is not burdened, beyond this, with establishing proof and demonstration for that, nor is he obligated to know the proof. This is the correct view, upon which the majority are agreed. The clarification of this issue has preceded at the beginning of the Book of Faith, along with what pertains to it. And with Allah is the success.

[538] His saying, in the ḥadīth of Ibn Masʿūd: "We used to greet the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, while he was in prayer, and he would respond to us. When we returned from [the land of] al-Najāshī, we greeted him, and he did not respond to us. So we said: O Messenger of Allah, we used to greet you in prayer, and you would respond to us. He said: 'Indeed, in prayer there is occupation [with Allah].'"

[539] And in the ḥadīth of Zayd ibn Arqam, may Allah be pleased with him: "We used to speak during prayer; a man would speak to his companion beside him in prayer, until the verse was revealed: {«And stand before Allah with devotion»} (Q 2:238). So we were commanded to remain silent and forbidden from speaking."

[540] And in the ḥadīth of Jābir, may Allah be pleased with him, he said: "The Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, sent me for a need. Then I caught up with him while he was praying, and I greeted him, and he gestured to me. When he finished, he called me and said: 'Indeed, you greeted just now while I was praying.'"

These ḥadīths contain benefits, among them: the prohibition of speech during prayer, whether it is for its benefit or not; the prohibition of responding to the greeting verbally during it; and that gesturing does not harm, rather responding to the greeting by gesture is recommended. This is the summary of al-Shāfiʿī's view and that of the majority. Al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ said: A group of scholars held the view of responding to the greeting during prayer verbally, among them Abū Hurayrah, Jābir, al-Ḥasan, Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab, Qatādah, and Isḥāq. It was also said: He responds to it in himself. ʿAṭāʾ, al-Nakhaʿī, and al-Thawrī said: He responds after the prayer. Abū Ḥanīfah, may Allah be pleased with him, said: He does not respond, neither verbally nor by gesture, in any case. ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz, Mālik, his companions, and a group said: He responds by gesture and does not respond verbally. And whoever says he responds verbally, it is as if the ḥadīths have not reached him. As for initiating the greeting to one who is praying, the school [of thought] is...

chapters.title_en: Section 303 — On Responding to Salām During Prayer, Cursing Shayṭān, and Permissible Minor Actions in Prayer
chapters.arabic_text:
الشافعي رحمه الله تعالى أنه لا يسلم عليه فإن سلم لم يستحق جوابا وقال به

جماعة من العلماء وعن مالك رضي الله عنه روايتان إحداهما كراهة السلام

والثانية جوازه قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم إن في الصلاة شغلا معناه أن المصلي

وظيفته أن يشتغل بصلاته فيتدبر ما يقوله ولا يعرج على غيرها فلا يرد سلاما

ولا غيره قوله حدثنا هريم هو بضم الهاء وفتح الراء قوله تعالى وقوموا لله

قانتين قيل معناه مطيعين وقيل ساكتين قوله أمرنا بالسكوت ونهينا عن الكلام

فيه دليل على تحريم جميع أنواع كلام الآدميين وأجمع العلماء على أن الكلام

فيها عامدا عالما بتحريمه بغير مصلحتها وبغير إنقاذها وشبهه مبطل للصلاة

وأما الكلام لمصلحتها فقال الشافعي ومالك وأبو حنيفة وأحمد رضي الله عنهم

والجمهور يبطل الصلاة وجوزه الأوزاعي وبعض أصحاب مالك وطائفة قليلة وكلام

الناسي لا يبطلها عندنا وعند الجمهور ما لم يطل وقال أبو حنيفة رضي الله

عنه والكوفيون يبطل وقد تقدم بيانه وفي حديث  جابر رضي الله عنه رد السلام

بالإشارة وأنه لا تبطل الصلاة بالإشارة ونحوها من الحركات اليسيرة وأنه

ينبغي لمن سلم عليه ومنعه من رد السلام مانع أن يعتذر إلى المسلم ويذكر له

ذلك المانع قوله وهو موجه قبل المشرق هو بكسر الجيم أي موجه وجهه وراحلته

وفيه دليل لجواز
# 
# النافلة في السفر حيث توجهت به راحلته وهو مجمع عليه قوله حدثنا كثير بن

شنظير هو بكسر الشين والظاء المعجمتين

| (باب جواز لعن الشيطان في أثناء الصلاة والتعوذ منه)
# وجواز العمل القليل في الصلاة
# [541] قوله إن عفريتا من الجن جعل يفتك علي البارحة ليقطع علي صلاتي هكذا

هو في مسلم
# 
# يفتك وفي رواية البخاري يفلت وهما صحيحان والفتك الأخذ في غفلة وخديعة

والعفريت العاتي المارد من الجن قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم فذعته هو بذال

معجمة وتخفيف العين المهملة أي خنقته قال مسلم وفي رواية أبي بكر بن أبي

شيبة فدعته يعني بالدال المهملة وهو صحيح أيضا ومعناه دفعته دفعا شديدا

والدعت والدع الدفع الشديد وأنكر الخطابي المهملة وقال لا تصح وصححها غيره

وصوبوها وإن كانت المعجمة أوضح وأشهر وفيه دليل على جواز العمل القليل في

الصلاة قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم فلقد هممت أن أربطه حتى تصبحوا تنظرون إليه

أجمعون أو كلكم فيه دليل على أن الجن موجودون وأنهم قد يراهم بعض الآدميين

وأما قول الله تعالى إنه يراكم هو وقبيله من حيث لا ترونهم فمحمول على

الغالب فلو كانت رؤيتهم محالا لما قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ما قال من

رؤيته إياه ومن أنه كان يربطه لينظروا كلهم إليه ويلعب به ولدان أهل

المدينة قال القاضي وقيل إن رؤيتهم على خلقهم وصورهم الأصلية ممتنعة لظاهر

الآية إلا للأنبياء صلوات الله وسلامه عليهم أجمعين ومن خرقت له العادة

وإنما يراهم بنو آدم في صور غير صورهم كما جاء في الآثار قلت هذه دعوى

مجردة فإن لم يصح لها مستند فهي مردودة قال الإمام أبو عبد الله المازري

الجن أجسام  لطيفة روحانية فيحتمل أنه تصور بصورة يمكن ربطه معها ثم يمتنع

من أن يعود إلى ما كان عليه حتى يتأتى اللعب به وإن خرقت العادة أمكن غير

ذلك قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم ثم ذكرت قول أخي سليمان صلاة الله وسلامه عليه

قال القاضي معناه أنه مختص بهذا فامتنع نبينا صلى الله عليه وسلم من ربطه

إما أنه لم يقدر عليه لذلك وإما لكونه لما تذكر ذلك لم يتعاط ذلك لظنه أنه

لم يقدر عليه أو تواضعا وتأدبا قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم فرده الله خاسئا أي

ذليلا صاغرا مطرودا مبعدا قوله وقال بن منصور شعبة عن محمد بن زياد يعني

قال إسحاق بن منصور في روايته حدثنا النضر قال أخبرنا شعبة عن محمد بن زياد
# 
# فخالف رواية رفيقه إسحاق بن إبراهيم السابقة في شيئين أحدهما أنه قال

شعبة عن محمد بن زياد وقال بن ابرهيم شعبة قال أخبرنا محمد والثاني أنه قال

محمد بن زياد وفي رواية بن ابراهيم محمد وهو بن زياد
# [542] قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم ألعنك بلعنة الله التامة قال القاضي يحتمل

تسميتها تامة أي لا نقص فيها ويحتمل الواجبة له المستحقة عليه أو الموجبة

عليه العذاب سرمدا وقال القاضي وقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم ألعنك بلعنة الله

وأعوذ بالله منك دليل جواز الدعاء لغيره وعلى غيره بصيغة المخاطبة خلافا

لابن شعبان من أصحاب مالك في قوله إن الصلاة تبطل بذاك قلت وكذا قال

أصحابنا تبطل الصلاة بالدعاء لغيره بصيغة المخاطبة كقوله للعاطس رحمك الله

أو يرحمك ولمن سلم عليه وعليك السلام وأشباهه والأحاديث السابقة في الباب

الذي قبله في السلام على المصلي تؤيد ما قاله أصحابنا فيتأول هذا الحديث أو

يحمل على أنه كان قبل تحريم الكلام في الصلاة أو غير ذلك قوله صلى الله

عليه وسلم والله لولا دعوة أخينا سليمان لأصبح موثقا يلعب به ولدان
# 
# أهل المدينة فيه جواز الحلف من غير استحلاف لتفخيم ما يخبر به الإنسان

وتعظيمه والمبالغة في صحته وصدقه  وقد كثرت الأحاديث بمثل هذا والولدان

الصبيان
chapters.anchors:
- Root: س-ل-م (s-l-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning of safety, peace, and deliverance from harm; salām as greeting invoking divine protection.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In Kalām, salām signifies the believer's state of submission and the greeting as a covenant of security (amān) between Muslims.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) — verbal greeting; metaphorical (majāz) — the act of turning away from worldly concerns toward worship.
- Root: ش-غ-ل (sh-gh-l)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Occupation, engagement, or preoccupation that absorbs one's full attention.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In worship context, shughl denotes the soul's complete absorption in the divine presence, precluding external distractions.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — being busy; metaphorical — the heart's exclusive orientation toward Allah during prayer.
- Root: ف-ت-ك (f-t-k)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To seize or attack suddenly, by stealth and deception, without prior warning.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological usage, describes the assault of demonic forces upon the worshipper's concentration.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — sudden violent seizure; metaphorical — the spiritual assault of Shayṭān upon the heart during devotion.
- Root: ع-ف-ر (ʿ-f-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Earth, dust; ʿifrīt — a powerful, rebellious, cunning being among the jinn.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Denotes the most defiant and potent of the jinn, embodying rebellion against divine order.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — dust-covered; metaphorical — the lowly, base nature of the rebellious jinn.
- Root: خ-س-ء (kh-s-ʾ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To be driven away with humiliation and disgrace; to be repelled in abasement.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In Quranic usage, khāsiʾan describes the state of being cast out from divine mercy, as with Shayṭān.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — being repelled; metaphorical — the spiritual degradation of the accursed.
- Sībawayh Rule: Rule of ʿAṭf al-Bayān (Appositional Clarification) — When the Prophet ﷺ says "فذعته" (I choked him), the subsequent variant "فدعته" (I pushed him) functions as an explanatory appositive, clarifying the semantic range of the action without altering the grammatical structure.
chapters.translation:
I say: Al-Shāfiʿī, may Allah Most High have mercy upon him, held that one does not initiate salām upon a person engaged in prayer; and if one does offer salām, the one praying is not obligated to respond. A group of scholars concurred with this view. From Mālik, may Allah be pleased with him, two narrations are transmitted: one indicating the disapproval (karāhah) of offering salām, and the second permitting it.

His saying, may Allah's peace and blessings be upon him: «إن في الصلاة شغلا» ("Verily, in prayer there is occupation") — its meaning is that the worshipper's function is to occupy himself with his prayer, reflecting upon what he recites, and not to turn aside to anything else. Thus, he does not respond to salām nor to anything else.

His saying: "Huraym narrated to us" — it is with ḍammah on the hāʾ and fatḥah on the rāʾ.

The saying of Allah Most High: {وَقُومُوا لِلَّهِ قَانِتِينَ} ("And stand before Allah with qunūt") — it is said its meaning is "obedient," and it is said "silent."

His saying: "We were commanded to observe silence and forbidden from speaking" — in this is evidence for the prohibition of all types of human speech [during prayer]. The scholars are unanimous that speaking during prayer deliberately, while knowing of its prohibition, without [the speech being] for the benefit of the prayer, nor for its rescue, nor similar [necessities], invalidates the prayer.

As for speaking for the benefit of the prayer, al-Shāfiʿī, Mālik, Abū Ḥanīfah, and Aḥmad, may Allah be pleased with them, and the majority (al-jumhūr) held that it invalidates the prayer. Al-Awzāʿī, some of Mālik's companions, and a small group permitted it. The speech of one who forgets does not invalidate the prayer according to us and the majority, as long as it is not prolonged. Abū Ḥanīfah, may Allah be pleased with him, and the Kūfans held that it does invalidate. This has been previously explained.

In the ḥadīth of Jābir, may Allah be pleased with him, [there is evidence] for responding to salām by gesture, and that the prayer is not invalidated by gestures and similar minor movements, and that it is incumbent upon the one who is greeted, when prevented from responding verbally by an impediment, to apologize to the one greeting and mention that impediment to him.

His saying: "While his mount was facing the east (muwajjih)" — it is with kasrah on the jīm, meaning he directed his face and his mount [toward the qiblah]. In this is evidence for the permissibility of the supererogatory prayer (al-nāfilah) during travel, in whatever direction one's mount turns, and this is a matter of consensus (mujmaʿ ʿalayh).

His saying: "Kathīr ibn Shanzīr narrated to us" — it is with kasrah on the shīn and the ẓāʾ, both being unpointed letters.

(Chapter: The Permissibility of Cursing Shayṭān During Prayer and Seeking Refuge from Him, and the Permissibility of Minor Actions During Prayer)

[541] His saying: "Verily, an ʿifrīt from among the jinn turned upon me (yaftiku) last night to interrupt my prayer" — thus it appears in Muslim: يفتك (yaftiku). In al-Bukhārī's narration: يفلت (yaflitu) — both are sound. Al-fatk is seizing [someone] in a moment of heedlessness and deception. Al-ʿifrīt is the rebellious, defiant one from among the jinn.

His saying, may Allah's peace and blessings be upon him: "So I choked him (fadhaʿtuhu)" — it is with an unpointed dhāl and tashdīd-less ʿayn, meaning "I strangled him." Muslim said: In the narration of Abū Bakr ibn Abī Shaybah: "fadaʿtuhu" — meaning with an unpointed dāl — and it is also sound, its meaning being "I pushed him with a forceful push." Al-daʿt and al-daʿ both mean forceful pushing. Al-Khaṭṭābī rejected the unpointed dāl [variant], saying it is not authentic, but others authenticated it and deemed it correct, even though the pointed dhāl is clearer and more famous.

In this is evidence for the permissibility of minor actions during prayer.

His saying, may Allah's peace and blessings be upon him: "And I indeed resolved to tie him to one of the pillars until morning, so that you could all look upon him" — or "all of you" — in this is evidence that the jinn exist and that some human beings may see them. As for the saying of Allah Most High: {إِنَّهُ يَرَاكُمْ هُوَ وَقَبِيلُهُ مِنْ حَيْثُ لَا تَرَوْنَهُمْ} ("Indeed, he and his tribe see you from where you cannot see them") — it is interpreted according to the predominant [condition]. For if their visibility were absolutely impossible, the Prophet, may Allah's peace and blessings be upon him, would not have said what he said about seeing him, nor about tying him so that they could all look at him, and the children of Madīnah could play with him.

Al-Qāḍī said: It is said that seeing them in their original forms and shapes is impossible due to the apparent meaning of the verse, except for the prophets, may Allah's peace and blessings be upon them all, and those for whom the natural order was breached (man khuriqat lahu al-ʿādah). Rather, the children of Adam only see them in forms other than their true forms, as has come in the traditions (āthār).

I say: This is a bare claim (daʿwā mujarradah); if no supporting basis (mustanad) is established for it, then it is rejected (mardūdah).

Imam Abū ʿAbdillāh al-Māzarī said: The jinn are subtle, spiritual bodies (ajsām laṭīfah rūḥāniyyah). It is possible that he [the ʿifrīt] appeared in a form in which he could be tied, then was prevented from returning to his original state until the playing with him could be accomplished. And if the natural order was breached, then something else could be possible.

His saying, may Allah's peace and blessings be upon him: "Then I remembered the saying of my brother Sulaymān, may Allah's peace and blessings be upon him" — Al-Qāḍī said: Its meaning is that he [Sulaymān] was uniquely granted this [power over the jinn]. Thus our Prophet, may Allah's peace and blessings be upon him, refrained from tying him — either because he was not empowered to do so, or because upon recalling this, he did not undertake it, thinking he was not capable of it, or out of humility and proper etiquette (tawāḍuʿan wa taʾadduban).

His saying, may Allah's peace and blessings be upon him: "So Allah returned him humiliated (khāsiʾan)" — meaning disgraced, abased, expelled, and driven far away.

His saying: "And Ibn Manṣūr said: Shuʿbah, from Muḥammad ibn Ziyād" — meaning Isḥāq ibn Manṣūr said in his narration: "Al-Naḍr narrated to us, he said: Shuʿbah informed us, from Muḥammad ibn Ziyād." This contradicts the narration of his companion Isḥāq ibn Ibrāhīm mentioned previously in two matters: first, he said "Shuʿbah, from Muḥammad ibn Ziyād," while Ibn Ibrāhīm said "Shuʿbah said: Muḥammad informed us"; and second, he said "Muḥammad ibn Ziyād," while in Ibn Ibrāhīm's narration it is "Muḥammad" — meaning Ibn Ziyād.

[542] His saying, may Allah's peace and blessings be upon him: "I curse you with the complete curse of Allah (al-laʿnah al-tāmmah)" — Al-Qāḍī said: It is possible that it is called "complete" meaning there is no deficiency in it; and it is possible [it means] the curse that is obligatory upon him, deserved by him, or that necessitates upon him eternal torment (sarmad).

Al-Qāḍī said: And his saying, may Allah's peace and blessings be upon him: "I curse you with the curse of Allah, and I seek refuge in Allah from you" — is evidence for the permissibility of supplicating for another person, and against another person, using the direct address form (ṣīghat al-mukhāṭabah), contrary to Ibn Shaʿbān from among Mālik's companions, who held that the prayer is invalidated by that.

I say: Likewise, our companions (aṣḥābunā) said that the prayer is invalidated by supplicating for another person using the direct address form, such as saying to one who sneezes: "May Allah have mercy upon you" (raḥimaka Allāh) or "yarḥamuka Allāh," or to the one who offers salām: "And upon you be peace" (wa ʿalayka al-salām), and similar examples. The previous ḥadīths in the preceding chapter concerning salām upon the one praying support what our companions have said. Thus, this ḥadīth is interpreted (yuʾawwal) or carried [as having occurred] before the prohibition of speech during prayer, or other [explanations].

His saying, may Allah's peace and blessings be upon him: "By Allah, were it not for the supplication of our brother Sulaymān, he would have remained bound until morning, played with by the children (wildān) of Madīnah" — in this is evidence for the permissibility of swearing without being asked to swear, in order to magnify and exalt what one reports, and to emphasize its correctness and truthfulness. The ḥadīths containing such [oaths] are numerous. Al-wildān are the young boys.
