Abū Ḥanīfah (may Allah be pleased with him) said: The foundational principle is prostration after the salām, and he interpreted some hadiths accordingly. Al-Shāfiʿī (may Allah have mercy on him) said: The foundational principle is prostration before the salām, and he referred the remaining hadiths back to it. Mālik (may Allah have mercy on him) said: If the forgetfulness was an addition (ziyādah), one prostrates after the salām; if it was a deficiency (nuqṣān), then before it.

As for al-Shāfiʿī (may Allah have mercy on him), he says regarding the hadith of Abū Saʿīd: "If it was a fifth, it completes it (shaffaʿahā)" — and he explicitly stated prostration before the salām while allowing for the possibility of addition, and the one who permits [the possibility] is like one for whom it is actualized (al-mujawwiz ka-al-mawjūd). He interprets the hadith of Ibn Masʿūd (may Allah be pleased with him) concerning standing for a fifth and prostrating after the salām as [a case where] the Prophet ﷺ did not become aware of the forgetfulness until after the salām — had he known of it before, he would have prostrated before it. He interprets the hadith of Dhū al-Yadayn as [a case of] a prayer in which forgetfulness occurred, and he forgot the prostration before the salām, so he made it up afterward.

This is al-Māzarī's discourse, and it is excellent and precious speech. The strongest of the schools (madhāhib) here is the school of Mālik (may Allah have mercy on him), then the school of al-Shāfiʿī. Al-Shāfiʿī (may Allah have mercy on him) has a position like Mālik's school (may Allah have mercy on him), acting by choice (al-takhyīr). And upon the position of Mālik's school (may Allah have mercy on him): if two forgetfulnesses combine in one prayer — one of addition and one of deficiency — one prostrates before the salām. Al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ (may Allah have mercy on him) and a group of our companions said: There is no disagreement among these [authorities]...

chapters.title_en: The Consensus on Sujūd al-Sahw and the Resolution of Doubt in Prayer
chapters.arabic_text:
المختلفين وغيرهم من العلماء أنه
# 
# لو سجد قبل السلام أو بعده للزيادة أو النقص أنه يجزئه ولا تفسد صلاته

وإنما اختلافهم في الأفضل والله أعلم قال الجمهور لو سها سهوين فأكثر كفاه

سجدتان للجميع وبهذا قال الشافعي ومالك وأبو حنيفة وأحمد رضوان الله عليهم

وجمهور التابعين وعن بن أبي ليلى رحمه الله تعالى لكل سهو سجدتان وفيه حديث

ضعيف قوله جاءه الشيطان فلبس هو بتخفيف الباء أي خلط عليه صلاته وهوشها

عليه وشككه فيها قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا نودي بالأذان أدبر الشيطان

إلى آخره هذا الحديث تقدم شرحه في باب الأذان قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم في

حديث أبي هريرة فإذا لم يدر أحدكم كم صلى فليسجد سجدتين وهو جالس اختلف

العلماء في المراد به فقال الحسن البصري وطائفة من السلف بظاهر
#

# الحديث وقالوا إذا شك المصلي فلم يدر زاد أو نقص فليس عليه إلا سجدتان

وهو جالس عملا بظاهر هذا الحديث وقال الشعبي والأوزاعي وجماعة كثيرة من

السلف إذا لم يدر كم صلى لزمه أن يعيد الصلاة مرة بعد أخرى أبدا حتى يستيقن

وقال بعضهم يعيد ثلاث مرات فإذا شك في الرابعة فلا إعادة عليه وقال مالك

والشافعي وأحمد رضي الله عنهم والجمهور متى شك في صلاته هل صلى ثلاثا أم

أربعا مثلا لزمه البناء على  اليقين فيجب أن يأتي برابعة ويسجد للسهو عملا

بحديث أبي سعيد وهو قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا شك أحدكم في صلاته فلم يدر

كم صلى ثلاثا أم أربعا فليطرح الشك وليبن على ما استيقن ثم يسجد سجدتين قبل

أن يسلم فإن كان صلى خمسا شفعن له صلاته وإن كان صلى إتماما لأربع كانتا

ترغيما للشيطان قالوا فهذا الحديث صريح في وجوب البناء على اليقين وهو مفسر

لحديث أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه فيحمل حديث أبي هريرة عليه وهذا متعين فوجب

المصير إليه مع ما في حديث أبي سعيد من الموافقة لقواعد الشرع في الشك في

الأحداث والميراث من المفقود وغير ذلك والله أعلم قوله نظرنا تسليمه أي

انتظرناه
# [570] قوله في حديث بن بحينة صلى لنا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إلى

قوله فسجد سجدتين وهو جالس قبل التسليم ثم سلم فيه حجة للشافعي رحمه الله

تعالى ومالك والجمهور على أبي حنيفة رضي الله عنه فإن عنده السجود للنقص

والزيادة بعد السلام
# 
# قوله عن عبد الله بن بحينة الأسدي حليف بني عبد المطلب أما الأسدي

فبإسكان السين ويقال فيه الأزدي كما ذكره في الرواية الأخرى والأزد والأسد

بإسكان السين قبيلة واحدة وهما اسمان مترادفان لها وهم أزد شنوءة وأما قوله

حليف بني عبد المطلب فكذا هو في نسخ صحيح البخاري ومسلم والذي ذكره بن سعد

وغيره من أهل السير والتواريخ أنه حليف بني المطلب وكان جده حالف المطلب بن

عبد مناف قوله عن عبد الله بن مالك بن بحينة والصواب في هذا أن ينون مالك

ويكتب بن بحينة بالالف لأن عبد الله هو بن مالك وبن بحينة فمالك أبوه

وبحينة أمه وهي زوجة مالك فمالك أبو عبد الله وبحينة أم عبد الله فإذا قرئ

كما ذكرناه انتظم على الصواب ولو قرئ بإضافة مالك إلى بن فسد المعنى واقتضى

أن يكون مالك ابنا لبحينة وهذا غلط وإنما هو زوجها وفي الحديث دليل لمسائل

كثيرة إحداها أن سجود السهو قبل السلام  إما مطلقا كما يقوله الشافعي وإما

في النقص كما يقوله مالك الثانية أن التشهد الأول والجلوس له ليسا بركنين

في الصلاة ولا واجبين إذ لو كانا واجبين لما جبرهما السجود كالركوع والسجود

وغيرهما وبهذا قال مالك وأبو حنيفة والشافعي رحمهم الله تعالى وقال أحمد في

طائفة قليلة هما واجبان وإذا سها جبرهما السجود على مقتضى الحديث الثالثة

فيه أنه يشرع التكبير لسجود السهو وهذا مجمع عليه واختلفوا فيما إذا فعلهما

بعد السلام هل يتحرم ويتشهد ويسلم أم لا والصحيح في مذهبنا أنه يسلم ولا

يتشهد وهكذا الصحيح عندنا في سجود التلاوة أنه يسلم ولا يتشهد كصلاة

الجنازة وقال مالك يتشهد ويسلم
# 
# في سجود السهو بعد السلام واختلف قوله هل يجهر بسلامهما كسائر الصلوات أم

لا وهل يحرم لهما أم لا وقد ثبت السلام لهما إذا فعلتا بعد السلام في حديث

بن مسعود وحديث ذي اليدين ولم يثبت في التشهد حديث واعلم أن جمهور العلماء

على أنه يسجد للسهو في صلاة التطوع كالفرض وقال بن سيرين وقتادة لا سجود

للتطوع وهو قول ضعيف غريب عن الشافعي رحمه الله تعالى
# [571] قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم في حديث أبي سعيد ثم يسجد سجدتين قبل أن

يسلم ظاهر الدلالة لمذهب الشافعي رحمه الله تعالى كما سبق في أنه يسجد

للزيادة والنقص قبل السلام وسبق تقريره في كلام المازري واعترض عليه بعض

أصحاب مالك بأن مالكا رحمه الله تعالى رواه مرسلا وهذا اعتراض باطل لوجهين

أحدهما أن الثقات الحفاظ الأكثرين رووه متصلا فلا يضر مخالفة واحد لهم في

إرساله لأنهم حفظوا ما لم يحفظه وهم ثقات ضابطون حفاظ متقنون الثاني أن

المرسل عند مالك رحمه الله تعالى حجة فهو وارد عليهم على كل تقدير قوله صلى

الله عليه وسلم كانتا ترغيما للشيطان أي إغاظة له وإذلالا مأخوذ من الرغام
chapters.anchors:
- Root: س-ج-د (s-j-d)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Physical prostration; the act of placing the forehead on the ground in worship.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The culminating posture of humility (khushūʿ) before Allah; in juristic discourse, a compensatory act (jabr) for ritual deficiency.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) in ritual context; metaphorically extended to denote "submission" or "remedy" for error.
- Root: س-ه-و (s-h-w)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Forgetfulness, inadvertence, or neglect arising from human fallibility.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): A lapse in attentiveness (ghaflah) during worship that requires ritual expiation (jabr) without invalidating the act.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for mental oversight; majāz when applied to the devil's "whispering" (waswasah) that induces such lapses.
- Root: ي-ق-ن (y-q-n)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Certainty, firm conviction, absence of doubt.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The epistemological foundation for legal rulings (uṣūl al-fiqh); in prayer, the baseline upon which one builds when doubt occurs.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for certitude; majāz for the legal presumption (aṣl) that one has not completed an obligation until proven otherwise.
- Sībawayh Rule: Taqdīr al-Maḥdhūf (Ellipsis Restoration) — When the text omits a grammatical element (e.g., the subject of "قالوا"), the translator must supply the implied referent (the scholars) to preserve syntactic coherence.
chapters.translation:
I say: The scholars — both those who differed and others — agree that if one prostrates before the salām or after it, whether for an increase or a decrease [in the prayer], it suffices him and his prayer is not rendered invalid. Their disagreement is only concerning what is superior (al-afḍal), and Allah knows best.

The majority (al-jumhūr) said: If one errs with two forgetfulnesses or more, two prostrations suffice for all of them. This is the position of al-Shāfiʿī, Mālik, Abū Ḥanīfah, and Aḥmad — may Allah be pleased with them — and the majority of the Followers (al-tābiʿīn). It is narrated from Ibn Abī Laylā — may Allah have mercy on him — that for every forgetfulness there are two prostrations, but there is a weak ḥadīth concerning this.

His statement — "the devil came to him and confused him" (jāʾahu al-shayṭānu fa-labbasa) — with the tashdīd removed from the bāʾ (i.e., labasa, not labbasa) means: he mixed up his prayer for him, caused him to err in it, and instilled doubt in him.

His statement — peace and blessings be upon him — "When the call to prayer is proclaimed, the devil retreats" (idhā nūdiya bil-adhāni adbara al-shayṭānu) — to its end: This ḥadīth has already been explained in the chapter on the adhān.

His statement — peace and blessings be upon him — in the ḥadīth of Abū Hurayrah: "If any of you does not know how many [rakʿahs] he has prayed, let him prostrate two prostrations while seated" — the scholars differed over its intended meaning. Al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī and a group of the Salaf took it according to its apparent wording (ẓāhir), saying: If the worshipper doubts and does not know whether he increased or decreased, nothing is incumbent upon him except two prostrations while seated, acting upon the apparent sense of this ḥadīth.

Al-Shaʿbī, al-Awzāʿī, and a large group of the Salaf said: If one does not know how many [rakʿahs] he has prayed, he must repeat the prayer time after time, forever, until he is certain. Some said: He repeats three times; if he doubts on the fourth, then no repetition is required of him.

Mālik, al-Shāfiʿī, Aḥmad — may Allah be pleased with them — and the majority said: Whenever one doubts in his prayer — e.g., whether he prayed three or four [rakʿahs] — he must build upon certainty (al-yaqīn). Thus he must perform a fourth [rakʿah] and prostrate for forgetfulness, acting upon the ḥadīth of Abū Saʿīd, namely his statement — peace and blessings be upon him: "If any of you doubts in his prayer and does not know whether he prayed three or four, let him cast aside the doubt and build upon what he is certain of, then prostrate two prostrations before the salām. If he had prayed five, they make his prayer even; if he had prayed a complete four, they are a humiliation (targhīm) for the devil."

They said: This ḥadīth is explicit (ṣarīḥ) concerning the obligation of building upon certainty, and it is an explicative (mufassir) of the ḥadīth of Abū Hurayrah — may Allah be pleased with him. Thus the ḥadīth of Abū Hurayrah is interpreted in light of it. This is the necessary course, so one must adopt it — especially given that the ḥadīth of Abū Saʿīd accords with the legal principles (qawāʿid al-sharʿ) concerning doubt in ritual impurities (aḥdāth), inheritance from a missing person, and other matters. And Allah knows best.

His statement — "we looked at his salām" (naẓarnā taslīmahu) — means: we waited for it.

[570] His statement in the ḥadīth of Ibn Buḥaynah — "The Messenger of Allah — peace and blessings be upon him — led us in prayer" — up to his saying: "Then he prostrated two prostrations while seated before the salām, then gave the salām." In this is an argument for al-Shāfiʿī — may Allah have mercy on him — Mālik, and the majority against Abū Ḥanīfah — may Allah be pleased with him — for in his view, the prostration for both decrease and increase is after the salām.

His statement: "From ʿAbdullāh ibn Buḥaynah al-Asadī, an ally (ḥalīf) of the Banū ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib." As for "al-Asadī," it is with sukūn on the sīn, and it is also said "al-Azdī," as mentioned in the other narration. Al-Azd and al-Asad — with sukūn on the sīn — are one tribe; they are two synonymous names for it, namely Azd Shanūʾah. As for his saying "an ally of the Banū ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib," thus it appears in the copies of Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī and Muslim. However, what Ibn Saʿd and other biographers and historians mention is that he was an ally of the Banū al-Muṭṭalib, for his grandfather had formed an alliance with al-Muṭṭalib ibn ʿAbd Manāf.

His statement: "From ʿAbdullāh ibn Mālik ibn Buḥaynah." The correct reading here is to nunate "Mālik" (i.e., ʿAbdullāh ibn Mālikin) and to write "ibn Buḥaynah" with an alif, because ʿAbdullāh is the son of Mālik and the son of Buḥaynah. Thus Mālik is his father, and Buḥaynah is his mother, and she was the wife of Mālik. So Mālik is the father of ʿAbdullāh, and Buḥaynah is the mother of ʿAbdullāh. When read as we have stated, it is correct and coherent. If one reads it as the genitive construction of Mālik to "ibn" (i.e., Mālik ibn Buḥaynah), the meaning is corrupted, implying that Mālik was a son of Buḥaynah — and this is an error, for he was only her husband.

In this ḥadīth is evidence for numerous issues:

**First**: That the prostration of forgetfulness is before the salām — either absolutely, as al-Shāfiʿī holds, or specifically for decrease, as Mālik holds.

**Second**: That the first tashahhud and its sitting are neither pillars (arkān) nor obligatory acts (wājibāt) in the prayer. For if they were obligatory, the prostration would not compensate for them, unlike the bowing (rukūʿ), prostration (sujūd), and other [pillars]. This is the position of Mālik, Abū Ḥanīfah, and al-Shāfiʿī — may Allah have mercy on them. Aḥmad and a small group said: They are obligatory, and if one errs [in them], the prostration compensates for them, in accordance with the implication of the ḥadīth.

**Third**: That it is legislated to pronounce the takbīr for the prostration of forgetfulness. This is a matter of consensus (ijmāʿ). They differed, however, concerning when one performs them after the salām: whether one enters into them with a takbīr al-taḥrīmah, recites the tashahhud, and gives the salām, or not. The correct view in our school (madhhab) is that one gives the salām and does not recite the tashahhud. Likewise, the correct view with us concerning the prostration of recitation (sujūd al-tilāwah) is that one gives the salām and does not recite the tashahhud, like the funeral prayer (ṣalāt al-janāzah). Mālik said: One recites the tashahhud and gives the salām in the prostration of forgetfulness after the salām. His opinion also differed on whether one pronounces the salām audibly, as in other prayers, or not, and whether one enters with a taḥrīmah or not. The salām for both [prostrations] when performed after the salām is established in the ḥadīth of Ibn Masʿūd and the ḥadīth of Dhū al-Yadayn, but no ḥadīth is established concerning the tashahhud [for them].

Know that the majority of scholars hold that one prostrates for forgetfulness in supererogatory prayers (al-taṭawwuʿ) just as in obligatory ones. Ibn Sīrīn and Qatādah said: There is no prostration for supererogatory prayers — a weak opinion, strange [and rejected] from al-Shāfiʿī — may Allah have mercy on him.

[571] His statement — peace and blessings be upon him — in the ḥadīth of Abū Saʿīd: "Then he prostrates two prostrations before the salām" — is clearly indicative of the school of al-Shāfiʿī — may Allah have mercy on him — as previously stated, namely that one prostrates for both increase and decrease before the salām. Its confirmation has already been presented in the discussion of al-Māzarī. Some of Mālik's companions objected to him, claiming that Mālik — may Allah have mercy on him — narrated it as disconnected (mursal). This objection is invalid for two reasons:

**First**: The trustworthy, meticulous preservers (al-thiqāt al-ḥuffāẓ) — the majority — narrated it as connected (muttaṣil). The opposition of one [narrator] in making it mursal does not harm them, because they preserved what he did not preserve, and they are trustworthy, precise, meticulous preservers.

**Second**: The mursal [narration] is, according to Mālik — may Allah have mercy on him — a valid proof (ḥujjah). Thus it is an argument against them in any case.

His statement — peace and blessings be upon him: "They are a humiliation (targhīm) for the devil" — means: a cause of enraging him and humiliating him. It is derived from al-rugḥām (dust), i.e., rubbing one's nose in the dust.

chapters.title_en: The Prostration of Forgetfulness and the Impermissibility of Forgetfulness in Prophetic Revelation
chapters.arabic_text:
وهو التراب ومنه أرغم الله أنفه والمعنى أن الشيطان لبس عليه صلاته وتعرض

لإفسادها ونقصها فجعل الله تعالى للمصلي طريقا إلى جبر صلاته وتدارك ما

لبسه  عليه وإرغام الشيطان ورده خاسئا مبعدا
# 
# عن مراده وكملت صلاة بن آدم وامتثل أمر الله تعالى الذي عصى به إبليس من

امتناعه من السجود والله أعلم قوله في اسناد
# [572] حديث بن مسعود حدثنا أبو بكر وعثمان ابنا أبي شيبة إلى آخره هذا

الإسناد كله كوفيون إلا إسحاق بن راهويه رفيق ابني أبي شيبة قوله فسجد

سجدتين ثم سلم دليل لمن قال يسلم إذا سجد للسهو بعد السلام وقد سبق بيان

الخلاف فيه قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم لو حدث في الصلاة شيء أنبأتكم به فيه

أنه لا يؤخر البيان وقت الحاجة قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم ولكن إنما أنا بشر

أنسى كما تنسون فإذا نسيت فذكروني فيه دليل على جواز النسيان عليه صلى الله

عليه وسلم في أحكام الشرع وهو مذهب جمهور العلماء وهو ظاهر القرآن والحديث

اتفقوا على أنه صلى الله عليه وسلم لا يقر عليه بل يعلمه الله تعالى به ثم

قال الأكثرون شرطه تنبهه صلى الله عليه وسلم على الفور متصلا بالحادثة ولا

يقع فيه تأخير وجوزت طائفة تأخيره مدة حياته صلى الله عليه وسلم واختاره

إمام الحرمين ومنعت طائفة من العلماء السهو عليه صلى الله عليه وسلم في

الأفعال البلاغية والعبادات كما أجمعوا على منعه واستحالته عليه صلى الله

عليه وسلم في الأقوال البلاغية وأجابوا عن الظواهر الواردة في ذلك وإليه

مال الاستاذ أبو إسحاق الإسفرائيني والصحيح الأول فإن السهو لا يناقض

النبوة وإذا لم يقر عليه لم يحصل منه مفسدة بل تحصل فيه فائدة وهو بيان
# 
# أحكام الناسي وتقرير الأحكام قال القاضي واختلفوا في جواز السهو عليه صلى

الله عليه وسلم في الأمور التي لا تتعلق بالبلاغ وبيان أحكام الشرع من

أفعاله وعاداته وأذكار قلبه فجوزه الجمهور وأما السهو في الأقوال البلاغية

فأجمعوا على منعه كما أجمعوا على امتناع تعمده وأما السهو في الأقوال

الدنيوية وفيما ليس سبيله البلاغ من الكلام الذي لا يتعلق بالأحكام ولا

أخبار القيامة وما يتعلق بها ولا يضاف إلى وحي  فجوزه قوم إذ لا مفسدة فيه

قال القاضي رحمه الله تعالى والحق الذي لا شك فيه ترجيح قول من منع ذلك على

الأنبياء في كل خبر من الأخبار كما لا يجوز عليهم خلف في خبر لا عمدا ولا

سهوا لا في صحة ولا في مرض ولارضاء ولا غضب وحسبك في ذلك أن سيرة نبينا صلى

الله عليه وسلم وكلامه وأفعاله مجموعة معتنى بها على مر الزمان يتداولها

الموافق والمخالف والمؤمن والمرتاب فلم يأت في شيء منها استدراك غلط في قول

ولا اعتراف بوهم في كلمة ولو كان لنقل كما نقل سهوه في الصلاة ونومه عنها

واستدراكه رأيه في تلقيح النخل وفي نزوله بأدنى مياه بدر وقوله صلى الله

عليه وسلم والله لا أحلف على يمين فأرى غيرها خيرا منها إلا فعلت الذي هو

خير وكفرت عن يميني وغير ذلك وأما جواز السهو في الاعتقادات في أمور الدنيا

فغير ممتنع والله أعلم قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم فإذا نسيت فذكروني فيه أمر

التابع بتذكير المتبوع بما ينساه قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم وإذا شك أحدكم في

صلاته فليتحر الصواب فليتم عليه ثم ليسجد سجدتين وفي رواية فلينظر أحرى ذلك

للصواب وفي رواية فليتحر أقرب ذلك إلى الصواب وفي رواية فليتحر الذي يرى

أنه الصواب فيه دليل لأبي حنيفة رحمه الله تعالى وموافقيه من أهل الكوفة

وغيرهم من أهل الرأي على أن من شك في صلاته في عدد ركعات تحرى وبنى على

غالب ظنه ولا يلزمه الاقتصار على الأقل والإتيان بالزيادة وظاهر هذا الحديث

حجة لهم ثم اختلف هؤلاء فقال أبو حنيفة ومالك رحمهما الله تعالى في طائفة

هذا لمن اعتراه الشك مرة بعد أخرى وأما غيره فيبني على اليقين
# 
# وقال آخرون هو على عمومه وذهب الشافعي والجمهور إلى أنه إذا شك هل صلى

ثلاثا أم أربعا مثلا لزمه البناء على اليقين وهو الأقل فيأتي بما بقي ويسجد

للسهو واحتجوا بقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم في حديث أبي سعيد رضي الله عنه

فليطرح الشك وليبن على ما استيقن ثم يسجد سجدتين قبل أن يسلم فإن كان صلى

خمسا شفعن له صلاته وإن كان صلى إتماما لأربع كانتا ترغيما للشيطان وهذا

صريح في وجوب البناء على اليقين وحملوا التحري في حديث بن مسعود رضي الله

عنه على الأخذ باليقين قالوا والتحري هو القصد ومنه قول الله تعالى تحروا

رشدا فمعنى الحديث فليقصد الصواب فليعمل به وقصد الصواب هو ما بينه في حديث

أبي سعيد وغيره فإن قالت الحنفية حديث أبي سعيد لا يخالف ما قلناه لأنه ورد

في الشك وهو ما استوى طرفاه ومن شك ولم يترجح له أحد الطرفين بنى على الأقل

بالإجماع بخلاف من غلب على ظنه أنه صلى أربعا مثلا فالجواب أن تفسير الشك

بمستوى الطرفين إنما هو اصطلاح طارئ للأصوليين وأما في اللغة فالتردد بين

وجود الشيء وعدمه كله يسمى شكا سواء المستوي والراجح والمرجوح والحديث يحمل
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ت-ر-ب (turāb)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Earth, dust; the substance from which Adam was created and to which he returns
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Symbol of humility and divine decree; "righam" (humiliation) linked to dust as the origin of man
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: dust; Metaphorical: "arghama Allāhu anfahu" — to force one's nose into dust, i.e., to humiliate utterly
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clause (al-sharṭ wa al-jawāb) — "fa-idhā nasītu fa-dhakkirūnī" (if I forget, then remind me) establishes a general command contingent upon a condition, with the imperative as the apodosis.
chapters.translation:
I say: It is the dust, and from it [the Prophet ﷺ said]: "May Allah rub his nose in the dust" — meaning that Satan confounded his prayer and sought to corrupt and diminish it. So Allah, exalted, made for the worshipper a path to repair his prayer and rectify what Satan had confounded upon him, and to humiliate Satan and drive him back, rejected and banished from his aim. Thus the prayer of the son of Adam is completed, and he complies with the command of Allah, exalted, which Iblīs disobeyed by his refusal to prostrate. And Allah knows best.

His saying in the chain of transmission of [572] — the ḥadīth of Ibn Masʿūd: "Abū Bakr and ʿUthmān, the two sons of Abī Shaybah, narrated to us..." to the end — this entire chain is Kūfan except for Isḥāq ibn Rāhawayh, the companion of the two sons of Abī Shaybah.

His saying: "He prostrated two prostrations, then gave the salutation" — this is evidence for those who hold that one gives the salutation when prostrating for forgetfulness after the salutation [already given]. The discussion of the disagreement on this has preceded.

His saying ﷺ: "If something had occurred in the prayer, I would have informed you of it" — in this is [the principle] that clarification is not delayed beyond the time of need.

His saying ﷺ: "But I am only a human being; I forget just as you forget. So if I forget, remind me" — in this is evidence for the permissibility of forgetfulness upon him ﷺ in the rulings of the Sacred Law. This is the doctrine of the majority of scholars, and it is the apparent [meaning] of the Qur'an and the Ḥadīth. They are agreed that he ﷺ is not left [in error] — rather, Allah, exalted, informs him of it. Then the majority said: its condition is that his ﷺ awareness [of the error] occurs immediately, connected to the incident, with no delay occurring. And a group permitted its delay for the duration of his ﷺ lifetime, and this was chosen by the Imām al-Ḥaramayn [al-Juwaynī]. And a group of scholars prohibited forgetfulness upon him ﷺ in the acts of conveying [revelation] and acts of worship, just as they were unanimous on its prohibition and impossibility upon him ﷺ in the words of conveying. And they responded to the apparent [texts] that came regarding that. And toward this leaned al-Ustādh Abū Isḥāq al-Isfarāyīnī. But the correct [view] is the first, for forgetfulness does not contradict prophethood, and when he is not left [in error], no harm results from it — rather, a benefit results from it, namely the clarification of the rulings for the one who forgets and the establishment of the rulings.

Al-Qāḍī [ʿIyāḍ] said: They differed regarding the permissibility of forgetfulness upon him ﷺ in matters that do not pertain to conveying [revelation] and clarifying the rulings of the Sacred Law — from his acts, his customs, and the remembrances of his heart. The majority permitted it. As for forgetfulness in the words of conveying, they were unanimous on its prohibition, just as they were unanimous on the impossibility of his deliberately [erring]. As for forgetfulness in worldly speech and in speech that is not a means of conveying — speech that does not pertain to rulings, nor to reports of the Resurrection and what pertains to it, nor is attributed to revelation — a group permitted it, since there is no harm in it.

Al-Qāḍī, may Allah have mercy on him, said: The truth, about which there is no doubt, is the preponderance of the view of those who prohibit that upon the prophets in every report of reports — just as it is not permissible upon them to break a promise in any report, neither deliberately nor by forgetfulness, neither in health nor in illness, neither in pleasure nor in anger. And sufficient for you in this is that the biography of our Prophet ﷺ, his speech, and his acts are collected and attended to across the ages, circulated by the agreeing and the disagreeing, the believer and the skeptic — and nothing has come in any of it of a correction of an error in speech, nor an acknowledgment of a mistake in a word. Had it been so, it would have been transmitted just as his forgetfulness in prayer was transmitted, and his sleeping past it, and his correction of his own opinion regarding the pollination of date-palms, and his descending at the lower waters of Badr, and his saying ﷺ: "By Allah, I do not swear an oath and then see something better than it, except that I do that which is better and expiate for my oath" — and other such matters. As for the permissibility of forgetfulness in beliefs regarding worldly matters, that is not impossible. And Allah knows best.

His saying ﷺ: "So if I forget, remind me" — in this is a command for the follower to remind the followed of what he forgets.

His saying ﷺ: "And if any of you is in doubt about his prayer, let him seek the correct [estimate] and complete upon it, then prostrate two prostrations" — and in one narration: "let him consider which is more likely to be correct" — and in another narration: "let him seek the closest of that to correctness" — and in another: "let him seek what he thinks is correct."

In this is evidence for Abū Ḥanīfah, may Allah have mercy on him, and his supporters from the people of Kūfah and others of the people of opinion (ahl al-ra'y), that whoever doubts in his prayer regarding the number of units (rakʿāt) should seek the correct estimate and build upon his predominant conjecture, and he is not obliged to restrict himself to the lesser [number] and perform the additional [unit]. And the apparent [meaning] of this ḥadīth is an argument for them.

Then these [scholars] differed: Abū Ḥanīfah and Mālik, may Allah have mercy on them both, said regarding a group: this [ruling] applies to one whom doubt afflicts repeatedly; as for other than him, he builds upon certainty.

And others said: it is upon its generality. And al-Shāfiʿī and the majority went to [the view] that if one doubts whether he prayed three or four, for example, he is obliged to build upon certainty, which is the lesser, so he performs what remains and prostrates for forgetfulness. They argued with his saying ﷺ in the ḥadīth of Abū Saʿīd, may Allah be pleased with him: "Let him cast aside the doubt and build upon what he is certain of, then prostrate two prostrations before the salutation. For if he prayed five, they make his prayer even, and if he prayed a completion of four, they are a humiliation for Satan." And this is explicit regarding the obligation of building upon certainty. And they interpreted the "seeking the correct estimate" (taḥarrī) in the ḥadīth of Ibn Masʿūd, may Allah be pleased with him, as [meaning] taking to certainty. They said: And al-taḥarrī is the intention [of correctness], and from it is the saying of Allah, exalted: {فَتَحَرَّوْا رَشَدًا} "So seek the path of right guidance" (Q. 18:10). So the meaning of the ḥadīth is: let him intend correctness and act upon it. And intending correctness is what is clarified in the ḥadīth of Abū Saʿīd and others.

If the Ḥanafīs say: The ḥadīth of Abū Saʿīd does not contradict what we have said, because it came regarding doubt (shakk), which is when both sides are equal; and whoever doubts without one side preponderating builds upon the lesser by consensus — unlike one whose predominant conjecture is that he prayed four, for example — then the answer is: The interpretation of "doubt" as [only] the equal-sided [case] is merely a terminological innovation of the uṣūliyyūn. As for in the language, hesitation between the existence of a thing and its non-existence — all of it is called "doubt" (shakk), whether equal, preponderant, or outweighed. And the ḥadīth is carried upon [this general meaning].

chapters.title_en: Section 312 — On the Addition of a Rakʿah in Prayer Due to Forgetfulness, and the Ruling on Prostration for Forgetfulness (Sujūd al-Sahw)
chapters.arabic_text:
على اللغة ما لم
# 
# يكن هناك حقيقة شرعية أو عرفية ولا يجوز حمله على ما يطرأ للمتأخرين من

الاصطلاح والله أعلم قوله عن عبد الله رضي الله عنه أن النبي صلى الله عليه

وسلم صلى الظهر خمسا فلما سلم قيل له أزيد في الصلاة قال وما ذاك قالوا

صليت خمسا فسجد سجدتين هذا فيه دليل لمذهب مالك والشافعي وأحمد والجمهور من

السلف والخلف أن من زاد في صلاته ركعة ناسيا لم تبطل صلاته بل إن علم بعد

السلام فقد مضت صلاته صحيحة ويسجد للسهو إن ذكر بعد السلام بقريب وإن طال

فالأصح عندنا أنه لا يسجد وإن ذكر قبل السلام عاد إلى القوم سواء كان في

قيام أو ركوع أو سجود أو غيرها ويتشهد ويسجد للسهو ويسلم وهل يسجد للسهو

قبل السلام أم بعده فيه خلاف العلماء السابق هذا مذهب الجمهور وقال أبو

حنيفة وأهل الكوفة رضي الله عنهم إذا زاد ركعة ساهيا بطلت صلاته ولزمه

إعادتها وقال أبو حنيفة رضي الله عنه إن كان تشهد في الرابعة ثم زاد خامسة

أضاف  إليها سادسة تشفعها وكانت نفلا بناء على أصله في أن السلام ليس بواجب

ويخرج من الصلاة بكل ما ينافيها وأن الركعة الفردة لا تكون صلاة قال وإن لم

يكن تشهد بطلت صلاته لأن الجلوس بقدر التشهد واجب ولم يأت به حتى أتى

بالخامسة وهذا الحديث يرد كل ما قالوه لأن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لم

يرجع من الخامسة ولم يشفعها وإنما تذكر بعد السلام ففيه رد عليهم وحجة

الجمهور ثم مذهب الشافعي ومن وافقه أن الزيادة على وجه السهو لا تبطل

الصلاة سواء قلت أو كثرت إذا كانت من جنس الصلاة فسواء زاد ركوعا أو سجودا

أو ركعة أو ركعات كثيرة ساهيا فصلاته صحيحة في كل ذلك ويسجد للسهو استحبابا

لا إيجابا وأما مالك فقال القاضي عياض مذهبه أنه إن زاد دون نصف الصلاة لم

تبطل صلاته بل هي صحيحة ويسجد للسهو وإن زاد النصف فأكثر فمن أصحابه من

أبطلها وهو قول مطرف وبن القاسم ومنهم من قال إن زاد ركعتين بطلت وإن زاد

ركعة فلا وهو قول عبد الملك وغيره ومنهم من قال
# 
# لا تبطل مطلقا وهو مروي عن مالك رحمه الله تعالى والله أعلم قوله حدثنا

بن نمير قال حدثنا بن إدريس إلى آخره وقال في الإسناد الآخر حدثنا عثمان بن

أبي شيبة إلى آخره هذان الإسنادان كلهم كوفيون قوله وأنت يا أعور فيه دليل

على جواز قول مثل هذا الكلام لقرابته وتلميذه وتابعه إذا لم يتأذ به قال

القاضي إبراهيم بن يزيد النخعي الكوفي وإبراهيم بن سويد النخعي الأعور آخر

وزعم الداودي أنه إبراهيم بن يزيد التيمي وهو وهم فإنه ليس بأعور وثلاثتهم

كوفيون فضلاء قال البخاري بن يزيد النخعي الأعور الكوفي سمع علقمة وذكر

الباجي إبراهيم بن يزيد النخعي الكوفي الفقيه وقال فيه الأعور ولم يصفه

البخاري بالأعور ولا رأيت من وصفه به وذكر بن قتيبة في العور إبراهيم

النخعي فيحتمل أنه بن سويد كما قال البخاري ويحتمل أنه إبراهيم بن يزيد هذا

آخر كلام  القاضي والصواب أن المراد بإبراهيم هنا إبراهيم بن سويد الأعور

النخعي وليس بإبراهيم بن يزيد النخعي الفقيه المشهور قوله توشوش القوم

ضبطناه بالشين المعجمة وقال القاضي روي بالمعجمة وبالمهملة وكلاهما صحيح

ومعناه تحركوا ومنه
# 
# وسواس الحلي بالمهملة وهو تحركه ووسوسة الشيطان قال أهل اللغة الوشوشة

بالمعجمة صوت في اختلاط قال الأصمعي ويقال رجل وشواش أي خفيف قوله حدثنا

منجاب بن الحارث إلى آخره هذا الإسناد كله كوفيون قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم

فزاد أو نقص فقيل يا رسول الله أزيد في الصلاة شيء فقال إنما أنا بشر مثلكم

أنسى كما تنسون فإذا نسي أحدكم فليسجد سجدتين وهو جالس ثم تحول رسول الله

صلى الله عليه وسلم فسجد سجدتين هذا الحديث مما يستشكل ظاهره لأن ظاهره أن

النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال لهم هذا الكلام بعد أن ذكر أنه زاد أو نقص

قبل أن يسجد للسهو ثم بعد أن قاله سجد للسهو ومتى ذكر ذلك فالحكم أنه يسجد

ولا يتكلم ولا يأتي بمناف للصلاة ويجاب عن هذا الاشكال بثلاثة أجوبة أحدها

أن ثم هنا ليست لحقيقة الترتيب وإنما هي لعطف جملة على جملة وليس معناه أن

التحول والسجود كانا بعد الكلام بل إنما كانا قبله ومما يؤيد هذا التأويل

أنه قد سبق في هذا الباب في أول طرق
# 
# حديث بن مسعود رضي الله عنه هذا بهذا الإسناد قال رسول الله صلى الله

عليه وسلم فزاد أو نقص فلما سلم قيل له يا رسول الله أحدث في الصلاة شيء

قال وما ذاك قالوا صليت كذا وكذا فثنى رجليه واستقبل القبلة فسجد سجدتين ثم

سلم ثم أقبل علينا بوجهه فقال إنه لو حدث في الصلاة شيء أنبأتكم به ولكن

إنما أنا بشر أنسى كما تنسون فإذا نسيت فذكروني وإذا شك أحدكم في صلاته

فليتحر الصواب فليتم عليه ثم ليسجد سجدتين فهذه الرواية صريحة في أن التحول

والسجود قبل الكلام فتحمل الثانية عليها جمعا بين الروايتين وحمل الثانية

على الأولى أولى من عكسه  لأن الأولى على وفق القواعد الجواب الثاني أن يكون

هذا قبل تحريم الكلام في الصلاة الثالث أنه وإن تكلم عامدا بعد السلام لا
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ز-ي-د (z-y-d)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Increase, augmentation, excess beyond measure or limit.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In ritual acts (ʿibādāt), an addition (ziyādah) that alters the prescribed form (hayʾah) — its ruling hinges on intentionality vs. forgetfulness (nisyān).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) for physical increase; metaphorical (majāz) for exceeding legal bounds.
- Root: س-ه-و (s-h-w)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Neglect, inadvertence, lapse of attention from an object.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): A legal category (ʿudhr) that nullifies culpability for error in worship, necessitating compensatory prostration (sujūd al-sahw).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for mental absence; technical in fiqh for unintentional deviation in prayer.
- Root: س-ج-د (s-j-d)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Bowing, prostration; humility before God.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The physical act of worship marking submission; in legal terms, a pillar (rukn) of prayer.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for the physical posture; metaphorical for total submission.
- Sībawayh Rule: ʿAṭf al-Jumal (Coordination of Sentences) — The particle «ثُمَّ» (thumma) may indicate narrative sequence (tartīb) or mere conjunction (mujarrad al-jamʿ), depending on contextual evidence (qarīnah).
chapters.translation:
I say: Regarding the language, as long as there is no legal (sharʿī) or customary (ʿurfī) reality [that overrides the literal], it is not permissible to carry it to the technical conventions that arise among later scholars. And God knows best.

His statement: "On the authority of ʿAbd Allāh, may God be pleased with him, that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, prayed Ẓuhr as five [rakʿahs]. When he gave the salutation, it was said to him: 'Has the prayer been increased?' He said: 'And what is that?' They said: 'You prayed five.' So he prostrated two prostrations."

In this [hadith] there is evidence for the school of Mālik, al-Shāfiʿī, Aḥmad, and the majority (jumhūr) of the early and later scholars: that whoever adds a rakʿah to his prayer forgetfully, his prayer is not invalidated. Rather, if he becomes aware after the salutation, his prayer has passed as valid, and he prostrates for forgetfulness if he remembers shortly after the salutation. But if [the interval] is prolonged, then the more correct (al-aṣaḥḥ) view in our school is that he does not prostrate. If he remembers before the salutation, he returns to the sitting position (qawm), whether he was in standing, bowing, prostration, or otherwise, and he recites the tashahhud, prostrates for forgetfulness, and gives the salutation. Whether the prostration for forgetfulness is before or after the salutation — therein lies the aforementioned disagreement of the scholars. This is the school of the majority.

Abū Ḥanīfah and the people of Kūfah, may God be pleased with them, said: If one adds a rakʿah forgetfully, his prayer is invalidated and he must repeat it. Abū Ḥanīfah, may God be pleased with him, said: If he had recited the tashahhud in the fourth [rakʿah] and then added a fifth, he should attach a sixth to it, making it a pair, and it would be supererogatory (nafl) — based on his principle that the salutation is not obligatory, that one exits the prayer by anything that contravenes it, and that a single rakʿah cannot constitute a prayer. He said: But if he had not recited the tashahhud, his prayer is invalidated, because sitting for the duration of the tashahhud is obligatory, and he did not perform it until he came to the fifth.

This hadith refutes all that they said, because the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, did not return from the fifth nor pair it [with a sixth]; rather, he only remembered after the salutation. Thus in it is a refutation against them and an argument for the majority.

Then, the school of al-Shāfiʿī and those who agree with him: that addition by way of forgetfulness does not invalidate the prayer, whether little or much, as long as it is of the same genus (jins) as the prayer. Thus, whether one adds a bowing, a prostration, a rakʿah, or many rakʿahs forgetfully, his prayer is valid in all that, and he prostrates for forgetfulness by recommendation (istihbāban), not obligation (ījāban).

As for Mālik, Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ said: His school is that if one adds less than half of the prayer, his prayer is not invalidated; rather, it is valid and he prostrates for forgetfulness. If he adds half or more, then some of his companions invalidate it — this is the saying of Muṭarrif and Ibn al-Qāsim. Among them are those who said: If he adds two rakʿahs, it is invalidated; if he adds one, then no — this is the saying of ʿAbd al-Malik and others. Among them are those who said: It is not invalidated absolutely — and this is narrated from Mālik, may God Most High have mercy on him. And God knows best.

His statement: "Ibn Numayr narrated to us, he said: Ibn Idrīs narrated to us," to the end. And in the other chain he said: "ʿUthmān ibn Abī Shaybah narrated to us," to the end. These two chains — all of their narrators are Kūfans.

His statement: "And you, O one-eyed (aʿwar)" — in it is evidence for the permissibility of saying such words to one's relative, student, and follower, when he is not harmed by it. Al-Qāḍī said: Ibrāhīm ibn Yazīd al-Nakhaʿī al-Kūfī, and Ibrāhīm ibn Suwayd al-Nakhaʿī al-Aʿwar — the latter. Al-Dāwūdī claimed that he is Ibrāhīm ibn Yazīd al-Taymī — and this is an error, for he was not one-eyed. All three are virtuous Kūfans. Al-Bukhārī said: "Ibn Yazīd al-Nakhaʿī al-Aʿwar al-Kūfī heard ʿAlqamah." Al-Bājī mentioned Ibrāhīm ibn Yazīd al-Nakhaʿī al-Kūfī, the jurist, and said of him "al-Aʿwar," but al-Bukhārī did not describe him as one-eyed, nor have I seen anyone who described him so. Ibn Qutaybah mentioned in [his book] al-ʿAwr "Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī," so it is possible he is Ibn Suwayd, as al-Bukhārī said, and possible he is this Ibrāhīm ibn Yazīd. This is the end of al-Qāḍī's speech. The correct view is that the intended Ibrāhīm here is Ibrāhīm ibn Suwayd al-Aʿwar al-Nakhaʿī, not Ibrāhīm ibn Yazīd al-Nakhaʿī, the famous jurist.

His statement: "The people stirred (tawashwasha)" — we have recorded it with the dotted shīn (shīn muʿjamah). Al-Qāḍī said: It is narrated with the dotted [shīn] and with the undotted [sīn], and both are correct. Its meaning is: they moved about. From it [derives] "the jingling of jewelry (waswās al-ḥulī)" with the undotted sīn — meaning its movement — and "the whispering of Satan (waswasah al-shayṭān)." The linguists said: "Al-washwashah" with the dotted shīn is a sound in confusion. Al-Aṣmaʿī said: One says "rajul wishwāsh" meaning a light, quick man.

His statement: "Munjāb ibn al-Ḥārith narrated to us," to the end — this chain is entirely Kūfan.

His statement, peace and blessings be upon him: "So he added or omitted. It was said: O Messenger of God, has something been added to the prayer? He said: I am only a human like you; I forget as you forget. So when any of you forgets, let him prostrate two prostrations while sitting." Then the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, turned and prostrated two prostrations.

This hadith is problematic in its apparent meaning (ẓāhir), because its apparent sense is that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said this speech to them after he mentioned that he had added or omitted, before prostrating for forgetfulness. Then after saying it, he prostrated for forgetfulness. But whenever he remembers that, the ruling is that he prostrates and does not speak, nor does he do anything that contravenes the prayer.

This difficulty is answered with three responses:

**The first:** That «ثُمَّ» (thumma) here is not for true sequential ordering (tartīb), but rather for coordinating one sentence with another (ʿaṭf jumlah ʿalā jumlah). Its meaning is not that the turning and prostrating occurred after the speech; rather, they occurred before it. Supporting this interpretation is that it has preceded in this chapter, in the first of the chains of the hadith of Ibn Masʿūd, may God be pleased with him, with this chain: The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "So he added or omitted. When he gave the salutation, it was said to him: O Messenger of God, has something new occurred in the prayer? He said: And what is that? They said: You prayed such-and-such. So he folded his legs, faced the qiblah, prostrated two prostrations, then gave the salutation. Then he turned to us with his face and said: If something new had occurred in the prayer, I would have informed you of it. But I am only a human; I forget as you forget. So when I forget, remind me. And when any of you doubts in his prayer, let him seek the correct [estimate] and complete upon it, then prostrate two prostrations." This narration is explicit that the turning and prostrating were before the speech. So the second [narration] is carried upon the first, reconciling between the two narrations. Carrying the second upon the first is more appropriate than the reverse, because the first conforms to the [established] rules.

**The second response:** That this [speech] occurred before the prohibition of speech during prayer.

**The third:** That even if he spoke deliberately after the salutation, [it does not invalidate]...

chapters.title_en: The Chapter on the Forgetful One in Prayer — Section 313: The Story of Dhū al-Yadayn and Rulings on Forgetfulness
chapters.arabic_text:
يضره ذلك ويسجد بعده للسهو وهذا على أحد الوجهين لأصحابنا أنه إذا سجد لا

يكون بالسجود عائدا إلى الصلاة حتى لو أحدث فيه لا تبطل صلاته بل قد مضت

على الصحة والوجه الثاني وهو الأصح عند أصحابنا أنه
# 
# يكون عائدا وتبطل صلاته بالحدث والكلام وسائر المنافيات للصلاة والله

أعلم
# [573] قوله في حديث أبي هريرة في قصة ذي اليدين إحدى صلاتي العشي إما

الظهر وإما العصر هو بفتح العين وكسر الشين وتشديد الياء قال الأزهري العشي

عند العرب ما بين زوال الشمس وغروبها قوله ثم أتى جذعا في قبلة المسجد

فاستند إليها هكذا هو في كل الأصول فاستند إليها والجذع مذكر ولكن أنثه على

إرادة الخشبة وكذا جاء في رواية البخاري وغيره خشبة قوله فاستند إليها

مغضبا هو بفتح الضاد قوله وخرج سرعان الناس قصرت الصلاة يعني يقولون قصرت

الصلاة والسرعان بفتح السين والراء هذا هو الصواب الذي قاله الجمهور من أهل

الحديث واللغة وهكذا ضبطه المتقنون والسرعان المسرعون إلى الخروج ونقل

القاضي عياض عن بعضهم إسكان الراء قال وضبطه الأصيلي في البخاري بضم السين

وإسكان الراء ويكون جمع سريع كقفيز وقفزان وكثيب وكثبان وقوله قصرت الصلاة

بضم القاف وكسر الصاد وروي بفتح القاف وضم الصاد وكلاهما صحيح ولكن الأول

أشهر وأصح قوله فقام ذو اليدين وفي رواية رجل من بني سليم وفي رواية رجل

يقال له الخرباق وكان في يده طول وفي رواية رجل بسيط اليدين هذا كله رجل

واحد اسمه الخرباق بن عمرو بكسر الخاء المعجمة والباء الموحدة
# 
# وآخره قاف ولقبه ذو اليدين لطول كان في يديه وهو معنى قوله بسيط اليدين

قوله صلى لنا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم صلاة العصر فسلم في ركعتين فقام

ذو اليدين وفي رواية صلاة الظهر قال المحققون هما قضيتان وفي حديث عمران بن

الحصين سلم رسول الله صلى  الله عليه وسلم في ثلاث ركعات من العصر ثم دخل

منزله فقام إليه رجل يقال له الخرباق فقال يا رسول الله فذكر له صنيعه وخرج

غضبان يجر رداءه وفي رواية له سلم في ثلاث ركعات من العصر ثم قام فدخل

الحجرة فقام رجل بسيط اليدين فقال أقصرت الصلاة وحديث عمران هذا قضية ثالثة

في يوم آخر والله أعلم قوله وأخبرت عن عمران بن حصين أنه قال وسلم القائل

وأخبرت هو محمد بن سيرين قوله أقصرت الصلاة أم نسيت فقال رسول الله صلى

الله عليه وسلم كل ذلك لم يكن فيه تأويلان أحدهما قاله جماعة من أصحابنا في

كتب المذهب أن معناه لم يكن المجموع فلا ينفي وجود أحدهما والثاني وهو

الصواب معناه لم يكن لا ذاك ولا ذا في ظني بل ظني أني أكملت الصلاة أربعا

ويدل على صحة هذا التأويل وأنه لا يجوز غيره أنه جاء في روايات البخاري في

هذا الحديث أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال لم تقصر ولم أنس فنفى الأمرين

قوله حدثنا هارون بن إسماعيل الخزاز هو بخاء معجمة وزاي مكررة
# 
# [574] قوله عن أبي المهلب اسمه عبد الرحمن بن عمر وقيل معاوية بن عمر

وقيل عمرو بن معاوية ذكر هذه الأقوال الثلاثة في اسمه البخاري في تاريخه

وآخرون وقيل اسمه النضر بن عمر الجرمي الأزدي البصري التابعي الكبير روى عن

عمر بن الخطاب وعثمان بن عفان وأبي بن كعب وعمران بن حصين رضي الله عنهم

أجمعين وهو عم أبي قلابة الراوي عنه هنا قوله وخرج غضبان يجر رداءه يعني

لكثرة اشتغاله بشأن الصلاة خرج يجر رداءه ولم يتمهل ليلبسه قوله في آخر

الباب في حديث إسحاق بن منصور سلم رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم من

الركعتين فقال رجل من بني سليم واقتص الحديث هكذا هو في بعض الأصول

المعتمدة من الركعتين وهو الظاهر الموافق لباقي الروايات وفي بعضها
# 
# بين الركعتين وهو صحيح أيضا ويكون المراد بين الركعتين الثانية والثالثة

واعلم أن حديث ذي  اليدين هذا فيه فوائد كثيرة وقواعد مهمة منها جواز

النسيان في الأفعال والعبادات على الأنبياء صلوات الله وسلامه عليهم أجمعين

وأنهم لا يقرون عليه وقد تقدمت هذه القاعدة في هذا الباب ومنها أن الواحد

إذا ادعى شيئا جرى بحضرة جمع كثير لا يخفى عليهم سئلوا عنه ولا يعمل بقوله

من غير سؤال ومنها إثبات سجود السهو وأنه سجدتان وأنه يكبر لكل واحدة منهما

وأنهما على هيئة سجود الصلاة لأنه أطلق السجود فلو خالف المعتاد لبينه وأنه

يسلم من سجود السهو وأنه لا تشهد له وأن سجود السهو في الزيادة يكون بعد

السلام وقد سبق أن الشافعي رحمه الله تعالى يحمله على أن تأخير سجود السهو

كان نسيانا لا عمدا ومنها أن كلام الناسي للصلاة والذي يظن أنه ليس فيها لا

يبطلها وبهذا قال جمهور العلماء من السلف والخلف وهو قول بن عباس وعبد الله

بن الزبير وأخيه عروة وعطاء والحسن والشعبي وقتادة والأوزاعي ومالك

والشافعي وأحمد وجميع المحدثين رضي الله عنهم وقال أبو حنيفة رضي الله عنه

وأصحابه والثوري في أصح الروايتين تبطل صلاته بالكلام ناسيا أو جاهلا لحديث

بن مسعود وزيد بن أرقم رضي الله عنهما وزعموا أن حديث قصة ذي اليدين منسوخ
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ض-ر-ر (ḍ-r-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning of harm, injury, or detriment; here, "it does not harm him" (lā yaḍurruhu) denotes absence of nullification or invalidation.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In legal-theological context, harm (ḍarar) contrasts with benefit (nafʿ); negation of harm implies the act remains valid and uncorrupted.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal usage — no metaphorical extension; the harm is concrete invalidation of the prayer.
- Root: ع-و-د (ʿ-w-d)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To return, revert, or come back to a prior state.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In ritual law, "returning" (ʿawd) to prayer signifies re-entering its state of sanctity (ḥurmat al-ṣalāh) after a lapse.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal here — the prostration either does or does not constitute a re-entry into prayer; no metaphor.
- Root: س-ه-و (s-h-w)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Forgetfulness, inadvertence, or neglect; the root implies a lapse of attention.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Technical term for unintentional error in worship (sahw), distinct from deliberate violation (ʿamd).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — forgetfulness as a psychological state; metaphorical extension to "prostration of forgetfulness" (sujūd al-sahw) as a remedial act.
- Root: ق-ص-ر (q-ṣ-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To shorten, curtail, or abridge; also "to fall short."
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In prayer context, "shortening" (qaṣr) refers to reducing the number of units (rakʿāt); here, the companions' exclamation "Has the prayer been shortened?" (aqṣurat al-ṣalāh).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — the question about actual reduction of prayer units; no metaphorical sense.
- Sībawayh Rule: Rule of Condition and Exception (al-sharṭ wa al-jawāb) — The phrase "if he prostrates, he does not thereby return to the prayer" establishes a conditional clause where the apodosis negates a consequence, requiring precise parsing of the protasis (condition) and apodosis (result).
chapters.translation:
I say: That [i.e., speaking out of forgetfulness] does not harm him, and he prostrates afterward for the forgetfulness (sahw). This is according to one of the two positions of our companions [the Shāfiʿīs]: that when he prostrates, he does not thereby return to the prayer by that prostration, such that even if he were to nullify his ablution during it, his prayer would not be invalidated; rather, it [the prayer] has already passed in a state of validity. The second position — and it is the more correct (aṣaḥḥ) one according to our companions — is that he does return [to the prayer] by it, and his prayer is invalidated by [nullifying] the ablution, by speech, and by all other things that invalidate the prayer. And Allah knows best.

[573] His saying — in the ḥadīth of Abū Hurayrah regarding the story of Dhū al-Yadayn — "one of the two prayers of the ʿashiyy, either the Ẓuhr or the ʿAṣr": the word ʿashiyy is with fatḥah on the ʿayn, kasrah on the shīn, and tashdīd on the yāʾ. Al-Azharī said: "The ʿashiyy among the Arabs is [the time] between the sun's declination from its zenith and its setting." His saying: "Then he came to a palm-trunk (jidhʿ) in the qiblah direction of the mosque and leaned against it" — thus it is in all the manuscripts: "and leaned against it" (fa-stanada ilayhā). The word jidhʿ is masculine, but it was feminized with the intention of [meaning] "the piece of wood" (khashabah). Likewise, it came in the narration of al-Bukhārī and others as "a piece of wood" (khashabah). His saying: "He leaned against it, angry" (mugḥḍaban) — it is with fatḥah on the ḍād. His saying: "And the swift people (surʿān) went out, saying: 'The prayer has been shortened' (quṣirat al-ṣalāh)" — meaning they were saying: "The prayer has been shortened." The word surʿān is with fatḥah on the sīn and the rāʾ; this is the correct [pronunciation] that the majority of the people of ḥadīth and language have stated, and thus the meticulous scholars have recorded it. Surʿān means "those who hasten to go out." Al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ transmitted from some of them [the pronunciation] with sukūn on the rāʾ. He said: "And al-Aṣīlī recorded it in al-Bukhārī with ḍammah on the sīn and sukūn on the rāʾ, and it would be a plural of sarīʿ (swift), like qafīz and qafzān, and kathīb and kuthbān." His saying: "The prayer has been shortened" (quṣirat al-ṣalāh) — with ḍammah on the qāf and kasrah on the ṣād; and it is narrated with fatḥah on the qāf and ḍammah on the ṣād, and both are correct, but the first is more famous and more correct. His saying: "Then Dhū al-Yadayn stood up" — and in one narration, "a man from Banū Sulaym," and in another narration, "a man called al-Khirbāq, and there was length in his hands," and in another narration, "a man with outstretched hands (basīṭ al-yadayn)." All of this is one and the same man, whose name is al-Khirbāq ibn ʿAmr — with kasrah on the khāʾ (unpointed) and the bāʾ (unpointed), and its final letter is qāf. His nickname was Dhū al-Yadayn (Possessor of Two Hands) due to a length that was in his hands, and that is the meaning of his saying "with outstretched hands."

His saying: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed the ʿAṣr prayer with us and gave the salutation after two rakʿahs, and Dhū al-Yadayn stood up" — and in one narration, "the Ẓuhr prayer." The verifying scholars (muḥaqqiqūn) said: These are two separate incidents. And in the ḥadīth of ʿImrān ibn Ḥuṣayn: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ gave the salutation after three rakʿahs of the ʿAṣr prayer, then entered his dwelling. A man called al-Khirbāq stood up to him and said: 'O Messenger of Allah,' and he mentioned to him what he had done. Then he came out angry, dragging his cloak (ridāʾ)." And in another narration of his: "He gave the salutation after three rakʿahs of the ʿAṣr, then stood and entered the chamber. A man with outstretched hands stood up and said: 'Has the prayer been shortened?'" This ḥadīth of ʿImrān is a third incident on another day. And Allah knows best.

His saying: "And I was informed (ukhbirtu) about ʿImrān ibn Ḥuṣayn that he said" — and the one who said [this] is Muḥammad ibn Sīrīn. His saying: "Has the prayer been shortened, or did you forget?" — and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Neither of that occurred." There are two interpretations (taʾwīlān) regarding this. The first — stated by a group of our companions in the books of the school [of Shāfiʿī] — is that its meaning is: "The combination of both did not occur," so it does not negate the existence of either one alone. The second — and it is the correct one — is that its meaning is: "Neither this nor that occurred in my estimation; rather, my estimation was that I had completed the prayer as four [rakʿahs]." And what indicates the correctness of this interpretation, and that no other is permissible, is that it came in the narrations of al-Bukhārī in this ḥadīth that the Prophet ﷺ said: "The prayer was not shortened, nor did I forget," thus negating both matters.

His saying: "Hārūn ibn Ismāʿīl al-Khazzāz narrated to us" — it is with an unpointed khāʾ and a doubled zāy.

[574] His saying: "From Abū al-Muhallab" — his name is ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAmr; and it is said, Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmr; and it is said, ʿAmr ibn Muʿāwiyah. Al-Bukhārī mentioned these three statements regarding his name in his Tārīkh, as did others. And it is said his name was al-Naḍr ibn ʿAmr al-Jarmī al-Azdī al-Baṣrī, the great Successor (tābiʿī), who narrated from ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān, Ubayy ibn Kaʿb, and ʿImrān ibn Ḥuṣayn — may Allah be pleased with them all. He is the paternal uncle of Abū Qilābah, who narrates from him here. His saying: "He came out angry, dragging his cloak" — meaning, due to his intense preoccupation with the matter of the prayer, he came out dragging his cloak and did not take his time to put it on properly.

His saying at the end of the chapter, in the ḥadīth of Isḥāq ibn Manṣūr: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ gave the salutation from the two rakʿahs (mina al-rakʿatayn), and a man from Banū Sulaym said..." — and he related the ḥadīth. Thus it is in some of the reliable manuscripts: "from the two rakʿahs" (mina al-rakʿatayn), and this is the apparent [reading] consistent with the rest of the narrations. And in some of them: "between the two rakʿahs" (bayna al-rakʿatayn), which is also correct, and the intended meaning would be "between the second and the third rakʿah."

Know that this ḥadīth of Dhū al-Yadayn contains many benefits (fawāʾid) and important principles (qawāʿid). Among them: the permissibility of forgetfulness (nisyān) in the actions and acts of worship of the prophets — may Allah's prayers and peace be upon them all — and that they are not left to persist upon it. This principle has already preceded in this chapter. Among them: that when a single individual claims something that occurred in the presence of a large multitude, to whom it would not be hidden, they are to be asked about it, and his statement is not acted upon without asking [them]. Among them: the establishment of the prostration of forgetfulness (sujūd al-sahw), that it is two prostrations, that one says the takbīr for each of them, and that they are in the form of the prostration of the prayer — because he [the Prophet ﷺ] absolutely [said] "prostration," and had it differed from the customary [form], he would have clarified it — and that one gives the salutation from the prostration of forgetfulness, and that there is no tashahhud for it. And that the prostration of forgetfulness in the case of an addition (ziyādah) is after the salutation. It has already preceded that al-Shāfiʿī — may Allah have mercy on him — interprets this as [the Prophet's] delaying the prostration of forgetfulness being out of forgetfulness, not deliberately. Among them: that the speech of one who is forgetful of his prayer, and who thinks he is not in it, does not invalidate it. This is the position of the majority of scholars from the predecessors (salaf) and successors (khalaf). It is the position of Ibn ʿAbbās, ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Zubayr and his brother ʿUrwah, ʿAṭāʾ, al-Ḥasan, al-Shaʿbī, Qatādah, al-Awzāʿī, Mālik, al-Shāfiʿī, Aḥmad, and all the ḥadīth scholars — may Allah be pleased with them. Abū Ḥanīfah — may Allah be pleased with him — and his companions, and al-Thawrī in the more correct of the two narrations, said: His prayer is invalidated by speech whether forgetful or ignorant, based on the ḥadīth of Ibn Masʿūd and Zayd ibn Arqam — may Allah be pleased with them both — and they claimed that the ḥadīth of the story of Dhū al-Yadayn is abrogated (mansūkh).

chapters.title_en: The Hadith of Dhu al-Yadayn: Refutation of Abrogation Claims and Clarification of the Narrator's Identity
chapters.arabic_text:
بحديث بن مسعود وزيد بن أرقم قالوا لأن ذا اليدين قتل يوم بدر ونقلوا عن

الزهري أن ذا اليدين قتل يوم بدر وأن قضيته في الصلاة كانت قبل بدر قالوا

ولا يمنع من هذا كون أبي هريرة رواه وهو متأخر الإسلام عن بدر لأن الصحابي

قد يروي ما لا يحضره بأن يسمعه من النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أو صحابي آخر

وأجاب أصحابنا وغيرهم من العلماء عن هذا بأجوبة صحيحة حسنة مشهورة أحسنها

وأتقنها ما ذكره أبو عمر بن عبد البر في التمهيد قال أما ادعاؤهم أن حديث

أبي هريرة منسوخ بحديث بن مسعود رضي الله عنه فغير صحيح لأنه لا خلاف بين

أهل الحديث والسير أن حديث بن مسعود كان بمكة حين رجع من أرض  الحبشة قبل

الهجرة وأن حديث أبي هريرة في قصة ذي اليدين كان بالمدينة وإنما أسلم أبو

هريرة عام خيبر سنة سبع من الهجرة بلا خلاف وأما حديث زيد بن أرقم رضي الله

عنه فليس فيه بيان أنه قبل حديث أبي هريرة أو بعده والنظر يشهد أنه قبل

حديث أبي هريرة وأما قولهم إن أبا هريرة رضي الله عنه لم يشهد ذلك فليس

بصحيح بل شهوده لها محفوظ من روايات الثقات الحفاظ ثم ذكر
# 
# بإسناده الرواية الثانية في صحيحي البخاري ومسلم وغيرهما أن أبا هريرة

قال صلى لنا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إحدى صلاتي العشي فسلم من اثنتين

وذكر الحديث وقصة ذي اليدين وفي روايات صلى بنا رسول الله صلى الله عليه

وسلم وفي رواية في مسلم وغيره بينا أنا أصلي مع رسول الله صلى الله عليه

وسلم وذكر الحديث وفي رواية في غير مسلم بينا نحن نصلي مع رسول الله صلى

الله عليه وسلم قال وقد روى قصة ذي اليدين عبد الله بن عمر ومعاوية بن حديج

بضم الحاء المهملة وعمران بن حصين وبن مسعدة رجل من الصحابة رضي الله عنهم

وكلهم لم يحفظ عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ولا صحبه إلا بالمدينة متأخرا

ثم ذكر أحاديثهم بطرقها قال وبن مسعدة هذا رجل من الصحابة يقال له صاحب

الجيوش اسمه عبد الله معروف في الصحابة له رواية قال وأما قولهم إن ذا

اليدين قتل يوم بدر فغلط وإنما المقتول يوم بدر ذو الشمالين ولسنا ندافعهم

أن ذا الشمالين قتل يوم بدر لأن بن إسحاق وغيره من أهل السير ذكره فيمن قتل

يوم بدر قال بن إسحاق ذو الشمالين هو عمير بن عمرو بن عيشان من خزاعة حليف

لبني زهرة قال أبو عمر فذو اليدين غير ذي الشمالين المقتول ببدر بدليل حضور

أبي هريرة ومن ذكرنا قصة ذي اليدين وأن المتكلم رجل من بني سليم كما ذكره

مسلم في صحيحه وفي رواية عمران بن الحصين رضي الله عنه  اسمه الخرباق ذكره

مسلم فذو اليدين الذي شهد السهو في الصلاة سلمي وذو الشمالين المقتول ببدر

خزاعي يخالفه في الاسم والنسب وقد يمكن أن يكون رجلان وثلاثة يقال لكل واحد

منهم ذو اليدين وذو الشمالين لكن المقتول ببدر غير المذكور في حديث السهو

هذا قول أهل الحذق والفهم من أهل الحديث والفقه ثم روي هذا بإسناده عن مسدد

وأما قول الزهري في حديث السهوان المتكلم ذو الشمالين فلم يتابع عليه وقد

اضطرب الزهري في حديث ذي اليدين اضطرابا أوجب عند أهل العلم بالنقل تركه من

روايته خاصة ثم ذكر طرقه وبين اضطرابها في المتن والإسناد وذكر أن مسلم بن

الحجاج غلط الزهري في حديثه قال أبو عمر رحمه الله تعالى لا أعلم أحدا من

أهل العلم بالحديث المصنفين فيه عول على حديث الزهري في قصة ذي اليدين

وكلهم تركوه لاضطرابه وأنه لم يتم له إسنادا ولا متنا وإن كان إماما عظيما

في هذا الشأن فالغلط لا يسلم منه بشر والكمال لله تعالى وكل أحد يؤخذ من

قوله ويترك إلا النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقول الزهري أنه قتل يوم بدر

متروك لتحقق غلطه فيه هذا كلام أبي
# 
# عمر بن عبد البر مختصرا وقد بسط رحمه الله تعالى شرح هذا الحديث بسطا لم

يبسطه غيره مشتملا على التحقيق والإتقان والفوائد الجمة رضي الله عنه فإن

قيل كيف تكلم ذو اليدين والقوم وهم بعد في الصلاة فجوابه من وجهين أحدهما

أنهم لم يكونوا على يقين من البقاء في الصلاة لأنهم كانوا مجوزين نسخ

الصلاة من أربع إلى ركعتين ولهذا قال أقصرت الصلاة أم نسيت والثاني أن هذا

كان خطابا للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وجوابا وذلك لا يبطل عندنا وعند غيرنا

والمسئلة مشهورة بذلك وفي رواية لأبي داود بإسناد صحيح أن الجماعة أومأوا

أي نعم فعلى هذه الرواية لم يتكلموا فإن قيل كيف رجع النبي صلى الله عليه

وسلم إلى قول الجماعة وعندكم لا يجوز للمصلي الرجوع في قدر صلاته إلى قول

غيره إماما كان أو مأموما ولا يعمل إلا على يقين نفسه فجوابه أن النبي صلى

الله عليه وسلم سألهم ليتذكر فلما ذكروه تذكر فعلم السهو فبنى عليه لا أنه

رجع إلى مجرد قولهم ولو جاز ترك يقين نفسه والرجوع إلى قول غيره لرجع ذو

اليدين حين قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لم تقصر ولم أنس وفي هذا الحديث

دليل على أن العمل الكثير والخطوات إذا كانت في الصلاة سهوا لا تبطلها كما

لا يبطلها الكلام سهوا وفي هذه المسألة وجهان لأصحابنا أصحهما عند المتولي
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ق-ت-ل (q-t-l)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To kill, slay; the act of taking life in battle or execution
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Physical death by violence; in historical context, martyrdom (shahādah) in battle
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal usage here—actual death in combat at Badr
- Root: ن-س-خ (n-s-kh)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To erase, abrogate, supersede; copying (istinsākh) as derivative
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Abrogation of a legal ruling (ḥukm) by a later revelation or prophetic practice
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Technical legal term—abrogation of one textual evidence by another, not metaphorical
- Root: س-ه-و (s-h-w)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Forgetfulness, inadvertence, oversight
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Mental lapse during worship; the legal category of sahw in prayer requiring prostration (sujūd al-sahw)
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal—actual forgetfulness, not negligence or willful omission
- Root: ض-ط-ر-ب (ḍ-ṭ-r-b)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To be disordered, agitated, inconsistent
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In hadith criticism, textual or isnād inconsistency rendering a narration weak (ḍaʿīf)
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Metaphorical extension—instability of a report's chain or text
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional and Exceptive Constructions (al-sharṭ wa al-istithnāʾ) — For parsing "لأن ذا اليدين قتل يوم بدر" as a causal clause (taʿlīl) with implied objection, and "فلا يمنع من هذا كون أبي هريرة رواه" as a negated impediment construction requiring careful subject-predicate alignment.
chapters.translation:
I say: Know that the scholars have addressed the report of Ibn Masʿūd and Zayd ibn Arqam—may God be pleased with them—who said that Dhu al-Yadayn was killed on the day of Badr. They transmitted from al-Zuhrī that Dhu al-Yadayn was killed at Badr and that his incident concerning the prayer occurred before Badr. They argued: This does not preclude Abū Hurayrah's narration of it, even though his acceptance of Islam came after Badr, because a Companion may narrate what he did not personally witness, having heard it from the Prophet—peace and blessings be upon him—or from another Companion.

Our colleagues and other scholars have answered this with sound, excellent, and well-known responses. The finest and most precise among them is what Abū ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-Barr mentioned in al-Tamhīd. He said: As for their claim that the hadith of Abū Hurayrah is abrogated by the hadith of Ibn Masʿūd—may God be pleased with him—this is incorrect, because there is no disagreement among the people of hadith and biography (sīrah) that the hadith of Ibn Masʿūd occurred in Mecca when he returned from the land of Abyssinia before the Hijrah, whereas the hadith of Abū Hurayrah concerning the incident of Dhu al-Yadayn occurred in Medina. Abū Hurayrah only embraced Islam in the year of Khaybar, in the seventh year after the Hijrah, without dispute. As for the hadith of Zayd ibn Arqam—may God be pleased with him—it contains no clarification whether it preceded or followed the hadith of Abū Hurayrah, though reasoned consideration (al-naẓar) testifies that it preceded it. As for their statement that Abū Hurayrah—may God be pleased with him—did not witness that event, it is not sound. Rather, his witnessing of it is preserved through the narrations of trustworthy and precise transmitters (al-thiqāt al-ḥuffāẓ).

Then he mentioned, with his chain of transmission, the second narration in the two Ṣaḥīḥs of al-Bukhārī and Muslim and others, that Abū Hurayrah said: "The Messenger of God—peace and blessings be upon him—led us in one of the two evening prayers, and he gave the salutation after two rakʿahs." He then mentioned the hadith and the incident of Dhu al-Yadayn. In other narrations: "The Messenger of God—peace and blessings be upon him—prayed with us." In a narration in Muslim and others: "While I was praying with the Messenger of God—peace and blessings be upon him—" and he mentioned the hadith. In a narration outside of Muslim: "While we were praying with the Messenger of God—peace and blessings be upon him—."

He said: The incident of Dhu al-Yadayn was also narrated by ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar, Muʿāwiyah ibn Ḥudayj—with the ḍammah on the unpointed ḥāʾ—ʿImrān ibn Ḥuṣayn, and Ibn Masʿadah, a man among the Companions—may God be pleased with them all. None of them had heard from the Prophet—peace and blessings be upon him—nor accompanied him except in Medina, at a later time. Then he mentioned their hadiths with their chains. He said: This Ibn Masʿadah is a man among the Companions, known as the companion of the armies (ṣāḥib al-juyūsh); his name is ʿAbd Allāh, well-known among the Companions, and he has narrations.

He said: As for their claim that Dhu al-Yadayn was killed at Badr, this is an error. Rather, the one killed at Badr was Dhu al-Shimālayn. We do not dispute that Dhu al-Shimālayn was killed at Badr, for Ibn Isḥāq and other biographers mentioned him among those killed on the day of Badr. Ibn Isḥāq said: Dhu al-Shimālayn is ʿUmayr ibn ʿAmr ibn ʿAyshān from Khuzāʿah, an ally (ḥalīf) of the Banū Zuhrah.

Abū ʿUmar said: Thus, Dhu al-Yadayn is other than Dhu al-Shimālayn who was killed at Badr, as evidenced by the presence of Abū Hurayrah and those we mentioned narrating the incident of Dhu al-Yadayn, and that the speaker was a man from the Banū Sulaym, as Muslim mentioned in his Ṣaḥīḥ. In the narration of ʿImrān ibn al-Ḥuṣayn—may God be pleased with him—his name is al-Khirbāq, as Muslim mentioned. So Dhu al-Yadayn, who witnessed the forgetfulness in prayer, was from Sulaym, while Dhu al-Shimālayn, killed at Badr, was from Khuzāʿah—differing in name and lineage. It is possible that there were two or three men, each called Dhu al-Yadayn and Dhu al-Shimālayn, but the one killed at Badr is not the one mentioned in the hadith of forgetfulness. This is the view of the skilled and discerning among the people of hadith and jurisprudence.

Then this was narrated with his chain from Musaddad.

As for al-Zuhrī's statement in the hadith of forgetfulness that the speaker was Dhu al-Shimālayn, he was not followed in this. Al-Zuhrī was so inconsistent (iḍṭaraba) in the hadith of Dhu al-Yadayn that this inconsistency compelled the scholars of transmission to abandon his narration specifically. Then he mentioned its chains and demonstrated their inconsistency in both text (matn) and chain (isnād), and noted that Muslim ibn al-Ḥajjāj faulted al-Zuhrī regarding his hadith.

Abū ʿUmar—may God have mercy on him—said: I know of no scholar of hadith among the compilers who relied upon al-Zuhrī's hadith concerning the incident of Dhu al-Yadayn. They all abandoned it due to its inconsistency, and because he never completed it in chain or text—even though he was a great imam in this field. For error is not exempt from any human, and perfection belongs to God alone. Every person's statement is taken and left, except the Prophet—peace and blessings be upon him. Thus, al-Zuhrī's statement that he was killed at Badr is abandoned due to the confirmed error in it.

This is the speech of Abū ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-Barr, summarized. May God—exalted is He—have mercy on him, for he expanded the explanation of this hadith in a manner no one else has, encompassing verification, precision, and abundant benefits. May God be pleased with him.

If it is said: How did Dhu al-Yadayn speak while the people were still in prayer? The answer is from two aspects. First: They were not certain of remaining in prayer, for they deemed permissible the abrogation of the prayer from four rakʿahs to two. For this reason he said: "Has the prayer been shortened (quṣirat) or did you forget?" Second: This was an address to the Prophet—peace and blessings be upon him—and a response, and this does not invalidate the prayer according to us and others; the issue is well-known in this regard. In a narration of Abū Dāwūd with a sound chain, the congregation gestured (awmaʾū)—i.e., "yes." According to this narration, they did not speak.

If it is said: How did the Prophet—peace and blessings be upon him—return to the statement of the congregation, when according to you it is not permissible for the one praying to revert in the measure of his prayer to the statement of another, whether imam or follower, and he acts only upon his own certainty? The answer is that the Prophet—peace and blessings be upon him—asked them to remind him. When they reminded him, he remembered and thus knew the forgetfulness, and he built upon that—not that he reverted to their mere statement. Had it been permissible to abandon one's own certainty and revert to another's statement, Dhu al-Yadayn would have reverted when the Prophet—peace and blessings be upon him—said: "The prayer was not shortened, nor did I forget."

This hadith contains evidence that abundant action and steps, if they occur in prayer inadvertently (sahwan), do not invalidate it, just as speech inadvertently does not invalidate it. On this issue, there are two views among our colleagues; the more correct of them, according to al-Mutawallī, is...

chapters.title_en: Section 315 — On the Prostration of Recitation (Sujūd al-Tilāwah)
chapters.arabic_text:
لا يبطلها لهذا الحديث فإنه ثبت في مسلم أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم مشى

إلى الجذع وخرج السرعان وفي رواية دخل الحجرة ثم خرج ورجع الناس وبنى على

صلاته والوجه الثاني وهو المشهور في المذهب أن الصلاة تبطل بذلك وهذا مشكل

وتأويل الحديث صعب على من أبطلها والله أعلم
#

| باب سجود التلاوة
# [575] قوله إن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يقرأ القرآن فيقرأ سورة فيها

سجدة فيسجد ونسجد معه حتى ما يجد بعضنا موضعا لمكان جبهته وفي رواية فيمر

بالسجدة فيسجد بنا في غير صلاة فيه إثبات سجود التلاوة وقد أجمع العلماء

عليه وهو عندنا وعند الجمهور سنة ليس بواجب وعند أبي حنيفة رضي الله عنه

واجب ليس بفرض على اصطلاحه في الفرق بين الواجب والفرض وهو سنة للقارئ

والمستمع له ويستحب أيضا للسامع الذي لا يسمع لكن لا يتأكد في حقه تأكده في

حق المستمع المصغي وقوله فيسجد بنا معناه يسجد ونسجد معه كما في الرواية

الأولى قال العلماء إذا سجد المستمع لقراءة غيره وهما في غير صلاة لم ترتبط

به بل له أن يرفع قبله وله أن يطول السجود بعده وله أن يسجد إن لم يسجد

القارئ سواء كان القارئ متطهرا أو محدثا أو امرأة أو صبيا أو غيرهم

ولأصحابنا وجه ضعيف أنه لا يسجد لقراءة الصبي والمحدث والكافر والصحيح

الأول
# [576] قوله عن عبد الله يعني بن مسعود رضي الله عنه عن  النبي صلى الله

عليه وسلم
# 
# أنه قرأ والنجم فسجد فيها وسجد من كان معه غير أن شيخا أخذ كفا من حصى أو

تراب فرفعه إلى جبهته وقال يكفيني هذا قال عبد الله لقد رأيته بعد قتل

كافرا هذا الشيخ هو أمية بن خلف وقد قتل يوم بدر كافرا ولم يكن أسلم قط

وأما قوله وسجد من كان معه فمعناه من كان حاضرا قراءته من المسلمين

والمشركين والجن والإنس قاله بن عباس رضي الله عنهما وغيره حتى شاع أن أهل

مكة أسلموا قال القاضي عياض رحمه الله تعالى وكان سبب سجودهم فيما قال بن

مسعود رضي الله عنه أنها أول سجدة نزلت قال القاضي رضي الله عنه وأما ما

يرويه الإخباريون والمفسرون أن سبب ذلك ما جرى على لسان رسول الله صلى الله

عليه وسلم من الثناء على آلهة المشركين في سورة النجم فباطل لا يصح فيه شيء

لا من جهة النقل ولا من جهة العقل لأن مدح إله غير الله تعالى كفر ولا يصح

نسبة ذلك إلى لسان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ولا أن يقوله الشيطان على

لسانه ولا يصح تسليط الشيطان على ذلك والله أعلم
# [577] قوله عن بن قسيط هو يزيد بن عبد الله بن قسيط بضم القاف وفتح السين

المهملة قوله سأل زيد بن ثابت رضي الله عنه عن القراءة مع الإمام فقال لا

قراءة مع الإمام في شيء وزعم أنه قرأ على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

والنجم اذا هوى فلم يسجد أما قوله لا قراءة مع الإمام في شيء فيستدل به أبو

حنيفة رضي الله عنه وغيره ممن يقول لا قراءة على المأموم في الصلاة سواء

كانت
# 
# سرية أو جهرية ومذهبنا أن قراءة الفاتحة واجبة على المأموم في الصلاة

السرية وكذا في الجهرية على أصح القولين والجواب عن قول زيد هذا من وجهين

أحدهما أنه قد ثبت قول رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لا صلاة لمن لم يقرأ

بأم القرآن وقوله صلى  الله عليه وسلم إذا كنتم خلفي فلا تقرءوا إلا بأم

القرآن وغير ذلك من الأحاديث وهي مقدمة على قول زيد وغيره والثاني أن قول

زيد محمول على قراءة السورة التي بعد الفاتحة في الصلاة الجهرية فإن

المأموم لا يشرع له قراءتها وهذا التأويل متعين ليحمل قوله على موافقة

الأحاديث الصحيحة ويؤيد هذا أنه يستحب عندنا وعند جماعة للإمام أن يسكت في

الجهرية بعد الفاتحة قدر ما يقرأ المأموم الفاتحة وجاء فيه حديث حسن في سنن

أبي داود وغيره في تلك السكتة يقرأ المأموم الفاتحة فلا يحصل قراءته مع

قراءة الإمام بل في سكتته وأما قوله وزعم أنه قرأ فالمراد بالزعم هنا القول

المحقق وقد قدمنا بيان هذه المسألة في أوائل هذا الشرح وأن الزعم يطلق على

القول المحقق والكذب وعلى المشكوك فيه وينزل في كل موضع على ما يليق به

وذكرنا هناك دلائله وأما قوله وزعم أنه قرأ على رسول الله صلى الله عليه

وسلم والنجم فلم يسجد فاحتج به مالك رحمه الله تعالى ومن وافقه في أنه لا

سجود في المفصل وأن سجدة النجم وإذا السماء انشقت واقرأ باسم ربك منسوخات

بهذا الحديث أو بحديث بن عباس أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لم يسجد في شيء

من المفصل منذ تحول إلى
# 
# المدينة وهذا مذهب ضعيف فقد ثبت حديث أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه المذكور

بعده في مسلم قال سجدنا مع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في إذا السماء

انشقت واقرأ باسم ربك وقد أجمع العلماء على أن إسلام أبي هريرة رضي الله

عنه كان سنة سبع من الهجرة فدل على السجود في المفصل بعد الهجرة وأما حديث

بن عباس رضي الله عنه فضعيف الإسناد لا يصح الاحتجاج به وأما حديث أبي زيد

فمحمول على بيان جواز ترك السجود وأنه سنة ليس بواجب ويحتاج إلى هذا

التأويل للجمع بينه وبين حديث أبي هريرة والله أعلم وقد اختلف العلماء في
chapters.anchors:
- Root: س-ج-د (s-j-d)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Physical prostration — placing the forehead on the ground in humble submission.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Acts of worship involving bodily humility; in Quranic usage, denotes the creature's absolute submission to the Creator.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) for physical prostration; metaphorical (majāz) for spiritual obedience and humility.
- Root: ق-ر-ء (q-r-ʾ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To gather, collect; to recite, to read aloud.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Recitation of the Quran as a devotional act; the technical term for Quranic recitation.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for vocal recitation; metaphorical for internalized comprehension and reflection.
- Root: س-م-ع (s-m-ʿ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To hear, to listen.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Auditory reception; in legal context, distinguishes the listener (mustamiʿ) from the attentive hearer (muṣghī).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for hearing; metaphorical for obedience and acceptance (samʿan wa-ṭāʿatan).
- Sībawayh Rule: ʿAṭf al-Bayān (Appositional Clarification) — The phrase "فيسجد بنا" is parsed as a coordinate clause where the preposition "بـ" indicates accompaniment, requiring the interpretation "he prostrates and we prostrate with him," as confirmed by the parallel narration.
