I say: [The previous ruling] is not invalidated by this hadith, for it is established in Muslim that the Prophet ﷺ walked to the tree trunk, and the people hurried out [in haste]. In another narration, he entered the chamber, then came out, and the people returned, and he built upon his prayer. The second opinion — which is the well-known one in our school (al-madhhab) — is that the prayer is invalidated by such an action. This is problematic, and the interpretation of the hadith is difficult for those who declare it invalidating. And Allah knows best.

#

| Chapter: The Prostration of Recitation (Sujūd al-Tilāwah)

# [575] His saying: "The Prophet ﷺ used to recite the Quran, and he would recite a chapter (sūrah) containing a prostration, and he would prostrate, and we would prostrate with him, until some of us could not find a place for his forehead." In another narration: "He would pass by a prostration verse and prostrate with us outside of prayer." This establishes the prostration of recitation (sujūd al-tilāwah). The scholars are unanimously agreed upon it. In our view and the view of the majority (al-jumhūr), it is a Sunnah (recommended practice), not obligatory (wājib). According to Abū Ḥanīfah — may Allah be pleased with him — it is obligatory (wājib), though not a strict obligation (farḍ), according to his terminology distinguishing between wājib and farḍ. It is a Sunnah for the reciter and for the one who listens to him. It is also recommended for the one who merely hears [without intending to listen], though it is not as strongly emphasized for him as it is for the attentive listener (al-muṣghī). His saying "he would prostrate with us" means: he prostrates and we prostrate with him, as in the first narration. The scholars said: When the listener prostrates due to the recitation of another, and both are outside of prayer, he is not bound to him. Rather, he may raise his head before him, he may prolong his prostration after him, and he may prostrate even if the reciter does not prostrate — whether the reciter is in a state of ritual purity (muṭahhar) or not (muḥdith), whether a woman, a child, or others. Among our companions there is a weak opinion (wajh ḍaʿīf) that one does not prostrate for the recitation of a child, a person in ritual impurity, or an unbeliever. The correct view is the first.

# [576] His saying: "From ʿAbd Allāh — meaning Ibn Masʿūd — may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet ﷺ: That he recited Sūrat al-Najm and prostrated therein, and those with him prostrated, except that an old man took a handful of pebbles or dust, raised it to his forehead, and said: 'This suffices me.'" ʿAbd Allāh said: "I saw him afterward killed as an unbeliever." This old man was Umayyah ibn Khalaf, and he was killed at Badr as an unbeliever; he had never embraced Islam at all. As for his saying "and those with him prostrated," its meaning is: those present at his recitation, from among the Muslims, the polytheists, the jinn, and mankind. Ibn ʿAbbās — may Allah be pleased with them both — and others said this, until it became widely known that the people of Mecca had embraced Islam. Al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ — may Allah have mercy on him — said: The cause of their prostration, according to what Ibn Masʿūd said, was that it was the first prostration verse revealed. Al-Qāḍī — may Allah be pleased with him — said: As for what the traditionists (al-akhbāriyyūn) and the exegetes (al-mufassirūn) narrate — that the cause of that was what occurred on the tongue of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ of praise for the deities of the polytheists in Sūrat al-Najm — this is false (bāṭil). Nothing of it is sound, neither from the standpoint of transmission (naql) nor from the standpoint of reason (ʿaql), because praising a deity other than Allah — exalted is He — is unbelief (kufr), and it is not sound to attribute that to the tongue of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, nor that Satan uttered it upon his tongue, nor is it sound that Satan be given power over that. And Allah knows best.

# [577] His saying: "From Ibn Qusayṭ" — he is Yazīd ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Qusayṭ, with ḍammah on the qāf and fatḥah on the sīn (the unpointed letter). His saying: "He asked Zayd ibn Thābit — may Allah be pleased with him — about recitation behind the imam, and he said: 'There is no recitation behind the imam in anything.' And he claimed that he recited before the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: {«وَالنَّجْمِ إِذَا هَوَىٰ»} (By the star when it falls) and he did not prostrate." As for his saying "there is no recitation behind the imam in anything," Abū Ḥanīfah — may Allah be pleased with him — and others who hold that there is no recitation for the one praying behind an imam, whether the prayer is silent (sirriyyah) or audible (jahriyyah), use this as evidence. Our school (madhhab) is that the recitation of al-Fātiḥah is obligatory (wājib) upon the one praying behind the imam in the silent prayer, and likewise in the audible prayer according to the sounder of the two opinions (al-aṣaḥḥ al-qawlayn). The answer to this statement of Zayd is from two aspects: First, the saying of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is established: "There is no prayer for the one who does not recite the Umm al-Qurʾān (the Opening Chapter)," and his saying ﷺ: "When you are behind me, do not recite except the Umm al-Qurʾān," and other hadiths of this nature. These take precedence over the statement of Zayd and others. Second, the statement of Zayd is to be interpreted as referring to the recitation of the chapter (sūrah) that follows al-Fātiḥah in the audible prayer, for the one behind the imam is not prescribed to recite it. This interpretation is necessitated in order to reconcile his statement with the authentic hadiths. This is supported by the fact that it is recommended in our view and the view of a group [of scholars] for the imam to pause in the audible prayer after al-Fātiḥah for the duration of the follower's recitation of al-Fātiḥah. A ḥasan (good) hadith to this effect is found in Sunan Abī Dāwūd and others, concerning that pause during which the follower recites al-Fātiḥah. Thus, his recitation does not occur simultaneously with the imam's recitation, but rather during his pause. As for his saying "and he claimed that he recited" — the intended meaning of "claimed" (zaʿama) here is verified speech (al-qawl al-muḥaqqaq). We have already explained this matter at the beginning of this commentary, that "zaʿama" is used for verified speech, for falsehood, and for doubtful matters, and it is interpreted in each context according to what befits it. We mentioned its evidences there. As for his saying "and he claimed that he recited before the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: {«وَالنَّجْمِ»} and he did not prostrate" — Mālik — may Allah have mercy on him — and those who agree with him used this as evidence that there is no prostration in the detailed chapters (al-mufaṣṣal), and that the prostration of Sūrat al-Najm, {«إِذَا السَّمَاءُ انشَقَّتْ»} (When the heaven is rent asunder), and {«اقْرَأْ بِاسْمِ رَبِّكَ»} (Recite in the name of your Lord) are abrogated (mansūkhāt) by this hadith, or by the hadith of Ibn ʿAbbās that the Prophet ﷺ did not prostrate in anything of the detailed chapters (al-mufaṣṣal) from the time he moved to Medina. This is a weak opinion (madhhab ḍaʿīf), for the hadith of Abū Hurayrah — may Allah be pleased with him — mentioned after this in Muslim is established: "We prostrated with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in {«إِذَا السَّمَاءُ انشَقَّتْ»} and {«اقْرَأْ بِاسْمِ رَبِّكَ»}." The scholars are unanimously agreed that the Islam of Abū Hurayrah — may Allah be pleased with him — was in the seventh year of the Hijrah. This indicates the prostration in the detailed chapters (al-mufaṣṣal) after the Hijrah. As for the hadith of Ibn ʿAbbās — may Allah be pleased with him — it is weak in its chain of transmission (ḍaʿīf al-isnād); it is not sound to use it as evidence. As for the hadith of Abū Zayd, it is to be interpreted as demonstrating the permissibility of omitting the prostration, and that it is a Sunnah, not obligatory. This interpretation is needed to reconcile between it and the hadith of Abū Hurayrah. And Allah knows best. The scholars have differed concerning...

chapters.arabic_text:
عدد سجدات التلاوة فمذهب الشافعي رضي الله عنه وطائفة  أنهن أربع عشرة سجدة

منها سجدتان في الحج وثلاث في المفصل وليست سجدة صاد منهن وإنما هي سجدة

شكر وقال مالك رحمه الله تعالى وطائفة هي إحدى عشرة أسقط سجدات المفصل وقال

أبو حنيفة رضي الله عنه هن أربع عشرة أثبت سجدات المفصل وسجدة صاد وأسقط

السجدة الثانية من الحج وقال أحمد وبن سريج من أصحابنا وطائفة هن خمسة عشرة

أثبتوا الجميع ومواضع السجدات معروفة واختلفوا في سجدة حم فقال مالك وطائفة

من السلف وبعض أصحابنا هي عقب قوله تعالى إن كنتم اياه تعبدون وقال أبو

حنيفة والشافعي رحمهما الله تعالى والجمهور عقب وهم لا يسئمون والله أعلم

قوله عن عطاء بن ميناء هو بكسر الميم ويمد ويقصر وقد سبق بيانه قوله عن

صفوان بن سليم عن عبد الرحمن الأعرج مولى بني مخزوم عن أبي هريرة رضي الله

عنه وفي الرواية الثانية عن عبد الله بن أبي جعفر عن عبد الرحمن الأعرج عن

أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه مثله قال الحميدي في الجمع بين الصحيحين في آخر

ترجمة أبي هريرة الأعرج الأول مولى بني مخزوم اسمه عبد الرحمن بن سعد

المقعد كنيته أبو أحمد وهو قليل الحديث وأما عبد الرحمن الأعرج الآخر فهو

بن هرمز كنيته أبو داود مولى ربيعة بن الحارث وهو كثير الحديث وروى عنه
# 
# جماعات من الأئمة قال وقد أخرج مسلم عنهما جميعا في سجود القرآن قال

فربما أشكل ذلك قال فمولى بني مخزوم يروي ذلك عنه صفوان بن سليم وأما بن

هرمز فيروي ذلك عنه عبيد الله بن أبي جعفر هذا كلام الحميدي وهو مليح نفيس

وكذا قال الدارقطني أن الأعرج اثنان يرويان عن أبي هريرة أحدهما وهو

المشهور عبد الرحمن بن هرمز والثاني عبد الرحمن بن سعد
# 
# مولى بني مخزوم وهذا هو الصواب وقال أبو مسعود الدمشقي هما واحد قال أبو

علي الغساني الجياني الصواب قول الدارقطني والله أعلم واعلم أنه يشترط

لجواز سجود التلاوة وصحته شروط صلاة النفل من الطهارة عن الحدث والنجس وستر

العورة واستقبال القبلة ولا يجوز السجود حتى يتم قراءة السجدة ويجوز عندنا

سجود التلاوة في الأوقات التي نهي عن الصلاة فيها لأنها ذات سبب ولا يكره

عندنا ذوات الأسباب وفي المسألة خلاف مشهور بين العلماء وفي سجود التلاوة

مسائل وتفريعات مشهورة في كتب الفقه وبالله التوفيق

| باب صفة الجلوس في الصلاة وكيفية وضع اليدين على
# الفخذين)
# [579] قوله عن بن الزبير رضي الله عنهما كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه

وسلم إذا قعد في الصلاة جعل قدمه اليسرى بين فخذه وساقه وفرش قدمه اليمنى

ووضع يده اليسرى على ركبته اليسرى ووضع يده اليمنى على فخذه اليمنى وأشار

بإصبعه وفي رواية أشار بإصبعه السبابة ووضع
# 
# إبهامه على إصبعه الوسطى ويلقم كفه اليسرى ركبته
# [580] وفي رواية بن عمر رضي الله عنهما أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان

إذا جلس في الصلاة وضع يديه على ركبتيه ووضع إصبعه اليمنى التي تلي الإبهام

فدعا بها ويده اليسرى على ركبته باسطها عليها وفي رواية عنه ووضع يده

اليمنى على ركبته اليمنى وعقد ثلاثا وخمسين وأشار بالسبابة هذا الذي ذكره

من صفة القعود هو التورك لكن قوله وفرش قدمه اليمنى مشكل لأن السنة في

القدم اليمنى أن تكون منصوبة باتفاق العلماء وقد تظاهرت الأحاديث الصحيحة

على ذلك في صحيح البخاري وغيره قال القاضي عياض رضي الله عنه قال الفقيه

أبو محمد الخشني صوابه وفرش قدمه اليسرى ثم أنكر القاضي قوله لأنه قد ذكر

في هذه الرواية ما يفعل باليسرى وأنه جعلها بين فخذه وساقه قال ولعل صوابه

ونصب قدمه اليمنى قال وقد تكون الرواية صحيحة في اليمنى ويكون معنى فرشها

أنه لم ينصبها على أطراف أصابعه في هذه المرة ولا فتح أصابعها كما كان يفعل

في غالب الأحوال هذا كلام القاضي وهذا التأويل الأخير الذي ذكره هو المختار

ويكون فعل هذا لبيان الجواز وأن وضع أطراف الأصابع على الأرض وإن كان

مستحبا يجوز تركه وهذا التأويل له نظائر كثيرة لا سيما في باب الصلاة وهو

أولى  من تغليط رواية ثابتة في الصحيح واتفق عليها جميع نسخ مسلم وقد سبق

اختلاف العلماء
# 
# في أن الأفضل في الجلوس في التشهدين التورك أم الافتراش فمذهب مالك

وطائفة تفضيل التورك فيهما لهذا الحديث ومذهب أبي حنيفة وطائفة تفضيل

الافتراش ومذهب الشافعي رضي الله عنه وطائفة يفترش في الأول ويتورك في

الأخير لحديث أبي حميد الساعدي ورفقته في صحيح البخاري وهو صريح في الفرق

بين التشهدين قال الشافعي رحمه الله تعالى والأحاديث الواردة بتورك أو

افتراش مطلقة لم يبين فيها أنه في التشهدين أو أحدهما وقد بينه أبو حميد

ورفقته ووصفوا الافتراش في الأول والتورك في الأخير وهذا مبين فوجب حمل ذلك

المجمل عليه والله أعلم وأما قوله ووضع يده اليسرى على ركبته وفي رواية

ويلقم كفه اليسرى ركبته فهو دليل على استحباب ذلك وقد أجمع العلماء على

استحباب وضعها عند الركبة أو على الركبة وبعضهم يقول بعطف أصابعها على
chapters.anchors:
- Root: س-ج-د (s-j-d)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning is "to prostrate," lowering oneself in humility; the noun "sajdah" denotes the act of placing the forehead on the ground in worship.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological usage, "sajdah" is the physical act of worship signifying utter submission (khudūʿ) to Allah, distinct from mere bowing (rukūʿ).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) in ritual context; metaphorically (majāz) used for humility of the soul, but here strictly literal.
- Root: ت-و-ر-ك (t-w-r-k)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Derived from "wark" (hip); "tawarruk" means to sit resting on the left hip with the right foot erect and the left foot tucked beneath.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In jurisprudential (fiqh) discourse, it denotes a specific sitting posture in prayer, symbolizing composed reverence.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal description of bodily posture; no metaphorical extension in this context.
- Root: ا-ف-ت-ر-ش (f-r-sh)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: "Iftirāsh" means to spread out or lay flat; in prayer, it refers to sitting on the left foot with the right foot erect.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Technical term in fiqh for a relaxed sitting posture, contrasting with tawarruk.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal; denotes physical spreading of the limb.
- Sībawayh Rule: Rule of Exception (Istithnāʾ) and Specification (Takhṣīṣ) — Used to parse the enumeration of prostration counts, where scholars specify exceptions (e.g., excluding Sād's prostration as a thanks-prostration) and qualify general statements with particular conditions.
chapters.translation:
I say: Know that the number of prostration verses in the Qur'an—according to the school of al-Shāfiʿī (may Allah be pleased with him) and a group of scholars—is fourteen prostrations. Among them are two in Sūrat al-Ḥajj and three in the Mufaṣṣal (the short surahs at the end of the Qur'an). The prostration in Sūrat Ṣād is not among them; rather, it is a prostration of thanksgiving (sajdat shukr).

Mālik (may Allah have mercy on him) and a group held that they are eleven, dropping the prostrations of the Mufaṣṣal. Abū Ḥanīfah (may Allah be pleased with him) held that they are fourteen, affirming the Mufaṣṣal prostrations and the prostration of Ṣād, but dropping the second prostration from al-Ḥajj. Aḥmad, Ibn Surayj from our companions, and a group held that they are fifteen, affirming all of them. The locations of these prostrations are well-known.

They differed regarding the prostration in Sūrat Ḥā-Mīm (Sūrat Fuṣṣilat). Mālik, a group of the Salaf, and some of our companions said it occurs after His saying (the Exalted): {«إِن كُنتُمْ إِيَّاهُ تَعْبُدُونَ»} ("If you are worshipping Him alone"). Abū Ḥanīfah, al-Shāfiʿī (may Allah have mercy on them both), and the majority said it occurs after His saying: {«وَهُمْ لَا يَسْأَمُونَ»} ("And they do not grow weary"). And Allah knows best.

His statement: "From ʿAṭāʾ ibn Mīnāʾ"—it is with a kasrah on the mīm, and it may be lengthened or shortened; its explanation has preceded.

His statement: "From Ṣafwān ibn Sulaym, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Aʿraj, the freed slave (mawlā) of Banī Makhzūm, from Abū Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him)." In the second narration: "From ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Jaʿfar, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Aʿraj, from Abū Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him)"—similar to it.

Al-Ḥumaydī said in al-Jamʿ bayn al-Ṣaḥīḥayn, at the end of the biography of Abū Hurayrah: "The first al-Aʿraj, the mawlā of Banī Makhzūm, his name is ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Saʿd al-Muqʿad, his kunyah is Abū Aḥmad, and he has few hadiths. As for the other ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Aʿraj, he is Ibn Hurmuz, his kunyah is Abū Dāwūd, the mawlā of Rabīʿah ibn al-Ḥārith, and he has many hadiths; a large group of imams narrated from him." He said: "Muslim narrated from both of them in the chapter on the prostrations of the Qur'an." He said: "This may cause confusion." He said: "The mawlā of Banī Makhzūm—Ṣafwān ibn Sulaym narrates that from him. As for Ibn Hurmuz, ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Abī Jaʿfar narrates that from him." This is the statement of al-Ḥumaydī, and it is excellent and precious.

Al-Dāraquṭnī likewise said that al-Aʿraj are two individuals who narrate from Abū Hurayrah: one of them—and he is the well-known one—is ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Hurmuz, and the second is ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Saʿd, the mawlā of Banī Makhzūm. This is the correct view. Abū Masʿūd al-Dimashqī said they are one and the same. Abū ʿAlī al-Ghassānī al-Jayyānī said: "The correct view is the statement of al-Dāraquṭnī." And Allah knows best.

Know that for the permissibility and validity of the prostration of recitation (sajdat al-tilāwah), the conditions of a supererogatory prayer (ṣalāt al-nafl) are required: purification from minor and major impurity (ṭahārah ʿan al-ḥadath), cleanliness from filth (najāsah), covering of the ʿawrah, and facing the qiblah. The prostration is not permissible until the recitation of the prostration verse is completed. In our school, the prostration of recitation is permissible during the times in which prayer is prohibited, because it has a cause (dhāt sabab); in our school, acts with causes are not disliked. There is a well-known disagreement among scholars on this issue. There are numerous issues and branches (masāʾil wa tafrīʿāt) concerning the prostration of recitation in the books of jurisprudence. And with Allah is the success.

[Chapter: The Description of Sitting in Prayer and the Manner of Placing the Hands on the Thighs]

[579] His statement: "From Ibn al-Zubayr (may Allah be pleased with them both): When the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) sat in prayer, he placed his left foot between his thigh and his shin, spread out his right foot, placed his left hand on his left knee, placed his right hand on his right thigh, and pointed with his finger." In another narration: "He pointed with his index finger and placed his thumb on his middle finger, and he clasped his left hand on his knee."

[580] In the narration of Ibn ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with them both): "When the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) sat in prayer, he placed his hands on his knees, placed his right finger adjacent to the thumb, and supplicated with it, while his left hand was on his left knee, spread upon it." In another narration from him: "He placed his right hand on his right knee, clasped fifty-three (i.e., made a fist with three fingers), and pointed with the index finger."

What he mentioned regarding the description of sitting is the tawarruk (sitting on the left hip). However, his statement "and he spread out his right foot" is problematic, because the Sunnah regarding the right foot is that it should be erect, by agreement of the scholars. The authentic hadiths have concurred on this in Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī and others.

Al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "The jurist Abū Muḥammad al-Khushanī said: 'The correct wording is: "and he spread out his left foot."'" Then al-Qāḍī rejected this statement, because in this narration it has already been mentioned what is done with the left foot—that he placed it between his thigh and shin. He said: "Perhaps the correct wording is: 'and he erected his right foot.'" He also said: "The narration may be sound regarding the right foot, and the meaning of 'spreading it' is that he did not erect it on the tips of his toes on this occasion, nor did he spread its toes as he usually did in most cases."

This is the statement of al-Qāḍī. The latter interpretation he mentioned is the chosen one (al-mukhtār). This action was done to demonstrate permissibility—that placing the tips of the toes on the ground, though recommended (mustaḥabb), may be omitted. This interpretation has many parallels, especially in the chapter of prayer, and it is preferable to declaring a narration established in the Ṣaḥīḥ—and agreed upon by all copies of Muslim—as erroneous.

The disagreement of scholars has preceded regarding what is superior in the sitting of the two tashahhuds: whether it is tawarruk or iftirāsh. The school of Mālik and a group prefer tawarruk in both, based on this hadith. The school of Abū Ḥanīfah and a group prefer iftirāsh. The school of al-Shāfiʿī (may Allah be pleased with him) and a group hold that one sits in iftirāsh in the first tashahhud and tawarruk in the last, based on the hadith of Abū Ḥumayd al-Sāʿidī and his companions in Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī, which is explicit in distinguishing between the two tashahhuds.

Al-Shāfiʿī (may Allah have mercy on him) said: "The hadiths reported regarding tawarruk or iftirāsh are absolute (muṭlaq), not specifying whether they refer to both tashahhuds or one of them. Abū Ḥumayd and his companions clarified this, describing iftirāsh in the first and tawarruk in the last. This is a clarifier (mubayyin), so it is obligatory to apply the ambiguous (mujmal) to it." And Allah knows best.

As for his statement: "and he placed his left hand on his knee"—and in another narration: "he clasped his left hand on his knee"—it is evidence for the recommendation (istihbāb) of that. The scholars have agreed upon the recommendation of placing the hand near the knee or upon the knee. Some of them say: bending its fingers upon it.
