chapters.arabic_text:
عند الشافعي ومن وافقه سواء كانت الصلاة قليلة أو كثيرة وإن فاتته سنة

راتبة ففيها قولان للشافعي أصحهما يستحب قضاؤها لعموم قوله صلى الله عليه

وسلم من نسي الصلاة فليصلها إذا ذكرها ولأحاديث أخر كثيرة في الصحيح كقضائه

صلى الله عليه وسلم سنة الظهر بعد العصر حين شغله عنها الوفد وقضائه سنة

الصبح في حديث الباب والقول الثاني لا يستحب وأما السنن التي شرعت لعارض

كصلاة الكسوف والاستسقاء ونحوهما فلا يشرع قضاؤها بلا خلاف والله أعلم
# [680] قوله قفل من غزوة خيبر أي رجع والقفول الرجوع ويقال غزوة وغزاة

وخيبر بالخاء المعجمة هذا هو الصواب وكذا ضبطناه وكذا هو في أصول بلادنا من

نسخ مسلم قال الباجي وأبو عمر بن عبد البر وغيرهما هذا هو الصواب قال

القاضي عياض هذا قول أهل السير وهو الصحيح قال وقال الأصيلي إنما هو حنين

بالحاء المهملة والنون وهذا غريب ضعيف واختلفوا هل كان هذا النوم
# 
# مرة أو مرتين وظاهر الأحاديث مرتان قوله إذا أدركه الكرى عرس الكرى بفتح

الكاف النعاس وقيل النوم يقال منه كري الرجل بفتح الكاف وكسر الراء يكري

كرى فهو كر وامرأة كرية بتخفيف الياء والتعريس نزول المسافرين آخر الليل

للنوم والاستراحة هكذا قاله الخليل والجمهور وقال أبو زيد هو النزول أي وقت

كان من ليل أو نهار وفي الحديث معرسون في نحر الظهيرة قوله وقال لبلال اكلأ

لنا الفجر هو بهمز آخره أي ارقبه واحفظه واحرسه ومصدره الكلأ بكسر الكاف

والمد ذكره الجوهري وقوله مواجه الفجر أي مستقبله بوجهه قوله ففزع رسول

الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أي انتبه وقام قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم أي بلال

هكذا هو في رواياتنا ونسخ بلادنا وحكى القاضي عياض عن جماعة أنهم ضبطوه أين

بلال بزيادة نون قوله فاقتادوا رواحلهم شيئا فيه دليل على أن قضاء الفائتة

بعذر ليس على الفور وإنما اقتادوها لما ذكره في الرواية الثانية فإن  هذا

منزل حضرنا فيه الشيطان قوله وأمر بلالا بالإقامة فأقام الصلاة فيه إثبات

الإقامة للفائتة وفيه إشارة إلى ترك الأذان للفائتة وفي حديث أبي قتادة بعد

إثبات الأذان للفائتة وفي المسألة خلاف مشهور والأصح عندنا إثبات الأذان

بحديث أبي قتادة وغيره من الأحاديث الصحيحة وأما ترك ذكر الأذان في حديث
# 
# أبي هريرة وغيره فجوابه من وجهين أحدهما لا يلزم من ترك ذكره أنه لم يؤذن

فلعله أذن وأهمله الراوي أو لم يعلم به والثاني لعله ترك الأذان في هذه

المرة لبيان جواز تركه وإشارة إلى أنه ليس بواجب متحتم لا سيما في السفر

قوله فصلى بهم الصبح فيه استحباب الجماعة في الفائتة وكذا قاله أصحابنا

قوله ص من نسي صلاة فليصلها إذا ذكرها فيه وجوب قضاء الفريضة الفائتة سواء

تركها بعذر كنوم ونسيان أم بغير عذر وإنما قيد في الحديث بالنسيان لخروجه

على سبب لأنه إذا وجب القضاء على المعذور فغيره أولى بالوجوب وهو من باب

التنبيه بالأدنى على الأعلى وأما قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم فليصلها إذا

ذكرها فمحمول على الاستحباب فإنه يجوز تأخير قضاء الفائتة بعذر على الصحيح

وقد سبق بيانه ودليله وشذ بعض أهل الظاهر فقال لا يجب قضاء الفائتة بغير

عذر وزعم أنها أعظم من أن يخرج من وبال معصيتها بالقضاء وهذا خطأ من قائله

وجهالة والله أعلم وفيه دليل لقضاء السنن الراتبة إذا فاتت وقد سبق بيانه

والخلاف في ذلك قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم فإن هذا منزل حضرنا فيه الشيطان

فيه دليل على استحباب اجتناب مواضع الشيطان وهو أظهر المعنيين في النهي عن

الصلاة في الحمام قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم فتوضأ ثم سجد سجدتين ثم أقيمت

الصلاة فصلى الغداة فيه استحباب قضاء النافلة الراتبة وجواز تسمية
# 
# صلاة الصبح الغداة وأنه لا يكره ذلك فإن قيل كيف نام النبي صلى الله عليه

وسلم عن صلاة الصبح حتى طلعت الشمس مع قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم إن عيني

تنامان ولا ينام قلبي فجوابه من وجهين  أصحهما وأشهرهما أنه لا منافاة

بينهما لأن القلب إنما يدرك الحسيات المتعلقة به كالحدث والألم ونحوهما ولا

يدرك طلوع الفجر وغيره مما يتعلق بالعين وإنما يدرك ذلك بالعين والعين

نائمة وإن كان القلب يقظان والثاني أنه كان له حالان أحدهما ينام فيه القلب

وصادف هذا الموضع والثاني لا ينام وهذا هو الغالب من أحواله وهذا التأويل

ضعيف والصحيح المعتمد هو الأول
# [681] قوله عن عبد الله بن رباح عن أبي قتادة رباح هذا بفتح الراء

وبالموحدة وأبو قتادة الحارث بن ربعي الأنصاري قوله خطبنا رسول الله صلى

الله عليه وسلم فقال إنكم تسيرون فيه أنه يستحب لأمير الجيش إذا رأى مصلحة

لقومه في إعلامهم بأمر أن يجمعهم كلهم ويشيع ذلك فيهم ليبلغهم كلهم

ويتأهبوا له ولا يخص به بعضهم وكبارهم لأنه ربما خفي على بعضهم فيلحقه

الضرر قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم وتأتون الماء إن شاء الله غدا فيه استحباب

قول إن شاء الله في الأمور المستقبلة وهو موافق للأمر به في القرآن قوله لا

يلوي أحد على أحد أي لا يعطف قوله ابهار الليل هو بالباء الموحدة وتشديد
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ق-ض-ي (qaḍā)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To fulfill, complete, or settle a matter; to render a judgment; in prayer context, to perform what was missed after its appointed time.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Theological nuance — qaḍā' as the divinely ordained compensation for an obligatory act (farḍ) that was not performed within its prescribed temporal limit, whether due to valid excuse or negligence.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense is "to finish" or "to decree"; here it is metaphorical (majāz) for "performing after the time has lapsed," as the act is a substitute, not the original.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clause (al-sharṭ wa al-jawāb) — In "من نسي صلاة فليصلها" (whoever forgets a prayer, let him pray it), the imperative (amr) in the apodosis indicates obligation (wujūb) when the protasis is a general condition, per the established uṣūl principle.
chapters.translation:
I say: According to al-Shāfiʿī and those who concur with him, [the ruling applies] whether the prayer was brief or lengthy. If a confirmed supererogatory prayer (sunnah rātibah) is missed, there are two opinions (qawlān) attributed to al-Shāfiʿī. The more correct of the two is that it is recommended (yustaḥabb) to make it up, due to the general import of his saying, peace and blessings be upon him: {«من نسي صلاة فليصلها إذا ذكرها»} ("Whoever forgets a prayer, let him pray it when he remembers it"), and due to numerous other authentic hadiths, such as his making up, peace and blessings be upon him, the sunnah of the noon prayer (ẓuhr) after the afternoon prayer (ʿaṣr) when the delegation had occupied him from it, and his making up the sunnah of the morning prayer (ṣubḥ) in the hadith of this chapter. The second opinion is that it is not recommended. As for supererogatory prayers that are legislated due to an incidental cause (ʿāriḍ), such as the eclipse prayer (ṣalāt al-kusūf), the rain-seeking prayer (al-istisqā'), and the like, it is not legislated to make them up, without disagreement. And Allah knows best.

[680] His saying: "He returned (qafala) from the expedition of Khaybar" — meaning he came back. Al-qafūl is the return. It is said [both] "ghazwah" and "ghazāh." Khaybar is with the dotted khā' (khā' muʿjamah) — this is the correct form, and likewise we have recorded it, and likewise it appears in the manuscripts of our lands from the copies of Muslim. Al-Bājī, Abū ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-Barr, and others said: This is the correct form. Al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ said: This is the statement of the scholars of prophetic expeditions (ahl al-siyar), and it is the sound one. He said: Al-Aṣīlī stated that it is only Ḥunayn, with the undotted ḥā' and nūn — and this is an odd and weak [variant]. They differed as to whether this sleep occurred once or twice; the apparent [import] of the hadiths is twice.

His saying: "When drowsiness (al-karā) overcame him" — al-karā, with the fatḥah on the kāf, is drowsiness (nuʿās), and it is said [also] sleep. From it one says: "karā al-rajul" — with fatḥah on the kāf and kasrah on the rā' — "yakrū karā," so he is "karin," and a woman is "kariyyah" with a lightened yā'. Al-taʿrīs is the descent of travelers at the end of the night for sleep and rest. This is what al-Khalīl and the majority stated. Abū Zayd said: It is descent at any time, whether night or day. In the hadith [it appears]: "We were making camp (muʿarrisūn) at the height of midday."

His saying: "And he said to Bilāl: 'Watch (iklā') the dawn for us'" — it is with a hamzah at its end, meaning: watch for it, guard it, and protect it. Its verbal noun is "kalā'" with kasrah on the kāf and elongation — al-Jawharī mentioned this. His saying: "Facing the dawn (muwājih al-fajr)" — meaning facing it with his face.

His saying: "The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, was startled (fazaʿa)" — meaning he awoke and stood up. His saying, peace and blessings be upon him: "O Bilāl" — this is how it appears in our transmissions and the manuscripts of our lands. Al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ reported from a group that they recorded it as "Where is Bilāl (ayna Bilāl)?" with an added nūn.

His saying: "So they led their mounts forward (faqtādū rawāḥilahum) a little" — in this is evidence that making up a missed prayer due to an excuse is not required immediately (al-fawr). They only led them forward because of what was mentioned in the second narration: "For this is a station in which Satan has attended us."

His saying: "And he commanded Bilāl to give the iqāmah, and he established the prayer" — in this is the affirmation of the iqāmah for the missed prayer, and in it is an indication of omitting the adhān for the missed prayer. In the hadith of Abū Qatādah, after [this], there is the affirmation of the adhān for the missed prayer. In this matter there is a well-known disagreement. The most correct [opinion] with us is the affirmation of the adhān, based on the hadith of Abū Qatādah and other authentic hadiths. As for the omission of mentioning the adhān in the hadith of Abū Hurayrah and others, the answer to it is from two angles: First — the omission of its mention does not necessitate that it was not given; perhaps he gave the adhān but the narrator omitted it or did not know of it. Second — perhaps he omitted the adhān on this occasion to demonstrate the permissibility of omitting it, and as an indication that it is not an absolutely binding obligation, especially during travel.

His saying: "So he led them in the morning prayer (ṣubḥ)" — in this is the recommendation of congregational prayer for the missed prayer. Likewise our companions stated this.

His saying, peace and blessings be upon him: {«من نسي صلاة فليصلها إذا ذكرها»} ("Whoever forgets a prayer, let him pray it when he remembers it") — in this is the obligation of making up a missed obligatory prayer, whether it was missed due to an excuse such as sleep or forgetfulness, or without an excuse. It is only restricted in the hadith to forgetfulness because it was issued regarding a specific cause, for if the making up is obligatory upon the excused one, then others are more deserving of the obligation — and this is of the category of alerting by the lesser to the greater (tanbīh bi al-adnā ʿalā al-aʿlā). As for his saying, peace and blessings be upon him: "Let him pray it when he remembers it," it is interpreted as indicating recommendation (istiḥbāb), for it is permissible to delay the making up of a missed prayer due to an excuse, according to the correct opinion — and its explanation and proof have preceded. Some of the Ẓāhirīs deviated [from this] and said: It is not obligatory to make up a missed prayer without an excuse, claiming that it is too great [in sin] to be absolved from the burden of its disobedience by making it up. This is an error on the part of its proponent and ignorance. And Allah knows best.

In it is also evidence for making up the confirmed supererogatory prayers (al-sunan al-rawātib) when missed — and its explanation and the disagreement therein have preceded.

His saying, peace and blessings be upon him: "For this is a station in which Satan has attended us" — in this is evidence for the recommendation of avoiding the places of Satan, and it is the more manifest of the two meanings in the prohibition of praying in the bathhouse (ḥammām).

His saying, peace and blessings be upon him: "Then he performed ablution, then prostrated two prostrations, then the iqāmah was given, and he prayed the morning prayer (al-ghadāh)" — in this is the recommendation of making up the confirmed supererogatory prayer, and the permissibility of calling the morning prayer (ṣalāt al-ṣubḥ) "al-ghadāh," and that this is not disliked.

If it is said: How did the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, sleep past the morning prayer until the sun had risen, despite his saying, peace and blessings be upon him: "My eyes sleep but my heart does not sleep"? The answer to it is from two angles. The more correct and more famous of them is that there is no contradiction between them, because the heart only perceives sensory matters connected to it, such as ritual impurity (ḥadath), pain, and the like — and it does not perceive the rising of dawn or other things connected to the eye. Rather, that is only perceived by the eye, and the eye sleeps even if the heart is awake. The second [angle] is that he had two states: one in which the heart slept — and this occasion coincided with that state — and another in which it does not sleep, and this is the predominant of his states. This second interpretation is weak, and the correct and relied-upon one is the first.

[681] His saying: "From ʿAbd Allāh ibn Rabāḥ, from Abū Qatādah" — Rabāḥ here is with fatḥah on the rā' and with a single bā'. Abū Qatādah is al-Ḥārith ibn Ribʿī al-Anṣārī.

His saying: "The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, addressed us and said: 'You will travel'" — in this is the recommendation that the commander of an army, when he sees a benefit for his people in informing them of a matter, should gather them all together and disseminate that among them, so that all of them are informed and prepared for it — and he should not single out some of them or their leaders, because it may be hidden from some of them and harm may befall them.

His saying, peace and blessings be upon him: "And you will come to the water tomorrow, if Allah wills" — in this is the recommendation of saying "if Allah wills" (in shā' Allāh) regarding future matters, and it is in accordance with the command to do so in the Qur'an.

His saying: "Let no one turn back (lā yalwī aḥadun ʿalā aḥad)" — meaning: let no one turn around [to wait for another].

His saying: "The depth of the night (ibhār al-layl)" — it is with a single bā' and tashdīd [on the rā'].

chapters.title_en: The Prophet's Sleep and the Dawn Prayer — Clarifying the Nature of Drowsiness, the Ruling on Qaḍā', and the Extension of Prayer Times
chapters.arabic_text:
الراء أي انتصف قوله فنعس هو بفتح العين والنعاس مقدمة النوم وهو ريح لطيفة

تأتي من قبل الدماغ تغطي على العين ولا تصل إلى القلب فإذا وصلت إلى القلب

كان نوما ولا ينتقض الوضوء بالنعاس من المضطجع وينتقض بنومه وقد بسطت الفرق

بين حقيقتهما في شرح المهذب قوله فدعمته أي أقمت ميله
# 
# من النوم وصرت تحته كالدعامة للبناء فوقها قوله تهور الليل أي ذهب أكثره

مأخوذ من تهور البناء وهو انهدامه يقال تهور الليل وتوهر قوله ينجفل أي

يسقط قوله قال من هذا قلت أبو قتادة فيه أنه إذا قيل للمستأذن ونحوه من هذا

يقول فلان باسمه وأنه لا بأس أن يقول أبو فلان إذا كان مشهورا بكنيته قوله

صلى الله عليه وسلم حفظك الله بما حفظت به نبيه أي بسبب حفظك نبيه وفيه أنه

يستحب لمن صنع إليه معروف أن يدعو  لفاعله وفيه حديث آخر صحيح مشهور قوله

سبعة ركب هو جمع راكب كصاحب وصحب ونظائره قوله ثم دعا بميضأة هي بكسر الميم

وبهمزة بعد الضاد وهي الإناء الذي يتوضأ به كالركوة قوله فتوضأ منها وضوءا

دون وضوء معناه وضوءا خفيفا مع أنه أسبغ الأعضاء ونقل القاضي عياض عن بعض

شيوخه أن المراد توضأ ولم يستنج بماء بل استجمر بالأحجار وهذا الذي زعمه

هذا
# 
# القائل غلط ظاهر والصواب ما سبق قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم فسيكون لها نبأ

هذا من معجزات النبوة قوله ثم أذن بلال بالصلاة فصلى رسول الله صلى الله

عليه وسلم ركعتين ثم صلى الغداة فصنع كما كان يصنع كل يوم فيه استحباب

الأذان للصلاة الفائتة وفيه قضاء السنة الراتبة لأن الظاهر أن هاتين

الركعتين اللتين قبل الغداة هما سنة الصبح وقوله كما كان يصنع كل يوم فيه

إشارة إلى أن صفة قضاء الفائتة كصفة أدائها فيؤخذ منه أن فائتة الصبح يقنت

فيها وهذا لا خلاف فيه عندنا وقد يحتج به من يقول يجهر في الصبح التي

يقضيها بعد طلوع الشمس وهذا أحد الوجهين لأصحابنا وأصحهما أنه يسر بها

ويحمل قوله كما كان يصنع أي في الأفعال وفيه إباحة تسمية الصبح غداة وقد

تكرر في الأحاديث قوله فجعل بعضنا يهمس إلى بعض هو بفتح الياء وكسر الميم

وهو الكلام الخفي قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم إنه ليس في النوم تفريط فيه دليل

لما أجمع عليه العلماء أن النائم ليس بمكلف وإنما يجب عليه قضاء الصلاة

ونحوها بأمر جديد هذا هو المذهب الصحيح المختار عند أصحاب الفقه والأصول

ومنهم من قال يجب القضاء بالخطاب السابق وهذا القائل يوافق على أنه في حال

النوم غير مكلف وأما إذا أتلف النائم بيده أو غيرها من أعضائه شيئا في حال

نومه فيجب ضمانه بالاتفاق وليس ذلك تكليفا للنائم لأن غرامة المتلفات لا

يشترط لها التكليف بالإجماع بل لو أتلف الصبي أو المجنون أو الغافل وغيرهم

ممن لا تكليف عليه شيئا وجب ضمانه  بالاتفاق ودليله من القرآن قوله تعالى

ومن قتل مؤمنا خطأ فتحرير رقبة مؤمنة ودية مسلمة إلى أهله فرتب سبحانه

وتعالى
# 
# على القتل خطأ الدية والكفارة مع أنه غير آثم بالإجماع قوله صلى الله

عليه وسلم إنما التفريط على من لم يصل الصلاة حتى يجيء وقت الصلاة الأخرى

فمن فعل ذلك فليصلها حين ينتبه لها فإذا كان من الغد فليصلها عند وقتها في

الحديث دليل على امتداد وقت كل صلاة من الخمس حتى يدخل وقت الأخرى وهذا

مستمر على عمومه في الصلوات إلا الصبح فإنها لا تمتد إلى الظهر بل يخرج

وقتها بطلوع الشمس لمفهوم قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم من أدرك ركعة من الصبح

قبل أن تطلع الشمس فقد أدرك الصبح وأما المغرب ففيها خلاف سبق بيانه في

بابه والصحيح المختار امتداد وقتها إلى دخول وقت العشاء للأحاديث الصحيحة

السابقة في صحيح مسلم وقد ذكرنا الجواب عن حديث إمامة جبريل صلى الله عليه

وسلم في اليومين في المغرب في وقت واحد وقال أبو سعيد الإصطخري من أصحابنا

تفوت العصر بمصير ظل الشيء مثليه وتفوت العشاء بذهاب ثلث الليل أو نصفه

وتفوت الصبح بالإسفار وهذا القول ضعيف والصحيح المشهور ما قدمناه من

الامتداد إلى دخول الصلاة الثانية وأما قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم فإذا كان

من الغد فليصلها عند وقتها فمعناه أنه إذا فاتته صلاة فقضاها لا يتغير

وقتها ويتحول في المستقبل بل يبقى كما كان فإذا كان الغد صلى صلاة الغد في

وقتها المعتاد ويتحول وليس معناه أنه يقضي الفائتة مرتين مرة في الحال ومرة

في الغد وإنما معناه ما قدمناه فهذا هو الصواب في معنى هذا الحديث وقد

اضطربت أقوال العلماء فيه واختار المحققون ما ذكرته والله أعلم قوله ثم قال

ما ترون الناس صنعوا قال ثم قال أصبح الناس فقدوا نبيهم فقال أبو بكر وعمر

رضي الله عنهما رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بعدكم لم يكن ليخلفكم وقال

الناس إن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
# 
# بين  أيديكم فإن يطيعوا أبا بكر وعمر يرشدوا معنى هذا الكلام أنه صلى الله

عليه وسلم لما صلى بهم الصبح بعد ارتفاع الشمس وقد سبقهم الناس وانقطع

النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وهؤلاء الطائفة اليسيرة عنهم قال ما تظنون الناس
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ن-ع-س (n-ʿ-s)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning is the initial stage of sleep; drowsiness (nuʿās) is a gentle vapor rising to the head.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In legal-theological discourse, nuʿās is distinguished from true sleep (nawm) by whether the vapor reaches the heart — a physiological criterion with juristic consequences.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal usage here; the term is used ḥaqīqah for the physical state, not metaphorically.
- Sībawayh Rule: ʿAṭf bayān (Appositional clarification) — the phrase "أي انتصف" (i.e., it reached its midpoint) functions as an explicative appositive, clarifying the preceding verb's meaning.
chapters.translation:
I say: His statement "he dozed" (fa-naʿasa) — the ʿayn is fatḥa. Drowsiness (nuʿās) is the precursor of sleep; it is a subtle vapor that arises from the brain and covers the eye but does not reach the heart. When it reaches the heart, it becomes true sleep. Ablution is not invalidated by drowsiness in one who is reclining, but it is invalidated by his [actual] sleep. I have already expounded at length the distinction between the two realities in my commentary on al-Muhadhdhab.

His statement "so I propped him up" (fa-daʿamtu-hu) — i.e., I straightened his inclination [caused] by sleep and became beneath him like a pillar supporting a structure above it.

His statement "the night had collapsed" (tahawwara al-layl) — i.e., most of it had passed. It is derived from the collapse of a building, meaning its falling down. One says "the night collapsed" (tahawwara al-layl) and "it poured forth" (tawahhara).

His statement "he was falling" (yanjafil) — i.e., he was dropping down.

His statement "he said: 'Who is this?' I said: 'Abū Qatādah'" — In this [narration] there is [the point] that when the one seeking permission and the like is asked "Who is this?", he should state his name; and that there is no harm in one saying "Abū so-and-so" if he is well-known by his kunyah.

His statement, peace and blessings be upon him: "May Allah preserve you as you have preserved His Prophet" — i.e., because of your preservation of His Prophet. In this [hadith] there is [the point] that it is recommended for the one who has received a kindness to supplicate for the one who did it. There is another authentic, well-known hadith to this effect.

His statement "seven riders" (sabʿatu rakb) — rakb is the plural of rākib, like ṣāḥib and ṣaḥb, and their analogues.

His statement "then he called for a miḍaʾah" — it is with kasra on the mīm and a hamza after the ḍād; it is the vessel used for ablution, like a small leather water-skin (rakwah).

His statement "and he performed ablution from it, an ablution less than [full] ablution" — meaning a light ablution, even though he thoroughly washed the limbs. Al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ transmitted from some of his teachers that the intended meaning is that he performed ablution without using water for istinjāʾ, but rather used stones (istajmara). What this speaker has claimed is a manifest error; the correct [interpretation] is what we have mentioned previously.

His statement, peace and blessings be upon him: "then it will have news" — this is among the miracles of prophethood.

His statement "then Bilāl gave the call to prayer for the [dawn] prayer, and the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, prayed two rakʿahs, then prayed the morning [prayer], doing as he used to do every day" — In this [hadith] there is [the point] that the adhān is recommended for the missed prayer. In it also is [the point] that the established sunnah [prayer] is made up (qaḍāʾ al-sunnah al-rātibah), because the apparent [meaning] is that these two rakʿahs before the morning prayer are the sunnah of the dawn. His statement "doing as he used to do every day" contains an indication that the manner of making up a missed prayer is like the manner of performing it on time. From this it is derived that one who makes up the missed dawn prayer performs qunūt in it — and there is no disagreement on this among us. It may also be used as evidence by those who say that one recites aloud in the dawn prayer that he makes up after sunrise. This is one of the two positions of our companions; the more correct of the two is that he recites quietly. His statement "as he used to do" is interpreted as referring to the actions [only]. In it also is the permissibility of calling the dawn prayer "ghadāh" (morning), and this recurs frequently in the hadiths.

His statement "some of us began whispering to others" (yahimisu) — it is with fatḥa on the yāʾ and kasra on the mīm; it means hidden, subdued speech.

His statement, peace and blessings be upon him: "Verily, there is no negligence in sleep" — In it is evidence for what the scholars have unanimously agreed upon: that the sleeper is not legally accountable (mukallaf). Rather, the obligation to make up the prayer and the like is [imposed] by a new command. This is the correct and chosen position of the scholars of jurisprudence (fiqh) and legal theory (uṣūl). Among them are those who say that the making up is obligatory by the prior address [before sleep]. This latter speaker agrees that during sleep one is not accountable. As for when a sleeper destroys something by his hand or other limbs while sleeping, his liability for compensation (ḍamān) is obligatory by consensus — and this is not a form of accountability imposed on the sleeper, because compensation for destroyed property does not require legal accountability by unanimous agreement. Rather, even if a child, an insane person, one who is heedless, or anyone else not under obligation destroys something, compensation is obligatory by consensus. Its evidence from the Qurʾān is His statement, exalted is He: {«وَمَن قَتَلَ مُؤْمِنًا خَطَأً فَتَحْرِيرُ رَقَبَةٍ مُّؤْمِنَةٍ وَدِيَةٌ مُّسَلَّمَةٌ إِلَىٰ أَهْلِهِ»} ("And whoever kills a believer by mistake — [the compensation is] the freeing of a believing slave and a compensation payment delivered to his family"). He, glorified and exalted, thus attached to mistaken killing the blood-wit and expiation, even though the killer is not sinful by consensus.

His statement, peace and blessings be upon him: "Negligence is only on the one who does not pray the prayer until the time of the next prayer arrives. Whoever does that, let him pray it when he wakes up for it; and if it is the next day, let him pray it at its [proper] time." — In this hadith is evidence that the time of each of the five prayers extends until the entry of the time of the next. This continues in its generality across the prayers, except for the dawn prayer: it does not extend to noon, rather its time exits at sunrise, due to the import of his statement, peace and blessings be upon him: "Whoever catches one rakʿah of the dawn prayer before the sun rises has caught the dawn prayer." As for the sunset prayer (maghrib), there is a disagreement concerning it, the exposition of which has preceded in its chapter. The correct and chosen [position] is that its time extends until the entry of the time of the night prayer ('ishāʾ), due to the authentic hadiths previously mentioned in Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim. We have already mentioned the answer concerning the hadith of Jibrīl's leading [the Prophet] in prayer over two days at one time for the maghrib.

Abū Saʿīd al-Iṣṭakhrī, one of our companions, said: "The ʿaṣr prayer is missed when the shadow of an object becomes twice its length; the night prayer is missed by the passing of a third or half of the night; and the dawn prayer is missed by the appearance of [full] morning light." This position is weak. The correct and well-known [position] is what we have presented: the extension [of time] until the entry of the second prayer.

As for his statement, peace and blessings be upon him: "and if it is the next day, let him pray it at its [proper] time" — its meaning is that when a prayer is missed and then made up, its time does not change or shift in the future; rather, it remains as it was. So when the next day comes, he prays that day's prayer at its customary time, and it shifts [accordingly]. It does not mean that he makes up the missed prayer twice — once immediately and once the next day. Rather, its meaning is what we have mentioned. This is the correct [understanding] of the meaning of this hadith. The statements of the scholars concerning it have been divergent, and the verifiers (muḥaqqiqūn) have chosen what I have mentioned. And Allah knows best.

His statement "then he said: 'What do you think the people have done?'" — He then said: "The people have awakened to find that they have lost their Prophet." Abū Bakr and ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: "The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, after you — he would not leave you." And the people said: "The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, is before you; if they obey Abū Bakr and ʿUmar, they will be rightly guided." The meaning of this speech is that when he, peace and blessings be upon him, led them in the dawn prayer after the sun had risen — while the people had gone ahead of them, and the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and this small group had been cut off from them — he said: "What do you think the people have done?"

chapters.title_en: Section 338 – The Miracles of the Prophet at the Water Trough, the Etiquette of Drinking, and Related Rulings
chapters.arabic_text:
يقولون فينا فسكت القوم فقال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أما أبو بكر وعمر

فيقولان للناس أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وراءكم ولا تطيب نفسه أن يخلفكم

وراءه ويتقدم بين أيديكم فينبغي لكم أن تنتظروه حتى يلحقكم وقال باقي الناس

إنه سبقكم فالحقوه فإن أطاعوا أبا بكر وعمر رشدوا فإنهما على الصواب والله

أعلم قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم لا هلك عليكم هو بضم الهاء وهو من الهلاك

وهذا من المعجزات قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم أطلقوا لي غمري هو بضم الغين

المعجمة وفتح الميم وبالراء هو القدح الصغير قوه فلم يعد أن رأى الناس ما

في الميضأة تكابوا عليها ضبطنا قوله ما هنا بالمد والقصر وكلاهما صحيح قوله

صلى الله عليه وسلم أحسنوا الملأ كلكم سيروى الملأ بفتح الميم واللام وآخره

همزة وهو منصوب مفعول أحسنوا والملأ الخلق والعشرة يقال ما أحسن ملأ فلان

أي خلقه وعشرته وما أحسن ملأ بني فلان أي عشرتهم وأخلاقهم ذكره الجوهري

وغيره وأنشد الجوهري ... تنادوا بال بهتة إذ رأونا ... فقلنا أحسني ملأ

جهينا
# 
# قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم إن ساقي القوم آخرهم فيه هذا الأدب من آداب

شاربي الماء واللبن ونحوهما وفي معناه ما يفرق على الجماعة من المأكول كلحم

وفاكهة ومشموم وغير ذلك والله أعلم قوله فأتى الناس الماء جامين رواء أي

نشاطا مستريحين قوله في مسجد الجامع هو من باب إضافة الموصوف إلى صفته فعند

الكوفين يجوز ذلك بغير تقدير وعند البصريين لا يجوز إلا بتقدير ويتأولون ما

جاء في هذا بحسب مواطنه والتقدير هنا مسجد المكان الجامع وفي قول الله

تعالى وما كنت بجانب الغربي صلى الله عليه وسلم أي المكان الغربي وقوله

تعالى ولدار الآخرة صلى الله عليه وسلم  أي الحياة الآخرة وقد سبقت المسألة

في مواضع والله أعلم قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم وما شعرت أن أحدا حفظه كما

حفظته ضبطناه حفظته بضم التاء وفتحها وكلاهما حسن وفي حديث أبي قتادة هذا

معجزات ظاهرات لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إحداها إخباره بأن الميضأة

سيكون لها نبأ وكان كذلك الثانية تكثير الماء القليل الثالثة قوله صلى الله

عليه وسلم كلكم سيروى وكان كذلك الرابعة قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال أبو

بكر وعمر كذا وقال الناس كذا الخامسة قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم إنكم تسيرون

عشيتكم وليلتكم وتأتون الماء وكان كذلك ولم يكن أحد من القوم يعلم ذلك

ولهذا قال فانطلق الناس لا يلوي أحد على أحد إذ لو كان أحد منهم يعلم ذلك

لفعلوا ذلك قبل قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم
# [682] قوله حدثنا سلم
# 
# بن زرير هو بزاي في أوله مفتوحة ثم راء مكررة قوله فأدلجنا ليلتنا هو

بإسكان الدال وهو سير الليل كله وأما أدلجنا بفتح الدال المشددة فمعناه

سرنا آخر الليل هذا هو الأشهر في اللغة وقيل هما لغتان بمعنى ومصدر الأول

إدلاج بإسكان الدال والثاني إدلاج بكسر الدال المشددة قوله بزغت الشمس هو

أول طلوعها وقوله وكنا لا نوقظ نبي الله صلى الله عليه وسلم من منامه إذا

نام حتى يستيقظ قال العلماء كانوا يمتنعون من إيقاظه صلى الله عليه وسلم

لما كانوا يتوقعون من الإيحاء إليه في المنام ومع هذا فكانت الصلاة قد فات

وقتها فلو نام آحاد الناس اليوم وحضرت صلاة وخيف فوتها نبهه من حضره لئلا

تفوت الصلاة قوله في الجنب فأمره رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فتيمم

بالصعيد فصلى فيه جواز التيمم للجنب إذا عجز عن الماء وهو مذهبنا ومذهب

الجمهور وقد سبق بيانه في بابه قوله إذا نحن بامرأة سادلة رجليها بين

مزادتين السادلة المرسلة المدنية والمزادة معروفة وهي أكبر من القربة

والمزادتان
# 
# حمل البعير سميت مزادة لأنه يزاد فيها من جلد آخر من غيرها قوله فقلنا

لها  أين الماء قالت أيهاه أيهاه لا ماء لكم هكذا هو في الأصول وهو بمعنى

هيهات هيهات ومعناه البعد من المطلوب واليأس منه كما قالت بعده لا ماء لكم

أي ليس لكم ماء حاضر ولا قريب وفي هذه اللفظة بضع عشرة لغة ذكرتها كلها

مفصلة واضحة متقنة مع شرح معناها وتصريفها وما يتعلق بها في تهذيب الأسماء

واللغات وقد تقدم أيضا ذلك قوله وأخبرته أنها مؤتمة بضم الميم وكسر التاء

أي ذات أيتام قوله فأمر براويتها فأنيخت والراوية عند العرب هي الجمل الذي

يحمل الماء وأهل العرف قد يستعملونه في المزادة استعارة والأصل البعير قوله

فمج في العزلاوين العلياوين المج زرق الماء بالفم والعزلاء بالمد هو المشعب

الأسفل للمزادة الذي يفرغ منه الماء ويطلق أيضا على فمها الأعلى كما قال في

هذه الرواية العزلاوين العلياوين وتثنيتها عزلاوان والجمع العزالي بكسر

اللام قوله وغسلنا صاحبنا يعني الجنب هو بتشديد السين أي أعطيناه ما يغتسل

به وفيه دليل على أن المتيمم عن الجنابة إذا أمكنه استعمال الماء اغتسل

قوله وهي تكاد تنضرج من الماء
# 
# أي تنشق وهو بفتح التاء وإسكان النون وفتح الضاد المعجمة وبالجيم وروي

بتاء أخرى بدل النون وهو بمعناه والأول هو المشهور قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم
chapters.anchors:
- Root: هـ ل ك (halaka)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Perishing, destruction, ruin; the opposite of survival (baqāʾ).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological usage, al-halāk denotes spiritual ruin through disobedience, distinct from mere physical death.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) for physical destruction; metaphorical (majāz) for loss of guidance or honor.
- Root: م ل أ (malaʾa)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To fill; al-malaʾ as a collective noun for a group of chiefs or the prominent people of a community.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In Quranic contexts, al-malaʾ refers to the leading council of a people, often in opposition to prophets.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for "filling"; metaphorical for the "fill" of a person—i.e., their character, company, and moral constitution.
- Root: ع ز ل (ʿazala)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To separate, set apart; al-ʿazlāʾ is the spout or outlet of a water-skin.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Not a theological term; retained in its concrete lexical sense.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for the physical spout; the dual form al-ʿazlawān indicates the two openings (upper and lower) of a waterskin.
- Root: ر و ي (rawiya)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To drink one's fill, to be quenched; al-riyy is satiation with water.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Used metaphorically for spiritual satisfaction with knowledge or faith.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for quenching thirst; metaphorical for being fully satisfied in any need.
- Sībawayh Rule: Al-Idāfah (Genitive Construction) – When a noun is attributed to its own adjective (e.g., "Masjid al-Jāmiʿ"), the Basrans require an implied deleted noun (taqdīr), while the Kufans permit it without ellipsis. The taqdīr here is "Masjid al-Makān al-Jāmiʿ" (the mosque of the gathering place).
chapters.translation:
I say: They were saying about us [things], and the people fell silent. Then the Prophet ﷺ said: "As for Abū Bakr and ʿUmar, they will say to the people: 'The Prophet ﷺ is behind you, and his soul does not consent to leave you behind him and advance ahead of you; so it behooves you to wait for him until he catches up with you.' And the rest of the people will say: 'He has preceded you, so catch up with him.'" If they obey Abū Bakr and ʿUmar, they will be rightly guided, for they are upon correctness. And Allah knows best.

His saying ﷺ: "No ruin (halāk) upon you" – it is with ḍammah on the hāʾ, and it is from al-halāk (perdition). And this is among the miracles [of the Prophet].

His saying ﷺ: "Uncover for me my small cup (ghumrī)" – it is with ḍammah on the ghayn (unpointed letter), fatḥah on the mīm, and with rāʾ; it is the small drinking vessel.

His saying: "He did not delay" – he did not see the people [rushing] toward what was in the water trough (al-mīḍaʾah) except that they crowded upon it. We have recorded his saying "mā" here with both prolongation (al-madd) and shortening (al-qaṣr), and both are correct.

His saying ﷺ: "Do well, all of you, in the company (al-malaʾ)" – it will be narrated as al-malaʾ with fatḥah on the mīm and the lām, and its final letter is a hamzah; it is in the accusative as the object of "do well" (aḥsinū). And al-malaʾ means character (al-khuluq) and companionship (al-ʿishrah). One says: "How excellent is the malaʾ of so-and-so," i.e., his character and his companionship; and "How excellent is the malaʾ of the Banū Fulān," i.e., their companionship and their morals. Al-Jawharī and others mentioned this, and al-Jawharī cited the verse: "They called out with astonishment when they saw us, so we said: 'Do well, O company of Juhaynah.'"

His saying ﷺ: "Indeed, the one who gives drink to the people is the last of them" – in this is an etiquette from the etiquettes of those who drink water, milk, and the like. And in its meaning is what is distributed among a group of food, such as meat, fruit, perfume, and other things. And Allah knows best.

His saying: "Then the people came to the water satisfied (riwāʾ)" – i.e., active and rested.

His saying: "In the congregational mosque (masjid al-jāmiʿ)" – this is of the type of annexing the described noun to its adjective. According to the Kufans, this is permissible without any implied deletion; according to the Basrans, it is not permissible except with an implied deletion, and they interpret what has come of this type according to its contexts. The implied deletion here is "the mosque of the gathering place (masjid al-makān al-jāmiʿ)." And in the saying of Allah Most High: {وَمَا كُنتَ بِجَانِبِ الْغَرْبِيِّ} "And you were not on the western side" – i.e., the western place; and His saying: {وَلَدَارُ الْآخِرَةِ} "And the abode of the Hereafter" – i.e., the final life. This matter has already been discussed in other places. And Allah knows best.

His saying ﷺ: "And I did not perceive that anyone had memorized it as I had memorized it" – we have recorded it as "ḥafiztuhu" with ḍammah on the tāʾ and with fatḥah on it, and both are good.

In this ḥadīth of Abū Qatādah there are manifest miracles of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. The first: his informing that the water trough would have a significant affair, and so it was. The second: the multiplication of the small amount of water. The third: his saying ﷺ: "All of you will be satisfied," and so it was. The fourth: his saying ﷺ: "Abū Bakr and ʿUmar will say such-and-such, and the people will say such-and-such." The fifth: his saying ﷺ: "You will travel this evening and your night, and you will come to the water," and so it was, and none of the people knew that. For this reason, he said: "The people set out, not one turning to another" – for had any of them known it, they would have done that before his saying ﷺ.

[682] His saying: "Salam ibn Zarīr narrated to us" – it is with zāy at its beginning, fatḥah on it, then rāʾ doubled.

His saying: "We traveled the night (adlajnā) through our night" – it is with sukūn on the dāl, and it means traveling the entire night. As for "adlajnā" with fatḥah on the doubled dāl, its meaning is: we traveled at the end of the night. This is the more famous [usage] in the language, and it is said they are two dialects with the same meaning. The verbal noun of the first is idlāj with sukūn on the dāl, and of the second idlāj with kasrah on the doubled dāl.

His saying: "The sun rose (bazaghat)" – it is its first rising.

His saying: "And we would not wake the Prophet of Allah ﷺ from his sleep when he slept until he woke himself" – the scholars said: They refrained from waking him ﷺ because of what they anticipated of revelation coming to him during sleep. Nevertheless, the time of prayer had passed. So if an ordinary person sleeps today and the prayer time arrives and one fears its passing, the one present should wake him so that the prayer is not missed.

His saying: "Regarding the one in major ritual impurity (al-junub)" – the Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded him, so he performed dry ablution (tayammum) with pure earth and prayed. In this is the permissibility of tayammum for the junub when he is unable to find water. This is our school and the school of the majority, and its explanation has already preceded in its chapter.

His saying: "When suddenly we came upon a woman letting her legs hang down (sādilah) between two water-skins (mazādatayn)" – al-sādilah is the one letting [her legs] hang down, and al-mazādah is well-known; it is larger than a water-bag (al-qirbah). And the two mazādahs are the load of a camel. It is called mazādah because additional leather from another [skin] is added (yuzād) to it.

His saying: "We said to her: 'Where is the water?' She said: 'Ayahāh, ayahāh, there is no water for you'" – thus it is in the manuscripts, and it means "hayahāt, hayahāt" (far away), and its meaning is the remoteness of the sought thing and despair of it, as she said afterward: "There is no water for you," i.e., you have no water present nor near. And this word has some ten-odd dialects, all of which I have mentioned in detail, clearly, precisely, with an explanation of its meaning, its conjugation, and what pertains to it, in Tahdhīb al-Asmāʾ wa al-Lughāt. And this has also preceded.

His saying: "And I informed her that she was a mother of orphans (muʾtimah)" – with ḍammah on the mīm and kasrah on the tāʾ, i.e., possessing orphans.

His saying: "He commanded regarding her water-camel (rāwiyatihā), so it was made to kneel" – al-rāwiyah among the Arabs is the camel that carries water. And the people of common usage may employ it for the water-skin metaphorically (istiʿārah), but the origin is the camel.

His saying: "Then he expelled water from his mouth (majja) into the two upper spouts (al-ʿazlawayn al-ʿulayawayn)" – al-majj is the ejection of water from the mouth. And al-ʿazlāʾ, with prolongation, is the lower spout of the water-skin from which the water is poured out; and it is also applied to its upper mouth, as stated in this narration: "the two upper spouts." Its dual is ʿazlawān, and the plural is al-ʿazālī with kasrah on the lām.

His saying: "And we washed our companion" – meaning the junub – it is with tashdīd on the sīn, i.e., we gave him what he could use to wash himself. And in this is evidence that the one who performed tayammum due to major impurity, when he is able to use water, must perform the full ritual bath (ghusl).

His saying: "While it was nearly bursting (tanḍarij) from the water" – i.e., splitting open; it is with fatḥah on the tāʾ, sukūn on the nūn, fatḥah on the ḍād (unpointed), and with jīm. And it is narrated with another tāʾ in place of the nūn, and it has the same meaning; the first is the more famous.

His saying ﷺ: ...
