- Root: ج-م-ع (j-m-ʿ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To bring together, unite, or combine; al-jamʿ denotes assembling disparate elements into a single whole.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In legal-theological usage, jamʿ bayn al-ṣalātayn refers to conjoining two obligatory prayers within one time frame, whether by advance (taqdīm) or delay (taʾkhīr), contingent upon valid concessions (rukhaṣ).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) = physical gathering; metaphorical (majāz) = temporal merging of prayer times, a juristic extension of the root's core sense.
- Root: ح-ر-ج (ḥ-r-j)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Constriction, straitness, or impediment; a narrow passage causing distress.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In Quranic and prophetic discourse, ḥaraj signifies moral or religious hardship that the Law seeks to remove (rafʿ al-ḥaraj), as in {«وَمَا جَعَلَ عَلَيْكُمْ فِي الدِّينِ مِنْ حَرَجٍ»}.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal = physical tightness; metaphorical = undue burden upon the community (umma), which the Prophet (ﷺ) aimed to preclude.
- Root: ن-ص-ر-ف (n-ṣ-r-f)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To turn away, depart, or withdraw from a place or action.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Technical term for concluding the prayer by turning the head right or left for the taslīm, or physically leaving the prayer space.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal = physical turning; metaphorical = completion and disengagement from the ritual act.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clause with Implied Apodosis (al-sharṭ wa-l-jawāb al-maḥdhūf) — In "أراد أن لا يحرج أحدا من أمته," the purpose clause (li-ʿadam al-ḥaraj) functions as an elliptical answer to the implicit question of causation, governed by the verb arāda, requiring naṣb on the subjunctive.
chapters.translation:
I say: And the ʿAṣr prayer together [with Ẓuhr] in Medina, without fear or travel. And Ibn ʿAbbās, when asked why he did that, said: "He intended thereby not to place any of his community in hardship."

And in the other narration from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) combined between the prayers during a journey he undertook in the expedition of Tabūk, combining Ẓuhr with ʿAṣr, and Maghrib with ʿIshāʾ. Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said: I said to Ibn ʿAbbās: "What impelled him to do that?" He said: "He intended not to place his community in hardship."

And in the narration of Muʿādh ibn Jabal, the like of it, exactly — that it was in the expedition of Tabūk, and he said the like of Ibn ʿAbbās's statement.

And in the other narration from Ibn ʿAbbās: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) combined between Ẓuhr and ʿAṣr, and between Maghrib and ʿIshāʾ, in Medina, without fear or rain. I said to Ibn ʿAbbās: "Why did he do that?" He said: "So as not to place his community in hardship."

And in a narration from ʿAmr ibn Dīnār, from Abū al-Shaʿthāʾ Jābir ibn Zayd, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: "I prayed with the Prophet (ﷺ) eight [cycles] together, and seven together." I said: "O Abū al-Shaʿthāʾ, I think he delayed Ẓuhr and hastened ʿAṣr, and delayed Maghrib and hastened ʿIshāʾ." He said: "And I think that too."

And in a narration from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Shaqīq, he said: Ibn ʿAbbās addressed us one day after ʿAṣr until the sun set and the stars appeared, and the people began saying: "The prayer! The prayer!" Then a man from the Banū Taym came and did not cease nor relent: "The prayer! The prayer!" Ibn ʿAbbās said: "Do you teach me the Sunnah? May you have no mother! I saw the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) combine between Ẓuhr and ʿAṣr, and Maghrib and ʿIshāʾ." ʿAbd Allāh ibn Shaqīq said: So something stirred in my chest regarding that, and I came to Abū Hurayrah and asked him, and he affirmed his statement.

These are the established narrations in Muslim, as you see them. And the scholars have regarding them interpretations and schools of thought. Al-Tirmidhī said at the end of his book: "There is not in my book a hadith upon which the umma has unanimously agreed to abandon acting, except the hadith of Ibn ʿAbbās on combining in Medina without fear or rain, and the hadith of executing the wine-drinker on the fourth occasion." And what al-Tirmidhī said regarding the wine-drinker hadith is as he said — it is an abrogated (mansūkh) hadith, and consensus (ijmāʿ) indicates its abrogation. As for the hadith of Ibn ʿAbbās, they have not unanimously agreed to abandon acting upon it; rather, they have multiple positions. Among them are those who interpreted it as combining due to the excuse of rain — and this is well-known from a group of the great early scholars — but it is weak due to the other narration [specifying] "without fear or rain." And among them are those who interpreted it as being during cloud cover: he prayed Ẓuhr, then the clouds cleared and it became evident that the time of ʿAṣr had entered, so he prayed it — and this too is false, because even if it has the slightest possibility regarding Ẓuhr and ʿAṣr, it has no possibility regarding Maghrib and ʿIshāʾ. And among them are those who interpreted it as delaying the first [prayer] to the end of its time, praying it therein, then when he finished it, the second [prayer's] time entered, so he prayed it — thus his prayer became a formal combining (ṣūrat jamʿ) — and this too is weak or false, because it contradicts the apparent meaning (ẓāhir) in an intolerable manner. And the action of Ibn ʿAbbās which we mentioned — when he delivered the sermon and adduced the hadith to validate his action, and Abū Hurayrah's affirmation of him and his lack of denial — is explicit in refuting this interpretation.

And among them are those who said: it is carried upon combining due to the excuse of illness or something similar to it in meaning from among the valid excuses. This is the position of Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal and al-Qāḍī Ḥusayn from our companions (the Shāfiʿīs), and it was chosen by al-Khaṭṭābī, al-Mutawallī, and al-Rūyānī from our companions. And it is the chosen position in its interpretation, due to the apparent meaning of the hadith, and due to the action of Ibn ʿAbbās and the agreement of Abū Hurayrah, and because the hardship therein is more severe than rain.

And a group of the imams held the permissibility of combining in one's place of residence (ḥaḍar) for a need, for one who does not make it a habit — this is the position of Ibn Sīrīn and Ashhab from the companions of Mālik. Al-Khaṭṭābī related it from al-Qaffāl and al-Shāshī al-Kabīr from the companions of al-Shāfiʿī, from Abū Isḥāq al-Marwazī, from a group of hadith scholars, and Ibn al-Mundhir chose it. And it is supported by the apparent meaning of Ibn ʿAbbās's statement: "He intended not to place his community in hardship" — for he did not condition it upon illness or anything else. And Allah knows best.

His statement: "Ḥaddathanā Abū al-Ṭufayl ʿĀmir ibn Wāthilah, he said: ḥaddathanā Muʿādh" — thus we have recorded it: ʿĀmir ibn Wāthilah, and so it is in some copies of our lands, and so al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ transmitted it from the majority of the narrators of Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim. And it occurred to some of them as "ʿAmr ibn Wāthilah," and so it occurred in many of the principal copies of our lands in this second narration. As for the first narration of Muslim, from Aḥmad ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from Zuhayr, from Abū al-Zubayr, from Abū al-Ṭufayl ʿĀmir — it is ʿĀmir by the agreement of the narrators there; the discrepancy is only in the second narration. And the well-known [name] of Abū al-Ṭufayl is ʿĀmir, and it was said ʿAmr. Among those who related the discrepancy is al-Bukhārī in his Tārīkh and other imams. And the reliable, well-known [name] is ʿĀmir. And Allah knows best.

His statement: "From al-Zubayr ibn al-Khurayyit" — it is with an unpointed khāʾ and a kasrah on both the khāʾ and the rāʾ, with a shaddah on the rāʾ, then a tāʾ marbūṭah below and above.

His statement: "So something stirred in my chest (fa-ḥāka fī ṣadrī) from that" — it is with ḥāʾ and kāf, meaning: there occurred in my soul a kind of doubt, wonderment, and deeming it far-fetched. One says: ḥāka yaḥīku, and ḥakka yaḥikku, and iḥtāka. And al-Khalīl also related aḥāka, and Ibn Durayd rejected it.

His statement: "May you have no mother (lā umma laka)" — it is like their saying "may you have no father," and its explanation has already preceded in the Book of Faith (Kitāb al-Īmān), in the hadith of Ḥudhayfah concerning the tribulation that surges like the waves of the sea.

| (Chapter: The Permissibility of Departing from Prayer to the Right or Left)

[707] His statement: "Ḥaddathanā Abū Bakr ibn Abī Shaybah, akhbaranā Muʿāwiyah and Wakīʿ, from al-Aʿmash, from ʿUmārah, from al-Aswad, from ʿAbd Allāh" — this entire chain is Kūfan, and in it are three Successors (tābiʿūn), one from another: al-Aʿmash, ʿUmārah, and al-Aswad.

His statement in the hadith of Ibn Masʿūd: "Let none of you give the devil a portion of his self, thinking that it is incumbent upon him not to depart except to his right — for indeed, most of what I saw of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was departing to his left."

[708] And in the hadith of Anas: "Most of what I saw of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) departing was to his..."

chapters.title_en: Section 345 – On the Desirability of the Imam Turning to the Right, and the Prohibition of Supererogatory Prayer After the Iqāmah
chapters.arabic_text:
يمينه وفي رواية كان  ينصرف عن يمينه وجه الجمع بينهما أن النبي صلى الله

عليه وسلم كان يفعل تارة هذا وتارة هذا فأخبر كل واحد بما اعتقد أنه الأكثر

فيما يعلمه فدل على جوازهما ولا كراهة في واحد منهما وأما الكراهة التي

اقتضاها كلام بن مسعود فليست بسبب أصل للإنصراف عن اليمين أو الشمال وإنما

هي في حق من يرى أن ذلك لا بد منه فإن من اعتقد وجوب واحد من الأمرين مخطئ

ولهذا قال يرى أن حقا عليه فإنما ذم من رآه حقا عليه ومذهبنا أنه لا كراهة

في واحد من الأمرين لكن يستحب أن ينصرف في جهة حاجته سواء كانت عن يمينه أو

شماله فإن استوى الجهتان في الحاجة وعدمها فاليمين أفضل لعموم الأحاديث

المصرحة بفضل اليمين في باب المكارم ونحوها هذا صواب الكلام في هذين

الحديثين وقد يقال فيهما خلاف الصواب والله أعلم
#

| (باب استحباب يمين الإمام)
# [709] فيه حديث البراء كنا إذا صلينا خلف رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

أحببنا أن نكون عن يمينه يقبل علينا بوجهه فسمعته يقول رب قني عذابك يوم

تبعث أو تجمع عبادك قال القاضي يحتمل أن يكون التيامن عند التسليم وهو

الأظهر لأن عادته صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا انصرف أن يستقبل جميعهم بوجهه قال

وإقباله صلى الله عليه وسلم يحتمل أن يكون بعد قيامه من الصلاة أو يكون حين

ينفتل

| باب كراهة المشوع في نافلة بعد شروع المؤذن
# في إقامة الصلاة سوى السنة الراتبة كسنة الصبح والظهر وغيرها سواء علم

أنه يدرك الركعة مع الإمام أم ل
# [710] اقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا أقيمت الصلاة فلا صلاة إلا المكتوبة

وفي الرواية الأخرى
# 
# إن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم مر برجل يصلي وقد أقيمت صلاة الصبح فقال

يوشك أن يصلي أحدكم الصبح أربعا فيها النهي الصريح عن افتتاح نافلة بعد

إقامة الصلاة سواء كانت راتبة كسنة الصبح والظهر والعصر أو غيرها وهذا مذهب

الشافعي والجمهور وقال أبو حنيفة وأصحابه إذا لم يكن صلى ركعتي  سنة الصبح

صلاهما بعد الإقامة في المسجد ما لم يخش فوت الركعة الثانية وقال
# 
# الثوري ما لم يخش فوت الركعة الأولى وقالت طائفة يصليهما خارج المسجد ولا

يصليهما بعد الإقامة في المسجد قوله ص أتصلي الصبح أربعا هو استفهام إنكار

ومعناه أنه لا يشرع بعد الإقامة للصبح إلا الفريضة فإذا صلى ركعتين نافلة

بعد الإقامة ثم صلى معهم الفريضة صار في معنى من صلى الصبح أربعا لأنه صلى

بعد الإقامة أربعا قال القاضي والحكمة في النهي عن صلاة النافلة بعد

الإقامة أن لا يتطاول عليها الزمان فيظن وجوبها وهذا ضعيف بل الصحيح أن

الحكمة فيه أن يتفرغ للفريضة من أولها فيشرع فيها عقب شروع الإمام وإذا

اشتغل بنافلة فاته الإحرام مع الإمام وفاته بعض مكملات الفريضة فالفريضة

أولى بالمحافظة على إكمالها قال القاضي وفيه حكمة أخرى وهو النهي عن

الاختلاف على الأئمة قوله قال حماد ثم لقيت عمرا فحدثني به ولم يرفعه هذا

الكلام لا يقدح في صحة الحديث ورفعه لأن أكثر الرواة رفعوه قال الترمذي

ورواية الرفع أصح وقد قدمنا في الفصول السابقة في مقدمة الكتاب أن الرفع

مقدم على الوقف على المذهب الصحيح وإن كان عدد الرفع أقل فكيف إذا كان أكثر
# [711] قوله عن عبد الله بن مالك بن بحينة ثم قال مسلم قال القعني عبد

الله بن مالك بن بحينة عن أبيه قال أبو الحسين قوله عن أبيه في هذا الحديث

خطأ أبو الحسين هو مسلم صاحب الكتاب وهذا الذي قاله مسلم هو الصواب عند

الجمهور وقوله عن أبيه خطأ وإنما هذا الحديث على رواية عبد الله عن النبي

صلى الله عليه وسلم وهو عبد الله بن مالك بن القشب بكسر القاف وبالشين

المعجمة الساكنة بحينة أم عبد الله والصواب في كتابته وقراءته عبد الله بن

مالك بن بحينة بتنوين مالك وكتابة بن بالألف لأنه صفة لعبد الله وقد سبق

بيانه في سجود السهو
# 
# وغيره والله أعلم قوله فلما انصرفنا أحطنا يقول هكذا هو في الأصول أحطنا

يقول وهو صحيح وفيه محذوف تقديره أحطنا به
# [712] قوله دخل رجل المسجد ورسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في صلاة الغداة

فصلى ركعتين في جانب المسجد ثم دخل مع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال يا

فلان بأي الصلاتين اعتددت أبصلاتك وحدك أم بصلاتك معنا فيه دليل على أنه لا

يصلي بعد الإقامة نافلة وإن كان يدرك الصلاة مع الإمام ورد على من قال إن

علم أنه يدرك الركعة الأولى أو الثانية يصلي النافلة وفيه دليل على إباحة

تسمية الصبح غداة وقد سبقت نظائره والله أعلم

| (باب ما يقول إذا دخل المسجد)
# [713] قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا دخل أحدكم المسجد فليقل اللهم افتح لي

أبواب رحمتك وإذا خرج فليقل اللهم إني أسألك من فضلك فيه استحباب هذا الذكر

وقد جاءت فيه أذكار كثيرة غير هذا في سنن أبي داود وغيره وقد جمعتها مفصلة

في أول كتاب الأذكار ومختصر مجموعها أعوذ بالله العظيم وبوجهه الكريم

وسلطانه القديم من الشيطان الرجيم بسم الله والحمد لله اللهم صل على محمد
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ص-ر-ف (ṣ-r-f)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Turning away, diverting, departing from a place or state.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Used for both physical departure and moral aversion; here, physical turning after prayer.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) for bodily direction; metaphorical (majāz) for abandoning an obligation.
- Root: ك-ر-ه (k-r-h)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Dislike, abhorrence, that which is burdensome.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In legal terminology, denotes a discouraged act (makrūh), distinct from the forbidden (ḥarām).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for inner aversion; technical in fiqh for a ruling of disapprobation.
- Root: ن-ف-ل (n-f-l)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Extra, additional; spoils of war (as a gift beyond obligation).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Supererogatory worship (nāfilah) — voluntary acts exceeding the obligatory.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for surplus; metaphorical for voluntary prayer.
- Root: ق-و-م (q-w-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Standing, rising, establishing.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Iqāmah — the call to commence the obligatory prayer, signifying the establishment of the ritual.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for physical standing; technical for the second call to prayer.
- Sībawayh Rule: Taqdīr al-Maḥdhūf (Ellipsis Restoration) — In "أحطنا" (we surrounded), the prepositional phrase "به" (him) is omitted but understood contextually, requiring reconstruction for syntactic completeness.
chapters.translation:
I say: Regarding his right side — and in another narration, "he used to depart to his right side" — the reconciliation between them is that the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) would sometimes do this and sometimes that. Thus, each narrator reported what he believed to be the more frequent occurrence based on his own knowledge. This indicates the permissibility of both actions, and there is no disapproval (karāhah) in either one. As for the disapproval implied by the statement of Ibn Masʿūd, it is not due to the act of departing to the right or left in itself; rather, it applies to one who holds that this direction is absolutely obligatory. For whoever believes that one of the two actions is obligatory is mistaken. Hence, he said, "he who sees it as a duty upon himself" — he only censured the one who deemed it an obligation. Our school (madhhab) holds that there is no disapproval in either action, but it is recommended (mustaḥabb) that one depart in the direction of his need, whether to his right or left. If both directions are equal in terms of need or lack thereof, then the right side is preferable, due to the general hadiths explicitly affirming the virtue of the right side in matters of honor and the like. This is the correct discourse concerning these two hadiths, though some have said otherwise about them, and Allah knows best.

#

| (Chapter: The Desirability of the Imam [Turning] to the Right)

[709] In it is the hadith of al-Barā': "When we prayed behind the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him), we loved to be on his right side, as he would turn his face toward us." He said: I heard him say: "My Lord, protect me from Your punishment on the Day You resurrect or gather Your servants." Al-Qāḍī said: It is possible that the turning to the right occurred at the time of the taslīm (salutation of peace), and this is the more apparent (aẓhar) [interpretation], because his custom (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) when departing was to face all of them with his countenance. He said: And his turning (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) could have been after his rising from the prayer, or at the moment of his turning away.

| Chapter: The Disapproval of Supererogatory Prayer After the Mu'adhdhin Begins the Iqāmah

# In the establishment of the prayer, except for the regular sunnah (al-sunnah al-rātibah) such as the sunnah of the dawn, noon, and others — whether one knows he will catch the rakʿah with the Imam or not.

[710] His statement (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him): "When the prayer is established (uqīmat al-ṣalāh), there is no prayer except the obligatory one." And in the other narration: "The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) passed by a man praying while the dawn prayer had already been established, and he said: 'Soon one of you will pray the dawn as four [rakʿahs].'" In this is an explicit prohibition (nahy ṣarīḥ) against commencing a supererogatory prayer after the establishment of the prayer, whether it be a regular sunnah like the sunnah of dawn, noon, or afternoon, or otherwise. This is the school of al-Shāfiʿī and the majority (al-jumhūr). Abū Ḥanīfah and his companions said: If one has not prayed the two rakʿahs of the dawn sunnah, he may pray them after the iqāmah in the mosque, as long as he does not fear missing the second rakʿah [of the obligatory prayer]. Al-Thawrī said: As long as he does not fear missing the first rakʿah. And a group (ṭā'ifah) said: He may pray them outside the mosque, but not after the iqāmah inside the mosque.

His statement (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him): "Do you pray the dawn as four?" is an interrogative of denial (istifhām inkār), and its meaning is that after the iqāmah for the dawn, nothing is legislated except the obligatory prayer. So if one prays two rakʿahs of supererogatory prayer after the iqāmah, then prays the obligatory prayer with them, he becomes in the meaning of one who prayed the dawn as four, because he prayed four [rakʿahs] after the iqāmah. Al-Qāḍī said: The wisdom (ḥikmah) in prohibiting supererogatory prayer after the iqāmah is that the time should not be prolonged over it, lest it be thought obligatory. This is weak (ḍaʿīf); rather, the correct [view] is that the wisdom in it is to devote oneself fully to the obligatory prayer from its beginning, so one enters into it immediately following the Imam's commencement. If one busies himself with a supererogatory prayer, he misses the initial takbīr (taḥrīmah) with the Imam and misses some of the completions of the obligatory prayer. Thus, the obligatory prayer is more deserving of being preserved and completed. Al-Qāḍī said: In it is another wisdom — the prohibition of differing from the Imams.

His statement: "Ḥammād said: Then I met ʿAmr and he narrated it to me, but he did not raise it [to the Prophet]" — this statement does not impugn the authenticity (ṣiḥḥah) of the hadith nor its elevation (rafʿ), because the majority of narrators elevated it. Al-Tirmidhī said: The narration with elevation (rafʿ) is more authentic (aṣaḥḥ). We have already stated in the preceding chapters of the introduction to this book that elevation (rafʿ) takes precedence over stopping (waqf) according to the correct school, even if the number of those who elevate is fewer — so how [much more so] when they are more numerous?

[711] His statement: "From ʿAbdullāh ibn Mālik ibn Buḥaynah" — then Muslim said: "Al-Qaʿnabī said: ʿAbdullāh ibn Mālik ibn Buḥaynah, from his father." Abū al-Ḥusayn said: His statement "from his father" in this hadith is an error. Abū al-Ḥusayn is Muslim, the author of the book [Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim]. What Muslim stated is correct according to the majority (al-jumhūr), and his statement "from his father" is an error. Rather, this hadith is on the authority of ʿAbdullāh directly from the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him). He is ʿAbdullāh ibn Mālik ibn al-Qushb — with a kasrah on the qāf and an unvocalized shīn with iʿjām (dot) — and Buḥaynah is the mother of ʿAbdullāh. The correct [form] in its writing and reading is "ʿAbdullāh ibn Mālik ibn Buḥaynah" with tanwīn on Mālik and writing "ibn" with an alif, because it is an attribute (ṣifah) of ʿAbdullāh. This has been previously explained in the chapter on the prostration of forgetfulness (sujūd al-sahw) and elsewhere. And Allah knows best.

His statement: "When we departed, we surrounded (aḥaṭnā)" — he says: Thus it is in the manuscripts: "aḥaṭnā" — he says: And it is correct, and in it there is an omitted [element], the estimation (taqdīr) being: "We surrounded him (aḥaṭnā bihi)."

[712] His statement: "A man entered the mosque while the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) was in the dawn prayer (ṣalāt al-ghadāh). He prayed two rakʿahs in a corner of the mosque, then entered with the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him). He said: 'O so-and-so, which of the two prayers did you count — your prayer alone, or your prayer with us?'" In this is evidence that one should not pray a supererogatory prayer after the iqāmah, even if he will catch the prayer with the Imam. And it refutes those who said: If one knows he will catch the first or second rakʿah, he may pray the supererogatory prayer. In it is also evidence for the permissibility of calling the dawn prayer "ghadāh" (morning). Similar examples have preceded, and Allah knows best.

| (Chapter: What One Says Upon Entering the Mosque)

[713] His statement (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him): "When one of you enters the mosque, let him say: 'O Allah, open for me the gates of Your mercy.' And when he exits, let him say: 'O Allah, I ask You of Your bounty.'" In this is the recommendation (istihbāb) of this remembrance (dhikr). Many other remembrances besides this have been reported in the Sunan of Abū Dāwūd and others, and I have compiled them in detail at the beginning of the Book of Remembrances (Kitāb al-Adhkār). A summary of their totality is: "I seek refuge with Allah the Magnificent, and with His Noble Face, and His Eternal Sovereignty, from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, and praise be to Allah. O Allah, send blessings upon Muḥammad."

chapters.title_en: Section 346 — The Greeting of the Mosque (Taḥiyyat al-Masjid), the Two Rakʿahs Upon Arrival from Travel, and the Duḥā Prayer
chapters.arabic_text:
وعلى آل محمد وسلم اللهم اغفر لي ذنوبي وافتح لي أبواب رحمتك وفي الخروج
# 
# يقوله لكن يقول اللهم إني أسألك من فضلك قوله عن أبي أسيد هو بضم الهمزة

وفتح السين قوله الحماني بكسر الحاء المهملة وتشديد الميم قال السمعاني هي

نسبة إلى بني حمان قبيلة نزلت الكوفة

| (باب استحباب تحية المسجد بركعتين وكراهة الجلوس قبل 
# صلاتهما)
# وأنها مشروعة في جميع الأوقات
# [714] قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا دخل أحدكم المسجد فليركع ركعتين قبل

أن يجلس وفي الرواية
# 
# الأخرى فلا يجلس حتى يركع ركعتين فيه استحباب تحية المسجد بركعتين وهي

سنة بإجماع المسلمين وحكى القاضي عياض عن داود وأصحابه وجوبهما وفيه

التصريح بكراهة الجلوس بلا صلاة وهي كراهة تنزيه وفيه استحباب التحية في أي

وقت دخل وهو مذهبنا وبه قال جماعة وكرهها أبو حنيفة والأوزاعي والليث في

وقت النهي وأجاب أصحابنا أن النهي إنما هو عما لا سبب له لأن النبي  صلى

الله عليه وسلم صلى بعد العصر ركعتين قضاء سنة الظهر فخص وقت النهي وصلى به

ذات السبب ولم يترك التحية في حال من الأحوال بل أمر الذي دخل المسجد يوم

الجمعة وهو يخطب فجلس أن يقوم فيركع ركعتين مع أن الصلاة في حال الخطبة

ممنوع منها إلا التحية فلو كانت التحية تترك في حال من الأحوال لتركت الآن

لأنه قعد وهي مشروعة قبل القعود ولأنه كان يجهل حكمها ولأن النبي صلى الله

عليه وسلم قطع خطبته وكلمه وأمره أن يصلي التحية فلولا شدة الاهتمام

بالتحية في جميع الأوقات لما اهتم عليه السلام هذا الاهتمام ولا يشترط أن

ينوي التحية بل تكفيه ركعتان من فرض أو سنة راتبة أو غيرهما ولو نوى بصلاته

التحية والمكتوبة انعقدت صلاته وحصلتا له ولو صلى على جنازة أو سجد شكرا أو

للتلاوة أو صلى ركعة بنية التحية لم تحصل التحية على الصحيح من مذهبنا وقال

بعض أصحابنا تحصل وهو خلاف ظاهر الحديث ودليله أن المراد إكرام المسجد

ويحصل بذلك والصواب أنه لا يحصل وأما المسجد الحرام فأول ما يدخله الحاج

يبدأ بطواف القدوم فهو تحيته ويصلي بعده ركعتي الطواف
#

| باب استحباب ركعتين في المسجد لمن قدم من سفر أول
# قدومه)
# فيه حديث جابر قال اشترى مني رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بعيرا فلما

قدم المدينة أمرني أن آتي المسجد فأصلي ركعتين وفي الرواية الأخرى قال جابر

قدم رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قبلي وقدمت فوجدته على باب المسجد قال

الآن جئت قلت نعم قال فدع جملك ثم ادخل فصل ركعتين فدخلت فصليت ثم رجعت

وفيه حديث كعب بن مالك أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كان لا يقدم من سفر

إلا نهارا في الضحى فإذا قدم بالمسجد فصلى فيه
# 
# ركعتين ثم جلس فيه في هذه الأحاديث استحباب ركعتين للقادم من سفره في

المسجد أول قدومه وهذه الصلاة مقصودة للقدوم من السفر لا أنها تحية المسجد

والأحاديث المذكورة صريحة فيما ذكرته وفيه  استحباب القدوم أوائل النهار

وفيه أنه يستحب للرجل الكبير في المرتبة ومن يقصده الناس إذا قدم من سفر

للسلام عليه أن يقعد أول قدومه قريبا من داره في موضع بارز سهل على زائريه

إما المسجد وإما غيره قوله حدثنا أحمد بن جواس هو بجيم مفتوحة وواو مشددة

مهملة وسين قوله محارب بن دثار بكسر الدال وبالثاء المثلثة قوله كان لي على

رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم دين فقضاني وزادني فيه استحباب أداء الدين

زائدا والله أعلم

| (باب استحباب صلاة الضحى وأن أقلها ركعتان)
# وأكملها ثمان ركعات وأوسطها أربع ركعات أو ست والحث على المحافظة عليها
# [717]
# [718] في الباب عن عائشة أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان لا يصلي الضحى

إلا أن يجيء من مغيبه وأنها
# 
# ما رأته صلى الله عليه وسلم يصلي سبحة الضحى قط قالت وإني لأسبحها وإن

كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ليدع العمل وهو يحب أن يعمل به خشية أن

يعمل به الناس فيفرض عليهم وفي رواية عنها أنه صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يصلي

الضحى أربع ركعات ويزيد ما شاء وفي رواية ما شاء الله وفي حديث أم هانئ أنه

صلى الله عليه وسلم صلى ثمان ركعات وفي حديث أبي ذر وأبي هريرة وأبي

الدرداء ركعتان هذه الأحاديث كلها متفقة لا اختلاف بينها عند أهل التحقيق
# 
# وحاصلها أن الضحى سنة مؤكدة وأن أقلها ركعتان وأكملها ثمان ركعات وبينهما

أربع أو ست كلاهما أكمل من ركعتين ودون ثمان وأما الجمع بين حديثي عائشة في

نفي صلاته صلى الله عليه وسلم الضحى وإثباتها فهو أن النبي صلى الله عليه

وسلم كان يصليها بعض الأوقات لفضلها ويتركها في بعضها خشية أن تفرض كما

ذكرته عائشة ويتأول قولها ما كان يصليها إلا أن يجيء من مغيبه على أن معناه

ما رأيته كما قالت في الرواية الثانية ما رأيت رسول الله صلى الله عليه

وسلم يصلي سبحة الضحى وسببه أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ما كان يكون  عند

عائشة في وقت الضحى إلا في نادر من الأوقات فإنه قد يكون في ذلك مسافرا وقد

يكون حاضرا ولكنه في المسجد أو في موضع آخر وإذا كان عند نسائه فإنما كان
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ح ي ي (ḥ-y-y)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning of life, vitality, and salutation; taḥiyyah is the act of greeting or honoring with a living address.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In sacred law, taḥiyyat al-masjid is the ritual honor rendered to the sacred space through prayer, not a verbal salutation.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) is the greeting of a person; metaphorical (majāz) is the consecration of a place by devotional act.
- Root: ق د م (q-d-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Precedence, arrival, and the front part; qudūm signifies the act of coming forth from a journey.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In legal discourse, it denotes the initial entry into a locality after travel, carrying ritual implications.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal is physical arrival; metaphorical is the priority of devotional commencement.
- Root: ض ح و (ḍ-ḥ-w)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: The forenoon when the sun has risen high; the spreading of daylight.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The Duḥā prayer is a supererogatory act tied to a specific temporal window, distinct from obligatory rites.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal is the time itself; metaphorical is the spiritual illumination sought through prayer.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clause with Imperative Apodosis (al-sharṭ wa al-jawāb) — The protasis "if one of you enters the mosque" (idhā dakhala aḥadukum al-masjid) governs an imperative apodosis, indicating a binding recommendation, not an absolute obligation, as parsed by the absence of a negating particle.
chapters.translation:
I say: And upon the family of Muḥammad, and peace. O Allah, forgive me my sins and open for me the doors of Your mercy. And regarding exiting [the mosque], he says: "O Allah, I ask You of Your bounty." His statement "on the authority of Abū Usayd" — it is with ḍammah on the hamzah and fatḥah on the sīn. His statement "al-Ḥammānī" — with kasrah on the unpointed ḥāʾ and tashdīd on the mīm. Al-Samʿānī said: It is a relative attribution to the Banū Ḥammān, a tribe that settled in Kūfah.

(Chapter: The Recommendation of Greeting the Mosque with Two Rakʿahs and the Dislike of Sitting Before Praying Them, and That It Is Prescribed in All Times)

[714] His statement, peace and blessings be upon him: "When one of you enters the mosque, let him pray two rakʿahs before sitting." And in the other narration: "Let him not sit until he prays two rakʿahs." In this is the recommendation of greeting the mosque with two rakʿahs, and it is a sunnah by the consensus of the Muslims. Al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ reported from Dāwūd and his companions the obligation of the two. And in it is the explicit statement of the dislike of sitting without prayer, and it is a dislike of tanzīh (prohibited only in the sense of being less meritorious). And in it is the recommendation of the greeting at any time one enters — and this is our school (madhhab), and a group held it. Abū Ḥanīfah, al-Awzāʿī, and al-Layth disliked it during the time of prohibition [of prayer]. Our companions answered that the prohibition applies only to what has no cause, because the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, prayed two rakʿahs after ʿAṣr as a make-up for the sunnah of Ẓuhr. Thus, the time of prohibition is specified [as applying] to what has no cause, and he prayed with him that which has a cause. And he did not abandon the greeting in any state whatsoever; rather, he commanded the one who entered the mosque on Friday while he was delivering the sermon and sat down to stand and pray two rakʿahs — even though prayer during the sermon is prohibited except for the greeting. For if the greeting were to be abandoned in any state, it would have been abandoned then, because he had sat down, and it is prescribed before sitting. And because he was ignorant of its ruling, and because the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, interrupted his sermon, spoke to him, and commanded him to pray the greeting — were it not for the intense concern for the greeting in all times, he, peace be upon him, would not have shown this concern. And it is not a condition that one intend the greeting; rather, two rakʿahs of an obligatory prayer, or a regular sunnah, or other than that, suffice him. And if one intends by his prayer both the greeting and the obligatory prayer, his prayer is validly contracted and both are attained for him. And if one prays over a funeral, or prostrates in gratitude, or for recitation, or prays one rakʿah with the intention of the greeting, the greeting is not attained — according to the soundest view of our school. Some of our companions said it is attained, and that contradicts the apparent meaning of the hadith. Their evidence is that the intent is to honor the mosque, and that is achieved thereby. The correct view is that it is not attained. As for the Sacred Mosque (al-Masjid al-Ḥarām), when the pilgrim first enters it, he begins with the circumambulation of arrival (ṭawāf al-qudūm), for that is its greeting, and he prays after it the two rakʿahs of the ṭawāf.

(Chapter: The Recommendation of Two Rakʿahs in the Mosque for One Who Arrives from Travel, at His First Arrival)

In it is the hadith of Jābir, who said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, bought a camel from me. When he arrived in Madīnah, he commanded me to come to the mosque and pray two rakʿahs. And in the other narration, Jābir said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, arrived before me, and I arrived and found him at the door of the mosque. He said: "Now you have come." I said: "Yes." He said: "Leave your camel, then enter and pray two rakʿahs." So I entered, prayed, then returned. And in it is the hadith of Kaʿb ibn Mālik that the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, never arrived from a journey except in the daytime during the forenoon (al-ḍuḥā). When he arrived, he would go to the mosque and pray two rakʿahs therein, then sit. In these hadiths is the recommendation of two rakʿahs for the one arriving from his journey in the mosque at his first arrival. And this prayer is intended for the arrival from travel, not that it is the greeting of the mosque. And the aforementioned hadiths are explicit regarding what I have mentioned. And in it is the recommendation of arriving at the beginning of the day. And in it is that it is recommended for a man of high rank, and one whom people seek out for greeting, when he arrives from travel, to sit at his first arrival near his dwelling in a conspicuous place, easy for his visitors — either the mosque or other than it. His statement: "Aḥmad ibn Jawwās narrated to us" — it is with an open jīm and a shaddah on the wāw, unpointed, and a sīn. His statement: "Muḥārib ibn Dithār" — with kasrah on the dāl and with the dotted thāʾ. His statement: "He owed me a debt, and he repaid me and increased me" — in it is the recommendation of repaying debt with an increase. And Allah knows best.

(Chapter: The Recommendation of the Duḥā Prayer, That Its Minimum Is Two Rakʿahs, Its Most Complete Is Eight Rakʿahs, Its Middle Is Four or Six, and the Encouragement to Persevere in It)

[717] [718] In this chapter, on the authority of ʿĀʾishah, that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, did not pray the Duḥā except when he returned from his absence, and that she never saw him, peace and blessings be upon him, pray the supererogatory Duḥā at all. She said: "And indeed I pray it, even though the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, would abandon an act while loving to perform it, fearing that the people would perform it and it would be made obligatory upon them." And in a narration from her, that he, peace and blessings be upon him, prayed the Duḥā as four rakʿahs and increased as he wished. And in a narration: "as Allah wished." And in the hadith of Umm Hāniʾ, that he, peace and blessings be upon him, prayed eight rakʿahs. And in the hadith of Abū Dharr, Abū Hurayrah, and Abū al-Dardāʾ: two rakʿahs. These hadiths are all concordant — there is no discrepancy among them for the people of verification. The sum of them is that the Duḥā is an emphasized sunnah, its minimum is two rakʿahs, its most complete is eight, and between them are four or six — both more complete than two and less than eight. As for reconciling the two hadiths of ʿĀʾishah — the negation of his praying the Duḥā and the affirmation of it — it is that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, prayed it at some times for its virtue and abandoned it at others, fearing that it would be made obligatory, as ʿĀʾishah mentioned. And her statement, "He did not pray it except when he returned from his absence," is interpreted such that its meaning is "I did not see him," just as she said in the second narration: "I never saw the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, pray the supererogatory Duḥā." The reason is that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, was not with ʿĀʾishah during the time of the Duḥā except in rare moments — for he might be traveling at that time, or present but in the mosque or another place. And when he was with his wives, he was only [with them]...

chapters.title_en: Section 347 — The Forenoon Prayer (Ṣalāt al-Ḍuḥā), Its Virtue, and Related Jurisprudential Points
chapters.arabic_text:
لها يوم من تسعة فيصح قولها ما رأيته يصليها وتكون قد علمت بخبره أو خبر

غيره أنه صلاها أو يقال قولها ما كان يصليها أي ما يداوم عليها فيكون نفيا

للمداومة لا لأصلها والله أعلم وأما ما صح عن بن عمر أنه قال في الضحى هي

بدعة فمحمول على أن صلاتها في المسجد والتظاهر بها كما كانوا يفعلونه بدعة

لا أن أصلها في البيوت ونحوها مذموم أو يقال قوله بدعة أي المواظبة عليها

لأن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لم يواظب عليها خشية أن تفرض وهذا في حقه صلى

الله عليه وسلم وقد ثبت استحباب المحافظة في حقنا بحديث أبي الدرداء وأبي

ذر أو يقال أن بن عمر لم يبلغه فعل النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم الضحى وأمره

بها وكيف كان فجمهور العلماء على استحباب الضحى وإنما نقل التوقف فيها عن

بن مسعود وبن عمر والله أعلم
# [718] قوله سبحة الضحى بضم السين أي نافلة الضحى قولها ليدع العمل وهو

يحب أن يعمل ضبطناه بفتح الياء أي يعمله وفيه بيان كمال شفقته صلى الله

عليه وسلم ورأفته بأمته وفيه أنه إذا تعارضت مصالح قدم أهمها قوله يزيد

الرشك بكسر الراء وإسكان الشين المعجمة قد تقدم بيانه مرات قوله أم هانئ هو

بهمزة بعد النون
# 
# كنيت بابنها هانئ واسمها فاختة على المشهور وقيل هند قوله سألت وحرصت هو

بفتح الراء على المشهور وبه جاء القرآن وفي لغة بكسرها قوله إن أبا مرة

مولى أم هانئ وفي رواية مولى عقيل بن أبي طالب قال العلماء هو مولى أم هانئ

حقيقة ويضاف إلى عقيل مجازا للزومه إياه وانتمائه إليه لكونه مولى أخته

قولها سلمت فيه سلام المرأة التي ليست بمحرم على الرجل بحضرة محارمه قولها

فقال من هذه قلت أم هانئ بنت  أبي طالب فيه أنه لا بأس أن يكني الإنسان نفسه

على سبيل التعريف إذا اشتهر بالكنية وفيه أنه إذا استأذن أن يقول المستأذن

عليه من هذا فيقول المستأذن فلان باسمه الذي يعرفه به المخاطب قوله صلى

الله عليه وسلم مرحبا بأم هانئ فيه استحباب قول الإنسان لزائره والوارد

عليه مرحبا ونحوه من ألفاظ الإكرام والملاطفة ومعنى مرحبا صادفت رحبا أي

سعة وسبق بسط الكلام فيه في حديث وفد عبد القيس وفيه أنه لا بأس بالكلام في

حال الاغتسال والوضوء ولا بالسلام عليه بخلاف
# 
# البائل وفيه جواز الاغتسال بحضرة امرأة من محارمه إذا كان مستور العورة

عنها وجواز تستيرها إياه بثوب ونحوه قوله فصلى ثمان ركعات ملتحفا في ثوب

واحد فيه جواز الصلاة في الثوب الواحد والالتحاف به مخالفا بين طرفيه كما

ذكره في الرواية الثانية قولها فلما انصرف قلت يا رسول الله زعم بن أمي علي

بن أبي طالب أنه قاتل رجلا أجرته فلان بن هبيرة فقال رسول الله صلى الله

عليه وسلم قد أجرنا من أجرت يا أم هانئ في هذه القطعة فوائد منها أن من قصد

إنسانا لحاجة ومطلوب فوجده مشتغلا بطهارة ونحوها لم يقطعها عليه حتى يفرغ

ثم يسأل حاجته إلا أن يخاف فوتها وقولها زعم معناه هنا ذكر أمرا لا أعتقد

موافقته فيه وإنما قالت بن أمي مع أنه بن أمها وأبيها لتأكيد الحرمة

والقرابة والمشاركة في بطن واحد وكثرة ملازمة الأم وهو موافق لقول هارون

صلى الله عليه وسلم يا بن أم لا تأخذ بلحيتي واستدل بعض أصحابنا وجمهور

العلماء بهذا الحديث على صحة أمان المرأة قالوا وتقدير الحديث حكم الشرع

صحة جواز من أجرت وقال بعضهم لا حجة فيه لأنه محتمل لهذا ومحتمل لابتداء

الأمان ومثل هذا الخلاف اختلافهم في قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم من قتل قتيلا

فله سلبه هل معناه أن هذا حكم الشرع في جميع الحروب إلى يوم القيامة أم هو

إباحة رآها الإمام في تلك المرة بعينها فإذا رآها الإمام  اليوم عمل بها

وإلا فلا وبالأول قال الشافعي وآخرون وبالثاني أبو حنيفة ومالك ويحتج

للأكثرين بأن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لم ينكر عليها الأمان ولا بين فساده

ولو كان فاسدا لبينه لئلا يغتر به وقولها فلان بن هبيرة وجاء في غير مسلم

فر إلي رجلان من أحماي وروينا في كتاب الزبير بن بكار أن فلان بن هبيرة هو

الحارث بن هشام المخزومي وقال آخرون هو عبد الله بن أبي ربيعة وفي تاريخ

مكة للأزرقي أنها أجارت رجلين أحدهما عبد الله بن أبي ربيعة بن المغيرة

والثاني الحارث بن هشام بن المغيرة وهما من بني مخزوم وهذا الذي ذكره

الأزرقي يوضح الاسمين ويجمع بين الأقوال في ذلك
# 
# قولها وذلك ضحى استدل به أصحابنا وجماهير العلماء على استحباب جعل الضحى

ثمان ركعات وتوقف فيه القاضي وغيره ومنعوا دلالته قالوا لأنها إنما أخبرت

عن وقت صلاته لا عن نيتها فلعلها كانت صلاة شكر الله تعالى على الفتح وهذا

الذي قالوه فاسد بل الصواب صحة الاستدلال به فقد ثبت عن أم هانئ أن النبي

صلى الله عليه وسلم يوم الفتح صلى سبحة الضحى ثمان ركعات يسلم من كل ركعتين

رواه أبو داود في سننه بهذا اللفظ بإسناد صحيح على شرط البخاري
# [720] قوله عن يحيى بن عقيل بضم العين قوله عن أبي الأسود الدؤلي في ضبطه

خلاف وكلام طويل سبق مبسوطا في كتاب الإيمان قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم على
