chapters.arabic_text:
الرواية الأخرى ولا قبرا مشرفا إلا سويته فيه أن السنة أن القبر لا يرفع

على الأرض رفعا كثيرا ولا يسنم بل يرفع نحو شبر ويسطح وهذا مذهب الشافعي

ومن وافقه ونقل القاضي عياض عن أكثر العلماء أن الأفضل عندهم تسنيمها وهو

مذهب مالك
# [969] قوله (أن لا تدع تمثالا إلا طمسته) فيه الأمر بتغيير صور ذوات

الأرواح قوله (عن أبي الهياج) هو بفتح الهاء وتشديد الياء واسمه
# 
# وأصحابه قاموا لجنازة فقالوا يا رسول الله إنها يهودية فقال إن الموت فزع

فإذا رأيتم الجنازة فقوموا وفي رواية قام النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وأصحابه

لجنازة يهودي حتى توارت وفي رواية قيل إنه يهودي فقال أليست نفسا وفي رواية

علي رضي الله عنه قام رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ثم قعد وفي رواية رأينا

رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قام فقمنا وقعد فقعدنا قال القاضي اختلف

الناس في هذه المسألة فقال مالك وأبو حنيفة والشافعى القيام منسوخ وقال

أحمد واسحاق وبن حبيب وبن الماجشون المالكيان هو مخير قال الشافعي في قيام

من يشيعها عند القبر فقال جماعة من الصحابة والسلف لا يقعد حتى توضع قالوا

والنسخ إنما هو  في قيام من مرت به وبهذا قال الأوزاعي وأحمد وإسحاق ومحمد

بن الحسن قال واختلفوا في القيام على القبر حتى تدفن فكره قوم وعمل به

آخرون روي ذلك عن عثمان وعلى وبن عمر وغيرهم رضي الله عنهم هذا كلام القاضي

والمشهور في مذهبنا أن القيام ليس مستحبا وقالوا هو منسوخ بحديث علي واختار
# 
# ولا قبرا مشرفا إلا سويته قوله (عن بسر بن عبيد الله) هو بضم الباء

وبالسين المهملة قوله
# [972] (عن أبي مرثد) هو بالمثلثة واسمه كناز بفتح الكاف وتشديد النون

وآخره زاي قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (لا تجلسوا على القبور ولا تصلوا إليها)

فيه تصريح بالنهى عن الصلاة إلى القبر قال الشافعي رحمه الله وأكره أن يعظم

مخلوق حتى يجعل قبره مسجدا مخافة الفتنة عليه وعلى من بعده من الناس
# [973] قولها (ما صلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم على سهيل بن بيضاء إلا

في
# 
# المسجد) وفي الرواية الأخرى (والله لقد صلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

على ابني بيضاء في المسجد) وفي الرواية الأخرى (والله لقد صلى رسول الله

صلى الله عليه وسلم على ابني بيضاء في المسجد سهيل وأخيه) قال العلماء بنو

بيضاء ثلاثة إخوة سهل وسهيل وصفوان وأمهم البيضاء اسمها دعد والبيضاء وصف

وأبوهم وهب بن ربيعة القرشي الفهري وكان سهيل قديم الإسلام
# 
# هاجر إلى الحبشة ثم عاد إلى مكة ثم هاجر إلى المدينة وشهد بدرا وغيرها

توفي سنة تسع من الهجرة رضي الله عنه وفي هذا الحديث دليل للشافعي

والأكثرين في جواز الصلاة على الميت في المسجد وممن قال به أحمد واسحاق قال

بن عبد البر ورواه المدنيون في الموطأ عن مالك وبه قال بن حبيب المالكى

وقال بن أبي ذئب وأبو حنيفة ومالك على المشهور عنه لا تصح الصلاة عليه في

المسجد بحديث في سنن أبي داود من صلى على جنازة في المسجد فلا شيء له ودليل

الشافعي والجمهور حديث سهيل بن بيضاء وأجابوا عن حديث سنن أبي داود بأجوبة

أحدها أنه  ضعيف لا يصح الاحتجاج به قال أحمد بن حنبل هذا حديث ضعيف تفرد به

صالح مولى التوأمة وهو ضعيف والثاني أن الذي في النسخ المشهورة المحققة

المسموعة من سنن أبي داود ومن صلى على جنازة في المسجد فلا شيء عليه ولا

حجة لهم حينئذ فيه الثالث أنه لو ثبت الحديث وثبت أنه قال فلا شيء لوجب

تأويله على فلا شيء عليه ليجمع بين الروايتين وبين هذا الحديث وحديث سهيل

بن بيضاء وقد جاء له بمعنى عليه كقوله تعالى وان أسأتم فلها الرابع أنه

محمول على نقص الأجر في حق من صلى في المسجد ورجع ولم يشيعها الىالمقبرة

لما فاته من تشييعه إلى المقبرة وحضور دفنه والله أعلم وفي حديث سهيل هذا

دليل لطهارة الآدمي الميت وهو الصحيح في مذهبنا قوله (وحدثني هارون بن عبد

الله ومحمد بن رافع قالا حدثنا بن أبي فديك أخبرنا الضحاك يعنى بن عثمان عن

أبي النضر عن أبي سلمة عن عائشة) هذا الحديث مما استدركه الدارقطني على

مسلم وقال خالف الضحاك حافظان مالك والماجشون فرواه عن أبي النضر عن عائشة

مرسلا وقيل عن الضحاك عن أبي النضر عن أبي بكر بن عبد الرحمن ولا يصح إلا

مرسلا هذا كلام الدارقطني وقد سبق الجواب عن مثل هذا الاستدراك في الفصول

السابقة في مقدمة هذا الشرح في مواضع منه وهو أن هذه الزيادة التي زادها

الضحاك زيادة
# 
# ثقة وهي مقبولة لأنه حفظ ما نسيه غيره فلا تقدح فيه والله أعلم
# [974] قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (السلام عليكم دار قوم مؤمنين) دار منصوب

على النداء أي يا أهل دار فحذف المضاف وأقام المضاف إليه مقامه وقيل منصوب

على الاختصاص قال صاحب المطالع ويجوز جره على البدل من الضمير في عليكم قال

الخطابي وفيه أن اسم الدار يقع على المقابر قال وهو صحيح فإن الدار في

اللغة يقع على الربع المسكون وعلى الخراب غير المأهول وأنشد فيه وقوله صلى
chapters.anchors:
- Root: س و ي (s-w-y)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To make level, equalize, straighten; removing protrusion or elevation.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In sacred law, signifies restoring the grave to a state of non-veneration, stripping it of markers of worldly honor.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) in physical levelling; metaphorical (majāz) in erasing signs of pre-Islamic exaltation.
- Root: ق ب ر (q-b-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Burial place; the hollow dug for interment.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): A site of transition (barzakh) between worldly abode and the Hereafter; hence rulings on its construction carry eschatological weight.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for the physical grave; metaphorical for the state of death itself.
- Root: ج ل س (j-l-s)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To sit, to remain seated.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In funerary context, denotes cessation of the standing obligation; linked to abrogation (naskh) analysis.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal posture; metaphorical for relinquishing a previously commanded act.
- Sībawayh Rule: Rule of Apposition (al-Badal) and Ellipsis of the Muḍāf (Ḥadhf al-Muḍāf) — In «السلام عليكم دار قوم مؤمنين», the noun «دار» is accusative as vocative with the muḍāf omitted, i.e., 'O people of the abode'; alternatively, it may be genitive as a badal of the pronoun in «عليكم».
chapters.translation:
I say: The other narration states: "Nor any elevated grave except that I levelled it." In it is [the ruling] that the Sunnah is that the grave is not raised high above the ground with a great elevation, nor is it made hump-backed (musannam); rather, it is raised about a handspan and made flat (musaṭṭaḥ). This is the school of al-Shāfiʿī and those who concur with him. Al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ transmitted from the majority of scholars that the superior practice in their view is to make it hump-backed (tasnīm), and this is the school of Mālik.

# [969] His saying (that you leave no image except that you efface it): In it is the command to alter the forms of beings possessing souls.

His saying (from Abū al-Hayyāj): It is with the opening of the hāʾ and the doubling of the yāʾ, and his name is...

And his companions stood for a funeral procession and said: "O Messenger of Allah, she is a Jewess." He said: "Death is a fright; when you see a funeral procession, stand." In another narration: The Prophet ﷺ and his companions stood for the funeral of a Jew until it disappeared from view. In another narration: It was said that he was a Jew, and he said: "Is it not a soul?" In another narration from ʿAlī (may Allah be pleased with him): The Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood, then sat. In another narration: We saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stand, so we stood; and he sat, so we sat.

Al-Qāḍī said: The people differed on this question. Mālik, Abū Ḥanīfah, and al-Shāfiʿī said the standing is abrogated (mansūkh). Aḥmad, Isḥāq, Ibn Ḥabīb, and Ibn al-Mājishūn — both Mālikīs — said he has the choice. Al-Shāfiʿī said regarding standing for one who accompanies the funeral to the grave: A group of the Companions and the Successors said one does not sit until it is placed [in the grave]. They said: The abrogation applies only to standing for one who passes by. This was also the view of al-Awzāʿī, Aḥmad, Isḥāq, and Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan.

He said: And they differed regarding standing at the grave until burial; some disapproved of it, and others acted upon it. That was narrated from ʿUthmān, ʿAlī, Ibn ʿUmar, and others (may Allah be pleased with them all). This is the speech of al-Qāḍī. The well-known view in our school is that standing is not recommended (mustaḥabb), and they said it is abrogated by the ḥadīth of ʿAlī. And he chose...

# Nor any elevated grave except that I levelled it. His saying (from Busr ibn ʿUbayd Allāh): It is with the ḍammah on the bāʾ and with the unpointed sīn.

# [972] (From Abū Marthad): It is with the thāʾ, and his name is Kanāz — with the fatḥah on the kāf, the doubled nūn, and its final letter is zāy. His saying ﷺ: "Do not sit upon graves, nor pray towards them." In it is an explicit prohibition of praying towards the grave. Al-Shāfiʿī (may Allah have mercy on him) said: I disapprove that any creature be venerated to the extent that his grave is made a mosque, out of fear of tribulation upon him and upon those after him among the people.

# [973] Her saying: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not pray over Suhayl ibn Bayḍāʾ except in the mosque." In the other narration: "By Allah, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed over the two sons of Bayḍāʾ in the mosque." In yet another narration: "By Allah, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed over the two sons of Bayḍāʾ in the mosque — Suhayl and his brother."

The scholars said: The Banū Bayḍāʾ were three brothers: Sahl, Suhayl, and Ṣafwān. Their mother was al-Bayḍāʾ, whose name was Daʿd; al-Bayḍāʾ is an epithet. Their father was Wahb ibn Rabīʿah al-Qurashī al-Fihrī. Suhayl was an early Muslim; he migrated to Abyssinia, then returned to Mecca, then migrated to Medina, and witnessed Badr and other [battles]. He died in the year nine of the Hijrah (may Allah be pleased with him).

In this ḥadīth is evidence for al-Shāfiʿī and the majority regarding the permissibility of praying over the deceased in the mosque. Among those who held this view are Aḥmad and Isḥāq. Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr said: The Medinese narrated it in the Muwaṭṭaʾ from Mālik, and Ibn Ḥabīb al-Mālikī held it. Ibn Abī Dhiʾb, Abū Ḥanīfah, and Mālik — according to the well-known view from him — said the prayer over him in the mosque is not valid, citing the ḥadīth in the Sunan of Abū Dāwūd: "Whoever prays over a funeral in the mosque, there is nothing for him."

The evidence of al-Shāfiʿī and the majority is the ḥadīth of Suhayl ibn Bayḍāʾ. They answered the ḥadīth of the Sunan of Abū Dāwūd with several responses:

First: It is weak (ḍaʿīf) and cannot be cited as proof. Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal said: This is a weak ḥadīth; it is exclusively transmitted by Ṣāliḥ, the freed slave of al-Tawʾamah, and he is weak.

Second: What appears in the well-known, verified, and heard copies of the Sunan of Abū Dāwūd is: "Whoever prays over a funeral in the mosque, there is nothing against him (fa-lā shayʾa ʿalayhi)." Thus there is no argument for them in it.

Third: Even if the ḥadīth were established and it were established that he said "there is nothing for him (fa-lā shayʾa lahu)," it would be obligatory to interpret it as meaning "there is nothing against him (fa-lā shayʾa ʿalayhi)" in order to reconcile the two narrations, and between this ḥadīth and the ḥadīth of Suhayl ibn Bayḍāʾ. And this meaning has come for it, as in His saying (Exalted is He): {وَإِنْ أَسَأْتُمْ فَلَهَا} — "And if you do evil, then it is against it" (Quran 17:7).

Fourth: It is carried upon the deficiency of reward for one who prays in the mosque and then returns without accompanying the funeral to the cemetery, due to what he missed of accompanying it to the cemetery and attending its burial. And Allah knows best.

In this ḥadīth of Suhayl is also evidence for the purity (ṭahārah) of the deceased human being — and this is the correct view in our school.

His saying: "And Hārūn ibn ʿAbd Allāh and Muḥammad ibn Rāfiʿ narrated to me; they said: Ibn Abī Fudayk narrated to us; al-Ḍaḥḥāk — meaning Ibn ʿUthmān — informed us, from Abū al-Naḍr, from Abū Salamah, from ʿĀʾishah." This ḥadīth is among those that al-Dāraquṭnī criticized against Muslim, saying: Two memorizers (ḥāfiẓān) — Mālik and al-Mājishūn — contradicted al-Ḍaḥḥāk, narrating it from Abū al-Naḍr from ʿĀʾishah as disconnected (mursal). And it was said: From al-Ḍaḥḥāk, from Abū al-Naḍr, from Abū Bakr ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān; and it is not authentic except as mursal. This is the speech of al-Dāraquṭnī.

The response to such criticism has already preceded in the earlier chapters of the introduction to this commentary, in several places therein: namely, that this addition (ziyādah) which al-Ḍaḥḥāk added is an addition of a trustworthy narrator, and it is accepted, because he preserved what others forgot. Thus it does not impugn him. And Allah knows best.

# [974] His saying ﷺ: "Peace be upon you, O abode of believing people (al-salāmu ʿalaykum dāra qawmin muʾminīn)." «Dār» is accusative as a vocative, i.e., "O people of the abode" — the muḍāf (the word "people") is omitted, and the muḍāf ilayh (the word "abode") is placed in its position. And it was said it is accusative as specification (ikhtiṣāṣ). The author of al-Maṭāliʿ said: It is permissible to make it genitive as a badal (apposition) of the pronoun in «ʿalaykum».

Al-Khaṭṭābī said: In it is [evidence] that the term "abode" (dār) applies to graveyards. He said: And this is correct, for in the language, "dār" applies both to an inhabited dwelling and to ruined, uninhabited land. And he cited poetry for it. And his saying ﷺ...

chapters.title_en: Section 409 — Visiting Graves, Supplication for the Deceased, and the Prophet's Night Visit to al-Baqīʿ
chapters.arabic_text:
الله عليه وسلم (وإنا إن شاء الله بكم لاحقون) التقييد  بالمشيئة على سبيل

التبرك وامتثال قول الله تعالى ولا تقولن لشيء إني فاعل ذلك غدا الا أن

يشاء الله وقيل المشيئة عائدة إلى تلك التربة بعينها وقيل غير ذلك وفي هذا

الحديث دليل لاستحباب زيارة القبور والسلام على أهلها والدعاء لهم والترحم

عليهم قولها (يخرج من آخر الليل إلى البقيع) فيه فضيلة زيارة قبور البقيع

قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم السلام عليكم دار قوم مؤمنين قال الخطابي وغيره

فيه أن السلام على الأموات والأحياء سواء في تقديم السلام على عليكم بخلاف

ما كانت عليه الجاهلية من قولهم ... عليك سلام الله قيس بن عاصم ... ورحمته

ما شاء أن يترحما ...

| (قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (اللهم اغفر لأهل بقيع 
# الغرقد) البقيع هنا بالباء بلا خلاف وهو مدفن أهل المدينة سمي بقيع

الغرقد لغرقد كان فيه وهو ما عظم من العوسج وفيه إطلاق لفظ الأهل على ساكن

المكان من حي وميت قوله (حدثنا هارون بن سعيد الأيلي حدثنا عبد الله بن وهب

أخبرنا بن جريج عن عبد الله بن كثير بن المطلب أنه سمع محمد بن قيس يقول

سمعت)
# 
# عائشة تحدث فقالت ألا أحدثكم عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وعني قلنا بلى

ح وحدثني من سمع حجاجا الأعور واللفظ له قال حدثنا حجاج بن محمد عن بن جريج

أخبرني عبد الله رجل من قريش عن محمد بن قيس بن مخرمة بن المطلب أنه قال

يوما ألا أحدثكم عني وعن أمي) إلى آخره قال القاضي هكذا وقع في مسلم في

إسناد حديث حجاج عن بن جريج أخبرني عبد الله رجل من قريش وكذا رواه أحمد بن

حنبل وقال النسائي وأبو نعيم الجرجاني وأبو بكر النيسابوري وأبو عبد الله

الجرجاني كلهم عن يوسف بن سعيد المصيصى حدثنا حجاج عن بن جريج أخبرني عبد

الله بن أبي ملكية وقال الدارقطني هو عبد الله بن كثير بن المطلب بن أبي

وداعة قال أبو علي الغساني الجياني هذا الحديث أحد الأحاديث المقطوعة في

مسلم قال وهو أيضا  من الأحاديث التي وهم في رواتها وقد رواه عبد الرزاق في

مصنفه عن بن جريج قال أخبرني محمد بن قيس بن مخرمة أنه سمع عائشة قال

القاضي قوله إن هذا مقطوع لا يوافق عليه بل هو مسند وإنما لم يسم رواته فهو

من باب المجهول لا من باب المنقطع إذ المنقطع ما سقط من رواته راو قبل

التابعى قال القاضي ووقع في سنده إشكال آخر وهو أن قول مسلم وحدثني من سمع

حجاجا الأعور واللفظ له قال حدثنا حجاج بن محمد يوهم أن حجاجا الأعور حدث

به عن آخر يقال له حجاج بن محمد وليس كذا بل حجاج الأعور هو حجاج بن محمد

بلا شك وتقدير كلام مسلم حدثني من سمع حجاجا الأعور قال هذا المحدث حدثني

حجاج بن محمد فحكى لفظ المحدث هذا كلام القاضي قلت ولا يقدح رواية مسلم

لهذا الحديث عن هذا المجهول الذي سمعه منه عن حجاج
# 
# الأعور لأن مسلما ذكره متابعة لا متأصلا معتمدا عليه بل الاعتماد على

الإسناد الصحيح قبله قولها (فلم يلبث إلا ريثما) هو بفتح الراء وإسكان

الياء وبعدها ثاء مثلثة أي قدرما قولها (فأخذ رداءه رويدا) أي قليلا لطيفا

لئلا ينبهها قولها (ثم أجافه) بالجيم أي أغلقه وإنما فعل ذلك صلى الله عليه

وسلم في خفية لئلا يوقظها ويخرج عنها فربما لحقها وحشة في انفرادها في ظلمة

الليل قولها (وتقنعت إزاري) هكذا هو في الأصول إزاري بغير باء في أوله

وكأنه بمعنى لبست إزاري فلهذا عدي بنفسه قولها (جاء البقيع فأطال القيام ثم

رفع يديه ثلاث مرات) فيه استحباب إطالة الدعاء وتكريره ورفع اليدين فيه

وفيه أن دعاء القائم أكمل من دعاء الجالس في القبور قولها (فأحضر فأحضرت)

الاحضار العدو قولها (فقال مالك يا عائش حشيا رابية) يجوز في عائش فتح

الشين وضمها وهما وجهان جاريان في كل المرخمات وفيه جواز ترخيم الاسم إذا

لم يكن فيه إيذاء للمرخم وحشيا بفتح الحاء المهملة وإسكان الشين المعجمة

مقصور معناه وقد وقع عليك  الحشا وهو الربو والتهيج الذي يعرض للمسرع في

مشيه والمحتد في كلامه من ارتفاع النفس وتواتره يقال امرأة حشياء وحشية

ورجل حشيان وحشش قيل أصله من أصاب الربو حشاه وقوله رابية أي مرتفعة البطن

قولها (لا بي شيء) وقع في بعض الأصول لا بي شيء بباء الجر وفي بعضها لأي

شيء بتشديد الياء وحذف الباء على الاستفهام وفي بعضها لا شيء وحكاها القاضي

قال وهذا الثالث
# 
# أصوبها قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (فأنت السواد) أي الشخص قولها (فلهدني)

هو بفتح الهاء والدال المهملة وروي فلهزني بالزاي وهما متقاربان قال أهل

اللغة لهده ولهده بتخفيف الهاء وتشديدها أي دفعه ويقال لهزه إذا ضربه بجمع

كفه في صدره ويقرب منهما لكزه ووكزه قوله (قالت مهما يكتم الناس يعلمه الله

نعم) هكذا هو في الأصول وهو صحيح وكأنها لما قالت مهما يكتم الناس يعلمه

الله صدقت نفسها فقالت نعم قولها (قلت كيف أقول يا رسول الله قال قولي

السلام على أهل الديار من المؤمنين والمسلمين ويرحم الله المستقدمين منكم

ومنا والمستأخرين وإنا إن شاء الله تعالى بكم للاحقون) فيه استحباب هذا
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ق-ب-ر (q-b-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: The place of burial; a grave as the final earthly abode of the body.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The grave as a station of transition (barzakh) between this world and the Hereafter; visiting it (ziyārah) is an act of remembrance of death and the afterlife.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) — the physical site of burial; metaphorical (majāz) — the state of the dead and the lesson of mortality.
- Root: س-ل-م (s-l-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Safety, peace, salutation; the greeting of peace as a mark of security.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The greeting of peace (salām) as a supplication for divine protection and well-being, extended to both living and dead.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — verbal greeting; metaphorical — the transfer of peace and mercy upon the addressed, whether present or absent.
- Root: د-ع-و (d-ʿ-w)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To call, invoke, summon; supplication as a direct appeal to God.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Duʿāʾ as an act of worship (ʿibādah) and a means of seeking intercession for the deceased.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — calling upon God; metaphorical — the raising of hands and prolonged standing as embodied forms of earnest invocation.
- Sībawayh Rule: Rule of Taqdīr (Ellipsis/Supposition) — In the phrase «وإنا إن شاء الله بكم لاحقون», the conditional clause with «إن شاء الله» is governed by the principle of taʿlīq (suspension), where the fulfillment of the statement is suspended upon divine will, requiring the listener to supply the implied condition (i.e., "if God wills, we shall join you").
chapters.translation:
I say: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "And we, God willing, shall be joining you." The restriction by the phrase "God willing" is by way of seeking blessing (tabarruk) and in compliance with the saying of God the Exalted: {«وَلَا تَقُولَنَّ لِشَيْءٍ إِنِّي فَاعِلٌ ذَٰلِكَ غَدًا إِلَّا أَن يَشَاءَ اللَّهُ»} ("And do not say of anything, 'Indeed, I will do that tomorrow,' except [adding], 'If God wills'") [Quran 18:23-24]. And it was said: the "willing" refers to that very soil (i.e., the specific grave of the Prophet in al-Baqīʿ). And it was said otherwise. In this hadith there is evidence for the recommendation (istihbāb) of visiting graves, greeting their inhabitants, supplicating for them, and seeking mercy upon them.

His saying, peace and blessings be upon him: "He went out at the end of the night to al-Baqīʿ" — in this is the virtue of visiting the graves of al-Baqīʿ.

His saying, peace and blessings be upon him: "Peace be upon you, O abode of believing people" — al-Khaṭṭābī and others said: In this is [the principle] that the greeting of peace upon the dead and the living is the same in the precedence of "peace" over "upon you" (i.e., saying "al-salāmu ʿalaykum" rather than "ʿalayka salām"), contrary to what the pre-Islamic era (Jāhiliyyah) practiced in their saying: "Upon you be the peace of God" — as said by Qays ibn ʿĀṣim... and His mercy, as much as He willed to have mercy...

| His saying, peace and blessings be upon him: "O God, forgive the people of Baqīʿ al-Gharqad" — "al-Baqīʿ" here is with the letter bāʾ, without dispute, and it is the burial ground of the people of Medina. It was named "Baqīʿ al-Gharqad" because of a gharqad (a large box-thorn tree) that was in it, and gharqad is what is large of the ʿawsaj (a thorny shrub). In this [phrase] is the usage of the word "people" (ahl) for the inhabitants of a place, whether living or dead.

His saying: "Hārūn ibn Saʿīd al-Aylī narrated to us, ʿAbdullāh ibn Wahb narrated to us, Ibn Jurayj informed us, from ʿAbdullāh ibn Kathīr ibn al-Muṭṭalib, that he heard Muḥammad ibn Qays saying: I heard ʿĀʾishah narrating and saying: 'Shall I not narrate to you about the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and about myself?' We said: 'Yes.'"

And [another chain]: "And one who heard Ḥajjāj al-Aʿwar narrated to me, and the wording is his, saying: Ḥajjāj ibn Muḥammad narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, ʿAbdullāh, a man from Quraysh, informed me, from Muḥammad ibn Qays ibn Makhramah ibn al-Muṭṭalib, that he said one day: 'Shall I not narrate to you about myself and my mother?'" — to the end of it.

Al-Qāḍī said: Thus it occurred in Muslim in the chain of the hadith of Ḥajjāj, from Ibn Jurayj: "ʿAbdullāh, a man from Quraysh, informed me." And likewise Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal narrated it. And al-Nasāʾī, Abū Nuʿaym al-Jurjānī, Abū Bakr al-Naysābūrī, and Abū ʿAbdullāh al-Jurjānī — all of them from Yūsuf ibn Saʿīd al-Miṣṣīṣī — narrated: "Ḥajjāj narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj: ʿAbdullāh ibn Abī Mulaykah informed me." And al-Dāraquṭnī said: "He is ʿAbdullāh ibn Kathīr ibn al-Muṭṭalib ibn Abī Wadāʿah."

Abū ʿAlī al-Ghassānī al-Jayyānī said: This hadith is one of the disconnected (maqṭūʿ) hadiths in Muslim. He also said: It is among the hadiths in which he erred regarding its narrators. And ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated it in his Muṣannaf from Ibn Jurayj, saying: "Muḥammad ibn Qays ibn Makhramah informed me that he heard ʿĀʾishah."

Al-Qāḍī said: His saying that this is disconnected (maqṭūʿ) is not agreed upon; rather, it is connected (musnad). The only issue is that its narrators were not named, so it falls under the category of the unknown (majhūl), not the category of the disconnected (munqaṭiʿ), for the disconnected is that from whose chain a narrator before the Successor (tābiʿī) has fallen.

Al-Qāḍī said: And in its chain another problem occurred, namely that Muslim's saying: "And one who heard Ḥajjāj al-Aʿwar narrated to me, and the wording is his, saying: Ḥajjāj ibn Muḥammad narrated to us" — suggests that Ḥajjāj al-Aʿwar narrated it from another person called Ḥajjāj ibn Muḥammad. But this is not so; rather, Ḥajjāj al-Aʿwar is Ḥajjāj ibn Muḥammad without doubt. And the estimation (taqdīr) of Muslim's speech is: "One who heard Ḥajjāj al-Aʿwar narrated to me, saying: This narrator said: Ḥajjāj ibn Muḥammad narrated to us" — thus he reported the wording of this narrator. This is the speech of al-Qāḍī.

I say: And Muslim's narration of this hadith from this unknown person whom he heard from, from Ḥajjāj al-Aʿwar, does not harm [the hadith's validity], because Muslim mentioned it as a corroboration (mutābaʿah), not as a primary relied-upon chain; rather, the reliance is upon the sound chain before it.

Her saying: "And he did not stay except as long as (riythamā)" — it is with the opening of the rāʾ and the stillness of the yāʾ, and after it a thāʾ with three dots (i.e., thāʾ), meaning "as much as" (qadr mā).

Her saying: "So he took his cloak slowly (ruwaydā)" — meaning a little, gently, so as not to wake her.

Her saying: "Then he closed it (ajāfahu)" — with the jīm, meaning he shut it. And the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, did this in secrecy so as not to wake her and leave her, for perhaps loneliness would befall her in her solitude in the darkness of the night.

Her saying: "And I wrapped myself in my waist-wrapper (taqannaʿtu izārī)" — thus it is in the manuscripts: "izārī" without a bāʾ at its beginning. And it is as if it means "I wore my waist-wrapper," and for this reason it is transitive by itself.

Her saying: "He came to al-Baqīʿ and prolonged the standing, then raised his hands three times" — in this is the recommendation of prolonging supplication, repeating it, and raising the hands therein. And in it is that the supplication of the standing person is more complete than the supplication of the sitting person at graves.

Her saying: "So he hastened (fa-aḥḍara) and I hastened (fa-aḥḍartu)" — "al-iḥḍār" means the enemy (i.e., the hastening of the enemy's approach).

Her saying: "So he said: 'What is the matter with you, O ʿĀʾish (ʿĀʾish)? — breathless (ḥashyā) with a heaving belly (rābiyah)'" — It is permissible in "ʿĀʾish" to open the shīn or to double it (i.e., ʿĀʾishah shortened), and these are two permissible forms in all truncated (murakhkham) names. And in this is the permissibility of truncating a name (tarkhīm) when there is no harm to the one truncated. "Ḥashyā" — with the opening of the ḥāʾ (unpointed) and the stillness of the shīn (pointed), and it is shortened (maqṣūr) — meaning: the breathlessness (ḥashā) has befallen you, which is the panting and agitation that occurs to one who hastens in his walking and is heated in his speech, from the rising of the breath and its repetition. It is said: "a woman ḥashyāʾ and ḥashiyah" (breathless), and "a man ḥashyān and ḥashish." It was said: its origin is from "the breathlessness (rabw) has afflicted his innards (ḥashāhu)." And his saying "rābiyah" means elevated in the belly.

Her saying: "Not by anything (lā bī shayʾ)" — It occurred in some manuscripts as "lā bī shayʾ" with the preposition bāʾ, and in some as "li-ayyi shayʾ" (for what thing?) with the doubling of the yāʾ and the omission of the bāʾ, as an interrogative, and in some as "lā shayʾ" (nothing). Al-Qāḍī reported these, and he said: This third one is the most correct of them.

His saying, peace and blessings be upon him: "Then you are the blackness (al-sawād)" — meaning the person (al-shakhṣ).

Her saying: "So he pushed me (falahadani)" — it is with the opening of the hāʾ and the dāl (unpointed), and it was narrated "falahazani" with the zāy, and they are close in meaning. The people of language said: "lahadahu" and "lahhadahu" — with the lightening and doubling of the hāʾ — meaning he pushed him. And it is said: "lahazahu" when he strikes him with the palm of his hand in his chest. And close to them are "lakazahu" and "wakazahu" (to poke or jab).

His saying: "She said: 'Whatever people conceal, God knows it — yes (naʿam)'" — Thus it is in the manuscripts, and it is correct. And it is as if she, when she said "Whatever people conceal, God knows it," affirmed the truth to herself, so she said "yes."

Her saying: "I said: 'How shall I say, O Messenger of God?' He said: 'Say: Peace be upon the inhabitants of the abodes from among the believers and the Muslims, and may God have mercy on those who have gone ahead from you and from us, and those who come later, and we, God the Exalted willing, shall be joining you.'" — In this is the recommendation of this [supplication].

chapters.title_en: The Utterance for Visitors of Graves, with a Preponderance for the View that "Peace Be Upon You, O People of a Believing Abode" Means "O Inhabitants of a Believing Abode"; and the Ruling on Praying over the Suicide
chapters.arabic_text:
القول لزائر القبور وفيه ترجيح لقول من قال في قوله سلام عليكم دار قوم

مؤمنين أن معناه أهل دار قوم مؤمنين وفيه أن المسلم والمؤمن قد يكونان

بمعنى واحد وعطف أحدهما على الآخر لاختلاف اللفظ وهو بمعنى قوله تعالى

فأخرجنا من كان فيها من المؤمنين فما وجدنا فيها غير بيت من المسلمين ولا

يجوز أن يكون المراد بالمسلم في هذا الحديث غير المؤمن لأن المؤمن إن كان

منافقا لا يجوز السلام عليه
# 
# والترحم وفيه دليل لمن جوز للنساء زيارة القبور وفيها خلاف للعلماء وهي

ثلاثة أوجه لأصحابنا أحدها تحريمها عليهن لحديث لعن الله زوارات القبور

والثاني يكره والثالث يباح ويستدل له بهذا الحديث وبحديث كنت نهيتكم عن

زيارة القبور فزوروها ويجاب عن هذا بأن نهيتكم ضمير ذكور فلا يدخل فيه

النساء على المذهب الصحيح المختار في الأصول والله أعلم قوله صلى الله  عليه

وسلم (استأذنت ربي أن أستغفر لأمي فلم يأذن لي واستأذنته أن أزور قبرها

فأذن لي) فيه جواز زيارة المشركين في الحياة وقبورهم بعد الوفاة لأنه إذا

جازت زيارتهم بعد الوفاة ففي الحياة أولى وقد قال الله تعالى وصاحبهما في

الدنيا معروفا وفيه النهي عن الاستغفار للكفار قال القاضي عياض رحمه الله

سبب زيارته صلى الله عليه وسلم قبرها أنه قصد قوة الموعظة والذكرى بمشاهدة

قبرها ويؤيده قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم في آخر الحديث فزوروا القبور فإنها

تذكركم الموت
# [975] قوله (حدثنا أبو بكر بن أبي شيبة وزهير بن حرب قالا حدثنا محمد بن

عبيد عن يزيد بن كيسان عن أبي حازم عن أبي هريرة قال زار النبي صلى الله

عليه وسلم
# 
# قبر أمه فبكى وأبكى من حوله فقال استأذنت ربي في أن أستغفر لها فلم يؤذن

لي واستأذنته في أن أزور قبرها فأذن لي فزوروا القبور فإنها تذكركم الموت)

هذا الحديث وجد في رواية أبي العلاء بن ماهان لأهل المغرب ولم يوجد في

روايات بلادنا من جهة عبد الغافر الفارسي ولكنه يوجد في كثير من الأصول في

آخر كتاب الجنائز ويصيب عليه وربما كتب في الحاشية رواه أبو داود في سننه

عن محمد بن سليمان الأنباري عن محمد بن عبيد بهذا الإسناد ورواه النسائي عن

قتيبة عن محمد بن عبيد ورواه بن ماجه عن أبي بكر بن أبي شيبة عن محمد بن

عبيد وهؤلاء كلهم ثقات فهو حديث صحيح بلا شك قوله (فبكى وأبكى من حوله) قال

القاضي بكاؤه صلى الله عليه وسلم على ما فاتها من إدراك أيامه والإيمان به
# [977] قوله (محارب بن دثار) هو بكسر الدال وتخفيف المثلثة قوله صلى الله

عليه وسلم (كنت نهيتكم عن زيارة القبور فزوروها) هذا من الأحاديث التي تجمع

الناسخ والمنسوخ وهو صريح في نسخ نهي الرجال عن زيارتها وأجمعوا على أن

زيارتها
# 
# سنة لهم وأما النساء ففيهن خلاف لأصحابنا قدمناه وقدمنا أن من منعهن قال

النساء لا يدخلن في خطاب الرجال  وهو الصحيح عند الأصوليين وأما الانتباذ في

الأسقية فسبق بيانه في كتاب الإيمان في حديث وفد عبد القيس وستأتي بقيته في

كتاب الأشربة إن شاء الله تعالى وأما الأضاحي فسيأتي إيضاحها في بابها إن

شاء الله تعالى
# [978] قوله (أتى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم برجل قتل نفسه بمشاقص فلم يصل

عليه) المشاقص سهام عراض واحدها مشقص بكسر الميم وفتح القاف وفي هذا الحديث

دليل لمن يقول لا يصلى على قاتل نفسه لعصيانه وهذا مذهب عمر بن عبد العزيز

والأوزاعي وقال الحسن والنخعي وقتادة ومالك وأبو حنيفة والشافعي وجماهير

العلماء يصلى عليه وأجابوا عن هذا الحديث بأن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لم

يصل عليه بنفسه زجرا للناس عن مثل فعله وصلت عليه الصحابة وهذا كما ترك

النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم الصلاة في أول الأمر على من عليه دين زجرا لهم عن

التساهل في الاستدانة وعن إهمال وفائه وأمر أصحابه بالصلاة عليه فقال صلى

الله عليه وسلم صلوا على صاحبكم قال القاضي مذهب العلماء كافة الصلاة على

كل مسلم ومحدود ومرجوم وقاتل نفسه وولد الزنى وعن مالك وغيره أن الإمام

يجتنب الصلاة على مقتول في حد وأن أهل الفضل لا يصلون على الفساق زجرا لهم

وعن الزهري لا يصلى على
# 
# مرجوم ويصلى على المقتول في قصاص وقال أبو حنيفة لا يصلى على محارب ولا

على قتيل الفئة الباغية وقال قتادة لا يصلى على ولد الزنى وعن الحسن لا

يصلى على النفساء تموت من زنا ولا على ولدها ومنع بعض السلف الصلاة على

الطفل الصغير واختلفوا في الصلاة على السقط فقال بها فقهاء المحدثين وبعض

السلف إذا مضى عليه أربعة أشهر ومنعها جمهور الفقهاء حتى يستهل وتعرف حياته

بغير ذلك وأما الشهيد المقتول في حرب الكفار فقال مالك والشافعي والجمهور

لا يغسل ولا يصلى عليه وقال أبو حنيفة يغسل ولا يصلى عليه وعن الحسن يغسل

ويصلى عليه والله أعلم

| (كتاب الزكاة هي في اللغة النماء والتطهير فالمال 
# ينمى بها من حيث  لا يرى وهي مطهرة لمؤديها من الذنوب وقيل ينمى أجرها عند

الله تعالى وسميت في الشرع زكاة لوجود المعنى اللغوي فيها وقيل لأنها تزكي
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ز-و-ر (z-w-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning is "to incline" or "to turn aside" (māla), hence "visiting" (ziyārah) as an act of turning toward someone or something; also denotes "intention" (niyyah) in some usages.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological context, ziyārah of graves is an act of remembrance (tadhkirah) of the Hereafter, aligning with the Quranic purpose of moral reflection; it is not mere social custom but a devotional act.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) sense is physical visitation; metaphorical (majāz) sense is the soul's inclination toward the deceased or toward divine contemplation.
- Root: س-ل-م (s-l-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Root denotes safety, peace, and freedom from harm (salāmah); the greeting "salām" is a prayer for the addressee's well-being.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In Kalām, salām is a divine attribute and a greeting of the inhabitants of Paradise; here it functions as a supplication (duʿā') for the deceased believers.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal greeting of peace; metaphorically, it signifies the speaker's acknowledgment of the addressee's state of faith and security from punishment.
- Root: ق-ب-ر (q-b-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning is "to bury" (dafana); the grave (qabr) is the place of interment, a locus of transition.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The grave is a station (marḥalah) of the afterlife (ākhirah), a reminder of death (tadhkīr al-mawt), and a site for moral exhortation.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal physical grave; metaphorically, it symbolizes the brevity of worldly life and the inevitability of the Hereafter.
- Sībawayh Rule: Rule of ʿAṭf (Coordination) — When two terms (e.g., "Muslim" and "believer") are conjoined by "wa," they may share one referent if the distinction is purely lexical (ikhtilāf al-lafẓ), as in the Quranic verse cited; this is a case of synonymous coordination for rhetorical emphasis, not necessarily implying distinct categories.
chapters.translation:
I say: This section contains a preponderance for the view of those who hold that in his saying, "Peace be upon you, O people of a believing abode" (salāmun ʿalaykum dāra qawmin muʾminīn), the meaning is "O inhabitants of a believing abode" (ahl dāri qawmin muʾminīn). It also establishes that "Muslim" and "believer" (muʾmin) may sometimes be synonymous, and the conjoining of one to the other is due to the difference of wording—this being analogous to the saying of Allah the Exalted: {«فَأَخْرَجْنَا مَنْ كَانَ فِيهَا مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ فَمَا وَجَدْنَا فِيهَا غَيْرَ بَيْتٍ مِنَ الْمُسْلِمِينَ»} ("So We brought forth from it whoever was of the believers, and We found not therein but one house of the Muslims"). It is not permissible that the intended meaning of "Muslim" in this hadith be other than "believer," because if the believer were a hypocrite (munāfiq), it would not be permissible to greet him with peace.

And regarding the supplication for mercy (al-tarāḥḥum) [upon visiting graves], therein is evidence for those who permit women to visit graves. There is a scholarly disagreement on this matter, and it comprises three views (awjuh) among our companions (aṣḥābinā): The first is that it is prohibited (taḥrīm) for them, due to the hadith, "Allah curses the women who frequently visit graves" (laʿana Allāhu zawwārāti al-qubūr). The second is that it is disliked (makrūh). The third is that it is permissible (mubāḥ), and this is supported by this hadith and by the hadith, "I had forbidden you from visiting graves, so visit them" (kuntu nahaytukum ʿan ziyārati al-qubūr fa-zūrūhā). This [latter] is answered by [saying] that the pronoun in "I had forbidden you" (nahaytukum) is masculine plural, and thus women are not included therein, according to the sound and chosen position (al-madhhab al-ṣaḥīḥ al-mukhtār) in the principles of jurisprudence (uṣūl). And Allah knows best.

His saying, peace and blessings be upon him: "I asked my Lord for permission to seek forgiveness for my mother, and He did not grant it to me; and I asked His permission to visit her grave, and He granted it to me" (istaʾdhantu rabbī an astaghfira li-ummī fa-lam yaʾdhan lī wa-staʾdhantuhu an azūra qabrahā fa-adhina lī). In this is the permissibility of visiting polytheists (mushrikīn) during their lifetime and their graves after their death, because if visiting them after death is permissible, then during life it is even more so. And Allah the Exalted has said: {«وَصَاحِبْهُمَا فِي الدُّنْيَا مَعْرُوفًا»} ("And accompany them in this world with kindness"). In it also is the prohibition of seeking forgiveness (istighfār) for the disbelievers (kuffār). Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ, may Allah have mercy on him, said: The reason for his visit, peace and blessings be upon him, to her grave was that he intended the strengthening of the admonition (quwwat al-mawʿiẓah) and remembrance (al-dhikrā) by witnessing her grave. This is supported by his saying, peace and blessings be upon him, at the end of the hadith: "So visit the graves, for they remind you of death" (fa-zūrū al-qubūr fa-innahā tudhakkirukum al-mawt).

[975] His saying: "Abū Bakr ibn Abī Shaybah and Zuhayr ibn Ḥarb narrated to us; they said: Muḥammad ibn ʿUbayd narrated to us, from Yazīd ibn Kaysān, from Abū Ḥāzim, from Abū Hurayrah, who said: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, visited the grave of his mother, and wept, and made those around him weep. Then he said: 'I asked my Lord for permission to seek forgiveness for her, and He did not grant it to me; and I asked His permission to visit her grave, and He granted it to me. So visit the graves, for they remind you of death.'" This hadith is found in the narration of Abū al-ʿAlāʾ ibn Māhān among the people of the Maghrib, and it is not found in the narrations of our lands via ʿAbd al-Ghāfir al-Fārisī. However, it is found in many manuscripts (uṣūl) at the end of the Book of Funerals (Kitāb al-Janāʾiz), and it is correct (yuṣīb ʿalayh). Perhaps it was written in the margin: Abū Dāwūd narrated it in his Sunan, from Muḥammad ibn Sulaymān al-Anbārī, from Muḥammad ibn ʿUbayd, with this chain; and al-Nasāʾī narrated it from Qutaybah, from Muḥammad ibn ʿUbayd; and Ibn Mājah narrated it from Abū Bakr ibn Abī Shaybah, from Muḥammad ibn ʿUbayd. All of these are trustworthy (thiqāt), so this hadith is authentic (ṣaḥīḥ) without doubt.

His saying: "And wept, and made those around him weep" (fa-bakā wa-abkā man ḥawlahu). Al-Qāḍī said: His weeping, peace and blessings be upon him, was over what she had missed of attaining his days and belief in him (īmān bihi).

[977] His saying: "Muḥārib ibn Dithār" — it is with a kasrah on the dāl and a lightening (takhfīf) of the thāʾ (i.e., the letter with three dots). His saying, peace and blessings be upon him: "I had forbidden you from visiting graves, so visit them" (kuntu nahaytukum ʿan ziyārati al-qubūr fa-zūrūhā). This is among the hadiths that combine the abrogating and the abrogated (al-nāsikh wa-al-mansūkh), and it is explicit in abrogating the prohibition for men against visiting them. They (the scholars) are unanimous (ajmaʿū) that visiting them is a Sunnah (sunnah) for them. As for women, there is a disagreement among our companions, which we have already mentioned. We have also mentioned that those who prohibit them say: Women are not included in the address to men (khitāb al-rijāl), and this is the sound position among the uṣūliyyūn (scholars of legal theory). As for the prohibition of drinking from water-skins (al-intibādh fī al-asqiyah), its explanation has preceded in the Book of Faith (Kitāb al-Īmān) in the hadith of the delegation of ʿAbd al-Qays, and the rest of it will come in the Book of Beverages (Kitāb al-Ashribah), Allah willing. As for the sacrificial animals (al-aḍāḥī), their clarification will come in their chapter, Allah willing.

[978] His saying: "A man was brought to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, who had killed himself with a sharp arrowhead (mashāqiṣ), and he did not pray over him." Al-mashāqiṣ are broad arrows; the singular is mishqaṣ, with a kasrah on the mīm and a fatḥah on the qāf. In this hadith is evidence for those who say that one does not pray over a suicide (qātil nafsihi) due to his disobedience (maʿṣiyah). This is the madhhab of ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz and al-Awzāʿī. Al-Ḥasan, al-Nakhaʿī, Qatādah, Mālik, Abū Ḥanīfah, al-Shāfiʿī, and the majority of scholars (jamāhīr al-ʿulamāʾ) say that prayer is performed over him. They answer this hadith by [saying] that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, did not pray over him himself as a deterrent (zajr) to the people against doing the like of his deed, and the Companions (ṣaḥābah) did pray over him. This is like when the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, at the beginning of the matter, refrained from praying over one who had a debt, as a deterrent to them against being lax in taking loans and neglecting their repayment, and he ordered his Companions to pray over him, saying, peace and blessings be upon him: "Pray over your companion" (ṣallū ʿalā ṣāḥibikum). Al-Qāḍī said: The madhhab of all scholars is to pray over every Muslim, whether he is one who has been flogged (maḥdūd), stoned (marjūm), a suicide, or a child of fornication (walad zinā). It is reported from Mālik and others that the Imām should avoid praying over one killed in a prescribed punishment (ḥadd), and that virtuous people (ahl al-faḍl) do not pray over the wicked (fussāq) as a deterrent to them. It is reported from al-Zuhrī that one does not pray over a stoned person (marjūm), but one prays over one killed in retaliation (qiṣāṣ). Abū Ḥanīfah said: One does not pray over a brigand (muḥārib) nor over one killed by the rebellious group (al-fīʾah al-bāghiyah). Qatādah said: One does not pray over a child of fornication. It is reported from al-Ḥasan that one does not pray over a woman who dies in childbirth (nafsāʾ) due to fornication, nor over her child. Some of the Salaf (predecessors) prohibited prayer over a young child (ṭifl ṣaghīr). They disagreed over praying over a miscarried fetus (saqṭ): the jurists among the hadith scholars (fuqahāʾ al-muḥaddithīn) and some of the Salaf affirmed it if four months had passed over it, while the majority of jurists (jumhūr al-fuqahāʾ) prohibited it until it cries out (yastaHill) or its life is known by other means. As for the martyr (shahīd) killed in war against the disbelievers, Mālik, al-Shāfiʿī, and the majority said: He is not washed (lā yughassal) nor is prayer performed over him. Abū Ḥanīfah said: He is washed but prayer is not performed over him. It is reported from al-Ḥasan that he is washed and prayer is performed over him. And Allah knows best.

| (The Book of Zakāh — In the language, it is growth (numuww) and purification (taṭhīr). So wealth grows by it in a way not perceived, and it purifies its giver from sins. It is said: Its reward grows with Allah the Exalted. In the Sacred Law (sharʿ), it is named zakāh because the linguistic meaning is present in it. It is also said: Because it purifies (tuzakkī) [the soul].
