- Root: د-ر-د-ر (d-r-d-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Repetition of the triliteral root with reduplication indicates intense, restless motion — to shake, tremble, and move to and fro.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Used here for physical agitation, not metaphorical or theological disturbance.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) sense of bodily commotion; no figurative extension.
- Sībawayh Rule: ʿAṭf bayān (Appositional explicative) — the second noun clarifies the first without a conjunction, as in "خير فرقة" explaining the variant reading.
chapters.translation:
I say: The word "tatadardaru" (تَتَدَرْدَرُ) means it trembles, moves to and fro, and comes and goes.

His saying, may God's peace and blessings be upon him: "They will emerge at a time of division among the people" — the scholars of ḥadīth have recorded this in the Ṣaḥīḥ with two variant readings. The first is "ḥīna firqah" (حين فرقة) with an unpointed ḥāʾ (ḥāʾ muhmalah) kasrah and nūn, and "firqah" with ḍammah on the fāʾ — meaning: at the time of the people's division, i.e., a division that occurs among the Muslims. This is the division that took place between ʿAlī and Muʿāwiyah, may God be pleased with them both. The second reading is "khayra firqah" (خير فرقة) with an open khāʾ (khāʾ muʿjamah) fatḥah and rāʾ, and "firqah" with kasrah on the fāʾ — meaning: the better of the two parties. The first reading is more famous and more widespread. It is supported by the narration that follows this one: "They will emerge in a faction of the people" (في فرقة من الناس) — for there it is with ḍammah on the fāʾ without any disagreement, and its meaning is apparent.

Al-Qāḍī said concerning the reading with the pointed khāʾ: The intended meaning is "the best of the generations" (khayr al-qurūn), namely the first generation (al-ṣadr al-awwal). He said: Or it may mean ʿAlī and his companions — for on this interpretation, their emergence was literal (ḥaqīqah), because he was the rightful Imām at that time. In this there is a proof for the People of the Sunnah (ahl al-sunnah) that ʿAlī was correct (muṣīban) in his fighting, and the others were transgressors (bughāh) — especially given his saying, may God's peace and blessings be upon him: "The party closer to the truth will kill them" — and ʿAlī and his companions were the ones who killed them.

In this ḥadīth there are manifest miracles (muʿjizāt ẓāhirah) of the Messenger of God, may God's peace and blessings be upon him. For he informed of this, and it all came to pass exactly as the splitting of the dawn (ka-falaq al-ṣubḥ). It also entails the continued existence of his community after him, may God's peace and blessings be upon him, and that they would possess might and strength — contrary to what the falsifiers (al-mubṭilūn) used to spread — and that they would split into two factions, and that a renegade group (ṭāʾifah māriqah) would rise against him, and that they would be extreme in religion in places where extremism is not warranted, and would overdo prayer and recitation, yet would not uphold the rights of Islam — rather, they would slip through it (yamruqūna minhu) — and that they would fight the people of truth, and that the people of truth would kill them, and that among them there would be a man with a mark on his hand of such-and-such description. These are all types of miracles that occurred in their entirety — praise be to God.

His saying, may God's peace and blessings be upon him: "Their mark is shaving (al-taḥālīq)" — "al-sīmā" (السِّيما) means the mark (al-ʿalāmah). It has three variant forms: the shortened form (al-qaṣr), which is the most eloquent and the one that came in the Qurʾān; the lengthened form (al-madd); and the third is "al-sīmiyāʾ" (السِّيمياء) with an added yāʾ and lengthening only. The intended meaning of "al-taḥālīq" is the shaving of the heads. In the other narration it is "al-taḥlīq" (التَّحْلِيق). Some people used this as evidence for the disapproval (karāhah) of shaving the head — but there is no indication of that in it. Rather, it is merely a mark for them, and a mark may be something forbidden or something permissible — just as he said, may God's peace and blessings be upon him: "Their sign is a black man, one of whose upper arms is like a woman's breast." It is well known that this is not forbidden. And it is established in the Sunan of Abū Dāwūd, with an isnād meeting the conditions of al-Bukhārī and Muslim, that the Messenger of God, may God's peace and blessings be upon him, saw a boy whose head had been partially shaved and said: "Shave it all or leave it all." This is explicit (ṣarīḥ) in permitting the shaving of the head, admitting no interpretation (lā yaḥtamilu taʾwīlan). Our companions (aṣḥābunā) said: Shaving the head is permissible in every case. However, if maintaining it causes hardship due to oiling and combing, then shaving is recommended (yustaḥabbu ḥalquhu); and if it does not cause hardship, then leaving it is recommended.

His saying, may God's peace and blessings be upon him: "They are the worst of creation, or from the worst of creation" (hum sharr al-khalq aw min ashrar al-khalq) — thus it appears in all copies: "aw min ashrar" with the alif, which is a rare dialectal form (lughah qalīlah); the well-known form is "sharr" without the alif. In this wording there is an indication for those who declare them disbelievers (takfīr). The majority (al-jumhūr) interpreted it as meaning: the worst of the Muslims, and the like.

His saying, may God's peace and blessings be upon him: "The party closer to the truth will kill them" — and in one narration: "The party more deserving of the truth" (awlā al-ṭāʾifatayn bil-ḥaqq), and in another narration: "My community will split into two factions, and from between them will emerge a renegade group (māriqah); the one closer to the truth will undertake their killing." These narrations are explicit (ṣarīḥah) that ʿAlī, may God be pleased with him, was the correct one and upon the truth (al-muṣīb al-muḥiqq), and the other faction — the companions of Muʿāwiyah, may God be pleased with him — were transgressors with a mistaken interpretation (bughāh mutaʾawwilīn). In this there is also the explicit statement that both factions were believers — they do not exit from faith by fighting, nor do they become sinners (lā yafsiquwn). This is our school (madhhabunā) and the school of those who agree with us.

His saying: "Qāsim narrated to us — and he is Ibn al-Faḍl al-Ḥaddānī" — it is with ḍammah on the unpointed ḥāʾ and tashdīd on the dāl, followed by an alif and nūn.

His saying: "From al-Ḍaḥḥāk al-Mashriqī" — it is with kasrah on the mīm, sukūn on the pointed shīn, fatḥah on the rāʾ, and kasrah on the qāf. This is the correct form, which all the scholars of "al-Muʾtalif wa-l-Mukhtalif" (works on identically named and differently named narrators) and the scholars of names and histories have mentioned. Al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ transmitted from some of them that he recorded it with fatḥah on the mīm and kasrah on the rāʾ — and he said it is a corruption (taṣḥīf), as he stated. They all agreed that he is attributed to "Mashriq" — with kasrah on the mīm and fatḥah on the rāʾ — a sub-tribe of Hamdān. He is al-Ḍaḥḥāk al-Hamdānī, mentioned in the previous narration transmitted by Ḥarmalah and Aḥmad ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān.

His saying: "In a ḥadīth in which he mentioned people emerging against a divided faction" — they recorded it with kasrah on the fāʾ and with ḍammah.

[1066] His saying: "From Suwayd ibn Ghafalah" — it is with fatḥah on the pointed ghayn and the fāʾ.

His saying: "And when I narrate to you something between me and you, for war is deception (al-ḥarb khudʿah)" — its meaning is: I exert my own judgment (ajtahidu raʾyī). Al-Qāḍī said: In it there is a permissibility of equivocation (tawriyah) and indirect expression (taʿrīḍ) in war — as if he interpreted the ḥadīth upon this. His saying "khudʿah" (خُدْعَة) is with fatḥah on the khāʾ and sukūn on the dāl — this being the most eloquent — and it is also said with ḍammah on the khāʾ, and it is said "khudaʿah" (خُدَعَة) with ḍammah on the khāʾ and fatḥah on the dāl — three well-known dialectal forms.

His saying, may God's peace and blessings be upon him: "Young in age, foolish in mind" (aḥdāth al-asnān, sufahāʾ al-aḥlām) — its meaning is: small in years, small in intellects.

His saying, may God's peace and blessings be upon him: "They say the best of what the creation says" (min khayr qawl al-barīyah) — its meaning is: in outward appearance (fī ẓāhir al-amr), like their saying "There is no judgment but God's" (lā ḥukma illā li-llāh) and similar calls of theirs to the Book of God, may He be exalted. And God knows best.

His saying, may God's peace and blessings be upon him: "When you meet them, kill them, for in killing them there is a reward" — this is an explicit statement of the obligation to fight the Khawārij and the transgressors (al-bughāh), and it is a consensus of the scholars (ijmāʿ al-ʿulamāʾ). Al-Qāḍī said: The scholars are unanimous that the Khawārij and those like them among the people of innovation (ahl al-bidaʿ) and transgression (al-baghy) — whenever they rise against the Imām, oppose the opinion of the community (jamāʿah), and break the staff of unity (shaqqū al-ʿaṣā) — it is obligatory to fight them after warning them and offering them the excuse (al-iʿtidhār ilayhim). God, may He be exalted, said: {«فَقَاتِلُوا الَّتِي تَبْغِي حَتَّىٰ تَفِيءَ إِلَىٰ أَمْرِ اللَّهِ»} ("So fight the one that transgresses until it returns to the command of God") [al-Ḥujurāt 49:9]. However, one does not finish off their wounded (lā yujahhazu ʿalā jarīḥihim), nor pursue their fugitives (lā yutbaʿu munhazimuhum), nor kill their prisoners (lā yuqtalu asīruhum), nor are their properties made permissible (lā tubāḥu amwāluhum). And as long as they have not exited from obedience (al-ṭāʿah), [none of this applies].

chapters.title_en: Section 440 — The Khawārij, Their Rulings, and the Prohibition of Zakāh for the Prophet's Family
chapters.arabic_text:
وينتصبوا للحرب لا يقاتلون بل يوعظون ويستتابون من بدعتهم وباطلهم وهذا كله

ما لم يكفروا ببدعتهم فإن كانت بدعة مما يكفرون به جرت عليهم أحكام

المرتدين وأما البغاة الذين لا يكفرون فيرثون ويورثون ودمهم في حال القتال

هدر وكذا أموالهم التي تتلف في القتال والأصح أنهم لا يضمنون أيضا ما

أتلفوه على أهل العدل في حال القتال من نفس ومال وما أتلفوه في غير حال

القتال من نفس ومال ضمنوه ولا يحل الانتفاع بشيء من دوابهم وسلاحهم في حال

الحرب عندنا وعند الجمهور وجوزه أبو حنيفة والله أعلم قوله عن محمد عن

عبيدة هو بفتح العين وهو
# 
# قوله (فيهم رجل مخدج اليد أو مودن اليد أو مثدون اليد) أما المخدج فبضم

الميم وإسكان الخاء المعجمة وفتح الدال أي ناقص اليد والمودن بضم الميم

وإسكان الواو وفتح الدال ويقال بالهمز وبتركه وهو ناقص اليد ويقال أيضا

ودين والمثدون بفتح الميم وثاء مثلثة ساكنة وهو صغير اليد مجتمعها كثندوة

الثدي وهي بفتح الثاء بلا همز وبضمها مع الهمز وكان أصله مثنود
# 
# فقدمت الدال على النون كما قالوا جبذ وجذب وعاث في الأرض وعثا قوله

(فنزلني زيد بن وهب منزلا حتى قال مررنا على قنطرة) هكذا هو في معظم النسخ

مرة واحدة وفي نادر منها منزلا منزلا مرتين وكذا ذكره الحميدي في الجمع بين

الصحيحين وهو وجه الكلام أي ذكر لي مراحلهم بالجيش منزلا منزلا حتى بلغ

القنطرة التي كان القتال عندها وهي قنطرة الدبرجان كذا جاء مبينا في سنن

النسائي وهناك خطبهم علي رضي الله عنه وروى لهم هذه الأحاديث والقنطرة بفتح

القاف قولهم (فوحشوا برماحهم) أي رموا بها عن بعد قوله (وشجرهم الناس

برماحهم) هو بفتح الشين المعجمة والجيم المخففة أي مددوها إليهم وطاعنوهم

بها ومنه التشاجر في الخصومة قوله (وما أصيب من الناس يؤمئذ إلا رجلان)

يعني من أصحاب علي وأما
# 
# الخوارج فقتلوا بعضهم على بعض قوله (فقام إليه عبيدة السلماني) إلى آخره

وحاصله أنه استحلف عليا ثلاثا وإنما استحلفه ليسمع الحاضرين ويؤكد ذلك

عندهم ويظهر لهم المعجزة التي أخبر بها رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ويظهر

لهم أن عليا وأصحابه أولى الطائفتين بالحق وأنهم محقون في قتالهم وغير ذلك

مما في هذه الأحاديث من الفوائد وقوله السلماني هو بإسكان اللام منسوب إلى

سلمان جد قبيلة معروفة وهم بطن من مراد قاله بن أبي داود السجستاني أسلم

عبيدة قبل وفاة النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بسنتين ولم يره وسمع عمر وعليا

وبن مسعود وغيرهم من الصحابة رضي الله عنهم قوله (قالوا لا حكم إلا لله قال

علي كلمة حق أريد بها باطل) معناه أن الكلمة أصلها صدق قال الله تعالى ان

الحكم الا لله لكنهم أرادوا بها
# 
# الإنكار على علي رضي الله عنه في تحكيمه قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (إحدى

يديه طبي شاة) هو بطاء مهملة مضمومة ثم باء موحدة ساكنة والمراد به ضرع

الشاة وهو فيها مجاز واستعارة إنما أصله للكلبة والسباع قال أبو عبيد ويقال

أيضا لذوات الحافر ويقال للشاة ضرع وكذا للبقرة ويقال للناقة خلف وقال أبو

عبيد الأخلاف لذوات الأخفاف والأظلاف وقال الهروي يقال في ذات الخف والظلف

خلف وضرع قوله (عن يسير بن عمرو) وفي الرواية الأخرى أسير بن عمرو وهو بضم
# 
# الياء المثناة من تحت وفتح السين المهملة والثاني مثله إلا أنه بهمزة

مضمومة وكلاهما صحيح يقال يسير وأسير قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (يتيه قوم

قبل المشرق) أي يذهبون عن الصواب وعن طريق الحق يقال تاه إذا ذهب ولم يهتد

لطريق الحق والله أعلم

| (باب تحريم الزكاة على رسول الله صلى  الله عليه وسلم)
# (وعلى آله وهم بنو هاشم وبنو المطلب دون غيرهم)
# [1069] قوله (أخذ الحسن بن علي تمرة من تمر الصدقة فجعلها في فيه فقال

رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كخ كخ ارم بها أما علمت أنا لا نأكل الصدقة)

وفي رواية لا تحل لنا الصدقة قال القاضي يقال كخ كخ بفتح الكاف وكسرها

وتسكين الخاء ويجوز كسرها مع التنوين وهي كلمة يزجر بها الصبيان عن

المستقذرات فيقال له كخ أي اتركه وارم به قال الداودي هي عجمية معربة بمعنى

بئس وقد أشار إلى هذا البخاري بقوله في ترجمة باب من تكلم بالفارسية

والرطانة وفي الحديث أن الصبيان يوقون ما يوقاه الكبار وتمنع من تعاطيه

وهذا واجب على الولي قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (أما علمت أنا لا نأكل

الصدقة) هذه اللفظة تقال في الشيء الواضح التحريم
# 
# ونحوه وإن لم يكن المخاطب عالما به وتقديره عجب كيف خفي عليك هذا مع ظهور

تحريم الزكاة على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وعلى آله وهم بنو هاشم وبنو

المطلب هذا مذهب الشافعي وموافقيه أن آله صلى الله عليه وسلم هم بنو هاشم

وبنو المطلب وبه قال بعض المالكية وقال أبو حنيفة ومالك هم بنو هاشم خاصة

قال القاضي وقال بعض العلماء هم قريش كلها وقال أصبغ المالكي هم بنو قصي

دليل الشافعي أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال إن بني هاشم وبني المطلب
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ح-ك-م (ḥ-k-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To judge, arbitrate, or decide between parties; core sense of preventing injustice (manʿ min al-ẓulm).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological usage, ḥukm is the divine decree and legislative command; "lā ḥukma illā li-llāh" is a true statement (kalimah ḥaqq) but misapplied by the Khawārij.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: judicial arbitration. Metaphorical (majāz): the Khārijī slogan uses it as a political protest against ʿAlī's arbitration, hence "a word of truth by which falsehood is intended."
- Root: خ-ر-ج (kh-r-j)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To exit, depart, rebel; khārijī = one who secedes from the community.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Technical term for those who rebel against the legitimate Imām based on a misguided interpretation (taʾwīl fāsid).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: physical exit. Metaphorical: secession from obedience and consensus.
- Root: ز-ك-و (z-k-w)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Growth, purification; zakāh as alms that purify wealth.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The obligatory alms; forbidden to the Prophet ﷺ and his family as a mark of honor (karāmah), not impurity.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: increase. Metaphorical: ritual purification of the giver's soul and wealth.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clause (al-Sharṭ wa al-Jawāb) — The phrase "in kānat bidʿatun mimmā yukaffarūna bihī" establishes a conditional ruling: the apostasy ruling applies only when the innovation reaches the degree of disbelief, requiring precise syntactic linkage between the condition and its consequent.
chapters.translation:
I say: They are to be arrayed for war—not to be fought against, but rather to be admonished and called to repentance (yustaʾtābūn) from their innovation (bidʿah) and falsehood. All of this applies so long as their innovation has not rendered them disbelievers. But if their innovation is of the kind that constitutes disbelief (kufr), then the rulings of apostates (murtaddūn) apply to them.

As for the rebels (bughāt) who do not become disbelievers, they inherit and are inherited from, and their blood is forfeit (hadar) during the state of fighting, as are their properties that are destroyed in battle. The more correct position (al-aṣaḥḥ) is that they are not held liable for what they destroy against the people of justice during combat—whether lives or property. However, whatever they destroy outside the state of fighting—whether lives or property—they are held liable for it. It is not permissible to benefit from any of their mounts or weapons during the state of war, in our school and the majority's view; Abū Ḥanīfah permitted it. And Allah knows best.

His saying: "From Muḥammad, from ʿUbaydah"—ʿUbaydah is with fatḥah on the ʿayn.

His saying ﷺ: "Among them is a man with a deformed hand (mukhdaj al-yad), or mūdan al-yad, or muthdūn al-yad." As for mukhdaj, it is with ḍammah on the mīm, sukūn on the khāʾ, and fatḥah on the dāl—meaning deficient in the hand. Al-mūdan is with ḍammah on the mīm, sukūn on the wāw, and fatḥah on the dāl; it is also pronounced with hamzah or without it, meaning deficient in the hand; it is also said wadīn. Al-muthdūn is with fatḥah on the mīm and sukūn on the thāʾ (with three dots), meaning small and contracted in the hand, like the nipple of a breast (thanduwat al-thady)—which is with fatḥah on the thāʾ without hamzah, or with ḍammah with hamzah. Its original form was muthnūd, with the dāl advanced before the nūn, just as they said jabadh and jadhab (to pull), and ʿātha fī al-arḍ and ʿathā (to corrupt).

His saying: "Then Zayd ibn Wahb gave me lodging (manzalan) until he said: We passed over a bridge (qanṭarah)." This is how it appears in most manuscripts—once. In a rare version, it appears twice: "manzalan manzalan." Al-Ḥumaydī mentioned this in al-Jamʿ bayn al-Ṣaḥīḥayn, and it is the proper form of expression—i.e., he narrated to me the army's stages one encampment at a time until reaching the bridge where the battle occurred, which is the Bridge of al-Dabarjān. Thus it is clarified in Sunan al-Nasāʾī. There, ʿAlī (may Allah be pleased with him) addressed them and narrated these ḥadīths to them. Al-qanṭarah is with fatḥah on the qāf.

Their saying: "They thrust with their spears (fawaḥshū birimāḥihim)"—i.e., they threw them from a distance.

His saying: "The people entangled them with their spears (shajarahum al-nās birimāḥihim)"—it is with fatḥah on the shīn (with three dots) and a lightened jīm, meaning they extended them toward them and stabbed them with them. From this derives "al-tashājur" (mutual contention) in disputes.

His saying: "No one from the people was struck that day except two men"—meaning from ʿAlī's companions. As for the Khawārij, they killed one another.

His saying: "ʿUbaydah al-Salmānī stood up to him," etc. The summary is that he administered an oath to ʿAlī three times. He only administered the oath so that those present would hear, so that the matter would be confirmed for them, so that the miracle (muʿjizah) that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had foretold would become manifest to them, and so that it would be clear to them that ʿAlī and his companions were the more deserving of the two parties of the truth, and that they were correct in their fighting—along with other benefits contained in these ḥadīths.

His saying "al-Salmānī"—it is with sukūn on the lām, attributed to Salmān, the ancestor of a well-known tribe; they are a branch of Murād. Ibn Abī Dāwūd al-Sijistānī said this. ʿUbaydah embraced Islam two years before the death of the Prophet ﷺ but did not see him. He heard from ʿUmar, ʿAlī, Ibn Masʿūd, and other Companions (may Allah be pleased with them).

His saying: "They said: 'No judgment but Allah's.' ʿAlī said: 'A word of truth by which falsehood is intended.'" Its meaning is that the word is fundamentally true—Allah the Exalted said: {«إِنِ الْحُكْمُ إِلَّا لِلَّهِ»} (Indeed, judgment is not but for Allah)—but they intended by it to denounce ʿAlī (may Allah be pleased with him) for his arbitration (taḥkīm).

His saying ﷺ: "One of his hands is like the udder of a sheep (ṭiby shaʿh)"—it is with a voiceless ṭāʾ (muḥmalah) with ḍammah, then a bāʾ (muwaḥḥadah) with sukūn. What is meant is the sheep's udder (ḍarʿ). It is here a metaphor (majāz) and an extended trope (istiʿārah); its original usage is for the bitch and beasts of prey. Abū ʿUbayd said: It is also said for hoofed animals. For the sheep, one says ḍarʿ, and likewise for the cow; for the she-camel, one says khilf. Abū ʿUbayd said: al-akhlāf is for animals with soft feet (khuff) and cloven hooves (ẓilf). Al-Harawī said: For animals with khuff and ẓilf, one says khilf and ḍarʿ.

His saying: "From Yasīr ibn ʿAmr"—and in the other narration, "Usayr ibn ʿAmr." The first is with ḍammah on the yāʾ (with two dots below) and fatḥah on the sīn (muhmalah); the second is the same except with a ḍammah on the hamzah. Both are correct; one says yasīr and usayr.

His saying ﷺ: "A people will go astray (yatīh) before the East"—i.e., they will depart from correctness and from the path of truth. One says tāha when one goes away and is not guided to the path of truth. And Allah knows best.

---

| CHAPTER: The Prohibition of Zakāh upon the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and His Family—They Being Banū Hāshim and Banū al-Muṭṭalib, to the Exclusion of Others |

[1069] His saying: "Al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī took a date from the dates of charity (ṣadaqah) and put it in his mouth. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'Kakh, kakh—throw it away! Do you not know that we do not eat charity?'" And in another narration: "Charity is not lawful for us."

Al-Qāḍī said: One says "kakh kakh" with fatḥah on the kāf or kasrah, and sukūn on the khāʾ; it is also permissible to use kasrah with tanwīn. It is a word used to rebuke children from filth; one says to him "kakh," i.e., leave it and throw it away. Al-Dāwūdī said: It is a foreign word arabicized (aʿjamiyyah muʿarrabah) meaning "how bad." Al-Bukhārī alluded to this in his chapter heading: "Whoever Speaks Persian or Gibberish (rāṭanah)." In this ḥadīth, children are warded off from what adults are warded off from, and are prevented from engaging in it. This is obligatory upon the guardian (walī).

His saying ﷺ: "Do you not know that we do not eat charity?" This expression is used for something whose prohibition is clear, even if the addressee is not aware of it. Its implied meaning is: How astonishing that this was hidden from you, given the manifest prohibition of zakāh upon the Prophet ﷺ and his family—they being Banū Hāshim and Banū al-Muṭṭalib.

This is the school of al-Shāfiʿī and those who agree with him: that his family (ālihī) ﷺ are Banū Hāshim and Banū al-Muṭṭalib. Some Mālikīs also held this. Abū Ḥanīfah and Mālik said: They are Banū Hāshim exclusively. Al-Qāḍī said: Some scholars said: They are all of Quraysh. Aṣbagh al-Mālikī said: They are Banū Quṣayy.

The evidence for al-Shāfiʿī is that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Indeed, Banū Hāshim and Banū al-Muṭṭalib..."

chapters.title_en: The Prohibition of Charity (Ṣadaqah) upon the Prophet's Family and the Ruling on Their Clients (Mawālī)
chapters.arabic_text:
شيء واحد وقسم بينهم سهم ذوي القربى وأما صدقة التطوع فللشافعي فيها ثلاثة

أقوال أصحها أنها تحرم على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وتحل لآله والثاني

تحرم عليه وعليهم والثالث تحل له ولهم وأما موالي بني هاشم وبني المطلب فهل

تحرم عليهم الزكاة فيه وجهان لأصحابنا أصحهما تحرم للحديث الذي ذكره مسلم

بعد هذا حديث أبي رافع والثاني تحل وبالتحريم قال أبو حنيفة وسائر الكوفيين

وبعض المالكية وبالاباحة قال مالك وادعى بن بطال المالكي أن الخلاف إنما هو

في موالي بني هاشم وأما موالي غيرهم  فتباح لهم بالإجماع وليس كما قال بل

الأصح عند أصحابنا تحريمها على موالي بني هاشم وبني المطلب ولا فرق بينهما

والله أعلم
# [1070] قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (أنا لا تحل لنا الصدقة) ظاهره تحريم

صدقة الفرض والنفل وفيهما الكلام السابق قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (إني

لأنقلب إلى أهلي فأجد التمرة ساقطة على فراشي
# 
# ثم أرفعها لآكلها ثم أخشى أن تكون صدقة فألقيها) فيه تحريم الصدقة عليه

صلى الله عليه وسلم وأنه لا فرق بين صدقة الفرض والتطوع لقوله صلى الله

عليه وسلم الصدقة بالألف واللام وهي تعم النوعين ولم يقل الزكاة وفيه

استعمال الورع لأن هذه التمرة لا تحرم بمجرد الاحتمال لكن الورع تركها قوله

(أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم مر بتمرة في الطريق فقال لولا أن تكون من

الصدقة لأكلتها) فيه استعمال الورع كما سبق وفيه أن التمرة ونحوها من

محقرات الأموال لا يجب تعريفها بل يباح أكلها والتصرف فيها في الحال لأنه

صلى الله عليه وسلم إنما تركها خشية أن تكون من الصدقة لا لكونها لقطة وهذا

الحكم متفق عليه وعلله أصحابنا وغيرهم
# 
# بأن صاحبها في العادة لا يطلبها ولا يبقى له فيها مطمع والله أعلم
# [1072] قوله (فانتحاه ربيعة بن الحارث) هو بالحاء ومعناه عرض له وقصده

(قوله ما تفعل هذا إلا نفاسة منك علينا) معناه حسدا منك لنا قوله (فما

نفسنا عليك) هو بكسر الفاء أي ما حسدناك ذلك قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم

(أخرجا ما تصرران) هكذا هو في معظم الأصول ببلادنا وهو الذي ذكره الهروي

والمازري وغيرهما من أهل الضبط تصرران بضم التاء وفتح الصاد وكسر الراء

وبعدها راء أخرى ومعناه تجمعانه في صدوركما من الكلام وكل شيء جمعته فقد

صررته ووقع في بعض النسخ تسرران بالسين من السر أي ما تقولانه لي سرا وذكر

القاضي عياض فيه أربع روايات هاتين الثنتين والثالثة تصدران بإسكان الصاد

وبعدها دال مهملة معناه ماذا ترفعان إلي قال وهذه رواية السمرقندي والرابعة

تصوران بفتح
# 
# الصاد وبواو  مكسورة قال وهكذا ضبطه الحميدي قال القاضي وروايتنا عن أكثر

شيوخنا بالسين واستبعد رواية الدال والصحيح ما قدمناه عن معظم نسخ بلادنا

ورجحه أيضا صاحب المطالع فقال الأصوب تصرران بالصاد والرائين قوله (قد

بلغنا النكاح) أي الحلم كقوله تعالى حتى اذا بلغوا النكاح قوله (وجعلت زينب

تلمع إلينا من وراء الحجاب) هو بضم التاء وإسكان اللام وكسر الميم ويجوز

فتح التاء والميم يقال ألمع ولمع إذا أشار بثوبه أو بيده قوله صلى الله

عليه وسلم لعبد المطلب بن ربيعة والفضل بن عباس وقد سألاه العمل على الصدقة

بنصيب العامل (إن الصدقة لا تنبغي لآل محمد) دليل على أنها محرمة سواء كانت

بسبب العمل أو بسبب الفقر والمسكنة وغيرهما من الأسباب الثمانية وهذا هو

الصحيح عند أصحابنا وجوز بعض أصحابنا لبني هاشم وبني المطلب العمل عليها

بسهم العامل لأنه إجارة وهذا ضعيف أو باطل وهذا الحديث صريح في رده قوله

صلى الله عليه وسلم (إنما هي أوساخ الناس) تنبيه على العلة في تحريمها على

بني هاشم وبني المطلب وأنها لكرامتهم وتنزيههم عن الأوساخ ومعنى أوساخ

الناس أنها تطهير لأموالهم ونفوسهم كما قال تعالى خذ من أموالهم صدقة

تطهرهم وتزكيهم بها فهي كغسالة الأوساخ قوله
# 
# (حدثنا هارون بن معروف حدثنا بن وهب أخبرني يونس بن يزيد عن بن شهاب عن

عبد الله بن الحارث بن نوفل الهاشمي أن عبد المطلب بن ربيعة بن الحارث بن

عبد المطلب أخبره) هكذا وقع في مسلم من رواية يونس عن بن شهاب وسبق في

الرواية التي قبل هذه عن جويرية عن مالك عن الزهري أن عبد الله بن عبد الله

بن نوفل وكلاهما صحيح والأصل هو رواية مالك ونسبه في رواية يونس إلى جده

ولا يمتنع ذلك قال النسائي ولا نعلم أحدا روى هذا الحديث عن مالك إلا

جويرية بن أسماء قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (أصدق عنهما من الخمس) يحتمل أن

يريد من سهم ذوي القربى من الخمس لأنهما من ذوي القربى ويحتمل أن يريد  من

سهم النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم من الخمس قوله عن علي رضي الله عنه (وقال أنا

أبو حسن القرم) هو بتنوين حسن وأما القرم فالبراء مرفوع وهو السيد وأصله

فحل الإبل قال الخطابي معناه المقدم في المعرفة بالأمور والرأي كالفحل هذا

أصح الأوجه في ضبطه وهو المعروف في نسخ بلادنا والثاني حكاه القاضي أبو

الحسن القوم بالواو بإضافة حسن إلى القوم ومعناه عالم القوم وذو رأيهم
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ح ر م (ḥ-r-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning is "to be forbidden" or "sacrosanct"; derived from the concept of that which is inviolable or set apart.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In Kalām, it denotes a divine injunction of prohibition (taḥrīm), establishing a legal and moral boundary that is not subject to human alteration.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Used literally (ḥaqīqah) for legal prohibition; metaphorically (majāz) for sanctity, as in the "sacred precinct" (ḥaram).
- Sībawayh Rule: ʿAṭf al-Bayān (Appositional Clarification) — The phrase "سهم ذوي القربى" (the share of the near kin) is an explicative appositive clarifying the preceding division, requiring precise parsing to distinguish it from other shares.
chapters.translation:
I say: The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) divided one thing among them, allotting the share of the near kin (dhawī al-qurbā). As for voluntary charity (ṣadaqat al-taṭawwuʿ), there are three opinions attributed to al-Shāfiʿī: the soundest of them is that it is forbidden upon the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) but permissible for his family (ālihī); the second is that it is forbidden upon him and upon them; the third is that it is permissible for him and for them. As for the clients (mawālī) of Banī Hāshim and Banī al-Muṭṭalib, there are two faces (wajhān) among our companions regarding whether zakāh is forbidden upon them: the sounder of the two is that it is forbidden, due to the hadith that Muslim mentioned after this, namely the hadith of Abū Rāfiʿ; the second is that it is permissible. Abū Ḥanīfah, the rest of the Kūfans, and some of the Mālikīs held the view of prohibition, while Mālik held the view of permissibility. Ibn Baṭṭāl al-Mālikī claimed that the disagreement pertains only to the clients of Banī Hāshim, whereas the clients of others are permissible for them by consensus (ijmāʿ). But this is not as he said; rather, the soundest view among our companions is the prohibition upon the clients of Banī Hāshim and Banī al-Muṭṭalib, with no distinction between the two. And Allah knows best.

# [1070] His saying (peace and blessings be upon him): "Charity (ṣadaqah) is not lawful for us" — its apparent meaning is the prohibition of obligatory and voluntary charity, and regarding both, the preceding discussion applies. His saying (peace and blessings be upon him): "I return to my family and find a date fallen upon my bed, then I raise it to eat it, then I fear that it might be charity, so I cast it away" — in this is the prohibition of charity upon him (peace and blessings be upon him), and that there is no distinction between obligatory and voluntary charity, due to his saying (peace and blessings be upon him) "al-ṣadaqah" with the definite article (al-lām), which encompasses both types, and he did not say "al-zakāh." In this also is the practice of scrupulousness (waraʿ), for this date is not forbidden merely by probability, but scrupulousness dictates leaving it. His saying: "The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) passed by a date on the road and said: 'Were it not that it might be from charity, I would eat it'" — in this is the practice of scrupulousness as previously mentioned. And in it is that a date and similar trifling items of wealth (muḥaqqirāt al-amwāl) do not require public announcement (taʿrīf), but rather it is permissible to eat them and dispose of them immediately, because he (peace and blessings be upon him) only left it out of fear that it might be from charity, not because it was a lost item (luqatah). This ruling is agreed upon, and our companions and others have reasoned it by the fact that its owner, by custom, does not seek it and retains no hope for it. And Allah knows best.

# [1072] His saying: "Then Rabīʿah ibn al-Ḥārith turned toward him (fāntaḥāhu)" — it is with ḥāʾ, and its meaning is he appeared before him and aimed for him. His saying: "You do this only out of envy (nafāsah) from you toward us" — its meaning is out of jealousy (ḥasad) from you toward us. His saying: "We do not envy you (fa-mā nafasnā ʿalayka)" — it is with kasrah on the fāʾ, meaning we did not begrudge you that. His saying (peace and blessings be upon him): "Bring out what you are concealing (tuṣarrirān)" — thus it appears in most of the manuscripts of our lands, and it is what al-Harawī, al-Māzarī, and other meticulous scholars mentioned: tuṣarrirān with ḍammah on the tāʾ, fatḥah on the ṣād, kasrah on the rāʾ, followed by another rāʾ. Its meaning is: what you are gathering in your chests of speech; for everything you have collected, you have "ṣarrartu" it. In some copies it appears as "tusirrān" with sīn, from "al-sirr" (secrecy), meaning: what you say to me in secret. Al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ mentioned four narrations regarding it: these two, the third being "taṣdirān" with sukūn on the ṣād followed by an unpointed dāl, meaning: what are you raising up to me? He said: this is the narration of al-Samarqandī. The fourth is "tuṣawwirān" with fatḥah on the ṣād and a wāw with kasrah; he said: thus al-Ḥumaydī recorded it. Al-Qāḍī said: our narration from most of our shaykhs is with the sīn, and he deemed the dāl narration improbable. The correct view is what we have presented from most copies of our lands, and the author of al-Maṭāliʿ also favored it, saying: the most correct is "tuṣarrirān" with ṣād and two rāʾs. His saying: "We have reached the age of marriage (al-nikāḥ)" — meaning puberty (al-ḥulum), as per His saying (Exalted is He): {«حَتَّىٰ إِذَا بَلَغُوا النِّكَاحَ»} (until when they reach the age of marriage). His saying: "And Zaynab kept signaling (tulmiʿ) to us from behind the veil" — it is with ḍammah on the tāʾ, sukūn on the lām, and kasrah on the mīm; it is also permissible with fatḥah on the tāʾ and mīm. One says "almaʿa" and "lamaʿa" when one gestures with one's garment or hand. His saying (peace and blessings be upon him) to ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib ibn Rabīʿah and al-Faḍl ibn al-ʿAbbās, when they asked him for employment on the charity (al-ṣadaqah) through the share of the worker (sahm al-ʿāmil): "Indeed, charity is not befitting for the family of Muḥammad" — this is evidence that it is forbidden, whether it be due to employment or due to poverty, destitution, or any of the other eight categories. This is the correct view among our companions. Some of our companions permitted Banī Hāshim and Banī al-Muṭṭalib to work on it through the share of the worker, because it is a hire contract (ijārah), but this is weak or invalid, and this hadith is explicit in refuting it. His saying (peace and blessings be upon him): "It is but the filth of the people (awsākh al-nās)" — this is an indication of the effective cause (ʿillah) for its prohibition upon Banī Hāshim and Banī al-Muṭṭalib, namely, their honor and their being kept pure from filth. The meaning of "the filth of the people" is that it purifies their wealth and their souls, as He (Exalted is He) said: {«خُذْ مِنْ أَمْوَالِهِمْ صَدَقَةً تُطَهِّرُهُمْ وَتُزَكِّيهِمْ بِهَا»} (Take from their wealth a charity to purify them and sanctify them thereby). Thus, it is like the washing water of filth. His saying:

# "Hārūn ibn Maʿrūf narrated to us; Ibn Wahb narrated to us; Yūnus ibn Yazīd informed me, from Ibn Shihāb, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Nawfal al-Hāshimī, that ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib ibn Rabīʿah ibn al-Ḥārith ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib informed him" — thus it occurs in Muslim from the narration of Yūnus from Ibn Shihāb. It was previously mentioned in the narration before this, from Juwayriyyah from Mālik from al-Zuhrī, that it was ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Nawfal, and both are authentic. The origin is the narration of Mālik, and in the narration of Yūnus, he is attributed to his grandfather, and that is not impossible. Al-Nasāʾī said: we know of no one who narrated this hadith from Mālik except Juwayriyyah ibn Asmāʾ. His saying (peace and blessings be upon him): "Give on their behalf from the fifth (al-khums)" — it is possible he meant from the share of the near kin from the fifth, because they are of the near kin; and it is possible he meant from the share of the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) from the fifth. His saying regarding ʿAlī (may Allah be pleased with him): "And he said: I am Abū Ḥasan al-Qaram" — it is with tanwīn on "Ḥasan." As for "al-Qaram," it is the noble one (al-barrāʾ), raised, and it is the master (al-sayyid); its origin is the stud camel (faḥl al-ibil). Al-Khaṭṭābī said: its meaning is the one foremost in knowledge of affairs and sound opinion, like the stud. This is the soundest of the faces in its vocalization, and it is the well-known one in the copies of our lands. The second is what al-Qāḍī Abū al-Ḥasan narrated: "al-Qawm" with wāw, adding "Ḥasan" to "al-Qawm," meaning the scholar of the people and the possessor of their opinion.

chapters.title_en: Section 442 — On Gifts to the Prophet (ﷺ), the Permissibility for Banū Hāshim and Banū al-Muṭṭalib, and the Ruling on Charity After Its Receipt
chapters.arabic_text:
والثالث حكاه القاضي أيضا أبو حسن بالتنوين والقوم بالواو مرفوع أي أنا من

علمتم رأيه أيها القوم وهذا ضعيف لأن حروف النداء لا تحذف في نداء القوم

ونحوه قوله (لا أريم مكاني) هو بفتح الهمزة وكسر الراء أي لا أفارقه قوله

(والله لا أريم مكاني حتى يرجع إليكما ابناكما بحور ما بعثتما به
# 
# قوله بحور هو بفتح الحاء المهملة أي بجواب ذلك قال الهروي في تفسيره يقال

كلمته فما رد علي حورا ولا حويرا أي جوابا قال ويجوز أن يكون معناه الخيبة

أي يرجعا بالخيبة وأصل الحور الرجوع إلى النقص قال القاضي هذا أشبه بسياق

الحديث أما قوله ابناكما فهكذا ضبطناه ابناكما بالتثنية ووقع في بعض الأصول

أبناؤكما بالواو على الجمع وحكاه القاضي أيضا قال وهو وهم والصواب الأول

وقال وقد يصح الثاني على مذهب من جمع الاثنين قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم

(ادعوا لي محمية بن جزء وهو رجل من بني أسد) أما محمية فبميم مفتوحة ثم حاء

مهملة ساكنة ثم ميم أخرى مكسورة ثم ياء مخففة وأما جزء فبجيم مفتوحة ثم زاي

ساكنة ثم همزة هذا هو الأصح قال القاضي هكذا تقوله عامة الحفاظ وأهل

الإتقان ومعظم الرواة وقال عبد الغني بن سعيد يقال جزي بكسر الزاي يعني

وبالياء وكذا وقع في بعض النسخ في بلادنا قال القاضي وقال أبو عبيد هو

عندنا جز مشدد الزاي وأما قوله وهو رجل من بني أسد فقال القاضي كذا وقع

والمحفوظ أنه من بني زبيد لا من بني أسد

| (باب إباحة الهدية للنبي صلى  الله عليه وسلم)
# (ولبني هاشم وبنى المطلب وان كان المهدى ملكها بطريق الصدقة) (وبيان أن

الصدقة اذا قبضها المتصدق عليه زال عنها وصف الصدقة) (وحلت لكل أحد ممن

كانت الصدقة محرمة عليه)
# [1073] قوله (أن عبيد بن السباق) هو بفتح السين المهملة وتشديد الباء

الموحدة قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم
# 
# في لحم الشاة الذي أعطيته مولاة جويرية من الصدقة (قربيه فقد بلغت محلها)

هو بكسر الحاء أي زال عنها حكم الصدقة وصارت حلالا لنا وفيه دليل للشافعي

وموافقيه أن لحم الأضحية إذا قبضه المتصدق عليه وسائر الصدقات يجوز لقابضها

بيعها ويحل لمن أهداها إليه أو ملكها منه بطريق آخر وقال بعض المالكية لا

يجوز بيع لحم الأضحية لقابضها
# [1075] قوله (كلاهما عن شعبة عن قتادة عن أنس) ثم قال في الطريق الآخر

(حدثنا شعبة عن قتادة سمع أنس بن مالك) فيه التنبيه على انتفاء تدليس قتادة

لأنه عنعن في الرواية الأولى وصرح بالسماع في الثانية وقد سبق مرات أن

المدلس لا يحتج بعنعنته إلا أن يثبت سماعه لذلك الحديث من ذلك الشيخ من

طريق آخر فنبه مسلم رحمه الله تعالى على ذلك
# 
# قوله (عن الأسود عن عائشة وأتي النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بلحم بقر) هكذا

هو في كثير من الأصول المعتمدة أو أكثرها وأتي بالواو وفي بعضها أتي بغير

واو وكلاهما صحيح والواو عاطفة على بعض من الحديث لم يذكره هنا قوله (كان

في بريرة ثلاث قضيات) فذكر منها قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم هو عليها صدقة

ولكم هدية ولم يذكر هنا الثانية والثالثة وهما
# 
# الولاء لمن أعتق وتخييرها في فسخ النكاح حين أعتقت تحت عبد وسيأتي بيان

الثلاث مشروحة إن شاء الله تعالى في كتاب النكاح
# [1076] قولها (إلا أن نسيبة بعثت إلينا) هي نسيبة بضم النون وفتح السين

المهملة وإسكان الياء ويقال فيها أيضا نسيبة بفتح النون وكسر السين وهي أم

عطية
# [1077] قوله (إن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان إذا أتي بطعام سأل عنه فإن

قيل هدية أكل منها  وإن قيل صدقة لم يأكل منها) فيه استعمال الورع والفحص عن

أصل المآكل والمشارب

| (باب الدعاء لمن أتى بصدقته)
# [1078] قوله (كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا أتاه قوم بصدقتهم قال

اللهم صل عليهم فأتاه أبي أبو أوفى بصدقته فقال اللهم صل على آل أبي أوفى)

هذا الدعاء وهو الصلاة امتثال لقول الله عز وجل
# 
# وصل عليهم ومذهبنا المشهور ومذهب العلماء كافة أن الدعاء لدافع الزكاة

سنة مستحبة ليس بواجب وقال أهل الظاهر هو واجب وبه قال بعض أصحابنا حكاه

أبو عبد الله الحناطي بالحاء المهملة واعتمدوا الأمر في الآية قال الجمهور

الأمر في حقنا للندب لأن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بعث معاذا وغيره لأخذ

الزكاة ولم يأمرهم بالدعاء وقد يجيب الآخرون بأن وجوب الدعاء كان معلوما

لهم من الآية الكريمة وأجاب الجمهور أيضا بأن دعاء النبي صلى الله عليه

وسلم وصلاته سكن لهم بخلاف غيره واستحب الشافعي في صفة الدعاء أن يقول آجرك

الله فيما أعطيت وجعله لك طهورا وبارك لك فيما أبقيت وأما قول الساعي اللهم

صل على فلان فكرهه جمهور أصحابنا وهو مذهب بن عباس ومالك وبن عيينة وجماعة

من السلف وقال جماعة من العلماء ويجوز ذلك بلا كراهة لهذا الحديث قال

أصحابنا لا يصلى على غير الأنبياء إلا تبعا لأن الصلاة في لسان السلف

مخصوصة بالأنبياء صلاة الله وسلامه عليهم كما أن قولنا عز وجل مخصوص بالله

سبحانه وتعالى فكما لا يقال محمد عز وجل وإن كان عزيزا جليلا لا يقال أبو
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ح-و-ر (ḥ-w-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning is "return" (rujūʿ), with derivations indicating diminution or deficiency after a state of fullness; also "reply" or "answer" in dialogue.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological usage, al-ḥawr signifies a return to a lesser state—often applied to the outcome of an action, i.e., disappointment or failure (khaybah).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense is "turning back"; metaphorically, it denotes the response to speech (jawāb) and, by extension, the result of a venture—success or its absence.
- Root: ن-د-ء (n-d-ʾ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: The act of calling out or summoning; the vocative particle (ḥarf al-nidāʾ) is integral to its syntactic function.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In Quranic and prophetic discourse, it marks direct address, often with a rhetorical or emphatic force.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): The vocative particle cannot be elided when addressing a collective noun like "O people" (ayyuhā al-qawm), as elision would obscure the grammatical case and intended address.
- Sībawayh Rule: Rule of Vocative Construction (Bāb al-Nidāʾ) — The vocative particle (yā, ayyuhā) governs the following noun in the nominative (rafʿ) when definite; its omission is impermissible in standard address, rendering the variant reading "anā man ʿalimtum raʾyahu" with "al-qawm" (nominative) weak, as the particle cannot be dropped in such a construction.
chapters.translation:
I say: The third variant was also related by al-Qāḍī Abū Ḥasan with tanwīn (on "man") and "al-qawm" with the wāw, raised (nominative), meaning: "I am one whose opinion you have known, O people." This is weak, because the vocative particles are not elided when addressing a group (al-qawm) and the like.

His statement (ﷺ): «لَا أَرِيمُ مَكَانِي» ("I will not leave my place") — it is with fatḥa on the hamza and kasra on the rāʾ, meaning: "I will not depart from it."

His statement (ﷺ): «وَاللَّهِ لَا أَرِيمُ مَكَانِي حَتَّى يَرْجِعَ إِلَيْكُمَا ابْنَاكُمَا بِحَوْرٍ مَا بَعَثْتُمَا بِهِ» ("By Allah, I will not leave my place until your two sons return to you with ḥawr of what you sent with them").

His statement "bi-ḥawr" — it is with fatḥa on the ḥāʾ (unpointed), meaning: "with a reply to that." Al-Harawī said in his commentary: One says, "I spoke to him, and he gave me neither ḥawr nor ḥuwayr," i.e., no answer. He said: And it is permissible that its meaning be "disappointment" (al-khaybah), i.e., "they return with disappointment." The origin of al-ḥawr is "return to deficiency." Al-Qāḍī said: This is more fitting to the context of the ḥadīth.

As for his statement "ibnākumā" ("your two sons") — thus we have recorded it: "ibnākumā" in the dual form. And in some manuscripts it occurs as "abnāʾukumā" with the wāw, indicating the plural. Al-Qāḍī also related this and said: It is an error, and the correct is the first. He said: Yet the second may be valid according to the school of those who treat the dual as plural.

His statement (ﷺ): «ادْعُوا لِي مَحْمِيَّةَ بْنَ جَزْءٍ وَهُوَ رَجُلٌ مِنْ بَنِي أَسَدٍ» ("Call for me Maḥmiyyah ibn Jazʾ, a man from Banū Asad"). As for "Maḥmiyyah" — it is with an open mīm, then an unpointed ḥāʾ (sākinah), then another kasra mīm, then a lightened yāʾ. As for "Jazʾ" — it is with an open jīm, then a sākin zāy, then a hamza. This is the most correct. Al-Qāḍī said: Thus the generality of the ḥuffāẓ (ḥadīth masters), the people of precision, and most transmitters pronounce it. ʿAbd al-Ghanī ibn Saʿīd said: It is said "Juzayy" with kasra on the zāy, meaning with a yāʾ, and thus it occurs in some manuscripts in our lands. Al-Qāḍī said: Abū ʿUbayd said: It is for us "Jazz" with a shaddah on the zāy.

As for his statement "a man from Banū Asad" — al-Qāḍī said: Thus it occurs, but the preserved (maḥfūẓ) version is that he was from Banū Zubayd, not from Banū Asad.

(Chapter: The Permissibility of Gifts to the Prophet (ﷺ), and for Banū Hāshim and Banū al-Muṭṭalib, even if the giver had acquired it by way of charity; and the clarification that when charity is received by the one to whom it is given, the description of charity is removed from it, and it becomes lawful for everyone for whom charity was previously forbidden.)

[1073] His statement: «أَنَّ عُبَيْدَ بْنَ السَّبَّاقِ» ("That ʿUbayd ibn al-Sabbāq") — it is with fatḥa on the sīn (unpointed) and tashdīd on the bāʾ (pointed).

His statement (ﷺ) regarding the meat of the sheep that the freed slave-girl of Juwayriyyah had given him from charity: «قَرِّبِيهِ فَقَدْ بَلَغَتْ مَحِلَّهَا» ("Bring it near, for it has reached its place of permissibility") — it is with kasra on the ḥāʾ, meaning: "The ruling of charity has been removed from it, and it has become lawful for us." In this is evidence for al-Shāfiʿī and his supporters that the meat of the udḥiyyah (sacrificial animal) — when received by the one to whom it is given, and likewise all charities — it is permissible for the recipient to sell it, and it is lawful for the one to whom it is gifted or from whom it is acquired by another means. Some Mālikīs said: It is not permissible for the recipient to sell the meat of the udḥiyyah.

[1075] His statement: «كِلَاهُمَا عَنْ شُعْبَةَ عَنْ قَتَادَةَ عَنْ أَنَسٍ» ("Both of them from Shuʿbah, from Qatādah, from Anas") — then he said in the other chain: «حَدَّثَنَا شُعْبَةُ عَنْ قَتادَةَ سَمِعَ أَنَسَ بْنَ مَالِكٍ» ("Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Qatādah, who heard Anas ibn Mālik"). In this is an indication of the absence of tadlīs (concealment) by Qatādah, because he used ʿanʿanah (the ambiguous "from" formulation) in the first narration and explicitly stated hearing (samāʿ) in the second. It has preceded multiple times that the mudallis (one who conceals) is not accepted by his ʿanʿanah unless his hearing of that specific ḥadīth from that specific shaykh is established through another chain. Thus Muslim (may Allah have mercy on him) drew attention to this.

His statement: «عَنِ الْأَسْوَدِ عَنْ عَائِشَةَ وَأُتِيَ النَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ بِلَحْمِ بَقَرٍ» ("From al-Aswad, from ʿĀʾishah: And the Prophet (ﷺ) was brought beef meat") — thus it is in many or most of the reliable manuscripts: "wa-utiya" with the wāw. In some of them it is "utiya" without the wāw, and both are correct. The wāw is conjunctive, linking to a portion of the ḥadīth not mentioned here.

His statement: «كَانَ فِي بَرِيرَةَ ثَلَاثُ قَضِيَّاتٍ» ("There were three rulings concerning Barīrah") — he mentioned from them his statement (ﷺ): «هُوَ عَلَيْهَا صَدَقَةٌ وَلَكُمْ هَدِيَّةٌ» ("It is charity for her and a gift for you"), but he did not mention here the second and third, which are: the walāʾ (clientage) belongs to the one who frees, and her choice (takhyīr) to annul the marriage when she was freed while under a slave husband. The explanation of the three will come, Allah willing, in the Book of Marriage.

[1076] Her statement: «إِلَّا أَنَّ نُسَيْبَةَ بَعَثَتْ إِلَيْنَا» ("Except that Nusaybah sent to us") — she is Nusaybah with ḍamma on the nūn, fatḥa on the sīn (unpointed), and sukūn on the yāʾ. It is also said: Nusaybah with fatḥa on the nūn and kasra on the sīn. She is Umm ʿAṭiyyah.

[1077] His statement: «إِنَّ النَّبِيَّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ كَانَ إِذَا أُتِيَ بِطَعَامٍ سَأَلَ عَنْهُ فَإِنْ قِيلَ هَدِيَّةٌ أَكَلَ مِنْهَا وَإِنْ قِيلَ صَدَقَةٌ لَمْ يَأْكُلْ مِنْهَا» ("The Prophet (ﷺ), when food was brought to him, would ask about it; if it was said 'a gift,' he would eat from it, and if it was said 'charity,' he would not eat from it") — in this is the practice of scrupulousness (waraʿ) and investigation into the origin of foods and drinks.

(Chapter: Supplication for the One Who Brings His Charity)

[1078] His statement: «كَانَ النَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ إِذَا أَتَاهُ قَوْمٌ بِصَدَقَتِهِمْ قَالَ اللَّهُمَّ صَلِّ عَلَيْهِمْ فَأَتَاهُ أَبِي أَبُو أَوْفَى بِصَدَقَتِهِ فَقَالَ اللَّهُمَّ صَلِّ عَلَى آلِ أَبِي أَوْفَى» ("The Prophet (ﷺ), when a people brought him their charity, would say: 'O Allah, send prayers upon them.' Then my father Abū Awfā brought him his charity, and he said: 'O Allah, send prayers upon the family of Abū Awfā'") — This supplication, which is the prayer (ṣalāh), is in compliance with the saying of Allah, Exalted and Majestic: {وَصَلِّ عَلَيْهِمْ} ("And pray upon them") [Quran 9:103]. Our well-known school (madhhab) and the school of all scholars is that supplication for the payer of zakāh is a sunnah, recommended (mustaḥabbah), not obligatory. The Ẓāhirīs said it is obligatory, and some of our companions also said this, as related by Abū ʿAbd Allāh al-Ḥannāṭī (with an unpointed ḥāʾ). They relied on the command in the verse. The majority (jumhūr) said: The command in our case indicates recommendation (nadb), because the Prophet (ﷺ) sent Muʿādh and others to collect zakāh and did not command them to supplicate. The others might respond that the obligation of supplication was known to them from the noble verse. The majority also responded that the Prophet's (ﷺ) supplication and prayer was a tranquility (sakan) for them, unlike others. Al-Shāfiʿī recommended, regarding the manner of supplication, that one say: "May Allah reward you for what you have given, make it a purification for you, and bless you in what you have retained." As for the collector's saying "O Allah, send prayers upon so-and-so," the majority of our companions disapproved of it, and it is the school of Ibn ʿAbbās, Mālik, Ibn ʿUyaynah, and a group of the Salaf. A group of scholars said: It is permissible without disapproval, due to this ḥadīth. Our companions said: Prayer (ṣalāh) is not sent upon other than the prophets except as a following (tabaʿan), because "prayer" in the language of the Salaf is specific to the prophets — may Allah's prayers and peace be upon them — just as our saying "ʿAzza wa Jall" is specific to Allah, Glorified and Exalted. So just as one does not say "Muḥammad ʿAzza wa Jall" — even though he is mighty and majestic — one does not say "Abū..."

chapters.title_en: The Ruling on Sending Salāh upon Non-Prophets and the Meaning of "Faqdirū Lah" (Estimate It) in the Hadith of the Crescent
chapters.arabic_text:
بكر صلى الله عليه وسلم وإن صح المعنى واختلف أصحابنا في النهي عن ذلك هل

هو نهي تنزيه أم محرم أو مجرد أدب على ثلاثة أوجه الأصح الأشهر أنه مكروه

كراهة تنزيه لأنه شعار لأهل البدع وقد نهينا عن شعارهم والمكروه هو ما ورد

فيه نهي مقصود واتفقوا على أنه يجوز أن يجعل غير الأنبياء تبعا لهم في ذلك

فيقال اللهم صل على محمد وعلى آل محمد وأزواجه وذريته وأتباعه لأن السلف لم

يمنعوا منه وقد أمرنا به في التشهد وغيره قال الشيخ أبو محمد الجويني من

أئمة أصحابنا السلام في معنى الصلاة ولا يفرد به غير الأنبياء لأن الله

تعالى قرن بينهما ولا يفرد به غائب ولا يقال قال فلان عليه السلام وأما

المخاطبة به لحي أو ميت فسنة فيقال السلام عليكم أو عليك أو سلام عليك أو

عليكم والله أعلم
# 
# (فاقدروا له) وفي رواية فاقدروا له ثلاثين وفي رواية إذا رأيتم الهلال

فصوموا وإذا رأيتموه فأفطروا فإن غم عليكم فاقدروا له وفي رواية فإن غم

عليكم فصوموا ثلاثين يوما وفي رواية فإن غمي عليكم فأكملوا العدد وفي رواية

فان غمي عليكم الشهر فعدوا ثلاثين وفي رواية فإن أغمي عليكم فعدوا ثلاثين

هذه الروايات كلها في الكتاب على هذا الترتيب وفي رواية للبخاري فإن غبي

عليكم فأكملوا عدة شعبان ثلاثين واختلف العلماء في معنى فاقدروا له فقالت

طائفة من العلماء معناه ضيقوا له وقدروه تحت السحاب وممن قال بهذا أحمد بن

حنبل وغيره ممن يجوز صوم يوم ليلة الغيم عن رمضان كما سنذكره إن شاء الله

تعالى وقال بن سريج وجماعة منهم مطرف بن عبد الله وبن قتيبة وآخرون معناه

قدروه بحساب المنازل وذهب مالك والشافعي وأبو حنيفة وجمهور السلف والخلف

إلى أن معناه قدروا له تمام العدد ثلاثين يوما قال أهل اللغة يقال قدرت

الشيء أقدره وأقدره وقدرته وأقدرته بمعنى واحد وهو من التقدير قال الخطابي

ومنه قول الله تعالى فقدرنا فنعم القادرون واحتج الجمهور بالروايات

المذكورة فأكملوا العدة ثلاثين وهو تفسير لاقدروا له ولهذا لم يجتمعا في

رواية بل تارة يذكر هذا وتارة يذكر هذا ويؤكده الرواية السابقة فاقدروا له

ثلاثين قال المازري حمل جمهور الفقهاء قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم فاقدروا له

على أن المراد اكمال العدة ثلاثين كما فسره في حديث آخر قالوا ولا يجوز أن

يكون المراد حساب المنجمين لأن الناس لو كلفوا به ضاق عليهم لأنه لا يعرفه

إلا أفراد والشرع إنما يعرف الناس بما يعرفه  جماهيرهم والله أعلم وأما قوله

صلى الله عليه وسلم (فإن غم عليكم) فمعناه حال بينكم وبينه غيم يقال غم

وأغمي وغمي وغمي بتشديد الميم وتخفيفها والغين مضمومة فيهما ويقال غبي بفتح

الغين وكسر الباء وكلها صحيحة وقد غامت السماء وغيمت وأغامت وتغيمت وأغمت

وفي هذه الأحاديث دلالة لمذهب مالك والشافعي والجمهور أنه لا يجوز صوم يوم

الشك ولا يوم الثلاثين
# 
# [1079] قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (إذا جاء رمضان فتحت أبواب الجنة وغلقت

أبواب النار وصفدت الشياطين) وفي الرواية الأخرى (إذا كان رمضان فتحت أبواب

الرحمة وغلقت أبواب جهنم وسلسلت الشياطين) وفي رواية (اذا دخل رمضان) فيه

دليل للمذهب الصحيح المختار الذي ذهب إليه البخاري والمحققون أنه يجوز أن

يقال رمضان من غير ذكر الشهر بلا كراهة وفي هذه المسألة ثلاثة مذاهب قالت

طائفة لا يقال رمضان على انفراده بحال وإنما يقال شهر رمضان هذا قول أصحاب

مالك وزعم هؤلاء أن رمضان اسم من أسماء الله تعالى فلا يطلق على غيره الا

بقيد وقال أكثر أصحابنا وبن الباقلاني إن كان هناك قرينة تصرفه إلى الشهر

فلا كراهة وإلا فيكره قالوا فيقال صمنا رمضان قمنا رمضان ورمضان أفضل

الأشهر ويندب طلب ليلة القدر في أواخر رمضان وأشباه ذلك ولا كراهة في هذا

كله وإنما يكره أن يقال جاء رمضان ودخل وحضر رمضان وأحب رمضان ونحو ذلك

والمذهب الثالث مذهب البخاري والمحققين أنه لا كراهة في إطلاق رمضان بقرينة

وبغير قرينة وهذا المذهب هو الصواب
# 
# والمذهبان الأولان فاسدان لأن الكراهة إنما تثبت بنهي الشرع ولم يثبت فيه

نهي وقولهم إنه اسم من أسماء الله تعالى ليس بصحيح ولم يصح في شيء وإن كان

قد جاء فيه أثر ضعيف وأسماء الله تعالى توقيفية لا تطلق إلا بدليل صحيح ولو

ثبت أنه اسم لم يلزم منه كراهة وهذا الحديث المذكور في الباب صريح في الرد

على المذهبين ولهذا الحديث نظائر كثيرة في الصحيح في إطلاق رمضان على الشهر

من غير ذكر الشهر وقد سبق التنبيه  على كثير منها في كتاب الإيمان وغيره

والله أعلم وأما قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم فتحت أبواب الجنة وغلقت أبواب

النار وصفدت الشياطين فقال القاضي عياض رحمه الله تعالى يحتمل أنه على

ظاهره وحقيقته وأن تفتيح أبواب الجنة وتغليق أبواب جهنم وتصفيد الشياطين

علامة لدخول الشهر وتعظيم لحرمته ويكون التصفيد ليمتنعوا من إيذاء المؤمنين

والتهويش عليهم قال ويحتمل أن يكون المراد المجاز ويكون إشارة إلى كثرة

الثواب والعفو وان الشياطين يقل اغواؤهم وايذاؤهم ليصيرون كالمصفدين ويكون
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ص-ل-و (ṣ-l-w)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning is "to pray" or "to invoke blessings," derived from the concept of supplication and devotion; in the context of Allāh, it denotes His mercy and praise of the servant.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological terms, "ṣalāh" from Allāh is His mercy and forgiveness; from angels, it is their seeking of pardon; from believers, it is supplication. It is a technical term for invoking divine blessings.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literally, it is "prayer" (duʿāʾ), but metaphorically (majāz), it is used for mercy and honor. The distinction here is crucial: the Prophet ﷺ is singled out for it in the Qur'anic command, but the Salaf permitted it for his followers as a subsidiary.
- Root: ق-د-ر (q-d-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: The root denotes "measure," "estimation," or "decree." "Qadara" means to measure or determine the extent of something.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In Kalām, "qadar" is divine decree and measure; here, it is the human act of estimating the length of the month, either by completing the count or by astronomical calculation.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literally, "faqdirū lah" means "estimate for it," but the rhetorical usage in the Hadith is ambiguous—either it is a command to complete the count (istiqbāl al-ʿiddah) or to calculate by the lunar mansions (ḥisāb al-manāzil). The majority interpret it as the former, a metaphorical extension of "estimation" to "completion."
- Root: غ-م-ي (gh-m-y)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: The root means "to cover" or "to obscure," specifically referring to cloud cover that hides the crescent.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In legal contexts, it denotes the state of uncertainty due to atmospheric obstruction, which triggers the legal ruling of completing the month's count.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literally, "ghumma" is the covering, but metaphorically, it is the legal cause (ʿillah) for the obligation to complete thirty days.
- Sībawayh Rule: The Rule of Conditional Clauses (al-Sharṭ wa al-Jawāb) — In the Hadith "If you see the crescent, fast; if you see it, break the fast; if it is obscured for you, then estimate it," the conditional particle "idhā" introduces a protasis and apodosis. The apodosis "faqdirū lah" is a command (amr), and its ambiguity in meaning is resolved by the parallel narrations that explicitly state "complete the count of thirty," which Sībawayh would parse as a syntactic clarification (tafsīr) of the elliptical command.
chapters.translation:
I say: And if the meaning is sound, our companions (the Shāfiʿīs) differed concerning the prohibition of that—whether it is a prohibition of disapprobation (tanzīh), or of unlawfulness (taḥrīm), or merely a matter of etiquette (adab)—on three views. The most correct and most famous is that it is disliked with a dislike of purification (karāhah tanzīh), because it is a distinguishing mark (shiʿār) of the people of innovation (ahl al-bidʿah), and we have been forbidden from their distinguishing marks. The disliked (makrūh) is that which has a deliberate prohibition reported concerning it. They (the scholars) agreed that it is permissible to make other than the prophets followers of them in that matter, so one may say: "O Allāh, send blessings upon Muḥammad and upon the family of Muḥammad, his wives, his offspring, and his followers," because the Salaf (the righteous predecessors) did not prevent it, and we have been commanded with it in the tashahhud and elsewhere. Shaykh Abū Muḥammad al-Juwaynī, one of the leading scholars of our companions, said: "Salām (peace) is in the meaning of ṣalāh (blessings), and it is not singled out for other than the prophets, because Allāh the Exalted paired them together (in the Qur'anic verse), and it is not singled out for an absent person, nor is it said: 'So-and-so, ʿalayhi al-salām (upon him be peace).'" As for addressing a living or dead person with it, it is a Sunnah, so one says: "Al-salāmu ʿalaykum" (peace be upon you) or "ʿalayka" (upon you), or "Salāmun ʿalayka" (peace upon you) or "ʿalaykum" (upon you). And Allāh knows best.

# 
# (His statement ﷺ: "Faqdirū lah" (estimate it)) — And in one narration: "Faqdirū lah thirty." And in another narration: "When you see the crescent, fast; and when you see it, break the fast; and if it is obscured for you, then estimate it." And in another narration: "If it is obscured for you, then fast thirty days." And in another narration: "If it is obscured for you, then complete the number." And in another narration: "If the month is obscured for you, then count thirty." And in another narration: "If it is obscured for you, then count thirty." All these narrations are in the Book (Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim) in this order. And in a narration of al-Bukhārī: "If it is hidden from you, then complete the count of Shaʿbān as thirty." The scholars differed concerning the meaning of "faqdirū lah." A group of scholars said: Its meaning is "be straitened for it" and "estimate it as being under the cloud." Among those who said this is Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal and others who permit fasting the day of cloudiness for Ramaḍān, as we will mention, if Allāh wills. Ibn Surayj and a group—among them Muṭarrif ibn ʿAbd Allāh, Ibn Qutaybah, and others—said: Its meaning is "estimate it by the calculation of the lunar mansions (manāzil)." Mālik, al-Shāfiʿī, Abū Ḥanīfah, and the majority of the Salaf and the Khalaf (later scholars) held that its meaning is "estimate for it the completion of the number of thirty days." The linguists said: One says "qadartu al-shayʾ aqdiruhu wa aqdiruhu" and "qaddartuhu uqaddiruhu" with a single meaning, and it is from "taqdīr" (estimation). Al-Khaṭṭābī said: And from it is the saying of Allāh the Exalted: {«فَقَدَرْنَا فَنِعْمَ الْقَادِرُونَ»} ("Then We measured, and how excellent are the measurers") [Sūrat al-Mursalāt 77:23]. The majority argued with the aforementioned narrations: "Complete the count of thirty," which is an interpretation (tafsīr) of "faqdirū lah." For this reason, they are not combined in a single narration; rather, sometimes this is mentioned and sometimes that. And this is confirmed by the previous narration: "Faqdirū lah thirty." Al-Māzarī said: The majority of the jurists interpreted the statement of the Prophet ﷺ, "faqdirū lah," as meaning the completion of the count of thirty, as was explained in another hadith. They said: It is not permissible that the intended meaning be the calculation of the astrologers (munajjimīn), because if the people were burdened with it, it would be straitening for them, since only individuals know it, and the Sacred Law only addresses the people with what the masses of them know. And Allāh knows best. As for his statement ﷺ, "If it is obscured for you" (fa-in ghummā ʿalaykum), its meaning is: a cloud intervened between you and it. One says: "ghumma," "ughmiya," "ghummiya," and "ghummiya" with the doubling of the mīm and its lightening, and the ghayn is damma in both; and one says "ghubbiya" with the fatḥa on the ghayn and kasra on the bāʾ, and all are correct. And one says: "ghāmat al-samāʾ" (the sky clouded), "ghayyamat," "aghāmat," "taghayyamat," and "aghammat." In these hadiths there is evidence for the school of Mālik, al-Shāfiʿī, and the majority that it is not permissible to fast the day of doubt (yawm al-shakk) nor the thirtieth day.

# 
# [1079] His statement ﷺ: "When Ramaḍān comes, the gates of Paradise are opened, the gates of the Fire are closed, and the devils are chained." And in the other narration: "When it is Ramaḍān, the gates of mercy are opened, the gates of Hell are closed, and the devils are fettered." And in another narration: "When Ramaḍān enters." In this there is evidence for the correct and chosen school, which al-Bukhārī and the verifiers (muḥaqqiqūn) adopted, that it is permissible to say "Ramaḍān" without mentioning "the month" (shahr), with no dislike. In this issue there are three schools. A group said: "Ramaḍān" is not said on its own at all; rather, one says "the month of Ramaḍān." This is the saying of the companions of Mālik, and these claimed that "Ramaḍān" is one of the names of Allāh the Exalted, so it is not applied to other than Him except with a restriction. The majority of our companions and Ibn al-Bāqillānī said: If there is a contextual indicator (qarīnah) that diverts it to the month, then there is no dislike; otherwise, it is disliked. They said: So one says: "We fasted Ramaḍān," "We stood in prayer in Ramaḍān," "Ramaḍān is the best of months," and "It is recommended to seek the Night of Decree in the last ten of Ramaḍān," and similar to that, and there is no dislike in all of this. Rather, it is only disliked to say: "Ramaḍān came," "Ramaḍān entered," "Ramaḍān arrived," "I love Ramaḍān," and similar to that. The third school is the school of al-Bukhārī and the verifiers: there is no dislike in uttering "Ramaḍān" with or without a contextual indicator, and this school is the correct one.

# 
# The first two schools are corrupt, because dislike is only established by a legal prohibition (nahy al-sharʿ), and no prohibition has been established concerning it. Their saying that it is a name of Allāh the Exalted is not sound, and it has not been authenticated in anything, even if a weak athar (report) has come concerning it. The names of Allāh the Exalted are tawqīfī (restricted to divine revelation), not applied except with a sound proof. And even if it were established that it is a name, dislike would not necessarily follow from it. This hadith mentioned in the chapter is explicit in refuting the two schools. And this hadith has many parallels in the Ṣaḥīḥ concerning the utterance of "Ramaḍān" for the month without mentioning "the month." We have previously pointed out many of them in the Book of Faith (Kitāb al-Īmān) and elsewhere. And Allāh knows best. As for his statement ﷺ: "The gates of Paradise are opened, the gates of the Fire are closed, and the devils are chained," Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ, may Allāh have mercy on him, said: It is possible that it is on its literal meaning and reality (ḥaqīqah), and that the opening of the gates of Paradise, the closing of the gates of Hell, and the chaining of the devils are a sign of the entry of the month and a veneration of its sanctity. And the chaining would be to prevent them (the devils) from harming the believers and causing turmoil among them. He said: And it is possible that the intended meaning is metaphorical (majāz), and it is an indication of the abundance of reward and pardon, and that the devils' misguidance and harm are reduced so that they become as if they were chained. And it would be...

إلا أبا ثور فجوزه بعدل قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (الشهر هكذا وهكذا) وفي

رواية الشهر تسع وعشرون معناه أن الشهر قد يكون تسعا وعشرين وحاصله أن

الاعتبار بالهلال فقد يكون تاما ثلاثين وقد  يكون ناقصا تسعا وعشرين وقد لا

يرى الهلال فيجب إكمال العدد ثلاثين قالوا وقد يقع النقص متواليا
# 
# في شهرين وثلاثة وأربعة ولا يقع في أكثر من أربعة وفي هذا الحديث جواز

اعتماد الإشارة المفهمة في مثل هذا قوله (حدثنا زياد بن عبد الله البكائي)

هو بفتح الباء وتشديد الكاف
# 
# قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (إنا أمة أمية لا نكتب ولا نحسب الشهر هكذا

وهكذا وهكذا) قال العلماء أمية باقون على ما ولدتنا عليه الأمهات لا نكتب

ولا نحسب ومنه النبي الأمي وقيل هو نسبة
# 
# إلى الأم وصفتها لأن هذه صفة النساء غالبا قوله (سمع بن عمر رجلا يقول

الليلة النصف فقال له وما يدريك أن الليلة النصف) وذكر الحديث معناه أنك لا

تدري أن الليلة النصف أم لا لأن الشهر قد يكون تسعا وعشرين وأنت أردت أن

الليلة ليلة اليوم الذي بتمامه يتم النصف وهذا إنما يصح على تقدير تمامه

ولا تدري أنه تام أم لا قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (فإن غمي عليكم الشهر) هو

بضم الغين وكسر الميم مشددة ومخففة
# [1082] قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم
# 
# (لا تقدموا رمضان بصوم يوم ولا يومين إلا رجل كان يصوم صوما فليصمه) فيه

التصريح بالنهي عن استقبال رمضان بصوم يوم ويومين لمن لم يصادف عادة له أو

يصله بما قبله فإن لم يصله ولا صادف عادة فهو حرام هذا هو الصحيح في مذهبنا

لهذا الحديث وللحديث الآخر في سنن أبي داود وغيره إذا انتصف شعبان فلا صيام
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ص-ف-د (ṣ-f-d)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To bind, fetter, chain tightly; al-ṣafad (with fatḥa on fā') is the iron shackle (al-ghull, with ḍamma on ghayn).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological context, denotes the divine restraint of rebellious jinn from their customary mischief during Ramadan — a real, not merely metaphorical, act of divine power.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage here — physical binding; the metaphorical extension (majāz) is the devils' incapacity to tempt the faithful toward disobedience.
- Root: ق-د-ر (q-d-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To measure, determine, apportion; taqdīr is the act of fixing a measure or limit.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In legal-theological discourse, it signifies completing the count (istikmāl al-ʿiddah) to thirty days when the crescent is obscured — a legislative determination, not astronomical calculation.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): The literal sense is "measure it"; the juristic interpretation restricts it to completing the month's number, as clarified by the Prophet's own gloss in other narrations.
- Root: غ-م-ي (gh-m-y)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To be overcast, obscured; ghama and aghmā both mean the sky is covered by clouds, veiling the crescent.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In ḥadīth, it denotes the state of uncertainty regarding the crescent's visibility due to atmospheric obstruction, triggering the legal substitute of completing thirty days.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal meteorological sense; the legal ruling (ḥukm) attaches to the obstruction itself, not to the subjective perception.
- Sībawayh Rule: The Conditional Clause with Implied Protasis (al-sharṭ al-muḍmar) — In "فإن غم عليكم فاقدروا له" (if it is obscured for you, then measure it), the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) carries the imperative, and the particle "fa" marks the resultative link, requiring the completion of the month's count as the operative command.
chapters.translation:
I say: Their being chained from some things and not others, and from some people and not others — and this second narration is supported by the opening of the doors of mercy. And in another ḥadīth it came: "The rebellious devils are chained." Al-Qāḍī said: It is possible that the opening of the doors of Paradise is an expression for what Allah the Exalted opens for His servants of acts of obedience in this month, which do not occur in other months generally — such as fasting, night prayer, performing good deeds, and refraining from many violations. These are causes for entering Paradise and doors to it. Likewise, the closing of the doors of Hellfire and the chaining of the devils is an expression for what they (the believers) refrain from of violations. And the meaning of "ṣuffidat" (they were chained) is "they were fettered" (ghullilat). And al-ṣafad, with fatḥa on the fā', is the fetter (al-ghull), with ḍamma on the ghayn — and it is the meaning of "sulsilat" (they were bound in chains) in the other narration. This is the speech of al-Qāḍī, or containing expressions equivalent to his speech.

| Chapter: The Obligation of Fasting Ramadan upon Sighting the Crescent, and Breaking the Fast upon Sighting It, and That If It Is Obscured at Its Beginning or End, the Count of the Month Is Completed to Thirty Days |

[1080] His saying, peace and blessings be upon him: "Do not fast until you see the crescent, and do not break the fast until you see it. And if it is obscured for you, then measure it (faqdurū lahu)." And in one narration: "Then measure it as thirty." And in another narration: "When you see the crescent, then fast; and when you see it, then break the fast. And if it is obscured for you, then measure it." And in another narration: "And if it is obscured for you, then fast thirty days." And in another narration: "And if the month is obscured for you, then complete the number." And in another narration: "And if the month is obscured for you, then count thirty." And in another narration: "And if it is obscured for you, then count thirty." All these narrations are in the Book in this order. And in a narration of al-Bukhārī: "And if it is concealed from you, then complete the count of Shaʿbān as thirty."

The scholars differed over the meaning of "faqdurū lahu" (then measure it). A group of scholars said: Its meaning is "be straitened for it" and "estimate it as being under the cloud." Among those who held this view is Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal and others who permit fasting the day of cloudiness from Ramadan, as we shall mention, Allah willing. And Ibn Surayj and a group — among them Muṭarrif ibn ʿAbdillāh, Ibn Qutaybah, and others — said: Its meaning is "measure it by the calculation of the lunar mansions." And Mālik, al-Shāfiʿī, Abū Ḥanīfah, and the majority of the Salaf and Khalaf held that its meaning is "measure it as the completion of the number to thirty days." The linguists said: One says "qadartu al-shayʾ aqdiruhu and aqdaruhu, and qaddartuhu and qaddaruhu" — all with a single meaning, and it is from taqdīr (measuring). Al-Khaṭṭābī said: And from it is the saying of Allah the Exalted: {«فَقَدَرْنَا فَنِعْمَ الْقَادِرُونَ»} (Then We measured, and excellent are the Measurers) [al-Mursalāt 23]. And the majority adduced the aforementioned narrations: "Then complete the number to thirty" — and this is an interpretation of "faqdurū lahu." For this reason, the two do not come together in a single narration; rather, sometimes this is mentioned and sometimes that. And it is confirmed by the preceding narration: "Then measure it as thirty."

Al-Māzarī said: The majority of the jurists interpreted his saying, peace and blessings be upon him, "faqdurū lahu" as meaning the completion of the count to thirty, as he explained in another ḥadīth. They said: It is not permissible that the intended meaning be the calculation of the astrologers, because if people were burdened with it, it would be straitened upon them, since none know it except individuals. And the Sacred Law only addresses people with what their masses know. And Allah knows best.

As for his saying, peace and blessings be upon him, "fa-in ghummā ʿalaykum" (if it is obscured for you), its meaning is: a cloud intervenes between you and it. One says: ghama, ughmiya, ghummiya, and ghummī — with tashdīd of the mīm and its takhfīf, the ghayn being ḍamma in both — and one says: ghubbiya, with fatḥa on the ghayn and kasra on the bāʾ. All are correct. And one says: ghāmat al-samāʾ, ghayyamat, aghāmat, taghayyamat, and aghammat.

And in these ḥadīths there is an indication for the school of Mālik, al-Shāfiʿī, and the majority that it is not permissible to fast the day of doubt, nor the thirtieth day of Shaʿbān as Ramadan, when the night of the thirtieth is a night of cloudiness.

His saying, peace and blessings be upon him: "Fast upon its sighting, and break the fast upon its sighting" — the intended meaning is the sighting of some Muslims, and it is not a condition that every person see it. Rather, it suffices for all people the sighting of two just witnesses — and likewise one just witness, on the most correct (al-aṣaḥḥ) opinion — regarding fasting. As for breaking the fast (al-fiṭr), it is not permissible upon the testimony of a single just witness for the crescent of Shawwāl, according to all scholars, except Abū Thawr, who permitted it with one just witness.

His saying, peace and blessings be upon him: "The month is thus and thus" — and in one narration: "The month is twenty-nine" — its meaning is that the month may be twenty-nine. And its gist is that the consideration is the crescent: it may be complete at thirty, and it may be deficient at twenty-nine. And when the crescent is not seen, completing the number to thirty becomes obligatory. They said: And deficiency may occur consecutively in two, three, or four months, but it does not occur in more than four. And in this ḥadīth is the permissibility of relying on an intelligible gesture in such matters.

His saying: "Ḥaddathanā Ziyād ibn ʿAbdillāh al-Bakkāʾī" — it is with fatḥa on the bāʾ and tashdīd on the kāf.

His saying, peace and blessings be upon him: "We are an illiterate nation (umma ummiyya); we do not write, nor do we calculate. The month is thus, thus, and thus." The scholars said: "Ummiyya" means remaining upon what our mothers (ummahāt) bore us upon — we do not write nor calculate. And from it is "the illiterate Prophet (al-nabī al-ummī)." And it was said: It is a relative attribution to the mother (umm), and its description, because this is predominantly the attribute of women.

His saying: "He heard Ibn ʿUmar — a man said: 'Tonight is the middle (al-niṣf).' So he said to him: 'And what makes you know that tonight is the middle?'" — and he mentioned the ḥadīth. Its meaning is: You do not know whether tonight is the middle or not, because the month may be twenty-nine, and you intended that tonight is the night of the day by whose completion the half is completed. And this is only valid upon the assumption of its completion, and you do not know whether it is complete or not.

His saying, peace and blessings be upon him: "Fa-in ghummī ʿalaykum al-shahr" (if the month is obscured for you) — it is with ḍamma on the ghayn and kasra on the mīm, with tashdīd and takhfīf.

[1082] His saying, peace and blessings be upon him: "Do not precede Ramadan by fasting a day or two days, except a man who was accustomed to fasting a fast — let him fast it." In it is an explicit prohibition (taṣrīḥ) against receiving Ramadan with fasting a day or two days, for one who does not coincide with a habit of his, nor connects it to what precedes it. For if he does not connect it, nor does it coincide with a habit, then it is forbidden (ḥarām). This is the correct (al-ṣaḥīḥ) view in our school, due to this ḥadīth and the other ḥadīth in Sunan Abī Dāwūd and others: "When half of Shaʿbān passes, then there is no fasting."

chapters.title_en: The Day of Doubt, the Prophet's Oath of Abstinence, and the Lunar Months — Clarifications on Fasting, Sighting, and the Two Dawns
chapters.arabic_text:
حتى يكون رمضان فإن وصله بما قبله أو صادف عادة له فإن كانت عادته صوم يوم

الاثنين ونحوه فصادفه فصامه تطوعا بنية ذلك جاز لهذا الحديث وسواء في النهي

عندنا لمن لم يصادف عادته ولا وصله يوم الشك وغيره فيوم الشك داخل في النهي

وفيه مذاهب للسلف فيمن صامه تطوعا وأوجب صومه عن رمضان أحمد وجماعة بشرط
# 
# أن يكون هناك غيم والله أعلم
# [1083] قوله في حلفه صلى الله عليه وسلم (لا يدخل على أزواجه شهرا  ثم دخل

لما مضت تسع وعشرون ليلة ثم قال الشهر تسع وعشرون) وفي رواية فخرج الينا في

تسعة وعشرين فقلنا له انما اليوم تسعة وعشرون وفي رواية فخرج إلينا صباح

تسع وعشرين فقال
# 
# إن الشهر يكون تسعا وعشرين وفي رواية فلما مضى تسع وعشرون يوما غدا عليهم

أو راح قال القاضي رحمه الله تعالى معناه كله بعد تمام تسعة وعشرين يوما

يدل عليه رواية فلما مضى تسع وعشرون يوما وقوله صباح تسع وعشرين أي صباح

الليلة التي بعد تسعة وعشرين يوما وهي صبيحة ثلاثين ومعنى الشهر تسعة

وعشرون أنه قد يكون تسعة وعشرين كما صرح به في بعض هذا الروايات والله أعلم
#

| (باب بيان أن لكل بلد رؤيتهم)
# (وأنهم إذا رأوا الهلال ببلد لا يثبت حكمه لما بعد عنهم) فيه حديث كريب

عن بن عباس وهو ظاهر الدلالة للترجمة والصحيح عند أصحابنا أن الرؤية لا تعم

الناس بل تختص بمن قرب على مسافة لا تقصر فيها الصلاة وقيل إن اتفق المطلع

لزمهم وقيل إن اتفق الإقليم وإلا فلا وقال بعض أصحابنا تعم الرؤية في موضع

جميع أهل الأرض فعلى هذا نقول إنما لم يعمل بن عباس بخبر كريب لأنه شهادة

فلا تثبت بواحد لكن ظاهر حديثه أنه لم يرده لهذا وإنما رده لأن الرؤية لم

يثبت حكمها في حق البعيد
# [1087] قوله (واستهل علي رمضان) هو بضم التاء من استهل
#

| (باب بيان أنه لا اعتبار بكبر الهلال وصغره)
# (وأن الله تعالى أمده للرؤية فإن غم فليكمل ثلاثون) فيه حديث أبي البختري

عن بن عباس وهو ظاهر الدلالة للترجمة
# [1088] وقوله (تراءينا الهلال) أي تكلفنا النظر إلى جهته لنراه قوله (عن

بن عباس فقال إن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم مده للرؤية) هكذا هو في

بعضالنسخ وفي بعضها فقال إن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال إن الله مده

للرؤية وجميع النسخ متفقة على مده من غير ألف فيها وفي الرواية الثانية

فقال بن عباس قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه  وسلم إن الله قد أمده لرؤيته

هكذا هو في جميع النسخ أمده بألف في أوله قال القاضي قال بعضهم الوجه أن

يكون أمده بالتشديد من الإمداد ومده من الامتداد قال
# 
# القاضي والصواب عندي بقاء الرواية على وجهها ومعناه أطال مدته إلى الرؤية

يقال منه مد وأمد قال الله تعالى وإخوانهم يمدونهم في الغي قرئ بالوجهين أي

يطيلون لهم قال وقد يكون أمده من المدة التي جعلت له قال صاحب الأفعال

أمددتكها أي أعطيتكها قوله في الإسناد (عن أبي البختري) هو بفتح الموحدة

وإسكان الخاء المعجمة وفتح التاء واسمه سعيد بن فيروز ويقال بن عمران ويقال

بن أبي عمران الطائي توفي سنة ثلاث وثمانين عام الجماجم

| (باب بيان معنى قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم شهرا عيد لا 
# ينقصان)
# [1089] قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (شهرا عيد لا ينقصان رمضان وذو الحجة)

الأصح أن معناه لا ينقص أجرهما والثواب المرتب عليهما وإن نقص عددهما وقيل

معناه لا ينقصان جميعا في سنة واحدة غالبا وقيل لا ينقص ثواب ذي الحجة عن

ثواب رمضان لأن فيه المناسك حكاه الخطابي وهو ضعيف والأول هو الصواب

المعتمد ومعناه أن قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم من صام رمضان إيمانا واحتسابا

غفر له ما تقدم من ذنبه وقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم من قام رمضان إيمانا

واحتسابا وغير ذلك فكل هذه الفضائل تحصل سواء تم عدد رمضان أم نقص والله

أعلم
#

| باب بيان أن الدخول في الصوم يحصل بطلوع الفجر
