He said: 'Who is able to do this for me, O Prophet of Allah?'"—its meaning is: this last trait, namely not fleeing, is difficult for me. How can I attain it?

His statement ﷺ: "He has not fasted who fasts perpetually; he has not fasted who fasts perpetually"—its explanation has already preceded in this chapter. And thus it appears in the manuscripts, repeated twice, and in some of them three times.

His statement ﷺ: "The eye has sunken (hajamat) and become exhausted (nahakat)"—the meaning of "hajamat" is "it sank" (ghārat); and "nahakat" is with fatḥah on the nūn and fatḥah or kasrah on the hāʾ, with the tāʾ quiescent, meaning "it weakened." Some scholars recorded it as "nuhikt" with ḍammah on the nūn, kasrah on the hāʾ, and fatḥah on the tāʾ, meaning "you have been emaciated" (ḍanayta). This is the apparent meaning of al-Qāḍī's statement.

His statement: "And the soul is exhausted (wanafahat)"—with fatḥah on the nūn and kasrah on the fāʾ, meaning "it is wearied."

His statement: "Sufyān ibn ʿUyaynah narrated to us from ʿAmr, from ʿAmr ibn Aws"—the first ʿAmr is Ibn Dīnār, as clarified in the second narration.

His statement: "So a cushion was thrown to him"—in it is the honoring of guests, the eminent, and people of virtue. His statement: "Then he sat on the ground, and the cushion remained between me and him"—in it is an exposition of the Prophet's ﷺ humility (tawāḍuʿ) and his avoidance of preferring himself exclusively over his companion and fellow-sitter.

His statement: "Salīm ibn Ḥayyān narrated to us"—with fatḥah on the sīn and kasrah on the lām. It has already preceded in the introduction of the book that there is no other Salīm with fatḥah on the sīn in Ṣaḥīḥ (Muslim) besides him.

His statement: "Saʿīd ibn Mīnāʾ"—it is with both long and short alif (madd and qaṣr), and the short form is more famous.

| Chapter: The Recommendation of Fasting Three Days of Every Month, and the Fasting of the Day of ʿArafah, ʿĀshūrāʾ, Monday, and Thursday |

[1161] In it is the hadith of ʿĀʾishah (may Allah be pleased with her) that the Prophet ﷺ used to fast three days of every month, and he did not care from which days of the month he fasted. And the hadith of ʿImrān ibn Ḥuṣayn that the Prophet ﷺ said to him—or said to a man while he was listening—"O so-and-so, did you fast from the middle (surrah) of this month?" He said, "No." He said: "Then when you break your fast, fast two days." Thus it appears in all manuscripts: "from the middle (surrah) of this month" with a hāʾ after the rāʾ. Muslim then mentioned after it the hadith of Abū Qatādah, then the hadith of ʿImrān also regarding the end (sarar) of Shaʿbān. This is an explicit statement from Muslim that the first narration of ʿImrān is with hāʾ and the second with rāʾ. For this reason, he distinguished between them and included the first with the hadith of ʿĀʾishah as an interpretation of it, as if he were saying: It is recommended that the three days be from the middle (surrah) of the month, i.e., its center. This is unanimously agreed upon as recommended—namely, that the three days be the white days (ayyām al-bīḍ), which are the thirteenth, fourteenth, and fifteenth. A hadith has come regarding this in Jāmiʿ al-Tirmidhī and others. It was also said they are the twelfth, thirteenth, and fourteenth. The scholars said: Perhaps the Prophet ﷺ did not persist upon three specific days lest it be thought they are obligatory (taʿyīn), and he pointed through "the middle of the month" and the hadith of al-Tirmidhī regarding the white days to their virtue.

[1162] His statement: "From ʿAbdullāh ibn Maʿbad al-Zamānī"—it is with a kasrah on the zāy, then a shaddah on the mīm. His statement: "From ʿAbdullāh ibn Maʿbad al-Zamānī, from Abū Qatādah: A man came to the Prophet ﷺ and said, 'How do you fast?'"—thus it appears in most manuscripts: "from Abū Qatādah: a man came," and upon this, "a man" (rajul) is read in the nominative (rafʿ) as the predicate of an omitted subject, i.e., "the matter and affair is: a man came to the Prophet ﷺ and said." Some manuscripts have corrected it to "that a man came" (anna rajulan atā), and the cause of this correction was the perceived obscurity of the first construction's coherence—yet it is coherent as I have stated, so it is not permissible to alter it.

chapters.title_en: The Fasting of One Who Fasts a Day and Breaks His Fast Two Days, and the Fasting of the Day of ʿArafah, and the Three Days of Each Month, and the Fasting of Shaʿbān

والله أعلم قوله (رجل أتى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال كيف تصوم فغضب

رسول الله
# 
# صلى الله عليه وسلم

| (قال العلماء سبب غضبه صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه كره 
# مسألته لأنه يحتاج إلى أن يجيبه ويخشى من جوابه مفسدة وهي أنه ربما اعتقد

السائل وجوبه أو استقله أو اقتصر عليه وكان يقتضي حاله  أكثر منه وإنما

اقتصر عليه النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لشغله بمصالح المسلمين وحقوقهم وحقوق

أزواجه وأضيافه والوافدين إليه لئلا يقتدي به كل أحد فيؤدي إلى الضرر في حق

بعضهم وكان حق السائل أن يقول كم أصوم أو كيف أصوم فيخص السؤال بنفسه

ليجيبه بما تقتضيه حاله كما أجاب غيره بمقتضى أحوالهم والله أعلم قوله (كيف

من يصوم يوما ويفطر يومين قال وددت أني طوقت ذاك) قال القاضي قيل معناه

وددت أن أمتي تطوقه لأنه صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يطيقه وأكثر منه وكان

يواصل ويقول إني لست كأحدكم إني أبيت عند ربي يطعمني ويسقيني قلت ويؤيد هذا

التأويل قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم في الرواية الثانية ليت أن الله قوانا

لذلك أو يقال إنما قاله لحقوق نسائه وغيرهن من المسلمين المتعلقين به

والقاصدين إليه قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (صيام يوم عرفة أحتسب على الله أن

يكفر السنة)
# 
# التي قبله والسنة التي بعده) معناه يكفر ذنوب صائمه في السنتين قالوا

والمراد بها الصغائر وسبق بيان مثل هذا في تكفير الخطايا بالوضوء وذكرنا

هناك أنه إن لم تكن صغائر يرجى التخفيف من الكبائر فإن لم يكن رفعت درجات

قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم في صيام الدهر (لا صام ولا أفطر) قد سبق بيانه

قوله في هذا الحديث من رواية شعبة (قال وسئل عن صوم يوم الاثنين والخميس

فسكتنا عن ذكر الخميس لما نراه وهما) ضبطوا نراه بفتح النون وضمها وهما

صحيحان قال القاضي
# 
# عياض رحمه الله إنما تركه وسكت عنه لقوله فيه ولدت وفيه بعثت أو أنزل علي

وهذا إنما هو في يوم الاثنين كما جاء في الروايات الباقيات يوم الاثنين دون

ذكر الخميس فلما كان في رواية شعبة ذكر الخميس تركه مسلم لأنه رآه وهما قال

القاضي ويحتمل صحة رواية شعبة ويرجع الوصف بالولادة والإنزال إلى الاثنين

دون الخميس وهذا الذي قاله القاضي متعين والله أعلم قال القاضي واختلفوا في

تعيين هذه الأيام الثلاثة المستحبة من كل شهر ففسره  جماعة من الصحابة

والتابعين بأيام البيض وهي الثالث عشر والرابع عشر والخامس عشر منهم عمر بن

الخطاب وبن مسعود وأبو ذر وبه قال أصحاب الشافعي واختار النخعي وآخرون آخر

الشهر واختار آخرون ثلاثة من أوله منهم الحسن واختارت عائشة وآخرون صيام

السبت والأحد والاثنين من شهر ثم الثلاثاء والأربعاء والخميس من الشهر الذي

بعده واختار آخرون الاثنين والخميس وفي حديث رفعه بن عمر أول اثنين في

الشهر وخميسان بعده وعن أم سلمة أول خميس والاثنين بعده ثم الاثنين وقيل

أول يوم من الشهر والعاشر والعشرين وقيل إنه صيام مالك بن أنس وروي عنه

كراهة صوم أيام البيض وقال بن شعبان المالكي أول يوم من الشهر والحادي عشر

والحادي وعشرون والله أعلم
#

| (باب صوم شهر شعبان
# [1161] فيه (عمران بن الحصين أن رسول
# الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال له أو لآخر أصمت من سرر شعبان قال لا قال

فإذا أفطرت فصم يومين) وفي رواية فإذا أفطرت من رمضان فصم يومين مكانه

ضبطوا سرر بفتح السين وكسرها وحكى القاضي ضمها قال وهو جمع سرة ويقال أيضا

سرار وسرار بفتح السين وكسرها وكله من الاستسرار قال الأوزاعي وأبو عبيد

وجمهور العلماء من أهل اللغة والحديث والغريب المراد بالسرر آخر الشهر سميت

بذلك لاستسرار القمر فيها قال القاضي قال أبو عبيد وأهل اللغة السرر آخر

الشهر قال وأنكر بعضهم هذا وقال المراد وسط الشهر قال وسرار كل شئ وسطه قال

هذا القائل لم يأت في صيام آخر الشهر ندب فلا يحمل الحديث عليه بخلاف وسطه

فإنها أيام البيض وروى أبو داود عن الأوزاعي سرره أوله ونقل الخطابي عن

الأوزاعي سرره آخره قال البيهقي في السنن الكبير بعد أن روى الروايتين عن

الأوزاعي الصحيح آخره ولم يعرف الأزهري أن سرره أوله قال الهروي والذي

يعرفه الناس أن سرره آخره ويعضد من فسره بوسطه الرواية السابقة في الباب

قبله سرة هذا الشهر وسرارة الوادي وسطه وخياره)
# 
# وقال بن السكيت سرار الأرض أكرمها ووسطها وسرار كل شئ  وسطه وأفضله فقد

يكون سرار الشهر من هذا قال القاضي والأشهر أن المراد آخر الشهر كما قاله

أبو عبيد والأكثرون وعلى هذا يقال هذا الحديث مخالف للأحاديث الصحيحة في

النهي عن تقديم رمضان بصوم يوم ويومين ويجاب عنه بما أجاب المازري وغيره

وهو أن هذا الرجل كان معتاد الصيام آخر الشهر أو نذره فتركه بخوفه من

الدخول في النهي عن تقدم رمضان فبين له النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أن الصوم

المعتاد لا يدخل في النهي وإنما ننهى عن غير المعتاد والله أعلم قوله صلى

الله عليه وسلم في رواية محمد بن مثنى (إذا أفطرت رمضان) هكذا هو في جميع
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ط-و-ق (ṭ-w-q)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning is "capacity" or "ability to bear a burden," from the notion of a collar (ṭāq) encircling the neck, implying what one can endure.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological usage, it denotes the moral and physical capacity (ṭāqah) granted by God for an act of obedience, often linked to divine facilitation.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense is "to be encircled" (as with a collar); metaphorically, it signifies being charged with a task within one's power, as in the Quranic {«لَا يُكَلِّفُ اللَّهُ نَفْسًا إِلَّا وُسْعَهَا»}.
- Sībawayh Rule: Rule of Taʿlīq (Suspension of the Verb's Operation) — The verb "waddadtu" (I wished) governs a nominal clause in the accusative, but here it is suspended from direct operation due to the semantic nuance of longing, allowing the clause to function as its object in a periphrastic manner.
chapters.translation:
And God knows best. His saying — the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace — (A man came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: "How do you fast?" So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, became angry). The scholars said: The cause of his anger, may God bless him and grant him peace, was that he disliked the man's question because he would need to answer him, and he feared from his answer a corruption — namely, that the questioner might come to believe its obligation, or deem it insignificant, or limit himself to it, while his state required more than that. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, only limited himself to it due to his preoccupation with the interests of the Muslims, their rights, the rights of his wives, his guests, and those who came to him as delegates, lest everyone imitate him and this lead to harm regarding some of them. The questioner's right was to say: "How much should I fast?" or "How should I fast?" — so that he would specify the question to himself, and he would answer him according to what his state required, just as he answered others according to their states. And God knows best.

His saying — the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace — (How about one who fasts a day and breaks his fast two days? He said: "I wish that I were given the capacity (ṭūwiqtu) for that"). Al-Qāḍī said: It was said its meaning is: "I wish that my community were given the capacity for it," because he, may God bless him and grant him peace, was able to bear it and more than it, and he used to practice continuous fasting (wiṣāl) and say: "I am not like any of you; I spend the night at my Lord's, Who feeds me and gives me to drink." I say: This interpretation is supported by his saying, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the second narration: "Would that God had given us strength for that." Or it may be said: He only said this due to the rights of his wives and other Muslims connected to him and those seeking him.

His saying, may God bless him and grant him peace: (Fasting the day of ʿArafah — I reckon upon God that He expiates the year before it and the year after it) — its meaning is: it expiates the sins of the one who fasts it in the two years. They said: What is meant by it is the minor sins (ṣaghāʾir). The clarification of something like this has preceded regarding the expiation of sins by ablution (wuḍūʾ), and we mentioned there that if there are no minor sins, relief from the major sins (kabāʾir) is hoped for; and if there are none, one's ranks are elevated.

His saying, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding perpetual fasting (ṣiyām al-dahr): (He has not fasted, nor has he broken his fast) — its clarification has preceded.

His saying in this ḥadīth from the narration of Shuʿbah: (He said: And he was asked about fasting Monday and Thursday, and we remained silent about mentioning Thursday because we saw it as an error (wahm)). They vocalized "narāhu" with the opening of the nūn and its ḍammah — both are correct. Al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ, may God have mercy on him, said: He only omitted it and remained silent about it because of his saying regarding it: "In it I was born, and in it I was sent" or "it was revealed to me." This is only for Monday, as came in the remaining narrations — Monday, without mentioning Thursday. So when Thursday was mentioned in Shuʿbah's narration, Muslim omitted it because he saw it as an error. Al-Qāḍī said: And it is possible that Shuʿbah's narration is sound, and the description of birth and revelation reverts to Monday, not Thursday. This is what al-Qāḍī said, and it is the determined view. And God knows best.

Al-Qāḍī said: They differed regarding the specification of these three recommended days of each month. A group of the Companions and the Followers interpreted them as the white days (ayyām al-bīḍ) — namely, the thirteenth, fourteenth, and fifteenth. Among them were ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, Ibn Masʿūd, and Abū Dharr. The companions of al-Shāfiʿī held this view. Al-Nakhaʿī and others chose the end of the month. Others chose three from its beginning, among them al-Ḥasan. ʿĀʾishah and others chose fasting Saturday, Sunday, and Monday of one month, then Tuesday, Wednesday, and Thursday of the following month. Others chose Monday and Thursday. In a ḥadīth raised (marfūʿ) by Ibn ʿUmar: "The first Monday of the month, and two Thursdays after it." And from Umm Salamah: "The first Thursday, and the Monday after it, then the Monday." And it was said: The first day of the month, the tenth, and the twentieth. And it was said: That is the fasting of Mālik ibn Anas, and dislike (karāhah) of fasting the white days was narrated from him. Ibn Shaʿbān al-Mālikī said: The first day of the month, the eleventh, and the twenty-first. And God knows best.

[Chapter: The Fasting of the Month of Shaʿbān]

[1161] In it: (ʿImrān ibn al-Ḥuṣayn that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him — or to another: "Did you fast the latter part (sarar) of Shaʿbān?" He said: "No." He said: "So when you break your fast, fast two days.") And in another narration: "So when you break your fast from Ramaḍān, fast two days in its place." They vocalized "sarar" with the opening of the sīn and its kasrah, and al-Qāḍī narrated its ḍammah. He said: It is the plural of "surrah," and it is also said "sarār" and "sirār" — with the opening of the sīn and its kasrah — and all of it derives from concealment (istisrār). Al-Awzāʿī, Abū ʿUbayd, and the majority of scholars of language, ḥadīth, and rare expressions said: What is meant by "al-sarar" is the end of the month; it was so named because of the moon's concealment (istisrār) during it. Al-Qāḍī said: Abū ʿUbayd and the people of language said: "al-sarar" is the end of the month. He said: And some denied this and said: What is meant is the middle of the month. He said: And "sarār" of everything is its middle. This speaker said: No recommendation has come regarding fasting the end of the month, so the ḥadīth should not be carried upon it, unlike its middle, for those are the white days. Abū Dāwūd narrated from al-Awzāʿī: "Its sarar is its beginning." Al-Khaṭṭābī transmitted from al-Awzāʿī: "Its sarar is its end." Al-Bayhaqī said in al-Sunan al-Kabīr, after narrating both narrations from al-Awzāʿī: "The correct one is its end, and al-Azharī did not know that its sarar is its beginning." Al-Harawī said: "What the people know is that its sarar is its end." And what supports the one who interpreted it as its middle is the preceding narration in the chapter before it: "The navel (surrah) of this month," and "the sarār of the valley is its middle and its best part." Ibn al-Sikkīt said: "The sarār of the land is its most honorable and middle part, and the sarār of everything is its middle and its best." So it may be that the sarār of the month is from this. Al-Qāḍī said: And the more famous view is that what is meant is the end of the month, as Abū ʿUbayd and the majority said. Upon this, it is said: This ḥadīth contradicts the sound ḥadīths prohibiting the anticipation of Ramaḍān by fasting a day or two days. It is answered by what al-Māzarī and others answered: This man was accustomed to fasting at the end of the month, or he had vowed it, and he abandoned it out of fear of entering into the prohibition of anticipating Ramaḍān. So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, clarified to him that habitual fasting does not enter into the prohibition; we only prohibit what is not habitual. And God knows best.

His saying, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the narration of Muḥammad ibn al-Muthannā: (When you break your fast from Ramaḍān) — thus it is in all [copies].

chapters.title_en: Section 464 — On the Virtue of Fasting in al-Muḥarram, the Six Days of Shawwāl, and the Night of Decree (Laylat al-Qadr)
chapters.arabic_text:
النسخ وهو صحيح أي أفطرت من رمضان كما في الرواية التي قبلها وحذف لفظة من

في هذه الرواية وهي مراده كقوله تعالى واختار موسى قومه أي من قومه والله

أعلم

| (باب فضل صوم المحرم
# [1163] قوله (عن حميد بن عبد الرحمن
# الحميري عن أبي هريرة) اعلم أن أبا هريرة يروي عنه اثنان كل واحد منهما

حميد بن عبد الرحمن أحدهما هذا الحميري والثاني حميد بن عبد الرحمن بن عوف)
# 
# الزهري قال الحميدي في الجمع بين الصحيحين كل ما في البخاري ومسلم حميد

بن عبد الرحمن عن أبي هريرة فهو الزهري إلا في هذا الحديث خاصة حديث أفضل

الصيام بعد شهر رمضان شهر الله المحرم وأفضل الصلاة بعد الفريضة صلاة الليل

فإن راويه حميد بن عبد الرحمن الحميري عن أبي هريرة وهذا الحديث لم يذكره

البخاري في صحيحه ولا ذكر للحميري في البخاري أصلا ولا في مسلم إلا في هذا

الحديث قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (أفضل الصيام بعد رمضان شهر الله المحرم)

تصريح بأنه أفضل الشهور للصوم وقد سبق الجواب عن إكثار النبي صلى الله عليه

وسلم من صوم شعبان دون المحرم وذكرنا فيه جوابين أحدهما لعله إنما علم فضله

في آخر حياته والثاني لعله كان يعرض فيه أعذار من سفر أو مرض أو غيرهما

قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (وأفضل  الصلاة بعد الفريضة صلاة الليل) فيه دليل

لما اتفق العلماء عليه أن تطوع الليل أفضل من تطوع النهار وفيه حجة لأبي

إسحاق المروزي من أصحابنا ومن وافقه أن صلاة الليل أفضل من السنن الراتبة

وقال أكثر أصحابنا الرواتب أفضل لأنها تشبه الفرائض والأول أقوى وأوفق

للحديث والله أعلم
#

| باب استحباب صوم ستة أيام من شوال اتباعا لرمضان
# [1164] قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (من صام رمضان ثم أتبعه ستا من شوال كان

كصيام الدهر) فيه دلالة صريحة لمذهب الشافعي وأحمد وداود وموافقيهم في

استحباب صوم هذه الستة وقال مالك وأبو حنيفة يكره ذلك قال مالك في الموطأ

ما رأيت أحدا من أهل العلم يصومها قالوا فيكره لئلا يظن وجوبه ودليل

الشافعي وموافقيه هذا الحديث الصحيح الصريح وإذا ثبتت السنة لا تترك لترك

بعض الناس أو أكثرهم أو كلهم لها وقولهم قد يظن وجوبها ينتقض بصوم عرفة

وعاشوراء وغيرهما من الصوم المندوب قال أصحابنا والأفضل أن تصام الستة

متوالية عقب يوم الفطر فإن فرقها أو أخرها عن أوائل شوال إلى أواخره حصلت

فضيلة المتابعة لأنه يصدق أنه أتبعه ستا من شوال قال العلماء وإنما كان ذلك

كصيام الدهر لأن الحسنة بعشر أمثالها فرمضان بعشرة أشهر والستة بشهرين وقد

جاء هذا في حديث مرفوع في كتاب النسائي وقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (ستا من

شوال) صحيح ولو قال ستة بالهاء جاز أيضا قال أهل اللغة يقال صمنا خمسا

وستا)
# 
# وخمسة وستة وإنما يلتزمون الهاء في المذكر إذا ذكروه بلفظه صريحا فيقولون

صمنا ستة أيام ولا يجوز ست أيام فإذا حذفوا الأيام جاز الوجهان ومما جاء

حذف الهاء فيه من المذكر إذا لم يذكر بلفظه قوله تعالى يتربصن بأنفسهن

أربعة أشهر وعشرا أي عشرة أيام وقد بسطت إيضاح هذه المسألة في تهذيب

الأسماء واللغات وفي شرح المهذب والله أعلم

| (باب فضل ليلة القدر والحث على طلبها وبيان محلها 
# وارجاء أوقات طلبها قال العلماء وسميت ليلة القدر لما يكتب فيها للملائكة

من الأقدار والأرزاق والآجال  التي تكون في تلك السنة كقوله تعالى فيها يفرق

كل أمر حكيم وقوله تعالى تنزل الملائكة والروح فيها بإذن ربهم من كل أمر

ومعناه يظهر للملائكة ما سيكون فيها ويأمرهم بفعل ما هو من وظيفتهم وكل ذلك

مما سبق علم الله تعالى به وتقديره له وقيل سميت ليلة القدر لعظم قدرها

وشرفها وأجمع من يعتد به على وجودها ودوامها إلى آخر الدهر للأحاديث

الصحيحة المشهورة قال القاضي واختلفوا في محلها فقال جماعة هي منتقلة تكون

في سنة في ليلة وفي سنة أخرى في ليلة أخرى وهكذا وبهذا يجمع بين الأحاديث

ويقال كل حديث جاء بأحد أوقاتها ولا تعارض فيها قال ونحو هذا قول مالك

والثوري وأحمد وإسحاق وأبي ثور وغيرهم قالوا وإنما تنتقل في العشر الأواخر

من رمضان وقيل بل في كله وقيل إنها معينة فلا تنتقل أبدا بل هي ليلة معينة

في جميع السنين لا تفارقها وعلى هذا قيل في السنة كلها وهو قول بن مسعود

وأبي حنيفة وصاحبيه وقيل بل في شهر رمضان كله وهو قول بن عمر وجماعة من

الصحابة وقيل بل في العشر الوسط والأواخر وقيل في العشر الأواخر وقيل تختص

بأوتار العشر وقيل بأشفاعها كما في حديث أبي سعيد وقيل بل في ثلاث وعشرين

أو سبع وعشرين وهو قول بن عباس وقيل تطلب في ليلة سبع عشرة)
# 
# أو إحدى وعشرين أو ثلاث وعشرين وحكي عن على وبن مسعود وقيل ليلة ثلاث

وعشرين وهو قول كثيرين من الصحابة وغيرهم وقيل ليلة أربع وعشرين وهو محكى

عن بلال وبن عباس والحسن وقتادة وقيل ليلة سبع وعشرين وهو قول جماعة من

الصحابة وقيل سبع عشرة وهو محكي عن زيد بن أرقم وبن مسعود أيضا وقيل تسع

عشرة وحكي عن بن مسعود أيضا وحكي عن علي أيضا وقيل آخر ليلة من الشهر قال
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ن-س-خ (n-s-kh)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To abrogate, erase, or supersede; here used in the technical sense of textual variant transmission (riwāyah), not legal abrogation.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In ḥadīth transmission, refers to the omission of a word in one narration while the meaning is retained via ellipsis (ḥadhf).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: copying/erasing; metaphorical: the narrator's omission of a preposition (min) without altering the intended sense, as in Quranic usage.
- Root: ف-ض-ل (f-ḍ-l)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Superiority, excellence, surplus; the root denotes an increase in merit or rank.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In Kalām, faḍl signifies a divinely granted excellence distinguishing an act or time above others, not inherent to the act itself but by divine decree.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: excess; metaphorical: virtue (faḍīlah) as a relative distinction, as in "afḍal al-ṣiyām" (the most virtuous fasting).
- Root: ق-د-ر (q-d-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Measure, decree, power; the root conveys both divine preordination and the specific determination of affairs.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological context, qadr denotes God's eternal knowledge and predetermination of all events; Laylat al-Qadr is named for the decreeing of annual affairs.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: measuring; metaphorical: the night's immense honor (sharaf) or the divine apportioning of destinies, as in {«فِيهَا يُفْرَقُ كُلُّ أَمْرٍ حَكِيمٍ»}.
- Sībawayh Rule: Ellipsis of the Preposition (Ḥadhf al-Jār) — When a verb or noun governs an object via a preposition, the preposition may be omitted if the meaning remains unambiguous, as in "wa-khtāra Mūsā qawmahu" (i.e., min qawmihi). This rule governs the transmission variant "afṭartu" without "min" in the ḥadīth.
chapters.translation:
I say: The abrogation (al-naskh) — and it is sound, meaning "I broke my fast in Ramaḍān," as in the preceding narration, with the word "min" (from) omitted in this transmission. This omission is permissible, as God Most High said: {«وَاخْتَارَ مُوسَى قَوْمَهُ»} (And Moses chose his people), meaning "from his people." And God knows best.

---

**Chapter: On the Virtue of Fasting in al-Muḥarram**

[1163] His saying (concerning Ḥumayd ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Ḥimyarī, from Abū Hurayrah): Know that two narrators named Ḥumayd ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān transmit from Abū Hurayrah — one is this al-Ḥimyarī, and the second is Ḥumayd ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf al-Zuhrī. Al-Ḥumaydī said in *al-Jamʿ bayn al-Ṣaḥīḥayn*: Every instance in al-Bukhārī and Muslim of "Ḥumayd ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān from Abū Hurayrah" is al-Zuhrī, except in this specific ḥadīth — "The most virtuous fasting after the month of Ramaḍān is the month of God, al-Muḥarram, and the most virtuous prayer after the obligatory is the night prayer" — for its narrator is Ḥumayd ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Ḥimyarī from Abū Hurayrah. This ḥadīth was not recorded by al-Bukhārī in his Ṣaḥīḥ, nor is al-Ḥimyarī mentioned in al-Bukhārī at all, nor in Muslim except in this ḥadīth.

His saying, peace and blessings be upon him: "The most virtuous fasting after Ramaḍān is the month of God, al-Muḥarram" — this is an explicit declaration that it is the most virtuous of months for fasting. We have already answered the question of why the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, fasted so much in Shaʿbān rather than al-Muḥarram, and we mentioned two answers: first, perhaps he only learned of its virtue late in his life; second, perhaps he encountered obstacles of travel, illness, or other matters during it.

His saying, peace and blessings be upon him: "And the most virtuous prayer after the obligatory is the night prayer" — in this is evidence for what the scholars have agreed upon: that voluntary night prayer is superior to voluntary day prayer. It also serves as proof for Abū Isḥāq al-Marwazī among our companions (the Shāfiʿīs) and those who agree with him that night prayer is superior to the regular Sunnah prayers (al-sunan al-rawātib). However, most of our companions hold that the regular Sunnah prayers are superior because they resemble the obligatory prayers. The first view is stronger and more consistent with the ḥadīth. And God knows best.

---

**Chapter: On the Recommendation of Fasting Six Days of Shawwāl Following Ramaḍān**

[1164] His saying, peace and blessings be upon him: "Whoever fasts Ramaḍān and then follows it with six days of Shawwāl, it is as if he fasted the entire year" — in this is an explicit indication of the school of al-Shāfiʿī, Aḥmad, Dāwūd, and those who agree with them regarding the recommendation of fasting these six days. Mālik and Abū Ḥanīfah said it is disliked (makrūh). Mālik said in *al-Muwaṭṭaʾ*: "I have not seen any of the people of knowledge fasting them." They said it is disliked lest people assume it is obligatory. The evidence of al-Shāfiʿī and his supporters is this authentic and explicit ḥadīth. When the Sunnah is established, it is not abandoned due to the abandonment of some people, or most of them, or all of them. Their claim that "people might assume it is obligatory" is refuted by the fasting of ʿArafah, ʿĀshūrāʾ, and other recommended fasts.

Our companions said: It is best to fast the six days consecutively immediately after the day of Fiṭr. If one separates them or delays them from the beginning of Shawwāl to its end, the virtue of following (Ramaḍān) is still attained, because it is truly said that he "followed it with six days of Shawwāl." The scholars said: This is only "like fasting the entire year" because a good deed is multiplied tenfold — so Ramaḍān equals ten months, and the six days equal two months. This has been reported in a marfūʿ ḥadīth in the book of al-Nasāʾī.

His saying, peace and blessings be upon him: "Sittan min Shawwāl" (six [feminine] of Shawwāl) is correct, and if one said "Sittah" (with the tāʾ marbūṭah) it is also permissible. The linguists said: One says "ṣimnā khamsan wa-sittan" (we fasted five and six) and "khamsah wa-sittah" (five and six). They only commit to the tāʾ marbūṭah in the masculine when it is mentioned explicitly, saying "ṣimnā sittata ayyām" (we fasted six days), and it is not permissible to say "sittu ayyām." But when "days" is omitted, both forms are permissible. Among the instances where the tāʾ is omitted from the masculine when not mentioned explicitly is the saying of God Most High: {«يَتَرَبَّصْنَ بِأَنفُسِهِنَّ أَرْبَعَةَ أَشْهُرٍ وَعَشْرًا»} (They shall wait for themselves four months and ten), meaning ten days. I have elaborated on this issue in *Tahdhīb al-Asmāʾ wa al-Lughāt* and in *Sharḥ al-Muhadhdhab*. And God knows best.

---

**Chapter: On the Virtue of the Night of Decree (Laylat al-Qadr), the Encouragement to Seek It, the Clarification of Its Location, and the Deferral of Its Times of Seeking**

The scholars said: It was named the Night of Decree (Laylat al-Qadr) because of what is written therein for the angels — the decrees (aqdār), provisions (arzāq), and lifespans (ājāl) that will occur in that year, as God Most High said: {«فِيهَا يُفْرَقُ كُلُّ أَمْرٍ حَكِيمٍ»} (In it is distinguished every wise matter), and His saying: {«تَنَزَّلُ الْمَلَائِكَةُ وَالرُّوحُ فِيهَا بِإِذْنِ رَبِّهِم مِّن كُلِّ أَمْرٍ»} (The angels and the Spirit descend therein by the permission of their Lord, with every matter). Its meaning is that what will occur in it is made manifest to the angels, and they are commanded to execute what is their function. All of this is from what God's knowledge has preceded and His decree has determined. It was also said: It was named the Night of Decree for the greatness of its measure (qadr) and its honor.

Those whose opinion is counted have unanimously agreed on its existence and its continuity until the end of time, based on the authentic and well-known ḥadīths. Al-Qāḍī said: They differed regarding its location. A group said it moves — being on one night in one year and another night in another year, and so on. By this, the ḥadīths are reconciled, and it is said that every ḥadīth that came specifying one of its times is valid, with no contradiction among them. He said: This is the view of Mālik, al-Thawrī, Aḥmad, Isḥāq, Abū Thawr, and others. They said: It only moves within the last ten nights of Ramaḍān. It was also said: Rather, within all of it.

It was said: It is fixed and never moves — rather, it is a specific night in all years, never departing from it. Based on this, it was said to be within the entire year, which is the view of Ibn Masʿūd, Abū Ḥanīfah, and his two companions. It was said: Rather, within all of Ramaḍān, which is the view of Ibn ʿUmar and a group of the Companions. It was said: Rather, in the middle and last ten. It was said: In the last ten. It was said: It is specific to the odd nights of the last ten. It was said: To its even nights, as in the ḥadīth of Abū Saʿīd. It was said: Rather, on the twenty-third or twenty-seventh, which is the view of Ibn ʿAbbās. It was said: It is sought on the seventeenth, twenty-first, or twenty-third night — narrated from ʿAlī and Ibn Masʿūd. It was said: The twenty-third night, which is the view of many of the Companions and others. It was said: The twenty-fourth night, narrated from Bilāl, Ibn ʿAbbās, al-Ḥasan, and Qatādah. It was said: The twenty-seventh night, which is the view of a group of the Companions. It was said: The seventeenth, narrated from Zayd ibn Arqam and also Ibn Masʿūd. It was said: The nineteenth, narrated from Ibn Masʿūd as well, and also from ʿAlī. It was said: The last night of the month. He said: ...

chapters.title_en: The Night of Decree (Laylat al-Qadr) — Clarification of Its Abrogation, Linguistic Variants, and Jurisprudential Rulings
chapters.arabic_text:
القاضي وشذ قوم فقالوا رفعت لقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم حين تلاحا الرجلان

فرفعت وهذا غلط من هؤلاء الشاذين لأن آخر الحديث يرد عليهم فإنه صلى  الله

عليه وسلم قال فرفعت وعسى أن يكون خيرا لكم فالتمسوها في السبع والتسع هكذا

هو في أول صحيح البخاري وفيه تصريح بأن المراد برفعها رفع بيان علم عينها

ولو كان المراد رفع وجودها لم يأمر بالتماسها
# [1165] قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (أرى رؤياكم قد تواطت) أي توافقت وهكذا

هو في النسخ بطاء ثم تاء وهو مهموز وكان ينبغي أن يكتب بألف بين الطاء

والتاء صورة للهمزة ولا بد من قراءته مهموزا قال الله تعالى ليواطئوا عدة

ما حرم الله قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (تحروا ليلة القدر) أي احرصوا على

طلبها واجتهدوا فيه
# 
# قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (فالتمسوها في العشر الغوابر) يعني البواقي وهي

الأواخر قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (فلا يغلبن على السبع البواقي) وفي بعض

النسخ عن السبع بدل على وكلاهما صحيح قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (تحينوا ليلة

القدر) أي اطلبوا حينها وهو زمانها
# 
# [1166] قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (أيقظنى بعض أهلي فنسيتها وقال حرملة

فنسيتها) الأول بضم النون وتشديد السين والثاني بفتح النون وتخفيف السين
# [1167] قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (فمن كان اعتكف معي فليبت في معتكفه)

هكذا هو في أكثر النسخ فليبت من المبيت وفي بعضها فليثبت من الثبوت وفي

بعضها فليلبث من اللبث وكله صحيح وقوله في الرواية الثانية غير أنه قال

فليثبت هو في أكثر النسخ بالثاء المثلثة من الثبوت وفي بعضها فليبت من

المبيت ومعتكفه بفتح الكاف وهو موضع الاعتكاف قوله (فوكف المسجد) أي قطر

ماء المطر من سقفه قوله (فنظرت إليه وقد انصرف من صلاة الصبح ووجهه مبتل

طينا
# 
# وماء) قال البخاري وكان الحميدي يحتج بهذا الحديث على أن السنة للمصلي أن

لا يمسح جبهته في الصلاة وكذا قال العلماء يستحب أن لا يمسحها في الصلاة

وهذا محمول على أنه كان شيئا يسيرا لا يمنع مباشرة بشرة الجبهة للأرض فإنه

لو كان كثيرا بحيث يمنع ذلك لم يصح سجوده بعده عند الشافعي وموافقيه في منع

السجود على حائل متصل  به قوله في الرواية الثانية (وجبينه ممتلئا طينا

وماء) لا يخالف ما تأولناه لأن الجبين غير الجبهة فالجبين في جانب الجبهة

وللإنسان جبينان يكتنفان الجبهة ولا يلزم من امتلاء الجبين امتلاء الجبهة

والله أعلم وقوله (ممتلئا) كذا هو في معظم النسخ ممتلئا بالنصب وفي بعضها

ممتلئ ويقدر للمنصوب فعل محذوف أي وجبينه رأيته ممتلئا قوله في حديث محمد

بن عبد الأعلى (ثم اعتكفت العشر الأوسط) هكذا هو في جميع النسخ والمشهور في

الاستعمال تأنيث العشر كما قال في أكثر الأحاديث العشر الأواخر وتذكيره

أيضا لغة صحيحة باعتبار الأيام أو باعتبار الوقت
# 
# والزمان ويكفي في صحتها ثبوت استعمالها في هذا الحديث من النبي صلى الله

عليه وسلم قوله (قبة تركية) أي قبة صغيرة من لبود قوله (وروثة أنفه) هي

بالثاء المثلثة وهي طرفه ويقال لها أيضا أرنبة الأنف كما جاء في الرواية

الأخرى قوله (وما نرى في السماء قزعة) أي قطعة سحاب قوله
# 
# (أمر بالبناء فقوض) هو بقاف مضمومة وواو مكسورة مشددة وضاد معجمة ومعناه

أزيل يقال قاض البناء وانقاض أي انهدم وقوضته أنا قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم

(رجلان يحتقان) هو بالقاف ومعناه يطلب كل واحد منهما حقه ويدعي أنه المحق

وفيه أن المخاصمة والمنازعة مذمومة وأنها سبب للعقوبة المعنوية قوله (فإذا

مضت واحدة وعشرون فالتي تليها ثنتين وعشرين فهي التاسعة) هكذا هو في أكثر

النسخ ثنتين وعشرين بالياء وفي بعضها اثنتان وعشرون بالالف
# 
# والواو والأول أصوب وهو منصوب بفعل محذوف تقديره أعني ثنتين وعشرين قوله

(وكان عبد الله بن أنيس يقول ثلاث وعشرين) هكذا هو في معظم النسخ وفي بعضها

ثلاث وعشرون وهذا ظاهر والأول جار على لغة شاذة أنه يجوز حذف المضاف ويبقى

المضاف إليه مجرورا أي ليلة ثلاث وعشرين
# [762] قوله (أنها تطلع يومئذ لا شعاع لها) هكذا هو في جميع النسخ أنها

تطلع
# 
# من غير ذكر الشمس وحذفت للعلم بها فعاد الضمير إلى معلوم كقوله تعالى

توارت بالحجاب ونظائره والشعاع بضم الشين قال أهل اللغة هو ما  يرى من ضوئها

عند بروزها مثل الحبال والقضبان مقبلة إليك إذا نظرت إليها قال صاحب المحكم

بعد أن ذكر هذا المشهور وقيل هو الذي تراه ممتدا بعد الطلوع قال وقيل هو

انتشار ضوئها وجمعه أشعة وشعع بضم الشين والعين وأشعت الشمس نشرت شعاعها

قال القاضي عياض قيل معنى لا شعاع لها أنها علامة جعلها الله تعالى لها قال

وقيل بل لكثرة اختلاف الملائكة في ليلتها ونزولها إلى الأرض وصعودها بما

تنزل به سترت بأجنحتها وأجسامها اللطيفة ضوء الشمس وشعاعها والله أعلم
# [1170] قوله (تذاكرنا
# 
# ليلة القدر عند رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال أيكم يذكر حين طلع

القمر وهو مثل شق جفنة) بكسر الشين وهو النصف والجفنة بفتح الجيم معروفة
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ر-ف-ع (r-f-ʿ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To raise, elevate, lift up; also to remove or annul (as in raising a decree).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological discourse, denotes either elevation of rank or abrogation/removal of a ruling; context determines whether it refers to existential removal or epistemic concealment.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) = physical lifting; metaphorical (majāz) = removal of knowledge or specification.
- Sībawayh Rule: Taqdīr al-Fiʿl al-Maḥdhūf (Ellipsis of the governing verb) — In phrases like "وجبينه ممتلئا" (and his forehead, filled), the accusative case requires an implied verb, e.g., "رأيته" (I saw it).
chapters.translation:
I say: The judge [ʿIyāḍ] — and a group deviated [from the consensus] and claimed that [the Night of Decree] was raised [from existence] due to his saying, peace and blessings be upon him, when the two men disputed: "So it was raised." This is an error from these deviants, because the end of the hadith refutes them. For he, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "So it was raised, and perhaps it is better for you. So seek it in the seven and the nine." Thus it is in the beginning of Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī, and in it is an explicit statement that the intended meaning of "its raising" is the raising of the clarification of the knowledge of its specific time. Had the intended meaning been the raising of its existence, he would not have commanded seeking it.

# [1165] His saying, peace and blessings be upon him: "I see your visions have concurred (tawāṭaʾat)" — i.e., they have agreed. Thus it is in the manuscripts with a ṭāʾ then a tāʾ, and it is hamzated. It should have been written with an alif between the ṭāʾ and the tāʾ as a representation of the hamzah, and it must be read with the hamzah. Allah the Exalted said: {لِيُوَاطِئُوا عِدَّةَ مَا حَرَّمَ اللَّهُ} (to make up the number of what Allah has forbidden). His saying, peace and blessings be upon him: "Seek earnestly (taḥarrū) the Night of Decree" — i.e., be eager in seeking it and strive diligently therein.

His saying, peace and blessings be upon him: "So seek it in the ten remaining (al-ʿashr al-ghawābir)" — meaning the remaining ones, which are the last [nights]. His saying, peace and blessings be upon him: "So let not the seven remaining (al-sabʿ al-bawāqī) overcome you" — and in some manuscripts "from the seven" (ʿan al-sabʿ) instead of "on the seven" (ʿalā al-sabʿ), and both are correct. His saying, peace and blessings be upon him: "Anticipate (taḥayyanū) the Night of Decree" — i.e., seek its time (ḥīn), which is its appointed moment.

# [1166] His saying, peace and blessings be upon him: "One of my family woke me (ayqaẓanī), and I forgot it" — and Ḥarmalah said: "So I forgot it (fasītuhā)." The first is with a ḍammah on the nūn and a shaddah on the sīn; the second is with a fatḥah on the nūn and a light sīn.

# [1167] His saying, peace and blessings be upon him: "So whoever was in iʿtikāf with me, let him stay the night (falyabit) in his place of iʿtikāf" — thus it is in most manuscripts: falyabit, from al-mabīt (spending the night). In some: falyathbit, from al-thubūt (remaining steadfast). In some: falyalbath, from al-lubth (tarrying). All are correct. His saying in the second narration: "except that he said: falyathbit" — in most manuscripts it is with the dotted thāʾ from al-thubūt, and in some falyabit from al-mabīt. His word "muʿtakafuh" (his place of iʿtikāf) is with a fatḥah on the kāf, and it is the place of iʿtikāf. His saying: "The mosque dripped (wakafa)" — i.e., rainwater dripped from its ceiling. His saying: "I looked at him as he had departed from the dawn prayer, his face smeared with mud and water." Al-Bukhārī said: Al-Ḥumaydī used this hadith as evidence that the Sunnah for the prayer is not to wipe one's forehead during prayer. Likewise, the scholars said: It is recommended not to wipe it during prayer. This is interpreted [as applying] when it is something slight that does not prevent direct contact of the forehead's skin with the ground. For were it copious, such that it prevented that, his prostration afterward would not be valid according to al-Shāfiʿī and those who agree with him in prohibiting prostration upon an intervening barrier attached [to the body]. His saying in the second narration: "And his temple (jabīnuh) filled with mud and water" does not contradict what we interpreted, because the temple is other than the forehead. The temple is on the side of the forehead, and a person has two temples flanking the forehead. The filling of the temple does not necessitate the filling of the forehead. And Allah knows best. His saying "filled" (mumtaliʾan) — thus it is in most manuscripts with the accusative (naṣb), and in some "mumtaliʾ" [nominative]. For the accusative, an omitted verb is implied, i.e., "and his temple, I saw it filled." His saying in the hadith of Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā: "Then I performed iʿtikāf for the middle ten (al-ʿashr al-awsaṭ)" — thus it is in all manuscripts. The well-known usage is the feminine for "ten" (al-ʿashr), as he said in most hadiths: "the last ten" (al-ʿashr al-awākhir). Its masculine form is also a valid language, considering the days or considering the time and the era. And it suffices for its validity that its usage is established in this hadith from the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him. His saying: "A Turkish dome (qubbah turkiyyah)" — i.e., a small dome of felt. His saying: "And the tip of his nose (warthat anfih)" — it is with the dotted thāʾ, and it is its extremity. It is also called "arrabat al-anf" (the nose's tip), as came in the other narration. His saying: "And we see no cloud fragment (qazaʿah) in the sky" — i.e., a piece of cloud. His saying: "He commanded the structure to be dismantled (faquwwiḍ)" — it is with a ḍammah on the qāf, a kasrah on the wāw with a shaddah, and a dotted ḍād. Its meaning: it was removed. One says: qāḍa al-bināʾ (the building collapsed) and inqāḍa (it fell down), and qawwaḍtuhu anā (I dismantled it). His saying, peace and blessings be upon him: "Two men disputing (yaḥtaqqān)" — it is with the qāf, and its meaning: each of them seeks his right and claims he is the rightful one. In it [is the lesson] that quarreling and contention are blameworthy and that they are a cause of spiritual punishment. His saying: "When twenty-one have passed, then the one following it, twenty-two, it is the ninth" — thus it is in most manuscripts: "twenty-two" (ithnatay ʿishrīn) with a yāʾ, and in some "twenty-two" (ithnatān wa-ʿishrūn) with an alif and wāw. The first is more correct, and it is accusative due to an omitted verb, its estimation being: "I mean twenty-two." His saying: "And ʿAbdullāh ibn Unays used to say: twenty-three" — thus it is in most manuscripts, and in some "twenty-three" (thalāth wa-ʿishrūn) [nominative]. This is apparent, and the first follows a rare dialectical usage that permits deleting the muḍāf (the annexed noun) while leaving the muḍāf ilayh (the annexed-to noun) in the genitive, i.e., "the night of twenty-three."

# [762] His saying: "That it rises that day with no rays (shuʿāʿ) for it" — thus it is in all manuscripts: "that it rises" without mentioning the sun, and it was omitted due to being known, so the pronoun reverted to the known entity, like His saying, the Exalted: {تَوَارَتْ بِالْحِجَابِ} (it concealed itself with the veil) and its parallels. "Al-shuʿāʿ" — with a ḍammah on the shīn — the linguists said: it is what is seen of its light upon its emergence, like ropes and rods coming toward you when you look at it. The author of al-Muḥkam said, after mentioning this well-known [definition]: And it was said: it is what you see extending after sunrise. And it was said: it is the spreading of its light. Its plural is ashiʿʿah and shuʿuʿ, with a ḍammah on the shīn and ʿayn. "Ashaʿʿat al-shams" (the sun spread its rays). Al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ said: It was said the meaning of "no rays for it" is that it is a sign that Allah the Exalted has made for it. And it was said: rather, due to the abundance of the angels' coming and going on that night, descending to the earth and ascending with what they descend with, they veiled with their wings and their subtle bodies the light of the sun and its rays. And Allah knows best.

# [1170] His saying: "We were discussing (tadhākarnā) the Night of Decree in the presence of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, and he said: 'Which of you remembers when the moon rose, and it was like a half of a bowl (shiq jafnah)?'" — with a kasrah on the shīn, meaning half; and "al-jafnah" with a fatḥah on the jīm is well-known [as a bowl].

chapters.title_en: The Reality of the Night of Decree and the Rulings of Spiritual Retreat (Iʿtikāf)
chapters.arabic_text:
قال القاضي فيه إشارة إلى أنها إنما تكون في أواخر الشهر لأن القمر لا يكون

كذلك عند طلوعه إلا في أواخر الشهر والله أعلم واعلم أن ليلة القدر موجودة

كما سبق بيانه في أول الباب فإنها ترى ويتحققها من شاء الله تعالى من بني

آدم كل سنة في رمضان كما تظاهرت عليه هذه الأحاديث السابقة في الباب وإخبار

الصالحين بها ورؤيتهم لها أكثر من أن تحصر وأما قول القاضي عياض عن المهلب

بن أبي صفرة لا يمكن رؤيتها حقيقة فغلط فاحش نبهت عليه لئلا يغتر به والله

أعلم

| (كتاب الاعتكاف هو في اللغة الحبس والمكث واللزوم 
# وفي الشرع المكث في المسجد من شخص مخصوص بصفة مخصوصة ويسمى الاعتكاف

جوارا ومنه الأحاديث الصحيحة منها حديث عائشة في أوائل الاعتكاف من صحيح

البخاري قالت كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يصغي إلي رأسه وهو مجاور في

المسجد فأرجله وأنا)
# 
# حائض وذكر مسلم الأحاديث في اعتكاف النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم العشر

الأواخر من رمضان والعشر الأول من شوال ففيها استحباب الاعتكاف وتأكد

استحبابه في العشر الأواخر من رمضان وقد أجمع المسلمون على استحبابه وأنه

ليس بواجب وعلى أنه متأكد في العشر الأواخر من رمضان ومذهب الشافعي وأصحابه

وموافقيهم أن الصوم ليس بشرط  لصحة الاعتكاف بل يصح اعتكاف الفطر ويصح

اعتكاف ساعة واحدة ولحظة واحدة وضابطه عند أصحابنا مكث يزيد على طمأنينة

الركوع أدنى زيادة هذا هو الصحيح وفيه خلاف شاذ في المذهب ولنا وجه أنه يصح

اعتكاف المار في المسجد من غير لبث والمشهور الأول فينبغي لكل جالس في

المسجد لانتظار صلاة أو لشغل آخر من آخرة أو دنيا أن ينوي الاعتكاف فيحسب

له ويثاب عليه مالم يخرج من المسجد فإذا خرج ثم دخل جدد نية أخرى وليس

للاعتكاف ذكر مخصوص ولا فعل آخر سوى اللبث في المسجد بنية الاعتكاف ولو

تكلم بكلام دنيا أو عمل صنعة من خياطة أو غيرها لم يبطل اعتكافه وقال مالك

وأبو حنيفة والأكثرون يشترط في الاعتكاف الصوم فلا يصح اعتكاف مفطر وحتجوا

بهذه الأحاديث واحتج الشافعي باعتكافه صلى الله عليه وسلم في العشر الأول

من شوال رواه البخاري ومسلم وبحديث عمر رضي الله عنه قال يارسول الله إني

نذرت أن أعتكف ليلة
# 
# في الجاهلية فقال أوف بنذرك ورواه البخاري ومسلم والليل ليس محلا للصوم

فدل على أنه ليس بشرط لصحة الاعتكاف وفي هذه الأحاديث أن الاعتكاف لا يصح

إلا في المسجد لأن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وأزواجه وأصحابه إنما اعتكفوا

في المسجد مع المشقة في ملازمته فلو جاز في البيت لفعلوه ولو مرة لاسيما

النساء لأن حاجتهن إليه في البيوت أكثر وهذا الذي ذكرناه من اختصاصه

بالمسجد وأنه لا يصح في غيره هو مذهب مالك والشافعي وأحمد وداود والجمهور

سواء الرجل والمرأة وقال أبو حنيفة يصح اعتكاف المرأة في مسجد بيتها وهو

الموضع المهيأ من بيتها لصلاتها قال ولا يجوز للرجل في مسجد بيته وكمذهب

أبي حنيفة قول قديم للشافعي ضعيف عند أصحابه وجوزه بعض أصحاب مالك وبعض

أصحاب الشافعي للمرأة والرجل في مسجد بيتهما ثم اختلف الجمهور المشترطون

المسجد العام فقال الشافعي ومالك وجمهورهم يصح الاعتكاف في كل مسجد وقال

أحمد يختص بمسجد تقام الجماعة الراتبة فيه وقال أبو حنيفة يختص بمسجد تصلى

فيه  الصلوات كلها وقال الزهري وآخرون يختص بالجامع الذي تقام فيه الجمعة

ونقلوا عن حذيفة بن اليمان الصحابي اختصاصه بالمساجد الثلاثة المسجد الحرام

ومسجد المدينة والأقصى وأجمعوا على أنه لاحد لأكثر الاعتكاف والله أعلم

قوله (إذا أراد أن يعتكف صلى الفجر ثم دخل معتكفه) احتج به من يقول يبدأ

بالاعتكاف من أول النهار وبه قال الأوزاعي والثوري والليث في أحد قوليه

وقال مالك وأبو حنيفة والشافعي وأحمد يدخل فيه قبل غروب الشمس إذا أراد

اعتكاف شهر أو اعتكاف عشر وأولوا الحديث على
# 
# أنه دخل المعتكف وانقطع فيه وتخلى بنفسه بعد صلاته الصبح لا أن ذلك وقت

ابتداء الاعتكاف بل كان من قبل المغرب معتكفا لابثا في جملة المسجد فلما

صلى الصبح انفرد قوله (وأنه أمر بخبائه فضرب) قالوا فيه دليل على جواز

اتخاذ المعتكف لنفسه موضعا من المسجد ينفرد فيه مدة اعتكافه مالم يضيق على

الناس واذا اتخذه يكون في آخر المسجد ورحابه لئلا يضيق على غيره وليكون

أخلى له وأكمل في انفراده قوله (نظر فإذا الأخبية فقال آلبر يردن فأمر

بخبائه فقوض) قوض بالقاف المضمومة والضاد المعجمة أي أزيل وقوله آلبر أي

الطاعة قال القاضي قال صلى الله عليه وسلم هذا الكلام انكار لفعلهن وقد كان

صلى الله عليه وسلم أذن لبعضهن في ذلك كما رواه البخاري قال وسبب إنكاره

أنه خاف أن يكن غير مخلصات في الاعتكاف بل أردن القرب منه لغيرتهن عليه أو

لغيرته عليهن فكره ملازمتهن المسجد مع أنه يجمع الناس ويحضره الأعراب

والمنافقون وهن محتاجات إلى الخروج والدخول لما يعرض لهن فيبتذلن بذلك أو

لأنه صلى الله عليه وسلم رآهن عنده في المسجد وهو في المسجد فصار كأنه في
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ر-أ-ي (ra-ʾa-yā)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Visual perception; direct ocular apprehension of an object.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological discourse, denotes experiential witnessing (mushāhadah) granted by divine will, distinct from rational inference.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) here—actual sight; metaphorical (majāz) would be intellectual insight, which is not intended in this context.
- Root: ل-ب-ث (la-ba-tha)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Remaining, tarrying, dwelling in a place for a duration.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In legal terminology (Sharʿ), it signifies a deliberate, sustained presence with intent, distinguishing it from mere passage.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal—physical abiding; metaphorically extended to spiritual perseverance, but here strictly physical.
- Root: خ-ل-و (kha-lā)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Emptiness; seclusion; being alone in a space.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In devotional practice, it implies voluntary isolation for worship, free from worldly distractions.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal—spatial solitude; metaphorical—heart's detachment, though the text uses the literal sense.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clause with Implied Protasis (al-sharṭ al-muḍmar) — In "إذا أراد أن يعتكف" (when he intended to retreat), the apodosis is understood from context, requiring the reader to infer the full syntactic completion from the narrated action.
chapters.translation:
The Qāḍī (ʿIyāḍ) said: In this (hadith) there is an indication that it (the Night of Decree) occurs only in the final part of the month, because the moon is not like that at its rising except in the last part of the month. And Allah knows best.

Know that the Night of Decree is existent (mawjūdah), as has been previously explained at the beginning of the chapter. For it is seen, and it is ascertained by whomever Allah—Exalted is He—wills among the children of Adam, every year in Ramaḍān, just as these preceding hadiths in the chapter have corroborated, and the reports of the righteous regarding it, and their seeing of it, are too numerous to be enumerated.

As for the statement of the Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ, transmitted from al-Muhallab ibn Abī Ṣafrah, that it cannot be seen in reality (ḥaqīqah)—this is a gross error (ghalaṭ fāḥish). I have drawn attention to it lest anyone be deceived by it. And Allah knows best.

---

(Book of Spiritual Retreat (Iʿtikāf))

Linguistically, it (iʿtikāf) means: confinement (al-ḥabs), remaining (al-makth), and adherence (al-luzūm).

In Sacred Law (al-Sharʿ), it is: remaining in the mosque, from a specific person, with a specific description. It is also called "neighboring" (jīwār). From this derive the authentic hadiths—among them the hadith of ʿĀʾishah at the beginning of the chapter on iʿtikāf in Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī. She said: "The Prophet ﷺ would incline his head toward me while he was neighboring (mujāwir) in the mosque, and I would comb his hair while I was menstruating."

Muslim mentioned the hadiths concerning the Prophet's ﷺ iʿtikāf during the last ten (days) of Ramaḍān and the first ten of Shawwāl. In these (hadiths) there is (evidence for) the recommendation (istihbāb) of iʿtikāf, and the emphasis of its recommendation in the last ten days of Ramaḍān.

The Muslims are unanimous (ijmāʿ) upon its recommendation, that it is not obligatory (wājib), and that it is emphasized in the last ten days of Ramaḍān.

The school of al-Shāfiʿī, his companions, and those who agree with them, is that fasting is not a condition (sharṭ) for the validity of iʿtikāf. Rather, the iʿtikāf of one who is not fasting is valid, and the iʿtikāf of a single hour, and of a single moment, is valid. Its criterion (ḍābiṭ) according to our companions is: a remaining (mukth) that exceeds the stillness (ṭumaʾnīnah) of the bowing (rukūʿ) by the slightest increase. This is the correct (opinion). There is an anomalous (shādhdh) disagreement within the school. And we have a position (wajh) that the iʿtikāf of one merely passing through the mosque, without tarrying, is valid. The well-known (opinion) is the first.

Therefore, it is befitting for everyone sitting in the mosque—awaiting a prayer, or for another matter of the Hereafter or of this world—to intend iʿtikāf. It will then be recorded for him, and he will be rewarded for it, as long as he does not exit the mosque. If he exits and then re-enters, he renews another intention.

There is no specific invocation (dhikr) for iʿtikāf, nor any other act, besides remaining in the mosque with the intention of iʿtikāf. Even if he speaks worldly speech, or performs a craft such as sewing or otherwise, his iʿtikāf is not invalidated.

Mālik, Abū Ḥanīfah, and the majority (al-aktharūn) said: Fasting is a condition in iʿtikāf, so the iʿtikāf of one not fasting is not valid. They adduced these hadiths as evidence.

Al-Shāfiʿī adduced as evidence his ﷺ iʿtikāf in the first ten (days) of Shawwāl—narrated by al-Bukhārī and Muslim—and the hadith of ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "O Messenger of Allah, I vowed to make iʿtikāf for one night in the Jāhiliyyah." He ﷺ said: "Fulfill your vow." Narrated by al-Bukhārī and Muslim. And the night is not a locus for fasting. This indicates that it (fasting) is not a condition for the validity of iʿtikāf.

In these hadiths (there is evidence) that iʿtikāf is not valid except in a mosque, because the Prophet ﷺ, his wives, and his companions only made iʿtikāf in the mosque, despite the hardship in adhering to it. Had it been permissible in the house, they would have done so—even once—especially the women, for their need of it in their houses is greater.

What we have mentioned—of its exclusivity to the mosque and that it is not valid elsewhere—is the school of Mālik, al-Shāfiʿī, Aḥmad, Dāwūd, and the majority (al-jumhūr), equally for men and women.

Abū Ḥanīfah said: The iʿtikāf of a woman is valid in the mosque of her house—that is, the place prepared in her house for her prayer. He said: It is not permissible for a man in the mosque of his house. Corresponding to the school of Abū Ḥanīfah is an old (qadīm) opinion of al-Shāfiʿī, deemed weak (ḍaʿīf) by his companions. Some companions of Mālik and some companions of al-Shāfiʿī permitted it for both woman and man in the mosque of their houses.

Then the majority who stipulate the general mosque differed. Al-Shāfiʿī, Mālik, and their majority said: Iʿtikāf is valid in every mosque. Aḥmad said: It is exclusive to a mosque in which the regular congregational prayer (al-jamāʿah al-rātibah) is established. Abū Ḥanīfah said: It is exclusive to a mosque in which all the prayers are performed. Al-Zuhrī and others said: It is exclusive to the congregational mosque (al-jāmiʿ) in which the Friday (prayer) is established. They transmitted from Ḥudhayfah ibn al-Yamān, the Companion, its exclusivity to the three mosques: the Sacred Mosque (al-Masjid al-Ḥarām), the Mosque of Madīnah, and al-Aqṣā.

They are unanimous (ajmaʿū) that there is no limit to the maximum duration of iʿtikāf. And Allah knows best.

His statement ﷺ: "When he intended to make iʿtikāf, he prayed the dawn (Fajr) prayer, then entered his place of retreat (muʿtakaf)"—this is adduced as evidence by those who say that iʿtikāf begins from the beginning of the day. This was the opinion of al-Awzāʿī, al-Thawrī, and al-Layth in one of his two opinions.

Mālik, Abū Ḥanīfah, al-Shāfiʿī, and Aḥmad said: He enters it before sunset, if he intends a month's iʿtikāf or ten (days') iʿtikāf. They interpreted the hadith as meaning that he entered the place of retreat, secluded himself therein, and devoted himself alone after his dawn prayer—not that this was the time of beginning the iʿtikāf. Rather, he had been from before sunset in a state of iʿtikāf, remaining (lābith) within the general precincts of the mosque. When he prayed the dawn, he isolated himself.

His statement ﷺ: "And he commanded that his tent (khibāʾ) be pitched"—they said: In this is evidence for the permissibility of one making iʿtikāf taking for himself a place in the mosque in which he isolates himself for the duration of his iʿtikāf, as long as he does not cause constriction upon the people. And when he takes it, it should be at the far end of the mosque and its open spaces (riḥāb), so as not to constrict others, and so that it is more private for him and more complete in his seclusion.

His statement ﷺ: "He looked, and behold, there were small tents (akhbiyah). He said: 'Do they intend righteousness (al-birr)?' Then he commanded his tent and it was dismantled (quwwiḍ)." "Quwwiḍ"—with the ḍammah on the qāf and the dotted ḍād—means: it was removed. His statement "al-birr" means: obedience (al-ṭāʿah).

The Qāḍī said: The Prophet ﷺ uttered this speech as a disapproval (inkār) of their action. He ﷺ had indeed permitted some of them in that, as narrated by al-Bukhārī. He said: The cause of his disapproval was that he feared they were not sincere (mukhliṣāt) in the iʿtikāf, but rather intended proximity to him out of jealousy for him, or jealousy over him. So he disliked their adherence to the mosque, given that it gathers the people, and the Bedouins (aʿrāb) and hypocrites (munāfiqūn) attend it, and they (the women) are in need of exiting and entering due to what occurs to them, and they would thus expose themselves (yubtadhalna) by that. Or—because he ﷺ saw them near him in the mosque while he was in the mosque, so it became as if he were...

chapters.arabic_text:
منزله بحضوره مع أزواجه وذهب المهم من مقصود الاعتكاف وهو التخلي عن

الأزواج ومتعلقات الدنيا وشبه ذلك أو لأنهن ضيقن المسجد بأبنيتهن وفي هذا

الحديث دليل
# 
# لصحة اعتكاف النساء لأنه صلى الله عليه وسلم كان أذن لهن وإنما منعهن بعد

ذلك لعارض وفيه أن للرجل منع زوجته  من الاعتكاف بغير إذنه وبه قال العلماء

كافة فلو أذن لها فهل له منعها بعد ذلك فيه خلاف للعلماء فعند الشافعي

وأحمد وداود له منع زوجته ومملوكه وإخراجهما من اعتكاف التطوع ومنعهما مالك

وجوز أبو حنيفة إخراج المملوك دون الزوجة

| (باب الاجتهاد في العشر الأواخر من شهر رمضان
# [1174] قولها
# (كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا دخل العشر أحيا الليل وأيقظ أهله

وجد وشد المئزر
# [1175] وفي رواية كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يجتهد في العشر

الأواخر مالم يجتهد في غيره) اختلف العلماء)
# 
# في معنى شد المئزر فقيل هو الاجتهاد في العبادات زيادة على عادته صلى

الله عليه وسلم في غيره ومعناه التشمير في العبادات يقال شددت لهذا الأمر

مئزري أي تشمرت له وتفرغت وقيل هو كناية عن اعتزال النساء للاشتغال

بالعبادات وقولها أحيا الليل أي استغرقه بالسهر في الصلاة وغيرها وقولها

وأيقظ أهله أي أيقظهم للصلاة في الليل وجد في العبادة زيادة على العادة ففي

هذا الحديث أنه يستحب أن يزاد من العبادات في العشر الأواخر من رمضان

واستحباب إحياء لياليه بالعبادات وأما قول أصحابنا يكره قيام الليل كله

فمعناه الدوام عليه ولم يقولوا بكراهة ليلة وليلتين والعشر ولهذا اتفقوا

على استحباب إحياء ليلتي العيدين وغير ذلك والمئزر بكسر الميم مهموز وهو

الإزار والله أعلم

| (باب صوم عشر ذي الحجة
# [1176] فيه قول عائشة (ما رأيت رسول
# الله صلى الله عليه وسلم صائما في العشر قط) وفي رواية لم يصم العشر قال

العلماء هذا الحديث مما يوهم كراهة صوم العشر والمراد بالعشر هنا الأيام

التسعة من أول ذي الحجة قالوا وهذا مما يتأول فليس في صوم هذه التسعة كراهة

بل هي مستحبة استحبابا شديدا لاسيما التاسع منها وهو يوم عرفة وقد سبقت

الأحاديث في فضله وثبت في صحيح البخاري إن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

قال ما من أيام العمل الصالح فيها أفضل منه في هذه يعني العشر الأوائل من

ذي الحجة فيتأول قولها لم يصم العشر  أنه لم يصمه)
# 
# لعارض مرض أو سفر أو غيرهما أو أنها لم تره صائما فيه ولا يلزم من ذلك

عدم صيامه في نفس الأمر ويدل على هذا التأويل حديث هنيدة بن خالد عن امرأته

عن بعض أزواج النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قالت كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه

وسلم يصوم تسع ذي الحجة ويوم عاشوراء وثلاثة أيام من كل شهر الاثنين من

الشهر والخميس ورواه أبو داود وهذا لفظه وأحمد والنسائي وفي روايتهما

وخميسين والله أعلم قوله في الإسناد الأخير (وحدثني أبو بكر بن نافع العبدي

حدثنا عبد الرحمن حدثنا سفيان عن الأعمش) وهو سفيان الثوري وفي بعضها شعبة

بدل سفيان وكذا نقله القاضي عياض عن رواية الفارسي ونقل الأول عن جمهور

الرواة لصحيح مسلم والله أعلم

| (كتاب الحج الحج بفتح الحاء هو المصدر وبالفتح 
# والكسر جميعا هو الاسم منه وأصله القصد ويطلق على العمل أيضا وعلى

الإتيان مرة بعد أخرى وأصل العمرة الزيارة واعلم أن الحج فرض عين على كل

مكلف حر مسلم مستطيع واختلف العلماء في وجوب العمرة فقيل واجبة وقيل مستحبة

وللشافعي قولان أصحهما وجوبها وأجمعوا على أنه لا يجب الحج ولا العمرة في

عمر الإنسان إلا مرة واحدة إلا أن ينذر فيجب الوفاء بالنذر بشرطه وإلا إذا

دخل مكة أو حرمها لحاجة لا تتكرر من تجارة أو زيارة ونحوهما ففي وجوب

الإحرام بحج أو عمرة خلاف العلماء وهما قولان للشافعي أصحهما استحبابه

والثاني وجوبه بشرط أن لا يدخل لقتال ولا خائفا من ظهوره وبروزه واختلفوا

في وجوب الحج هل هو على الفور أو التراخي فقال الشافعي وأبو يوسف)
# 
# وطائفة هو على التراخي إلا أن ينتهي إلى حال يظن فواته لو أخره عنها وقال

أبو حنيفة ومالك وآخرون هو على الفور والله أعلم

| باب ما يباح للمحرم بحج أو عمرة لبسه ومالا يباح
# (وبيان تحريم الطيب عليه)
# [1177] قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم وقد سئل ما يلبس المحرم (لا تلبسوا القمص

ولا العمائم ولا السراويلات ولا البرانس  ولا الخفاف الا أحد لايجد النعلين

فليلبس الخفين وليقطعهما أسفل من الكعبين ولا تلبسوا من الثياب شيئا مسه

الزعفران ولاالورس) قال العلماء هذا من بديع الكلام وجزله فإنه صلى الله

عليه وسلم سئل عما يلبسه المحرم فقال لا يلبس كذا وكذا فحصل في الجواب أنه

لا يلبس المذكورات ويلبس ما سوى ذلك وكان التصريح بما لا يلبس أولى لأنه

منحصر وأما الملبوس الجائز للمحرم فغير منحصر فضبط الجميع بقوله صلى الله

عليه وسلم لا يلبس كذا وكذا يعني ويلبس ما سواه وأجمع العلماء على أنه لا

يجوز للمحرم لبس شئ من هذه المذكورات وأنه نبه بالقميص والسراويل على جميع
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ع ز ل (ʿ-z-l)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Separation, withdrawal, or isolation from something; al-ʿazl is the act of setting apart.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In devotional contexts, it denotes physical and intentional severance from worldly or permissible pleasures to devote oneself wholly to worship.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Used literally here for physical separation from wives; metaphorically for spiritual detachment from worldly attachments.
- Root: ج ه د (j-h-d)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Exertion of effort, striving, or toiling; jahd is capacity, juhd is effort.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In religious terminology, it is the expenditure of one's utmost capacity in worship and obedience, often exceeding one's customary practice.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for physical exertion; here it is a ḥaqīqah for intensified devotional effort, not metaphorical.
- Root: ش م ر (sh-m-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To tuck up one's garment, to gird oneself, to prepare and dedicate oneself fully to a task.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Symbolizes readiness and total commitment to worship, stripping away distractions.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for tucking the izār; metaphorically (majāz) for earnestness and dedication in acts of obedience.
- Root: ح ج ج (ḥ-j-j)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: The intent or aim (al-qaṣd) toward something; also repeated coming (al-taraddud).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The pilgrimage to the Sacred House, a pillar of Islam, denoting the intention to visit the Kaʿbah for worship.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for the pilgrimage rite; the root's core meaning of "intending" is retained in the technical religious sense.
- Root: ع م ر (ʿ-m-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Visiting, populating, or cultivating; al-ʿimārah is the act of inhabiting.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The lesser pilgrimage, a visit to the Sacred House, distinct from ḥajj in scope and timing.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for visiting; technically applied to the ritual visit to the Kaʿbah.
- Sībawayh Rule: The Rule of Exception (al-istithnāʾ) — In the Prophet's statement "except one who does not find sandals," the exception clause (illā) governs the permissibility of wearing khuffs, with the condition of cutting them below the ankles, parsed as a conditional exception.
chapters.translation:
I say: His statement — meaning the Prophet's (peace and blessings be upon him) — "his abode by his presence with his wives," and the essential purpose of iʿtikāf, which is seclusion from wives and the attachments of the world and the like, was lost. Or because they (the wives) narrowed the mosque with their tents. In this hadith there is evidence for the validity of women's iʿtikāf, for the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) had permitted them, and he only prevented them afterward due to an incidental cause. In it also is that a man may prevent his wife from iʿtikāf without her permission, and this is the position of all scholars. If he grants her permission, then whether he may prevent her afterward is a matter of scholarly disagreement. According to al-Shāfiʿī, Aḥmad, and Dāwūd, he may prevent his wife and his slave and remove them from voluntary iʿtikāf. Mālik prevented him from that, and Abū Ḥanīfah permitted the removal of the slave but not the wife.

| (Chapter: Striving in the Last Ten Days of the Month of Ramadan)

[1174] Her statement: "When the ten days entered, the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) would revive the night, awaken his family, gird himself, and tighten his izār."

[1175] In another narration: "The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) would strive in the last ten days as he did not strive in others." The scholars differed regarding the meaning of "tightening the izār." It was said: it is striving in acts of worship beyond his customary practice (peace and blessings be upon him) in other times, and its meaning is earnest dedication in worship. One says: "I tightened my izār for this matter," meaning I girded myself for it and devoted myself fully. It was also said: it is a metaphor (kināyah) for abstaining from women to devote oneself to worship. Her statement "he revived the night" means he spent it entirely in wakefulness for prayer and other acts. Her statement "he awakened his family" means he woke them for prayer in the night. He strove in worship beyond his custom. In this hadith is that it is recommended to increase acts of worship in the last ten days of Ramadan, and the recommendation of reviving its nights with worship. As for the statement of our companions — that praying the entire night is disliked — its meaning is the perpetual continuation of it; they did not declare a single night, two nights, or the ten nights as disliked. For this reason, they unanimously agreed on the recommendation of reviving the two nights of the two ʿĪds and other occasions. The "izār" (mīzar) — with a kasrah on the mīm and a hamzah — is the waist-wrapper. And Allah knows best.

| (Chapter: Fasting the Ten Days of Dhul-Hijjah)

[1176] In it is the statement of ʿĀʾishah: "I never saw the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) fasting in the ten days at all." In another narration: "He did not fast the ten days." The scholars said: This hadith suggests the dislike of fasting the ten days, but the intended meaning of "the ten days" here is the nine days from the beginning of Dhul-Hijjah. They said: This requires interpretation, for there is no dislike in fasting these nine days; rather, they are strongly recommended, especially the ninth of them, which is the Day of ʿArafah. The hadiths on its virtue have preceded. It is established in Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī that the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "There are no days in which righteous deeds are more beloved to Allah than in these" — meaning the first ten days of Dhul-Hijjah. Thus her statement "he did not fast the ten days" is interpreted as meaning he did not fast them due to an incidental cause such as illness, travel, or other reasons, or that she did not see him fasting in them, and it does not necessarily follow that he did not fast them in reality. Supporting this interpretation is the hadith of Hunaydah ibn Khālid, from his wife, from one of the wives of the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him), who said: "The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) used to fast the nine days of Dhul-Hijjah, the Day of ʿĀshūrāʾ, and three days of every month: the first Monday of the month and Thursday." Abū Dāwūd narrated it — and this is his wording — as did Aḥmad and al-Nasāʾī, and in their narration: "and two Thursdays." And Allah knows best.

His statement in the last chain: "And ʿUbaydullāh ibn Muʿādh narrated to me, from his father, from Shuʿbah, from al-Aʿmash" — and in some versions, Sufyān instead of Shuʿbah. Likewise, al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ transmitted it from the narration of al-Fārisī, and he transmitted the first from the majority of the narrators of Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim. And Allah knows best.

| (The Book of Hajj)

"Ḥajj" — with a fatḥah on the ḥāʾ — is the verbal noun, and with both fatḥah and kasrah it is the noun derived from it. Its root meaning is intention (al-qaṣd), and it is also applied to the act itself and to coming repeatedly. The root of ʿumrah is visitation (al-ziyārah). Know that ḥajj is an individual obligation upon every legally responsible, free, Muslim person who has the capacity. The scholars differed regarding the obligation of ʿumrah: it was said it is obligatory, and it was said it is recommended. Al-Shāfiʿī has two positions, the more correct of which is its obligation. They unanimously agreed that neither ḥajj nor ʿumrah is obligatory upon a person more than once in a lifetime, unless one makes a vow, in which case fulfilling the vow becomes obligatory under its conditions. And unless one enters Mecca or its sanctuary for a non-recurring need, such as trade, visitation, or the like — then there is scholarly disagreement regarding the obligation of assuming iḥrām for ḥajj or ʿumrah. These are two positions of al-Shāfiʿī, the more correct of which is its recommendation, and the second is its obligation, provided one does not enter for fighting and is not in fear of being exposed or revealed. They differed regarding the obligation of ḥajj: whether it is immediate (ʿalā al-fawr) or deferred (ʿalā al-tarākhī). Al-Shāfiʿī, Abū Yūsuf, and a group said it is deferred, unless one reaches a state where one fears its loss if delayed beyond it. Abū Ḥanīfah, Mālik, and others said it is immediate. And Allah knows best.

| Chapter: What is Permitted for the Muḥrim Undertaking Ḥajj or ʿUmrah to Wear, and What is Not Permitted (and the Clarification of the Prohibition of Perfume upon Him)

[1177] His statement (peace and blessings be upon him), when asked what the muḥrim may wear: "Do not wear shirts, turbans, trousers, burnouses, or khuffs — except one who does not find sandals, so let him wear the khuffs and cut them below the ankles. And do not wear any garment touched by saffron or wars." The scholars said: This is among the most exquisite and concise speech, for he (peace and blessings be upon him) was asked what the muḥrim wears, and he said: "Do not wear such-and-such," so the answer resulted in not wearing the mentioned items and wearing everything else. Specifying what is not worn was more appropriate because it is limited, whereas the permissible garments for the muḥrim are not limited. Thus he encompassed all of them by his statement (peace and blessings be upon him): "Do not wear such-and-such," meaning, and wear what is other than that. The scholars unanimously agreed that it is not permissible for the muḥrim to wear any of these mentioned items, and that he indicated by the shirt and trousers all [similar garments].

ما في معناهما وهو ما كان محيطا أو مخيطا معمولا على)
# 
# قدر البدن أو قدر عضو منه كالجوشن والتبان والقفاز وغيرها ونبه صلى الله

عليه وسلم بالعمائم والبرانس على كل ساتر للرأس مخيطا كان أو غيره حتى

العصابة فإنها حرام فإن احتاج إليها لشجة أو صداع أو غيرهما شدها ولزمته

الفدية ونبه صلى الله عليه وسلم بالخفاف على كل ساتر للرجل من مداس وجمجم

وجورب وغيرها وهذا كله حكم الرجال وأما المرأة فيباح لها ستر جميع بدنها

بكل ساتر من مخيط وغيره إلا ستر وجهها فإنه حرام بكل ساتر وفي ستر يديها

بالقفازين خلاف للعلماء وهما قولان للشافعي أصحهما تحريمه ونبه صلى الله

عليه وسلم بالورس والزعفران على مافي معناهما وهو الطيب فيحرم على الرجل

والمرأة جميعا في الإحرام جميع أنواع الطيب والمراد ما يقصد به الطيب وأما

الفواكه كالأترج والتفاح وأزهار البراري كالشيح والقيصوم ونحوهما فليس

بحرام لأنه لا يقصد للطيب قال العلماء والحكمة في تحريم اللباس المذكور على

المحرم ولباسه الإزار والرداء أن يبعد عن الترفه ويتصف بصفة الخاشع الذليل

وليتذكر أنه محرم في كل وقت فيكون أقرب إلى كثرة أذكاره وأبلغ في مراقبته

وصيانته لعبادته وامتناعه من ارتكاب المحظورات وليتذكر به الموت ولباس

الأكفان ويتذكر البعث يوم القيامة والناس حفاة عراة مهطعين إلى الداعي

والحكمة في تحريم الطيب  والنساء أن يبعد عن الترفه وزينة الدنيا وملاذها

ويجتمع همه لمقاصد الآخرة وقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم إلا أحد لا يجد النعلين

فليلبس الخفين وليقطعهما أسفل من الكعبين وذكر مسلم بعد هذا من رواية بن

عباس وجابر من لم يجد نعلين فليلبس خفين ولم يذكر قطعهما واختلف العلماء في

هذين
#

# الحديثين فقال أحمد يجوز لبس الخفين بحالهما ولا يجب قطعهما لحديث بن

عباس وجابر وكان أصحابه يزعمون نسخ حديث بن عمر المصرح بقطعهما وزعموا أن

قطعهما إضاعة مال وقال مالك وأبو حنيفة والشافعي وجماهير العلماء لا يجوز

لبسهما إلا بعد قطعهما أسفل من الكعبين لحديث بن عمر قالوا وحديث بن عباس

وجابر مطلقان فيجب حملهما على المقطوعين لحديث بن عمر فإن المطلق يحمل على

المقيد والزيادة من الثقة مقبولة وقولهم إنه إضاعة مال ليس بصحيح لأن

الإضاعة إنما تكون فيما نهي عنه وأما ما ورد الشرع به فليس بإضاعة بل حق

يجب الإذعان له والله أعلم ثم اختلف العلماء في لابس الخفين لعدم النعلين

هل عليه فدية أم لا فقال مالك والشافعي ومن وافقهما لاشيء عليه لأنه لو

وجبت فدية لبينها صلى الله عليه وسلم وقال أبو حنيفة وأصحابه عليه الفدية

كما إذا احتاج إلى حلق الرأس يحلقه ويفدي والله أعلم
# [1177] قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (ولا تلبسوا من الثياب شيئا مسه الزعفران

ولا الورس) أجمعت الأمة على تحريم لباسهما لكونهما طيبا وألحقوا بهما جميع

أنواع ما يقصد به الطيب وسبب تحريم الطيب أنه داعية إلى الجماع ولأنه ينافي

تذلل الحاج فإن الحاج أشعث أغبر وسواء في تحريم الطيب الرجل والمرأة وكذا

جميع محرمات الإحرام سوى اللباس كما سبق بيانه ومحرمات الإحرام سبعة اللباس

بتفصيله السابق والطيب وإزالة الشعر والظفر ودهن الرأس واللحية وعقد النكاح

والجماع وسائر الاستمتاع حتى الاستمناء والسابع إتلاف الصيد والله أعلم

وإذا تطيب أو لبس ما نهي عنه لزمته الفدية إن كان عامدا بالإجماع وإن كان

ناسيا فلا فدية عند الثوري والشافعي وأحمد وإسحاق وأوجبها أبو  حنيفة ومالك

ولا يحرم المعصفر عند مالك والشافعي وحرمه الثوري وأبو حنيفة وجعلاه طيبا

وأوجبا فيه الفدية ويكره للمحرم لبس الثوب المصبوغ بغير طيب ولا يحرم والله

أعلم قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (السراويل لمن لم يجد الإزار والخفان لمن لم

يجد النعلين) يعني المحرم هذا صريح في الدلالة
# 
# للشافعي والجمهور في جواز لبس السراويل للمحرم إذا لم يجد إزارا ومنعه

مالك لكونه لم يذكر وفي حديث بن عمر السابق والصواب اباحته بحديث بن عباس

هذا مع حديث جابر بعده أما حديث بن عمر فلا حجة فيه لأنه ذكر فيه حالة وجود

الازار وذكر في حديث بن عباس وجابر حالة العدم فلا منافاة والله أعلم قوله

(وهو بالجعرانة) فيها لغتان مشهورتان إحداهما إسكان العين وتخفيف الراء

والثانية كسر العين وتشديد الراء والأولى أفصح وبهما قال الشافعي وأكثر أهل

اللغة وهكذا اللغتان في تخفيف الحديبية وتشديدها والأفصح التخفيف وبه قال

الشافعي وموافقوه
# [1180] قوله (عليه جبة وعليها خلوق) هو بفتح الخاء وهو نوع من الطيب يعمل
# 
# فيه زعفران قوله (له غطيط) هو كصوت النائم الذي يردده مع نفسه قوله

(كغطيط البكر) هو بفتح الباء وهو الفتي من الإبل قوله (فلما سري عنه) هو

بضم السين وكسر الراء المشددة أي أزيل ما به وكشف عنه والله أعلم قوله صلى

الله عليه وسلم للسائل عن العمرة (اغسل عنك أثر الصفرة) فيه تحريم الطيب

على المحرم ابتداء ودواما لأنه إذا حرم دواما فالابتداء أولى بالتحريم وفيه
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ح-ر-م (ḥ-r-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning of sacred prohibition, setting apart as inviolable; the state of iḥrām renders certain acts and garments sacrosanct in their prohibition.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Theological nuance of divine boundary (ḥadd) — what Allah has declared unlawful for the pilgrim as an act of worship and submission.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal prohibition (taḥrīm) versus metaphorical distancing (ibʿād) from worldly luxury (tarafuh); the garment ban is literal, the wisdom (ḥikmah) behind it is metaphorical elevation of the pilgrim's state.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clause with Omitted Protasis (al-sharṭ al-maḥdhūf) — "If he needs it..." (fa-in iḥtāja) implies an unstated condition governing the permissibility of the act with obligatory compensation (fidyah).
chapters.translation:
I say: And what is in their meaning — that which is encompassing or sewn, fashioned according to the measure of the body or the measure of a limb thereof, such as the breastplate (jawshan), the drawers (tubbān), the gloves (quffāz), and other similar items. And he, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, indicated by the turbans (ʿamāʾim) and hooded cloaks (barānis) that every head-covering is prohibited — whether sewn or otherwise — even the headband (ʿiṣābah), for it is unlawful. But if one needs it due to a head wound, migraine, or other cause, he may bind it, and the compensation (fidyah) becomes incumbent upon him. And he, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, indicated by the leather socks (khifāf) that every foot-covering is prohibited — whether sandal (midās), boot (jumjum), sock (jawrab), or other. And all of this is the ruling for men. As for the woman, it is permissible for her to cover her entire body with any covering — sewn or otherwise — except covering her face, for that is unlawful with any covering. And regarding covering her hands with gloves (quffāzayn), there is a divergence among the scholars — two opinions of al-Shāfiʿī, the more correct of which is its prohibition.

And he, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, indicated by wars (yellow dye) and saffron (zaʿfarān) that what is in their meaning — namely perfume (ṭīb) — is unlawful for both men and women alike during iḥrām: all types of perfume. And what is intended is that which is sought for its fragrance. As for fruits such as citron (utrujj) and apple, and wildflowers such as wormwood (shīḥ) and chamomile (qayṣūm) and the like, these are not unlawful, for they are not sought for fragrance.

The scholars said: The wisdom (ḥikmah) in prohibiting the aforementioned garments upon the pilgrim — while his clothing is the waist-wrapper (izār) and cloak (ridāʾ) — is that he be distanced from luxury (tarafuh) and characterized by the attribute of the humble, abased one; that he be reminded that he is in a state of consecration at every moment, thus drawing nearer to abundant remembrance (dhikr) of Allah, more effective in his watchfulness (murāqabah) and safeguarding of his worship, and his abstention from committing prohibited acts; and that he be reminded thereby of death and the shrouds (akfān) of the dead, and be reminded of the Resurrection on the Day of Judgment when people will be barefoot, naked, hastening (muhṭiʿīn) toward the Caller. And the wisdom in prohibiting perfume and women is that he be distanced from luxury, the adornment of this world, and its pleasures, and that his concern be gathered solely for the purposes of the Hereafter.

And his saying, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: "Except one who finds no sandals — let him wear leather socks, and let him cut them below the ankles." Muslim mentioned after this, from the narration of Ibn ʿAbbās and Jābir: "Whoever finds no sandals, let him wear leather socks" — and he did not mention cutting them. The scholars diverged regarding these two ḥadīths. Aḥmad said: It is permissible to wear the leather socks as they are, and cutting is not obligatory, due to the ḥadīth of Ibn ʿAbbās and Jābir. And his companions claimed that the ḥadīth of Ibn ʿUmar — which explicitly states cutting — was abrogated (naskh), and they claimed that cutting them is a waste of wealth (iḍāʿat māl).
