Mālik, Abū Ḥanīfah, al-Shāfiʿī, and the majority of scholars said: It is not permissible to wear them except after cutting them below the ankles, due to the ḥadīth of Ibn ʿUmar. They said: The ḥadīths of Ibn ʿAbbās and Jābir are absolute (muṭlaq), so they must be carried upon the cut ones, due to the ḥadīth of Ibn ʿUmar — for the absolute is carried upon the restricted (muqayyad), and the addition from a trustworthy narrator is accepted. And their saying that it is a waste of wealth is not sound, for wastefulness is only in what is prohibited; as for what the Sacred Law has commanded, it is not wastefulness, but rather a right (ḥaqq) to which submission is obligatory. And Allah knows best.

Then the scholars diverged regarding one who wears leather socks due to the lack of sandals — whether compensation (fidyah) is due from him or not. Mālik, al-Shāfiʿī, and those who agreed with them said: Nothing is due from him, for had compensation been obligatory, he, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, would have clarified it. Abū Ḥanīfah and his companions said: Compensation is due from him, just as when one needs to shave his head — he shaves it and pays compensation. And Allah knows best.

[1177] His saying, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: "And do not wear any garment touched by saffron or wars." The ummah is unanimous upon the prohibition of wearing them, for they are perfume, and they analogized to them all types of what is sought for fragrance. And the cause (sabab) of prohibiting perfume is that it is an incitement to sexual intercourse, and because it contradicts the humility of the pilgrim — for the pilgrim is disheveled and dusty (ashʿath aghbar). And in the prohibition of perfume, men and women are equal, as are all other prohibitions of iḥrām except garments, as previously explained. And the prohibitions of iḥrām are seven: garments with their aforementioned detail; perfume; removal of hair and nail; oiling the head and beard; contracting marriage; sexual intercourse and all forms of enjoyment — even masturbation; and the seventh: the destruction of game. And Allah knows best.

And if one applies perfume or wears what is prohibited, compensation (fidyah) becomes incumbent upon him if he was deliberate (ʿāmid), by consensus. If he was forgetful (nāsī), then no compensation — according to al-Thawrī, al-Shāfiʿī, Aḥmad, and Isḥāq. Abū Ḥanīfah and Mālik made it obligatory. And the garment dyed with safflower (muʿaṣfar) is not unlawful according to Mālik and al-Shāfiʿī; al-Thawrī and Abū Ḥanīfah declared it unlawful, deeming it perfume, and made compensation obligatory therein. And it is disliked (makrūh) for the pilgrim to wear a garment dyed with something other than perfume, but it is not unlawful. And Allah knows best.

His saying, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: "The trousers (sirwāl) for one who finds no waist-wrapper, and the leather socks for one who finds no sandals" — meaning the pilgrim. This is explicit in its indication for al-Shāfiʿī and the majority regarding the permissibility of the pilgrim wearing trousers when he finds no waist-wrapper. Mālik prohibited it, for it was not mentioned in the aforementioned ḥadīth of Ibn ʿUmar. And the correct view is its permissibility, due to the ḥadīth of Ibn ʿAbbās, along with the ḥadīth of Jābir that follows. As for the ḥadīth of Ibn ʿUmar, there is no proof in it, for it mentions the state of the waist-wrapper's existence, while the ḥadīth of Ibn ʿAbbās and Jābir mentions the state of its absence — so there is no contradiction. And Allah knows best.

His saying: "While he was at al-Jiʿrānah" — in it are two well-known pronunciations: one with the sukūn on the ʿayn and the lightening of the rāʾ, and the second with the kasrah on the ʿayn and the doubling of the rāʾ. The first is the more eloquent (afṣaḥ), and both were stated by al-Shāfiʿī and most of the linguists. And likewise the two pronunciations in the lightening and doubling of al-Ḥudaybiyyah — the more eloquent is the lightening, and this is what al-Shāfiʿī and his supporters stated.

[1180] His saying: "Upon him was a jubba (jubbah) and upon it was khilūq" — it is with the fatḥah on the khāʾ, and it is a type of perfume in which saffron is used. His saying: "He had ghaṭīṭ" — it is like the sound of a sleeper which he repeats to himself. His saying: "Like the ghaṭīṭ of the bakr" — it is with the fatḥah on the bāʾ, and it is the young male camel. His saying: "When it was relieved from him (surriya ʿanhu)" — it is with the ḍammah on the sīn and the kasrah on the doubled rāʾ, meaning: what afflicted him was removed and unveiled from him. And Allah knows best.

His saying, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, to the questioner about ʿumrah: "Wash from yourself the trace of yellowness" — in it is the prohibition of perfume upon the pilgrim from the outset and continuously, for if it is prohibited continuously, then the outset is more deserving of prohibition. And in it...

chapters.title_en: The Lesser Pilgrimage (ʿUmrah) and Its Prohibitions; The Case of One Who Applies Perfume Forgetfully or Ignorantly; The Miqāt (Appointed Stations) for Pilgrimage
chapters.arabic_text:
إن العمرة يحرم فيها من الطيب واللباس وغيرهما من المحرمات السبعة السابقة

ما يحرم في الحج وفيه أن من أصابه طيب ناسيا أو جاهلا ثم علم وجبت عليه

المبادرة إلى إزالته وفيه أن من أصابه في إحرامه طيب ناسيا أو جاهلا لا

كفارة عليه وهذا مذهب الشافعي وبه قال عطاء والثوري وإسحاق وداود وقال مالك

وأبو حنيفة والمزني وأحمد في أصح الروايتين عنه عليه الفدية لكن الصحيح من

مذهب مالك أنه إنما تجب الفدية على المتطيب ناسيا أو جاهلا  إذا طال لبثه

عليه والله أعلم قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (واخلع عنك جبتك) دليل لمالك وأبي

حنيفة والشافعي والجمهور أن المحرم إذا صار عليه مخيط ينزعه ولا يلزمه شقه

وقال الشعبي والنخعي لا يجوز نزعه لئلا يصير مغطيا رأسه بل يلزمه شقه وهذا

مذهب ضعيف قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (واصنع في عمرتك ما أنت صانع في حجك)

معناه من اجتناب المحرمات ويحتمل أنه صلى الله عليه وسلم
# 
# أراد مع ذلك الطواف والسعي والحلق بصفاتها وهيئاتها وإظهار التلبية وغير

ذلك مما يشترك فيه الحج والعمرة ويخص من عمومه ما لا يدخل في العمرة من

أفعال الحج كالوقوف والرمي والمبيت بمنى ومزدلفة وغير ذلك وهذا الحديث ظاهر

في أن هذا السائل كان عالما بصفة الحج دون العمرة فلهذا قال له صلى الله

عليه وسلم واصنع في عمرتك ما أنت صانع في حجك وفي هذا الحديث دليل للقاعدة

المشهورة أن القاضي والمفتي إذا لم يعلم حكم المسألة أمسك عن جوابها حتى

يعلمه أو يظنه بشرطه وفيه أن من الأحكام التي ليست في القرآن ما هو بوحي لا

يتلى وقد يستدل به من يقول من أهل الأصول أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لم

يكن له الاجتهاد وإنما كان يحكم بوحي ولا دلالة فيه لأنه يحتمل أنه صلى

الله عليه وسلم لم يظهر له بالاجتهاد حكم ذلك أو أن الوحي بدره قبل تمام

الاجتهاد والله أعلم قوله (وكان يعلى يقول وددت أني أرى النبي صلى الله

عليه وسلم وقد نزل عليه الوحي فقال أيسرك أن تنظر إلى النبي صلى الله عليه

وسلم) هكذا هو في جميع النسخ فقال أيسرك ولم يبين القائل من هو ولا سبق له

ذكر وهذا القائل هو عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه كما بينه في الرواية التي

بعد هذه قوله (وعليه مقطعات) هي بفتح الطاء المشددة وهي الثياب المخيطة

وأوضحه بقوله يعنى جبة قوله (متضمخ) هو بالضاد والخاء المعجمتين أي متلوث

به مكثر منه
# 
# قوله (محمر الوجه  يغط) هو بكسر الغين وسبب ذلك شدة الوحى وهو له قال الله

تعالى إنا سنلقي عليك قولا ثقيلا قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (أما الطيب الذي

بك فاغسله ثلاث مرات) إنما أمر بالثلاث مبالغة في إزالة لونه وريحه والواجب

الإزالة فإن حصلت بمرة كفت ولم تجب الزيادة ولعل الطيب الذي كان على هذا

الرجل كثير ويؤيده قوله متضمخ قال القاضي ويحتمل أنه قال له ثلاث مرات

اغسله فكرر القول ثلاثا والصواب ما سبق والله أعلم قوله (عقبة بن مكرم) هو

بفتح الراء قوله في بعض هذه الرواية (صفوان
# 
# بن يعلى بن أمية) وفي بعضها بن منية وهما صحيحان فأمية أبو يعلى ومنية أم

يعلى وقيل جدته والمشهور الأول فنسب تارة إلى أبيه وتارة إلى أمه وهي منية

بضم الميم بعدها نون ساكنة قوله (حدثنا رباح) هو بالباء الموحدة قوله (فسكت

عنه فلم يرجع إليه) أي لم يرد جوابه قوله (خمره عمر بالثوب) أي غطاه وأما

إدخال يعلى رأسه ورؤيته النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في تلك الحال وإذن عمر له

في ذلك فكله محمول على أنهم علموا من النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه لا يكره

الاطلاع عليه في ذلك الوقت وتلك الحال لأن فيه تقوية الإيمان بمشاهدة حالة

الوحي الكريم والله أعلم
#

| (باب مواقيت الحج)

# ذكر مسلم في الباب ثلاثة أحاديث حديث بن عباس أكملها لأنه صرح فيه بنقله

المواقيت الأربعة من رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فلهذا ذكره مسلم في أول

الباب ثم حديث بن عمر لأنه لم يحفظ ميقات أهل اليمن بل بلغه بلاغا ثم حديث

جابر لأن أبا الزبير قال أحسب جابرا رفعه وهذا لا يقتضي ثبوته مرفوعا فوقت

رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لأهل المدينة ذا الحليفة بضم الحاء المهملة

وبالفاء وهي أبعد المواقيت من مكة بينهما نحو عشر مراحل أو تسع وهي قريبة

من المدينة على نحو ستة أميال منها ولأهل الشام الجحفة وهي ميقات لهم ولأهل

مصر وهي بجيم مضمومة ثم  حاء مهملة ساكنة قيل سميت بذلك لأن السيل أجحفها في

وقت ويقال لها مهيعة بفتح الميم وإسكان الهاء وفتح المثناة تحت كما ذكره في

بعض روايات مسلم وحكى القاضي عياض عن بعضهم كسر الهاء والصحيح المشهور

إسكانها وهي على نحو ثلاث مراحل من مكة على طريق المدينة ولأهل اليمن يلملم

بفتح المثناة تحت واللامين ويقال أيضا ألملم بهمزة بدل الياء لغتان

مشهورتان وهو جبل من جبال تهامة على مرحلتين من مكة ولأهل نجد قرن المنازل

بفتح القاف وإسكان الراء بلا خلاف بين أهل العلم من أهل الحديث واللغة

والتاريخ والأسماء وغيرهم وغلط الجوهري في صحاحه فيه غلطين فاحشين فقال
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ع-م-ر (ʿ-m-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning is "visitation" or "a journey for a purpose"; in sacred law, it denotes the specific rites of circumambulation (ṭawāf), running (saʿy), and shaving/trimming (ḥalq/taqṣīr) performed at the Sacred Mosque.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Theologically, ʿumrah is an act of devotion (qurbah) that shares in the sanctity of ḥajj but is distinguished by its lesser scope; it is a "lesser visitation" (al-ziyārah al-ṣughrā) to the House of Allah.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literally, ʿumrah is "a visit"; metaphorically, it is the ritual act itself, as the physical journey is a sign (majāz) of the spiritual intent (niyyah).
- Root: ط-ي-ب (ṭ-y-b)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Root meaning is "goodness, purity, fragrance"; in the state of iḥrām, it refers to perfumes and scented substances.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In Kalām, ṭīb is associated with what is lawful and pure (ṭayyibāt); its prohibition in iḥrām is a test of obedience, as it is a sensory pleasure that distracts from the spiritual focus.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: perfume; metaphorical: any pleasant scent that lingers, hence the command to wash it off thrice to remove both color and odor.
- Root: م-ي-ق-ت (m-y-q-t) / و-ق-ت (w-q-t)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: The root w-q-t means "time" or "appointed term"; miqāt (pl. mawāqīt) is the fixed place or time for entering iḥrām.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In sacred law, the mawāqīt are divinely ordained boundaries (ḥudūd) that demarcate the spatial and temporal commencement of pilgrimage rites, symbolizing the believer's submission to divine ordinance.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: an appointed time/place; metaphorical: a boundary set by the Lawgiver, beyond which one must assume the state of iḥrām.
- Sībawayh Rule: Rule of Condition and Exception (al-sharṭ wa-l-jawāb) — In the phrase "if one is struck by perfume forgetfully or ignorantly, then he must hasten to remove it," the conditional clause (sharṭ) is followed by the apodosis (jawāb) that is obligatory (wājib) upon knowledge, distinguishing between the state of ignorance and the state of awareness.
chapters.translation:
I say: The ʿumrah entails the prohibition of perfume, tailored garments, and the other seven previously mentioned prohibitions that apply to ḥajj.

Within this [section] is [the ruling] that if one is struck by perfume while forgetful (nāsiyan) or ignorant (jāhilan), then upon becoming aware, he is obligated to hasten to remove it. And within it is [the ruling] that if one is struck by perfume during his iḥrām forgetfully or ignorantly, there is no expiation (kafārah) upon him. This is the school (madhhab) of al-Shāfiʿī, and it is also the view of ʿAṭāʾ, al-Thawrī, Isḥāq, and Dāwūd. Mālik, Abū Ḥanīfah, al-Muzanī, and Aḥmad — in the more authentic of the two narrations from him — held that he owes a ransom (fidyah). However, the correct view in the school of Mālik is that the fidyah is only obligatory upon one who applies perfume forgetfully or ignorantly if his remaining [in that state] is prolonged. And Allah knows best.

His statement, peace and blessings be upon him: {«وَاخْلَعْ عَنْكَ جُبَّتَكَ»} ("And take off your cloak") is evidence for Mālik, Abū Ḥanīfah, al-Shāfiʿī, and the majority (al-jumhūr) that if a person in iḥrām has a sewn garment upon him, he must remove it, and he is not obligated to tear it. Al-Shaʿbī and al-Nakhaʿī said: It is not permissible to remove it, lest he become one who covers his head; rather, he must tear it. This is a weak view (madhhab ḍaʿīf).

His statement, peace and blessings be upon him: {«وَاصْنَعْ فِي عُمْرَتِكَ مَا أَنْتَ صَانِعٌ فِي حَجِّكَ»} ("And do in your ʿumrah what you do in your ḥajj") means [doing so] in terms of avoiding the prohibitions (ijtināb al-muḥarramāt). It is also possible that he, peace and blessings be upon him, intended thereby the ṭawāf, the saʿy, the shaving (ḥalq), with their descriptions and forms, the proclamation of the talbiyah, and other acts shared between ḥajj and ʿumrah. Excluded from its generality are those acts of ḥajj that do not enter into ʿumrah, such as the standing at ʿArafah (wuqūf), the stoning (ramy), the overnight stay at Minā and Muzdalifah, and other such acts.

This ḥadīth is apparent in [indicating] that this questioner was knowledgeable of the description of ḥajj but not of ʿumrah; for this reason, he, peace and blessings be upon him, said to him: "Do in your ʿumrah what you do in your ḥajj."

In this ḥadīth is evidence for the well-known principle (al-qāʿidah al-mashhūrah) that the judge (al-qāḍī) and the muftī, when they do not know the ruling of a matter, should refrain from answering it until they know it or have a strong presumption (ẓann) of it, under its conditions.

And in it is [evidence] that among the rulings not [found] in the Qurʾān are those that are [derived from] revelation not recited (waḥy ghayr matlū). One may adduce it from those among the scholars of uṣūl who say that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, did not exercise personal reasoning (ijtihād); rather, he ruled only by revelation. But there is no indication [of that] in it, because it is possible that he, peace and blessings be upon him, did not have a ruling of that matter manifest to him through ijtihād, or that revelation preceded him before the completion of his ijtihād. And Allah knows best.

His statement — and Yaʿlā was saying: "I wish (wadadtu) that I could see the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, when revelation descended upon him" — [the narrator] said: "Would it please you (a-yasurruka) to look at the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him?" Thus it is in all copies: "a-yasurruka," and the speaker is not identified, nor was there any prior mention of him. This speaker is ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, may Allah be pleased with him, as clarified in the narration that follows this one.

His statement: {«وَعَلَيْهِ مَقَطَّعَاتٌ»} ("And upon him were cut garments") — with a fatḥah on the shaddah ṭāʾ — meaning sewn garments (al-thiyāb al-mukhayyaṭah). He clarified it by his saying: "meaning a cloak (jubbah)."

His statement: {«مُتَضَمِّخٌ»} ("smeared") — with ḍād and khāʾ, both unpointed — meaning saturated with it, having applied much of it.

His statement: {«مُحْمَرَّ الْوَجْهِ يَغُطُّ»} ("with a reddened face, breathing heavily") — with kasrah on the ghayn — and the cause of that is the intensity of revelation, and it is so for him. Allah, the Exalted, said: {«إِنَّا سَنُلْقِي عَلَيْكَ قَوْلًا ثَقِيلًا»} ("Indeed, We will cast upon you a heavy word") [73:5].

His statement, peace and blessings be upon him: {«أَمَّا الطِّيبُ الَّذِي بِكَ فَاغْسِلْهُ ثَلَاثَ مَرَّاتٍ»} ("As for the perfume on you, wash it three times") — he only commanded three times as an exaggeration (mubālaghah) in removing its color and its scent. The obligatory [requirement] is removal; if it is achieved with one washing, that suffices, and no increase is obligatory. Perhaps the perfume on this man was copious, supported by his statement "smeared." Al-Qāḍī said: It is possible that he said to him "three times — wash it," repeating the statement three times. The correct [view] is what preceded. And Allah knows best.

His statement: {«عُقْبَةُ بْنُ مَكْرَمٍ»} — with fatḥah on the rāʾ.

His statement in some of these narrations: {«صَفْوَانُ بْنُ يَعْلَى بْنِ أُمَيَّةَ»} ("Ṣafwān ibn Yaʿlā ibn Umayyah"), and in some: {«ابْنُ مُنْيَةَ»} ("ibn Munyah") — both are correct. Umayyah is the father of Yaʿlā, and Munyah is the mother of Yaʿlā; it is also said [she was] his grandmother. The well-known [view] is the first. Thus he is attributed sometimes to his father and sometimes to his mother, and she is Munyah — with ḍammah on the mīm, followed by a sukūn on the nūn.

His statement: {«حَدَّثَنَا رَبَاحٌ»} — with a single unpointed bāʾ.

His statement: {«فَسَكَتَ عَنْهُ فَلَمْ يَرْجِعْ إِلَيْهِ»} ("He remained silent toward him and did not return to him") — meaning he did not answer him.

His statement: {«خَمَّرَهُ عُمَرُ بِالثَّوْبِ»} ("ʿUmar covered him with the garment") — meaning he concealed him. As for Yaʿlā inserting his head and seeing the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, in that state, and ʿUmar's permission to him for that — all of that is understood [as occurring] because they knew from the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, that he did not dislike being seen at that time and in that state, because in it there is a strengthening of faith (taqwiyat al-īmān) through witnessing the state of noble revelation. And Allah knows best.

---

| (Chapter: The Appointed Stations (Mawāqīt) for Pilgrimage)

Muslim mentioned in this chapter three ḥadīths. The ḥadīth of Ibn ʿAbbās is the most complete of them, because he explicitly transmitted the four mawāqīt from the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him; for this reason, Muslim placed it at the beginning of the chapter. Then the ḥadīth of Ibn ʿUmar, because he did not memorize the miqāt of the people of Yemen; rather, it reached him as a report (balāghan). Then the ḥadīth of Jābir, because Abū al-Zubayr said: "I reckon Jābir raised it (rafaʿahu)" — and this does not necessitate its authenticity as marfūʿ.

The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, appointed for the people of Medina Dhū al-Ḥulayfah — with ḍammah on the unpointed ḥāʾ and with fāʾ — and it is the farthest of the mawāqīt from Mecca; between them is approximately ten or nine stages (marāḥil). It is near Medina, about six miles from it. For the people of Syria (al-Shām), [he appointed] al-Juḥfah, which is a miqāt for them and for the people of Egypt. It is with jīm, ḍammah on it, then an unpointed ḥāʾ with sukūn. It is said it was named thus because a flood (al-sayl) swept it away (ajḥafahā) at some time. It is also called Mahyaʿah — with fatḥah on the mīm, sukūn on the hāʾ, and fatḥah on the tāʾ (the second letter of the word, i.e., the yāʾ) — as mentioned in some narrations of Muslim. Al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ reported from some [scholars] the kasrah of the hāʾ; the correct and well-known [pronunciation] is its sukūn. It is approximately three stages from Mecca, on the road to Medina.

For the people of Yemen, [he appointed] Yalamlam — with fatḥah on the tāʾ (the second letter) and the two lāms. It is also said Alamlam, with a hamzah in place of the yāʾ — two well-known dialects. It is a mountain of the mountains of Tihāmah, two stages from Mecca.

For the people of Najd, [he appointed] Qarn al-Manāzil — with fatḥah on the qāf and sukūn on the rāʾ, without disagreement among the people of knowledge from the scholars of ḥadīth, language, history, genealogy, and others. Al-Jawharī erred in his al-Ṣiḥāḥ concerning it with two flagrant errors, for he said...

chapters.title_en: The Miqāt Boundaries and Their Legal Rulings (Section 470)
chapters.arabic_text:
بفتح الراء وزعم أن أويسا القرني رضي الله عنه منسوب إليه والصواب إسكان

الراء وأن أويسا منسوب إلى قبيلة معروفة يقال لهم بنو قرن وهي بطن من مراد

القبيلة المعروفة ينسب إليها المرادي وقرن المنازل على نحو مرحلتين من مكة

قالوا وهو أقرب المواقيت إلى مكة وأما ذات عرق بكسر العين فهي ميقات أهل

العراق واختلف العلماء هل صارت ميقاتهم بتوقيت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أم

باجتهاد عمر بن الخطاب وفي المسألة وجهان لأصحاب الشافعي أصحهما وهو نص

الشافعي رضي الله عنه في الأم بتوقيت عمر رضي الله عنه وذلك صريح في صحيح

البخاري ودليل من قال بتوقيت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم حديث جابر لكنه غير

ثابت لعدم جزمه برفعه وأما قول الدارقطني إنه حديث ضعيف لأن العراق لم تكن
# 
# فتحت في زمن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فكلامه في تضعيفه صحيح ودليله ما

ذكرته وأما استدلاله لضعفه بعدم فتح العراق ففاسد لأنه لا يمتنع أن يخبر به

النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم به لعلمه بأنه سيفتح ويكون ذلك من معجزات النبي

صلى الله عليه وسلم والإخبار بالمغيبات المستقبلات كما أنه صلى الله عليه

وسلم وقت لأهل الشام الجحفة في جميع الأحاديث الصحيحة ومعلوم أن الشام لم

يكن فتح حينئذ وقد ثبتت الأحاديث الصحيحة عنه صلى الله عليه وسلم  أنه أخبر

بفتح الشام واليمن والعراق وأنهم يأتون إليهم يبسون والمدينة خير لهم لو

كانوا يعلمون وأنه صلى الله عليه وسلم أخبر بأنه زويت له مشارق الارض

ومغاربها وقال سيبلغ ملك أمتي مازوى لي منها وأنهم سيفتحون مصر وهي أرض

يذكر فيها القيراط وأن عيسى عليه السلام ينزل على المنارة البيضاء شرقي

دمشق وكل هذه الأحاديث في الصحيح وفي الصحيح من هذا القبيل ما يطول ذكره

والله أعلم وأجمع العلماء على أن هذه المواقيت مشروعة ثم قال مالك وأبو

حنيفة والشافعي وأحمد والجمهور هي واجبة لو تركها وأحرم بعد مجاوزتها أثم

ولزمه دم وصح حجه وقال عطاء والنخعي لا شيء عليه وقال سعيد بن جبير لا يصح

حجه وفائدة المواقيت أن من أراد حجا أو عمرة حرم عليه مجاوزتها بغير إحرام

ولزمه الدم كما ذكرنا قال أصحابنا فإن عاد إلى الميقات قبل التلبس بنسك سقط

عنه الدم وفي المراد بهذا النسك خلاف منتشر وأما من لا يريد حجا ولاعمرة

فلا يلزمه الإحرام لدخول مكة على الصحيح من مذهبنا سواء دخل لحاجة تتكرر

كحطاب وحشاش وصياد ونحوهم أولا تتكرر كتجارة وزيارة ونحوهما وللشافعي قول

ضعيف أنه يجب الإحرام بحج أو عمرة إن دخل مكة أو غيرها من الحرم لما يتكرر

بشرط سبق بيانه في أول كتاب الحج وأما من مر بالميقات غير مريد دخول الحرم

بل لحاجة دونه ثم بدا له أن يحرم فيحرم من موضعه الذي بدا له فيه فإن جاوزه

بلا إحرام ثم أحرم أثم ولزمه الدم وإن أحرم من الموضع الذي بدا له أجزأه

ولا دم عليه ولا يكلف الرجوع إلى الميقات هذا مذهبنا ومذهب الجمهور وقال

أحمد وإسحاق يلزمه الرجوع إلى الميقات
# 
# [1181] قوله (وقت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لأهل المدينة ذا الحليفة

ولأهل الشام الجحفة ولأهل نجد قرن) هكذا وقع في أكثر النسخ قرن من غير ألف

بعد النون وفي بعضها قرنا بالألف وهو الأجود لأنه موضع واسم لجبل فوجب صرفه

والذي وقع بغير ألف  يقرأ منونا وإنما حذفوا الألف كما جرت عادة بعض

المحدثين يكتبون يقول سمعت أنس بغير ألف ويقرأ بالتنوين ويحتمل على بعد أن

يقرأ قرن منصوبا بغير تنوين ويكون أراد به البقعة فيترك صرفه قوله صلى الله

عليه وسلم (فهن لهن ولمن أتى عليهن من غير أهلهن) قال القاضي كذا جاءت

الرواية في الصحيحين وغيرهما عند أكثر الرواة قال ووقع عند بعض رواة

البخاري ومسلم فهن لهم وكذا رواه أبو داود وغيره وكذا ذكره مسلم من رواية

بن أبي شيبة وهو الوجه لأنه ضمير أهل هذه المواضع قال ووجه الرواية

المشهورة أن الضمير في لهن عائد على المواضع والأقطار المذكورة وهي المدينة

والشام واليمن ونجد أي هذه المواقيت لهذه الأقطار والمراد لأهلها فحذف

المضاف وأقام المضاف إليه مقامه وقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم ولمن أتى عليهن

من غير أهلهن معناه أن الشامي مثلا إذا مر بميقات المدينة في ذهابه لزمه أن

يحرم من ميقات المدينة ولا يجوز له تأخيره إلى ميقات الشام الذي هو الجحفة

وكذا الباقي من المواقيت وهذا لاخلاف فيه قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم فهن لهن

ولمن أتى عليهن من غير أهلهن ممن أراد الحج والعمرة فيه دلالة للمذهب

الصحيح فيمن مر بالميقات لا يريد حجا ولا عمرة أنه لا يلزمه الإحرام لدخول

مكة وقد سبقت المسألة واضحة قال بعض العلماء وفيه دلالة على أن الحج على

التراخي لا على الفور وقد سبقت المسألة واضحة في أول كتاب الحج قوله صلى

الله عليه وسلم (فمن كان دونهن فمن أهله) هذا صريح في أن من كان مسكنه بين

مكة والميقات فميقاته مسكنه إلى الميقات ولا يجوز له مجاوزة مسكنه بغير

احرام
# 
# هذا مذهبنا ومذهب العلماء كافة إلا مجاهدا فقال ميقاته مكة بنفسها قوله
chapters.anchors:
- Root: و-ق-ت (waqata)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To specify, delimit, or appoint a time or place; a defined boundary (mīqāt) for ritual acts.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The divinely or prophetically instituted boundary for entering the state of iḥrām; a legal limit (ḥadd) set by revelation.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) designation of spatial limits; metaphorical (majāz) extension to "appointed times" for worship.
- Sībawayh Rule: ʾIḍāfah (Construct State) — The omission of the governed noun (ḥadhf al-muḍāf) with the genitive standing in its place, as in "for them (lahunna)" referring to the inhabitants via the lands.
chapters.translation:
I say: With the opening of the letter rāʾ (Qaran), and it was claimed that Uways al-Qaranī, may Allah be pleased with him, is attributed to it. The correct view is the stilling of the rāʾ (Qarn), and that Uways is attributed to a well-known tribe called Banū Qarn, which is a subdivision of Murād — the well-known tribe to which al-Murādī is attributed. And Qarn al-Manāzil is approximately two stages from Mecca. They said: It is the closest of the mawāqīt (appointed boundaries) to Mecca. As for Dhāt ʿIrq — with the kasrah on the ʿayn — it is the mīqāt of the people of Iraq. The scholars differed as to whether it became their mīqāt by the Prophet's (peace and blessings be upon him) designation or by the ijtihād (independent reasoning) of ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb. There are two positions among the Shāfiʿī jurists; the more correct of them — and it is the explicit text (naṣṣ) of al-Shāfiʿī, may Allah be pleased with him, in al-Umm — is that it was by ʿUmar's designation, and this is explicit in Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī. The evidence of those who say it was by the Prophet's designation is the ḥadīth of Jābir, but it is not established (thābit) due to the lack of certainty in its elevation (rafʿ) to the Prophet. As for al-Dāraquṭnī's statement that it is a weak ḥadīth because Iraq had not yet been conquered in the Prophet's time — his critique of its weakness is sound, and the evidence is what I have mentioned. But his inference of its weakness from the non-conquest of Iraq is corrupt, because it is not impossible that the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) informed of it, due to his knowledge that it would be conquered — and this would be among his miracles. And informing of future unseen matters — just as he (peace and blessings be upon him) designated al-Juḥfah for the people of Syria in all the authentic ḥadīths, while it is known that Syria had not been conquered at that time. The authentic ḥadīths are established from him (peace and blessings be upon him) that he informed of the conquest of Syria, Yemen, and Iraq, and that they would come to them hastening, and that Medina is better for them if they but knew; and that he (peace and blessings be upon him) informed that the east and west of the earth were folded for him, and he said: "The dominion of my nation will reach what was folded for me of it," and that they would conquer Egypt — a land in which the qīrāṭ is mentioned — and that Jesus (peace be upon him) would descend upon the white minaret east of Damascus. All these ḥadīths are in the Ṣaḥīḥ, and in the Ṣaḥīḥ there is much of this kind whose mention would be lengthy. And Allah knows best.

The scholars are unanimous that these mawāqīt are legislated (mashrūʿah). Then Mālik, Abū Ḥanīfah, al-Shāfiʿī, Aḥmad, and the majority (al-jumhūr) said: They are obligatory (wājibah); if one abandons them and enters iḥrām after passing them, he sins, a blood-offering (dam) is incumbent upon him, and his ḥajj is valid. ʿAṭāʾ and al-Nakhaʿī said: Nothing is incumbent upon him. Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said: His ḥajj is not valid. The benefit of the mawāqīt is that whoever intends ḥajj or ʿumrah, it is forbidden for him to pass them without iḥrām, and the blood-offering is incumbent upon him, as we mentioned. Our companions said: If he returns to the mīqāt before engaging in the rite (nusuk), the blood-offering is dropped from him. There is a widespread disagreement regarding the meaning of this "rite." As for one who does not intend ḥajj or ʿumrah, iḥrām is not incumbent upon him for entering Mecca, according to the correct view of our school — whether he enters for a recurring need, like a firewood-gatherer, a grass-cutter, a hunter, and the like, or a non-recurring one, like trade, visitation, and the like. There is a weak position attributed to al-Shāfiʿī that iḥrām for ḥajj or ʿumrah is obligatory if one enters Mecca or any part of the Sacred Precinct (al-ḥaram) for a recurring need, with the condition previously explained at the beginning of the Book of Ḥajj. As for one who passes by the mīqāt not intending to enter the Sacred Precinct, but rather for a need before it, then it occurs to him to enter iḥrām — he enters iḥrām from his location where it occurred to him. If he passes it without iḥrām and then enters iḥrām, he sins and the blood-offering is incumbent upon him. But if he enters iḥrām from the location where it occurred to him, it suffices him, and no blood-offering is upon him, nor is he required to return to the mīqāt. This is our school and the school of the majority. Aḥmad and Isḥāq said: He must return to the mīqāt.

[1181] His statement (peace and blessings be upon him): "The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) designated for the people of Medina Dhū al-Ḥulayfah, for the people of Syria al-Juḥfah, and for the people of Najd Qarn." Thus it occurs in most copies as "Qarn" without an alif after the nūn, and in some of them "Qaran" with an alif — and this is the more excellent (ajwad), because it is a place-name and the name of a mountain, so its full declension (ṣarf) is obligatory. What occurs without the alif is read with tanwīn; they merely omitted the alif, as is the custom of some ḥadīth transmitters who write "he said: I heard Anas" without an alif and read it with tanwīn. It is also possible, though remotely, that "Qarn" is read as a non-declined accusative (manṣūb bi-ghayr tanwīn), intending thereby the land (al-buqʿah), thus leaving it undeclined.

His statement (peace and blessings be upon him): "These are for them (lahunna), and for whoever comes upon them from other than their people." Al-Qāḍī said: Thus the narration came in the two Ṣaḥīḥs and others according to most transmitters. He said: It occurs with some transmitters of al-Bukhārī and Muslim as "for them (lahum)," and thus Abū Dāwūd and others narrated it, and Muslim mentioned it likewise in the narration of Ibn Abī Shaybah — and this is the proper form (al-wajh), because it is the pronoun for the people of these places. He said: The justification for the well-known narration is that the pronoun in "lahunna" refers back to the places and regions mentioned — namely Medina, Syria, Yemen, and Najd — meaning: these mawāqīt are for these regions, and the intent is for their people; thus the governed noun was omitted and the genitive was made to stand in its place. His statement (peace and blessings be upon him): "And for whoever comes upon them from other than their people" means: a Syrian, for example, if he passes by the mīqāt of Medina on his way, it is incumbent upon him to enter iḥrām from the mīqāt of Medina, and it is not permissible for him to delay it to the Syrian mīqāt, which is al-Juḥfah. Likewise for the rest of the mawāqīt. There is no disagreement on this.

His statement (peace and blessings be upon him): "These are for them, and for whoever comes upon them from other than their people, of those intending ḥajj and ʿumrah" — in this there is an indication for the correct school (al-madhhab al-ṣaḥīḥ) regarding one who passes by the mīqāt not intending ḥajj or ʿumrah: that iḥrām is not incumbent upon him for entering Mecca. The matter has already been discussed clearly. Some scholars said: In it there is an indication that ḥajj is on deferment (al-tarākhī) and not on immediacy (al-fawr). The matter has already been discussed clearly at the beginning of the Book of Ḥajj.

His statement (peace and blessings be upon him): "And whoever is before them (dūnahunna), then his mīqāt is from his own people (min ahlihi)" — this is explicit (ṣarīḥ) that whoever's residence is between Mecca and the mīqāt, his mīqāt is his residence up to the mīqāt, and it is not permissible for him to pass his residence without iḥrām. This is our school and the school of all the scholars, except Mujāhid, who said: His mīqāt is Mecca itself. His statement —

chapters.title_en: The Miqāt of the People of Mecca and the Legal Rulings of the Talbiyah
chapters.arabic_text:
صلى الله عليه وسلم (فمن كان دونهن فمن أهله وكذا فكذلك حتى أهل مكة يهلون

منها) هكذا هو في جميع النسخ وهو صحيح ومعناه وهكذا فهكذا من جاوز مسكنه

الميقات حتى أهل مكة يهلون منها وأجمع  العلماء على هذا كله فمن كان في مكة

من أهلها أو واردا إليها وأراد الإحرام بالحج فميقاته نفس مكة ولا يجوز له

ترك مكة والإحرام بالحج من خارجها سواء الحرم والحل هذا هو الصحيح عند

أصحابنا وقال بعض أصحابنا يجوز له أن يحرم به من الحرم كما يجوز من مكة لأن

حكم الحرم حكم مكة والصحيح الأول لهذا الحديث قال أصحابنا ويجوز أن يحرم من

جميع نواحي مكة بحيث لا يخرج عن نفس المدينة وسورها وفي الأفضل قولان

أصحهما من باب داره والثاني من المسجد الحرام تحت الميزاب والله أعلم وهذا

كله في إحرام المكي بالحج والحديث إنما هو في إحرامه بالحج وأما ميقات

المكي للعمرة فأدنى الحل لحديث عائشة الآتي أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
# 
# أمرها في العمرة أن تخرج إلى التنعيم وتحرم بالعمرة منه والتنعيم في طرف

الحل والله أعلم قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (مهل أهل المدينة) هو بضم الميم

وفتح الهاء وتشديد اللام أي موضع إهلالهم قوله (قال عبد الله بن عمر

وزعموا) أي قالوا وقد سبق في أول الكتاب أن الزعم قد يكون بمعنى القول

المحقق
# 
# [1183] قوله (أخبرني أبو الزبير أنه سمع جابر بن عبد الله يسأل عن المهل

فقال سمعته ثم انتهى فقال أراه يعني النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم) معنى هذا

الكلام أن أبا الزبير قال سمعت جابرا ثم انتهى أي وقف عن رفع الحديث إلى

النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وقال أراه بضم الهمزة أي أظنه رفع الحديث فقال

أراه يعني النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كما قال في الرواية الأخرى أحسبه رفع

إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وقوله أحسبه رفع لا يحتج بهذا الحديث مرفوعا

لكونه لم يجزم برفعه قوله في حديث جابر (ومهل أهل العراق من ذات عرف) هذا

صريح في كونه ميقات أهل العراق لكن ليس رفع الحديث ثابتا كما سبق وقد سبق

الإجماع على أن ذات عرق ميقات أهل العراق ومن في معناهم قال الشافعي ولو

أهلوا من العقيق كان أفضل والعقيق أبعد من ذات عرق بقليل فاستحبه الشافعي

لأثر فيه ولأنه قيل إن ذات عرق كانت أولا في موضعه ثم حولت وقربت إلى مكة

والله أعلم واعلم أن للحج ميقات مكان وهو ما سبق في هذه الأحاديث وميقات

زمان وهو شوال وذو القعدة وعشر ليال من ذي الحجة ولا يجوز الا حرام بالحج

في غير هذا الزمان هذا مذهب الشافعي ولو أحرم بالحج في غير هذا الزمان لم

ينعقد حجا وانعقد عمرة وأما العمرة فيجوز الإحرام بها وفعلها في جميع السنة

ولا يكره في شيء منها لكن شرطها أن لا يكون
# 
# في الحج ولا مقيما على شيء من أفعاله ولا يكره تكرار العمرة في السنة بل

يستحب عندنا وعند الجمهور وكره تكرارها في السنة بن سيرين ومالك ويجوز

الإحرام بالحج مما فوق الميقات أبعد من مكة سواء دويرة أهله وغيرها وأيهما

أفضل فيه قولان للشافعي أصحهما من الميقات أفضل للاقتداء برسول الله صلى

الله عليه وسلم والله أعلم

| (باب التلبية وصفتها ووقتها)
# قال القاضي قال المازري التلبية مثناة للتكثير والمبالغة ومعناه إجابة

بعد إجابة ولزوما لطاعتك فتثنى للتوكيد لا تثنية حقيقية بمنزلة قوله تعالى

بل يداه مبسوطتان أي نعمتاه على تأويل اليد بالنعمة هنا ونعم الله تعالى لا

تحصى وقال يونس بن حبيب البصري لبيك اسم مفرد لا مثنى قال وألفه انما

انقلبت ياء لا تصالها بالضمير كلدي وعلى مذهب سيبويه أنه مثنى بدليل قلبها

ياء مع المظهر وأكثر الناس على ما قاله سيبويه قال بن الأنباري ثنوا لبيك

كما ثنوا حنانيك أي تحننا بعد تحنن وأصل لبيك لببتك فاستثقلوا الجمع بين

ثلاث باءات فأبدلوا من الثالثة ياء كما قالوا من الظن تظنيت والأصل تظننت

واختلفوا في معنى لبيك واشتقاقها فقيل معناها اتجاهي وقصدي إليك مأخوذ من

قولهم داري تلب دارك أي تواجهها وقيل معناها محبتي قولهم لك مأخوذ من قولهم

امرأة لبة إذا كانت محبة لولدها عاطفة عليه وقيل معناها إخلاص لك مأخوذ من

قولهم حب لباب إذا كان خالصا محضا ومن ذلك لب الطعام ولبابه وقيل معناها

أنا مقيم على طاعتك وإجابتك مأخوذ من قولهم لب الرجل بالمكان وألب إذا أقام

فيه قال بن الأنباري وبهذا قال الخليل قال القاضي قيل هذه الإجابة لقوله

تعالى لإبراهيم صلى الله عليه وسلم وأذن في الناس بالحج وقال إبراهيم

الحربي في معنى لبيك أي قربا منك وطاعة والإلباب القرب وقال أبو نصر معناه

أنا ملب بين يديك أي خاضع هذا آخر كلام القاضي
# 
# [1184] قوله (لبيك إن الحمد والنعمة) يروى بكسر الهمزة من إن وفتحها

وجهان مشهوران لأهل الحديث وأهل اللغة قال الجمهور الكسر أجود قال الخطابي

الفتح رواية العامة وقال ثعلب الاختيار الكسر وهو الأجود في المعنى من

الفتح لأن من كسر جعل معناه إن الحمد والنعمة لك على كل حال ومن فتح قال

معناه لبيك لهذا السبب قوله (والنعمة لك) المشهور فيه نصب النعمة قال
chapters.anchors:
- Root: م-ك-ن (m-k-n)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Place of settlement, abode, dwelling; the root denotes spatial fixation and establishment.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The designated spatial boundary (miqāt) as a legally-instituted locus of ritual entry (iḥrām).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) for physical location; metaphorical (majāz) for the legal designation of a boundary.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clause with Ellipsis (al-sharṭ wa-l-jawāb bi-ḥadhf) — the phrase "فمن كان دونهن" (whoever resides before them) operates as a conditional whose apodosis is contextually implied, requiring the reader to supply the governing verb from the preceding discourse.
chapters.translation:
I say — and Allah knows best:

The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said: «And whoever resides before them [i.e., before the mawāqīt], then his miqāt is from his own dwelling-place; and likewise, so likewise, until the people of Mecca — they enter iḥrām from Mecca itself.» This is how it appears in all manuscript copies, and it is sound. Its meaning is: "And likewise, so likewise" — whoever passes beyond his dwelling-place [toward Mecca] beyond the miqāt, even the people of Mecca, they enter iḥrām from Mecca itself.

The scholars are in unanimous agreement (ijmāʿ) upon all of this. Thus, whoever is in Mecca — whether a resident of its people or one arriving into it — and intends to enter iḥrām for the Ḥajj, then his miqāt is Mecca itself. It is not permissible for him to leave Mecca and enter iḥrām for the Ḥajj from outside it — whether [that place be] within the Sacred Precinct (al-ḥaram) or outside it (al-ḥill). This is the correct position (al-ṣaḥīḥ) according to our companions [the Shāfiʿīs].

Some of our companions said: It is permissible for him to enter iḥrām from within the Sacred Precinct, just as it is permissible from Mecca, because the legal ruling of the Sacred Precinct is the ruling of Mecca. But the correct position is the first, on account of this ḥadīth.

Our companions said: It is permissible to enter iḥrām from all directions of Mecca, provided he does not exit the city itself and its wall. Regarding what is more virtuous (al-afḍal), there are two opinions: the more correct of them is from the door of his house; the second is from the Sacred Mosque (al-Masjid al-Ḥarām) beneath the water-spout (al-mīzāb). And Allah knows best.

All of this concerns the iḥrām of the Meccan for the Ḥajj, and the ḥadīth is only concerning his iḥrām for the Ḥajj. As for the miqāt of the Meccan for the ʿUmrah, it is the nearest point of al-ḥill (the area outside the Sacred Precinct), on account of the ḥadīth of ʿĀʾishah, forthcoming, that the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) commanded her in the ʿUmrah to go out to al-Tanʿīm and to enter iḥrām for the ʿUmrah from it. And al-Tanʿīm is at the edge of al-ḥill. And Allah knows best.

His saying (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him): «The muhill of the people of Madīnah» — it is with ḍammah on the mīm, fatḥah on the hāʾ, and tashdīd on the lām, meaning: the place of their iḥrām (i.e., their miqāt).

His saying: «ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar said: "And they claimed (zaʿamū)"» — meaning: they said. It has preceded at the beginning of the Book that "al-zaʿm" may carry the meaning of verified speech (al-qawl al-muḥaqqaq).

[1183] His saying: «Abū al-Zubayr informed me that he heard Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh being asked about the muhill, and he said: "I heard him, then he stopped (intahā), then he said: 'I think (arāhu) he meant the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him).'"» The meaning of this statement is that Abū al-Zubayr said: "I heard Jābir," then he stopped — i.e., he refrained from raising (rafʿ) the ḥadīth to the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) — and said: "I think (arāhu)" — with ḍammah on the hamzah, i.e., "I suppose" — that he raised the ḥadīth. Thus he said: "I think he meant the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him)," just as he said in the other narration: "I reckon (aḥsibuhu) he raised it to the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him)." And his saying "I reckon he raised it" — this ḥadīth is not adduced as evidence as marfūʿ (raised to the Prophet), because he did not affirm its elevation with certainty.

His saying in the ḥadīth of Jābir: «And the muhill of the people of Iraq is from Dhāt ʿIrq» — this is explicit (ṣarīḥ) in that it is the miqāt of the people of Iraq. However, the elevation of the ḥadīth (rafʿuhu) is not established, as has preceded. And the consensus (ijmāʿ) has already been mentioned that Dhāt ʿIrq is the miqāt of the people of Iraq and those in their category.

Al-Shāfiʿī said: If they were to enter iḥrām from al-ʿAqīq, that would be more virtuous. And al-ʿAqīq is slightly farther than Dhāt ʿIrq. Al-Shāfiʿī deemed it recommended (istaḥabbahu) due to an athar (narration) concerning it, and because it was said that Dhāt ʿIrq was originally in the location of al-ʿAqīq, then it was relocated and brought closer to Mecca. And Allah knows best.

Know that the Ḥajj has a temporal miqāt (miqāt zamān) and a spatial miqāt (miqāt makān). The spatial is what has preceded in these ḥadīths. The temporal is Shawwāl, Dhū al-Qaʿdah, and ten nights of Dhū al-Ḥijjah. It is not permissible to enter iḥrām for the Ḥajj outside this time. This is the madhhab of al-Shāfiʿī. If one were to enter iḥrām for the Ḥajj outside this time, it would not be concluded as a Ḥajj, but would be concluded as an ʿUmrah.

As for the ʿUmrah, it is permissible to enter iḥrām for it and to perform it throughout the entire year, and it is not disliked (makrūh) in any part of it. However, its condition is that it not be during the Ḥajj, nor while one is staying (muqīm) upon any of its acts. It is not disliked to repeat the ʿUmrah within the year; rather, it is recommended (mustaḥabb) according to us and according to the majority (al-jumhūr). Ibn Sīrīn and Mālik disliked repeating it within the year.

It is permissible to enter iḥrām for the Ḥajj from a place above the miqāt — i.e., farther from Mecca — whether it be the dwelling of one's family or otherwise. Regarding which of the two is more virtuous, there are two opinions for al-Shāfiʿī: the more correct of them is that entering iḥrām from the miqāt is more virtuous, following the example of the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him). And Allah knows best.

| (Chapter: The Talbiyah — Its Description and Its Time)

Al-Qāḍī said: Al-Māzarī said: "The talbiyah is dualized (muthannāh) for the purpose of multiplication and exaggeration (al-takthīr wa-l-mubālaghah). Its meaning is: 'Answering after answering, and adherence to Your obedience.' It is dualized for emphasis (tawkīd), not as a true dual — analogous to the saying of Allah the Exalted: {«بَلْ يَدَاهُ مَبْسُوطَتَانِ»} (Rather, both His hands are outstretched) [al-Māʾidah 5:64], meaning: His two favors (niʿmatāhu), upon the interpretation of "hand" as "favor" here. And the favors of Allah the Exalted cannot be enumerated."

Yūnus ibn Ḥabīb al-Baṣrī said: "Labbayka is a singular noun, not a dual." He said: "Its alif was only converted to a yāʾ due to its connection with the pronoun (al-ḍamīr), like [the case of] laday (لدى)." And according to the madhhab of Sībawayh, it is a true dual, as evidenced by the conversion of its alif to yāʾ even with the explicit noun (al-muẓhar). The majority of people follow what Sībawayh said.

Ibn al-Anbārī said: "They dualized labbayka just as they dualized ḥanānayka (حنانيك), i.e., 'mercy after mercy.' The origin of labbayka is labbaytuka (لببتك), but they found the combination of three bāʾs heavy, so they substituted the third with a yāʾ — just as they said, from al-ẓann (ظن), taẓannaytu (تظنيت), whose origin is taẓannantu (تظننت)."

They differed concerning the meaning of labbayka and its derivation. It was said: Its meaning is "my direction and my intention are toward You," derived from their saying: "Dārī talbu dārak" (داري تلب دارك), i.e., "my house faces your house." It was said: Its meaning is "my love for You," derived from their saying: "imraʾah labbah" (امرأة لبة) — a woman who is loving and affectionate toward her child. It was said: Its meaning is "my sincerity (ikhlāṣ) to You," derived from their saying: "ḥubb lubāb" (حب لباب) — pure and unadulterated love. From this [same root] is "lubb al-ṭaʿām" (لب الطعام) and "lubābuhu" — the core and essence of food. It was said: Its meaning is "I am steadfast upon Your obedience and answering You," derived from their saying: "labba al-rajul bi-l-makān wa-alabba" (لب الرجل بالمكان وألب) — if he remained therein. Ibn al-Anbārī said: "And upon this [last meaning] al-Khalīl [ibn Aḥmad] held."

Al-Qāḍī said: "It was said that this answering [in the talbiyah] is [a response] to His saying the Exalted to Ibrāhīm (peace be upon him): {«وَأَذِّنْ فِي النَّاسِ بِالْحَجِّ»} (And proclaim to the people the Ḥajj) [al-Ḥajj 22:27]."

Ibrāhīm al-Ḥarbī said, concerning the meaning of labbayka: "i.e., nearness to You and obedience; and al-iblāb (الإلباب) is nearness." Abū Naṣr said: "Its meaning is: 'I am submissive (mulibb) before Your hands,' i.e., humbled (khāḍiʿ)." This is the end of the speech of al-Qāḍī.

[1184] His saying: «Labbayka inna al-ḥamda wa-l-niʿmah» — it is narrated with kasrah on the hamzah of "inna" and with fatḥah [i.e., "anna"], two well-known readings (wajhān) among the people of ḥadīth and the people of language. The majority (al-jumhūr) said: the kasrah is more excellent (ajwad). Al-Khaṭṭābī said: "The fatḥah is the narration of the common people (al-ʿāmmah)." Thaʿlab said: "The choice (al-ikhtiyār) is the kasrah, and it is more excellent in meaning than the fatḥah — because whoever reads with kasrah makes its meaning: 'Indeed, all praise and all favor belong to You in every circumstance.' And whoever reads with fatḥah makes its meaning: 'I answer You for this reason.'"

His saying: «wa-l-niʿmah laka» (and the favor is Yours) — the well-known reading is with naṣb (accusative) on al-niʿmah.

chapters.title_en: The Talbiyah: Its Rulings, Wording, and the Pilgrim's State of Iḥrām
chapters.arabic_text:
القاضي ويجوز رفعها على الابتداء ويكون الخبر محذوفا قال بن الأنباري وإن

شئت جعلت خبر إن محذوفا تقديره إن الحمد لك والنعمة مستقرة لك وقوله

(وسعديك) قال القاضي إعرابها وتثنيتها كما سبق في لبيك ومعناه مساعدة

لطاعتك بعد مساعدة قوله (والخير بيديك) أي الخير كله بيد الله تعالى ومن

فضله قوله (والرغباء إليك والعمل) قال القاضي قال المازري يروى بفتح الراء

والمد وبضم الراء مع القصر ونظيره العلا والعلياء والنعمى والنعماء قال

القاضي وحكى أبو علي فيه أيضا الفتح مع القصر الرغبى مثل سكرى ومعناه هنا

الطلب والمسألة إلى من بيده الخير وهو
# 
# المقصود بالعمل المستحق للعبادة قوله (عن بن عمر تلقفت التلبية) هو بقاف

ثم فاء أي أخذتها بسرعة قال القاضي وروي تلقنت بالنون قال والأول رواية

الجمهور قال وروي تلقيت بالياء ومعانيها متقاربة قوله (أهل فقال لبيك اللهم

لبيك) قال العلماء الإهلال رفع الصوت بالتلبية عند الدخول في الإحرام وأصل

الإهلال في اللغة رفع الصوت ومنه استهل المولود أي صاح ومنه قوله تعالى وما

أهل به لغير الله  أي رفع الصوت عند ذبحه بغير ذكر الله تعالى وسمي الهلال

هلالا لرفعهم الصوت عند رؤيته قوله (سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يهل

ملبدا) فيه استحباب تلبيد الرأس قبل الإحرام وقد نص عليه الشافعي وأصحابنا

وهو موافق للحديث الآخر في الذي
# 
# خر عن بعيره فإنه يبعث يوم القيامة ملبدا قال العلماء التلبيد ضفر الرأس

بالصمغ أو الخطمي وشبههما مما يضم الشعر ويلزق بعضه ببعض ويمنعه التمعط

والقمل فيستحب لكونه أرفق به
# [1185] قوله (كان المشركون يقولون لبيك لا شريك لك قال فيقول رسول الله

صلى الله عليه وسلم ويلكم قد قد إلا شريكا هو لك تملكه وما ملك يقولون هذا

وهم يطوفون بالبيت) فقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم قدقد قال القاضي روي بإسكان

الدال وكسرها مع التنوين ومعناه كفا كم هذا الكلام فاقتصروا عليه ولا

تزيدوا وهنا انتهى كلام النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ثم عاد الراوي إلى حكاية

كلام المشركين فقال الاشريكا هو لك إلى آخره معناه أنهم كانوا يقولون هذه

الجملة وكان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول اقتصروا على قولكم لبيك لا شريك

لك والله أعلم وأما حكم التلبية فأجمع المسلمون على أنها مشروعة ثم اختلفوا

في إيجابها فقال الشافعي وآخرون هي سنة ليست بشرط لصحة الحج ولا بواجبة فلو

تركها صح حجه ولا دم عليه لكن فاتته الفضيلة وقال بعض أصحابنا هي واجبة

تجبر بالدم ويصح الحج بدونها وقال بعض أصحابنا هي شرط لصحة الإحرام قال ولا

يصح الإحرام ولا الحج إلا بها والصحيح من مذهبنا ما قدمناه عن الشافعي وقال

مالك ليست بواجبة ولكن لو تركها لزمه دم وصحه حجه قال الشافعي ومالك ينعقد

الحج بالنية بالقلب من غير لفظ كما ينعقد الصوم بالنية فقط وقال أبو حنيفة

لا ينعقد إلا بانضمام التلبية أو سوق الهدي إلى النية قال أبو حنيفة ويجزي

عن التلبية ما في معناها من التسبيح والتهليل وسائر الأذكار كما قال هو أن

التسبيح وغيره يجزئ في الإحرام بالصلاة عن التكبير  والله أعلم قال أصحابنا

ويستحب رفع الصوت بالتلبية بحيث لا يشق عليه والمرأة ليس لها الرفع لأنه

يخاف الفتنة
# 
# بصوتها ويستحب الإكثار منها لا سيما عند تغاير الأحوال كإقبال الليل

والنهار والصعود والهبوط واجتماع الرفاق والقيام والقعود والركوب والنزول

وأدبار الصلوات وفي المساجد كلها والأصح أنه لا يلبي في الطواف والسعي لأن

لهما أذكارا مخصوصة ويستحب أن يكرر التلبية كل مرة ثلاث مرات فأكثر

ويواليها ولا يقطعها بكلام فإن سلم عليه رد السلام باللفظ ويكره السلام

عليه في هذه الحال وإذا لبى صلى على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وسأل

الله تعالى ما شاء لنفسه ولمن أحبه وللمسلمين وأفضله سؤال الرضوان والجنة

والاستعاذة من النار وإذا رأى شيئا يعجبه قال لبيك إن العيش عيش الآخرة ولا

تزال التلبية مستحبة للحاج حتى يشرع في رمي جمرة العقبة يوم النحر أو يطوف

طواف الإفاضة إن قدمه عليها أو الحلق عند من يقول الحلق نسك وهو الصحيح

وتستحب للعمرة حتى يشرع في الطواف وتستحب التلبية للمحرم مطلقا سواء الرجل

والمرأة والمحدث والجنب والحائض لقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم لعائشة رضي الله

عنها اصنعي ما يصنع الحاج غير أن لا تطوفي

| (باب أمر أهل المدينة بالإحرام من عند مسجد ذي 
# الحليفة)
# [1186] قوله عن بن عمر (قال بيداؤكم هذه التي تكذبون على رسول الله صلى

الله عليه وسلم فيها ما أهل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إلا من عند

المسجد يعني ذا الحليفة) وفي الرواية الأخرى
# 
# (ما أهل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إلا من عند الشجرة حين قام به

بعيره) قال العلماء هذه البيداء هي الشرف الذي قدام ذي الحليفة إلى جهة مكة

وهي بقرب ذي الحليفة وسميت بيداء لأنه ليس فيها بناء ولا أثر وكل مفازة

تسمى بيداء وأما هنا فالمراد بالبيداء ما ذكرناه وقوله تكذبون فيها أي
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ق-ض-ي (qaḍā)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To settle, decide, or fulfill; the judge (al-qāḍī) is one who settles disputes definitively.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In legal-theological usage, it denotes the authoritative determination of a ruling (ḥukm) by a qualified jurist.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense is "cutting off" or "finalizing"; metaphorically applied to judicial decree and divine ordinance.
- Sībawayh Rule: Nominal Sentence with Omitted Predicate (al-mubtadaʾ wa-l-khabar maḥdhūf) — When the predicate is contextually understood, it may be elided, as in "labbayka" where the implied verb is "I answer" (ujību).
chapters.translation:
I say: The judge (al-Qāḍī) stated that it is permissible to raise [the word "al-ḥamdu"] as the subject (al-ibtidāʾ), with the predicate being omitted. Ibn al-Anbārī said: If you wish, you may make the predicate of "inna" omitted, with the estimated meaning: "Indeed, praise belongs to You, and favor is firmly established for You."

His saying: "And at Your service (wa-saʿdayka)" — the judge said: Its grammatical parsing and its dual form are as previously mentioned in "labbayka" (here I am). Its meaning is: "assisting Your obedience after assisting [it again]."

His saying: "And all good is in Your hands (wa-l-khayru bi-yadayka)" — meaning: all good entirely belongs to God Most High and is from His bounty.

His saying: "And supplication is to You, and deeds (wa-l-raghbāʾu ilayka wa-l-ʿamal)" — the judge said: Al-Māzarī reported that it is narrated with the opening of the letter rāʾ and prolongation (al-madd), and with the damma of the rāʾ with shortening (al-qaṣr). Its parallel is "al-ʿalā" and "al-ʿalyāʾ," and "al-naʿmā" and "al-naʿmāʾ." The judge said: Abū ʿAlī also related the opening with shortening — "al-raghbā" like "sukrā." Its meaning here is: seeking and asking from Him in whose hands lies all good — and He is the intended object of deeds deserving worship.

His saying: "On the authority of Ibn ʿUmar: 'I caught the talbiyah (talaqqaftu al-talbiyah)'" — it is with a qāf followed by a fāʾ, meaning: I took it swiftly. The judge said: It is also narrated as "talaqqantu" with a nūn. He said: The first is the narration of the majority. He said: It is also narrated as "talaqqaytu" with a yāʾ, and their meanings are close.

His saying: "He raised his voice (ahalla) and said: 'Here I am, O Allah, here I am (labbayka Allāhumma labbayka)'" — The scholars said: "al-ihlāl" is the raising of the voice with the talbiyah upon entering the state of iḥrām. The origin of "al-ihlāl" in the language is the raising of the voice. From it is derived "istahalla al-mawlūd" (the newborn cried out), i.e., it screamed. And from it is the saying of God Most High: {«وَمَا أُهِلَّ بِهِ لِغَيْرِ اللَّهِ»} (and that over which the name of other than Allah is invoked) — meaning: raising the voice at its slaughter without mentioning the name of God Most High. The crescent moon (al-hilāl) is called "hilāl" because they raise their voices upon seeing it.

His saying: "I heard the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, raising his voice in talbiyah with matted hair (mulabbidan)" — In this is the recommendation of matting the head (talbīd) before entering iḥrām. Al-Shāfiʿī and our companions have explicitly stated this. It is consistent with the other hadith concerning the one who falls from his camel — that he will be raised on the Day of Resurrection with matted hair.

The scholars said: "al-talbīd" is the plaiting of the head with gum, or marshmallow (khiṭmī), or similar substances that bind the hair together, sticking some parts to others, and preventing it from becoming disheveled and infested with lice. It is recommended because it is more gentle upon it.

[1185] His saying: "The polytheists used to say: 'Here I am, no partner do You have.' He said: Then the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, would say: 'Woe to you! Enough, enough (qad qad)! Only a partner whom you own and what he owns.' They would say this while circumambulating the House (al-Bayt)."

His saying, peace be upon him: "qad qad" — the judge said: It is narrated with the sukūn of the dāl and with its kasra with tanwīn. Its meaning is: "Enough of this speech for you; restrict yourselves to it and do not add more." Here ends the speech of the Prophet, peace be upon him. Then the narrator returns to relating the speech of the polytheists, saying: "Only a partner whom you own and what he owns" to the end of it. Its meaning is that they used to say this sentence, and the Prophet, peace be upon him, used to say: "Restrict yourselves to your saying: 'Here I am, no partner do You have.'" And Allah knows best.

As for the ruling of the talbiyah: The Muslims are unanimous that it is legislated (mashrūʿah). Then they differed concerning its obligation. Al-Shāfiʿī and others said: It is a sunnah, not a condition for the validity of the ḥajj, nor obligatory. If one abandons it, his ḥajj is valid and no blood (dam) is due upon him, but he has missed the virtue. Some of our companions said: It is obligatory, compensated by blood, and the ḥajj is valid without it. Some of our companions said: It is a condition for the validity of the iḥrām — he said: Neither the iḥrām nor the ḥajj is valid except with it. The correct view in our school is what we have previously transmitted from al-Shāfiʿī.

Mālik said: It is not obligatory, but if one abandons it, blood is due upon him, and his ḥajj is valid. Al-Shāfiʿī and Mālik said: The ḥajj is contracted by the intention in the heart without any utterance, just as the fast is contracted by intention alone. Abū Ḥanīfah said: It is not contracted except by the addition of the talbiyah or the driving of the sacrificial animal (sawn al-hady) to the intention. Abū Ḥanīfah said: What is equivalent to the talbiyah suffices for it — such as glorification (tasbīḥ), declaration of God's oneness (tahlīl), and the rest of the remembrances (adhkār) — just as he said that glorification and other than it suffice in the iḥrām of prayer in place of the takbīr. And Allah knows best.

Our companions said: It is recommended to raise the voice with the talbiyah to a degree that is not burdensome upon oneself. The woman should not raise her voice, because there is fear of temptation (fitnah) from her voice. It is recommended to multiply it, especially at the changing of circumstances — such as the coming of night and day, ascending and descending, the gathering of companions, standing and sitting, riding and dismounting, and after the prayers, and in all the mosques. The most correct view is that one does not recite the talbiyah during the ṭawāf and the saʿy, because they have their own specific remembrances. It is recommended to repeat the talbiyah each time three times or more, and to be continuous in it, not interrupting it with speech. If one is greeted with salām, he returns the greeting verbally. It is disliked (makrūh) to greet him with salām in this state. When he recites the talbiyah, he sends blessings upon the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and asks Allah Most High for whatever he wishes for himself, for those he loves, and for the Muslims. The most virtuous of it is asking for divine pleasure (al-riḍwān) and Paradise, and seeking refuge from the Fire. When he sees something that pleases him, he says: "Here I am, indeed life is the life of the Hereafter."

The talbiyah remains recommended for the pilgrim until he begins the stoning of the Jamrat al-ʿAqabah on the Day of Sacrifice (Yawm al-Naḥr), or performs the ṭawāf al-ifāḍah if he advances it before that, or shaves his head — for those who hold that shaving is a ritual act (nusuk), which is the correct view. It is recommended for the ʿumrah until he begins the ṭawāf. The talbiyah is recommended for the muḥrim absolutely — whether man or woman, the one in minor impurity (muḥdith), the one in major impurity (junub), and the menstruating woman — due to his saying, peace be upon him, to ʿĀʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her: "Do what the pilgrim does, except do not circumambulate the House."

| (Chapter: The Command for the People of Madīnah to Enter Iḥrām from the Mosque of Dhū al-Ḥulayfah) |

[1186] His saying, on the authority of Ibn ʿUmar: "He said: 'This is your Baydāʾ (open plain) about which you lie against the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, did not enter iḥrām except from the mosque' — meaning Dhū al-Ḥulayfah." And in the other narration: "The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, did not enter iḥrām except from the tree, when his camel stood up with him."

The scholars said: This Baydāʾ is the elevated ground (al-sharaf) that lies before Dhū al-Ḥulayfah in the direction of Mecca, and it is near Dhū al-Ḥulayfah. It was called "Baydāʾ" because there is no building or trace in it. Every open desert (mafāzah) is called "Baydāʾ." As for here, what is meant by "al-Baydāʾ" is what we have mentioned. His saying: "about which you lie (takdhibūn fīhā)" — meaning: [you lie] concerning it.

chapters.title_en: The Ruling on the Miqāt, the Two Rakʿahs Before Iḥrām, and the Yemeni Corners of the Kaʿbah
chapters.arabic_text:
تقولون إنه صلى الله عليه وسلم أحرم منها ولم يحرم منها وإنما أحرم قبلها

من عند مسجد ذي الحليفة ومن عند الشجرة  التي كانت هناك وكانت عند المسجد

وسماهم بن عمر كاذبين لأنهم أخبروا بالشيء على خلاف ما هو وقد سبق في أول

هذا الشرح في مقدمة صحيح مسلم أن الكذب عند أهل السنة هو الإخبار عن الشيء

بخلاف ما هو سواء تعمده أم غلط فيه أو سها وقالت المعتزلة يشترط فيه

العمدية وعندنا أن العمدية شرط لكونه إثما لا لكونه يسمى كذبا فقول بن عمر

جار على قاعدتنا وفيه أنه لا بأس بإطلاق هذه اللفظة وفيه دلالة على أن

ميقات أهل المدينة من عند مسجد ذي الحليفة ولا يجوز لهم تأخير الإحرام إلى

البيداء وبهذا قال جميع العلماء وفيه أن الإحرام من الميقات أفضل من دويرة

أهله لأنه صلى الله عليه وسلم ترك الإحرام من مسجده مع كمال شرفه فإن قيل

إنما أحرم من الميقات لبيان الجواز قلنا هذا غلط لوجهين أحدهما أن البيان

قد حصل بالأحاديث الصحيحة في بيان المواقيت والثاني أن فعل رسول الله صلى

الله عليه وسلم إنما يحمل على بيان الجواز في شيء يتكرر فعله كثيرا فيفعله

مرة أو مرات على الوجه الجائز لبيان الجواز ويواظب غالبا على فعله على أكمل

وجوهه وذلك كالوضوء مرة ومرتين وثلاثا كله ثابت والكثير أنه صلى الله عليه

وسلم توضأ ثلاثا ثلاثا وأما الإحرام بالحج فلم يتكرر وإنما جرى منه صلى

الله عليه وسلم مرة واحدة فلا يفعله إلا على أكمل وجوهه والله أعلم قوله

(كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يركع بذي الحليفة ركعتين ثم إذا استوت

به الناقة قائمة عند مسجد ذي الحليفة أهل) فيه استحباب صلاة الركعتين عند

إرادة الإحرام ويصليهما قبل الإحرام ويكونان نافلة هذا مذهبنا ومذهب

العلماء كافة إلا ما حكاه القاضي
# 
# وغيره عن الحسن البصري أنه استحب كونهما بعد صلاة فرض قال لأنه روي أن

هاتين الركعتين كانتا صلاة الصبح والصواب ما قاله الجمهور وهو ظاهر الحديث

قال أصحابنا وغيرهم من العلماء وهذه الصلاة سنة لو تركها فاتته الفضيلة ولا

إثم عليه ولا دم  قال أصحابنا فإن كان إحرامه في وقت من الأوقات المنهي فيها

عن الصلاة لم يصلهما هذا هو المشهور وفيه وجه لبعض أصحابنا أنه يصليهما فيه

لأن سببهما إرادة الإحرام وقد وجد ذلك وأما وقت الإحرام فسنذكره في الباب

بعده إن شاء الله تعالى

| (باب بيان أن الأفضل أن يحرم حين تنبعث به راحلته)
# (متوجها إلى مكة لا عقب الركعتين)
# [1187] قوله في هذا الباب عن بن عمر قال (فإني لم أر رسول الله صلى الله

عليه وسلم يهل حتى تنبعث
# 
# به راحلته) وقال في الحديث السابق ثم إذا استوت به الناقة قائمة عند مسجد

ذي الحليفة أهل وفي الحديث الذي قبله كان إذا استوت به راحلته قائمة عند

مسجد ذي الحليفة أهل وفي رواية حين قام به بعيره وفي رواية يهل حين تستوي

به راحلته قائمة هذه الروايات كلها متفقة في المعنى وابنعاثها هو استواؤها

قائمة وفيها دليل لمالك والشافعي والجمهور أن الأفضل أن يحرم إذا انبعثت به

راحلته وقال أبو حنيفة يحرم عقب الصلاة وهو جالس قبل ركوب دابته وقبل قيامه

وهو قول ضعيف للشافعي وفيه حديث من رواية بن عباس لكنه ضعيف وفيه أن

التلبية لا تقدم على الإحرام قوله عن عبيد بن جريج أنه قال لابن عمر (رأيتك

تصنع أربعا لم أر أحدا من أصحابك يصنعها) إلى آخره قال المازري يحتمل أن

مراده لا يصنعها غيرك مجتمعة وإن كان يصنع بعضها قوله (رأيتك لا تمس من

الأركان الا اليمانيين) ثم ذكر بن عمر في جوابه أنه لم ير رسول الله صلى

الله عليه وسلم يمس إلا اليمانيين هما بتخفيف الياء هذه اللغة الفصيحة

المشهورة وحكى سيبويه وغيره من الأئمة تشديدها في لغة قليلة والصحيح

التخفيف قالوا لأن نسبه إلى اليمن فحقه أن يقال اليمني وهو جائز فلما قالوا

اليماني أبدلوا من إحدى ياءي النسب ألفا فلو قالوا اليماني بالتشديد لزم

منه الجمع بين البدل والمبدل والذين شددوها قالوا هذه الألف زائدة وقد تزاد

في النسب كما قالوا في  النسب إلى صنعا صنعاني فزادوا النون الثانية وإلى

الري رازي فزادوا الزاي وإلى الرقبة رقباني فزادوا النون والمراد بالركنين

اليمانيين الركن اليماني والركن الذي فيه الحجر الأسود ويقال له العراقي

لكونه إلى جهة العراق وقيل للذي قبله اليماني لأنه إلى جهة اليمن ويقال

لهما اليمانيان تغليبا لأحد الاسمين كما قالوا الأبوان للأب والأم والقمران

للشمس والقمر والعمران لأبي بكر وعمر رضي الله عنهما ونظائره مشهورة فتارة

يغلبون بالفضيلة كالأبوين وتارة بالخفة كالعمرين وتارة بغير ذلك وقد بسطته

في تهذيب الأسماء واللغات قال العلماء ويقال للركنين الآخرين اللذين يليان

الحجر بكسر الحاء الشاميان لكونهما بجهة الشام قالوا فاليمانيان باقيان على

قواعد إبراهيم صلى الله عليه وسلم بخلاف الشاميين فلهذا لم يستلما
# 
# واستلم اليمانيان لبقائهما على قواعد إبراهيم صلى الله عليه وسلم ثم إن
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ك-ذ-ب (k-dh-b)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To report something contrary to its actual reality; falsehood in speech.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological usage, it denotes any statement that does not correspond to fact, regardless of the speaker's intent.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) in the sense of factual mismatch; metaphorical (majāz) when applied to actions, e.g., "the earth lied" meaning it failed to produce.
- Sībawayh Rule: ʿAṭf al-Bayān (Appositional clarification) — the phrase "من عند مسجد ذي الحليفة" functions as an explicative appositive specifying the precise location of the tree, requiring precise syntactic linkage.
chapters.translation:
I say: They claim that he (peace and blessings be upon him) entered iḥrām from it (i.e., the mosque) and did not enter iḥrām from it — rather, he entered iḥrām before it, from the vicinity of the mosque of Dhū al-Ḥulayfah and from the vicinity of the tree that was there, which was adjacent to the mosque. Ibn ʿUmar called them liars because they reported the matter contrary to its actual reality. It has already preceded at the beginning of this commentary, in the introduction to Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim, that lying (kadhib) according to the Ahl al-Sunnah is reporting something contrary to its reality, whether one does so deliberately, erroneously, or forgetfully. The Muʿtazilah held that deliberateness is a stipulated condition. In our view, deliberateness is a condition for it being a sin, not for it being called a lie. Thus, Ibn ʿUmar's statement proceeds upon our principle. In this [narration] there is [evidence] that there is no harm in uttering this expression (i.e., calling them liars). It also contains an indication that the miqāt for the people of Madīnah is from the mosque of Dhū al-Ḥulayfah, and it is not permissible for them to delay iḥrām until al-Baydāʾ. All scholars have affirmed this. It also shows that entering iḥrām from the miqāt is superior to doing so from one's own dwelling, because he (peace and blessings be upon him) abandoned entering iḥrām from his own mosque despite its complete nobility. If it is said: "He only entered iḥrām from the miqāt to demonstrate permissibility," we reply: This is an error for two reasons. First, the demonstration (of permissibility) has already been established through the authentic hadiths clarifying the miqātāt. Second, the action of the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) is only interpreted as demonstrating permissibility in matters that are frequently repeated, where he performs it once or several times in a permissible manner to show permissibility, while he generally persists in performing it in its most complete form — such as ablution (wuḍūʾ) performed once, twice, or thrice, all of which are established, though the predominant practice was that he performed ablution three times each. As for entering iḥrām for ḥajj, it was not repeated; rather, it occurred from him (peace and blessings be upon him) only once, so he would not perform it except in its most complete manner. And Allah knows best.

His statement: "The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) used to pray two rakʿahs at Dhū al-Ḥulayfah, then when his she-camel stood upright with him at the mosque of Dhū al-Ḥulayfah, he would enter iḥrām" — in this is [evidence for] the recommendation of praying two rakʿahs when intending iḥrām, and that they are prayed before the iḥrām, and they are supererogatory (nāfilah). This is our school and the school of all scholars, except what al-Qāḍī and others have related from al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī, that he recommended they be after an obligatory prayer, saying: "Because it has been narrated that these two rakʿahs were the dawn prayer." The correct view is what the majority (al-jumhūr) held, and it is the apparent meaning of the hadith. Our companions and other scholars said: This prayer is a Sunnah; if one abandons it, the virtue is missed, but there is no sin upon him and no blood (i.e., no sacrificial offering required). Our companions said: If his iḥrām occurs at a time in which prayer is prohibited, he does not pray them. This is the well-known view. There is another view from some of our companions that he does pray them at such a time, because their cause (sabab) is the intention of iḥrām, which has already occurred. As for the time of iḥrām, we shall mention it in the following chapter, Allah willing.

| (Chapter: Clarifying that the superior practice is to enter iḥrām when one's mount sets off with him, heading toward Makkah, not immediately after the two rakʿahs)

[1187] His statement in this chapter from Ibn ʿUmar, who said: "For I have not seen the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) raise his voice in talbiyah until his she-camel set off with him." And in the preceding hadith: "Then when his she-camel stood upright with him at the mosque of Dhū al-Ḥulayfah, he entered iḥrām." And in the hadith before that: "When his she-camel stood upright with him at the mosque of Dhū al-Ḥulayfah, he entered iḥrām." And in one narration: "When his camel stood up with him." And in another narration: "He would raise the talbiyah when his she-camel stood upright with him." All these narrations agree in meaning, and its setting off (inbiʿāthuhā) is its standing upright. In this is evidence for Mālik, al-Shāfiʿī, and the majority that the superior practice is to enter iḥrām when one's mount sets off with him. Abū Ḥanīfah said: He enters iḥrām immediately after the prayer, while seated, before mounting his beast and before standing up. This is a weak view attributed to al-Shāfiʿī, and there is a hadith in its support from Ibn ʿAbbās, but it is weak. In this [chapter] there is also [evidence] that the talbiyah is not to be advanced before the iḥrām.

His statement from ʿUbayd ibn Jurayj, who said to Ibn ʿUmar: "I have seen you do four things that I have not seen any of your companions do" — to the end of the narration. Al-Māzarī said: It is possible that he meant: "No one other than you does them all together," even if some do some of them.

His statement: "I have seen you not touch any of the corners except the two Yemeni ones." Then Ibn ʿUmar mentioned in his reply that he had not seen the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) touch except the two Yemeni ones. These two words (al-Yamāniyyān) are with a lightened yāʾ (i.e., single yāʾ) — this is the well-known eloquent language. Sībawayh and other imams have related the shaddah (doubled yāʾ) as a rare dialect. The correct form is the lightened one. They said: Because it is a relative adjective (nisbah) to Yemen, its proper form would be al-Yamanī, which is permissible. When they said al-Yamānī, they substituted an alif for one of the two yāʾs of the nisbah. If they said al-Yamānī with shaddah, it would necessitate combining the substitute and the substituted. Those who doubled it said: This alif is extra, and extra letters may be added in nisbah, just as they said for nisbah to Ṣanʿāʾ: Ṣanʿānī, adding a second nūn; to al-Rayy: Rāzī, adding a zāy; and to al-Raqbah: Raqbanī, adding a nūn. What is meant by "the two Yemeni corners" is the Yemeni corner and the corner containing the Black Stone, which is also called the Iraqi corner because it faces the direction of Iraq. It is said that the former is called Yemeni because it faces the direction of Yemen. Both are called "the two Yemeni ones" by way of predominance (taghlīb) of one of the two names, just as they say "the two parents" (al-abawayn) for father and mother, "the two moons" (al-qamarān) for the sun and the moon, and "the two ʿUmars" (al-ʿUmarān) for Abū Bakr and ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with them both), and similar well-known examples. Sometimes they give predominance by virtue of excellence, as in "the two parents," sometimes by brevity, as in "the two ʿUmars," and sometimes for other reasons. I have elaborated on this in Tahdhīb al-Asmāʾ wa al-Lughāt.

The scholars said: The other two corners that are adjacent to the Ḥijr (with a kasrah on the ḥāʾ) are called "the two Syrian ones" (al-Shāmiyyān) because they face the direction of Syria. They said: Thus, the two Yemeni corners remain upon the foundations of Ibrāhīm (peace be upon him), unlike the two Syrian ones. For this reason, he did not touch (istalama) the two Syrian ones, but he touched the two Yemeni ones because they remain upon the foundations of Ibrāhīm (peace be upon him). Then —
