They were only commanded to do so that year to oppose what the Jāhiliyyah had been upon, namely the prohibition of ʿUmrah during the months of Ḥajj.

Among the evidence cited by the majority is the ḥadīth of Abū Dharr (may God be pleased with him) which Muslim mentions shortly after this: "The tamattuʿ in Ḥajj was specific to the companions of Muḥammad (peace and blessings upon him)" — meaning the dissolution of Ḥajj into ʿUmrah. And in the book of al-Nasāʾī, from al-Ḥārith ibn Bilāl from his father, who said: "I said: O Messenger of God, is the dissolution of Ḥajj specific to us, or general for all people? He said: Rather, it is specific to us."

As for what is in the ḥadīth of Suraqah — "Is this for our year or forever? He said: Forever and ever" — its meaning is the permissibility of performing ʿUmrah during the months of Ḥajj, as previously explained. The conclusion from the totality of the chains of these ḥadīths is that ʿUmrah during the months of Ḥajj is permissible until the Day of Resurrection, and likewise Qirān; and that the dissolution of Ḥajj into ʿUmrah was specific to that year. And God knows best.

His saying (peace and blessings upon him): «حتى إذا كان يوم التروية فأهلوا بالحج واجعلوا الذي قدمتم بها متعة قالوا كيف نجعلها متعة وقد سمينا الحج فقال افعلوا ما آمركم به فلولا أني سقت الهدي لفعلت مثل الذي أمرتكم به» — "Until when the Day of Tarwiyah came, enter iḥrām for Ḥajj, and make that which you have brought with you a tamattuʿ. They said: How can we make it a tamattuʿ when we have named it Ḥajj? He said: Do what I command you. Were it not that I have driven the hady, I would have done the same as I command you."

This is clear evidence for the school of al-Shāfiʿī and Mālik and their supporters regarding the preference of Ifrād (single Ḥajj), and that the majority of them were in iḥrām for Ḥajj. They interpret the narration of those who reported "mutamattiʿīn" (those performing tamattuʿ) as meaning that at the end of the matter they became mutamattiʿīn, as previously established at the beginning of this chapter.

In it is also evidence for al-Shāfiʿī and his supporters that whoever is in Mecca and wishes to perform Ḥajj should only enter iḥrām for it from the Day of Tarwiyah. We have already mentioned this matter multiple times.

[1217] His saying: «كان بن عباس يأمرنا بالمتعة وكان بن الزبير ينهى عنها قال فذكرت ذلك لجابر بن عبد الله فقال على يدي دار الحديث تمتعنا مع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فلما قام عمر قال إن الله يحل لرسوله ما شاء بما شاء وإن القرآن قد نزل منازله فأتموا الحج والعمرة كما أمركم الله وأبتوا نكاح هذه النساء فلن أوتى برجل نكح امرأة إلى أجل إلا رجمته بالحجارة» — "Ibn ʿAbbās used to command us to perform tamattuʿ, and Ibn al-Zubayr used to forbid it. He said: I mentioned that to Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh, and he said: Upon my hands the ḥadīth circulated — we performed tamattuʿ with the Messenger of God (peace and blessings upon him). When ʿUmar stood [to lead], he said: 'Indeed God makes lawful for His Messenger whatever He wills, by whatever He wills. And indeed the Qurʾān has descended in its stations. So complete the Ḥajj and the ʿUmrah as God has commanded you, and desist from marrying these women. For I shall not be brought a man who marries a woman for a fixed term except that I will stone him with stones.'"

In the other narration from ʿUmar (may God be pleased with him): «فافصلوا حجكم من عمرتكم فإنه أتم لحجكم وأتم لعمرتكم» — "Separate your Ḥajj from your ʿUmrah, for that is more complete for your Ḥajj and more complete for your ʿUmrah."

And after this, he mentioned from the narration of Abū Mūsā al-Ashʿarī (may God be pleased with him) that he used to give legal rulings permitting tamattuʿ, citing the Prophet's (peace and blessings upon him) command to him to do so, and the saying of ʿUmar (may God be pleased with him) that we should take hold of the Book of God, for God Almighty commanded completion (itmām). And he mentioned that ʿUthmān used to forbid tamattuʿ — or ʿUmrah [during Ḥajj] — and that ʿAlī opposed him in that, entering iḥrām for both together. And he mentioned the saying of Abū Dharr (may God be pleased with him): "The tamattuʿ in Ḥajj was specific to the companions of Muḥammad (peace and blessings upon him)." And in another narration...

chapters.title_en: Section 492 — On the Permissibility (Rukhsah) of Tamattuʿ and the Report of ʿImrān ibn Ḥuṣayn; The Chapter on the Prophet's Pilgrimage (Ḥajj); The Hadith of Jābir
chapters.arabic_text:
رخصة وذكر قول عمران بن حصين أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أعمر طائفة من

أهله في العشر فلم تنزل آية تفسخ ذلك وفي رواية جمع بين حج وعمرة ثم لم

ينزل فيها كتاب ولم ينه قال المازري اختلف في المتعة التي نهى عنها عمر في

الحج فقيل هي فسخ الحج إلى العمرة وقيل هي العمرة في أشهر الحج ثم الحج من

عامه وعلى هذا إنما نهى عنها ترغيبا في الإفراد الذي هو أفضل لا أنه يعتقد

بطلانها أو تحريمها وقال القاضي عياض ظاهر حديث جابر وعمران وأبي موسى أن

المتعة التي اختلفوا فيها إنما هي فسخ الحج إلى العمرة قال ولهذا كان عمر

رضي الله عنه يضرب الناس عليها ولا يضربهم على مجرد التمتع في أشهر الحج

وإنما ضربهم على ما اعتقده هو وسائر الصحابة أن فسخ الحج إلى العمرة كان

مخصوصا في تلك السنة للحكمة التي قدمنا ذكرها قال بن عبد البر لا خلاف بين

العلماء أن التمتع المراد بقول الله تعالى فمن تمتع بالعمرة إلى الحج فما

استيسر من الهدي هو الاعتمار في أشهر الحج قبل الحج قال ومن التمتع أيضا

القران لأنه تمتع بسقوط سفره للنسك الآخر من بلده قال ومن  التمتع أيضا فسخ

الحج إلى العمرة هذا كلام القاضي قلت والمختار أن عمر وعثمان وغيرهما إنما

نهوا عن المتعة التي هي الاعتمار في أشهر الحج ثم الحج من عامه ومرادهم نهي

أولوية للترغيب في الإفراد لكونه أفضل وقد انعقد الإجماع بعد هذا على جواز

الإفراد والتمتع والقران من غير كراهة وإنما اختلفوا في الأفضل منها وقد

سبقت هذه المسألة في أوائل هذا الباب مستوفاة والله أعلم وأما قوله في متعة

النكاح وهي نكاح المرأة إلى أجل فكان مباحا ثم نسخ يوم
# 
# خيبر ثم أبيح يوم الفتح ثم نسخ في أيام الفتح واستمر تحريمه إلى الآن

وإلى يوم القيامة وقد كان فيه خلاف في العصر الأول ثم ارتفع وأجمعوا على

تحريمه وسيأتي بسط أحكامه في كتاب النكاح إن شاء الله تعالى

| (باب حجة النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم)
# فيه حديث جابر رضي الله عنه وهو حديث عظيم مشتمل على جمل من الفوائد

ونفائس من مهمات القواعد وهو من أفراد مسلم لم يروه البخاري في صحيحه ورواه

أبو داود كرواية مسلم قال القاضي وقد تكلم الناس على ما فيه من الفقه

وأكثروا وصنف فيه أبو بكر بن المنذر جزءا كبيرا وخرج فيه من الفقه مائة

ونيفا وخمسين نوعا ولو تقصي لزيد على هذا القدر قريب منه وقد سبق الاحتجاج

بنكت منه في أثناء شرح الأحاديث السابقة وسنذكر ما يحتاج إلى التنبيه عليه

على ترتيبه إن شاء الله تعالى
# [1218] قوله (عن جعفر بن محمد عن أبيه قال دخلنا على جابر بن عبد الله

فسأل عن القوم حتى انتهى إلي فقلت أنا محمد بن علي بن حسين فأهوى بيده إلى

رأسي فنزع زري الأعلى ثم نزع زري الأسفل ثم وضع كفه بين ثديي وأنا يومئذ

غلام شاب فقال مرحبا بك يا بن أخي سل عما شئت فسألته وهو أعمى فحضر وقت

الصلاة فقام في نساجة ملتحفا بها كلما وضعها على منكبه رجع طرفاها إليه من

صغرها ورداؤه إلى جنبه على
# 
# المشجب فصلى بنا) هذه  القطعة فيها فوائد منها أنه يستحب لمن ورد عليه

زائرون أو ضيفان ونحوهم أن يسأل عنهم لينزلهم منازلهم كما جاء في حديث

عائشة رضي الله عنها أمرنا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أن ننزل الناس

منازلهم وفيه إكرام أهل بيت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كما فعل جابر

بمحمد بن علي ومنها استحباب قوله للزائر والضيف ونحوهما مرحبا ومنها ملاطفة

الزائر بما يليق به وتأنيسه وهذا سبب حل جابر زري محمد بن علي ووضع يده بين

ثدييه وقوله وأنا يومئذ غلام شاب فيه تنبيه على أن سبب فعل جابر ذلك

التأنيس لكونه صغيرا وأما الرجل الكبير فلا يحسن إدخال اليد في جيبه والمسح

بين ثدييه ومنها جواز إمامة الأعمى البصراء ولا خلاف في جواز ذلك لكن

اختلفوا في الأفضل على ثلاثة مذاهب وهي ثلاثة أوجه لأصحابنا أحدها إمامة

الأعمى أفضل من إمامة البصير لأن الأعمى أكمل خشوعا لعدم نظره إلى الملهيات

والثاني البصير أفضل لأنه أكثر احترازا من النجاسات والثالث هما سواء

لتعادل فضيلتهما وهذا الثالث هو الأصح عند أصحابنا وهو نص الشافعي ومنها أن

صاحب البيت أحق بالإمامة من غيره ومنها جواز الصلاة في ثوب واحد مع التمكن

من الزيادة عليه ومنها جواز تسمية الثدي للرجل وفيه خلاف لأهل اللغة منهم

من جوزه كالمرأة ومنهم من منعه وقال يختص الثدي بالمرأة ويقال في الرجل

ثندؤة وقد سبق إيضاحه في أوائل كتاب الإيمان في حديث الرجل الذي قتل نفسه

فقال فيه النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه من أهل النار وقوله (قام في نساجة)

هي بكسر النون وتخفيف السين المهملة وبالجيم هذا هو المشهور في نسخ بلادنا

ورواياتنا لصحيح مسلم وسنن أبي داود ووقع في بعض النسخ في ساجة بحذف النون

ونقله القاضي عياض عن رواية الجمهور قال وهو الصواب قال والساجة والساج

جميعا ثوب كالطيلسان وشبهه قال ورواية النون وقعت في رواية الفارسي قال

ومعناه ثوب ملفق قال قال بعضهم النون خطأ وتصحيف قلت ليس كذلك بل  كلاهما
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ر-خ-ص (r-kh-ṣ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Ease, leniency, concession after strictness; a dispensation (rukhṣah) permitting what was previously restricted.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): A divine or prophetic concession indicating permissibility (ibāḥah) without abrogation of the original ruling's virtue.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: softening of a prohibition; metaphorical: legal facilitation (takhfīf) in ritual practice.
- Sībawayh Rule: ʿAṭf al-Bayān (Appositional Clarification) — The phrase "وفي رواية جمع بين حج وعمرة" clarifies the preceding report's variance, requiring precise coordination of narrational alternatives.
chapters.translation:
I say: Know that the discussion here concerns the concession (rukhṣah) regarding tamattuʿ, and the mention of the statement of ʿImrān ibn Ḥuṣayn — may God be pleased with him — that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, performed ʿumrah for a group of his family during the ten days [of Dhū al-Ḥijjah], and no verse was revealed to abrogate that. In another narration, he combined ḥajj and ʿumrah, and then no scripture was revealed concerning it, nor did he prohibit it.

Al-Māzarī said: There is disagreement concerning the tamattuʿ which ʿUmar prohibited during the ḥajj. It was said: it is the dissolution (faskh) of the ḥajj into ʿumrah. And it was said: it is performing ʿumrah during the months of ḥajj, then performing ḥajj in the same year. Upon this [second view], he only prohibited it as an encouragement (targhīb) toward ifrād [the exclusive performance of ḥajj], which is superior — not that he believed in its invalidity or prohibition.

Al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ said: The apparent meaning of the hadith of Jābir, ʿImrān, and Abū Mūsā is that the tamattuʿ over which they differed was only the dissolution of ḥajj into ʿumrah. He said: For this reason, ʿUmar — may God be pleased with him — used to strike people for it, but he did not strike them merely for tamattuʿ during the months of ḥajj. Rather, he struck them for what he and the rest of the Companions believed — that the dissolution of ḥajj into ʿumrah was specific to that year, due to the wisdom we have previously mentioned.

Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr said: There is no disagreement among the scholars that the tamattuʿ intended by the statement of God the Exalted — {«فَمَن تَمَتَّعَ بِالْعُمْرَةِ إِلَى الْحَجِّ فَمَا اسْتَيْسَرَ مِنَ الْهَدْيِ»} [Whoever performs ʿumrah before the ḥajj, then [offer] whatever is easy of the sacrificial animal] — is the performance of ʿumrah during the months of ḥajj before the ḥajj. He said: And from tamattuʿ also is qirān [the combined performance], because one enjoys the benefit of not undertaking a separate journey for the other rite from his own land. He said: And from tamattuʿ also is the dissolution of ḥajj into ʿumrah. This is the statement of al-Qāḍī.

I say: The chosen position (al-mukhtār) is that ʿUmar, ʿUthmān, and others only prohibited the tamattuʿ which is the performance of ʿumrah during the months of ḥajj, then ḥajj in the same year. Their intent was a prohibition of preference (nahy al-awlawiyyah), to encourage ifrād, because it is superior. And consensus (ijmāʿ) has been established after this on the permissibility of ifrād, tamattuʿ, and qirān without any dislike (karāhah). They only differed concerning which is superior. This matter has already been discussed exhaustively at the beginning of this chapter. And God knows best.

As for his statement concerning the tamattuʿ of marriage — which is the marriage of a woman for a fixed term — it was permissible, then abrogated on the day of Khaybar, then permitted on the day of the Conquest [of Mecca], then abrogated during the days of the Conquest, and its prohibition has continued until now and until the Day of Resurrection. There had been disagreement concerning it in the first era, then it ceased, and they reached consensus on its prohibition. Its detailed rulings will come in the Book of Marriage, God willing.

| (Chapter: The Prophet's Pilgrimage, Peace and Blessings Be Upon Him)

In it is the hadith of Jābir — may God be pleased with him — and it is a momentous hadith, comprising numerous benefits and precious matters of important principles. It is one of the exclusive narrations of Muslim; al-Bukhārī did not narrate it in his Ṣaḥīḥ. Abū Dāwūd narrated it like the narration of Muslim.

Al-Qāḍī said: The people have spoken extensively on the jurisprudence contained within it. Abū Bakr ibn al-Mundhir composed a large volume on it, extracting from it over one hundred and fifty types of jurisprudential points. Had one pursued it exhaustively, it would have increased to nearly double that amount. We have already cited some of its subtleties in the course of explaining previous hadiths, and we shall mention what requires attention in its proper order, God willing.

[1218] His statement (from Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from his father, who said: We entered upon Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh. He asked about the people until he reached me. I said: I am Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Ḥusayn. He extended his hand to my head, then unbuttoned my upper button, then unbuttoned my lower button, then placed his palm between my breasts — and I was at that time a young lad. He said: Welcome (marḥaban) to you, O son of my brother! Ask whatever you wish. So I asked him, and he was blind. When the time of prayer came, he stood in a milayyah [a small wrap], wrapping himself in it; whenever he placed it on his shoulder, its two ends would return to him due to its smallness, and his cloak (ridāʾ) was beside him on the clothes rack, and he led us in prayer.)

This passage contains benefits. Among them: it is recommended (mustaḥabb) for one upon whom visitors or guests or the like arrive to ask about them, in order to place them in their proper stations — as comes in the hadith of ʿĀʾishah — may God be pleased with her — that the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, commanded us to place people in their proper stations. And in it is the honoring of the family of the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, as Jābir did with Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī.

Among them: the recommendation of saying to the visitor, guest, and the like: "Welcome" (marḥaban). And among them: the gentleness (mulāṭafah) toward the visitor with what befits him, and putting him at ease. This is the reason for Jābir unbuttoning the buttons of Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī and placing his hand between his breasts. His statement "and I was at that time a young lad" contains an indication that the cause of Jābir's action was to put him at ease, because he was young. As for a grown man, it is not proper to insert one's hand into his collar and wipe between his breasts.

Among them: the permissibility of a blind man leading the sighted in prayer. There is no disagreement concerning its permissibility, but they differed concerning which is superior, on three schools — and these are three positions (wujūh) among our companions: First: the blind man's leading is superior to the sighted man's leading, because the blind man is more complete in humility (khushūʿ), due to his not looking at distractions. Second: the sighted man is superior, because he is more cautious regarding impurities (najāsāt). Third: they are equal, because their merits are balanced. This third is the most correct (al-aṣaḥḥ) among our companions, and it is the explicit text (naṣṣ) of al-Shāfiʿī.

Among them: the owner of the house has greater right to lead the prayer than others. And among them: the permissibility of praying in a single garment while able to add more. And among them: the permissibility of calling the chest (thady) of a man [by that term]. There is disagreement among the linguists concerning this: some permit it, as for a woman; others prohibit it, saying that "thady" is specific to women, and for a man one says "thanduʾah." We have already clarified this at the beginning of the Book of Faith, in the hadith of the man who killed himself, whereupon the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said he was among the people of the Fire.

His statement "he stood in a milayyah (نساجة)" — it is with a kasrah on the nūn, a tashdīd-free sīn (unpointed), and a jīm. This is the well-known form in the manuscripts of our lands and our narrations of Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim and Sunan Abī Dāwūd. In some manuscripts it occurs as "sājah" (ساجة) with the nūn omitted, and al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ transmitted this from the narration of the majority, saying it is correct. He said: "al-sājah" and "al-sāj" both refer to a garment like a ṭaylasān and the like. He said: The narration with the nūn occurred in the narration of al-Fārisī. He said: Its meaning is a patched garment (thawb mulaffaq). He said: Some said the nūn [version] is an error and a corruption (taṣḥīf). I say: It is not so; rather, both are [valid].

chapters.title_en: Section 493 — The Prophet's Farewell Pilgrimage: Garments, Mounts, and the Talbiyah of Tawḥīd
chapters.arabic_text:
صحيح ويكون ثوبا ملفقا على هيئة الطيلسان قال القاضي في المشارق الساج

والساجة الطيلسان وجمعه سيجان قال وقيل هي الخضر منها خاصة وقال الأزهري هو

طيلسان مقور ينسج كذلك قال وقيل هو الطيلسان الحسن قال ويقال الطيلسان بفتح

اللام وكسرها وضمها وهي أقل وقوله (ورداؤه إلى جنبه على المشجب) هو بميم

مكسورة ثم شين معجمة ساكنة ثم جيم ثم باء موحدة وهو اسم لأعواد يوضع عليها

الثياب ومتاع البيت
# 
# قوله (أخبرني عن حجة رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم) هي بكسر الحاء وفتحها

والمراد حجة الوداع قوله (أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم مكث تسع سنين لم

يحج) يعني مكث بالمدينة بعد الهجرة قوله (ثم أذن في الناس في العاشرة إن

رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم حاج) معناه أعلمهم بذلك وأشاعه بينهم

ليتأهبوا للحج معه ويتعلموا المناسك والأحكام ويشهدوا أقواله وأفعاله

ويوصيهم ليبلغ الشاهد الغائب وتشيع دعوة الإسلام وتبلغ الرسالة القريب

والبعيد وفيه أنه يستحب للإمام إيذان الناس بالأمور المهمة ليتأهبوا لها

قوله (كلهم يلتمس أن يأتم برسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم) قال القاضي هذا

مما يدل على أنهم كلهم أحرموا بالحج لأنه صلى الله عليه وسلم أحرم بالحج

وهم لا يخالفونه ولهذا قال جابر وما عمل من شيء عملنا به ومثله توقفهم عن

التحلل بالعمرة ما لم يتحلل حتى أغضبوه واعتذر إليهم ومثله تعليق علي وأبي

موسى إحرامهما على إحرام النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم

لأسماء بنت عميس وقد ولدت (اغتسلي واستثفري بثوب وأحرمي) فيه استحباب غسل

الإحرام للنفساء وقد سبق بيانه في باب مستقل فيه أمر الحائض والنفساء

والمستحاضة بالاستثفار وهو أن تشد في وسطها شيئا وتأخذ خرقة عريضة تجعلها

على محل الدم وتشد طرفيها من قدامها ومن ورائها في ذلك المشدود في وسطها

وهو شبيه بثفر الدابة بفتح الفاء وفيه صحة إحرام النفساء وهو مجمع عليه
# 
# والله أعلم قوله (فصلى ركعتين) فيه استحباب ركعتي الإحرام وقد سبق الكلام

فيه مبسوطا قوله (ثم ركب القصواء) هي بفتح القاف وبالمد قال القاضي ووقع في

نسخة العذري القصوى بضم القاف والقصر قال وهو خطأ قال القاضي قال بن قتيبة

كانت للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم نوق القصواء والجدعاء والعضباء قال أبو عبيد

العضباء اسم لناقة النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ولم تسم بذلك لشيء أصابها قال

القاضي قد ذكر هنا أنه ركب القصواء وفي آخر هذا الحديث خطب على القصواء وفي

غير مسلم خطب على ناقته الجدعاء وفي حديث آخر على ناقة خرماء وفي آخر

العضباء وفي حديث آخر كانت له ناقة لا تسبق وفي آخر تسمى مخضرمة وهذا كله

يدل على أنها ناقة واحدة خلاف ما قاله بن قتيبة وأن هذا كان اسمها أو وصفها

لهذا الذي بها خلاف ما قال أبو عبيد لكن يأتي في كتاب النذر أن القصواء غير

العضباء كما سنبينه هناك قال الحربي العضب والجدع والخرم والقصو والخضرمة

في الآذان قال بن الأعرابي القصواء التي قطع طرف أذنها والجدع أكثر منه

وقال الأصمعي والقصو مثله قال وكل قطع في الأذن جدع فإن جاوز الربع فهي

عضباء والمخضرم مقطوع الأذنين فإن اصطلمتا فهي صلماء وقال أبو عبيد القصواء

المقطوعة الأذن عرضا والمخضرمة المستأصلة والمقطوعة النصف فما فوقه وقال

الخليل المخضرمة مقطوعة الواحدة والعضباء مشقوقة الأذن قال الحربي فالحديث

يدل على أن العضباء اسم لها وإن كانت عضباء الأذن فقد جعل اسمها هذا آخر

كلام القاضي وقال محمد بن إبراهيم التيمي التابعي وغيره إن العضباء

والقصواء والجدعاء اسم لناقة واحدة كانت لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

والله أعلم قوله (نظرت إلى مد بصري) هكذا هو في جميع النسخ مد بصري وهو

صحيح ومعناه منتهى بصري وأنكر بعض أهل اللغة مد بصري وقال الصواب مدى بصري

وليس هو بمنكر بل هما لغتان المد أشهر قوله (بين يديه من راكب وماش) فيه

جواز الحج راكبا وماشيا وهو مجمع عليه وقد تظاهرت عليه دلائل الكتاب والسنة

وإجماع الأمة قال الله  تعالى وأذن في الناس
# 
# بالحج يأتوك رجالا وعلى كل ضامر واختلف العلماء في الأفضل منهما فقال

مالك والشافعي وجمهور العلماء الركوب أفضل اقتداء بالنبي صلى الله عليه

وسلم ولأنه أعون له على وظائف مناسكه ولأنه أكثر نفقة وقال داود ماشيا أفضل

لمشقته وهذا فاسد لأن المشقة ليست مطلوبة قوله (وعليه ينزل القرآن وهو يعرف

تأويله) معناه الحث على التمسك بما أخبركم عن فعله في حجته تلك قوله (فأهل

بالتوحيد) يعني قوله لبيك لا شريك لك وفيه إشارة إلى مخالفة ما كانت

الجاهلية تقوله في تلبيتها من لفظ الشرك وقد سبق ذكر تلبيتهم في باب

التلبية قوله (فأهل بالتوحيد لبيك اللهم لبيك لا شريك لك لبيك إن الحمد

والنعمة لك والملك لا شريك لك وأهل الناس بهذا الذي يهلون به فلم يرد رسول

الله صلى الله عليه وسلم شيئا منه ولزم رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

تلبيته) قال القاضي عياض رحمه الله تعالى فيه إشارة إلى ما روي من زيادة
chapters.anchors:
- Root: س-ج (s-j)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: A type of wide, flowing garment; the ṭaylasān (hooded cloak) woven in a rounded shape.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Denotes a distinctive outer covering, symbolically linked to the pilgrim's state of iḥrām.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for the garment itself; metaphorically extended to any enveloping cloth.
- Root: ش-ج-ب (sh-j-b)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Wooden rods or a frame upon which clothes are hung.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): A household implement, indicating practical domestic usage.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal object; no metaphorical extension in classical usage.
- Root: ق-ص-و (q-ṣ-w)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To be distant, remote; for an ear, to be cut off at the tip.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In prophetic narratives, a proper name for a she-camel, denoting a physical characteristic.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal physical description; not metaphorical.
- Sībawayh Rule: ʿAṭf al-Bayān (Appositional Clarification) — When multiple names (e.g., al-Qaṣwā', al-Jadʿā', al-ʿAḍbā') are cited for the same entity, the syntax allows apposition to clarify identity, as analyzed in the discussion of the Prophet's mounts.
chapters.translation:
I say: It is authentic, and it refers to a patched garment fashioned in the shape of a ṭaylasān (hooded cloak). Al-Qāḍī said in al-Mashāriq: "Al-sāj and al-sājah mean the ṭaylasān, and its plural is sījān." He said: "And it is said that it refers specifically to the green ones among them." Al-Azharī said: "It is a rounded ṭaylasān, woven in that manner." He said: "And it is said it is the beautiful ṭaylasān." He said: "And one says ṭaylasān with fatḥah (a) on the lām, with kasrah (i), and with ḍammah (u), the last being the least common."

His statement: "And his cloak was beside him on the mashjab" — the word is with a kasrah on the mīm, then a sukkūn on the shīn (with iʿjām, i.e., dotted), then a jīm, then a bāʾ (with single dot). It is a name for the wooden rods upon which clothes and household goods are placed.

His statement: "He informed me about the ḥajjah (pilgrimage) of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace" — it is with kasrah on the ḥāʾ and also with fatḥah. The intended meaning is the Farewell Pilgrimage (ḥajjat al-wadāʿ).

His statement: "The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, remained nine years without performing the pilgrimage" — meaning he remained in Medina after the emigration (hijrah).

His statement: "Then he announced to the people in the tenth year that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was going to perform the pilgrimage" — its meaning is that he informed them of that and spread it among them, so that they might prepare themselves for the pilgrimage with him, learn the rites (manāsik) and rulings (aḥkām), witness his words and deeds, and so that he might instruct them that the one present should convey to the absent. Thus the call of Islam would spread, and the message would reach the near and the far. In this is [the ruling] that it is recommended (mustaḥabb) for the leader (imām) to announce important matters to the people so they may prepare for them.

His statement: "All of them seeking to follow the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace" — Al-Qāḍī said: This indicates that all of them entered iḥrām for the pilgrimage (ḥajj), because he, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, entered iḥrām for the pilgrimage, and they would not contradict him. For this reason, Jābir said: "Whatever he did, we did the same." Similar to this is their refraining from exiting iḥrām through ʿumrah until he exited, to the point that they angered him, and he apologized to them. Also similar is the attachment of ʿAlī and Abū Mūsā's iḥrām to the iḥrām of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.

His statement, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, to Asmāʾ bint ʿUmays — and she had just given birth: "Perform ghusl (ritual bath), and use istithfār with a cloth, and enter iḥrām" — In this is the recommendation (istiḥbāb) of the ghusl for iḥrām for a woman in post-natal bleeding (nufasāʾ). Its explanation has already preceded in a separate chapter, including the command for the menstruating woman (ḥāʾiḍ), the post-natal bleeder (nufasāʾ), and the one with prolonged bleeding (mustaḥāḍah) to perform istithfār. That is, she ties something around her waist, takes a wide rag, places it over the site of the blood, and ties its two ends — from her front and from her back — to that which is tied around her waist. This resembles the thafar (girth) of a beast of burden, with fatḥah on the fāʾ. In this is the validity of the iḥrām of the post-natal bleeder, and this is a matter of consensus (ijmāʿ).

And Allah knows best.

His statement: "Then he prayed two rakʿahs" — In this is the recommendation of the two rakʿahs of iḥrām, and the discussion of this has already preceded in detail.

His statement: "Then he rode al-Qaṣwāʾ" — it is with fatḥah on the qāf and with prolongation (madd). Al-Qāḍī said: "In the copy of al-ʿUdhrī, it appears as al-Quṣwā with ḍammah on the qāf and without prolongation (qaṣr)." He said: "That is an error." Al-Qāḍī said: Ibn Qutaybah said: "The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, had she-camels named al-Qaṣwāʾ, al-Jadʿāʾ, and al-ʿAḍbāʾ." Abū ʿUbayd said: "Al-ʿAḍbāʾ is the name of a she-camel of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and she was not named that due to any defect that afflicted her." Al-Qāḍī said: "It is mentioned here that he rode al-Qaṣwāʾ, and at the end of this ḥadīth he delivered the sermon atop al-Qaṣwāʾ. In other than Muslim, he delivered the sermon atop his she-camel al-Jadʿāʾ. In another ḥadīth, atop a she-camel with a slit ear (kharmāʾ). In another, al-ʿAḍbāʾ. In another ḥadīth, he had a she-camel that was never outrun. In another, she was called Mukhḍaramah. All of this indicates that it was one single she-camel, contrary to what Ibn Qutaybah said, and that this was her name or a description of her due to what she had, contrary to what Abū ʿUbayd said. However, it will come in the Book of Vows (Kitāb al-Nudhūr) that al-Qaṣwāʾ is other than al-ʿAḍbāʾ, as we will clarify there."

Al-Ḥarbī said: "Al-ʿaḍb, al-jadʿ, al-kharm, al-qaṣw, and al-khuḍramah all refer to [cuts] in the ears." Ibn al-Aʿrābī said: "Al-Qaṣwāʾ is the one whose ear tip has been cut off, and al-jadʿāʾ is more extensive than that." Al-Aṣmaʿī said: "Al-qaṣw is similar to it." He said: "Every cut in the ear is jadʿ; if it exceeds the quarter, then it is ʿaḍbāʾ. Al-Mukhḍaram is the one with both ears cut off; if they are completely severed, then it is ṣalmāʾ." Abū ʿUbayd said: "Al-Qaṣwāʾ is the one whose ear is cut across, and al-Mukhḍaramah is the one whose ear is completely removed, or cut to half or more." Al-Khalīl said: "Al-Mukhḍaramah is the one with a single ear cut off, and al-ʿAḍbāʾ is the one with a slit ear." Al-Ḥarbī said: "Thus the ḥadīth indicates that al-ʿAḍbāʾ was a name for her, and even if she was ʿaḍbāʾ of the ear, her name was made this." This is the end of Al-Qāḍī's speech.

Muḥammad ibn Ibrāhīm al-Taymī, the Tābiʿī, and others said: "Al-ʿAḍbāʾ, al-Qaṣwāʾ, and al-Jadʿāʾ are names for one single she-camel that belonged to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace." And Allah knows best.

His statement: "I looked to the extent of my sight (madd baṣarī)" — Thus it appears in all copies: madd baṣarī, and it is correct. Its meaning is "the limit of my sight." Some linguists rejected madd baṣarī and said the correct form is madā baṣarī. But it is not objectionable; rather, both are two dialects, with madd being the more famous.

His statement: "Before him, between rider and walker" — In this is the permissibility of performing the pilgrimage riding and walking, and this is a matter of consensus (ijmāʿ). The evidences of the Book, the Sunnah, and the consensus of the ummah have concurred upon it. Allah, the Exalted, said: {«وَأَذِّن فِي النَّاسِ بِالْحَجِّ يَأْتُوكَ رِجَالًا وَعَلَىٰ كُلِّ ضَامِرٍ»} ("And proclaim to the people the Hajj; they will come to you on foot and on every lean camel").

The scholars differed over which of the two is superior. Mālik, al-Shāfiʿī, and the majority of scholars said: Riding is superior, following the example of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and because it is more helpful for him in fulfilling the duties of his rites, and because it involves greater expenditure. Dāwūd said: Walking is superior due to its hardship. This is corrupt, because hardship is not something sought after.

His statement: "And upon him the Qurʾān descends, and he knows its interpretation (taʾwīl)" — Its meaning is the urging to adhere to what he informed you of regarding his actions in that pilgrimage of his.

His statement: "So he entered iḥrām with tawḥīd (monotheism)" — meaning his saying: "Labbayk, no partner do You have." In this is an indication of opposing what the pre-Islamic era (Jāhiliyyah) used to say in its talbiyah, which contained the word of shirk (polytheism). Their talbiyah has already been mentioned in the chapter on talbiyah.

His statement: "So he entered iḥrām with tawḥīd: 'Labbayk, O Allah, Labbayk. No partner do You have. Labbayk. Indeed, all praise and grace are Yours, and the dominion. No partner do You have.' And the people entered iḥrām with this same talbiyah, and the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, did not reject any of it, and he adhered to his talbiyah." Al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ, may Allah have mercy on him, said: In this is an indication of what has been narrated regarding the addition...

chapters.title_en: Section 494 — On the Talbiyah, Entering Mecca, the Circumambulation of Arrival (Ṭawāf al-Qudūm), Raml, Iḍṭibāʿ, and the Two Rakʿahs Behind the Maqām
chapters.arabic_text:
الناس في التلبية من الثناء والذكر كما روي في ذلك عن عمر رضي الله عنه أنه

كان يزيد لبيك ذا النعماء والفضل الحسن لبيك مرهوبا منك ومرغوبا اليك وعن

بن عمر رضي الله عنه لبيك وسعديك والخير بيديك والرغباء إليك والعمل وعن

أنس رضي الله عنه لبيك حقا تعبدا ورقا قال القاضي قال أكثر العلماء المستحب

الاقتصار على تلبية رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وبه قال مالك والشافعي

والله أعلم قوله (قال جابر لسنا ننوي إلا الحج لسنا نعرف العمرة) فيه دليل

لمن قال بترجيح الإفراد وقد سبقت المسألة مستقصاة في أول الباب السابق قوله

(حتى أتينا البيت) فيه بيان أن السنة للحاج أن يدخلوا مكة قبل الوقوف

بعرفات ليطوفوا
# 
# للقدوم وغير ذلك قوله (حتى إذا أتينا البيت معه استلم الركن فرمل ثلاثا

ومشى أربعا) فيه أن المحرم إذا دخل مكة قبل الوقوف بعرفات يسن له طواف

القدوم وهو مجمع عليه وفيه أن الطواف سبع طوافات وفيه أن السنة  أيضا الرمل

في الثلاث الأول ويمشي على عادته في الأربع الأخيرة قال العلماء الرمل هو

أسرع المشي مع تقارب الخطا وهو الخبب قال أصحابنا ولا يستحب الرمل إلا في

طواف واحد في حج أو عمرة أما إذا طاف في غير حج أو عمرة فلا رمل بلا خلاف

ولا يسرع أيضا في كل طواف حج وإنما يسرع في واحد منها وفيه قولان مشهوران

للشافعي أصحهما طواف يعقبه سعي ويتصور ذلك في طواف القدوم ويتصور في طواف

الإفاضة ولا يتصور في طواف الوداع والقول الثاني أنه لا يسرع إلا في طواف

القدوم سواء أراد السعي بعده أم لا ويسرع في طواف العمرة اذ ليس فيها إلا

طواف واحد والله أعلم قال أصحابنا والاضطباع سنة في الطواف وقد صح فيه

الحديث في سنن أبي داود والترمذي وغيرهما وهو أن يجعل وسط ردائه تحت عاتقه

الأيمن ويجعل طرفيه على عاتقه الأيسر ويكون منكبه الأيمن مكشوفا قالوا

وإنما يسن الاضطباع في طواف يسن فيه الرمل على ما سبق تفصيله والله أعلم

وأما قوله استلم الركن فمعناه مسحه بيده وهو سنة في كل طواف وسيأتي شرحه

واضحا حيث ذكره مسلم بعد هذا إن شاء الله تعالى قوله (ثم نفر إلى مقام

إبراهيم عليه السلام فقرأ واتخذوا من مقام ابراهيم مصلى فجعل المقام بينه

وبين البيت) هذا دليل لما أجمع عليه العلماء أنه ينبغي لكل طائف إذا فرغ من

طوافه أن يصلي خلف المقام ركعتي الطواف واختلفوا هل هما واجبتان أم سنتان

وعندنا فيه خلاف حاصله ثلاثة أقوال أصحها أنهما سنة والثاني أنهما واجبتان

والثالث إن كان طوافا واجبا فواجبتان وإلا فسنتان وسواء قلنا واجبتان أو

سنتان لو تركهما لم يبطل طوافه والسنة أن يصليهما خلف المقام فإن لم يفعل

ففي الحجر وإلا ففي المسجد وإلا ففي مكة وسائر الحرم ولو صلاهما في وطنه

وغيره من أقاصي الأرض جاز وفاتته الفضيلة ولا تفوت هذه الصلاة ما دام حيا

ولو أراد أن يطوف أطوفة استحب أن يصلي عقب  كل طواف
# 
# ركعتيه فلو أراد أن يطوف أطوفة بلا صلاة ثم يصلي بعد الأطوفة لكل طواف

ركعتيه قال أصحابنا يجوز ذلك وهو خلاف الأولى ولا يقال مكروه وممن قال بهذا

المسور بن مخرمة وعائشة وطاوس وعطاء وسعيد بن جبير وأحمد وإسحاق وأبو يوسف

وكرهه بن عمر والحسن البصري والزهري ومالك والثوري وأبو حنيفة وأبو ثور

ومحمد بن الحسن وبن المنذر ونقله القاضي عن جمهور الفقهاء قوله (فكان أبي

يقول ولا أعلمه ذكره إلا عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يقرأ في الركعتين

قل هو الله أحد وقل يا أيها الكافرون) معنى هذا الكلام أن جعفر بن محمد روى

هذا الحديث عن أبيه عن جابر قال كان أبي يعني محمدا يقول إنه قرأ هاتين

السورتين قال جعفر ولا أعلم أبي ذكر تلك القراءة عن قراءة جابر في صلاة

جابر بل عن جابر عن قراءة النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في صلاة هاتين الركعتين

قوله (قل هو الله أحد وقل يا أيها الكافرون) معناه قرأ في الركعة الأولى

بعد الفاتحة قل يا أيها الكافرون وفي الثانية بعد الفاتحة قل هو الله أحد

وأما قوله لا أعلم ذكره إلا عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ليس هو شكا في ذلك

لأن لفظة العلم تنافي الشك بل جزم برفعه إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وقد

ذكره البيهقي بإسناد صحيح على شرط مسلم عن جعفر بن محمد عن أبيه عن جابر أن

النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم طاف بالبيت فرمل من الحجر الأسود ثلاثا ثم صلى

ركعتين قرأ فيهما قل يا أيها الكافرون وقل هو الله أحد قوله (ثم رجع إلى

الركن فاستلمه ثم خرج من الباب إلى الصفا) فيه دلالة لما قاله الشافعي

وغيره من العلماء أنه يستحب للطائف طواف القدوم إذا فرغ من الطواف وصلاته

خلف المقام أن يعود إلى الحجر الأسود فيستلمه ثم يخرج من باب الصفا ليسعى

واتفقوا على أن هذا الاستلام ليس بواجب وإنما هو سنة لو تركه  لم يلزمه دم

قوله (ثم خرج من الباب إلى الصفا فلما دنا من الصفا قرأ إن الصفا والمروة

من شعائر الله أبدأ بما بدأ الله به فبدأ
# 
# بالصفا فرقى عليه حتى رأى البيت فاستقبل القبلة فوحد الله وكبر وقال لا
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ث-ن-ي (th-n-y)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Repetition, doubling; secondary mention; praise (thanāʾ) as reiterated commendation.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In devotional context, thanāʾ denotes the act of extolling God through repeated formulae, distinct from mere supplication (duʿāʾ).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense is "bending/folding back"; metaphorically, praise that returns to the praiser in merit.
- Root: ر-م-ل (r-m-l)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Sand; to hasten with short, quick steps (ramal) — the gait of one treading on sandy ground.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Ritual briskness in ṭawāf, symbolizing vigor against polytheists, a Sunnah not an obligation.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: "to walk swiftly with close steps" (khabab); metaphorical: spiritual urgency in worship.
- Root: ض-ط-ب-ع (ḍ-ṭ-b-ʿ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To place something under the armpit; from ḍabʿ (hyena) — the garment tucked like a beast's limb.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Ritual exposure of the right shoulder in ṭawāf, a Sunnah signifying readiness and humility.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: "to put under the arm"; technical: the specific draping of the ridāʾ.
- Root: ق-د-م (q-d-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Foot, precedence, arrival; qudūm as the act of coming forth.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Ṭawāf al-Qudūm — the arrival circumambulation for the pilgrim entering Mecca, a consensus Sunnah.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: "arrival"; metaphorical: the inaugural act of presence before the Sacred House.
- Sībawayh Rule: ʿAṭf al-Bayān (Appositional Clarification) — In "لبيك ذا النعماء والفضل الحسن", the accusative "dhā" functions as an explanatory appositive to the implied object of praise, governed by the vocative-accusative regime of "labbayka". Also, the conditional-answer structure in "فلو أراد أن يطوف أطوفة..." employs the hypothetical (sharṭ) with jumla jawābiyya, requiring the apodosis to be a nominal or explicit verbal clause.
chapters.translation:
I say: The people vary in the talbiyah between praise and remembrance, as has been narrated concerning that from ʿUmar (may God be pleased with him) that he used to add: "Here I am at Your service, O Possessor of bounties and excellent grace — here I am at Your service, held in awe by You and drawn in desire to You." And from Ibn ʿUmar (may God be pleased with him): "Here I am at Your service, and at Your felicity — good is in Your hands, and the yearning is to You, and the deed [is for You]." And from Anas (may God be pleased with him): "Here I am at Your service, truly, in worship and servitude." Al-Qāḍī said: The majority of scholars held that the preferable course is to restrict oneself to the talbiyah of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him), and this is the position of Mālik and al-Shāfiʿī. And God knows best.

His saying (Jābir said: "We did not intend anything but the Ḥajj; we did not know ʿUmrah") — in this is evidence for those who held the preponderance of Ifrād (single intention for Ḥajj alone), and this matter has already been fully discussed at the beginning of the preceding chapter.

His saying ("until we came to the House") — in this is an exposition that the Sunnah for the pilgrim is to enter Mecca before the standing at ʿArafāt, in order to perform the circumambulation of arrival and other rites.

His saying ("until when we came to the House with him, he touched the Corner, then hastened (ramal) for three circuits and walked normally for four") — in this is [the ruling] that when the muḥrim enters Mecca before the standing at ʿArafāt, the Ṭawāf al-Qudūm is Sunnah for him, and it is a matter of consensus. And in it is [the ruling] that the ṭawāf consists of seven circuits. And in it is [the ruling] that the Sunnah also includes ramal in the first three circuits, and walking at his normal pace in the last four. The scholars said: Ramal is the swiftest walking with close steps, and it is the khabab. Our companions (the Shāfiʿīs) said: Ramal is not recommended except in a single ṭawāf in a Ḥajj or ʿUmrah. As for one who circumambulates outside of Ḥajj or ʿUmrah, there is no ramal without disagreement. Nor does one hasten in every ṭawāf of the Ḥajj; rather, one hastens only in one of them. There are two well-known opinions of al-Shāfiʿī on this: the more correct of them is that it is the ṭawāf followed by the saʿy (running between Ṣafā and Marwah) — this is conceivable in the Ṭawāf al-Qudūm and in the Ṭawāf al-Ifāḍah, but not in the Ṭawāf al-Wadāʿ (farewell). The second opinion is that one hastens only in the Ṭawāf al-Qudūm, whether he intends the saʿy after it or not. And one hastens in the Ṭawāf of ʿUmrah, since there is only one ṭawāf in it. And God knows best.

Our companions said: Iḍṭibāʿ (draping the garment under the right armpit) is a Sunnah in the ṭawāf, and the ḥadīth concerning it is authentic in the Sunan of Abū Dāwūd, al-Tirmidhī, and others. It is that one places the middle of his ridāʾ (upper garment) under his right armpit, and places its two ends upon his left shoulder, so that his right shoulder is uncovered. They said: Iḍṭibāʿ is only Sunnah in a ṭawāf in which ramal is Sunnah, according to the detailed exposition mentioned previously. And God knows best.

As for his saying "he touched the Corner" (istalama al-rukn), its meaning is that he wiped it with his hand, and it is a Sunnah in every ṭawāf. Its detailed explanation will come clearly where Muslim mentions it after this, God willing.

His saying ("then he went forth to the Maqām of Ibrāhīm (peace be upon him) and recited {«And take yourselves the Maqām of Ibrāhīm as a place of prayer»} (Q 2:125), and he placed the Maqām between him and the House") — this is evidence for what the scholars have unanimously agreed upon: that every circumambulator, when he finishes his ṭawāf, should pray the two rakʿahs of the ṭawāf behind the Maqām. They differed as to whether these two rakʿahs are obligatory (wājib) or Sunnah. In our school there is a disagreement whose summary is three opinions: the most correct is that they are Sunnah; the second is that they are obligatory; the third is that if the ṭawāf was obligatory, then they are obligatory, and otherwise they are Sunnah. Whether we say obligatory or Sunnah, if he omits them, his ṭawāf is not invalidated. The Sunnah is to pray them behind the Maqām; if he does not, then in the Ḥijr (the semicircle of Ismāʿīl); if not, then in the Mosque; if not, then in Mecca and the rest of the Sacred Precinct. And if he prays them in his own land or other distant places of the earth, it is permissible, but the virtue is missed. This prayer is not forfeited as long as he is alive. If he wishes to perform multiple circumambulations, it is recommended that he pray two rakʿahs after each ṭawāf. If he wishes to perform multiple circumambulations without prayer, then pray after all of them two rakʿahs for each ṭawāf — our companions said: this is permissible, though it is contrary to the preferable, and it is not said to be disliked (makrūh). Among those who held this [permissibility] are al-Miswar ibn Makhramah, ʿĀʾishah, Ṭāwūs, ʿAṭāʾ, Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, Aḥmad, Isḥāq, and Abū Yūsuf. And Ibn ʿUmar, al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī, al-Zuhrī, Mālik, al-Thawrī, Abū Ḥanīfah, Abū Thawr, Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan, and Ibn al-Mundhir disapproved of it. Al-Qāḍī transmitted this [disapproval] from the majority of jurists.

His saying ("and my father used to say — and I do not know him to have mentioned it except from the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) — that he used to recite in the two rakʿahs {«Say: He is God, the One»} and {«Say: O disbelievers»}") — the meaning of this statement is that Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad narrated this ḥadīth from his father, from Jābir. He said: My father — meaning Muḥammad — said that he (the Prophet) recited these two sūrahs. Jaʿfar said: I do not know my father to have mentioned that recitation from Jābir's recitation in Jābir's prayer; rather, from Jābir, from the recitation of the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) in the prayer of these two rakʿahs.

His saying ("{«Say: He is God, the One»} and {«Say: O disbelievers»}") — its meaning is that he recited in the first rakʿah after the Fātiḥah {«Say: O disbelievers»}, and in the second after the Fātiḥah {«Say: He is God, the One»}.

As for his saying "I do not know him to have mentioned it except from the Prophet" — this is not a doubt in that matter, for the word "knowledge" (ʿilm) negates doubt; rather, it is an affirmation (jazm) of its elevation to the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him). Al-Bayhaqī has mentioned it with an authentic chain on the condition of Muslim, from Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from Jābir, that the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) circumambulated the House, hastened (ramal) from the Black Stone for three circuits, then prayed two rakʿahs in which he recited {«Say: O disbelievers»} and {«Say: He is God, the One»}.

His saying ("then he returned to the Corner and touched it, then went out from the gate to al-Ṣafā") — in this is an indication of what al-Shāfiʿī and other scholars said: that it is recommended for the circumambulator of arrival, when he finishes his ṭawāf and his prayer behind the Maqām, to return to the Black Stone and touch it, then go out from the gate of al-Ṣafā to perform the saʿy. And they agreed that this touching is not obligatory; rather, it is a Sunnah — if he omits it, no blood (dam) is required of him.

His saying ("then he went out from the gate to al-Ṣafā; when he drew near to al-Ṣafā, he recited {«Indeed al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah are among the rites of God»} (Q 2:158) — I begin with what God began with — so he began with al-Ṣafā, and climbed upon it until he saw the House, then faced the qiblah, proclaimed the oneness of God (wahḥada Allāh), and magnified Him (kabbara), and said...")

chapters.title_en: The Rites of Saʿy Between al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah — Section 495
chapters.arabic_text:
إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له له الملك وله الحمد وهو على كل شيء قدير لا

إله إلا الله وحده أنجز وعده ونصر عبده وهزم الأحزاب وحده ثم دعا بين ذلك

قال مثل هذا ثلاث مرات ثم نزل إلى المروة) في هذا اللفظ أنواع من المناسك

منها أن السعي يشترط فيه أن يبدأ من الصفا وبه قال الشافعي ومالك والجمهور

وقد ثبت في رواية النسائي في هذا الحديث بإسناد صحيح أن النبي صلى الله

عليه وسلم قال ابدءوا بما بدأ الله به هكذا بصيغة الجمع ومنها أنه ينبغي أن

يرقى على الصفا والمروة وفي هذا الرقي خلاف قال جمهور أصحابنا هو سنة ليس

بشرط ولا واجب فلو تركه صح سعيه لكن فاتته الفضيلة وقال أبو حفص بن الوكيل

من أصحابنا لا يصح سعيه حتى يصعد على شيء من الصفا والصواب الأول قال

أصحابنا لكن يشترط أن لا يترك شيئا من المسافة بين الصفا والمروة فليلصق

عقبيه بدرج الصفا واذا وصل المروة ألصق أصابع رجليه بدرجها وهكذا في المرات

السبع يشترط في كل مرة أن يلصق عقبيه بما يبدأ منه وأصابعه بما ينتهي إليه

قال أصحابنا يستحب أن يرقى على الصفا والمروة حتى يرى البيت إن أمكنه ومنها

أنه يسن أن يقف على الصفا مستقبل الكعبة ويذكر الله تعالى بهذا الذكر

المذكور ويدعو ويكرر الذكر والدعاء ثلاث مرات هذا هو المشهور عند أصحابنا

وقال جماعة من أصحابنا يكرر الذكر ثلاثا والدعاء مرتين فقط والصواب الأول

قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (وهزم الأحزاب وحده) معناه هزمهم بغير قتال من

الآدميين ولا بسبب من جهتهم والمراد بالأحزاب الذين تحزبوا على رسول الله

صلى الله عليه وسلم يوم الخندق وكان الخندق في شوال  سنة أربع من الهجرة

وقيل سنة خمس قوله (ثم نزل إلى المروة حتى
# 
# انصبت قدماه في بطن الوادي حتى إذا صعدتا مشى حتى أتى المروة) هكذا هو في

النسخ وكذا نقله القاضي عياض عن جميع النسخ قال وفيه إسقاط لفظة لا بد منها

وهي حتى انصبت قدماه رمل في بطن الوادي ولا بد منها وقد ثبتت هذه اللفظة في

غير رواية مسلم وكذا ذكرها الحميدي في الجمع بين الصحيحين وفي الموطأ حتى

إذا انصبت قدماه في بطن الوادي سعى حتى خرج منه وهو بمعنى رمل هذا كلام

القاضي وقد وقع في بعض نسخ صحيح مسلم حتى إذا انصبت قدماه في بطن الوادي

سعى كما وقع في الموطأ وغيره والله أعلم وفي هذا الحديث استحباب السعي

الشديد في بطن الوادي حتى يصعد ثم يمشي باقي المسافة إلى المروة على عادة

مشيه وهذا السعي مستحب في كل مرة من المرات السبع في هذا الموضع والمشي

مستحب فيما قبل الوادي وبعده ولو مشى في الجميع أو سعى في الجميع أجزأه

وفاتته الفضيلة هذا مذهب الشافعي وموافقيه وعن مالك فيمن ترك السعي الشديد

في موضعه روايتان إحداهما كما ذكر والثانية تجب عليه إعادته قوله (ففعل على

المروة مثل ما فعل على الصفا) فيه أنه يسن عليها من الذكر والدعاء والرقي

مثل ما يسن على الصفا وهذا متفق عليه قوله (حتى إذا كان آخر طواف على

المروة) فيه دلالة لمذهب الشافعي والجمهور أن الذهاب من الصفا إلى المروة

يحسب مرة والرجوع إلى الصفا ثانية والرجوع إلى المروة ثالثة وهكذا فيكون

ابتداء السبع من الصفا وآخرها بالمروة وقال بن بنت الشافعي وأبو بكر

الصيرفي من أصحابنا يحسب الذهاب إلى المروة والرجوع إلى الصفا مرة واحدة

فيقع آخر السبع في الصفا وهذا الحديث الصحيح يرد عليهما وكذلك عمل المسلمين

على تعاقب الأزمان والله أعلم قوله (فقام سراقة بن مالك بن جعشم
# 
# فقال يا رسول الله ألعامنا هذا أم لأبد) إلى آخره هذا الحديث سبق شرحه

واضحا في  آخر الباب الذي قبل هذا وجعشم بضم الجيم وبضم الشين المعجمة

وفتحها ذكره الجوهري وغيره قوله (فوجد فاطمة ممن حل ولبست ثيابا صبيغا

واكتحلت فأنكر ذلك عليها) فيه إنكار الرجل على زوجته ما رآه منها من نقص في

دينها لأنه ظن أن ذلك لا يجوز فأنكره قوله (فذهبت إلى رسول الله صلى الله

عليه وسلم محرشا على فاطمة) التحريش الإغراء والمراد هنا أن يذكر له ما

يقتضي عتابها قوله (قلت إني أهل بما أهل به رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم)

هذا قد سبق شرحه في الباب قبله وأنه يجوز تعليق الإحرام بإحرام كإحرام فلان

قوله (فحل الناس كلهم وقصروا إلا النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ومن كان معه

هدي) هذا أيضا تقدم شرحه في الباب السابق وفيه إطلاق اللفظ العام وإرادة

الخصوص لأن عائشة لم تحل ولم تكن ممن ساق الهدي والمراد بقوله حل الناس

كلهم أي معظمهم والهدى بإسكان الدال وكسرها وتشديد الياء مع الكسر وتخفف مع

الاسكان وأما قوله وقصروا فانما قصروا ولم يحلقوا مع أن الحلق أفضل
# 
# لأنهم أرادوا أن يبقى شعر يحلق في الحج فلو حلقوا لم يبق شعر فكان

التقصير هنا أحسن ليحصل في النسكين إزالة شعر والله أعلم قوله (فلما كان

يوم التروية توجهوا إلى منى فأهلوا بالحج) يوم التروية هو الثامن من ذي

الحجة سبق بيانه واشتقاقه مرات وسبق أيضا مرات أن الأفضل عند الشافعي

وموافقيه أن من كان بمكة وأراد الإحرام بالحج أحرم يوم التروية عملا بهذا
chapters.anchors:
- Root: س-ع-ي (sa-ʿa-ya)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To strive, run, or walk briskly with effort; the act of exertion toward a goal.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In ritual context, the specific devotional pacing between al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah, symbolizing earnest seeking (ṭalab) and obedience (ṭāʿah).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) for physical exertion; metaphorical (majāz) for spiritual striving in devotion.
- Root: ر-ق-ي (ra-qā-ya)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To ascend, climb, or mount upon an elevated place.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Elevation in rank or physical ascent; here, the recommended act of climbing upon the hills for visibility of the Kaʿbah.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for physical climbing; metaphorical for spiritual elevation in ritual.
- Root: ه-ز-م (hā-zā-mīm)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To defeat, rout, or scatter an enemy in battle.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Divine victory (naṣr) over confederates (aḥzāb) without human agency, emphasizing supernatural intervention.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for military defeat; here, metaphorical for God's sole power in vanquishing foes.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clause (al-Sharṭ wa al-Jawāb) — The phrase "law tarakah" (if he leaves it) introduces a conditional with the jawāb indicating the consequence (ṣaḥḥa saʿyuhu), governing the legal ruling on omission.
chapters.translation:
I say: In this wording are several types of the rites (manāsik). Among them is that the saʿy (pacing) requires that one begin from al-Ṣafā. This is the position of al-Shāfiʿī, Mālik, and the majority (al-jumhūr). It has been established in the narration of al-Nasāʾī in this ḥadīth with a sound chain (isnād ṣaḥīḥ) that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Begin with what Allah began with" — thus in the plural form (ṣīghat al-jamʿ).

Among them is that one should ascend (yarqā) upon al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah. Regarding this ascent, there is a divergence of opinion. The majority of our companions (aṣḥābunā) say it is a sunnah (recommended practice), not a condition (sharṭ) nor an obligation (wājib). If one abandons it, his saʿy is valid, but he misses the virtue (al-faḍīlah). Abū Ḥafṣ ibn al-Wakīl, from our companions, said: His saʿy is not valid until he ascends upon something of al-Ṣafā. The correct view (al-ṣawāb) is the first. Our companions said: However, it is a condition that he not leave any part of the distance between al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah. So let him affix his heels (ʿaqibayhi) to the steps of al-Ṣafā, and when he reaches al-Marwah, let him affix the toes of his feet (aṣābiʿ rijlayhi) to its steps. Likewise, in all seven times, it is a condition in each time that he affix his heels to what he begins from and his toes to what he ends at.

Our companions said: It is recommended (yustaḥabb) to ascend upon al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah until one sees the House (al-Bayt), if possible. Among them is that it is sunnah to stand upon al-Ṣafā facing the Kaʿbah, and to remember Allah, the Exalted, with this mentioned remembrance (dhikr), and to supplicate (duʿāʾ), and to repeat the remembrance and supplication three times. This is the well-known view (al-mashhūr) among our companions. A group of our companions said: He repeats the remembrance three times and the supplication only twice. The correct view is the first.

His saying, peace and blessings be upon him: "And He defeated the confederates (al-aḥzāb) alone" — its meaning is: He defeated them without combat from human beings and without any cause from their direction. The intended meaning of "the confederates" is those who confederated against the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, on the Day of the Trench (al-Khandaq). The Trench was in Shawwāl, in the fourth year of the Hijrah. It is also said: the fifth year.

His saying: "Then he descended to al-Marwah until his feet were immersed in the bottom of the valley (baṭn al-wādī); when they ascended, he walked until he came to al-Marwah" — thus it is in the copies (al-nusakh), and likewise al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ transmitted it from all the copies. He said: In it, there is an omission of a word that is indispensable, namely: "until his feet were immersed in the bottom of the valley, he ran (ramala)." It is indispensable. This word has been established in other than the narration of Muslim. Likewise, al-Ḥumaydī mentioned it in "al-Jamʿ bayn al-Ṣaḥīḥayn," and in al-Muwaṭṭaʾ: "Until when his feet were immersed in the bottom of the valley, he hastened (saʿā) until he exited from it" — and it is equivalent in meaning to "ramala." This is the speech of al-Qāḍī. It has occurred in some copies of Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim: "Until when his feet were immersed in the bottom of the valley, he hastened (saʿā)" — just as it occurred in al-Muwaṭṭaʾ and others. And Allah knows best.

In this ḥadīth is the recommendation (istihbāb) of intense hastening (al-saʿy al-shadīd) in the bottom of the valley until one ascends, then walks the remaining distance to al-Marwah in his usual manner of walking. This hastening is recommended in each of the seven times in this specific place, and walking is recommended before the valley and after it. If one walks throughout all of it, or hastens throughout all of it, it suffices him, but he misses the virtue. This is the madhhab of al-Shāfiʿī and those who agree with him. Regarding Mālik, concerning one who abandons the intense hastening in its place, there are two narrations (riwāyatān): one is as mentioned, and the second is that he must repeat it (iʿādatuhu).

His saying: "And he did upon al-Marwah the like of what he did upon al-Ṣafā" — in it is that it is sunnah upon it, of remembrance, supplication, and ascent, the like of what is sunnah upon al-Ṣafā. This is agreed upon (muttafaq ʿalayhi).

His saying: "Until when it was the last circuit (ṭawāf) upon al-Marwah" — in it is an indication of the madhhab of al-Shāfiʿī and the majority that going from al-Ṣafā to al-Marwah counts as one time, and returning to al-Ṣafā as a second, and returning to al-Marwah as a third, and so on. Thus, the beginning of the seven is from al-Ṣafā and their end is at al-Marwah. Ibn Bint al-Shāfiʿī and Abū Bakr al-Ṣayrafī, from our companions, said: Going to al-Marwah and returning to al-Ṣafā counts as a single time, so the end of the seven falls at al-Ṣafā. This authentic ḥadīth refutes both of them, as does the practice of the Muslims (ʿamal al-Muslimīn) across successive eras. And Allah knows best.

His saying: "Then Surāqah ibn Mālik ibn Juʿshum stood and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, is this for our year or forever?'" — to the end. This ḥadīth has already been explained clearly at the end of the chapter preceding this one. "Juʿshum" is with a ḍammah on the jīm and a ḍammah on the shīn, and also with a fatḥah on it — al-Jawharī and others mentioned this.

His saying: "And he found Fāṭimah among those who had become permissible (ḥall) and had donned dyed garments (thiyāb ṣabīgh) and applied kohl (iktahalat), and he disapproved of that against her" — in it is a man's disapproval of his wife for what he saw from her of deficiency in her religion (dīn), because he thought that was not permissible, so he disapproved of it.

His saying: "So she went to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, inciting (muḥarrishan) against Fāṭimah" — al-taḥrīsh is incitement (al-ighrāʾ). The intended meaning here is that she mentions to him what necessitates rebuking her (ʿitāb).

His saying: "I said: 'I enter into iḥrām with what the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, enters into iḥrām'" — this has already been explained in the preceding chapter, and that it is permissible to attach one's iḥrām to the iḥrām of another, like the iḥrām of so-and-so.

His saying: "So all the people became permissible (ḥall) and shortened (qaṣṣarū), except the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and those who had the sacrificial animal (hady) with them" — this also has been explained previously in the preceding chapter. In it is the application of a general expression (al-lafẓ al-ʿāmm) while intending specificity (al-khuṣūṣ), because ʿĀʾishah did not become permissible and was not among those who drove the sacrificial animal. The intended meaning of his saying "all the people became permissible" is: most of them. "Al-Hady" is with sukūn on the dāl, and with kasrah on it, and with tashdīd on the yāʾ with kasrah, and it is lightened with sukūn.

As for his saying: "And they shortened" — they only shortened and did not shave (ḥalaqū), even though shaving is superior, because they intended that hair would remain to be shaved during the Ḥajj. If they had shaved, no hair would remain. Thus, shortening (al-taqṣīr) here was better, so that in both rites (nusukayn) there would be removal of hair. And Allah knows best.

His saying: "And when it was the Day of Tarwiyah, they set out to Minā and entered into iḥrām for the Ḥajj" — the Day of Tarwiyah is the eighth of Dhū al-Ḥijjah. Its explanation and derivation (ishtiqāq) have preceded multiple times. It has also preceded multiple times that the superior view (al-afḍal) according to al-Shāfiʿī and those who agree with him is that whoever is in Makkah and intends to enter into iḥrām for the Ḥajj should do so on the Day of Tarwiyah, acting upon this ḥadīth.

chapters.title_en: The Prophet's Hajj: Rites, Timing, and the Abolition of Pre-Islamic Customs
chapters.arabic_text:
الحديث وسبق بيان مذاهب العلماء فيه وفي هذا بيان أن السنة أن لا يتقدم أحد

إلى منى قبل يوم التروية وقد كره مالك ذلك وقال بعض السلف لا بأس به

ومذهبنا أنه خلاف السنة قوله (وركب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فصلى بها

الظهر والعصر والمغرب والعشاء والفجر) فيه بيان سنن إحداها أن الركوب في

تلك المواطن أفضل من المشي كما أنه في جملة الطريق أفضل من المشي هذا هو

الصحيح في الصورتين أن  الركوب أفضل وللشافعي قول آخر ضعيف أن المشي أفضل

وقال بعض أصحابنا الأفضل في جملة الحج الركوب إلا في مواطن المناسك وهي مكة

ومنى ومزدلفة وعرفات والتردد بينهما والسنة الثانية أن يصلي بمنى هذه

الصلوات الخمس والثالثة أن يبيت بمنى هذه الليلة وهي ليلة التاسع من ذي

الحجة وهذا المبيت سنة ليس بركن ولا واجب فلو تركه فلا دم عليه بالإجماع

قوله (ثم مكث قليلا حتى طلعت الشمس) فيه أن السنة أن لا يخرجوا من منى حتى

تطلع الشمس وهذا متفق عليه قوله (وأمر بقبة من شعر تضرب له بنمرة) فيه

استحباب النزول بنمرة إذا ذهبوا من منى لأن السنة أن لا يدخلوا عرفات إلا

بعد زوال الشمس وبعد صلاتي الظهر والعصر جمعا فالسنة أن ينزلوا بنمرة فمن

كان له قبة ضربها ويغتسلون للوقوف قبل الزوال فإذا زالت الشمس سار بهم

الإمام إلى مسجد إبراهيم عليه السلام وخطب بهم خطبتين خفيفتين ويخفف

الثانية جدا فإذا فرغ منها صلى بهم الظهر والعصر جامعا بينهما فإذا فرغ من

الصلاة سار إلى الموقف وفي هذا الحديث جواز الاستظلال للمحرم بقبة وغيرها

ولا
# 
# خلاف في جوازه للنازل واختلفوا في جوازه للراكب فمذهبنا جوازه وبه قال

كثيرون وكرهه مالك وأحمد وستأتي المسألة مبسوطة في موضعها إن شاء الله

تعالى وفيه جواز اتخاذ القباب وجوازها من شعر وقوله (بنمرة) هي بفتح النون

وكسر الميم هذا أصلها ويجوز فيها ما يجوز في نظيرها وهو إسكان الميم مع فتح

النون وكسرها وهي موضع بجنب عرفات وليست من عرفات قوله (ولا تشك قريش إلا

أنه واقف عند المشعر الحرام كما كانت قريش تصنع في الجاهلية) معنى هذا أن

قريشا كانت في الجاهلية تقف بالمشعر الحرام وهو جبل في المزدلفة يقال له

قزح وقيل إن المشعر الحرام كل المزدلفة وهو بفتح الميم على المشهور وبه جاء

القرآن وقيل بكسرها وكان سائر العرب يتجاوزون المزدلفة ويقفون بعرفات فظنت

قريش أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يقف في المشعر الحرام على عادتهم  ولا

يتجاوزه فتجاوزه النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إلى عرفات لأن الله تعالى أمره

بذلك في قوله تعالى ثم أفيضوا من حيث أفاض الناس أي سائر العرب غير قريش

وإنما كانت قريش تقف بالمزدلفة لأنها من الحرم وكانوا يقولون نحن أهل حرم

الله فلا نخرج منه قوله (فأجاز رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم حتى أتى عرفة

فوجد القبة قد ضربت له بنمرة فنزل بها حتى إذا زاغت الشمس) أما أجاز فمعناه

جاوز المزدلفة ولم يقف بها بل توجه إلى عرفات وأما قوله حتى أتى عرفة فمجاز

والمراد قارب عرفات لأنه فسره بقوله وجد القبة قد ضربت بنمرة فنزل بها وقد

سبق أن نمرة ليست من عرفات وقد قدمنا أن دخول عرفات قبل صلاتي الظهر والعصر

جميعا خلاف السنة قوله (حتى إذا زاغت الشمس أمر بالقصواء فرحلت له فأتى بطن

الوادي فخطب الناس) أما القصواء فتقدم ضبطها وبيانها واضحا في أول هذا

الباب وقوله فرحلت هو بتخفيف الحاء أي جعل عليها الرحل وقوله (بطن الوادي)

هو وادي عرنة بضم العين وفتح الراء وبعدها نون وليست عرنة من أرض
# 
# عرفات عند الشافعي والعلماء كافة إلا مالكا فقال هي من عرفات وقوله فخطب

الناس فيه استحباب الخطبة للإمام بالحجيج يوم عرفة في هذا الموضع وهو سنة

باتفاق جماهير العلماء وخالف فيها المالكية ومذهب الشافعي أن في الحج أربع

خطب مسنونة إحداها يوم السابع من ذي الحجة يخطب عند الكعبة بعد صلاة الظهر

والثانية هذه التي ببطن عرنة يوم عرفات والثالثة يوم النحر والرابعة يوم

النفر الأول وهو اليوم الثاني من أيام التشريق قال أصحابنا وكل هذه الخطب

أفراد وبعد صلاة الظهر إلا التي يوم عرفات فإنها خطبتان وقبل الصلاة قال

أصحابنا ويعلمهم في كل خطبة من هذه ما يحتاجون إليه إلى الخطبة الأخرى

والله أعلم قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (إن دماءكم وأموالكم حرام عليكم كحرمة

يومكم هذا في شهركم هذا) معناه متأكدة التحريم شديدته وفي هذا دليل لضرب

الأمثال وإلحاق النظير  بالنظير قياسا قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (ألا كل شيء

من أمر الجاهلية تحت قدمي موضوع ودماء الجاهلية موضوعة وإن أول دم أضع دم

بن ربيعة بن الحارث كان مسترضعا في بني سعد فقتلته هذيل وربا الجاهلية

موضوعة وأول ربا أضع ربانا ربا العباس بن عبد المطلب فإنه موضوع كله) في

هذه الجملة إبطال أفعال الجاهلية وبيوعها التي لم يتصل بها قبض وأنه لا

قصاص في قتلها وأن الإمام وغيره ممن يأمر بمعروف أو ينهى عن منكر ينبغي أن

يبدأ بنفسه وأهله فهو أقرب إلى قبول قوله وإلى طيب نفس من قرب عهده
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ق-د-م (q-d-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To precede, to go before; also "ancient" or "prior" — here, acting before the prescribed time.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Temporal precedence (taqaddum) in ritual acts; contrasts with the divinely ordained sequence (tartīb) of Hajj.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: physical forward movement; Metaphorical: violating the Sunnah's temporal order.
- Sībawayh Rule: ʿAṭf al-Bayān (Appositional Clarification) — e.g., "بطن الوادي" is clarified by "وادي عرنة" as a specific designation, not a new sentence.
chapters.translation:
I say: The Hadith has been mentioned, and the exposition of the scholars' schools of thought regarding it has already preceded. In this [Hadith] there is a clarification that the Sunnah is that no one should proceed to Minā before the Day of Tarwiyah (the 8th of Dhul-Ḥijjah). Mālik disapproved of that [i.e., proceeding early], and some of the Salaf (predecessors) said there is no harm in it. Our school (the Shāfiʿīs) holds that it is contrary to the Sunnah.

His statement (and the Prophet ﷺ rode and prayed at Minā the Ẓuhr, ʿAṣr, Maghrib, ʿIshāʾ, and Fajr) contains a clarification of Sunnans (recommended practices). One of them is that riding in those places is superior to walking, just as riding is superior to walking on the road in general. This is the correct view in both situations: that riding is superior. There is another weak saying of al-Shāfiʿī that walking is superior. Some of our companions said: The superior practice in the entirety of Hajj is riding, except at the sites of the rituals (manāsik), which are Makkah, Minā, Muzdalifah, and ʿArafāt, and there is a difference of opinion regarding the travel between them.

The second Sunnah is to pray these five prayers at Minā. The third is to spend the night at Minā on this night, which is the night of the 9th of Dhul-Ḥijjah. This overnight stay is a Sunnah, not a pillar (rukn) nor an obligation (wājib). If one abandons it, there is no expiatory blood (dam) upon him by consensus (ijmāʿ).

His statement (then he stayed a little until the sun rose) indicates that the Sunnah is that they should not depart from Minā until the sun has risen. This is agreed upon (muttafaq ʿalayh).

His statement (and he ordered a dome of hair (qubbah min shaʿr) to be pitched for him at Namirah) indicates the recommendation (istihbāb) of descending at Namirah when they depart from Minā, because the Sunnah is that they should not enter ʿArafāt except after the sun's declination (zawāl) and after the two prayers of Ẓuhr and ʿAṣr combined (jamʿ). Thus, the Sunnah is that they descend at Namirah. Whoever has a dome should pitch it, and they perform the ritual bath (ghusl) for the standing (wuqūf) before the zawāl. When the sun declines, the Imām leads them to the Mosque of Ibrāhīm (peace be upon him) and delivers two light sermons (khuṭbahs) to them, making the second extremely brief. When he finishes them, he leads them in Ẓuhr and ʿAṣr, combining them. When he finishes the prayer, he proceeds to the standing place (mawqif).

In this Hadith there is the permissibility of seeking shade (istizlāl) for the muḥrim (one in iḥrām) under a dome or other cover. There is no disagreement regarding its permissibility for the one who is stationary (nāzil). They differed regarding its permissibility for the rider. Our school holds it permissible, and many scholars concur. Mālik and Aḥmad disapproved of it. The issue will be presented in detail in its proper place, God willing.

In it also is the permissibility of erecting domes, and their permissibility from hair. His statement (at Namirah) — it is with the opening of the nūn (fatḥah) and the kasrah of the mīm; this is its original form. What is permissible in its analogues is permissible in it, namely, the sukkūn (quiescence) of the mīm with the fatḥah or kasrah of the nūn. It is a place adjacent to ʿArafāt, and it is not part of ʿArafāt.

His statement (and the Quraysh did not doubt except that he was standing at the Mashʿar al-Ḥarām, just as the Quraysh used to do in the Jāhiliyyah) — the meaning of this is that the Quraysh in the Jāhiliyyah used to stand at the Mashʿar al-Ḥarām, which is a mountain in Muzdalifah called Quzaḥ. It is also said that the Mashʿar al-Ḥarām is all of Muzdalifah. It is with the fatḥah of the mīm according to the well-known view, and the Qurʾān came with this; it is also said with its kasrah. The rest of the Arabs would pass beyond Muzdalifah and stand at ʿArafāt. The Quraysh thus thought that the Prophet ﷺ would stand at the Mashʿar al-Ḥarām according to their custom and would not pass beyond it. But the Prophet ﷺ passed beyond it to ʿArafāt, because God Almighty commanded him to do so in His saying: {«Then depart from where the people depart»} (Q 2:199) — meaning the rest of the Arabs, not the Quraysh. The Quraysh only stood at Muzdalifah because it is within the Sacred Precinct (Ḥaram), and they would say: "We are the people of God's Sanctuary, so we do not leave it."

His statement (then the Messenger of God ﷺ passed on until he came to ʿArafah, and he found the dome had been pitched for him at Namirah, and he descended there until the sun declined) — as for "he passed on" (ajāza), its meaning is that he crossed beyond Muzdalifah and did not stand there, but rather headed toward ʿArafāt. As for his statement "until he came to ʿArafah," it is metaphorical (majāz), and the intended meaning is that he approached ʿArafāt, because he explained it by his saying "he found the dome had been pitched at Namirah and descended there." It has already been mentioned that Namirah is not part of ʿArafāt. We have also already stated that entering ʿArafāt before the two prayers of Ẓuhr and ʿAṣr combined is contrary to the Sunnah.

His statement (until when the sun declined, he ordered the Qaṣwāʾ [his she-camel] to be saddled for him, and he came to the middle of the valley (baṭn al-wādī) and addressed the people) — as for "al-Qaṣwāʾ," its correct spelling and clarification have already been presented clearly at the beginning of this chapter. His statement "he saddled" (fa-ruḥḥilat) is with the takhfīf (lightening) of the ḥāʾ, meaning the saddle (raḥl) was placed upon it. His statement "the middle of the valley" is the valley of ʿUranah — with the ḍammah of the ʿayn and the fatḥah of the rāʾ, followed by a nūn. ʿUranah is not part of the land of ʿArafāt according to al-Shāfiʿī and all the scholars, except Mālik, who said it is part of ʿArafāt.

His statement (and he addressed the people) indicates the recommendation of the Imām delivering a sermon to the pilgrims on the Day of ʿArafah at this location. It is a Sunnah by the agreement of the majority of scholars (jumhūr). The Mālikīs dissented from this. The Shāfiʿī school holds that in Hajj there are four recommended sermons (khuṭbahs): The first is on the 7th of Dhul-Ḥijjah, delivered at the Kaʿbah after the Ẓuhr prayer. The second is this one at Baṭn ʿUranah on the Day of ʿArafah. The third is on the Day of Sacrifice (Yawm al-Naḥr). The fourth is on the Day of the First Departure (Yawm al-Nafr al-Awwal), which is the second day of the Days of Tashrīq. Our companions said: All these sermons are single (afrād) and after the Ẓuhr prayer, except the one on the Day of ʿArafah, for it is two sermons and before the prayer. Our companions said: In each of these sermons, the Imām teaches the people what they need until the next sermon. And God knows best.

His statement ﷺ (Indeed, your blood and your wealth are sacred to you, like the sanctity of this day of yours, in this month of yours) — its meaning is that the prohibition is emphatic and severe. In this is evidence for the striking of parables (ḍarb al-amthāl) and the analogical attachment of the similar to the similar (ilḥāq al-naẓīr bil-naẓīr) via qiyās.

His statement ﷺ (Behold, every matter of the Jāhiliyyah is placed under my feet, abolished. The blood [revenge claims] of the Jāhiliyyah are abolished, and the first blood I abolish is the blood of Ibn Rabīʿah ibn al-Ḥārith, who was fostered among the Banū Saʿd and was killed by Hudhayl. The usury (ribā) of the Jāhiliyyah is abolished, and the first usury I abolish is our usury, the usury of al-ʿAbbās ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib, for it is all abolished) — in this passage is the nullification of the practices of the Jāhiliyyah and its transactions that were not accompanied by possession (qabḍ), and that there is no retaliation (qiṣāṣ) for its killings. It also indicates that the Imām and anyone else who commands good or forbids evil should begin with himself and his family, for that is more conducive to the acceptance of his words and to the contentment of the soul of the one who is near in his covenant (i.e., the listener).

chapters.title_en: The Farewell Sermon: Abrogation of Blood-Vengeance, Usury, and Rights of Women
chapters.arabic_text:
بالإسلام وأما قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم تحت قدمي فإشارة إلى إبطاله وأما

قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم وإن أول دم أضع دم بن ربيعة فقال المحققون

والجمهور اسم هذا الابن إياس بن ربيعة بن الحارث بن عبد المطلب وقيل اسمه

حارثة وقيل آدم قال الدارقطني وهو تصحيف وقيل اسمه تمام وممن سماه آدم

الزبير
# 
# بن بكار قال القاضي عياض ورواه بعض رواة مسلم دم ربيعة بن الحارث قال

وكذا رواه أبو داود قيل هو وهم والصواب بن ربيعة لأن ربيعة عاش بعد النبي

صلى الله عليه وسلم إلى زمن عمر بن الخطاب وتأوله أبو عبيد فقال دم ربيعة

لأنه ولي الدم فنسبه إليه قالوا وكان هذا الابن المقتول طفلا صغيرا يحبو

بين البيوت فأصابه حجر في حرب كانت بين بني سعد وبني ليث بن بكر قاله

الزبير بن بكار قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم في الربا (إنه موضوع كله) معناه

الزائد على رأس المال كما قال الله تعالى وان تبتم فلكم رؤوس أموالكم وهذا

الذي ذكرته إيضاح وإلا فالمقصود مفهوم من نفس لفظ الحديث لأن الربا هو

الزيادة فإذا وضع الربا فمعناه وضع الزيادة والمراد بالوضع الرد والإبطال

قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (فاتقوا الله في النساء فإنكم أخذتموهن بأمان

الله) فيه الحث على مراعاة حق النساء والوصية بهن ومعاشرتهن بالمعروف وقد

جاءت أحاديث كثيرة صحيحة  في الوصية بهن وبيان حقوقهن والتحذير من التقصير

في ذلك وقد جمعتها أو معظمها في رياض الصالحين وقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم

(أخذتموهن بأمان الله) هكذا هو في كثير من الأصول وفي بعضها بأمانة الله

قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (واستحللتم فروجهن بكلمة الله) قيل معناه قوله

تعالى فإمساك بمعروف أو تسريح باحسان وقيل المراد كلمة التوحيد وهي لا إله

إلا الله محمد رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إذ لا تحل مسلمة لغير مسلم

وقيل المراد بإباحة الله والكلمة قوله تعالى فانكحوا ما طاب لكم من النساء

وهذا الثالث هو الصحيح وبالأول قال الخطابي والهروي وغيرهما وقيل المراد

بالكلمة الإيجاب والقبول ومعناه على هذا بالكلمة التي أمر الله تعالى بها

والله أعلم قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (ولكم عليهن أن لا يوطئن فرشكم أحدا

تكرهونه فإن فعلن ذلك فاضربوهن ضربا غير مبرح) قال المازري قيل المراد بذلك

أن لا يستخلين بالرجال ولم يرد زناها لأن ذلك يوجب جلدها ولأن ذلك حرام مع

من يكرهه الزوج ومن لا يكرهه وقال القاضي عياض كانت عادة العرب حديث الرجال

مع النساء ولم يكن ذلك عيبا ولا
# 
# ريبة عندهم فلما نزلت آية الحجاب نهوا عن ذلك هذا كلام القاضي والمختار

أن معناه أن لا يأذن لأحد تكرهونه في دخول بيوتكم والجلوس في منازلكم سواء

كان المأذون له رجلا أجنبيا أو امرأة أو أحدا من محارم الزوجة فالنهي

يتناول جميع ذلك وهذا حكم المسألة عند الفقهاء أنها لا يحل لها أن تأذن

لرجل أو امرأة ولا محرم ولا غيره في دخول منزل الزوج إلا من علمت أو ظنت أن

الزوج لا يكرهه لأن الأصل تحريم دخول منزل الإنسان حتى يوجد الإذن في ذلك

منه أو ممن أذن له في الإذن في ذلك أو عرف رضاه باطراد العرف بذلك ونحوه

ومتى حصل الشك في الرضا ولم يترجح شيء ولا وجدت قرينة لا يحل الدخول ولا

الإذن والله أعلم وأما الضرب المبرح فهو الضرب الشديد الشاق  ومعناه اضربوهن

ضربا ليس بشديد ولا شاق والبرح المشقة والمبرح بضم الميم وفتح الموحدة وكسر

الراء وفي هذا الحديث إباحة ضرب الرجل امرأته للتأديب فإن ضربها الضرب

المأذون فيه فماتت منه وجبت ديتها على عاقلة الضارب ووجبت الكفارة في ماله

قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (ولهن عليكم رزقهن وكسوتهن بالمعروف) فيه وجوب

نفقة الزوجة وكسوتها وذلك ثابت بالإجماع قوله (فقال بإصبعه السبابة يرفعها

إلى السماء وينكتها إلى الناس اللهم اشهد) هكذا ضبطناه ينكتها بعد الكاف

تاء مثناة فوق قال القاضي كذا الرواية بالتاء المثناة فوق قال وهو بعيد

المعنى قال قيل صوابه ينكبها بباء موحدة قال ورويناه في سنن أبي داود

بالتاء المثناة من طريق بن الأعرابي وبالموحدة من طريق أبي بكر التمار

ومعناه يقلبها ويرددها إلى الناس مشيرا إليهم ومنه نكب كنانته إذا قلبها

هذا كلام القاضي قوله (ثم أذن ثم أقام فصلى الظهر ثم أقام فصلى العصر ولم

يصل بينهما شيئا) فيه أنه يشرع الجمع بين الظهر والعصر
# 
# هناك في ذلك اليوم وقد أجمعت الأمة عليه واختلفوا في سببه فقيل بسبب

النسك وهو مذهب أبي حنيفة وبعض أصحاب الشافعي وقال أكثر أصحاب الشافعي هو

بسبب السفر فمن كان حاضرا أو مسافرا دون مرحلتين كأهل مكة لم يجز له الجمع

كما لا يجوز له القصر وفيه أن الجامع بين الصلاتين يصلي الأولى أولا وأنه

يؤذن للأولى وأنه يقيم لكل واحدة منهما وأنه لا يفرق بينهما وهذا كله متفق

عليه عندنا قوله (ثم ركب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم حتى أتى الموقف فجعل

بطن ناقته القصواء إلى الصخرات وجعل حبل المشاة بين يديه واستقبل القبلة

فلم يزل واقفا حتى غربت الشمس وذهبت الصفرة قليلا حتى غاب القرص) في هذا
chapters.anchors:
- Root: و-ض-ع (wa-ḍa-ʿa)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To place, put down, lay aside; also to abrogate, nullify, or cancel (as in placing a burden down).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In legal-theological context, denotes annulment of pre-Islamic obligations (ʿadāʾ al-jāhilīyah), specifically the cancellation of claims.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal = physical placement; metaphorical = rescission of a legal right or claim, as here "placed under my feet" signifies total abrogation.
- Sībawayh Rule: ʿAṭf al-Bayān (Appositional Clarification) — The phrase "دم بن ربيعة" is clarified by the following genitive construction, requiring precise identification of the referent (the slain child's name).
chapters.translation:
I say: Regarding his statement (peace and blessings be upon him), "under my feet," it is an indication of its annulment. As for his statement (peace and blessings be upon him), "And the first blood-vengeance I place is that of the son of Rabīʿah," the verifiers (muḥaqqiqūn) and the majority (jumhūr) hold that the name of this son was Iyās ibn Rabīʿah ibn al-Ḥārith ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib. It was also said his name was Ḥārithah, and it was said Ādam — al-Dāraquṭnī stated this is a corruption (taṣḥīf). It was also said his name was Tamām. Among those who named him Ādam was al-Zubayr ibn Bakkār. Al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ said: Some transmitters of Muslim narrated it as "the blood of Rabīʿah ibn al-Ḥārith." He said: Likewise Abū Dāwūd narrated it. It was said this is an error (wahm), and the correct version is "son of Rabīʿah," because Rabīʿah lived after the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) until the time of ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb. Abū ʿUbayd interpreted it saying "the blood of Rabīʿah" because he was the guardian of the blood-claim (walī al-dam), so it was attributed to him. They said: This slain son was a small infant crawling between the houses, and a stone struck him during a war between Banū Saʿd and Banū Layth ibn Bakr. This was stated by al-Zubayr ibn Bakkār.

His statement (peace and blessings be upon him) concerning usury (ribā): "Indeed it is entirely placed aside" — its meaning is the excess over the principal capital, as Allah the Exalted said: {«وَإِنْ تُبْتُمْ فَلَكُمْ رُءُوسُ أَمْوَالِكُمْ»} ("And if you repent, then you shall have your principal sums"). What I have mentioned is clarification; otherwise, the intended meaning is understood from the very wording of the ḥadīth itself, because usury is the excess. So when usury is "placed aside," its meaning is the annulment of the excess. The intended meaning of "placing aside" is restitution and abrogation.

His statement (peace and blessings be upon him): "Fear Allah regarding women, for you have taken them as a trust from Allah" — in this is an exhortation to observe the rights of women, to enjoin kindness toward them, and to consort with them in a goodly manner (bi-al-maʿrūf). Many authentic ḥadīths have come regarding enjoining kindness to them, clarifying their rights, and warning against negligence in that regard. I have collected them, or most of them, in Riyāḍ al-Ṣāliḥīn. His statement (peace and blessings be upon him), "you have taken them as a trust from Allah" — thus it appears in many manuscripts (uṣūl), and in some of them "as a trust from Allah" (bi-amānati-Allāh).

His statement (peace and blessings be upon him): "And you have made lawful their private parts by the word of Allah" — it was said its meaning is His statement the Exalted: {«فَإِمْسَاكٌ بِمَعْرُوفٍ أَوْ تَسْرِيحٌ بِإِحْسَانٍ»} ("Then either retain them with kindness or release them with goodness").
