It was also said the intended meaning is the word of monotheism (kalimat al-tawḥīd), namely "There is no god but Allah, Muḥammad is the Messenger of Allah" (peace and blessings be upon him), for a Muslim woman is not lawful for a non-Muslim. It was also said the intended meaning is the permissibility granted by Allah, and the "word" is His statement the Exalted: {«فَانْكِحُوا مَا طَابَ لَكُمْ مِنَ النِّسَاءِ»} ("Then marry what is pleasing to you of women"). This third interpretation is the correct one. The first was stated by al-Khaṭṭābī, al-Harawī, and others. It was also said the intended meaning of "word" is the offer and acceptance (ījāb wa qabūl), and its meaning on this basis is "by the word which Allah the Exalted has commanded." And Allah knows best.

His statement (peace and blessings be upon him): "And you have the right over them that they do not admit onto your beds anyone whom you dislike. If they do that, then strike them with a non-severe beating (ḍarban ghayra mubarriḥ)." Al-Māzarī said: It was said the intended meaning is that they should not seclude themselves with men, and fornication is not intended — because that would necessitate flogging (jald), and because it is forbidden whether the husband dislikes the man or not. Al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ said: The custom of the Arabs was for men to converse with women, and this was not considered shameful nor suspicious among them. When the verse of the hijāb was revealed, they were prohibited from that. This is the statement of al-Qāḍī. The chosen view (al-mukhtār) is that its meaning is that she should not permit anyone whom he dislikes to enter their houses or sit in their dwellings — whether the permitted person is a foreign man, a woman, or any of the wife's male relatives (maḥārim). The prohibition encompasses all of that. This is the ruling of the matter according to the jurists: it is not lawful for her to permit a man, a woman, a maḥram, or anyone else to enter the husband's home, except one whom she knows or strongly believes the husband does not dislike — because the default principle is the prohibition of entering a person's home until permission is granted by him, or by one whom he has authorized to grant permission, or his satisfaction is known through the continuity of custom (iṭṭirād al-ʿurf) and the like. Whenever there is doubt about satisfaction and nothing is preponderant, and no indication (qarīnah) exists, then neither entry nor permission is lawful. And Allah knows best.

As for the "severe beating" (al-ḍarb al-mubarriḥ), it is the intense, painful beating. Its meaning is: strike them with a beating that is neither intense nor painful. "Al-barḥ" is hardship, and "al-mubarriḥ" is with ḍammah on the mīm, fatḥah on the bāʾ, and kasrah on the rāʾ. In this ḥadīth is the permissibility of a man striking his wife for discipline (taʾdīb). If he strikes her with the permitted beating and she dies from it, then her blood-money (diyah) is obligatory upon the striker's ʿāqilah (agnatic kin), and expiation (kaffārah) is obligatory from his own wealth.

His statement (peace and blessings be upon him): "And they have the right upon you of their provision (rizq) and clothing (kiswah) in a goodly manner" — in this is the obligation of the wife's maintenance (nafaqah) and clothing, which is established by consensus (ijmāʿ).

His statement: "Then he pointed with his index finger, raising it toward the sky and turning it toward the people, saying: 'O Allah, bear witness'" — thus we have recorded it: "yanikutuhā" (turning it) with a tāʾ marbūṭah (tāʾ with two dots above) after the kāf. Al-Qāḍī said: Thus is the narration with the tāʾ with two dots above, and he said it is far-fetched in meaning. He said: It was said the correct form is "yankibuhā" with a single bāʾ. He said: We narrated it in Sunan Abī Dāwūd with the tāʾ with two dots via the chain of Ibn al-Aʿrābī, and with the single bāʾ via the chain of Abū Bakr al-Tammār. Its meaning is: he turned it and directed it repeatedly toward the people, pointing at them. From this is the expression "nakaba kanānatahu" (he turned over his quiver) when he overturns it. This is the statement of al-Qāḍī.

His statement: "Then he gave the call to prayer (adhān), then the iqāmah, and prayed Ẓuhr; then he gave the iqāmah and prayed ʿAṣr, and he did not pray anything between them" — in this is that combining (jamʿ) between Ẓuhr and ʿAṣr is legislated (yushraʿu) there on that day. The ummah has consensus upon it, but they differed regarding its cause. It was said it is due to the rites (nusuk) — this is the madhhab of Abū Ḥanīfah and some of al-Shāfiʿī's companions. The majority of al-Shāfiʿī's companions said it is due to travel (safar). Thus, whoever is a resident (ḥāḍir) or a traveler of less than two stages (marḥalatayn) — like the people of Makkah — it is not permissible for him to combine, just as it is not permissible for him to shorten (qaṣr). In this is also that the one combining the two prayers prays the first one first, that he gives the adhān for the first, that he gives the iqāmah for each of them, and that he does not separate between them. All of this is agreed upon in our school.

His statement: "Then the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) rode until he came to the standing-place (mawqif), and he turned the belly of his she-camel al-Qaṣwāʾ toward the rocky outcrops (ṣakharāt), placed the rope of the pedestrians before him, faced the qiblah, and remained standing until the sun set and the yellowness diminished slightly until the disk disappeared" — in this [is the description of the standing at ʿArafāt].

chapters.title_en: Section 498 — The Standing at ʿArafāt: Rulings, Etiquettes, and the Prophet's Conduct (Ṣalʿallāhu ʿalayhi wa-sallam)
chapters.arabic_text:
الفصل مسائل وآداب للوقوف منها أنه إذا فرغ من الصلاتين عجل الذهاب إلى

الموقف ومنها أن الوقوف راكبا أفضل وفيه خلاف بين العلماء وفي مذهبنا ثلاثة

أقوال أصحها أن الوقوف راكبا أفضل والثاني غير الراكب أفضل والثالث هما

سواء ومنها  أنه يستحب أن يقف عند الصخرات المذكورات وهي صخرات مفترشات في

أسفل جبل الرحمة وهو الجبل الذي بوسط أرض عرفات فهذا هو الموقف المستحب

وأما ما اشتهر بين العوام من الاعتناء بصعود الجبل وتوهمهم أنه لا يصح

الوقوف إلا فيه فغلط بل الصواب جواز الوقوف في كل جزء من أرض عرفات وأن

الفضيلة في موقف رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عند الصخرات فإن عجز فليقرب

منه بحسب الإمكان وسيأتي في آخر الحديث بيان حدود عرفات إن شاء الله تعالى

عند قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم وعرفة كلها موقف ومنها استحباب استقبال الكعبة

في الوقوف ومنها أنه ينبغي أن يبقى في الوقوف حتى تغرب الشمس ويتحقق كمال

غروبها ثم يفيض إلى مزدلفة فلو أفاض قبل غروب الشمس صح وقوفه وحجه ويجبر

ذلك بدم وهل الدم واجب أم مستحب فيه قولان للشافعي أصحهما أنه سنة والثاني

واجب وهما مبنيان على أن الجمع بين الليل والنهار واجب على من وقف بالنهار

أم لا وفيه قولان أصحهما سنة والثاني واجب وأما وقت الوقوف فهو ما بين زوال

الشمس
# 
# يوم عرفة وطلوع الفجر الثاني يوم النحر فمن حصل بعرفات في جزء من هذا

الزمان صح وقوفه ومن فاته ذلك فاته الحج هذا مذهب الشافعي وجماهير العلماء

وقال مالك لا يصح الوقوف في النهار منفردا بل لا بد من الليل وحده فإن

اقتصر على الليل كفاه وإن اقتصر على النهار لم يصح وقوفه وقال أحمد يدخل

وقت الوقوف من الفجر يوم عرفة وأجمعوا على أن أصل الوقوف ركن لا يصح الحج

إلا به والله أعلم وأما قوله (وجعل حبل المشاة بين يديه) فروي حبل بالحاء

المهملة وإسكان الباء وروي جبل بالجيم وفتح الباء قال القاضي عياض رحمه

الله الأول أشبه بالحديث وحبل المشاة أي مجتمعهم وحبل الرمل ما طال منه

وضخم وأما بالجيم فمعناه طريقهم وحيث تسلك الرجالة وأما قوله (فلم يزل

واقفا حتى غربت الشمس وذهبت الصفرة قليلا حتى غاب القرص) هكذا هو في  جميع

النسخ وكذا نقله القاضي عن جميع النسخ قال قيل لعل صوابه حين غاب القرص هذا

كلام القاضي ويحتمل أن الكلام على ظاهره ويكون قوله حتى غاب القرص بيانا

لقوله غربت الشمس وذهبت الصفرة فإن هذه تطلق مجازا على مغيب معظم القرص

فأزال ذلك الاحتمال بقوله حتى غاب القرص والله أعلم قوله وأردف أسامة خلفه

فيه جواز الإرداف إذا كانت الدابة مطيقة وقد تظاهرت به الأحاديث قوله (وقد

شنق للقصواء الزمام حتى أن رأسها ليصيب مورك رحله) معنى شنق ضم وضيق وهو

بتخفيف النون ومورك الرحل قال الجوهري قال أبو عبيد المورك والموركة يعني

بفتح الميم وكسر الراء هو الموضع الذي يثني الراكب رجله عليه قدام واسطة

الرحل إذا مل من الركوب وضبطه القاضي بفتح الراء قال وهو قطعة أدم يتورك

عليها الراكب تجعل في مقدم الرحل شبه المخدة الصغيرة وفي هذا استحباب الرفق

في السير من الراكب بالمشاة وبأصحاب الدواب الضعيفة قوله (ويقول بيده

السكينة السكينة) مرتين منصوبا أي الزموا السكينة وهي الرفق والطمأنينة

ففيه أن السكينة في الدفع من عرفات سنة فإذا وجد فرجة يسرع كما ثبت في

الحديث الآخر
# 
# قوله (كلما أتى حبلا من الحبال أرخى لها قليلا حتى تصعد حتى أتى

المزدلفة) الحبال هنا بالحاء المهملة المكسورة جمع حبل وهو التل اللطيف من

الرمل الضخم وقوله (حتى تصعد) هو بفتح الياء المثناة فوق وضمها يقال صعد في

الحبل وأصعد ومنه قوله تعالى إذ تصعدون وأما المزدلفة فمعروفة سميت بذلك من

التزلف والازدلاف وهو التقرب لأن الحجاج إذا أفاضوا من عرفات ازدلفوا إليها

تقربوا منها وقيل سميت بذلك لمجيء الناس إليها في زلف من الليل أي ساعات

وتسمى جمعا بفتح الجيم وإسكان الميم سميت بذلك لاجتماع الناس فيها واعلم أن

المزدلفة كلها من الحرم قال الأزرقي في تاريخ مكة والماوردي وأصحابنا في

كتب المذهب وغيرهم حد مزدلفة ما بين مأزمي عرفة ووادي محسر وليس الحدان

منها ويدخل في المزدلفة جميع تلك الشعاب والجبال الداخلية في الحد المذكور

قوله (حتى أتى المزدلفة فصلى بها المغرب والعشاء بأذان واحد وإقامتين ولم

يسبح بينهما شيئا) فيه فوائد منها أن السنة للدافع من عرفات أن يؤخر المغرب

إلى وقت العشاء ويكون هذا التأخير بنية الجمع ثم يجمع بينهما في المزدلفة

في وقت العشاء وهذا مجمع عليه لكن مذهب أبي حنيفة وطائفة أنه يجمع بسبب

النسك ويجوز لأهل مكة والمزدلفة ومنى وغيرهم والصحيح عند أصحابنا أنه جمع

بسبب السفر فلا يجوز إلا لمسافر سفرا يبلغ به مسافة القصر وهو مرحلتان

قاصدتان وللشافعي قول ضعيف أنه يجوز الجمع في كل سفر وإن كان قصيرا وقال

بعض أصحابنا هذا الجمع بسبب النسك كما قال أبو حنيفة والله أعلم قال

أصحابنا ولو جمع بينهما في وقت المغرب في أرض عرفات أو في الطريق أو في
chapters.anchors:
- Root: و-ق-ف (w-q-f)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning is "to stand still, to halt, to pause"; in ritual context, it denotes the prescribed standing at ʿArafāt during the Ḥajj.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In Kalām, al-wuqūf signifies the "standing" of the soul before God in obedience; here, it is the physical ritual stance that symbolizes spiritual presence.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) = physical standing; metaphorical (majāz) = persistence in devotion. The text uses it literally for the ritual.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clause (al-sharṭ) — "If he fails to do so, the Ḥajj is missed" (fa-in fātahu dhālika fātahu al-ḥajj) follows the pattern of sharṭ + jazāʾ, where the apodosis is a verbal sentence indicating consequence.
chapters.translation:
I say: Know that this chapter concerns matters and etiquettes pertaining to the standing (al-wuqūf). Among them: when one completes the two prayers (i.e., the combined Ẓuhr and ʿAṣr at ʿArafāt), he should hasten to depart to the standing place (al-mawqif). Among them: that standing while riding is superior—though there is scholarly disagreement; in our school (al-Shāfiʿī) there are three opinions: the soundest (al-aṣaḥḥ) is that standing while riding is superior; the second is that standing otherwise (i.e., on foot) is superior; the third is that both are equal. Among them: it is recommended (mustaḥabb) to stand at the aforementioned rocks (al-ṣakhrāt)—these are flat rocks spread at the base of the Mountain of Mercy (Jabal al-Raḥmah), which is the mountain at the center of the land of ʿArafāt. This is the recommended standing place. As for what is popularly known among the common folk—their excessive concern with climbing the mountain and their assumption that standing is only valid upon it—this is an error. Rather, the correct view is the permissibility of standing in any part of the land of ʿArafāt, and that the virtue lies in the standing place of the Messenger of Allāh (Ṣalʿallāhu ʿalayhi wa-sallam) at the rocks. If one is unable, let him draw near to it as much as possible. The boundaries of ʿArafāt will be explained at the end of the ḥadīth, God willing, at his saying (Ṣalʿallāhu ʿalayhi wa-sallam): «And all of ʿArafāt is a standing place» (wa-ʿArafatu kulluhā mawqif). Among them: the recommendation of facing the Kaʿbah during the standing. Among them: one should remain in the standing until the sun sets and its complete setting is certain, then depart to Muzdalifah. If one departs before sunset, his standing and his Ḥajj are valid, but he must compensate with a blood sacrifice (dam). Whether this blood is obligatory or recommended—there are two opinions from al-Shāfiʿī: the sounder is that it is a Sunnah (recommended); the second is that it is obligatory. These two opinions are built upon whether combining the night and the day (in the standing) is obligatory for one who stood during the day or not—and there are two opinions: the sounder is that it is a Sunnah; the second is that it is obligatory. As for the time of the standing, it is from the sun's decline (zawāl) on the Day of ʿArafah until the dawn of the second day (i.e., the Day of Sacrifice, Yawm al-Naḥr). Whoever is present in ʿArafāt during any part of this time, his standing is valid; whoever misses it, misses the Ḥajj. This is the school of al-Shāfiʿī and the majority of scholars. Mālik said: "Standing during the day alone is not valid; rather, the night alone is indispensable. If one limits himself to the night, it suffices him; if he limits himself to the day, his standing is not valid." Aḥmad said: "The time of the standing enters from the dawn of the Day of ʿArafah." They all agree that the standing in its essence is a pillar (rukn) without which the Ḥajj is not valid. And Allāh knows best.

As for his saying (Ṣalʿallāhu ʿalayhi wa-sallam): "And he placed the rope of the walkers before him" (wa-jaʿala ḥabl al-mushāti bayna yadayhi)—it is narrated as "ḥabl" with the unpointed ḥāʾ and silent bāʾ, and also as "jabal" with the jīm and opened bāʾ. Al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ (may Allāh have mercy on him) said: "The first is more fitting to the ḥadīth." "Ḥabl al-mushāti" means their gathering place; "ḥabl" of sand is what is long and massive. As for "jabal" (mountain), its meaning is their path—where the foot-travelers tread. As for his saying: "He remained standing until the sun set and the yellowness had mostly disappeared until the disk vanished" (fa-lam yazal wāqifan ḥattā gharabat al-shams wa-dhahabat al-ṣufrah qalīlan ḥattā ghāba al-qurṣ)—this is how it appears in all copies, and al-Qāḍī transmitted it thus from all copies. He said: "It was said: perhaps the correct reading is 'when the disk vanished' (ḥīna ghāba al-qurṣ)." This is al-Qāḍī's statement. Yet it is possible that the wording is literal, and his saying "until the disk vanished" is an explanation of his saying "the sun set and the yellowness disappeared"—for this (i.e., "sunset") is used metaphorically for the vanishing of most of the disk, so he removed that ambiguity by saying "until the disk vanished." And Allāh knows best.

His saying: "And he seated Usāmah behind him" (wa-ardafa Usāmah khalfahu)—in this is the permissibility of riding double (al-irdāf) when the mount is capable, and the ḥadīths have concurred upon it. His saying: "And he had tightened the reins of al-Qaṣwāʾ (his she-camel) until her head touched the front of his saddle" (wa-qad shannaqa lil-Qaṣwāʾ al-zimām ḥattā inna raʾsahā layuṣību mawrik raḥlih)—the meaning of "shannaqa" is to draw together and tighten, with the nūn ungeminated. "Mawrik al-rah" (the saddle's front pommel area)—al-Jawharī said: Abū ʿUbayd said: "al-mawrik" and "al-mawrikah" (with fatḥah on the mīm and kasrah on the rāʾ) is the place where the rider bends his leg upon it, in front of the saddle's middle, when he tires of riding. Al-Qāḍī recorded it with fatḥah on the rāʾ, and he said: "It is a piece of leather upon which the rider sits, placed at the front of the saddle, like a small cushion." In this is the recommendation of gentleness (al-rifq) in travel by the rider toward the walkers and toward the owners of weak mounts. His saying: "And he gestured with his hand: 'Tranquility, tranquility' (al-sakīnah, al-sakīnah)"—twice, in the accusative (manṣūb), meaning "adhere to tranquility," which is gentleness and composure. In this is that tranquility in the departure (al-dafʿ) from ʿArafāt is a Sunnah; when a gap appears, one may hasten, as established in the other ḥadīth.

His saying: "Whenever he came to a sand-hill (ḥabl) among the sand-hills, he loosened the reins slightly until she climbed, until he reached Muzdalifah" (kullamā atā ḥablan min al-ḥibāl arkha lahā qalīlan ḥattā taṣʿada ḥattā atā al-Muzdalifah)—"al-ḥibāl" here is with the unpointed ḥāʾ, kasrah, plural of "ḥabl," which is a gentle, elevated mound of massive sand. His saying "until she climbed" (ḥattā taṣʿada) is with fatḥah on the second-person feminine yaʾ and its ḍammah; one says "ṣaʿida fī al-ḥabl" and "aṣʿada." From it is His saying (Exalted): «When you were climbing» (idh taṣʿadūn) [Q. 3:153]. As for Muzdalifah, it is well-known; it was named thus from "al-tazalluf" and "al-izdilāf," which is drawing near (al-taqarrub), because when the pilgrims depart from ʿArafāt, they draw near to it (yazdalifūna ilayhā), approaching [God]. It was also said: it was named thus because people come to it in a "zulf" of the night, i.e., its hours. It is also called "Jamʿ" (with fatḥah on the jīm and sukūn on the mīm), named thus for the gathering of people therein. Know that all of Muzdalifah is within the Sacred Precinct (al-Ḥaram). Al-Azraqī said in his History of Mecca, as did al-Māwardī, our companions in the school's books, and others: "The boundary of Muzdalifah is between the two defiles of ʿArafāt (maʾzimay ʿArafah) and the Valley of Muḥassir (Wādī Muḥassir), and the two boundaries themselves are not part of it. All those ravines and mountains within the aforementioned boundary are included in Muzdalifah."

His saying: "Until he reached Muzdalifah, and prayed there the Maghrib and ʿIshāʾ with one adhān and two iqāmahs, and he did not perform supererogatory prayers (tasbīḥ) between them"—in this are several benefits. Among them: the Sunnah for one departing from ʿArafāt is to delay the Maghrib until the time of ʿIshāʾ, and this delay should be with the intention of combining (al-jamʿ); then he combines both prayers at Muzdalifah in the time of ʿIshāʾ. This is a matter of consensus (mujmaʿ ʿalayh). However, the school of Abū Ḥanīfah and a group is that he combines due to the ritual (al-nusuk), and it is permissible for the people of Mecca, Muzdalifah, Minā, and others. The correct view according to our companions is that it is a combination due to travel (al-safar), so it is only permissible for a traveler traveling a distance that reaches the distance of shortening (qasr)—which is two stages (marḥalatān) of moderate travel. Al-Shāfiʿī has a weak opinion that combining is permissible in every travel, even if short. Some of our companions said: "This combination is due to the ritual, as Abū Ḥanīfah said." And Allāh knows best. Our companions said: "If he combines both prayers in the time of Maghrib in the land of ʿArafāt, or on the road, or in..."

chapters.title_en: The Rites of Muzdalifah: Combining Prayers, Overnight Stay, and the Standing at al-Mashʿar al-Ḥarām
chapters.arabic_text:
موضع آخر وصلى كل واحدة في وقتها جاز جميع ذلك لكنه خلاف الأفضل هذا مذهبنا

وبه قال جماعات من الصحابة والتابعين وقاله الأوزاعي وأبو يوسف وأشهب

وفقهاء أصحاب الحديث وقال أبو حنيفة وغيره من الكوفيين يشترط أن يصليهما

بالمزدلفة ولا يجوز قبلها وقال مالك لا يجوز أن يصليهما قبل المزدلفة إلا

من به أو بدابته عذرفلة أن يصليهما قبل المزدلفة بشرط كونه بعد مغيب الشفق

ومنها أن يصلي الصلاتين
# 
# في وقت الثانية بأذان للأولى وإقامتين لكل واحدة إقامة وهذا هو الصحيح

عند أصحابنا وبه قال أحمد بن حنبل وأبو ثور وعبد الملك الماجشون المالكي

والطحاوي الحنفي وقال مالك يؤذن ويقيم للأولى ويؤذن ويقيم أيضا للثانية وهو

محكى عن عمر وبن مسعود رضي الله عنهما وقال أبو حنيفة وأبو يوسف أذان واحد

وإقامة واحدة وللشافعي وأحمد قول أنه يصلي كل واحدة بإقامتها بلا أذان وهو

محكي عن القاسم بن محمد وسالم بن عبد الله بن عمر وقال الثوري يصليهما

جميعا بإقامة واحدة وهو يحكي أيضا عن بن عمر والله أعلم وأما قوله (لم يسبح

بينهما) فمعناه لم يصل بينهما نافلة والنافلة تسمى سبحة لاشتمالها على

التسبيح ففيه الموالاة بين الصلاتين المجموعتين  ولا خلاف في هذا لكن

اختلفوا هل هو شرط للجمع أم لا والصحيح عندنا أنه ليس بشرط بل هو سنة

مستحبة وقال بعض أصحابنا هو شرط أما إذا جمع بينهما في وقت الأولى

فالموالاة شرط بلا خلاف قوله (ثم اضطجع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم حتى

طلع الفجر فصلى الفجر حين تبين له الصبح بأذان وإقامة) في هذا الفصل مسائل

إحداها أن المبيت بمزدلفة ليلة النحر بعد الدفع من عرفات نسك وهذا مجمع

عليه لكن اختلف العلماء هل هو واجب أم ركن أم سنة والصحيح من قولي الشافعي

أنه واجب لو تركه أثم وصح حجه ولزمه دم والثاني أنه سنة لا إثم في تركه ولا

يجب فيه دم ولكن يستحب وقال جماعة من أصحابنا هو ركن لا يصح الحج إلا به

كالوقوف بعرفات قاله من أصحابنا بن بنت الشافعي وأبو بكر محمد بن إسحاق بن

خزيمة وقاله خمسة من أئمة التابعين وهم علقمة والأسود والشعبي والنخعي

والحسن البصري والله أعلم والسنة أن يبقى بالمزدلفة حتى يصلي بها الصبح إلا

الضعفة فالسنة لهم الدفع قبل الفجر كما سيأتي في موضعه إن شاء الله تعالى

وفي أقل المجزي من هذا المبيت ثلاثة أقوال عندنا الصحيح ساعة في النصف

الثاني من الليل والثاني ساعة في النصف الثاني أو بعد الفجر قبل طلوع الشمس

والثالث معظم الليل والله أعلم المسألة الثانية السنة أن يبالغ بتقديم صلاة

الصبح في هذا الموضع ويتأكد التبكير بها في هذا اليوم أكثر من تأكده في

سائر السنة للاقتداء برسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ولأن وظائف هذا
# 
# اليوم كثيرة فسن المبالغة بالتبكير بالصبح ليتسع الوقت للوظائف الثالثة

يسن الأذان والإقامة لهذه الصلاة وكذلك غيرها من صلوات المسافر وقد تظاهرت

الأحاديث الصحيحة بالأذان لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في السفر كما في

الحضر والله أعلم قوله (ثم ركب القصواء حتى أتى المشعر الحرام فاستقبل

القبلة فدعاه وكبره وهلله ووحده فلم يزل واقفا حتى أسفر جدا ودفع قبل أن

تطلع الشمس) أما القصواء فسبق في أول الباب بيانها وأما قوله ثم ركب ففيه

أن السنة الركوب وأنه أفضل من المشي وقد سبق بيانه مرات وبيان الخلاف فيه

وأما المشعر الحرام فبفتح الميم هذا هو الصحيح وبه جاء القرآن وتظاهرت به

روايات الحديث ويقال أيضا بكسر الميم والمراد به هنا قزح بضم القاف وفتح

الزاي وبحاء مهملة وهو جبل معروف في المزدلفة وهذا الحديث حجة الفقهاء في

أن المشعر الحرام هو قزح وقال جماهير المفسرين وأهل السير والحديث المشعر

الحرام جميع المزدلفة وأما قوله فاستقبل القبلة يعني الكعبة فدعاه إلى آخره

فيه أن الوقوف على قزح من مناسك الحج وهذا لاخلاف فيه لكن اختلفوا في وقت

الدفع منه فقال بن مسعود وبن عمر وأبو حنيفة والشافعي وجماهير العلماء لا

يزال واقفا فيه يدعو ويذكر حتى يسفر الصبح جدا كما في هذا الحديث وقال مالك

يدفع منه قبل الإسفار والله أعلم وقوله (أسفر جدا) الضمير في أسفر يعود إلى

الفجر المذكور أولا وقوله (جدا) بكسر الجيم أي إسفارا بليغا قوله في صفة

الفضل بن عباس (أبيض وسيما) أي حسنا قوله (مرت به ظعن يجرين) الظعن بضم

الظاء والعين ويجوز إسكان العين جميع ظعينة كسفينة وسفن وأصل الظعينة

البعير الذي عليه امرأة ثم تسمى به المرأة مجازا لملابستها البعير كما أن

الرواية أصلها الجمل الذي
# 
# يحمل الماء ثم تسمى به القربة لما ذكرناه وقوله يجرين بفتح الياء قوله

(فطفق الفضل ينظر إليهن فوضع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يده على وجه

الفضل) فيه الحث على غض البصر عن الأجنبيات وغضهن عن الرجال الأجانب وهذا

معنى قوله وكان أبيض وسيما حسن الشعر يعني أنه بصفة من تفتتن النساء به

لحسنه وفي رواية الترمذي وغيره في هذا الحديث أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ج-م-ع (j-m-ʿ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To bring together, unite, or combine disparate elements into a single whole; the core sense is aggregation (ḍamm) of parts.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In legal-theological usage, denotes the ritual conjoining of two obligatory prayers (jamʿ bayn al-ṣalātayn) within one time-frame, a dispensation (rukḥṣah) rooted in divine facilitation.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) for physical gathering; metaphorical (majāz) for temporal merging of worship acts, where time becomes the "container" of the rite.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clause (al-Sharṭ wa al-Jawāb) — The particle "law" (لو) introduces a hypothetical condition whose apodosis is governed by the protasis, as in "لو تركه أثم" (if he abandons it, he sins), requiring precise modal alignment.
chapters.translation:
I say: Another position—that he prays each of the two prayers within its own time—all of this is permissible, yet it contravenes the superior practice (al-afḍal). This is our school (madhhab).

This was held by numerous groups among the Companions (al-Ṣaḥābah) and the Followers (al-Tābiʿīn), and it was stated by al-Awzāʿī, Abū Yūsuf, and Ashhab, as well as the jurists of the Hadith scholars. Abū Ḥanīfah and others among the Kūfans said: It is a condition that he pray both of them at Muzdalifah, and it is not permissible before it. Mālik said: It is not permissible to pray both before Muzdalifah except for one who has an excuse affecting himself or his mount; then he may pray them before Muzdalifah, on the condition that this occurs after the disappearance of the twilight (ghasaq al-shafaq).

Among these matters is that he prays the two prayers in the time of the second one, with one call to prayer (adhān) for the first and two iqāmahs—one for each prayer. This is the correct view (al-ṣaḥīḥ) in our school. It was also held by Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal, Abū Thawr, ʿAbd al-Malik al-Mājishūn al-Mālikī, and al-Ṭaḥāwī al-Ḥanafī. Mālik said: He gives the adhān and iqāmah for the first, and gives the adhān and iqāmah also for the second. This is reported from ʿUmar and Ibn Masʿūd, may God be pleased with them both. Abū Ḥanīfah and Abū Yūsuf said: One adhān and one iqāmah. There is a saying from al-Shāfiʿī and Aḥmad that he prays each one with its own iqāmah, without an adhān—this is reported from al-Qāsim ibn Muḥammad and Sālim ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar. Al-Thawrī said: He prays both together with a single iqāmah—this is also reported from Ibn ʿUmar. And God knows best.

As for his statement (peace be upon him): "He did not pray supererogatory (sabbaḥa) between them"—its meaning is that he did not pray a voluntary prayer (nāfilah) between them. The voluntary prayer is called a "sabḥah" (glorification) because it encompasses the glorification of God (tasbīḥ). Thus, this indicates the requirement of immediate succession (muwālāh) between the two conjoined prayers. There is no disagreement on this point, but they differed as to whether it is a condition (sharṭ) for the combining (jamʿ) or not. The correct view in our school is that it is not a condition, but rather a recommended practice (sunnah mustaḥabbah). Some of our companions said it is a condition. However, if he combines them in the time of the first prayer, then immediate succession is a condition without disagreement.

His statement: "Then the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) lay down until dawn broke, then he prayed the dawn prayer (al-Fajr) when the morning became clear to him, with an adhān and iqāmah"—in this section there are several issues.

The first: That spending the night at Muzdalifah on the night of the Sacrifice (laylat al-Naḥr), after the departure (al-dafʿ) from ʿArafāt, is a rite (nusuk). This is a matter of consensus (ijmāʿ). However, the scholars differed as to whether it is obligatory (wājib), a pillar (rukn), or a sunnah. The correct of the two sayings of al-Shāfiʿī is that it is obligatory: if one abandons it, he sins, yet his pilgrimage (ḥajj) is valid, and a blood-offering (dam) is incumbent upon him. The second saying is that it is a sunnah—no sin in abandoning it, no blood-offering required, but it is recommended. A group of our companions said: It is a pillar (rukn); the pilgrimage is not valid without it, like the standing at ʿArafāt. This was stated by Ibn Bint al-Shāfiʿī and Abū Bakr Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq ibn Khuzaymah from our companions, and it was stated by five of the leading Followers: ʿAlqamah, al-Aswad, al-Shaʿbī, al-Nakhaʿī, and al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī. And God knows best.

The sunnah is to remain at Muzdalifah until he prays the dawn prayer there, except for the weak (al-ḍuʿafāʾ); for them, the sunnah is to depart before dawn, as will come in its proper place, God willing. Regarding the minimum that suffices of this overnight stay, there are three sayings in our school. The correct one: a moment in the second half of the night. The second: a moment in the second half, or after dawn before sunrise. The third: the greater part of the night. And God knows best.

The second issue: The sunnah is to be emphatic in advancing the dawn prayer at this place, and the emphasis on performing it early on this day is stronger than its emphasis on other days of the year—following the example of the Messenger of God (peace be upon him), and because the duties (waẓāʾif) of this day are numerous. Thus, it is legislated to be emphatic in performing the dawn prayer early, so that time may be ample for the duties.

The third: It is sunnah to give the adhān and iqāmah for this prayer, and likewise for other prayers of the traveler. The authentic hadiths have concurred (tawātur) on the adhān for the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) during travel, just as in residence. And God knows best.

His statement: "Then he rode al-Qaṣwāʾ until he came to al-Mashʿar al-Ḥarām, and he faced the qiblah, and he supplicated to Him, and magnified Him (kabbara), and hallowed Him (hallala), and declared His oneness (waḥḥada), and he remained standing until the morning was very bright (asfara jiddan), and he departed before the sun rose."

As for al-Qaṣwāʾ, its explanation has preceded at the beginning of the chapter. As for his statement "then he rode"—in it is that the sunnah is to ride, and that it is superior to walking; its explanation and the disagreement therein have preceded multiple times.

As for al-Mashʿar al-Ḥarām—it is with the opening (fatḥ) of the mīm; this is the correct pronunciation, and with it the Qurʾān came, and the hadith transmissions concurred. It is also said with the kasrah of the mīm. What is meant here is Quzaḥ—with the ḍammah of the qāf, the fatḥah of the zāy, and an unpointed ḥāʾ—which is a well-known mountain in Muzdalifah. This hadith is the proof of the jurists that al-Mashʿar al-Ḥarām is Quzaḥ. The majority of the exegetes (al-mufassirūn), the scholars of biography (ahl al-siyar), and hadith scholars said: al-Mashʿar al-Ḥarām is all of Muzdalifah.

As for his statement "he faced the qiblah"—meaning the Kaʿbah—then "he supplicated" to the end: in it is that the standing at Quzaḥ is among the rites of the pilgrimage. There is no disagreement on this, but they differed regarding the time of departure from it. Ibn Masʿūd, Ibn ʿUmar, Abū Ḥanīfah, al-Shāfiʿī, and the majority of scholars said: He continues standing there, supplicating and remembering, until the morning is very bright (yusfir al-ṣubḥ jiddan), as in this hadith. Mālik said: He departs from it before the brightening (al-isfār). And God knows best.

His statement "asfara jiddan" (very bright)—the pronoun in "asfara" refers back to the dawn (al-fajr) mentioned earlier. His statement "jiddan" is with the kasrah of the jīm, meaning an intense brightening (isfāran balīghan).

His statement describing al-Faḍl ibn al-ʿAbbās: "white and comely (wasiym)"—meaning handsome. His statement: "there passed by him some women on camels (ẓaʿāʾin) hastening (yajrīn)"—al-ẓaʿāʾin is with the ḍammah of the ẓāʾ and the ʿayn, and it is permissible to still the ʿayn; it is the plural of ẓaʿīnah, like safīnah and sufun. The origin of ẓaʿīnah is the camel upon which a woman rides; then the woman herself is called by it metaphorically (majāzan), due to her close association with the camel—just as al-rāwiyah originally is the camel that carries water, then the water-skin is called by it, for the reason we have mentioned. His statement "yajrīn" is with the fatḥah of the yāʾ.

His statement: "Then al-Faḍl began to look at them, and the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) placed his hand on the face of al-Faḍl"—in it is the urging to lower the gaze (ghaḍḍ al-baṣar) from foreign women, and for them to lower their gaze from foreign men. This is the meaning of his statement: "He was white and comely, with beautiful hair"—meaning he was of the description of one whom women are tempted by, due to his beauty. In the narration of al-Tirmidhī and others in this hadith, the Prophet (peace be upon him)...

chapters.title_en: The Prophet's Actions at Minā: Stoning, Sacrifice, and Related Rulings
chapters.arabic_text:
لوى عنق الفضل فقال له العباس لويت عنق بن عمك قال رأيت شابا وشابة فلم آمن

الشيطان عليهما فهذا يدل على أن وضعه صلى الله عليه وسلم يده على  وجه الفضل

كان لدفع الفتنة عنه وعنها وفيه أن من رأى منكرا وأمكنه إزالته بيده لزمه

إزالته فإن قال بلسانه ولم ينكف المقول له وأمكنه بيده أثم ما دام مقتصرا

على اللسان والله أعلم قوله (حتى أتى بطن محسر فحرك قليلا) أما محسر فبضم

الميم وفتح الحاء وكسر السين المشددة المهملتين سمي بذلك لأن فيل أصحاب

الفيل حصر فيه أي أعي فيه وكل منه قوله تعالى ينقلب إليك البصر خاسئا وهو

حسير وأما قوله فحرك قليلا فهي سنة من سنن السير في ذلك الموضع قال أصحابنا

يسرع الماشي ويحرك الراكب دابته في وادي محسر ويكون ذلك قدر رمية حجر والله

أعلم قوله (ثم سلك الطريق الوسطى التي تخرج على الجمرة الكبرى حتى أتى

الجمرة التي عند الشجرة فرماها بسبع حصيات يكبر مع كل حصاة منها حصى الخذف

رمى من بطن الوادي) أما قوله سلك الطريق الوسطى ففيه أن سلوك هذا الطريق في

الرجوع من عرفات سنة وهو غير الطريق الذي ذهب فيه إلى عرفات وهذا معنى قول

أصحابنا يذهب إلى عرفات في طريق ضب ويرجع في طريق المأزمين ليخالف الطريق

تفاؤلا بتغير الحال كما فعل النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في دخول مكة حين

دخلها من
# 
# الثنية العليا وخرج من الثنية السفلى وخرج إلى العيد في طريق ورجع في

طريق آخر وحول رداءه في الاستسقاء وأما الجمرة الكبرى فهي جمرة العقبة وهي

التي عند الشجرة وفيه أن السنة للحاج إذا دفع من مزدلفة فوصل منى أن يبدأ

بجمرة العقبة ولا يفعل شيئا قبل رميها ويكون ذلك قبل نزوله وفيه أن الرمي

بسبع حصيات وأن قدرهن بقدر حصى الخذف وهو نحو حبة الباقلاء وينبغي ألا يكون

أكبر ولا أصغر فإن كان أكبر أو أصغر أجزأه بشرط كونها حجرا ولا يجوز عند

الشافعي والجمهور الرمي بالكحل والزرنيخ والذهب والفضة وغير ذلك مما لا

يسمى حجرا وجوزه أبو حنيفة بكل ما كان من أجزاء الأرض وفيه أنه يسن التكبير

مع كل حصاة وفيه  أنه يجب التفريق بين الحصيات فيرميهن واحدة واحدة فإن رمى

السبعة رمية واحدة حسب ذلك كله حصاة واحدة عندنا وعند الأكثرين وموضع

الدلالة لهذه المسألة يكبر مع كل حصاة فهذا تصريح بأنه رمى كل حصاة وحدها

مع قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم في الحديث الآتي بعد هذا في أحاديث الرمي

لتأخذوا عني مناسككم وفيه أن السنة أن يقف للرمي في بطن الوادي بحيث تكون

منى وعرفات والمزدلفة عن يمينه ومكة عن يساره وهذا هو الصحيح الذي جاءت به

الأحاديث الصحيحة وقيل يقف مستقبل الكعبة وكيفما رمى أجزأه بحيث يسمى رميا

بما يسمى حجرا والله أعلم وأما حكم الرمي فالمشروع منه يوم النحر رمي جمرة

العقبة لا غير بإجماع المسلمين وهو نسك بإجماعهم ومذهبنا أنه واجب ليس بركن

فإن تركه حتى فاتته أيام الرمي عصى ولزمه دم وصح حجه وقال مالك يفسد حجه

ويجب رميها بسبع حصيات فلو بقيت منهن واحدة لم تكفه الست وأما قوله فرماها

بسبع حصيات يكبر مع كل حصاة منها حصى الخذف فهكذا هو في النسخ وكذا نقله

القاضي عياض عن معظم النسخ قال وصوابه مثل حصى الخذف قال وكذلك رواه غير

مسلم وكذا رواه بعض رواة مسلم هذا كلام القاضي قلت والذي في النسخ من غير

لفظة مثل هو الصواب بل لا يتجه غيره ولا يتم الكلام الا كذلك ويكون قوله

حصى الخذف متعلقا بحصيات أي رماها بسبع حصيات حصى الخذف يكبر مع كل حصاة

فحصى الخذف متصل بحصيات واعترض بينهما يكبر مع كل حصاة وهذا هو الصواب

والله أعلم قوله (ثم انصرف إلى
# 
# النحر فنحر ثلاثا وستين بيده ثم أعطى عليا فنحر ما غبر وأشركه في هديه)

هكذا هو في النسخ ثلاثا وستين بيده وكذا نقله القاضي عن جميع الرواة سوى بن

ماهان فإنه رواه بدنة قال وكلامه صواب والأول أصوب قلت وكلاهما حري فنحر

ثلاثا وستين بدنة بيده قال القاضي فيه دليل على أن المنحر موضع معين من منى

وحيث ذبح منها أو من  الحرم أجزأه وفيه استحباب تكثير الهدي وكان هدي النبي

صلى الله عليه وسلم في تلك السنة مائة بدنة وفيه استحباب ذبح المهدي هديه

بنفسه وجواز الاستنابة فيه وذلك جائز بالإجماع إذا كان النائب مسلما ويجوز

عندنا أن يكون النائب كافرا كتابيا بشرط أن ينوي صاحب الهدي عند دفعه إليه

أو عند ذبحه وقوله ما غبر أي ما بقي وفيه استحباب تعجيل ذبح الهدايا وإن

كانت كثيرة في يوم النحر ولا يؤخر بعضها إلى أيام التشريق وأما قوله وأشركه

في هديه فظاهره أنه شاركه في نفس الهدي قال القاضي عياض وعندي أنه لم يكن

تشريكا حقيقة بل أعطاه قدرا يذبحه والظاهر أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم نحر

البدن التي جاءت معه من المدينة وكانت ثلاثا وستين كما جاء في رواية

الترمذي وأعطى عليا البدن التي جاءت معه من اليمين وهي تمام المائة والله

أعلم قوله (أمر من كل بدنة ببضعة فجعلت في قدر فطبخت فأكلا من لحمها وشربا

من مرقها) البضعة بفتح الباء لا غير وهي القطعة من اللحم وفيه استحباب
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ل-و-ى (l-w-y)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To bend, twist, or turn something from its natural course; also used for turning the neck.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In prophetic contexts, signifies a deliberate physical action to avert harm or temptation (fitnah), not mere gesture.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) here—physical bending of the neck; metaphorical extension implies diverting attention or preventing approach.
- Sībawayh Rule: ʿAṭf al-Bayān (Appositional Clarification) — The phrase "حصى الخذف" functions as an appositive clarifying the nature of the seven pebbles, with an intervening clause permissible.
chapters.translation:
I say: He (the Prophet, peace be upon him) bent the neck of al-Faḍl, whereupon al-ʿAbbās said to him, "You bent the neck of your cousin's son." He replied, "I saw a young man and a young woman, and I did not trust Satan against them." This indicates that the Prophet's (peace be upon him) placing his hand on al-Faḍl's face was to repel temptation (fitnah) from him and from her. In this [hadith] is [the ruling] that whoever witnesses a wrong (munkar) and is able to remove it with his hand, it is obligatory upon him to remove it. If he speaks with his tongue but the addressed person does not desist, and he is able [to act] with his hand, he sins as long as he confines himself to the tongue. And Allah knows best.

His saying (until he came to Baṭn Muḥassir and urged [his mount] slightly): As for Muḥassir, it is with ḍammah on the mīm, fatḥah on the ḥāʾ, and kasrah on the shīn with tashdīd, both unpointed letters. It was so named because the elephant of the Companions of the Elephant was constrained (ḥuṣira) there, i.e., exhausted therein. And from it is the saying of Allah the Exalted: {«يَنْقَلِبْ إِلَيْكَ الْبَصَرُ خَاسِئًا وَهُوَ حَسِيرٌ»} (The sight turns back to you humiliated and weary) (Al-Mulk: 4). As for his saying "and urged slightly," it is a Sunnah among the practices of travel in that location. Our companions said: The pedestrian quickens his pace, and the rider urges his mount in the valley of Muḥassir, and that should be approximately the distance of a stone's throw. And Allah knows best.

His saying (then he took the middle road that exits onto the Grand Jamrah until he reached the Jamrah by the tree, and he stoned it with seven pebbles, saying the takbīr with each pebble—pebbles of the size of khadhf—throwing from the bottom of the valley): As for his saying "he took the middle road," in it is [the ruling] that taking this road upon returning from ʿArafāt is a Sunnah, and it is not the road by which he went to ʿArafāt. This is the meaning of our companions' statement: One goes to ʿArafāt via the road of Ḍabb and returns via the road of al-Maʾzamayn, to differ in the route, seeking a good omen of changed circumstances—just as the Prophet (peace be upon him) did upon entering Mecca when he entered from the upper pass and exited from the lower pass, and went out to the ʿĪd prayer by one road and returned by another, and turned his cloak around during the prayer for rain (istisqāʾ).

As for the Grand Jamrah, it is Jamrat al-ʿAqabah, which is the one by the tree. In it is [the ruling] that the Sunnah for the pilgrim, when he departs from Muzdalifah and reaches Minā, is to begin with Jamrat al-ʿAqabah and not do anything before stoning it, and that this be before his descent [from his mount]. In it is [the ruling] that the stoning is with seven pebbles, and that their size is that of khadhf pebbles, which is approximately the size of a broad bean (bāqillāʾ). It is recommended that they be neither larger nor smaller. If they are larger or smaller, it suffices him, provided they are stones. According to al-Shāfiʿī and the majority, it is not permissible to stone with kohl (kuḥl), arsenic (zirnīkh), gold, silver, or anything else not called a stone. Abū Ḥanīfah permitted it with anything that is part of the earth's substances.

In it is [the ruling] that the takbīr with each pebble is Sunnah. In it is [the ruling] that it is obligatory to separate the pebbles, throwing them one by one. If one throws all seven in a single throw, that counts as only one pebble in our view and that of the majority. The evidence for this matter is his saying "saying the takbīr with each pebble"—this is an explicit statement that he threw each pebble individually, along with the Prophet's (peace be upon him) saying in the hadith that follows this one among the hadiths on stoning: "Take your rites from me" (khudhū ʿannī manāsikakum).

In it is [the ruling] that the Sunnah is to stand for the stoning in the bottom of the valley such that Minā, ʿArafāt, and Muzdalifah are to his right, and Mecca to his left. This is the correct [view] that the authentic hadiths have conveyed. It was also said: He stands facing the Kaʿbah. However he stones, it suffices him, as long as it is called "stoning" with what is called a stone. And Allah knows best.

As for the ruling on stoning: What is legislated on the Day of Sacrifice (Yawm al-Naḥr) is stoning Jamrat al-ʿAqabah only, by consensus of the Muslims. It is a ritual (nusuk) by their consensus. In our school, it is obligatory (wājib), not a pillar (rukn). If one abandons it until the days of stoning have passed, he has sinned, and a blood [sacrifice] (dam) is incumbent upon him, yet his Hajj is valid. Mālik said: His Hajj is corrupted. It is obligatory to stone it with seven pebbles; if one of them remains [unthrown], the six do not suffice him.

As for his saying "he stoned it with seven pebbles, saying the takbīr with each pebble—pebbles of khadhf": Thus it is in the manuscripts, and thus al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ transmitted from most manuscripts. He said: The correct [reading] is "like the pebbles of khadhf" (mithl ḥaṣā al-khadhf). He said: Likewise, other than Muslim narrated it, and so did some of Muslim's narrators. This is al-Qāḍī's statement. I say: What is in the manuscripts without the word "like" (mithl) is the correct [reading]; indeed, nothing else is plausible, and the speech is not complete except thus. His saying "pebbles of khadhf" is attached to "pebbles" (ḥaṣayāt), i.e., he stoned it with seven pebbles—pebbles of khadhf—saying the takbīr with each pebble. Thus "pebbles of khadhf" is connected to "pebbles," and between them is interposed "saying the takbīr with each pebble." This is the correct [reading]. And Allah knows best.

His saying (then he turned to the sacrifice and slaughtered sixty-three with his own hand, then gave [the rest] to ʿAlī, who slaughtered what remained, and he shared him in his sacrificial animals (hady)): Thus it is in the manuscripts: "sixty-three with his own hand." Al-Qāḍī transmitted this from all the narrators except Ibn Māhān, who narrated it as "a camel" (badanah). He said: His speech is correct, but the first is more accurate. I say: Both are plausible—he slaughtered sixty-three camels with his own hand. Al-Qāḍī said: In it is evidence that the place of slaughter is a specific location in Minā, and wherever one slaughters from it or from the Sanctuary (al-Ḥaram), it suffices him. In it is the recommendation of multiplying the sacrificial animals; the Prophet's (peace be upon him) hady in that year was one hundred camels. In it is the recommendation that the one offering the hady slaughter it himself, and the permissibility of deputizing another in it. That is permissible by consensus if the deputy is a Muslim. In our view, it is permissible for the deputy to be a Kitābī (People of the Book) infidel, on condition that the owner of the hady intends [the sacrifice] when handing it to him or at the time of its slaughter.

His saying "what remained" (mā ghabara) means what was left. In it is the recommendation of hastening the slaughter of the sacrificial animals, even if numerous, on the Day of Sacrifice, and not delaying some of them to the days of Tashrīq. As for his saying "and he shared him in his hady," its apparent meaning is that he shared with him in the very hady. Al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ said: In my view, it was not a real sharing, but rather he gave him a portion to slaughter. The apparent [truth] is that the Prophet (peace be upon him) slaughtered the camels that came with him from Madīnah, which were sixty-three, as came in al-Tirmidhī's narration, and he gave ʿAlī the camels that came with him from Yemen, which completed the hundred. And Allah knows best.

His saying (he commanded that from each camel a piece (baḍʿah) be taken, placed in a pot, cooked, and they ate from its meat and drank from its broth): "al-baḍʿah" is with fatḥah on the bāʾ only, and it is a piece of meat. In it is the recommendation...

chapters.title_en: Eating from Voluntary Hady and Udhiyyah, and the Tawaf of Ifadah (Section 501)
chapters.arabic_text:
الأكل من هدي التطوع وأضحيته قال العلماء لما كان الأكل من كل واحدة سنة

وفي الأكل من كل واحدة من المائة منفردة كلفة جعلت في قدر ليكون آكلا من

مرق الجميع الذي فيه جزء من كل واحدة ويأكل من اللحم المجتمع في المرق ما

تيسر وأجمع العلماء على أن الأكل من هدي التطوع وأضحيته سنة ليس بواجب قوله

(ثم ركب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فأفاض إلى البيت فصلى بمكة الظهر)

هذا الطواف هو طواف الإفاضة وهو ركن من أركان الحج بإجماع المسلمين وأول

وقته عندنا من نصف ليلة النحر وأفضله بعد رمي جمرة العقبة وذبح الهدي

والحلق ويكون ذلك ضحوة يوم النحر ويجوز
# 
# في جميع يوم النحر بلا كراهة ويكره تأخيره عنه بلا عذر وتأخيره عن أيام

التشريق أشد كراهة ولا يحرم تأخيره سنين متطاولة ولا آخر لوقته بل يصح ما

دام الإنسان حيا وشرطه أن يكون  بعد الوقوف بعرفات حتى لو طاف للإفاضة بعد

نصف ليلة النحر قبل الوقوف ثم أسرع إلى عرفات فوقف قبل الفجر لم يصح طوافه

لأنه قدمه على الوقوف واتفق العلماء على أنه لا يشرع في طواف الإفاضة رمل

ولا اضطباع إذا كان قد رمل واضطبع عقب طواف القدوم ولو طاف بنية الوداع أو

القدوم أو التطوع وعليه طواف إفاضة وقع عن طواف الإفاضة بلا خلاف عندنا نص

عليه الشافعي واتفق الأصحاب عليه كما لو كان عليه حجة الإسلام فحج بنية

قضاء أو نذر أو تطوع فإنه يقع عن حجة الإسلام وقال أبو حنيفة وأكثر العلماء

لا يجزئ طواف الإفاضة بنية غيره واعلم أن طواف الإفاضة له أسماء فيقال أيضا

طواف الزيارة وطواف الفرض والركن وسماه بعض أصحابنا طواف الصدر وأنكره

الجمهور قالوا وإنما طواف الصدر طواف الوداع والله أعلم وفي هذا الحديث

استحباب الركوب في الذهاب من منى إلى مكة ومن مكة إلى منى ونحو ذلك من

مناسك الحج وقد ذكرنا قبل هذا مرات المسألة وبينا أن الصحيح استحباب الركوب

وأن من أصحابنا من استحب المشي هناك وقوله (فأفاض إلى البيت فصلى الظهر)

فيه محذوف تقديره فأفاض فطاف بالبيت طواف الإفاضة ثم صلى الظهر فحذف ذكر

الطواف لدلالة الكلام عليه وأما قوله فصلى بمكة الظهر فقد ذكر مسلم بعد هذا

في أحاديث طواف الإفاضة من حديث بن عمر رضي الله عنهما أن النبي صلى الله

عليه وسلم أفاض يوم النحر فصلى الظهر بمنى ووجه الجمع بينهما أنه صلى الله

عليه وسلم طاف للإفاضة قبل الزوال ثم صلى الظهر بمكة في أول وقتها ثم رجع

إلى منى فصلى بها الظهر مرة أخرى بأصحابه حين سألوه ذلك فيكون متنفلا

بالظهر الثانية التي بمنى وهذا كما ثبت في الصحيحين في صلاته صلى الله عليه

وسلم ببطن نخل أحد أنواع صلاة الخوف فإنه صلى الله عليه وسلم صلى بطائفة من

أصحابه الصلاة بكمالها وسلم بهم ثم صلى بالطائفة الأخرى تلك الصلاة مرة

أخرى فكانت له  صلاتان ولهم صلاة وأما الحديث الوارد عن عائشة وغيرها أن

النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أخر الزيارة يوم النحر إلى الليل فمحمول على أنه

عاد للزيارة مع نسائه لا لطواف الإفاضة ولا بد من هذا التأويل للجمع بين

الأحاديث وقد بسطت إيضاح هذا الجواب في شرح المهذب والله أعلم
# 
# قوله (فأتى بني عبد المطلب يسقون على زمزم فقال انزعوا بني عبد المطلب

فلولا أن يغلبكم الناس على سقايتكم لنزعت معكم فناولوه دلوا فشرب منه) أما

قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم انزعوا فبكسر الزاي ومعناه استقوا بالدلاء

وانزعوها بالرشاء وأما قوله فأتى بني عبد المطلب فمعناه أتاهم بعد فراغه من

طواف الإفاضة وقوله يسقون على زمزم معناه يغرفون بالدلاء ويصبونه في الحياض

ونحوها ويسبلونه للناس وقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم لولا أن يغلبكم الناس

لنزعت معكم معناه لولا خوفي أن يعتقد الناس ذلك من مناسك الحج ويزدحمون

عليه بحيث يغلبونكم ويدفعونكم عن الاستقاء لاستقيت معكم لكثرة فضيلة هذا

الاستقاء وفيه فضيلة العمل في هذا الاستقاء واستحباب شرب ماء زمزم وأما

زمزم فهي البئر المشهورة في المسجد الحرام بينها وبين الكعبة ثمان وثلاثون

ذراعا قيل سميت زمزم لكثرة مائها يقال ماء زمزوم وزمزم وزمازم إذا كان

كثيرا وقيل لضم هاجر رضي الله عنها لمائها حين انفجرت وزمها إياه وقيل

لزمزمة جبريل عليه السلام وكلامه عند فجره إياها وقيل إنها غير مشتقة ولها

أسماء أخر ذكرتها في تهذيب اللغات مع نفائس أخرى تتعلق بها منها أن عليا

رضي الله عنه قال خير بئر في الأرض زمزم وشر بئر في الأرض برهوت والله أعلم

قوله (وكانت العرب يدفع بهم أبو سيارة) هو بسين مهملة ثم ياء مثناة تحت

مشددة أي كان يدفع بهم في الجاهلية قوله فلما أجاز رسول الله صلى الله عليه

وسلم من المزدلفة بالمشعر الحرام لم تشك قريش أنه سيقتصر عليه ويكون منزله

ثم فأجاز ولم يعرض له حتى أتى عرفات فنزل أما المشعر فسبق بيانه وأنه
# 
# بفتح الميم على المشهور  وقيل بكسرها وأن قزح الجبل المعروف في المزدلفة

وقيل كل المزدلفة وأوضحنا الخلاف فيه بدلائله وهذا الحديث ظاهر الدلالة في
chapters.anchors:
- Root: أ-ك-ل (ʾ-k-l)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To eat, consume; core sense of ingesting food for nourishment.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In legal context, denotes permissive consumption (ibāḥah) versus obligation (wujūb); here, a recommended act (sunnah).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) eating of meat; metaphorical extension to "partaking" of a collective benefit.
- Root: ف-ي-ض (f-y-ḍ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To flow abundantly, pour forth; of water, to overflow.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In Ḥajj terminology, "Ifāḍah" is the ritual pouring forth from ʿArafāt to Minā, and the subsequent circumambulation (ṭawāf) of the Kaʿbah.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal flowing; metaphorical for the multitudes surging in ritual movement.
- Root: ر-م-ل (r-m-l)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Sand; also, the act of walking briskly with a slight trot, moving the shoulders.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Technical term for the quick-paced circumambulation with shoulder movement, a specific Sunnah in certain ṭawāfs.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal "sand" (ḥaqīqah); metaphorical (majāz) for the brisk gait resembling movement over sand.
- Sībawayh Rule: Taqdīr al-Maḥdhūf (Ellipsis Restoration) — When a verb is omitted but contextually implied, the sentence's syntactic completeness is restored by supplying the missing element, as in "fa-a fāḍa" implying "fa-ṭāfa" (then he circumambulated).
chapters.translation:
I say: The scholars have stated that since eating from each one—whether the voluntary hady or the udhiyyah—is a Sunnah, and since eating from each one of the hundred individually would be a burden, a portion was placed in a cooking pot so that one might eat from the broth of all of them, which contains a part of each one, and eat from the meat gathered in the broth whatever is easy. The scholars are unanimous that eating from the voluntary hady and his udhiyyah is a Sunnah, not an obligation.

His statement (then the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, rode and poured forth (afāḍa) to the House and prayed the noon prayer in Mecca): This ṭawāf is the Ṭawāf al-Ifāḍah, and it is a pillar (rukn) of the Ḥajj by the consensus of the Muslims. Its earliest time, in our school, is from the middle of the night of the Sacrifice (laylat al-naḥr). Its most virtuous time is after stoning the Jamrah of ʿAqabah, slaughtering the hady, and shaving the head, and that occurs in the forenoon of the Day of Sacrifice. It is permissible throughout the entire Day of Sacrifice without any dislike (karāhah). It is disliked to delay it beyond that day without an excuse, and delaying it beyond the Days of Tashrīq is more severely disliked. It is not forbidden to delay it for many years, nor is there a final limit to its time; rather, it remains valid as long as a person is alive. Its condition is that it must be after the standing at ʿArafāt, such that if one performed the Ṭawāf al-Ifāḍah after the middle of the night of Sacrifice before the standing, then hurried to ʿArafāt and stood before dawn, his ṭawāf would not be valid, because he preceded it to the standing. The scholars agree that in the Ṭawāf al-Ifāḍah, neither the brisk walk (ramal) nor the draping of the cloak (iḍṭibāʿ) is prescribed, if one had already performed ramal and iḍṭibāʿ following the Ṭawāf al-Qudūm. If one performs a ṭawāf with the intention of farewell (wadāʿ), arrival (qudūm), or voluntary worship, while the Ṭawāf al-Ifāḍah is incumbent upon him, it counts for the Ṭawāf al-Ifāḍah without dispute in our school; al-Shāfiʿī explicitly stated this, and the companions agreed upon it—just as if one owes the Ḥajj of Islam and performs the pilgrimage with the intention of making up a missed obligation (qaḍāʾ), a vow (nadhr), or voluntary worship, it counts for the Ḥajj of Islam. Abū Ḥanīfah and most scholars said: The Ṭawāf al-Ifāḍah is not sufficient if performed with an intention other than it.

Know that the Ṭawāf al-Ifāḍah has several names: it is also called the Ṭawāf al-Ziyārah (Visitation), the Ṭawāf al-Farḍ (Obligatory), and the Pillar (al-Rukn). Some of our companions called it the Ṭawāf al-Ṣadr (Chest/Departure), but the majority rejected this, saying: The Ṭawāf al-Ṣadr is only the Farewell Ṭawāf. And Allah knows best.

In this ḥadīth, there is the recommendation of riding when going from Minā to Mecca and from Mecca to Minā, and similar rites of the Ḥajj. We have mentioned this issue multiple times before this, and we clarified that the correct view is the recommendation of riding, and that some of our companions recommended walking there.

His statement (then he poured forth to the House and prayed the noon prayer): There is an ellipsis in it; its estimated form is: "Then he poured forth, circumambulated the House with the Ṭawāf al-Ifāḍah, then prayed the noon prayer." The mention of the ṭawāf was omitted due to the context indicating it.

As for his statement (and he prayed the noon prayer in Mecca), Muslim has mentioned after this, in the ḥadīths of the Ṭawāf al-Ifāḍah, from the ḥadīth of Ibn ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with them both, that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, poured forth on the Day of Sacrifice and prayed the noon prayer in Minā. The way to reconcile them is that he, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, performed the Ṭawāf al-Ifāḍah before noon, then prayed the noon prayer in Mecca at its earliest time, then returned to Minā and prayed the noon prayer there a second time with his companions when they asked him to do so. Thus, the second noon prayer in Minā was voluntary for him. This is like what is established in the two Ṣaḥīḥs regarding his prayer, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, in Baṭn Nakhl, one of the types of the Prayer of Fear: he prayed the complete prayer with one group of his companions and gave the salutation with them, then prayed that same prayer a second time with the other group. So he had two prayers, while they had one.

As for the ḥadīth reported from ʿĀʾishah and others that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, delayed the visitation (ziyārah) on the Day of Sacrifice until night, it is interpreted to mean that he returned for the visitation with his wives, not for the Ṭawāf al-Ifāḍah. This interpretation is necessary to reconcile the ḥadīths. I have elaborated this reconciliation in my commentary on al-Muhadhdhab. And Allah knows best.

His statement (then he came to the Banū ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib, who were drawing water at Zamzam, and said: "Draw, O Banū ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib! Were it not that the people would overcome you regarding your watering, I would draw with you." They handed him a bucket, and he drank from it): As for his statement, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, "Draw" (inzāʿū), it is with a kasrah on the zāy, meaning: draw water with buckets, pulling them up by the ropes. As for his statement (then he came to the Banū ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib), its meaning is that he came to them after finishing the Ṭawāf al-Ifāḍah. His statement (who were drawing water at Zamzam) means they were scooping with buckets and pouring it into basins and similar vessels, and letting it flow for the people. His statement, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, (Were it not that the people would overcome you, I would draw with you) means: Were it not for my fear that the people would consider this one of the rites of the Ḥajj and crowd upon it such that they would overcome you and push you away from drawing, I would draw with you, due to the great virtue of this drawing. In this, there is the virtue of working in this drawing, and the recommendation of drinking Zamzam water.

As for Zamzam, it is the well known in the Sacred Mosque, between it and the Kaʿbah is thirty-eight cubits. It is said it was named Zamzam for the abundance of its water; one says "māʾ zamzūm" and "zamzam" and "zamāzim" when it is abundant. It is also said it was named for Hājar, may Allah be pleased with her, pressing (zammahā) the water when it burst forth, and her containing it. It is also said for the murmuring (zamzamah) of Gabriel, peace be upon him, and his speech when he caused it to gush forth. It is also said it is not derived at all. It has other names which I have mentioned in Tahdhīb al-Lughāt, along with other precious points related to it. Among them is that ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "The best well on earth is Zamzam, and the worst well on earth is Barhūt." And Allah knows best.

His statement (and the Arabs used to be driven by Abū Sayyārah): It is with an unpointed sīn, then a doubled yāʾ with a kasrah below—meaning, he used to drive them in the pre-Islamic period (Jāhiliyyah).

His statement (when the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, passed on from Muzdalifah by the Sacred Monument (al-Mashʿar al-Ḥarām), Quraysh did not doubt that he would stop at it and make his abode there. But he passed on and did not stop at it until he came to ʿArafāt and alighted): As for al-Mashʿar, its explanation has preceded—that it is with a fatḥah on the mīm according to the well-known view, and it is said with a kasrah—and that Quzaḥ is the known mountain in Muzdalifah, and it is said it is all of Muzdalifah. We have clarified the disagreement about it with its proofs. This ḥadīth is clearly indicative of this.

chapters.title_en: The Station of Arafat, Muzdalifah, and Mina — Clarifying the Rites of Standing (Wuqūf) and Sacrifice (Nahr)
chapters.arabic_text:
أنه ليس كل المزدلفة وقوله أجاز أي جاوز وقوله ولم يعرض هو بفتح الياء وكسر

الراء ومعنى الحديث أن قريشا كانت قبل الإسلام تقف بالمزدلفة وهي من الحرم

ولا يقفون بعرفات وكان سائر العرب يقفون بعرفات وكانت قريش تقول نحن أهل

الحرم فلا نخرج منه فلما حج النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ووصل المزدلفة

اعتقدوا أنه يقف بالمزدلفة على عادة قريش فجاوز إلى عرفات لقول الله عز وجل

ثم أفيضوا من حيث أفاض الناس أي جمهور الناس فإن من سوى قريش كانوا يقفون

بعرفات ويفيضون منها وأما قوله (فأجاز ولم يعرض له حتى أتى عرفات فنزل)

ففيه مجاز تقديره فأجاز متوجها إلى عرفات حتى قاربها فضربت له القبة بنمرة

قريب من عرفات فنزل هناك حتى زالت الشمس ثم خطب وصلى الظهر والعصر ثم دخل

أرض عرفات حتى وصل الصخرات فوقف هناك وقد سبق هذا واضحا في الرواية الاولى

قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (نحرت ها هنا ومنى كلها منحر فانحروا في رحالكم

ووقفت ها هنا وعرفة كلها موقف ووقفت ها هنا وجمع كلها موقف) في هذه الألفاظ

بيان رفق النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بأمته وشفقته عليهم في تنبيههم على

مصالح دينهم ودنياهم فإنه صلى الله عليه وسلم ذكر لهم الأكمل والجائز

فالأكمل موضع نحره ووقوفه والجائز كل جزء من أجزاء المنحر وجزء من أجزاء

عرفات وخيرهن أجزاء المزدلفة وهي جمع بفتح الجيم وإسكان الميم وسبق بيانها

وبيان حدها وحد منى في هذا الباب وأما عرفات فحدها
# 
# ما جاوز وادي عرنة إلى الجبال القابلة مما يلي بساتين بن عامر هكذا نص

عليه الشافعي وجميع أصحابه ونقل الأزرقي عن بن عباس أنه قال حد عرفات من

الجبل المشرف على بطن عرنة إلى جبال عرفات إلى وصيق بفتح الواو وكسر الصاد

المهملة وآخره قاف إلى ملتقى وصيق وادي عرنة وقيل في حدها  غير هذا مما هو

متقارب له وقد بسطت القول في إيضاحه في شرح المهذب وكتاب المناسك والله

أعلم قال الشافعي وأصحابنا يجوز نحر الهدي ودماء الحيوانات في جميع الحرم

لكن الأفضل في حق الحاج النحر بمنى وأفضل موضع منها للنحر موضع نحر رسول

الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وما قاربه والأفضل في حق المعتمر أن ينحر في

المروة لأنها موضع تحلله كما أن منى موضع تحلل الحاج قالوا ويجوز الوقوف

بعرفات في أي جزء كان منها وكذا يجوز الوقوف على المشعر الحرام وفي كل جزء

من أجزاء المزدلفة لهذا الحديث والله أعلم وأما قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم

ومنى كلها منحر فانحروا في رحالكم فالمراد بالرحال المنازل قال أهل اللغة

رحل الرجل منزله سواء كان من حجر أو مدر أو شعر أو وبر ومعنى الحديث منى

كلها منحر يجوز النحر فيها فلا تتكلفوا النحر في موضع نحري بل يجوز لكم

النحر في منازلكم من منى قوله (أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لما قدم

مكة أتى الحجر فاستلمه ثم مشى على يمينه فرمل ثلاثا ومشى أربعا) في هذا

الحديث أن السنة للحاج أن يبدأ أول قدومه بطواف القدوم ويقدمه على كل شيء

وأن يستلم الحجر الأسود في أول طوافه وأن يرمل في ثلاث طوفات من السبع

ويمشي في الأربع الأخيرة وسيأتي هذا كله واضحا حيث ذكر مسلم أحاديثه والله

أعلم
# [1219] قوله (كانت
# 
# قريش ومن دان دينها يقفون بالمزدلفة وكانوا يسمون الحمس) إلى آخره الحمس

بضم الحاء المهملة وإسكان الميم وبسين مهملة قال أبو الهيثم الحمس هم قريش

ومن ولدته قريش وكنانة وجديلة قيس سموا حمسا لأنهم تحمسوا في دينهم أي

تشددوا وقيل سموا حمسا بالكعبة لأنها حمساء حجرها أبيض يضرب إلى السواد وقد

سبق قريبا شرح هذا الحديث وسبب وقوفهم بالمزدلفة قوله (كانت العرب تطوف

بالبيت عراة إلا الحمس) هذا من الفواحش التي كانوا عليها في الجاهلية وقيل

نزل فيه قوله تعالى وإذا فعلوا فاحشة قالوا وجدنا عليها آباءنا  ولهذا أمر

النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في الحجة التي حجها أبو بكر رضي الله عنه سنة تسع

أن ينادي مناديه أن لا يطوف بالبيت عريان
# 
# [1220] قوله (عن جبير بن مطعم قال أضللت بعيرا لي فذهبت أطلبه يوم عرفة

فرأيت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم واقفا مع الناس بعرفة فقلت والله إن

هذا لمن الحمس فما شأنه ها هنا وكانت قريش تعد من الحمس) قال القاضي عياض

كان هذا في حجه قبل الهجرة وكان جبير حينئذ كافرا وأسلم يوم الفتح وقيل يوم

خيبر فتعجب من وقوف النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بعرفات والله أعلم

| (باب جواز تعليق الإحرام)
# (وهو أن يحرم بإحرام كإحرام فلان فيصير محرما بإحرام مثل إحرام فلان)
# [1221] في الباب حديث أبي موسى الأشعري رضي الله عنه (أن النبي صلى الله

عليه وسلم قال له أحججت قال فقلت نعم فقال بم أهللت قال قلت لبيك بإهلال

كإهلال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال قد أحسنت طف بالبيت وبالصفا والمروة

وأحل قال فطفت بالبيت وبالصفا والمروة ثم أتيت امرأة
# 
# من بني قيس ففلت رأسي ثم أهللت بالحج) في هذا الحديث فوائد منها جواز

تعليق الإحرام فإذا قال أحرمت بإحرام كإحرام زيد صح إحرامه وكان إحرامه
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ج-و-ز (j-w-z)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To pass through, traverse, cross over; permissibility of passage.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In ritual law, denotes what is licit (jāʾiz) as opposed to obligatory (wājib) — the permissible boundary of action.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: physical crossing (majāz: passing beyond a limit); metaphorical: exceeding the bounds of strict obligation into the realm of allowance.
- Sībawayh Rule: Taqdīr (Elliptical Reconstruction) — The phrase "fa-ajāza" requires an implied object/path (muqaddar: mutawajjihan ilā ʿArafāt), restoring the omitted directional complement for syntactic completeness.
chapters.translation:
I say: Know that the Prophet's (peace and blessings be upon him) statement "he passed on" (ajāza) means "he crossed beyond" (jāwaza). His statement "and he did not turn aside" (wa-lam yaʿriḍ) — the letter yāʾ is opened (fatḥah) and the rāʾ is broken (kasrah).

The meaning of the hadith is that the Quraysh, before Islam, used to stand at Muzdalifah — which is within the Sacred Precinct (al-Ḥaram) — and they would not stand at ʿArafāt. The rest of the Arabs, however, would stand at ʿArafāt. The Quraysh would say: "We are the people of the Sacred Precinct, so we do not depart from it." Thus, when the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) performed the Hajj and reached Muzdalifah, they assumed he would stand there according to the Quraysh's custom. But he crossed beyond to ʿArafāt, in obedience to the saying of Allah the Mighty and Majestic: {«ثُمَّ أَفِيضُوا مِنْ حَيْثُ أَفَاضَ النَّاسُ»} — "Then depart from where the people depart" (Q2:199) — meaning the multitude of the people, for those other than Quraysh used to stand at ʿArafāt and depart from it.

As for his statement "he passed on and did not turn aside until he came to ʿArafāt and halted there" — therein is an elliptical construction (majāz). Its estimated meaning is: "he passed on, heading toward ʿArafāt, until he drew near it." Then the dome was pitched for him at Namirah, near ʿArafāt, and he halted there until the sun passed its zenith. Then he delivered the sermon, prayed the Ẓuhr and ʿAṣr prayers, then entered the land of ʿArafāt until he reached the rocky outcrops (al-Ṣakharāt) and stood there. This has already been explained clearly in the first narration.

His statement (peace and blessings be upon him): "I have sacrificed here, and all of Minā is a place of sacrifice, so sacrifice at your dwellings. And I have stood here, and all of ʿArafāt is a place of standing. And I have stood here, and all of Jamʿ (Muzdalifah) is a place of standing" — in these words is an exposition of the Prophet's (peace and blessings be upon him) gentleness toward his community and his compassion for them, in alerting them to the interests of their religion and their worldly affairs. For he (peace and blessings be upon him) mentioned to them both the most complete (al-akmal) and the permissible (al-jāʾiz). The most complete is his own place of sacrifice and standing; the permissible is every part of the place of sacrifice, every part of ʿArafāt, and every part of Muzdalifah — which is Jamʿ, with the jīm opened (fatḥah) and the mīm made silent (sukūn). Its explanation and the explanation of its boundary, and the boundary of Minā, have preceded in this chapter.

As for ʿArafāt, its boundary is: whatever lies beyond the valley of ʿUranah, up to the facing mountains on the side of the orchards of Banī ʿĀmir. Thus did al-Shāfiʿī and all his companions explicitly state. Al-Azraqī transmitted from Ibn ʿAbbās that he said: "The boundary of ʿArafāt is from the mountain overlooking the hollow of ʿUranah to the mountains of ʿArafāt, to Uṣayq — with the wāw opened (fatḥah) and the ṣād broken (kasrah), its final letter qāf — to the confluence of Uṣayq and the valley of ʿUranah." Another saying has been reported regarding its boundary, close in meaning to this. I have expanded the discourse clarifying this in my commentary on al-Muhadhdhab and in the Book of Rituals (Kitāb al-Manāsik). And Allah knows best.

Al-Shāfiʿī and our companions said: It is permissible to sacrifice the hady (offering) and the blood of animals anywhere in the entire Sacred Precinct. However, the most virtuous for the pilgrim is to sacrifice at Minā, and the most virtuous place therein is the place where the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) sacrificed, and what is near it. The most virtuous for the one performing ʿUmrah is to sacrifice at al-Marwah, because it is the place of his ritual release (taḥallul), just as Minā is the place of the pilgrim's ritual release. They said: It is permissible to stand at ʿArafāt in any part thereof, and likewise it is permissible to stand at al-Mashʿar al-Ḥarām and in every part of Muzdalifah, due to this hadith. And Allah knows best.

As for his statement (peace and blessings be upon him): "And all of Minā is a place of sacrifice, so sacrifice at your dwellings" — the intended meaning of "dwellings" (al-riḥāl) is the encampments (al-manāzil). The linguists said: "A man's riḥl is his dwelling, whether it be of stone, clay, hair, or wool." The meaning of the hadith is: all of Minā is a place of sacrifice — sacrifice therein is permissible — so do not burden yourselves to sacrifice at my precise place of sacrifice. Rather, it is permissible for you to sacrifice in your own encampments within Minā.

His statement: "That the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him), when he arrived at Mecca, came to the Black Stone (al-Ḥajar), touched it (istalama), then walked on his right side, jogging (ramala) three circuits and walking four" — in this hadith is the ruling that the Sunnah for the pilgrim is to begin, upon his first arrival, with the circumambulation of arrival (ṭawāf al-qudūm), and to give it precedence over everything else; and to touch the Black Stone at the beginning of his circumambulation; and to jog (yarmul) in three circuits of the seven, and to walk in the final four. All of this will come clearly where Muslim mentions its hadiths. And Allah knows best.

[1219] His statement: "The Quraysh and those who followed their religion used to stand at Muzdalifah, and they were called al-Ḥums" — to the end. Al-Ḥums: with the ḥāʾ opened (ḍammah), the mīm made silent, and an unpointed sīn. Abū al-Haytham said: "Al-Ḥums are the Quraysh, and those whom Quraysh gave birth to, and Kinānah, and Judaylah of Qays." They were called Ḥums because they hardened themselves (taḥammasū) in their religion, i.e., they became strict. It was also said they were called Ḥums after the Kaʿbah, because it is ḥamsāʾ — its stone is white tending to black. The explanation of this hadith and the reason for their standing at Muzdalifah has already preceded recently.

His statement: "The Arabs used to circumambulate the House naked, except for the Ḥums" — this is among the abominations (fawāḥish) they practiced in the pre-Islamic era (Jāhiliyyah). It was said that concerning this was revealed the saying of Allah the Exalted: {«وَإِذَا فَعَلُوا فَاحِشَةً قَالُوا وَجَدْنَا عَلَيْهَا آبَاءَنَا»} — "And when they commit an immorality, they say: 'We found our fathers upon it'" (Q7:28). For this reason, the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) commanded, in the Hajj that Abū Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) led in the year nine, that his crier proclaim that no one should circumambulate the House naked.

[1220] His statement: "From Jubayr ibn Muṭʿim, who said: 'I lost a camel of mine, so I went searching for it on the Day of ʿArafah. I saw the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) standing with the people at ʿArafāt. I said: "By Allah, this man is among the Ḥums — what is his business here?" For the Quraysh were counted among the Ḥums.'" — Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ said: This was during his Hajj before the Hijrah, and Jubayr at that time was an unbeliever. He embraced Islam on the day of the Conquest (of Mecca), and it was also said on the day of Khaybar. He marveled at the Prophet's (peace and blessings be upon him) standing at ʿArafāt. And Allah knows best.

| (Chapter: The Permissibility of Suspending the Iḥrām)
(That is: that one say "I assume iḥrām with an iḥrām like so-and-so's iḥrām," thereby becoming a muḥrim with an iḥrām equivalent to that person's iḥrām.)

[1221] In this chapter is the hadith of Abū Mūsā al-Ashʿarī (may Allah be pleased with him): "That the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said to him: 'Have you performed the Hajj?' He said: 'I said: Yes.' He said: 'With what did you enter the state of iḥrām (ahlalta)?' He said: 'I said: Labbayka with an ihlāl like the ihlāl of the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him).' He said: 'You have done well. Circumambulate the House and (go between) al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah, and then release yourself (aḥlil).' He said: 'So I circumambulated the House and (went between) al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah, then I came to a woman of Banī Qays who combed my hair, and then I entered the state of iḥrām for the Hajj.'"

In this hadith are several benefits, among them: the permissibility of suspending the iḥrām (taʿlīq al-iḥrām). Thus, if one says: "I assume iḥrām with an iḥrām like the iḥrām of Zayd," his iḥrām is valid, and his iḥrām becomes...

chapters.title_en: The Suspension of Iḥrām Upon Another's Iḥrām, Commendation of Virtuous Acts, and the Rulings on Tamattuʿ and Qirān
chapters.arabic_text:
كإحرام زيد فإن كان زيد محرما بحج أو بعمرة أو قارنا كان المعلق مثله وإن

كان زيد أحرم مطلقا كان المعلق مطلقا ولا يلزمه أن يصرف إحرامه إلى ما يصرف

زيد إحرامه إليه فلو صرف زيد إحرامه إلى حج كان للمعلق صرف إحرامه إلى عمرة

وكذا عكسه ومنها استحباب الثناء على من فعل فعلا جميلا لقوله صلى الله عليه

وسلم أحسنت وأما قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (طف بالبيت وبالصفا والمروة وأحل)

فمعناه أنه صار كالنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وتكون وظيفته أن يفسخ حجه إلى

عمرة فيأتي بأفعالها وهي الطواف والسعي والحلق فإذا فعل ذلك صار حلالا وتمت

عمرته وإنما لم يذكر الحلق هنا لأنه كان مشهورا عندهم ويحتمل أنه داخل في

قوله وأحل وقوله (ثم أتيت امرأة من بني قيس ففلت رأسي) هذا محمول على أن

هذه المرأة كانت محرما له وقوله (ثم أهللت بالحج) يعني أنه تحلل بالعمرة

وأقام بمكة حلالا إلى يوم التروية وهو الثامن من ذي الحجة ثم أحرم بالحج

يوم التروية كما جاء مبينا في غير هذه الرواية فإن قيل قد علق علي بن أبي

طالب وأبو موسى رضي الله عنهما إحرامهما بإحرام النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

فأمر عليا بالدوام على إحرامه قارنا وأمر أبا موسى بفسخه إلى عمرة فالجواب

أن عليا رضي الله عنه كان معه الهدي كما كان مع النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

الهدي فبقي على إحرامه كما بقي النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وكل من معه هدي

وأبو موسى لم يكن معه هدي فتحلل بعمرة كمن لم يكن معه هدي ولولا الهدي مع

النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لجعلها عمرة وقد سبق إيضاح هذا الجواب في الباب

الذي قبل هذا قوله ففلت رأسي هو بتخفف اللام قوله (رويدك بعض فتياك) معنى

رويدك ارفق قليلا وأمسك عن الفتيا ويقال فتيا وفتوى لغتان مشهورتان
# 
# قوله إن عمر رضي الله عنه قال (إن نأخذ بكتاب الله فإن كتاب الله يأمر

بالتمام وإن نأخذ بسنة رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فإن رسول الله صلى

الله عليه وسلم لم يحل حتى بلغ الهدي محله) قال القاضي عياض رحمه الله

تعالى ظاهر كلام عمر هذا إنكار فسخ الحج إلى العمرة وأن نهيه عن التمتع

إنما هو من باب ترك الأولى لأنه منع ذلك منع تحريم وإبطال ويؤيد هذا قوله

بعد هذا قد علمت أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قد فعله وأصحابه لكن كرهت أن

يظلوا معرسين
# 
# بهن في الأراك
# [1222] وقوله (معرسين) هو بإسكان العين وتخفيف الراء والضمير في بهن يعود

إلى النساء للعلم بهن وإن لم يذكرن ومعناه كرهت التمتع لأنه يقتضي التحلل

ووطء النساء إلى حين الخروج إلى عرفات
#

| (باب جواز التمتع)
# [1223] قوله (كان عثمان  رضي الله عنه ينهى عن المتعة وكان علي يأمر بها)

المختار أن المتعة التي نهى عنها عثمان هي التمتع المعروف في الحج وكان عمر

وعثمان ينهيان عنها نهي تنزيه لا تحريم وإنما نهيا عنها لأن الإفراد أفضل

فكان عمر وعثمان يأمران بالإفراد لأنه أفضل وينهيان عن التمتع نهي تنزيه

لأنه مأمور بصلاح رعيته وكان يرى الأمر بالإفراد من جملة صلاحهم والله أعلم

قوله (ثم قال علي لقد علمت أنا قد تمتعنا مع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

قال أجل ولكن كنا خائفين) فقوله أجل بإسكان اللام أي نعم وقوله كنا خائفين

لعله أراد بقوله خائفين يوم عمرة القضاء سنة سبع قبل فتح مكة لكن لم يكن

تلك السنة حقيقة تمتع إنما كان عمرة وحدها قوله (فقال عثمان دعنا عنك فقال

يعني عليا إني لا أستطيع أن أدعك فلما أن رأى علي ذلك أهل بهما) ففيه إشاعة

العلم وإظهاره ومناظرة ولاة الأمور وغيرهم في تحقيقه ووجوب مناصحة المسلم

في ذلك وهذا معنى قول
# 
# علي لا أستطيع أن أدعك وأما إهلال علي بهما فقد يحتج به من يرجح القران

وأجاب عنه من رجح الإفراد بأنه إنما أهل بهما ليبين جوازهما لئلا يظن الناس

أو بعضهم أنه لا يجوز القران ولا التمتع وأنه يتعين الإفراد والله أعلم

قوله (عن أبي ذر قال كانت المتعة في الحج لأصحاب محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

خاصة) وفي الرواية الأخرى كانت لنا رخصة يعني المتعة في الحج وفي الرواية

الأخرى قال أبو ذر لا تصلح المتعتان إلا لنا خاصة يعني متعة النساء ومتعة

الحج وفي الرواية الأخرى إنما كانت لنا خاصة دونكم قال العلماء معنى هذه

الروايات كلها أن فسخ الحج إلى العمرة كان للصحابة في تلك السنة وهي حجة

الوداع ولا يجوز بعد ذلك وليس مراد أبي ذر إبطال التمتع مطلقا بل مراده فسخ

الحج كما ذكرنا وحكمته إبطال ما كانت عليه الجاهلية من منع العمرة في أشهر

الحج وقد سبق بيان هذا كله في  الباب السابق والله أعلم قوله (لا تصلح

المتعتان إلا لنا خاصة) معناه إنما صلحتا لنا خاصة في الوقت الذي فعلناهما

فيه ثم صارتا حراما بعد ذلك
# 
# إلى يوم القيامة والله أعلم
# [1225] قوله (سألت سعد بن أبي وقاص عن المتعة فقال فعلناها وهذا يومئذ

كافر بالعرش يعني بيوت مكة) وفي الرواية الأخرى يعني معاوية وفي الرواية

الأخرى المتعة في الحج أما العرش فبضم العين والراء وهي بيوت مكة كما فسره
chapters.anchors:
- Root: عَلَّقَ (ʿ-l-q)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To hang, suspend, or attach something to another; to make conditional upon.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In legal terminology, taʿlīq denotes the conditional suspension of an act's validity upon a specified condition (sharṭ).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) in physical suspension; metaphorical (majāz) in legal conditional linkage.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Sentence Structure (al-sharṭ wa al-jawāb) — The suspended iḥrām (jawāb) follows the condition of the model's (Zayd's) iḥrām type, requiring precise syntactic parallelism.
chapters.translation:
I say: Know that the suspension of one's iḥrām upon another's iḥrām follows the model precisely. If Zayd is in a state of iḥrām for Ḥajj, ʿUmrah, or Qirān (combining both), then the one who suspends his iḥrām upon Zayd's is like him. But if Zayd entered iḥrām in an absolute, unrestricted manner (muṭlaq), then the suspended one is likewise unrestricted, and he is not obligated to divert his iḥrām to whatever Zayd diverts his own. So if Zayd diverted his iḥrām to Ḥajj, the suspended one may divert his to ʿUmrah, and likewise the reverse.

Among the rulings of this section is the commendability (istiḥbāb) of praising one who performs a virtuous act, due to his saying, peace and blessings be upon him: "You have done well" (aḥsanta). As for his saying, peace and blessings be upon him: "Circumambulate the House, and (go between) al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah, and then become lawful (aḥlil)" — its meaning is that he became like the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and his task was to annul his Ḥajj into ʿUmrah, performing its rites: the circumambulation (ṭawāf), the running (saʿy), and the shaving of the head (ḥalq). When he did this, he became lawful (ḥalāl) and his ʿUmrah was complete. The shaving was not mentioned here because it was well-known among them, and it is possible that it is included in his saying "and become lawful" (wa-aḥlil).

His saying: "Then I came to a woman from Banū Qays, and she deloused my head" (fa-falayt raʾsī) — this is interpreted as that woman being a lawful (non-muḥrim) relative for him. His saying: "Then I raised my voice in talbiyah for Ḥajj" (thumma ahhaltu bil-ḥajj) means that he had become lawful through ʿUmrah and remained in Mecca in a lawful state until the Day of Tarwiyah, which is the eighth of Dhū al-Ḥijjah. Then he entered iḥrām for Ḥajj on the Day of Tarwiyah, as is clarified in other narrations.

If it is said: ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib and Abū Mūsā, may Allah be pleased with them both, had suspended their iḥrām upon the iḥrām of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him. He commanded ʿAlī to persist in his iḥrām as a qārin (one combining Ḥajj and ʿUmrah), and commanded Abū Mūsā to annul his into ʿUmrah. The answer is that ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with him, had the sacrificial animal (hadī) with him, just as the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, had the hadī. So he remained in his iḥrām as the Prophet remained, and so did everyone who had a hadī with him. Abū Mūsā had no hadī with him, so he became lawful through ʿUmrah, like one who had no hadī. Had there been no hadī with the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, he would have made it a ʿUmrah. The clarification of this answer has already preceded in the chapter before this one.
