His saying "fa-falayt raʾsī" — the lām is pronounced with a single (unshaddah) consonant. His saying "ruwaydaka baʿḍa fatyāk" — the meaning of ruwaydaka is: be gentle a little, and refrain from issuing legal rulings (fatwā). It is said "fatya" and "fatwā" — two well-known dialectal variants.

His saying that ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "If we take by the Book of Allah, then the Book of Allah commands completion (al-tamām); and if we take by the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah, then the Messenger of Allah did not become lawful until the hadī reached its place of sacrifice." Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ, may Allah have mercy on him, said: The apparent meaning of ʿUmar's statement is a rejection of annulling Ḥajj into ʿUmrah, and that his prohibition of tamattuʿ was only from the category of abandoning the superior (tark al-awlā), because he prohibited it as a prohibition of preference, not of unlawfulness or nullification. This is supported by his subsequent saying: "I have known that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, did it, and so did his companions, but I disliked that they should remain in a state of intimate retreat (muʿarrisīn) with them (the women) in the arāk trees."

[1222] His saying "muʿarrisīn" — the ʿayn is unvowelled (sukūn) and the rāʾ is unshaddah. The pronoun in "bihinna" (with them) refers to the women, known by context even though not explicitly mentioned. Its meaning: I disliked tamattuʿ because it necessitates becoming lawful and engaging in sexual intercourse with women until the time of departure to ʿArafāt.

| (Chapter: The Permissibility of Tamattuʿ)

[1223] His saying: "ʿUthmān, may Allah be pleased with him, used to prohibit mutʿah (tamattuʿ), and ʿAlī used to command it." The chosen position (al-mukhtār) is that the mutʿah which ʿUthmān prohibited is the well-known tamattuʿ in Ḥajj. ʿUmar and ʿUthmān prohibited it as a prohibition of dispreference (nahy tanzīh), not unlawfulness (taḥrīm). They only prohibited it because ifrād (performing Ḥajj alone) is superior. Thus ʿUmar and ʿUthmān commanded ifrād because it is superior, and prohibited tamattuʿ as a prohibition of dispreference, because he (the ruler) was commanded to seek the welfare of his flock (ṣalāḥ raʿiyyatihi), and he saw that commanding ifrād was part of their welfare. And Allah knows best.

His saying: "Then ʿAlī said: 'I have known that we performed tamattuʿ with the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him.' He (ʿUthmān) said: 'Indeed (ajal), but we were fearful.'" His saying "ajal" — the lām is unvowelled, meaning "yes" (naʿam). His saying "we were fearful" — perhaps he meant by "fearful" the day of the ʿUmrah of al-Qaḍāʾ (the compensatory ʿUmrah) in the year seven, before the conquest of Mecca. But that year was not truly tamattuʿ; it was only a ʿUmrah by itself.

His saying: "Then ʿUthmān said: 'Leave us alone (daʿnā ʿanka).' He said — meaning ʿAlī — 'I cannot leave you.' When ʿAlī saw that, he raised his voice in talbiyah for both (ahalla bihimā)." In this is the dissemination of knowledge and its public declaration, and the disputation with rulers and others in verifying it, and the obligation of sincere counsel (nuṣḥ) to the Muslim in that matter. This is the meaning of ʿAlī's saying: "I cannot leave you." As for ʿAlī's raising the talbiyah for both (Ḥajj and ʿUmrah), it may be cited as evidence by those who prefer Qirān. Those who prefer Ifrād respond that he only raised the talbiyah for both to demonstrate their permissibility, lest the people — or some of them — think that Qirān and Tamattuʿ are not permissible and that Ifrād is exclusively required. And Allah knows best.

His saying, on the authority of Abū Dharr: "Tamattuʿ in Ḥajj was exclusively for the companions of Muḥammad, peace and blessings be upon him." In another narration: "It was a concession (rukḥṣah) for us" — meaning tamattuʿ in Ḥajj. In yet another narration, Abū Dharr said: "The two mutʿahs are not permissible except for us exclusively" — meaning mutʿah of women and mutʿah of Ḥajj. In another narration: "It was only for us exclusively, not for you." The scholars said: The meaning of all these narrations is that the annulment of Ḥajj into ʿUmrah was for the companions in that year — the Farewell Pilgrimage — and it is not permissible after that. Abū Dharr did not intend the nullification of tamattuʿ absolutely; rather, he intended the annulment of Ḥajj (into ʿUmrah) as we have mentioned. Its wisdom was to nullify what the pre-Islamic era (Jāhiliyyah) had established — the prohibition of ʿUmrah during the months of Ḥajj. The clarification of all this has already preceded in the previous chapter. And Allah knows best.

His saying: "The two mutʿahs are not permissible except for us exclusively" — its meaning is that they were only permissible for us exclusively at the time we performed them. Then they became forbidden after that until the Day of Resurrection. And Allah knows best.

[1225] His saying: "I asked Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ about mutʿah, and he said: 'We did it, and this one — on that day — was a disbeliever in the ʿArsh (throne)'" — meaning the houses of Mecca. In another narration: "meaning Muʿāwiyah." In yet another narration: "mutʿah in Ḥajj." As for "al-ʿArsh" — it is with ḍammah on the ʿayn and the rāʾ, and it refers to the houses of Mecca, as he himself interpreted it.

chapters.arabic_text:
في الرواية قال أبو عبيد سميت بيوت مكة عرشا لأنها عيدان تنصب وتظلل قال

ويقال لها أيضا عروش بالراء وواحدها عرش كفلس وفلوس ومن قال عرش فواحدها

عريش كقليب وقلب وفي حديث آخر أن عمر رضي الله عنه كان إذا نظر إلى عروش

مكة قطع التلبية وأما قوله وهذا يومئذ كافر بالعرش فالإشارة بهذا إلى

معاوية بن أبي سفيان وفي المراد بالكفر هنا وجهان أحدهما ما قاله المازري

وغيره المراد وهو مقيم في بيوت مكة قال ثعلب يقال اكتفر الرجل إذا لزم

الكفور وهي القرى وفي الأثر عن عمر رضي الله عنه أهل الكفور هم أهل القبور

يعني القرى البعيدة عن الأمصار وعن العلماء والوجه الثاني المراد الكفر

بالله تعالى والمراد أنا تمتعنا ومعاوية يومئذ كافر على دين الجاهلية مقيم

بمكة وهذا اختيار القاضي عياض وغيره وهو الصحيح المختار والمراد بالمتعة

العمرة التي كانت سنة سبع من
# 
# الهجرة وهي عمرة القضاء وكان معاوية يومئذ كافرا وإنما أسلم بعد ذلك عام

الفتح سنة ثمان وقيل إنه أسلم بعد عمرة القضاء سنة سبع والصحيح الأول وأما

غير هذه العمرة من عمر النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فلم يكن معاوية فيها كافرا

ولا مقيما بمكة بل كان معه صلى الله عليه وسلم قال القاضي عياض وقاله بعضهم

كافر بالعرش بفتح العين وإسكان الراء والمراد عرش الرحمن قال القاضي هذا

تصحيف وفي هذا الحديث جواز المتعة في الحج
# [1226] قوله (عن عمران بن حصين أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أعمر

طائفة من أهله في  العشر فلم تنزل آية تنسخ ذلك ولم ينه عنه حتى مضى لوجهه)

وفي الرواية الأخرى أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم جمع بين حج وعمرة ثم

لم ينه عنه حتى مات ولم ينزل فيه قرآن يحرمه وفي الرواية الأخرى نحوه ثم

قال قال رجل برأيه ما شاء يعني عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه وفي الرواية

الأخرى تمتعنا مع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فلم ينزل فيه القرآن قال

رجل برأيه ما شاء وفي الرواية الأخرى تمتع وتمتعنا معه وفي الرواية الأخرى

نزلت آية المتعة في كتاب الله يعني متعة الحج وأمرنا بها رسول الله صلى

الله عليه
# 
# وسلم وهذه الروايات كلها متفقة على أن مراد عمران أن التمتع بالعمرة إلى

الحج جائز وكذلك القران وفيه التصريح بإنكاره على عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله

عنه منع التمتع وقد سبق تأويل فعل عمر أنه لم يرد إبطال التمتع بل ترجيح

الإفراد عليه قوله (وقد كان يسلم علي حتى اكتويت فتركت ثم تركت الكي فعاد)

فقوله يسلم علي هو بفتح اللام المشددة وقوله فتركت هو بضم التاء أي انقطع

السلام علي ثم تركت بفتح التاء أي تركت الكي فعاد السلام علي ومعنى الحديث

أن عمران بن الحصين رضي الله عنه كانت به بواسير فكان يصبر على المهمات

وكانت الملائكة تسلم عليه فاكتوى فانقطع سلامهم عليه ثم ترك الكي فعاد

سلامهم عليه قوله (بعث إلي عمران بن حصين في مرضه الذي توفي فيه فقال إني

كنت محدثك بأحاديث لعل الله أن ينفعك بها بعدي فإن عشت فاكتم عني وإن مت

فحدث بها إن شئت أنه قد سلم علي واعلم أن نبي الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قد

جمع بين حج وعمرة أما قوله فإن عشت فاكتم عني فأراد به الإخبار بالسلام

عليه لأنه كره
# 
# أن يشاع عنه ذلك في حياته لما فيه من التعرض للفتنة بخلاف ما بعد الموت

وأما قوله لعل الله أن ينفعك بها فمعناه تعمل بها وتعلمها غيرك  وأما قوله

أحاديث فظاهره أنها ثلاثة فصاعدا ولم يذكر منها إلا حديثا واحدا وهو الجمع

بين الحج والعمرة وأما إخباره بالسلام فليس حديثا فيكون باقي الأحاديث

محذوفا من الرواية قوله (حدثنا حامد بن عمر البكراوي) هو
# 
# منسوب إلى جد جد أبيه أبي بكرة الصحابي رضي الله عنه فإنه حامد بن عمر بن

حفص بن عمر بن عبيد الله بن أبي بكرة الثقفي رضي الله عنه

| (باب وجوب الدم على المتمتع وأنه إذا عدمه لزمه)
# (صوم ثلاثة أيام في الحج وسبعة إذا رجع إلى أهله)
# [1227] قوله (عن بن عمر رضي الله عنه قال تمتع رسول الله صلى الله عليه

وسلم في حجة الوداع بالعمرة إلى الحج وأهدى وساق معه الهدي من ذي الحليفة

وبدأ رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فأهل بالعمرة ثم أهل بالحج وتمتع الناس

مع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بالعمرة إلى الحج) قال القاضي قوله تمتع

هو محمول على التمتع اللغوي وهو القران آخرا ومعناه أنه صلى الله عليه وسلم

أحرم أولا بالحج مفردا ثم أحرم بالعمرة فصار قارنا في آخر أمره والقارن هو

متمتع من حيث اللغة ومن حيث المعنى لأنه ترفه باتحاد الميقات والإحرام

والفعل ويتعين هذا التأويل هنا لما قدمناه في الأبواب السابقة من الجمع بين

الأحاديث في ذلك وممن روى إفراد النبى صلى الله عليه وسلم بن عمر الراوي

هنا وقد ذكره مسلم بعد هذا وأما قوله بدأ رسول الله صلى
# 
# الله عليه وسلم فأهل بالعمرة ثم أهل بالحج فهو محمول على التلبية في

أثناء الإحرام وليس المراد أنه أحرم في أول أمره بعمرة ثم أحرم بحج لأنه

يفضي إلى مخالفة الأحاديث السابقة وقد سبق بيان الجمع بين الروايات فوجب
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ع-ر-ش (ʿ-r-sh)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning is a constructed canopy, trellis, or roofed structure; also a throne (sarīr al-mulk). The plural ʿurūsh refers to wooden frames erected for shade.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In Quranic usage, ʿarsh denotes the divine throne (ʿarsh al-Raḥmān), a metaphysical locus of sovereignty, distinct from the physical canopies of Makkah.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) = physical trellis/booth; metaphorical (majāz) = royal throne or divine dominion. The narrator's phrase "kāfir bil-ʿarsh" is parsed contextually: either "dwelling in the booths" (literal) or "unbeliever regarding the Throne" (metaphorical, if read as ʿarsh with fatḥah on ʿayn).
- Sībawayh Rule: Taqdīr al-Maḥdhūf (Ellipsis Restoration) — When a phrase like "kāfir bil-ʿarsh" is ambiguous, the syntactic context (jar-majrūr attached to kāfir) requires determining the referent via external evidence (qarīnah), here the historical setting of Mu'āwiyah's pre-Islam residence.
chapters.translation:
I say: In one narration, Abū ʿUbayd said: "The houses of Makkah were called ʿarsh (plural ʿurūsh) because they are wooden poles erected and shaded over." He said: "They are also called ʿurūsh with the rā', and their singular is ʿarsh, like fals and fulūs. And whoever says ʿarsh, its singular is ʿarīsh, like qalīb and qulb." In another ḥadīth, ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with him), when he looked upon the ʿurūsh of Makkah, would cease the talbiyah.

As for his statement: "And this one, on that day, was a disbeliever with respect to the ʿarsh (kāfir bil-ʿarsh)" — the reference in "this" is to Muʿāwiyah ibn Abī Sufyān. Regarding the intended meaning of "kufr" here, there are two aspects:

**First**: What al-Māzarī and others stated — the meaning is that he was residing in the houses of Makkah. Thaʿlab said: "One says 'iktafara al-rajul' when he clings to the kufūr, which are the villages." In the athar from ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with him): "The people of the kufūr are the people of the graves" — meaning the villages distant from the major cities and from the scholars.

**Second**: The intended meaning is disbelief in Allah the Exalted. The meaning is: "We performed tamattuʿ, while Muʿāwiyah on that day was a disbeliever upon the religion of the Jāhiliyyah, residing in Makkah." This is the choice of Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ and others, and it is the correct and preferred view.

The intended meaning of "mutʿah" here is the ʿumrah that occurred in the year seven of the Hijrah — namely, the ʿumrah of al-Qaḍā (the compensatory ʿumrah). Muʿāwiyah was on that day a disbeliever; he only embraced Islam after that, in the year of the Conquest (year eight). It is also said he embraced Islam after the ʿumrah of al-Qaḍā in year seven, but the correct view is the first. As for the other ʿumrahs of the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) besides this one, Muʿāwiyah was neither a disbeliever nor a resident of Makkah during them; rather, he was with him (peace and blessings be upon him).

Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ said — and some others also said — that "kāfir bil-ʿarsh" with fatḥah on the ʿayn and sukūn on the rā' means the Throne of the Most Merciful. Qāḍī said: This is a taṣḥīf (corruption of the text).

In this ḥadīth is the permissibility of tamattuʿ in Hajj.

**[1226]** His statement (from ʿImrān ibn Ḥuṣayn that the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, performed ʿumrah for a group of his family in the ten days [of Dhul-Ḥijjah], and no verse was revealed abrogating that, nor did he prohibit it until he departed on his way) — and in the other narration: "The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, combined Hajj and ʿumrah, then he did not prohibit it until he died, nor was any Qur'an revealed forbidding it." In another narration similar to it, then he said: "A man said his own opinion as he wished" — meaning ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, may Allah be pleased with him. In another narration: "We performed tamattuʿ with the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, and no Qur'an was revealed about it. A man said his own opinion as he wished." In another narration: "He performed tamattuʿ, and we performed tamattuʿ with him." In another narration: "The verse of mutʿah was revealed in the Book of Allah" — meaning the tamattuʿ of Hajj — "and the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, commanded us with it."

All these narrations agree that ʿImrān's intent was that tamattuʿ of ʿumrah to Hajj is permissible, and likewise qirān. In them is an explicit rejection of ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb's (may Allah be pleased with him) prohibition of tamattuʿ. The interpretation of ʿUmar's action has already preceded — that he did not intend to nullify tamattuʿ, but rather to prefer ifrād (separate performance) over it.

His statement: "He used to greet me with salām until I was cauterized, then it stopped; then I abandoned cauterization, and it returned" — his statement "yusallimu ʿalayya" is with fatḥah on the shaddah lām. His statement "fa-taraktu" is with ḍammah on the tā', meaning the salām upon me ceased. Then "taraktu" with fatḥah on the tā', meaning: I abandoned cauterization, so the salām upon me returned.

The meaning of the ḥadīth: ʿImrān ibn al-Ḥuṣayn (may Allah be pleased with him) had hemorrhoids, and he would endure hardships patiently, and the angels would greet him with salām. When he was cauterized, their salām upon him ceased. Then he abandoned cauterization, and their salām upon him returned.

His statement: "ʿImrān ibn Ḥuṣayn sent for me during his illness from which he died, and said: 'I used to narrate to you ḥadīths — perhaps Allah will benefit you with them after me. If I live, then conceal them from me; and if I die, then narrate them if you wish — that salām was indeed given to me. And know that the Prophet of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, combined between Hajj and ʿumrah.'"

As for his statement: "If I live, then conceal them from me" — he intended thereby the report of the salām upon him, because he disliked that this should become widespread about him during his lifetime, due to what it entails of exposure to tribulation (fitnah) — unlike after death.

As for his statement: "Perhaps Allah will benefit you with them" — its meaning is: act upon them and teach them to others.

As for his statement: "ḥadīths" — its apparent form indicates three or more, yet he mentioned only one ḥadīth from them, namely the combination of Hajj and ʿumrah. As for his report of the salām, that is not a ḥadīth. Thus, the remaining ḥadīths are omitted from the narration.

His statement: "Ḥāmid ibn ʿUmar al-Bakrāwī narrated to us" — he is attributed to the grandfather of his grandfather, Abū Bakrah the Companion (may Allah be pleased with him). For he is Ḥāmid ibn ʿUmar ibn Ḥafṣ ibn ʿUmar ibn ʿUbaydillāh ibn Abī Bakrah al-Thaqafī (may Allah be pleased with him).

---

**(Chapter: The Obligation of the Blood-Offering (dam) upon the Mutamattiʿ, and that if he does not find it, he must fast three days during Hajj and seven when he returns to his family)**

**[1227]** His statement (from Ibn ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, performed tamattuʿ in the Farewell Pilgrimage, with ʿumrah to Hajj, and he offered a sacrificial animal (hady) and drove the hady with him from Dhul-Ḥulayfah. The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, began and entered iḥrām with ʿumrah, then entered iḥrām with Hajj, and the people performed tamattuʿ with the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, with ʿumrah to Hajj.")

Qāḍī said: His statement "tamattaʿa" is to be interpreted according to the linguistic tamattuʿ, which is qirān ultimately. Its meaning: He (peace and blessings be upon him) first entered iḥrām with Hajj alone (ifrād), then entered iḥrām with ʿumrah, so he became a qārin (one combining) at the end of his affair. The qārin is a mutamattiʿ linguistically and in meaning, because he enjoys ease (taraffaha) through the unity of the mīqāt, the iḥrām, and the actions.

This interpretation is necessitated here by what we have presented in the preceding chapters regarding the reconciliation between the ḥadīths on this matter. Among those who narrated the ifrād of the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) is Ibn ʿUmar, the narrator here — and Muslim has mentioned this after this point.

As for his statement: "The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, began and entered iḥrām with ʿumrah, then entered iḥrām with Hajj" — it is to be interpreted as the talbiyah during the course of the iḥrām. It is not intended that he entered iḥrām at the beginning of his affair with ʿumrah, then entered iḥrām with Hajj, because that would lead to contradicting the previous ḥadīths. The reconciliation between the narrations has already been explained, so it is obligatory [to adopt it].

chapters.title_en: The Interpretation of Mut'ah (Tamattu') and the Rulings of the Qārin in Hajj
chapters.arabic_text:
تأويل هذا على موافقتها ويؤيد هذا التأويل قوله تمتع الناس مع رسول الله

صلى الله عليه وسلم بالعمرة إلى الحج ومعلوم أن كثيرا منهم أو أكثرهم

أحرموا بالحج أولا مفردا وإنما فسخوه إلى العمرة آخرا فصاروا متمتعين فقوله

وتمتع الناس يعني في  آخر الأمر والله أعلم قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (ومن لم

يكن منكم أهدى فليطف بالبيت وبالصفا والمروة وليقصر وليحلل ثم ليهل بالحج

وليهد فمن لم يجد هديا فليصم ثلاثة أيام في الحج وسبعة إذا رجع إلى أهله)

أما قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم فليطف بالبيت وبالصفا والمروة وليقصر وليحلل

فمعناه يفعل الطواف والسعي والتقصير وقد صار حلالا وهذا دليل على أن

التقصير أو الحلق نسك من مناسك الحج وهذا هو الصحيح في مذهبنا وبه قال

جماهير العلماء وقيل إنه استباحة محظور وليس بنسك وهذا ضعيف وسيأتي إيضاحه

في موضعه إن شاء الله تعالى وإنما أمره رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

بالتقصير ولم يأمر بالحلق مع أن الحلق أفضل ليبقى له شعر يحلقه في الحج فإن

الحلق في تحلل الحج أفضل منه في تحلل العمرة وأما قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم

وليحلل فمعناه وقد
# 
# صار حلالا فله فعل ما كان محظورا عليه في الإحرام من الطيب واللباس

والنساء والصيد وغير ذلك وأما قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم ثم ليهل بالحج

فمعناه يحرم به في وقت الخروج إلى عرفات لا أنه يهل به عقب تحلل العمرة

ولهذا قال ثم ليهل فأتى بثم التي هي للتراخي والمهلة وأما قوله صلى الله

عليه وسلم وليهد فالمراد به هدي التمتع فهو واجب بشروط اتفق أصحابنا على

أربعة منها واختلفوا في ثلاثة أحد الأربعة أن يحرم بالعمرة في أشهر الحج

الثاني أن يحج من عامه الثالث أن يكون أفقيا لا من حاضري المسجد وحاضروه

أهل الحرم ومن كان منه على مسافة لا تقصر فيها الصلاة الرابع أن لا يعود

إلى الميقات لإحرام الحج وأما الثلاثة فأحدها نية التمتع والثاني كون الحج

والعمرة في سنة في شهر واحد الثالث كونهما عن شخص واحد والأصح أن هذه

الثلاثة لا تشترط والله أعلم وأما قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم فمن لم يجد هديا

فالمراد لم يجده هناك إما لعدم الهدي وإما لعدم ثمنه وإما لكونه يباع بأكثر

من ثمن المثل وإما لكونه موجودا لكنه لا يبيعه صاحبه ففي كل هذه الصور يكون

عادما للهدي فينتقل إلى الصوم سواء كان واجدا لثمنه في بلده أم لا وأما

قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم فمن لم يجد هديا فليصم ثلاثة أيام في الحج وسبعة

إذا رجع فهو موافق لنص كتاب الله تعالى ويجب صوم هذه الثلاثة قبل يوم النحر

ويجوز صوم يوم عرفة منها لكن الأولى أن يصوم الثلاثة قبله والأفضل أن لا

يصومها حتى يحرم بالحج بعد فراغه من العمرة فإن صامها بعد فراغه من العمرة

وقبل الإحرام بالحج أجزأه على المذهب الصحيح عندنا وإن صامها بعد الإحرام

بالعمرة وقبل فراغها لم يجزه على الصحيح فإن لم يصمها قبل يوم النحر وأراد

صومها في أيام التشريق ففي صحته قولان مشهوران للشافعي أشهرهما في المذهب

أنه لا يجوز وأصحهما من حيث
# 
# الدليل جوازه هذا تفصيل مذهبنا ووافقنا أصحاب مالك في أنه لا يجوز صوم

الثلاثة قبل الفراغ من العمرة وجوزه الثوري وأبو حنيفة ولو ترك صيامها حتى

مضى العيد والتشريق لزمه قضاؤها عندنا وقال أبو حنيفة يفوت صومها ويلزمه

الهدي إذا استطاعه والله أعلم وأما صوم السبعة فيجب إذا رجع وفي المراد

بالرجوع خلاف الصحيح في مذهبنا أنه إذا رجع إلى أهله وهذا هو الصواب لهذا

الحديث الصحيح الصريح والثاني إذا فرغ من الحج ورجع إلى مكة من منى وهذان

القولان للشافعي ومالك وبالثاني قال أبو حنيفة ولو لم يصم الثلاثة ولا

السبعة حتى عاد إلى وطنه لزمه صوم عشرة أيام وفي اشتراط التفريق بين

الثلاثة والسبعة إذا أراد صومها خلاف قيل لا يجب والصحيح أنه يجب التفريق

الواقع في الأداء وهو بأربعة أيام ومسافة الطريق بين مكة ووطنه والله أعلم

قوله (وطاف رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم حين قدم مكة واستلم الركن أول شيء

ثم حسب ثلاثة أطواف) من السبع ومشى أربعة أطواف إلى آخر الحديث فيه إثبات

طواف القدوم واستحباب الرمل فيه وأن الرمل هو الخبب وأنه  يصلي ركعتي الطواف

وأنهما يستحبان خلف المقام وقد سبق بيان هذا كله وسنذكره أيضا حيث ذكره

مسلم بعد هذا إن شاء الله تعالى

| باب بيان أن القارن لا يتحلل الا في وقت تحلل الحاج
# المفرد)
# [1229] فيه قول حفصة رضي الله عنها (يا رسول الله ما شأن الناس حلوا ولم

تحلل أنت من عمرتك قال إني لبدت رأسي وقلدت هديي فلا أحل حتى أنحر) وهذا

دليل للمذهب الصحيح المختار الذي قدمناه
# 
# واضحا بدلائله في الأبواب السابقة مرات أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان

قارنا في حجة الوداع فقولها من عمرتك إلى العمرة المضمومة إلى الحج وفيه أن

القارن لا يتحلل بالطواف والسعي ولا بد له في تحلله من الوقوف بعرفات

والرمي والحلق والطواف كما في الحاج المفرد وقد تأوله من يقول بالإفراد
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ف-س-خ (f-s-kh)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To annul, abrogate, or dissolve a contract; to cancel and replace with another.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Technical term for the dissolution of one ritual state (iḥrām) and its substitution with another, indicating a legal reconfiguration of intention.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) in legal contracts; metaphorical (majāz) here as the "unbinding" of the ḥajj iḥrām to ʿumrah.
- Root: ق-ر-ن (q-r-n)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To join, couple, or unite two things together.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The technical designation for the pilgrim who combines ḥajj and ʿumrah in a single iḥrām (qirān).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal joining of two rituals; metaphorical in the sense of a single continuous state of consecration.
- Root: ت-ل-ب-ي-د (t-l-b-y-d)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To mat or plaster the hair with gum or sticky substance to prevent lice and tangling.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): A physical act signifying the pilgrim's firm commitment to remain in iḥrām, precluding premature dissolution.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal action on the hair; metaphorical for the intention of persistence in the state of consecration.
- Sībawayh Rule: Rule of "al-Tarākhī" (التّراخي) — The particle "thumma" (ثُمَّ) denotes sequential delay and interval, not immediate succession, governing the legal ordering of rituals.
chapters.translation:
I say: The interpretation of this (hadith) is in accordance with its (the majority's) view. This interpretation is supported by his saying: "The people performed tamattu' with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ from ʿumrah to ḥajj." It is known that many of them, or most of them, had entered iḥrām for ḥajj first as individuals (mufridūn), and only later annulled it (fasakhūhu) in favor of ʿumrah, thereby becoming mutamattiʿūn. Thus, his saying "the people performed tamattu'" means at the end of the matter. And Allah knows best.

His saying ﷺ: "And whoever among you has not brought a sacrificial animal (hady), let him circumambulate the House (ṭawāf), and (perform the saʿy) between al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah, and let him shorten (his hair), and let him become free from iḥrām (taḥallul), then let him enter iḥrām for ḥajj, and let him bring a sacrificial animal. And whoever cannot find a sacrificial animal, let him fast three days during ḥajj and seven when he returns to his family."

As for his saying ﷺ: "Let him circumambulate the House, and (perform saʿy) between al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah, and let him shorten (his hair), and let him become free from iḥrām" — its meaning is: he performs the ṭawāf, the saʿy, and the shortening (of hair), and thereby he becomes free from iḥrām (ḥalāl). This is evidence that the shortening of hair or shaving (al-ḥalq) is a ritual act (nusuk) among the rituals of ḥajj. This is the correct view in our school (madhhab), and the majority of scholars (jumhūr al-ʿulamā') have stated it. It was also said that it is merely a permission to do what was prohibited (istibāḥat maḥẓūr) and not a ritual act — but this is weak (ḍaʿīf), and its clarification will come in its proper place, Allah willing.

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ only commanded the shortening (taqṣīr) and did not command shaving (ḥalq), even though shaving is superior, so that he would retain hair to shave during the ḥajj. For shaving in the taḥallul of ḥajj is superior to shaving in the taḥallul of ʿumrah.

As for his saying ﷺ: "And let him become free from iḥrām (wa-l-yaḥlil)" — its meaning is: he has become ḥalāl (free from iḥrām), so it is permissible for him to do what was prohibited during iḥrām, such as perfume, clothing, women, hunting, and other things.

As for his saying ﷺ: "Then let him enter iḥrām for ḥajj (thumma l-yuhill bi-l-ḥajj)" — its meaning is: he enters iḥrām for it at the time of departing to ʿArafāt, not that he enters iḥrām immediately after the taḥallul of ʿumrah. For this reason, he said "thumma" (then), which indicates delay and respite (al-tarākhī wa-l-muhlah).

As for his saying ﷺ: "And let him bring a sacrificial animal (wa-l-yuhdī)" — what is intended is the hady of tamattu'. It is obligatory under certain conditions. Our companions (aṣḥābunā) agreed upon four of them and differed on three. The four are: (1) that he enters iḥrām for ʿumrah during the months of ḥajj; (2) that he performs the ḥajj in the same year; (3) that he be from the distant horizon (ufuqī), not from the residents of the Sacred Mosque (ḥāḍirī al-masjid) — and its residents are the people of the Ḥaram and those who are at a distance from it where prayer is not shortened; (4) that he does not return to the mīqāt to enter iḥrām for ḥajj. As for the three (disputed conditions): (1) the intention (niyyah) of tamattu'; (2) that the ḥajj and ʿumrah be in one year, in one month; (3) that they be for one person. The most correct (al-aṣaḥḥ) view is that these three are not conditions. And Allah knows best.

As for his saying ﷺ: "And whoever cannot find a sacrificial animal (fa-man lam yajid hadyan)" — what is intended is that he does not find it there (at the place), either due to the absence of the animal, or the absence of its price, or because it is sold for more than its fair value (thaman al-mithl), or because it exists but its owner refuses to sell it. In all these cases, he is considered lacking the hady, so he shifts to fasting, whether he possesses its price in his own country or not.

As for his saying ﷺ: "And whoever cannot find a sacrificial animal, let him fast three days during ḥajj and seven when he returns" — this is in agreement with the text of the Book of Allah. It is obligatory to fast these three days before the Day of Sacrifice (yawm al-naḥr). It is permissible to fast the Day of ʿArafah among them, but the better (al-ūlā) is to fast the three days before it. The most virtuous (al-afḍal) is not to fast them until he enters iḥrām for ḥajj after completing his ʿumrah. If he fasts them after completing his ʿumrah and before entering iḥrām for ḥajj, it suffices him according to the correct view (al-madhhab al-ṣaḥīḥ) in our school. If he fasts them after entering iḥrām for ʿumrah and before completing it, it does not suffice him according to the correct view. If he does not fast them before the Day of Sacrifice and wishes to fast them during the Days of Tashrīq, there are two well-known opinions (qawlān mashhūrān) of al-Shāfiʿī: the more famous one in the school is that it is not permissible; the more correct one in terms of evidence is that it is permissible.

This is the detail of our school. The companions of Mālik agreed with us that it is not permissible to fast the three days before completing the ʿumrah. Al-Thawrī and Abū Ḥanīfah permitted it. If one abandons fasting them until the ʿĪd and the Tashrīq have passed, it is obligatory upon him to make them up (qaḍā') in our view. Abū Ḥanīfah said: their time is missed, and the hady becomes obligatory upon him if he can afford it. And Allah knows best.

As for fasting the seven days, it becomes obligatory when he returns. There is a difference of opinion regarding the meaning of "return" (al-rujūʿ). The correct view in our school is that it means when he returns to his family. This is the correct view due to this authentic and explicit hadith. The second view is: when he completes the ḥajj and returns to Mecca from Minā. These two views are attributed to al-Shāfiʿī and Mālik. Abū Ḥanīfah adopted the second view. If he does not fast the three nor the seven until he returns to his homeland, it is obligatory upon him to fast ten days. Regarding the condition of separating (tafrīq) between the three and the seven if he wishes to fast them, there is a difference of opinion. It was said that it is not obligatory. The correct view is that the separation that occurs in the performance (al-tafrīq al-wāqiʿ fī al-adā') is obligatory, which is four days, and the distance of the road between Mecca and his homeland. And Allah knows best.

His saying: "And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ circumambulated when he arrived in Mecca, and touched the Corner (al-rukn) first, then he walked briskly (ramala) in three circuits of the seven, and walked normally in four circuits" — to the end of the hadith. In this is the affirmation of the Ṭawāf of Arrival (ṭawāf al-qudūm), the recommendation of ramal (brisk walking) in it, that ramal is the quick pace (al-khabab), that he prays the two rakʿahs of ṭawāf, and that they are recommended behind the Station of Abraham (maqām Ibrāhīm). All of this has been previously explained, and we will also mention it where Muslim mentions it later, Allah willing.

| Chapter: The Clarification that the Qārin Does Not Dissolve His Iḥrām Except at the Time of the Ḥājj al-Mufrid's Dissolution

[1229] In it is the saying of Ḥafṣah, may Allah be pleased with her: "O Messenger of Allah, what is the matter with the people — they have dissolved their iḥrām, but you have not dissolved yours from your ʿumrah?" He said: "I have matted my hair (labbadtu ra'sī) and garlanded my sacrificial animal (qalladtu hadyī), so I will not dissolve my iḥrām until I slaughter (my sacrifice)."

This is evidence for the correct and chosen view (al-madhhab al-ṣaḥīḥ al-mukhtār) which we have presented clearly with its proofs in the preceding chapters multiple times: that the Prophet ﷺ was a qārin (combining ḥajj and ʿumrah) in the Farewell Pilgrimage (ḥajjat al-wadāʿ). Thus, her saying "from your ʿumrah" refers to the ʿumrah that was joined to the ḥajj. In this (hadith) is also (the proof) that the qārin does not dissolve his iḥrām through ṭawāf and saʿy alone, but rather, for his dissolution, he must stand at ʿArafāt (wuqūf), stone the jamarāt (ramy), shave (ḥalq), and perform ṭawāf, just as the ḥājj al-mufrid (the one performing ḥajj alone). And those who hold the view of ifrād (separate performance) have interpreted it (differently).

chapters.arabic_text:
تأويلات ضعيفة منها أنها أرادت بالعمرة الحج لأنهما يشتركان في كونهما قصدا

وقيل المراد بها الإحرام وقيل إنها ظنت أنه معتمر وقيل معنى من عمرتك أي

بعمرتك بأن تفسخ حجك إلى عمرة كما فعل غيرك وكل هذا ضعيف والصحيح ماسبق

وقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (لبدت رأسي وقلدت هديي) فيه استحباب التلبيد

وتقليد الهدي وهما سنتان بالاتفاق وقد سبق بيان هذا كله
#

| باب جواز التحلل بالاحصار وجواز القران واقتصار
# (القارن على طواف واحد وسعى واحد)
# [1230] قوله (عن نافع أن عبد الله بن عمر خرج في الفتنة معتمرا وقال إن

صددت عن البيت صنعنا كما صنعنا مع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فخرج فأهل

بعمرة وسار حتى إذا ظهر على البيداء التفت إلى أصحابه فقال ما أمرهما إلا

واحد أشهدكم أني قد أوجبت الحج مع العمرة فخرج حتى إذا جاء البيت طاف سبعا

وبين الصفا والمروة سبعا لم يزد ورأى أنه مجزئ عنه وأهدى) في هذا الحديث

جواز القران وجواز إدخال الحج على العمرة قبل الطواف وهو مذهبنا ومذهب

جماهير العلماء وسبق بيان المسألة وفيه جواز التحلل بالإحصار وأما قوله

(أشهدكم) فإنما قاله ليعلمه من أراد الاقتداء به  فلهذا قال أشهدكم ولم يكتف

بالنية مع أنها كافية في صحة الإحرام وقوله (ما أمرهما إلا واحد) يعني في

جواز التحلل منهما بالإحصار وفيه صحة القياس والعمل به وأن الصحابة رضي

الله عنهم كانوا يستعملونه فلهذا قاس الحج على العمرة لأن النبي صلى الله

عليه وسلم إنما تحلل من الإحصار عام الحديبية من إحرامه بالعمرة وحدها وفيه

أن القارن يقتصر على طواف واحد وسعي واحد هو مذهبنا ومذهب الجمهور وخالف

فيه أبو حنيفة وطائفة وسبقت المسألة وأما قوله (صنعنا كما صنعنا مع رسول

الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فخرج فأهل بعمرة) فالصواب في معناه أنه أراد إن

صددت وحصرت
# 
# تحللت كما تحللنا عام الحديبية مع النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وقال القاضي

يحتمل أنه أراد أهل بعمرة كما أهل النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بعمرة في العام

الذي أحصر قال ويحتمل أنه أراد الأمرين قال وهو الأظهر وليس هو بظاهر كما

ادعاه بل الصحيح الذي يقتضيه سياق كلامه ما قدمناه والله أعلم قوله (حتى

أهل منهما بحجة يوم النحر) معناه حتى أهل منهما يوم النحر بعمل حجة مفردة
#

| باب في الافراد والقران
# [1231] قوله (عن بن عمر رضي الله عنه قال أهللنا مع رسول الله صلى الله

عليه وسلم بالحج مفردا) وفي رواية أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أهل

بالحج مفردا هذا موافق للروايات السابقة عن جابر وعائشة وبن عباس وغيرهم أن

النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أحرم بالحج مفردا وفيه بيان أن الرواية السابقة

قريبا عن بن عمر التي أخبر فيها بالقران متأولة وسبق بيان تأوليها
# [1232] قوله (عن أنس سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول لبيك عمرة

وحجا) يحتج به من يقول بالقران وقد قدمنا أن الصحيح المختار في حجة النبي

صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه كان في أول إحرامه مفردا ثم أدخل العمرة على الحج

فصار قارنا وجمعنا بين الأحاديث أحسن جمع فحديث بن عمر هنا محمول على أول

إحرامه صلى الله عليه وسلم وحديث  أنس محمول على أواخره وأثنائه وكأنه
# 
# لم يسمعه أولا ولا بد من هذا التأويل أو نحوه لتكون رواية أنس موافقة

لرواية الاكثرين كما سبق والله أعلم

| باب استحباب طواف القدوم للحاج والسعى بعده
# [1233] قوله (عن وبرة) هو بفتح الباء قوله (كنت جالسا عند بن عمر فجاءه

رجل فقال أيصلح لي أن أطوف قبل أن آتي الموقف فقال نعم فقال فان بن عباس

يقول لا تطف بالبيت حتى تأتي الموقف فقال بن عمر فقد حج رسول الله صلى الله

عليه وسلم فطاف بالبيت قبل أن يأتي الموقف فبقول رسول الله صلى الله عليه

وسلم أحق أن تأخذ أو بقول بن عباس إن كنت صادقا) هذا الذي قاله بن عمر هو

إثبات طواف القدوم للحاج وهو مشروع قبل الوقوف بعرفات وبهذا الذي قاله بن

عمر قال العلماء كافة سوى بن عباس وكلهم يقولون إنه سنة ليس بواجب إلا بعض

أصحابنا ومن وافقه فيقولون واجب يجبر تركه بالدم والمشهور أنه سنة ليس

بواجب ولا دم في تركه فإن وقف بعرفات قبل طواف القدوم فات فإن طاف بعد ذلك

بنية طواف القدوم لم يقع عن طواف القدوم بل يقع عن طواف الإفاضة إن لم يكن

طاف للإفاضة فإن كان
# 
# طاف للإفاضة وقع الثاني تطوعا لا عن القدوم ولطواف القدوم أسماء طواف

القدوم والقادم والورود والوارد والتحية وليس في العمرة طواف قدوم بل

الطواف الذي يفعله فيها يقع ركنا لها حتى لو نوى به طواف القدوم وقع ركنا

ولغت نيته كما لو كان عليه حجة واجبة فنوى حجة تطوع فإنها تقع واجبة والله

أعلم وأما قوله إن كنت صادقا فمعناه إن كنت صادقا في إسلامك واتباعك رسول

الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فلا تعدل عن فعله وطريقته إلى قول بن عباس وغيره

والله أعلم قوله (رأيناه قد فتنته الدنيا) هكذا في كثير من الأصول فتنته

الدنيا وفي كثير منها أو أكثرها أفتنته وكذا نقله القاضي عن رواية الأكثرين
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ض-ع-ف (ḍa-ʿa-f)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning is feebleness, frailty, or weakness in a thing; a "weak" interpretation (taʼwīl ḍaʿīf) is one lacking firm evidentiary support.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In scholarly discourse, it denotes an exegetical opinion that fails to meet the epistemic standard of certainty (yaqīn) or strong probability (ghalabat al-ẓann).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense is physical weakness; metaphorically applied to arguments and interpretations that are unsound or untenable.
- Sībawayh Rule: Rule of ʿAṭf al-Bayān (Appositional Clarification) — where a following noun clarifies the preceding one without a conjunction, as in "تأويلات ضعيفة منها..." where the subsequent clauses specify the categories of those weak interpretations.
chapters.translation:
I say: Among the weak interpretations [of ʿĀʼishah's statement] is that she intended by "ʿumrah" the ḥajj, because both share in being a purposeful journey (qaṣd). And it was said: what she meant was the state of iḥrām. And it was said: she thought that he was performing ʿumrah. And it was said: the meaning of "from your ʿumrah" (min ʿumratik) is "by your ʿumrah," i.e., that you dissolve your ḥajj into an ʿumrah, as others did. All of this is weak, and the correct [interpretation] is what has preceded.

And his statement, peace and blessings be upon him: «I have matted my hair (labbadtu raʼsī) and garlanded my sacrificial animal (qalladtu hadyī)» — in this is the recommendation (istiḥbāb) of matting the hair and garlanding the sacrificial animal, and both are Sunnah by consensus (ittifāq). The clarification of all this has already preceded.

---

CHAPTER: On the Permissibility of Disengagement (Taḥallul) due to Obstruction (Iḥṣār), and the Permissibility of Qirān, and that the Qārin Limits Himself to a Single Ṭawāf and a Single Saʿy.

[1230] His statement (on the authority of Nāfiʿ that ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar set out during the turmoil (fitnah) for ʿumrah and said: "If I am obstructed from the House, we shall do as we did with the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him." So he set out and entered iḥrām for ʿumrah, and traveled until, when he appeared at al-Baydāʼ, he turned to his companions and said: "Their command is but one — I call you to witness that I have made the ḥajj obligatory together with the ʿumrah." So he set out until, when he came to the House, he performed seven circuits (ṭawāf) and seven [circuits] between al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah, adding nothing beyond that, and he deemed it sufficient for him, and he offered a sacrificial animal (ahdā).)

In this ḥadīth is the permissibility of Qirān and the permissibility of inserting the ḥajj upon the ʿumrah before the ṭawāf — and this is our school (madhhab) and the school of the majority of scholars, and the clarification of the issue has preceded. In it also is the permissibility of disengagement (taḥallul) due to obstruction (iḥṣār). As for his statement «I call you to witness» (ushhidukum), he only said it to inform whoever wished to follow his example. For this reason he said "I call you to witness" and did not content himself with the intention (niyyah), even though intention suffices for the validity of iḥrām. And his statement «Their command is but one» means: regarding the permissibility of disengagement from both of them due to obstruction. In it is the validity of analogical reasoning (qiyās) and acting upon it, and that the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, used to employ it. For this reason he analogized the ḥajj to the ʿumrah, because the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, only disengaged from obstruction in the year of al-Ḥudaybiyyah from his iḥrām for ʿumrah alone. In it also is that the Qārin limits himself to a single ṭawāf and a single saʿy — this is our school and the school of the majority. Abū Ḥanīfah and a group differed on this, and the issue has preceded.

As for his statement «we shall do as we did with the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, so he set out and entered iḥrām for ʿumrah» — the correct [understanding] of its meaning is that he intended: "If I am obstructed and detained (ḥuṣirtu), I shall disengage as we disengaged in the year of al-Ḥudaybiyyah with the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him." And al-Qāḍī said: It is possible that he intended: "He entered iḥrām for ʿumrah just as the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, entered iḥrām for ʿumrah in the year in which he was obstructed." He said: And it is possible that he intended both matters. He said: And this is the more apparent (aẓhar). But it is not as apparent as he claimed. Rather, the correct [view], which the context of his speech necessitates, is what we have presented. And Allah knows best.

His statement «until he entered iḥrām from both of them for ḥajj on the Day of Sacrifice (yawm al-naḥr)» — its meaning is: until he entered iḥrām from both of them on the Day of Sacrifice with the action of an isolated ḥajj (ḥajj mufradah).

---

CHAPTER: On Ifrād and Qirān.

[1231] His statement (on the authority of Ibn ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "We entered iḥrām with the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, for ḥajj alone (mufradan)"). And in another narration: "The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, entered iḥrām for ḥajj alone." This is consistent with the previous narrations from Jābir, ʿĀʼishah, Ibn ʿAbbās, and others, that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, entered iḥrām for ḥajj alone. In it is a clarification that the earlier narration from Ibn ʿUmar, in which he reported Qirān, is subject to interpretation (mutāʼawwalah), and the clarification of its interpretation has preceded.

[1232] His statement (on the authority of Anas: "I heard the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, say: «Labbayka ʿumratan wa ḥajjan» (Here I am, for ʿumrah and ḥajj)") — this is cited as evidence by those who affirm Qirān. We have already stated that the correct and chosen [view] regarding the ḥajj of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, is that at the beginning of his iḥrām he was mufrid (performing ifrād), then he inserted the ʿumrah upon the ḥajj, becoming a Qārin. And we have reconciled the ḥadīths in the best manner of reconciliation. Thus, the ḥadīth of Ibn ʿUmar here is carried upon the beginning of his iḥrām, peace and blessings be upon him, and the ḥadīth of Anas is carried upon its later stages and during it — as if he had not heard him at first. This interpretation or something similar is necessary, so that the narration of Anas may accord with the narration of the majority, as has preceded. And Allah knows best.

---

CHAPTER: On the Recommendation of the Ṭawāf of Arrival (Ṭawāf al-Qudūm) for the Pilgrim, and the Saʿy After It.

[1233] His statement (on the authority of Wabarah) — it is with the fatḥah on the bāʼ. His statement: ("I was sitting with Ibn ʿUmar when a man came to him and said: 'Is it permissible for me to perform ṭawāf before I come to the standing-place (al-mawqif)?' He said: 'Yes.' He said: 'But Ibn ʿAbbās says: Do not perform ṭawāf of the House until you come to the standing-place.' Ibn ʿUmar said: 'The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, performed the ḥajj and performed ṭawāf of the House before coming to the standing-place. So is the statement of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, more deserving for you to take, or the statement of Ibn ʿAbbās — if you are truthful?'")

What Ibn ʿUmar said here is an affirmation of the Ṭawāf of Arrival for the pilgrim, and it is legislated (mashrūʿ) before standing at ʿArafāt. And upon what Ibn ʿUmar said, all scholars agree, except Ibn ʿAbbās. And all of them say it is a Sunnah, not an obligation (wājib), except some of our companions and those who agree with them, who say it is an obligation whose omission is compensated by a sacrificial animal (dam). The well-known [view] is that it is a Sunnah, not an obligation, and there is no dam for omitting it. If one stands at ʿArafāt before the Ṭawāf of Arrival, then it is missed. If he performs ṭawāf after that with the intention of the Ṭawāf of Arrival, it does not count as the Ṭawāf of Arrival; rather, it counts as the Ṭawāf of Ifāḍah if he has not performed the Ṭawāf of Ifāḍah. But if he had performed the Ṭawāf of Ifāḍah, then the second one falls as voluntary (taṭawwuʿ), not for the Arrival. The Ṭawāf of Arrival has several names: Ṭawāf al-Qudūm, al-Qādim, al-Wurūd, al-Wārid, and al-Taḥiyyah (greeting). There is no Ṭawāf of Arrival in the ʿumrah; rather, the ṭawāf performed in it falls as a pillar (rukn) of it, such that even if one intends by it the Ṭawāf of Arrival, it falls as a pillar and his intention is nullified — just as if one owed an obligatory ḥajj and intended a voluntary ḥajj, it would fall as obligatory. And Allah knows best.

As for his statement «if you are truthful» — its meaning is: "If you are truthful in your Islam and your following of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, then do not turn away from his action and his way to the statement of Ibn ʿAbbās and others." And Allah knows best.

His statement «we saw that the world had tempted him» (raʼaynāhu qad fatanat-hu al-dunyā) — thus it appears in many of the manuscripts: "fatant-hu al-dunyā" (the world tempted him), and in many of them, or most of them: "aftanat-hu" (it seduced him). Al-Qāḍī likewise transmitted it from the narration of the majority.

chapters.title_en: The Commentary on Sahih Muslim — Section 507: On the Rites of ʿUmrah and Ḥajj, and the Non-Dissolution of Iḥrām by Ṭawāf Alone
chapters.arabic_text:
وهما لغتان صحيحتان فتن وأفتن والأولى أصح  وأشهر وبها جاء القرآن وأنكر

الأصمعي أفتن ومعنى قولهم فتنته الدنيا لأنه تولى البصرة والولايات محل

الخطر والفتنة وأما بن عمر فلم يتول شيئا وأما قول بن عمر وأينا لم تفتنه

الدنيا فهذا من زهده وتواضعه وإنصافه وفي بعض النسخ وأينا أو أيكم وفي

بعضها وأينا أو قال وأيكم وكله صحيح

| باب بيان أن المحرم بعمرة لا يتحلل بالطواف قبل
# السعى)
# (وان المحرم بحج لا يتحلل بطواف القدوم وكذلك القارن)
# [1234] قوله (سألنا بن عمر رضي الله عنه عن رجل قدم بعمرة فطاف بالبيت

ولم يطف بين الصفا
# 
# والمروة أيأتي امرأته فقال قدم رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فطاف بالبيت

سبعا وصلى خلف المقام ركعتين وبين الصفا والمروة سبعا وقد كان لكم في رسول

الله أسوة حسنة) معناه لا يحل له ذلك لأن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لم

يتحلل من عمرته حتى طاف وسعى فتجب متابعته والاقتداء به وهذا الحكم الذي

قاله بن عمر هو مذهب العلماء كافة وهو أن المعتمر لا يتحلل إلا بالطواف

والسعي والحلق الا ما حكاه القاضي عياض عن بن عباس وإسحاق بن راهويه أنه

يتحلل بعد الطواف وإن لم يسع وهذا ضعيف مخالف للسنة
# [1235] قوله (فتصداني الرجل) أي تعرض لي
# 
# هكذا هو في جميع النسخ تصداني بالنون والأشهر في اللغة تصدى لي قوله (أول

شيء بدأ به حين قدم مكة أنه توضأ ثم طاف بالبيت) فيه دليل لإثبات الوضوء

للطواف لأن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فعله ثم قال صلى الله عليه وسلم

لتأخذوا عني مناسككم وقد أجمعت الأئمة على أنه يشرع الوضوء للطواف ولكن

اختلفوا في أنه واجب وشرط لصحته أم لا فقال مالك والشافعي وأحمد والجمهور

هو شرط لصحة الطواف وقال أبو حنيفة مستحب ليس بشرط واحتج الجمهور بهذا

الحديث ووجه الدلالة أن هذا الحديث مع حديث خذوا عني مناسككم يقتضيان أن

الطواف واجب لأن كل ما فعله هو داخل في المناسك فقد أمرنا بأخذ المناسك وفي

حديث بن عباس في الترمذي  وغيره أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال الطواف

بالبيت صلاة إلا أن الله أباح فيه الكلام ولكن رفعه ضعيف والصحيح عند

الحفاظ أنه موقوف على بن عباس وتحصل به الدلالة مع أنه موقوف لأنه قول

لصحابي انتشر وإذا انتشر قول الصحابي بلا مخالفة كان حجة على الصحيح قوله

(ثم لم يكن غيره) وكذا قال فيما بعده ولم يكن غيره هكذا هو في جميع النسخ
# 
# غيره بالغين المعجمة والياء قال القاضي عياض كذا هو في جميع النسخ قال

وهو تصحيف وصوابه ثم لم تكن عمرة بضم العين المهملة وبالميم وكان السائل

لعروة إنما سأله عن نسخ الحج إلى العمرة على مذهب من رأى ذلك واحتج بأمر

النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لهم بذلك في حجة الوداع فأعلمه عروة أن النبي صلى

الله عليه وسلم لم يفعل ذلك بنفسه ولا من جاء بعده هذا كلام القاضي قلت هذا

الذي قاله من أن قول غيره تصحيف ليس كما قال بل هو صحيح في الرواية وصحيح

في المعنى لأن قوله غيره يتناول العمرة وغيرها ويكون تقدير الكلام ثم حج

أبو بكر فكان أول شيء بدأ به الطواف بالبيت ثم لم يكن غيره أي لم يغير الحج

ولم ينقله وينسخه إلى غيره لا عمرة ولا قران والله أعلم قوله (ثم حججت مع

أبي الزبير بن العوام) أي مع والده الزبير فقوله الزبير بدل من أبي قوله

(ولا أحد ممن مضى ما كانوا يبدءون شيئا حين يضعون أقدامهم أول من الطواف

بالبيت ثم لا يحلون) فيه أن المحرم بالحج إذا قدم مكة ينبغي له أن يبدأ

بطواف القدوم ولا يفعل شيئا قبله ولا يصلي تحية المسجد بل أول شيء يصنعه

الطواف وهذا بطواف القدوم ولا يفعل شيئا قبله ولا يصلي تحية المسجد بل أول

شئ يصنعه الطواف وهذا كله متفق عليه عندنا وقوله يضعون أقدامهم يعني يصلون

مكة وقوله ثم لا يحلون فيه التصريح بأنه لا يجوز التحلل بمجرد طواف القدوم

كما سبق قوله (وقد  أخبرتني أمي أنها أقبلت هي وأختها والزبير وفلان وفلان

بعمرة قط فلما مسحوا الركن حلوا) فقولها مسحوا المراد بالماسحين من سوى

عائشة وإلا فعائشة لم تمسح الركن قبل الوقوف بعرفات في حجة الوداع بل كانت

قارنة ومنعها الحيض من الطواف قبل يوم النحر وهكذا قول أسماء بعد هذا

اعتمرت أنا وأختي عائشة والزبير وفلان وفلان فلما مسحنا البيت أحللنا ثم

أهللنا بالحج
# 
# المراد به أيضا من سوى عائشة وهكذا تأوله القاضي عياض والمراد الإخبار عن

حجتهم مع النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم حجة الوداع على الصفة التي ذكرت في أول

الحديث وكان المذكورون سوى عائشة محرمين بالعمرة وهي عمرة الفسخ التي فسخوا

الحج إليها وإنما لم تستثن عائشة لشهرة قصتها قال القاضي عياض وقيل يحتمل

أن أسماء أشارت إلى عمرة عائشة التي فعلتها بعد الحج مع أخيها عبد الرحمن

من التنعيم قال القاضي وأما قول من قال يحتمل أنها أرادت في غير حجة الوداع

فخطأ لأن في الحديث التصريح بأن ذلك كان في حجة الوداع هذا كلام القاضي

وذكر مسلم بعد هذه الرواية رواية إسحاق بن إبراهيم وفيها أن أسماء قالت
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ف ت ن (f-t-n)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning is trial, affliction, or seduction—derived from the smelting of gold in fire to test purity (fitnat al-dhahab).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological usage, fitnah denotes a divinely ordained trial that tests faith, often involving worldly allurements that distract from obedience.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) refers to burning or testing; metaphorical (majāz) applies to any tribulation that exposes one's inner state, including political office and wealth.
- Root: ح ل ل (ḥ-l-l)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning is to untie, loosen, or become permissible; in pilgrimage context, it signifies exiting the state of iḥrām.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Technically, taḥallul is the lawful cessation of pilgrimage prohibitions, contingent upon completing prescribed rites.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal is untying a knot; metaphorical is the removal of ritual restrictions.
- Root: س ع ي (s-ʿ-y)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning is to strive, run, or exert effort; in pilgrimage, it denotes the ritual walking between Ṣafā and Marwah.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In Quranic usage (e.g., {«وَأَن لَّيْسَ لِلْإِنسَانِ إِلَّا مَا سَعَىٰ»}), it signifies earnest endeavor toward a goal, here the ritual act.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal is physical exertion; metaphorical is spiritual striving in obedience.
- Sībawayh Rule: Rule of Badal (Substitution) — In the phrase "مع أبي الزبير بن العوام" (with my father al-Zubayr ibn al-ʿAwwām), the word "الزبير" functions as a substitute (badal) for "أبي" (my father), clarifying the referent without repeating the governing preposition.
chapters.translation:
I say: Both forms—"fatantu" and "aftantu"—are valid and correct in the Arabic language, though the first is more authentic and more widely attested, and it is the form in which the Qur'an was revealed. Al-Aṣmaʿī rejected the form "aftantu." The meaning of their statement, "the world has tried him (fatanathu al-dunyā)," is because he (i.e., ʿUthmān, may Allah be pleased with him) assumed the governorship of Basrah and other administrative posts—positions that are places of danger and trial (fitnah). As for Ibn ʿUmar, he never assumed any such office. Regarding Ibn ʿUmar's statement, "Which of us has not been tried by the world?"—this stems from his asceticism (zuhd), humility, and fairness. In some manuscript copies, the wording is "wa-ayyunā" or "wa-ayyukum" (which of us), and in others "wa-ayyunā" or "qāla wa-ayyukum"—all of these are correct.

[Chapter: The Explanation that One in Iḥrām for ʿUmrah Does Not Dissolve by Ṭawāf Alone Before Saʿy, and that One in Iḥrām for Ḥajj Does Not Dissolve by the Ṭawāf of Arrival, and Likewise the Qārin (One Performing Ḥajj and ʿUmrah Jointly)]

[1234] His statement (i.e., the narrator's): "We asked Ibn ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, about a man who arrived for ʿUmrah, circumambulated the House (ṭāfa bi-al-bayt), but did not walk between Ṣafā and Marwah—may he approach his wife?" He replied: "The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, arrived, circumambulated the House seven times, prayed two units behind the Station of Abraham (maqām Ibrāhīm), and walked between Ṣafā and Marwah seven times. Indeed, you have in the Messenger of Allah an excellent example {«لَقَدْ كَانَ لَكُمْ فِي رَسُولِ اللَّهِ أُسْوَةٌ حَسَنَةٌ»}." Its meaning is that it is not permissible for him to do so, because the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, did not dissolve from his ʿUmrah until he had performed both Ṭawāf and Saʿy. Thus, following him and emulating him is obligatory. This ruling stated by Ibn ʿUmar is the consensus of all scholars (madhhab al-ʿulamāʾ kāffah): that the one performing ʿUmrah does not dissolve except by Ṭawāf, Saʿy, and shaving (ḥalq). The only exception is what Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās and Isḥāq ibn Rāhawayh—that he dissolves after Ṭawāf even without Saʿy. This view is weak (ḍaʿīf) and contradicts the Sunnah.

[1235] His statement: "The man confronted me (fa-taṣaddānī)"—meaning he came toward me and presented himself to me. This is how it appears in all manuscript copies: "taṣaddānī" with a nūn. The more famous form in the language is "taṣaddā lī" (he confronted me). His statement: "The first thing he did upon arriving in Mecca was that he performed ablution (tawaddaʾa), then circumambulated the House"—in this is evidence for the prescription of ablution for Ṭawāf, because the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, did it, and then he said, peace and blessings be upon him: "Take from me your rites of pilgrimage (khudhū ʿannī manāsikakum)." The imams have unanimously agreed that ablution is legislated (yushraʿ) for Ṭawāf, but they differed on whether it is obligatory and a condition for its validity or not. Mālik, al-Shāfiʿī, Aḥmad, and the majority (al-jumhūr) held that it is a condition for the validity of Ṭawāf. Abū Ḥanīfah held that it is recommended (mustaḥabb) but not a condition. The majority adduced this ḥadīth as proof, and the indication (wajh al-dalālah) is that this ḥadīth, combined with the ḥadīth "Take from me your rites," entails that Ṭawāf is obligatory, because everything he did is included in the rites (manāsik), and we have been commanded to take the rites from him. In the ḥadīth of Ibn ʿAbbās in al-Tirmidhī and others, the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Ṭawāf around the House is prayer (ṣalāh), except that Allah has permitted speech in it." However, its elevation (rafʿuhu) to the Prophet is weak, and the correct view according to the ḥadīth scholars (ḥuffāẓ) is that it is stopped (mawqūf) at Ibn ʿAbbās. Nevertheless, it still provides evidence even though it is mawqūf, because it is the statement of a Companion that became widespread (intashara), and when a Companion's statement spreads without opposition, it is a proof (ḥujjah) according to the correct view.

His statement: "Then there was nothing after that (thumma lam yakun ghayruhu)"—and likewise he said in what follows: "and there was nothing after that (wa-lam yakun ghayruhu)." This is how it appears in all manuscript copies: "ghayruhu" with a ghayn (unpointed) and a yāʾ. Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ said: "This is how it is in all copies." He said: "This is a scribal corruption (taṣḥīf), and the correct reading is 'thumma lam takun ʿumrah' (then there was no ʿUmrah) with a ḍammah on the ʿayn (unpointed) and a mīm. The questioner had asked ʿUrwah about abrogating Ḥajj into ʿUmrah (naskh al-ḥajj ilā al-ʿumrah), according to the view of those who held this, adducing the Prophet's command to them to do so during the Farewell Pilgrimage. ʿUrwah informed him that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, did not do this himself, nor did anyone after him." This is the statement of Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ.

I say: What he stated—that the wording "ghayruhu" is a scribal corruption—is not as he said. Rather, it is correct in transmission (ṣaḥīḥ fī al-riwāyah) and correct in meaning (ṣaḥīḥ fī al-maʿnā), because his statement "ghayruhu" (other than it) encompasses ʿUmrah and other things. The estimated meaning of the speech is: "Then Abū Bakr performed Ḥajj, and the first thing he began with was Ṭawāf of the House, then there was nothing other than it (lam yakun ghayruhu)"—i.e., he did not change the Ḥajj, nor transfer it, nor abrogate it into something else—neither ʿUmrah nor Qirān (joint performance). And Allah knows best.

His statement: "Then I performed Ḥajj with my father al-Zubayr ibn al-ʿAwwām"—meaning with his father al-Zubayr. Thus, "al-Zubayr" is a substitute (badal) for "my father" (abī).

His statement: "And no one among those who came before—they would not begin anything when they placed their feet (first) other than Ṭawāf of the House, then they would not dissolve (lā yaḥillūn)"—in this is that the one in iḥrām for Ḥajj, upon arriving in Mecca, should begin with the Ṭawāf of Arrival (ṭawāf al-qudūm), doing nothing before it, and should not pray the mosque greeting prayer (taḥiyyat al-masjid). Rather, the first thing he does is Ṭawāf. This all is agreed upon in our school (madhhab). His statement "they placed their feet" means they arrived in Mecca. His statement "then they would not dissolve" contains an explicit declaration that dissolution is not permissible by mere Ṭawāf of Arrival, as previously mentioned.

His statement (i.e., ʿĀʾishah's): "My mother informed me that she, her sister, al-Zubayr, so-and-so, and so-and-so set out for ʿUmrah, and when they wiped the Corner (masaḥū al-rukn), they dissolved." Her statement "they wiped" refers to those who wiped other than ʿĀʾishah, for ʿĀʾishah herself did not wipe the Corner before standing at ʿArafāt during the Farewell Pilgrimage. Rather, she was a qārinah (performing Ḥajj and ʿUmrah jointly), and menstruation (ḥayḍ) prevented her from Ṭawāf before the Day of Sacrifice (yawm al-naḥr). Likewise, the statement of Asmāʾ after this: "I performed ʿUmrah, myself, my sister ʿĀʾishah, al-Zubayr, so-and-so, and so-and-so, and when we wiped the House (masaḥnā al-bayt), we dissolved, then we assumed iḥrām for Ḥajj"—the intended meaning here also is those other than ʿĀʾishah. This is how Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ interpreted it. The intent is to report their pilgrimage with the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, during the Farewell Pilgrimage, in the manner described at the beginning of the ḥadīth. Those mentioned, other than ʿĀʾishah, were in iḥrām for ʿUmrah—the ʿUmrah of Abrogation (ʿumrat al-faskh) to which they had converted their Ḥajj. ʿĀʾishah was not excepted only because her story was well-known (shuhrah). Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ said: "And it is said that it is possible that Asmāʾ referred to ʿĀʾishah's ʿUmrah that she performed after the Ḥajj with her brother ʿAbd al-Raḥmān from al-Tanʿīm." Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ said: "As for the statement of those who said it is possible she meant something other than the Farewell Pilgrimage, it is an error, because the ḥadīth explicitly states that this occurred during the Farewell Pilgrimage." This is the statement of Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ. Muslim mentioned after this narration the narration of Isḥāq ibn Ibrāhīm, in which Asmāʾ said...

chapters.title_en: The Commentary on Sahih Muslim — Section 508: On the Tamattuʿ of the Pilgrim, the Prohibition of Certain Acts in Iḥrām, and Related Rulings
chapters.arabic_text:
خرجنا محرمين فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم من كان معه هدي فليقم على

إحرامه ومن لم يكن معه هدي فليحلل فلم يكن معي هدي فحللت وكان مع الزبير

هدي فلم يحل فهذا تصريح بأن الزبير لم يتحلل في حجة الوداع قبل يوم النحر

فيجب استثناؤه مع عائشة أو يكون إحرامه بالعمرة وتحلله منها في غير حجة

الوداع والله أعلم وقولها فلما مسحوا الركن حلوا هذا متأول عن ظاهره لأن

الركن هو الحجر الأسود ومسحه يكون في أول الطواف ولا يحصل التحلل بمجرد

مسحه بإجماع المسلمين وتقديره فلما مسحوا الركن وأتموا طوافهم وسعيهم

وحلقوا أو قصروا أحلوا ولا بد من تقدير هذا المحذوف وإنما حذفته للعلم به

وقد أجمعوا على أنه لا يتحلل قبل إتمام الطواف ومذهبنا ومذهب الجمهور أنه

لا بد أيضا من السعي بعده ثم الحلق  أو التقصير وشذ بعض السلف فقال السعي

ليس بواجب ولا حجة
# 
# لهذا القائل في هذا الحديث لأن ظاهره غير مراد بالإجماع فيتعين تأويله

كما ذكرنا ليكون موافقا لباقي الأحاديث والله أعلم قولها (عن الزبير فقال

قومي عني فقالت أتخشى أن أثب عليك) إنما أمرها بالقيام مخافة من عارض قد

يندر منه كلمس بشهوة أو نحوه فإن اللمس بشهوة حرام في الإحرام فاحتاط لنفسه

بمباعدتها من حيث إنها زوجة متحللة تطمع بها النفس قوله (استرخي عني استرخي

عني) هكذا هو في النسخ مرتين أي تباعدي
# [1237] قوله (مرت بالحجون) هو بفتح الحاء وضم الجيم وهو من حرم مكة وهو

الجبل المشرف على مسجد الحرس بأعلى مكة على يمينك وأنت مصعد عند المحصب

قولها (خفاف الحقائب) جمع حقيبة وهو
# 
# كل ما حمل في مؤخر الرحل والقتب ومنه احتقب فلان كذا
# [1239] قوله عن مسلم القري هو بقاف مضمومة ثم راء مشددة قال السمعاني هو

منسوب إلى بني قرة حي من عبد القيس قال وقال بن ماكولا هذا ثم قال وقيل بل

لأنه كان ينزل فنظره قرة
#

| باب جواز العمرة في اشهر الحج
# [1240] قوله كانوا يرون العمرة في أشهر الحج من أفجر الفجور في الأرض

الضمير في كانوا يعود إلى الجاهلية قوله ويجعلون المحرم صفر هكذا هو في

النسخ صفر من غير ألف بعد الراء وهو منصوب مصروف بلا خلاف وكان ينبغي أن

يكتب بالألف وسواء كتب بالألف أم بحذفها لا بد من قراءته هنا منصوبا لأنه

مصروف قال العلماء المراد الإخبار عن النسيء الذي كانوا يفعلونه وكانوا

يسمون المحرم صفرا ويحلونه وينسئون المحرم أي يؤخرون تحريمه إلى ما بعد صفر

لئلا يتوالى عليهم ثلاثة أشهر محرمة تضيق عليهم أمورهم من الغارة وغيرها

فأضلهم الله تعالى في ذلك فقال تعالى إنما النسيء زيادة في الكفر الآية

قوله (ويقولون إذا برأ الدبر) يعنون دبر ظهور الإبل بعد انصرافها من الحج

فإنها كانت تدبر بالسير عليها للحج قوله (وعفا الأثر) أي درس وأمحي والمراد

أثر الإبل وغيرها  في سيرها عفا أثرها لطول مرور الأيام هذا هو المشهور وقال

الخطابي المراد أثر الدبر والله أعلم وهذه الألفاظ تقرأ
# 
# كلها ساكنة الآخر ويوقف عليها لأن مرادهم السجع قوله (عن أبي العالية

البراء) هو بتشديد الراء لأنه كان يبري النبل قوله (حدثنا أبو داود

المباركي) هو سليمان بن محمد ويقال سليمان بن داود وأبو محمد المباركي بفتح

الراء منسوب إلى المبارك وهي بليدة بقرب واسط بينها وبين بغداد وهي على طرف

دجلة قوله (صلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم الصبح بذي طوى
# 
# هو بفتح الطاء وضمها وكسرها ثلاث لغات حكاهن القاضي وغيره الأصح الأشهر

الفتح ولم يذكر الأصمعي وآخرون غيره وهو مقصور منون وهو واد معروف بقرب مكة

قال القاضي ووقع لبعض الرواة في البخاري بالمد وكذا ذكره ثابت وفي هذا

الحديث دليل لمن قال يستحب للمحرم دخول مكة نهارا لا ليلا وهو أصح الوجهين

لأصحابنا وبه قال بن عمر وعطاء والنخعي وإسحاق بن راهويه وبن المنذر

والثاني دخولها ليلا ونهارا سواء لا فضيلة لأحدهما على الآخر وهو قول

القاضي أبى الطيب والماوردي وبن الصباغ والعبدرى من أصحابنا وبه قال طاوس

والثوري وقالت عائشة وسعيد بن جبير وعمر بن عبد العزيز يستحب دخولها ليلا

وهو أفضل من النهار والله أعلم

| باب اشعار الهدى وتقليده عند الاحرام
# [1243] قوله (صلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم الظهر بذي الحليفة ثم دعا

بناقته فأشعرها في صفحة سنامها
# 
# الأيمن وسلت الدم وقلدها نعلين ثم ركب راحلته فلما استوت به على البيداء

أهل بالحج) أما الإشعار فهو أن يجرحها في صفحة سنامها اليمنى بحربة أو سكين

أو حديدة أو نحوها ثم يسلت الدم عنها وأصل الإشعار والشعور الإعلام

والعلامة وإشعار الهدي لكونه علامة له وهو مستحب ليعلم أنه هدي فإن ضل رده

واجده وإن اختلط بغيره تميز ولأن فيه إظهار شعار وفيه تنبيه غير صاحبه على

فعل مثل فعله وأما صفحة السنام فهي جانبه والصفحة مؤنثة فقوله الأيمن بلفظ

التذكير يتأول على أنه وصف  لمعنى الصفحة لا للفظها ويكون المراد بالصفحة

الجانب فكأنه قال جانب سنامها الأيمن ففي هذا الحديث استحباب الإشعار
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ح ل ل (ḥ-l-l)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning is "to untie, loosen, or dissolve a knot or binding"; from this derives the sense of exiting a state of ritual consecration (iḥlāl) by completing or abandoning its prohibitions.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In Kalām and fiqh, taḥallul signifies the lawful cessation of iḥrām restrictions, contingent upon the completion of prescribed rites (manāsik); it is a technical term for ritual desacralization.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literally "untying" (ḥaqīqah); metaphorically (majāz), it denotes the removal of a legal prohibition, as in "the pilgrim became lawful (ḥalla)" — the metaphor is so pervasive it functions as a legal ḥaqīqah in juristic discourse.
- Sībawayh Rule: Taqdīr al-Maḥdhūf (Reconstruction of the Ellipsed Element) — When a sentence omits a syntactically required element for brevity (ikhtiṣār) or due to contextual knowledge (ʿilm bihi), the parser must supply the ellipsed phrase to restore full grammatical and semantic coherence, as in "fa-lammā masaḥū al-rukn" where "wa-atammū ṭawāfahum" is necessarily implied.
chapters.translation:
We set out in a state of iḥrām, and the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Whoever among you has a sacrificial animal (hady) with him, let him remain in his iḥrām; and whoever does not have a sacrificial animal with him, let him exit his iḥrām (taḥallal)." I did not have a sacrificial animal with me, so I exited my iḥrām. Al-Zubayr had a sacrificial animal with him, so he did not exit his iḥrām. This is an explicit statement (taṣrīḥ) that al-Zubayr did not perform taḥallul during the Farewell Pilgrimage (Ḥajjat al-Wadāʿ) before the Day of Sacrifice (Yawm al-Naḥr). Therefore, it is obligatory to except him (with ʿĀʾishah) from the general ruling, or else [one must say] that his iḥrām was for ʿUmrah and his taḥallul from it occurred at a time other than the Farewell Pilgrimage. And Allah knows best.

Her statement: "When they wiped the Corner (al-Rukn), they exited their iḥrām" — this must be interpreted away from its literal sense (taʾwīl ʿan ẓāhirihi), because "the Corner" is the Black Stone (al-Ḥajar al-Aswad), and wiping it occurs at the beginning of the ṭawāf (circumambulation). Taḥallul is not achieved merely by wiping it, by the consensus of the Muslims (ijmāʿ al-Muslimīn). The intended meaning is: "When they wiped the Corner and completed their ṭawāf and their saʿy (running between al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah), and shaved or shortened their hair, they exited their iḥrām." It is indispensable to reconstruct this ellipsed phrase, and it was omitted only because it is known from context. They have unanimously agreed that one does not exit iḥrām before completing the ṭawāf. Our school (madhhab) and the school of the majority (jumhūr) hold that saʿy after it is also obligatory, followed by shaving or shortening the hair. Some of the Salaf deviated from this, saying that saʿy is not obligatory — but there is no proof for this claimant in this ḥadīth, because its literal sense is not intended by consensus, so its interpretation (taʾwīl) is necessarily required, as we have mentioned, so that it may accord with the rest of the ḥadīths. And Allah knows best.

Her statement concerning al-Zubayr: "He said to me: 'Stand away from me.' She said: 'Do you fear that I might leap upon you?'" — He only commanded her to stand away out of fear of an incidental occurrence that might emanate from him, such as touching with desire (lams bi-shahwah) or the like. For touching with desire is forbidden (ḥarām) during iḥrām, so he took precaution for himself by distancing her, given that she was a wife who had exited iḥrām, and the soul might covet her. His statement: "Move away from me, move away from me" — thus it appears in the manuscripts, repeated twice, meaning "distance yourself."

[1237] His statement: "She passed by al-Ḥajūn" — it is with fatḥah on the ḥāʾ and ḍammah on the jīm. It is part of the sacred precinct (ḥaram) of Mecca, and it is the mountain overlooking the Mosque of the Guard (Masjid al-Ḥaras) at the upper part of Mecca, on your right as you ascend, near al-Muḥaṣṣab.

Her statement: "Light saddlebags (khifāf al-ḥaqāʾib)" — it is the plural of ḥaqībah, which is everything carried at the rear of the camel saddle (raḥl) and the quṭb (saddle frame). From this derives the expression "so-and-so iḥtaqaba such-and-such" (i.e., carried it behind him).

[1239] His statement, on the authority of Muslim al-Qurī — al-Qurī is with a ḍammah on the qāf, then a shaddah on the rāʾ. Al-Samʿānī said: He is attributed to Banī Qurrah, a tribe of ʿAbd al-Qays. He said: Ibn Mākūlā said this. Then he said: It is also said that he was so called because he used to dwell in a place whose sight was cooling (qurrah) to the eye.

| Chapter: The Permissibility of ʿUmrah During the Months of Ḥajj

[1240] His statement: "They used to consider ʿUmrah during the months of Ḥajj as one of the most wicked acts of wickedness on earth" — the pronoun in "they used to" (kānū) refers to the people of the Jāhiliyyah (pre-Islamic era). His statement: "And they made al-Muḥarram into Ṣafar" — thus it appears in the manuscripts: "Ṣafar" without an alif after the rāʾ, and it is in the accusative case, fully declinable (maṣrūf), without disagreement. It would have been proper to write it with an alif, but whether written with the alif or with its omission, it must be read here in the accusative because it is maṣrūf. The scholars said: The intended meaning is to report about the nasīʾ (intercalation) that they used to practice. They used to call al-Muḥarram "Ṣafar," and they would make it lawful (yuḥillūnahu), and they would postpone (yunsīʾūn) al-Muḥarram — i.e., they would delay its sacredness to after Ṣafar — so that three sacred months would not follow consecutively upon them, which would constrict their affairs regarding raids and other matters. So Allah (exalted be He) led them astray in that, and He said: {«إِنَّمَا النَّسِيءُ زِيَادَةٌ فِي الْكُفْرِ»} ("Indeed, the intercalation is an increase in disbelief") — the verse.

His statement: "And they would say: 'When the camel's back (al-dabar) heals'" — meaning the backs of the camels after their return from the ḥajj, for they would become galled (tadbir) by being ridden during the pilgrimage. His statement: "And the track (al-athar) is effaced (ʿafā)" — i.e., it became obliterated and erased. The intended meaning is the tracks of the camels and others in their journeying — their tracks were effaced due to the passage of many days. This is the well-known interpretation. Al-Khaṭṭābī said: The intended meaning is the track of the camel's back (al-dabar). And Allah knows best. These expressions are all read with a final sukūn (pause), and one stops upon them, because their intent was sajʿ (rhymed prose).

His statement, on the authority of Abū al-ʿĀliyah al-Barrāʾ — it is with tashdīd on the rāʾ, because he used to fashion arrowheads (yabrī al-nabl). His statement: "Abū Dāwūd al-Mubārakī narrated to us" — he is Sulaymān ibn Muḥammad, and it is also said Sulaymān ibn Dāwūd, and Abū Muḥammad al-Mubārakī, with fatḥah on the rāʾ, attributed to al-Mubārak, which is a small town near Wāsiṭ, between it and Baghdad, on the bank of the Tigris.

His statement: "The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) prayed the dawn prayer (ṣubḥ) at Dhī Ṭuwā" — it is with fatḥah on the ṭāʾ, ḍammah, and kasrah — three dialects, as narrated by al-Qāḍī and others. The most correct and most famous is the fatḥah, and al-Aṣmaʿī and others mentioned no other. It is diptote (maqṣūr) and nunated (munawwan), and it is a well-known valley near Mecca. Al-Qāḍī said: Some narrators of al-Bukhārī recorded it with elongation (madd), and Thābit likewise mentioned it. In this ḥadīth there is evidence for those who say it is recommended (mustaḥabb) for the pilgrim (muḥrim) to enter Mecca by day, not by night. This is the more correct of the two positions (wajhayn) of our companions. Ibn ʿUmar, ʿAṭāʾ, al-Nakhaʿī, Isḥāq ibn Rāhawayh, and Ibn al-Mundhir held this view. The second position is that entering by night and by day are equal, with no virtue of one over the other — this is the saying of al-Qāḍī Abū al-Ṭayyib, al-Māwardī, Ibn al-Ṣabbāgh, and al-ʿAbdarī from our companions. Ṭāwūs and al-Thawrī held this view. ʿĀʾishah, Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, and ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz said: It is recommended to enter by night, and it is more virtuous than by day. And Allah knows best.

| Chapter: The Marking (Ishʿār) of the Sacrificial Animal and Its Garlanding (Taqlīd) at the Time of Iḥrām

[1243] His statement: "The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) prayed the noon prayer (ẓuhr) at Dhū al-Ḥulayfah, then he called for his she-camel, marked it (ashʿarahā) on the side of its hump — the right side — and wiped away the blood, and garlanded it with two sandals. Then he mounted his riding beast, and when it stood upright with him upon al-Baydāʾ, he raised his voice in talbiyah for the ḥajj." — As for al-ishʿār, it is to wound the animal on the side of its right hump with a spear, knife, iron implement, or the like, then to wipe the blood away from it. The origin of ishʿār and shuʿūr is "informing" and "marking" (iʿlām wa ʿalāmah). The ishʿār of the sacrificial animal is because it serves as a mark for it. It is recommended (mustaḥabb) so that it may be known that it is a sacrificial animal: if it goes astray, the finder returns it; if it becomes mixed with others, it is distinguished; and because in it there is a display of the ritual symbol (shiʿār) and a prompting of others besides its owner to do the like of his deed. As for "the side of the hump" (ṣafḥat al-sanām), it is its flank. The word ṣafḥah is feminine, so his statement "the right" (al-ayman) in the masculine form is interpreted as describing the meaning of ṣafḥah, not its literal word — the intended meaning being "the side," as if he said: "the right side of its hump." In this ḥadīth there is the recommendation of ishʿār.
