# [1325] قوله (عن أبي التياح الضبعي) التياح بمثناة فوق ثم مثناة تحت

وبحاء مهملة والضبعي بضاد
# 
# معجمة مضمومة وباء موحدة مفتوحة اسمه يزيد بن حميد البصري منسوب إلى بني

ضبيعة بن قيس بن ثعلبة بن عكابة بن صعب بن علي بن بكر بن وائل بن قاسط بن

هنب بن أقصى بن رعمى بن جديلة بن أسد بن ربيعة بن نزار بن معد بن عدنان قال

السمعاني نزل أكثر هذه القبيلة البصرة وكانت بها محلة تنسب إليهم قوله

(وانطلق ببدنة يسوقها فأزحفت عليه) هو بفتح الهمزة وإسكان الزاي وفتح الحاء

المهملة هذا رواية المحدثين لا خلاف بينهم فيه قال الخطابي كذا يقوله

المحدثون قال وصوابه والأجود فأزحفت بضم الهمزة يقال زحف البعير إذا قام

وأزحفه وقال الهروي وغيره يقال أزحف البعير وأزحفه السير بالألف فيهما وكذا

قال الجوهري وغيره يقال زحف البعير وأزحف لغتان وأزحفه السير وأزحف الرجل

وقف بعيره فحصل أن إنكار الخطابي ليس بمقبول بل الجميع جائز ومعنى أزحف وقف

من الكلال والاعياء قوله (فعي بشأنها إن هي أبدعت كيف يأتي بها) أما قوله

فعيي فذكر صاحب المشارق والمطالع أنه روي على ثلاثة أوجه أحدها وهي رواية

الجمهور فعي بياءين من الإعياء وهو العجز ومعناه عجز عن معرفة حكمها لو

عطبت عليه في الطريق كيف يعمل بها والوجه الثاني فعي بياء واحدة مشددة وهي

لغة بمعنى الأولى والوجه الثالث فعني بضم العين وكسر النون من العناية

بالشيء والاهتمام به وأما قوله أبدعت فبضم الهمزة وكسر الدال وفتح العين

وإسكان التاء ومعناه كلت وأعيت ووقفت قال أبو عبيد قال بعض الأعراب لا يكون

الإبداع إلا بظلع وأما قوله (كيف يأتي لها) ففي بعض الأصول لها وفي بعضها

بها وكلاهما صحيح قوله (لئن قدمت البلد لأستحفين عن ذلك) وقع في معظم النسخ
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ش-ع-ر (sha-ʿa-ra)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To mark or pierce the hump of a sacrificial camel to distinguish it as a offering; from shaʿr (hair) — the act of making the animal recognizable.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Ritual marking of the hady (sacrificial animal) to signify its consecration for the sacred precincts; a physical symbol of devotional intent.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal act of piercing/marking; metaphorically extended to any sign of consecration, but here strictly ḥaqīqah (literal).
- Root: ق-ل-د (qa-la-da)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To place a garland or collar (qilādah) around the neck; from qalada (to twist/braid).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Suspending a marked object on the sacrificial animal to denote its status as hady; a ritual act of devotion.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal act of hanging; no metaphorical extension in this ritual context.
- Root: ع-ه-ن (ʿa-ha-na)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Wool; specifically colored or dyed wool used for braiding qalāʾid (garlands).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Material substance for ritual objects; denotes the physicality of devotional implements.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal reference to wool; no figurative sense.
- Root: ز-ح-ف (za-ḥa-fa)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To crawl or move slowly; for a camel, to stand up or become exhausted and stop.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Physical incapacity of the sacrificial animal; a state of ritual impediment.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal exhaustion; metaphorical for any hindrance in ritual performance.
- Sībawayh Rule: ʿAṭf al-Bayān (Appositional Clarification) — The phrase "أو هدية" (or hady) in the narrator's report functions as an explanatory appositive, clarifying the nature of the animal without altering the grammatical structure; also, the conditional construction "إن هي أبدعت" (if it becomes incapacitated) employs the conditional particle "in" with a following verb in the perfect tense, indicating a hypothetical future event.
chapters.translation:
I say: This section provides evidence for the recommendation of combining ishʿār (marking) and taqlīd (garlanding) for camels (budn) and likewise for cattle. Within it [is the ruling] that when one sends his hady (sacrificial offering), he should mark it and garland it from his own town; but if he takes it with him, he delays the taqlīd and ishʿār until the time he enters the state of iḥrām from the mīqāt (station of pilgrimage) or from elsewhere.

Her statement — "I braided those garlands (qalāʾid) from ʿihn" — refers to wool, and it is said: wool dyed in various colors.

Her statement — "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ once sent sheep as a hady to the House (Kaʿbah) and garlanded them" — in this is an indication for our school (al-Shāfiʿī) and the school of many scholars that garlanding sheep is recommended. Mālik and Abū Ḥanīfah said: It is not recommended; rather, they restricted taqlīd to camels and cattle. This ḥadīth is explicit in its indication against them both.

His statement — "Ḥaddathanā Muḥammad ibn Juḥādah" — the Jīm is ḍammah (u-vowel), then an unpointed Ḥāʾ (muhmalah) with takhfīf (lightening). His statement — "from ʿAmrah bint ʿAbd al-Raḥmān that she informed him that Ibn Ziyād wrote to ʿĀʾishah that ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās said: 'Whoever sends a hady, what is forbidden for the pilgrim becomes forbidden for him'" — thus it occurred in all copies of Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim: "Ibn Ziyād." Abū ʿAlī al-Ghassānī, al-Māzarī, al-Qāḍī, and all the commentators on Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim said: This is an error. The correct version is "Ziyād ibn Abī Sufyān," known as Ziyād ibn Abīh. Thus it occurred correctly in Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī, al-Muwaṭṭaʾ, Sunan Abī Dāwūd, and other reliable books. This is because Ibn Ziyād did not reach the era of ʿĀʾishah. And Allah knows best.

| Chapter: The Permissibility of Riding a Sacrificial Camel (Badana) That Is Being Sent as an Offering, for One Who Needs It

His statement — "That the Messenger of Allah ﷺ saw a man leading a badana (sacrificial camel) and said: 'Ride it.' He said: 'O Messenger of Allah, it is a badana.' He said: 'Ride it, woe to you' — in the second or third [instance]." In the other narration: "Woe to you, ride it; woe to you, ride it." In Jābir's narration: "Ride it in a fitting manner (bil-maʿrūf) when you are compelled to it, until you find a mount [to spare]."

This is evidence for riding a badana that is being sent as an offering. On this matter there are several schools: The school of al-Shāfiʿī is that one rides it when in need, and does not ride it without need; rather, he rides it in a fitting manner without causing harm. Ibn al-Mundhir and a group held this view, and it is a narration from Mālik. ʿUrwah ibn al-Zubayr, Mālik in the other narration, Aḥmad, and Isḥāq held that he may ride it without need, provided he does not harm it; the Ẓāhirīs (people of apparent meaning) held this view. Abū Ḥanīfah said: He may not ride it unless he finds no alternative. Al-Qāḍī reported from some scholars that they deemed riding it absolutely obligatory, due to the command [of the Prophet] and in opposition to what the pre-Islamic era (Jāhiliyyah) practiced of honoring the baḥīrah, sāʾibah, waṣīlah, and ḥāmī, and neglecting them without riding. The evidence of the majority (jumhūr) is that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent a hady and did not ride his own offering, nor did he command people to ride their offerings. Our evidence against ʿUrwah and his supporters is the aforementioned narration of Jābir. And Allah knows best.

As for his statement ﷺ — "Woe to you, ride it" — this word (waylaka) is originally used for one who has fallen into destruction (halakah). It is said: [It was used] because he was in need and had fallen into fatigue and hardship. It is also said: It is a word that flows on the tongue and is used without intending its original meaning; rather, the Arabs use it to reinforce their speech, like their sayings: "May he have no mother," "May he have no father," "May his hands be covered with dust (taribat yadāhu)," "May Allah kill him, how courageous he is," "May she be barren and bereaved (ʿuqrā ḥalqā)," and similar expressions. This word has already been discussed in full in the Book of Purification (Kitāb al-Ṭahārah) under "taribat yadāk."

His statement — "Ḥaddathanā Hushaym, he said: Akhbaranā Ḥumayd, from Thābit, from Anas, he said: 'And I think I heard it from Anas'" — the one saying "And I think I heard it from Anas" is Ḥumayd. In most copies it occurs as "wa-aẓunnunī" with two nūns, and in some as "wa-aẓunnī" with one nūn, which is a [valid] dialect.

His statement — "He said: 'It is a badana or a hady,' so he said: 'Even if (wa-in)'" — thus it is in all copies: "wa-in" only, meaning "even if it is a badana." And Allah knows best.

| Chapter: What Is Done with the Hady If It Becomes Incapacitated (ʿaṭiba) on the Road

[1325] His statement — "from Abū al-Tayyāḥ al-Ḍubaʿī" — al-Tayyāḥ is with a tāʾ muthannāh (above, i.e., tāʾ marbūṭah or tāʾ) then a tāʾ muthannāh (below, i.e., yāʾ), and with an unpointed ḥāʾ. Al-Ḍubaʿī is with a ḍād (muʿjamah, pointed) with ḍammah, and a bāʾ muwaḥḥadah with fatḥah. His name is Yazīd ibn Ḥumayd al-Baṣrī, attributed to the tribe of Ḍubayʿah ibn Qays ibn Thaʿlabah ibn ʿUkābah ibn Ṣaʿb ibn ʿAlī ibn Bakr ibn Wāʾil ibn Qāsit ibn Hinb ibn Afṣā ibn Duʿmī ibn Jadīlah ibn Asad ibn Rabīʿah ibn Nizār ibn Maʿd ibn ʿAdnān. Al-Samʿānī said: Most of this tribe settled in Baṣrah, and there was a quarter there attributed to them.

His statement — "And he set off with a badana leading it, and it became exhausted (azḥafat) upon him" — this is with fatḥah on the hamzah, sukūn on the zāy, and fatḥah on the ḥāʾ (muhmalah). This is the narration of the ḥadīth scholars (muḥaddithūn), with no disagreement among them on it. Al-Khaṭṭābī said: Thus the muḥaddithūn say it, but the correct and more eloquent form is "azḥafat" with ḍammah on the hamzah. It is said: "zaḥafa al-baʿīr" (the camel stood up) and "azḥafahu" (it exhausted him). Al-Harawī and others said: One says "azḥafa al-baʿīr" and "azḥafahu al-sayr" (the journey exhausted it), with the alif in both. Likewise al-Jawharī and others said: "zaḥafa al-baʿīr" and "azḥafa" are two dialects, and "azḥafahu al-sayr" (the journey exhausted it), and "azḥafa al-rajul" (the man made his camel stop). Thus it is established that al-Khaṭṭābī's objection is not acceptable; rather, all forms are permissible. The meaning of "azḥafa" is: it stopped due to fatigue and exhaustion.

His statement — "He was perplexed (fa-ʿayya) about its affair: if it deviates (abdaʿat), how should he bring it?" — As for his statement "fa-ʿayya," the author of al-Mashāriq and al-Maṭāliʿ mentioned that it is narrated in three ways: First, and it is the narration of the majority, "fa-ʿayya" with two yāʾs, from al-iʿyāʾ, which is incapacity; its meaning is: he was incapable of knowing its ruling if it were to become incapacitated on the road, how he should act with it. The second way: "fa-ʿayya" with one yāʾ, shaddah (doubled), which is a dialect with the same meaning as the first. The third way: "fa-ʿunniya" with ḍammah on the ʿayn and kasrah on the nūn, from al-ʿināyah (care) with the thing and concern for it. As for his statement "abdaʿat," it is with ḍammah on the hamzah, kasrah on the dāl, fatḥah on the ʿayn, and sukūn on the tāʾ; its meaning is: it became fatigued, exhausted, and stopped. Abū ʿUbayd said: Some Bedouins said that ibdāʿ (deviation) only occurs with lameness (ẓalaʿ). As for his statement "kayfa yaʾtī lahā" (how should he bring it), in some manuscripts it is "lahā" and in others "bihā," and both are correct.

His statement — "If I reach the city (al-balad), I will certainly inquire thoroughly (lastaḥfiyanna) about that" — it occurs in most copies...

chapters.title_en: The Commentary on Sahih Muslim — Section 528: On the Injured Sacrificial Animal (Hady), the Farewell Tawaf (Ṭawāf al-Wadāʿ), and Its Abrogation for the Menstruating Woman
chapters.arabic_text:
قدمت البلد وفي بعضها قدمت الليلة وكلاهما صحيح وفي بعض النسخ عن ذلك وفي

بعضها عن ذاك بغير لام وقوله لأستحفين بالحاء المهملة وبالفاء ومعناه

لأسألن سؤالا بليغا عن  ذلك يقال أحفى في المسألة إذا ألح فيها وأكثر منها

قوله (فأضحيت) هو بالضاد المعجمة وبعد الحاء ياء مثناة تحت قال صاحب

المطالع معناه صرت في وقت الضحى قوله أن بن عباس حين
# 
# سألوه (قال على الخبير سقطت) فيه دليل لجواز ذكر الإنسان بعض ممادحته

للحاجة وإنما ذكر بن عباس ذلك ترغيبا للسامع في الاعتناء بخبره وحثا له على

الاستماع له وأنه علم محقق قوله (يا رسول الله كيف أصنع بما أبدع علي منها

قال انحرها ثم اصبغ نعليها في دمها ثم اجعله على صفحتها ولا تأكل منها أنت

ولا أحد من أهل رفقتك) فيه فوائد منها أنه إذا عطب الهدي وجب ذبحه وتخليته

للمساكين ويحرم الأكل منها عليه وعلى رفقته الذين معه في الركب سواء كان

الرفيق مخالطا له أو في جملة الناس من غير مخالطة والسبب في نهيهم قطع

الذريعة لئلا يتوصل بعض الناس إلى نحره أو تعييبه قبل أوانه واختلف العلماء

في الأكل من الهدي إذا عطب فنحره فقال الشافعي إن كان هدي تطوع كان له أن

يفعل فيه ما شاء من بيع وذبح وأكل وإطعام وغير ذلك وله تركه ولا شيء عليه

في كل ذلك لأنه ملكه وإن كان هديا منذورا لزمه ذبحه فإن تركه حتى هلك لزمه

ضمانه كما لو فرط في حفظ الوديعة حتى تلفت فإذا ذبحه غمس نعله التي قلده

إياها في دمه وضرب بها صفحة سنامه وتركه موضعه ليعلم من مر به أنه هدي

فيأكله ولا يجوز للمهدي ولا لسائق هذا الهدي وقائده الأكل منه ولا يجوز

للأغنياء الأكل منه مطلقا لأن الهدي مستحق للمساكين فلا يجوز لغيرهم ويجوز

للفقراء من غير أهل هذه الرفقة ولا يجوز لفقراء الرفقة وفي المراد بالرفقة

وجهان لأصحابنا أحدهما أنهم الذين يخالطون المهدي في الأكل وغيره دون باقي

القافلة والثاني وهو الأصح وهو الذي يقتضيه ظاهر الحديث وظاهر نص الشافعي

وكلام جمهور أصحابنا أن المراد بالرفقة جميع القافلة لأن السبب الذي منعت

به الرفقة هو خوف  تعطيبهم إياه وهذا موجود في جميع القافلة فإن قيل إذا لم

تجوزوا لأهل القافلة أكله وترك في البرية كان طعمة للسباع وهذا
# 
# إضاعة مال قلنا ليس فيه إضاعة بل العادة الغالبة أن سكان البوادي وغيرهم

يتبعون منازل الحج لالتقاط ساقطة ونحوه وقد تأتي قافلة في إثر قافلة والله

أعلم والرفقة بضم الراء وكسرها لغتان مشهورتان قوله في حديث بن عباس رضي

الله عنه (بعث رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بست عشرة بدنة) وفي الرواية

الأخرى بثمان عشرة بدنة يجوز أنهما قضيتان ويجوز أن تكون قضية واحدة

والمراد ثمان عشرة وليس في قوله ست عشرة نفي الزيادة لأنه مفهوم عدد ولا

عمل عليه والله أعلم

| باب وجوب طواف الوداع وسقوطه عن الحائض
# [1327] قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (لا ينفرن أحد حتى يكون آخر عهده بالبيت)

فيه دلالة لمن قال
# 
# بوجوب طواف الوداع وأنه إذا تركه لزمه دم وهو الصحيح في مذهبنا وبه قال

أكثر العلماء منهم الحسن البصري والحكم وحماد والثوري وأبو حنيفة وأحمد

وإسحاق وأبو ثور وقال مالك وداود وبن المنذر هو سنة لا شيء في تركه وعن

مجاهد روايتان كالمذهبين
# [1328] قوله (أمر الناس أن يكون آخر عهدهم بالبيت إلا أنه خفف عن المرأة

الحائض) هذا دليل لوجوب طواف الوداع على غير الحائض وسقوطه عنها ولا يلزمها

دم بتركه هذا مذهب الشافعي ومالك وأبي حنيفة وأحمد والعلماء كافة إلا ما

حكاه بن المنذر عن عمر وبن عمر وزيد بن ثابت رضي الله عنهم أنهم أمروها

بالمقام لطواف الوداع دليل الجمهور هذا الحديث وحديث صفية المذكور بعده

قوله (فقال بن عباس إما لا فسل فلانة الأنصارية) هو بكسر الهمزة وفتح اللام

وبالإمالة الخفيفة هذا هو الصواب المشهور وقال القاضي ضبطه الطبري والأصيلي

أمالي بكسر اللام قال والمعروف في كلام العرب فتحها إلا أن تكون على لغة من

يميل قال المازري قال بن الأنباري قولهم افعل هذا إما لا فمعناه افعله إن

كنت لا تفعل غيره فدخلت ما زائدة لأن كما  قال الله تعالى فإما ترين
# 
# من البشر أحدا فاكتفوا بلا عن الفعل كما تقول العرب إن زارك فزره وإلا

فلا هذا ما ذكره القاضي وقال بن الأثير في نهاية الغريب أصل هذه الكلمة إن

وما فأدغمت النون في الميم وما زائدة في اللفظ لا حكم لها وقد أمالت العرب

لا إمالة خفيفة قال والعوام يشبعون إمالتها فتصير ألفها ياء وهو خطأ ومعناه

إن لم تفعل هذا فليكن هذا والله أعلم
# [1211] قولها (صفية بنت حيي) بضم الحاء وكسرها الضم أشهر وفي حديثها دليل

لسقوط طواف الوداع عن الحائض وأن طواف الإفاضة ركن لا بد منه وأنه لا يسقط

عن الحائض ولا غيرها وأن الحائض تقيم له حتى تطهر فإن
# 
# ذهبت إلى وطنها قبل طواف الإفاضة بقيت محرمة وقد سبق حديث صفية هذا وبيان

إحرامه وضبطه ومعناه وفقهه في أوائل كتاب الحج في باب بيان وجوه الإحرام
chapters.anchors:
- Root: عطب (ʿaṭaba)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning is "to break, to become defective, to be injured or incapacitated" — applied to a beast that becomes lame or unfit.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In ritual law, it denotes the state of a sacrificial animal (hady) that becomes physically incapacitated before reaching the sanctuary, triggering specific legal obligations.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Used literally here (ḥaqīqah) for physical injury; no metaphorical extension in this juristic context.
- Root: حفا (ḥafā)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: "To be earnest, persistent, and intense in asking" — derived from the notion of wearing away the ground by repeated treading.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Indicates the intensity of inquiry, not mere questioning, but a pressing, exhaustive demand for information.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense of persistence; the rhetorical force is amplification (mubālaghah) of the act of asking.
- Root: ضحا (ḍaḥā)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: "To be in the time of forenoon (ḍuḥā)" — the period when the sun has risen high.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Temporal marker for ritual times; here it simply denotes the time of day, not a technical theological term.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal temporal usage; no metaphorical sense.
- Root: رفق (rafaqa)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: "A company, a caravan, a group of travelers" — from the root meaning "to be kind, gentle," but lexically extended to denote a traveling party.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In legal discourse, it specifies the group accompanying the pilgrim; the term's scope is contested among jurists.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal designation of a caravan; the juristic debate concerns whether it includes the entire qāfilah (caravan) or only those who share meals with the donor.
- Sībawayh Rule: Rule of Conditionality and Exception (al-Sharṭ wa al-Istithnāʾ) — The phrase "إما لا" (imā lā) is parsed as "in" (conditional) + "mā" (extra/ redundant) + "lā" (negation standing in for the omitted verb), following the pattern of {فَإِمَّا تَرَيْنَ مِنَ الْبَشَرِ أَحَدًا} where "mā" is extra and the conditional force remains.
chapters.translation:
I say: The Prophet ﷺ said, "I arrived at the city," and in some narrations, "I arrived last night," and both are authentic. In some copies, the wording is "about that" (ʿan dhālika), and in others "about that" (ʿan dhāka) without the lam. His statement, "I will ask persistently" (la-astaḥfiyanna) — with the unpointed ḥāʾ and the fāʾ — means: "I will ask a most searching and exhaustive question about that matter." One says "aḥfā fī al-masʾalah" when one is insistent and excessive in questioning.

His statement, "So I came to be in the forenoon" (fa-aḍḥaytu) — it is with the pointed ḍād, and after the ḥāʾ there is a yāʾ (the second letter of the dual form). The author of al-Maṭāliʿ said: Its meaning is "I entered the time of the forenoon (ḍuḥā)."

His statement — when Ibn ʿAbbās was asked and he said, "You have fallen upon an expert" (ʿalā al-khabīri saqaṭtum) — contains evidence for the permissibility of a person mentioning some of his own praiseworthy qualities when there is a need. Ibn ʿAbbās only mentioned this to encourage the listener to pay attention to his report and to urge him to listen to him, and to indicate that he possessed verified knowledge.

His statement, "O Messenger of Allah, what shall I do with what has become incapacitated (ubdiʿa) among my sacrificial animals?" He said: "Slaughter it, then dye its sandals in its blood, then place that upon its hump, and do not eat from it — neither you nor anyone from the people of your caravan (rifqah)." In this there are several benefits. Among them: when the sacrificial animal (hady) becomes incapacitated, it is obligatory to slaughter it and leave it for the poor, and it is forbidden for the donor and for his companions in the caravan to eat from it — whether the companion is one who mixes with him intimately or is merely among the general body of people without such mixing. The reason for their prohibition is the cutting off of the pretext (sadd al-dharīʿah), lest some people be led to slaughter it or find fault with it before its proper time.

The scholars differed concerning eating from the hady when it becomes incapacitated and is then slaughtered. Al-Shāfiʿī said: If it is a voluntary hady (hady taṭawwuʿ), he may do with it whatever he wishes — selling, slaughtering, eating, feeding others, and other things — and he may also leave it, and nothing is incumbent upon him in all of that, because it is his property. But if it is a vowed hady (hady mandhūr), then slaughtering it is obligatory upon him; if he leaves it until it perishes, he must guarantee its value, just as if he were negligent in guarding a deposit (wadīʿah) until it was lost. When he slaughters it, he dips the sandal which he had hung upon it into its blood, strikes the side of its hump with it, and leaves it in its place, so that whoever passes by it may know that it is a hady and eat from it.

It is not permissible for the donor (al-muhdī), nor for the one who drives or leads this hady, to eat from it. Nor is it permissible for the wealthy to eat from it at all, because the hady is due to the poor, so it is not permissible for anyone else. It is permissible for the poor who are not from the people of this caravan, but it is not permissible for the poor of the caravan itself. Concerning the meaning of "the caravan" (al-rifqah), there are two views among our companions (the Shāfiʿīs): One is that they are those who mix with the donor in eating and other matters, to the exclusion of the rest of the qāfilah (caravan). The second — and this is the more correct view, and it is what is required by the apparent meaning of the ḥadīth, the explicit text of al-Shāfiʿī, and the statements of the majority of our companions — is that "the caravan" means the entire qāfilah, because the reason for which the caravan was prohibited is the fear that they might cause it to become incapacitated (taʿṭīb), and this exists with respect to the entire qāfilah.

If it is said: "Since you do not permit the people of the qāfilah to eat it, and it is left in the wilderness, it becomes prey for wild beasts, and this is a waste of wealth (iḍāʿat māl)," we say: There is no waste in this. Rather, the prevailing custom is that the inhabitants of the deserts and others follow the pilgrimage encampments to pick up what has fallen and the like, and a qāfilah may come in the wake of another qāfilah. And Allah knows best.

"Al-rifqah" — with ḍammah on the rāʾ and with kasrah — are two well-known dialects.

His statement in the ḥadīth of Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with him: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent sixteen badanah (sacrificial camels)," and in the other narration, "eighteen badanah" — it is possible that these were two separate incidents, and it is possible that it was one incident and the intended number was eighteen. There is no negation of the greater number in his saying "sixteen," because it is a number-concept (mafhūm al-ʿadad), and no legal weight is given to it. And Allah knows best.

---

**Chapter: On the Obligation of the Farewell Tawaf (Ṭawāf al-Wadāʿ) and Its Abrogation for the Menstruating Woman**

[1327] His statement ﷺ: "Let no one depart until his last act at the House (al-Bayt) is the tawaf" — in this is evidence for those who hold the obligation of the farewell tawaf, and that if one abandons it, a dam (blood sacrifice) is incumbent upon him. This is the correct view in our school (the Shāfiʿī), and it is the view of most scholars, among them: al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī, al-Ḥakam, Ḥammād, al-Thawrī, Abū Ḥanīfah, Aḥmad, Isḥāq, and Abū Thawr. Mālik, Dāwūd, and Ibn al-Mundhir said: It is a sunnah, and nothing is incumbent upon its abandonment. From Mujāhid there are two narrations, corresponding to the two schools.

[1328] His statement: "He commanded the people that their last act at the House should be the tawaf, except that He granted a concession to the menstruating woman" — this is evidence for the obligation of the farewell tawaf upon the non-menstruating woman, and its abrogation for her (the menstruating woman), and no dam is incumbent upon her for abandoning it. This is the school of al-Shāfiʿī, Mālik, Abū Ḥanīfah, Aḥmad, and all the scholars, except what Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from ʿUmar, Ibn ʿUmar, and Zayd ibn Thābit, may Allah be pleased with them, that they ordered her to remain (in Mecca) for the farewell tawaf. The evidence of the majority is this ḥadīth and the ḥadīth of Ṣafiyyah mentioned after it.

His statement: "Ibn ʿAbbās said: 'If not, then ask so-and-so, the Anṣāriyyah woman'" — the phrase "imā lā" is with kasrah on the hamzah, fatḥah on the lām, and with light imālah (inclination of the vowel). This is the correct and well-known pronunciation. Al-Qāḍī said: Al-Ṭabarī and al-Aṣīlī recorded it as "imālī" with kasrah on the lām. He said: The known practice in the speech of the Arabs is fatḥah (on the lām), unless it follows the dialect of those who incline (yumīlūn). Al-Māzarī said: Ibn al-Anbārī said: Their saying "If not, then do this" (ifʿal hādhā imā lā) means: "Do it if you do not do anything else." The "mā" is extra (zāʾidah), because — as Allah the Exalted said: {فَإِمَّا تَرَيْنَ مِنَ الْبَشَرِ أَحَدًا} — they sufficed with "lā" in place of the verb, just as the Arabs say: "If he visits you, then visit him; and if not (wa-illā falā)." This is what al-Qāḍī mentioned. Ibn al-Athīr said in al-Nihāyah fī Gharīb al-Ḥadīth: The origin of this word is "in" and "mā," so the nūn was assimilated into the mīm, and the "mā" is extra in pronunciation with no grammatical effect. The Arabs incline the "lā" with a light imālah. He said: The common people exaggerate the imālah until its alif becomes a yāʾ, and this is an error. Its meaning is: "If you do not do this, then let this be (the alternative)." And Allah knows best.

[1211] Her statement: "Ṣafiyyah bint Ḥuyayy" — with ḍammah on the ḥāʾ and with kasrah; the ḍammah is more famous. In her ḥadīth there is evidence for the abrogation of the farewell tawaf for the menstruating woman, and that the tawaf of visitation (ṭawāf al-ifāḍah) is a pillar (rukn) that is indispensable, that it is not abrogated for the menstruating woman nor for anyone else, and that the menstruating woman must remain (in Mecca) until she becomes pure. If she departs to her homeland before the tawaf of visitation, she remains in a state of iḥrām. The ḥadīth of Ṣafiyyah has already preceded, along with the explanation of her iḥrām, its precise wording, its meaning, and its jurisprudence, in the beginning of the Book of Pilgrimage, in the chapter on the explanation of the modes of iḥrām.

chapters.title_en: The Chapter on the Recommendation of Entering the Kaʿbah for the Pilgrim and Others, and Prayer Therein and Supplication in All Its Corners
chapters.arabic_text:
بالحج قوله (حدثني الحكم بن موسى حدثنا يحيى بن حمزة عن الأوزاعي لعله قال

عن يحيى بن أبي كثير عن محمد بن إبراهيم التيمي عن أبي سلمة عن عائشة) هكذا

وقع في معظم النسخ وكذا نقله القاضي عن معظم النسخ قال وسقط عند الطبري

قوله لعله قال عن يحيى بن أبي كثير قال وسقط لعله قال فقط لابن الحذاء قال

القاضي وأظن أن الاسم كله سقط من كتب بعضهم أوشك فيه فألحقه على المحفوظ

الصواب ونبه على إلحاقه بقوله لعله قوله (قالوا يا رسول الله إنها قد زارت

يوم النحر) فيه دليل لمذهب الشافعي وأبي حنيفة وأهل العراق أنه لا يكره أن

يقال لطواف الإفاضة طواف الزيارة وقال مالك يكره وليس للكراهة حجة تعتمد

قولها (تنفر) بكسر الفاء وضمها الكسر أفصح
# 
# وبه جاء القرآن والله أعلم

| (باب استحباب دخول الكعبة للحاج وغيره)
# (والصلاة فيها والدعاء في نواحيها كلها)
# [1329] ذكر مسلم رحمه الله في الباب بأسانيده عن بلال رضي الله عنه (أن

النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم دخل الكعبة وصلى فيها بين العمودين) وبإسناده عن

أسامة  رضي الله عنه (أنه صلى الله عليه وسلم دعا في نواحيها ولم يضل) وأجمع

أهل الحديث علىالأخذ برواية بلال لأنه مثبت فمعه زيادة علم فواجب ترجيحه

والمراد الصلاة المعهودة ذات الركوع والسجود ولهذا قال بن عمر ونسيت أن

أسأله كم صلى وأما نفي أسامة فسببه أنهم لما دخلوا الكعبة أغلقوا الباب

واشتغلوا بالدعاء فرأى أسامة النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يدعو ثم اشتغل أسامة

بالدعاء في ناحية من نواحي البيت والنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في ناحية أخرى

وبلال قريب منه ثم صلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فرآه بلال لقربه ولم يره

أسامة لبعده واشتغاله وكانت صلاة خفيفة فلم يرها أسامة لإغلاق الباب مع
# 
# بعده واشتغاله بالدعاء وجاز له نفيها عملا بظنه وأما بلال فحققها فأخبر

بها والله أعلم واختلف العلماء في الصلاة في الكعبة إذا صلى متوجها إلى

جدار منها أو إلى الباب وهو مردود فقال الشافعي والثوري وأبو حنيفة وأحمد

والجمهور تصح فيها صلاة النفل وصلاة الفرض وقال مالك تصح فيها صلاة النفل

المطلق ولا يصح الفرض ولا الوتر ولا ركعتا الفجر ولا ركعتا الطواف وقال

محمد بن جرير وأصبغ المالكي وبعض أهل الظاهر لا تصح فيها صلاة أبدا لا

فريضة ولا نافلة وحكاه القاضي عن بن عباس أيضا ودليل الجمهور حديث بلال

وإذا صحت النافلة صحت الفريضة لأنهما في الموضع سواء في الاستقبال في حال

النزول وإنما يختلفان في الاستقبال في حال السير في السفر والله أعلم قوله

(وعثمان بن طلحة الحجبي) هو بفتح الحاء والجيم منسوب إلى حجابة الكعبة وهي

ولايتها وفتحها وإغلاقها وخدمتها ويقال له ولأقاربه الحجبيون وهو عثمان بن

طلحة بن أبي طلحة واسم أبي طلحة عبد الله بن عبد العزى بن عثمان بن عبد

الدار بن قصي القرشي العبدري أسلم مع خالد بن الوليد وعمرو بن العاص في

هدنة الحديبية وشهد فتح مكة ودفع النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم مفتاح الكعبة

إليه وأبي شيبة بن عثمان بن أبي طلحة وقال خذوها يا  بني طلحة خالدة تالدة

لا ينزعها منكم إلا ظالم ثم نزل المدينة فأقام بها إلى وفاة النبي صلى الله

عليه وسلم ثم تحول إلى مكة فأقام بها حتى توفي سنة اثنتين وأربعين وقيل إنه

استشهد يوم أجنادين بفتح الدال وكسرها وهي موضع بقرب بيت المقدس كانت غزوته

في أوائل خلافة عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه وثبت في الصحيح قوله صلى الله

عليه وسلم كل مأثرة كانت في الجاهلية فهي تحت قدمي الاسقاية الحاج وسدانة

البيت قال القاضي عياض
# 
# قال العلماء لا يجوز لأحد أن ينزعها منهم قال وهي ولاية لهم عليها من

رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فتبقى دائمة لهم ولذرياتهم أبدا ولا ينازعون

فيها ولا يشاركون ما داموا موجودين صالحين لذلك والله أعلم قوله (دخل

الكعبة فأغلقها عليه إنما أغلقها عليه صلى الله عليه وسلم ليكون أسكن لقلبه

وأجمع لخشوعه ولئلا يجتمع الناس ويدخلوا ويزدحموا فينالهم ضرر ويتهوش عليه

الحال بسبب لغطهم والله أعلم قوله (جعل عمودين عن يساره وعمودا عن يمينه)

هكذا هو هنا وفي رواية للبخاري عمودين عن يمينه وعمودا عن يساره وهكذا هو

في الموطأ وفي سنن أبي داود وكله من رواية مالك وفي رواية للبخاري عمودا عن

يمينه وعمودا عن يساره قوله (قدم رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يوم الفتح

فنزل بفناء الكعبة) هذا دليل على أن هذا المذكور في أحاديث الباب من دخوله

صلى الله عليه وسلم الكعبة وصلاته فيها كان يوم الفتح وهذا لا خلاف فيه ولم

يكن يوم حجة الوداع وفناء الكعبة بكسر الفاء وبالمد جانبها وحريمها والله

أعلم قوله (فجاء بالمفتح) هو بكسر الميم وفي الرواية الأخرى المفتاح وهما

لغتان قوله (فلبثوا فيه مليا) أي طويلا قوله (ونسيت أن أسأله كم صلى) هكذا

ثبت في الصحيحين من رواية بن عمر وجاء في سنن أبي داود بإسناد فيه ضعف عن

عبد الرحمن بن صفوان قال قلت لعمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه كيف صنع رسول
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ز-و-ر (z-w-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To visit, to incline toward; core sense of intentional approach.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In ritual context, denotes the circumambulation of visitation (ṭawāf al-ziyārah) as a distinct devotional act.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal visitation vs. metaphorical; here literal, as a technical term for the post-Ṭawāf al-Ifāḍah.
- Sībawayh Rule: The Rule of Appositional Correction (al-Badal) — the transmitter's phrase "perhaps he said" (laʿallahu qāla) functions as an editorial insertion, syntactically marking uncertainty in the chain, requiring the reader to treat the following name as a conjectural emendation.
chapters.translation:
I say: Regarding his statement (ḥaddathanī al-Ḥakam ibn Mūsā, ḥaddathanā Yaḥyā ibn Ḥamzah, ʿan al-Awzāʿī — perhaps he said, ʿan Yaḥyā ibn Abī Kathīr, ʿan Muḥammad ibn Ibrāhīm al-Taymī, ʿan Abī Salamah, ʿan ʿĀʾishah) — thus it occurs in most copies, and al-Qāḍī likewise transmitted it from most copies. He said: And it was omitted in al-Ṭabarī's version, his statement "perhaps he said, ʿan Yaḥyā ibn Abī Kathīr." He said: And only "perhaps he said" was omitted in Ibn al-Ḥadhāʾ's version. Al-Qāḍī said: I think that the entire name fell out from the books of some of them, or he was uncertain about it, so he appended it according to the preserved correct version, and he alerted to his appending it by his saying "perhaps he said."

His statement (they said: O Messenger of Allah, she has indeed performed the visitation (zārat) on the Day of Sacrifice) — in this is evidence for the school of al-Shāfiʿī, Abū Ḥanīfah, and the people of Iraq that it is not disliked (makrūh) to say of the circumambulation of ifāḍah (ṭawāf al-ifāḍah) "the circumambulation of visitation" (ṭawāf al-ziyārah). Mālik said: It is disliked. And there is no valid proof for the dislike that can be relied upon.

Her statement (tanfiru) — with kasrah of the fāʾ and its ḍammah; the kasrah is more eloquent, and with it the Qurʾān came. And Allah knows best.

[Chapter: The Recommendation of Entering the Kaʿbah for the Pilgrim and Others, and Prayer Therein and Supplication in All Its Corners]

[1329] Muslim, may Allah have mercy on him, mentioned in this chapter with his chains of transmission, on the authority of Bilāl, may Allah be pleased with him (that the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, entered the Kaʿbah and prayed therein between the two pillars). And with his chain on the authority of Usāmah, may Allah be pleased with him (that he, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, supplicated in its corners and did not pray). The people of ḥadīth are unanimous in accepting the narration of Bilāl, because he is an affirmatory transmitter (muthbit), and with him is an increase of knowledge, so it is obligatory to give his report precedence.

The intended meaning is the customary prayer having bowing (rukūʿ) and prostration (sujūd). For this reason Ibn ʿUmar said: "And I forgot to ask him how much he prayed." As for Usāmah's negation, its cause is that when they entered the Kaʿbah, they closed the door and occupied themselves with supplication. Usāmah saw the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, supplicating; then Usāmah occupied himself with supplication in one corner of the corners of the House, while the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, was in another corner, and Bilāl was near him. Then the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, prayed, and Bilāl saw him due to his proximity, but Usāmah did not see him due to his distance and his occupation. And it was a light prayer, so Usāmah did not see it because of the closing of the door, along with his distance and his occupation with supplication. And it was permissible for him to negate it, acting upon his presumption (ẓann). As for Bilāl, he ascertained it and so reported it. And Allah knows best.

The scholars differed concerning prayer inside the Kaʿbah when one prays facing a wall of it or the door — and this is rejected (mardūd). Al-Shāfiʿī, al-Thawrī, Abū Ḥanīfah, Aḥmad, and the majority (al-jumhūr) said: Supererogatory prayer (ṣalāt al-nafl) and obligatory prayer (ṣalāt al-farḍ) are valid therein. Mālik said: Absolute supererogatory prayer is valid therein, but the obligatory prayer, the witr, the two rakʿahs of dawn (fajr), and the two rakʿahs of circumambulation (ṭawāf) are not valid. Muḥammad ibn Jarīr, Aṣbagh al-Mālikī, and some of the Ẓāhirīs said: No prayer is ever valid therein, neither obligatory nor supererogatory. Al-Qāḍī transmitted this also from Ibn ʿAbbās. The proof of the majority is the ḥadīth of Bilāl. And if the supererogatory prayer is valid, then the obligatory prayer is valid, because they are the same in respect of facing the qiblah (istiqbāl) in the state of descent (nuzūl); they differ only in respect of facing the qiblah in the state of travel (sayr) during a journey. And Allah knows best.

His statement (and ʿUthmān ibn Ṭalḥah al-Ḥajabī) — he is, with fatḥah of the ḥāʾ and the jīm, attributed to the ḥijābah of the Kaʿbah, which is its custodianship, opening, closing, and service. It is said of him and his relatives: the Ḥajabiyyūn. He is ʿUthmān ibn Ṭalḥah ibn Abī Ṭalḥah — and the name of Abū Ṭalḥah is ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbd al-ʿUzzā ibn ʿUthmān ibn ʿAbd al-Dār ibn Quṣayy al-Qurashī al-ʿAbdarī. He embraced Islam with Khālid ibn al-Walīd and ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ during the truce of al-Ḥudaybiyyah, and he witnessed the conquest of Mecca. The Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, handed the key of the Kaʿbah to him and to Abū Shaybah ibn ʿUthmān ibn Abī Ṭalḥah, and said: "Take it, O Banī Ṭalḥah, eternally and hereditarily; none shall take it from you except a tyrant." Then he went to Medina and remained there until the death of the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him. Then he moved to Mecca and remained there until he died in the year forty-two. And it is said that he was martyred on the day of Ajnādayn — with fatḥah of the dāl and its kasrah — which is a place near Jerusalem (Bayt al-Maqdis); his expedition was in the early part of the caliphate of ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, may Allah be pleased with him. It is established in the Ṣaḥīḥ his statement, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him: "Every mark of honor (maʾtharah) that was in the Jāhiliyyah is under my feet, except the giving of water to pilgrims (siqāyah) and the custodianship of the House (sidānah)." Al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ said: The scholars said: It is not permissible for anyone to remove it from them. He said: And it is a custodianship for them from the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, so it remains perpetual for them and their descendants forever; they are not contested therein nor shared with, as long as they exist and are fit for that. And Allah knows best.

His statement (he entered the Kaʿbah and closed it upon himself) — he only closed it upon himself, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, so that it would be more tranquil for his heart and more complete for his humility (khushūʿ), and so that the people would not gather and enter and crowd, causing harm to befall them and his state to be disturbed by their clamor. And Allah knows best.

His statement (he placed two pillars on his left and one pillar on his right) — thus it is here, and in a narration of al-Bukhārī: "two pillars on his right and one pillar on his left," and thus it is in al-Muwaṭṭaʾ and in the Sunan of Abū Dāwūd — all of it from the narration of Mālik. And in a narration of al-Bukhārī: "one pillar on his right and one pillar on his left."

His statement (the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, arrived on the day of the Conquest and alighted in the courtyard (fināʾ) of the Kaʿbah) — this is evidence that what is mentioned in the ḥadīths of this chapter — his entering the Kaʿbah and praying therein — occurred on the day of the Conquest, and there is no disagreement about this. It was not on the day of the Farewell Pilgrimage. And fināʾ of the Kaʿbah — with kasrah of the fāʾ and with elongation (madd) — is its side and its precinct. And Allah knows best.

His statement (he came with the miftah) — it is with kasrah of the mīm, and in the other narration "al-miftāḥ"; they are two dialects.

His statement (they remained therein for a long while (maliyyan)) — meaning: a long time.

His statement (and I forgot to ask him how much he prayed) — thus it is established in the two Ṣaḥīḥs from the narration of Ibn ʿUmar. And it came in the Sunan of Abū Dāwūd with a chain containing weakness, on the authority of ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ṣafwān, who said: I said to ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, may Allah be pleased with him: How did the Messenger of Allah...

chapters.title_en: Section 530 — On Entering the Kaʿbah, Prayer Within It, and the Abrogation of Its Reconstruction
chapters.arabic_text:
الله صلى الله عليه  وسلم حين
# 
# دخل الكعبة قال صلى ركعتين قوله (فأجافوا عليهم الباب) أي أغلقوه قوله

(وحدثني حميد بن مسعده حدثنا خالد يعنى بن الحرث حدثنا عبد الله بن عون عن

نافع عن عبد الله بن عمر رضي الله عنه أنه انتهى إلى الكعبة وقد دخلها

النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وبلال وأسامة وأجاف عليهم عثمان بن طلحة الباب

قال ومكثوا فيه مليا ثم فتح الباب فخرج النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فرقيت
# 
# الدرجة فدخلت البيت فقلت أين صلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قالوا ها هنا

ونسيت أن أسألهم كم صلى) هكذا وقعت هذه الرواية هنا وظاهرة أن بن عمر سأل

بلالا وأسامة وعثمان جميعهم قال القاضي عياض ولكن أهل الحديث وهنوا هذه

الرواية فقال الدارقطني وهم بن عون هنا وخالفه غيره فأسندوه عن بلال وحده

قال القاضي وهذا هو الذي ذكره مسلم في باقي الطرق فسألت بلالا فقال إلا أنه

وقع في رواية حرملة عن بن وهب فأخبرني بلال وعثمان بن طلحة أن رسول الله

صلى الله عليه وسلم صلى في جوف الكعبة هكذا هو عند عامة شيوخنا وفي بعض

النسخ وعثمان بن أبي طلحة قال وهذا يعضد رواية بن عون والمشهور انفراد بلال

برواية ذلك والله أعلم
# 
# [1330] قوله (فلما خرج ركع في قبل البيت ركعتين وقال هذه القبلة) قوله

قبل البيت هو بضم القاف والباء ويجوز إسكان الباء كما في نظائره قيل معناه

ما استقبلك منها وقيل مقابلها وفي رواية في الصحيح فصلى ركعتين في وجه

الكعبة وهذا هو المراد بقبلها ومعناه عند بابها وأما قوله ركع في قبل البيت

فمعناه صلى وقوله ركعتين دليل لمذهب الشافعي والجمهور أن تطوع النهار يستحب

أن يكون مثنى وقال أبو حنيفة أربعا وسبقت المسألة في كتاب الصلاة وأما قوله

صلى الله عليه وسلم هذه القبلة فقال الخطابي معناه أن أمر القبلة قد استقر

على استقبال هذا البيت فلا ينسخ بعد اليوم فصلوا إليه أبدا قال ويحتمل أنه

علمهم سنة موقف الإمام وأنه  يقف في وجهها دون أركانها وجوانبها وإن كانت

الصلاة في جميع جهاتها مجزئة هذا كلام الخطابي ويحتمل معنى ثالثا وهو أن

معناه هذه الكعبة هي المسجد الحرام الذي أمرتم باستقباله لا كل الحرام ولا

مكة ولا كل المسجد الذي حول الكعبة بل هي الكعبة نفسها فقط والله أعلم
# [1332] قوله (أدخل النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
# 
# البيت في عمرته قال لا) هذا مما اتفقوا عليه قال العلماء والمراد به عمرة

القضاء التي كانت سنة سبع من الهجرة قبل فتح مكة قال العلماء وسبب عدم

دخوله صلى الله عليه وسلم ما كان في البيت من الأصنام والصور ولم يكن

المشركون يتركونه لتغييرها فلما فتح الله تعالى عليه مكة دخل البيت وصلى

فيه وأزال الصور قبل دخوله والله أعلم

| (باب نقض الكعبة وبنائها)
# قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (لولا حداثة عهد قومك بالكفر لنقضت الكعبة

ولجعلتها على أساس إبراهيم فإن قريشا حين بنت البيت استقصرت ولجعلت لها

خلفا) وفي الرواية الأخرى اقتصروا
# 
# عن قواعد إبراهيم وفي الأخرى فإن قريشا اقتصرتها وفي الأخرى استقصروا من

بنيان البيت وفي الأخرى قصروا في البناء وفي الأخرى قصرت بهم النفقة قال

العلماء هذه الروايات كلها بمعنى واحد ومعنى استقصرت قصرت عن تمام بنائها

واقتصرت على هذا القدر لقصور النفقة بهم عن تمامها وفي هذا الحديث دليل

لقواعد من الأحكام منها إذا تعارضت المصالح أو تعارضت مصلحة ومفسدة وتعذر

الجمع بين فعل المصلحة وترك المفسدة بدئ بالأهم لأن النبي صلى الله عليه

وسلم أخبر أن نقض الكعبة وردها إلى ما كانت عليه من قواعد إبراهيم صلى الله

عليه وسلم مصلحة ولكن تعارضه مفسدة أعظم منه وهي خوف فتنة بعض من أسلم

قريبا وذلك لما كانوا يعتقدونه من فضل الكعبة فيرون تغييرها عظيما فتركها

صلى الله عليه وسلم ومنها فكر ولي الأمر في مصالح رعيته واجتنابه ما يخاف

منه تولد ضرر عليهم في دين أو دنيا إلا الأمور الشرعية كأخذ الزكاة وإقامة

الحدود ونحو ذلك ومنها تألف قلوب الرعية  وحسن حياطتهم وأن لا ينفروا ولا

يتعرض لما يخاف تنفيرهم بسببه ما لم يكن فيه ترك أمر شرعي كما سبق قال

العلماء بني البيت خمس مرات بنته الملائكة ثم إبراهيم صلى الله عليه وسلم

ثم قريش في الجاهلية وحضر النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم هذا البناء وله خمس

وثلاثون سنة وقيل خمس وعشرون وفيه سقط على الأرض حين وقع إزاره ثم بناه بن

الزبير ثم الحجاج بن يوسف واستمر إلى الآن على بناء الحجاج وقيل بني مرتين

أخريين أو ثلاثا وقد أوضحته في كتاب إيضاح المناسك الكبير قال العلماء ولا

يغير عن هذا البناء وقد ذكروا أن هارون الرشيد سأل مالك بن أنس عن هدمها

وردها إلى بناء بن الزبير للأحاديث المذكورة في الباب فقال مالك ناشدتك

الله يا أمير المؤمنين ألا تجعل هذا البيت لعبة للملوك لا يشاء أحد إلا

نقضه وبناه فتذهب هيبته من صدور الناس وبالله التوفيق قوله صلى الله عليه

وسلم (ولجعلت لها خلفا) هو بفتح الخاء المعجمة وإسكان اللام وبالفاء هذا هو
chapters.anchors:
- Root: د-خ-ل (dakhala)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Entry, penetration into an interior; opposite of khurūj (exit).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Physical ingress; metaphorically, entering into a state or covenant.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal here — bodily entry into the Kaʿbah; no metaphorical extension.
- Root: أ-ج-ف (ajāfa)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To close, shut firmly; to make something flush against another.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Closure implying security and seclusion.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal action of shutting a door; no figurative sense in this context.
- Root: م-ل-أ (malaʾa)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To fill; derived form (makkatha) — to remain, stay for a duration.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Temporal extension of presence; patience in staying.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Here used literally for duration of stay; not metaphorical.
- Root: ن-ق-ض (naqaḍa)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To demolish, undo, break apart a structure.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Annulment of a covenant or undoing of a physical edifice; theological nuance of abrogation.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal demolition of the Kaʿbah; metaphorical for abrogating rulings.
- Root: ق-ص-ر (qaṣara)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To fall short, be deficient, limit.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Deficiency in completing an obligation or act.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal shortcoming in construction; metaphorical for insufficiency of means.
- Sībawayh Rule: ʿAṭf al-Bayān (Appositional Clarification) — When multiple narrators are listed (Bilāl, Usāmah, ʿUthmān), the pronoun reference requires careful parsing to determine who was actually asked; also, the rule of ḥāl (circumstantial clause) applies in "دخلها النبي" where the verb governs the accusative state of the subject's action.
chapters.translation:
I say: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace — when he entered the Kaʿbah, he prayed two rakʿahs. His statement (and they shut the door upon them) means they closed it.

(And ʿUbayd ibn Muʿādh narrated to me — Khalid, meaning Ibn al-Ḥārith, narrated to us — ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAwn narrated to us, from Nāfiʿ, from ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with them both, that he arrived at the Kaʿbah while the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, had already entered it, along with Bilāl and Usāmah, and ʿUthmān ibn Ṭalḥah had shut the door upon them. He said: And they remained therein for a long while, then the door was opened, and the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, came out. So I ascended the steps, entered the House, and said: Where did the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, pray? They said: Here. And I forgot to ask them how many rakʿahs he prayed.)

Thus this narration occurred here, and its apparent meaning is that Ibn ʿUmar asked Bilāl, Usāmah, and ʿUthmān all together. Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ said: But the hadith scholars weakened this narration. Al-Dāraquṭnī said: Ibn ʿAwn erred here, and another contradicted him, attributing it solely to Bilāl. Qāḍī said: And this is what Muslim mentioned in the remaining chains — so he asked Bilāl, who said... Except that in the narration of Ḥarmalah from Ibn Wahb, it occurred: Bilāl and ʿUthmān ibn Ṭalḥah informed me that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, prayed in the interior of the Kaʿbah. Thus it is with the majority of our shaykhs, and in some copies: ʿUthmān ibn Abī Ṭalḥah. He said: And this supports the narration of Ibn ʿAwn. But the well-known view is that Bilāl alone narrated this matter. And Allah knows best.

[1330] His statement (When he came out, he prayed two rakʿahs facing the front of the House, and said: This is the qiblah). His statement "qibla al-bayt" — with ḍammah on the qāf and bāʾ, and it is permissible to give sukūn to the bāʾ as in its parallels. It was said: Its meaning is what faces you from it; and it was said: Its opposite. In a narration in the Ṣaḥīḥ: He prayed two rakʿahs facing the face of the Kaʿbah — and this is what is meant by its "qibla," meaning at its door. As for his statement "he prayed (rakʿa) in the qibla of the House," its meaning is he prayed. And his statement "two rakʿahs" is evidence for the school of al-Shāfiʿī and the majority that supererogatory prayer during the day is recommended to be in pairs. Abū Ḥanīfah said: Four. And this issue has preceded in the Book of Prayer. As for his statement, peace be upon him, "This is the qiblah," al-Khaṭṭābī said: Its meaning is that the matter of the qiblah has been settled upon facing this House, so it will not be abrogated after this day — so pray toward it forever. He said: And it is possible that he taught them the sunnah of the imam's position — that he stands facing its face, not its corners or sides, even though prayer in all its directions is sufficient. This is the speech of al-Khaṭṭābī. And a third meaning is possible: that its meaning is — this Kaʿbah is the Sacred Mosque which you have been commanded to face, not all of the ḥaram, nor Mecca, nor the entire mosque surrounding the Kaʿbah, but rather the Kaʿbah itself alone. And Allah knows best.

[1332] His statement (Did the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, enter the House during his ʿUmrah? He said: No). This is among what they unanimously agreed upon. The scholars said: What is meant is the ʿUmrah of compensation (al-qaḍāʾ) which occurred in year seven of the Hijrah, before the conquest of Mecca. The scholars said: The reason for his not entering, peace be upon him, was the idols and images that were in the House, and the polytheists would not leave him to change them. So when Allah, exalted is He, granted him the conquest of Mecca, he entered the House and prayed therein, and removed the images before his entry. And Allah knows best.

| (Chapter: On the Demolition and Reconstruction of the Kaʿbah)

His statement, peace be upon him: (Were it not for the recentness of your people's covenant with disbelief, I would have demolished the Kaʿbah and built it upon the foundations of Abraham — for the Quraysh, when they built the House, fell short (istaqṣarat), and I would have made for it a rear door (khalfan)). And in the other narration: (They economized (iqtaṣarū) regarding the foundations of Abraham). And in another: (For the Quraysh restricted it (iqtaṣarathā)). And in another: (They fell short (istaqṣarū) of the building of the House). And in another: (They were deficient (qaṣṣarū) in the construction). And in another: (The expenditure fell short for them (qaṣurat bihim al-nafaqah)). The scholars said: All these narrations have one meaning. The meaning of "istaqṣarat" is: they fell short of completing its construction and restricted themselves to this extent due to the insufficiency of their expenditure for its completion.

In this hadith there is evidence for foundational rulings, including: When interests conflict, or a benefit and a harm conflict, and combining the performance of the benefit with the avoidance of the harm is impossible, one begins with the more important — because the Prophet, peace be upon him, informed that demolishing the Kaʿbah and returning it to what it was upon the foundations of Abraham, peace be upon him, was a benefit, but a greater harm conflicted with it, namely the fear of tribulation for some of those who had recently embraced Islam, due to what they believed of the Kaʿbah's virtue — they would see its alteration as something grave. So he, peace be upon him, left it.

And from it: The ruler must consider the interests of his subjects and avoid what he fears would generate harm upon them in religion or worldly matters — except for Sharīʿah-mandated matters, such as taking the zakāh, establishing the ḥudūd, and the like. And from it: Winning the hearts of the subjects and good guardianship over them — that they not be alienated, and that one not expose oneself to what is feared would cause their alienation, so long as it does not involve abandoning a Sharīʿah-mandated matter, as previously mentioned.

The scholars said: The House was built five times. The angels built it, then Abraham, peace be upon him, then the Quraysh in the Jāhiliyyah — and the Prophet, peace be upon him, witnessed this construction at thirty-five years of age, and it was said: twenty-five. In it, he fell to the ground when his waist-wrapper slipped. Then Ibn al-Zubayr built it, then al-Ḥajjāj ibn Yūsuf, and it has remained until now upon al-Ḥajjāj's construction. And it was said: It was built two or three other times — and I have clarified this in my book "Īḍāḥ al-Manāsik al-Kabīr."

The scholars said: It is not to be altered from this construction. And they mentioned that Hārūn al-Rashīd asked Mālik ibn Anas about demolishing it and returning it to Ibn al-Zubayr's construction, due to the hadiths mentioned in this chapter. Mālik said: I adjure you by Allah, O Commander of the Faithful — do not make this House a plaything for kings; no one would wish anything but to demolish it and rebuild it, and thus its awe would depart from people's hearts. And with Allah is success.

chapters.arabic_text:
الصحيح المشهور والمراد به باب من خلفها وقد جاء مفسرا في الرواية الأخرى

ولجعلت لها بابا شرقيا وبابا غربيا وفي صحيح البخاري قال هشام خلفا يعني

بابا وفي الرواية الأخرى لمسلم بابين أحدهما يدخل منه والآخر يخرج منه وفي

رواية البخاري ولجعلت لها خلفين قال القاضي وقد ذكر الحربي هذا الحديث هكذا

وضبطه خلفين بكسر الخاء وقال الخالفة عمود في مؤخر البيت وقال الهروي خلفين

بفتح
# 
# الخاء قال القاضي وكذا ضبطناه على شيخنا أبي الحسين قال وذكر الهروى عن

بن الأعرابي أن الخلف الظهر وهذا يفسر أن المراد الباب كما فسرته الأحاديث

الباقية والله أعلم قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (لولا حدثان قومك) هو بكسر

الحاء وإسكان الدال أي قرب عهدهم بالكفر والله أعلم قوله (فقال عبد الله بن

عمر لئن كانت عائشة سمعت هذا) قال القاضي ليس هذا اللفظ من بن عمر على سبيل

التضعيف لروايتها والتشكيك في صدقها وحفظها فقد كانت  من الحفظ والضبط بحيث

لا يستراب في حديثها ولا فيا تنقله ولكن كثيرا ما يقع في كلام العرب صورة

التشكيك والتقرير والمراد به اليقين كقوله تعالى وإن أدري لعله فتنة لكم

ومتاع إلى حين وقوله تعالى قل إن ضللت فإنما أضل على نفسي وإن اهتديت الآية

قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (لولا أن قومك حديثوا عهد بجاهلية أو قال بكفر

لأنفقت كنز الكعبة في سبيل الله) فيه دليل لتقديم أهم المصالح عند تعذر

جميعها كما سبق إيضاحه في أول الحديث وفيه دليل لجواز إنفاق كنز الكعبة

ونذورها الفاضلة عن مصالحها في سبيل الله لكن جاء في رماية لأنفقت كنز

الكعبة في بنائها وبناؤها من سبيل الله فلعله المراد بقوله في الرواية

الأولى في سبيل الله والله أعلم ومذهبنا أن الفاضل من وقف مسجد أو غيره لا

يصرف في مصالح مسجد آخر ولا غيره بل يحفظ دائما للمكان الموقوف عليه الذي

فضل منه فربما احتاج إليه والله اعلم قوله ص
# 
# (ولأدخلت فيها من الحجر) وفي رواية وزدت فيها ستة أذرع من الحجر فإن

قريشا اقتصرتها حين بنت الكعبة وفي رواية خمس أذرع وفي رواية قريبا من سبع

أذرع وفي رواية قالت عائشة سألت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عن الجدار

أمن البيت هو قال نعم وفي رواية لولا أن قومك حديث عهدهم في الجاهلية فأخاف

أن تنكره قلوبهم لنظرت أن أدخل الجدار في البيت قال أصحابنا ست أذرع من

الحجر مما يلي البيت محسوبة من البيت بلا خلاف وفي الزائد خلاف فإن طاف في

الحجر وبينه وبين البيت أكثر من ستة أذرع ففيه وجهان لأصحابنا أحدهما يجوز

لظواهر هذه الأحاديث وهذا هو الذي رجحه جماعات من أصحابنا الخراسانيين

والثاني لا يصح طوافه في شيء من الحجر ولا على جداره ولا يصح حتى يطوف

خارجا من جميع الحجر وهذا هو الصحيح وهو الذي نص عليه الشافعي وقطع به

جماهير أصحابنا العراقيين ورجحه جمهور الأصحاب وبه قال جميع علماء المسلمين

سوى أبي  حنيفة فإنه قال إن طاف في الحجر وبقي في مكة أعاده وإن رجع من مكة

بلا إعادة أراق دما وأجزأه طوافه واحتج الجمهور بأن النبي صلى الله عليه

وسلم طاف من وراء الحجر وقال لتأخذوا مناسككم ثم أطبق المسلمون عليه من

زمنه صلى الله عليه وسلم إلى الآن وسواء كان كله من البيت أم بعضه فالطواف

يكون من ورائه كما فعل النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم والله أعلم ووقع في رواية

ستة أذرع بالهاء وفي رواية خمس وفي رواية قريبا من سبع بحذف الهاء وكلاهما

صحيح ففي الذارع لغتان مشهورتان التأنيث والتذكير والتأنيث أفصح قوله
# 
# (لما احترق البيت زمن يزيد بن معاوية حين غزاه أهل الشام تركه بن الزبير

حتى قدم الناس الموسم يريد أن يجرئهم أو يحربهم على أهل الشام) أما الحرف

الأول فهو يجرثهم بالجيم والراء بعدها همزة من الجراءة أي يشجعهم على

قتالهم بإظهار قبح فعالهم هذا هو المشهور في ضبطه قال القاضي ورواه العذري

يجربهم بالجيم والباء الموحدة ومعناه يختبرهم وينظر ما عندهم في ذلك من

حمية وغضب لله تعالى ولبيته وأما الثاني وهو قوله أو يحربهم فهو بالحاء

المهملة والراء والباء الموحدة وأوله مفتوح ومعناه يغيظهم بما يرونه قد فعل

بالبيت من قولهم حربت الأسد إذا أغضبته قال القاضي وقد يكون معناه يحملهم

على الحرب ويحرضهم عليها ويؤكد عزائمهم لذلك قال ورواه آخرون يحزبهم بالحاء

والزاي يشد قوتهم ويميلهم إليه ويجعلهم حزبا له وناصرين له على مخالفيه

وحزب الرجل من مال إليه وتحازب القوم تمالوا قوله (يا أيها الناس أشيروا

علي في الكعبة) فيه دليل لاستحباب مشاورة الإمام أهل الفضل والمعرفة في

الأمور المهمة قوله (قال بن عباس فإني قد فرق لي فيه رأي) هو بضم الفاء

وكسر الراء أي كشف وبين قال الله تعالى وقرآنا فرقناه أي فصلناه وبيناه هذا

هو الصواب في ضبطه هذه اللفظة ومعناها وهكذا ضبطه القاضي والمحققون وقد

جعله الحميدي صاحب الجمع بين الصحيحين في كتابه غريب الصحيحين فرق بفتح

chapters.anchors:
- Root: خ-ل-ف (khā'-lām-fā')
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: The root denotes "that which comes after" or "the rear/back part" of something; a "successor" or "that which remains behind."
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological usage, it can denote the "afterlife" (al-ākhirah) as the "successor" to this world, but here it is literal: the rear or back portion of a structure.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage refers to the physical back; metaphorical (majāz) usage would be "a successor" or "a deputy." Here, the dispute is whether it means "door" (bāb) or "back" (ẓahr).
- Root: ح-د-ث (ḥā'-dāl-thā')
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To be new, recent, or to originate; "ḥudūth" is the state of being recent or newly occurring.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In Kalām, "ḥudūth" is the technical term for "origination" or "temporal contingency" of the created world, as opposed to divine eternity (qidam).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Here it is literal: "recentness of their affair" (qurb ʿahdihim) with unbelief, i.e., their recent conversion from paganism.
- Root: ج-ر-ء (jīm-rā'-hamzah)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Boldness, courage, audacity; to embolden or encourage someone to act.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Not a technical theological term; used literally for moral encouragement toward a course of action.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal usage: to make someone bold (yujri'uhum). The variant "yujarribuhum" (from j-r-b) means "to test/try them."
- Root: ح-ر-ب (ḥā'-rā'-bā')
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: War; to provoke or incite to anger; "ḥaribtu al-asad" means "I angered the lion."
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Literal: to provoke to war or anger; also used for "to incite" (taḥrīḍ).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: to enrage; metaphorical: to incite to battle. The variant "yuḥazzibuhum" (from ḥ-z-b) means "to make them a party/faction (ḥizb)."
- Sībawayh Rule: The Rule of Grammatical Variation in Narrated Variants (ikhtilāf al-riwāyāt fī al-lughāt): When multiple authentic narrations differ in vocalization (e.g., "khalfayn" with kasrah vs. fatḥah on the khā'), each is parsed according to its own morphological pattern, and the commentator must reconcile them without declaring one corrupt, unless a clear grammatical or contextual proof (dalīl) necessitates preference.
chapters.translation:
I say: The authentic and well-known [narration] — and what is meant by it — is "a door behind it" (bāb min khalfihā). This has come explicitly explained in the other narration: "And I would have made for it an eastern door and a western door." In Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī, Hishām said: "khalfayn," meaning a door. In the other narration of Muslim: "two doors — one through which they enter and the other through which they exit." In the narration of al-Bukhārī: "And I would have made for it two khalfayn." Al-Qāḍī said: Al-Ḥarbī mentioned this ḥadīth in this manner and vocalized it as "khalfayn" with kasrah on the khā', and he said: "al-khālifah" is a pillar at the rear of the house. Al-Harawī said: "khalfayn" with fatḥah on the khā'. Al-Qāḍī said: Thus we also vocalized it upon our shaykh Abū al-Ḥusayn. He said: Al-Harawī mentioned from Ibn al-Aʿrābī that "al-khalf" is the back (al-ẓahr). And this explains that what is meant is the door, just as the remaining ḥadīths have explained it. And Allāh knows best.

His statement, peace and blessings be upon him: "Were it not for the recentness (ḥidathān) of your people" — it is with kasrah on the ḥā' and sukūn on the dāl, meaning: the recentness of their covenant with unbelief. And Allāh knows best.

His statement: "ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar said: 'If ʿĀ'ishah heard this...'" — Al-Qāḍī said: This wording from Ibn ʿUmar is not in the mode of weakening her narration or casting doubt upon her truthfulness and memory. For she was of such memory and precision that no doubt could be entertained regarding her ḥadīth or what she transmits. Rather, frequently in the speech of the Arabs there occurs the form of doubt and affirmation (taqrīr) where what is meant is certainty — as in His statement, the Exalted: {«وَإِنْ أَدْرِي لَعَلَّهُ فِتْنَةٌ لَكُمْ وَمَتَاعٌ إِلَى حِينٍ»} ("And I do not know — perhaps it is a trial for you and enjoyment for a time") — and His statement, the Exalted: {«قُلْ إِنْ ضَلَلْتُ فَإِنَّمَا أَضِلُّ عَلَى نَفْسِي وَإِنِ اهْتَدَيْتُ»} ("Say: If I go astray, I only go astray against myself; and if I am guided...") — to the end of the verse.

His statement, peace and blessings be upon him: "Were it not that your people have recently (ḥuddithū) departed from Jāhiliyyah — or he said: from unbelief — I would have spent the treasure of the Kaʿbah in the path of Allāh." In this is evidence for giving precedence to the most important of interests (ahamm al-maṣāliḥ) when it is impossible to achieve all of them, as was previously clarified at the beginning of the ḥadīth. And in it is evidence for the permissibility of spending the treasure of the Kaʿbah and its supererogatory vows (nudhūr) that exceed its needs, in the path of Allāh. However, there has come in another narration: "I would have spent the treasure of the Kaʿbah upon its construction — and its construction is from the path of Allāh." So perhaps this is what is meant by his statement in the first narration: "in the path of Allāh." And Allāh knows best. And our school (madhhab) is that the surplus from a waqf of a mosque or other than it is not diverted to the needs of another mosque nor to anything else. Rather, it is preserved perpetually for the place endowed upon which it was surplus, for perhaps it may come to need it. And Allāh knows best.

His statement, peace and blessings be upon him: "And I would have included in it from the Ḥijr" — and in one narration: "And I would have added to it six cubits (adhruʿ) from the Ḥijr, for the Quraysh had shortened it when they built the Kaʿbah." And in another narration: "five cubits." And in another: "close to seven cubits." And in another narration: ʿĀ'ishah said: "I asked the Messenger of Allāh, peace and blessings be upon him, about the wall (al-jidār): 'Is it part of the House?' He said: 'Yes.'" And in another narration: "Were it not that your people have recently departed from Jāhiliyyah, and I fear that their hearts would reject it, I would have considered including the wall (al-jidār) within the House."

Our companions (aṣḥābunā) said: Six cubits from the Ḥijr adjacent to the House are counted as part of the House without dispute. Regarding the additional portion, there is a dispute. For if one performs the ṭawāf within the Ḥijr while between him and the House there is more than six cubits, there are two faces (wajhān) among our companions: One of them — that it is permissible, due to the apparent meanings (ẓawāhir) of these ḥadīths; and this is what groups of our Khurāsānī companions preferred. The second — that his ṭawāf is not valid in any part of the Ḥijr, nor upon its wall, and it is not valid until he circumambulates outside the entirety of the Ḥijr. And this is the correct (al-ṣaḥīḥ) view, and it is what al-Shāfiʿī explicitly stated, and the masses of our ʿIrāqī companions affirmed it definitively, and the majority of the companions preferred it. And upon it are all the scholars of the Muslims, except Abū Ḥanīfah — for he said: If one performs ṭawāf within the Ḥijr and remains in Mecca, he repeats it; but if he has departed from Mecca without repeating, he offers a sacrificial animal (adhā) and his ṭawāf suffices him. The majority adduced as proof that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, performed ṭawāf from behind the Ḥijr and said: {«خُذُوا عَنِّي مَنَاسِكَكُمْ»} ("Take from me your rites of pilgrimage"). Then the Muslims have continuously followed him in this from his time, peace and blessings be upon him, until now. And it is equal whether all of it is part of the House or some of it — the ṭawāf is from behind it, just as the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, did. And Allāh knows best.

It occurs in one narration: "six cubits" (sittu adhruʿ) with the tā' marbūṭah (i.e., "sittah"), and in another: "five" (khams) and in another: "close to seven" (sabʿ) with the elision of the tā'. Both are correct, for in the word "dhirāʿ" (cubit) there are two well-known genders — feminine and masculine — and the feminine is more eloquent.

His statement: "When the House burned during the time of Yazīd ibn Muʿāwiyah, when the people of Syria attacked it, Ibn al-Zubayr left it until the people arrived for the season of pilgrimage (mawsim), intending to embolden them (yujri'ahum) or to provoke them (yuḥribahum) against the people of Syria." As for the first word, it is "yujri'uhum" — with jīm, rā', followed by hamzah — from "al-jarā'ah" (boldness), meaning: to encourage them to fight them by displaying the ugliness of their deeds. This is the well-known vocalization. Al-Qāḍī said: Al-ʿUdhrī narrated it as "yujarribuhum" — with jīm and unpointed bā' — meaning: he would test them and see what they possessed of zeal and anger for Allāh, the Exalted, and for His House. As for the second word — his statement "yuḥribahum" — it is with unpointed ḥā', rā', and unpointed bā', with fatḥah on its first letter, meaning: he would enrage them by what they saw had been done to the House — from their saying "ḥaribtu al-asad" (I angered the lion) when one enrages it. Al-Qāḍī said: And it may mean: he would carry them to war and incite them upon it and strengthen their resolve for it. He said: And others narrated it as "yuḥazzibuhum" — with ḥā' and zāy — meaning: he would strengthen their power and incline them to him, and make them a party (ḥizb) for him and supporters of him against his opponents. And "ḥizb al-rajul" is those who incline to him; and "taḥāzaba al-qawm" means they became partisan.

His statement: "O people, counsel me regarding the Kaʿbah" — in this is evidence for the desirability (istiḥbāb) of the Imām consulting the people of virtue and knowledge in important matters.

His statement: "Ibn ʿAbbās said: 'Indeed, a view has been revealed (furrija) to me concerning it'" — it is with ḍammah on the fā' and kasrah on the rā', meaning: it was unveiled and clarified. Allāh, the Exalted, said: {«وَقُرْآنًا فَرَّقْنَاهُ»} ("And a Qur'ān which We have separated") — meaning: We detailed it and clarified it. This is the correct vocalization of this word and its meaning, and thus al-Qāḍī and the verifiers (al-muḥaqqiqūn) vocalized it. Al-Ḥumaydī, the author of "al-Jamʿ bayn al-Ṣaḥīḥayn," rendered it in his book "Gharīb al-Ṣaḥīḥayn" as "fariqa" with fatḥah on the fā', meaning "he feared" — and they rejected this upon him and declared al-Ḥumaydī mistaken in his vocalization and interpretation. بن الزبير لو كان أحدكم احترق بيته
# 
# ما رضي حتى يجده) هكذا هو في أكثر النسخ يجده بضم الياء وبدال واحدة وفي

كثير منها يجدد بدالين وهما بمعنى قوله (تتابعوا فنقضوه) هكذا ضبطناه

تتابعوا بياء موحدة قبل العين وهكذا هو في جميع نسخ بلادنا وكذا ذكره

القاضي عن رواية الأكثرين وعن أبي بحر تتابعوا وهو بمعناه إلا أن أكثر ما

يستعمل بالمثناة في الشر خاصة وليس هذا موضعه قوله (فجعل بن الزبير أعمدة

فستر عليها الستور حتى ارتفع بناؤه) المقصود بهذه الأعمدة والستور أن

يستقبلها المصلون في تلك الأيام ويعرفوا موضع الكعبة ولم تزل تلك الستور

حتى ارتفع البناء وصار مشاهدا للناس فأزالها لحصول المقصود بالبناء المرتفع

من الكعبة واستدل القاضي عياض بهذا لمذهب مالك في أن المقصود بالاستقبال

البناء لا البقعة قال وقد كان بن عباس أشار على بن الزبير بنحو هذا وقال له

إن كنت هادمها فلا تدل الناس بلا قبلة فقال له جابر صلوا إلى موضعها فهي

القبلة ومذهب الشافعي وغيره جواز الصلاة إلى أرض الكعبة ويجزيه ذلك بلا

خلاف عند سواء
# 
# كان بقي منها شاخص أم لا والله أعلم قوله (إنا لسنا من تلطيخ بن الزبير

في شيء) يريد بذلك سبه وعيب فعله يقال لطخته أي رميته بأمر قبيح قوله (وفد

الحرث بن عبد الله على عبد الملك بن مروان في خلافته) هكذا هو في جميع

النسخ الحرث بن عبد الله وليس في شيء منها خلاف ونسخ بلادنا هي رواية عبد

الغفار بن الفارسي وادعى القاضي عياض أنه وقع هكذا لجميع الرواة سوى

الفارسي فإن في روايته الحرث بن عبد الأعلى قال وهو خطأ بل الصواب الحرث بن

عبد الله وهذا الذي نقله عن رواية الفارسي غير مقبول بل الصواب أنها كرواية

غيره الحرث بن عبد الله ولعله وقع للقاضي نسخة عن الفارسي فيها هذه اللفظة

مصحفة على الفارسي لا من الفارسي والله أعلم  قوله (ما أظن أبا خبيب) هو بضم

الخاء المعجمة وسبق بيانه مرات
# 
# قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (لولا حداثة عهدهم) هو بفتح الحاء أي قربه قوله

صلى الله عليه وسلم (فإن بدا لقومك) هو بغير همزة يقال بداله في الأمر بداء

بالمد أي حدث له فيه رأي لم يكن وهو ذو بدوات أي يتغير رأيه والبداء محال

على الله تعالى بخلاف النسخ قوله (فهلمي لأريك) هذا جار على إحدى اللغتين

في هلم قال الجوهري تقول هلم يا رجل بفتح الميم بمعنى تعال قال الخليلي

أصله لم من قولهم لم الله شعثه أي جمعه كأنه أراد لم نفسك الينا أي اقرب

وها للتنبيه وحذفت ألفها لكثرة الاستعمال وجعلا اسما واحدا يستوى فيه

الواحد والاثنان والجمع المؤنث فيقال في الجماعة هلم هذه لغة أهل الحجاز

قال الله تعالى والقائلين لإخوانهم هلم الينا وأهل نجد يصرفونها فيقولون

للاثنين هلما وللجمع هلموا وللمرأة هلمى وللنساء هلمن والأول أفصح هذا كلام

الجوهري قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (حتى إذا كان أن يدخل) هكذا هو في النسخ

كلها كاد أن يدخل وفيه حجة لجواز دخول أن بعد كاد وقد كثر ذلك وهي لغة

فصيحة ولكن الأشهر عدمه قوله (فنكت ساعة بعصاه) أي بحث بطرفها في الأرض

وهذه عادة من تفكر في أمر مهم قوله
# 
# (فقال الحرث بن عبد الله بن أبي ربيعة لا تقل هذا يا أمير المؤمنين فأنا

سمعت أم المؤمنين تحدث) هذا فيه الانتصار للمظلوم ورد الغيبة وتصديق الصادق

إذا كذبه إنسان والحرث هذا تابعي وهو الحرث بن عبد الله بن عياش بن أبي

ربيعة قولها (سألت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عن الجدر) وفي آخر الحديث

(لنظرت أن أدخل الجدر في البيت) هو بفتح الجيم وإسكان الدال المهملة وهو

الحجر وسبق بيان حكمه قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم في حديث سعيد بن منصور
# 
# (ولولا أن قومك حديث عهدهم في الجاهلية) هكذا هو في جميع النسخ في

الجاهلية وهو بمعنى بالجاهلية كما في  سائر الروايات والله أعلم

| (باب الحج عن العاجز لزمانة وهرم ونحوهما أو للموت)
# [1334] قوله (كان الفضل بن عباس رديف رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

فجاءته امرأة من خثعم تستفتيه فجعل الفضل ينظر إليها وتنظر إليه فجعل رسول

الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يصرف وجه الفضل إلى الشق الآخر فقالت يا رسول الله

إن فريضة الله على عباده في الحج أدركت أبي شيخا
# 
# كبيرا لا يستطيع أن يثبت على الراحلة أفأحج عنه قال نعم وذلك في حجة

الوداع) وفي الرواية الأخرى فحجي عنه هذا الحديث فيه فوائد منها جواز

الإرداف على الدابة إذا كانت مطيقة وجواز سماع صوت الأجنبية عند الحاجة في

الاستفتاء والمعاملة وغير ذلك ومنها تحريم النظر إلى الأجنبية ومنها إزالة

المنكر باليد لمن أمكنه ومنها جواز النيابة في الحج عن العاجز المأيوس منه

بهرم أو زمانة أو موت ومنها جواز حج المرأة عن الرجل ومنها بر الوالدين

بالقيام بمصالحهما من قضاء دين وخدمة ونفقة وحج عنهما وغير ذلك ومنها وجوب

الحج على من هو عاجز بنفسه مستطيع بغيره كولده وهذا مذهبنا لأنها قالت

أدركته فريضة الحج شيخا كبيرا لا يستطيع أن يثبت على الراحلة ومنها جواز
