في الموطأ وسفيان بن عيينة والعمري ويونس وغيرهم عن الزهري وفيه يوم خيبر

وكذا ذكره مسلم عن جماعة عن الزهري وهذا هو الصحيح وقد روى أبو داود من

حديث الربيع بن سبرة عن أبيه النهي عنها في حجة الوداع قال أبو داود وهذا

أصح ما روي في ذلك وقد روي عن سبرة أيضا إباحتها في حجة الوداع ثم نهى

النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم عنها حينئذ إلى يوم القيامة وروي عن الحسن البصري

أنها ما حلت قط إلا في عمرة القضاء وروي هذا عن سبرة الجهني أيضا ولم يذكر

مسلم في روايات حديث سبرة تعيين وقت إلا في رواية محمد بن سعيد الدارمي

ورواية إسحاق بن إبراهيم ورواية يحيى بن يحيى فإنه ذكر فيها يوم فتح مكة

قالوا وذكر الرواية بإباحتها يوم حجة الوداع خطأ لأنه لم يكن يؤمئذ ضرورة

ولا عزوبة وأكثرهم حجوا بنسائهم والصحيح أن الذي جرى في حجة الوداع مجرد

النهي كما جاء في غير رواية ويكون تجديده صلى الله عليه وسلم النهي عنها

يومئذ لاجتماع الناس وليبلغ الشاهد الغائب ولتمام الدين وتقرر الشريعة كما

قرر غير شيء وبين الحلال والحرام يومئذ وبت تحريم المتعة حينئذ لقوله إلى

يوم القيامة قال القاضي ويحتمل ما جاء من تحريم المتعة يوم خيبر وفي عمرة

القضاء ويوم الفتح ويوم أوطاس أنه جدد النهي عنها في هذه المواطن لأن حديث

تحريمها يوم خيبر صحيح لا مطعن فيه بل هو ثابت من رواية الثقات الأثبات لكن

في رواية سفيان أنه نهى عن المتعة وعن لحوم الحمر الأهلية يوم خيبر فقال

بعضهم هذا الكلام فيه انفصال ومعناه أنه حرم المتعة ولم يبين زمن تحريمها

ثم قال ولحوم الحمر الأهلية يوم خيبر فيكون يوم خيبر لتحريم الحمر خاصة ولم

يبين وقت تحريم المتعة ليجمع بين الروايات قال هذا القائل وهذا هو الأشبه

أن تحريم المتعة كان بمكة وأما لحوم الحمر فبخيبر بلا شك قال
# 
# القاضي وهذا أحسن لو ساعده سائر الروايات عن غير  سفيان قال والأولى ما

قلناه أنه قرر التحريم لكن يبقى بعد هذا ما جاء من ذكر إباحته في عمرة

القضاء ويوم الفتح ويوم أوطاس فتحتمل أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أباحها

لهم للضرورة بعد التحريم ثم حرمها تحريما مؤبدا فيكون حرمها يوم خيبر وفي

عمرة القضاء ثم أباحها يوم الفتح للضرورة ثم حرمها يوم الفتح أيضا تحريما

مؤبدا وتسقط رواية إباحتها يوم حجة الوداع لأنها مروية عن سبرة الجهني

وإنما روى الثقات الأثبات عنه الإباحة يوم فتح مكة والذي في حجة الوداع

إنما هو التحريم فيؤخذ من حديثه ما اتفق عليه جمهور الرواة ووافقه عليه
chapters.anchors:
- Root: م-ت-ع (m-t-ʿ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Enjoyment, gratification, or usufruct; the root denotes taking pleasure or benefit from something for a specified duration.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In legal-theological usage, it designates a contractual union for a fixed term with stipulated compensation (ajr), a category distinct from permanent marriage (nikāḥ) in its temporal limitation.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense is 'enjoyment' (ḥaqīqah); the technical marital sense is a metaphorical extension (majāz) fixed by juristic convention, not by linguistic necessity.
- Root: ن-س-خ (n-s-kh)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To erase, supersede, or abrogate; a later ruling removing or replacing an earlier one.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In uṣūl al-fiqh, it denotes the divine abrogation of a prior legal ruling by a subsequent revelation, preserving the earlier text but nullifying its operative force.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal 'copying' or 'erasure'; metaphorically applied to legal supersession, not physical deletion.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional and Temporal Clause Coordination (al-ʿaṭf ʿalā al-sharṭ wa al-ẓarf) — When multiple temporal adverbs (e.g., 'day of Khaybar', 'day of the Conquest') are coordinated, each governs its own verb, requiring careful parsing to distinguish distinct events from reiterated emphasis.
chapters.translation:
I say: Know that Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ has expanded the commentary on this chapter with an eloquent exposition, presenting in it precious matters and other matters in which he is opposed. The proper approach is to transmit what he mentioned in summary, then to mention what is objected to and opposed in it, and to alert to the chosen position.

Al-Māzarī said: It is established that temporary marriage (nikāḥ al-mutʿah) was permissible in the early period of Islam. Then it is established through the sound hadiths mentioned here that it was abrogated, and consensus (ijmāʿ) was concluded upon its prohibition. None opposed this except a faction of the innovators (al-mustabdiʿah). They clung to the hadiths reported concerning its permissibility, and we have already mentioned that these are abrogated, so there is no evidential force in them for their claim. They also clung to His saying, the Exalted: {«فَمَا اسْتَمْتَعْتُمْ بِهِ مِنْهُنَّ فَآتُوهُنَّ أُجُورَهُنَّ»} ("So for whatever you have enjoyed from them, give them their compensation"), and in the reading of Ibn Masʿūd: "So for whatever you have enjoyed from them until a specified term." This reading of Ibn Masʿūd is anomalous (shādhdhah); it is not admissible as evidence, neither as Qur'an nor as report, and acting upon it is not obligatory.

Al-Māzarī said: And Zufar said: Whoever contracts a temporary marriage, his marriage becomes perpetual (taʾabbada nikāḥuhu). It is as though he considered the mention of the term to fall under the category of corrupt conditions (shurūṭ fāsidah) in marriage, for these are nullified and the marriage remains valid.

Al-Māzarī said: The reports in Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim concerning the prohibition of temporary marriage differ. In one report, he — peace and blessings be upon him — prohibited it on the day of Khaybar; in another, he prohibited it on the day of the Conquest of Mecca. If one who permits temporary marriage clings to this, claiming that the hadiths are contradictory and that this discrepancy impugns them, we say: This claim is erroneous, and this is not a contradiction. For it is valid that he prohibited it in one period, then prohibited it in another period as a confirmation (tawkīd), or so that the prohibition might become widely known and be heard by those who had not heard it initially. Thus, some narrators heard the prohibition in one period, and others heard it in another period, and each transmitted what he heard and attributed it to the time of his hearing. This is the statement of al-Māzarī.

Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ said: A group of the Companions reported the hadith of the permissibility of temporary marriage. Muslim mentioned it from the narration of Ibn Masʿūd, Ibn ʿAbbās, Jābir, Salamah ibn al-Akwaʿ, and Sabrah ibn Maʿbad al-Juhanī. In none of these hadiths is it mentioned that this occurred in settled habitation (al-ḥaḍar); rather, it occurred in their journeys during military expeditions (al-ghazw) at times of necessity and the absence of women, especially since their lands were hot and their patience regarding women was little. It has been mentioned in the hadith of Ibn Abī ʿUmar that it was a concession (rukḥṣah) in the early period of Islam for one who was compelled to it, like carrion (al-maytah) and the like. Something similar is reported from Ibn ʿAbbās, may God be pleased with them both. Muslim mentioned from Salamah ibn al-Akwaʿ its permissibility on the day of Awtās, and from the narration of Sabrah its permissibility on the day of the Conquest — and these two are one [event]. Then it was prohibited on that very day. In the hadith of ʿAlī, its prohibition is mentioned on the day of Khaybar, which is before the Conquest. Other than Muslim mentioned from ʿAlī that the Prophet — peace and blessings be upon him — prohibited it in the expedition of Tabūk, from the narration of Isḥāq ibn Rāshid, from al-Zuhrī, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī, from his father, from ʿAlī. No one followed him in this, and it is an error on his part. This hadith was narrated by Mālik in al-Muwaṭṭaʾ, Sufyān ibn ʿUyaynah, al-ʿUmarī, Yūnus, and others, from al-Zuhrī, and in it [the prohibition is] on the day of Khaybar. Likewise, Muslim mentioned it from a group from al-Zuhrī, and this is the correct version.

Abū Dāwūd narrated from the hadith of al-Rabīʿ ibn Sabrah, from his father, the prohibition of it in the Farewell Pilgrimage (ḥajjat al-wadāʿ). Abū Dāwūd said: This is the most authentic of what has been reported concerning that matter. It has also been reported from Sabrah its permissibility in the Farewell Pilgrimage, then the Prophet — peace and blessings be upon him — prohibited it at that time until the Day of Resurrection. It has been reported from al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī that it was never permitted except in the ʿUmrah of al-Qaḍāʾ (the compensatory ʿUmrah). This has also been reported from Sabrah al-Juhanī. Muslim did not mention in the narrations of the hadith of Sabrah a specification of time except in the narration of Muḥammad ibn Saʿīd al-Dārimī, the narration of Isḥāq ibn Ibrāhīm, and the narration of Yaḥyā ibn Yaḥyā, for in these the day of the Conquest of Mecca is mentioned.

They said: The report of its permissibility on the day of the Farewell Pilgrimage is an error, because at that time there was neither necessity nor bachelorhood, and most of them had performed the pilgrimage with their wives. The correct view is that what occurred in the Farewell Pilgrimage was merely the prohibition, as has come in more than one narration. His renewal of the prohibition on that day — peace and blessings be upon him — was due to the gathering of the people, so that the present might convey to the absent, and for the completion of the religion and the establishment of the Sacred Law, just as he established other matters and clarified the lawful and the unlawful on that day. The prohibition of temporary marriage was thereby made definitive at that time, due to his saying "until the Day of Resurrection."

Qāḍī [ʿIyāḍ] said: It is possible that what has come concerning the prohibition of temporary marriage on the day of Khaybar, in the ʿUmrah of al-Qaḍāʾ, on the day of the Conquest, and on the day of Awtās — that he renewed the prohibition in these places. For the hadith of its prohibition on the day of Khaybar is sound, with no ground for objection; rather, it is established from the narration of trustworthy, solid narrators (al-thiqāt al-athbāt). However, in the narration of Sufyān, he prohibited temporary marriage and the flesh of domesticated donkeys on the day of Khaybar. Some said: In this statement there is a point of differentiation (infiṣāl). Its meaning is that he prohibited temporary marriage without specifying the time of its prohibition, then said "and the flesh of domesticated donkeys on the day of Khaybar," so that the day of Khaybar is for the prohibition of donkey flesh specifically, and the time of the prohibition of temporary marriage was not specified, in order to reconcile the narrations. This speaker said: This is the most fitting view — that the prohibition of temporary marriage was in Mecca, while the prohibition of donkey flesh was in Khaybar without doubt.

Qāḍī [ʿIyāḍ] said: This would be excellent if the other narrations from other than Sufyān supported it. He said: The preferable view is what we have stated — that he confirmed the prohibition. But there remains after this what has come concerning the mention of its permissibility in the ʿUmrah of al-Qaḍāʾ, on the day of the Conquest, and on the day of Awtās. It is possible that the Prophet — peace and blessings be upon him — permitted it for them due to necessity after the prohibition, then prohibited it with an eternal prohibition. Thus, he prohibited it on the day of Khaybar and in the ʿUmrah of al-Qaḍāʾ, then permitted it on the day of the Conquest due to necessity, then prohibited it on the day of the Conquest as well with an eternal prohibition. And the narration of its permissibility on the day of the Farewell Pilgrimage falls away, because it is narrated from Sabrah al-Juhanī, and the trustworthy, solid narrators only narrated from him its permissibility on the day of the Conquest of Mecca. What occurred in the Farewell Pilgrimage is only the prohibition. Thus, from his hadith, what the majority of narrators agreed upon is taken, and what accords with it.

chapters.title_en: The Abrogation and Permissibility of Temporary Marriage (Nikāḥ al-Mutʿah) — Section 555
chapters.arabic_text:
غيره من الصحابة رضي الله عنهم من النهي عنها يوم الفتح ويكون تحريمها يوم

حجة الوداع تأكيدا وإشاعة له كما سبق وأما قول الحسن إنما كانت في عمرة

القضاء لا قبلها ولا بعدها فترده الأحاديث الثابتة في تحريمها يوم خيبر وهي

قبل عمرة القضاء وما جاء من إباحتها يوم فتح مكة ويوم أوطاس مع أن الرواية

بهذا إنما جاءت عن سبرة الجهني وهو راوي الروايات الأخر وهي أصح فيترك ما

خالف الصحيح وقد قال بعضهم هذا مما تداوله التحريم والإباحة والنسخ مرتين

والله أعلم هذا آخر كلام القاضي والصواب المختار أن التحريم والإباحة كانا

مرتين وكانت حلالا قبل خيبر ثم حرمت يوم خيبر ثم أبيحت يوم فتح مكة وهو يوم

أوطاس لا تصالهما ثم حرمت يومئذ بعد ثلاثة أيام تحريما مؤبدا إلى يوم

القيامة واستمر التحريم ولا يجوز أن يقال إن الإباحة مختصة بما قبل خيبر

والتحريم يوم خيبر للتأبيد وأن الذي كان يوم الفتح مجرد توكيد التحريم من

غير تقدم إباحة يوم الفتح كما اختاره المازرى والقاضي لأن الروايات التي

ذكرها مسلم في الإباحة يوم الفتح صريحة في ذلك فلا يجوز إسقاطها ولا مانع

يمنع تكرير الإباحة والله أعلم قال القاضي واتفق العلماء على أن هذه المتعة

كانت نكاحا إلى أجل لا ميراث فيها وفراقها يحصل بانقضاء الأجل من غير طلاق

ووقع الإجماع  بعد ذلك على تحريمها من جميع العلماء إلا الروافض وكان بن

عباس رضي الله عنه يقول بإباحتها وروي عنه أنه رجع عنه قال وأجمعوا على أنه

متى وقع نكاح المتعة الآن حكم ببطلانه سواء كان قبل الدخول أو بعده إلا ما

سبق عن زفر واختلف أصحاب مالك هل يحد الواطئ فيه ومذهبنا أنه لا يحد لشبهة

العقد وشبهة الخلاف ومأخذ الخلاف اختلاف الأصوليين في أن الإجماع بعد

الخلاف هل يرفع الخلاف ويصير المسألة مجمعا عليها والأصح عند أصحابنا أنه

لا يرفعه بل يدوم
# 
# الخلاف ولا يصير المسألة بعد ذلك مجمعا عليها أبدا وبه قال القاضي أبو

بكر الباقلاني قال القاضي وأجمعوا على أن من نكح نكاحا مطلقا ونيته أن لا

يمكث معها إلا مدة نواها فنكاحه صحيح حلال وليس نكاح متعة وإنما نكاح

المتعة ما وقع بالشرط المذكور ولكن قال مالك ليس هذا من أخلاق الناس وشذ

الأوزاعي فقال هو نكاح متعة ولا خير فيه والله أعلم
# [1404] قوله (فقلنا ألا نستخصي فنهانا عن ذلك) فيه موافقة لما قدمناه في

الباب السابق من تحريم الخصي لما فيه من تغيير خلق الله ولما فيه من قطع

النسل وتعذيب الحيوان والله أعلم قوله (رخص لنا أن ننكح المرأة بالثوب) أي

بالثوب وغيره مما نتراضى به قوله (ثم قرأ عبد الله يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا

تحرموا طيبات ما أحل الله لكم) فيه إشارة إلى أنه كان يعتقد إباحتها كقول

بن عباس وأنه لم يبلغه نسخها قوله (وحدثني أمية بن بسطام العيشي حدثنا يزيد

بن زريع حدثنا روح وهو بن القاسم عن
# 
# عمرو بن دينار عن الحسن بن محمد عن سلمة بن الأكوع وجابر) هكذا هو في بعض

النسخ وسقط في بعضها ذكر الحسن بن محمد بل قال عن عمرو بن دينار عن سلمة

وجابر وذكر المازري أيضا أن النسخ اختلف فيه وأنه ثبت ذكر الحسن في رواية

بن ماهان وسقط في رواية الجلودي وسبق بيان أمية بن بسطام وأنه يجوز صرف

بسطام وترك  صرفه وأن الباء تكسر وقد تفتح والعيشى بالشين المعجمة
# [1405] قوله (عن جابر بن عبد الله وسلمة بن الأكوع قالا خرج علينا منادي

رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال قد أذن لكم أن تستمتعوا) وفي الرواية

الثانية عن سلمة وجابر أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أتانا فأذن لنا في

المتعة فقوله في الثانية أتانا يحتمل أتانا رسوله ومناديه كما صرح به في

الرواية الأولى ويحتمل أنه صلى الله عليه وسلم مر عليهم فقال لهم ذلك

بلسانه قوله (استمتعنا على عهد رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وأبي بكر

وعمر) هذا محمول على أن الذي استمتع في عهد أبي بكر وعمر لم يبلغه النسخ

وقوله (حتى نهانا عنه عمر) يعني حين بلغه النسخ وقد سبق إيضاح هذا قوله

(كنا نستمتع بالقبضة من التمر والدقيق) القبضة بضم القاف وفتحها والضم أفصح

قال الجوهري القبضة بالضم ما قبضت عليه من الشيء يقال أعطاه قبضة من سويق
# 
# أو تمر قال وربما فتح قوله (حدثنا حامد بن عمر البكراوي) ذكرنا مرات أنه

منسوب إلى جده الأعلى أبي بكر الصحابي قوله (رخص رسول الله صلى الله عليه

وسلم عام أوطاس في المتعة ثلاثا ثم نهى عنها) هذا تصريح بأنها أبيحت يوم

فتح مكة وهو ويوم أوطاس شيء واحد وأوطاس واد بالطائف ويصرف ولا يصرف فمن

صرفه أراد الوادي والمكان ومن لم يصرفه أراد البقعة كما في نظائره وأكثر

استعمالهم له غير مصروف
# [1406] قوله (الربيع بن سبرة) هو بفتح السين المهملة وإسكان الباء

الموحدة قوله (فانطلقت أنا ورجل إلى امرأة من بني عامر كأنها بكرة عيطاء)

أما البكرة فهي الفتية من الإبل أي الشابة القوية وأما العيطاء فبفتح العين

المهملة وإسكان الياء
# 
# المثناة تحت وبطاء مهملة وبالمد وهي الطويلة العنق في اعتدال وحسن قوام
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ح-ر-م (ḥ-r-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning of prohibition, sanctity, and that which is rendered inviolable or forbidden.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In Kalām, taḥrīm denotes a divine legislative prohibition (manʿ) that establishes legal culpability (taklīf) and is subject to abrogation (naskh) until superseded.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage denotes the act of forbidding; metaphorical (majāz) usage may refer to declaring something sacred or inviolable in a ritual sense.
- Root: أ-ب-ح (a-b-ḥ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To permit, make lawful, or render something accessible without restriction.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Ibaḥah signifies divine permission (idhn) that removes legal impediment, distinct from obligation (wujūb) or recommendation (nadb).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal usage denotes explicit legal permissibility; metaphorical usage may indicate mere toleration or absence of prohibition.
- Root: ن-س-خ (n-s-kh)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To abrogate, supersede, or remove a prior ruling by a subsequent one.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Naskh in uṣūl al-fiqh is the divine replacement of a ḥukm by a later revelation, indicating temporal progression in legislation.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal usage is the act of erasure or substitution; metaphorical usage applies to legal rulings being lifted or replaced.
- Sībawayh Rule: Rule of ʿAṭf (Coordination) and Ḥāl (Circumstantial Clause) — The text employs coordinated clauses (wa-ʿaṭf) to juxtapose opposing rulings (taḥrīm vs. ibāḥah) and circumstantial phrases (ḥāl) to specify temporal conditions (e.g., "day of Khaybar," "day of the Conquest"), requiring precise parsing to distinguish sequential events from simultaneous ones.
chapters.translation:
I say: And the rest of the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, [are agreed] upon the prohibition of it on the Day of the Conquest, and its prohibition on the Day of the Farewell Pilgrimage was a confirmation (taʾkīd) and a public proclamation of that, as has preceded. As for the statement of al-Ḥasan that it was only [permissible] during the ʿUmrah of al-Qaḍāʾ, neither before it nor after it — the established hadiths concerning its prohibition on the Day of Khaybar, which was before the ʿUmrah of al-Qaḍāʾ, refute this, along with what has come regarding its permissibility on the Day of the Conquest of Mecca and the Day of Awtās. Moreover, the narration of this [permissibility] came only from Sabrah al-Juhanī, who is also the narrator of the other reports, and those [prohibiting reports] are more authentic (aṣaḥḥ); thus, what contradicts the authentic is abandoned. Some have said: This is a matter that was subject to prohibition and permissibility, with abrogation occurring twice. And Allah knows best. This is the end of al-Qāḍī's discourse.

The correct and chosen view (al-ṣawāb al-mukhtār) is that the prohibition and permissibility occurred twice: it was lawful before Khaybar, then it was prohibited on the Day of Khaybar, then it was permitted on the Day of the Conquest of Mecca — which is the Day of Awtās, as the two are conjoined — then it was prohibited on that very day after three days, with an eternal prohibition (taḥrīman muʾabbadan) until the Day of Resurrection, and the prohibition has continued. It is not permissible to say that the permissibility was specific to what preceded Khaybar, and that the prohibition on the Day of Khaybar was eternal, and that what occurred on the Day of the Conquest was merely a confirmation of the prohibition without a prior permissibility on the Day of the Conquest — as chosen by al-Māzarī and al-Qāḍī — because the narrations that Muslim mentioned regarding permissibility on the Day of the Conquest are explicit (ṣarīḥah) in that regard. Thus, it is not permissible to discard them, and there is no impediment preventing the repetition of permissibility. And Allah knows best.

Al-Qāḍī said: The scholars have agreed that this temporary marriage (mutʿah) was a marriage (nikāḥ) for a fixed term (ilā ajal), with no inheritance in it, and its dissolution occurs by the expiration of the term without divorce. Consensus (ijmāʿ) was subsequently established upon its prohibition by all scholars, except the Rāfiḍah. Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with him, held its permissibility, and it is narrated from him that he retracted that view. He said: And they have agreed that whenever a temporary marriage occurs now, it is judged invalid (bāṭil), whether before consummation or after, except what has been reported from Zufar. The companions of Mālik differed as to whether the one who engages in intercourse [in such a marriage] is subject to the ḥadd punishment. Our school (madhhab) holds that he is not subject to the ḥadd due to the ambiguity of the contract (shubhat al-ʿaqd) and the ambiguity of the disagreement (shubhat al-khilāf). The basis of the disagreement is the differing of the uṣūliyyūn regarding whether consensus after disagreement (al-ijmāʿ baʿd al-khilāf) removes the disagreement and renders the matter unanimously agreed upon. The more correct view (al-aṣaḥḥ) according to our companions is that it does not remove it; rather, the disagreement endures, and the matter does not become unanimously agreed upon thereafter, ever. This is also the view of al-Qāḍī Abū Bakr al-Bāqillānī.

Al-Qāḍī said: And they have agreed that whoever contracts an absolute marriage (nikāḥ muṭlaq) with the intention in his mind not to remain with her except for a period he has intended — his marriage is valid and lawful, and it is not a temporary marriage. Rather, temporary marriage is only that which occurs with the aforementioned condition. However, Mālik said: This is not from the character of people. Al-Awzāʿī deviated [from this] and said: It is a temporary marriage, and there is no good in it. And Allah knows best.

[1404] His statement: "So we said, 'Shall we not castrate ourselves?' And he forbade us from that" — In it is agreement with what we have presented in the previous chapter regarding the prohibition of castration (al-khiṣāʾ), due to what it entails of altering Allah's creation (taghyīr khalq Allāh), cutting off progeny (qaṭʿ al-nasl), and torturing animals. And Allah knows best.

His statement: "He permitted us to marry a woman with a garment (al-thawb)" — i.e., with a garment or other than it, whatever we mutually agree upon.

His statement: "Then ʿAbdullāh recited: {«يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لَا تُحَرِّمُوا طَيِّبَاتِ مَا أَحَلَّ اللَّهُ لَكُمْ»} (O you who believe, do not prohibit the good things that Allah has made lawful for you)" — In it is an indication that he believed in its permissibility, like the statement of Ibn ʿAbbās, and that the report of its abrogation had not reached him.

His statement: "And narrated to me Umayyah ibn Bisṭām al-ʿAyshī, narrated to us Yazīd ibn Zurayʿ, narrated to us Rawḥ — and he is Ibn al-Qāsim — from ʿAmr ibn Dīnār, from al-Ḥasan ibn Muḥammad, from Salamah ibn al-Akwaʿ and Jābir" — Thus it is in some copies, and in others the mention of al-Ḥasan ibn Muḥammad is omitted, rather [they say]: from ʿAmr ibn Dīnār, from Salamah and Jābir. Al-Māzarī also mentioned that the copies differed regarding it, and that the mention of al-Ḥasan is established in the narration of Ibn Māhān and omitted in the narration of al-Julūdī. The clarification of Umayyah ibn Bisṭām has preceded — that it is permissible to decline Bisṭām (i.e., treat it as diptote) or not to decline it, and that the bāʾ is kasrah and may be fatḥah, and al-ʿAyshī is with the dotted shīn.

[1405] His statement: "From Jābir ibn ʿAbdillāh and Salamah ibn al-Akwaʿ, they said: The crier (munādī) of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, came out to us and said: 'Permission has been granted to you to enjoy (tastamtiʿū).'" And in the second narration from Salamah and Jābir: "That the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, came to us and granted us permission for the mutʿah." So his statement in the second [narration], "came to us" (atānā), possibly means his messenger and his crier came to us, as is explicit in the first narration, and possibly means that he, peace and blessings be upon him, passed by them and said that to them with his own tongue.

His statement: "We enjoyed (istamtaʿnā) during the era of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, and Abū Bakr and ʿUmar" — This is interpreted as [meaning] that the one who enjoyed during the era of Abū Bakr and ʿUmar had not been reached by the abrogation. And his statement: "Until ʿUmar forbade us from it" — meaning when the abrogation reached him. The clarification of this has preceded.

His statement: "We used to enjoy [marriage] with a handful (al-qabḍah) of dates and flour" — al-qabḍah is with ḍammah on the qāf and with fatḥah on it, and the ḍammah is more eloquent (afṣaḥ). Al-Jawharī said: al-qabḍah with ḍammah is what you grasp of a thing; one says: "He gave him a qabḍah of sawīq or dates." And he said: It is sometimes opened (i.e., with fatḥah).

His statement: "Narrated to us Ḥāmid ibn ʿUmar al-Bakrāwī" — We have mentioned multiple times that he is attributed to his great-grandfather Abū Bakr, the Companion.

His statement: "The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, permitted mutʿah in the year of Awtās for three [days], then forbade it" — This is an explicit statement that it was permitted on the Day of the Conquest of Mecca, and it and the Day of Awtās are one and the same thing. Awtās is a valley (wādī) in al-Ṭāʾif, and it is declined and not declined: whoever declines it intends the valley and the place, and whoever does not decline it intends the land (al-buqʿah), as in its parallels. And the more frequent usage of theirs is without declension.

[1406] His statement: "al-Rabīʿ ibn Sabrah" — It is with fatḥah on the sīn (unpointed) and sukūn on the bāʾ (single-pointed).

His statement: "So I went, I and a man, to a woman from Banū ʿĀmir, as if she were a young she-camel, ʿayṭāʾ" — As for al-bakrah, it is the young female camel, i.e., the youthful and strong one. As for al-ʿayṭāʾ, it is with fatḥah on the ʿayn (unpointed), sukūn on the yāʾ (double-pointed below), and a maddah, and it is the one with a long neck in moderation and beauty of form (qawām).

chapters.title_en: The Prohibition of Combining a Woman with Her Paternal or Maternal Aunt in Marriage, and Related Rulings on Temporary Marriage (Mutʿah)
chapters.arabic_text:
والعيط بفتح العين والياء طول العنق قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (من كان عنده

شيء من هذه النساء التي يتمتع فليخل سبيلها) هكذا هو في جميع النسخ التي

يتمتع فليخل أي  يتمتع بها فحذف بها لدلالة الكلام عليه أو أوقع يتمتع موقع

يباشر أي يباشرها وحذف المفعول قوله (وهو قريب من الدمامة) هي بفتح الدال

المهملة وهي القبح في الصورة قوله (فبردي خلق) هو بفتح اللام أي قريب من

البالي قوله (فتلقتنا فتاة مثل البكرة العنطنطة) هي بعين مهملة مفتوحة

وبنونين الأولى مفتوحة وبطاءين مهملتين وهي كالعيطاء وسبق بيانها وقيل هي

الطويلة فقط والمشهور الأول قوله (ينظر إلى عطفها) هو بكسر العين أي جانبها

وقيل من رأسها إلى وركها وفي هذا الحديث دليل على
# 
# أنه لم يكن في نكاح المتعة ولي ولا شهود قوله (إن برد هذا خلق مح) هو

بميم مفتوحة وحاء مهملة مشددة وهو البالي ومنه مح الكتاب إذا بلي ودرس قوله

صلى الله عليه وسلم (قد كنت أذنت لكم في الاستمتاع من النساء وإن الله قد

حرم ذلك إلى يوم القيامة فمن كان عنده منهن شيء فليخل سبيلها ولا تأخذوا

مما آتيتموهن شيئا) وفي هذا الحديث التصريح بالمنسوخ والناسخ في حديث واحد

من كلام رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كحديث كنت نهيتكم عن زيارة القبور

فزوروها وفيه التصريح بتحريم نكاح المتعة إلى يوم القيامة وأنه يتعين تأويل

قوله في الحديث السابق أنهم كانوا يتمتعون إلى عهد أبي بكر وعمر على أنه لم

يبلغهم الناسخ كما سبق وفيه أن المهر الذي كان أعطاها يستقر لها ولا يحل

أخذ شيء منه وإن فارقها قبل الأجل المسمى كما أنه
# 
# يستقر في النكاح المعروف المهر المسمى بالوطء ولا يسقط منه شيء بالفرقة

بعده قوله (فآمرت نفسها ساعة) هو بهمزة ممدودة أي شاورت نفسها وأفكرت في

ذلك ومنه قوله تعالى أن الملأ
# 
# يأتمرون بك قوله (إن ناسا أعمى الله قلوبهم كما أعمى أبصارهم يفتون

بالمتعة يعرض برجل) يعني يعرض بابن عباس قوله (إنك لجلف جاف) الجلف بكسر

الجيم قال بن السكيت وغيره الجلف هو الجافي وعلى هذا قيل إنما جمع بينهما

توكيدا لاختلاف اللفظ والجافي هو الغليظ الطبع القليل الفهم والعلم والأدب

لبعده عن أهل ذلك قوله (فوالله لئن فعلتها لأرجمنك بأحجارك) هذا محمول على

أنه أبلغه الناسخ لها وأنه لم يبق شك في تحريمها فقال إن فعلتها بعد ذلك

ووطئت فيها كنت زانيا ورجمتك بالأحجار التي يرجم بها الزاني قوله (فأخبرني

خالد بن المهاجر بن سيف الله) سيف الله هو خالد بن الوليد المخزومي سماه

بذلك رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لأنه ينكأ في أعداء الله
# 
# [1407] قوله (نهى عن متعة النساء يوم خيبر وعن أكل لحوم الحمر الإنسية)

قوله الإنسية ضبطوه بوجهين أحدهما كسر الهمزة وإسكان النون والثاني فتحهما

جميعا وصرح القاضي بترجيح الفتح وأنه رواية الأكثرين وفي هذا تحريم لحوم

الحمر الإنسية وهو مذهبنا ومذهب العلماء كافة إلا طائفة يسيرة من السلف فقد

روي عن بن عباس وعائشة وبعض السلف إباحته وروي عنهم تحريمه وروي عن مالك

كراهته وتحريمه قوله (إنك رجل تائه) هو الحائر الذاهب عن الطريق المستقيم

والله أعلم
#

| (باب تحريم الجمع بين المرأة وعمتها أو خالتها في 
# النكاح)
# [1408] قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (لا يجمع بين المرأة وعمتها ولا بين

المرأة وخالتها) وفي رواية لا تنكح العمة على بنت الأخ ولا ابنة الأخت على

الخالة هذا دليل لمذاهب العلماء كافة أنه يحرم الجمع بين المرأة وعمتها

وبينها وبين خالتها سواء كانت عمة وخالة حقيقة وهي أخت الأب وأخت الأم
# 
# أو مجازية وهي أخت أبي الأب وأبي الجد وإن علا أو أخت أم الأم وأم الجدة

من جهتي الأم والأب وإن علت فكلهن بإجماع العلماء يحرم الجمع بينهما وقالت

طائفة من الخوارج والشيعة يجوز واحتجوا بقوله تعالى وأحل لكم ما وراء ذلكم

واحتج الجمهور بهذه الأحاديث خصوا بها الآية والصحيح الذي عليه جمهور

الأصوليين جواز تخصيص عموم القرآن بخبر الواحد لأنه صلى الله عليه وسلم

مبين للناس ما أنزل إليهم من كتاب الله وأما الجمع بينهما في الوطء بملك

اليمين كالنكاح فهو حرام عند العلماء كافة وعند الشيعة مباح قالوا ويباح

أيضا الجمع بين الأختين بملك اليمين  قالوا وقوله تعالى وأن تجمعوا بين

الأختين إنما هو في النكاح قال وقال العلماء كافة هو حرام
# 
# كالنكاح لعموم قوله تعالى وأن تجمعوا بين الأختين وقولهم إنه مختص

بالنكاح لا يقبل بل جميع المذكورات في الآية محرمات بالنكاح وبملك اليمين

جميعا ومما يدل عليه قوله تعالى والمحصنات من النساء إلا ما ملكت أيمانكم

فإن معناه أن ملك اليمين يحل وطؤها بملك اليمين لإنكاحها فإن عقد النكاح

عليها لا يجوز لسيدها والله أعلم وأما باقي الأقارب كالجمع بين بنتي العم

أو بنتي الخالة أو نحوهما فجائز عندنا وعند العلماء كافة إلا ما حكاه

القاضي عن بعض السلف أنه حرمه دليل الجمهور قوله تعالى وأحل لكم ما وراء
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ع-ي-ط (ʿ- y- ṭ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Length and elongation of the neck; a woman described as such is tall and graceful in stature.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Denotes physical elongation as a natural attribute, not a metaphorical or moral quality.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Used literally here for bodily form; no figurative extension.
- Root: د-م-م (d-m-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Ugliness or repulsiveness in appearance; opposite of beauty (ḥusn).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Aesthetic deficiency in the created form, not a moral failing.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal description of physical unattractiveness; no metaphorical sense.
- Root: خ-ل-ق (kh-l-q)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Worn-out, threadbare garment; also creation, but here specifically the former.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In this context, denotes the state of being effaced or eroded by use.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for physical wear; distinct from the theological sense of "creation" (khalq).
- Root: ج-ل-ف (j-l-f)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Rough, coarse, uncouth; lacking refinement.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Moral and intellectual roughness, indicating distance from knowledge and propriety.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for harshness of character; used here as a reproach.
- Root: ت-و-ه (t-w-h)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Perplexity, wandering, deviation from the straight path.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Spiritual and intellectual bewilderment, straying from truth.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for being lost; metaphorical for error in judgment.
- Sībawayh Rule: Ellipsis of the object (ḥadhf al-mafʿūl) and prepositional phrase (ḥadhf al-jār wa-al-majrūr) when context indicates it; also, the rule of specification (takhṣīṣ) of a general Quranic verse by a solitary hadith (khabar al-wāḥid), as upheld by the majority of uṣūliyyūn.
chapters.translation:
I say: The word "al-ʿayṭ" (العيط) — with the fatḥah on the ʿayn and the yāʾ — means length of the neck. His saying, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him: «Whoever has anything of these women with whom he engaged in temporary marriage, let him let her go» — thus it appears in all the manuscripts: "with whom he engaged in temporary marriage" (yastamtiʿ), i.e., "with whom he engaged in temporary marriage with her" (yastamtiʿ bihā), but the prepositional phrase "with her" was omitted because the context indicates it; or the verb "yastamtiʿ" was placed in the position of "yubāshir" (to have direct intercourse), i.e., "he had direct intercourse with her," and the object was omitted. His saying: «and she is close to being ugly (damāmah)» — "damāmah" is with fatḥah on the dāl (the unpointed letter), and it means ugliness in appearance. His saying: «so a worn-out (khalaq) garment of mine» — it is with fatḥah on the lām, i.e., close to being threadbare. His saying: «so a young girl met us, like a tall, long-necked camel (al-bakrah al-ʿanṭanṭah)» — it is with an unpointed ʿayn, opened, and with two nūns, the first opened, and with two unpointed ṭāʾs; she is like the ʿayṭāʾ (long-necked woman), and its explanation has preceded. It was also said: she is merely tall; but the well-known (opinion) is the first. His saying: «looking at her side (ʿaṭfihā)» — it is with kasrah on the ʿayn, i.e., her side; and it was said: from her head to her hip. In this hadith there is evidence that in the temporary marriage (nikāḥ al-mutʿah) there was no guardian (walī) nor witnesses.

His saying: «Indeed, this garment of mine is worn-out (khalq muḥ)» — it is with an opened mīm and a shaddah on the unpointed ḥāʾ, and it means threadbare; from it is derived: "the book was effaced (muḥ)" when it is worn out and obliterated. His saying, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him: «I had permitted you temporary enjoyment of women, but God has indeed forbidden that until the Day of Resurrection. So whoever has anything of them, let him let her go, and do not take back anything of what you have given them.» In this hadith there is an explicit statement of the abrogated (mansūkh) and the abrogating (nāsikh) in a single hadith, from the speech of the Messenger of God, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him — like the hadith: «I had forbidden you from visiting graves, so visit them.» And in it there is an explicit statement of the prohibition of temporary marriage until the Day of Resurrection, and that it is obligatory to interpret his saying in the previous hadith — that they were engaging in temporary marriage until the era of Abū Bakr and ʿUmar — as meaning that the abrogating (revelation) had not reached them, as has preceded. And in it (is the ruling) that the dowry (mahr) which he had given her becomes firmly established for her, and it is not lawful to take anything of it back, even if he separates from her before the specified term — just as in the well-known marriage (nikāḥ), the specified dowry becomes firmly established by intercourse, and nothing of it falls away by separation after it.

His saying: «so she consulted herself (fāmarat nafsahā) for an hour» — it is with a prolonged hamzah, i.e., she consulted herself and reflected upon that matter. From it is the saying of God, the Exalted: {that the chiefs are plotting against you (yaʾtamirūna bika)} (Q 28:20). His saying: «Indeed, some people whose hearts God has blinded, just as He blinded their eyes, give legal rulings permitting temporary marriage» — he is alluding to a man, meaning he is alluding to Ibn ʿAbbās. His saying: «Indeed, you are a coarse, rough man (jilf jāf)» — "al-jilf" is with kasrah on the jīm. Ibn al-Sikkīt and others said: "al-jilf" is the rough, coarse man. On this basis, it was said that both terms were combined for emphasis due to the difference of wording. "Al-jāfī" is the one of harsh nature, little understanding, knowledge, and refinement, due to his distance from the people of such qualities. His saying: «For by God, if you do it, I will surely stone you with your own stones» — this is interpreted as meaning that the abrogating (prohibition) had reached him, and that there remained no doubt in its prohibition; so he said: "If you do it after this, and you engage in intercourse therein, you would be an adulterer, and I would stone you with the stones with which the adulterer is stoned." His saying: «So Khālid ibn al-Muhājir ibn Sayf Allāh informed me» — Sayf Allāh (the Sword of God) is Khālid ibn al-Walīd al-Makhzūmī; the Messenger of God, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, named him thus because he struck deeply (yankaʾu) against the enemies of God.

[1407] His saying: «He forbade temporary marriage of women on the Day of Khaybar, and the eating of the flesh of domesticated donkeys (al-ḥumur al-insiyyah)» — his saying "al-insiyyah": they recorded it in two ways: one with kasrah on the hamzah and sukūn on the nūn; the second with fatḥah on both. Al-Qāḍī explicitly stated the preponderance of the fatḥah, and that it is the narration of the majority. In this (hadith) is the prohibition of the flesh of domesticated donkeys, and this is our school (madhhab) and the school of all the scholars — except a small group of the Salaf, for it is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās, ʿĀʾishah, and some of the Salaf that it is permissible; and it is narrated from them that it is prohibited; and it is narrated from Mālik that he disliked it and prohibited it. His saying: «Indeed, you are a bewildered man (tāʾih)» — he is the perplexed one who deviates from the straight path. And God knows best.

| (Chapter: The Prohibition of Combining a Woman with Her Paternal Aunt or Maternal Aunt in Marriage)

[1408] His saying, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him: «One does not combine a woman with her paternal aunt, nor a woman with her maternal aunt» — and in another narration: «The paternal aunt is not married to the daughter of one’s brother, nor the daughter of one’s brother to the maternal aunt.» This is evidence for the schools of all the scholars that it is prohibited to combine a woman with her paternal aunt, and with her maternal aunt — whether the aunt is a real (ḥaqīqiyyah) paternal or maternal aunt, i.e., the sister of the father or the sister of the mother — or a figurative (majāziyyah) one, i.e., the sister of the grandfather or the sister of the great-grandfather, however high; or the sister of the grandmother or the great-grandmother, from both the maternal and paternal lines, however high. For all of these, by the consensus of the scholars, it is prohibited to combine them (in marriage). A group of the Khawārij and the Shīʿah said it is permissible, and they argued with His saying, the Exalted: {And lawful to you are all beyond those} (Q 4:24). The majority (jumhūr) argued with these hadiths, and they specified the verse by them. The correct view, upon which the majority of the uṣūliyyūn (scholars of legal theory) agree, is the permissibility of specifying the general (ʿāmm) of the Qurʾān by a solitary hadith (khabar al-wāḥid), because he, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, is the explainer to the people of what was revealed to them from the Book of God.

As for combining them (a woman and her aunt) in intercourse by right of ownership (milk al-yamīn), it is like marriage — it is prohibited by the consensus of all scholars, while the Shīʿah hold it permissible. They said: it is also permissible to combine two sisters by right of ownership. They said: His saying, the Exalted: {And that you combine between two sisters} (Q 4:23) applies only to marriage. He (al-Nawawī) said: And all the scholars said: it is prohibited, just as in marriage, due to the generality of His saying, the Exalted: {And that you combine between two sisters}, and their claim that it is specific to marriage is not accepted. Rather, all that is mentioned in the verse is prohibited both by marriage and by right of ownership alike. Among what indicates this is His saying, the Exalted: {And married women, except what your right hands possess} (Q 4:24) — for its meaning is that the right of ownership makes lawful the intercourse with her by virtue of ownership, not by contracting marriage upon her; for if a marriage contract is made upon her, it is not permissible for her master. And God knows best.

As for the rest of the relatives — like combining the two daughters of a paternal uncle, or the two daughters of a maternal aunt, or similar — it is permissible in our school and in the school of all the scholars, except what al-Qāḍī narrated from some of the Salaf that he prohibited it. The evidence of the majority is His saying, the Exalted: {And lawful to you are all beyond those} (Q 4:24).

chapters.title_en: The Prohibition of Combining a Woman and Her Niece in Marriage, and the Rulings on Betrothal and Marriage for the Pilgrim in Iḥrām
chapters.arabic_text:
ذلكم والله أعلم وأما الجمع بين زوجة الرجل وبنته من غيرها فجائز عندنا

وعند مالك وأبي حنيفة والجمهور وقال الحسن وعكرمة وبن أبي ليلى لا يجوز

دليل الجمهور قوله تعالى وأحل لكم ما وراء ذلكم وقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم

لا يجمع بين المرأة وعمتها ولا بين المرأة وخالتها ظاهر في أنه لا فرق بين

أن ينكح البنتين معا أو تقدم هذه أو هذه فالجمع بينهما حرام كيف كان وقد

جاء في رواية أبي داود وغيره لا تنكح الصغرى على الكبرى ولا الكبرى على

الصغرى لكن إن عقد عليهما معا بعقد واحد فنكاحهما باطل وإن عقد على إحداهما

ثم الأخرى فنكاح الأولى صحيح ونكاح الثانية باطل والله أعلم قوله صلى الله

عليه وسلم (لا يخطب الرجل على خطبة أخيه ولا يسوم على سوم أخيه) هكذا هو في

جميع النسخ ولا يسوم بالواو وهكذا يخطب مرفوع وكلاهما لفظه لفظ الخبر

والمراد به النهى وهو أبلغ في النهى لأن خبر الشارع لا يتصور وقوع خلافه

والنهي قد تقع مخالفته فكان المعنى عاملوا هذا النهي معاملة الخبر المتحتم

وأما حكم الخطبة فسيأتي في بابها قريبا إن شاء الله تعالى وكذلك السوم في

كتاب البيع قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (ولا تسأل المرأة طلاق أختها لتكتفيء

صحفتها ولتنكح  فإنما لها ما كتب الله لها) يجوز في تسأل الرفع والكسر الأول

على الخبر الذي يراد به النهي وهو المناسب لقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم قبله

لا يخطب ولا يسوم والثاني على النهي الحقيقي ومعنى هذا
#

# الحديث نهي المرأة الأجنبية أن تسأل الزوج طلاق زوجته وأن ينكحها ويصير

لها من نفقته ومعروفه ومعاشرته ونحوها ما كان للمطلقة فعبر عن ذلك باكتفاء

ما في الصحفة مجازا قال الكسائي وأكفأت الإناء كببته وكفأته وأكفأته أملته

والمراد بأختها غيرها سواء كانت أختها من النسب أو أختها في الإسلام أو

كافرة

| (باب تحريم نكاح المحرم وكراهة خطبته)
# [1409] قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (لا ينكح المحرم ولا ينكح ولا يخطب) ثم

ذكر مسلم الاختلاف أن
# 
# النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم تزوج ميمونة وهو محرم أو وهو حلال فاختلف

العلماء بسبب ذلك في نكاح المحرم فقال مالك والشافعي وأحمد وجمهور العلماء

من الصحابة فمن بعدهم لا يصح نكاح المحرم واعتمدوا أحاديث الباب وقال أبو

حنيفة والكوفيون يصح نكاحه لحديث قصة ميمونة وأجاب الجمهور عن حديث ميمونة

بأجوبة أصحها أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إنما تزوجها حلالا هكذا رواه

أكثر الصحابة قال القاضي وغيره ولم يرو أنه تزوجها محرما الا بن عباس وحده

وروت ميمونة وأبو رافع وغيرهما أنه تزوجها حلالا وهم أعرف بالقضية لتعلقهم

به بخلاف بن عباس ولأنهم أضبط من بن عباس وأكثر الجواب الثاني تأويل حديث

بن عباس على أنه تزوجها في الحرم وهو حلال ويقال لمن هو في الحرم محرم وإن

كان حلالا وهي لغة شائعة معروفة ومنه البيت المشهور ... قتلوا بن عفان

الخليفة محرما ... ... أي في حرم المدينة والثالث أنه تعارض القول والفعل

والصحيح حينئذ عند الأصوليين ترجيح القول لأنه يتعدى إلى الغير والفعل قد

يكون مقصورا عليه والرابع جواب جماعة من أصحابنا أن النبي صلى الله عليه

وسلم كان له أن يتزوج في حال الإحرام وهو مما خص به دون الأمة وهذا أصح

الوجهين عند أصحابنا والوجه الثاني أنه حرام  في حقه كغيره وليس من الخصائص

وأما قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم
# 
# ولا ينكح فمعناه لا يزوج امرأة بولاية ولا وكالة قال العلماء سببه أنه

لما منع في مدة الإحرام من العقد لنفسه صار كالمرأة فلا يعقد لنفسه ولا

لغيره وظاهر هذا العموم أنه لا فرق بين أن يزوج بولاية خاصة كالأب والأخ

والعم ونحوهم أو بولاية عامة وهو السلطان والقاضي ونائبه وهذا هو الصحيح

عندنا وبه قال جمهور أصحابنا وقال بعض أصحابنا يجوز أن يزوج المحرم

بالولاية العامة لأنها يستفاد بها ما لا يستفاد بالخاصة ولهذا يجوز للمسلم

تزويج الذمية بالولاية العامة دون الخاصة واعلم أن النهي عن النكاح

والإنكاح في حال الإحرام نهي تحريم فلو عقد لم ينعقد سواء كان المحرم هو

الزوج والزوجة أو العاقد لهما بولاية أو وكالة فالنكاح باطل في كل ذلك حتى

لو كان الزوجان والولي محلين ووكل الولي أو الزوج محرما في العقد لم ينعقد

وأما قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم ولا يخطب فهو نهي تنزيه ليس بحرام وكذلك يكره

للمحرم أن يكون شاهدا في نكاح عقده المحلون وقال بعض أصحابنا لا ينعقد

بشهادته لأن الشاهد ركن في عقد النكاح كالولي والصحيح الذي عليه الجمهور

انعقاده قوله (حدثنا يحيى بن يحيى عن مالك عن نافع عن نبيه بن وهب أن عمر

بن عبيد الله أراد أن يزوج طلحة بن عمر بنت شيبة بن جبير) ثم ذكره بعد ذلك

من رواية حماد بن زيد عن أيوب عن نافع عن نبيه قال بعثني عمر بن عبيد الله

بن معمر وكان يخطب بنت شيبة بن عثمان على ابنه هكذا قال أحمد عن أيوب في

رواية بنت شيبة بن
# 
# عثمان وكذا قال محمد بن راشد بن عثمان بن عمرو القرشي وزعم أبو داود في

سننه أنه الصواب وأن مالكا وهم فيه وقال الجمهور بل قول مالك هو الصواب
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ج-م-ع (j-m-ʿ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To bring together, unite, assemble; conjoining of two things in a single bond or contract.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In legal contexts, the simultaneous inclusion of two objects under one ruling or contract, often bearing on permissibility (ḥalāl) or prohibition (ḥarām).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) in the sense of physical or contractual union; metaphorical (majāz) when applied to legal categories, e.g., combining two marriage ties.
- Root: خ-ط-ب (kh-ṭ-b)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To address, propose, or seek marriage; the act of requesting a woman's hand.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): A formal request of marriage, distinguished from the contract itself (ʿaqd); carries a temporal and conditional nuance.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for the spoken proposal; metaphorical extension to the entire process of seeking a match.
- Root: ح-ر-م (ḥ-r-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To forbid, make sacred, or render inviolable; the state of iḥrām as a sacred restriction.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In Kalām, the legal prohibition (taḥrīm) versus the state of ritual consecration (iḥrām); both derive from the root's core sense of inviolability.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for the sacred precinct (ḥaram) and the pilgrim's state; metaphorical for legal prohibition as a "sanctified" boundary.
- Sībawayh Rule: The Rule of Khabar vs. Inshāʾ (Declarative vs. Performative Syntax) — When a command or prohibition is phrased in the indicative mood (rafʿ), it functions as an emphatic declarative that implies an unalterable divine decree, surpassing the force of a mere imperative.
chapters.translation:
That is so, and God knows best. As for combining a man's wife with his daughter from another woman [in marriage], it is permissible in our school, and likewise according to Mālik, Abū Ḥanīfah, and the majority of scholars. Al-Ḥasan, ʿIkrimah, and Ibn Abī Laylā said it is not permissible.

The evidence of the majority is the saying of God the Exalted: {«وَأُحِلَّ لَكُم مَّا وَرَاءَ ذَٰلِكُمْ»} ("And lawful to you are all beyond that") [Qurʾān 4:24], and His saying, peace and blessings be upon him: "One must not combine a woman with her paternal aunt, nor a woman with her maternal aunt." This is apparent in that there is no difference between marrying the two daughters together, or one preceding the other — the combination of the two is forbidden in whatever manner it occurs. It has come in the narration of Abū Dāwūd and others: "Do not marry the younger over the elder, nor the elder over the younger." However, if he contracts both simultaneously with a single contract, then both marriages are void. If he contracts upon one of them, then the other, the first marriage is valid and the second is void. And God knows best.

His saying, peace and blessings be upon him: "A man must not propose over the proposal of his brother, nor bid over the bidding of his brother." Thus it appears in all copies: "nor bid" (wa-lā yasūmu) with the conjunction wāw, and likewise "propose" (yakhtibu) is raised (in the indicative). Both are phrased in the form of a declarative statement, but the intended meaning is prohibition — and this is more emphatic in prohibition, because the declarative of the Lawgiver cannot conceivably be contravened, whereas a prohibition may be violated. Thus the meaning is: treat this prohibition with the same gravity as an irrevocable decree. As for the ruling on betrothal, it will follow in its proper chapter shortly, God willing. Likewise, the ruling on bidding will come in the Book of Sales.

His saying, peace and blessings be upon him: "And let not a woman ask for the divorce of her sister to empty her dish and to marry — for indeed she shall have only what God has decreed for her." In "ask" (tasʾal), both the raising (rafʿ) and the kasrah (jussive) are permissible. The first is on the pattern of a declarative intended as prohibition, which is consistent with his preceding words, "must not propose" and "must not bid." The second is on the pattern of a true prohibition. The meaning of this hadith is the prohibition of an unrelated woman asking the husband to divorce his wife so that he may marry her, and she would then receive from his expenditure, kindness, companionship, and the like what the divorced woman had — and this is expressed metaphorically as "emptying the dish." Al-Kisāʾī said: "Akfaʾtu al-ināʾ" means I overturned it, and "kafaʾtuhu" and "akfaʾtuhu" mean I tilted it. The reference to "her sister" means any other woman, whether she is a sister by lineage, a sister in Islam, or an unbeliever.

| (Chapter: The Prohibition of a Pilgrim in Iḥrām Marrying, and the Dislike of His Proposing)

[1409] His saying, peace and blessings be upon him: "The pilgrim in iḥrām must not marry, nor give in marriage, nor propose." Then Muslim mentioned the disagreement that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, married Maymūnah while in iḥrām, or while in a state of ḥill (non-iḥrām). The scholars differed on account of this regarding the marriage of one in iḥrām. Mālik, al-Shāfiʿī, Aḥmad, and the majority of scholars — from the Companions and those after them — held that the marriage of one in iḥrām is not valid, relying on the hadiths of this chapter. Abū Ḥanīfah and the Kūfans held that his marriage is valid, based on the hadith of Maymūnah's story. The majority responded to the hadith of Maymūnah with several answers, the soundest of which is that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, only married her while in a state of ḥill — this is how the majority of the Companions narrated it. Al-Qāḍī and others said: none narrated that he married her in iḥrām except Ibn ʿAbbās alone. Maymūnah, Abū Rāfiʿ, and others narrated that he married her in ḥill, and they are more knowledgeable of the matter due to their direct involvement with it, unlike Ibn ʿAbbās, and because they are more precise than Ibn ʿAbbās.

The second answer is the interpretation of Ibn ʿAbbās's hadith as meaning that he married her in the Sacred Precinct (al-ḥaram) while in ḥill — and one who is in the Sacred Precinct is called "muḥrim" (consecrated) even if he is in ḥill, this being a well-known, widespread usage. From this is the famous verse: "They killed Ibn ʿAffān, the caliph, muḥriman" — meaning in the sacred precinct of Madīnah.

The third answer is that the statement and the action are in conflict, and the sound principle with the uṣūliyyūn (legal theorists) in such a case is to give precedence to the statement, because it extends to others, whereas the action may be particular to him alone.

The fourth answer, given by a group of our companions, is that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, was permitted to marry during iḥrām, and this is among the matters exclusively granted to him over the ummah. This is the sounder of the two positions with our companions. The second position is that it is forbidden for him as it is for others, and it is not among his exclusive prerogatives.

As for his saying, peace and blessings be upon him: "nor give in marriage" (wa-lā yunkihu), its meaning is: he must not give a woman in marriage, whether by guardianship (wilāyah) or by agency (wakālah). The scholars said the reason for this is that since he is prevented during the period of iḥrām from contracting for himself, he becomes like a woman — he does not contract for himself nor for another. The apparent sense of this generality is that there is no difference between giving in marriage by specific guardianship, such as the father, brother, paternal uncle, and the like, or by general guardianship, which is the ruler, the judge, and his deputy. This is the correct position in our school, and the majority of our companions hold it. Some of our companions said that the pilgrim in iḥrām may give in marriage by general guardianship, because through it one obtains what cannot be obtained through specific guardianship — for this reason, a Muslim may give a dhimmī woman in marriage by general guardianship but not by specific guardianship.

Know that the prohibition of marriage and giving in marriage during iḥrām is a prohibition of unlawfulness (taḥrīm). If he contracts, it does not take effect — whether the one in iḥrām is the husband, the wife, or the one contracting for them by guardianship or agency. The marriage is void in all such cases, even if the spouses and the guardian are in ḥill but the guardian or husband appoints a pilgrim in iḥrām as agent for the contract — it does not take effect.

As for his saying, peace and blessings be upon him: "nor propose" (wa-lā yakhtub), it is a prohibition of disapproval (tanzīh), not unlawfulness. Likewise, it is disliked for the pilgrim in iḥrām to serve as a witness in a marriage contracted by those in ḥill. Some of our companions said it does not take effect with his testimony, because the witness is a pillar in the marriage contract like the guardian. The correct position, held by the majority, is that it takes effect.

His saying: "Yaḥyā ibn Yaḥyā narrated to us, from Mālik, from Nāfiʿ, from Nubayh ibn Wahb, that ʿUmar ibn ʿUbayd Allāh intended to give Ṭalḥah ibn ʿUmar in marriage to the daughter of Shaybah ibn Jubayr." Then he mentioned it afterward from the narration of Ḥammād ibn Zayd, from Ayyūb, from Nāfiʿ, from Nubayh, who said: "ʿUmar ibn ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Maʿmar sent me — and he was seeking to marry the daughter of Shaybah ibn ʿUthmān to his son." Thus Aḥmad said from Ayyūb in his narration: "the daughter of Shaybah ibn ʿUthmān," and likewise Muḥammad ibn Rāshid said: "ibn ʿUthmān ibn ʿAmr al-Qurashī." Abū Dāwūd claimed in his Sunan that this is correct and that Mālik erred in it. The majority said: rather, the statement of Mālik is the correct one.

chapters.title_en: The Commentary on Sahih Muslim — Section 558: On the Prohibition of Betrothing Over One's Brother's Betrothal, and the Invalidity of Shighār Marriage
chapters.arabic_text:
فإنها بنت شيبة بن جبير بن عثمان الحجبي كذا حكاه الدارقطني عن رواية

الأكثرين قال القاضي ولعل من قال  شيبة بن عثمان نسبه إلى جده فلا يكون خطأ

بل الروايتان صحيحتان إحداهما حقيقة والأخرى مجاز وذكر الزبير بن بكار أن

هذه البنت تسمى أمة الحميد واعلم أنه وقع في إسناد رواية حماد عن أيوب

رواية أربعة تابعيين بعضهم على بعض وهم أيوب السختياني ونافع ونبيه وأبان

بن عثمان وقد نبهت على نظائر كثيرة لهذا سبقت في هذا الكتاب وقد أفردتها في

جزء مع رباعيات الصحابة رضي الله عنهم قوله (فقال له أبا أن لا أراك عراقيا

جافيا) هكذا هو في جميع نسخ بلادنا عراقيا وذكر القاضي أنه وقع في بعض

الروايات عراقيا وفي بعضها أعرابيا قال وهو الصواب أي جاهلا بالسنة

والأعرابي
# 
# هو ساكن البادية قال وعراقيا هنا خطأ إلا أن يكون قد عرف من مذهب أهل

الكوفة حينئذ جواز نكاح المحرم فيصح عراقيا أي آخذا بمذهبهم في هذا جاهلا

بالسنة والله أعلم

| (باب تحريم الخطبة على خطبة أخيه حتى يأذن أو يترك)
# [1412] قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (لا يبع الرجل على بيع أخيه ولا يخطب

بعضكم على خطبة بعض) وفي رواية لا يبع الرجل على بيع أخيه ولا يخطب على

خطبة أخيه إلا أن يأذن له وفي رواية المؤمن أخو المؤمن فلا يحل للمؤمن أن

يبتاع على بيع أخيه ولا يخطب على خطبة أخيه حتى يذر هذه الأحاديث ظاهرة في

تحريم الخطبة على خطبة أخيه وأجمعوا على تحريمها إذا كان قد صرح للخاطب

بالإجابة ولم يأذن ولم يترك فلو خطب على خطبته وتزوج والحالة هذه عصى وصح

النكاح ولم يفسخ هذا مذهبنا ومذهب الجمهور وقال داود يفسخ النكاح وعن مالك

روايتان كالمذهبين وقال جماعة من أصحاب مالك يفسخ قبل الدخول لا بعده أما

إذا عرض له بالإجابة ولم يصرح ففي تحريم الخطبة على خطبته قولان للشافعي

أصحهما لا يحرم وقال بعض المالكية لا يحرم حتى يرضوا بالزوج ويسمى المهر

واستدلوا لما ذكرناه من أن التحريم إنما هو إذا حصلت الإجابة بحديث فاطمة

بنت قيس فإنها قالت خطبني
# 
# أبو  جهم ومعاوية فلم ينكر النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم خطبة بعضهم على بعض

بل خطبها لأسامة وقد يعترض على هذا الدليل فيقال لعل الثاني لم يعلم بخطبة

الأول وأما النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فأشار بأسامة لا أنه خطب له واتفقوا

على أنه إذا ترك الخطبة رغبة عنها وأذن فيها جازت الخطبة على خطبته وقد صرح

بذلك في هذه الأحاديث
# [1413] وقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (على خطبة أخيه) قال الخطابي وغيره

ظاهره اختصاص التحريم بما إذا كان الخاطب مسلما فإن كان كافرا فلا تحريم

وبه قال الأوزاعي وقال جمهور العلماء تحرم الخطبة على خطبة الكافر أيضا

ولهم أن يجيبوا عن الحديث بأن التقييد بأخيه خرج على الغالب فلا يكون له

مفهوم يعمل به كما في قوله تعالى ولا تقتلوا أولادكم من إملاق وقوله تعالى

وربائبكم اللاتي في حجوركم من نسائكم ونظائره واعلم أن الصحيح الذي تقتضيه

الأحاديث وعمومها أنه لا فرق بين الخاطب الفاسق وغيره وقال بن القاسم

المالكي تجوز الخطبة على خطبة الفاسق والخطبة في هذا كله
# 
# بكسر الخاء وأما الخطبة في الجمعة والعيد والحج وغير ذلك وبين يدي عقد

النكاح فبضمها وأما قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (ولا يبع بعضكم على بيع بعض

ولا يسم على سوم أخيه ولا تناجشوا ولا يبع حاضر لباد) فسيأتي شرحها في كتاب

البيوع إن شاء الله تعالى قوله (حدثنا شعبة عن العلاء وسهيل عن أبيهما)

هكذا صورته في جميع النسخ وأبو العلاء غير أبي سهيل فلا يجوز أن يقال عن

أبيهما قالوا وصوابه أبويهما قال القاضي وغيره ويصح أن يقال عن أبيهما بفتح

الباء على لغة من قال في تثنية الأب أبان كما قال في تثنية اليد يدان فتكون

الرواية صحيحة لكن الباء مفتوحة والله أعلم
#

| باب تحريم نكاح الشغار وبطلانه
# [1415] قوله (أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم نهى عن الشغار) والشغار أن

يزوج الرجل ابنته على أن يزوجه ابنته وليس بينهما صداق وفي الرواية الأخرى

بيان أن تفسير الشغار من  كلام نافع وفي الأخرى ابنته أو أخته قال العلماء

الشغار بكسر الشين المعجمة وبالغين المعجمة أصله في اللغة الرفع يقال شغر

الكلب إذا رفع رجله ليبول كأنه قال لا ترفع رجل بنتي حتى أرفع رجل بنتك

وقيل هو من شغر البلد إذا خلا لخلوه عن الصداق ويقال شغرت المرأة إذا رفعت

رجلها عند الجماع
# 
# قال بن قتيبة كل واحد منهما يشغر عند الجماع وكان الشغار من نكاح

الجاهلية وأجمع العلماء على أنه منهي عنه لكن اختلفوا هل هو نهي يقتضي

إبطال النكاح أم لا فعند الشافعي يقتضي إبطاله وحكاه الخطابي عن أحمد واسحق

وأبي عبيد وقال مالك يفسخ قبل الدخول وبعده وفي رواية عنه قبله لا بعده

وقال جماعة يصح بمهر المثل وهو مذهب أبي حنيفة وحكي عن عطاء والزهري والليث

وهو رواية عن أحمد واسحق وبه قال أبو ثور وبن جرير وأجمعوا على أن غير

البنات من الأخوات وبنات الأخ والعمات وبنات الأعمام والإماء كالبنات في
chapters.anchors:
- Root: خ ط ب (kha-ṭā-ba)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To address, to deliver a speech; khuṭbah (with kasrah on khā') denotes the act of seeking marriage, while khuṭbah (with ḍammah) denotes the sermon.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological usage, khuṭbah is the formal address of counsel; in marriage, it is the explicit request for a woman's hand, entailing legal consequences.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) — the spoken proposal; metaphorical (majāz) — the right of priority in seeking marriage, as if the proposal itself were a property right.
- Sībawayh Rule: Rule of Dual Construction (Tathniyah) — The dual of 'ab (father) is 'abawān in the standard dialect, but a variant dialect forms 'abān, analogous to yadān for yad; hence 'an abayhi may be read with fatḥah on the bā' as a valid dialectal variant.
chapters.translation:
I say: Know that she is the daughter of Shaybah ibn Jubayr ibn ʿUthmān al-Ḥajabī — thus al-Dāraquṭnī related it from the narration of the majority. Al-Qāḍī said: Perhaps the one who said "Shaybah ibn ʿUthmān" attributed him to his grandfather, so it is not an error. Rather, both narrations are sound — one is literal (ḥaqīqah) and the other metaphorical (majāz). Al-Zubayr ibn Bakkār mentioned that this daughter is named Umm al-Ḥamīd.

Know that in the chain of Ḥammād's narration from Ayyūb, there occur four Successors (tābiʿūn) in succession upon one another: Ayyūb al-Sakhtiyānī, Nāfiʿ, Nubayh, and Abān ibn ʿUthmān. I have already drawn attention to many parallels of this kind earlier in this book, and I have collected them in a separate volume along with the quadruple chains of the Companions — may Allah be pleased with them all.

His saying (peace and blessings be upon him): "He said to him: O Abā! I see you are an ʿIrāqī, harsh" — thus it appears in all copies of our lands: ʿIrāqiyan. Al-Qāḍī mentioned that in some narrations it occurs as ʿIrāqiyan, and in others as Aʿrābiyyan. He said: The latter is the correct version, meaning ignorant of the Sunnah — for the Aʿrābī is the dweller of the desert. He said: "ʿIrāqiyan" here is an error, unless one understands that the school of the people of Kūfah permitted marriage while in iḥrām — in that case, ʿIrāqiyan would be valid, meaning: one who adopts their school in this matter while being ignorant of the Sunnah. And Allah knows best.

| Chapter: The Prohibition of Betrothing Over One's Brother's Betrothal Until He Permits or Abandons It

[1412] His saying (peace and blessings be upon him): "Let no man sell over the sale of his brother, nor let any of you seek betrothal over the betrothal of another." In another narration: "Let no man sell over the sale of his brother, nor seek betrothal over the betrothal of his brother, unless he permits him." In yet another narration: "The believer is the brother of the believer, so it is not lawful for a believer to purchase over the purchase of his brother, nor to seek betrothal over the betrothal of his brother, until he desists."

These ḥadīths are explicit in prohibiting betrothal over one's brother's betrothal. The scholars are unanimous on its prohibition when the woman has explicitly expressed acceptance to the first suitor, and he has neither permitted nor abandoned. If one seeks betrothal over his betrothal and marries in this state, he has sinned, yet the marriage is valid and not annulled. This is our school (al-Shāfiʿī) and the school of the majority. Dāwūd said: The marriage is annulled. From Mālik there are two narrations, corresponding to the two positions. A group of Mālik's companions said: It is annulled before consummation, not after.

As for when she hints at acceptance without explicit declaration — concerning the prohibition of betrothing over his betrothal, there are two opinions from al-Shāfiʿī, the more correct of which is that it is not prohibited. Some Mālikīs said: It is not prohibited until they are satisfied with the husband and the dowry (mahr) is named. They adduced for what we have mentioned — that prohibition only applies when acceptance has occurred — the ḥadīth of Fāṭimah bint Qays, for she said: "Abū Jahm and Muʿāwiyah sought my hand," and the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) did not disapprove of one seeking betrothal over the other's betrothal; rather, he married her to Usāmah. One may object to this evidence, saying: Perhaps the second did not know of the first's betrothal. As for the Prophet's (peace and blessings be upon him) indication toward Usāmah, it was a suggestion, not a formal betrothal on his behalf.

They are unanimous that when the first suitor abandons the betrothal out of disinclination toward her and permits it, then betrothing over his betrothal becomes permissible — and this is explicitly stated in these ḥadīths.

[1413] His saying (peace and blessings be upon him): "over the betrothal of his brother" — al-Khaṭṭābī and others said: Its apparent meaning restricts the prohibition to when the suitor is a Muslim; if he is an unbeliever, there is no prohibition. This is also the position of al-Awzāʿī. The majority of scholars, however, hold that betrothing over the betrothal of an unbeliever is also prohibited. They may answer the ḥadīth by saying that the restriction to "his brother" is expressed according to the predominant case (al-ghālib), and thus carries no operative implication (lā mafhūm lahu yuʿmal bihi) — as in His saying (Exalted is He): {«وَلَا تَقْتُلُوا أَوْلَادَكُمْ مِنْ إِمْلَاقٍ»} "And do not kill your children out of poverty" (Q. 6:151), and His saying: {«وَرَبَائِبُكُمُ اللَّاتِي فِي حُجُورِكُمْ مِنْ نِسَائِكُمْ»} "And your step-daughters under your guardianship from your wives" (Q. 4:23), and their parallels.

Know that the correct position, which the ḥadīths and their generality require, is that there is no difference between a sinful suitor and any other. Ibn al-Qāsim al-Mālikī said: Betrothing over the betrothal of a sinful person is permissible.

In all of this, "khuṭbah" (betrothal) is with kasrah on the khā'. As for "khuṭbah" in the Friday sermon, the ʿĪd sermon, the Ḥajj sermon, and other occasions, and before the marriage contract — it is with ḍammah.

As for his saying (peace and blessings be upon him): "Let none of you sell over the sale of another, nor bid over the bidding of his brother, nor practice najash (artificial price inflation), nor let a townsman sell for a Bedouin" — its explanation will come in the Book of Sales (Kitāb al-Buyūʿ), Allah willing.

His saying: "Shuʿbah narrated to us from al-ʿAlāʾ and Suhayl, from their father (an abayhi)" — thus is its form in all copies. Abū al-ʿAlāʾ is not Abū Suhayl, so it is not permissible to say "from their father" (abayhi). They said: The correct form is "from their two fathers" (abawayhi). Al-Qāḍī and others said: It is valid to say "an abayhi" with fatḥah on the bā', according to the dialect of those who form the dual of "ab" as "abān," just as they say in the dual of "yad" (hand) "yadān." Thus the narration is sound, but the bā' is with fatḥah. And Allah knows best.

| Chapter: The Prohibition of Shighār Marriage and Its Invalidity

[1415] His saying: "The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) prohibited shighār." Shighār is that a man marries his daughter to another on the condition that the other marries his daughter to him, with no dowry (ṣadāq) between them. In the other narration, it is clarified that the explanation of shighār is from the speech of Nāfiʿ; in yet another, "his daughter or his sister."

The scholars said: Shighār — with kasrah on the shīn (the dotted one) and with the dotted ghayn — its origin in language is "raising" (al-rafʿ). One says "shaghara al-kalb" (the dog raised its leg) when it lifts its leg to urinate — as if he said: "Do not raise the leg of my daughter until I raise the leg of your daughter." It is also said to derive from "shaghara al-balad" (the land became empty) — because of its emptiness of the dowry. And one says "shaghurat al-marʾah" when she raises her leg during intercourse. Ibn Qutaybah said: Each of the two raises his leg during intercourse.

Shighār was among the marriages of the Jāhiliyyah (pre-Islamic era). The scholars are unanimous that it is prohibited, but they differed as to whether this prohibition entails the nullification of the marriage or not. According to al-Shāfiʿī, it entails its nullification — and al-Khaṭṭābī related this from Aḥmad, Isḥāq, and Abū ʿUbayd. Mālik said: It is annulled before and after consummation; in one narration from him: before it, not after. A group said: It is valid with the equivalent dowry (mahr al-mithl) — this is the school of Abū Ḥanīfah, and it is related from ʿAṭāʾ, al-Zuhrī, and al-Layth; it is also a narration from Aḥmad and Isḥāq, and Abū Thawr and Ibn Jarīr adopted it.

They are unanimous that other than daughters — such as sisters, nieces (daughters of brothers), paternal aunts, daughters of paternal uncles, and slave-girls — are like daughters in this ruling.

chapters.title_en: The Fulfillment of Conditions in Marriage and the Consent of the Previously Married Woman and the Virgin
chapters.arabic_text:
هذا وصورته الواضحة زوجتك بنتي على أن تزوجني بنتك ويضع كل واحدة صداقا

للأخرى فيقول قبلت والله أعلم

| (باب الوفاء بالشرط في النكاح)
# قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (إن أحق الشروط أن يوفى به ما استحللتم به

الفروج) قال
# 
# الشافعي وأكثر العلماء إن هذا محمول على شروط لا تنافي مقتضى النكاح بل

تكون من مقتضياته ومقاصده كاشتراط العشرة بالمعروف والإنفاق عليها وكسوتها

وسكناها بالمعروف وأنه لا يقصر في شيء من حقوقها ويقسم لها كغيرها وأنها لا

تخرج من بيته إلا بإذنه ولا تنشز عليه ولا تصوم تطوعا بغير إذنه ولا تأذن

في بيته إلا بإذنه ولا تتصرف في متاعه إلا برضاه ونحو ذلك وأما شرط يخالف

مقتضاه كشرط أن لا يقسم لها ولا يتسرى عليها ولا ينفق عليها ولا يسافر بها

ونحو ذلك فلا يجب الوفاء به بل يلغو الشرط ويصح النكاح بمهر المثل لقوله

صلى الله عليه وسلم كل شرط ليس في كتاب الله فهو باطل وقال أحمد وجماعة يجب

الوفاء بالشرط  مطلقا لحديث إن أحق الشروط والله أعلم

| (باب استئذان الثيب في النكاح بالنطق والبكر بالسكوت)
# [1419] قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (لا تنكح الأيم حتى تستأمر ولا تنكح

البكر حتى تستأذن قالوا
# 
# يا رسول الله وكيف إذنها قال أن تسكت) وفي رواية الأيم أحق بنفسها من

وليها والبكر تستأذن في نفسها وإذنها صماتها وفي رواية الثيب أحق بنفسها من

وليها والبكر تستأمر وإذنها سكوتها وفي رواية والبكر يستأذنها أبوها في

نفسها وإذنها صماتها قال العلماء الأيم هنا الثيب كما فسرته الرواية الأخرى

التي ذكرنا وللأيم معان أخر والصمات بضم الصاد هو السكوت قال القاضي اختلف

العلماء في المراد بالأيم هنا مع اتفاق أهل اللغة على أنها تطلق على امرأة

لا زوج لها صغيرة كانت أو كبيرة بكرا كانت أو ثيبا قاله إبراهيم الحربي

وإسماعيل القاضي وغيرهما والأيمة في اللغة العزوبة ورجل أيم وامرأة أيم

وحكى أبو عبيد أنه أيمة أيضا قال القاضي ثم اختلف العلماء في المراد بها

هنا فقال علماء الحجاز والفقهاء كافة المراد الثيب واستدلوا بأنه جاء مفسرا

في الرواية الأخرى بالثيب كما ذكرناه وبأنها جعلت مقابلة للبكر وبأن أكثر

استعمالها في اللغة للثيب وقال الكوفيون وزفر الأيم هنا كل امرأة لا زوج

لها بكرا كانت أو ثيبا كما هو مقتضاه في اللغة قالوا فكل امرأة بلغت فهي

أحق بنفسها من وليها وعقدها على نفسها النكاح صحيح وبه قال الشعبي والزهري

قالوا وليس الولي من أركان صحة النكاح بل من تمامه وقال الأوزاعي وأبو يوسف

ومحمد تتوقف صحة النكاح على إجازة الولي قال القاضي واختلفوا أيضا في قوله

صلى الله عليه وسلم أحق من وليها هل هي أحق بالإذن فقط أو بالإذن والعقد

على نفسها فعند الجمهور بالإذن فقط وعند هؤلاء بهما جميعا وقوله صلى الله

عليه وسلم أحق بنفسها يحتمل من حيث اللفظ أن المراد أحق من وليها في كل شيء

من عقد وغيره كما قاله أبو حنيفة وداود ويحتمل أنها أحق بالرضا
# 
# أي لا تزوج حتى تنطق  بالإذن بخلاف البكر ولكن لما صح قوله صلى الله عليه

وسلم لا نكاح إلا بولي مع غيره من الأحاديث الدالة على اشتراط الولي تعين

الاحتمال الثاني واعلم أن لفظة أحق هنا للمشاركة معناه أن لها في نفسها في

النكاح حقا ولوليها حقا وحقها أوكد من حقه فإنه لو أراد تزويجها كفؤا

وامتنعت لم تجبر ولو أرادت أن تتزوج كفؤا فامتنع الولي أجبر فإن أصر زوجها

القاضي فدل على تأكيد حقها ورجحانه وأما قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم في البكر

ولا تنكح البكر حتى تستأمر فاختلفوا في معناه فقال الشافعي وبن ابي ليلى

وأحمد واسحق وغيرهم الاستئذان في البكر مأمور به فإن كان الولي أبا أو جدا

كان الاستئذان مندوبا إليه ولو زوجها بغير استئذانها صح لكمال شفقته وإن

كان غيرهما من الأولياء وجب الاستئذان ولم يصح إنكاحها قبله وقال الأوزاعي

وأبو حنيفة وغيرهما من الكوفيين يجب الاستئذان في كل بكر بالغة وأما قوله

صلى الله عليه وسلم في البكر إذنها صماتها فظاهره العموم في كل بكر وكل ولي

وأن سكوتها يكفي مطلقا وهذا هو الصحيح وقال بعض أصحابنا إن كان الولي أبا

أو جدا فاستئذانه مستحب ويكفي فيه سكوتها وإن كان غيرهما فلا بد من نطقها

لأنها تستحي من الأب والجد أكثر من غيرهما والصحيح الذي عليه الجمهور أن

السكوت كاف في جميع الأولياء لعموم الحديث لوجود الحياء وأما الثيب فلا بد

فيها من النطق بلا خلاف سواء كان الولي أبا أو غيره لأنه زال كمال حيائها

بممارسة الرجال وسواء زالت بكارتها بنكاح صحيح أو فاسد أو بوطء شبهة أو

بزنا ولو زالت بكارتها بوثبة أو بإصبع أو بطول المكث أو وطئت في دبرها فلها

ح كم الثيب على الأصح وقيل
# 
# حكم البكر والله أعلم ومذهبنا ومذهب الجمهور أنه لا يشترط إعلام البكر

بأن سكوتها إذن وشرطه بعض المالكية واتفق عليه أصحاب مالك على استحبابه

واختلف العلماء في اشتراط الولي في صحة النكاح فقال مالك والشافعي يشترط
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ش-ر-ط (sharṭ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: A mark, sign, or stipulation; a condition that is binding upon agreement.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): A contractual stipulation that defines the scope of an obligation; in legal theology, it is valid only if it aligns with divine law (Sharʿ).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) in contractual contexts; metaphorical (majāz) when referring to divine decrees, as God's conditions are absolute.
- Root: أ-ي-م (ayyim)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: A woman without a husband, whether virgin or previously married; derived from ʿuzūbah (celibacy).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In legal discourse, it denotes a woman who has been married and divorced or widowed (thayyib), though lexically it is broader.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): The rhetorical contrast with "virgin" (bikr) in the Hadith narrows the literal sense to the previously married.
- Root: ص-م-ت (ṣamat)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Silence; the absence of speech.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In consent contexts, silence indicates tacit approval, distinct from verbal assent.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal silence; metaphorically, it is a sign of consent due to modesty (ḥayāʾ).
- Sībawayh Rule: The Rule of Contrastive Pairing (Muqābalah) — When two terms are juxtaposed in a legal maxim, their meanings are mutually delimiting; thus, "ayyim" is defined by its opposition to "bikr" in the prophetic statement.
chapters.translation:
This is its clear form: "I have married you my daughter on the condition that you marry me your daughter, and each one places a dowry for the other." Then he says, "I accept." And God knows best.

| (Chapter: The Fulfillment of Conditions in Marriage)

His saying, peace and blessings be upon him: {«The most deserving of conditions to be fulfilled are those by which you make private parts lawful»} — he said: Al-Shāfiʿī and the majority of scholars hold that this is carried upon conditions that do not contradict the requisite of marriage, but rather are among its requisites and purposes, such as stipulating good companionship, spending upon her, clothing her, and housing her in a becoming manner, that he not be remiss in any of her rights, that he divide (his time) for her as for others, that she not leave his house except with his permission, that she not be rebellious against him, that she not fast voluntarily without his permission, that she not admit anyone into his house except with his permission, and that she not dispose of his belongings except with his approval, and similar matters. As for a condition that contradicts its requisite, such as stipulating that he not divide (time) for her, not take a concubine over her, not spend upon her, not travel with her, and similar matters — it is not obligatory to fulfill it. Rather, the condition is void, and the marriage is valid with the equivalent dowry (mahr al-mithl), due to his saying, peace and blessings be upon him: {«Every condition not in the Book of God is void»}. Aḥmad and a group said: Fulfillment of the condition is obligatory absolutely, due to the Hadith {«The most deserving of conditions...»}. And God knows best.

| (Chapter: Seeking the Consent of the Previously Married Woman in Marriage by Speech, and the Virgin by Silence)

[1419] His saying, peace and blessings be upon him: {«The previously unmarried woman (ayyim) is not married until she is consulted, and the virgin is not married until she is asked permission»} — they said: "O Messenger of God, how is her permission?" He said: {«That she remain silent»}. In another narration: {«The ayyim has more right over herself than her guardian, and the virgin is asked permission regarding herself, and her permission is her silence»}. In another narration: {«The thayyib has more right over herself than her guardian, and the virgin is consulted, and her permission is her silence»}. In another narration: {«And the virgin — her father seeks her permission regarding herself, and her permission is her silence»}. The scholars said: The ayyim here is the thayyib (previously married), as clarified by the other narration we mentioned. The ayyim has other meanings. Al-Ṣamāt, with a ḍammah on the ṣād, is silence. Al-Qāḍī said: The scholars differed regarding the intended meaning of ayyim here, despite the agreement of linguists that it is applied to a woman with no husband, whether young or old, virgin or previously married — so said Ibrāhīm al-Ḥarbī, Ismāʿīl al-Qāḍī, and others. Al-Ayyimah in language is celibacy; a man is ayyim and a woman is ayyim. Abū ʿUbayd reported that it is also ayyimah. Al-Qāḍī said: Then the scholars differed regarding the intended meaning here. The scholars of the Hijaz and all the jurists said: The intended meaning is the thayyib, and they adduced as evidence that it was interpreted in the other narration as thayyib, as we mentioned, and that it was made parallel to the virgin, and that its most frequent usage in the language is for the thayyib. The Kūfans and Zufar said: The ayyim here is every woman with no husband, whether virgin or thayyib, as is its linguistic requisite. They said: Every woman who has reached maturity has more right over herself than her guardian, and her contracting marriage for herself is valid. Al-Shaʿbī and al-Zuhrī held this view. They said: The guardian is not among the pillars of the validity of marriage, but rather among its completions. Al-Awzāʿī, Abū Yūsuf, and Muḥammad said: The validity of marriage is contingent upon the guardian's ratification. Al-Qāḍī said: They also differed regarding his saying, peace and blessings be upon him: {«More right than her guardian»} — is she more right only regarding permission, or regarding both permission and contracting for herself? According to the majority (jumhūr), it is only regarding permission; according to these others, it is regarding both. His saying, peace and blessings be upon him: {«More right over herself»} — from a linguistic standpoint, it is possible that the intended meaning is that she has more right than her guardian in everything, whether contracting or otherwise, as Abū Ḥanīfah and Dāwūd said. And it is possible that she is more right regarding consent — i.e., she is not married until she speaks with permission, unlike the virgin. But since his saying, peace and blessings be upon him: {«No marriage except with a guardian»} is established, along with other Hadiths indicating the condition of the guardian, the second possibility is determined. Know that the word "more right" (aḥaqq) here denotes participation (mushārakah), meaning that she has a right regarding herself in marriage, and her guardian has a right, and her right is more emphatic than his. For if he wanted to marry her to a suitable match and she refused, she is not compelled; and if she wanted to marry a suitable match and the guardian refused, he is compelled; if he persists, the judge marries her. This indicates the emphasis and preponderance of her right. As for his saying, peace and blessings be upon him, regarding the virgin: {«And the virgin is not married until she is consulted»} — they differed regarding its meaning. Al-Shāfiʿī, Ibn Abī Laylā, Aḥmad, Isḥāq, and others said: Seeking permission in the case of the virgin is commanded.
