If the guardian is the father or grandfather, seeking permission is recommended (mandūb) for him, and if he marries her without her permission, it is valid due to the completeness of his compassion. If it is other than them from the guardians, seeking permission is obligatory, and her marriage is not valid before it. Al-Awzāʿī, Abū Ḥanīfah, and others from the Kūfans said: Seeking permission is obligatory for every mature virgin. As for his saying, peace and blessings be upon him, regarding the virgin: {«Her permission is her silence»} — its apparent meaning is general for every virgin and every guardian, and that her silence suffices absolutely. This is the correct view. Some of our companions said: If the guardian is the father or grandfather, seeking permission is recommended, and her silence suffices; if it is other than them, her speech is necessary, because she is more shy of the father and grandfather than others. The correct view, upon which the majority (jumhūr) are agreed, is that silence suffices with all guardians, due to the generality of the Hadith, because modesty exists. As for the thayyib, speech is necessary without dispute, whether the guardian is the father or other, because her complete modesty has been removed by the practice of men. Whether her virginity was removed by a valid marriage, an invalid one, a doubtful intercourse (waṭʾ shubhah), or fornication — and if her virginity was removed by a jump, a finger, prolonged duration, or anal intercourse, she has the ruling of the thayyib according to the most correct view. It was said: The ruling of the virgin. And God knows best. Our school and the school of the majority hold that it is not a condition to inform the virgin that her silence is permission; some Mālikīs made it a condition, and the companions of Mālik agreed upon its recommendation. The scholars differed regarding the condition of the guardian in the validity of marriage: Mālik and al-Shāfiʿī said it is a condition.

chapters.title_en: The Requirement of a Guardian (Walī) in Marriage and the Marriage of a Minor Virgin by Her Father
chapters.arabic_text:
ولا يصح نكاح  إلا بولي وقال أبو حنيفة لا يشترط في الثيب ولا في البكر

البالغة بل لها أن تزوج نفسها بغير إذن وليها وقال أبو ثور يجوز أن تزوج

نفسها بإذن وليها ولا يجوز بغير إذنه وقال داود يشترط الولي في تزويج البكر

دون الثيب واحتج مالك والشافعي بالحديث المشهور لا نكاح إلا بولي وهذا

يقتضي نفي الصحة واحتج داود بأن الحديث المذكور في مسلم صريح في الفرق بين

البكر والثيب وأن الثيب أحق بنفسها والبكر تستأذن وأجاب أصحابنا عنه بأنها

أحق أي شريكة في الحق بمعنى أنها لا تجبر وهي أيضا أحق في تعيين الزوج

واحتج أبو حنيفة بالقياس على البيع وغيره فإنها تستقل فيه بلا ولي وحمل

الأحاديث الواردة في اشتراط الولي على الأمة والصغيرة وخص عمومها بهذا

القياس وتخصيص العموم بالقياس جائز عند كثيرين من أهل الأصول واحتج أبو ثور

بالحديث المشهور أيما امرأة نكحت بغير إذن وليها فنكاحها باطل ولأن الولي

إنما يراد ليختار كفؤا لدفع العار وذلك يحصل بإذنه قال العلماء ناقض داود

مذهبه في شرط الولي في البكر دون الثيب لأنه إحداث قول في مسألة مختلف فيها

ولم يسبق إليه ومذهبه أنه لا يجوز احداث مثل هذا والله أعلم
#

| باب جواز تزويج الأب البكر الصغيرة
# [1422] فيه حديث عائشة رضي الله عنها قالت (تزوجني رسول الله صلى الله

عليه وسلم لست سنين وبنى بي وأنا بنت تسع سنين) وفي رواية تزوجها وهي بنت

سبع سنين هذا صريح في جواز تزويج الأب الصغيرة بغير اذنها لأنه لا إذن لها

والجد كالأب عندنا وقد سبق في الباب الماضي بسط الاختلاف في اشتراط الولي

وأجمع المسلمون على جواز تزويجه بنته البكر الصغيرة لهذا الحديث وإذا بلغت

فلا خيار لها في فسخه عند مالك والشافعي وسائر فقهاء الحجاز وقال أهل

العراق لها الخيار إذا بلغت أما غير الأب والجد من الأولياء فلا يجوز أن

يزوجها عند الشافعي والثوري ومالك وبن أبي ليلى وأحمد وأبي ثور وأبي عبيد

والجمهور قالوا فإن زوجها  لم يصح وقال الأوزاعي وأبو حنيفة وآخرون من السلف

يجوز لجميع الأولياء ويصح ولها الخيار إذا بلغت إلا أبا يوسف فقال لا خيار

لها واتفق الجماهير على أن الوصي الأجنبي لا يزوجها وجوز شريح وعروة وحماد

له تزويجها قبل البلوغ وحكاه الخطابي عن مالك أيضا والله أعلم واعلم أن

الشافعي وأصحابه قالوا يستحب أن لا يزوج الأب والجد البكر حتى تبلغ

ويستأذنها لئلا يوقعها في أسر الزوج وهي كارهة وهذا الذي قالوه لا يخالف

حديث عائشة لأن مرادهم أنه لا يزوجها قبل البلوغ إذا لم تكن مصلحة ظاهرة

يخاف فوتها بالتأخير كحديث عائشة فيستحب تحصيل ذلك الزوج لأن الأب مأمور

بمصلحة ولده فلا يفوتها والله أعلم وأما وقت زفاف الصغيرة المزوجة والدخول

بها فإن اتفق الزوج والولي على شيء لا ضرر فيه على الصغيرة عمل به وإن

اختلفا فقال أحمد وأبو عبيد تجبر على ذلك بنت تسع سنين دون غيرها وقال مالك

والشافعي وأبو حنيفة حد ذلك أن تطيق الجماع ويختلف ذلك باختلافهن ولا يضبط

بسن وهذا هو الصحيح وليس في حديث عائشة تحديد ولا المنع من ذلك فيمن أطاقته

قبل تسع ولا الإذن فيمن لم تطقه وقد بلغت تسعا قال الداودي وكانت عائشة قد

شبت شبابا حسا رضى الله
# 
# عنها وأما قولها في رواية تزوجني وأنا بنت سبع وفي أكثر الروايات بنت ست

فالجمع بينهما أنه كان لها ست وكسر ففي رواية اقتصرت على السنين وفي رواية

عدت السنة التي دخلت فيها والله أعلم قوله (وحدثنا أبو بكر بن أبي شيبة قال

وجدت في كتابي عن أبي أسامة هذا) معناه أنه وجد في كتابه ولم يذكر أنه سمعه

ومثل هذا تجوز روايته على الصحيح وقول الجمهور ومع هذا فلم يقتصر مسلم عليه

بل ذكره متابعة لغيره قولها (فوعكت شهرا فوفى شعري جميمة) الوعك ألم الحمى

ووفى أي كمل وجميمة تصغير جمة وهي الشعر النازل إلى الأذنين ونحوهما أي صار

إلى هذا الحد بعد أن كان قد ذهب بالمرض قولها  (فأتتني أم رومان وأنا على

أرجوحة) أم رومان هي أم عائشة وهي بضم الراء وإسكان الواو وهذا هو المشهور

ولم يذكر الجمهور غيره وحكى بن عبد البر في الاستيعاب ضم الراء وفتحها ورجح

الفتح وليس هو براجح والارجوحة بضم الهمزة هي خشبة يلعب عليها الصبيان

والجواري الصغار يكون وسطها على مكان مرتفع ويجلسون على طرفيها ويحركونها

فيرتفع جانب منها وينزل جانب قولها (فقلت هه هه حتى ذهب نفسي) هو بفتح

الفاء هذه كلمة يقولها المبهور حتى يتراجع إلى حال سكونه وهي بإسكان الهاء

الثانية فهي هاء السكت قولها (فإذا نسوة من الأنصار فقلن على الخير والبركة

وعلى خير طائر) النسوة بكسر النون وضمها لغتان الكسر أفصح وأشهر والطائر

الحظ يطلق على الحظ من الخير والشر والمراد هنا على أفضل حظ وبركة وفيه

استحباب الدعاء بالخير والبركة لكل واحد من الزوجين ومثله في حديث عبد

الرحمن بن عوف بارك الله لك قولها (فغسلن رأسي وأصلحنني
# 
# فيه استحباب تنظيف العروس وتزيينها لزوجها واستحباب اجتماع النساء لذلك
chapters.anchors:
- Root: و-ل-ي (w-l-y)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Proximity, closeness, guardianship; the walī is one who undertakes affairs (al-qiyām bi’l-amr) due to nearness of kinship or authority.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Wilāyah denotes legal authority and protective charge; in marriage, it is a condition for validity (ṣiḥḥah) because the woman’s consent alone lacks the requisite custodial power over the contract’s public and religious dimensions.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) — the walī as one who manages; metaphorical (majāz) — “she is more entitled to herself” (aḥaqq bi-nafsihā) means priority in choice, not exclusive autonomy, as the ḥadīth’s wording is interpreted restrictively.
- Root: ن-ك-ح (n-k-ḥ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Marriage, wedlock; the contract of union (al-ʿaqd) between spouses.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Nikāḥ in legal usage is the valid marriage contract; its negation in the ḥadīth «لا نكاح إلا بولي» entails negation of validity (nafy al-ṣiḥḥah), not mere perfection.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): The particle “lā” here is for negation of genus (nafy al-jins), indicating absolute nullity without a guardian.
- Root: ب-ك-ر (b-k-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Virgin; one who has not been deflowered; also the first-born.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In legal discourse, al-bikr is the unmarried virgin; her consent is sought (istiʾdhān) but her silence suffices, unlike the thayyib whose explicit consent is required.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): The distinction between bikr and thayyib in the ḥadīth is literal in terms of consent procedure, but not in terms of guardian requirement — a point of contention among jurists.
- Root: ص-غ-ر (ṣ-gh-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Smallness, youth; minor (ṣaghīrah) — one below the age of majority.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The minor has no valid consent (lā idhna lahā); hence the father’s authority is absolute in marrying her for a manifest benefit.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — the father’s act is valid without her permission; metaphorical — “no choice upon majority” (lā khiyār lahā) means no option to annul, as per Mālik and al-Shāfiʿī.
- Sībawayh Rule: Rule of ʿAṭf al-Bayān (Appositional Clarification) — In «تزوجني رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لست سنين وبنى بي وأنا بنت تسع سنين», the sentence «وأنا بنت تسع سنين» is a circumstantial clause (ḥāl) providing the age at consummation, while «لست سنين» is an adverbial of time for the contract; the coordination (ʿaṭf) links two distinct temporal events without conflating them.
chapters.translation:
I say: A marriage is not valid except with a guardian (walī). Abū Ḥanīfah said: It is not a condition for the thayyib (previously married woman) nor for the virgin who has reached majority; rather, she may marry herself without her guardian’s permission. Abū Thawr said: She may marry herself with her guardian’s permission, but not without it. Dāwūd (al-Ẓāhirī) said: The guardian is a condition for marrying the virgin, but not the thayyib. Mālik and al-Shāfiʿī adduced the well-known ḥadīth: «لا نكاح إلا بولي» (“No marriage except with a guardian”), and this entails negation of validity. Dāwūd adduced that the aforementioned ḥadīth in Muslim is explicit in distinguishing between the virgin and the thayyib — that the thayyib is more entitled to herself (aḥaqq bi-nafsihā), while the virgin is to be asked permission (tustaʾdhan). Our companions (the Shāfiʿīs) answered this by saying: “More entitled” means she is a partner in the right, in the sense that she is not to be coerced (lā tujbar), and she is also more entitled in specifying the husband. Abū Ḥanīfah adduced an analogy (qiyās) to sale and other contracts, for she acts independently therein without a guardian. He interpreted the ḥadīths requiring a guardian as applying to the slave-woman (al-amah) and the minor (al-ṣaghīrah), and he specified their general application (khuṣūṣ al-ʿumūm) by this analogy. Specifying a general text by analogy is permissible according to many scholars of uṣūl (jurisprudential principles). Abū Thawr adduced the well-known ḥadīth: «أيما امرأة نكحت بغير إذن وليها فنكاحها باطل» (“Any woman who marries without her guardian’s permission, her marriage is void”), and because the guardian is only intended to choose a suitable match (kufʾ) to repel disgrace (al-ʿār), and that is achieved by his permission. The scholars said: Dāwūd contradicted his own school (madhhab) in requiring the guardian for the virgin but not the thayyib, because this is an innovation of an opinion (iḥdāth qawl) in a matter of scholarly disagreement, and none preceded him in it; and his principle is that such innovation is not permissible. And God knows best.

#
| Chapter: The Permissibility of a Father Marrying His Minor Virgin Daughter
# [1422] In it is the ḥadīth of ʿĀʾishah, may God be pleased with her, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, married me when I was six years old, and consummated the marriage with me when I was a girl of nine years.” In another narration: “He married her when she was seven years old.” This is explicit in the permissibility of a father marrying his minor daughter without her permission, because she has no valid consent (lā idhna lahā). The grandfather is like the father in our school (ʿindanā). The detailed disagreement on the condition of the guardian has already preceded in the previous chapter. The Muslims are unanimous (ajmaʿa al-muslimūn) on the permissibility of a father marrying his virgin minor daughter on the basis of this ḥadīth. When she reaches majority, she has no option to annul it (lā khiyār lahā fī faskhihi) according to Mālik, al-Shāfiʿī, and the rest of the jurists of the Ḥijāz. The people of Iraq (ahl al-ʿIrāq) said: She has the option upon reaching majority. As for other than the father and grandfather among the guardians, it is not permissible for him to marry her according to al-Shāfiʿī, al-Thawrī, Mālik, Ibn Abī Laylā, Aḥmad, Abū Thawr, Abū ʿUbayd, and the majority (al-jumhūr). They said: If he marries her, it is not valid. Al-Awzāʿī, Abū Ḥanīfah, and others among the Salaf said: It is permissible for all guardians, and it is valid, and she has the option upon reaching majority — except Abū Yūsuf, who said: She has no option. The masses (al-jamāhīr) agreed that a non-relative executor (al-waṣī al-ajnabī) does not marry her. Shurayḥ, ʿUrwah, and Ḥammād permitted him to marry her before puberty, and al-Khaṭṭābī reported this from Mālik as well. And God knows best. Know that al-Shāfiʿī and his companions said: It is recommended (yustaḥabb) that the father and grandfather not marry the virgin until she reaches majority and they seek her permission, lest they place her in the captivity of a husband while she is averse. What they said does not contradict the ḥadīth of ʿĀʾishah, because their intent is that he should not marry her before puberty unless there is a manifest benefit (maṣlaḥah ẓāhirah) feared to be lost by delay — like the case of ʿĀʾishah’s ḥadīth — then it is recommended to secure that husband, for the father is commanded to pursue his child’s benefit and must not let it slip away. And God knows best. As for the time of the minor’s wedding procession (zifāf) and consummation (dukhūl): if the husband and guardian agree on something with no harm to the minor, it is acted upon. If they differ, Aḥmad and Abū ʿUbayd said: A girl of nine is compelled to that, but not others. Mālik, al-Shāfiʿī, and Abū Ḥanīfah said: The limit is that she can endure intercourse (tuṭīq al-jimāʿ), and this varies among women and cannot be fixed by age. This is the correct view (al-ṣaḥīḥ). There is in ʿĀʾishah’s ḥadīth neither a specification of age, nor a prohibition of it for one who can endure it before nine, nor a permission for one who cannot endure it though she has reached nine. Al-Dāwūdī said: ʿĀʾishah had already blossomed into noticeable youth (shabbat shabāban ḥassan). May God be pleased with her.
# 
# As for her saying in one narration: “He married me when I was seven,” while in most narrations: “six” — the reconciliation (al-jamʿ) between them is that she was six and some months; in one narration she mentioned only the full years, and in another she counted the year she entered. And God knows best. His saying — “Abū Bakr ibn Abī Shaybah said: I found in my book from Abū Usāmah this” — means he found it in his book and did not mention that he heard it directly. Such a narration is permissible to transmit according to the correct view and the majority’s position. Nevertheless, Muslim did not rely solely on it but mentioned it as corroboration (mutābaʿah) of others. Her saying: “I fell ill with a fever (waʿaktu) for a month, and my hair reached my earlobes (fa-wafā shaʿrī jumaymah)” — al-waʿk is the pain of fever; “wafā” means completed; “jumaymah” is the diminutive of “jummah,” which is hair descending to the ears and similar — i.e., it reached that length after having been lost due to illness. Her saying: “Then Umm Rūmān came to me while I was on a swing (arjūḥah)” — Umm Rūmān is ʿĀʾishah’s mother; her name is with ḍammah on the rāʾ and sukūn on the wāw, and this is the well-known pronunciation; the majority mentioned none other. Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr in al-Istīʿāb reported both ḍammah and fatḥah on the rāʾ and preferred the fatḥah, but it is not preferable. Al-arjūḥah, with ḍammah on the hamzah, is a wooden board on which young boys and girls play; its middle is on an elevated place, they sit on its two ends and move it, so one side rises and the other descends. Her saying: “I said, ‘Hah, hah’ until my breath left (dhahaba nafasī)” — it is with fatḥah on the fāʾ; this is a word uttered by one who is breathless (mabhūr) until he returns to a state of calm; it is with sukūn on the second hāʾ, being the hāʾ of pausing (hāʾ al-sakt). Her saying: “Then there were women of the Anṣār who said: ‘Upon good and blessing, and upon a good omen (ṭāʾir)’” — “al-niswah” with kasrah on the nūn and ḍammah are two dialects; the kasrah is more eloquent and famous. “Al-ṭāʾir” is fortune (al-ḥaẓẓ), applied to fortune in good and evil; the intent here is “upon the best fortune and blessing.” In it is the recommendation of supplicating for good and blessing for each of the two spouses. Similar to it is in the ḥadīth of ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf: «بارك الله لك» (“May God bless you”). Her saying: “Then they washed my head and adorned me (aṣlaḥnani)” — in it is the recommendation of cleaning the bride and beautifying her for her husband, and the recommendation of women gathering for that purpose.

chapters.title_en: The Commentary on Sahih Muslim — Section 561: On Marriage, the Wedding Night, and Related Rulings
chapters.arabic_text:
ولأنه يتضمن إعلان النكاح ولأنهن يؤانسنها ويؤدبنها ويعلمنها آدابها حال

الزفاف وحال لقائها الزوج قولها (فلم يرعني إلا ورسول الله صلى الله عليه

وسلم ضحى فأسلمنني إليه) أي لم يفجأني ويأتني بغتة إلا هذا وفيه جواز

الزفاف والدخول بالعروس نهارا وهو جائز ليلا ونهارا واحتج به البخاري في

الدخول نهارا وترجم عليه بابا قوله (وزفت إليه وهي ابنة تسع سنين ولعبها

معها (المراد هذه اللعب المسماة بالبنات التي تلعب بها الجواري الصغار

ومعناه التنبيه على صغر سنها قال القاضي وفيه جواز اتخاذ اللعب وإباحة لعب

الجواري بهن وقد جاء في الحديث الآخر أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم رأى ذلك

فلم ينكره قالوا وسببه تدريبهن لتربية الأولاد وإصلاح شأنهن وبيوتهن هذا

كلام القاضي ويحتمل أن يكون مخصوصا من أحاديث النهي عن اتخاذ الصور لما

ذكره
# 
# من المصلحة ويحتمل أن يكون هذا منهيا عنه وكانت قصة عائشة هذه ولعبها في

أول الهجرة قبل تحريم الصور والله أعلم

| باب استحباب التزوج والتزويج في شوال
# (واستحباب الدخول فيه)
# [1423] قوله (عن عائشة رضي الله عنها قالت تزوجني رسول الله صلى الله

عليه وسلم في شوال وبنى بي في شوال فأي نساء رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

كان أحظى عنده مني قال وكانت عائشة تستحب أن تدخل نسائها في شوال) فيه

استحباب التزويج والتزوج والدخول في شوال وقد نص أصحابنا على استحبابه

واستدلوا بهذا الحديث وقصدت عائشة بهذا الكلام رد ما كانت الجاهلية عليه

وما يتخيله بعض العوام اليوم من كراهة التزوج والتزويج والدخول في شوال

وهذا باطل لا أصل له وهو من آثار الجاهلية كانوا يتطيرون بذلك لما في اسم

شوال من الإشالة والرفع
#

| باب ندب من أراد نكاح امرأة إلى أن ينظر إلى وجهها
# (وكفيها قبل خطبتها) قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم للمتزوج امرأة من الأنصار

(أنظرت إليها قال لا قال فاذهب فانظر إليها فإن في أعين الأنصار شيئا) هكذا

الرواية شيئا بالهمز وهو واحد الأشياء قيل المراد صغر وقيل زرقة وفي هذا

دلالة لجواز ذكر مثل هذا للنصيحة وفيه استحباب النظر إلى وجه من يريد

تزوجها وهو مذهبنا ومذهب مالك وأبي حنيفة وسائر الكوفيين وأحمد وجماهير

العلماء وحكى القاضي عن قوم كراهته وهذا خطأ مخالف لصريح هذا الحديث ومخالف

لإجماع الأمة على جواز النظر للحاجة عند البيع والشراء والشهادة ونحوها ثم

إنه إنما يباح له النظر إلى وجهها وكفيها فقط لأنهما ليسا بعورة ولأنه

يستدل بالوجه على الجمال أو ضده وبالكفين على خصوبة البدن أو عدمها هذا

مذهبنا ومذهب الأكثرين وقال الأوزاعي ينظر إلى مواضع اللحم وقال داود ينظر

إلى جميع بدنها وهذا خطأ ظاهر منابذ لأصول السنة والإجماع ثم مذهبنا ومذهب

مالك وأحمد والجمهور أنه لا يشترط في جواز هذا النظر رضاها بل له ذلك في

غفلتها ومن غير تقدم إعلام لكن قال مالك أكره نظره في غفلتها مخافة من وقوع

نظره على عورة وعن مالك رواية ضعيفة أنه لا ينظر اليها إلا بإذنها وهذا

ضعيف  لأن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قد أذن في ذلك مطلقا ولم يشترط

استئذانها ولأنها تستحي غالبا من الإذن ولأن في ذلك تغريرا فربما رآها
# 
# فلم تعجبه فيتركها فتنكسر وتتأذى ولهذا قال أصحابنا يستحب أن يكون نظره

إليها قبل الخطبة حتى إن كرهها تركها من غير إيذاء بخلاف ما إذا تركها بعد

الخطبة والله أعلم قال أصحابنا وإذا لم يمكنه النظر استحب له أن يبعث امرأة

يثق بها تنظر إليها وتخبره ويكون ذلك قبل الخطبة لما ذكرناه قوله صلى الله

عليه وسلم (كأنما تنحتون الفضة من عرض هذا الجبل) العرض بضم العين وإسكان

الراء هو الجانب والناحية وتنحتون بكسر الحاء أي تقشرون وتقطعون ومعنى هذا

الكلام كراهة إكثار المهر بالنسبة إلى حال الزوج

| (باب الصداق وجواز كونه تعليم قرآن وخاتم حديد)
# (وغير ذلك من قليل وكثير واستحباب كونه خمسمائة درهم لمن لا يجحف به)

قوله (حدثنا يعقوب) يعنى بن عبد الرحمن القارىء هو القارىء بتشديد الياء

منسوب إلى القارة قبيلة معروفة وسبق بيانه
# [1425] قولها (جئت أهب لك نفسي) مع سكوته صلى الله عليه وسلم فيه دليل

لجواز هبة المرأة نكاحها له كما قال الله وامرأة مؤمنة إن وهبت نفسها للنبي

إن أراد النبي أن يستنكحها خالصة لك من دون المؤمنين قال أصحابنا فهذه

الآية وهذا الحديث
# 
# دليلان لذلك فإذا وهبت امرأة نفسها له صلى الله عليه وسلم فتزوجها بلا

مهر حل له ذلك ولا يجب عليه بعد ذلك مهرها بالدخول ولا بالوفاة ولا بغير

ذلك بخلاف غيره فإنه لا يخلو نكاحه وجوب مهر إما مسمى وإما مهر المثل وفي

انعقاد نكاح النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بلفظ الهبة وجهان لأصحابنا أحدهما

ينعقد لظاهر الآية وهذا الحديث والثاني لا ينعقد بلفظ الهبة بل لا ينعقد

إلا بلفظ التزويج أو الإنكاح كغيره من الأمة فإنه لا ينعقد إلا بأحد هذين

اللفظين عندنا بلا خلاف ويحمل هذا القائل الآية والحديث على أن المراد
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ز-ف-ف (z-f-f)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: The core meaning is "to convey, to escort" — specifically, the act of escorting a bride to her groom (izfāf), derived from the notion of swift, ceremonial conveyance.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological/social context, it denotes the public procession of the bride, emphasizing the communal announcement of marriage (iʿlān al-nikāḥ).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) — physical escorting; metaphorical (majāz) — the public declaration of the marital bond, as the act itself symbolizes openness.
- Sībawayh Rule: Rule of "Fa-ʿidā" (الفجائية) — The particle "fa" introducing an unexpected clause (fa-lam yarʿanī illā...), indicating suddenness (mufājaʾah), where the predicate follows without prior expectation.
chapters.translation:
I say: And because it entails the public announcement of marriage (iʿlān al-nikāḥ), and because they (the women) keep her company, discipline her, and teach her proper conduct (ādāb) at the time of the wedding procession (zifāf) and at the time of her meeting with her husband. Her saying: «فلم يرعني إلا ورسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ضحى فأسلمنني إليه» — meaning: "Nothing startled me or came upon me suddenly except that the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) came at mid-morning (ḍuḥā), and they handed me over to him." This contains the permissibility of the wedding procession and entering with the bride during the day — and it is permissible both by night and by day. Al-Bukhārī adduced this as evidence for entering during the day and titled a chapter upon it.

His saying: «وزفت إليه وهي ابنة تسع سنين ولعبها معها» — "She was escorted to him while she was nine years old, and her playthings (luʿab) were with her" — the intended meaning is those playthings called "dolls" (banāt) with which young girls play. Its significance is to draw attention to her young age. Al-Qāḍī said: In this is the permissibility of making playthings and the permissibility of young girls playing with them. It has come in another ḥadīth that the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) saw that and did not disapprove of it. They said: The reason for this is to train them for raising children and rectifying their affairs and their homes. This is the speech of Al-Qāḍī. And it is possible that this is specified (makhṣūṣ) from the ḥadīths prohibiting the making of images (ṣuwar), due to the benefit (maṣlaḥah) mentioned. And it is possible that this was prohibited, and the story of ʿĀʾishah and her playthings occurred at the beginning of the Hijrah, before the prohibition of images. And Allah knows best.

| Chapter: The Recommendation of Marrying and Giving in Marriage in Shawwāl, and the Recommendation of Entering (with the Bride) Therein

[1423] His saying: «عن عائشة رضي الله عنها قالت تزوجني رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في شوال وبنى بي في شوال فأي نساء رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كان أحظى عنده مني» — "On the authority of ʿĀʾishah (may Allah be pleased with her), she said: The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) married me in Shawwāl and consummated the marriage with me in Shawwāl. So which of the wives of the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) was more favored by him than me?" She said: "And ʿĀʾishah used to like that her women (relatives) be entered into marriage in Shawwāl." — In this is the recommendation of giving in marriage, marrying, and entering (with the bride) in Shawwāl. Our companions (the Shāfiʿīs) have explicitly stated its recommendation and adduced this ḥadīth as evidence. ʿĀʾishah intended by this speech to refute what the pre-Islamic era (Jāhiliyyah) was upon, and what some common people today imagine of the dislike (karāhah) of marrying, giving in marriage, and entering in Shawwāl. This is false, having no basis, and it is from the remnants of the Jāhiliyyah — they used to augur ill (taṭayyur) from it because of what is in the name "Shawwāl" of elevation and raising (ishālah wa rafʿ).

| Chapter: The Recommendation for One Who Desires to Marry a Woman to Look at Her Face and Palms Before Proposing to Her

His saying (peace and blessings be upon him) to the man who married a woman from the Anṣār: «أنظرت إليها قال لا قال فاذهب فانظر إليها فإن في أعين الأنصار شيئا» — "Did you look at her? He said: No. He said: Then go and look at her, for in the eyes of the Anṣār there is something." This is the narration: "شيئا" (shayʾan) with a hamzah, and it is one of the things (ashyāʾ). It is said the intended meaning is smallness (of the eyes), and it is said blueness. In this is an indication of the permissibility of mentioning such things for the purpose of sincere advice (naṣīḥah). And in it is the recommendation of looking at the face of the one one desires to marry — and this is our school (madhhab), the school of Mālik, Abū Ḥanīfah, the rest of the Kūfans, Aḥmad, and the majority of scholars. Al-Qāḍī has related from some people the dislike of that — and this is an error, contradicting the explicit text of this ḥadīth, and contradicting the consensus (ijmāʿ) of the Ummah on the permissibility of looking when there is a need, such as in buying, selling, giving testimony, and the like. Then, he is only permitted to look at her face and her palms (kafayhā) alone, because they are not ʿawrah (parts to be covered), and because one infers from the face beauty or its opposite, and from the palms the plumpness of the body or its lack. This is our school and the school of the majority. Al-Awzāʿī said: He looks at the places of flesh. Dāwūd said: He looks at her entire body — and this is a manifest error, opposed to the principles of the Sunnah and consensus. Then, our school, the school of Mālik, Aḥmad, and the majority, is that her consent is not a condition for the permissibility of this looking; rather, he may do so while she is heedless (ghaflah) and without prior notification. However, Mālik said: I dislike his looking at her while she is heedless, out of fear that his gaze might fall upon an ʿawrah. And from Mālik there is a weak narration that he does not look at her except with her permission — and this is weak, because the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) permitted that absolutely and did not condition her permission, and because she is usually too shy to grant permission, and because in that is a risk — perhaps he sees her and she does not please him, so he leaves her, and she is broken-hearted and harmed. For this reason, our companions said: It is recommended that his looking at her be before the proposal (khiṭbah), so that if he dislikes her, he leaves her without harming her — unlike the case if he leaves her after the proposal. And Allah knows best.

Our companions said: And if he cannot look, it is recommended that he send a woman he trusts to look at her and inform him, and that this be before the proposal, for the reason we mentioned.

His saying (peace and blessings be upon him): «كأنما تنحتون الفضة من عرض هذا الجبل» — "As if you are carving out silver from the side of this mountain." "العرض" (al-ʿarḍ) — with ḍammah on the ʿayn and sukūn on the rāʾ — is the side and the direction. "تنحتون" (tanḥitūn) — with kasrah on the ḥāʾ — meaning: you are scraping and cutting off. The meaning of this speech is the disapproval of excessive dowry (mahr) relative to the husband's situation.

| Chapter: The Dowry (Ṣadāq) and the Permissibility of It Being the Teaching of the Qurʾān or an Iron Ring, and Other Things, Little or Much, and the Recommendation of It Being Five Hundred Dirhams for One Whom It Does Not Burden

His saying: «حدثنا يعقوب» — meaning Yaʿqūb ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Qārī. "Al-Qārī" is with tashdīd on the yāʾ, attributed to the Qārah tribe, a well-known tribe, and its explanation has preceded.

[1425] Her saying: «جئت أهب لك نفسي» — "I have come to gift myself to you" — with his silence (peace and blessings be upon him). In this is evidence for the permissibility of a woman gifting her marriage to him, as Allah said: {وامرأة مؤمنة إن وهبت نفسها للنبي إن أراد النبي أن يستنكحها خالصة لك من دون المؤمنين} — "And a believing woman if she gifts herself to the Prophet, if the Prophet desires to marry her — exclusively for you, not for the believers." Our companions said: So this verse and this ḥadīth are two pieces of evidence for that. Thus, if a woman gifts herself to him (peace and blessings be upon him) and he marries her without a dowry, that is lawful for him, and no dowry is obligatory upon him thereafter — neither by consummation, nor by death, nor by anything else — unlike other than him, for his marriage is not free from the obligation of a dowry, either a specified one (musammā) or the equivalent dowry (mahr al-mithl). And regarding the validity of the Prophet's (peace and blessings be upon him) marriage by the wording of "gift" (hibah), there are two views (wajhān) among our companions: One — it is valid, due to the apparent meaning of the verse and this ḥadīth. The second — it is not valid by the wording of "gift"; rather, it is only valid by the wording of "marriage" (tazwīj) or "giving in marriage" (inkāḥ), like other than him from the Ummah, for it is only valid by one of these two wordings in our school without dispute. And this proponent interprets the verse and the ḥadīth as meaning that the intent is...

chapters.title_en: The Contract of Marriage by the Word "Gift" and Related Rulings on the Dowry
chapters.arabic_text:
بالهبة أنه لا مهر لأجل العقد بلفظ الهبة وقال أبو  حنيفة ينعقد نكاح كل أحد

بكل لفظ يقتضي التمليك على التأبيد وبمثل مذهبنا قال الثوري وأبو ثور

وكثيرون من أصحاب مالك وغيرهم وهو إحدى الروايتين عن مالك والرواية الأخرى

عنه أنه ينعقد بلفظ الهبة والصدقة والبيع إذا قصد به النكاح سواء ذكر

الصداق أم لا ولا يصح بلفظ الرهن والإجارة والوصية ومن أصحاب مالك من صححه

بلفظ الإحلال والإباحة حكاه القاضي عياض قوله (فنظر إليها رسول الله صلى

الله عليه وسلم فصعد النظر فيها وصوبه ثم طأطأ) أما صعد فبتشديد العين أي

رفع وأما صوب فبتشديد الواو أي خفض وفيه دليل لجواز النظر لمن أراد أن

يتزوج امرأة وتأمله إياها وفيه استحباب عرض المرأة نفسها على الرجل الصالح

ليتزوجها وفيه أنه يستحب لمن طلبت منه حاجة لا يمكنه قضاؤها أن يسكت سكوتا

يفهم السائل منه ذلك ولا يخجله بالمنع إلا إذا لم يحصل الفهم إلا بصريح

المنع فيصرح قال الخطابي وفيه جواز نكاح المرأة من غير أن تسأل هل هي في

عدة أم لا حملا على ظاهر الحال قال وعادة الحكام يبحثون عن ذلك احتياطا قلت

قال الشافعي لا يزوج القاضي من جاءته لطلب الزواج حتى
# 
# يشهد عدلان أنه ليس لها ولي خاص وليست في زوجية ولا عدة فمن أصحابنا من

قال هذا شرط واجب والأصح عندهم أنه استحباب واحتياط وليس بشرط قوله صلى

الله عليه وسلم (انظر ولو خاتم من حديد) هكذا هو في النسخ خاتم من حديد وفي

بعض النسخ خاتما وهذا واضح والأول صحيح أيضا أي ولو حضر خاتم من حديد وفيه

دليل على أنه يستحب أن لا ينعقد النكاح إلا بصداق لأنه أقطع للنزاع وأنفع

للمرأة من حيث إنه لو حصل طلاق قبل الدخول وجب نصف المسمى فلو لم تكن تسمية

لم يجب صداق بل تجب المتعة فلو عقد النكاح بلا صداق صح قال الله تعالى لا

جناح عليكم إن طلقتم النساء ما لم تمسوهن أو تفرضوا لهن فريضة فهذا تصريح

بصحة النكاح والطلاق من غير  مهر ثم يجب لها المهر وهل يجب بالعقد أم

بالدخول فيه خلاف مشهور وهما قولان للشافعي أصحهما بالدخول وهو ظاهر هذه

الآية وفي هذا الحديث أنه يجوز أن يكون الصداق قليلا وكثيرا مما يتمول إذا

تراضى به الزوجان لأن خاتم الحديد في نهاية من القلة وهذا مذهب الشافعي وهو

مذهب جماهير العلماء من السلف والخلف وبه قال ربيعة وأبو الزناد وبن أبي

ذئب ويحيى بن سعيد والليث بن سعد والثوري والأوزاعي ومسلم بن خالد الزنجي

وبن أبي ليلى وداود وفقهاء أهل الحديث وبن وهب من أصحاب مالك قال القاضي هو

مذهب العلماء كافة من الحجازيين والبصريين والكوفيين والشاميين وغيرهم أنه

يجوز ما تراضى به الزوجان من قليل وكثير كالسوط والنعل وخاتم الحديد ونحوه

وقال مالك أقله ربع دينار كنصاب السرقة قال القاضي هذا مما انفرد به مالك

وقال أبو حنيفة وأصحابه أقله عشر دراهم وقال بن شبرمة أقله خمسة دراهم

اعتبارا بنصاب القطع في السرقة عندهما وكره النخعي أن يتزوج بأقل من أربعين

درهما وقال مرة عشرة وهذه المذاهب سوى مذهب الجمهور مخالفة للسنة وهم

محجوجون بهذا الحديث الصحيح الصريح وفي هذا الحديث جواز اتخاذ خاتم الحديد

وفيه خلاف للسلف حكاه القاضي ولأصحابنا في كراهته وجهان أصحهما لا يكره لأن

الحديث في النهي عنه ضعيف وقد أوضحت المسألة في شرح المهذب وفيه استحباب

تعجيل تسليم المهر إليها قوله (لا والله يا رسول الله ولا خاتم من حديد)

فيه جواز الحلف من غير استحلاف ولا ضرورة لكن قال أصحابنا يكره من
# 
# غير حاجة وهذا كان محتاجا ليؤكد قوله وفيه جواز تزويج المعسر وتزوجه قوله

(ولكن هذا إزاري فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ما تصنع بإزارك إن

لبسته لم يكن عليها منه شيء وإن لبسته لم يكن عليك منه شيء) فيه دليل على

نظر كبير القوم في مصالحهم وهدايته إياهم إلى ما فيه الرفق بهم وفيه جواز

لبس الرجل ثوب امرأته إذا رضيت أو غلب على ظنه رضاها وهو المراد  في هذا

الحديث قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (اذهب فقد ملكتها بما معك) هكذا هو في معظم

النسخ وكذا نقله القاضي عن رواية الأكثرين ملكتها بضم الميم وكسر اللام

المشددة على ما لم يسم فاعله وفي بعض النسخ ملكتكها بكافين وكذا رواه

البخاري وفي الرواية الأخرى زوجتكها قال القاضي قال الدارقطني رواية من روى

ملكتها وهم قال والصواب رواية من روى زوجتكها قال وهم أكثر وأحفظ قلت

ويحتمل صحة اللفظين ويكون جرى لفظ التزويج أولا فملكها ثم قال له اذهب فقد

ملكتها بالتزويج السابق والله أعلم وفي هذا الحديث دليل لجواز كون الصداق

تعليم القرآن وجواز الاستئجار لتعليم القرآن وكلاهما جائز عند الشافعي وبه

قال عطاء والحسن بن صالح ومالك وإسحاق وغيرهم ومنعه جماعة منهم الزهري وأبو

حنيفة وهذا الحديث مع الحديث الصحيح إن أحق ما أخذتم عليه أجرا كتاب الله

يردان قول من منع ذلك ونقل القاضي عياض جواز الاستئجار لتعليم القرآن عن
# 
# العلماء كافة سوى أبي حنيفة قولها (كان صداق رسول الله صلى الله عليه
chapters.anchors:
- Root: و-ه-ب (w-h-b)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: The root denotes the act of bestowal or giving without expectation of compensation; a "gift" (hibah) is a unilateral transfer of ownership.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In legal-theological terms, it signifies a gratuitous conveyance (tamlīk) that establishes ownership, distinct from commutative contracts like sale (bayʿ).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literally, it is the physical act of giving; metaphorically, it can be extended to verbal formulations that effect transfer of rights, but in marriage (nikāḥ), its use is contested—whether it is ḥaqīqah (literal) or majāz (metaphorical) for the marriage contract.
- Sībawayh Rule: Rule of ʿAṭf al-Bayān (Appositional Clarification) — When multiple verbs or phrases are coordinated (e.g., "صعد" and "صوب"), each retains its distinct syntactic object and semantic force, requiring precise parsing to avoid conflation of meanings.
chapters.translation:
I say: Regarding the [validity of marriage contracted] by the word "gift" (hibah), [our position is] that there is no dowry (mahr) due by virtue of the contract [if concluded] with the utterance of "gift." Abū Ḥanīfah said: The marriage of every person is validly contracted by any expression that implies permanent transfer of ownership (tamlīk ʿalā al-taʾbīd). Al-Thawrī, Abū Thawr, and many of Mālik's companions and others followed our school of thought. This is also one of two narrations from Mālik; the other narration from him is that the marriage is validly contracted by the words "gift," "charity" (ṣadaqah), and "sale" (bayʿ) if the intention is marriage, whether the dowry is mentioned or not. However, it is not valid by the words "pledge" (rahn), "hire" (ijārah), or "bequest" (waṣiyyah). Among Mālik's companions, some deemed it valid by the words "making lawful" (iḥlāl) and "permitting" (ibāḥah); al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ narrated this.

His statement (peace and blessings be upon him): "He looked at her, and the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) raised his gaze towards her and lowered it, then he bowed his head." As for "ṣaʿada" (raised), it is with tashdīd on the ʿayn, meaning he lifted [his gaze]; as for "ṣawwaba" (lowered), it is with tashdīd on the wāw, meaning he cast it down. In this [hadith] is evidence for the permissibility of looking at a woman for one who intends to marry her and contemplating her. It also contains the recommendation (istiḥbāb) of a woman presenting herself to a righteous man to marry her. Furthermore, it indicates that it is recommended for one who is asked for a need he cannot fulfill to remain silent in a manner that conveys this to the petitioner without shaming him by refusal—unless understanding is not achieved except through explicit refusal, in which case he should be explicit. Al-Khaṭṭābī said: In this [hadith] is the permissibility of marrying a woman without asking whether she is in a waiting period (ʿiddah) or not, relying on the apparent state of affairs. He said: The custom of judges is to investigate this as a precaution. I say: Al-Shāfiʿī said: The judge should not marry off a woman who comes to him seeking marriage until two just witnesses testify that she has no specific guardian (walī khāṣṣ), and that she is not in an existing marriage nor in a waiting period. Some of our companions said this is a mandatory condition; the more correct view among them is that it is a recommendation and precaution, not a condition.

His statement (peace and blessings be upon him): "Look, even if it be an iron ring." This is how it appears in the copies: "خاتم من حديد" (an iron ring), and in some copies "خاتما" (with tanwīn), which is clear. The first is also correct, meaning: even if an iron ring is present. In this is evidence that it is recommended that marriage not be concluded except with a dowry, because it is more decisive in preventing disputes and more beneficial for the woman, since if divorce occurs before consummation, half of the specified [dowry] becomes obligatory. If no specification were made, no dowry would be obligatory; rather, a gift of consolation (mutʿah) would be due. If the marriage is contracted without a dowry, it is valid. Allah the Exalted said: {«لَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيْكُمْ إِنْ طَلَّقْتُمُ النِّسَاءَ مَا لَمْ تَمَسُّوهُنَّ أَوْ تَفْرِضُوا لَهُنَّ فَرِيضَةً»} ("There is no blame upon you if you divorce women you have not touched nor specified for them an obligation"). This is an explicit statement of the validity of marriage and divorce without a dowry. Then the dowry becomes obligatory for her. Whether it is obligatory by the contract or by consummation is a well-known point of disagreement—two opinions of al-Shāfiʿī, the more correct of which is that it is by consummation, and this is the apparent meaning of this verse.

In this hadith [there is evidence] that the dowry may be little or much, whatever is considered wealth (māl), if the two spouses agree upon it, because the iron ring is at the utmost limit of insignificance. This is the school of al-Shāfiʿī and the school of the majority of scholars among the predecessors (salaf) and successors (khalaf). Rabīʿah, Abū al-Zinād, Ibn Abī Dhiʾb, Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd, al-Layth ibn Saʿd, al-Thawrī, al-Awzāʿī, Muslim ibn Khālid al-Zanjī, Ibn Abī Laylā, Dāwūd, the jurists of the people of hadith, and Ibn Wahb among Mālik's companions all held this view. Al-Qāḍī said: It is the school of all scholars—from the Ḥijāzīs, Baṣrīs, Kūfīs, Shāmīs, and others—that whatever the two spouses agree upon, whether little or much, is permissible, such as a whip, a sandal, an iron ring, and the like. Mālik said: Its minimum is a quarter of a dīnār, like the threshold for theft (niṣāb al-sariqah). Al-Qāḍī said: This is something unique to Mālik. Abū Ḥanīfah and his companions said: Its minimum is ten dirhams. Ibn Shubrumah said: Its minimum is five dirhams, by analogy with the threshold for amputation in theft according to them. Al-Nakhaʿī disapproved of marrying for less than forty dirhams, and on one occasion he said ten. These schools, other than the majority view, contradict the Sunnah, and they are refuted by this authentic and explicit hadith.

In this hadith [there is evidence] for the permissibility of wearing an iron ring. There is a disagreement among the predecessors about this, narrated by al-Qāḍī. Among our companions, there are two views on its disapproval; the more correct of them is that it is not disapproved, because the hadith prohibiting it is weak. I have clarified this issue in Sharḥ al-Muhadhdhab.

In this hadith [there is evidence] for the recommendation of promptly delivering the dowry to her.

Her statement: "No, by Allah, O Messenger of Allah, not even an iron ring." In this is the permissibility of swearing an oath without being asked to do so and without necessity. However, our companions said: It is disapproved when there is no need, and this [woman] was in need to emphasize her statement. In it is also the permissibility of marrying a man in financial difficulty and his marrying [her].

His statement (peace and blessings be upon him): "But this is my waist-wrapper (izār)." The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "What will you do with your waist-wrapper? If you wear it, she will have nothing of it; and if she wears it, you will have nothing of it." In this is evidence of the leader of a people considering their interests and guiding them to what is gentle for them. In it is also the permissibility of a man wearing his wife's garment if she is pleased or he strongly suspects her pleasure—and this is the intended meaning in this hadith.

His statement (peace and blessings be upon him): "Go, for I have given her to you in marriage (malkatuhā) with what you have." This is how it appears in most copies, and al-Qāḍī narrated it from the narration of the majority: "مَلَكْتُهَا" (malkatuhā) with a ḍammah on the mīm and a kasrah on the shaddah lām, in the passive voice (mā lam yusamma fāʿiluhu). In some copies it is "مَلَّكْتُكَهَا" (mallaktukahā) with two kāfs, and thus al-Bukhārī narrated it. In another narration: "زَوَّجْتُكَهَا" (zawwajtukahā, "I have married her to you"). Al-Qāḍī said: Al-Dāraquṭnī said: The narration of those who narrated "مَلَكْتُهَا" is erroneous; the correct version is the narration of those who narrated "زَوَّجْتُكَهَا." He said: They are more numerous and more precise. I say: It is possible that both wordings are sound, and that the wording of marriage (tazwīj) occurred first, then he said to him: "Go, for I have given her to you in marriage (malkatuhā) by the preceding marriage contract." And Allah knows best.

In this hadith is evidence for the permissibility of the dowry being the teaching of the Qurʾān, and the permissibility of hiring (istiʾjār) for teaching the Qurʾān. Both are permissible according to al-Shāfiʿī, and ʿAṭāʾ, al-Ḥasan ibn Ṣāliḥ, Mālik, Isḥāq, and others held this view. A group prohibited it, among them al-Zuhrī and Abū Ḥanīfah. This hadith, along with the authentic hadith: "The most worthy thing for which you take payment is the Book of Allah," refutes the view of those who prohibit that. Al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ narrated the permissibility of hiring for teaching the Qurʾān from all scholars except Abū Ḥanīfah.

Her statement: "The dowry of the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him)..."

chapters.title_en: The Dowry of the Mothers of the Believers and the Wedding Feast (Walīmah)
chapters.arabic_text:
وسلم لأزواجه ثنتي عشرة أوقية ونشا قالت أتدري ما النش قلت لا قالت نصف

أوقية فتلك خمسمائة درهم) أما الأوقية فبضم الهمزة وبتشديد الياء والمراد

أوقية الحجاز وهي أربعون درهما وأما النش فبنون مفتوحة ثم شين معجمة مشددة

واستدل أصحابنا بهذا الحديث على أنه يستحب كون الصداق خمسمائة درهم والمراد

في حق من يحتمل ذلك فإن قيل فصداق أم حبيبة زوج النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

كان أربعة آلاف درهم وأربعمائة دينار فالجواب أن هذا القدر تبرع به النجاشي

من ماله إكراما
# 
# للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لا أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أداه أو عقد به

والله أعلم
# [1427] قوله (إن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم رأى على عبد الرحمن أثر صفرة

قال ما هذا) فيه أنه يستحب للإمام والفاضل تفقد أصحابه والسؤال عما يختلف

من أحوالهم وقوله (أثر صفرة) وفي رواية في غير كتاب مسلم رأى عليه صفرة وفي

رواية ردع  من زعفران والردع براء ودال وعين مهملات هو أثر الطيب والصحيح في

معنى هذا الحديث أنه تعلق به أثر من الزعفران وغيره من طيب العروس ولم

يقصده ولا تعمد التزعفر فقد ثبت في الصحيح النهي عن التزعفر للرجال وكذا

نهي الرجال عن الخلوق لأنه شعار النساء وقد نهى الرجال عن التشبه بالنساء

فهذا هو الصحيح في معنى الحديث وهو الذي اختاره القاضي والمحققون قال

القاضي وقيل إنه يرخص في ذلك للرجل العروس وقد جاء ذلك في أثر ذكره أبو

عبيد أنهم كانوا يرخصون في ذلك للشاب أيام عرسه قال وقيل لعله كان يسيرا

فلم ينكر قال وقيل كان في أول الإسلام من تزوج لبس ثوبا مصبوغا علامة

لسروره وزواجه قال وهذا غير معروف وقيل يحتمل أنه كان في ثيابه دون بدنه

ومذهب مالك وأصحابه جواز لبس الثياب المزعفرة وحكاه مالك عن علماء المدينة

وهذا مذهب بن عمر وغيره وقال الشافعي وأبو حنيفة لا يجوز ذلك للرجل قوله

(تزوجت امرأة على وزن نواة من ذهب) قال القاضي قال الخطابي النواة اسم لقدر

معروف عندهم فسروها بخمسة دراهم من ذهب قال القاضي كذا فسرها أكثر العلماء

وقال أحمد بن حنبل هي ثلاثة دراهم وثلث وقيل المراد نواة التمر أي وزنها من

ذهب والصحيح الأول وقال بعض المالكية النواة ربع دينار عند أهل المدينة

وظاهر كلام أبي عبيد أنه دفع خمسة دراهم قال ولم يكن هناك ذهب إنما هي خمسة

دراهم تسمى نواة كما تسمى الأربعون أوقية قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (فبارك

الله لك) فيه استحباب الدعاء للمتزوج وأن يقال بارك الله لك أو نحوه وسبق

في الباب قبله إيضاحه قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (أو لم ولو بشاة) قال

العلماء من أهل اللغة والفقهاء وغيرهم الوليمة الطعام المتخذ للعرس مشتقة
# 
# من الولم وهو الجمع لأن الزوجين يجتمعان قاله الأزهري وغيره وقال

الأنباري أصلها تمام الشيء واجتماعه والفعل منها أو لم قال أصحابنا وغيرهم

الضيافات ثمانية أنواع الوليمة للعرس والخرس بضم الخاء  المعجمة ويقال الخرص

أيضا بالصاد المهملة للولادة والإعذار بكسر الهمزة وبالعين المهملة والذال

المعجمة للختان والوكيرة للبناء والنقيعة لقدوم المسافر مأخوذة من النقع

وهو الغبار ثم قيل إن المسافر يصنع الطعام وقيل يصنعه غيره له والعقيقة يوم

سابع الولادة والوضيمة بفتح الواو وكسر الضاد المعجمة الطعام عند المصيبة

والمأدبة بضم الدال وفتحها الطعام المتخذ ضيافة بلا سبب والله أعلم واختلف

العلماء في وليمة العرس هل هي واجبة أم مستحبة والأصح عند أصحابنا أنها سنة

مستحبة ويحملون هذا الأمر في هذا الحديث على الندب وبه قال مالك وغيره

وأوجبها داود وغيره واختلف العلماء في وقت فعلها فحكى القاضي أن الأصح عند

مالك وغيره أنه يستحب فعلها بعد الدخول وعن جماعة من المالكية استحبابها

عند العقد وعن بن حبيب المالكي استحبابها عند العقد وعند الدخول وقوله
# 
# صلى الله عليه وسلم

| (أولم ولو بشاة دليل على أنه يستحب للموسر أن لا 
# ينقص عن شاة ونقل القاضي الإجماع على أنه لا حد لقدرها المجزئ بل بأي شيء

أولم من الطعام حصلت الوليمة وقد ذكر مسلم بعد هذا وفي وليمة عرس صفية أنها

كانت بغير لحم وفي وليمة زينب أشبعنا خبزا ولحما وكل هذا جائز تحصل به

الوليمة لكن يستحب أن تكون على قدر حال الزوج قال القاضي واختلف السلف في

تكرارها أكثر من يومين فكرهته طائفة ولم تكرهه طائفة قال واستحب أصحاب مالك

للموسر كونها أسبوعا)

| باب فضيلة اعتاقه أمته ثم يتزوجها
# [1365] قوله (فصلينا عندها صلاة الغداة) دليل على أنه لا كراهة في

تسميتها الغداة وقال بعض أصحابنا
# 
# يكره والصواب الأول قوله (وأنا رديف أبي طلحة) دليل لجواز الإرداف إذا

كانت الدابة مطيقة وقد كثرت الأحاديث الصحيحة بمثله قوله (فأجرى نبي الله

صلى الله عليه وسلم في زقاق خيبر) دليل لجواز ذلك وأنه لا يسقط المروءة ولا

يخل بمراتب أهل الفضل لا سيما عند الحاجة للقتال أو رياضة الدابة أو تدريب

النفس ومعاناة أسباب الشجاعة قوله (وإن ركبتي لتمس فخذ نبي الله صلى الله
chapters.anchors:
- Root: و-ل-م (w-l-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning is 'gathering' or 'assembling' (al-jamʿ); the walīmah is the feast made for a wedding because the two spouses gather together.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological usage, it denotes the communal celebration of a licit union, emphasizing social cohesion and gratitude.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) for the act of gathering; metaphorical (majāz) for the feast itself as a symbol of union.
- Sībawayh Rule: ʿAṭf al-Bayān (Appositional Clarification) — the term 'al-nashsh' is clarified by 'niṣf ūqiyyah' as an explicative appositive, requiring precise nominal parsing.
chapters.translation:
I say: And he (the Prophet, peace be upon him) gave to his wives twelve ūqiyyahs and a nashsh. She (ʿĀʾishah) said: 'Do you know what the nashsh is?' I said: 'No.' She said: 'It is half an ūqiyyah; thus that is five hundred dirhams.' As for the ūqiyyah, it is with a ḍammah on the hamzah and a shaddah on the yāʾ, and what is meant is the Ḥijāzī ūqiyyah, which is forty dirhams. As for the nashsh, it is with an open nūn, then a shaddah on the shīn with iʿjām (dotting). Our companions (the Shāfiʿīs) adduced this ḥadīth as evidence that it is recommended (mustaḥabb) for the dowry (ṣadāq) to be five hundred dirhams, and this is meant for the one who can afford that. If it is said: 'But the dowry of Umm Ḥabībah, the wife of the Prophet, peace be upon him, was four thousand dirhams and four hundred dīnārs,' the answer is that this amount was a voluntary gift (tabarruʿ) from the Negus (al-Najāshī) from his own wealth, as an honor to the Prophet, peace be upon him — not that the Prophet, peace be upon him, paid it or contracted the marriage with it. And God knows best.

[1427] His saying: 'The Prophet, peace be upon him, saw on ʿAbd al-Raḥmān a trace of yellowness (athar ṣufrah) and said: "What is this?"' — In this is [the ruling] that it is recommended for the leader (imām) and the virtuous person to inquire about his companions and to ask about the varying conditions among them. His saying 'a trace of yellowness' — and in a narration outside the book of Muslim: 'He saw on him yellowness,' and in another narration: 'a stain (radʿ) of saffron.' The radʿ, with an unpointed rāʾ, dāl, and ʿayn, is the trace of perfume. The correct [understanding] of the meaning of this ḥadīth is that a trace of saffron or other bridal perfume clung to him, and he neither intended it nor deliberately applied saffron (tazaʿfara). For it is established in the Ṣaḥīḥ the prohibition of applying saffron for men, and likewise men are forbidden from khālūq (a type of perfume) because it is a distinctive mark of women, and men have been forbidden from imitating women. This is the correct [interpretation] of the meaning of the ḥadīth, and it is what al-Qāḍī and the verifying scholars (al-muḥaqqiqūn) chose. Al-Qāḍī said: 'And it was said that concession is granted in that for the bridegroom, and this has come in an athar mentioned by Abū ʿUbayd that they used to permit it for the young man during the days of his wedding.' He said: 'And it was said: Perhaps it was little, so he did not disapprove.' He said: 'And it was said: In early Islam, whoever married wore a dyed garment as a sign of his joy and marriage.' He said: 'And this is not well-known.' And it was said: 'Perhaps it was on his clothes, not his body.' The madhhab of Mālik and his companions is the permissibility of wearing saffron-dyed garments, and Mālik narrated this from the scholars of Madīnah, and this is the madhhab of Ibn ʿUmar and others. Al-Shāfiʿī and Abū Ḥanīfah said: That is not permissible for a man.

His saying: 'I married a woman for the weight of a nawāh of gold' — Al-Qāḍī said: Al-Khaṭṭābī said: 'The nawāh is a name for a known measure among them, and they interpreted it as five dirhams of gold.' Al-Qāḍī said: 'Thus did most scholars interpret it.' Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal said: 'It is three dirhams and a third.' And it was said: What is meant is the date-pit (nawāt al-tamr), i.e., its weight in gold. The correct [view] is the first. Some Mālikīs said: 'The nawāh is a quarter of a dīnār among the people of Madīnah.' The apparent meaning of Abū ʿUbayd's statement is that he paid five dirhams, and there was no gold there; rather, it was five dirhams called a nawāh, just as forty [dirhams] are called an ūqiyyah.

His saying, peace be upon him: 'May God bless you (bāraka Allāhu laka)' — In this is the recommendation of supplication (duʿāʾ) for the married person, and that one should say: 'May God bless you' or similar. Its clarification has preceded in the chapter before this one.

His saying, peace be upon him: 'Give a wedding feast (awlim), even with a sheep' — The scholars of language, the jurists, and others said: The walīmah is the food prepared for the wedding, derived from al-walm, which is gathering, because the two spouses gather together. Al-Azharī and others said this. Al-Anbārī said: 'Its origin is the completion of a thing and its gathering together, and the verb from it is awlama.' Our companions and others said: The hospitality feasts (ḍiyāfāt) are eight types: the walīmah for the wedding; the khurs, with a ḍammah on the khāʾ with iʿjām — and it is also said al-khurs with a ṣād unpointed — for childbirth; the iʿdhār, with a kasrah on the hamzah, an unpointed ʿayn, and a dotted dhāl, for circumcision; the wakīrah for building [a house]; the naqīʿah for the arrival of a traveler, derived from al-naqʿ, which is dust, then it is said that the traveler makes the food, or it is said that someone else makes it for him; the ʿaqīqah on the seventh day after birth; the waḍīmah, with a fatḥah on the wāw and a kasrah on the dotted ḍād, is the food at a calamity; and the maʾdabah, with a ḍammah or fatḥah on the dāl, is food prepared as hospitality without a specific cause. And God knows best.

The scholars differed over the wedding feast (walīmat al-ʿurs): is it obligatory (wājibah) or recommended (mustaḥabbah)? The most correct [view] among our companions is that it is a recommended Sunnah, and they interpret this command in this ḥadīth as indicating recommendation (nadb). Mālik and others held this view, while Dāwūd and others made it obligatory. The scholars also differed over the time of performing it. Al-Qāḍī narrated that the most correct [view] with Mālik and others is that it is recommended to do it after consummation (al-dukhūl), and a group of Mālikīs held its recommendation at the contract (al-ʿaqd), and Ibn Ḥabīb al-Mālikī held its recommendation at both the contract and consummation.

His saying, peace be upon him: 'Give a wedding feast, even with a sheep' — This is evidence that it is recommended for the wealthy person not to go below a sheep. Al-Qāḍī transmitted consensus (ijmāʿ) that there is no limit to its sufficient amount; rather, with whatever food one gives a feast, the walīmah is achieved. Muslim has mentioned after this, regarding the wedding feast of Ṣafiyyah, that it was without meat, and in the feast of Zaynab, 'we were satiated with bread and meat.' All of this is permissible, and the walīmah is achieved by it, but it is recommended that it be proportionate to the husband's condition. Al-Qāḍī said: 'The Salaf differed over repeating it for more than two days; a group disapproved of it, and a group did not disapprove.' He said: 'And the companions of Mālik recommended for the wealthy that it be for a week.'

CHAPTER: The Virtue of a Man Freeing His Slave-Girl and Then Marrying Her
[1365] His saying: 'We prayed the morning prayer (ṣalāt al-ghadāh) at her house' — This is evidence that there is no dislike (karāhah) in calling it al-ghadāh, and some of our companions said it is disliked, but the correct [view] is the first. His saying: 'And I was riding behind Abū Ṭalḥah' — This is evidence for the permissibility of riding behind [another] (al-irdāf) when the animal is capable, and many authentic ḥadīths have come with similar [content]. His saying: 'So the Prophet of God, peace be upon him, ran in the alley of Khaybar' — This is evidence for the permissibility of that, and that it does not diminish chivalry (murūʾah) nor impair the ranks of virtuous people, especially when there is a need for fighting, or training the animal, or disciplining the soul, and engaging in the means of courage. His saying: 'And my knee was touching the thigh of the Prophet of God, peace be upon him' —

chapters.title_en: The Unveiling of the Thigh, the Conquest of Khaybar, and the Marriage to Safiyyah
chapters.arabic_text:
عليه وسلم وانحسر الإزار عن فخذ نبي الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فإني لأرى

بياض فخذ نبي الله صلى الله عليه وسلم) هذا مما يستدل به أصحاب مالك وغيرهم

ممن يقول الفخذ ليس بعورة ومذهبنا أنه عورة ويحمل أصحابنا هذا الحديث على

أن انحسار الإزار وغيره كان بغير اختياره صلى الله عليه وسلم فانحسر للزحمة

وإجراء المركوب ووقع نظر أنس إليه فجأة لا تعمدا وكذلك مست ركبته الفخذ من

غير اختيارهما بل للزحمة ولم يقل إنه تعمد ذلك ولا أنه حسر الإزار بل قال

انحسر بنفسه قوله (فلما دخل القرية قال الله أكبر خربت خيبر) فيه دليل

لاستحباب الذكر والتكبير عند الحرب وهو موافق لقول الله تعالى يا أيها

الذين آمنوا إذا لقيتم فئة فاثبتوا واذكروا الله كثيرا ولهذا قالها ثلاث

مرات ويؤخذ منه أن الثلاث كثير وأما قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم خربت خيبر

فذكروا فيه وجهين أحدهما أنه دعاء تقديره أسأل الله خرابها والثاني أنه

إخبار بخرابها على الكفار وفتحها للمسلمين قوله (محمد والخميس) هو بالخاء

المعجمة وبرفع السين
# 
# المهملة وهو الجيش قال الأزهري وغيره سمي خميسا لأنه خمسة أقسام مقدمة

وساقة وميمنة وميسرة وقلب وقيل لتخميس الغنائم وأبطلوا هذا القول لأن هذا

الاسم كان معروفا في الجاهلية ولم يكن لهم تخميس قوله (وأصبناها عنوة) هو

بفتح العين أي قهرا لا صلحا وبعض حصون خيبر أصيب صلحا وسنوضحه في بابه إن

شاء الله تعالى قوله (فجاءه دحية إلى قوله فأخذ صفية بنت حيي) أما دحية

فبفتح الدال وكسرها وأما صفية فالصحيح أن هذا كان اسمها قبل السبي وقيل كان

اسمها زينب فسميت بعد السبي والاصطفاء صفية قوله (أعطيت دحية صفية بنت حيي

سيد قريظة والنضير ما تصلح إلا لك قال ادعوه بها قال فجاء بها فلما نظر

إليها النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال خذ جارية من السبي غيرها) قال المازري

وغيره يحتمل ما جرى مع دحية وجهين أحدهما أن يكون رد الجارية برضاه وأذن له

في غيرها  والثاني أنه إنما أذن له في جارية له من حشو السبي لا أفضلهن فلما

رأى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه أخذ أنفسهن وأجودهن نسبا وشرفا في قومها

وجمالا استرجعها لأنه لم يأذن فيها ورأى في إبقائها لدحية مفسدة لتميزه

بمثلها على باقي الجيش ولما فيه من انتهاكها مع مرتبتها وكونها بنت سيدهم

ولما يخاف من استعلائها على دحية بسبب مرتبتها وربما ترتب على ذلك شقاق أو

غيره فكان أخذه صلى الله عليه وسلم إياها لنفسه قاطعا لكل هذه المفاسد

المتخوفة ومع هذا فعوض دحية عنها وقوله في الرواية الأخرى إنها وقعت في سهم

دحية فاشتراها رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بسبعة أرؤس يحتمل أن المراد

بقوله وقعت في سهمه أي حصلت بالإذن في أخذ جارية ليوافق باقي الروايات

وقوله اشتراها أي أعطاه بدلها سبعة أنفس تطييبا لقلبه لا أنه جرى عقد بيع

وعلى هذا تتفق الروايات وهذا الإعطاء لدحية
# 
# محمول على التنفيل فعلى قول من يقول التنفيل يكون من أصل الغنيمة لا

إشكال فيه وعلى قول من يقول إن التنفيل من خمس الخمس يكون هذا التنفيل من

خمس الخمس بعد أن ميز أو قبله ويحسب منه فهذا الذي ذكرناه هو الصحيح

المختار وحكى القاضي معنى بعضه ثم قال والأولى عندي أن تكون صفية فيئا

لأنها كانت زوجة كنانة بن الربيع وهو وأهله من بني أبي الحقيق كانوا صالحوا

رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وشرط عليهم أن لا يكتموه كنزا فإن كتموه فلا

ذمة لهم وسألهم عن كنز حيي بن أخطب فكتموه وقالوا أذهبته النفقات ثم عثر

عليه عندهم فانتقض عهدهم فسباهم ذكر ذلك أبو عبيد وغيره فصفية من سبيهم فهي

فيء لا يخمس بل يفعل فيه الإمام ما رأى هذا كلام القاضي وهذا تفريع منه على

مذهبه أن الفيء لا يخمس ومذهبنا أنه يخمس كالغنيمة والله أعلم قوله (فقال

له ثابت يا أبا حمزة ما أصدقها قال نفسها أعتقها وتزوجها) فيه أنه يستحب أن

يعتق الأمة ويتزوجها  كما قال في الحديث الذي بعده له أجران وقوله أصدقها

نفسها اختلف في معناه فالصحيح الذي اختاره المحققون أنه أعتقها تبرعا بلا

عوض ولا شرط ثم تزوجها برضاها بلا صداق وهذا من خصائصه صلى الله عليه وسلم

أنه يجوز نكاحه بلا مهر لا في الحال ولا فيما بعد بخلاف غيره وقال بعض

أصحابنا معناه أنه شرط عليها أن يعتقها ويتزوجها فقبلت فلزمها الوفاء به

وقال بعض أصحابنا أعتقها وتزوجها على قيمتها وكانت مجهولة ولا يجوز هذا ولا

الذي قبله لغيره صلى الله عليه وسلم بل هما من الخصائص كما قال أصحاب القول

الأول واختلف العلماء فيمن أعتق أمته على أن تتزوج به ويكون عتقها صداقها

فقال الجمهور لا يلزمها أن تتزوج به ولا يصح هذا الشرط وممن قاله مالك

والشافعي وأبو حنيفة ومحمد بن الحسن وزفر قال الشافعي فإن أعتقها على هذا

الشرط فقبلت عتقت ولا يلزمها أن تتزوجه بل له عليها قيمتها لأنه لم يرض

بعتقها مجانا فإن رضيت وتزوجها على مهر يتفقان عليه فله عليها القيمة ولها

عليه المهر المسمى من قليل أو كثير وإن تزوجها على قيمتها فإن كانت القيمة
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ك-ش-ف (kashafa)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To uncover, reveal, remove a covering; the act of exposing what was concealed.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In legal contexts, refers to the physical exposure of the body (ʿawrah) and its juridical implications.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) for physical uncovering; metaphorical (majāz) for divine disclosure of affairs.
- Root: غ-ن-م (ghanima)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Spoils of war acquired from enemies by force; booty.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): War gains subject to the rule of khums (one-fifth) per Quranic ordinance.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for material plunder; metaphorical for spiritual reward.
- Root: ف-ي-ء (fay')
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Return; in legal usage, property acquired from non-Muslims without combat.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Distinct from ghanīmah; scholars differ on whether khums applies.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for returning; technical for war acquisitions without battle.
- Sībawayh Rule: ʿAṭf al-Bayān (Appositional Clarification) — The rule governing the syntactic relationship where a second noun clarifies the first, as in "Safiyyah bint Ḥuyayy" where the lineage specifies the identity.
chapters.translation:
I say: The Prophet's (peace and blessings be upon him) thigh was exposed when the waist-wrapper slipped from the thigh of the Prophet of God (peace and blessings be upon him), and indeed I see the whiteness of the thigh of the Prophet of God (peace and blessings be upon him). This is a proof used by the followers of Mālik and others who hold that the thigh is not part of the ʿawrah (private parts). Our school (Shāfiʿī) holds that it is ʿawrah. Our scholars interpret this hadith as indicating that the slipping of the waist-wrapper and other such exposure occurred without his choice (peace and blessings be upon him); it slipped due to the crowding and the movement of the mount, and Anas's sight fell upon it suddenly, not deliberately. Likewise, his knee touched the thigh unintentionally, but rather due to the crowd. He (Anas) did not say that he (the Prophet) did this deliberately, nor that he lifted the waist-wrapper himself, but rather he said it slipped by itself.

His statement (peace and blessings be upon him): "When he entered the village, he said: God is Greatest, Khaybar is destroyed" — in this is evidence for the recommendation (istihbāb) of remembrance (dhikr) and takbīr during warfare. This aligns with the saying of God the Exalted: {«يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا إِذَا لَقِيتُمْ فِئَةً فَاثْبُتُوا وَاذْكُرُوا اللَّهَ كَثِيرًا»} (O you who believe, when you meet a company, stand firm and remember God much). For this reason, he said it three times, and from this it is taken that three constitutes "much."

As for his saying (peace and blessings be upon him): "Khaybar is destroyed" — they mentioned two interpretations: First, that it is a supplication (duʿā'), with the implied meaning: "I ask God for its destruction." Second, that it is an announcement (ikhbār) of its destruction upon the disbelievers and its conquest for the Muslims.

His saying: "Muhammad and the army (al-khamīs)" — it is with the dotted khāʾ (خ) and with the vowel u on the sīn (س). Al-Azharī and others said: It is called khamīs because it consists of five divisions: the vanguard (muqaddimah), the rearguard (sāqah), the right flank (maymanah), the left flank (maysarah), and the heart (qalb). It was also said: because of the division of spoils into fifths (takhmīs). But they rejected this latter view because this name was known in the pre-Islamic era (Jāhiliyyah), and they had no system of takhmīs.

His saying: "And we took it by force (ʿanwatan)" — it is with the opening of the ʿayn (ع), meaning by compulsion, not by treaty. Some forts of Khaybar were taken by treaty, and we will clarify this in its proper place, God willing.

His saying: "Then Dihyah came to him... until his saying: 'And he took Safiyyah bint Ḥuyayy'" — As for Dihyah, it is with the opening of the dāl (د) and also with its kasrah. As for Safiyyah, the correct view is that this was her name before captivity; it was also said her name was Zaynab, and she was named Safiyyah after captivity and being chosen (al-ṣafiyy).

His saying: "You have given Dihyah Safiyyah bint Ḥuyayy, the mistress of Qurayẓah and al-Naḍīr; she is only fitting for you. He said: Call him with her. He said: So he brought her. When the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) looked at her, he said: Take another slave-girl from the captives." Al-Māzarī and others said: What transpired with Dihyah admits two interpretations: First, that he returned the slave-girl with his consent, and he was permitted to take another. Second, that he was only permitted to take a slave-girl from the common captives (ḥashw al-saby), not the best among them. When the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) saw that he had taken the most precious of them, the noblest in lineage and honor among her people, and the most beautiful, he took her back because he had not permitted her. He saw in keeping her with Dihyah a corruption (mafsadah), due to his being distinguished with someone like her over the rest of the army, and because of what it entailed of degrading her given her rank, and her being the daughter of their chief, and the fear of her lording over Dihyah due to her status, which might lead to discord or other harms. Thus, the Prophet's (peace and blessings be upon him) taking her for himself cut off all these feared corruptions. Despite this, he compensated Dihyah for her.

His saying in the other narration: "She fell into Dihyah's share (sahm), and the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) bought her for seven heads" — It is possible that the meaning of "she fell into his share" is that she was obtained through the permission to take a slave-girl, to harmonize with the other narrations. And his saying "he bought her" means he gave him seven persons in her place to appease his heart, not that an actual sale contract occurred. On this basis, the narrations are reconciled. This giving to Dihyah is construed as a bonus (tanfīl). According to those who say that tanfīl is from the original spoils (aṣl al-ghanīmah), there is no issue. According to those who say tanfīl is from the fifth of the fifth (khums al-khums), this tanfīl would be from the fifth of the fifth, whether before or after setting it aside, and it is counted from it. What we have mentioned is the correct and chosen view.

Al-Qāḍī related part of this meaning, then said: "The preferable view in my opinion is that Safiyyah was fayʾ (tribute property), because she was the wife of Kinānah ibn al-Rabīʿ, and he and his family, from the Banū Abī al-Ḥuqayq, had made a treaty with the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) stipulating that they would not conceal any treasure from him. If they concealed it, they would have no covenant (dhimmah). He asked them about the treasure of Ḥuyayy ibn Akhṭab, and they concealed it, saying: 'The expenditures consumed it.' Then he discovered it with them, so their covenant was nullified, and he took them captive." Abū ʿUbayd and others mentioned this. Thus, Safiyyah was among their captives, so she is fayʾ, not subject to khums; rather, the Imām does with her what he sees fit. This is the statement of al-Qāḍī, and it is a branching from his school that fayʾ is not subject to khums. Our school holds that it is subject to khums like ghanīmah. And God knows best.

His saying: "Thābit said to him: O Abā Ḥamzah, what was her dowry (ṣadāq)? He said: Herself — he freed her and married her." In this is the recommendation that one free a slave-girl and marry her, as stated in the subsequent hadith: "He has two rewards." His saying "her dowry was herself" — there is disagreement over its meaning. The correct view, chosen by the verifiers (muḥaqqiqūn), is that he freed her as a gratuitous act (tabarruʿ) without compensation or condition, then married her with her consent without a dowry. This is among his special prerogatives (khaṣāʾiṣ) (peace and blessings be upon him), that his marriage is permissible without a mahr, neither immediately nor later, unlike others. Some of our companions said: Its meaning is that he stipulated upon her that he would free her and marry her, and she accepted, so it became binding upon her to fulfill it. Some of our companions said: He freed her and married her for her value (qīmah), which was unknown. Neither this nor the previous view is permissible for anyone other than him (peace and blessings be upon him); rather, both are among his special prerogatives, as stated by the proponents of the first view.

The scholars differed regarding one who frees his slave-girl on the condition that she marry him, making her freedom her dowry. The majority (jumhūr) said: She is not obligated to marry him, and this condition is invalid. Among those who held this are Mālik, al-Shāfiʿī, Abū Ḥanīfah, Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan, and Zufar. Al-Shāfiʿī said: If he frees her on this condition and she accepts, she is freed, but she is not obligated to marry him; rather, he has her value (qīmah) against her, because he did not consent to freeing her for free. If she consents and marries him for a dowry they agree upon, then he has her value against her, and she has the named dowry against him, whether little or much. If he marries her for her value, then if the value...

chapters.title_en: The Ruling on Manumission as Dowry and Related Wedding Customs in the Prophet's Marriage to Safiyyah
chapters.arabic_text:
معلومة له ولها صح الصداق ولا تبقى له عليها قيمة ولا لها عليه صداق وإن

كانت مجهولة ففيه وجهان لأصحابنا أحدهما يصح الصداق كما لو كانت معلومة لأن

هذا العقد فيه ضرب من المسامحة والتخفيف وأصحهما وبه قال جمهور
# 
# أصحابنا لا يصح الصداق بل يصح النكاح ويجب لها مهر المثل وقال سعيد بن

المسيب والحسن والنخعي والزهري والثوري والأوزاعي وأبو يوسف وأحمد وإسحاق

يجوز أن يعتقها على أن تتزوج به ويكون عتقها صداقها ويلزمها ذلك ويصح

الصداق على ظاهر لفظ هذا الحديث وتأوله الآخرون بما سبق قوله (حتى إذا كان

بالطريق جهزتها له أم سليم فأهدتها له من الليل فأصبح رسول الله صلى الله

عليه وسلم عروسا) وفي الرواية التي بعد هذه ثم دفعها إلى أم سليم تصنعها

وتهيئها قال وأحسبه قال وتعتد في بيتها أما قوله  تعتد فمعناه تستبريء فإنها

كانت مسبية يجب استبراؤها وجعلها في مدة الاستبراء في بيت أم سليم فلما

انقضى الاستبراء جهزتها أم سليم وهيأتها أي زينتها وجملتها على عادة العروس

بما ليس بمنهي عنه من وشم ووصل وغير ذلك من المنهي عنه وقوله أهدتها أي

زفتها يقال أهديت العروس إلى زوجها أي زففتها والعروس يطلق على الزوج

والزوجة جميعا وفي الكلام تقديم وتأخير ومعناه اعتدت أي استبرأت ثم هيأتها

ثم أهدتها والواو لا تقتضي ترتيبها وفيه الزفاف بالليل وقد سبق في حديث

تزوجه صلى الله عليه وسلم عائشة رضي الله عنها الزفاف نهارا وذكرنا هناك

جواز الأمرين والله أعلم قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (من كان عنده شيء فليجئني

به) وفي بعض النسخ فليجيء به بغير نون فيه دليل لوليمة العرس وأنها بعد

الدخول وقد سبق أنها تجوز قبله وبعده وفيه إدلال الكبير على أصحابه وطلب

طعامهم في نحو هذا وفيه أنه يستحب لأصحاب الزوج وجيرانه مساعدته في وليمته

بطعام من عندهم قوله (وبسط نطعا) فيه أربع لغات مشهورات فتح النون وكسرها

مع فتح الطاء وإسكانها أفصحهن كسر النون مع فتح الطاء وجمعه نطوع وأنطاع

قوله (فجعل الرجل يجيء بالأقط وجعل الرجل يجيء بالتمر وجعل الرجل يجيء

بالسمن فحاسوا حيسا) الحيس هو الأقط والتمر والسمن يخلط ويعجن ومعناه جعلوا

ذلك حيسا ثم أكلوه قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم في الذي يعتق جاريته ثم يتزوجها

له أجران هذا الحديث سبق بيانه وشرحه
# 
# واضحا في كتاب الإيمان حيث ذكره مسلم وإنما أعاده هنا تنبيها على أن

النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فعل ذلك في صفية لهذه الفضيلة الظاهرة
# [1365] قوله (حين بزغت الشمس) هو بفتح الباء والزاي ومعناه عند ابتداء

طلوعها قوله (وخرجوا بفؤوسهم ومكاتلهم ومرورهم) أما الفؤوس فبهمزة
# 
# ممدودة على وزن فعول جمع فأس بالهمز وهي معروفة والمكاتل جمع مكتل وهو

القفة والزنبيل والمرور جمع مر بفتح الميم وهو معروف نحو المجرفة وأكبر

منها يقال لها المساحي هذا هو الصحيح في معناه وحكى  القاضي قولين أحدهما

هذا والثاني المراد بالمرور هنا الحبال كانوا يصعدون بها إلى النخيل قال

وأحدها مر بفتح الميم وكسرها لأنه يمر حين يفتل قوله (فحصت الأرض أفاحيص)

هو بضم الفاء وكسر الحاء المهملة المخففة أي كشف التراب من أعلاها وحفرت

شيئا يسيرا ليجعل الأنطاع في المحفور ويصب فيها السمن فيثبت ولا يخرج من

جوانبها وأصل الفحص الكشف وفحص عن الأمر وفحص الطائر لبيضه والأفاحيص جمع

أفحوص قوله (فعثرت الناقة العضباء وندر رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وندرت

فقام فسترها) قوله عثرت بفتع
# 
# الثاء وندر بالنون أي سقط وأصل الندور الخروج والانفراد ومنه كلمة نادرة

أي فردة عن النظائر
# [1428] قوله (فجعل يمر على نسائه فيسلم على كل واحدة منهن سلام عليكم كيف

أنتم يا أهل البيت فيقولون بخير يا رسول الله كيف وجدت أهلك فيقول بخير) في

هذه القطعة فوائد منها أنه يستحب للإنسان إذا أتى منزله أن يسلم على امرأته

وأهله وهذا مما يتكبر عنه كثير من الجاهلين المترفعين ومنها أنه إذا سلم

على واحد قال سلام عليكم أو السلام عليكم بصيغة الجمع قالوا ليتناوله

وملكيه ومنها سؤال الرجل أهله عن حالهم فربما كانت في نفس المرأة حاجة

فتستحي أن تبتدئ بها فإذا سألها انبسطت لذكر حاجتها ومنها أنه يستحب أن

يقال للرجل عقب دخوله كيف حالك ونحو هذا قوله (فلما وضع رجله في أسكفة

الباب) هي بهمزة قطع مضمومة وبإسكان
# 
# السين
# [1365] قوله فجعل الرجل يجئ بفضل التمر وفضل السويق حتى جعلوا من ذلك

سوادا حيسا السواد بفتح السين وأصل السواد الشخص ومنه في حديث الإسراء رأى

آدم عن يمينه أسودة وعن يساره أسودة أي أشخاصا والمراد هنا حتى جعلوا من

ذلك كوما شاخصا مرتفعا فخلطوه وجعلوا حيسا قوله حتى إذا رأينا جدر المدينة

هشنا إليها هكذا هو في النسخ هشنا بفتح الهاء وتشديد الشين المعجمة ثم نون

وفي بعضها هششنا بشينين الأولى مكسورة مخففة ومعناهما نشطنا وخففنا وانبعثت

نفوسنا إليها يقال منه هششت بكسر الشين في الماضي  وفتحها في المضارع وذكر
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ع-ل-م (ʿalima)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Knowledge, cognizance; the opposite of ignorance (jahl); denotes certainty or awareness of a thing's reality.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In legal contexts, ʿilm signifies definitive knowledge that removes ambiguity, distinguishing known (maʿlūmah) from unknown (majhūlah) matters in contractual validity.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense is mental apprehension; metaphorically used for legal determination, as in "known dowry" (ṣadāq maʿlūm) versus "unknown" (majhūl), where the latter is a juristic extension.
- Sībawayh Rule: ʿAṭf al-Nasaq (Coordination) — The conjunction "wa" (و) does not inherently imply sequence (tartīb); it merely joins clauses, allowing for reordering of actions as Nawawī notes regarding "iʿtadat, thumma hayya'at, thumma ahdat."
chapters.translation:
I say: If the dowry is known to him and to her, the dowry is valid, and neither does he retain any claim against her for value, nor does she have any claim against him for a dowry. But if it is unknown, then there are two positions (wajhān) among our companions (aṣḥābunā): One of them is that the dowry is valid, just as if it were known, because this contract contains a measure of leniency and facilitation. The more correct of the two—and it is the view of the majority of our companions—is that the dowry is not valid; rather, the marriage is valid, and she is entitled to the equivalent dowry (mahr al-mithl). Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib, al-Ḥasan, al-Nakhaʿī, al-Zuhrī, al-Thawrī, Abū Yūsuf, Aḥmad, and Isḥāq said: It is permissible for a man to manumit a slave-girl on the condition that she marry him, making her manumission her dowry, and this is binding upon her, and the dowry is valid according to the apparent wording of this ḥadīth. Others interpreted it in the manner previously mentioned.

His statement (until when he was on the road, Umm Sulaym prepared her for him and presented her to him at night, and the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, awoke as a bridegroom). In the narration that follows this one: "Then he handed her over to Umm Sulaym to prepare and adorn her." He said: "And I think he said: 'And she observed her waiting period in her house.'" As for his statement "she observed the waiting period" (taʿtadd), its meaning is that she underwent a period of istibrāʾ (ascertaining the purity of the womb), for she was a captive (sabiyyah) whose istibrāʾ was obligatory. He placed her during the period of istibrāʾ in the house of Umm Sulaym. When the istibrāʾ concluded, Umm Sulaym prepared and adorned her—that is, beautified and embellished her in the customary manner of a bride, with what is not prohibited such as tattooing (washm), hair extensions (waṣl), and other things that are prohibited. His statement "she presented her" (ahdat-hā) means she escorted her in procession; it is said, "I presented the bride to her husband," i.e., I escorted her. The term "bride" (ʿarūs) applies to both the husband and the wife. In the wording there is forward and backward arrangement (taqdīm wa taʾkhīr), and its meaning is: she observed the waiting period, i.e., istibrāʾ, then she adorned her, then she presented her—and the conjunction "wa" does not necessitate sequence. In this is the permissibility of the wedding procession at night. It has already preceded in the ḥadīth of his marriage, peace and blessings be upon him, to ʿĀʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her, that the procession was during the day, and we mentioned there the permissibility of both matters. And Allah knows best.

His statement, peace and blessings be upon him: "Whoever has something with him, let him bring it to me"—and in some copies "fal-yajiʾ bihi" without the nūn—contains evidence for the wedding feast (walīmah) and that it occurs after consummation. It has already been stated that it is permissible before and after it. In this is the great one's familiarity with his companions and his requesting their food in such matters. And in it is that it is recommended for the husband's companions and neighbors to assist him in his walīmah with food from their own homes.

His statement "and he spread out a leather mat" (nṭʿ): There are four well-known pronunciations: with fatḥah on the nūn and kasrah on it, both with fatḥah on the ṭāʾ and its sukūn. The most eloquent of them is kasrah on the nūn with fatḥah on the ṭāʾ. Its plural is nṭūʿ and anṭāʿ.

His statement "and one man began bringing iqṭ (dried yogurt), another bringing dates, another bringing clarified butter (samn), and they mixed it into ḥays": al-ḥays is iqṭ, dates, and samn mixed and kneaded together. Its meaning is that they made that into ḥays, then ate it.

His statement, peace and blessings be upon him, regarding the one who manumits his slave-girl then marries her: "He has two rewards." This ḥadīth has already been explained and clarified comprehensively in the Book of Faith (Kitāb al-Īmān), where Muslim recorded it. He only repeated it here to draw attention to the fact that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, did that with Ṣafiyyah for this manifest virtue.

[1365] His statement "when the sun had risen" (ḥīna bazaqhat al-shams): It is with fatḥah on the bāʾ and the zāy, and its meaning is at the beginning of its rising.

His statement "and they went out with their axes (fuʾūs), baskets (makātil), and spades (murūr)": As for the axes, they are with a prolonged hamzah, on the pattern of fuʿūl, the plural of faʾs with hamzah, and they are well-known. The makātil is the plural of miktal, which is the quffah (large basket) and the zanbīl (woven basket).
