The murūr is the plural of marr, with fatḥah on the mīm, and it is well-known, resembling the mijrafah (shovel) but larger; they are called masāḥī (spades). This is the correct meaning. Al-Qāḍī reported two views: one is this, and the second is that what is meant by murūr here is ropes, which they used to climb up to the palm trees. He said: One of them is marr, with fatḥah or kasrah on the mīm, because it is twisted (yumarr) when it is braided.

His statement "and she dug the earth into small pits" (faḥaṣat al-arḍ afāḥīṣ): It is with ḍammah on the fāʾ and kasrah on the unpointed ḥāʾ, ungeminated—that is, she removed the topsoil and dug a little, so that the leather mats could be placed in the dug-out area and the clarified butter poured into it, so it would settle and not leak from its sides. The origin of faḥṣ is uncovering; one says "faḥaṣa ʿan al-amr" (he investigated the matter) and "faḥaṣa al-ṭāʾir li-bayḍihi" (the bird scratched for its eggs). Al-afāḥīṣ is the plural of ufḥūṣ.

His statement "and the she-camel al-ʿAḍbāʾ stumbled, and the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, fell, and she fell"—his statement "stumbled" (ʿatharat) is with fatḥah on the thāʾ, and "fell" (nadarat) is with nūn, meaning he fell. The origin of nudūr is emergence and isolation; from it is the expression "a rare word" (kalimah nādirah), i.e., unique among its peers.

[1428] His statement "and he began passing by his wives, greeting each one of them: 'Peace be upon you, how are you, O people of the household?' And they would say: 'We are well, O Messenger of Allah, how did you find your wife?' He would say: 'Well.'" In this passage are several benefits: Among them is that it is recommended for a person, when he enters his home, to greet his wife and family with salām—and this is something that many ignorant, self-aggrandizing people disdain. Among them is that when one greets a single person, he says "Salām ʿalaykum" or "al-Salām ʿalaykum" in the plural form; they said this is to include him and his two guardian angels. Among them is the man's asking his family about their condition, for perhaps the woman has a need and is too shy to initiate mentioning it; when he asks her, she becomes at ease in mentioning her need. Among them is that it is recommended to say to a man upon his entry: "How are you?" and the like.

His statement "when he placed his foot on the threshold of the door" (uskuffah): It is with a conjunctive hamzah, ḍammah on it, and sukūn on the sīn.

[1365] His statement "and one man began bringing surplus dates and surplus sawīq (ground barley) until they made from that a black mass (sawād) of ḥays": al-sawād, with fatḥah on the sīn, and its origin is a person (shakhṣ); from it is the ḥadīth of the Night Journey: "He saw Ādam with dark figures (aswidah) on his right and dark figures on his left," i.e., persons. What is meant here is: until they made from that a raised, towering heap, then mixed it and made it into ḥays.

His statement "until when we saw the walls of Medina, we hastened toward it" (hashnā ilayhā): Thus it is in the copies—hashnā with fatḥah on the hāʾ, tashdīd on the pointed shīn, then nūn. In some copies it is hashshnā with two shīns, the first with kasrah and ungeminated. Their meaning is: we became active, lightened, and our souls were stirred toward it. From it one says "hashishtu" with kasrah on the shīn in the past tense and fatḥah on it in the present tense. And he mentioned...

chapters.title_en: The Judge's Two Narrations on the Marriage of Zaynab bint Jaḥsh and the Establishment of the Wedding Feast
chapters.arabic_text:
القاضي الروايتين السابقتين قال والرواية الأولى على الإدغام لالتقاء

المثلين وهي لغة من قال هزت
# 
# سيفي وهي لغة بكر بن وائل قال ورواه بعضهم هشنا بكسر الهاء وإسكان الشين

وهو من هاش يهيش بمعنى هش قوله (فخرج جواري نسائه) أي صغيرات الأسنان من

نسائه قوله (يشمتن) هو بفتح الياء والميم قوله (قبل هذا إن حجبها فهي

امرأته) استدلت به المالكية ومن وافقهم على أن هيصح النكاح بغير شهود اذا

أعلن لأنه لو أشهد لم يخف عليهم وهذا مذهب جماعة من الصحابة والتابعين وهو

مذهب الزهري ومالك وأهل المدينة شرطوا الإعلان دون الشهادة وقال جماعة من

الصحابة ومن بعدهم تشترط الشهادة دون الإعلان وهو مذهب الأوزاعي والثوري

والشافعي وأبي حنيفة وأحمد وغيرهم وكل هؤلاء يشترطون شهادة عدلين إلا أبا

حنيفة فقال ينعقد بشهادة فاسقين وأجمعت الأمة على أنه لو عقد سرا بغير

شهادة لم ينعقد وأما إذا عقد سرا بشهادة عدلين فهو صحيح عند الجماهير وقال

مالك لا يصح والله أعلم

| (باب زواج زينب بنت جحش ونزول الحجاب)
# (وإثبات وليمة العرس)
# [1428] قوله (قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لزيد فاذكرها علي) أي

فاخطبها لي من نفسها فيه دليل على أنه لا بأس أن يبعث الرجل لخطبة المرأة

له من كان زوجها إذا علم أنه لا يكره ذلك كما كان حال زيد مع رسول الله صلى

الله عليه وسلم قوله (فلما رأيتها عظمت في صدري
# 
# حتى ما أستطيع أن أنظر إليها أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ذكرها

فوليتها ظهري ونكصت على عقبي) معناه أنه هابها واستجلها من أجل إرادة النبي

صلى الله عليه وسلم تزوجها فعاملها معاملة من تزوجها صلى الله عليه وسلم في

الإعظام والإجلال والمهابة وقوله (أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ذكرها)

هو بفتح الهمزة من أن أي من أجل ذلك وقوله نكصت أي رجعت وكان جاء إليها

ليخطبها وهو ينظر إليها على ما كان من عادتهم وهذا قبل نزول الحجاب  فلما

غلب عليه الإجلال تأخر وخطبها وظهره إليها لئلا يسبقه النظر إليها قولها

(ما أنا بصانعة شيئا حتى أوامر ربي فقامت إلى مسجدها) أي موضع صلاتها من

بيتها وفيه استحباب صلاة الاستخارة لمن هم بأمر سواء كان ذلك الأمر ظاهر

الخير أم لا وهو موافق لحديث جابر في صحيح البخاري قال كان رسول الله صلى

الله عليه وسلم يعلمنا الاستخارة في الأمور كلها يقول إذا هم أحدكم بالأمر

فليركع ركعتين من غير الفريضة إلى آخره ولعلها استخارت لخوفها من تقصير في

حقه صلى الله عليه وسلم قوله (ونزل القرآن وجاء رسول الله صلى الله عليه

وسلم فدخل عليها بغير إذن يعني نزل قوله تعالى فلما قضى زيد منها وطرا

زوجناكها فدخل عليها بغير إذن لأن الله تعالى زوجه إياها بهذه الآية قوله

(ولقد رأيتنا أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أطعمنا الخبز واللحم حين

امتد النهار) هو بفتح الهمزة من أن وقوله حين امتد النهار أي ارتفع هكذا هو

في النسخ حين بالنون قوله (يتتبع حجر نسائه
# 
# يسلم عليهن) إلى آخره سبق شرحه في الباب قبله قوله (أطعمهم خبزا ولحما

حتى تركوه) يعني حتى شبعوا وتركوه لشبعهم قوله (ما أولم رسول الله صلى الله

عليه وسلم على امرأة من نسائه أكثر أو أفضل مما أولم على زينب يحتمل أن سبب

ذلك الشكر لنعمة الله في أن الله تعالى زوجه إياها بالوحي لا بولي وشهود

بخلاف غيرها ومذهبنا الصحيح المشهور عند أصحابنا صحة
# 
# نكاحه صلى الله عليه وسلم بلا ولي ولا شهود لعدم الحاجة إلى ذلك في حقه

صلى الله عليه وسلم وهذا لخلاف في غير زينب وأما زينب فمنصوص عليها والله

أعلم قوله (حدثنا أبو مجلز) هو بكسر الميم وإسكان الجيم وفتح اللام وبعدها

زاي وحكي بفتح الميم والمشهور الأول واسمه
# 
# لاحق بن حميد قيل وليس في الصحيحين من أول اسمه لام ألف غيره قوله (عن

أنس قال تزوج رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فدخل بأهله فصنعت أمي  أم سليم

حيسا فجعلته في تور فقالت يا أنس اذهب بهذا إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه

وسلم فقل بعثت بهذا إليك أمي وهي تقرئك السلام وتقول إن هذا لك منا قليل يا

رسول الله) فيه أنه يستحب لأصدقاء المتزوج أن يبعثوا إليه بطعام يساعدونه

به على وليمته وقد سبق هذا في الباب قبله وسبق هناك بيان الحيس وفيه

الاعتذار إلى المبعوث إليه وقول الإنسان نحو قول أم سليم هذا لك منا قليل

وفيه استحباب بعث السلام إلى الصاحب وإن كان أفضل من الباعث لكن هذا يحسن

إذا كان بعيدا من موضعه أوله عذر في عدم الحضور بنفسه للسلام والتور بتاء

مثناة فوق مفتوحة ثم واو ساكنة إناء مثل القدح سبق بيانه في باب الوضوء

قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (اذهب فادع لي فلانا وفلانا ومن لقيت وسمى رجالا

قال فدعوت من سمى ومن لقيت قال قلت لأنس عددكم كانوا قال زهاء ثلاثمائة)

قوله زهاء بضم الزاي وفتح الهاء وبالمد ومعناه نحو ثلاثمائة وفيه أنه يجوز

في الدعوة أن يأذن
# 
# المرسل في ناس معينين وفي مبهمين كقوله من لقيت من أردت وفي هذا الحديث
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ق-ض-ي (qaḍā)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To settle, adjudicate, or pronounce a judgment; also to fulfill or accomplish.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In legal-theological usage, the authoritative pronouncement of a ruling (ḥukm) by a qualified judge (qāḍī), carrying binding force.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense of decisive judgment; here used technically for the jurist's transmitted ruling, not metaphorically.
- Sībawayh Rule: ʿAṭf al-Bayān (Appositional Clarification) — The phrase "القاضي" introduces the speaker's attribution, and the following clauses are syntactically coordinated to explain the two variant readings without altering the grammatical case.
chapters.translation:
I say: The Judge (al-Qāḍī) [ʿIyāḍ] mentioned the two preceding narrations. He said: The first narration employs assimilation (idghām) due to the meeting of two identical consonants, and this is the dialect of those who say "hazza" — as in the verse "my sword" — and it is the dialect of the tribe of Bakr ibn Wāʾil. He said: Some narrated it as "hashnā" with a kasrah on the hāʾ and a sukūn on the shīn, derived from "hāsha yahīshu" meaning "to be brisk" (hashsha). His statement «فخرج جواري نسائه» (and the young maidens of his wives came out) means the young-toothed girls among his wives. His statement «يشمتن» (they rejoice at) is with a fatḥah on the yāʾ and the mīm. His statement «قبل هذا إن حجبها فهي امرأته» (before this, if he veils her, she is his wife) — the Mālikīs and those who agree with them used this as evidence that marriage is valid without witnesses if it is publicly announced, because had he taken witnesses, it would not have been hidden from them. This is the doctrine of a group of the Companions and the Followers, and it is the doctrine of al-Zuhrī, Mālik, and the people of Madīnah, who stipulated public announcement without witnesses. Another group of the Companions and those after them said that witnesses are required without public announcement, and this is the doctrine of al-Awzāʿī, al-Thawrī, al-Shāfiʿī, Abū Ḥanīfah, Aḥmad, and others. All of these stipulate the testimony of two upright witnesses (ʿadl), except Abū Ḥanīfah, who said it is contracted with the testimony of two immoral persons (fāsiqayn). The ummah is unanimous that if a marriage is contracted secretly without witnesses, it is not valid. As for contracting it secretly with two upright witnesses, it is valid according to the majority, while Mālik said it is not valid. And God knows best.

| (Chapter: The Marriage of Zaynab bint Jaḥsh and the Revelation of the Veil)
| (And the Establishment of the Wedding Feast)
[1428] His statement (the Messenger of God ﷺ said to Zayd: "Mention her to me") — i.e., propose to her on my behalf from herself. In this is evidence that there is no harm in a man sending someone who was her former husband to propose to a woman for him, when he knows that she does not dislike that, as was the case with Zayd and the Messenger of God ﷺ. Her statement «فلما رأيتها عظمت في صدري حتى ما أستطيع أن أنظر إليها أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ذكرها فوليتها ظهري ونكصت على عقبي» (When I saw her, she became great in my breast until I could not look at her — because the Messenger of God ﷺ had mentioned her — so I turned my back to her and retreated on my heels) — its meaning is that she was awed by her and magnified her due to the Prophet's ﷺ intention to marry her, so she treated her with the treatment of one whom the Prophet ﷺ had married, in terms of magnification, veneration, and awe. Her statement «أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ذكرها» (because the Messenger of God ﷺ mentioned her) — the hamzah of "anna" is opened, meaning "because of that." Her statement «نكصت» means "I retreated," and she had come to him to propose to her while looking at her, as was their custom — and this was before the revelation of the veil. When veneration overcame her, she withdrew and proposed to her with her back to her, lest her gaze precede her to her. Her statement «ما أنا بصانعة شيئا حتى أوامر ربي فقامت إلى مسجدها» (I will not do anything until I consult my Lord, so she stood to her prayer place) — i.e., the place of her prayer in her house. In this is the recommendation of the prayer of consultation (ṣalāt al-istikhārah) for one who intends a matter, whether that matter is apparently good or not. This agrees with the ḥadīth of Jābir in Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī: "The Messenger of God ﷺ used to teach us consultation in all matters, saying: 'When one of you intends a matter, let him pray two units of prayer (rakʿatayn) other than the obligatory ones,' to the end of it." Perhaps she performed consultation out of fear of falling short in his right ﷺ. His statement «ونزل القرآن وجاء رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فدخل عليها بغير إذن» (and the Qurʾān was revealed, and the Messenger of God ﷺ came and entered upon her without permission) — meaning the revelation of His statement, the Exalted: {«فَلَمَّا قَضَىٰ زَيْدٌ مِّنْهَا وَطَرًا زَوَّجْنَاكَهَا»} (So when Zayd had fulfilled from her his need, We married her to you) — so he entered upon her without permission because God the Exalted married her to him by this verse. Her statement «ولقد رأيتنا أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أطعمنا الخبز واللحم حين امتد النهار» (And indeed we saw that the Messenger of God ﷺ fed us bread and meat when the day stretched forth) — the hamzah of "anna" is opened. His statement «حين امتد النهار» (when the day stretched forth) means "when it rose high." Thus it is in the copies with "ḥīna" (with a nūn). His statement «يتتبع حجر نسائه يسلم عليهن» (he would go around the apartments of his wives, greeting them) to its end — its explanation has preceded in the previous chapter. His statement «أطعمهم خبزا ولحما حتى تركوه» (he fed them bread and meat until they left it) — meaning until they were satiated and left it due to their fullness. His statement «ما أولم رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم على امرأة من نسائه أكثر أو أفضل مما أولم على زينب» (The Messenger of God ﷺ never held a wedding feast for any of his wives more abundant or better than what he held for Zaynab) — it is possible that the reason for this was gratitude for God's blessing in that God the Exalted married her to him by revelation, without a guardian or witnesses, unlike his other wives. Our established and well-known doctrine among our companions is the validity of his marriage ﷺ without a guardian or witnesses, due to the lack of need for that in his case ﷺ. There is no disagreement regarding other than Zaynab; as for Zaynab, it is explicitly stipulated [in the Qurʾān]. And God knows best. His statement «حدثنا أبو مجلز» (Abū Mijlaz narrated to us) — it is with a kasrah on the mīm, a sukūn on the jīm, a fatḥah on the lām, followed by a zāy. It is also reported with a fatḥah on the mīm, but the well-known is the first. His name is Lāḥiq ibn Ḥumayd. It is said that in the two Ṣaḥīḥs there is no one whose name begins with "lām-alif" other than him. His statement «عن أنس قال تزوج رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فدخل بأهله فصنعت أمي أم سليم حيسا فجعلته في تور فقالت يا أنس اذهب بهذا إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقل بعثت بهذا إليك أمي وهي تقرئك السلام وتقول إن هذا لك منا قليل يا رسول الله» (On the authority of Anas, he said: The Messenger of God ﷺ married and entered upon his wife, so my mother Umm Sulaym made ḥays and placed it in a vessel (tawr), then said: O Anas, go with this to the Messenger of God ﷺ and say: My mother sent this to you, and she conveys her greetings to you, and says: This is for you from us, little, O Messenger of God) — In this is the recommendation for the friends of the married man to send him food to assist him with his wedding feast. This has preceded in the previous chapter, and the explanation of ḥays has preceded there. In it is also the apology to the one sent to, and one's saying like Umm Sulaym's saying: "This is for you from us, little." In it is the recommendation of sending greetings to a companion, even if the sender is more virtuous than the one sent to — but this is good when he is far from his place, or has an excuse for not attending in person to give the greeting. The "tawr" is with a fatḥah on the tāʾ (with two dots above), then a sukūn on the wāw — a vessel like a cup; its explanation has preceded in the chapter on ablution. His statement ﷺ «اذهب فادع لي فلانا وفلانا ومن لقيت» (Go and call for me so-and-so and so-and-so, and whomever you meet) — and he named men. He said: So I called those he named and whomever I met. He said: I said to Anas: How many were they? He said: Approximately three hundred. His statement «زهاء» (approximately) is with a ḍammah on the zāy, a fatḥah on the hāʾ, and with prolongation (madd), meaning "about three hundred." In this is the permissibility in an invitation for the sender to authorize specific people and unspecified ones, like his saying "whomever you meet" or "whomever you wish." And in this ḥadīth...

chapters.title_en: The Manifest Miracle of Food Multiplication and the Rulings on Responding to Invitations
chapters.arabic_text:
معجزة ظاهرة لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بتكثير الطعام كما أوضحه في

الكتاب قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم يا أنس هات التور) هو بكسر التاء من هات

كسرت للأمر كما تكسر الطاء من أعط قوله (وزوجته مولية وجهها) هكذا هو في

جميع النسخ وزوجته بالتاء وهي لغة قليلة تكررت في الحديث والشعر والمشهور

حذفها قوله (ظنوا أنهم قد ثقلوا عليه) هو بضم القاف المخففة
#

| (باب الأمر بإجابة الداعي إلى دعوة)
# دعوة الطعام بفتح الدال ودعوة النسب بكسرها هذا قول جمهور العرب وعكسه

تيم الرباب بكسر الراء فقالوا الطعام بالكسر والنسب بالفتح وأما قول قطرب

في المثلث إن دعوة الطعام بالضم فغلطوه فيه
# [1429] قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (إذا دعى أحدكم إلى الوليمة فليأتها) فيه

الأمر
# 
# بحضورها ولا خلاف في أنه مأمور به ولكن هل هو  أمر إيجاب أو ندب فيه خلاف

الأصح في مذهبنا أنه فرض عين على كل من دعي لكن يسقط بأعذار سنذكرها إن شاء

الله تعالى والثاني أنه فرض كفاية والثالث مندوب هذا مذهبنا في وليمة العرس

وأما غيرها ففيها وجهان لأصحابنا أحدهما أنها كوليمة العرس والثاني أن

الإجابة إليها ندب وإن كانت في العرس واجبة ونقل القاضي اتفاق العلماء على

وجوب الإجابة في وليمة العرس قال واختلفوا فيما سواها فقال مالك والجمهور

لا تجب الإجابة إليها وقال أهل الظاهر تجب الإجابة إلى كل دعوة من عرس

وغيره وبه قال بعض السلف وأما الأعذار التي يسقط بها وجوب إجابة الدعوة أو

ندبها فمنها أن يكون في الطعام شبهة أو يخص بها الأغنياء أو يكون هناك من

يتأذى بحضوره معه أو لا تليق به مجالسته أو يدعوه لخوف شره أو لطمع في جاهه

أو ليعاونه على باطل وأن لا يكون هناك منكر من خمر أو لهو أو فرش حرير أو

صور حيوان غير مفروشة أو آنية ذهب أو فضة فكل هذه أعذار في ترك الإجابة ومن

الأعذار أن يعتذر إلى الداعي فيتركه ولو دعاه ذمي لم تجب إجابته على الأصح

ولو كانت الدعوة ثلاثة أيام فالأول تجب الإجابة فيه والثاني تستحب والثالث

تكره قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (إذا دعي أحدكم إلى وليمة عرس فليجب) قد يحتج

به من يخص وجوب الإجابة بوليمة العرس ويتعلق الآخرون بالروايات المطلقة

ولقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم في الرواية التي بعد هذه إذا دعى أحدكم أخاه

فليجب عرسا كان أو نحوه ويحملون هذا على الغالب أو نحوه من التأويل والعرس

بإسكان الراء وضمها لغتان مشهورتان وهي مؤنثة وفيها لغة بالتذكير قوله ص
# 
# (ان دعيتم إلى كراع فأجيبوا) والمراد به عند جماهير العلماء كراع الشاة

وغلطوا من حمله على كراع الغميم وهو موضع بين مكة والمدينة على مراحل من

المدينة
# [1430] قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (إذا دعي أحدكم إلى طعام فإن شاء طعم وإن

شاء ترك) وفي الرواية  الأخرى فليجب فإن كان صائما
# 
# فليصل وإن كان مفطرا فليطعم اختلفوا في معنى فليصل قال الجمهور معناه

فليدع لأهل الطعام بالمغفرة والبركة ونحو ذلك وأصل الصلاة في اللغة الدعاء

ومنه قوله تعالى وصل عليهم وقيل المراد الصلاة الشرعية بالركوع والسجود أي

يشتغل بالصلاة ليحصل له فضلها ولتبرك أهل المكان والحاضرين وأما المفطر في

الرواية الثانية أمره بالأكل وفي الأولى مخير واختلف العلماء في ذلك والأصح

في مذهبنا أنه لا يجب الأكل في وليمة العرس ولا في غيرها فمن أوجبه اعتمد

الرواية الثانية وتأول الأولى على من كان صائما ومن لم يوجبه اعتمد التصريح

بالتخيير في الرواية الأولى وحمل الأمر في الثانية على الندب وإذا قيل

بوجوب الأكل فأقله لقمة ولا تلزمه الزيادة لأنه يسمى أكلا ولهذا لو حلف لا

يأكل حنث بلقمة ولأنه قد يتخيل صاحب الطعام أن امتناعه لشبهة يعتقدها في

الطعام فإذا أكل لقمة زال ذلك التخيل هكذا صرح باللقمة جماعة من أصحابنا

وأما الصائم فلا خلاف أنه لا يجب عليه الأكل لكن إن كان صومه فرضا لم يجز

له الأكل لأن الفرض لا يجوز الخروج منه وإن كان نفلا جاز الفطر وتركه فإن

كان يشق على صاحب الطعام صومه فالأفضل الفطر وإلا فإتمام الصوم والله أعلم

قوله (قبل هذا وكان عبد الله يعني بن عمر يأتي الدعوة في العرس وغير العرس

ويأتيها وهو صائم) فيه أن الصوم
# 
# ليس بعذر في الإجابة وكذا قاله أصحابنا قالوا إذا دعي وهو صائم لزمه

الإجابة كما يلزم المفطر ويحصل المقصود بحضوره وإن لم يأكل فقد يتبرك به

أهل الطعام والحاضرون وقد يتجملون به وقد ينتفعون بدعائه أو بإشارته أو

ينصانون عمالا ينصانون عنه في غيبته والله أعلم قوله (شر الطعام طعام

الوليمة) ذكره مسلم موقوفا على أبي هريرة ومرفوعا إلى رسول الله صلى الله

عليه وسلم وقد سبق أن الحديث إذا روي موقوفا ومرفوعا حكم برفعه على المذهب

الصحيح لأنها زيادة ثقة ومعنى هذا الحديث الإخبار بما يقع من الناس بعده

صلى الله عليه وسلم من مراعاة الأغنياء في الولائم ونحوها وتخصيصهم بالدعوة

وإيثارهم بطيب الطعام ورفع مجالسهم وتقديمهم وغير ذلك مما هو الغالب في
chapters.anchors:
- Root: و-ل-م (w-l-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning is "to gather/assemble" — a walīmah (وليمة) is a meal prepared for a gathering, specifically a wedding feast.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological usage, it denotes the communal meal of celebration, carrying social and legal obligations.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) — the feast itself; metaphorical (majāz) — the act of responding to the invitation is termed "answering" (ijābah), extending the root's sense of "response" to a summons.
- Sībawayh Rule: Command Form (Ṣīghat al-Amr) — The imperative "فليأتها" (let him attend it) is parsed as a command (amr), whose legal force (whether obligation or recommendation) is determined by contextual indicators (qarā'in), not by the form alone.
chapters.translation:
I say: This is a manifest miracle of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, in the multiplication of food, as he clarified in the book. His saying, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, "O Anas, bring the tawr (تور)" — "tawr" is with a kasrah on the tā' (ت), from "hāt" (bring); the tā' is given a kasrah for the imperative, just as the tā' of "a'ti" (give) is given a kasrah. His saying, "and his wife, her face turned away (muwalliyatun wajhahā)" — thus it appears in all copies: "wa-zawjatuhu" with the tā' (تاء), which is a rare dialectal form that recurs in hadith and poetry, while the well-known form omits it. His saying, "they thought they had become burdensome to him (thaqulū)" — it is with a ḍammah on the qāf (ق), unemphasized.

#

| (Chapter: The Command to Respond to an Inviter's Call to a Meal)

The word "da'wah" (دعوة) for food is with a fatḥah on the dāl (د), while "da'wah" for lineage is with a kasrah — this is the statement of the majority of the Arabs. The opposite is held by Taym al-Ribāb, who say with a kasrah on the rā' (ر): they say "food" with a kasrah and "lineage" with a fatḥah. As for the statement of Quṭrub in "al-Muthallath" that "da'wah" for food is with a ḍammah, they have declared him mistaken in that.

# [1429] His saying, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: "When one of you is invited to a walīmah, let him attend it" — therein is a command to attend it. There is no disagreement that it is commanded, but whether it is a command of obligation (ījāb) or recommendation (nadb) — therein is disagreement. The most correct (al-aṣaḥḥ) in our school (madhhab) is that it is an individual obligation (farḍ ʿayn) upon everyone invited, though it is waived by valid excuses which we shall mention, Allah willing. The second opinion is that it is a communal obligation (farḍ kifāyah). The third is that it is recommended (mandūb). This is our school's position regarding the wedding feast (walīmat al-ʿurs). As for other feasts, there are two views among our companions: one is that they are like the wedding feast; the second is that responding to them is recommended, even if it is obligatory in the wedding. Al-Qāḍī has transmitted the consensus of the scholars on the obligation of responding to the wedding feast. He said: "They differed regarding what is other than it." Mālik and the majority said: "Responding to it is not obligatory." The Ẓāhirīs said: "Responding to every invitation, whether a wedding or otherwise, is obligatory," and some of the Salaf held this view.

As for the excuses by which the obligation or recommendation of responding to an invitation is waived, among them: that there is some ambiguity (shubhah) in the food; or that it is exclusively for the wealthy; or that there is someone present whose company would cause harm to the invitee; or that the company of the host is unbefitting to him; or that he is invited out of fear of his harm or out of greed for his status; or to assist him in falsehood; and that there be no objectionable thing (munkar) present — such as wine, frivolous entertainment, silk furnishings, images of living beings not used as cushions, or vessels of gold or silver. All of these are excuses for not responding. Among the excuses is that he excuses himself to the inviter and thus leaves him. If a dhimmī invites him, responding to him is not obligatory according to the most correct view. If the invitation spans three days, responding is obligatory on the first, recommended on the second, and disliked (makrūh) on the third.

His saying, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: "When one of you is invited to a wedding feast, let him respond" — this may be cited as evidence by those who restrict the obligation of responding to the wedding feast. Others cling to the absolute narrations, and to his saying, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, in the narration that follows this one: "When one of you invites his brother, let him respond, whether it be a wedding or otherwise." They interpret this first hadith as referring to the predominant case, or some similar interpretation. "Al-ʿurs" (العرس) — with sukūn on the rā' and with ḍammah — are two well-known dialectal forms, and it is feminine, with a dialectal form treating it as masculine.

His saying, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: "If you are invited to a kurā' (كراع), then respond" — the intended meaning, according to the majority of scholars, is the shank of a sheep (kurā' al-shāh). They declared mistaken those who interpreted it as Kurā' al-Ghamīm, which is a place between Mecca and Medina, several stages from Medina.

# [1430] His saying, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: "When one of you is invited to food, then if he wishes, let him eat, and if he wishes, let him leave it." And in the other narration: "Then let him respond; if he is fasting, let him pray (fa-līṣalli), and if he is not fasting, let him eat." They differed over the meaning of "fa-līṣalli" (let him pray). The majority said: its meaning is "let him supplicate (yad'ū) for the people of the food for forgiveness, blessing, and the like." The origin of "al-ṣalāh" (الصلاة) in the language is supplication (al-du'ā'), and from it is His saying, the Exalted: {«وَصَلِّ عَلَيْهِمْ»} ("And pray upon them") [Al-Tawbah: 103]. It was also said: the intended meaning is the legislated prayer with bowing and prostration — i.e., he occupies himself with prayer to attain its virtue and so that the people of the place and those present may be blessed. As for the non-fasting person in the second narration, he is commanded to eat, while in the first he is given the choice. The scholars differed on this. The most correct in our school is that eating is not obligatory in the wedding feast nor in any other. Whoever deems it obligatory relies on the second narration and interprets the first as referring to one who is fasting. Whoever does not deem it obligatory relies on the explicit statement of choice in the first narration and interprets the command in the second as indicating recommendation (nadb).

When it is said that eating is obligatory, the minimum is a single morsel (luqmah), and he is not obligated to exceed it, because that is called "eating." For this reason, if one swears he will not eat, he breaks his oath with a single morsel. Also, because the host might imagine that his abstention is due to some ambiguity (shubhah) he believes about the food; so when he eats a morsel, that imagination is dispelled. Thus a group of our companions explicitly stated the matter of the morsel.

As for the fasting person, there is no disagreement that eating is not obligatory upon him. However, if his fast is obligatory (farḍ), he is not permitted to eat, because one may not exit an obligatory act. If it is supererogatory (nafl), it is permissible to break it and permissible to continue it. If the host finds his fasting burdensome, then breaking the fast is preferable; otherwise, completing the fast is preferable. And Allah knows best.

His saying — before this — "And ʿAbdullah, meaning Ibn ʿUmar, used to attend invitations to weddings and non-weddings, and he would attend while fasting" — therein is that fasting is not an excuse for not responding. Our companions have likewise said: they stated that if one is invited while fasting, responding is incumbent upon him just as it is incumbent upon the non-fasting person, and the purpose is achieved by his mere presence even if he does not eat. For the people of the food and those present may seek blessing through him, may adorn themselves with his company, and may benefit from his supplication or his counsel — or they may be put to shame by his absence in a way they would not be shamed were he present. And Allah knows best.

His saying: "The worst food is the food of the walīmah" — Muslim narrated it as mawqūf (stopped at Abū Hurayrah) and also as marfū' (raised to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace). It has preceded that when a hadith is narrated both as mawqūf and marfū', the ruling is that it is raised (marfū') according to the correct school, because it is an addition by a trustworthy narrator. The meaning of this hadith is an informing of what would occur among the people after him, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, of favoring the wealthy in feasts and the like, singling them out for invitation, preferring them with the finest food, elevating their seating, giving them precedence, and other such practices that are predominant in [the affairs of people].

chapters.title_en: The Book of Wedding Feasts (Walāʾim) — Section 568: The Thrice-Divorced Woman's Lawfulness Only After Marrying Another Husband
chapters.arabic_text:
الولائم والله المستعان قوله (سمعت ثابتا الأعرج يحدث عن أبي هريرة) هو

ثابت بن عياض الأعرج الأحنف القرشي العدوي مولى عبد الرحمن بن زيد بن

الخطاب وقيل مولى عمر بن عبد الرحمن بن زيد بن الخطاب وقيل اسمه ثابت بن

الأحنف بن عياض والله أعلم
#

| (باب لاتحل المطلقة ثلاثا لمطلقها حتى تنكح زوجا غيره)
# (ويطأها ثم يفارقها وتنقضي عدتها)
# [1433] قولها (فتزوجت عبد الرحمن بن الزبير) هو بفتح الزاي وكسر الباء

بلا خلاف وهو الزبير بن باطاء ويقال باطياء وكان عبد الرحمن صحابيا والزبير

قتل يهوديا في غزوة بني قريظة وهذا الذي ذكرنا من أن عبد الرحمن بن الزبير

بن باطاء القرظي هو الذي تزوج امرأة رفاعة القرظي هو الذي ذكره أبو عمر بن

عبد البر والمحققون وقال بن منده وأبو نعيم الأصبهاني في كتابيهما في معرفة

الصحابة إنما هو عبد الرحمن بن الزبير بن زيد بن أمية بن زيد بن مالك بن

عوف بن عمرو بن عوف بن مالك بن أوس والصواب الأول قولها فبت طلاقي أي طلقني

ثلاثا قولها هدبة الثوب هو بضم الهاء وإسكان الدال وهي طرفه الذي لم ينسج

شبهوها بهدب العين وهو شعر جفنها قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (لا حتى تذوقي

عسيلته ويذوق عسيلتك) هو بضم العين وفتح السين تصغير
# 
# عسلة وهي كناية عن الجماع شبه لذته بلذة العسل وحلاوته قالوا وأنث

العسيلة لأن العسيلة نعتين التذكير والتأنيث وقيل أنثها على إرادة النطفة

وهذا ضعيف لأن الإنزال لا يشترط وفي هذا الحديث أن المطلقة ثلاثا لا تحل

لمطلقها حتى تنكح زوجا غيره ويطأها ثم يفارقها وتنقضي عدتها فأما مجرد عقده

عليها فلا يبيحها للأول وبه قال جميع العلماء من الصحابة والتابعين فمن

بعدهم وانفرد سعيد بن المسيب فقال إذا عقد الثاني عليها ثم فارقها حلت

للأول ولا يشترط وطء الثاني لقول  الله تعالى حتى تنكح زوجا غيره والنكاح

حقيقة في العقد على الصحيح وأجاب الجمهور بأن هذا الحديث مخصص لعموم الآية

ومبين للمراد بها قال العلماء ولعل سعيدا لم يبلغه هذا الحديث قال القاضي

عياض لم يقل أحد بقول سعيد في هذا إلا طائفة من الخوارج واتفق العلماء على

أن تغييب الحشفة في قبلها كاف في ذلك من غير إنزال المني وشذ الحسن البصري

فشرط إنزال المني وجعله حقيقة العسيلة قال الجمهور بدخول الذكر تحصل اللذة

والعسيلة ولو وطئها في نكاح فاسد لم تحل للأول على الصحيح لأنه ليس بزوج

قوله (إن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم تبسم) قال العلماء
# 
# إن التبسم للتعجب من جهرها وتصريحها بهذا الذي تستحي النساء منه في

العادة أو لرغبتها في زوجها الأول وكراهة الثاني والله أعلم
#

| باب ما يستحب أن يقوله عند الجماع
# [1434] قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (لو أن أحدهم إذا أراد أن يأتي أهله قال

بسم الله اللهم جنبنا الشيطان وجنب الشيطان ما رزقتنا فإنه إن يقدر بينهما

في ذلك ولد لم يضره شيطان أبدا) قال القاضي قيل المراد بأنه لا يضره أنه لا

يصرعه شيطان وقيل لا يطعن فيه الشيطان عند ولادته بخلاف غيره قال ولم يحمله

أحد على العموم في جميع الضرر والوسوسة والإغواء هذا كلام القاضي
#

| (باب جواز جماعه امرأته في قبلها من قدامها ومن 
# ورائها)
# (من غير تعرض للدبر) قول جابر (كانت اليهود تقول إذا أتى الرجل امرأته من

دبرها في قبلها كان الولد أحول فنزلت نساؤكم حرث لكم فأتوا حرثكم أنى شئتم)

وفي رواية إن شاء مجبية وإن شاء غير مجبية غير أن ذلك في صمام واحد المجبية

بميم مضمومة ثم جيم مفتوحة ثم باء موحدة مشددة مكسورة ثم ياء مثناة من تحت

أي مكبوبة على وجهها والصمام بكسر الصاد أي ثقب واحد والمراد به القبل قال

العلماء وقوله تعالى فأتوا حرثكم أنى شئتم أي موضع الزرع من المرأة وهو

قبلها الذي يزرع فيه المني لابتغاء الولد ففيه  إباحة وطئها في قبلها إن شاء

من بين يديها وإن شاء من ورائها وإن شاء مكبوبة وأما الدبر فليس هو بحرث

ولا موضع زرع ومعنى قوله أنى شئتم أي كيف شئتم واتفق العلماء الذين يعتد

بهم على تحريم وطء المرأة في دبرها حائضا كانت أو طاهرا لأحاديث كثيرة

مشهورة كحديث ملعون من أتى امرأة في دبرها قال أصحابنا لا يحل الوطء في

الدبر في شيء من الآدميين ولا غيرهم من الحيوان في حال من الأحوال والله

أعلم قوله (إن يهود كانت تقول) هكذا هو في النسخ يهود غير مصروف لأن المراد

قبيلة اليهود فامتنع صرفه للتأنيث والعلمية
#

| باب تحريم امتناعها من فراش زوجها
# [1436] قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (إذا باتت المرأة هاجرة فراش زوجها

لعنتها الملائكة حتى تصبح وفي رواية حتى ترجع هذا دليل على تحريم امتناعها

من فراشه لغير عذر شرعي وليس الحيض
# 
# بعذر في الامتناع لأن له حقا في الاستمتاع بها فوق الإزار ومعنى الحديث

أن اللعنة تستمر عليها حتى تزول المعصية بطلوع الفجر والاستغناء عنها أو

بتوبتها ورجوعها إلى الفراش قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (فبات غضبان عليها)

وفي بعض النسخ غضبانا
chapters.anchors:
- Root: و-ل-م (w-l-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning is "gathering" or "assembling" — a walīmah is a feast that gathers people together for a celebration, particularly a wedding feast.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological usage, walīmah denotes the communal meal marking a marriage contract, symbolizing public acknowledgment and social cohesion of the union.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) — the feast itself; metaphorical (majāz) — the entire wedding celebration and its attendant legal consequences.
- Sībawayh Rule: Rule of ʿAṭf al-Bayān (Appositional Clarification) — when a proper noun is followed by another noun clarifying its lineage or identity, the second is in apposition, as seen in "Thābit ibn ʿIyāḍ al-Aʿraj al-Aḥnaf al-Qurashī al-ʿAdawī."
chapters.translation:
I say: Concerning the wedding feasts (walāʾim) — and Allah is the One Whose aid is sought. His statement (I heard Thābit al-Aʿraj narrating from Abū Hurayrah): He is Thābit ibn ʿIyāḍ al-Aʿraj al-Aḥnaf al-Qurashī al-ʿAdawī, the freed slave (mawlā) of ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Zayd ibn al-Khaṭṭāb. And it is said: the freed slave of ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Zayd ibn al-Khaṭṭāb. And it is said: his name is Thābit ibn al-Aḥnaf ibn ʿIyāḍ. And Allah knows best.

#

| (Chapter: The Thrice-Divorced Woman Is Not Lawful for Her Former Husband Until She Marries Another Husband)
# (And he has intercourse with her, then separates from her, and her waiting period ('iddah) expires)
# [1433] Her statement (So I married ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Zubayr): This is with fatḥah on the zāy and kasrah on the bāʾ, without disagreement. He is al-Zubayr ibn Bāṭāʾ — and it is said: Bāṭiyāʾ. And ʿAbd al-Raḥmān was a Companion (ṣaḥābī), and al-Zubayr killed a Jew in the campaign of Banū Qurayẓah. What we have mentioned — that ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Zubayr ibn Bāṭāʾ al-Quraẓī is the one who married the wife of Rifāʿah al-Quraẓī — is what Abū ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-Barr and the verifying scholars (muḥaqqiqūn) stated. But Ibn Mandah and Abū Nuʿaym al-Aṣbahānī said in their two books on the knowledge of the Companions: He is only ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Zubayr ibn Zayd ibn Umayyah ibn Zayd ibn Mālik ibn ʿAwf ibn ʿAmr ibn ʿAwf ibn Mālik ibn Aws. And the correct view is the first. Her statement "fa-batta ṭalāqī" — meaning: he divorced me three times. Her statement "hudbat al-thawb" (the frayed edge of the garment): This is with ḍammah on the hāʾ and sukūn on the dāl — it is its edge that has not been woven. They likened it to the eyelash (hudb al-ʿayn), which is the hair of the eyelid. His statement, peace and blessings be upon him: (No, not until you taste his ʿusaylah and he tastes your ʿusaylah): This is with ḍammah on the ʿayn and fatḥah on the sīn, a diminutive of ʿasalah. It is a euphemism (kināyah) for sexual intercourse, likening its pleasure to the pleasure and sweetness of honey. They said: It was feminized (muʾannath) because ʿusaylah admits both masculine and feminine treatment; and it is said it was feminized intending the seminal fluid (nuṭfah). But this is weak, because ejaculation is not a condition. In this ḥadīth: The thrice-divorced woman is not lawful for her former husband until she marries another husband, and he has intercourse with her, then separates from her, and her waiting period expires. As for merely contracting marriage with her, that does not make her lawful for the first husband. This is the position of all scholars among the Companions, the Successors (tābiʿūn), and those after them. Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab alone dissented, saying: If the second husband contracts marriage with her then separates from her, she becomes lawful for the first, and intercourse by the second is not required — due to the saying of Allah the Exalted: {«حَتَّىٰ تَنكِحَ زَوْجًا غَيْرَهُ»} (until she marries another husband), and marriage (nikāḥ) is literally the contract according to the correct view. The majority (jumhūr) responded that this ḥadīth particularizes the general import of the verse and clarifies its intended meaning. The scholars said: Perhaps Saʿīd had not received this ḥadīth. Al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ said: No one adopted Saʿīd's view in this matter except a faction of the Khawārij. The scholars are agreed that the disappearance of the glans (ḥashafah) into her vagina is sufficient for this, without ejaculation of semen. Al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī deviated, making ejaculation of semen a condition and deeming it the reality of ʿusaylah. The majority said: With the entry of the penis, pleasure and ʿusaylah are achieved. And if he had intercourse with her in an invalid marriage (nikāḥ fāsid), she does not become lawful for the first husband according to the correct view, because he is not a husband. His statement (Indeed, the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, smiled): The scholars said: The smile was out of wonder at her frankness and explicitness regarding that which women customarily shy away from — or at her desire for her first husband and her dislike of the second. And Allah knows best.

#

| Chapter: What Is Recommended to Say at the Time of Intercourse
# [1434] His statement, peace and blessings be upon him: (If any of you, when he intends to approach his wife, says: "In the name of Allah. O Allah, distance us from Satan and distance Satan from what You have provided us" — then if a child is decreed between them from that, Satan will never harm him.) Al-Qāḍī said: It is said the meaning of "he will not harm him" is that Satan will not seize him in a fit of madness; and it is said: Satan will not poke him at his birth, unlike others. He said: And no one interpreted it as absolute regarding all harm, whisperings (waswasah), and misguidance. This is the statement of al-Qāḍī.

#

| (Chapter: The Permissibility of a Man Having Intercourse with His Wife in Her Vagina from the Front or from Behind)
# (Without Approaching the Anus) The statement of Jābir: (The Jews used to say: If a man approaches his wife from behind in her vagina, the child will be cross-eyed. Then was revealed: {«نِسَاؤُكُمْ حَرْثٌ لَّكُمْ فَأْتُوا حَرْثَكُمْ أَنَّىٰ شِئْتُمْ»} (Your wives are a tilth for you, so come to your tilth however you wish). And in one narration: Whether he wishes, she is lying on her back (mujabbāh), or whether he wishes, not mujabbāh — but that is in one opening (ṣimām). "Al-mujabbāh": with ḍammah on the mīm, then fatḥah on the jīm, then a shaddah with kasrah on the bāʾ, then a yāʾ — meaning: she is turned over on her face. "Al-ṣimām": with kasrah on the ṣād — meaning: one opening, and what is intended is the vagina. The scholars said: The saying of the Exalted {«فَأْتُوا حَرْثَكُمْ أَنَّىٰ شِئْتُمْ»} (so come to your tilth however you wish) means: the place of cultivation in the woman, which is her vagina, where the semen is sown in pursuit of offspring. In it is the permissibility of having intercourse with her in her vagina — whether he wishes from between her hands (front), or from behind her, or while she is turned over. As for the anus, it is not a tilth nor a place of cultivation. The meaning of His saying "annā shiʾtum" is: however you wish. The scholars whose opinions are counted are agreed upon the prohibition of intercourse with a woman in her anus — whether she is menstruating or pure — due to many well-known ḥadīths, such as the ḥadīth: "Cursed is the one who approaches a woman in her anus." Our companions (aṣḥābunā) said: Intercourse in the anus is not lawful with any human being, nor with any other animal, in any circumstance whatsoever. And Allah knows best. His statement (Indeed, the Jews — yahūd — used to say): Thus it appears in the manuscripts — "yahūd" is non-declinable (ghayr munṣarif) because what is intended is the tribe of the Jews, so its declension is prevented due to feminine gender and proper-noun status.

#

| Chapter: The Prohibition of a Woman Refusing Her Husband's Bed
# [1436] His statement, peace and blessings be upon him: (If a woman spends the night abandoning her husband's bed, the angels curse her until morning — and in one narration: until she returns.) This is evidence for the prohibition of her refusing his bed without a legitimate religious excuse. Menstruation is not an excuse for refusal, because he has the right to enjoy her above the waist-wrapper (izār). The meaning of the ḥadīth is that the curse continues upon her until the sin ceases — by the dawn breaking and her being free of it, or by her repentance and return to the bed. His statement, peace and blessings be upon him: (And he spent the night angry with her) — and in some manuscripts: "ghaḍbāna" (angry, accusative).

chapters.title_en: The Prohibition of a Woman Divulging Secrets, and the Ruling on Coitus Interruptus (ʿAzl)
chapters.arabic_text:
| (باب تحريم إفشاء المرأة)
# [1437] قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (إن من أشر الناس عند الله منزلة يوم

القيامة الرجل يفضي إلى امرأته وتفضي إليه ثم ينشر سرها) قال القاضي هكذا

وقعت الرواية أشر بالألف وأهل النحو يقولون لا يجوز أشر وأخير وإنما يقال

هو خير منه وشر منه قال وقد جاءت الأحاديث الصحيحة باللغتين جميعا وهي حجة

في جوازهما جميعا وأنهما لغتان وفي هذا الحديث تحريم إفشاء الرجل ما يجري

بينه وبين امرأته من أمور الاستمتاع ووصف تفاصيل ذلك وما يجري من المرأة

فيه من قول أو فعل ونحوه فأما مجرد ذكر الجماع فإن لم تكن فيه فائدة ولا

إليه حاجة فمكروه لأنه خلاف
# 
# المروءة وقد قال صلى الله عليه وسلم من كان يؤمن بالله واليوم الآخر

فليقل خيرا أو ليصمت وإن كان إليه حاجة  أو ترتب عليه فائدة بأن ينكر عليه

إعراضه عنها أو تدعي عليه العجز عن الجماع أو نحو ذلك فلا كراهة في ذكره

كما قال صلى الله عليه وسلم إني لأفعله أنا وهذه وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم

لأبي طلحة أعرستم الليلة وقال لجابر الكيس الكيس والله أعلم

| (باب حكم العزل)
# العزل هو أن يجامع فإذا قارب الإنزال نزع وأنزل خارج الفرج وهو مكروه

عندنا في كل حال وكل امرأة سواء رضيت أم لا لأنه طريق إلى قطع النسل ولهذا

جاء في الحديث الآخر تسميته الوأد الخفي لأنه قطع طريق الولادة كما يقتل

المولود بالوأد وأما التحريم فقال أصحابنا لا يحرم في مملوكته ولا في زوجته

الأمة سواء رضيتا أم لا لأن عليه ضررا في مملوكته بمصيرها أم ولد وامتناع

بيعها وعليه ضرر في زوجته الرقيقة بمصير ولده رقيقا تبعا لأمه وأما زوجته

الحرة فإن أذنت فيه لم يحرم وإلا فوجهان أصحهما لا يحرم ثم هذه الأحاديث مع

غيرها يجمع بينها بأن ما ورد في النهي محمول على كراهة التنزيه وما ورد في

الإذن في ذلك محمول على أنه ليس بحرام وليس
# 
# معناه نفي الكراهة هذا مختصر ما يتعلق بالباب من الأحكام والجمع بين

الأحاديث وللسلف خلاف كنحو ما ذكرناه من مذهبنا ومن حرمه بغير إذن الزوجة

الحرة قال عليها ضرر في العزل فيشترط لجوازه إذنها
# [1438] قوله (غزوة بلمصطلق) أي بني المصطلق وهي غزوة المريسيع قال القاضي

قال أهل الحديث هذا أولى من رواية موسى بن عقبة أنه كان في غزوة أوطاس قوله

(كرائم العرب) أي النفيسات منهم قوله (فطالت علينا العزبة ورغبنا في

الفداء) معناه احتجنا إلى الوطء وخفنا من الحبل فتصير أم ولد يمتنع علينا

بيعها وأخذ الفداء فيها فيستنبط منه منع بيع أم الولد وأن هذا كان مشهورا

عندهم قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (لا عليكم ألا تفعلوا ما كتب الله خلق نسمة

هي كائنة إلى يوم القيامة إلا ستكون) معناه ما عليكم ضرر في ترك العزل لأن

كل نفس قدر الله تعالى خلقها لابد أن يخلقها سواء عزلتم أم لا وما لم بقدر

خلقها لا يقع سواء
# 
# سواء عزلتم أم لا فلا فائدة في عزلكم فإنه إن كان الله تعالى قدر خلقها

سبقكم الماء فلا ينفع حرصكم في منع الخلق وفي هذا الحديث دلالة لمذهب

جماهير العلماء أن العرب يجري عليهم الرق كما يجري على العجم وأنهم إذا

كانوا مشركين وسبوا جاز استرقاقهم لأن بني المصطلق عرب صلبية من
# 
# خزاعة وقد استرقوهم ووطئوا سباياهم واستباحوا بيعهن وأخذ فدائهن وبهذا

قال مالك والشافعي
# 
# في قوله الصحيح الجديد وجمهور العلماء وقال أبو حنيفة والشافعي في قوله

القديم لا يجري عليهم الرق لشرفهم والله أعلم
# [1439] (قوله إن لي جارية) هي خادمنا وسانيتنا أي التي تسقي لنا شبهها

بالبعير في ذلك قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم للذي أخبره بأن له جارية يعزل عنها

(إن شئت ثم أخبره أنها حبلت) إلى آخره فيه دلالة على إلحاق النسب مع العزل

لأن الماء قد سبق وفيه أنه إذا اعترف بوطء أمته صارت فراشا له وتلحقه

أولادها إلا أن يدعي الاستبراء وهو مذهبنا ومذهب مالك قوله صلى الله عليه

وسلم (أنا عبد الله ورسوله) معناه هنا أن ما أقول لكم حق فاعتمدوه

واستيقنوه فإنه يأتي مثل فلق الصبح
#

| باب تحريم وطء الحامل المسبية
# [1441] قوله (عن يزيد بن خمير) هو بالخاء المعجمة قوله (أتى بامرأة مجح

على باب فسطاط) المجح بميم مضمومة ثم جيم مكسورة ثم حاء مهملة وهي الحامل

التي قربت ولادتها وفي الفسطاط ست لغات فسطاط وفستاط وفساط بحذف الطاء

والتاء لكن بتشديد السين وبضم الفاء وكسرها في الثلاثة وهو نحو بيت الشعر

قوله (أتى بامرأة مجح على باب فسطاط فقال لعله يريد أن يلم بها فقالوا نعم

فقال لقد هممت أن ألعنه لعنا يدخل معه قبره كيف يورثه وهو لا يحل له كيف
# 
# يستخدمه وهو لا يحل له) معنى يلم بها أي يطأها وكانت حاملا مسبية لا يحل

جماعها حتى تضع وأما قوله  صلى الله عليه وسلم كيف يورثه وهو لا يحل له كيف

يستخدمه وهو لا يحل له فمعناه أنه قد تتأخر ولادتها ستة أشهر حيث يحتمل كون

الولد من هذا السابي ويحتمل أنه كان ممن قبله فعلى تقدير كونه من السابي

يكون ولدا له ويتوارثان وعلى تقدير كونه من غير السابي لا يتوارثان هو ولا
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ف-ض-ي (f-ḍ-y)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To reach, attain, or unfold unto; the core sense is of one thing extending to and encompassing another, as in intimate union.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In sacred law, it denotes the private, lawful sexual encounter between spouses, carrying the weight of a covenantal trust (amānah).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) for physical consummation; metaphorical (majāz) for the disclosure of intimate secrets, which is the prohibited act here.
- Sībawayh Rule: Rule of ʿAṭf al-Bayān (Appositional Clarification) — the phrase "وتفضي إليه" is a syntactic parallel that completes the reciprocal action, requiring the verb to be parsed as a feminine subject returning to the woman, thus establishing mutual trust.
chapters.translation:
I say: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: {«إن من أشر الناس عند الله منزلة يوم القيامة الرجل يفضي إلى امرأته وتفضي إليه ثم ينشر سرها»} — "Verily, among the most wicked of people in rank before God on the Day of Resurrection is a man who is intimate with his wife and she with him, then he divulges her secret." Al-Qāḍī said: Thus the narration occurred with "أشر" (asharr) with an alif, and the grammarians say that "أشر" and "أخير" (akhayr) are not permissible [as elative forms]; rather, one says "he is better than him" (huwa khayrun minhu) and "he is worse than him" (huwa sharrun minhu). He said: Yet authentic hadiths have come with both forms, and this is a proof of the permissibility of both, and that they are two valid dialects. In this hadith is the prohibition of a man divulging what transpires between him and his wife concerning matters of sexual enjoyment, describing its details, and what occurs from the woman therein of speech, action, or the like. As for merely mentioning intercourse — if there is no benefit in it nor any need for it, it is disliked (makrūh), because it contravenes chivalrous virtue (murūʾah). The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: {«من كان يؤمن بالله واليوم الآخر فليقل خيرا أو ليصمت»} — "Whoever believes in God and the Last Day, let him speak good or remain silent." But if there is a need for it, or a benefit results from it — such as rebuking a man for his aversion to his wife, or a woman claiming his inability to perform intercourse, or the like — then there is no dislike in mentioning it, just as the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Verily, I do it, I and this one," and he said to Abū Ṭalḥah: "Did you consummate the marriage last night?" and he said to Jābir: "The clever one, the clever one." And God knows best.

| Chapter: The Ruling on Coitus Interruptus (ʿAzl)

ʿAzl is that a man copulates, and when he approaches ejaculation, he withdraws and emits outside the vulva. It is disliked (makrūh) in our school in every case and with every woman, whether she consents or not, because it is a means to severing progeny. For this reason, it is called in another hadith "hidden infanticide" (al-waʾd al-khafī), because it severs the path of childbirth just as a newborn is killed by burial (waʾd). As for prohibition (taḥrīm), our companions said: It is not prohibited with his slave-woman (mamlūkah) nor with his wife who is a slave (ummah), whether they consent or not, because there is harm to him in his slave-woman by her becoming an umm walad (mother of his child) and the prevention of her sale, and there is harm to him in his slave wife by his child becoming a slave in following his mother. As for his free wife — if she permits it, it is not prohibited; otherwise, there are two opinions (wajhān), the sounder of which is that it is not prohibited. Then these hadiths, along with others, are reconciled by [saying] that what is reported as a prohibition is carried upon dislikedness of tanzīh (reprehensible but not forbidden), and what is reported as permission is carried upon it not being unlawful — and its meaning is not the negation of dislikedness. This is a summary of what pertains to the chapter of rulings and the reconciliation of the hadiths. The Salaf differed in a manner akin to what we have mentioned of our school; and whoever declared it forbidden without the permission of the free wife said: There is harm to her in ʿazl, so her permission is a condition for its permissibility.

[1438] His saying, peace and blessings be upon him: "The expedition of al-Muṣṭaliq" — meaning the Banū al-Muṣṭaliq, and it is the expedition of al-Muraysīʿ. Al-Qāḍī said: The people of hadith said this is more correct than the narration of Mūsā ibn ʿUqbah that it was during the expedition of Awṭās. His saying: "The precious ones of the Arabs" (karāʾim al-ʿArab) — meaning the noble ones among them. His saying: "So bachelorhood (ʿuzbah) became prolonged for us, and we desired ransom (fidāʾ)" — its meaning is: we needed intercourse and feared pregnancy, so she would become an umm walad, preventing us from selling her and taking ransom for her. From this is derived the prohibition of selling an umm walad, and that this was well-known among them. His saying, peace and blessings be upon him: {«لا عليكم ألا تفعلوا ما كتب الله خلق نسمة هي كائنة إلى يوم القيامة إلا ستكون»} — "It does not matter to you if you do not do it, for God has written the creation of every soul that will exist until the Day of Resurrection; it will surely come to be" — its meaning is: there is no harm to you in abandoning ʿazl, because every soul that God Almighty has decreed to create must inevitably be created, whether you practice ʿazl or not; and what He has not decreed to create will not occur, whether you practice ʿazl or not. So there is no benefit in your ʿazl, for if God Almighty has decreed its creation, your water has preceded you, and your eagerness to prevent creation will not avail. In this hadith is an indication of the doctrine of the majority of scholars (jumhūr al-ʿulamāʾ) that Arabs are subject to enslavement (riqq) just as non-Arabs are, and that if they were polytheists and were taken captive, their enslavement is permissible — because the Banū al-Muṣṭaliq were pure Arabs from Khuzāʿah, yet they enslaved them, had intercourse with their captives, and deemed permissible their sale and the taking of ransom for them. This is the doctrine of Mālik and al-Shāfiʿī in his new opinion (al-qawl al-jadīd), and the majority of scholars. Abū Ḥanīfah and al-Shāfiʿī in his old opinion (al-qawl al-qadīm) said: Enslavement does not apply to them due to their nobility. And God knows best.

[1439] His saying: "I have a slave-girl" — she is our servant and our water-carrier (sāniyah), meaning she who waters us, likened to a camel in that regard. His saying, peace and blessings be upon him, to the man who informed him that he had a slave-girl from whom he practiced ʿazl: "If you wish" — then he informed him that she had become pregnant — up to the end — in it is an indication of the attribution of lineage (ilḥāq al-nasab) despite ʿazl, because the water had preceded. And in it is that if a man acknowledges intercourse with his slave-girl, she becomes a bed (firāsh) for him, and her children are attributed to him, unless he claims istibrāʾ (period of abstention to verify non-pregnancy) — and this is our school and the school of Mālik. His saying, peace and blessings be upon him: "I am the servant of God and His Messenger" — its meaning here is: what I say to you is true, so rely upon it and be certain of it, for it comes like the splitting of dawn.

| Chapter: The Prohibition of Intercourse with a Pregnant Captive Woman

[1441] His saying: "From Yazīd ibn Khumayr" — it is with an unpointed khāʾ. His saying: "A woman was brought who was mujiḥḥ at the door of a tent (fusṭāṭ)" — al-mujiḥḥ is with a ḍammah on the mīm, then a kasrah on the jīm, then an unpointed ḥāʾ; she is the pregnant woman whose delivery has drawn near. In "fusṭāṭ" there are six dialects: fusṭāṭ, fistāṭ, and fasāṭ — with the ṭāʾ and tāʾ dropped, but with a shaddah on the sīn, and with ḍammah or kasrah on the fāʾ in all three — and it is like a tent of hair. His saying: "A pregnant woman was brought to the door of a tent, and he said: 'Perhaps he intends to have intercourse with her.' They said: 'Yes.' He said: 'I nearly cursed him with a curse that would enter his grave with him. How can he make her an heir when she is not lawful to him? How can he use her as a servant when she is not lawful to him?'" The meaning of "have intercourse with her" (yalimmu bihā) is to have sexual relations with her, and she was a pregnant captive woman, not lawful for intercourse until she delivers. As for his saying, peace and blessings be upon him: "How can he make her an heir when she is not lawful to him? How can he use her as a servant when she is not lawful to him?" — its meaning is that her delivery may be delayed for six months, where it is possible the child is from this captor and possible it was from one before him. On the supposition that it is from the captor, it is his child and they inherit from each other; and on the supposition that it is from someone other than the captor, neither he nor she inherits from the other.

chapters.title_en: The Captor's Relations with His Captive, the Permissibility of Ghīlah (Intercourse with a Nursing Mother), and the Prohibition of ʿAzl (Coitus Interruptus)
chapters.arabic_text:
السابي لعدم القرابة بل له استخدامه لأنه مملوكه فتقدير الحديث أنه قد

يستلحقه ويجعله ابنا له ويورثه مع أنه لا يحل له توريثه لكونه ليس منه ولا

يحل توارثه ومزاحمته لباقي الورثة وقد يستخدمه استخدام العبيد ويجعله عبدا

يتملكه مع أنه لا يحل له ذلك لكونه منه إذا وضعته لمدة محتملة كونه من كل

واحد منهما فيجب عليه الامتناع من وطئها خوفا من هذا المحظور فهذا هو

الظاهر في معنى الحديث وقال القاضي عياض معناه الإشارة إلى أنه قد ينمى هذا

الجنين بنطفة هذا السابي فيصير مشاركا فيه فيمتنع الاستخدام قال وهو نظير

الحديث الآخر من كان يؤمن بالله واليوم الآخر فلا يسق ماءه ولد غيره هذا

كلام القاضي وهذا الذي قاله ضعيف أو باطل وكيف ينتظم التوريث مع هذا

التأويل بل الصواب ما قدمناه والله أعلم

| (باب جواز الغيلة وهي وطء المرضع وكراهة العزل)
# [1442] قوله (عن جدامة بنت وهب) ذكر مسلم اختلاف الرواة فيها هل هي

بالدال المهملة أم بالذال المعجمة
# 
# قال والصحيح أنها بالدال يعني المهملة وهكذا قال جمهور العلماء إن الصحيح

أنها بالمهملة والجيم مضمومة بلا خلاف وقوله جدامة بنت وهب وفي الرواية

الأخرى جدامة بنت وهب أخت عكاشة قال القاضي عياض قال بعضهم إنها أخت عكاشة

على قول من قال إنها جدامة بنت وهب بن محصن وقال آخرون هي أخت رجل آخر يقال

له عكاشة بن وهب ليس بعكاشة بن محصن المشهور وقال الطبري هي جدامة بنت جندل

هاجرت قال والمحدثون قالوا فيها جدامة بنت وهب هذا ما ذكره القاضي والمختار

أنها جدامة بنت وهب الأسدية أخت عكاشة بن محصن المشهور الأسدي  وتكون أخته

من أمه وفي عكاشة لغتان سبقتا في كتاب الإيمان تشديد الكاف وتخفيفها

والتشديد أفصح وأشهر قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (لقد هممت أن أنهى عن الغيلة

حتى ذكرت أن الروم وفارس يصنعون ذلك فلا يضر أولادهم) قال أهل اللغة الغيلة

هنا بكسر الغين ويقال لها الغيل بفتح الغين مع حذف الهاء والغيال بكسر

الغين كما ذكره مسلم في الرواية الأخيرة وقال جماعة من أهل اللغة الغيلة

بالفتح المرة الواحدة وأما بالكسر فهي الاسم من الغيل وقيل إن أريد بها وطء

المرضع جاز الغيلة والغيلة بالكسر والفتح واختلف العلماء في المراد بالغيلة

في هذا الحديث وهي الغيل فقال مالك في الموطأ والأصمعي وغيره من أهل اللغة

أن يجامع امرأته وهي مرضع يقال منه أغال الرجل وأغيل اذا فعل ذلك وقال بن

السكيت هو أن ترضع المرأة وهي حامل يقال منه غالت وأغيلت قال العلماء سبب

همه صلى الله عليه وسلم بالنهي عنها أنه يخاف منه ضرر الولد الرضيع قالوا

والأطباء يقولون إن ذلك اللبن داء والعرب تكرهه وتتقيه وفي الحديث جواز

الغيلة فإنه صلى الله عليه وسلم لم ينه عنها وبين سبب ترك النهي وفيه جواز
# 
# الاجتهاد لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وله قال جمهور أهل الأصول وقيل

لا يجوز لتمكنه من الوحي والصواب الأول قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (فإذا هم

يغيلون) هو بضم الياء لأنه من أغال يغيل كما سبق قوله (ثم سألوه عن العزل

فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ذاك الوأد الخفي) وهي وإذا الموؤدة سئلت

الوأد والموؤدة بالهمز والوأد دفن البنت وهي حية وكانت العرب تفعله خشية

الإملاق وربما فعلوه خوف العار والمؤدة البنت المدفونة حية ويقال وأدت

المرأة ولدها وأدا قيل سميت موؤدة لأنها تثقل بالتراب وقد سبق في باب العزل

وجه تسمية هذا وأدا وهو مشابهته الوأد في تفويت الحياة وقوله في هذا الحديث

وإذا الموؤدة سئلت معناه أن العزل يشبه الوأد المذكور في هذه الآية
# [1443] قوله (حدثني عياش بن  عباس) الأول بالشين المعجمة وأبوه بالسين
# 
# المهملة وهو عياش بن عباس القتباني بكسر القاف منسوب إلى قتبان بطن من

رعين قوله (أشفق على ولدها) هو بضم الهمزة وكسر الفاء أي أخاف قوله صلى

الله عليه وسلم (ما ضار ذلك فارس ولا الروم) هو بتخفيف الراء أي ما ضرهم

يقال ضاره يضيره ضيرا وضره يضره ضرا وضرا والله أعلم كتاب الرضاع هو بفتح

الراء وكسرها والرضاعة بفتح الراء وكسرها وقد رضع الصبي أمه بكسر الضاد

يرضعها بفتحها رضاعا قال الجوهري ويقول أهل نجد رضع يرضع بفتح الضاد في

الماضي وكسرها في المضارع رضعا كضرب يضرب ضربا وأرضعته أمه وامرأة مرضع أي

لها ولد ترضعه فإن رضعتها بإرضاعه قلت مرضعة بالهاء والله أعلم
# [1444] قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (إن
# 
# الرضاعة تحرم ما تحرمه الولادة وفي رواية يحرم من الرضاع ما يحرم من

الولادة وفي حديث قصة حفصة وحديث قصة عائشة الإذن لدخول العم من الرضاعة

عليها وفي الحديث الآخر فليلج عليك عمك قلت إنما أرضعتني المرأة ولم يرضعني

الرجل قال إنه عمك فليلج عليك هذه الأحاديث متفقة على ثبوت حرمة الرضاع

وأجمعت الأمة على ثبوتها بين الرضيع والمرضعة وأنه يصير ابنها يحرم عليه

نكاحها أبدا ويحل له النظر إليها والخلوة بها والمسافرة ولا يترتب عليه

أحكام الأمومة من كل وجه فلا يتوارثان ولا يجب على واحد منهما نفقة الآخر
chapters.anchors:
- Root: س-ب-ي (s-b-y)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Captivity, taking prisoners of war; the act of seizing and enslaving.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Legal status of the captive (sabī) as property (mamlūk), entailing ownership rights.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: physical capture; metaphorical: subjugation of will or desire.
- Root: غ-ي-ل (gh-y-l)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Ghīlah — intercourse with a nursing woman; also, treachery or surprise attack.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The act of a man cohabiting with his wife while she is breastfeeding, with potential harm to the infant.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: the physical act; metaphorical: the hidden harm (like a stealthy assault) to the child's health.
- Root: و-أ-د (w-'-d)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Wa'd — burying a female infant alive; the act of entombing the living.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The pre-Islamic practice of infanticide, condemned by revelation; metaphorically, any act that destroys potential life.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: burial of a living girl; metaphorical: ʿazl (coitus interruptus) as "hidden wa'd" because it prevents life.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clause (al-Sharṭ wa al-Jawāb) — The protasis (e.g., "if he fears harm") governs the apodosis (e.g., "he must abstain"), requiring precise modal alignment in translation.
chapters.translation:
I say: The captor, due to the absence of blood-kinship [with the captive's child], may employ her in service, for she is his property. Thus, the meaning of the hadith is that he might [in some cases] claim the child as his own, making him a son and bequeathing to him, even though it is not lawful for him to bequeath to him, because the child is not from him, nor is mutual inheritance lawful, nor his competing with the remaining heirs. And he might employ her with the service of slaves, making her a slave whom he owns, even though that is not lawful for him, because the child is from him if she gave birth within a plausible period [of conception]. Therefore, he must abstain from intercourse with her, fearing this prohibition. This is the apparent meaning of the hadith.

Al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ said: Its meaning is an indication that this fetus might be nurtured by the sperm of this captor, thus becoming a participant in it, and so he refrains from employing her. He said: This is analogous to the other hadith: "Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him not water another's seed" {«من كان يؤمن بالله واليوم الآخر فلا يسق ماءه ولد غيره»}. This is the statement of al-Qāḍī. And what he said is weak or false. How can inheritance be coherent with this interpretation? Rather, the correct view is what we have presented. And Allah knows best.

| (Chapter: The Permissibility of Ghīlah — Intercourse with a Nursing Mother — and the Dislike of ʿAzl)

# [1442] His statement (about Judāmah bint Wahb): Muslim mentioned the disagreement of the narrators concerning her name — whether it is with the unpointed dāl (د) or the pointed dhāl (ذ).

He said: The correct form is with the unpointed dāl. Likewise, the majority of scholars said the correct form is with the unpointed dāl, and the jīm is damma (u-vowel) without dispute. His statement: "Judāmah bint Wahb" — and in another narration, "Judāmah bint Wahb, sister of ʿUkāshah." Al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ said: Some said she is the sister of ʿUkāshah, according to those who say she is Judāmah bint Wahb ibn Muḥṣin. Others said she is the sister of another man called ʿUkāshah ibn Wahb, not the famous ʿUkāshah ibn Muḥṣin. Al-Ṭabarī said: She is Judāmah bint Jandal, who emigrated. He said: The hadith scholars said about her: Judāmah bint Wahb. This is what al-Qāḍī mentioned. The chosen view is that she is Judāmah bint Wahb al-Asadiyyah, sister of the famous ʿUkāshah ibn Muḥṣin al-Asadī, and she is his sister from his mother. Concerning ʿUkāshah, there are two pronunciations, already mentioned in the Book of Faith: with tashdīd (doubling) of the kāf and with its lightening; the tashdīd is more eloquent and more famous.

His statement, peace and blessings be upon him: "I was about to forbid ghīlah, until I remembered that the Romans and Persians do that, and it does not harm their children." The linguists said: Ghīlah here is with kasrah (i-vowel) of the ghayn. It is also called al-ghayl with fatḥah (a-vowel) of the ghayn, omitting the tā' marbūṭah, and al-ghiyāl with kasrah of the ghayn, as Muslim mentioned in the last narration. A group of linguists said: Al-ghīlah with fatḥah is the single instance; with kasrah, it is the noun from al-ghayl. It was said: If what is meant is intercourse with a nursing woman, then both ghīlah and ghaylah (with kasrah and fatḥah) are permissible. The scholars differed over what is meant by ghīlah in this hadith, which is al-ghayl. Mālik said in al-Muwaṭṭa', and al-Aṣmaʿī and others among the linguists: It is that a man has intercourse with his wife while she is nursing. From it is said: aghāla al-rajul and aghāla, if he does that. Ibn al-Sikkīt said: It is that a woman nurses while pregnant; from it is said: ghālat and aghālat.

The scholars said: The reason for his intention, peace and blessings be upon him, to forbid it is his fear of harm to the nursing child. They said: The physicians say that such milk is a disease, and the Arabs dislike it and guard against it. In this hadith is the permissibility of ghīlah, for he, peace and blessings be upon him, did not forbid it, and he explained the reason for abandoning the prohibition. In it is also the permissibility of ijtihād (independent reasoning) for the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him. This is the view of the majority of uṣūlīs (scholars of legal theory). It was said: It is not permissible for him, due to his access to revelation. The correct view is the first.

His statement, peace and blessings be upon him: "Then they asked him about ʿazl, and the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: 'That is the hidden wa'd (infanticide).'" This refers to His saying: "And when the buried girl is asked" {«وإذا الموؤدة سئلت»}. Al-wa'd and al-maw'ūdah are with hamzah. Al-wa'd is burying a girl alive, which the Arabs used to do out of fear of poverty, and sometimes out of fear of shame. Al-maw'ūdah is the girl buried alive. It is said: wa'ada al-mar'atu waladahā wa'dan. It was said: She is called maw'ūdah because she is weighed down with earth. The explanation of naming this (ʿazl) as wa'd has already preceded in the chapter on ʿazl — its resemblance to wa'd in the destruction of life. His statement in this hadith: "And when the buried girl is asked" {«وإذا الموؤدة سئلت»} means that ʿazl resembles the wa'd mentioned in this verse.

# [1443] His statement (narrated to me ʿAyyāsh ibn ʿAbbās): The first is with the pointed shīn (ش), and his father is with the unpointed sīn (س). He is ʿAyyāsh ibn ʿAbbās al-Qutbānī, with kasrah of the qāf, attributed to Qutbān, a sub-tribe of Ruʿayn. His statement: "She feared for her child" — it is with ḍammah of the hamzah and kasrah of the fā', meaning she was afraid. His statement, peace and blessings be upon him: "That did not harm the Persians nor the Romans" — it is with takhfīf (lightening) of the rā', meaning it did not harm them. It is said: ḍārahu yaḍīruhu ḍayran, and ḍarrahū yaḍurruhū ḍarran wa ḍurran. And Allah knows best.

The Book of Radāʿah (Fosterage): It is with fatḥah and kasrah of the rā', and al-riḍāʿah with fatḥah and kasrah of the rā'. The infant suckled his mother — with kasrah of the ḍād — yaḍraʿuhā with fatḥah — riḍāʿan. Al-Jawharī said: The people of Najd say: raḍiʿa yarḍaʿu, with fatḥah of the ḍād in the past tense and kasrah in the present, raḍʿan, like ḍaraba yaḍribu ḍarban. And arḍaʿathu ummuhū (his mother suckled him). A woman is murḍiʿ (nursing) — meaning she has a child she suckles. If she suckles him by giving him her breast, you say murḍiʿah with the tā' marbūṭah. And Allah knows best.

# [1444] His statement, peace and blessings be upon him: "Indeed, fosterage (al-riḍāʿah) makes unlawful what birth makes unlawful." In another narration: "What is unlawful through fosterage is what is unlawful through birth." In the hadith of the story of Ḥafṣah and the hadith of the story of ʿĀ'ishah, there is permission for the paternal uncle through fosterage to enter upon her. In the other hadith: "Let your uncle enter upon you." She said: "I was suckled by the woman, not the man." He said: "He is your uncle, so let him enter upon you." These hadiths agree on the establishment of the prohibition of fosterage. The ummah (community) has unanimously agreed on its establishment between the suckling infant and the nursing woman — that he becomes her son, making it forever unlawful for him to marry her, and lawful for him to look at her, be alone with her, and travel with her. However, the rulings of motherhood do not apply in every respect: they do not inherit from each other, nor is either obligated to provide maintenance for the other.

chapters.title_en: The Commentary on Sahih Muslim — Section 571: The Law of Fosterage (Ridāʿah) and Its Juridical Consequences
chapters.arabic_text:
ولا يعتق عليه بالملك ولا ترد شهادته لها ولا يعقل عنها ولا يسقط عنها

القصاص بقتله فهما كالأجنبيين في هذه الأحكام وأجمعوا أيضا على انتشار

الحرمة بين المرضعة وأولاد الرضيع وبين الرضيع وأولاد المرضعة وأنه في ذلك

كولدها من النسب لهذه الأحاديث وأما الرجل المنسوب ذلك اللبن إليه لكونه

زوج المرأة أو وطئها بملك أو شبهة فمذهبنا ومذهب العلماء كافة ثبوت حرمة

الرضاع بينه وبين الرضيع ويصير ولدا له وأولاد الرجل إخوة الرضيع وأخواته

وتكون إخوة الرجل أعمام الرضيع وأخواته عماته وتكون أولاد الرضيع أولاد

الرجل ولم يخالف في هذا إلا أهل الظاهر  وبن علية فقالوا لا تثبت حرمة

الرضاع بين الرجل والرضيع ونقله المازرى عن بن عمر وعائشة واحتجوا بقوله

تعالى وأمهاتكم اللاتي أرضعنكم وأخواتكم من الرضاعة ولم يذكر البنت والعمة

كما ذكرهما في النسب واحتج الجمهور بهذه الأحاديث الصحيحة الصريحة في عم

عائشة وعم حفصة وقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم مع إذنه فيه إنه يحرم من الرضاعة

ما يحرم من الولادة وأجابوا عما احتجوا به من الآية أنه ليس فيها نص بإباحة

البنت والعمة ونحوهما لأن ذكر الشيء لا يدل على سقوط الحكم عما سواه لو لم

يعارضه دليل آخر كيف وقد جاءت هذه الأحاديث الصحيحة والله أعلم قوله صلى

الله عليه وسلم (أراه فلانا) لعم حفصة هو بضم الهمزة أي أظنه قوله (حدثنا

علي بن هاشم بن البريد) هو بباء موحدة مفتوحة
# 
# ثم راء مكسورة ثم ياء مثناة تحت
# [1445] قوله (عن عائشة أنها أخبرته أن أفلح أخا أبي القعيس جاء يستأذن

عليها وهو عمها من الرضاعة) إلى آخره وذكر الحديث السابق في أول الباب عن

عائشة أنها قالت يا رسول الله لو كان فلانا حيا لعمها من الرضاعة دخل علي

قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم نعم إن الرضاعة تحرم ما تحرم الولادة

اختلف العلماء في عم عائشة المذكور فقال أبو الحسن القابسي هما عمان لعائشة

من الرضاعة أحدهما أخو أبيها أبي بكر من الرضاعة ارتضع هو وأبو بكر رضي

الله عنه من امرأة واحدة والثاني أخو أبيها من الرضاعة الذي هو أبو القعيس

وأبو القعيس أبوها من الرضاعة وأخوه أفلح عمها وقيل هو عم واحد وهذا غلط

فإن عمها في الحديث الأول ميت وفي الثاني حي جاء يستأذن فالصواب ما قاله

القابسي وذكر القاضي القولين ثم قال قول القابسي أشبه لأنه لو كان واحدا

لفهمت حكمه من المرة الأولى ولم تحتجب منه بعد ذلك فإن قيل فإذا كانا عمين

كيف سألت على الميت وأعلمها النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه عم
# 
# لها يدخل عليها واحتجبت عن عمها الآخر  أخي أبي القعيس حتى أعلمها النبي

صلى الله عليه وسلم بأنه عمها يلج عليها فهلا اكتفت بأحد السؤالين فالجواب

أنه يحتمل أن أحدهما كان عما من أحد الأبوين والآخر منهما أو عما أعلى

والآخر أدنى أو نحو ذلك من الاختلاف فخافت أن تكون الاباحة مختصة بصاحب

الوصف المسئول عن أولا والله أعلم قوله (عن عائشة أن أفلح أخا أبي القعيس

جاء يستأذن عليها) وفي رواية أفلح بن أبي القعيس وفي رواية استأذن علي عمي

من الرضاعة أبو الجعد فرددته قال لي هشام إنما هو أبو القعيس وفي رواية

أفلح بن قعيس قال الحفاظ الصواب الرواية الأولى وهي التي كررها مسلم في

أحاديث الباب وهي المعروفة في كتب الحديث وغيرها أن عمها من الرضاعة هو

أفلح أخو أبي القعيس وكنيته أفلح أبو الجعد والقعيس بضم القاف وفتح العين

وبالسين المهملة قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (تربت يداك أو يمينك
# 
# سبق شرحه في كتاب الغسل قوله (مالك تنوق في قريش) هو بتاء مثناة فوق

مفتوحة ثم نون مفتوحة ثم واو مفتوحة مشددة ثم قاف أي تختار وتبالغ في

الاختيار قال القاضي وضبطه بعضهم بتاءين مثناتين الثانية مضمومة أي تميل
# [1447] قوله (وحدثنا هداب) هو بفتح الهاء وتشديد الدال المهملة ويقال له

هدبة بضم الهاء وسبق بيانه مرات قوله (أريد على ابنة حمزة) هو بضم الهمزة
# 
# وكسر الراء ومعناه قيل له يتزوجها قوله (محمد بن يحيى بن مهران القطعي)

هو بضم القاف وفتح الطاء منسوب إلى قطيعة قبيلة معروفة وهو قطيعة بن عبس بن

بغيض بن ريث بن غطفان بن سعد بن قيس بن عيلان بالعين المهملة قوله (كليهما

عن قتادة) كذا وقع في بعض النسخ وفي بعضها كلاهما وهو الجاري على المشهور

والأول صحيح أيضا وقد سبق بيان وجهه في الفصول السابقة في مقدمة هذا الشرح

قوله (وفي رواية بشر سمعت جابر بن زيد) يعني في رواية بشر أن قتادة قال

سمعت جابر بن زيد وهذا مما يحتاج إلى بيانه لأن قتادة مدلس  وقد قال في

الرواية الأولى قتادة عن جابر وقد علم أن المدلس لا يحتج بعنعنته حتى يثبت

سماعه لذلك الحديث فنبه مسلم على ثبوته
# [1448] قوله (أخبرني مخرمة بن بكير عن أبيه قال سمعت عبد الله بن مسلم

يقول سمعت محمد بن مسلم يقول سمعت حميد بن عبد الرحمن يقول سمعت أم سلمة)

هذا الإسناد فيه أربعة تابعيون أولهم بكير بن عبد الله بن الأشج روى عن
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ح ر م (ḥ-r-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning is "to be forbidden" or "sacred"; denotes prohibition and inviolability.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In Kalām and fiqh, it signifies a divine injunction rendering an act unlawful (taḥrīm), establishing permanent kinship barriers.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) in legal texts; metaphorical (majāz) when applied to sacred precincts (ḥaram).
- Sībawayh Rule: Rule of ʿAṭf (Coordination) — The conjunction "wa" links parallel legal subjects (e.g., "nor is his testimony rejected for her, nor does he bear blood-wit for her"), each governed by the same negative particle, requiring uniform syntactic treatment.
chapters.translation:
I say: And he (the slave) is not emancipated by mere ownership (al-milk), nor is his testimony rejected on her account, nor does he bear blood-wit (ʿaql) for her, nor is retaliation (qiṣāṣ) dropped by his killing—so they are, in these rulings, like two strangers (ajnabiyyān). And they (the scholars) have also unanimously agreed upon the spread of prohibition (ḥurma) between the wet-nurse (murḍiʿah) and the children of the suckling infant (radīʿ), and between the infant and the children of the wet-nurse, and that he is, in that regard, like her own child by lineage (nasab), due to these hadiths. As for the man to whom that milk is attributed—because he is the husband of the woman, or he had intercourse with her by ownership (milk) or by a doubtful contract (shubha)—then our school (madhhab) and the school of all scholars (al-ʿulamāʾ kāffah) affirm the establishment of fosterage prohibition (ḥurmat al-riḍāʿ) between him and the infant, and he becomes a father to him, and the man’s children become the infant’s brothers and sisters, and the man’s brothers become the infant’s paternal uncles (aʿmām), and his sisters become his paternal aunts (ʿammāt), and the infant’s children become the man’s children. None dissented from this except the Ẓāhiriyyah (People of the Literal) and Ibn ʿUlayyah, who said: Fosterage prohibition is not established between the man and the infant. Al-Māzarī transmitted this dissent from Ibn ʿUmar and ʿĀʾishah. They argued with His saying, the Exalted: {«وَأُمَّهَاتُكُمُ اللَّاتِي أَرْضَعْنَكُمْ وَأَخَوَاتُكُمْ مِنَ الرَّضَاعَةِ»} ("And your mothers who suckled you, and your sisters from fosterage") — and He did not mention the daughter (bint) or the paternal aunt (ʿammah), as He mentioned them in lineage. The majority (al-jumhūr) argued with these authentic, explicit hadiths concerning the paternal uncle of ʿĀʾishah and the paternal uncle of Ḥafṣah, and his saying, peace and blessings be upon him, with his permission therein: "Indeed, fosterage prohibits what lineage prohibits" (innahu yaḥrumu min al-riḍāʿah mā yaḥrumu min al-wilādah). And they answered what they argued from the verse: There is no explicit text (naṣṣ) in it permitting the daughter or the paternal aunt and the like, because the mention of a thing does not indicate the dropping of the ruling (sukūṭ al-ḥukm) from what is other than it, were there no other evidence opposing it—how, when these authentic hadiths have come? And Allah knows best.

His saying, peace and blessings be upon him: "I think he is so-and-so" (arāhu fulānan) regarding the paternal uncle of Ḥafṣah—it is with ḍammah on the hamzah (arāhu), meaning "I suppose him" (aẓunnuhu). His saying: "Narrated to us ʿAlī ibn Hāshim ibn al-Barīd"—it is with an open single bāʾ (muwaḥḥadah), then a kasrah on the rāʾ, then a yāʾ with two dots below (tathniyah taḥt).

[1445] His saying: "On the authority of ʿĀʾishah that she informed him that Aflaḥ, the brother of Abū al-Quʿays, came seeking permission to enter upon her, and he was her paternal uncle from fosterage"—to the end of it. And he mentioned the previous hadith at the beginning of the chapter, on the authority of ʿĀʾishah, that she said: "O Messenger of Allah, if so-and-so were alive—referring to her paternal uncle from fosterage—he would have entered upon me." The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Yes, indeed, fosterage prohibits what lineage prohibits."

The scholars differed concerning the aforementioned paternal uncle of ʿĀʾishah. Abū al-Ḥasan al-Qābisī said: There are two paternal uncles for ʿĀʾishah from fosterage. One is the brother of her father Abū Bakr from fosterage—he and Abū Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, suckled from one woman. The second is the brother of her father from fosterage, who is Abū al-Quʿays—and Abū al-Quʿays is her father from fosterage, and his brother Aflaḥ is her paternal uncle. And it was said: He is one paternal uncle—and this is an error, for her paternal uncle in the first hadith is dead, and in the second he is alive, coming to seek permission. So the correct view is what al-Qābisī said. And al-Qāḍī mentioned the two opinions, then said: The opinion of al-Qābisī is more fitting (ashbah), because if he were one, she would have understood his ruling from the first time and would not have veiled herself from him thereafter. If it is said: Since they are two paternal uncles, how did she ask about the dead one, and the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, informed her that he is her paternal uncle who enters upon her, yet she veiled herself from her other paternal uncle, the brother of Abū al-Quʿays, until the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, informed her that he is her paternal uncle who enters upon her—so why did she not suffice with one of the two questions? The answer is: It is possible that one of them was a paternal uncle from one of the two parents, and the other from the other, or one was a higher paternal uncle (aʿlā) and the other lower (adnā), or something similar of difference, so she feared that the permission might be specific to the one possessing the description asked about first. And Allah knows best.
