- Root: ن-ق-ض (n-q-ḍ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To unravel, break apart, or reverse a binding structure; the opposite of establishing (ibrām).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Technical legal term for annulment of a prior judicial ruling (naqḍ al-ḥukm) by another mujtahid.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: physical untying; metaphorical: rescinding a legal determination.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clause (al-Sharṭ) — The protasis (law/fa) governs the apodosis, requiring careful parsing of "law rafaʿahu" to distinguish hypothetical from actual judicial acts.
chapters.translation:
I say: [The objection is raised] regarding David (peace be upon him) in the single story, and the nullification of his ruling — for a mujtahid does not nullify the ruling of another mujtahid. The answer is from several aspects, one of which is that David had not definitively settled the ruling. The second is that it may have been a legal opinion (fatwā) from David, not a binding judgment. The third is that perhaps in their sacred law, it was permissible to rescind a ruling when the litigant raised it before another judge who held a contrary view. The fourth is that Solomon did this as a stratagem to manifest the truth and reveal the veracity [of the claimant]. Thus, when the elder [woman] confessed to it, he acted upon her confession, even if it was after the ruling — just as when the one judged in favor confesses after the ruling that the right belongs to his opponent.

His saying {«فقالت الصغرى لا يرحمك الله هو ابنها»} — its meaning is: "Do not split him" — then she paused her speech and resumed, saying: "May God have mercy on you, he is her son." The scholars said: It is recommended to say in such a case with the conjunctive "and" (wāw), so one says: "No, and may God have mercy on you."

His saying (السكين والمدية) — as for "al-mudyah" (the knife), it is with ḍammah on the mīm, kasrah, and fatḥah. It is so named because it cuts through the span of the animal's life (madā ḥayāt al-ḥayawān). "Al-sikkīn" (the knife) is both masculine and feminine — two dialects. It is also said "sikkīnah" because it stills (tusakkin) the movement of the animal.

| (Chapter: The Recommendation of the Judge Reforming Between Two Litigants)

[1721] Mentioned in this chapter is the ḥadīth of the man who sold real estate, and the buyer found in it a jar of gold. They disputed over it, and a man reformed between them on the condition that one marry his daughter to the other, and that they both spend from it and give charity from it. In this is the virtue of reconciliation between disputants, and that it is recommended for the judge to reconcile between disputants just as it is recommended for others.

His saying, peace be upon him: (اشترى رجل عقارا) — "a man bought real estate" — meaning land and what is connected to it. The literal reality of "al-ʿiqār" is the root/foundation; it is so named from "al-ʿaqr" (with ḍammah on the ʿayn and fatḥah), which is the origin. From this is "ʿaqr al-dār" (the foundation of the house) with ḍammah and fatḥah.

His saying, peace be upon him: (فقال الذي شرى الأرض إنما بعتك الأرض وما فيها) — "the one who bought the land said: I only sold you the land and what is in it" — thus it is in most copies: "sharā" without an alif. In some copies: "ishtarā" with an alif. The scholars said: The first is more correct. "Sharā" here means "sold," just as in His saying, the Exalted: {«وشروه بثمن بخس»} ("and they sold him for a paltry price"). For this reason, he said: "the one who bought (sharā) the land said: I only sold you" — and God knows best.

| (Book of Found Property — al-Luqatah)

It is with fatḥah on the qāf according to the well-known dialect that the majority stated. The second dialect is "luqṭah" with its sukkūn. The third is "luqāṭah" with ḍammah on the lām. The fourth is "luqaṭ" with fatḥah on the lām and qāf.

[1722] His saying: (جاء رجل إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فسأله عن اللقطة فقال اعرف عفاصها ووكاءها ثم عرفها سنة فإن جاء صاحبها وإلا فشأنك بها) — "A man came to the Prophet, peace be upon him, and asked him about found property. He said: Know its container (ʿifāṣ) and its tie (wikāʾ), then announce it for a year. If its owner comes, [give it to him]; otherwise, it is your affair." He said: "What about a stray sheep?" He said: "It is for you, or for your brother, or for the wolf." He said: "What about a stray camel?" He said: "What is it to you? With it is its water-skin and its sandals — it drinks water and eats trees until its master finds it."

In the second narration: "Announce it for a year, then know its tie and its container, then spend from it. If its owner comes, give it to him."

Al-Azharī and others said: The name "al-ḍāllah" (stray) applies only to animals. One says: "A man, a camel, or other animals strayed (ḍalla)" — and they are "al-ḍawāll." As for goods and what is other than animals, one says "luqaṭah" for them, and one does not say "ḍāllah." Al-Azharī and others said: For strays, one also says "al-hawāmī" and "al-hawāfī" — their singular being "hāmiyah" and "hāfiyah" — and "hamat," "hafat," and "hamalat" when they go off on their own without a shepherd.

His saying, peace be upon him: (اعرف عفاصها) — "know its container" — its meaning is that you know it so as to distinguish the truthfulness of its describer from his falsehood, and so that it does not mix with his wealth and become confused. As for "al-ʿifāṣ," it is with kasrah on the ʿayn, fāʾ, and unpointed ṣād — it is the receptacle in which the money is kept, whether leather or otherwise. "Al-ʿifāṣ" is also applied to the leather covering the head of a bottle, because it is like a receptacle for it. As for what enters the mouth of the bottle — whether wood, leather, or gathered cloth and the like — it is "al-ṣimām" with kasrah on the ṣād. One says: "ʿafaṣtuhā ʿafṣan" (I fastened it) when you tighten the ʿifāṣ upon it, and "aʿfaṣtuhā iʿfāṣan" when you make a ʿifāṣ for it. As for "al-wikāʾ," it is the string with which the receptacle is tied. One says: "awkaytuhu īkāʾan" — it is "mawkā" without hamzah.

His saying, peace be upon him: (فشأنك بها) — "it is your affair" — it is with naṣb on the nūn. As for his saying, peace be upon him: (معها سقاؤها) — "with it is its water-skin" — its meaning is that it is strong enough to reach water sources and drink in a single day, filling its stomach (karish) sufficiently for days. As for "ḥidhāʾuhā" (its sandals) — it is with madd — they are its hooves (akhfāf), because it is strong enough by them for travel and crossing deserts.

In this ḥadīth is the permissibility of saying "the lord of the wealth," "the lord of the goods," and "the lord of the livestock," meaning its human owner. This is the correct view upon which the majority of scholars agree. Among them is one who disliked its addition to wealth that has a soul, unlike wealth and houses and the like. This is an error, due to his saying, peace be upon him: (فإن جاء ربها فأدها إليه) — "if its lord comes, give it to him" — and (حتى يلقاها ربها) — "until its lord finds it" — and in the ḥadīth of ʿUmar, may God be pleased with him: "and the admission of the lord of the small herd (ṣarīmah) and the flock (ghanīmah)" — and similar examples are numerous. And God knows best.

As for his saying, peace be upon him: (ثم عرفها سنة) — "then announce it for a year" — its meaning is: when you take it, announce it for a year. As for the taking itself — is it obligatory or recommended? There are schools of thought on this. The summary of what our companions mentioned is three opinions: The most correct of them in their view is that it is recommended, not obligatory. The second: it is obligatory. The third: if the found property is in a place where it is safe from loss if left, then taking it is recommended; otherwise, it is obligatory.

As for announcing it for a year, the Muslims have unanimously agreed upon its obligation when the found property is not trivial nor in the category of the trivial, and [the finder] does not intend to preserve it for its owner but rather intends to own it. It is indispensable to announce it for a year by consensus. As for when he does not intend to own it but rather intends to preserve it for its owner — is the announcement incumbent upon him? There are two faces (wajhān) among our companions: One: it is not incumbent upon him; rather, if its owner comes and proves it, he gives it to him, and preservation (al-īdām) suffices. The second — and it is the more correct — is that the announcement is incumbent upon him, lest it be lost to its owner, for he does not know where it is until he seeks it. Thus, it became obligatory.

chapters.title_en: Section 681 — The Definition of Found Property (Luqṭah) and Its Announcement (Taʿrīf)
chapters.arabic_text:
تعريفها وأما الشيء الحقير فيجب تعريفه  زمنا يظن أن فاقده لا يطلبه في

العادة أكثر من ذلك الزمان قال أصحابنا والتعريف أن ينشدها في الموضع الذي

وجدها فيه وفي الأسواق وأبواب المساجد ومواضع اجتماع الناس فيقول من ضاع

منه شيء من ضاع منه حيوان من ضاع منه دراهم ونحو ذلك ويكرر ذلك بحسب العادة

قال أصحابنا فيعرفها أولا في كل يوم ثم في الأسبوع ثم في أكثر منه والله

أعلم قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (فإن جاء صاحبها وإلا فشأنك بها) معناه إن

جاءها صاحبها فادفعها إليه وإلا فيجوز لك أن تتملكها قال أصحابنا إذا عرفها

فجاء صاحبها في أثناء مدة التعريف أو بعد انقضائها وقبل أن يتملكها الملتقط

فأثبت أنه صاحبها أخذها بزيادتها المتصلة والمنفصلة فالمتصلة كالسمن في

الحيوان وتعليم صنعة ونحو ذلك والمنفصلة كالولد واللبن والصوف واكتساب

العبد ونحو ذلك وأما إن جاء من يدعيها ولم يثبت ذلك فإن لم يصدقه الملتقط
# 
# لم يجز له دفعها إليه وإن صدقه جاز له الدفع إليه ولا يلزمه حتى يقيم

البينة هذا كله إذا جاء قبل أن يتملكها الملتقط فأما إذا عرفها سنة ولم يجد

صاحبها فله أن يديم حفظها لصاحبها وله أن يتملكها سواء كان غنيا أو فقيرا

فإن أراد تملكها فمتى يملكها فيه أوجه لأصحابنا أصحها لا يملكها حتى يتلفظ

بالتملك بأن يقول تملكتها أو اخترت تملكها والثاني لا يملكها إلا بالتصرف

فيها بالبيع ونحوه والثالث يكفيه نية التملك ولا يحتاج إلى لفظ والرابع

يملك بمجرد مضي السنة فإذا تملكها ولم يظهر لها صاحب فلا شيء عليه بل هو

كسب من أكسابه لا مطالبة عليه به في الآخرة وإن جاء صاحبها بعد تملكها

أخذها بزيادتها المتصلة دون المنفصلة فإن كانت قد تلفت بعد التملك لزم

الملتقط بدلها عندنا وعند الجمهور وقال داود لا يلزمه والله أعلم قوله

(فضالة الغنم قال لك أو لأخيك أو للذئب) معناه الإذن في أخذها بخلاف الإبل

وفرق صلى الله عليه وسلم بينهما وبين الفرق بأن الإبل مستغنية عن من يحفظها

لاستقلالها بحذائها وسقائها وورودها الماء والشجر وامتناعها من الذئاب

وغيرها من صغار السباع والغنم بخلاف ذلك فلك أن تأخذها أنت أو صاحبها أو

أخوك المسلم الذي يمر بها أو الذئب فلهذا جاز أخذها دون الإبل ثم إذا أخذها

وعرفها سنة وأكلها ثم جاء صاحبها لزمته غرامتها عندنا وعند أبي حنيفة رضي

الله عنه وقال مالك لا تلزمه غرامتها لأن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لم يذكر

له غرامة واحتج أصحابنا بقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم في الرواية الأخرى فإن

جاء صاحبها فأعطها إياه وأجابوا عن دليل مالك بأنه لم يذكر في هذه الرواية

الغرامة ولا نفاها وقد عرف وجوبها بدليل آخر قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم

(عرفها سنة ثم اعرف وكاءها وعفاصها ثم استنفق بها) هذا ربما أوهم أن معرفة

الوكاء والعفاص تتأخر على تعريفها سنة وباقي الروايات صريحة في تقديم

المعرفة على التعريف فيجاب عن هذه الرواية أن هذه معرفة أخرى ويكون مأمورا

بمعرفتين فيتعرفها أول ما يلتقطها حتى يعلم صدق واصفها إذا وصفها ولئلا

تختلط وتشتبه فإذا عرفها سنة وأراد تملكها استحب له أن يتعرفها أيضا مرة

أخرى تعرفا وافيا محققا ليعلم قدرها وصفتها فيردها إلى صاحبها إذا جاء بعد

تملكها وتلفها ومعنى استنفق بها تملكها ثم أنفقها على نفسك قوله (فغضب رسول

الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
# 
# حتى احمرت وجنتاه أو احمر وجهه ثم قال مالك ولها) الوجنة بفتح الواو

وضمها وكسرها وفيها لغة رابعة أجنة بضم الهمزة وهي اللحم المرتفع من الخدين

ويقال رجل موجن وواجن أي عظيم الوجنة وجمعها وجنات ويجيء فيها اللغات

المعروفة في جمع قصعة وحجرة وكسرة وفيه جواز الفتوى والحكم في حال الغضب

وأنه نافذ لكن يكره ذلك في حقنا ولا يكره في حق النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

لأنه لا يخاف عليه في الغضب ما يخاف علينا والله أعلم قوله صلى الله عليه

وسلم (ثم عرفها سنة فإن لم يجيء صاحبها كانت وديعة عندك) وفي الرواية

الثانية ثم عرفها سنة فإن  لم تعرف فاستنفقها ولتكن وديعة عندك فإن جاء

طالبها يوما من الدهر فأدها إليه معناه تكون أمانة عندك بعد السنة مالم

تتملكها فإن تلفت بغير تفريط فلا ضمان عليك وليس معناه منعه من تملكها بل

له تملكها على ما ذكرناه للأحاديث الباقية الصريحة وهي قوله صلى الله عليه

وسلم ثم استنفق بها فاستنفقها وقد أشار صلى الله عليه وسلم إلى هذا في

الرواية الثانية بقوله فإن لم تعرف فاستنفقها ولتكن وديعة عندك أي لا ينقطع

حق صاحبها بل متى جاءها فأدها إليه إن كانت باقية وإلا فبدلها وهذا معنى

قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم فإن جاء صاحبها يوما من الدهر فأدها إليه والمراد

أنه لا ينقطع حق صاحبها
# 
# بالكلية وقد نقل القاضي وغيره إجماع المسلمين على أنه إذا جاء صاحبها بعد

التمليك ضمنها المتملك إلا داود فأسقط الضمان والله أعلم قوله صلى الله

عليه وسلم (فإن جاء صاحبها فعرف عفاصها وعددها ووكاءها فأعطها إياه وإلا
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ع-ر-ف (ʿ-r-f)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning is knowledge and recognition; taʿrīf (announcement) derives from making something known publicly.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In legal-theological context, taʿrīf is the obligatory public declaration of a found item to establish its lawful disposition.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense is "to make known"; here it is a technical legal act, not mere cognition.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clause (al-Sharṭ wa al-Jawāb) — The phrase "if its owner comes, then..." establishes a legal consequence contingent upon a condition, with the jawāb (apodosis) carrying the ruling.
chapters.translation:
I say: As for the insignificant thing (al-shayʾ al-ḥaqīr), it must be announced for a period of time such that it is presumed that its loser would not, by custom, seek it beyond that duration. Our companions (aṣḥābunā) said: The announcement (al-taʿrīf) is that he proclaims it in the place where he found it, in the markets, at the doors of mosques, and in places of public gathering, saying: "Whoever has lost something — whoever has lost an animal — whoever has lost dirhams" and the like, repeating that according to custom. Our companions said: He announces it first every day, then weekly, then less frequently than that. And Allah knows best.

His saying, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: {«فإن جاء صاحبها وإلا فشأنك بها»} ("Then if its owner comes, and if not, then it is your affair with it") — its meaning is: if its owner comes to it, then return it to him; and if not, then it is permissible for you to take possession of it (tamalluk). Our companions said: When he has announced it, and its owner comes during the period of announcement, or after its conclusion but before the finder has taken possession of it, and he proves that he is its owner, he takes it with its connected and disconnected increases. The connected (al-muttaṣilah) is like fatness in an animal, learning a craft, and the like; the disconnected (al-munfaṣilah) is like offspring, milk, wool, the earnings of a slave, and the like. As for one who comes claiming it but does not prove that — if the finder does not believe him, it is not permissible for him to hand it to him; and if he believes him, it is permissible for him to hand it to him, but he is not obligated to do so until he produces evidence (al-bayyinah). All this applies when he comes before the finder has taken possession of it.

But if he has announced it for a year and has not found its owner, he may either continue preserving it for its owner, or he may take possession of it, whether he is rich or poor. If he wishes to take possession of it, then when does he own it? There are several opinions (awjuh) among our companions. The soundest of them (aṣaḥḥuhā) is that he does not own it until he verbally utters the taking of possession, saying: "I have taken possession of it" or "I choose to take possession of it." The second opinion is that he owns it only by disposing of it, such as selling it and the like. The third is that the intention (niyyah) of taking possession suffices him, and he does not need an utterance. The fourth is that he owns it merely by the passage of the year. When he has taken possession of it and no owner appears for it, then nothing is incumbent upon him; rather, it is gain from his gains (kasb min aksābihi), with no claim against him for it in the Hereafter. And if its owner comes after his taking possession, he takes it with its connected increases but not the disconnected ones. If it has perished after the taking of possession, the finder is liable for its replacement (badal) in our view and in the view of the majority (al-jumhūr). Dāwūd said: He is not liable. And Allah knows best.

His saying: {«فضالة الغنم قال لك أو لأخيك أو للذئب»} ("The stray sheep — he said: it is for you, or for your brother, or for the wolf") — its meaning is the permission to take it, unlike the camel. He, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, distinguished between the two, and the distinction is that the camel is self-sufficient from one who would preserve it, due to its independence with its own water and pasture, its access to water and trees, and its resistance to wolves and other small predators; whereas the sheep is not like that. So you may take it — you, or its owner, or your Muslim brother who passes by it, or the wolf. For this reason, taking it is permissible, unlike the camel. Then, when he has taken it, announced it for a year, and consumed it, and then its owner comes, he is liable for its value (gharāmah) in our view and in the view of Abū Ḥanīfah, may Allah be pleased with him. Mālik said: He is not liable for its value, because the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, did not mention liability for him. Our companions adduced as proof his saying, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, in the other narration: {«فإن جاء صاحبها فأعطها إياه»} ("Then if its owner comes, give it to him"). And they answered Mālik's evidence by saying that he did not mention liability in this narration, nor did he negate it; and its obligation is known through another proof.

His saying, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: {«عرفها سنة ثم اعرف وكاءها وعفاصها ثم استنفق بها»} ("Announce it for a year, then know its tie-string (wikāʾ) and its container (ʿifāṣ), then spend it") — this might suggest that knowing the tie-string and container is delayed until after announcing it for a year. But the remaining narrations are explicit in presenting the knowledge before the announcement. So this narration is answered by saying that this is another act of knowing, and he is commanded with two acts of knowing: he comes to know it at the very first when he picks it up, so that he may know the truthfulness of its describer when he describes it, and so that it does not become mixed and confused. Then, when he has announced it for a year and wishes to take possession of it, it is recommended (mustaḥabb) for him to know it again, a complete and verified knowing, so that he may know its measure and description, and thus return it to its owner if he comes after his taking possession and its perishing. The meaning of {«استنفق بها»} ("spend it") is: take possession of it, then spend it upon yourself.

His saying: {«فغضب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم حتى احمرت وجنتاه أو احمر وجهه ثم قال مالك ولها»} ("Then the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, became angry until his cheeks reddened, or his face reddened, then said: 'What is wrong with you and it?'") — al-wajnah (cheek) is with the opening of the wāw, its ḍammah, and its kasrah; and there is a fourth dialectal form, ujnah, with ḍammah of the hamzah. It is the raised flesh of the two cheeks. It is said: rajul mawjin and wājin, meaning one with great cheeks; its plural is wajināt, and the known dialectal forms in the plural of qaṣʿah, ḥujrah, and kasrah apply to it. In this [hadith] there is the permissibility of issuing legal rulings (fatwā) and judgments in a state of anger, and that it is effective (nāfidh); however, that is disliked (makrūh) in our case, but not disliked in the case of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, because what is feared for us in anger is not feared for him. And Allah knows best.

His saying, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: {«ثم عرفها سنة فإن لم يجيء صاحبها كانت وديعة عندك»} ("Then announce it for a year; if its owner does not come, it is a trust (wadīʿah) with you") — and in the second narration: {«ثم عرفها سنة فإن لم تعرف فاستنفقها ولتكن وديعة عندك فإن جاء طالبها يوما من الدهر فأدها إليه»} ("Then announce it for a year; if you do not know [its owner], then spend it, and let it be a trust with you; if its claimant comes any day of time, then render it to him") — its meaning is that it is an amānah (trust) with you after the year, as long as you have not taken possession of it. If it perishes without negligence (tafrīṭ), then there is no liability (ḍamān) upon you. It does not mean preventing him from taking possession of it; rather, he may take possession of it as we have stated, according to the remaining explicit hadiths, namely his saying, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: {«ثم استنفق بها فاستنفقها»} ("Then spend it — so he spent it"). And he, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, alluded to this in the second narration by his saying: {«فإن لم تعرف فاستنفقها ولتكن وديعة عندك»} ("If you do not know [its owner], then spend it, and let it be a trust with you") — that is, the right of its owner is not cut off; rather, whenever he comes to it, render it to him if it remains, and if not, then its replacement. This is the meaning of his saying, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: {«فإن جاء صاحبها يوما من الدهر فأدها إليه»} ("If its owner comes any day of time, then render it to him"). The intent is that the right of its owner is not cut off entirely. Al-Qāḍī and others have transmitted the consensus (ijmāʿ) of the Muslims that if its owner comes after the taking of possession, the one who took possession is liable for it (ḍamana-hā), except Dāwūd, who dropped the liability. And Allah knows best.

His saying, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: {«فإن جاء صاحبها فعرف عفاصها وعددها ووكاءها فأعطها إياه وإلا»} ("Then if its owner comes and knows its container, its number, and its tie-string, then give it to him; and if not...")

chapters.title_en: The Found Object (Luqatah): Its Definition, Return, and Related Rulings; Prohibition of Milking Another's Livestock; and the Obligation of Hospitality
chapters.arabic_text:
فهي لك) في هذا دلالة لمالك وغيره ممن يقول إذا جاء من وصف اللقطة بصفاتها

وجب دفعها إليه بلا بينة وأصحابنا يقولون لا يجب دفعها إليه إلا ببينة وبه

قال أبو حنيفة وأصحابه رحمهم الله تعالى ويتأولون هذا الحديث على أن المراد

أنه إذا صدقه جاز له الدفع إليه ولا يجب فالأمر بدفعها بمجرد تصديقه ليس

للوجوب والله أعلم قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم في روايات حديث زيد بن خالد

(عرفها سنة)
# [1723] وفي حديث أبي بن كعب رضي الله عنه أنه
# 
# صلى الله عليه وسلم

| (أمر بتعريفها ثلاث سنين وفي رواية سنة واحدة وفي 
# رواية أن الراوي شك قال لا أدري قال حول أو ثلاثة أحوال وفي رواية عامين

أو ثلاثة قال القاضي عياض قيل في الجمع بين الروايات قولان أحدهما أن يطرح

الشك والزيادة ويكون المراد سنة في رواية الشك وترد الزيادة لمخالفتها باقي

الأحاديث والثاني أنهما قضيتان فرواية زيد في التعريف سنة محمولة على أقل

ما يجزئ ورواية أبي بن كعب في التعريف  ثلاث سنين محمولة على الورع وزيادة

الفضيلة قال وقد أجمع العلماء على الاكتفاء بتعريف سنة ولم يشترط أحد تعريف

ثلاثة أعوام إلا ما روى)
# 
# عن عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه ولعله لم يثبت عنه
# 
# [1724] قوله (نهى عن لقطة الحاج) يعني عن التقاطها للتملك وأما التقاطها

للحفظ فقط فلا منع منه وقد أوضح هذا صلى الله عليه وسلم في قوله صلى الله

عليه وسلم في الحديث الآخر ولا تحل لقطتها إلا لمنشد وقد سبقت المسألة

مبسوطة في آخر كتاب الحج قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (من آوى ضالة فهو ضال ما

لم يعرفها) هذا دليل للمذهب المختار أنه يلزمه تعريف اللقطة مطلقا سواء

أراد تملكها أو حفظها على صاحبها وهذا هو الصحيح وقد سبق بيان الخلاف فيه

ويجوز أن يكون المراد بالضالة هنا ضالة الإبل ونحوها مما لا يجوز التقاطها

للتملك بل إنها تلتقط للحفظ على صاحبها فيكون معناه من آوى ضالة فهو ضال

مالم يعرفها أبدا ولا يتملكها والمراد بالضال المفارق للصواب وفي جميع

أحاديث الباب دليل على أن التقاط اللقطة وتملكها لا يفتقر إلى حكم حاكم ولا

إلى إذن السلطان وهذا مجمع عليه وفيها أنه لا فرق بين الغني والفقير وهذا

مذهبنا ومذهب الجمهور والله أعلم

| (باب تحريم حلب الماشية بغير إذن مالكها قوله
# [1726] صلى
# الله عليه وسلم (لا يحلبن أحد ماشية أحد إلا بإذنه أيحب أحدكم أن تؤتى

مشربته فتكسر)
# 
# خزانته فينتقل طعامه فإنما تخزن لهم ضروع مواشيهم أطعمتهم فلا يحلبن أحد

ماشية أحد إلا بإذنه) وفي روايات فينتثل بالثاء المثلثة في آخره بدل القاف

ومعنى ينتثل ينثر كله ويرمى المشربة بفتح الميم وفي الراء لغتان الضم

والفتح وهي كالغرفة يخزن فيها الطعام وغيره ومعنى الحديث أنه صلى الله عليه

وسلم شبه اللبن في الضرع بالطعام المخزون المحفوظ في الخزانة في أنه لا يحل

أخذه بغير إذنه وفي الحديث فوائد منها تحريم أخذ مال الإنسان بغير إذنه

والأكل منه والتصرف فيه وأنه لا فرق بين اللبن وغيره  وسواء المحتاج وغيره

وسواء المحتاج وغيره إلا المضطر الذي لا يجد ميتة ويجد طعاما لغيره فيأكل

الطعام للضرورة ويلزمه بدله لمالكه عندنا وعند الجمهور وقال بعض السلف وبعض

المحدثين لا يلزمه وهذا ضعيف فإن وجد ميتة وطعاما لغيره ففيه خلاف مشهور

للعلماء وفي مذهبنا الأصح عندنا أكل الميتة أما غير المضطر إذا كان له

إدلال على صاحب اللبن أو غيره من الطعام بحيث يعلم أو يظن أن نفسه تطيب

بأكله منه بغير إذنه فله الأكل بغير إذنه وقد قدمنا بيان هذا مرات وأما شرب

النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وأبي بكر وهما قاصدان المدينة في الهجرة من لبن

غنم الراعي فقد قدمنا بيان وجهه وأنه يحتمل أنهما شرباه إدلالا على صاحبه

لأنهما كانا يعرفانه أو أنه أذن للراعي أن يسقي منه من مر به أو أنه كان

عرفهم إباحة ذلك أو أنه مال حربي لا أمان له والله أعلم وفي هذا الحديث
# 
# أيضا إثبات القياس والتمثيل في المسائل وفيه أن اللبن يسمى طعاما فيحنث

به من حلف لا يتناول طعاما إلا أن يكون له نية تخرج اللبن وفيه أن بيع لبن

الشاة بشاة في ضرعها لبن باطل وبه قال الشافعي ومالك والجمهور وجوزه

الأوزاعي والله أعلم

| (باب الضيافة ونحوها
# [48] قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (من كان
# يؤمن بالله واليوم الآخر فليكرم ضيفه جائزته قالوا وما جائزته يا رسول

الله قال يومه وليلته والضيافة ثلاثة أيام فما كان وراء ذلك فهو صدقة عليه)

وقال من كان يؤمن بالله واليوم الآخر فليقل خيرا أو ليصمت وفي رواية

الضيافة ثلاثة أيام وجائزته يوم وليلة ولا يحل لرجل مسلم أن يقيم عند أخيه

حتى يؤثمه قالوا يا رسول الله وكيف يؤثمه قال يقيم عنده ولا شئ له يقر به

وفي رواية إن نزلتم بقوم فأمروا لكم بما ينبغي للضيف فاقبلوا فإن لم يفعلوا

فخذوا منهم حق الضيف الذي ينبغي لهم هذه الأحاديث متظاهرة على الأمر

بالضيافة والاهتمام بها وعظيم موقعها وقد أجمع المسلمون على  الضيافة وأنها
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ل-ق-ط (la-qa-ta)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To pick up, to gather from the ground; a found object (luqatah) is that which is picked up and preserved.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In legal-theological usage, the luqatah is a lost property taken into custody; its ruling hinges on the intent of the finder—preservation (ḥifẓ) versus appropriation (tamalluk).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense is physical picking up; metaphorical extension applies to "taking charge" of a matter. Here, the ḥadīth distinguishes between lawful custody and unlawful possession.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clause (al-Sharṭ) — The phrase "if he describes it" (idhā jā'a bi-ṣifātihā) establishes a condition whose fulfillment triggers the obligation of return, but the juristic debate concerns whether mere description suffices or whether legal evidence (bayyinah) is required.

- Root: ض-ي-ف (ḍa-ya-fa)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To host, to shelter a guest; hospitality (ḍiyāfah) as a communal and individual duty.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The guest (ḍayf) is one who is received; the term carries connotations of honor and protection, elevated to a religious obligation in the prophetic command.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: lodging and feeding; metaphorical: the "guest's due" (jā'izah) as a defined right, not mere charity.
- Sībawayh Rule: Command Form (Ṣīghat al-Amr) — "Let him honor" (fa-l-yukrim) is an imperative indicating obligation (wujūb) in the context of faith, though scholars differ on its degree (obligatory vs. recommended).
chapters.translation:
I say: In his statement «it is yours» there is an indication for Mālik and others who hold that when a claimant comes describing the found object by its characteristics, it must be handed over to him without requiring legal evidence (bayyinah). Our companions (the Shāfiʿīs) say: It is not obligatory to hand it over to him except with evidence; and Abū Ḥanīfah and his companions—may Allah have mercy on them—also held this view. They interpret this ḥadīth to mean that if the finder believes him truthful, it is permissible for him to hand it over, but it is not obligatory. Thus, the command to hand it over merely upon his affirmation is not for obligation. And Allah knows best.

His statement—peace and blessings be upon him—in the narrations of the ḥadīth of Zayd ibn Khālid: «Announce it for a year» [1723]. And in the ḥadīth of Ubayy ibn Kaʿb—may Allah be pleased with him—that the Prophet—peace and blessings be upon him—commanded announcing it for three years. In one narration: for one year. In another narration: the narrator doubted, saying: "I do not know—he said one year or three years." In yet another narration: two or three years.

Al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ said: Concerning reconciling these narrations, there are two opinions. First: that the doubt and the addition are discarded, and the intended meaning is one year in the narration containing doubt, and the addition is rejected for contradicting the rest of the ḥadīths. Second: that they are two separate cases—the narration of Zayd concerning announcing for one year is carried upon the minimum that suffices, while the narration of Ubayy ibn Kaʿb concerning announcing for three years is carried upon scrupulousness (waraʿ) and additional merit. He said: The scholars are unanimous that announcing for one year suffices, and no one has stipulated announcing for three years except what has been narrated from ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb—may Allah be pleased with him—and perhaps it is not authentically established from him.

[1724] His statement—peace and blessings be upon him: «He forbade picking up the found object of the pilgrim»—means forbidding picking it up for the purpose of appropriation (tamalluk). As for picking it up merely for preservation, there is no prohibition in that. The Prophet—peace and blessings be upon him—clarified this in his statement in the other ḥadīth: «And it is not lawful for its found object except for one who announces it.» The matter has already been discussed in detail at the end of the Book of Pilgrimage (Ḥajj).

His statement—peace and blessings be upon him: «Whoever shelters a stray animal is astray (ḍāll) as long as he does not announce it»—this is evidence for the chosen school (al-madhhab al-mukhtār) that one is obligated to announce the found object absolutely, whether he intends to appropriate it or to preserve it for its owner. This is the correct view, and the difference of opinion on it has been explained previously. It is also possible that the intended meaning of "stray animal" (ḍāllah) here is stray camels and the like, which are not permissible to pick up for appropriation; rather, they are picked up for preservation on behalf of their owner. Thus, its meaning would be: Whoever shelters a stray animal is astray as long as he does not announce it ever and does not appropriate it. The intended meaning of "astray" (ḍāll) is the one who departs from what is correct.

In all the ḥadīths of this chapter there is evidence that picking up a found object and appropriating it does not require the ruling of a judge nor the permission of the ruler (sulṭān), and this is a matter of consensus (mujmaʿ ʿalayh). In them also is that there is no difference between the rich and the poor—and this is our school and the school of the majority. And Allah knows best.

Chapter: The Prohibition of Milking Another's Livestock Without the Owner's Permission

[1726] His statement—peace and blessings be upon him: «Let no one milk another's livestock except with his permission. Would any of you like his storage room to be approached, his pantry broken into, and his food taken out? For indeed, the udders of their livestock store their food for them. So let no one milk another's livestock except with his permission.» In some narrations: "yuntathal" (with the letter thāʾ, a dotted three-lettered consonant at the end, instead of qāf). The meaning of "yuntathal" is: to scatter everything and throw it out. "Al-Mishrabah" (with fatḥa on the mīm, and in the rāʾ there are two pronunciations: ḍamm and fatḥ) is like a small upper room in which food and other things are stored.

The meaning of the ḥadīth is that the Prophet—peace and blessings be upon him—likened milk in the udder to stored, preserved food in a pantry, in that it is not lawful to take it without the owner's permission. In this ḥadīth are several benefits, including: the prohibition of taking a person's property without his permission, eating from it, and disposing of it; and that there is no difference between milk and other things; and that there is no difference between the needy and the non-needy—except for the one compelled by necessity (muḍṭarr) who finds no carrion and finds food belonging to another; he may eat the food due to necessity, and he is obligated to compensate its owner for it—according to us and the majority. Some of the Salaf and some ḥadīth scholars said: He is not obligated to compensate. This is weak. If he finds carrion and food belonging to another, there is a well-known difference of opinion among the scholars; in our school, the most correct view with us is that he eats the carrion. As for the one not compelled by necessity, if he has a familiarity (idlāl) with the owner of the milk or other food such that he knows or thinks that the owner's soul would be pleased with him eating from it without permission, then he may eat without permission. We have already explained this matter multiple times.

As for the Prophet—peace and blessings be upon him—and Abū Bakr drinking from the milk of the shepherd's sheep while they were heading to Medina during the Hijrah, we have already explained its aspect: that it is possible they drank it out of familiarity with its owner, because they knew him; or that he had permitted the shepherd to give drink from it to whoever passed by; or that he had made known to them the permissibility of that; or that it was the property of a belligerent (ḥarbī) with no covenant of safety. And Allah knows best.

In this ḥadīth also is the affirmation of analogical reasoning (qiyās) and exemplification in legal matters. In it also is that milk is called "food" (ṭaʿām), so one who swears not to consume food would break his oath by consuming milk—unless he has an intention that excludes milk. In it also is that selling a sheep for a sheep whose udder contains milk is invalid (bāṭil)—and this is the view of al-Shāfiʿī, Mālik, and the majority; al-Awzāʿī permitted it. And Allah knows best.

Chapter: Hospitality and Related Matters

[48] His statement—peace and blessings be upon him: «Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him honor his guest with his due (jāʾizah).» They said: "O Messenger of Allah, what is his due?" He said: «His day and his night; and hospitality is three days, and whatever is beyond that is charity upon him.» And he said: «Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him speak good or remain silent.» In another narration: «Hospitality is three days, and its due is a day and a night; and it is not lawful for a Muslim man to stay with his brother until he causes him to sin.» They said: "O Messenger of Allah, how does he cause him to sin?" He said: «He stays with him while he has nothing with which to entertain him.» In another narration: «If you alight with a people and they provide for you what is befitting for a guest, then accept it; but if they do not, then take from them the right of the guest that is due from them.»

These ḥadīths are mutually corroborating (mutathāḥirah) on the command of hospitality, the concern for it, and the greatness of its standing. The Muslims are unanimous on hospitality and that it is...

chapters.title_en: Section 683 — The Obligatory and Recommended Aspects of Hospitality, and the Encouragement of Mutual Assistance (Al-Muwāsāh) with Surplus Provisions
chapters.arabic_text:
من متأكدات الإسلام ثم قال الشافعي ومالك وأبو حنيفة رحمهم الله تعالى

والجمهور هي سنة ليست بوجبة وقال الليث وأحمد هي واجبة يوما وليلة قال أحمد

رضي الله عنه هي واجبة يوما وليلة على أهل البادية وأهل)
# 
# القرى دون أهل المدن وتأول الجمهور هذه الأحاديث وأشباهها على الاستحباب

ومكارم الأخلاق وتأكد حق الضيف كحديث غسل الجمعة واجب على كل محتلم أي

متأكد الاستحباب وتأولها الخطابي رضي الله عنه وغيره على المضطر والله أعلم

قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (فليكرم ضيفه جائزته يوما وليلة والضيافة ثلاثة

أيام) قال العلماء معناه الاهتمام به في اليوم والليلة وإتحافه بما يمكن من

بر وإلطاف وأما في اليوم الثاني والثالث فيطعمه ما تيسر ولا يزيد على عادته

وأما ما كان بعد الثلاثة فهو صدقة ومعروف إن شاء فعل وإن شاء ترك قالوا

وقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم ولا يحل له أن يقيم عنده حتى يؤثمه معناه لا يحل

للضيف أن يقيم عنده بعد الثلاث حتى يوقعه في الإثم لأنه قد يغتابه لطول

مقامه أو يعرض له بما يؤذيه أو يظن به مالا يجوز وقد قال الله تعالى

اجتنبوا كثيرا من الظن إن بعض الظن إثم وهذا كله محمول على ما إذا أقام بعد

الثلاث من غير استدعاء من المضيف أما إذا استدعاه وطلب زيادة إقامته أو علم

أو ظن أنه لا يكره إقامته فلا بأس بالزيادة لأن النهي إنما كان لكونه يؤثمه

وقد زال هذا المعنى والحالة هذه فلو شك في حال المضيف هل تكره الزيادة

ويلحقه بها حرج أم لا تحل الزيادة إلا بإذنه لظاهر الحديث والله أعلم وأما

قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم من كان يؤمن بالله واليوم الآخر فليقل خيرا أو

ليصمت فقد سبق شرحه مبسوطا في كتاب الإيمان وفيه التصريح بأنه ينبغي له

الإمساك عن الكلام الذي ليس فيه خير ولا شر لأنه مما لايعنيه ومن حسن إسلام

المرء تركه مالا يعنيه ولأنه قد ينجر الكلام المباح إلى حرام  وهذا موجود في

العادة وكثير والله
# 
# أعلم
# [1727] وأما قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (إن نزلتم بقوم فأمروا لكم بما

ينبغي للضيف فاقبلوا منهم فإن لم يفعلوا فخذوا منهم حق الضيف الذي ينبغي

لهم) فقد حمله الليث وأحمد على ظاهره وتأوله الجمهور على أوجه أحدها أنه

محمول على المضطرين فإن ضيافتهم واجبة فإذا لم يضيفوهم فلهم أن يأخذوا

حاجتهم من مال الممتسين والثاني أن المراد أن لكم أن تأخذوا من أعراضهم

بألسنتكم وتذكرون للناس لؤمهم وبخلهم والعيب عليهم وذمهم والثالث أن هذا

كان في أول الإسلام وكانت المواساة واجبة فلما اتسع الإسلام نسخ ذلك هكذا

حكاه القاضي وهو تأويل ضعيف أو باطل لأن هذا الذي ادعاه قائله لا يعرف

والرابع أنه محمول على من مر بأهل الذمة الذين شرط عليهم ضيافة من يمر بهم

من المسلمين وهذا أيضا ضعيف إنما صار هذا في زمن عمر رضي الله عنه قوله (عن

أبي شريح العدوي) وفي الرواية الثانية عن أبي شريح الخزاعي هو واحد يقال له

العدوي والخزاعي والكعبي وقد سبق بيانه قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (ولا شئ له

يقريه) هو بفتح أوله وكذا قوله في الرواية الأخرى فلا يقروننا بفتح أوله

يقال قريت الضيف أقريه قرى
#

| (باب استحباب المواساة بفضول المال
# [1728] قوله (بينما نحن
# مع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في سفر إذ جاء رجل على راحلته فجعل يصرف

بصره يمينا وشمالا فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم من كان معه فضل ظهر

فليعد به على من لا ظهر له ومن كان معه فضل زاد فليعد به على من لا زاد له

قال فذكر من أصناف المال ما ذكر حتى رأينا أنه لا حق لأحد منا في فضل) أما

قوله فجعل يصرف بصره فهكذا وقع في بعض النسخ وفي بعضها يصرف فقط بحذف بصره

وفي بعضها يضرب بالضاد المعجمة والباء وفي رواية أبي داود وغيره يصرف

راحلته في هذا الحديث الحث على الصدقة والجود والمواساة والإحسان إلى

الرفقة والأصحاب  والاعتناء بمصالح الأصحاب وأمر كبير القوم أصحابه بمواساة

المحتاج وأنه يكتفى في حاجة المحتاج بتعرضه للعطاء وتعريضه من غير سؤال

وهذا معنى قوله فجعل يصرف بصره أي متعرضا لشيء يدفع به حاجته وفيه مواساة

بن السبيل والصدقة عليه إذا كان محتاجا وإن كان له راحلة وعليه ثياب أو كان

موسرا في وطنه ولهذا يعطى من الزكاة في هذه الحال والله أعلم)
#

| (باب استحباب خلط الأزواد إذا قلت والمواساة فيها
# [1729] قوله (خرجنا مع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في غزوة فأصابنا جهد

حتى هممنا أن ننحر بعض ظهرنا فأمر نبي الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فجمعنا

مزاودنا فبسطنا له نطعا فاجتمع زاد القوم على النطع قال فتطاولت لأحزره كم

هو فحزرته كربضة العنز ونحن أربع عشرة مائة قال فأكلنا حتى شبعنا جميعا ثم

حشونا جربنا فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم هل من وضوء فجاء رجل بإداوة

فيها نطفة فأفرغها في قدح فتوضأنا كلنا ندغفقه دغفقة أربع عشرة مائة قال ثم

جاء بعد ثمانية فقالوا هل من طهور فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فرغ

الوضوء) أما قوله جهد فبفتح الجيم وهو المشقة وقوله مزاودنا هكذا هو في بعض
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ض-ي-ف (ḍ-y-f)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning is "to incline, to lean toward" — the guest (ḍayf) is so named because he inclines toward the host's abode; hospitality (ḍiyāfah) is the act of receiving and honoring such a one.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological usage, the right of the guest (ḥaqq al-ḍayf) is a covenantal obligation rooted in the prophetic law, graded between recommendation (nadb) and obligation (wujūb) depending on circumstance (e.g., necessity, iḍṭirār).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) sense is physical reception and feeding; metaphorical (majāz) sense extends to "taking from their reputations" (akhdh min aʿrāḍihim) — i.e., verbal redress — as cited in the third interpretation of the ḥadīth on seizing the guest's due.
- Root: و-س-ي (w-s-y) / أ-س-و (a-s-w)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Muwāsāh derives from the root meaning "to share equally, to treat as an equal" — the act of distributing one's surplus so that none retains excess while another suffers want.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In the ethical lexicon, muwāsāh is a virtue of communal solidarity (takāful), distinct from ṣadaqah in that it is directed specifically toward companions in travel (rifqah) and is recommended (mustaḥabb) rather than obligatory.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense is material sharing of provisions (zād); metaphorical sense is the "turning of the eye" (taṣrīf al-baṣar) as a non-verbal request — a rhetorical figure of speech (kināyah) for seeking aid without explicit asking.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional and Exceptive Constructions (al-sharṭ wa al-istithnāʾ) — The phrase "fa-in lam yafʿalū fa-khudhū" (if they do not, then take) is parsed as a conditional clause where the protasis (sharṭ) governs the apodosis (jawāb), with the imperative "khudhū" carrying permissive (ibāḥah) rather than obligatory force, as determined by contextual evidence (qarāʾin) from the consensus of the majority (jumhūr).
chapters.translation:
I say: Know that the scholars have differed concerning the ruling on hospitality (ḍiyāfah). Al-Shāfiʿī, Mālik, Abū Ḥanīfah — may Allah Most High have mercy on them — and the majority (al-jumhūr) held that it is a Sunnah (recommended practice), not an obligation (wujūbah). Al-Layth and Aḥmad held that it is obligatory for a day and a night. Aḥmad — may Allah be pleased with him — said: "It is obligatory for a day and a night upon the people of the desert (ahl al-bādiyah) and the people of the villages (ahl al-qurā), but not upon the people of the cities (ahl al-mudun)." The majority interpreted these ḥadīths and their like as indicating recommendation (istihbāb) and noble character (makārim al-akhlāq), and as affirming the right of the guest — just as the ḥadīth "The washing of Friday is obligatory upon every pubescent person" (i.e., {«غسل الجمعة واجب على كل محتلم»}) means "strongly recommended." Al-Khaṭṭābī — may Allah be pleased with him — and others interpreted it [the obligation] as applying to the one in dire necessity (al-muḍṭarr). And Allah knows best.

His statement — peace and blessings be upon him — "Let him honor his guest, whose due is a day and a night, and hospitality is three days" — the scholars said: Its meaning is to attend to him with care during the day and night, and to offer him generously whatever is possible of kindness (birr) and gentleness (ilṭāf). As for the second and third days, he feeds him what is readily available, without exceeding his customary practice. As for what is beyond the three days, it is charity (ṣadaqah) and beneficence (maʿrūf) — if he wishes, he does it, and if he wishes, he leaves it. They said: And his statement — peace and blessings be upon him — "It is not lawful for him to remain with him until he causes him to sin (yuʾthimahu)" means: It is not lawful for the guest to remain with him after the three days until he causes him to fall into sin — because the host may backbite him (yaghtābahu) due to the length of his stay, or treat him with something that harms him, or harbor suspicions about him that are not permissible. Allah Most High has said: {«اجتنبوا كثيرا من الظن إن بعض الظن إثم»} ("Avoid much suspicion; indeed, some suspicion is sin") — [Sūrat al-Ḥujurāt, 49:12]. All of this is carried upon the case where he remains after the three days without being invited by the host. But if the host invites him and requests an extension of his stay, or he knows or thinks it likely that the host does not dislike his remaining, then there is no harm in the extension — because the prohibition was only due to the fact that he would cause him to sin, and this meaning has ceased in such a state. If he doubts the host's disposition — whether the extension is disliked and would cause him hardship, or not — then the extension is not permissible except with his explicit permission, due to the apparent meaning of the ḥadīth. And Allah knows best.

As for his statement — peace and blessings be upon him — "Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him speak good or remain silent" — its explanation has already preceded in detail in the Book of Faith (Kitāb al-Īmān). In it is the explicit statement that one should refrain from speech that contains neither good nor evil, because it is among what does not concern him — and "from the excellence of a person's Islam is his leaving what does not concern him" — and because permissible speech (al-kalām al-mubāḥ) may drag one into the forbidden (ḥarām). This is well-attested in custom and frequent. And Allah knows best.

[1727] As for his statement — peace and blessings be upon him — "If you alight among a people, and they provide for you what is due to a guest, then accept it from them; but if they do not, then take from them the right of the guest that is due to them" — Al-Layth and Aḥmad carried it upon its apparent meaning (ẓāhir). The majority interpreted it in several ways: First, that it applies to those in dire necessity (al-muḍṭarrūn) — for their hospitality is obligatory, and if they are not hosted, they may take their need from the wealth of the refusers (al-mumtaniʿīn). Second, that the meaning is: you may take from their reputations (aʿrāḍihim) with your tongues, mentioning to the people their baseness (luʾm) and miserliness (bukhl), censuring them and blaming them. Third, that this was in the early period of Islam, when mutual assistance (al-muwāsāh) was obligatory; but when Islam expanded, that was abrogated (naskh). Thus al-Qāḍī narrated it — and it is a weak or false interpretation, because what its proponent claims is not known [to be authentic]. Fourth, that it applies to one who passes by the People of the Covenant (ahl al-dhimmah) who had stipulated upon themselves the hospitality of Muslims passing by them. This too is weak — for this only came about in the time of ʿUmar — may Allah be pleased with him.

His statement "on the authority of Abū Shurayḥ al-ʿAdawī" — and in the second narration "Abū Shurayḥ al-Khuzāʿī" — he is one and the same person, called al-ʿAdawī, al-Khuzāʿī, and al-Kaʿbī. Its clarification has already preceded.

His statement — peace and blessings be upon him — "and he has nothing with which to host him (wa lā shayʾ lahu yuqrīhi)" — the first letter is opened (fatḥah), as is his statement in the other narration "so they did not host us (fa-lā yuqrūnā)" — with the first letter opened. One says: "qaraytu al-ḍayfa, aqrīhi, qiran" (I hosted the guest).

| (Chapter: The Recommendation of Mutual Assistance (al-Muwāsāh) with Surplus Wealth)

[1728] His statement: "While we were with the Messenger of Allah — peace and blessings be upon him — on a journey, a man came upon his mount, and he began to turn his gaze right and left. The Messenger of Allah — peace and blessings be upon him — said: 'Whoever has surplus mount (faḍl ẓahr), let him offer it to him who has no mount; and whoever has surplus provision (faḍl zād), let him offer it to him who has no provision.' He mentioned such categories of wealth until we saw that none of us had any right to any surplus."

As for his statement "he began to turn his gaze (fa-jaʿala yaṣrifu baṣarahu)" — thus it occurs in some manuscripts; in others, "yaṣrifu" only, omitting "baṣarahu"; in others, "yaḍribu" with the dotted ḍād and bāʾ; and in the narration of Abū Dāwūd and others, "yaṣrifu rāḥilatahu" (he turned his mount). In this ḥadīth is the encouragement of charity (ṣadaqah), generosity (jūd), mutual assistance (muwāsāh), and kindness (iḥsān) toward companions and friends; the care for the interests of companions; and the command of the leader of a people to his companions to assist the needy — and that the need of the needy is satisfied by his mere exposure of himself to giving and his indirect indication (taʿrīḍ), without asking. This is the meaning of his statement "he began to turn his gaze" — i.e., seeking something to relieve his need. In it is also the [permissibility of] assisting the wayfarer (ibn al-sabīl) and giving him charity if he is in need, even if he has a mount and clothing, or is wealthy in his own land — and for this reason he is given from the zakāh in such a state. And Allah knows best.

| (Chapter: The Recommendation of Mixing Provisions (Khalṭ al-Azwād) When They Are Scarce, and Mutual Assistance Therein)

[1729] His statement: "We went out with the Messenger of Allah — peace and blessings be upon him — on a campaign, and hardship (juhd) befell us until we nearly slaughtered some of our mounts. Then the Prophet of Allah — peace and blessings be upon him — commanded, and we gathered our provision-bags (mazāwidanā). We spread out a leather cloth (niṭʿ) for him, and the provisions of the people gathered upon the cloth. He said: 'I stretched myself to estimate how much it was, and I estimated it as the size of a she-goat's resting place (karbiḍat al-ʿanz), while we were fourteen hundred [in number].' He said: 'We ate until we were all satiated, then we filled our bags (jirābanā).' Then the Messenger of Allah — peace and blessings be upon him — said: 'Is there any water for ablution (wuḍūʾ)?' A man came with a small waterskin (idāwah) containing a little water (nuṭfah), and he poured it into a cup (qadaḥ), and we all performed ablution, splashing it (nadghifuhu daghfaqah) — fourteen hundred of us. He said: 'Then eight [more] came afterward and said: Is there any purifier (ṭahūr)? The Messenger of Allah — peace and blessings be upon him — said: The ablution has been exhausted.'"

As for his statement "juhd" — it is with a fatḥah on the jīm, meaning hardship (mashaqqah). His statement "mazāwidanā" — thus it is in some [manuscripts]...

chapters.arabic_text:
النسخ أو أكثرها وفي بعضها أزوادنا وفي بعضها تزوادنا بفتح التاء وكسرها

وفي النطع لغات سبقت أفصحن كسر النون وفتح الطاء وقوله كربضة العنز أي

كمبركها أو كقدرها وهي رابضة قال القاضي الرواية فيه بفتح الراء وحكاه بن

دريد بكسرها قوله (حشونا جربنا) هو بضم الراء وإسكانها جمع جراب بكسر الجيم

على المشهور ويقال بفتحها قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (هل من وضوء) أي ما

يتوضأ به وهو بفتح الواو على المشهور وحكي ضمها! وسبق بيانه في كتاب

الطهارة قوله (فيها نطفة) هو بضم النون أي قليل من الماء قوله (ندغفقه

دغفقة) أي نصبه صبا شديدا وفي هذا الحديث معجزتان ظاهرتان)
# 
# لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وهما تكثير الطعام وتكثير الماء هذه

الكثرة الظاهرة قال المازري في تحقيق  المعجزة في هذا أنه كلما أكل منه جزء

أو شرب جزء خلق الله تعالى جزءا آخر يخلفه قال ومعجزات النبي صلى الله عليه

وسلم ضربان أحدهما القرآن وهو منقول تواترا والثاني مثل تكثير الطعام

والشراب ونحو ذلك ولك فيه طريقان أحدهما أن تقول تواترت على المعنى كتواتر

جود حاتم طيئ وحلم الأحنف بن قيس فإنه لا ينقل في ذلك قصة بعينها متواترة

ولكن تكاثرت أفرادها بالآحاد حتى أفاد مجموعها تواتر الكرم والحلم وكذلك

تواتر انخراق العادة للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بغير القرآن والطريق الثاني

أن تقول إذا روى الصحابي مثل هذا الأمر العجيب وأحال على حضوره فيه مع سائر

الصحابة وهم يسمعون روايته ودعواه أو بلغهم ذلك ولا ينكرون عليه كان ذلك

تصديقا له يوجب العلم بصحة ما قال والله أعلم وفي هذا الحديث استحباب

المواساة في الزاد وجمعه عند قلته وجواز أكل بعضهم مع بعض في هذه الحالة

وليس هذا من الربا في شيء وإنما هو من نحو الإباحة وكل واحد مبيح لرفقته

الأكل من طعامه وسواء تحقق الإنسان أنه أكل أكثرمن حصته أو دونها أو مثلها

فلا بأس بهذا لكن يستحب له الإيثار والتقلل لا سيما إن كان في الطعام قلة

والله أعلم

| (كتاب الجهاد والسير)

| (باب جواز الإغارة على الكفار الذين بلغتهم دعوة 
# الإسلام (من غير تقدم إعلام بالإغارة)
# [1730] قوله (حدثنا يحيى بن يحيى التميمي قال حدثنا سليم بن أخضر عن بن

عون قال كتبت إلى نافع أسأله)
# 
# عن الدعاء قبل القتال قال فكتب إلي إنما كان في أول الإسلام قد أغار رسول

الله صلى الله عليه وسلم على بني المصطلق وهم غارون وأنعامهم تسقى على

الماء فقتل مقاتلتهم وسبى سبيهم وأصاب يومئذ قال يحيى بن يحيى أحسبه قال

جويرية أو ألبتة ابنة الحارث وحدثني هذا الحديث عبد الله بن عمر وكان في

ذلك الجيش) قال وقال في الرواية الأخرى جويرية بنت الحارث ولم يشك أما قوله

أو ألبتة فمعناه أن يحيى بن يحيى قال أصاب  يومئذ بنت الحارث وأظن شيخي سليم

بن أخضر سماها في روايته جويرية أو أعلم ذلك وأجزم به وأقوله ألبتة وحاصله

أنها جويرية فيما أحفظه إما ظنا وإما علما وفي الرواية الثانية قال هي

جويرية بنت الحارث بلا شك قوله وهم غارون هو بالغين المعجمة وتشديد الراء

أي غافلون وفي هذا الحديث جواز الإغارة على الكفار الذين بلغتهم الدعوة من

غير إنذار بالإغارة وفي هذه المسألة ثلاثة مذاهب حكاها المازري والقاضي

أحدها يجب الإنذار مطلقا قال مالك وغيره وهذا ضعيف والثاني لا يجب مطلقا

وهذا أضعف منه أو باطل والثالث يجب إن لم تبلغهم الدعوة ولا يجب إن بلغتهم

لكن يستحب وهذا هو الصحيح وبه قال نافع مولى بن عمر والحسن البصري والثوري

والليث والشافعي وأبو ثور وبن المنذر والجمهور قال بن المنذر وهو قول أكثر

أهل العلم وقد تظاهرت الأحاديث الصحيحة على معناه فمنها هذا الحديث وحديث

قتل كعب بن الأشرف وحديث قتل أبي الحقيق وفي هذا الحديث جواز استرقاق العرب

لأن بني المصطلق عرب من خزاعة وهذا قول الشافعي في الجديد وهو الصحيح وبه

قال مالك وجمهور أصحابه وأبو حنيفة والأوزاعي وجمهور العلماء وقال جماعة
# 
# من العلماء لا يسترقون وهذا قول الشافعي في القديم

| (باب تأمير الإمام الأمراء على البعوث (ووصيته إياهم 
# بآداب الغزو وغيرها) قوله (كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا أمر

أميرا على جيش أو سرية أوصاه في خاصته بتقوى الله تعالى ومن معه من

المسلمين خيرا ثم قال اغزوا باسم الله في سبيل الله قاتلوا من كفر بالله

اغزوا ولا تغلوا ولا تغدروا ولا تمثلوا ولا تقتلوا وليدا) أما السرية فهي

قطعة من الجيش تخرج منه تغير وترجع إليه قال إبراهيم الحربي هي الخيل تبلغ

أربعمائة ونحوها قالوا سميت سرية لأنها تسري في الليل ويخفى ذهابها وهي

فعيلة بمعنى فاعلة يقال سرى وأسرى إذا ذهب ليلا قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم

(ولا تغدروا) بكسر الدال والوليد الصبي وفي هذه الكلمات من الحديث فوائد

مجمع  عليها وهي تحريم الغدر وتحريم الغلول وتحريم قتل الصبيان إذا لم

يقاتلوا وكراهة المثلة واستحباب وصية الإمام أمراءه وجيوشه بتقوى الله

تعالى والرفق بأتباعهم وتعريفهم ما يحتاجون في غزوهم وما يجب عليهم وما يحل

- Root: ن-س-خ (n-s-kh)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Erasure, cancellation, supersession; in legal terms, the removal of a prior ruling by a later revelation.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Technical term for divine abrogation (naskh) of a ḥukm sharʿī, denoting the temporal limitation of a ruling's validity.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense of "copying" or "transcribing" (istinsākh) vs. metaphorical sense of "removing" (izālah); here used in the latter, technical sense.
- Sībawayh Rule: Nominal sentence with predicate (al-mubtadaʾ wa al-khabar) – "النسخ أو أكثرها" (the abrogation, or most of it) functions as an elliptical topic, with the implied predicate being "occurs in such-and-such narrations."

- Root: غ-ر-ر (gh-r-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To be heedless, unaware, negligent; also "to deceive" (ghurūr).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In the context of warfare, "ghārilūn" (غارون) denotes a state of negligence and lack of preparedness, a condition of being caught off guard.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: "unaware" (ghāfil); metaphorical extension: a military target taken by surprise.
- Sībawayh Rule: Active participle (ism al-fāʿil) with emphatic shaddah – "غارون" (ghārilūn) is the plural of "ghāril," with the shaddah on the rāʾ indicating the intensive form.

- Root: س-ر-ي (s-r-y)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To travel by night; "sarīyah" (سرية) is a detachment that moves covertly under cover of darkness.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Military unit dispatched for a raid; the term carries the nuance of concealed movement and strategic surprise.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: "night journey" (sayr laylī); metaphorical: a military expedition that operates with secrecy, as if moving in the night.
- Sībawayh Rule: Pattern faʿīlah (فعيلة) with the meaning of fāʿilah (فاعلة) – "sarīyah" is a verbal noun/adjective indicating an active sense, as explained by Ibrāhīm al-Ḥarbī.
chapters.translation:
I say: The abrogation, or most of it [occurs in these narrations]. In some of them [the word appears as] "azwādanā" (أزوادنا), and in others "tazawwadnā" (تزوادنا) – with a fatḥah on the tāʾ and also with a kasrah [on it].

As for the word "al-niṭʿ" (النطع), there are several dialects [of it] which have preceded [in earlier sections]; the most eloquent of them is with a kasrah on the nūn and a fatḥah on the ṭāʾ. His saying "ka-rabḍat al-ʿanz" (كربضة العنز) – i.e., like its resting place (mabrakuhā) or like its measure (qadruhā) while it is lying down (rābiḍah). Al-Qāḍī said: the narration [of this word] is with a fatḥah on the rāʾ, and Ibn Durayd reported it with a kasrah [on the rāʾ].

His saying "ḥashawnā jirbanā" (حشونا جربنا) – it is with a ḍammah on the rāʾ and also with a sukūn [on it], being the plural of "jirāb" (جراب) with a kasrah on the jīm according to the well-known [pronunciation], and it is also said with a fatḥah [on the jīm].

His saying, peace and blessings be upon him, "hal min wuḍūʾ" (هل من وضوء) – i.e., "is there anything with which one may perform ablution?" It is with a fatḥah on the wāw according to the well-known [pronunciation], and a ḍammah [on the wāw] has been reported. Its explanation has already preceded in the Book of Purification (Kitāb al-Ṭahārah).

His saying "fīhā nuṭfah" (فيها نطفة) – it is with a ḍammah on the nūn, i.e., a small amount of water.

His saying "nadghifuhu daghfah" (ندغفقه دغفقة) – i.e., we pour it out with a violent pouring (naṣubbuhu ṣabban shadīdan).

In this ḥadīth there are two manifest miracles (muʿjizatān ẓāhiratān) of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him: the multiplication of food and the multiplication of water – this evident abundance. Al-Māzarī said, in verifying the miracle in this: that whenever a portion of it was eaten or a portion drunk, Allah, the Exalted, created another portion to replace it.

He said: The miracles of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, are of two types: one of them is the Qurʾān, which is transmitted by mass transmission (tawātur); and the second is like the multiplication of food and drink and similar matters. Regarding this [second type], there are two ways [of establishing its authenticity] for you: One of them is that you say it has reached the level of tawātur in its collective meaning (tawāturat ʿalā al-maʿnā), like the well-known generosity of Ḥātim al-Ṭāʾī and the forbearance of al-Aḥnaf ibn Qays – for no single specific story of these is transmitted by tawātur, but their individual reports (āḥād) multiplied until their totality conveyed the tawātur of [their] generosity and forbearance. Likewise, the tawātur of the breach of customary [natural] laws (inkhirāq al-ʿādah) for the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, other than the Qurʾān [is established]. The second way is that you say: When a Companion narrates such an astonishing matter and refers to his own presence at it along with the rest of the Companions, and they hear his narration and his claim – or it reaches them – and they do not reject it against him, then that constitutes a confirmation (taṣdīq) of him that necessitates certain knowledge (ʿilm) of the correctness of what he said. And Allah knows best.

In this ḥadīth [there is established] the recommendation (istihbāb) of mutual sharing (muwāsāh) in provisions, and gathering them together when they are scarce, and the permissibility of some of them eating with others in this situation. This is not from usury (ribā) in any way; rather, it is of the nature of permissibility (ibāḥah). Each person permits his companions to eat from his food. It is equal whether a man ascertains that he ate more than his share, or less than it, or equal to it – there is no harm in this. However, it is recommended for him to prefer others (īthār) and to reduce [his own consumption], especially if there is scarcity in the food. And Allah knows best.

---

(Book of Jihad and Military Expeditions – Kitāb al-Jihād wa al-Siyar)

(Chapter: The Permissibility of Raiding the Disbelievers Who Have Been Reached by the Call of Islam – without Prior Notification of the Raid)

[1730] His saying: "Yahyā ibn Yaḥyā al-Tamīmī narrated to us, he said: Sulaym ibn Akhḍar narrated to us, from Ibn ʿAwn, who said: I wrote to Nāfiʿ asking him about supplication before fighting." He said: He wrote back to me: "This was only in the early period of Islam. The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, raided the Banū al-Muṣṭaliq while they were heedless (ghārilūn), and their cattle were being watered at the water source. He killed their fighters and took their women and children as captives (sabā). He obtained on that day – Yaḥyā ibn Yaḥyā said: I think he said – Juwayriyyah, or definitely (al-battah), the daughter of al-Ḥārith. And ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar narrated this ḥadīth to me, and he was in that army." He said: And in the other narration he said: "Juwayriyyah bint al-Ḥārith" without doubt.

As for his saying "or definitely" (aw al-battah), its meaning is that Yaḥyā ibn Yaḥyā said: "He obtained on that day the daughter of al-Ḥārith, and I think my shaykh Sulaym ibn Akhḍar named her in his narration as Juwayriyyah – or I know that and am certain of it and say it definitively (al-battah)." The upshot of it is that she was Juwayriyyah, according to what I remember – either by conjecture (ẓann) or by knowledge (ʿilm). In the second narration, he said: "She is Juwayriyyah bint al-Ḥārith" without doubt.

His saying "while they were heedless" (wa-hum ghārilūn) – it is with the dotted ghayn (al-ghayn al-muʿjamah) and a shaddah on the rāʾ, i.e., unaware (ghāfilūn).

In this ḥadīth [there is established] the permissibility of raiding the disbelievers who have been reached by the call [of Islam] without prior warning of the raid. On this question there are three schools of thought (madhāhib), which al-Māzarī and al-Qāḍī have related: One of them: warning is obligatory absolutely (yajibu al-indhār muṭlaqan) – this is [the view of] Mālik and others, and it is weak. The second: it is not obligatory absolutely – and this is weaker than it, or false. The third: it is obligatory if the call has not reached them, and it is not obligatory if it has reached them, but it is recommended (yustaḥabb). This is the correct view (al-ṣaḥīḥ), and it is the view of Nāfiʿ, the freed slave of Ibn ʿUmar, al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī, al-Thawrī, al-Layth, al-Shāfiʿī, Abū Thawr, Ibn al-Mundhir, and the majority (al-jumhūr). Ibn al-Mundhir said: It is the view of most of the people of knowledge. The authentic ḥadīths have concurred (taẓāharat) upon its meaning, among them this ḥadīth, the ḥadīth of the killing of Kaʿb ibn al-Ashraf, and the ḥadīth of the killing of Abū al-Ḥuqayq.

In this ḥadīth [there is established] the permissibility of enslaving (istirqāq) the Arabs, because the Banū al-Muṣṭaliq are Arabs from Khuzāʿah. This is the view of al-Shāfiʿī in his new [school] (al-jadīd), and it is the correct one. It is also the view of Mālik and the majority of his companions, Abū Ḥanīfah, al-Awzāʿī, and the majority of the scholars. A group of scholars said: They are not to be enslaved – and this is the view of al-Shāfiʿī in his old [school] (al-qadīm).

---

(Chapter: The Imam's Appointment of Commanders over Expeditions – and His Admonition to Them Regarding the Etiquettes of Warfare and Other Matters)

His saying: "When the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, appointed a commander over an army (jaysh) or a raiding party (sarīyah), he would admonish him privately (fī khāṣṣatihi) to fear Allah, the Exalted, and [to treat] the Muslims with him well. Then he would say: 'Fight in the name of Allah, in the path of Allah. Fight those who disbelieve in Allah. Fight, and do not be treacherous (lā taghlū), do not act treacherously (lā taghdurū), do not mutilate (lā tumaththilū), and do not kill a child (walīd).'"

As for the "sarīyah" (سرية), it is a detachment from the army that goes out from it to raid and returns to it. Ibrāhīm al-Ḥarbī said: It is the cavalry that reaches four hundred [in number] or thereabouts. They said: It is called "sarīyah" because it travels by night (tasrī fī al-layl) and its departure is concealed. It is on the pattern of "faʿīlah" (فعيلة) with the meaning of "fāʿilah" (فاعلة). One says "sarā" and "asrā" when one travels by night.

His saying, peace and blessings be upon him, "and do not act treacherously" (wa-lā taghdurū) – with a kasrah on the dāl. And "al-walīd" (الوليد) is the young boy (al-ṣabī).

In these words of the ḥadīth there are benefits upon which there is consensus (mujmaʿ ʿalayhā): the prohibition of treachery (taḥrīm al-ghadr), the prohibition of embezzlement from the spoils (taḥrīm al-ghulūl), the prohibition of killing boys when they do not fight, the disapproval (karāhah) of mutilation (al-muthlah), and the recommendation (istihbāb) of the Imam's admonition to his commanders and armies to fear Allah, the Exalted, and to be gentle with their followers, and to inform them of what they need in their warfare, what is obligatory upon them, and what is lawful [for them].

chapters.title_en: The Command to Call the Enemy to Three Qualities, the Ruling on Jizyah, and the Etiquette of Siege
chapters.arabic_text:
لهم وما يحرم عليهم وما يكره وما يستحب قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (وإذا لقيت

عدوك من المشركين فادعهم إلى ثلاث خصال أو خلال)
# 
# فأيتهن ما أجابوك فاقبل منهم وكف عنهم ثم ادعهم إلى الإسلام فإن أجابوك

فاقبل منهم وكف عنهم ثم ادعهم إلى التحول من دارهم) قوله ثم ادعهم إلى

الإسلام هكذا هو في جميع نسخ صحيح مسلم ثم ادعهم قال القاضي عياض رضي الله

تعالى عنه صواب الرواية ادعهم بإسقاط ثم وقد جاء بإسقاطها على الصواب في

كتاب أبي عبيد وفي سنن أبي داود وغيرهما لأنه تفسير للخصال الثلاث وليست

غيرها وقال المازري ليست ثم هنا زائدة بل دخلت لاستفتاح الكلام والأخذ قوله

صلى الله عليه وسلم (ثم ادعهم إلى التحول من دارهم إلى دار المهاجرين

وأخبرهم أنهم إن فعلوا ذلك فلهم ماللمهاجرين وعليهم ما على المهاجرين فإن

أبوا أن يتحولوا منها فأخبرهم أنهم يكونون كأعراب المسلمين يجري عليهم حكم

الله الذي يجري على المؤمنين ولا يكون لهم في الغنيمة والفيء شيء إلا أن

يجاهدوا مع المسلمين معنى هذا الحديث أنهم إذا أسلموا استحب لهم أن يهاجروا

إلى المدينة فإن فعلوا ذلك كانوا كالمهاجرين قبلهم في استحقاق الفيء

والغنيمة وغير ذلك والأفهم أعراب كسائر أعراب المسلمين الساكنين في البادية

من غير هجرة ولا غزو فتجري عليهم أحكام الإسلام ولا حق لهم في الغنيمة

والفئ وإنما يكون لهم نصيب من الزكاة إن كانوا بصفة استحقاقها قال الشافعي

الصدقات للمساكين ونحوهم ممن لا حق له في الفئ والفئ للأجناد قال ولا يعطى

أهل الفيء من الصدقات ولا أهل الصدقات من الفيء واحتج بهذا الحديث وقال

مالك وأبو حنيفة المالان سواء ويجوز صرف كل واحد منهما إلى النوعين وقال

أبو عبيد هذا الحديث منسوخ قال وإنما كان  هذا الحكم في أول الإسلام لمن لم

يهاجر ثم نسخ ذلك بقوله
# 
# تعالى وأولوا الأرحام بعضهم أولى ببعض وهذا الذي ادعاه أبو عبيد لا يسلم

له قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (فإن هم أبوا فسلهم الجزية فإن هم أجابوك فاقبل

منهم وكف عنهم) هذا مما يستدل به مالك والأوزاعي وموافقوهما في جواز أخذ

الجزية من كل كافر عربيا كان أو عجميا كتابيا أو مجوسيا أو غيرهما وقال أبو

حنيفة رضي الله تعالى عنه تؤخذ الجزية من جميع الكفار إلا مشركي العرب

ومجوسهم وقال الشافعي لا يقبل إلا من أهل الكتاب والمجوس عربا كانوا أو

عجما ويحتج بمفهوم آية الجزية وبحديث سنوا بهم سنة أهل الكتاب ويتأول هذا

الحديث على أن المراد بأخذ الجزية أهل الكتاب لأن اسم المشرك يطلق على أهل

الكتاب وغيرهم وكان تخصيصهم معلوما عند الصحابة واختلفوا في قدر الجزية

فقال الشافعي أقلها دينار على الغني ودينار على الفقير أيضا في كل سنة

وأكثرها ما يقع به التراضي وقال مالك هي أربعة دنانير على أهل الذهب

وأربعون درهما على أهل الفضة وقال أبو حنيقة رضي الله تعالى عنه وغيره من

الكوفيين وأحمد رضي الله تعالى عنه على الغني ثمانية وأربعون درهما

والمتوسط أربعة وعشرون والفقير اثنا عشر قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (وإذا

حاصرت أهل حصن فأرادوك أن تجعل لهم ذمة الله وذمة نبيه فلا تجعل لهم ذمة

الله وذمة نبيه ولكن اجعل لهم ذمتك وذمة أصحابك فإنكم إن تخفروا ذممكم وذمم

أصحابكم أهون من أن تخفروا ذمة الله وذمة رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم)

قال العلماء الذمة هنا العهد وتخفروا بضم التاء يقال أخفرت الرجل إذا نقضت

عهده وخفرته أمنته وحميته قالوا وهذا نهي تنزيه أي لا تجعل لهم ذمة الله

فإنه قد ينقضها من لا يعرف حقها وينتهك حرمتها بعض الأعراب وسواد الجيش

قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (وإذا حاصرت أهل حصن
# 
# فأرادوك أن تنزلهم على حكم الله فلا تنزلهم على حكم الله ولكن أنزلهم  على

حكمك فإنك لا تدري أتصيب حكم الله فيهم أم لا) هذا النهي أيضا على التنزيه

والاحتياط وفيه حجة لمن يقول ليس كل مجتهد مصيبا بل المصيب واحد وهو

الموافق لحكم الله تعالى في نفس الأمر وقد يجيب عنه القائلون بأن كل مجتهد

مصيب بأن المراد أنك لا تأمن أن ينزل علي وحي بخلاف ما حكمت وهذا المعنى

منتف بعد النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قوله (حدثنا مسلم بن هيصم) بفتح الهاء

والصاد المهملة قوله صلى الله
# [1732] عليه وسلم (بشروا ولا تنفروا ويسروا ولا تعسروا) وفي
# [1733] الحديث الآخر أنه صلى الله عليه وسلم قال لمعاذ وأبي موسى الأشعري

رضي الله تعالى عنهما يسرا ولا تعسرا وبشرا ولا تنفرا
# 
# وتطاوعا ولا تختلفا وفي
# [1734] حديث أنس رضي الله تعالى عنه يسروا ولا تعسروا وسكنوا ولا تنفروا

إنما جمع في هذه الألفاظ بين الشيء وضده لأنه قد يفعلهما في وقتين فلو

اقتصر على يسروا لصدق ذلك على من يسر مرة أومرات وعسر في معظم الحالات فإذا

قال ولا تعسروا انتفى التعسير في جميع الأحوال من جميع وجوهه وهذا هو

المطلوب وكذا يقال في يسرا ولا تنفرا وتطاوعا ولا تختلفا لأنهما قد

يتطاوعان في وقت ويختلفان في وقت وقد يتطاوعان في شيء ويختلفان في شيء وفي
chapters.anchors:
- Root: د-ع-و (da-ʿa-wa)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To call, summon, invoke; the act of supplication or invitation.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological context, daʿwah is the summons to faith (īmān) and submission (islām), distinguishing the prophetic call from mere communication.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) — verbal calling; metaphorical (majāz) — the comprehensive invitation to a way of life, as in the Prophet's summons to the three qualities.
- Sībawayh Rule: ʿAṭf (Coordination) — The particle "thumma" (ثُمَّ) in the hadith is analyzed for its function; whether it denotes sequential order (tartīb) or is merely for initiating speech (istiftāḥ), affecting the syntactic parsing of the sentence.
chapters.translation:
I say: Know that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: "And when you meet your enemy from the polytheists, call them to three qualities (khiṣāl) or traits (khilāl)." Whichever of these they respond to, accept it from them and refrain from them. Then call them to Islam; if they respond to you, accept it from them and refrain from them. Then call them to move from their abode.

His saying, peace be upon him: "Then call them to Islam" — thus it appears in all copies of Sahih Muslim: "Then call them." Qadi ʿIyāḍ, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, said: The correct narration is "call them" (udʿuhum) with the omission of "thumma" (then). It has been transmitted with its omission correctly in the book of Abu ʿUbayd and in the Sunan of Abu Dawud and others, because it is an explanation of the three qualities and not something additional to them. Al-Māzarī said: "Thumma" here is not redundant; rather, it was introduced to open the discourse and to begin the address.

His saying, peace be upon him: "Then call them to move from their abode to the abode of the emigrants (muhājirīn), and inform them that if they do that, they will have what the emigrants have, and upon them is what is upon the emigrants. If they refuse to move from it, then inform them that they will be like the Bedouin Muslims (aʿrāb al-muslimīn); the judgment of Allah that applies to the believers will apply to them, and they will have no share in the spoils (ghanīmah) or the fayʾ (tribute/state property) unless they fight alongside the Muslims."

The meaning of this hadith is that when they embrace Islam, it is recommended (mustaḥabb) for them to emigrate to Medina. If they do that, they become like the emigrants before them in deserving the fayʾ, the ghanīmah, and other things. Otherwise, they are Bedouins like the rest of the Bedouin Muslims dwelling in the desert without emigration or raiding; thus, the rulings of Islam apply to them, but they have no right to the ghanīmah or the fayʾ. They only receive a share of the zakāh (alms) if they meet the conditions of deserving it. Al-Shāfiʿī said: The charitable donations (ṣadaqāt) are for the poor and their like who have no right to the fayʾ, and the fayʾ is for the soldiers (ajnād). He said: The people of the fayʾ are not given from the ṣadaqāt, nor are the people of the ṣadaqāt given from the fayʾ. He cited this hadith as evidence. Mālik and Abu Ḥanīfah said: The two funds are the same, and it is permissible to disburse each one to both categories. Abu ʿUbayd said: This hadith is abrogated (mansūkh). He said: This ruling was only in the early period of Islam for those who did not emigrate; then it was abrogated by His saying, Most High: {«وَأُولُو الْأَرْحَامِ بَعْضُهُمْ أَوْلَىٰ بِبَعْضٍ»} ("And those of [blood] relationship are more entitled [to inheritance] to one another") — and this claim of Abu ʿUbayd is not conceded to him.

His saying, peace be upon him: "If they refuse, then ask them for the jizyah (poll tax); if they respond to you, accept it from them and refrain from them." This is used as evidence by Mālik, al-Awzāʿī, and their followers for the permissibility of taking the jizyah from every disbeliever — whether Arab or non-Arab, whether a People of the Book, a Magian, or others. Abu Ḥanīfah, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, said: The jizyah is taken from all disbelievers except the Arab polytheists and their Magians. Al-Shāfiʿī said: It is accepted only from the People of the Book and the Magians, whether they are Arabs or non-Arabs. He argues by the implication (mafhūm) of the verse of jizyah and by the hadith: "Treat them as you treat the People of the Book." He interprets this hadith to mean that the intended recipients of the jizyah are the People of the Book, because the name "polytheist" (mushrik) is applied to the People of the Book and others, and their specification was known to the Companions.

They differed over the amount of the jizyah. Al-Shāfiʿī said: Its minimum is one dīnār on the rich and one dīnār on the poor as well, each year; its maximum is whatever is agreed upon by mutual consent. Mālik said: It is four dīnārs on the people of gold and forty dirhams on the people of silver. Abu Ḥanīfah, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, and others among the Kufans, and Aḥmad, may Allah be pleased with him, said: On the rich, forty-eight dirhams; on the middle class, twenty-four; and on the poor, twelve.

His saying, peace be upon him: "And when you besiege the people of a fortress, and they ask you to grant them the protection (dhimmah) of Allah and the protection of His Prophet, do not grant them the protection of Allah and the protection of His Prophet, but grant them your protection and the protection of your companions. For if you violate your protections and the protections of your companions, it is lighter than violating the protection of Allah and the protection of His Messenger, peace be upon him."

The scholars said: "Dhimmah" here means covenant (ʿahd). "Tukhfirū" (you violate) is with a ḍammah on the tāʾ. One says: "akhfartu al-rajul" when one breaks his covenant, and "khafartuhu" when one grants him safety and protection. They said: This is a prohibition of disapproval (nahy tanzīh), meaning: do not make for them the protection of Allah, for it may be violated by one who does not know its right, and its sanctity may be desecrated by some Bedouins and the rabble of the army.

His saying, peace be upon him: "And when you besiege the people of a fortress, and they ask you to bring them down upon the judgment of Allah, do not bring them down upon the judgment of Allah, but bring them down upon your own judgment. For you do not know whether you will hit the judgment of Allah concerning them or not." This prohibition is also one of disapproval (tanzīh) and precaution (iḥtiyāṭ). In it is an argument for those who say that not every mujtahid is correct; rather, the correct one is only one — the one who conforms to the judgment of Allah Most High in the matter itself. Those who say that every mujtahid is correct may respond that the meaning is: you are not safe from a revelation descending upon you contrary to what you have judged — and this meaning is negated after the Prophet, peace be upon him.

His saying — he narrated to us Muslim ibn Hayṣam — with a fatḥah on the hāʾ and the ṣād (unpointed). His saying, peace be upon him: "Give glad tidings and do not repel; make things easy and do not make them difficult." In the other hadith, he, peace be upon him, said to Muʿādh and Abu Mūsā al-Ashʿarī, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both: "Make things easy and do not make them difficult; give glad tidings and do not repel; and cooperate and do not differ." And in the hadith of Anas, may Allah be pleased with him: "Make things easy and do not make them difficult; give tranquility and do not repel."

The reason these expressions combine a thing with its opposite is that a person might do both at different times. If the command were limited to "make things easy," it would apply to one who makes things easy once or a few times but makes them difficult in most situations. When he says "and do not make them difficult," the difficulty is negated in all situations and from all aspects — and this is what is required. The same is said regarding "give glad tidings and do not repel" and "cooperate and do not differ," because two people might cooperate at one time and differ at another, or cooperate in one matter and differ in another.

chapters.title_en: The Command to Give Glad Tidings, the Prohibition of Repelling, the Severity of Treachery, the Permissibility of Deception in War, and the Dislike of Wishing to Meet the Enemy
chapters.arabic_text:
هذا الحديث الأمر بالتبشير بفضل الله وعظيم ثوابه وجزيل عطائه وسعة رحمته

والنهي عن التنفير بذكر التخويف وأنواع الوعيد محضة من غير ضمها إلى

التبشير وفيه تأليف من قرب إسلامه وترك التشديد عليهم وكذلك من قارب البلوغ

من الصبيان ومن بلغ ومن تاب من المعاصي كلهم يتلطف بهم ويدرجون في أنواع

الطاعة قليلا قليلا وقد كانت أمور الإسلام في التكليف على التدريج فمتى يسر

على الداخل في الطاعة أو المريد للدخول فيها سهلت عليه وكانت عاقبته غالبا

التزايد منها ومتى عسرت عليه أو شك أن لا يدخل فيها وإن دخل أو شك أن لا

يدوم أو لا يستحليها وفيه أمر الولاة بالرفق واتفاق المتشاركين في ولاية

ونحوها وهذا  من المهمات فإن غالب المصالح لا يتم إلا بالاتفاق ومتى حصل

الاختلاف فات وفيه وصية الإمام الولاة وإن كانوا أهل فضل وصلاح كمعاذ وأبي

موسى فإن الذكرى تنفع المؤمنين قوله (حدثنا محمد بن عباد حدثنا سفيان عن

عمرو عن سعيد بن أبي بردة) هذا مما استدركه الدارقطني وقال لم
# 
# يتابع بن عباد عن سفيان عن عمرو عن سعيد وقد روى عن سفيان عن مسعر عن
