If the army has dispersed and delivering the right of each individual becomes impossible, then there is a disagreement among the scholars. Al-Shāfiʿī and a group said: It must be handed over to the Imām or the judge, like other lost wealth. Ibn Masʿūd, Ibn ʿAbbās, Muʿāwiyah, al-Ḥasan, al-Zuhrī, al-Awzāʿī, Mālik, al-Thawrī, al-Layth, Aḥmad, and the majority (al-jumhūr) said: One-fifth of it is given to the Imām, and the rest is given in charity.

They differed over the nature of the punishment of the embezzler. The majority of scholars and the Imāms of the regions said: He is given a discretionary punishment (taʿzīr) according to what the Imām deems fit, and his goods are not burned. This is the saying of Mālik, al-Shāfiʿī, Abū Ḥanīfah, and countless Companions, Followers, and those after them. Makḥūl, al-Ḥasan, and al-Awzāʿī said: His saddlebag and all his goods are burned. Al-Awzāʿī said: Except his weapon and the clothes on him. Al-Ḥasan said: Except animals and the muṣḥaf. They adduced the hadith of ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar regarding the burning of his saddlebag. The majority said: This hadith is weak (ḍaʿīf), because it is solely transmitted by Ṣāliḥ ibn Muḥammad from Sālim, and he is weak. Al-Ṭaḥāwī said: Even if it were authentic, it is to be interpreted as applying when the punishment was through wealth—like taking half of the wealth from the one who withholds zakāh, the stray camel, and the thief of dates—and all of that is abrogated (mansūkh). And Allah knows best.

Chapter: The Prohibition of Gifts to Officials

[1832] His saying: "The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, appointed a man from Asad, called Ibn al-Lutbiyyah." As for Asad, it is with a sukūn on the sīn. It is also said: al-Azdī, from Azd Shanūʾah; and they are called al-Azd and al-Asad. And he has been mentioned...

chapters.title_en: Section 730 — On Gifts to Officials Being Unlawful (Ghalūl), the Obligation of Obeying Rulers in What Is Not Disobedience, and Its Prohibition in Disobedience
chapters.arabic_text:
مسلم في الرواية الثانية وأما اللتبية فبضم اللام وإسكان التاء ومنهم من

فتحها قالوا وهو خطأ ومنهم من يقول بفتحها وكذا وقع في مسلم في رواية أبي

كريب المذكورة بعد هذا قالوا وهو خطأ أيضا والصواب اللتبية بإسكانها نسبة

إلى بني لتب قبيلة معروفة وإسم بن اللتبية هذا عبد الله وفي هذا الحديث

بيان أن هدايا العمال حرام وغلول لأنه خان في ولايته وأمانته ولهذا ذكر في

الحديث في عقوبته وحمله ما أهدي إليه يوم القيامة كما ذكر مثله في الغال

وقد بين صلى الله عليه وسلم في نفس الحديث السبب في تحريم الهدية عليه

وأنها بسبب الولاية بخلاف الهدية لغير العامل فإنها مستحبة وقد سبق بيان

حكم ما يقبضه العالم ونحوه باسم الهدية وأنه يرده إلى مهديه فإن تعذر فإلى

بيت المال قوله صلى الله عليه  وسلم (أو شاة تيعر) هو بمثناة فوق مفتوحة ثم

مثناة تحت ساكنة ثم عين مهملة مكسورة ومفتوحة ومعناه تصيح واليعار صوت

الشاة قوله (ثم رفع يديه حتى رأينا عفرتي إبطيه) هي بضم العين المهملة

وفتحها والفاء ساكنة فيهما وممن ذكر اللغتين في العين القاضي هنا وفي

المشارق وصاحب المطالع والأشهر الضم قال الأصمعي وآخرون عفرة الإبط هي

البياض ليس بالناصع
# 
# بل فيه شيء كلون الأرض قالوا وهو مأخوذ من عفر الأرض بفتح العين والفاء

وهو وجهها قوله (فلما جاء حاسبه) فيه محاسبة العمال ليعلم ما قبضوه وما

صرفوا قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (فلأعرفن أحدا منكم لقي الله يحمل بعيرا)

هكذا هو ببعض النسخ فلا عرفن وفي بعضها لا أعرفن بالألف على النفي قال

القاضي هذا أشهر قال والأول هو رواية أكثر رواة صحيح مسلم قوله (بصر عيني

وسمع أذني) معناه أعلم هذا الكلام يقينا وأبصرت عيني النبي صلى الله عليه

وسلم حين
# 
# تكلم به وسمعته أذني فلا شك في علمي به قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (والله

الذي نفسي بيده) فيه توكيد اليمين بذكر اسمين أو أكثر من أسماء الله تعالى

قوله (وسلوا زيد بن ثابت فإنه كان حاضرا معي) فيه استشهاد الراوي والقائل

بقول من يوافقه ليكون أوقع في نفس السامع وأبلغ في طمأنينته قوله (وحدثناه

إسحاق بن إبراهيم حدثنا جرير عن الشيباني عن عبد الله بن ذكوان عن عروة بن

الزبير أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم استعمل رجلا على الصدقة إلى قوله

قال عروة فقلت لأبي حميد أسمعته من رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال من

فيه إلى أذني) هكذا هو في أكثر النسخ عن عروة أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه

وسلم ولم يذكر أبا حميد وكذا نقله القاضي هنا عن رواية الجمهور ووقع في

جماعة من النسخ عن عروة بن الزبير عن أبي حميد وهذا واضح وأما الأول فهو

متصل أيضا لقوله قال عروة فقلت لأبي حميد أسمعته من رسول الله صلى  الله

عليه وسلم فقال من فيه إلى أذني فهذا تصريح من عروة بأنه سمعه من أبي حميد

فاتصل الحديث ومع هذا فهو متصل بالطرق الكثيرة السابقة قوله (فجاء بسواد

كثير) أي بأشياء كثيرة وأشخاص بارزة من حيوان وغيره والسواد يقع على كل شخص
# 
# [1833] قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (كتمنا مخيطا) هو بكسر الميم وإسكان

الخاء وهو الإبرة قوله (عدي بن عميرة) بفتح العين قال القاضي ولا يعرف من

الرجال أحد يقال له عميرة بالضم بل كلهم بالفتح ووقع في النسائي الأمران

| (باب وجوب طاعة الأمراء في غير معصية (وتحريمها في 
# المعصية) أجمع العلماء على وجوبها في غير معصية وعلى تحريمها في المعصية

نقل الإجماع على هذا القاضي)
# 
# عياض وآخرون
# [1834] قوله (نزل قوله تعالى أطيعوا الله وأطيعوا الرسول وأولي الأمر

منكم في عبد الله بن حذافة أمير السرية قال العلماء المراد بأولي الأمر من

أوجب الله طاعته من الولاة والأمراء هذا قول جماهير السلف والخلف من

المفسرين والفقهاء وغيرهم وقيل هم العلماء وقيل الأمراء والعلماء وأما من

قال الصحابة خاصة فقط فقد أخطأ
# [1835] قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (من أطاعني فقد أطاع الله ومن أطاع أميري

فقد
# 
# أطاعني) وقال في المعصية مثله لأن الله تعالى أمر بطاعة رسول الله صلى

الله عليه وسلم وأمر هو صلى الله عليه وسلم بطاعة الأمير فتلازمت الطاعة

قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم
# [1836] (عليك السمع والطاعة في عسرك ويسرك ومنشطك ومكرهك وأثرة عليك) قال

العلماء معناه تجب طاعة ولاة الأمور فيما يشق وتكرهه النفوس وغيره مما ليس

بمعصية فإن كانت لمعصية فلا سمع ولا طاعة كما صرح به في الأحاديث الباقية

فتحمل هذه الأحاديث المطلقة لوجوب طاعة ولاة
# 
# الأمور على موافقة تلك الأحاديث المصرحة بأنه لا سمع ولا طاعة في المعصية

والأثرة بفتح الهمزة والثاء ويقال بضم الهمزة وإسكان الثاء وبكسر الهمزة

وإسكان الثاء ثلاث لغات حكاهن في المشارق وغيره وهي الاستئثار والاختصاص

بأمور الدنيا عليكم أي اسمعوا وأطيعوا وإن اختص الأمراء بالدنيا ولم

يوصلوكم حقكم  مما عندهم وهذه الأحاديث في الحث على السمع والطاعة في جميع

الأحوال وسببها اجتماع كلمة المسلمين فإن الخلاف سبب لفساد أجوالهم في
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ل-ت-ب (L-T-B)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: A tribe named Banū Litb; the nisbah (attributive form) is "Litbiyyah" with sukkūn on the tā'.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Denotes lineage attribution to a specific known tribe, establishing the proper noun's referent.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage here — a genealogical attribution, not metaphorical.
- Sībawayh Rule: Nisbah Formation (النسبة) — The relative adjective is formed by kasrah on the final letter of the base noun; deviations (fatḥ) are rejected as solecisms (khaṭa').

- Root: غ-ل-ل (Gh-L-L)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning: treachery in war spoils; secretly taking from the public trust.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Theological nuance: ghalūl is a major sin (kabīrah) involving breach of amānah (trust) in public office.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: hidden theft; metaphorical extension to any unlawful acquisition by an official.
- Sībawayh Rule: Masdar Formation (المصدر) — "Ghalūl" is a verbal noun pattern (fu'ūl) indicating the act of treachery.

- Root: ع-ف-ر (ʿ-F-R)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: ʿafarah — the surface of the earth; ʿufrah — a whiteness mixed with earth-like color.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Describes a physical attribute of the body (the armpit's whiteness), not a theological term.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal description of a bodily feature; no metaphorical layer.
- Sībawayh Rule: Vowel Variation (الضبط) — Both ḍamm and fatḥ on the ʿayn are attested; the more famous is ḍamm.

- Root: س-و-د (S-W-D)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Sawād — blackness; also used for a visible mass or collective body of things.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In legal contexts, refers to tangible property or chattel.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: blackness; metaphorical (majāz): any visible aggregate of objects.
- Sībawayh Rule: Ishtiqāq (Derivation) — The noun "sawād" is used for a collective visible entity.

- Root: خ-ي-ط (Kh-Y-T)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Khayṭ — thread; mikhyāṭ — needle (instrument noun).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In ḥadīth context, denotes a trivial item, emphasizing the gravity of taking even the smallest public property.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: needle; used to illustrate minimal value.
- Sībawayh Rule: Instrumental Noun (اسم الآلة) — "Mikhyāṭ" follows the mif'āl pattern for tools.

- Root: أ-ث-ر (A-Th-R)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Atharah — preference, exclusivity; istīthār — taking exclusively for oneself.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In political context: rulers' exclusive enjoyment of worldly goods over subjects.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: preference; contextual: rulers' self-appropriation.
- Sībawayh Rule: Vowel Patterns (لغات) — Three attested vocalizations: fatḥatān, ḍammah + sukkūn, kasrah + sukkūn.
chapters.translation:
I say: Muslim [recorded] in the second narration [the word "al-Litbiyyah"]. As for "al-Litbiyyah," it is with ḍammah on the lām and sukkūn on the tā'. Some scholars open the tā' — they said this is an error. Others say it is with fatḥah, and likewise it occurs in Muslim in the narration of Abū Kurayb mentioned later — they said this too is an error. The correct form is "al-Litbiyyah" with sukkūn [on the tā'], being a nisbah to Banū Litb, a well-known tribe. The name of Ibn al-Litbiyyah here is ʿAbd Allāh.

In this ḥadīth there is a clarification that gifts given to officials (ʿummāl) are unlawful and constitute ghalūl (treachery), because he betrayed in his governorship and his trust. For this reason, the ḥadīth mentions in his punishment that he will carry what was gifted to him on the Day of Resurrection, just as the like is mentioned regarding the one who steals from the war spoils (al-ghāll). The Prophet ﷺ clarified in the very ḥadīth the reason for the prohibition of the gift upon him — that it is due to the office (wilāyah) — unlike a gift to a non-official, for it is recommended (mustaḥabbah). The ruling on what a scholar (ʿālim) and the like receives under the name of a gift has already been explained: he must return it to the giver; if that is not possible, then to the public treasury (bayt al-māl).

His saying ﷺ: «أو شاة تيعر» ("or a sheep that yaʿiru") — it is with an open thā' (tā' muthannāh) followed by a silent yā', then an unvocalized or open ʿayn. Its meaning: it cries out. Al-yaʿār is the sound of the sheep.

His saying ﷺ: «ثم رفع يديه حتى رأينا عفرتي إبطيه» ("then he raised his hands until we saw the whiteness of his armpits") — it is with ḍammah on the ʿayn and also with fatḥah, with the fā' silent in both. Among those who mentioned both readings of the ʿayn are al-Qāḍī here, [the author of] al-Mashāriq, and the author of al-Maṭāliʿ. The more famous is ḍammah. Al-Aṣmaʿī and others said: ʿufrat al-ibṭ is the whiteness that is not pure white, but rather has something of the color of the earth in it. They said it is derived from ʿafr al-arḍ (the surface of the earth), with fatḥah on the ʿayn and fā'.

His saying: «فلما جاء حاسبه» ("when he came, he called him to account") — in this is the accounting of officials, so that what they have taken and what they have disbursed may be known.

His saying ﷺ: «فلأعرفن أحدا منكم لقي الله يحمل بعيرا» ("I will surely know a man among you who meets Allah carrying a camel") — thus it is in some copies: "fa-la-aʿrifanna" (with lām of oath). In others: "lā aʿrifanna" (with alif, on negation). Al-Qāḍī said: this latter is the more famous. He said: the first is the narration of the majority of the transmitters of Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim.

His saying: «بصر عيني وسمع أذني» ("with the sight of my eye and the hearing of my ear") — its meaning: I know this statement with certainty; my eye saw the Prophet ﷺ when he spoke it, and my ear heard it, so there is no doubt in my knowledge of it.

His saying ﷺ: «والله الذي نفسي بيده» ("By Allah, in Whose hand is my soul") — in this is the strengthening of the oath by mentioning two or more of the Names of Allah Almighty.

His saying: «وسلوا زيد بن ثابت فإنه كان حاضرا معي» ("and ask Zayd ibn Thābit, for he was present with me") — in this is the narrator and speaker seeking corroboration from one who agrees with him, so that it may be more impactful upon the listener's soul and more effective in his reassurance.

His saying: «وحدثناه إسحاق بن إبراهيم حدثنا جرير عن الشيباني عن عبد الله بن ذكوان عن عروة بن الزبير أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم استعمل رجلا على الصدقة... إلى قوله قال عروة فقلت لأبي حميد أسمعته من رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال من فيه إلى أذني» ("and Isḥāq ibn Ibrāhīm narrated it to us: Jarīr narrated to us, from al-Shaybānī, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Dhakwān, from ʿUrwah ibn al-Zubayr, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ appointed a man over the ṣadaqah... up to his saying: ʿUrwah said: I said to Abū Ḥumayd: Did you hear it from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ? He said: From his mouth to my ear") — thus it is in most copies: "from ʿUrwah that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ," without mentioning Abū Ḥumayd. Al-Qāḍī likewise transmitted it here from the narration of the majority. In a group of copies it occurs: "from ʿUrwah ibn al-Zubayr, from Abū Ḥumayd" — and this is clear. As for the first, it is also connected (muttaṣil), because of his saying: "ʿUrwah said: I said to Abū Ḥumayd: Did you hear it from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ? He said: From his mouth to my ear" — this is an explicit statement from ʿUrwah that he heard it from Abū Ḥumayd, so the ḥadīth is connected. Moreover, it is connected through the many preceding chains.

His saying: «فجاء بسواد كثير» ("he came with much sawād") — meaning: with many things and prominent entities, from animals and otherwise. "Sawād" applies to every visible person or thing.

[1833] His saying ﷺ: «كتمنا مخيطا» ("we concealed even a mikhyāṭ") — it is with kasrah on the mīm and sukkūn on the khā', and it is the needle.

His saying: «عدي بن عميرة» ("ʿAdī ibn ʿAmīrah") — with fatḥah on the ʿayn. Al-Qāḍī said: no man is known among the narrators called ʿUmayrah with ḍammah; rather, all of them are with fatḥah. Both forms occur in al-Nasā'ī.

| (Chapter: The Obligation of Obeying Rulers in What Is Not Disobedience, and Its Prohibition in Disobedience)

The scholars are unanimous (ijmāʿ) upon its obligation in what is not disobedience, and upon its prohibition in disobedience. Al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ and others transmitted this consensus.

[1834] His saying: «نزل قوله تعالى: {أطيعوا الله وأطيعوا الرسول وأولي الأمر منكم}» ("the saying of Allah Almighty: {Obey Allah and obey the Messenger and those in authority among you} was revealed concerning ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥudhāfah, the commander of the expedition") — The scholars said: the intended meaning of "those in authority" (ulū al-amr) is those rulers and commanders whose obedience Allah has made obligatory. This is the saying of the majority of the Salaf and Khalaf among the exegetes, jurists, and others. It was also said: they are the scholars. And it was said: they are the commanders and the scholars. As for the one who said they are only the Companions specifically — he has erred.

[1835] His saying ﷺ: «من أطاعني فقد أطاع الله ومن أطاع أميري فقد أطاعني» ("whoever obeys me has obeyed Allah, and whoever obeys my commander has obeyed me") — and he said the like regarding disobedience, because Allah Almighty commanded obedience to His Messenger ﷺ, and he ﷺ commanded obedience to the commander, so the obediences are mutually entailed.

His saying ﷺ:

[1836] «عليك السمع والطاعة في عسرك ويسرك ومنشطك ومكرهك وأثرة عليك» ("upon you is hearing and obedience in your hardship and your ease, in your enthusiasm and your reluctance, and even when others are preferred over you") — The scholars said: its meaning is that obedience to the rulers is obligatory in what is burdensome and disliked by the souls, and other than that, as long as it is not disobedience. For if it is disobedience, then there is no hearing and no obedience, as explicitly stated in the remaining ḥadīths. Thus these absolute ḥadīths on the obligation of obeying the rulers are interpreted in accordance with those ḥadīths that explicitly state that there is no hearing and no obedience in disobedience.

"Al-Atharah" — with fatḥah on the hamzah and thā', and it is also said with ḍammah on the hamzah and sukkūn on the thā', and with kasrah on the hamzah and sukkūn on the thā' — three dialects, as related in al-Mashāriq and elsewhere. It means istīthār (exclusive appropriation) and special claim to worldly matters. "Upon you" — i.e., hear and obey, even if the commanders exclusively take the worldly goods and do not deliver to you your right from what they hold. These ḥadīths urge hearing and obedience in all circumstances, and their cause is the unity of the Muslims' word, for discord is a cause of the corruption of their affairs in...

chapters.title_en: The Obligation of Obedience to Rulers, Its Limits, and the Impermissibility of Rebellion
chapters.arabic_text:
دينهم ودنياهم قوله
# [1837] (إن خليلي صلى الله عليه وسلم أوصاني أن أسمع وأطيع وإن كان عبدا

مجدع الأطراف) يعني مقطوعها والمراد أخس العبيد أي أسمع وأطيع للأمير وإن

كان دنيء النسب حتى لو كان عبدا أسود مقطوع الأطراف فطاعته واجبة وتتصور

إمارة العبد إذا ولاه بعض الأئمة أو إذا تغلب على البلاد بشوكته وأتباعه

ولا يجوز ابتداء عقد الولاية له مع الاختيار بل شرطها
# 
# الحرية قوله
# [1840] (أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بعث جيشا وأمر عليهم رجلا فأوقد

نارا وقال
# 
# ادخلوها إلى قوله لا طاعة في معصية إنما الطاعة في المعروف) هذا موافق

للأحاديث الباقية أنه لا طاعة في معصية إنما هي في المعروف وهذا الذي فعله

هذا الأمير قيل أراد امتحانهم وقيل كان مازحا قيل إن هذا الرجل عبد الله بن

حذافة السهمي وهذا ضعيف لأنه قال في الرواية التي بعدها إنه رجل من الأنصار

فدل على أنه غيره قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (لو دخلتموها لم تزالوا فيها إلى

يوم القيامة) هذا مما علمه صلى الله عليه وسلم بالوحي وهذا التقييد بيوم

القيامة مبين
# 
# للرواية المطلقة بأنهم لا يخرجون منها لو دخلوها قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم

(إلا أن تروا كفرا بواحا عندكم من الله فيه برهان) هكذا هو لمعظم الرواة

وفي معظم النسخ بواحا بالواو وفي بعضها
# 
# براحا والباء مفتوحة فيهما ومعناهما كفرا ظاهرا والمراد بالكفر هنا

المعاصي ومعنى عندكم من الله فيه برهان أي تعلمونه من دين الله تعالى ومعنى

الحديث لا تنازعوا ولاة الأمور في ولايتهم ولا تعترضوا عليهم إلا أن تروا

منهم منكرا محققا تعلمونه من قواعد الإسلام فإذا رأيتم ذلك فأنكروه عليهم

وقولوا بالحق حيث ما كنتم وأما الخروج عليهم وقتالهم فحرام بإجماع المسلمين

وإن كانوا فسقة ظالمين وقد تظاهرت الأحاديث بمعنى ما ذكرته وأجمع أهل السنة

أنه لا ينعزل  السلطان بالفسق وأما الوجه المذكور في كتب الفقه لبعض أصحابنا

أنه ينعزل وحكي عن المعتزلة أيضا فغلط من قائله مخالف للإجماع قال العلماء

وسبب عدم انعزاله وتحريم الخروج عليه ما يترتب على ذلك من الفتن وإراقة

الدماء وفساد ذات البين فتكون المفسدة في عزله أكثر منها في بقائه قال

القاضي عياض أجمع العلماء على أن الإمامة لا تنعقد لكافر وعلى أنه لو طرأ

عليه الكفر انعزل قال وكذا لو ترك إقامة الصلوات والدعاء إليها قال وكذلك

عند جمهورهم البدعة قال وقال بعض البصريين تنعقد له وتستدام له لأنه متأول

قال القاضي فلو طرأ عليه كفر وتغيير للشرع أو بدعة خرج عن حكم الولاية

وسقطت طاعته ووجب على المسلمين القيام عليه وخلعه ونصب إمام عادل إن أمكنهم

ذلك فإن لم يقع ذلك إلا لطائفة وجب عليهم القيام بخلع الكافر ولا يجب في

المبتدع إلا إذا ظنوا القدرة عليه فإن تحققوا العجز لم يجب القيام وليهاجر

المسلم عن أرضه إلى غيرها ويفر بدينه قال ولا تنعقد لفاسق ابتداء فلو طرأ

على الخليفة فسق قال بعضهم يجب خلعه إلا أن تترتب عليه فتنة وحرب وقال

جماهير أهل السنة من الفقهاء والمحدثين والمتكلمين لا ينعزل بالفسق والظلم

وتعطيل الحقوق ولا يخلع ولا يجوز الخروج عليه بذلك بل يجب وعظه وتخويفه

للأحاديث الواردة في ذلك قال القاضي وقد ادعى أبو بكر بن مجاهد في هذا

الإجماع وقد رد عليه بعضهم هذا بقيام الحسن وبن الزبير وأهل المدينة على

بني أمية وبقيام جماعة عظيمة من التابعين والصدر الأول على الحجاج مع بن

الأشعث وتأول هذا القائل قوله أن لا ننازع الأمر أهله في أئمة العدل وحجة

الجمهور أن قيامهم على الحجاج ليس بمجرد الفسق بل لما غير من الشرع وظاهر

من الكفر قال القاضي وقيل إن هذا الخلاف كان أولا ثم حصل الإجماع على منع

الخروج عليهم والله أعلم
# [1709] قوله (بايعنا على السمع) المراد بالمبايعة المعاهدة وهي مأخوذة من

البيع لأن كل واحد من المتبايعين كان  يمد يده إلى صاحبه وكذا هذه البيعة
# 
# تكون بأخذ الكف وقيل سميت مبايعة لما فيها من المعاوضة لما وعدهم الله

تعالى من عظيم الجزاء قال الله تعالى إن الله اشترى من المؤمنين أنفسهم

وأموالهم بأن لهم الجنة الآية قوله (وعلى أن نقول بالحق أينما كنا لا نخاف

في الله لومة لائم معناه نأمر بالمعروف وننهى عن المنكر في كل زمان ومكان

الكبار والصفار لا نداهن فيه أحدا ولا نخافه هو ولا نلتفت إلى الأئمة ففيه

القيام بالأمر بالمعروف والنهي عن المنكر وأجمع العلماء على أنه فرض كفاية

فإن خاف من ذلك على نفسه أو ماله أو على غيره سقط الإنكار بيده ولسانه

ووجبت كراهته بقلبه هذا مذهبنا ومذهب الجماهير وحكى القاضي هنا في بعضهم

أنه ذهب إلى الإنكار مطلقا في هذه الحالة وغيرها وقد سبق في باب الأمر

بالمعروف في كتاب الإيمان وبسطته بسطا شافيا

| (باب الإمام جنة يقاتل من ورائه ويتقى به) هذا الحديث 
# أول الفوات الثالث الذي لم يسمعه إبراهيم بن سفيان عن مسلم بل رواه عنه

بالإجازة ولهذا قال عن مسلم وقد قدمنا بيانه في الفصول السابقة في مقدمة
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ط-و-ع (ṭ-w-ʿ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Obedience, compliance, submission to command; the act of yielding willingly to authority.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological discourse, ṭāʿah denotes conformity to divine and prophetic command, the operative virtue of the believer; its negation is maʿṣiyah (disobedience).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) — physical and verbal compliance; metaphorical (majāz) — internal acquiescence of the heart. Here, the literal sense governs: audible and visible obedience to the appointed amīr.
- Root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Covering, concealing; ingratitude; disbelief. The derived form kufr bawāḥ means manifest, unconcealed disbelief.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In the prophetic dictum, kufr is extended (majāz) to major sins (maʿāṣī) — a technical broadening, not literal apostasy.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): bawāḥ (from b-w-ḥ) is that which is openly disclosed, as opposed to concealed; the variant barāḥ carries the same sense of public exposure.
- Root: خ-ر-ج (kh-r-j)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To go out, exit; in political terminology, al-khurūj ʿalā — rebellion against constituted authority.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Khurūj in legal-theological usage denotes armed insurrection against the ruler, a grave breach of communal order (jamāʿah).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — physical departure; metaphorical — secession from obedience and communal unity.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Restriction (al-Sharṭ wa al-Jawāb) — The phrase "illā an taraw kufran bawāḥan" functions as an exceptive condition (istithnāʾ) limiting the general command of obedience; the jawāb (apodosis) is implied in the prohibition of resistance, rendering the exception as the sole permissible ground for action.
chapters.translation:
I say: His statement — meaning the Prophet's, peace and blessings be upon him — "My intimate friend (khalīlī), peace and blessings be upon him, enjoined upon me that I hear and obey, even if [the commander] be a slave with severed extremities" — "severed extremities" (mujaddaʿ al-aṭrāf) means cut off, and the intent is the most contemptible of slaves. That is, I hear and obey the amīr even if he be of base lineage, to the point that even if he were a black slave with severed limbs, obedience to him is obligatory. The governance (imārah) of a slave is conceivable if one of the leading imāms appoints him, or if he seizes dominion over a land through his force and followers. However, it is not permissible to initiate a contract of governance for him when there is a choice [of a free person]; rather, freedom is a condition [for such initial appointment].

His statement — peace and blessings be upon him — "The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, dispatched an army and placed a man in command over them. He kindled a fire and said: 'Enter it' — up to his words: 'There is no obedience in disobedience; obedience is only in what is recognized as good (maʿrūf).'" This accords with the remaining hadiths that there is no obedience in disobedience; it is only in what is recognized as good. Regarding what this commander did, it is said he intended to test them, and it is said he was jesting. It is said this man was ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥudhāfah al-Sahmī, but this is weak, because he stated in the subsequent narration that he was a man from the Anṣār, which indicates he was someone else.

His statement — peace and blessings be upon him — "Had you entered it, you would never cease to be in it until the Day of Resurrection" — this is among the things he, peace and blessings be upon him, knew by revelation (waḥy). This restriction to the Day of Resurrection clarifies the unqualified narration that they would not emerge from it had they entered it.

His statement — peace and blessings be upon him — "Unless you see clear disbelief (kufran bawāḥan) regarding which you have from God a proof" — thus it is in the majority of narrations and in most copies: bawāḥan with the wāw; in some copies: barāḥan, with the bāʾ open in both. Their meaning is manifest disbelief. The intent of "disbelief" here is acts of disobedience (maʿāṣī). The meaning of "regarding which you have from God a proof" is that you know it from the religion of God, Exalted is He. The meaning of the hadith is: Do not dispute with the governors of affairs over their governance, and do not object to them, except that you see from them a confirmed wrongdoing (munkar) which you know from the foundations of Islam. When you see that, then denounce it upon them, and speak the truth wherever you may be. As for rebelling against them (al-khurūj ʿalayhim) and fighting them, it is forbidden (ḥarām) by the consensus (ijmāʿ) of the Muslims, even if they are wicked and oppressive. The hadiths have corroborated the meaning of what I have mentioned, and the people of the Sunnah (Ahl al-Sunnah) have agreed that the ruler is not removed from office by wickedness (fisq). As for the view mentioned in the books of jurisprudence by some of our companions that he is removed, and which is also related from the Muʿtazilah, it is an error on the part of its proponent, contradicting the consensus.

The scholars said: The reason for his non-removal and the prohibition of rebelling against him is what results from that — namely, tribulation (fitan), the shedding of blood, and the corruption of communal harmony (fasād dhāt al-bayn). Thus, the harm (mafsadah) in his removal is greater than that in his remaining. Al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ said: The scholars have agreed that the imāmate is not contracted for a disbeliever, and that if disbelief were to occur upon him, he is removed. He said: Likewise, if he abandons the establishment of the prayers and the call to them. He said: And likewise, according to the majority of them, [he is removed] for innovation (bidʿah). He said: And some of the Baṣrans said it is contracted for him and continues for him, because he is an interpreter (mutāʾawwil). Al-Qāḍī said: So if disbelief, alteration of the sacred law, or innovation were to occur upon him, he exits from the rule of governance, his obedience becomes void, and it becomes obligatory upon the Muslims to rise against him, depose him, and appoint a just imām if they are able to do so. If that is not possible except for a group [among them], then it is obligatory upon that group to rise and depose the disbeliever. As for the innovator, [rising against him] is not obligatory except when they deem themselves capable of it. If they ascertain their incapacity, then rising is not obligatory, and the Muslim should emigrate from his land to another and flee with his religion.

He said: And it is not contracted for a wicked person (fāsiq) initially. So if wickedness were to occur upon the caliph, some said it is obligatory to depose him, unless tribulation and war would result from that. The masses of the Ahl al-Sunnah — from the jurists, hadith scholars, and theologians — said: He is not removed by wickedness, oppression, or the suspension of rights; he is not deposed, and it is not permissible to rebel against him on that account. Rather, it is obligatory to admonish him and frighten him [with God's punishment], due to the hadiths narrated on that. Al-Qāḍī said: Abū Bakr ibn Mujāhid claimed consensus (ijmāʿ) on this, but some have refuted him by the rising of al-Ḥasan, Ibn al-Zubayr, and the people of Madīnah against the Umayyads, and by the rising of a great group of the Successors (tābiʿūn) and the first generation against al-Ḥajjāj with Ibn al-Ashʿath. This proponent interpreted his statement — "that we do not dispute the people of authority over their authority" — as [applying] to just imāms. The proof of the majority is that their rising against al-Ḥajjāj was not merely due to his wickedness, but because he altered the sacred law and manifested disbelief. Al-Qāḍī said: It is said this disagreement was initially [present], then consensus was reached on prohibiting rebellion against them. And God knows best.

His statement — "We pledged allegiance (bāyaʿnā) upon hearing" — the intent of the pledge (mubāyaʿah) is the covenant (muʿāhadah), and it is derived from selling (bayʿ), because each of the two parties in a sale would extend his hand to his companion, and likewise this pledge is made by clasping the palm. It is also said it was called mubāyaʿah due to what it contains of exchange (muʿāwaḍah) for what God, Exalted is He, promised them of immense recompense. God, Exalted is He, said: {«إِنَّ اللَّهَ اشْتَرَىٰ مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ أَنفُسَهُمْ وَأَمْوَالَهُم بِأَنَّ لَهُمُ الْجَنَّةَ»} — "Indeed, God has purchased from the believers their lives and their properties, for which they will have Paradise" — the verse.

His statement — "And upon [the pledge] that we speak the truth wherever we may be, not fearing in God the blame of a blamer" — its meaning is: We enjoin what is recognized as good (al-amr bi al-maʿrūf) and forbid what is denounced (al-nahy ʿan al-munkar) in every time and place, for the great and the small; we do not flatter anyone in it, nor fear him, nor pay heed to the rulers. In this is the establishment of enjoining good and forbidding evil. The scholars have agreed that it is a communal obligation (farḍ kifāyah). If one fears from that [harm] to himself, his wealth, or to others, then the denunciation by hand and tongue is dropped, and the abhorrence by heart becomes obligatory. This is our school (madhhab) and the school of the masses. Al-Qāḍī has related here from some of them that he went to the view of denunciation absolutely in this state and others. This has already preceded in the chapter on enjoining good in the Book of Faith, where I have expanded it with a sufficient elaboration.

| (Chapter: The Imām is a Shield — One Fights Behind Him and Seeks Protection Through Him) This hadith is the first of the third section (al-fawāt al-thālith) which Ibrāhīm ibn Sufyān did not hear from Muslim, but rather narrated it from him by permission (ijāzah); for this reason he said "from Muslim" (ʿan Muslim). We have already explained this in the preceding chapters in the Introduction.

chapters.title_en: The Imam as a Shield, and the Obligation of Loyalty to the First Caliph
chapters.arabic_text:
هذا الشرح قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (الإمام جنة) أي كالستر لأنه يمنع العدو

من أذى المسلمين ويمنع الناس بعضهم من بعض ويحمي بيضة الإسلام ويتقيه الناس

ويخافون سطوته ومعنى يقاتل من ورائه أي يقاتل معه الكفار والبغاة والخوارج

وسائر أهل الفساد والظلم مطلقا والتاء في يتقى مبدلة من الواو)
#

| (باب وجوب الوفاء ببيعة الخليفة الأول فالأول قوله
# [1842] صلى الله عليه وسلم (كانت بنو إسرائيل تسوسهم الأنبياء كلما هلك

نبي خلفه نبي) أي يتولون أمورهم كما تفعل الأمراء والولاة بالرعية والسياسة

القيام على الشيء بما يصلحه وفي هذا الحديث جواز قول هلك فلان إذا مات وقد

كثرت الأحاديث به وجاء في القرآن العزيز قوله تعالى حتى إذا هلك قلتم لن

يبعث الله من بعده رسولا قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (وتكون خلفاء فتكثر قالوا

فما تأمرنا قال فوابيعة  الأول فالأول) قوله فتكثر بالثاء المثلثة من الكثرة

هذا هو الصواب المعروف قال القاضي وضبطه بعضهم فتكبر بالباء الموحدة كأنه

من إكبار قبيح أفعالهم وهذا تصحيف وفي هذا الحديث معجزة ظاهرة لرسول الله

صلى الله عليه وسلم ومعنى هذا الحديث إذا بويع لخليفة بعد خليفة فبيعة

الأول صحيحة يجب الوفاء بها وبيعة الثاني باطلة يحرم الوفاء بها ويحرم عليه

طلبها وسواء عقدوا للثاني عالمين بعقد الأول جاهلين وسواء كانا في بلدين أو

بلد أو أحدهما في بلد الإمام المنفصل)
# 
# والآخر في غيره هذا هو الصواب الذي عليه أصحابنا وجماهير العلماء وقيل

تكون لمن عقدت له في بلد الإمام وقيل يقرع بينهم وهذان فاسدان واتفق

العلماء على أنه لا يجوز أن يعقد لخليفتين في عصر واحد سواء اتسعت دار

الإسلام أم لا وقال إمام الحرمين في كتابه الإرشاد قال أصحابنا لا يجوز

عقدها شخصين قال وعندي أنه لا يجوز عقدها لاثنين في صقع واحد وهذا مجمع

عليه قال فإن بعد ما بين الإمامين وتخللت بينهما شسوع فللاحتمال فيه مجال

قال وهو خارج من القواطع وحكى المازري هذا القول عن بعض المتأخرين من أهل

الأصل وأراد به إمام الحرمين وهو قول فاسد مخالف لما عليه السلف والخلف

ولظواهر إطلاق الأحاديث والله أعلم قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم
# [1843] (ستكون بعدي أثرة وأمور تنكرونها قالوا يا رسول الله كيف تأمر من

أدرك منا ذلك قال تؤدون الحق الذي عليكم وتسألون الله الذي لكم) هذا من

معجزات النبوة وقد وقع هذا الإخبار متكررا ووجد مخبره متكررا وفيه الحث على

السمع والطاعة وإن كان المتولي ظالما عسوفا فيعطى حقه من الطاعة ولا يخرج

عليه ولا يخلع بل يتضرع إلى الله تعالى في كشف أذاه ودفع شره وإصلاحه وتقدم

قريبا ذكر اللغات الثلاث في الأثرة وتفسيرها والمراد بها هنا استئثار

الأمراء بأموال بيت المال والله أعلم قوله
# 
# [1844] (ومنا من ينتضل) هو من المناضلة وهي المراماة بالنشاب قوله (ومنا

من هو في جشره) هو بفتح الجيم والشين وهي  الدواب التي ترعى وتبيت مكانها

قوله (الصلاة جامعة) هو بنصب الصلاة على الإغراء وجامعة على الحال قوله صلى

الله عليه وسلم (وتجيء فتنة فيرقق بعضها بعضا) هذه اللفظة رويت على أوجه

أحدها وهو الذي نقله القاضي عن جمهور الرواة يرقق بضم الياء وفتح الراء

وبقافين أي يصير بعضها رقيقا أي خفيفا لعظم ما بعده فالثاني يجعل الأول

رقيقا وقيل معناه يشبه بعضها بعضا وقيل يدور بعضها في بعض ويذهب ويجيء وقيل

معناه يسوق بعضها إلى بعض بتحسينها وتسويلها والوجه الثاني فيرفق بفتح

الياء وإسكان الراء وبعدها فاء مضمومة والثالث فيدفق بالدال المهملة

الساكنة وبالفاء المكسورة أي يدفع ويصب والدفق الصب قوله صلى الله عليه

وسلم (وليأت إلى الناس الذي يجب أن يؤتى إليه) هذا من جوامع كلمه صلى الله

عليه وسلم وبديع حكمه وهذه قاعدة مهمة فينبغي الاعتناء بها وأن الإنسان

يلزم أن لا يفعل مع الناس إلا ما يحب أن يفعلوه معه قوله صلى الله عليه

وسلم
# 
# (فإن جاء آخر ينازعه فاضربوا عنق الآخر) معناه ادفعوا الثاني فإنه خارج

على الإمام فإن لم يندفع إلا بحرب وقتال فقاتلوه فإن دعت المقاتلة إلى قتله

جاز قتله ولا ضمان فيه لأنه ظالم متعد في قتاله قوله (فقلت له هذا بن عمك

معاوية يأمرنا أن نأكل أموالنا بيننا بالباطل ونقتل أنفسنا والله تعالى

يقول ولا تأكلوا أموالكم بينكم بالباطل إلى آخره) المقصود بهذا الكلام أن

هذا القائل لما سمع كلام عبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص وذكر الحديث في تحريم

منازعة الخليفة الأول وأن الثاني يقتل فاعتقد هذا القائل هذا الوصف في

معاوية لمنازعته عليا رضي الله عنه وكانت قد سبقت بيعة علي فرأى هذا أن

نفقة معاوية على أجناده وأتباعه في حرب علي ومنازعته ومقاتلته إياه من أكل

المال بالباطل ومن قتل النفس لأنه قتال بغير حق فلا يستحق أحد مالا في

مقاتلته قوله (أطعه في طاعة الله واعصه في معصية الله) هذا فيه دليل لوجوب

طاعة المتولين للإمامة بالقهر من  غير إجماع ولا عهد قوله (عن عبد الرحمن بن
chapters.anchors:
- Root: و ق ى (wa-qā-ya)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Protection, guarding, shielding from harm; the root denotes warding off injury.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological usage, taqwā is the safeguarding of the soul from divine wrath; here, the imam is a literal shield (junnah) against physical and societal harm.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): The term "junnah" is used metaphorically (majāz) in the hadith, likening the imam to a shield, but the protective function is real (ḥaqīqah) in its effect.
- Sībawayh Rule: Nominal sentence with predicate (al-mubtadaʾ wa al-khabar) — "al-imāmu junnah" is a subject-predicate construction where the predicate is a metaphor, requiring the listener to infer the comparison.

- Root: ب ي ع (bā-ya-ʿa)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: The root signifies the striking of hands in a pact; bayʿah is the contractual oath of allegiance.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In political theology, bayʿah is the covenantal act establishing legitimate authority, binding the community to obedience.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sale (bayʿ) is transferred metaphorically to the exchange of obedience for protection.
- Sībawayh Rule: ʿAṭf (coordination) — "al-awwal fa-al-awwal" (the first, then the first) uses the particle "fa" to denote sequential priority, not simultaneity.
chapters.translation:
I say: His statement, peace and blessings be upon him, "(The imam is a shield (junnah))" means he is like a covering, because he prevents the enemy from harming the Muslims, and prevents the people from one another, and protects the core of Islam (bayḍat al-Islām). The people guard themselves against him (yattaqīhi) and fear his authority. The meaning of "fighting behind him" (yuqātal min warāʾih) is fighting alongside him against the disbelievers, the rebels (al-bughāh), the Khawārij, and all people of corruption and injustice, without exception. The tāʾ in "yuttaqā" is substituted from the wāw (i.e., from ittiqāʾ).

#

| (Chapter: The Obligation of Fulfilling the Allegiance to the First Caliph, Then the Next)

His statement, peace and blessings be upon him, [1842] "(The Children of Israel were governed by their prophets; whenever a prophet perished, another prophet succeeded him)" — meaning they took charge of their affairs just as princes and governors do with their subjects. Governance (al-siyāsah) is the undertaking of a matter in a manner that rectifies it. In this hadith is the permissibility of saying "so-and-so perished (halaka)" when he dies, and the hadiths on this are numerous. It has come in the Mighty Quran, His saying, the Exalted: {«حَتَّىٰ إِذَا هَلَكَ قُلْتُمْ لَنْ يَبْعَثَ اللَّهُ مِنْ بَعْدِهِ رَسُولًا»} (Until when he perished, you said, 'Allah will never send a messenger after him.') His statement, peace and blessings be upon him, "(Then there will be caliphs, and they will be many. They said: What do you command us? He said: Fulfill the allegiance to the first, then the first (fa-bi-bayʿat al-awwal fa-al-awwal).)" His word "fatakthuru" (they will be many) is with the dotted thāʾ (thāʾ muthallathah) from kathrah (multiplicity) — this is the correct and well-known reading. Al-Qāḍī said: Some of them recorded it as "fatakburu" with the dotted bāʾ (bāʾ muwaḥḥadah), as if from takbīr (magnifying) the ugliness of their deeds — and this is a corruption (taṣḥīf). In this hadith is a manifest miracle of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him. The meaning of this hadith: If allegiance is given to a caliph after a caliph, the allegiance of the first is valid and its fulfillment is obligatory, while the allegiance of the second is void and its fulfillment is forbidden, and seeking it is forbidden for him. It is equal whether they contracted for the second knowing of the first's contract or ignorant of it, and whether they were in two lands or one land, or one of them was in the land of the separated imam — and the other elsewhere. This is the correct view upon which our companions (the Shāfiʿīs) and the majority of scholars (jumhūr al-ʿulamāʾ) agree. It was said: The allegiance belongs to the one for whom it was contracted in the imam's land. And it was said: They draw lots between them. These two views are corrupt. The scholars are unanimous that it is not permissible to contract for two caliphs in a single era, whether the abode of Islam (dār al-Islām) is vast or not. Imām al-Ḥaramayn said in his book al-Irshād: Our companions said it is not permissible to contract it for two persons. He said: In my view, it is not permissible to contract it for two in a single region (ṣuqʿ) — and this is agreed upon. He said: But if the distance between the two imams is great and vast expanses (shusūʿ) intervene between them, then there is room for possibility. He said: And this is outside the definitive matters (al-qawāṭiʿ). Al-Māzarī related this view from some later scholars of uṣūl (al-aṣl), meaning Imām al-Ḥaramayn — and it is a corrupt view, contrary to what the predecessors (al-salaf) and successors (al-khalaf) held, and contrary to the apparent unrestricted meanings of the hadiths. And Allah knows best.

His statement, peace and blessings be upon him, [1843] "(After me there will be favoritism (atharah) and matters you will disapprove of. They said: O Messenger of Allah, what do you command the one among us who reaches that time? He said: You fulfill the right owed to you, and ask Allah for what is due to you.)" This is among the miracles of prophethood. This report has occurred repeatedly, and its reported content has been found repeatedly. In it is encouragement toward hearing and obedience, even if the ruler is unjust and oppressive — he is given his right of obedience, and one does not rebel against him nor depose him. Rather, one supplicates humbly to Allah, the Exalted, for the removal of his harm, the repulsion of his evil, and his rectification. The three linguistic meanings of "atharah" and its interpretation have already been mentioned nearby. What is meant here is the rulers' exclusive appropriation of the wealth of the treasury (bayt al-māl). And Allah knows best.

His statement [1844] "(And among us is one who shoots arrows (yantaḍil))" — this is from munāḍalah, which is shooting with arrows (nishāb). His statement "(And among us is one who is with his grazing beasts (jashr))" — it is with fatḥah on the jīm and shīn, meaning the beasts that graze and spend the night in their place. His statement "(The prayer is congregational (al-ṣalātu jāmiʿah))" — "al-ṣalāh" is in the accusative (naṣb) for exhortation (al-ighrāʾ), and "jāmiʿah" is in the accusative as a circumstantial adverb (ḥāl). His statement, peace and blessings be upon him, "(And a tribulation will come, and some of it will soften (yuraqqiq) others)" — this word has been transmitted in several ways. One of them, which al-Qāḍī transmitted from the majority of transmitters, is "yuraqqiq" with ḍammah on the yāʾ, fatḥah on the rāʾ, and two qāfs — meaning some of it becomes thin (raqīq), i.e., light, due to the greatness of what follows it, so the second makes the first seem thin. It was said: Its meaning is that some of it resembles others. It was said: Some of it revolves within others, going and coming. It was said: Its meaning is that some of it drives others by embellishing and seducing them. The second way is "yurafiq" with fatḥah on the yāʾ, sukūn on the rāʾ, followed by a ḍammah on the fāʾ. The third is "yudfiq" with the unpointed dāl (dāl muhmalah) in sukūn and the fāʾ in kasrah — meaning it pushes and pours; al-dafq is pouring. His statement, peace and blessings be upon him, "(And let a person come to the people with what he would love to be done to him)" — this is among the comprehensive sayings (jawāmiʿ al-kalim) of him, peace and blessings be upon him, and his exquisite wisdom. This is an important principle, and one should attend to it — that a person must not do to people except what he loves for them to do to him.

His statement, peace and blessings be upon him, "(If another comes to dispute with him, strike the neck of the other)" — its meaning is: repel the second, for he is a rebel against the imam. If he is not repelled except by war and fighting, then fight him. If the fighting necessitates killing him, his killing is permissible, and there is no liability (ḍamān) for it, because he is an unjust aggressor in his fighting. His statement "(I said to him: This is your cousin Muʿāwiyah, commanding us to consume our wealth among ourselves unjustly and to kill ourselves, while Allah, the Exalted, says: {«وَلَا تَأْكُلُوا أَمْوَالَكُمْ بَيْنَكُمْ بِالْبَاطِلِ»} (And do not consume your wealth among yourselves unjustly) to the end of the verse)" — the purpose of this speech is that this speaker, when he heard the words of ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ and the mention of the hadith prohibiting disputing the first caliph and that the second would be killed, believed this description applied to Muʿāwiyah for his disputing ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with him. Since the allegiance to ʿAlī had already preceded, this man saw that Muʿāwiyah's expenditure on his troops and followers in the war against ʿAlī, disputing him and fighting him, was consuming wealth unjustly and killing souls, because it was fighting without right — so no one deserves wealth in fighting him. His statement "(Obey him in obedience to Allah, and disobey him in disobedience to Allah)" — in this is evidence for the obligation of obeying those who assume the imamate by force (al-qahr), without consensus (ijmāʿ) or covenant (ʿahd). From ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn...

chapters.title_en: Section 733 — On the Obligation of Adhering to the Muslim Congregation During Tribulations, the Prohibition of Seceding from Obedience and Splitting from the Group, and Related Matters
chapters.arabic_text:
عبد رب
# 
# الكعبة الصائدي) هكذا هو في جميع النسخ بالصاد والدال المهملة وكذا نقله

القاضي عياض عن جميع النسخ قال وهو غلط وصوابه العائذي بالعين والذال

المعجمة قاله بن الحباب والنسابة هذا كلام القاضي وقد ذكره البخاري في

تاريخه والسمعاني في الأنساب فقالا هو الصائدي ولم يذكرا غير ذلك فقد اجتمع

مسلم والبخاري والسمعاني على الصائدي قال السمعاني هو منسوب إلى صائد بطن

من همدان قال وصائد اسم كعب بن شرحبيل بن شراحبيل بن عمرو بن حشم بن حاسد

بن حشيم بن حوان بن نوف بن همدان بن مالك بن زيد بن سهلان بن سلمة بن ربيعة

بن أحبار بن مالك بن زيد بن كهلان بن سبأ

| (باب الأمر بالصبر عند ظلم الولاة واستئثارهم
# [1845]
# [1846] تقدم
# شرح أحاديثه في الأبواب قبله وحاصله الصبر على ظلمهم وأنه لا تسقط طاعتهم

بظلمهم والله أعلم)
#

| (باب وجوب ملازمة جماعة المسلمين عند ظهور الفتن (وفي
# كل حال وتحريم الخروج من الطاعة ومفارقة الجماعة) قوله
# [1847] (قلت يا رسول الله إنا كنا في جاهلية وشر فجاءنا الله بهذا الخير

فهل بعد هذا الخير شر قال نعم فقلت فهل بعد ذاك الشر من خير قال نعم وفيه

دخن) قال أبو عبيد وغيره الدخن بفتح الدال المهملة والخاء المعجمة أصله أن

تكون في لون الدابة كدورة إلى سواد قالوا والمراد)
# 
# هنا أن لا تصفو القلوب بعضها لبعض ولا يزول خبثها ولا ترجع إلى ما كانت

عليه من الصفا قال القاضي قيل المراد بالخير بعد الشر أيام عمر بن عبد

العزيز رضي الله عنه قوله بعده تعرف منهم وتنكر المراد الأمر بعد عمر بن

عبد العزيز رضي الله عنه قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (ويهتدون بغير هديي)

الهدي الهيئة والسيرة والطريقة قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (دعاة على أبواب

جهنم من أجابهم إليها قذفوه فيها) قال العلماء هؤلاء من كان من الأمراء

يدعو إلى بدعة أو ضلال آخر كالخوارج والقزامطة وأصحاب  المحنة وفي حديث

حذيفة هذا لزوم جماعة المسلمين وإمامهم ووجوب طاعته وإن فسق وعمل المعاصي

من أخذ الأموال وغير ذلك فتجب طاعته في غير معصية وفيه معجزات لرسول الله

صلى الله عليه وسلم وهي هذه الأمور التي أخبر بها وقد وقعت كلها قوله (عن

أبي سلام قال قال حذيفة بن اليمان) قال الدارقطني هذا عندي مرسل لأن أبا

سلام لم يسمع حذيفة وهو كما قال الدارقطني لكن المتن صحيح متصل بالطريق
# 
# الأول وإنما أتى مسلم بهذا متابعة كما ترى وقد قدمنا في الفصول وغيرها أن

الحديث المرسل إذا روي من طريق آخر متصلا تبينا به صحة المرسل وجاز

الاحتجاج به ويصير في المسألة حديثان صحيحان
# [1848] قوله (عن أبي قيس بن رياح) هو بكسر الراء وبالمثناة وهو زياد بن

رياح القيسي المذكور في الإسناد بعده وقاله البخاري بالمثناة وبالموحدة

وقاله الجماهير بالمثناة لا غير قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (من فارق الجماعة

مات ميتة جاهلية) هي بكسر الميم أي على صفة موتهم من حيث هم فوضى لا إمام

لهم قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (ومن قاتل تحت راية عمية) هي بضم العين وكسرها

لغتان مشهورتان والميم مكسورة مشددة والياء مشددة أيضا قالوا هي الأمر

الأعمى لا يستبين وجهه كذا قاله أحمد بن حنبل والجمهور قال إسحاق بن راهويه

هذا كتقاتل القوم للعصبية قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (يغضب لعصبة أو يدعو إلى

عصبة أو ينصر عصبة) هذه الألفاظ الثلاثة بالعين والصاد المهملتين هذا هو

الصواب المعروف في نسخ بلادنا وغيرها وحكى القاضي عن رواية العذري بالغين

والضاد المعجمتين
# 
# في الألفاظ الثلاثة ومعناها أنه يقاتل لشهوة نفسه وغضبة لها ويؤيد

الرواية الأولى الحديث المذكور بعدها يغضب للعصبة ويقاتل للعصبة ومعناه

إنما يقاتل عصبية لقومه وهواه قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (ومن خرج على أمتي

يضرب برها وفاجرها ولا يتحاشى من مؤمنها وفي بعض النسخ يتحاشى بالياء

ومعناه لا يكترث بما يفعله فيها ولا يخاف وباله
# 
# وعقوبته
# [1851] قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (من  خلع يدا من طاعة لقي الله تعالى يوم

القيامة) لا حجة له) أي لاحجة له في فعله ولا عذر له ينفعه
#

| (باب حكم من فرق أمر المسلمين وهو مجتمع
# [1852] قوله صلى
# الله عليه وسلم (ستكون هنات وهنات) الهنات جمع هنة وتطلق على كل شيء

والمراد بها هنا الفتن والأمور الحادثة قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (فمن أراد

أن يفرق أمر هذه الأمة وهي جميع فاضربوه بالسيف كائنا من كان) فيه الأمر

بقتال من خرج على الإمام أو أراد تفريق كلمة المسلمين ونحو ذلك وينهى عن

ذلك فإن لم ينته قوتل وإن لم يندفع شره إلا بقتله فقتل)
# 
# كان هدرا فقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم فاضربوه بالسيف وفي الرواية الأخرى

فاقتلوه معناه إذا لم يندفع إلا بذلك وقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (يريد أن

يشق عصاكم) معناه يفرق جماعتكم كما تفرق العصاة االمشقوقة وهو عبارة عن

اختلاف الكلمة وتنافر النفوس
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ص-ي-د (ṣ-y-d)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To hunt, to capture prey; a hunter (ṣāʾid). The nisba (attributive name) "al-Ṣāʾidī" derives from this root, denoting one belonging to the tribe or clan of Ṣāʾid.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In biographical/transmission contexts, the term functions as a proper-name attribution, not a theological concept; precision in such names is critical for ḥadīth authentication (taṣḥīḥ al-asanīd).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal usage — a patronymic/tribal attribution; no metaphorical extension here. The dispute over ṣād/dāl vs. ʿayn/dhāl is purely orthographic and genealogical, not rhetorical.
- Root: ع-ص-ب (ʿ-ṣ-b)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: A band, ligature, or nerve; ʿaṣabiyyah — partisanship, group solidarity, zeal for one's kin or faction.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In prophetic discourse, ʿaṣabiyyah denotes blameworthy tribal or partisan zeal that overrides religious duty — a moral failing opposed to communal unity (jamāʿah).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: binding/twisting (as a turban or sinew); metaphorical: the "binding" of a group by shared passion, often leading to unjust aggression.
- Root: ش-ق-ق (sh-q-q)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To split, cleave, divide; shiqāq — discord, schism, severance of unity.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Shaqq al-ʿaṣā (splitting the staff) is a Quranic and prophetic metaphor for fracturing communal cohesion; the "staff" symbolizes collective authority and order.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Metaphorical usage — the staff (ʿaṣā) is not literal wood but the unified body of Muslims under one leader; splitting it signifies rebellion and fragmentation.
- Root: ه-ن-و (h-n-w)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: A thing, matter, affair (hannah, pl. hanāt); often used vaguely for unspecified events.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In prophetic eschatology, hanāt refers to emergent tribulations (fitan) and unforeseen calamities — morally neutral in root but contextually negative here.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: any object/thing; metaphorical: euphemistic reference to evils and trials, softening the direct mention of discord.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional/Imperative Construction (al-Sharṭ wa al-Jawāb) — In "man farraqa... fa-ḍribūhu" (whoever splits... strike him), the protasis (sharṭ) is a relative clause with man, and the apodosis (jawāb) is an imperative, indicating a universal, binding command contingent on the condition. Also, the accusative of specification (tamyīz) in "mawtatan jāhilīyatan" (a death of ignorance) specifies the manner of dying.
chapters.translation:
I say: Know that the name "al-Ṣāʾidī" — thus it appears in all copies with the unpointed ṣād and unpointed dāl, and likewise al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ transmitted it from all copies. He said: This is an error, and the correct form is "al-ʿĀʾidhī" with ʿayn and pointed dhāl, as stated by Ibn al-Ḥabāb and the genealogist. This is the statement of al-Qāḍī. However, al-Bukhārī mentioned him in his Tārīkh and al-Samʿānī in al-Ansāb, and both said he is "al-Ṣāʾidī," mentioning nothing else. Thus Muslim, al-Bukhārī, and al-Samʿānī concur on "al-Ṣāʾidī." Al-Samʿānī said: He is attributed to Ṣāʾid, a sub-tribe of Hamdān. He said: Ṣāʾid is the name of Kaʿb ibn Sharāḥīl ibn Sharāḥīl ibn ʿAmr ibn Ḥashm ibn Ḥāsid ibn Ḥushaym ibn Ḥawān ibn Nawf ibn Hamdān ibn Mālik ibn Zayd ibn Sahlān ibn Salamah ibn Rabīʿah ibn Aḥbār ibn Mālik ibn Zayd ibn Kahlān ibn Sabaʾ.

| (Chapter: The Command to Exercise Patience Upon the Injustice of Rulers and Their Appropriation of Privileges)
[1845] [1846] The explanation of its ḥadīths has already preceded in the chapters before this. The sum of it is: patience upon their injustice, and that their obedience is not nullified by their injustice. And Allāh knows best.

| (Chapter: The Obligation of Adhering to the Congregation of Muslims Upon the Appearance of Tribulations, and in Every Circumstance; and the Prohibition of Seceding from Obedience and Separating from the Group)
His statement [1847]: "I said: O Messenger of Allāh, we were in a state of ignorance (jāhilīyyah) and evil, then Allāh brought us this good. Is there after this good any evil?" He said: "Yes." I said: "Is there after that evil any good?" He said: "Yes, but in it is dakh an." Abū ʿUbayd and others said: al-dakh an — with the unpointed dāl and pointed khāʾ — its origin is a duskiness tending toward blackness in the color of a beast. They said: The intended meaning here is that hearts do not become pure toward one another, their malice does not vanish, and they do not return to the purity they formerly had. Al-Qāḍī said: It was said the intended meaning of "good after evil" is the days of ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz, may Allāh be pleased with him. His statement afterward: "You will recognize from them and deny" — the intended meaning is the period after ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz, may Allāh be pleased with him. His statement, peace and blessings be upon him: "And they will be guided by other than my guidance" — al-hady is the disposition, the manner, and the way. His statement, peace and blessings be upon him: "Callers at the gates of Hell; whoever answers them, they will cast him into it" — the scholars said: These are those among the rulers who call to an innovation (bidʿah) or misguidance, such as the Khawārij, the Qarāmiṭah, and the partisans of the Inquisition (aṣḥāb al-miḥnah). In this ḥadīth of Ḥudhayfah is the obligation of adhering to the congregation of Muslims and their leader, and the obligation of obeying him even if he is corrupt and commits sins — such as taking wealth and otherwise — so obedience to him is obligatory in that which is not disobedience. In it are miracles of the Messenger of Allāh, peace and blessings be upon him, namely these matters he foretold, all of which have occurred. His statement: "On the authority of Abū Salām, who said: Ḥudhayfah ibn al-Yamān said" — al-Dāraquṭnī said: This is in my view mursal (broken chain), because Abū Salām did not hear from Ḥudhayfah. And it is as al-Dāraquṭnī said. However, the text (matn) is sound and connected via the first chain. Muslim only brought this as a corroborating chain (mutābaʿah), as you see. We have already stated in the chapters and elsewhere that a mursal ḥadīth, when narrated through another connected chain, establishes the soundness of the mursal by that means, and it becomes permissible to cite it as proof, and the matter becomes two sound ḥadīths.

[1848] His statement: "On the authority of Abū Qays ibn Riyāḥ" — it is with kasrah on the rāʾ and with the dotted tāʾ (i.e., "Riyāḥ"), and he is Ziyād ibn Riyāḥ al-Qaysī, mentioned in the chain after it. Al-Bukhārī said it with the dotted tāʾ and the unpointed bāʾ (i.e., "Riyāb"), while the majority said it with the dotted tāʾ only. His statement, peace and blessings be upon him: "Whoever separates from the congregation dies a death of ignorance (jāhilīyyah)" — it is with kasrah on the mīm (i.e., mītah), meaning: upon the manner of their death, in that they were without order (fawḍā), having no leader over them. His statement, peace and blessings be upon him: "And whoever fights under a blind banner (rāyah ʿummiyyah)" — it is with ḍammah on the ʿayn and kasrah on it, two well-known dialects; the mīm is kasrah with shaddah, and the yāʾ is also with shaddah. They said: It is the blind matter whose course is not discernible. Thus said Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal and the majority. Isḥāq ibn Rāhawayh said: This is like a people fighting out of partisanship (ʿaṣabiyyah). His statement, peace and blessings be upon him: "He becomes angry for a faction (ʿaṣabah), or calls to a faction, or aids a faction" — these three expressions are with the unpointed ʿayn and unpointed ṣād. This is the correct and well-known reading in the copies of our lands and others. Al-Qāḍī reported from the narration of al-ʿUdhrī with the pointed ghayn and pointed ḍād in the three expressions. Its meaning is: he fights for the desire of his own soul and its anger. The first narration is supported by the ḥadīth mentioned after it: "He becomes angry for the faction and fights for the faction" — its meaning is: he only fights out of partisanship for his people and his whim. His statement, peace and blessings be upon him: "And whoever rebels against my community (ummah), striking its righteous and its wicked, not sparing its believer" — and in some copies "lā yataḥāshā" with the yāʾ — its meaning: he does not care about what he does within it, nor fears its consequence and punishment.

[1851] His statement, peace and blessings be upon him: "Whoever withdraws his hand from obedience will meet Allāh, the Exalted, on the Day of Resurrection with no proof (ḥujjah) for him" — that is, no proof for his deed, and no excuse that will avail him.

| (Chapter: The Ruling on One Who Divides the Affairs of the Muslims While They Are United)
[1852] His statement, peace and blessings be upon him: "There will be calamities (hanāt) and calamities" — al-hanāt is the plural of hannah, and it is applied to every thing; the intended meaning here is tribulations and emergent matters. His statement, peace and blessings be upon him: "Whoever desires to divide the affair of this community while it is united, then strike him with the sword, whoever he may be" — in it is the command to fight whoever rebels against the leader (imām) or desires to split the word of the Muslims and the like. He is forbidden from that; if he does not desist, he is fought; and if his evil is not repelled except by killing him, then his killing is permissible (hadar). Thus his statement, peace and blessings be upon him, "strike him with the sword," and in the other narration, "kill him," means: when it is not repelled except by that. His statement, peace and blessings be upon him: "Desiring to split your staff (ʿaṣā)" — its meaning is: to divide your congregation just as the split staff is divided; it is an expression for divergence of the word and mutual aversion of souls.

chapters.title_en: Section on the Obligation of Enjoining Good and Forbidding Evil Regarding Rulers, and the Prohibition of Fighting Them While They Pray
chapters.arabic_text:
| (باب إذا بويع لخليفتين قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم
# [1853] (إذا
# بويع لخليفتين فاقتلوا الآخر منهما) هذا محمول على ما إذا لم يندفع إلا

بقتله وقد سبق إيضاح هذا في الأبواب السابقة وفيه أنه لا يجوز عقدها

لخليفتين وقد سبق قريبا نقل الإجماع فيه واحتمال إمام الحرمين)

# باب وجوب الإنكار على الأمراء فيما يخالف الشرع (وترك قتالهم ما صلوا

ونحو ذلك) قوله
# [1854] صلى الله عليه وسلم (ستكون أمراء فتعرفون وتنكرون فمن عرف فقد برئ

ومن أنكر
# 
# سلم ولكن من رضي وتابع قالوا أفلا نقاتلهم قال لا ماصلوا) هذا الحديث فيه

معجزة ظاهرة بالإخبار بالمستقبل ووقع ذلك كما أخبر صلى الله عليه وسلم وأما

قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم فمن عرف فقد برئ وفي الرواية التي بعدها فمن كره

فقد برئ فأما رواية من روى فمن كره فقد برئ فظاهرة ومعناه من كره ذلك

المنكر فقد برئ من إثمه وعقوبته وهذا في حق من لا يستطيع إنكاره بيده ولا

لسانه فليكرهه بقلبه وليبرأ وأما من روى فمن عرف فقد برئ فمعناه والله أعلم 

فمن عرف المنكر ولم يشتبه عليه فقد صارت له طريق إلى البراءة من إثمه

وعقوبته بأن يغيره بيديه أو بلسانه فإن عجز فليكرهه بقلبه وقوله صلى الله

عليه وسلم ولكن من رضي وتابع معناه ولكن الإثم والعقوبة على من رضي وتابع

وفيه دليل على أن من عجز عن إزالة المنكر لا يأثم بمجرد السكوت بل إنما

يأثم بالرضى به أو بأن لا يكرهه بقلبه أو بالمتابعة عليه وأما قوله أفلا

نقاتلهم قال لا ماصلوا ففيه معنى ما سبق أنه لا يجوز الخروج على الخلفاء
# 
# بمجرد الظلم أو الفسق مالم يغيروا شيئا من قواعد الإسلام

| (باب خيار الأئمة وشرارهم قوله
# [1855] (عن رزيق بن حيان
# اختلفوا في تقديم الراء على الزاي وتأخيرها على وجهين) ذكره البخاري وبن

أبي حاتم والدارقطني وعبد الغني بن سعيد المصري وبن ماكولا وغيرهم من أصحاب

المؤتلف بتقديم الراء المهملة وهو الموجود في معظم نسخ صحيح مسلم وقال أبو

زرعة الرازي والدمشقي بتقديم الزاي المعجمة والله أعلم قوله (عن مسلم بن

قرظة) بفتح القاف والراء وبالظاء المعجمة وقد سبق في الباب قبله شرح هذه

الأحاديث قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (خيار أئمتكم الذين تحبونهم)
# 
# ويحبونكم ويصلون عليكم وتصلون عليهم) معنى يصلون أي يدعون قوله (فجثا على

ركبتيه واستقبل القبلة) هكذا هو في أكثر النسخ فجثا بالثاء المثلثة وفي

بعضها فجذا بالذال المعجمة وكلاهما صحيح فأما بالثاء فيقال منه جثا على

ركبتيه يجثو وجثا يجثى جثوا وجثيا فيهما وأجثاه غيره وتجاثوا على الركب جثى

وجثى بضم الجيم وكسرها وأما جذا فهو الجلوس على أطراف أصابع الرجلين ناصب

القدمين وهو الجاذي والجمع جذا مثل نائم ونيام قال الجمهور الجاذي أشد

استيفازا من الجاثي وقال أبو عمرو هما لغتان
#

# باب استحباب مبايعة الإمام الجيش عند إرادة القتال وبيان بيعة الرضوان

تحت الشجرة قوله
# [1856] (كنا يوم الحديبية ألفا وأربعمائة) وفي رواية ألفا وخمسمائة
# [1857] وفي رواية ألفا وثلاثمائة وقد ذكر البخاري ومسلم هذه الروايات

الثلاث في صحيحهما وأكثر روايتهما ألف وأربعمائة وكذا ذكر  البيهقي أن أكثر

روايات هذا الحديث ألفا وأربعمائة ويمكن أن يجمع بينهما بأنهم كانوا

أربعمائة وكسرا فمن قال أربعمائة لم يعتبر الكسر ومن قال خمسمائة اعتبره

ومن قال ألف وثلاثمائة ترك بعضهم لكونه لم يتقن العد أو لغير ذلك قوله في

رواية جابر ورواية معقل بن يسار
# [1858] (بايعناه يوم الحديبية على أن لا نفر ولم نبايعه على الموت) وفي

رواية سلمة أنهم بايعوه
# 
# يومئذ على الموت وهو معنى رواية عبد الله بن زيد بن عاصم وفي رواية مجاشع

بن مسعود البيعة على الهجرة والبيعة على الاسلام والجهاد وفى حديث بن عمر

وعبادة بايعنا على السمع والطاعة وأن لا ننازع الأمر أهله وفى رواية عن بن

عمر في غير صحيح مسلم البيعة على الصبر قال العلماء هذه الرواية تجمع

المعاني كلها وتبين مقصود كل الروايات فالبيعة على أن لا نفر معناه الصبر

حتى نظفر بعدونا أو نقتل وهو معنى البيعة على الموت أي نصبر وإن آل بنا ذلك

إلى الموت لا أن الموت مقصود في نفسه وكذا البيعة على الجهاد أي والصبر فيه

والله أعلم وكان في أول الإسلام يجب على العشرة من المسلمين أن يصبروا

لمائة من الكفار ولا يفروا منهم وعلى المائة الصبر لألف كافر ثم نسخ ذلك

وصار الواجب مصابرة المثلين فقط هذا مذهبنا ومذهب بن عباس ومالك
# 
# والجمهور أن الآية منسوخة وقال أبو حنيفة وطائفة ليست بمنسوخة واختلفوا

في أن المعتبر مجرد العدد من غير مراعاة القوة والضعف أم يراعى والجمهور

على أنه لا يراعى لظاهر القرآن وأما حديث عبادة بايعنا رسول الله صلى الله

عليه وسلم على أن لا تشركوا بالله شيئا ولا تسرقوا إلى آخره فإنما كان ذلك

في أول الأمر في ليلة العقبة قبل الهجرة من مكة وقبل فرض الجهاد قوله (سألت
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ن-ك-ر (n-k-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To disavow, to reject, to recognize as wrong; the opposite of ʿirfān (recognition).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In Sharīʿah, it denotes the moral censure of a prohibited act (munkar) as a communal obligation (farḍ kifāyah), rooted in the heart's innate disposition (fiṭrah).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) = cognitive recognition; metaphorical (majāz) = active disapproval by hand, tongue, or heart, graded by capacity.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clause (al-sharṭ wa-l-jawāb) — "man ʿarafa fa-qad bariʾa" (whoever recognizes, he is absolved) uses the conditional particle "man" with the perfect tense to indicate a universal, timeless legal ruling (ḥukm mustaqirr).
chapters.translation:
I say: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: {«If allegiance is sworn to two caliphs, then kill the latter of them»}. This is interpreted as applying to the case where the matter cannot be repelled except by killing him. The clarification of this has already preceded in the previous sections. In it is the ruling that it is not permissible to contract the caliphate for two caliphs simultaneously, and the transmission of consensus (ijmāʿ) on this has already preceded shortly ago, along with the possibility raised by Imām al-Ḥaramayn.

As for his saying, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: {«There will be rulers, and you will recognize [the good] and disapprove [the evil]. Whoever recognizes is absolved, and whoever disapproves is safe. But whoever is pleased and follows [them]»} — they said: "Shall we not fight them?" He said: {«No, as long as they pray»}. This hadith contains a manifest miracle (muʿjizah ẓāhirah) in the foretelling of the unseen, and it occurred exactly as he, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, informed. As for his saying, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: "Whoever recognizes is absolved" — and in the narration that follows: "Whoever disapproves is absolved" — as for the narration of those who transmitted "whoever disapproves is absolved," it is clear in meaning: whoever disapproves of that evil deed in his heart is absolved of its sin and punishment. This applies to the one who is unable to forbid it with his hand or tongue; let him disapprove it with his heart and be absolved. As for those who transmitted "whoever recognizes is absolved," its meaning — and Allah knows best — is: whoever recognizes the evil deed and it is not ambiguous to him, then a path to absolution from its sin and punishment has become available to him, namely by changing it with his hands or tongue; if he is incapable, then let him disapprove it with his heart. His saying, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: "But whoever is pleased and follows" — its meaning is: rather, the sin and punishment fall upon the one who is pleased with it and follows it. In this is proof that the one who is incapable of removing the evil deed does not sin by mere silence; rather, he only sins by being pleased with it, or by not disapproving it in his heart, or by following along with it. As for his saying: "Shall we not fight them?" He said: "No, as long as they pray" — in it is the meaning of what has preceded: it is not permissible to rebel against the caliphs merely due to injustice or immorality (fisq), as long as they have not altered any of the foundations of Islam.

As for his saying, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: {«The best of your rulers are those whom you love and who love you, and who pray for you and you pray for them»} — the meaning of "they pray for you" is that they supplicate (yadʿūna) for you.

His saying: {«He knelt on his knees and faced the qiblah»} — thus it is in most copies: "fa-jathā" with the dotted thāʾ (th). In some copies it is "fa-jadhā" with the dotted dhāl (dh), and both are correct. As for the thāʾ, one says: "jathā ʿalā rukbatayhi yajthū" and "jathā yajthā" — "juthuwwan" and "jathiyyan" in both; another makes him kneel ("ajthāhu"), and they kneel together ("tajāthaw ʿalā al-rukab") — "juthiyyan" and "jithiyyan" with ḍammah or kasrah on the jīm. As for "jadhā," it is sitting on the tips of the toes with the feet erect; such a one is "al-jādhī," and the plural is "jadhā" like "nāʾim" and "niyām." The majority (al-jumhūr) said: the jādhī is more alert and poised than the jāthī. Abū ʿAmr said: they are two dialects.

I say: We were on the day of al-Ḥudaybiyyah one thousand four hundred [in number]. In another narration: one thousand five hundred. In another narration: one thousand three hundred. Al-Bukhārī and Muslim have mentioned these three narrations in their two Ṣaḥīḥs, and the majority of their narrations are one thousand four hundred. Likewise, al-Bayhaqī mentioned that the majority of narrations of this hadith are one thousand four hundred. It is possible to reconcile between them by saying that they were four hundred and some fraction; whoever said "four hundred" did not count the fraction, whoever said "five hundred" counted it, and whoever said "one thousand three hundred" — some of them omitted [some] because he was not precise in the count, or for another reason.

His saying in the narration of Jābir and the narration of Maʿqil ibn Yasār: {«We pledged allegiance to him on the day of al-Ḥudaybiyyah on the condition that we would not flee, and we did not pledge to him on death»}. In the narration of Salamah, they pledged to him that day on death, and that is the meaning of the narration of ʿAbdullāh ibn Zayd ibn ʿĀṣim. In the narration of Mujāshiʿ ibn Masʿūd, the pledge was on emigration (hijrah), on Islam, and on jihād. In the hadith of Ibn ʿUmar and ʿUbādah: we pledged on hearing and obedience, and on not disputing the authority of its people. In a narration from Ibn ʿUmar, not in Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim, the pledge was on patience (ṣabr). The scholars said: this narration encompasses all the meanings and clarifies the intent of all the narrations. For the pledge on "not fleeing" means patience until we triumph over our enemy or are killed — and that is the meaning of the pledge on death, i.e., we are patient even if that leads us to death, not that death is intended in itself. Likewise, the pledge on jihād means patience therein. And Allah knows best.

In the early days of Islam, it was obligatory upon ten Muslims to be patient against one hundred disbelievers and not flee from them, and upon one hundred to be patient against one thousand disbelievers. Then this was abrogated (naskh), and the obligation became only to hold firm against twice the number. This is our school (madhhab), and the school of Ibn ʿAbbās and Mālik, and the majority — that the verse is abrogated. Abū Ḥanīfah and a group said it is not abrogated. They differed as to whether the consideration is mere number without regard to strength and weakness, or whether that is regarded. The majority hold that it is not regarded, due to the apparent meaning of the Qurʾān. As for the hadith of ʿUbādah — "We pledged to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, on the condition that we would not associate anything with Allah, nor steal," to the end — that was only in the early period, on the night of al-ʿAqabah, before the emigration from Mecca and before the obligation of jihād was prescribed. His saying: "I asked..."

chapters.title_en: Section 735 — The Tree of Allegiance, the Well of al-Hudaybiyyah, the Prohibition of the Emigrant's Return, and the Meaning of "No Hijrah After the Conquest"
chapters.arabic_text:
جابرا عن أصحاب الشجرة فقال لو كنا مائة ألف لكفانا كنا ألفا وخمسمائة) هذا

مختصر من الحديث الصحيح في بئر الحديبية ومعناه أن الصحابة لما وصلوا

الحديبية وجدوا بئرها إنما تنزه مثل  الشراك فبسق النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

فيها ودعا فيها
# 
# بالبركة فجاست فهي إحدى المعجزات لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فكأن

السائل في هذا الحديث علم أصل الحديث والمعجزة في تكثير الماء وغير ذلك مما

جرى فيها ولم يعلم عددهم فقال جابر كنا ألفا وخمسمائة ولو كنا مائة ألف أو

أكثر لكفانا وقوله في الرواية التي قبل هذه دعا على بئر الحديبية أي دعا

فيها بالبركة قوله في الشجرة
# [1859] (إنها خفي عليهم مكانها في العام المقبل) قال العلماء سبب خفائها

أن لا يفتتن الناس بها لما جرى تحتها من الخير ونزول الرضوان والسكينة وغير

ذلك فلو بقيت ظاهرة معلومة لخيف تعظيم الأعراب والجهال إياها وعبادتهم لها

فكان خفاؤها رحمة من الله تعالى
#

| (باب تحريم رجوع المهاجر إلى استيطان وطنه
# [1862] قوله (إن
# الحجاج قال لسلمة بن الأكوع رضي الله عنه ارتددت على عقبيك تعربت قال لا

ولكن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أذن لي في البدو) قال القاضي عياض أجمعت

الأمة على تحريم ترك المهاجر هجرته ورجوعه إلى وطنه وعلى أن ارتداد المهاجر

أعرابيا من الكبائر قال ولهذا أشار الحجاج إلى أن أعلمه سلمة أن خروجه إلى

البادية إنما هو بإذن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال ولعله رجع إلى غير وطنه

أو لأن الغرض في ملازمة المهاجر أرضه التي هاجر إليها وفرض ذلك عليه إنما

كان في زمن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لنصرته أو ليكون معه أو لأن ذلك إنما

كان قبل فتح مكة فلما كان الفتح وأظهر الله الإسلام على الدين كله وأذل

الكفر وأعز المسلمين سقط فرض الهجرة فقال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لا هجرة

بعد الفتح وقال مضت الهجرة لأهلها أي الذين هاجروا من ديارهم وأموالهم قبل

فتح مكة لمواساة النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ومؤازرته)
# 
# ونصرة دينه وضبط شريعته قال القاضي ولم يختلف العلماء في وجوب الهجرة على

أهل مكة قبل الفتح واختلف في غيرهم فقيل لم تكن واجبة على غيرهم بل  كانت

ندبا ذكره أبو عبيد في كتاب الأموال لأنه صلى الله عليه وسلم لم يأمر

الوفود عليه قبل الفتح بالهجرة وقيل إنما كانت واجبة على من لم يسلم كل أهل

بلدة لئلا يبقى فى طلوع أحكام الكفار

| (باب المبايعة بعد فتح مكة على الإسلام والجهاد 
# والخير وبيان معنى لا هجرة بعد الفتح
# [1863] قوله (أتيت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أبايعه على الهجرة فقال إن

الهجرة قد مضت لأهلها ولكن على الإسلام والجهاد والخير) معناه أن الهجرة

الممدوحة الفاضلة التي لأصحابها المزية الظاهرة)
# 
# إنما كانت قبل الفتح ولكن أبايعك على الإسلام والجهاد وسائر أفعال الخير

وهو من باب ذكر العام بعد الخاص فإن الخير أعم من الجهاد ومعناه أبايعك على

أن تفعل هذه الأمور
# [1353] قوله (قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يوم الفتح فتح مكة لا

هجرة ولكن جهاد ونية) وفي الرواية الأخرى لا هجرة بعد الفتح قال أصحابنا

وغيرهم من العلماء الهجرة من دار الحرب إلى دار الإسلام باقية إلى يوم

القيامة وتأولوا هذا الحديث تأويلين أحدهما لا هجرة بعد الفتح من مكة لأنها

صارت دار إسلام فلا تتصور منها الهجرة والثاني وهو الأصح أن معناه أن

الهجرة الفاضلة المهمة المطلوبة التي يمتاز بها أهلها امتيازا ظاهرا انقطعت

بفتح مكة ومضت لأهلها الذين هاجروا قبل فتح مكة لأن الإسلام قوي وعز بعد

فتح مكة عزا ظاهرا بخلاف ما قبله قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم
# [1864] (ولكن جهاد ونية) معناه أن تحصيل الخير بسبب الهجرة قد انقطع بفتح

مكة ولكن حصلوه بالجهاد والنية الصالحة وفي هذا الحث على نية الخير مطلقا

وأنه يثاب على النية قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (وإذا استنفرتم فانفروا)

معناه إذا طلبكم الإمام للخروج إلى الجهاد
# 
# فاخرجوا وهذا دليل على أن الجهاد ليس فرض عين بل فرض كفاية إذا فعله من

تحصل بهم الكفاية سقط الحرج عن الباقين وإن تركوه كلهم أثموا كلهم قال

أصحابنا الجهاد اليوم فرض كفاية إلا أن ينزل الكفار ببلد المسلمين فيتعين

عليهم  الجهاد فإن لم يكن في أهل ذلك البلد كفاية وجب على من يليهم تتميم

الكفاية وأما في زمن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فالأصح عند أصحابنا أنه كان

أيضا فرض كفاية والثاني أنه كان فرض عين واحتج القائلون بأنه كان فرض كفاية

بأنه كان تغزو السرايا وفيها بعضهم دون بعض قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم

للأعرابي الذي سأله عن الهجرة
# [1865] (إن شأن الهجرة لشديد فهل لك من إبل قال نعم قال فهل تؤتي صدقتها

قال نعم قال فاعمل من وراء البحار فإن الله لن يترك من عملك شيئا) أما يترك

فبكسر التاء معناه لن ينقصك من ثواب أعمالك شيئا حيث كنت قال العلماء

والمراد بالبحار هنا القرى والعرب تسمي القرى البحار والقرية البحيرة قال
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ن-ز-ه (n-z-h)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To be distant, elevated, pure; to withdraw from contamination
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Used for the well's water being scarce — its water "withdrew" from abundance, indicating paucity
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense of spatial elevation/distance; here metaphorical for scarcity of water
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clause (الشّرط) — "لو كنا مائة ألف" (if we had been a hundred thousand) governs a hypothetical apodosis, indicating sufficiency regardless of number

- Root: خ-ف-ي (kh-f-y)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To be concealed, hidden, imperceptible
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Divine concealment as mercy (raḥmah) — the veiling of the tree prevents fitnah (trial) and idolatrous veneration
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal concealment of location; metaphorical concealment of wisdom from the masses
- Sībawayh Rule: Causal Clause (التعليل) — "سبب خفائها أن لا يفتتن" (the cause of its concealment is that people not be tried) introduces a purpose clause with 'an' + subjunctive

- Root: ر-د-د (r-d-d)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To return, turn back, repel
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Apostasy (irtidād) — the technical term for abandoning the hijrah and reverting to Bedouin life
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal physical return; metaphorical religious regression
- Sībawayh Rule: Accusative of Specification (التمييز) — "ارتددت على عقبيك" (you have turned back on your heels) uses the prepositional phrase adverbially

- Root: ه-ج-ر (h-j-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To abandon, emigrate, sever ties
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The religious emigration from Dār al-Ḥarb to Dār al-Islām — a perpetual obligation with temporal modalities
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal physical migration; metaphorical spiritual severance from polytheism
- Sībawayh Rule: Exception (الاستثناء) — "لا هجرة بعد الفتح" (no hijrah after the conquest) is a general negation with specific application, requiring ta'wīl (interpretive qualification)
chapters.translation:
I say: Jābir's statement concerning the People of the Tree — "If we had been a hundred thousand, it would have sufficed us; we were one thousand five hundred" — this is an abridgment of the authentic ḥadīth concerning the well of al-Ḥudaybiyyah. Its meaning is that when the Companions (may Allah be pleased with them) arrived at al-Ḥudaybiyyah, they found its well yielding water only in the measure of a sandal-strap's trickle. The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) then spat into it and supplicated therein for blessing, whereupon it gushed forth abundantly. This is one of the miracles of the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him). It is as though the questioner in this ḥadīth knew the original report and the miracle of the multiplication of water and other occurrences that transpired there, but did not know their number. Thus Jābir said: "We were one thousand five hundred, and had we been a hundred thousand or more, it would have sufficed us."

His statement in the preceding narration, "He supplicated at the well of al-Ḥudaybiyyah," means he supplicated therein for blessing.

His statement concerning the tree — {[1859] "Indeed, its location was concealed from them in the following year"} — the scholars said: The cause of its concealment is that the people might not be tried by it, given the good that transpired beneath it, the descent of divine pleasure (al-riḍwān), tranquility (al-sakīnah), and other such matters. Had it remained visible and known, there would have been fear of the Bedouins and the ignorant venerating it and worshipping it. Thus its concealment was a mercy from Allah the Exalted.

---

**(Chapter: The Prohibition of the Emigrant's Return to Settling in His Homeland)**

{[1862] His statement: "Indeed, al-Ḥajjāj said to Salamah ibn al-Akwaʿ (may Allah be pleased with him): 'You have turned back on your heels; you have become a Bedouin.' He said: 'No, but the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) permitted me to live in the desert.'"}

Al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ said: The ummah is unanimous upon the prohibition of the emigrant abandoning his emigration and returning to his homeland, and upon the fact that the emigrant's reversion to Bedouin life is among the major sins (al-kabāʾir). He said: For this reason, al-Ḥajjāj indicated that Salamah informed him that his departure to the desert was only by the permission of the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him). He said: Perhaps he returned to other than his homeland, or because the purpose in the emigrant's adherence to the land to which he emigrated — and its being obligatory upon him — was only in the time of the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him), for his support, or to be with him, or because that was only before the conquest of Mecca. When the conquest occurred, and Allah manifested Islam over the entire religion, humiliated disbelief, and honored the Muslims, the obligation of emigration lapsed.
