Thus the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "There is no emigration after the conquest," and said: "Emigration has passed for its people" — meaning those who emigrated from their homes and wealth before the conquest of Mecca, for the consolation of the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him), his assistance, the support of his religion, and the preservation of his sacred law.

Al-Qāḍī said: The scholars did not differ concerning the obligation of emigration upon the people of Mecca before the conquest. They differed concerning others: It was said it was not obligatory upon others, but rather commendable (nadb) — Abū ʿUbayd mentioned this in Kitāb al-Amwāl, because the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) did not command the delegations that came to him before the conquest to emigrate. And it was said it was only obligatory upon one who was not a Muslim among the people of a town, lest he remain under the ascendancy of the rulings of the disbelievers.

---

**(Chapter: The Pledge of Allegiance After the Conquest of Mecca Upon Islam, Jihād, and Goodness, and the Clarification of the Meaning of "No Emigration After the Conquest")**

{[1863] His statement: "I came to the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) to pledge allegiance upon emigration, and he said: 'Indeed, emigration has passed for its people, but rather upon Islam, jihād, and goodness.'"}

Its meaning is that the praiseworthy, virtuous emigration — whose people possess the manifest distinction — was only before the conquest. But I pledge you upon Islam, jihād, and all acts of goodness. This is of the category of mentioning the general after the specific, for goodness is more general than jihād. Its meaning: I pledge you upon your performance of these matters.

{[1353] His statement: "The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said on the Day of the Conquest — the conquest of Mecca — 'There is no emigration, but rather jihād and intention.'" And in the other narration: "There is no emigration after the conquest."}

Our companions and other scholars said: Emigration from the abode of war to the abode of Islam remains until the Day of Resurrection. They interpreted this ḥadīth with two interpretations: First, there is no emigration after the conquest from Mecca, because it has become an abode of Islam, so emigration from it is inconceivable. The second — and it is the more correct (al-aṣaḥḥ) — is that its meaning is that the virtuous, important, sought-after emigration by which its people are distinguished with a manifest distinction ceased with the conquest of Mecca and passed for its people who emigrated before the conquest of Mecca, because Islam became strong and honored after the conquest of Mecca with a manifest honor, unlike what preceded it.

His statement (peace and blessings be upon him) {[1864] "But rather jihād and intention"} — its meaning is that the attainment of good through emigration has ceased with the conquest of Mecca, but attain it through jihād and sincere intention. In this is an exhortation upon intending good absolutely, and that one is rewarded for the intention.

His statement (peace and blessings be upon him): "And when you are summoned to mobilize, then mobilize" — its meaning is: When the leader (imām) requests you to go forth to jihād, then go forth. This is evidence that jihād is not an individual obligation (farḍ ʿayn) but rather a collective obligation (farḍ kifāyah). When those by whom sufficiency is achieved perform it, the burden falls from the rest; and if all abandon it, all are sinful. Our companions said: Jihād today is a collective obligation, except that if the disbelievers descend upon a land of the Muslims, it becomes individually obligatory upon them. If there is not sufficiency among the people of that land, then it is obligatory upon those adjacent to them to complete the sufficiency. As for the time of the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him), the more correct view (al-aṣaḥḥ) among our companions is that it was also a collective obligation; the second view is that it was an individual obligation. Those who held it was a collective obligation adduced as proof that expeditions (al-sarāyā) would go forth with some of them and not others.

His statement (peace and blessings be upon him) to the Bedouin who asked him about emigration — {[1865] "Indeed, the matter of emigration is severe. Do you have camels? He said: Yes. He said: Do you pay their charity (ṣadaqah)? He said: Yes. He said: Then work from beyond the seas, for Allah will not leave anything of your deeds unrequited."}

As for "will not leave" (lā yatruk) — with the kasrah on the tāʾ — its meaning is: He will not diminish anything of the reward of your deeds, wherever you may be. The scholars said: The intended meaning of "seas" here is the villages (al-qurā), for the Arabs call villages "seas," and the village is called "al-buḥayrah."

العلماء والمراد بالهجرة التي سأل عنها هذا الأعرابي ملازمة المدينة مع

النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وترك أهله ووطنه فخاف عليه النبي صلى الله عليه

وسلم أن لا يقوى لها ولا يقوم بحقوقها وأن ينكص على عقبيه فقال له إن شأن

الهجرة التي سألت عنها لشديد ولكن اعمل بالخير في وطنك وحيث ما كنت فهو

ينفعك ولاينقصك الله منه شيئا والله أعلم
#

| (باب كيفية بيعة النساء
# [1866] قولها (كان المؤمنات إذا
# هاجرن يمتحن بقول الله تعالى يا أيها النبى إذا جاءك المؤمنات إلى آخره

معنى يمتحن يبايعهن على هذا المذكور في الآية الكريمة وقولها (فمن أقر بهذا

فقد أقر بالمحنة) معناه فقد بايع البيعة الشرعية قولها (والله ما مست يد

رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يد امرأة قط غير أنه يبايعهن بالكلام) فيه أن

بيعة النساء بالكلام من غير أخذ كف وفيه أن بيعة الرجال بأخذ الكف مع

الكلام وفيه أن كلام الأجنبية يباح سماعه عند الحاجة وأن صوتها ليس بعورة

وأنه لايلمس بشرة الأجنبية من غير ضرورة كتطبب وقصد وحجامة وقلع ضرس وكحل

عين ونحوها مما لا توجد امرأة تفعله جاز للرجل الأجنبي فعله للضرورة وفي قط

خمس لغات)
# 
# فتح القاف وتشديد الطاء مضمومة ومكسورة  وبضمهما والطاء مشددة وفتح القاف

مع تخفيف الطاء ساكنة ومكسورة وهي لنفي الماضي قولها في الرواية الأخرى (ما

مس رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بيده امرأة قط إلا أن يأخذ عليها فإذا أخذ

عليها فأعطته قال اذهبي فقد بايعتك) هذا الاستثناء منقطع وتقدير الكلام ما

مس امرأة قط لكن يأخذ عليها البيعة بالكلام فإذا أخذها بالكلام قال اذهبي

فقد بايعتك وهذا التقدير مضرح به في الرواية الأولى ولا بد منه والله أعلم

| (باب البيعة على السمع والطاعة فيما استطاع
# [1867] قوله (كنا
# نبايع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم على السمع والطاعة يقول لنا فيما

استطعت) هكذا هو في جميع النسخ فيما استطعت أي قل فيما استطعت وهذا من كمال

شفقته صلى الله عليه وسلم ورأفته بأمته يلقنهم أن يقول أحدهم فيما استطعت

لئلا يدخل في عموم بيعة مالا يطيقه وفيه أنه إذا رأى الإنسان من يلتزم مالا

يطيقه ينبغي أن يقول له لا تلتزم مالا تطيق فيترك بعضه وهو من نحو قوله صلى

الله عليه وسلم عليكم من الأعمال ما تطيقون)
#

| (باب بيان سن البلوغ وهو السن الذي يجعل صاحبه من 
# المقاتلين ويجري عليه حكم الرجال في أحكام القتال وغير ذلك
# [1868] قوله (عن بن عمر أنه عرض على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يوم أحد

وهو بن أربع عشرة سنة فلم يجزه وعرض عليه يوم الخندق وهو بن خمس عشرة سنة

فأجازه) هذا دليل لتحديد البلوغ بخمس عشرة سنة وهو مذهب الشافعي والأوزاعى

وبن وهب وأحمد وغيرهم قالوا باستكمال خمس عشرة سنة يصير مكلفا وإن لم يحتلم

فتجري عليه الأحكام من وجوب العبادة وغيره ويستحق سهم الرجل من الغنيمة

ويقتل إن كان من أهل الحرب وفيه دليل على أن الخندق كانت سنة أربع من

الهجرة وهو الصحيح وقال جماعة من أهل السير والتواريخ كانت سنة خمس وهذا

الحديث يرده لأنهم أجمعوا على أن أحدا كانت سنة ثلاث فيكون الخندق سنة أربع

لأنه جعلها في هذا الحديث بعده بسنة قوله  (لم يجزني وأجازني) المراد جعله

رجلا له حكم الرجال المقاتلين)
#

| (باب النهي أن يسافر بالمصحف إلى أرض الكفار إذا خيف 
# وقوعه بأيديهم)
# [1869] قوله (نهى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أن يسافر بالقرآن إلى أرض

العدو) وفي الرواية الأخرى مخافة أن يناله العدو وفي الرواية الأخرى فإني

لا آمن أن يناله العدو فيه النهي عن المسافرة بالمصحف إلى أرض الكفار للعلة

المذكورة في الحديث وهي خوف أن ينالوه فينتهكوا حرمته فإن أمنت هذه العلة

بأن يدخل في جيش المسلمين الظاهرين عليهم فلا كراهة ولا منع منه حينئذ لعدم

العلة هذا هو الصحيح وبه قال أبو حنيفة والبخاري وآخرون وقال مالك وجماعة

من أصحابنا بالنهى مطلقا وحكى بن المنذر عن أبي حنيفة الجواز مطلقا والصحيح

عنه ما سبق وهذه العلة المذكورة في الحديث هي من كلام النبي صلى الله عليه

وسلم وغلط بعض المالكية فزعم أنها من كلام مالك واتفق العلماء على أنه يجوز

أن يكتب
# 
# إليهم كتاب فيه آية أو آيات والحجة فيه كتاب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

إلى هرقل قال القاضي وكره مالك وغيره معاملة الكفار بالدراهم والدنانير

التي فيها اسم الله تعالى وذكره سبحانه وتعالى

| (باب المسابقة بين الخيل وتضميرها)
# فيه ذكر حديث مسابقة النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بين الخيل المضمرة وغير

المضمرة وفيه جواز المسابقة بين الخيل وجواز تضميرها وهما مجمع عليهما

للمصلحة في ذلك وتدريب الخيل ورياضتها وتمرنها على الجري وإعدادها لذلك

لينتفع بها عند الحاجة في القتال كرا وفرا واختلف العلماء في أن المسابقة

بينهما مباحة أم مستحبة ومذهب أصحابنا أنها مستحبة لما ذكرناه وأجمع

العلماء على جواز المسابقة بغير عوض بين جميع أنواع الخيل قويها مع ضعيفها
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ل-ز-م (l-z-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To cling, adhere, remain attached; mulāzama denotes constant companionship and staying put.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In legal-theological context, it implies obligatory adherence to a place or covenant.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) for physical remaining; metaphorical (majāz) for steadfastness in obedience.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clause (al-sharṭ) — The protasis (condition) and apodosis (result) structure governs the legal hypotheticals in the ḥadīth commentary.
chapters.translation:
I say: The scholars (may Allah have mercy on them) hold that the hijrah (emigration) about which this Bedouin inquired means remaining perpetually in Medina alongside the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him), abandoning his family and homeland. The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) feared that he would not have the strength for it, nor fulfill its obligations, and that he would turn back on his heels (revert to his former state). Thus he said to him: "Verily, the matter of the hijrah you asked about is indeed severe. However, do good in your homeland and wherever you may be, for it will benefit you, and Allah will not diminish anything of your reward thereby." And Allah knows best.

---

CHAPTER: The Manner of the Women's Oath of Allegiance (Bayʿah)

[1866] Her saying: "When the believing women emigrated, they were examined (yumtaḥanna) by the saying of Allah the Exalted: {«O Prophet, when the believing women come to you...»} (Qur'an 60:12) to the end of the verse."

The meaning of "they were examined" (yumtaḥanna) is that he (peace and blessings be upon him) would take their pledge of allegiance (yubāyiʿuhunna) upon what is mentioned in the noble verse. Her saying: "Whoever acknowledged this, then he has acknowledged the examination (al-miḥnah)" means: he has thereby given the legally valid oath of allegiance (al-bayʿah al-sharʿiyyah). Her saying: "By Allah, the hand of the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) never touched the hand of any woman, except that he would take their allegiance by speech (al-kalām)" — In this [ḥadīth] there is [proof] that the women's oath of allegiance is by speech without the taking of the palm [in handshake]. And in it there is [proof] that the men's oath of allegiance is by taking the palm along with speech. And in it there is [proof] that hearing the speech of a non-mahram woman is permissible when there is a need, and that her voice is not ʿawrah (a part of the body that must be covered). And that it is not permissible to touch the skin of a non-mahram woman without necessity — such as medical treatment, cupping (ḥijāmah), tooth extraction, applying kohl to the eye, and similar acts which no woman is available to perform — then it is permissible for a non-mahram man to do so out of necessity. In the word "qaṭṭ" (ever) there are five variant pronunciations: with the opening of the qāf and the doubling of the ṭāʾ, both ḍammah (u) and kasrah (i); and with both ḍammah and kasrah while the ṭāʾ is doubled; and with the opening of the qāf while the ṭāʾ is lightened, both with sukūn and kasrah. It is used for the negation of the past.

Her saying in the other narration: "The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) never touched a woman with his hand, except that he would take [the pledge] from her. When he took [the pledge] from her and she gave him [her word], he said: 'Go, for I have accepted your allegiance.'" This exception (istithnāʾ) is disconnected (munqaṭiʿ), and the estimated meaning (taqdīr al-kalām) is: "He never touched a woman, but he would take the allegiance by speech. When he took it by speech, he said: 'Go, for I have accepted your allegiance.'" This estimation is made explicit in the first narration, and it is indispensable. And Allah knows best.

---

CHAPTER: The Oath of Allegiance on Hearing and Obedience in What One Is Able

[1867] His saying: "We used to pledge allegiance to the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) on hearing and obedience, and he would say to us: 'In what you are able' (fīmā istaṭaʿt)." Thus it is in all copies: "fīmā istaṭaʿt" — meaning: say "in what I am able." This is from the perfection of his compassion (peace and blessings be upon him) and his mercy upon his nation — he would teach them that each one should say "in what I am able," so that one does not enter into the general scope of the pledge that which he cannot bear. And in it there is [proof] that when a person sees someone undertaking what he cannot bear, he should say to him: "Do not undertake what you cannot bear," so that he does not abandon part of it. This is akin to his saying (peace and blessings be upon him): "Upon you are the deeds which you are able to endure."

---

CHAPTER: Clarifying the Age of Puberty (Bulūgh) — The Age at Which One Becomes a Combatant and Upon Which the Rulings of Men Apply in Matters of Fighting and Otherwise

[1868] His saying: "On the authority of Ibn ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with him) that he was presented to the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) on the Day of Uḥud when he was fourteen years old, and he did not permit him [to fight]. And he was presented to him on the Day of al-Khandaq (the Trench) when he was fifteen years old, and he permitted him." This is evidence for determining puberty at fifteen years — and this is the school (madhhab) of al-Shāfiʿī, al-Awzāʿī, Ibn Wahb, Aḥmad, and others. They said: upon completing fifteen years, one becomes legally accountable (mukallaf) even if he has not had a wet dream (iḥtilām). Thus the rulings apply to him — the obligation of worship and other matters — and he deserves the share of a man from the spoils of war (ghanīmah), and he may be killed if he is among the people of war. And in it there is evidence that al-Khandaq occurred in the fourth year of the Hijrah — and this is the correct [view]. A group of the people of sīrah (biography) and history said it was in the fifth year. This ḥadīth refutes them, because they are unanimous that Uḥud was in the third year, so al-Khandaq must be in the fourth year, since this ḥadīth places it one year after Uḥud. His saying: "He did not permit me and he permitted me" — the intended meaning is that he made him a man with the rulings of fighting men.

---

CHAPTER: The Prohibition of Traveling with the Muṣḥaf to the Lands of the Disbelievers When There Is Fear That It May Fall into Their Hands

[1869] His saying: "The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) forbade traveling with the Qur'an to the land of the enemy." And in the other narration: "For fear that the enemy might reach it." And in yet another narration: "For I do not feel secure that the enemy might reach it." In this there is the prohibition of traveling with the muṣḥaf to the lands of the disbelievers due to the reason (ʿillah) mentioned in the ḥadīth — namely, the fear that they might obtain it and thereby violate its sanctity. If this reason is rendered secure — such as entering with the army of the Muslims who are victorious over them — then there is no dislike (karāhah) nor prohibition at that time, due to the absence of the reason. This is the correct [view], and it is the position of Abū Ḥanīfah, al-Bukhārī, and others. Mālik and a group of our companions (the Shāfiʿīs) held the prohibition absolutely. Ibn al-Mundhir reported from Abū Ḥanīfah the absolute permissibility, but the correct [view] from him is what preceded. This reason mentioned in the ḥadīth is from the speech of the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him). Some Mālikīs erred and claimed it was from the speech of Mālik. The scholars are unanimous that it is permissible to write to them a letter containing a verse or verses — and the proof for this is the letter of the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) to Heraclius. Al-Qāḍī said: Mālik and others disliked dealing with the disbelievers using dirhams and dīnārs upon which the name of Allah the Exalted and His remembrance (glorified and exalted be He) are inscribed.

---

CHAPTER: Horse Racing and Their Training (Taḍmīr)

In this [chapter] there is the mention of the ḥadīth of the Prophet's (peace and blessings be upon him) racing between trained horses (al-khayl al-muḍammarah) and untrained ones. In it there is [proof of] the permissibility of racing between horses and the permissibility of training them — both of which are agreed upon (mujmaʿ ʿalayhā) due to the benefit in that, and the drilling of horses, their exercise, their practice in running, and preparing them for that, so that they may be benefited from at the time of need in battle — in attack and retreat. The scholars differed as to whether racing between them is permissible (mubāḥ) or recommended (mustaḥabb). The school of our companions (the Shāfiʿīs) is that it is recommended, for what we have mentioned. And the scholars are unanimous on the permissibility of racing without a stake (ʿiwaḍ) between all types of horses — the strong among them with the weak.

chapters.arabic_text:
وسابقها مع غيره سواء كان معها ثالث أم لا فأما المسابقة بعوض فجائزة

بالإجماع لكن يشترط أن يكون العوض من غير المتسابقين أو يكون بينهما ويكون

معهما محلل وهو ثالث على فرس مكافئ لفرسيهما ولا يخرج المحلل من عنده شيئا

ليخرج هذا العقد عن صورة  القمار وليس في هذا الحديث ذكر عوض في المسابقة
# [1870] قوله (سابق بالخيل التي أضمرت) يقال أضمرت وضمرت وهو أن يقلل

علفها مدة وتدخل بيتا كنينا وتجلل فيه لتعرق ويجف عرقها فيجف لحمها وتقوى

على الجري قوله (من الحفياء إلى ثنية الوداع) هي بحاء مهملة وفاء ساكنة

وبالمد والقصر حكاهما القاضي وآخرون القصر أشهر والحاء مفتوحة بلا خلاف

وقال صاحب المطالع وضبطه بعضهم بضمها قال وهو خطأ قال الحازمي في المؤتلف

ويقال فيها أيضا الحيفاء بتقديم الياء على الفاء والمشهور المعروف في كتب

الحديث وغيرها الحفياء قال سفيان بن عيينة بين ثنية الوداع والحفياء خمسة

أميال أو ستة وقال موسى بن عقبة ستة أو سبعة وأما ثنية الوداع فهي عند

المدينة سميت بذلك لأن الخارج من المدينة يمشي معه المودعون إليها
# 
# قوله (مسجد بني زريق) بتقديم الزاي وفيه دليل لجواز قول مسجد فلان ومسجد

بني فلان وقد ترجم له البخاري بهذه الترجمة وهذه الإضافة للتعريف قوله

(وحدثني زهير بن حرب حدثنا إسماعيل عن أيوب عن نافع عن بن عمر) هكذا هو في

جميع النسخ قال أبو علي الغساني وذكره أبو مسعود الدمشقي عن مسلم عن زهير

بن حرب عن إسماعيل بن علية عن أيوب عن بن نافع عن نافع عن بن عمر فزاد بن

نافع قال والذي قاله أبو مسعود محفوظ عن الجماعة من أصحاب بن علية قال

الدارقطني في كتاب العلل في هذا الحديث يرويه أحمد بن حنبل وعلي بن المديني

وداود عن بن علية عن أيوب عن بن نافع عن نافع عن بن عمر وهذا شاهد لما ذكره

أبو مسعود ورواه جماعة عن زهير عن بن علية عن أيوب عن نافع كما رواه مسلم

من غير ذكر بن نافع قوله
# 
# (عن بن عمر فجئت سابقا فطفف بي الفرس المسجد) أى علا وثب إلى المسجد وكان

جداره قصيرا وهذا بعد مجاوزته الغاية لأن الغاية هي هذا المسجد وهو مسجد

بني زريق والله أعلم

| باب فضيلة الخيل وأن الخير معقود بنواصيها 
# [1871] قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (الخيل معقود بنواصيها الخير إلى يوم

القيامة الأجر والغنيمة) وفي رواية الخير معقوص بنواصي الخيل وفي رواية

البركة في نواصي الخيل المعقود والمعقوص بمعنى ومعناه ملوي مضفور فيها

والمراد بالناصية هنا الشعر المسترسل على الجبهة قال الخطابي وغيره قالوا

وكنى بالناصية عن جميع ذات الفرس يقال فلان مبارك الناصية ومبارك الغرة أي

الذات وفي هذه الأحاديث استحباب رباط الخيل واقتنائها للغزو وقتال أعداء

الله وأن فضلها وخيرها والجهاد باق إلى يوم القيامة وأما الحديث الآخر

الشؤم قد يكون في الفرس فالمراد به غير الخيل المعدة للغزو ونحوه أو أن

الخير والشؤم يجتمعان فيها فإنه فسر الخير بالأجر والمغنم ولايمتنع مع هذا

أن يكون
# 
# الفرس مما يتشاءم به
# [1872] قوله (رأيت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يلوي ناصية فرس بإصبعه)

قال القاضي فيه استحباب خدمة الرجل فرسه المعدة للجهاد
# [1873] قوله (عن عروة البارقي) هو بالموحدة
# 
# والقاف وهو منسوب إلى بارق وهو جبل باليمن تركته الأزد وهم الأسد بإسكان

السين فنسبوا إليه وقيل إلى بارق بن عوف بن عدي ويقال له عروة بن الجعد كما

وقع في رواية مسلم وعروة بن أبي الجعد وعروة بن عياض بن أبي الجعد

| باب ما يكره من صفات الخيل
# [1875] قوله (كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يكره الشكال من الخيل)

وفسره في الرواية الثانية بأن يكون في رجله اليمنى بياض وفي يده اليسرى أو

يده اليمنى ورجله اليسرى وهذا التفسير أحد الأقوال في الشكال وقال أبو عبيد

وجمهور أهل اللغة والغريب هو أن يكون منه ثلاث قوائم محجلة وواحدة
# 
# مطلقة تشبيها بالشكال الذي تشكل به الخيل فإنه يكون في ثلاث قوائم غالبا

قال أبو عبيد وقد يكون الشكال ثلاث قوائم مطلقة وواحدة محجلة قال ولاتكون

المطلقة من الأرجل أو المحجلة إلا الرجل وقال بن دريد الشكال أن يكون محجلا

من شق واحد في يده ورجله فإن كان مخالفا قيل الشكال مخالف قال القاضي قال

أبو عمرو المطرز قيل الشكال بياض  الرجل اليمنى واليد اليمنى وقيل بياض

الرجل اليسرى واليد اليسرى وقيل بياض اليدين وقيل بياض الرجلين وقيل بياض

الرجلين ويد واحدة وقيل بياض اليدين ورجل واحدة وقال العلماء إنما كرهه

لأنه على صورة المشكول وقيل يحتمل أن يكون قد جرب ذلك الجنس فلم يكن فيه

نجابة قال بعض العلماء إذا كان مع ذلك أغر زالت الكراهة لزوال شبه الشكال

| (باب فضل الجهاد والخروج في سبيل الله)
# [1876] قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (تضمن الله لمن خرج في سبيله لا يخرجه

إلا جهادا إلى قوله أن أدخله
# 
# الجنة) وفي الرواية الأخرى تكفل الله ومعناهما أوجب الله تعالى له الجنة
chapters.anchors:
- Root: س-ب-ق (s-b-q)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Precedence, outstripping, racing; the act of surpassing in a contest of speed.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In legal-theological terms, a contractual competition (musābaqah) with a stipulated prize, distinct from gambling (qimār) by the presence of a lawful condition.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) for physical racing; metaphorical (majāz) for precedence in virtue or divine reward.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clause (al-sharṭ wa al-jawāb) — The permissibility of the wager is parsed as a conditional legal ruling, where the condition (the third party's horse being equivalent) governs the validity of the contract.
chapters.translation:
I say: And the one who races against it [the horse] with another — whether there is a third with them or not — as for racing with a wager (ʿiwaḍ), it is permissible by consensus (ijmāʿ). However, it is a condition that the wager come from someone other than the two racers, or that it be between them, and that there be with them a "legalizer" (muḥallil) — a third person on a horse equivalent to their two horses — and the legalizer must not contribute anything from his own wealth, so that this contract is removed from the form of gambling (qimār). And in this hadith, there is no mention of a wager in the racing.

# [1870] His saying (peace be upon him): "He raced with horses that had been made lean (aḍmart)" — It is said "aḍmart" and "ḍammart," meaning that one reduces their fodder for a period, and brings them into a sheltered house, and covers them therein so that they sweat, and their sweat dries, and their flesh becomes firm, and they become strong for running. His saying: "From al-Ḥafyāʾ to Thaniyyat al-Wadāʿ" — It is with an unpointed ḥāʾ (ḥ) and a silent fāʾ (f), and with both prolongation (mad) and shortening (qaṣr); al-Qāḍī and others have narrated both, but the shortening is more famous, and the ḥāʾ is open (fatḥah) without dispute. The author of al-Maṭāliʿ said: Some have recorded it with ḍammah (u), and he said that is an error. Al-Ḥāzimī said in al-Muʾtalif: It is also said in it "al-Ḥayfāʾ" with the yāʾ preceding the fāʾ, but the famous and well-known form in the books of hadith and others is "al-Ḥafyāʾ." Sufyān ibn ʿUyaynah said: Between Thaniyyat al-Wadāʿ and al-Ḥafyāʾ is five or six miles. Mūsā ibn ʿUqbah said: Six or seven. As for Thaniyyat al-Wadāʿ, it is near Medina, so named because the one departing from Medina is accompanied by those bidding him farewell (al-muwaddiʿūn) to it.

# His saying: "The mosque of Banī Zurayq" — with the zāy (z) preceding. In this is evidence for the permissibility of saying "the mosque of so-and-so" and "the mosque of Banī so-and-so." Al-Bukhārī has titled a chapter with this very title, and this attribution is for definition (taʿrīf). His saying: "And ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Muʿādh narrated to me — Shuʿbah narrated to us from ʿĀṣim ibn ʿUbayd Allāh — from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿĀmir — from Ibn ʿUmar" — Thus it is in all copies. Abū ʿAlī al-Ghassānī said: Abū Masʿūd al-Dimashqī mentioned it from Muslim, from Zuhayr ibn Ḥarb, from Ismāʿīl ibn ʿUlayyah, from Ayyūb, from Ibn Nāfiʿ, from Nāfiʿ, from Ibn ʿUmar, and thus he added Ibn Nāfiʿ. And what Abū Masʿūd said is preserved (maḥfūẓ) from the group of companions of Ibn ʿUlayyah. Al-Dāraquṭnī said in his book al-ʿIlal regarding this hadith: Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal, ʿAlī ibn al-Madīnī, and Dāwūd narrate it from Ibn ʿUlayyah, from Ayyūb, from Ibn Nāfiʿ, from Nāfiʿ, from Ibn ʿUmar — and this is a witness to what Abū Masʿūd mentioned. And a group narrated it from Zuhayr, from Ibn ʿUlayyah, from Ayyūb, from Nāfiʿ, just as Muslim narrated it, without mentioning Ibn Nāfiʿ. His saying:

# "From Ibn ʿUmar: 'So I came as a winner, and the horse leapt with me into the mosque'" — That is, it rose and jumped into the mosque, and its wall was short. And this was after it had passed the goal (ghāyah), because the goal is this mosque — the mosque of Banī Zurayq. And Allāh knows best.

| Chapter: On the Virtue of Horses, and that Goodness is Tied to Their Forelocks

# [1871] His saying (peace be upon him): "Horses — goodness is tied to their forelocks until the Day of Resurrection: reward and spoils." And in another narration: "Goodness is braided (maʿqūṣ) into the forelocks of horses." And in another: "Blessing is in the forelocks of horses." "Al-maʿqūd" and "al-maʿqūṣ" are synonymous, meaning twisted and plaited therein. What is meant by "forelock" (nāṣiyah) here is the hair that hangs down over the forehead. Al-Khaṭṭābī and others said: They used the forelock metaphorically for the entire essence of the horse. It is said: "So-and-so is blessed of forelock" and "blessed of blaze (ghurrah)," i.e., blessed of essence. In these hadiths is the recommendation (istihbāb) of keeping horses and acquiring them for raiding (ghazw) and fighting the enemies of Allāh, and that their virtue and goodness, and that jihad remains until the Day of Resurrection. As for the other hadith — "ill luck (shuʾm) may be in a horse" — what is meant by it is other than horses prepared for raiding and the like, or that good and ill luck may be combined in it, for he interpreted "good" as reward and spoils, and it is not impossible, along with this, that the horse be one from which one seeks an omen of ill.

# [1872] His saying: "I saw the Messenger of Allāh (peace be upon him) twisting the forelock of a horse with his finger" — Al-Qāḍī said: In it is the recommendation of a man serving his horse prepared for jihad.

# [1873] His saying: "From ʿUrwah al-Bāriqī" — It is with a single-pointed bāʾ (b) and qāf (q), and he is attributed to Bāriq, which is a mountain in Yemen that the Azd tribe — they are al-Azd with a silent sīn (s) — left, and so they were attributed to it. And it is said: attributed to Bāriq ibn ʿAwf ibn ʿAdī. And he is called ʿUrwah ibn al-Jaʿd, as occurs in Muslim's narration, and ʿUrwah ibn Abī al-Jaʿd, and ʿUrwah ibn ʿIyāḍ ibn Abī al-Jaʿd.

| Chapter: On What is Disliked of the Characteristics of Horses

# [1875] His saying: "The Messenger of Allāh (peace be upon him) disliked shikāl in horses" — And he explained it in the second narration as being: whiteness in its right hind leg and its left foreleg, or its right foreleg and its left hind leg. And this explanation is one of the sayings regarding shikāl. Abū ʿUbayd and the majority of the people of language and of strange (gharīb) [lexicography] said: It is that three of its legs be white-stockinged (muḥajjal) and one be unmarked (muṭlaq), by analogy to the hobble (shikāl) with which horses are hobbled, for it is mostly on three legs. Abū ʿUbayd said: And shikāl may be three legs unmarked and one white-stockinged. He said: And the unmarked or white-stockinged one is only the hind leg. Ibn Durayd said: Shikāl is that it be white-stockinged on one side — in its foreleg and hind leg; if it is opposite, it is called "opposite shikāl." Al-Qāḍī said: Abū ʿAmr al-Muṭarriz said: It is said shikāl is whiteness of the right hind leg and right foreleg; and it is said: whiteness of the left hind leg and left foreleg; and it is said: whiteness of both forelegs; and it is said: whiteness of both hind legs; and it is said: whiteness of both hind legs and one foreleg; and it is said: whiteness of both forelegs and one hind leg. And the scholars said: He only disliked it because it is in the form of the hobbled (mashkūl). And it is said: Perhaps he had tested that type [of horse] and found no excellence (najābah) in it. Some scholars said: If, along with that, it has a blaze (agharr), the dislike is removed, because the resemblance to the hobble is removed.

| (Chapter: On the Virtue of Jihad and Going Forth in the Path of Allāh)

# [1876] His saying (peace be upon him): "Allāh has guaranteed (ḍamina) for the one who goes forth in His path — nothing sends him forth but jihad — up to his saying: 'that He admit him into Paradise.'" And in the other narration: "Allāh has undertaken (takaffala)" — and their meaning is: Allāh, the Exalted, has made obligatory for him Paradise.

chapters.title_en: Section 738 — The Virtue of Martyrdom in the Path of Allah (باب فضل الشهادة في سبيل الله تعالى)
chapters.arabic_text:
بفضله وكرمه سبحانه وتعالى وهذا الضمان والكفالة موافق لقوله تعالى إن الله

اشترى من المؤمنين أنفسهم وأموالهم بأن لهم الجنة الآية قوله سبحانه وتعالى

(لا يخرجه إلا جهادا في سبيلي) هكذا هو في جميع النسخ جهادا بالنصب وكذا

قال بعده وإيمانا بي وتصديقا وهو منصوب على أنه مفعول له وتقديره لا يخرجه

المخرج ويحركه المحرك إلا للجهاد والإيمان والتصديق قوله (لا يخرجه إلا

جهادا في سبيلي وإيمانا بي وتصديقا برسلي) معناه لا يخرجه إلا محض الإيمان

والإخلاص لله تعالى قوله في الرواية الأخرى (وتصديق كلمته) أي كلمة

الشهادتين وقيل تصديق كلام الله في الإخبار بما للمجاهد من عظيم ثوابه قوله

تعالى (فهو علي ضامن) ذكروا في ضامن هنا وجهين أحدهما أنه بمعنى مضمون كماء

دافق ومدفوق والثاني أنه بمعنى ذو ضمان قوله تعالى (أن أدخله الجنة) قال

القاضي يحتمل أن يدخل عند موته كما قال تعالى في الشهداء أحياء عند ربهم

يرزقون
# 
# وفي الحديث أرواح الشهداء في الجنة قال ويحتمل أن يكون المراد دخوله

الجنة عند دخول السابقين والمقربين بلا حساب ولا عذاب ولا مؤاخذة بذنب

وتكون الشهادة مكفرة لذنوبه كما صرح به في الحديث الصحيح قوله (أو أرجعه

إلى مسكنه نائلا ما نال من أجر أو غنيمة) قالوا معناه ما حصل له من الأجر

بلا غنيمة إن لم يغنم أو من الأجر  والغنيمة معا إن غنموا وقيل إن أو هنا

بمعنى الواو أي من أجر وغنيمة وكذا وقع بالواو في رواية أبي داود وكذا وقع

في مسلم في رواية يحيى بن يحيى التي بعد هذه بالواو ومعنى الحديث أن الله

تعالى ضمن أن الخارج للجهاد ينال خيرا بكل حال فإما أن يستشهد فيدخل الجنة

وإما أن يرجع بأجر وإما أن يرجع بأجر وغنيمة قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم

(والذي نفس محمد بيده مامن كلم يكلم في سبيل الله إلا جاء يوم القيامة

كهيئته حين كلم لونه لون دم وريحه مسك) أما الكلم بفتح الكاف وإسكان اللام

فهو الجرح ويكلم بإسكان الكاف أي يجرح وفيه دليل على أن الشهيد لايزول عنه

الدم بغسل ولاغيره والحكمة في مجيئه يوم القيامة على هيئته أن يكون معه

شاهد فضيلته وبذله نفسه في طاعة الله تعالى وفيه دليل على جواز اليمين

وانعقادها بقوله والذي نفسي بيده ونحو هذه الصيغة من الحلف بما يدل على

الذات ولا خلاف في هذا قال أصحابنا اليمين تكون بأسماء الله تعالى وصفاته

أو ما دل على ذاته قال القاضي واليد هنا
# 
# بمعنى القدرة والملك قوله (والذي نفس محمد بيده لولا أن يشق على المسلمين

ما قعدت خلاف سرية تغزو في سبيل الله) أي خلفها وبعدها وفيه ما كان عليه

صلى الله عليه وسلم من الشفقة على المسلمين والرأفة بهم وأنه كان يترك بعض

ما يختاره للرفق بالمسلمين وأنه إذا تعارضت المصالح بدأ بأهمها وفيه مراعاة

الرفق بالمسلمين والسعي في زوال المكروه والمشقة عنهم قوله (لوددت أن أغزو

في سبيل الله فأقتل ثم أغزو فأقتل ثم أغزو فأقتل) فيه فضيلة الغزو والشهادة

وفيه تمني الشهادة والخير وتمني ما لايمكن في العادة من الخيرات وفيه أن

الجهاد فرض كفاية لافرض عين قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (والله أعلم بمن يكلم

في سبيله) هذا تنبيه على الإخلاص في الغزو وأن الثواب المذكور فيه إنما هو

لمن أخلص فيه وقاتل لتكون كلمة الله هي العليا قالوا  وهذا الفضل وإن كان

ظاهره أنه في قتال الكفار فيدخل فيه من خرج في سبيل الله في قتال البغاة

وقطاع الطريق وفي إقامة الأمر بالمعروف والنهي عن المنكر ونحو ذلك والله

أعلم قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (وجرحه يثعب هو) بفتح الياء والعين وإسكان

المثلثة بينهما ومعناه يجري متفجرا أي كثيرا وهو بمعنى الرواية الأخرى

يتفجر دما قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (تكون يوم القيامة كهيئتها إذا طعنت)

الضمير في كهيئتها يعود على الجراحة وإذا طعنت بالألف بعد الذال كذا في

جميع النسخ قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (والعرف عرف المسك) هو
# 
# بفتح العين المهملة وإسكان الراء وهو الريح

| (باب فضل الشهادة في سبيل الله تعالى)
# [1877] قوله (حدثنا أبو خالد الأحمر عن شعبة عن قتادة وحميد عن أنس) قال

أبو علي الغساني ظاهر هذا الإسناد أن شعبة ترويه عن قتادة وحميد جميعا عن

أنس قال وصوابه أن أبا خالد يرويه عن حميد عن أنس ويرويه أبو خالد أيضا عن

شعبة عن قتادة عن أنس قال وهكذا قاله عبد الغني بن سعيد قال القاضي فيكون

حميد معطوفا على شعبة لا على قتادة قال وقد ذكره بن أبي شيبة في كتابه عن

أبي خالد عن حميد وشعبة عن قتادة عن أنس فبينه وإن كان فيه أيضا إيهام فإن

ظاهره أن حميدا يرويه عن قتادة وليس المراد كذلك بل المراد أن
# 
# حميدا يرويه عن أنس كما سبق قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (مامن نفس تموت لها

عند الله خير يسرها أنها ترجع إلى الدنيا ولاأن لها الدنيا وما فيها

الاالشهيد إلى آخره) هذا من صرائح الأدلة في عظيم فضل الشهادة والله

المحمود المشكور وأما سبب تسميته شهيدا فقال النضر بن شميل لأنه حي فإن
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ض-م-ن (ḍ-m-n)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning of inclusion, guarantee, and undertaking responsibility for another's affair.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological context, denotes Allah's binding promise (waʿd) as a secure covenant, not a contingent obligation.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense is "one who guarantees"; metaphorical extension here applies to divine assurance, as in «ضامن» meaning "guaranteed" (maḍmūn), like «ماء دافق» for "poured water."
- Root: ك-ل-م (k-l-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Primary sense is "wound" (jarḥ) with the form «كَلْم» (fatḥa on kāf, sukūn on lām); distinct from «كَلَام» (speech).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In the hadith context, the wound is a physical mark of sacrifice, carrying eschatological significance as a witness.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal wound; metaphorically, its preservation on the Day of Resurrection is a visible proof of virtue, not a literal bodily state.
- Root: ش-ه-د (sh-h-d)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Root meaning "to witness, be present"; the martyr (shahīd) is so named because he is alive and witnessing, or because Allah and angels witness his rank.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Technical term for one killed in Allah's path, whose soul is alive with Allah, as per {«أحياء عند ربهم يرزقون»}.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal "witness"; metaphorical extension to the martyr as a witness over his own sincerity and over the community.
- Sībawayh Rule: Naṣb on the Maʿfūl lahu (accusative of purpose) — «جهادا» and «إيمانا» are parsed as objects of purpose, with an implied verb like "nothing drives him out except for jihad," requiring the accusative case for the reason (ʿilla).
chapters.translation:
By His grace and bounty, He is glorified and exalted. This guarantee and suretyship accords with His saying, the Exalted: {«إن الله اشترى من المؤمنين أنفسهم وأموالهم بأن لهم الجنة»} (Indeed, Allah has purchased from the believers their lives and their properties, for that they will have Paradise) — the verse.

His saying, the Exalted and Glorified: (لا يخرجه إلا جهادا في سبيلي) — "Nothing drives him out except jihad in My path." Thus it appears in all copies: «جهادا» in the accusative (naṣb). Likewise, he said afterward: «وإيمانا بي وتصديقا» — "and faith in Me and belief" — and it is accusative as a maʿfūl lahu (object of purpose). Its estimated meaning: "Nothing drives him out, the driver, nor moves him, the mover, except for jihad, faith, and belief."

His saying: (لا يخرجه إلا جهادا في سبيلي وإيمانا بي وتصديقا برسلي) — "Nothing drives him out except jihad in My path, faith in Me, and belief in My messengers" — its meaning is: nothing drives him out except pure faith and sincere devotion (ikhlāṣ) to Allah, the Exalted.

His saying in the other narration: (وتصديق كلمته) — "and belief in His word" — meaning the word of the two testimonies (shahādatayn). And it is said: belief in Allah's speech concerning what He has informed of the immense reward of the mujāhid.

His saying, the Exalted: (فهو علي ضامن) — "then He is upon me a guarantor." They mentioned two aspects regarding «ضامن» here: First, that it means "guaranteed" (maḍmūn), like «ماء دافق» and «مدفوق» (poured water). Second, that it means "possessor of a guarantee" (dhū ḍamān).

His saying, the Exalted: (أن أدخله الجنة) — "that I admit him to Paradise." Al-Qāḍī said: It is possible that this occurs at his death, as the Exalted said regarding the martyrs: {«أحياء عند ربهم يرزقون»} (Alive with their Lord, provided for). And in the hadith: "The souls of the martyrs are in Paradise." He said: And it is possible that the intended meaning is his entry into Paradise at the time of the entry of the foremost and the near-stationed (al-sābiqūn wa al-muqarrabūn), without reckoning, without punishment, and without being taken to task for sin. And martyrdom becomes an expiation (mukaffira) for his sins, as explicitly stated in the authentic hadith.

His saying: (أو أرجعه إلى مسكنه نائلا ما نال من أجر أو غنيمة) — "or I return him to his dwelling, having attained what he attained of reward or spoils." They said: Its meaning is what accrued to him of reward without spoils if he did not gain spoils, or of reward and spoils together if they gained spoils. And it is said: «أو» (or) here carries the meaning of «الواو» (and), i.e., "of reward and spoils." Likewise, it occurs with the wāw in the narration of Abū Dāwūd, and likewise in Muslim in the narration of Yaḥyā ibn Yaḥyā which follows this one, with the wāw. The meaning of the hadith is that Allah, the Exalted, has guaranteed that the one who goes out for jihad attains good in every case: either he is martyred and enters Paradise, or he returns with reward, or he returns with reward and spoils.

His saying, peace and blessings be upon him: (والذي نفس محمد بيده ما من كلم يكلم في سبيل الله إلا جاء يوم القيامة كهيئته حين كلم لونه لون دم وريحه مسك) — "By Him in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, no one is wounded in the path of Allah but that he will come on the Day of Resurrection in the same state as when he was wounded: his color the color of blood, and his scent the scent of musk." As for «الكلم» with fatḥa on the kāf and sukūn on the lām, it is the wound. And «يكلم» with sukūn on the kāf means "he is wounded." In this is evidence that the martyr's blood does not depart from him by washing or anything else. The wisdom in his coming on the Day of Resurrection in that state is that he may bear with him a witness to his virtue and his offering of himself in obedience to Allah, the Exalted. In this is also evidence for the permissibility of the oath and its validity by his saying "By Him in whose hand is my soul" and similar formulas of swearing by what indicates the Essence (al-dhāt). There is no disagreement on this. Our companions (aṣḥābunā) said: The oath is by Allah's names and attributes, or by what indicates His Essence. Al-Qāḍī said: The "hand" here means power (qudra) and dominion (mulk).

His saying: (والذي نفس محمد بيده لولا أن يشق على المسلمين ما قعدت خلاف سرية تغزو في سبيل الله) — "By Him in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, were it not that it would be burdensome upon the Muslims, I would not remain behind any expedition (sariyya) that goes out to fight in the path of Allah" — meaning behind it and after it. In this is what the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, possessed of compassion (shafaqa) for the Muslims and mercy (raʾfa) toward them, and that he would abandon some of what he preferred for the sake of gentleness with the Muslims, and that when interests (maṣāliḥ) conflict, he would begin with the most important of them. In it is also the observance of gentleness toward the Muslims and striving to remove what is disliked and burdensome from them.

His saying: (لوددت أن أغزو في سبيل الله فأقتل ثم أغزو فأقتل ثم أغزو فأقتل) — "I would love to fight in the path of Allah and be killed, then fight and be killed, then fight and be killed" — in this is the virtue of raiding (ghazw) and martyrdom, and in it is the desiring of martyrdom and good, and the desiring of goods that are not ordinarily possible. And in it is that jihad is a communal obligation (farḍ kifāya), not an individual obligation (farḍ ʿayn).

His saying, peace and blessings be upon him: (والله أعلم بمن يكلم في سبيله) — "And Allah knows best who is wounded in His path" — this is a reminder of sincerity (ikhlāṣ) in raiding, and that the mentioned reward is only for the one who is sincere in it and fights so that the word of Allah may be the highest. They said: And this virtue, although its apparent scope is in fighting the disbelievers, includes the one who goes out in the path of Allah in fighting the rebels (al-bughāt) and highway robbers (quṭṭāʿ al-ṭarīq), and in establishing the enjoining of good and forbidding of evil, and similar matters. And Allah knows best.

His saying, peace and blessings be upon him: (وجرحه يثعب هو) — "and his wound gushes forth" — with fatḥa on the yāʾ and the ʿayn, and sukūn on the thāʾ between them. Its meaning: it flows abundantly, i.e., copiously. It is equivalent to the other narration: «يتفجر دما» (it bursts forth with blood).

His saying, peace and blessings be upon him: (تكون يوم القيامة كهيئتها إذا طعنت) — "it will be on the Day of Resurrection in the same state as when it was stabbed" — the pronoun in «كهيئتها» refers back to the wound (jarāḥa), and «إذا طعنت» with an alif after the dhāl, as in all copies.

His saying, peace and blessings be upon him: (والعرف عرف المسك) — "and the scent is the scent of musk" — with fatḥa on the ʿayn and sukūn on the rāʾ, meaning the odor (rīḥ).

| (Section: The Virtue of Martyrdom in the Path of Allah, the Exalted)

[1877] His saying: (حدثنا أبو خالد الأحمر عن شعبة عن قتادة وحميد عن أنس) — "Abū Khālid al-Aḥmar narrated to us from Shuʿba from Qatāda and Ḥumayd from Anas." Abū ʿAlī al-Ghassānī said: The apparent form of this chain (isnād) is that Shuʿba narrates it from Qatāda and Ḥumayd both, from Anas. He said: And the correct form is that Abū Khālid narrates it from Ḥumayd from Anas, and Abū Khālid also narrates it from Shuʿba from Qatāda from Anas. He said: And thus ʿAbd al-Ghanī ibn Saʿīd stated it. Al-Qāḍī said: Thus Ḥumayd is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to Shuʿba, not to Qatāda. He said: And Ibn Abī Shayba mentioned it in his book from Abū Khālid from Ḥumayd and Shuʿba from Qatāda from Anas, and he clarified it, although there is in it also an ambiguity (īhām), for its apparent form is that Ḥumayd narrates it from Qatāda, but that is not the intended meaning. Rather, the intended meaning is that Ḥumayd narrates it from Anas, as previously mentioned.

His saying, peace and blessings be upon him: (ما من نفس تموت لها عند الله خير يسرها أنها ترجع إلى الدنيا ولا أن لها الدنيا وما فيها إلا الشهيد) — "There is no soul that dies, having good with Allah, that would be pleased to return to this world, nor to have the world and all that is in it, except the martyr" — to the end of the hadith. This is among the clearest evidences of the immense virtue of martyrdom. And Allah is the Praised, the Thanked. As for the reason he is called a "martyr" (shahīd), al-Naḍr ibn Shumayl said: Because he is alive, for indeed...

chapters.title_en: The Souls of Martyrs Witness the Abode of Islam, and the Virtue of the Morning and Evening Journey in the Path of Allah
chapters.arabic_text:
أرواحهم شهدت وحضرت دار الاسلام وأرواح غيرهم إنما تشهدها يوم القيامة وقال

بن الأنباري إن الله تعالى وملائكته عليهم الصلاة والسلام يشهدون له بالجنة

وقيل لأنه شهد عند خروج روحه ما أعده الله تعالى له من الثواب والكرامة

وقيل  لأن ملائكة الرحمة يشهدونه فيأخذون روحه وقيل لأنه شهد له بالإيمان

وخاتمة الخير بظاهر حاله وقيل لأن عليه شاهدا بكونه شهيدا وهو الدم وقيل

لأنه ممن يشهد على الأمم يوم القيامة بإبلاغ الرسل الرسالة إليهم وعلى هذا

القول يشاركهم غيرهم في هذا الوصف
# [1878] قوله (ما يعدل الجهاد في سبيل الله قال لا تستطيعوه) هكذا هو في

معظم النسخ لاتستطيعوه وفي بعضها لا تستطيعونه
# 
# بالنون وهذا جار على اللغة المشهورة والأول صحيح أيضا وهي لغة فصيحة حذف

النون من غير ناصب ولاجازم وقد سبق بيانها ونظائرها مرات قوله صلى الله

عليه وسلم (مثل المجاهد في سبيل الله كمثل الصائم القائم القانت بآيات الله

إلى آخره) معنى القانت هنا المطيع وفي هذا الحديث عظيم فضل الجهاد لأن

الصلاة والصيام والقيام بآيات الله أفضل الأعمال وقد جعل المجاهد مثل من

لايفتر عن ذلك في لحظة من اللحظات ومعلوم أن هذا لايتأتى لأحد ولهذا قال

صلى الله عليه وسلم لاتستطيعونه والله أعلم
# [1879] قوله (إن عمر رضي الله عنه زجر الرجال الذين رفعوا أصواتهم يوم

الجمعة عند المنبر) فيه كراهة رفع الصوت فى المساجد يوم الجمعة وغيره وأنه

لايرفع الصوت بعلم ولاغيره عند اجتماع الناس للصلاة لما فيه من التشويش

عليهم وعلى المصلين والذاكرين والله أعلم
#

| (باب فضل الغدوة والروحة في سبيل الله)
# [1880] قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (لغدوة في سبيل الله أو روحة خير من

الدنيا وما فيها) الغدوة بفتح الغين السير أول النهار إلى الزوال والروحة

السير من الزوال إلى آخر النهار وأو هنا للتقسيم لا للشك ومعناه أن الروحة

يحصل بها هذا الثواب وكذا الغدوة والظاهر أنه لايختص ذلك بالغدو والرواح من

بلدته بل يحصل هذا الثواب بكل غدوة أو روحة في طريقه إلى الغزو وكذا غدوه

وروحة في موضع القتال لأن الجميع يسمى غدوة وروحة في سبيل الله ومعنى هذا

الحديث أن فضل الغدوة والروحة في سبيل الله وثوابهما خير من نعيم الدنيا

كلها لو ملكها انسان وتصور تنعمه بها كلها  لأنه زائل ونعيم الآخرة باق قال

القاضي وقيل في معناه ومعنى نظائره من تمثيل
# 
# أمور الآخرة وثوابها بأمور الدنيا أنها خيرمن الدنيا وما فيها لو ملكها

إنسان وملك جميع ما فيها وأنفقه في أمور الآخرة قال هذا القائل وليس تمثيل

الباقي بالفاني على ظاهر إطلاقه والله أعلم
# [1882] قوله (وحدثنا بن أبي عمر حدثنا مروان بن معاوية عن يحيى بن سعيد)

هكذا هو في جميع نسخ بلادنا وكذا نقله أبو علي الغساني عن رواية الجلودي

قال ووقع في نسخة بن ماهان حدثنا أبو بكر بن أبي شيبة حدثنا مروان فذكر بن

أبى شيبة بدل بن أبي عمر قال والصواب الأول
#

| باب بيان ما أعده الله تعالى للمجاهد فى الجنة من
# الدرجات)
# [1884] قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (وأخرى يرفع بها العبد مائة درجة في

الجنة ما بين كل درجتين كما بين السماء والأرض قال وما هي يا رسول الله قال

الجهاد في سبيل الله) قال القاضي عياض رضي الله عنه يحتمل أن هذا على ظاهره

وأن الدرجات هنا المنازل التي بعضها أرفع من بعض في الظاهر وهذه صفة منازل

الجنة كما جاء في أهل الغرف أنهم يتراءون كالكوكب الدري قال ويحتمل أن

المراد الرفعة بالمعنى من كثرة النعيم وعظيم الإحسان مما لم يخطر على قلب

بشر ولابصفة مخلوق وأن أنواع ما أنعم الله به عليه من البر والكرامة يتفاضل

تفاضلا كثيرا ويكون تباعده في الفضل كما بين السماء والأرض في البعد قال

القاضي والاحتمال الأول أظهر وهو كما قال والله أعلم
#

| (باب من قتل في سبيل الله كفرت خطاياه إلا الدين)
# قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم للذي سأله عن تكفير خطاياه إن قتل
# [1885] (نعم إن قتلت في سبيل الله وأنت صابر محتسب مقبل غير مدبر ثم

أعاده فقال إلا الدين فإن جبريل قال لي ذلك) فيه هذه الفضيلة العظيمة

للمجاهد وهى تكفير خطاياه كلها إلاحقوق الآدميين وإنما يكون تكفيرها بهذه

الشروط المذكورة وهو أن يقتل صابرا محتسبا مقبلا غير مدبر وفيه أن  الأعمال

لاتنفع إلابالنية والإخلاص لله تعالى قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (مقبل غير

مدبر) لعله احتراز ممن يقبل في وقت ويدبر في وقت والمحتسب هو المخلص لله

تعالى فإن قاتل لعصبية أو لغنيمة أو لصيت أو نحو ذلك فليس له هذا الثواب

ولاغيره وأما قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم ألا الدين ففيه تنبيه على جميع حقوق

الآدميين وأن الجهاد والشهادة وغيرهما من أعمال البر لا يكفر حقوق الآدميين

وإنما يكفر حقوق الله تعالى وأما قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم نعم ثم قال بعد

ذلك إلا الدين فمحمول على أنه أوحي إليه به في الحال ولهذا قال صلى الله
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ش-ه-د (sh-h-d)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To witness, to be present, to testify; presence of the eye or mind at an event.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Testimony (shahādah) as the highest form of certitude—both sensory presence and juridical attestation; in eschatology, the martyr's soul is a witness to its own honor.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) for physical presence; metaphorical (majāz) for the soul's spiritual attendance at the Abode of Islam.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clause (al-sharṭ wa al-jawāb) — The protasis "if killed" governs the apodosis "sins are expiated," with the exception clause (istithnāʾ) interrupting the sequence, as in "except debt."
chapters.translation:
I say: Their souls witnessed and attended the Abode of Islam, whereas the souls of others only witness it on the Day of Resurrection. Ibn al-Anbārī said: It means that Allah the Exalted and His angels, upon them be prayers and peace, testify for him with Paradise. And it was said: Because at the moment his soul departs, he witnesses what Allah the Exalted has prepared for him of reward and honor. And it was said: Because the angels of mercy witness him and take his soul. And it was said: Because he testified to faith and a good ending by his apparent state. And it was said: Because upon him there is a witness to his being a martyr—namely, the blood. And it was said: Because he is among those who will testify against the nations on the Day of Resurrection that the messengers conveyed the message to them; and upon this view, others share with them in this attribute.

# [1878] His saying, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: ("What equals jihad in the path of Allah?" He said: "You cannot do it.") — Thus it appears in most manuscripts: "lā tastaṭīʿūhu" (you cannot do it), and in some of them: "lā tastaṭīʿūnahu" with the nūn. This latter follows the well-known dialect, and the former is also correct, being an eloquent dialect in which the nūn is elided without any governing nāṣib or jāzim. We have already explained this and its parallels on multiple occasions. His saying, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: ("The example of the mujāhid in the path of Allah is like the example of the one who fasts, stands in prayer, and is qānit (devoutly obedient) to the verses of Allah," to the end of the hadith) — the meaning of qānit here is "obedient." In this hadith is the immense virtue of jihad, for prayer, fasting, and standing with the verses of Allah are the most virtuous of deeds, and the mujāhid has been made like one who does not slacken from that for a single moment. It is known that this is not attainable by anyone, and for this reason he said, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: "You cannot do it." And Allah knows best.

# [1879] His saying: ("Indeed ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, rebuked the men who raised their voices on Friday at the pulpit") — In this is the disapproval of raising the voice in mosques on Friday and at other times, and that one should not raise one's voice with knowledge or otherwise when people gather for prayer, because of the disturbance it causes to them and to those praying and those remembering Allah. And Allah knows best.

| (Chapter: The Virtue of the Morning and Evening Journey in the Path of Allah)

# [1880] His saying, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: ("A morning journey (ghadwah) in the path of Allah or an evening journey (rawḥah) is better than the world and all that is in it") — al-ghadwah, with the fatḥah on the ghayn, is the journey at the beginning of the day until noon, and al-rawḥah is the journey from noon until the end of the day. The "or" here is for division (taqsīm), not for doubt. Its meaning is that by the evening journey this reward is obtained, and likewise the morning journey. The apparent view is that this is not restricted to the morning and evening departure from one's own town; rather, this reward is obtained by every morning or evening journey on one's way to the raid, and likewise his morning and evening journey at the place of combat, because all of that is called a morning and evening journey in the path of Allah. The meaning of this hadith is that the virtue of the morning and evening journey in the path of Allah and their reward is better than all the delights of the world, were a man to possess them and imagine himself enjoying them entirely—because it is transitory, while the delight of the Hereafter is everlasting. Al-Qāḍī said: And it was said regarding its meaning and the meaning of its parallels, of likening the matters of the Hereafter and their reward to the matters of the world, that they are better than the world and all that is in it, were a man to possess it and possess all that is in it and spend it in the matters of the Hereafter. This speaker said: And the likening of the everlasting to the transitory is not upon its apparent unrestricted sense. And Allah knows best.

# [1882] His saying: ("And Ibn Abī ʿUmar narrated to us; Marwān ibn Muʿāwiyah narrated to us from Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd") — Thus it is in all the copies of our lands, and likewise Abū ʿAlī al-Ghassānī transmitted it from the narration of al-Julūdī. He said: And in the copy of Ibn Māhān it occurred: "Abū Bakr ibn Abī Shaybah narrated to us; Marwān narrated to us," mentioning Ibn Abī Shaybah instead of Ibn Abī ʿUmar. He said: And the correct one is the first.

| Chapter: The Explanation of What Allah the Exalted Has Prepared for the Mujāhid in Paradise of Degrees

# [1884] His saying, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: ("And another [thing] by which the servant is raised one hundred degrees in Paradise, between every two degrees of which is as [the distance] between the heaven and the earth." He said: "And what is it, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Jihad in the path of Allah.") — Al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ, may Allah be pleased with him, said: It is possible that this is upon its apparent meaning, and that the degrees here are the stations, some of which are higher than others in appearance, and this is the description of the stations of Paradise, as has come regarding the people of the chambers (al-ghuraf) that they see one another like a brilliant star. He said: And it is possible that what is meant is elevation in meaning, by the abundance of delight and the greatness of beneficence, of what has not occurred to the heart of any human nor to the description of any creature, and that the kinds of what Allah has bestowed upon him of piety and honor differ in excellence with great differentiation, and their distance in virtue is like the distance between the heaven and the earth in remoteness. Al-Qāḍī said: And the first possibility is more apparent. And it is as he said. And Allah knows best.

| (Chapter: Whoever Is Killed in the Path of Allah, His Sins Are Expiated Except Debt)

His saying, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, to the one who asked him about the expiation of his sins if he were killed:

# [1885] ("Yes, if you are killed in the path of Allah while being patient, seeking reward (muḥtasib), advancing and not retreating." Then he repeated it and said: "Except debt, for Gabriel said that to me.") — In this is this great virtue for the mujāhid, namely the expiation of all his sins except the rights of human beings. And its expiation is only with the mentioned conditions—that he be killed while patient, seeking reward, advancing and not retreating. And in this is that deeds do not avail except with intention and sincerity to Allah the Exalted. His saying, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: ("Advancing and not retreating") — perhaps it is a precaution against one who advances at one time and retreats at another. And al-muḥtasib is the one who is sincere to Allah the Exalted; for if one fights out of partisanship, or for booty, or for fame, or something like that, then he has neither this reward nor any other. As for his saying, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: "Except debt" — in this is a notification of all the rights of human beings, and that jihad, martyrdom, and other deeds of righteousness do not expiate the rights of human beings; rather, they only expiate the rights of Allah the Exalted. As for his saying, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: "Yes," then his saying after that: "Except debt" — it is understood that it was revealed to him at that very moment, and for this reason he said, may Allah bless him and grant him peace...

chapters.title_en: Section 740 — On the Explanation that the Souls of the Martyrs are in Paradise and that They are Alive with Their Lord, Provided For
chapters.arabic_text:
عليه وسلم إلاالدين فإن جبريل قال لي ذلك والله أعلم
# [1886] قوله (حدثنا سعيد بن منصور حدثنا سفيان عن عمرو بن دينار عن محمد

بن قيس قال
# 
# وحدثنا بن عجلان عن محمد بن قيس عن أبي عبد الله بن أبي قتادة) القائل

وحدثنا بن عجلان هو سفيان قوله (عن عياش بن عباس القتباني) الأول بالشين

المعجمة والثاني بالمهملة والقتباني بالقاف مكسورة ثم مثناة فوق ساكنة ثم

موحدة منسوب إلى قتبان بطن من رعين

| باب فى بيان أن أرواح الشهداء فى الجنة وأنهم احياء
# عند ربهم يرزقون)
# [1887] قوله (حدثني يحيى بن يحيى وأبو بكر بن أبي شيبة وذكر إسناده إلى

مسروق قال سألنا عبد الله
# 
# عن هذه الآية ولا تحسبن الذين قتلوا في سبيل الله أمواتا بل أحياء عند

ربهم يرزقون قال أما إنا قد سألنا عن ذلك فقال أرواحهم في جوف طير خضر) قال

المازري كذا جاء عبد الله غير منسوب قال أبو علي الغساني ومن الناس من

ينسبه فيقول عبد الله بن عمرو وذكره أبومسعود الدمشقى فى مسند بن مسعود قال

القاضي عياض ووقع في بعض النسخ من صحيح مسلم عبد الله بن مسعود قلت وكذا

وقع في بعض نسخ بلادنا المعتمدة ولكن لم يقع منسوبا في معظمها وذكره خلف

الواسطي والحميدي وغيرهما في مسند بن مسعود وهوالصواب وهذا الحديث مرفوع

لقوله  إنا قد سألنا عن ذلك فقال يعني النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قوله صلى

الله عليه وسلم في الشهداء (أرواحهم في جوف طير خضر لها قناديل معلقة

بالعرش تسرح من الجنة حيث شاءت ثم تأوي إلى تلك القناديل) فيه بيان أن

الجنة مخلوقة موجودة وهو مذهب أهل السنة وهي التي أهبط منها آدم وهي التي

ينعم فيها المؤمنون في الآخرة هذا إجماع أهل السنة وقالت المعتزلة وطائفة

من المبتدعة أيضا وغيرهم إنها ليست موجودة وإنما توجد بعد البعث في القيامة

قالوا والجنة التي أخرج منها آدم غيرها وظواهر القرآن والسنة تدل لمذهب أهل

الحق وفيه إثبات مجازاة الأموات بالثواب والعقاب قبل القيامة قال القاضي

وفيه أن الأرواح باقية لاتفنى فينعم المحسن ويعذب المسيء وقد جاء به القرآن

والآثار وهو مذهب أهل السنة خلافا لطائفة من المبتدعة قالت تفنى قال القاضي

وقال هنا أرواح الشهداء وقال في حديث مالك إنما نسمة المؤمن والنسمة تطلق

على ذات الإنسان جسما وروحا وتطلق على الروح مفردة وهو المراد بها فى هذا

التفسير في الحديث الآخر بالروح ولعلمنا بأن الجسم يفنى ويأكله التراب

ولقوله في الحديث حتى
# 
# يرجعه الله تعالى إلى جسده يوم القيامة قال القاضي وذكر في حديث مالك

رحمه الله تعالى نسمة المؤمن وقال هنا الشهداء لأن هذه صفتهم لقوله تعالى

أحياء عند ربهم يرزقون وكما فسره في هذا الحديث وأما غيرهم فإنما يعرض عليه

مقعده بالغداة والعشي كما جاء فى حديث بن عمر وكما قال في آل فرعون النار

يعرضون عليها غدوا وعشيا قال القاضي وقيل بل المراد جميع المؤمنين الذين

يدخلون الجنة بغير عذاب فيدخلونها الآن بدليل عموم الحديث وقيل بل أرواح

المؤمنين على أفنية قبورهم والله أعلم قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم في هذا

الحديث في جوف طير خضر وفي غير مسلم بطير خضر وفي حديث آخر بحواصل طير وفي

الموطأ إنما نسمة المؤمن طير وفي حديث آخر عن قتادة في صورة طير أبيض قال

القاضي قال بعض المتكلمين على  هذا الأشبه صحة قول من قال طير أو صورة طير

وهو أكثر ما جاءت به الرواية لاسيما مع قوله تأوي إلى قناديل تحت العرش قال

القاضي واستبعد بعضهم هذا ولم ينكره آخرون وليس فيه ما ينكر ولا فرق بين

الأمرين بل رواية طير أو جوف طير أصح معنى وليس للأقيسة والعقول في هذا حكم

وكله من المجوزات فإذا أراد الله أن يجعل هذه الروح إذا خرجت من المؤمن

أوالشهيد في قناديل أو أجواف طير أو حيث يشاء كان ذلك ووقع ولم يبعد لاسيما

مع القول بأن الأرواح أجسام قال القاضي وقيل إن هذا المنعم أو المعذب من

الأرواح جزء من الجسد تبقى فيه الروح وهو الذي يتألم ويعذب ويلتذ وينعم وهو

الذى يقول رب ارجعون وهو الذي يسرح في شجر الجنة فغير مستحيل أن يصور هذا

الجزء طائرا أو يجعل في جوف طائر وفي قناديل تحت العرش وغير ذلك مما يريد

الله عز وجل قال القاضي وقد اختلف الناس في الروح ما هي اختلافا لايكاد

يحصر فقال كثير من أرباب المعاني وعلم الباطن المتكلمين لاتعرف حقيقته

ولايصح وصفه وهو مما جهل العباد علمه واستدلوا بقوله تعالى قل الروح من أمر

ربي وغلت الفلاسفة فقالت بعدم الروح وقال جمهور الأطباء هو البخار اللطيف

الساري في البدن وقال كثيرون من شيوخنا هو الحياة وقال آخرون هي أجسام

لطيفة مشابكة للجسم يحيى لحياته أجرى الله تعالى العادة بموت الجسم عند

فراقه وقيل هو بعض الجسم ولهذا وصف بالخروج والقبض وبلوغ الحلقوم وهذه صفة

الأجسام لاالمعانى وقال بعض مقدمي أئمتنا هو جسم لطيف متصور على صورة

الإنسان داخل الجسم وقال بعض مشايخنا وغيرهم إنه النفس الداخل
# 
# والخارج وقال آخرون هو الدم هذا ما نقله القاضي والأصح عند أصحابنا أن
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ر-و-ح (r-w-ḥ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: The root denotes breath, wind, and that which animates; al-rūḥ is the principle of life that departs at death.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological usage, al-rūḥ is the subtle, life-giving substance created by Allah, distinct from the body; its survival after death is a matter of creed (ʿaqīdah).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage refers to the breath/wind; metaphorical (majāz) usage extends to the soul as the animating essence, and here it is used literally for the post-mortem entity.
- Root: ش-ه-د (sh-h-d)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To witness, be present, or testify; shahīd (martyr) is one whose testimony is sealed by death in Allah's path.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The shahīd is alive (ḥayy) in a specific, non-bodily sense, as affirmed by the Quranic verse; this is a metaphysical state, not a physical one.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): The phrase "alive with their Lord" is literal in affirming a real, though unknown, mode of life, not a mere metaphor for honor.
- Root: ج-ن-ن (j-n-n)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To cover or conceal; al-jannah (Paradise) is the concealed garden, hidden from human perception.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In Kalām, al-jannah is a created, existing reality (makhliqah mawjūdah), the abode of reward, affirmed by Ahl al-Sunnah against the Muʿtazilah.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal existence of Paradise is asserted; the Muʿtazilī claim that it is not yet created is rejected as a deviation from the apparent (ẓāhir) of revelation.
- Sībawayh Rule: ʿAṭf al-Bayān (Appositional Clarification) — The phrase "أرواحهم في جوف طير خضر" (their souls are in the bellies of green birds) is a nominal sentence (jumlah ismiyyah) functioning as a predicate (khabar) for the martyrs' state, with "في جوف" (in the belly) as a locative predicate (ẓarf) indicating a real, spatial modality as understood by the Salaf, without taʿṭīl (denial) or takyīf (qualification).
chapters.translation:
...upon him be peace, except religion, for Gabriel said that to me, and Allah knows best.

# [1886] His saying (حدثنا سعيد بن منصور حدثنا سفيان عن عمرو بن دينار عن محمد بن قيس قال) — and he also narrated via Ibn ʿAjlān from Muhammad ibn Qays from Abū ʿAbdullāh ibn Abī Qatādah. The one who said "حدثنا ابن عجلان" is Sufyān. His saying (عن عياش بن عباس القتباني) — the first [ʿAyyāsh] is with an unpointed shīn (ش), and the second [ʿAbbās] is with an unpointed ʿayn (ع) and a pointed bāʾ (ب); al-Qatbānī is with a kasrah on the qāf (ق), then a sukūn on the tāʾ (ت), then a bāʾ (ب), attributed to Qatbān, a sub-tribe of Ruʿayn.

| Chapter on the Explanation that the Souls of the Martyrs are in Paradise and that They are Alive with Their Lord, Provided For |

# [1887] His saying (حدثني يحيى بن يحيى وأبو بكر بن أبي شيبة وذكر إسناده إلى مسروق قال سألنا عبد الله) — about this verse: {«وَلَا تَحْسَبَنَّ الَّذِينَ قُتِلُوا فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ أَمْوَاتًا ۚ بَلْ أَحْيَاءٌ عِندَ رَبِّهِمْ يُرْزَقُونَ»} (And do not think of those who are killed in the path of Allah as dead; rather, they are alive with their Lord, provided for). He said: "As for us, we had asked about that, and he said: 'Their souls are in the bellies of green birds.'"

Al-Māzarī said: Thus it came as "ʿAbdullāh" without attribution. Abū ʿAlī al-Ghassānī said: Some people attribute him, saying "ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr," and Abū Masʿūd al-Dimashqī mentioned him in the Musnad of Ibn Masʿūd. Al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ said: In some copies of Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim, it occurs as "ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd." I say: Thus it also occurred in some reliable copies of our lands, but it did not occur attributed in most of them. Khalaf al-Wāsiṭī, al-Ḥumaydī, and others mentioned him in the Musnad of Ibn Masʿūd, and that is correct. This ḥadīth is raised (marfūʿ) due to his saying "As for us, we had asked about that, and he said" — meaning the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him.

His saying, peace and blessings be upon him, concerning the martyrs: "Their souls are in the bellies of green birds, having lamps suspended from the Throne; they roam freely in Paradise wherever they wish, then they return to those lamps." In this is an explanation that Paradise is created and existing — this is the doctrine of Ahl al-Sunnah. It is the Paradise from which Adam was descended, and it is that in which the believers will be blessed in the Hereafter. This is the consensus (ijmāʿ) of Ahl al-Sunnah. The Muʿtazilah, a faction of the innovators, and others said that it is not existing, but rather will only come into being after the Resurrection on the Day of Judgment. They said: The Paradise from which Adam was expelled is something else. The apparent meanings (ẓawāhir) of the Quran and the Sunnah support the doctrine of the people of truth.

In this is also the affirmation of the recompense of the dead with reward and punishment before the Resurrection. Al-Qāḍī said: In this is that the souls are enduring (bāqiyah), not perishing; thus the good-doer is rewarded and the evil-doer is punished. The Quran and the traditions (āthār) have brought this, and it is the doctrine of Ahl al-Sunnah, contrary to a faction of the innovators who said they perish.

Al-Qāḍī said: Here he mentioned "the souls of the martyrs," while in the ḥadīth of Mālik he said: "Indeed, the soul (nasamah) of the believer." The term nasamah is applied to the entire person, body and soul, and it is also applied to the soul alone — and that is what is meant in this interpretation. In the other ḥadīth, it is expressed as "the spirit (rūḥ)," and because we know that the body perishes and is consumed by the earth, and due to his saying in the ḥadīth: "until Allah returns it to his body on the Day of Resurrection."

Al-Qāḍī said: In the ḥadīth of Mālik, may Allah have mercy on him, he mentioned "the soul of the believer," and here he mentioned "the martyrs" because this is their attribute, due to His saying, the Exalted: {«أَحْيَاءٌ عِندَ رَبِّهِمْ يُرْزَقُونَ»} (alive with their Lord, provided for), and as He explained in this ḥadīth. As for others, their seat is only shown to them morning and evening, as came in the ḥadīth of Ibn ʿUmar, and as He said concerning the family of Pharaoh: {«النَّارُ يُعْرَضُونَ عَلَيْهَا غُدُوًّا وَعَشِيًّا»} (The Fire, they are exposed to it morning and evening).

Al-Qāḍī said: It was also said that the intent is all believers who enter Paradise without punishment, for they enter it now, based on the generality of the ḥadīth. And it was said: Rather, the souls of the believers are at the courtyards of their graves. And Allah knows best.

His saying, peace and blessings be upon him, in this ḥadīth: "in the bellies of green birds," and in other than Muslim: "with green birds," and in another ḥadīth: "in the crops of birds," and in the Muwaṭṭaʾ: "Indeed, the soul of the believer is a bird," and in another ḥadīth from Qatādah: "in the form of a white bird."

Al-Qāḍī said: Some of the theologians commenting on this said: The most likely correct is the statement of those who said "a bird" or "the form of a bird," for it is the most frequent in the narrations, especially with his saying "they return to lamps beneath the Throne." Al-Qāḍī said: Some deemed this improbable, while others did not reject it. There is nothing in it to reject, and there is no difference between the two matters; rather, the narration of "a bird" or "the belly of a bird" is more sound in meaning. There is no ruling for analogical reasoning (qiyās) or intellects in this matter — all of it falls under what is possible (jāʾizāt). So if Allah wills to place this soul, when it departs from the believer or the martyr, in lamps, or in the bellies of birds, or wherever He wills, that occurs and is not improbable — especially given the view that souls are bodies (ajsām).

Al-Qāḍī said: It was said that this rewarded or punished entity from the souls is a part of the body in which the soul remains; it is that which feels pain and is punished, and delights and is rewarded; it is that which says: {«رَبِّ ارْجِعُونِ»} (My Lord, return me); and it is that which roams in the trees of Paradise. So it is not impossible that this part be formed as a bird, or placed in the belly of a bird, or in lamps beneath the Throne, or other than that which Allah, Mighty and Majestic, wills.

Al-Qāḍī said: The people have differed concerning the soul — what it is — in a difference that can scarcely be encompassed. Many of the masters of meanings and the esoteric scholars among the theologians said: Its reality is not known, and its description is not sound; it is among what Allah has made the servants ignorant of its knowledge. They adduced His saying, the Exalted: {«قُلِ الرُّوحُ مِنْ أَمْرِ رَبِّي»} (Say: The soul is of the command of my Lord). The philosophers went to extremes and denied the soul entirely. The majority of physicians said it is the subtle vapor permeating the body. Many of our shaykhs said it is life (ḥayāh). Others said they are subtle bodies interpenetrating the body, living by its life; Allah, the Exalted, has made it the custom that the body dies upon their separation. It was said it is a part of the body, and for this reason it is described as exiting, being seized, and reaching the throat — and these are attributes of bodies, not of meanings. Some of the leading imams of ours said it is a subtle body formed in the image of a human within the body. Some of our shaykhs and others said it is the soul (nafs) entering and exiting. Others said it is the blood. This is what al-Qāḍī transmitted. The most correct (al-aṣaḥḥ) with our companions is that...
