chapters.title_en: The Prophet's Use of Non-Arabic Words, the Meaning of "Hayya Hala," and the Miracle of Food Multiplication in the Hadiths of Abu Hurayrah, Jabir, and Anas
chapters.arabic_text:
صلى الله عليه وسلم تكلم بألفاظ غير العربية فيدل على جوازه وأما حى هلا

بتنوين هلا وقيل بلا تنوين على وزن علا ويقال حي هل فمعناه عليك بكذا إو

ادع بكذا قاله أبوعبيد وغيره وقيل معناه أعجل به وقال الهروي معناه هات

وعجل به قوله (وجاء رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقدم الناس) إنما فعل هذا

لأنه صلى الله عليه وسلم دعاهم فجاؤا تبعا له كصاحب الطعام إذا دعا طائفة

يمشي قدامهم وكان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في غير هذا الحال لا

يتقدمهم ولا يمكنهم من وطء
# 
# عقبيه وفعله هنا لهذه المصلحة قوله (حتى جئت امرأتي فقالت بك وبك) أي

ذمته ودعت عليه وقيل معناه بك تلحق الفضيحة وبك يتعلق الذم وقيل معناه جرى

هذا برأيك وسوء نظرك وتسببك قوله (قد فعلت الذي قلت لي) معناه أنى أخبرت

النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بما عندنا فهو أعلم بالمصلحة قوله (ثم عمد إلى

برمتنا فبصق فيها وبارك ثم قال ادعي خابزة فلتخبز معك) هذه اللفظة وهي ادعي

وقعت في بعض الأصول هكذا ادعي بعين ثم ياء وهو الصحيح الظاهر لأنه خطاب

للمرأة ولهذا قال فلتخبز معك وفى بعضها اذعونى بواو ونون وفي بعضها ادعني

وهما أيضا صحيحان وتقديره اطلبوا واطلب لي خابزة وقوله عمد بفتح الميم

وقوله بصق هكذا هو في أكثر الأصول وفي بعضها بسق وهي لغة قليلة والمشهور

بصق وبزق وحكى جماعة من أهل اللغة بسق لكنها قليلة كما ذكرنا قوله صلى الله

عليه وسلم (واقدحي من برمتكم) أي اغرفي والقدح المغرفة يقال قدحت المرق

أقدحه بفتح الدال غرفته قوله (وهم ألف فأقسم بالله لأكلوا حتى تركوه

وانحرفوا وإن برمتنا لتغط كما هي وإن عجينتنا لتخبز كما هو) قوله تركوه

وانحرفوا أي شبعوا وانصرفوا وقوله تغط بكسر الغين المعجمة وتشديد الطاء أي

تغلي ويسمع غليانها وقوله كما هو يعود إلى العجين وقد تضمن هذا الحديث

علمين من أعلام النبوة أحدهما تكثير  الطعام القليل والثاني علمه صلى الله

عليه وسلم بأن هذا الطعام القليل الذي يكفي في العادة خمسة أنفس أو نحوهم

سيكثر فيكفي ألفا وزيادة فدعا له ألفا قبل أن يصل إليه وقد علم أنه صاع

شعير وبهيمة والله أعلم وأما الحديث الثالث وهو حديث أنس في طعام أبي طلحة

ففيه أيضا هذان العلمان من أعلام النبوة وهما تكثير القليل وعلمه
# 
# صلى الله عليه وسلم بأن هذا القليل سيكثره الله تعالى فيكفي هؤلاء الخلق

الكثير فدعاهم له واعلم أن أنسا رضي الله عنه روى هنا حديثين الأول من طريق

والثاني من طريق وهما قضيتان جرت فيهما هاتان المعجزتان وغيرهما من

المعجزات ففي الحديث الأول أن أبا طلحة وأم سليم رضي الله عنهما أرسلا أنسا

رضي الله عنه إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بأقراص شعير قال أنس فذهبت

فوجدت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم جالسا في المسجد ومعه أصحابه فقمت

عليهم فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أرسلك أبو طلحة فقلت نعم فقال

ألطعام فقلت نعم فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لمن معه قوموا فانطلق

وانطلقت بين أيديهم حتى جئت أبا طلحة فأخبرته فقال أبو طلحة يا أم سليم قد

جاء رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بالناس وليس عندنا ما نطعمهم فقالت الله

ورسوله أعلم قال فانطلق أبو طلحة حتى لقي رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

فأقبل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم معه حتى دخلا فقال رسول الله صلى الله

عليه وسلم هلمي ما عندك يا أم سليم فأتت بذلك الخبز فأمر به صلى الله عليه

وسلم ففت وعصرت عليه عكة لها فأدمته ثم قال فيه رسول الله صلى الله عليه

وسلم ما شاء الله أن يقول ثم قال ائذن لعشرة فأذن لهم فأكلوا حتى شبعوا ثم

خرجوا ثم قال ائذن لعشرة حتى أكل القوم كلهم وشبعوا والقوم سبعون رجلا أو

ثمانون قوله صلى الله
# 
# عليه وسلم
# [2040] (أرسلك أبو طلحة فقلت نعم) وقوله (ألطعام  فقلت نعم) هذان علمان من

أعلام النبوة وذهابه صلى الله عليه وسلم بهم علم ثالث كما سبق وتكثير

الطعام علم رابع وفيه ما تقدم في حديث أبي هريرة وحديث جابر من ابتلاء

الأنبياء صلوات الله عليهم وسلامه والاختبار بالجوع وغيره من المشاق

ليصبروا فيعظم أجرهم ومنازلهم وفيه ما كانوا عليه من كتمان مابهم وفيه ما

كانت الصحابة رضي الله عنهم عليه من الاعتناء بأحوال رسول الله صلى الله

عليه وسلم وفيه استحباب بعث الهدية وإن كانت قليلة بالنسبة إلى مرتبة

المبعوث إليه لأنها وإن قلت فهي خير من العدم وفيه جلوس العالم لأصحابه

يفيدهم ويؤدبهم واستحباب ذلك في المساجد وفيه انطلاق صاحب الطعام بين يدي

الضيفان وخروجه ليتلقاهم وفيه منقبة لأم سليم رضي الله عنها ودلالة على

عظيم فقهها ورجحان عقلها لقولها الله ورسوله أعلم ومعناه أنه قد عرف الطعام

فهو أعلم بالمصلحة فلو لم يعلمها في مجئ الجمع العظيم لم يفعلها فلاتحزن من

ذلك وفيه استحباب فت الطعام واختيار الثريد على الغمس باللقم وقوله (عصرت

عليه عكة) هي بضم العين وتشديد الكاف وهي وعاء صغير من جلد للسمن خاصة
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ح ي ي (ḥayya)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: The root denotes life (ḥayāh), and in the vocative formula "ḥayya ʿalā," it carries the sense of hastening toward something, as if summoning one to "come alive" to it.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological usage, "ḥayya ʿalā al-ṣalāh" (come to prayer) is a summons to an act of worship, implying an existential urgency toward obedience.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literally, it is a call to approach; metaphorically (majāz), it signifies "hasten to" or "devote yourself to," as in "ḥayya hala" meaning "come to this matter."
- Root: ق د ح (qadaḥa)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: The core meaning is to scoop or ladle out (gharafa); the noun "qadaḥ" is a vessel or ladle used for drawing liquid.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In the context of food and provision, it denotes the act of extracting sustenance, symbolizing divine abundance.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal usage for physical scooping; no metaphorical extension here, as it refers to the concrete act of serving broth.
- Root: غ ل ي (ghalā)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To boil, seethe, or bubble up; the sound of boiling is described as "taghiṭ" with intensified articulation.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In Quranic and theological contexts, boiling (ghalyān) often signifies intense heat or agitation, but here it is purely physical.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for the audible boiling of a pot; no figurative sense intended.
- Sībawayh Rule: Rule of Vocative and Imperative Syntax (Nidā' wa Amr) — The phrase "udʿī" (call) is parsed as a feminine imperative addressed to Umm Sulaym, with the yā' indicating the feminine subject, while "udʿūnī" (call for me) uses the plural imperative with the nūn of emphasis, showing variant readings across manuscript traditions.
chapters.translation:
I say: The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) spoke words that were not Arabic, and this indicates the permissibility of doing so. As for the phrase "ḥayya hala" — with tanwīn on "hala," and it is also said without tanwīn, on the pattern of "ʿalā" — and it is said "ḥayya hal." Its meaning is: "Upon you is such-and-such," or "call to such-and-such." This was stated by Abū ʿUbayd and others. It is also said its meaning is: "Hasten to it." Al-Harawī said its meaning is: "Bring it and hasten to it."

His statement (and the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, came leading the people): He only did this because he, peace and blessings be upon him, had invited them, so they came following him — like the host of a meal who, when he invites a group, walks ahead of them. And the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, in other situations did not walk ahead of them, nor did he allow them to tread on his heels. His action here was for this specific benefit (maṣlaḥah).

His statement (until I came to my wife, and she said: "By you and by you"): That is, she censured him and invoked evil upon him. It is also said its meaning is: "By you will the disgrace attach, and by you will the blame cling." And it is said its meaning is: "This happened due to your opinion, your poor judgment, and your instigation."

His statement (I have done what you told me): Its meaning is that he informed the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, of what they had, for he (the Prophet) knew best what served the benefit (maṣlaḥah).

His statement (then he went to our cooking pot, spat into it, and blessed it, then said: "Call the baker to bake with you"): This word — namely "udʿī" (call) — appears in some manuscript copies as "udʿī" with a ʿayn followed by a yā', and this is the correct and apparent reading, because it is an address to a woman, and for this reason he said "let her bake with you." In some copies it appears as "udʿūnī" with a wāw and nūn, and in others "udʿinnī" — both are also correct, and their meaning is: "Seek out, and seek for me, a baker."

His statement "ʿamada" (he went) — with fatḥah on the mīm. His statement "baṣaqa" (he spat) — thus it is in most copies, and in some it is "basaqa," which is a rare dialect. The well-known forms are "baṣaqa" and "bazaqa." A group of linguists have reported "basaqa," but it is rare, as we have mentioned.

His statement, peace and blessings be upon him (and ladle from your pot): That is, "scoop out." The "qadaḥ" is the ladle. One says: "I ladled the broth, I ladle it" — with fatḥah on the dāl — meaning "I scooped it out."

His statement (and they were a thousand — I swear by Allah, they ate until they left it and turned away, while our pot was still boiling as it was, and our dough was still baking as it was): His statement "they left it and turned away" means they were satiated and departed. His statement "taghiṭ" — with kasrah on the ghayn (the dotted letter) and tashdīd on the ṭā' — means it was boiling, and its boiling sound was heard. His statement "as it was" refers back to the dough.

This hadith has encompassed two signs of prophethood (aʿlām al-nubuwwah): one is the multiplication of little food, and the second is his knowledge, peace and blessings be upon him, that this small amount of food — which ordinarily would suffice for five persons or thereabouts — would increase and suffice for a thousand and more. So he invited them for a thousand before the food reached him, and he knew it was a ṣāʿ of barley and an animal. And Allah knows best.

As for the third hadith — namely the hadith of Anas concerning the food of Abū Ṭalḥah — it also contains these two signs of prophethood: the multiplication of the little, and his knowledge, peace and blessings be upon him, that Allah the Exalted would multiply this little amount so that it would suffice for these many creatures. So he invited them to it.

Know that Anas, may Allah be pleased with him, narrated two hadiths here: the first via one chain, and the second via another — and they are two incidents in which these two miracles and others occurred. In the first hadith, Abū Ṭalḥah and Umm Sulaym, may Allah be pleased with them both, sent Anas, may Allah be pleased with him, to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, with barley loaves. Anas said: "So I went and found the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, sitting in the mosque with his companions. I stood over them, and the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: 'Did Abū Ṭalḥah send you?' I said: 'Yes.' He said: 'For food?' I said: 'Yes.' So the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said to those with him: 'Rise.' So he set out, and I went ahead of them until I came to Abū Ṭalḥah and informed him. Abū Ṭalḥah said: 'O Umm Sulaym, the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, has come with the people, and we have nothing to feed them.' She said: 'Allah and His Messenger know best.' Anas said: 'So Abū Ṭalḥah went out until he met the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, and the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, came with him until they both entered. The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Bring what you have, O Umm Sulaym." So she brought that bread. He, peace and blessings be upon him, ordered it to be crumbled, and she squeezed over it a small leather container of hers (ʿukkah), and seasoned it. Then the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said over it what Allah willed for him to say. Then he said: "Admit ten." So he admitted them, and they ate until they were full, then they left. Then he said: "Admit ten" — until all the people had eaten and were satiated, and the people were seventy or eighty men.'"

His statement, peace and blessings be upon him (Did Abū Ṭalḥah send you? — and I said: Yes), and his statement (For food? — and I said: Yes): These are two signs of prophethood. And his going, peace and blessings be upon him, with them is a third sign, as previously mentioned. And the multiplication of the food is a fourth sign.

In this hadith is what has preceded in the hadith of Abū Hurayrah and the hadith of Jābir — namely, the affliction of the prophets, peace and blessings be upon them, and their being tested with hunger and other hardships, so that they might be patient and thus their reward and stations be magnified. In it is what they used to conceal of their own conditions. In it is what the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, were upon — namely, their care for the affairs of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him. In it is the recommendation of sending a gift, even if it is little relative to the rank of the one to whom it is sent, because even if it is little, it is better than nothing. In it is the sitting of a scholar with his companions to benefit them and discipline them, and the recommendation of that in mosques. In it is the host's going ahead of the guests and going out to receive them. In it is a virtue for Umm Sulaym, may Allah be pleased with her, and an indication of her great jurisprudence (fiqh) and the soundness of her intellect, due to her saying: "Allah and His Messenger know best." Its meaning is that he (the Prophet) knew the food, so he knew best the benefit (maṣlaḥah); had he not known it regarding the coming of the great multitude, he would not have done it — so do not grieve over that.

In it is the recommendation of crumbling bread and choosing tharīd (bread soaked in broth) over dipping morsels. His statement (she squeezed over it an ʿukkah) — it is with ḍammah on the ʿayn and tashdīd on the kāf — and it is a small leather vessel used specifically for clarified butter (samn).

chapters.title_en: Section 783 — On the Permissibility of Eating Broth, the Recommendation of Eating Pumpkin, and the Preference of Table Companions for One Another
chapters.arabic_text:
وقوله (فآدمته) هو بالمد والقصر لغتان آدمته وأدمته أي جعلت فيه إداما

وإنما أذن لعشرة عشرة ليكون أرفق بهم فإن القصعة التي فت فيها تلك الأقراص
# 
# لايتحلق عليها أكثر من عشرة الابضرر يلحقهم لبعدها عنهم والله أعلم وأما

الحديث الآخر ففيه أن أنسا قال بعثني أبو طلحة إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه

وسلم لأدعوه وقد جعل طعاما فأقبلت ورسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم مع الناس

فنظر إلي فاستحييت فقلت أجب أبا طلحة فقال للناس قوموا وذكر الحديث وأخرج

لهم شيئا من بين أصابعه وهذا الحديث قضية أخرى بلاشك
# 
# وفيها ما سبق في الحديث الأول وزيادة هذا العلم الآخر من أعلام النبوة

وهو اخراج ذلك الشئ من بين أصابعه الكريمات صلى الله عليه وسلم قوله

(وتركوا سؤرا) هو بالهمزأى بقية قوله (فقام أبو طلحة على الباب حتى أتى

رسول  الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال له يارسول الله إنما كان شئ يسير قال

هلمه فإن الله سيجعل فيه البركة) أما قيام أبي طلحة فلانتظار إقبال النبى

صلى الله عليه وسلم فلماأقبل تلقاه وقوله إنما كان شئ يسير هكذا هو في

الأصول وهو صحيح وكان هنا تامة لاتحتاج خبرا وقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (فإن

الله سيجعل فيه البركة) فيه علم ظاهر من
# 
# أعلام النبوة وقوله (ثم أكل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وأكل أهل

البيت) فيه أن يستحب لصاحب الطعام وأهله أن يكون أكلهم بعد فراغ الضيفان

والله أعلم قوله (يتقلب ظهرا لبطن) وفي الرواية الأخرى وقد عصب بطنه بعصابة

لا مخالفة بينهما وأحدهما يبين الآخر ويقال عصب وعصب بالتخفيف والتشديد

قوله (فذهبت إلى أبي طلحة وهو زوج
# 
# أم سليم بنت ملحان فقلت يا أبتاه) فيه استعمال المجاز لقوله يا أبتاه

وإنما هو زوج أمه وقوله بنت ملحان هو بكسر الميم والله أعلم

| (باب جواز أكل المرق واستحباب أكل اليقطين وإيثار 
# أهل المائدة بعضهم بعضا وإن كانوا ضيفانا إذا لم يكره ذلك صاحب الطعام)
# [2041] فيه حديث أنس رضي الله عنه (أن خياطا دعا رسول الله صلى الله عليه

وسلم فقرب إليه خبزا من شعير ومرقا فيه دباء وقديد قال أنس فرأيت رسول الله

صلى الله عليه وسلم يتتبع الدباء
# 
# من حوالي الصحفة فلم أزل أحب الدباء من يومئذ) وفي رواية قال أنس فلما

رأيت ذلك جعلت ألقيه إليه ولاأطعمه وفي رواية قال أنس فما صنع لي طعام بعد

أقدر على أن بصنع فيه دباء الاصنع فيه فوائد منها إجابة الدعوة وإباحة كسب

الخياط وإباحة المرق وفضيلة أكل الدباء وأنه يستحب أن يحب الدباء وكذلك كل

شئ كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يحبه وأنه يحرص على تحصيل ذلك وأنه

يستحب لأهل المائدة إيثار بعضهم بعضا إذا لم يكرهه صاحب الطعام وأما تتبع

الدباء من حوالي الصحفة فيحتمل وجهين أحدهما من حوالى جانبه وناحيته من

الصحفة لامن حوالى  جميع جوانبها فقد أمر بالأكل ممايلى الإنسان والثاني أن

يكون من جميع جوانبها وإنما نهى ذلك لئلا يتقذره جليسه ورسول الله صلى الله

عليه وسلم لايتقذره أحد بل يتبركون بآثاره صلى الله عليه وسلم فقد كانوا

يتبركون ببصاقه صلى الله عليه وسلم ونخامته ويدلكون بذلك وجوههم وشرب بعضهم

بوله وبعضهم دمه وغير ذلك مما هو معروف من عظيم اعتنائهم بآثاره صلى الله

عليه وسلم التي يخالفه فيها غيره والدباء
# 
# هو اليقطين وهو بالمد هذا هو المشهور وحكى القاضي عياض فيه القصر

أيضاالواحدة دباءة أو دباة والله أعلم

| باب استحباب وضع النوى خارج التمر واستحباب دعاء
# الضيف لأهل الطعام وطلب الدعاء من الضيف الصالح واجابته إلى ذلك)
# [2042] فيه (يزيد بن خمير عن عبد الله بن بسر رضي الله عنه قال نزل رسول

الله صلى الله عليه وسلم على أبى فقربنا له طعاما ورطبة فأكل منها ثم أتي

بتمر فكان يأكله ويلقي النوى بين إصبعيه ويجمع السبابة والوسطى قال شعبة هو

ظني وهو فيه إن شاء الله إلقاء النوى بين الإصبعين ثم أتي بشراب فشربه ثم

ناوله الذي عن يمينه فقال أبي وأخذ بلجام دابته ادع الله لنا فقال اللهم

بارك لهم فيما رزقتهم واغفرلهم وارحمهم) وفي الرواية الأخرى ذكره وقال لم

يشك في إلقاء النوى بين الإصبعين عبد الله بن بسر بضم الباء ويزيد بن خمير

بضم الخاء المعجمة وفتح الميم وقوله ووطبة هكذا رواية الأكثرين وطبة بالواو

وإسكان الطاء وبعدها باء موحدة وهكذا رواه النضر بن شميل راوي هذا الحديث

عن شعبة والنضر إمام من أئمة اللغة وفسره النضر فقال الوطبة الحيس يجمع

التمر البرني والأقط المدقوق والسمن وكذا ضبطه أبو مسعود الدمشقي وأبو بكر

البرقاني وآخرون وهكذا هو عندنا في معظم النسخ وفي بعضها رطبة
# 
# براء مضمومة وفتح الطاء وكذا ذكره الحميدي وقال هكذا جاء فيما رأيناه من

نسخ مسلم رطبة بالراء قال وهو تصحيف من الراوي وإنما هو بالواو وهذا الذي

ادعاه على نسخ مسلم هو فيما رآه  هو وإلا فأكثرها بالواو وكذا نقله أبو

مسعود البرقاني والأكثرون عن نسخ مسلم ونقل القاضي عياض عن رواية بعضهم في
chapters.anchors:
- Root: أ د م (ʾ-d-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: The core meaning is "to season" or "to make something palatable with a condiment (idām)"; the verbal form with medial alif (ādamtu) and without (adamtu) are two classical variants.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological usage, the root conveys the idea of "reconciliation" or "harmonizing," but here it is purely culinary—making bread palatable with a relish.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage—seasoning food; no metaphorical extension is intended in this prophetic context.
- Sībawayh Rule: Verbal Variants (al-lughāt fī al-fiʿl) — The dual forms (ādamtu/adamtu) are both valid morphological variants of the same triliteral verb, demonstrating permissible phonetic flexibility in classical Arabic.

- Root: ق ر ب (q-r-b)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: "To draw near" or "to approach"; the form IV (aqraba) means "to bring near" or "to offer."
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological contexts, qurbah denotes "nearness to God" through devotional acts; here it is physical proximity at a meal.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal spatial proximity, distinct from the metaphorical "nearness to God" (qurbah ilā Allāh).
- Sībawayh Rule: Prepositional Phrase Attachment (taʿalluq al-jār wa-al-majrūr) — The phrase "min ḥawālī al-ṣaḥfah" attaches to the verb "yatatabbaʿu," indicating the direction from which the Prophet ate.

- Root: د ب ء (d-b-ʾ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: "Pumpkin" or "gourd" (dubbāʾ); the single unit is dubbāʾah or dabbāʾah, with the common form having a long alif (madd) and a rare short form (qaṣr).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): No theological nuance; purely a botanical term in the Quranic and prophetic lexicon.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal reference to the plant; the Prophet's preference for it is a physical, not allegorical, act.
- Sībawayh Rule: Nominal Morphology (bināʾ al-ism) — The pattern fuʿʿāl (dubbāʾ) is a standard intensive or specific noun form, here denoting a specific vegetable.
chapters.translation:
I say: Regarding his statement (فآدمته) — "and I seasoned it" — it is transmitted with both the long alif (madd) and the short form (qaṣr), as two variant readings: ādamtu and adamtu, meaning "I made in it a condiment (idām)."

And the permission for ten at a time was only granted so that it would be more comfortable for them, for the bowl in which those loaves were crumbled could not accommodate more than ten gathered around it without harm befalling them due to their distance from it. And God knows best.

As for the other hadith, it contains that Anas said: "Abū Ṭalḥah sent me to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) to invite him, having prepared food. So I went, and the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) was with the people. He looked at me, and I felt shy, so I said: 'Answer Abū Ṭalḥah's invitation.' He said to the people: 'Rise,' and he mentioned the hadith — and he brought out for them something from between his fingers." This hadith is another incident, without doubt, and in it is what preceded in the first hadith, plus this additional sign among the signs of prophethood — namely, the bringing forth of that thing from between his noble fingers (peace and blessings be upon him).

His statement (وتركوا سؤرا) — "and they left a remnant" — is with a hamzah, meaning "a remainder."

His statement (فقام أبو طلحة على الباب حتى أتى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال له يا رسول الله إنما كان شئ يسير قال هلمه فإن الله سيجعل فيه البركة) — "So Abū Ṭalḥah stood at the door until the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) arrived, and he said to him: 'O Messenger of God, it was only a small thing.' He said: 'Bring it, for God will place blessing in it.'" As for Abū Ṭalḥah's standing, it was to await the Prophet's arrival (peace and blessings be upon him); when he approached, he met him. His statement "it was only a small thing" — thus it is in the manuscripts, and it is correct; here kāna is complete (tāmmah), not requiring a predicate. And his statement (peace and blessings be upon him) "for God will place blessing in it" contains a manifest sign among the signs of prophethood.

His statement (ثم أكل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وأكل أهل البيت) — "Then the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) ate, and the people of the household ate" — in it is that it is recommended (mustaḥabb) for the host and his family to eat after the guests have finished. And God knows best.

His statement (يتقلب ظهرا لبطن) — "turning over back to belly" — and in the other narration, "and he had bound his belly with a bandage" — there is no contradiction between them; each clarifies the other. And it is said ʿaṣaba and ʿaṣṣaba, with lightening and doubling of the consonant.

His statement (فذهبت إلى أبي طلحة وهو زوج أم سليم بنت ملحان فقلت يا أبتاه) — "So I went to Abū Ṭalḥah, who was the husband of Umm Sulaym bint Milḥān, and I said: 'O my father'" — in it is the use of metaphor (majāz), for he said "O my father" when he was only his mother's husband. And his statement "bint Milḥān" is with a kasrah on the mīm. And God knows best.

| Chapter: On the Permissibility of Eating Broth, the Recommendation of Eating Pumpkin, and the Preference of Table Companions for One Another, Even If They Are Guests, When the Host Does Not Disapprove of It |

[2041] In it is the hadith of Anas (may God be pleased with him): "A tailor invited the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him), and he placed before him barley bread and broth containing pumpkin (dubbāʾ) and dried meat. Anas said: 'I saw the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) following the pumpkin from around the edge of the plate, and I have loved pumpkin ever since that day.'" In another narration, Anas said: "When I saw that, I began to place it before him and did not eat it myself." In yet another narration, Anas said: "No food was prepared for me afterward that I could make with pumpkin without making it with pumpkin."

Among the benefits [derived from this hadith]: the acceptance of the invitation, the permissibility of a tailor's earnings, the permissibility of broth, the virtue of eating pumpkin, that it is recommended to love pumpkin — and likewise everything the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) loved — that one should be eager to obtain that, and that it is recommended for table companions to prefer one another when the host does not disapprove of it.

As for his following the pumpkin from around the edge of the plate, it admits two interpretations: First, from around his own side and direction of the plate, not from all its sides — for he was commanded to eat from what is before him. Second, that it was from all its sides, and the prohibition [in the general command] was only lest his companion be disgusted; but no one was disgusted by the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him); rather, they sought blessings from his traces (peace and blessings be upon him). Indeed, they used to seek blessings from his saliva (peace and blessings be upon him) and his spittle, wiping their faces with them; some of them drank his urine, and some his blood, and other things well known of their immense devotion to his traces (peace and blessings be upon him), in which others differ from him.

And dubbāʾ is the pumpkin (yaqṭīn), and it is with a long alif (madd) — this is the well-known form. Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ narrated the short form (qaṣr) as well. The singular is dubbāʾah or dabbāʾah. And God knows best.

| Chapter: On the Recommendation of Placing Date Pits Outside the Dates, the Recommendation of the Guest Praying for the Hosts, and Seeking Prayer from a Righteous Guest and His Responding to That |

[2042] In it is (Yazīd ibn Khumayr from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Busr (may God be pleased with him), who said): "The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) alighted at my father's, and we brought him food and waṭbah, and he ate from it. Then dates were brought, and he ate them, throwing the pits between his two fingers, joining the forefinger and middle finger." Shuʿbah said: "This is my conjecture, and in it, God willing, is the throwing of pits between the two fingers." "Then a drink was brought, and he drank, then handed it to the one on his right. My father said — and he had taken hold of his mount's reins — 'Pray to God for us.' He said: 'O God, bless them in what You have provided them, and forgive them, and have mercy on them.'"

In the other narration, he mentioned it and said he did not doubt the throwing of pits between the two fingers.

ʿAbd Allāh ibn Busr is with a ḍammah on the bāʾ, and Yazīd ibn Khumayr with a ḍammah on the khāʾ (with a dot) and a fatḥah on the mīm.

His statement "waṭbah" — thus is the narration of the majority: waṭbah with a wāw, a sukūn on the ṭāʾ, and after it a single bāʾ. Thus narrated al-Naḍr ibn Shumayl, the transmitter of this hadith from Shuʿbah — and al-Naḍr is an imam among the imams of language. Al-Naḍr interpreted it, saying: "Al-waṭbah is the ḥays — a mixture of pressed dates (tamr barnī), crushed dried yogurt (aqiṭ), and clarified butter (samn)." Thus also did Abū Masʿūd al-Dimashqī, Abū Bakr al-Barqānī, and others fix it, and thus it is in our copies in most versions. In some copies, it is "ruṭbah" with a rāʾ, ḍammah on the rāʾ, and fatḥah on the ṭāʾ. Thus al-Ḥumaydī mentioned it, saying: "Thus it came in what we saw of Muslim's copies: ruṭbah with a rāʾ." He said: "It is a corruption (taṣḥīf) by the transmitter; it is only with a wāw." But this claim he made about Muslim's copies applies to what he himself saw; otherwise, most of them have it with a wāw. Thus Abū Masʿūd al-Barqānī and the majority transmitted it from Muslim's copies. And Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ transmitted from the narration of some of them in...

chapters.arabic_text:
مسلم وطئة بفتح الواو وكسر الطاء وبعدها همزة وادعى أنه الصواب وهكذا ادعاه

آخرون والوطئة بالهمز عند أهل اللغة طعام يتخذ من التمر كالحيس هذا ما

ذكروه ولامنافاة بين هذا كله فيقبل ما صحت به الروايات وهو صحيح في اللغة

والله أعلم وقوله ويلقى النوى بين أصبعيه أى يجعله بينهما لقلته ولم يلقه

في إناء التمر لئلا يختلط بالتمر وقيل كان يجمعه على ظهر الأصبعين ثم يرمي

به وقوله قال شعبة هو ظني وهو فيه إن شاء الله إلقاء النوى معناه أن شعبة

قال الذي أظنه أن إلقاء النوى مذكور في الحديث فأشار إلى تردد فيه وشك وفي

الطريق الثاني جزم بإثباته ولم يشك فهو ثابت بهذه الرواية وأما رواية الشك

فلاتضر سواء تقدمت على هذه أو تأخرت لأنه تيقن في وقت وشك في وقت فاليقين

ثابت ولايمنعه النسيان في وقت آخر وقوله فشربه ثم ناوله الذي عن يمينه فيه

أن الشراب ونحوه يدارعلى اليمين كما سبق تقريره في بابه قريبا وفيه استحباب

طلب الدعاء من الفاضل ودعاء الضيف بتوسعة الرزق والمغفرة والرحمة وقد جمع

صلى الله عليه وسلم في هذا الدعاء خيرات الدنيا والآخرة والله أعلم
#

| (باب أكل القثاء بالرطب)
# [2043] فيه عبد الله بن جعفر رضي الله عنه (رأيت رسول الله صلى الله عليه

وسلم يأكل القثاء بالرطب) والقثاء بكسر القاف هو المشهور وفيه لغة بضمها

وقد جاء في غير مسلم زيادة قال يكسر حرهذا برد هذا فيه جواز أكلهما معا

وأكل الطعامين معا والتوسع فى الأطعمة ولاخلاف بين العلماء فى جواز هذا

ومانقل عن بعض السلف من خلاف هذا فمحمول على كراهة اعتياد التوسع والترفه

والإكثار منه لغير مصلحة دينية والله أعلم

| (باب استحباب تواضع الآكل وصفة قعوده)
# [2044] فيه أنس رضي الله عنه (رأيت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم مقعيا

يأكل تمرا) وفي الرواية الأخرى أتي بتمر  فجعل النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

يقسمه وهو محتفر يأكل منه أكلا ذريعا وفي رواية أكلا حثيثا قوله (مقعيا) أي

جالسا على أليتيه ناصبا ساقيه ومحتفز هو بالزاي أي مستعجل مستوفز غير متمكن

في جلوسه وهو بمعنى قوله مقعيا وهو أيضا معنى قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم في

الحديث الآخر في صحيح البخارى وغيره لاآكل متكئا على ما فسره الإمام

الخطابي فإنه قال المتكئ هنا المتمكن في جلوسه من التربع وشبهه المعتمد على

الوطاء تحته قال وكل من استوى قاعدا على وطاء فهو متكئ ومعناه لاآكل أكل من

يريد الاستكثار من الطعام ويقعد له متمكنا بل أقعد مستوفزا وآكل قليلا

وقوله أكلاذريعا وحثيثا هما بمعنى أي مستعجلا صلى الله عليه وسلم لاستيفازه

لشغل آخر فأسرع في الأكل وكان استعجاله ليقضي حاجته منه ويرد الجوعة ثم

يذهب في ذلك الشغل وقوله فجعل النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
# 
# يقسمه أي يفرقه على من يراه أهلا لذلك وهذا التمر كان لرسول الله صلى

الله عليه وسلم وتبرع بتفريقه صلى الله عليه وسلم فلهذا كان يأكل منه والله

أعلم

| (باب نهي الآكل مع جماعة عن قران تمرتين ونحوهما فى 
# لقمة إلاباذن أصحابه)
# [2045] فيه شعبة عن جبلة بن سحيم قال كان بن الزبير رضي الله عنه يرزقنا

التمر وكان أصاب الناس يومئذ جهد فكنا نأكل فيمر علينا بن عمر رضي الله عنه

ونحن نأكل فيقول لاتقارنوا فإن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم نهى عن

الإقران إلا أن يستأذن الرجل أخاه قال شعبة لاأرى هذه الكلمة إلامن كلمة بن

عمر رضي الله عنه يعني الاستئذان) وفي الرواية الأخرى عن سفيان عن جبلة عن

بن عمر نهى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أن يقرن الرجل بين التمرتين حتى

يستأذن أصحابه هذا النهي متفق عليه حتى يستأذنهم فإذا أذنوا فلا بأس

واختلفوا في أن هذا النهي على التحريم أو على الكراهة والأدب فنقل القاضي

عياض عن أهل الظاهر أنه للتحريم وعن غيرهم أنه للكراهة والأدب والصواب

التفصيل فإن كان الطعام مشتركا بينهم فالقران حرام إلابرضاهم
# 
# ويحصل الرضا بتصريحهم به أو بما يقوم مقام التصريح من قرينة حال أو إدلال

عليهم كلهم بحيث يعلم يقينا أو ظنا قويا أنهم يرضون به ومتى شك في رضاهم

فهو حرام وإن كان الطعام لغيرهم أولأحدهم اشترط رضاه وحده فإن قرن بغير

رضاه فحرام ويستحب أن يستأذن الآكلين معه ولايجب وإن كان الطعام لنفسه وقد

ضيفهم به فلايحرم عليه القران ثم إن كان في الطعام قلة فحسن ألا يقرن

لتساويهم وإن كان كثيرا بحيث يفضل عنهم فلا بأس بقرانه لكن الأدب مطلقا

التأدب في الأكل وترك الشره الاأن يكون مستعجلا ويريد الإسراع لشغل آخر كما

سبق في الباب قبله وقال الخطابي إنما كان هذا في زمنهم وحين كان الطعام

ضيقا فأما اليوم مع اتساع الحال فلاحاجة إلى الإذن وليس كما قال بل الصواب

ماذكرنا من التفصيل فإن الاعتبار بعموم اللفظ لابخصوص السبب لو ثبت السبب

كيف وهو غير ثابت والله أعلم وقوله أصاب الناس جهد يعني قلة وحاجة ومشقة

وقوله يقرن أي يجمع وهو بضم الراء وكسرها لغتان وقوله نهى عن الإقران هكذا

هو في الأصول والمعروف في اللغة القران يقال قرن بين الشيئين قالوا ولا
chapters.anchors:
- Root: و-ط-أ (wa-ṭa-ʾa)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: The core meaning is "to tread, to press down, to make level"; al-waṭīʾah (with hamzah) denotes a food made from pressed dates mixed with other ingredients, akin to ḥays.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological usage, the root conveys the idea of "settling" or "establishing" something firmly, though here it is purely culinary.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): The literal sense is "treading"; the metaphorical extension to "a pressed date dish" is a recognized lexical transfer (majāz) in food terminology.
- Root: ق-ر-ن (q-r-n)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To join, couple, or pair two things together; al-iqrān is the act of pairing.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In legal contexts, it denotes combining two items in a single act, here specifically eating two dates together in one mouthful.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal "joining"; used metaphorically for the physical act of placing two dates together in the hand or mouth.
- Root: ق-ث-أ (q-th-ʾ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: The cucumber (qiththāʾ), a well-known vegetable; the vowel on the qāf may be kasrah (most famous) or ḍammah (a lesser dialectal variant).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): No specific theological nuance; purely a botanical term.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal designation of the fruit; no metaphorical usage.
- Root: ق-ع-ي (q-ʿ-y)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To sit on the buttocks with the shins erect (iqʿāʾ); also related to squatting in a state of readiness.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In ritual contexts, iqʿāʾ is discussed regarding prayer postures; here it is a mundane sitting posture.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal posture description; the metaphorical sense of "hastiness" is conveyed by the synonym muḥtafiz (with zāy), meaning "quick, not fully settled."
- Sībawayh Rule: Rule of ʿAṭf al-Bayān (Appositional Clarification) — When two terms are juxtaposed to clarify one another (e.g., "muqʿiyan" and "muḥtafizan"), the second serves as an explicative gloss, not a separate predicate, ensuring the syntactic unity of the description.
chapters.translation:
I say: The word "waṭīʾah" is pronounced with a fatḥah on the wāw, a kasrah on the ṭāʾ, followed by a hamzah. One scholar claimed this is the correct form, and others have made the same claim. According to the linguists, "al-waṭīʾah" (with hamzah) is a food made from dates, similar to ḥays. This is what they have mentioned, and there is no contradiction between all these statements, so what is established by sound narrations is accepted, and it is linguistically correct. And Allah knows best.

His saying: "And he would throw the date pits between his two fingers" — meaning he would place them between the two fingers because they were few in number, and he would not throw them into the vessel containing the dates, lest they mix with the dates. It was also said that he would gather them on the back of his two fingers and then toss them away.

His saying: "Shuʿbah said: 'This is my conjecture'" — regarding the throwing of the pits, the meaning is that Shuʿbah said: "What I conjecture is that the throwing of the pits is mentioned in the ḥadīth," thus indicating his hesitation and doubt about it. In the second chain of transmission, he affirmed it with certainty and did not doubt, so it is established through that narration. As for the narration of doubt, it does no harm, whether it precedes or follows this one, because he was certain at one time and doubtful at another. Certainty remains established, and forgetfulness at another time does not negate it.

His saying: "Then he drank it, and then gave it to the one on his right" — this indicates that drinks and similar things are passed around to the right, as has already been established in its proper chapter recently. It also indicates the recommendation of seeking supplication from a virtuous person, and the guest's supplication for the expansion of provision, forgiveness, and mercy. The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) gathered in this supplication the goods of this world and the Hereafter. And Allah knows best.

#

| (Chapter: Eating Cucumber with Fresh Dates)

# [2043] In it: ʿAbdullāh ibn Jaʿfar, may Allah be pleased with him, (said: "I saw the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, eating cucumber with fresh dates"). "Al-qiththāʾ" is with a kasrah on the qāf, which is the famous form, and there is a variant with a ḍammah. In other than Muslim's collection, there is an addition: "He said: 'The heat of this is broken by the coolness of this.'" This indicates the permissibility of eating them together, and of eating two foods together, and of being expansive in foods. There is no disagreement among the scholars regarding the permissibility of this. What has been reported from some of the Salaf contrary to this is interpreted as a dislike of habitually seeking expansion and luxury, and of overindulging in it without a religious benefit. And Allah knows best.

| (Chapter: The Recommendation of Humility in the Eater and the Description of His Sitting)

# [2044] In it: Anas, may Allah be pleased with him, (said: "I saw the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, squatting and eating dates"). In the other narration: "Dates were brought to him, and the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, began to distribute them while he was squatting, eating from them with a quick eating." In another narration: "with a hasty eating." His saying "muqʿiyan" — meaning sitting on his buttocks with his shins erect. "Muḥtafiz" (with zāy) means hastening, sitting in a ready posture, not fully settled in his sitting. It is synonymous with his saying "muqʿiyan," and it is also the meaning of his saying, peace and blessings be upon him, in the other ḥadīth in Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī and others: "I do not eat reclining," according to what Imam al-Khaṭṭābī explained. For he said: "The 'recliner' here is the one fully settled in his sitting, such as sitting cross-legged and the like, leaning on a cushion beneath him." He said: "Anyone who sits evenly on a cushion is reclining." Its meaning is: I do not eat like one who seeks to consume much food and sits for it in a settled manner, but rather I sit in a ready posture and eat little.

His saying "aklan dharīʿan" and "ḥathīthan" — both mean the same, i.e., hastening, peace and blessings be upon him, because of his readiness for another task. So he hurried in eating, and his haste was to fulfill his need from it and to repel hunger, then to go to that task.

His saying: "Then the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, began to distribute it" — meaning he would give it out to those he deemed worthy of it. This dates were the property of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, and he voluntarily distributed them, peace and blessings be upon him, and for this reason he ate from them. And Allah knows best.

| (Chapter: The Prohibition of the Eater, When with a Group, from Pairing Two Dates or the Like in One Mouthful, Except with the Permission of His Companions)

# [2045] In it: Shuʿbah, from Jabalah ibn Suḥaym, who said: "Ibn al-Zubayr, may Allah be pleased with him, used to provide us with dates, and the people had been afflicted with hardship that day. So we would eat, and Ibn ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, would pass by us while we were eating and say: 'Do not pair (dates), for the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, prohibited pairing, except that a man seeks permission from his brother.'" Shuʿbah said: "I do not see this word — meaning the seeking of permission — except as from the word of Ibn ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him." In the other narration, from Sufyān, from Jabalah, from Ibn ʿUmar: "The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, prohibited a man from pairing two dates until he seeks permission from his companions." This prohibition is agreed upon — until he seeks their permission. So if they permit, there is no harm.

The scholars differed as to whether this prohibition indicates unlawfulness (taḥrīm) or merely dislike (karāhah) and etiquette. Al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ reported from the Ẓāhirī school that it is for unlawfulness, and from others that it is for dislike and etiquette. The correct view is the detailed one: if the food is shared among them, then pairing is unlawful except with their consent. Consent is obtained by their explicit statement or by what stands in place of explicit statement, such as an indication from the situation or their familiarity with all of them, such that one knows with certainty or strong probability that they would consent. Whenever there is doubt about their consent, it is unlawful. If the food belongs to someone else, or to one of them, then his consent alone is required; if he pairs without his consent, it is unlawful. It is recommended, though not obligatory, that he seek permission from those eating with him. If the food is his own and he has hosted them with it, then pairing is not unlawful for him. Then, if the food is scarce, it is good that he not pair, so that they may be equal. If it is abundant, such that there is surplus beyond them, then there is no harm in pairing. However, the etiquette in all cases is to be well-mannered in eating and to avoid greed, except when one is hastening and wishes to speed up for another task, as mentioned in the previous chapter.

Al-Khaṭṭābī said: "This was only in their time, when food was scarce. As for today, with the expansion of circumstances, there is no need for permission." This is not as he said; rather, the correct view is what we have detailed, for consideration is given to the generality of the wording, not the specificity of the cause — even if the cause were established, how could it be, when it is not established? And Allah knows best.

His saying: "The people had been afflicted with hardship" — meaning scarcity, need, and difficulty.

His saying: "yufrid" — meaning he pairs, i.e., he combines. It is with ḍammah on the rāʾ and kasrah, two variant forms.

His saying: "He prohibited al-iqrān" — this is how it appears in the authoritative sources, and the well-known form in the language is "al-qirān." It is said: "qarana bayna al-shayʾayn" (he paired between two things). They said: and it is not...
