chapters.arabic_text:
سبق إلى موضع من الشوارع ومقاعد الأسواق لمعاملة وأماقوله وكان بن عمر إذا

قام له رجل عن مجلسه لم يجلس فيه فهذا
# 
# ورع منه وليس قعوده فيه حراما إذا قام برضاه لكنه تورع عنه لوجهين أحدهما

أنه ربما استحى منه إنسان فقام له من مجلسه من غير طيب قلبه فسد بن عمر

الباب ليسلم من هذا والثاني أن الإيثار بالقرب مكروه أو خلاف الأولى فكان

بن عمر يمتنع من ذلك لئلا يرتكب أحد بسببه مكروها أو خلاف الأولى بأن يتأخر

عن موضعه من  الصف الأول ويؤثره به وشبه ذلك قال أصحابنا وإنما يحمد الإيثار

بحظوظ النفوس وأمور الدنيا دون القرب والله أعلم

| (باب اذا قام من مجلسه ثم عاد فهو أحق به)
# قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم
# [2179] (من قام من مجلسه ثم رجع إليه فهو أحق به) قال أصحابنا هذا الحديث

فيمن جلس في موضع من المسجد أو غيره لصلاة مثلاثم فارقه ليعود بأن فارقه

ليتوضأ أو يقضي
# 
# شغلا يسيرا ثم يعود لم يبطل اختصاصه بل إذا رجع فهو أحق به في تلك الصلاة

فإن كان قد قعد فيه غيره فله أن يقيمه وعلى القاعد أن يفارقه لهذا الحديث

هذا هو الصحيح عند أصحابنا وأنه يجب على من قعد فيه مفارقته اذا رجع الأول

وقال بعض العلماء هذا مستحب ولايجب وهو مذهب مالك والصواب الأول قال

أصحابنا ولافرق بين أن يقوم منه ويترك فيه سجادة ونحوها أم لافهذا أحق به

في الحالين قال أصحابنا وإنما يكون أحق به في تلك الصلاة وحدها دون غيرها

والله أعلم

| (باب منع المخنث من الدخول على النساء الاجانب)
# قولها
# [2181] (كان يدخل على أزواج النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم مخنث فكانوا يعدونه

من غير أولي الإربة فدخل النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يوما وهو عند بعض نسائه

وهو ينعت امرأة قال إذا أقبلت
# 
# أقبلت بأربع وإذا أدبرت أدبرت بثمان فقال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ألا

أرى هذا يعرف ماههنا لايدخل عليكن فحجبوه) قال أهل اللغة المخنث هو بكسر

النون وفتحها وهو الذي يشبه النساء في أخلاقه وكلامه وحركاته وتارة يكون

هذا خلقه من الأصل وتارة بتكلف وسنوضحهما قال أبو عبيد وسائر العلماء معنى

قوله تقبل بأربع وتدبر بثمان أي أربع عكن وثمان عكن قالوا ومعناه أن لها

أربع عكن تقبل بهن من كل ناحية اثنتان ولكل واحدة طرفان فإذا أدبرت صارت

الأطراف ثمانية قالوا وإنما ذكر فقال بثمان وكان أصله أن يقول بثمانية فإن

المراد الأطراف وهي مذكرة لأنه لم يذكر لفظ المذكر ومتى لم يذكره جاز  حذف

الهاء كقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم من صام رمضان وأتبعه بست من شوال سبقت

المسألة هناك واضحة وأما دخول هذا المخنث أولا على أمهات المؤمنين فقد بين

سببه في هذا الحديث بأنهم كانوا يعتقدونه من غير أولي الإربة وأنه مباح

دخوله عليهن فلما سمع منه هذا الكلام علم أنه من أولي الإربة فمنعه صلى

الله عليه وسلم الدخول ففيه منع المخنث من الدخول على النساء ومنعهن من

الظهور عليه وبيان أن له حكم الرجال الفحول الراغبين في النساء في هذا

المعنى وكذا حكم الخصي والمجبوب ذكره والله أعلم واختلف في اسم هذا المخنث

قال القاضي الأشهر أن اسمه هيت بكسر الهاء ومثناة تحت ساكنة ثم مثناة فوق

قال وقيل صوابه هنب بالنون والباء الموحدة قاله بن درستويه وقال إنما سواه

تصحيف قال والهنب الأحمق وقيل ماتع بالمثناة فوق مولى فاختة المخزومية وجاء

هذا في حديث آخر ذكر فيه أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم غرب ماتعا هذا وهيتا

إلى الحمى ذكره الواقدى وذكر أبومنصور البادردي نحو الحكاية عن مخنث كان

بالمدينة يقال له أنه وذكر أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم نفاه إلى حمراء

الأسد والمحفوظأنه هيت قال العلماء وإخراجه ونفيه كان لثلاثة معان أحدها

المعنى المذكور في الحديث أنه كان يظن أنه من غير أولي الإربة وكان منهم

ويتكتم بذلك والثاني وصفه النساء ومحاسنهن وعوراتهن بحضرة الرجال وقد نهي

أن تصف المرأة المرأة لزوجها
# 
# فكيف إذا وصفها الرجل للرجال والثالث أنه ظهر له منه أنه كان يطلع من

النساء وأجسامهن وعوراتهن على ما لا يطلع عليه كثير من النساء فكيف الرجال

لاسيما على ما جاء في غير مسلم أنه وصفها حتى وصف مابين رجليها أى فرجها

وحواليه والله أعلم
# قوله
# [2182] (عن أسماء إنها كانت تعلف فرس زوجها الزبير وتكفيه مؤنته وتسوسه

وتدق النو لناضحه وتعلفه وتستقي الماء وتعجن) هذا كله من المعروف والمروآت

التي أطبق الناس عليها وهو أن المرأة تخدم زوجها بهذه الأمور المذكورة

ونحوها من الخبز  والطبخ وغسل الثياب وغير ذلك وكله تبرع من المرأة وإحسان

منها إلى زوجها وحسن معاشرة وفعل معروف معه ولايجب عليها شيء من ذلك بل

لوامتنعت من جميع هذا لم تأثم ويلزمه هو تحصيل هذه الأمور لها ولا يحل
# 
# له إلزامها بشيء من هذا وإنما تفعله المرأة تبرعا وهي عادة جميلة استمر

عليها النساء من الزمن الأول إلى الآن وإنما الواجب على المرأة شيئان

تمكينها زوجها من نفسها وملازمة بيته قولها (وأخرز غربه) هو بغين معجمة
chapters.anchors:
- Root: و-ر-ع (w-r-ʿ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning is "to be cautious, to abstain, to avoid" — scrupulous avoidance of what is doubtful or potentially blameworthy.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological usage, *waraʿ* denotes a heightened state of piety where one abstains not only from the forbidden (ḥarām) but also from the permissible (mubāḥ) out of fear of approaching the unlawful.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense is "to shrink back" or "to keep away"; metaphorically, it signifies moral scrupulousness in refraining from acts that are legally permissible but spiritually perilous.
- Root: أ-ث-ر (a-th-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Root denotes "preference, choosing one thing over another" — from *athara* (to mention, narrate) and *īthār* (to prefer another over oneself).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): *Īthār* in ethical discourse is "self-preference of others" — giving precedence to another's need over one's own, especially in worldly matters.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: "to choose"; metaphorical: "altruism" — the act of yielding one's own advantage for another's benefit, which is praiseworthy in worldly goods but blameworthy in religious ranks.
- Root: خ-ن-ث (kh-n-th)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Root denotes "softness, effeminacy" — a man who resembles women in mannerisms, speech, and movement.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In legal discourse, *mukhannath* is a technical term for a man with effeminate traits, either innate or acquired, whose legal rulings depend on the degree of his inclination toward women.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: "to bend, to be pliant"; metaphorical: effeminacy as a deviation from the normative masculine disposition.
- Root: ع-ك-ن (ʿ-k-n)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Root denotes "folds of fat on the belly" — *ʿakan* (pl. *aʿkān*) are the rolls of flesh around the abdomen.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Used here in its literal anatomical sense, describing the physical features of a woman in the hadith.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Purely literal — no metaphorical extension; the term is confined to corporeal description.
- Sībawayh Rule: Rule of Numeric Agreement (al-Muṭābaqah al-ʿAdadiyyah) — When the noun being counted is masculine, the numeral takes the feminine form, and vice versa; however, if the noun is omitted and only the numeral is mentioned, the speaker may choose either form based on the implied referent. Here, "eight" (thamān) is used without the feminine *tāʾ* because the implied noun (*aṭrāf*, "extremities") is masculine.
chapters.translation:
I say: The discussion has preceded concerning one who precedes to a place in the thoroughfares and the seats of the markets for transactions. As for his saying — and Ibn ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with him) was such that when a man stood up for him from his seat, he would not sit in it — this is an act of scrupulous piety (waraʿ) on his part, and his sitting therein is not unlawful (ḥarām) when the man stands with his consent. Rather, he abstained from it for two reasons: First, that perhaps a man might feel shy before him and stand from his seat without his heart being pleased, so Ibn ʿUmar closed the door to avoid this. Second, that preferring others (īthār) with regard to religious ranks is disliked (makrūh) or contrary to what is more proper (khilāf al-awlā). Thus, Ibn ʿUmar refrained from that lest someone, on his account, commit a disliked act or one contrary to what is more proper — such as a man moving back from his place in the first row and preferring him with it, and the like. Our companions (aṣḥābunā) said: Indeed, īthār is only praiseworthy with regard to the shares of the soul and the matters of this world, not with regard to religious ranks. And Allah knows best.

| (Chapter: When One Stands from His Place Then Returns, He Has More Right to It)

His saying, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: {«[2179] Whoever stands from his place then returns to it, he has more right to it»}. Our companions said: This hadith concerns one who sits in a place in the mosque or elsewhere for a prayer, such as a supererogatory prayer, then leaves it intending to return — such as leaving to perform ablution or to fulfill a minor need — then returns; his claim (ikhtiṣāṣ) is not nullified. Rather, when he returns, he has more right to it for that prayer. If another has sat in it, he has the right to make him stand, and it is incumbent upon the one sitting to vacate it, according to this hadith. This is the correct view (al-ṣaḥīḥ) among our companions: that it is obligatory upon the one who sat in it to vacate it when the first returns. Some scholars said this is recommended (mustaḥabb) and not obligatory — and this is the school of Mālik. The correct view is the first. Our companions said: There is no difference between his leaving a prayer rug (sajjādah) or the like in it or not — he has more right to it in both cases. Our companions said: He only has more right to it for that particular prayer alone, not for other than it. And Allah knows best.

| (Chapter: Prohibiting the Effeminate Man (Mukhannath) from Entering upon Unrelated Women)

Her saying: {«[2181] An effeminate man (mukhannath) used to enter upon the wives of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and they used to count him among those who possess no desire (ghayr ulī al-irbah). Then the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, entered one day while he was with one of his wives, and he was describing a woman, saying: "When she approaches, she approaches with four, and when she retreats, she retreats with eight." The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: 'Do I not see that this man knows what is here? Let him not enter upon you.' So they veiled him from them.»} The people of language (ahl al-lughah) said: *Al-mukhannath* — with kasrah on the *nūn* and also with fatḥah — is one who resembles women in his morals, speech, and movements. Sometimes this is his innate nature from the origin, and sometimes it is affected (bi-takalluf). We will clarify both. Abū ʿUbayd and the rest of the scholars said: The meaning of his saying "she approaches with four and retreats with eight" is four folds of fat (ʿakan) and eight folds. They said: Its meaning is that she has four folds of fat with which she approaches — from each side two, and each one has two extremities. So when she retreats, the extremities become eight. They said: He mentioned "eight" (thamān) without the feminine *tāʾ*, whereas the original would be "eight" (thamāniyah), because the intended referent is the extremities (aṭrāf), which are masculine — for he did not mention the masculine noun explicitly. And whenever he does not mention it, it is permissible to drop the *tāʾ*, as in his saying, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: "Whoever fasts Ramadan and follows it with six (sitt) from Shawwāl" — the matter has been clarified there.

As for the entry of this effeminate man initially upon the Mothers of the Believers, its cause has been explained in this hadith: they used to believe he was among those who possess no desire, and that his entry upon them was permissible. When they heard this speech from him, they knew he was among those who possess desire, so the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, prohibited him from entering. In this is the prohibition of the effeminate man from entering upon women, and the prohibition of women from appearing before him, and the clarification that he has the ruling of virile men (al-rijāl al-fuḥūl) who desire women in this regard. Likewise is the ruling of the eunuch (khaṣī) and the one whose male organ has been cut off (majbūb). And Allah knows best.

There is disagreement over the name of this effeminate man. Al-Qāḍī said: The most well-known (al-ashhar) is that his name is Hīt — with kasrah on the *hāʾ*, a silent *tāʾ marbūṭah* (i.e., *yāʾ*), then a *tāʾ* with fatḥah. He said: And it was said the correct form is Hunab — with *nūn* and a single *bāʾ* — as stated by Ibn Duraystawayh, who said that anything else is a scribal corruption (taṣḥīf). And *al-hunab* means "the foolish one." And it was said: Mātiʿ — with a *tāʾ* with fatḥah — the freed slave of Fākhitah al-Makhzūmiyyah. This appears in another hadith in which it is mentioned that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, exiled this Mātiʿ and Hīt to the protected pasture (al-ḥimā). Al-Wāqidī mentioned this, and Abū Manṣūr al-Bādarī mentioned a similar account about an effeminate man in Medina called Anah, and that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, banished him to Ḥamrāʾ al-Asad. The preserved (al-maḥfūẓ) version is that it was Hīt.

The scholars said: His expulsion and banishment were for three reasons: First, the meaning mentioned in the hadith — that he was thought to be among those who possess no desire, but he was among them (i.e., those who do desire), and he concealed that. Second, his describing women, their beauties, and their private parts in the presence of men — for a woman has been prohibited from describing a woman to her husband, so how much more so when a man describes her to men? Third, that it became apparent from him that he used to observe of women, their bodies, and their private parts what many women themselves do not observe — so how much more so men? Especially given what has come in other than Muslim: that he described her until he described what is between her legs — meaning her vulva (farj) and its surroundings. And Allah knows best.

His saying: {«[2182] On the authority of Asmāʾ — that she used to feed the horse of her husband al-Zubayr, and suffice him its maintenance, and tend it, and pound the date-stones for his watering camel, and feed it, and draw water, and knead dough»} — All of this is from the acts of kindness (maʿrūf) and virtuous deeds (muruwwāt) upon which the people are in agreement: that a woman serves her husband in these mentioned matters and the like — such as baking bread, cooking, washing clothes, and other things. All of it is a voluntary gift (tabarruʿ) from the woman and an act of beneficence (iḥsān) from her to her husband, and good companionship, and an act of kindness toward him. None of it is obligatory upon her. Rather, if she refrained from all of this, she would not sin. And it is incumbent upon him to procure these matters for her, and it is not lawful for him to compel her to any of this. The woman only does it voluntarily, and it is a beautiful custom (ʿādah jamīlah) upon which women have continued from the earliest times until now. The only two things obligatory upon the woman are: granting her husband access to herself and remaining in his house.

Her saying: "And I stitch his water-skin (ukhrīzu ghirbah)" — *Ghirbah* is with a ghayn (muʿjamah, i.e., pointed).
