Al-Qāḍī said: This was a practice (sunnah) that the Salaf and people of knowledge would observe, confining themselves in that time to remembrance and supplication until the sun rose. In it also is the permissibility of conversing about the reports of the Jāhiliyyah and other nations, and the permissibility of laughter. However, the superior practice is to confine oneself to smiling (tabassum), as the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did in most of his times. They said: Excessive laughter is disliked (makrūh), and it is even more reprehensible among people of rank and knowledge. And Allah knows best.

| (Chapter: On His Mercy ﷺ Toward Women and Gentleness with Them)

His saying ﷺ [2323]: "O Anjashah, drive slowly with the glass vessels (al-qawārīr)!" And in another transmission: "Woe to you, O Anjashah, drive slowly with the glass vessels!" And in another transmission: "O Anjashah, do not break the glass vessels" — meaning the weak women.

As for Anjashah, it is with fatḥah on the hamzah, sukūn on the nūn, then jīm, then shīn with iʿjām (dotting). As for rawīdaka (slowly), it is in the accusative as an adjective (ṣifah) of an elided verbal noun (maṣdar), i.e., "drive a slow driving" (suq sawqan rawīdan). Its meaning is the command of gentleness with them. And "your driving" (sawquka) is accusative by the elision of the preposition, i.e., "be gentle in your driving with the glass vessels."

The scholars said: Women were called "glass vessels" (qawārīr) for the weakness of their resolutions, by way of analogy to the glass bottle for its fragility and the swiftness of breakage upon it. The scholars differed concerning the intended meaning of naming them qawārīr on two views, mentioned by al-Qāḍī and others. The more correct of the two according to al-Qāḍī and others — and the one affirmed by al-Harawī, the author of al-Taḥrīr, and others — is that its meaning is: Anjashah had a beautiful voice, and he would chant (yaḥdū) to the women and recite some poetry (qarīḍ) and rajaz containing amorous allusion (tashbīb), and it was not safe that he would captivate them and that his chanting would fall into their hearts. So he ﷺ commanded him to desist from that. Among their well-known proverbs is: "The song of the camel-driver is fornication." Al-Qāḍī said: This is more fitting to the intent of the Prophet ﷺ and to the requirement of the wording. He said: And it is what the statement of Abū Qilābah, mentioned in this hadith in Muslim, indicates. And the saying —

chapters.title_en: Section 857 — On Gentleness in Travel, the Prophet's Proximity to People, His Humility, Avoidance of Sin, and His Goodly Scent
chapters.arabic_text:
الثاني أن المراد به الرفق في السير لأن الإبل إذا سمعت الحداء أسرعت في

المشي واستلذته فأزعجت الراكب وأتعبته فنهاه عن ذلك لأن النساء يضعفن عند

شدة الحركة ويخاف ضررهن وسقوطهن وأما ويحك فهكذا وقع في مسلم ووقع في غيره

ويلك قال القاضي قال سيبويه ويل كلمة تقال لمن وقع في هلكة وويح زجر لمن

أشرف على الوقوع في هلكة وقال الفراء ويل وويح وويس بمعنى وقيل ويح كلمة

لمن وقع في هلكة لا يستحقها يعني في عرفنا فيرثي له ويترحم عليه وويل ضده

قال القاضي قال بعض أهل اللغة لا يراد بهذه الألفاظ حقيقة الدعاء وإنما

يراد بها المدح والتعجب وفي هذه الأحاديث جواز الحداء وهو بضم الحاء ممدود

وجواز السفر بالنساء واستعمال المجاز وفيه مباعدة النساء من الرجال ومن

سماع كلامهم إلا الوعظ ونحوه
#

| (باب قربه صلى الله عليه وسلم من الناس (وتبركهم به
# وتواضعه لهم) قوله
# [2324] (كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا صلى الغداة جاء خدم

المدينة بآنيتهم فيها الماء فما يؤتى بإناء إلا غمس يده فيها فربما جاءوه

في الغداة الباردة فيغمس يده فيها) وفي الرواية الأخرى
# [2325] (رأيت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم والحلاق يحلقه وأطاف به

أصحابه فما يريدون أن تقع شعرة إلا في يد رجل) وفي الآخر
# [2326] (أن امرأة كانت في عقلها شيء فقالت يا رسول الله إن لي اليك حاجة

فقال ياأم فلان انظري أي السكك شئت حتى أقضي لك حاجتك فخلا معها في بعض

الطرق حتى فرغت من حاجتها) في هذه الأحاديث بيان  بروزه صلى الله عليه وسلم

للناس وقربه منهم ليصل أهل الحقوق إلى حقوقهم ويرشد مسترشدهم ليشاهدوا

أفعاله وحركاته فيقتدى بها وهكذا ينبغي لولاة الأمور وفيها صبره صلى الله

عليه وسلم على المشقة في نفسه لمصلحة المسلمين وإجابته من سأله حاجة أو

تبريكا بمس يده وإدخالها في الماء كما ذكروا وفيه التبرك بآثار الصالحين

وبيان ما كانت الصحابة عليه من التبرك بآثاره صلى الله عليه وسلم وتبركهم

بإدخال يده الكريمة في الآنية وتبركهم بشعره الكريم وإكرامهم إياه أن يقع

شيء منه إلا في يد رجل سبق إليه وبيان تواضعه بوقوفه مع المرأة الضعيفة

قوله)
# 
# (خلا معها في بعض الطرق) أي وقف معها في طريق مسلوك ليقضي حاجتها ويفتيها

في الخلوة ولم يكن ذلك من الخلوة بالأجنبية فإن هذا كان في ممر الناس

ومشاهدتهم إياه وإياها لكن لا يسمعون كلامها لأن مسألتها مما لا يظهره

والله أعلم

| (باب مباعدته صلى الله عليه وسلم للآثام واختياره من 
# المباح أسهله)
# (وانتقامه لله تعالى عند انتهاك حرماته) قولها
# [2327] (ماخير رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بين أمرين إلا أخذ أيسرهما

ما لم يكن إثما فإن كان إثما كان أبعد الناس منه) فيه استحباب الأخذبالأيسر

والأرفق ما لم يكن حراما أو مكروها قال القاضي ويحتمل أن يكون تخييره صلى

الله عليه وسلم هنا من الله تعالى فيخيره فيما فيه عقوبتان أو فيما بينه

وبين الكفار من القتال وأخذ الجزية أو في حق أمته في المجاهدة في العبادة

أو الاقتصار وكان يختار الأيسر في كل هذا قال وأما قولها ما لم يكن إثما

فيتصوراذا خيره الكفار والمنافقون فأما إن كان التخيير من الله تعالى أو من

المسلمين فيكون الاستثناء منقطعا قولها (وما انتقم رسول الله صلى الله عليه

وسلم لنفسه إلا أن تنتهك حرمة الله) وفي رواية
# [2328] ما نيل منه شيء قط فينتقم من صاحبه إلا أن ينتهك
# 
# شيءمن محارم الله تعالى فينتقم لله تعالى) معنى نيل منه أصيب بأذى من قول

أو فعل وانتهاك حرمة الله  تعالى هو ارتكاب ما حرمه قولها (إلا أن تنتهك

حرمة الله) استثناء منقطع معناه لكن إذا انتهكت حرمة الله انتصر لله تعالى

وانتقم ممن ارتكب ذلك في هذا الحديث الحث على العفو والحلم واحتمال الأذى

والانتصار لدين الله تعالى ممن فعل محرما أو نحوه وفيه أنه يستحب للأئمة

والقضاة وسائر ولاة الأمور التخلق بهذا الخلق الكريم فلا ينتقم لنفسه ولا

يهمل حق الله تعالى قال القاضي عياض وقد أجمع العلماء على أن القاضي لا

يقضي لنفسه ولا لمن لا يجوز شهادته له قولها (ما ضرب رسول الله صلى الله

عليه وسلم شيئا قط بيده ولا امرأة ولا خادما إلا أن يجاهد في سبيل الله)

فيه أن ضرب الزوجة والخادم والدابة وإن كان مباحا للأدب فتركه أفضل
#

| باب طيب ريحه صلى الله عليه وسلم ولين مسه
# قوله
# [2329] (صلاة الأولى) يعنى الظهر والوالدان الصبيان واحدهم وليد وفي مسحه

صلى الله عليه وسلم الصبيان بيان حسن خلقه ورحمته للأطفال وملاطفتهم وفي

هذه الأحاديث بيان طيب ريحه صلى الله عليه وسلم وهو مما أكرمه الله تعالى

قال العلماء كانت هذه الريح الطيبة صفته صلى الله عليه وسلم وإن لم يمس

طيبا ومع هذا فكان يستعمل الطيب في كثير من الأوقات مبالغة في طيب ريحه

لملاقاة الملائكة وأخذ الوحي الكريم ومجالسة المسلمين قوله (كأنما أخرجت من

جؤنة عطار) هي بضم الجيم وهمزة بعدها ويجوز ترك الهمزة بقلبها واوا كما في
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ر-ف-ق (rafaqa)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Gentleness, kindness, and ease in conduct; the opposite of harshness (ʿunf).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Refers to the virtue of leniency (rifq) as a praiseworthy trait in all affairs, aligning with divine command.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) in physical motion; metaphorical (majāz) in moral disposition.
- Root: و-ي-ل (wayl) / و-ي-ح (wayḥ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Wayl denotes one fallen into ruin (halakah); wayḥ denotes one approaching ruin.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Theological nuance — wayl is a threat of punishment; wayḥ is an expression of pity.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Both are exclamatory; not literal imprecation but rhetorical devices for praise or wonder.
- Sībawayh Rule: Istithnāʾ Munqaṭiʿ (Discontinuous Exception) — The exception clause (e.g., "except that a sanctity of Allah be violated") is not from the same category as the negated antecedent, requiring reanalysis as a separate affirmation.
chapters.translation:
I say: The second [interpretation] is that the intended meaning is gentleness in travel, for when camels hear the driver's chant (ḥudāʾ), they hasten in their pace and find pleasure in it, thereby jolting the rider and wearying him. Thus he (peace and blessings be upon him) forbade that, because women grow weak under intense motion, and harm and falling are feared for them.

As for his saying "wayḥaka" (woe to you) — thus it occurred in Muslim, and in other [books] it occurred as "waylaka." Al-Qāḍī [ʿIyāḍ] said: Sībawayh stated that "wayl" is an expression uttered for one who has fallen into ruin (halakah), while "wayḥ" is a rebuke for one who is on the verge of falling into ruin. Al-Farrāʾ said: "wayl," "wayḥ," and "ways" are synonymous. And it was said: "wayḥ" is an expression for one who has fallen into ruin without deserving it — meaning, in our customary usage — so one expresses pity for him and invokes mercy upon him, whereas "wayl" is its opposite. Al-Qāḍī said: Some philologists stated that these expressions do not intend the literal meaning of supplication (duʿāʾ); rather, they intend praise and wonderment.

In these ḥadīths is the permissibility of the driver's chant (ḥudāʾ) — with ḍammah on the ḥāʾ and lengthened — and the permissibility of traveling with women, and the use of metaphor (majāz). And in them is [the principle of] keeping women distant from men and from hearing their speech, except for admonition and the like.

---

| Chapter: On His (peace and blessings be upon him) Proximity to People and Their Seeking Blessings from Him, and His Humility Toward Them |

His saying — [2324]: "When the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) prayed the morning prayer, the servants of Medina would come with their vessels containing water, and no vessel was brought except that he dipped his hand into it — and sometimes they came to him in the cold morning, and he would dip his hand into it." And in the other narration — [2325]: "I saw the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) while the barber was shaving his head, and his companions surrounded him, such that they did not want a single hair to fall except into the hand of a man." And in the other — [2326]: "That a woman who had some mental affliction said: 'O Messenger of Allah, I have a need of you.' He said: 'O mother of so-and-so, look at whichever of the streets you wish, until I fulfill your need.' So he secluded himself with her in one of the paths until she finished her need."

In these ḥadīths is an exposition of his (peace and blessings be upon him) coming forth to the people and his proximity to them, so that those with rights might attain their rights, and the seeker of guidance might be guided, and so that they might witness his actions and movements and emulate them. Thus should it be for those in authority. And in them is his (peace and blessings be upon him) patience upon hardship to himself for the benefit of the Muslims, and his answering whoever asked him for a need or sought blessing through the touch of his hand and its insertion into water, as they mentioned. And in them is the seeking of blessings (tabarruk) through the traces of the righteous, and an exposition of what the Companions were upon of seeking blessings through his traces (peace and blessings be upon him) — their seeking blessings through the insertion of his noble hand into vessels, and their seeking blessings through his noble hair, and their honoring of it such that nothing of it fell except into the hand of a man who preceded [others] to it. And in them is an exposition of his humility in standing with the weak woman.

His saying — "he secluded himself with her in one of the paths" — meaning, he stood with her in a traveled road to fulfill her need and give her a legal ruling in private. This was not of the [forbidden] seclusion with a foreign woman, for this was in the passage of people and their witnessing of him and her — though they did not hear her speech, because her question was of the sort not to be made public. And Allah knows best.

---

| Chapter: On His (peace and blessings be upon him) Distancing from Sins and His Choosing the Easiest of the Permissible, and His Taking Revenge for Allah Almighty When His Sanctities Are Violated |

Her saying — [2327]: "The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) was never given a choice between two matters except that he took the easier of them, so long as it was not a sin; if it was a sin, he was the most distant of people from it." In it is the recommendation of taking the easier and gentler [option] so long as it is not forbidden (ḥarām) or disliked (makrūh). Al-Qāḍī said: It is possible that his (peace and blessings be upon him) being given a choice here was from Allah Almighty, who gave him choice regarding matters involving two punishments, or regarding what was between him and the disbelievers of fighting or taking the jizyah, or regarding the right of his community in striving in worship or limiting [oneself]. And he would choose the easier in all of this. He said: As for her saying "so long as it was not a sin" — this is conceivable if the disbelievers and hypocrites gave him the choice. But if the choice was from Allah Almighty or from the Muslims, then the exception is discontinuous (munqaṭiʿ).

Her saying: "And the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) never took revenge for himself, except that a sanctity of Allah be violated." And in another narration — [2328]: "Nothing was ever inflicted upon him such that he would take revenge from its perpetrator, except that something of the sacred prohibitions of Allah Almighty be violated, and he would take revenge for Allah Almighty." The meaning of "inflicted upon him" (nīla minhu) is: he was harmed by speech or action. And the violation of the sanctity of Allah Almighty is the commission of what He has forbidden. Her saying "except that a sanctity of Allah be violated" is a discontinuous exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ); its meaning is: but when a sanctity of Allah is violated, he would defend the religion of Allah and take revenge from the one who committed that.

In this ḥadīth is an encouragement toward pardon (ʿafw), forbearance (ḥilm), and enduring harm, and toward defending the religion of Allah Almighty against one who commits a forbidden act or the like. And in it is that it is recommended for the imams, judges, and all those in authority to adopt this noble character — not taking revenge for themselves, nor neglecting the right of Allah Almighty. Al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ said: The scholars have unanimously agreed that the judge does not adjudicate for himself, nor for one whose testimony is not permissible for him.

Her saying: "The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) never struck anything with his hand — neither a woman nor a servant — except when striving in the path of Allah." In it is that striking one's wife, servant, or animal, though permissible for discipline, its abandonment is more virtuous.

---

| Chapter: On the Pleasantness of His (peace and blessings be upon him) Scent and the Softness of His Touch |

His saying — [2329]: "The first prayer" — meaning the ẓuhr. And "al-waladān" (the two children) — their singular is "walīd." And in his (peace and blessings be upon him) wiping over the children is an exposition of his beautiful character, his mercy toward children, and his gentleness with them.

In these ḥadīths is an exposition of the pleasantness of his (peace and blessings be upon him) scent — which is among the things with which Allah Almighty honored him. The scholars said: This pleasant scent was his (peace and blessings be upon him) inherent quality, even if he had not touched perfume. Nevertheless, he would use perfume on many occasions, as an excess in the pleasantness of his scent, for meeting the angels, receiving the noble revelation, and sitting with the Muslims.

His saying — "as though it had been brought out from a perfumer's chest (juʾnah)" — it is with ḍammah on the jīm and a hamzah after it, and it is permissible to omit the hamzah by converting it to a wāw, as in [the variant reading].

chapters.title_en: Section 858 — On the Prophet's Sweat, Its Fragrance, and Seeking Blessing Through It; The Description of His Hair and Attributes
chapters.arabic_text:
نظائرها وقد ذكرها كثيرون أو الأكثرون في الواو قال القاضي هي مهموزة وقد

يترك همزها وقال الجوهري هي بالواو وقد تهمز وهي السقط الذي فيه متاع

العطار هكذا فسره الجمهور وقال صاحب العين هي سليلة مستديرة
# 
# مغشاة وأما قوله
# [2330] (ماشممت) هو بكسر الميم الأولى على المشهور وحكى أبو عبيد وبن

السكيت والجوهري وآخرون فتحها قوله (أزهر اللون) هو الأبيض المستنير وهي

أحسن الألوان قوله (كأن عرقه اللؤلؤ) أي في الصفاء والبياض واللؤلؤ بهمز

أوله وآخره وبتركهما وبهمز الأول دون الثاني وعكسه قوله (إذا مشى تكفأ)  هو

بالهمز وقد يترك همزه وزعم كثيرون أن أكثر ما يروى بلا همز وليس كما قالوا

قال شمر أي مال يمينا وشمالا كما تكفأ السفينة قال الأزهري هذا خطأ لأن هذا

صفة المختال وإنما معناه أن يميل إلى سمته وقصد مشيه كما قال في الرواية

الأخرى كأنما ينحط في صبب قال القاضي لابعد فيما قاله شمر إذا كان خلقة

وجبلة والمذموم منه ما كان مستعملا مقصودا

| (باب طيب عرقه صلى الله عليه وسلم والتبرك به قوله
# [2331] (فقال عندنا فعرق) أي نام للقيلولة قوله (تسلت العرق) أي تمسحه

وتتبعه بالمسح قوله)
# 
# (كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يدخل بيت أم سليم فينام على فراشها) قد

سبق أنها كانت محرما له صلى الله عليه وسلم ففيه الدخول على المحارم والنوم

عندهن وفي بيوتهن وجواز النوم على الأدم وهي الأنطاع والجلود قوله (ففتحت

عتيدتها) هي بعين مهملة مفتوحة ثم مثناة من فوق ثم من تحت وهي كالصندوق

الصغير تجعل المرأة فيه ما يعز من متاعها قوله (ففزع النبي صلى الله عليه

وسلم فقال ما تصنعين) معنى فزع استيقظ من نومه قولها
# [2332] (عرقك أدوف به طيبي) هو بالدال المهملة وبالمعجمة
# 
# والأكثرون على المهملة وكذا نقله القاضي عن رواية الأكثرين ومعناه غلط

وسبق بيان هذه اللفظة في أول كتاب الايمان قوله (كيف يأتيك الوحي فقال

أحيانا يأتيني مثل صلصلة الجرس وهو أشد علي ثم يفصم عني وقد وعيته وأحيانا

ملك في مثل صورة الرجل فأعي ما يقول) أما الأحيان فالأزمان ويقع على القليل

والكثير ومثل صلصلة هو بنصب مثل وأما الصلصلة فبفتح الصادين وهي الصوت

المتدارك قال الخطابي معناه أنه صوت متدارك يسمعه ولا يثبته أول ما يقرع

سمعه حتى يفهمه من بعد ذلك قال العلماء والحكمة في ذلك أن يتفرغ سمعه صلى

الله عليه وسلم ولا يبقى فيه ولا في قلبه مكان لغير صوت الملك ومعنى وعيت

جمعت وفهمت وحفظت وأما يفصم فبفتح الياء وإسكان الفاء وكسر الصاد المهملة

أي يقلع وينجلي ما يتغشاني  منه قاله الخطابي قال العلماء الفصم هو القطع من

غير إبانة وأما القصم بالقاف فقطع مع الإبانة والانفصال ومعنى الحديث أن

الملك يفارق على أن يعود ولا يفارقه مفارقة قاطع لا يعود وروي هذا الحرف

أيضا يفصم بضم الياء وفتح الصاد على ما لم يسم فاعله وروي بضم الياء وكسر

الصاد على أنه أفصم يفصم
# 
# رباعي وهي لغة قليلة وهي من أفصم المطر إذا أقلع وكف قال العلماء ذكر في

هذا الحديث حالين من أحوال الوحي وهما مثل صلصلة الجرس وتمثل الملك رجلا

ولم يذكر الرؤيا في النوم وهي من الوحي لأن مقصود السائل بيان ما يختص به

النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ويخفى فلا يعرف إلا من جهته وأما الرؤيا فمشتركة

معروفة قوله
# [2334] (كرب لذلك وتربد وجهه) هو بضم الكاف وكسر الراء ومعنى تربد أي

تغير وصار كلون الرماد وفي ظاهر هذا مخالفة لما سبق في أول كتاب الحج في

حديث المحرم الذي أحرم بالعمرة وعليه خلوق وأن يعلى بن أمية نظر إلى النبي

صلى الله عليه وسلم حال نزول الوحي وهو محمر الوجه وجوابه أنها حمرة كدرة

وهذا معنى التربد وأنه في أوله يتربد ثم يحمر أو بالعكس قوله
# [2335] (أتلي عنه) هكذا هو في معظم نسخ بلادنا أتلي بهمزة ومثناة فوق

ساكنة ولام وياء ومعناه ارتفع عنه الوحي هكذا فسره صاحب التحرير وغيره ووقع

في بعض النسخ أجلى بالجيم وفي رواية بن ماهان انجلى ومعناهما أزيل عنه وزال

عنه وفي رواية البخاري انجلى والله أعلم
#

| باب صفة شعره صلى الله عليه وسلم وصفاته وحليته
# قوله
# [2336] (كان أهل الكتاب يسدلون أشعارهم وكان المشركون يفرقون رؤسهم وكان

رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يحب موافقة أهل الكتاب فيما لم يؤمر به فسدل

ناصيته ثم فرق بعد) قال أهل اللغة يقال سدل يسدل ويسدل بضم الدال وكسرها

قال القاضي سدل الشعر إرساله قال والمراد به هنا عند العلماء إرساله على

الجبين واتخاذه كالقصة يقال سدل شعره وثوبه إذا أرسله ولم يضم  جوانبه وأما

الفرق فهو فرق الشعر بعضه من بعض قال العلماء والفرق سنة لأنه الذي رجع

إليه النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قالوا فالظاهر أنه إنما رجع إليه بوحي لقوله

إنه كان يوافق أهل الكتاب فيما لم يؤمر به قال القاضي حتى قال بعضهم نسخ

المسدل فلا يجوز فعله ولا اتخاذ الناصية والجمة قال ويحتمل أن المراد جواز

الفرق لا وجوبه ويحتمل أن الفرق كان باجتهاد في مخالفة أهل الكتاب لا بوحي
chapters.anchors:
- Root: و-ت-ر (watara) / س-د-ل (sadala)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: "Watara" denotes a single strand or cord; "sadala" means to let hang loosely, to release without gathering the sides.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological usage, "sadl" (letting hair hang) contrasts with "farq" (parting), the latter being the divinely endorsed practice after abrogation.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for physical hair; metaphorical for obedience — "sadl" implies passive conformity, "farq" implies deliberate distinction.
- Sībawayh Rule: Rule of Verbal Noun Derivation (Maṣdar) — The variation in voweling (e.g., "yasdulu" vs. "yasdilu") reflects dialectal (lughāt) rather than syntactic shifts, permissible in classical prose.
chapters.translation:
I say: And its parallels have been mentioned by many — or most — scholars regarding the letter "wāw." Al-Qāḍī said: It is hamzated, and its hamza may occasionally be dropped. Al-Jawharī said: It is with "wāw," and it may be hamzated; it is the small basket containing the perfumer's wares — thus the majority have explained it. The author of Kitāb al-ʿAyn said: It is a round, covered basket.

As for his saying {[2330] "mā shamamtu"} — it is with kasra on the first mīm according to the well-known transmission. Abū ʿUbayd, Ibn al-Sikkīt, al-Jawharī, and others have related its fatḥa. His saying "azhar al-lawn" (bright of color) means the luminous white, which is the most excellent of colors. His saying "as if his sweat were pearls" — meaning in purity and whiteness. "Pearls" (al-luʾluʾ) is with hamza on its first and last letters, or with both dropped, or with hamza on the first but not the last, or the reverse.

His saying "when he walked, he leaned (takaffaʾa)" — it is with hamza, and its hamza may be dropped. Many have claimed that the predominant transmission is without hamza, but they are not correct in this. Shammar said: It means he inclined right and left as a ship leans. Al-Azharī said: This is an error, for this is the description of one who walks with vain conceit; rather, its meaning is that he inclined toward his natural bearing and the direction of his gait, as stated in the other narration: "as if he were descending a slope." Al-Qāḍī said: There is no harm in what Shammar stated if it were innate and natural; the blameworthy form is that which is affected and intentional.

| Chapter: On the Fragrance of the Prophet's Sweat (peace and blessings be upon him) and Seeking Blessing Through It.

His saying {[2331] "she said: We have it with us, so he sweated"} — meaning he slept for the midday nap (qaylūlah). Her saying "she wiped away the sweat (tasallat al-ʿaraq)" — meaning she wiped it and followed it with her hand.

His saying "The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) used to enter the house of Umm Sulaym and sleep on her mattress" — it has already been mentioned that she was a close relative unlawful for him to marry (maḥram). In this is the permissibility of entering upon maḥram women, sleeping in their presence and in their houses, and the permissibility of sleeping on leather (adam) — which are the hides and skins.

His saying "she opened her ʿatīdah" — it is with an open ʿayn (unpointed), then a doubled tāʾ above, then a tāʾ below; it is like a small chest in which a woman places her precious belongings.

His saying "the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) was startled (fazaʿa) and said: What are you doing?" — the meaning of "fazaʿa" here is that he awoke from his sleep.

Her saying {[2332] "your sweat, which I mix into my perfume (adūfu bihi ṭībī)"} — it is with an unpointed dāl, and also with a pointed one; the majority transmit the unpointed. Al-Qāḍī likewise transmitted this from the narration of the majority. Its meaning is "to mix," and the explanation of this word has preceded in the beginning of the Book of Faith.

His saying "How does revelation come to you? He said: Sometimes it comes to me like the ringing of a bell (ṣalṣalah), and that is most severe upon me; then it leaves me (yufṣamu ʿannī) and I have comprehended it. And sometimes the angel appears to me in the form of a man, and I retain what he says." — As for "aḥyān" (times), it denotes periods and applies to both few and many. "Like the ringing" (mithla ṣalṣalah) — "mithla" is in the accusative. As for "ṣalṣalah," it is with fatḥa on both ṣāds; it is the continuous, successive sound. Al-Khaṭṭābī said: Its meaning is a continuous sound that he hears but does not firmly grasp at the first striking of his ear, until he comprehends it afterward. The scholars said: The wisdom in this is that his hearing (peace and blessings be upon him) becomes entirely devoted, leaving no place in it or in his heart for anything other than the angel's voice. The meaning of "waʿaytu" is: I gathered, understood, and preserved. As for "yufṣamu" — it is with fatḥa on the yāʾ, sukūn on the fāʾ, and kasra on the unpointed ṣād; i.e., it is pulled away and dispelled from me. Al-Khaṭṭābī said this. The scholars said: "Faṣm" is cutting without complete separation, whereas "qaṣm" (with qāf) is cutting with complete separation and detachment. The meaning of the ḥadīth is that the angel departs with the intention of returning; he does not part from him as one who cuts off and never returns. This word is also transmitted as "yufṣamu" with ḍamma on the yāʾ and fatḥa on the ṣād, in the passive voice; and with ḍamma on the yāʾ and kasra on the ṣād, as a quadrilateral verb "afṣama-yufṣimu" — a rare dialect, derived from "afṣama al-maṭar" (the rain ceased and held back).

The scholars said: In this ḥadīth, two states of revelation are mentioned — the ringing of the bell and the angel's manifestation as a man — but the dream-vision (ruʾyā) in sleep is not mentioned, though it is a form of revelation, because the questioner's purpose was to clarify what is specific to the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) and hidden, known only from him. As for the ruʾyā, it is shared and well-known.

His saying {[2334] "his face became troubled (kariba) and changed color (tarabbada)"} — it is with ḍamma on the kāf and kasra on the rāʾ. The meaning of "tarabbada" is: it changed and became the color of ashes. In its apparent sense, this contradicts what preceded in the beginning of the Book of Pilgrimage in the ḥadīth of the muḥrim who entered iḥrām for ʿumrah wearing perfume (khalūq), where Yaʿlā ibn Umayyah looked at the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) during revelation and his face was red. The answer is that it was a dull, turbid redness — and this is the meaning of "tarabbud"; that at first it becomes ashen, then reddens, or the reverse.

His saying {[2335] "atalā ʿannī"} — thus it is in most copies of our lands: with hamza, a silent tāʾ (above), lām, and yāʾ. Its meaning is: the revelation lifted from him. Thus the author of al-Taḥrīr and others explained it. In some copies it occurs as "ajlā" with jīm, and in Ibn Māhān's narration "injalā" — both meaning: it was removed from him and departed from him. In al-Bukhārī's narration it is "injalā." And God knows best.

| Chapter: On the Description of the Prophet's Hair (peace and blessings be upon him), His Attributes, and His Physical Beauty.

His saying {[2336] "The People of the Book used to let their hair hang down (yasdilūna ashʿārahum), and the polytheists used to part their hair (yufarriqūna ruʾūsahum). The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) loved to conform to the People of the Book in matters he was not commanded otherwise, so he let his forelock hang, then afterward he parted it."} — The linguists say: One says "sadala yasdulu" and "yasdilu" — with ḍamma or kasra on the dāl. Al-Qāḍī said: "Sadl" of hair is letting it hang loose. The intended meaning here, according to the scholars, is letting it hang over the forehead and making it like a forelock (qaṣṣah). One says "sadala shaʿrahu wa thawbahu" when he lets it hang and does not gather its sides. As for "farq," it is parting the hair, some from some. The scholars said: Parting is Sunnah, because it is what the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) ultimately adopted. They said: The apparent view is that he only reverted to it by revelation, given his statement that he used to conform to the People of the Book in matters he was not commanded otherwise. Al-Qāḍī said: Some even held that the "musdal" (hanging style) was abrogated, so it is impermissible to practice it or to adopt a forelock and full mane. He said: It is also possible that the intended meaning is the permissibility of parting, not its obligation; and it is possible that the parting was by his own ijtihād to differ from the People of the Book, not by revelation.

chapters.title_en: Section 859 — On the Permissibility of Letting Hair Hang Loose (Sadl) versus Parting It (Farq), and Descriptions of the Prophet's (ﷺ) Physical Attributes
chapters.arabic_text:
ويكون الفرق مستحبا ولهذا اختلف السلف فيه ففرق منهم جماعة واتخذ اللمة

آخرون وقد جاء في الحديث أنه كان للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لمة فإن انفرقت

فرقها وإلا تركها قال مالك فرق الرجل أحب إلي هذا كلام القاضي والحاصل أن

الصحيح المختار جواز السدل والفرق وأن الفرق أفضل والله أعلم قال القاضي

واختلف العلماء في تأويل موافقة أهل الكتاب فيما لم ينزل عليه شيء فقيل

فعله استئلافا لهم في أول الإسلام وموافقة لهم على مخالفة عبدة الأوثان

فلما أغنى الله تعالى عن استئلافهم وأظهر الإسلام على الدين كله صرح

بمخالفتهم في غير شيء منها صبغ الشيب وقال آخرون يحتمل أنه أمر باتباع

شرائعهم فيما لم يوح إليه شيء وإنما كان هذا فيما علم أنهم لم يبدلوه

واستدل بعض الأصوليين بهذا الحديث أن شرع من قبلنا شرع لنا ما لم)
# 
# يرد شرعنا بخلافه وقال آخرون بل هذا دليل أنه ليس بشرع لنا لأنه قال يحب

موافقتهم فأشار إلى أنه إلى خيرته ولو كان شرعا لنا لتحتم اتباعه والله

أعلم قوله
# [2337] (كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم مربوعا) هو بمعنى قوله في

الرواية الثانية ليس بالطويل ولا بالقصير قوله (عظيم الجمة إلى شحمة أذنيه)

وفي رواية ما رأيت من ذي لمة أحسن منه وفي رواية كان يضرب شعره منكبيه وفي

رواية إلى أنصاف أذنيه وفي رواية بين أذنيه وعاتقه قال أهل اللغة الجمة

أكثر من الوفرة فالجمة الشعر الذي نزل إلى المنكبين والوفرة مانزل إلى شحمة

الأذنين واللمة  التي ألمت بالمنكبين قال القاضي والجمع بين هذه الروايات أن

ما يلي الأذن هو الذي يبلغ شحمة أذنيه وهو الذي بين أذنيه وعاتقه وما خلفه

هو الذي يضرب منكبيه قال وقيل بل ذلك لاختلاف الأوقات فإذا غفل عن تقصيرها

بلغت المنكب وإذا قصرها كانت إلى أنصاف الأذنين فكان يقصر ويطول بحسب ذلك

والعاتق ما بين المنكب والعنق وأما شحمة الأذن فهو اللين منها في أسفلها

وهو معلق القرط منها وتوضح هذه الروايات رواية إبراهيم الحربي كان
# 
# شعر رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فوق الوفرة ودون الجمة قوله في حديث

البراء (كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أحسن الناس وجها وأحسنهم خلقا)

قال القاضي ضبطناه خلقا بفتح الخاء وإسكان اللام هنا لأن مراده صفات جسمه

قال وأما في حديث أنس فرويناه بالضم لأنه إنما أخبر عن حسن معاشرته وأما

قوله وأحسنه فقال أبو حاتم وغيره هكذا تقوله العرب وأحسنه يريدون وأحسنهم

ولكن لا يتكلمون به وإنما يقولون أجمل الناس وأحسنه ومنه الحديث خير نساء

ركبن الإبل نساء قريش أشفقه على ولد وأعطفه على زوج وحديث أبي سفيان عندي

أحسن نساء العرب وأجمله قوله
# [2338] (كان شعرا رجلا ليس بالجعد ولا السبط) هو بفتح الراء وكسر الجيم

وهو الذي بين الجعودة والسبوطة قاله الأصمعي
# 
# وغيره قوله
# [2339] (عن شعبة عن سماك بن حرب قال سمعت جابر بن سمرة قال كان رسول الله

صلى الله عليه وسلم ضليع الفم أشكل العين منهوس العقبين قال قلت لسماك ما

ضليع الفم قال عظيم الفم قلت ما أشكل العين قال طويل شق العين قلت ما منهوس

العقب قال قليل لحم العقب) أما قوله في ضليع الفم فكذا قاله الأكثرون وهو

الأظهر قالوا والعرب تمدح بذلك وتذم صغر الفم وهو معنى قول ثعلب في ضليع

الفم واسع الفم وقال شمر عظيم الأسنان وأما قوله في أشكل العين فقال القاضي

هذا وهم من سماك باتفاق العلماء وغلط ظاهر وصوابه ما اتفق عليه العلماء

ونقله أبو عبيد وجميع أصحاب  الغريب أن الشكلة حمرة في بياض العينين وهو

محمود والشهلة بالهاء حمرة في سواد العين وأما المنهوس فبالسين المهملة

هكذا ضبطه الجمهور وقال صاحب التحرير وبن الأثير روي بالمهملة والمعجمة

وهما متقاربان ومعناه قليل لحم العقب كما قال والله أعلم
# 
# قوله
# [2340] (كان أبيض مليحا مقصدا) هو بفتح الصاد المشددة وهو الذي ليس بجسيم

ولا نحيف ولا طويل ولا قصير وقال شمر هو نحو الربعة والقصد بمعناه والله

أعلم

| (باب شيبه صلى الله عليه وسلم)
# قوله
# [2341] (سألت أنس بن مالك هل كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم خضب فقال

لم يبلغ الخضاب كان في لحيته شعرات بيض) وفي رواية لم ير من الشيب إلا

قليلا وفي رواية لو شئت أن أعد شمطات كن في رأسه ولم يخضب وفي رواية لم

يخضب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إنما كان البياض في عنفقته وفي الصدغين

وفي الرأس نبذ وفي رواية ما شانه الله ببيضاء
# [2342] وفي رواية أبي جحيفة رأيت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم هذه منه

بيضاء ووضع الراوي بعض أصابعه على عنفقته
# [2343] وفي رواية له رأيت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أبيض قد شاب
# [2344] وفي رواية جابر بن سمرة أنه سئل عن شيب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

فقال كان إذا دهن رأسه لم ير منه شيء وإذا لم يدهن رئي منه وفي رواية له

كان قد شمط مقدم رأسه ولحيته وفي رواية لأنس يعد عدا توفي وليس
# 
# في رأسه ولحيته عشرون شعرة بيضاء وفي حديث أم سلمة أنها أخرجت لهم شعرات
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ف-ر-ق (f-r-q)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Separation, division, distinguishing between two things; al-farq is the parting of hair.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Differentiation as an act of discernment; in legal context, distinguishing between permissible options.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) — physical parting of hair; metaphorical (majāz) — discernment between rulings.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional-Resultative Construction (al-sharṭ wa al-jawāb) — "If it parted, he parted it; otherwise he left it" (fa-in infaraqat farraqahā wa-illā tarakahā), showing habitual action in past tense with conditional particles.

- Root: ج-م-م (j-m-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Abundance, totality; al-jummah is hair that reaches the shoulders.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Quantitative fullness as a descriptive attribute of created form.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — hair length; no metaphorical extension here.
- Sībawayh Rule: Gradational Comparison (al-tafḍīl) — "more than the wafrah" (akthar min al-wafrah), requiring genitive construction after comparative adjective.

- Root: ش-ك-ل (sh-k-l)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Resemblance, similarity; shuklah is redness in the whites of the eyes.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Physical trait terminology in prophetic description (ṣifāt).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — ocular coloration; the narrator's error (wahm) is flagged as a misapplication.
- Sībawayh Rule: Apposition (al-badal) — "ashkal al-ʿayn" as explanatory substitute for the correct "ashkal" meaning, requiring correction of transmitted error.
chapters.translation:
I say: And the parting (al-farq) is recommended (mustaḥabb), and for this reason the Salaf differed concerning it — a group among them parted [their hair], while others adopted the lummah [hair reaching the shoulders]. It has come in the ḥadīth that the Prophet (ﷺ) had a lummah; if it parted naturally, he would part it, and otherwise he would leave it. Mālik said: "A man's parting [of hair] is more beloved to me." This is the speech of al-Qāḍī. The summary is that the correct and chosen [view] is the permissibility of both letting [hair] hang loose (al-sadl) and parting it (al-farq), and that parting is superior. And Allāh knows best.

Al-Qāḍī said: The scholars differed concerning the interpretation of [the command to] conform to the People of the Book in matters regarding which nothing had been revealed. It was said: He did so to win their hearts (istiʾlāf) in the early days of Islam, and to concur with them in opposing the idol-worshippers. When Allāh — exalted is He — rendered [him] independent of winning their hearts, and made Islam prevail over all religion, He explicitly commanded opposition to them in matters including dyeing grey hair. Others said: It is plausible that he was commanded to follow their laws in matters not yet revealed, and this was only in what he knew they had not altered. Some uṣūliyyūn adduced this ḥadīth as evidence that "the law of those before us is a law for us" (sharʿu man qablanā sharʿun lanā) so long as our law does not contradict it. Others said: Rather, this is proof that it is not a law for us, because he said "he loves to conform to them," indicating that it was left to his choice; had it been a law for us, its following would have been obligatory. And Allāh knows best.

His saying — [Ḥadīth 2337]: "The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) was marbūʿ" — it carries the meaning of his saying in the second narration: "neither tall nor short."

His saying: "having a great jummah reaching to his earlobes." In another narration: "I have not seen anyone with a lummah more handsome than him." In another narration: "his hair would strike his shoulders." In another: "reaching the middle of his ears." In another: "between his ears and his ʿātiq." The linguists said: The jummah is more [hair] than the wafrah — the jummah is hair that descends to the shoulders, the wafrah is what descends to the earlobes, and the lummah is that which reaches (alammat bi) the shoulders. Al-Qāḍī said: The reconciliation of these narrations is that what is adjacent to the ear is what reaches his earlobes, and it is what lies between his ears and his ʿātiq; what is behind it is what strikes his shoulders. He said: And it was said: Rather, this is due to differing times — when he neglected trimming it, it reached the shoulders, and when he trimmed it, it was at the middle of the ears. Thus it would be shortened and lengthened accordingly. The ʿātiq is what lies between the shoulder and the neck. As for the earlobe (shiḥmah), it is the soft part at the bottom of the ear, from which the earring hangs. These narrations are clarified by the narration of Ibrāhīm al-Ḥarbī: "The hair of the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) was above the wafrah and below the jummah."

His saying in the ḥadīth of al-Barāʾ: "The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) was the most handsome of people in face and the best of them in khuluq." Al-Qāḍī said: We have recorded it as khuluq with fatḥah on the khāʾ and sukūn on the lām here, because his intent is the attributes of his body. He said: As for the ḥadīth of Anas, we have narrated it with ḍammah [on the lām], because he only reported on the excellence of his companionship. As for his saying "wa-aḥsanuhu," Abū Ḥātim and others said: Thus the Arabs say, "wa-aḥsanuhu," meaning "the best of them" (wa-aḥsanuhum), but they do not utter it [with the plural suffix]; rather they say "the most beautiful of people and the best of them" (ajmal al-nās wa-aḥsanuhu). From this is the ḥadīth: "The best of women who ride camels are the women of Quraysh — the most compassionate to their children and the most caring to their husbands," and the ḥadīth of Abū Sufyān: "With me, the most beautiful of Arab women and the most handsome."

His saying — [Ḥadīth 2338]: "His hair was rajil, neither jaʿd nor sabṭ" — it is with fatḥah on the rāʾ and kasrah on the jīm, meaning hair that is between curliness (juʿūdah) and straightness (subūṭah). Al-Aṣmaʿī and others said this.

His saying — [Ḥadīth 2339]: "From Shuʿbah, from Simāk ibn Ḥarb, who said: I heard Jābir ibn Samurah say: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) was ḍalīʿ al-fam, ashkal al-ʿayn, manhūs al-ʿaqibayn." He said: I said to Simāk: "What is ḍalīʿ al-fam?" He said: "Wide of mouth." I said: "What is ashkal al-ʿayn?" He said: "Long of eye-slit." I said: "What is manhūs al-ʿaqib?" He said: "Having little flesh on the heel."

As for his saying "ḍalīʿ al-fam," thus the majority said, and it is the most apparent [view]. They said: The Arabs praise this and disparage smallness of mouth. This is the meaning of Thaʿlab's saying concerning ḍalīʿ al-fam: "wide of mouth." Shammar said: "great of teeth."

As for his saying "ashkal al-ʿayn," al-Qāḍī said: This is an error (wahm) from Simāk, by agreement of the scholars, and a manifest mistake. The correct [reading] is what the scholars have agreed upon, and which Abū ʿUbayd and all the authorities on rare expressions (gharīb) transmitted: that al-shuklah is redness in the whites of the eyes, and it is praiseworthy; while al-shah lah — with hāʾ — is redness in the black of the eye.

As for al-manhūs — it is with the unpointed sīn (muhmalah); thus the majority have recorded it. The author of al-Taḥrīr and Ibn al-Athīr narrated it with both the unpointed and pointed sīn, and they are close in meaning. Its meaning is "little flesh on the heel," as he said. And Allāh knows best.

His saying — [Ḥadīth 2340]: "He was white, handsome, muqaṣṣad" — it is with fatḥah on the ṣād and tashdīd, meaning one who is neither bulky nor thin, neither tall nor short. Shammar said: It is approximately al-ribʿah [medium stature], and al-qaṣd carries its meaning. And Allāh knows best.

| (Chapter: On the Whitening of His Hair ﷺ)

His saying — [Ḥadīth 2341]: "I asked Anas ibn Mālik: Did the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) dye [his hair]? He said: He did not reach the point of dyeing; there were a few white hairs in his beard." In another narration: "Nothing of grey hair was seen except a little." In another: "If I wished, I could count the white hairs that were in his head — and he did not dye." In another: "The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) did not dye; the whiteness was only in his ʿanfaqah [the hair below the lower lip], in his temples, and a few strands in his head." In another: "Allāh did not afflict him with a single white hair."

[Ḥadīth 2342]: In the narration of Abū Juḥayfah: "I saw the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) — this much of it was white" — and the narrator placed some of his fingers on his ʿanfaqah.

[Ḥadīth 2343]: In another narration of his: "I saw the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ), white [skinned], and he had indeed aged."

[Ḥadīth 2344]: In the narration of Jābir ibn Samurah, he was asked about the greying of the Prophet (ﷺ), and he said: "When he oiled his head, nothing of it was seen; and when he did not oil it, some of it was visible." In another narration of his: "The front of his head and his beard had become streaked with grey." In the narration of Anas: "He counted them one by one — he died with fewer than twenty white hairs in his head and beard." And in the ḥadīth of Umm Salamah, she brought out for them some hairs [of the Prophet ﷺ].

chapters.title_en: Section 860 — On the Dyeing of the Prophet's Hair, His Grey Hairs, the Seal of Prophethood, and the Duration of His Life
chapters.arabic_text:
من شعر رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم حمرا مخضوبة بالحناء والكتم قال

القاضي اختلف العلماء هل خضب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أم لا فمنعه

الأكثرون بحديث أنس وهو مذهب مالك وقال بعض المحدثين خضب لحديث أم سلمة هذا

ولحديث بن عمر أنه رأى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يصبغ بالصفرة قال وجمع

بعضهم بين الأحاديث بما أشار إليه في حديث أم سلمة من كلام  أنس في قوله

فقال ما أدري في هذا الذي يحدثون إلا أن يكون شيء من الطيب الذي كان يطيب

به شعره لأنه صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يستعمل الطيب كثيرا وهو يزيل سواد

الشعر فأشار أنس إلى أن تغيير ذلك ليس بصبغ وإنما هو لضعف لون سواده بسبب

الطيب قال ويحتمل أن تلك الشعرات تغيرت بعده لكثرة تطييب أم سلمة لها

إكراما هذا آخر كلام القاضي والمختار أنه صلى الله عليه وسلم صبغ في وقت

وتركه في معظم الأوقات فأخبر كل بما رأى وهوصادق وهذا التأويل كالمتعين

فحديث بن عمر في الصحيحين ولا يمكن تركه ولا تأويل له والله أعلم وأما

اختلاف الرواية في قدر شيبه فالجمع بينها أنه رأى شيئا يسيرا فمن أثبت شيبه

أخبر عن ذلك اليسير ومن نفاه أراد أنه لم يكثر فيه كما قال في الرواية

الأخرى لم يشتد الشيب أي لم يكثر ولم يخرج شعره عن سواده وحسنه كما قال في

الرواية الأخرى لم ير من الشيب إلا قليلا قوله (أعد شمطاته) وفي الرواية

الأخرى كان قد شمط بكسر الميم اتفق العلماء على أن المراد بالشمط هنا

ابتداء الشيب يقال منه شمط وأشمط قوله (خضب أبو بكر وعمر وعثمان رضي الله

عنهم بالحناء والكتم) أما الحناء فممدود وهو معروف وأما الكتم فبفتح
# 
# الكاف والتاء المثناة من فوق المخففة هذا هو المشهور وقال أبو عبيدة هو

بتشديد التاء وحكاه غيره وهو نبات يصبغ به الشعر يكثر بياضه أو حمرته إلى

الدهمة قوله (اختضب عمر بالحناء) هو بالحاء المهملة معناه خالصا لم يخلط

بغيره قوله (عن أنس رضي الله عنه قال يكره أن ينتف الرجل الشعرة البيضاء من

رأسه ولحيته) هذا متفق عليه قال أصحابنا وأصحاب مالك يكره ولا يحرم قوله

(وفي الرأس نبذ) ضبطوه بوجهين أحدهما ضم النون وفتح الباء والثاني بفتح

النون وإسكان الباء وبه جزم القاضي ومعناه شعرات متفرقة قوله (سمع أبا

إياس) هو معاوية بن قرة قوله (أبري النبل وأريشها) أما أبري فبفتح  الهمزة

وأما أريشها
# 
# فبفتح الهمزة أيضا وكسر الراء وإسكان الياء أي أجعل للنبل ريشا

| (باب إثبات خاتم النبوة وصفته ومحله من جسده صلى 
# الله عليه وسلم)
# قوله (ورأيت الخاتم عند كتفه مثل بيضة الحمامة يشبه جسده) وفي
# [2345] رواية بين كتفيه مثل زر الحجلة
# 
# وفي
# [2346] رواية فنظرت إلى خاتم النبوة بين كتفيه عند ناغض كتفه اليسرى جمعا

عليه خيلان كأمثال الثآليل أما بيضة الحمامة فهو بيضتها المعروفة واما زر

الحجلة فبزاي ثم ياء والحجلة بفتح الحاء والجيم هذا هو الصحيح المشهور الذي

قاله الجمهور وقال بعضهم المراد بالحجلة واحدة الحجال وهي بيت كالقبة لها

أزرار كباز وعرى هذا هو الصواب المشهور الذي قاله الجمهور وقال بعضهم

المراد بالحجلة الطائر المعروف وزرها بيضتها وأشار إليه الترمذي وأنكره

عليه العلماء وقال الخطابي روي أيضا بتقديم الراء على الزاي ويكون المراد

البيض يقال أرزت الجرادة بفتح الراء وتشديد الزاي إذا كبست ذنبها في الأرض

فباضت وجاء في صحيح البخاري كانت بضعة ناشزة أي مرتفعة على جسده وأما ناغض

كتفه فبالنون والغين والضاد المعجمتين والغين مكسورة وقال الجمهور النغض

والنغض والناغض أعلى الكتف وقيل هو العظم الرقيق الذي على طرفه وقيل ما

يظهر منه عند التحرك وأما قوله جمعا فبضم الجيم وإسكان الميم ومعناه أنه

كجمع الكف وهو صورته بعد أن
# 
# تجمع الأصابع وتضمها وأما الخيلان فبكسر الخاء المعجمة وإسكان الياء جمع

خال وهو الشامة في الجسد والله أعلم قال القاضي وهذه الروايات متقاربة

متفقة على أنها شاخص في جسده قدر بيضة الحمامة وهو نحو بيضة الحجلة وزر

الحجلة وأما رواية جمع الكف وناشز فظاهرها المخالفة فتؤول على وفق الروايات

الكثيرة ويكون معناه على هيئة جمع الكف لكنه أصغر منه في قدر بيضة الحمامة

قال القاضي وهذا الخاتم هو أثر شق الملكين بين الكتفين وهذا الذي قاله ضعيف

بل باطل لأن شق الملكين إنما كان في صدره وبطنه والله اعلم

| باب قدر عمره صلى الله عليه وسلم وإقامته بمكة
# والمدينة)
# [2348]
# [2349] ذكر في الباب ثلاث روايات  إحداها أنه صلى الله عليه وسلم توفى وهو

بن ستين سنة والثانية خمس وستون والثالثة ثلاث وستون وهي أصحها وأشهرها

رواه مسلم هنا من رواية عائشة وأنس وبن عباس رضي الله عنهم واتفق العلماء

على أن أصحها ثلاث وستون وتأولوا الباقي عليه فرواية ستين اقتصر فيها على

العقود وترك الكسر ورواية الخمس متأولة أيضا وحصل فيها اشتباه وقد أنكر

عروة على بن عباس قوله (خمس وستون) ونسبه إلى الغلط وأنه لم يدرك أول
chapters.anchors:
- Root: خ-ض-ب (kh-ḍ-b)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To dye, to color, to stain; the act of changing the natural color of hair or cloth.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological discourse, refers to the physical alteration of appearance; not a ritual or metaphysical act but a permissible bodily practice.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage for dyeing with substances like henna; metaphorical (majāz) when extended to "staining" character or honor.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional and Exceptive Constructions (al-sharṭ wa al-istithnāʾ) — For parsing "ما أدري... إلا أن يكون" (I do not know... except that it might be), where the exceptive particle restricts the preceding negation.

- Root: ش-م-ط (sh-m-ṭ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: The appearance of white hairs among black; the onset of greyness; a state of mixed black and white hair.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Used to denote the natural aging process; in prophetic reports, it marks a physical sign of human mortality.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for the intermingling of white and black; no metaphorical extension in this context.
- Sībawayh Rule: Verbal Noun Derivation (maṣdar) — "شمط" as a verbal noun from "شمط" (to become grey), with the active participle "أشمط" (one who is grey).

- Root: خ-ي-ل (kh-y-l)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Moles, birthmarks, or spots on the body; a collection of small raised marks.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In prophetic descriptions, these are physical signs (ʿalāmāt) of divine favor, not to be allegorized.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for bodily marks; no metaphorical sense here.
- Sībawayh Rule: Plural Formation (jamʿ takṣīr) — "خیلان" as a broken plural of "خال" (mole), following the pattern fiʿlān.

- Root: ن-غ-ض (n-gh-ḍ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: The upper part of the shoulder blade; the thin bone at its edge; that which moves when the limb stirs.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Anatomical term in prophetic reports; precise physical location for the seal.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal anatomical reference; no metaphorical usage.
- Sībawayh Rule: Noun of Place/Part (ism ʿayn) — "الناغض" as a specific bodily part, governed by the preposition "عند" (near).
chapters.translation:
I say: The Prophet of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, had some red hairs dyed with henna and katam. The Qāḍī said: The scholars differed as to whether the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, dyed his hair or not. The majority forbade it (i.e., held that he did not dye) based on the ḥadīth of Anas, and this is the school of Mālik. Some traditionists said he did dye, based on this ḥadīth of Umm Salamah and on the ḥadīth of Ibn ʿUmar that he saw the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, dyeing with yellow. He said: Some scholars reconciled the reports by what Anas indicated in his statement within the ḥadīth of Umm Salamah, where he said: "I do not know about this that they narrate, except that it might be some perfume with which he used to perfume his hair" — because he, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used perfume frequently, and it removes the blackness of hair. Anas thus indicated that this change was not dyeing but rather a weakening of the intensity of its blackness due to perfume. He said: It is also possible that those hairs changed after his death due to Umm Salamah's frequent perfuming of them, as an honor to him. This concludes the Qāḍī's speech. The chosen view is that he, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, dyed at some time and left it at most times, so each narrator reported what he saw, and he was truthful. This interpretation is virtually necessitated, for the ḥadīth of Ibn ʿUmar is in the two Ṣaḥīḥs, and it cannot be abandoned, nor does it admit another interpretation. And Allah knows best.

As for the discrepancy in the reports concerning the amount of his grey hairs, the reconciliation is that he had a small amount of greyness. Whoever affirmed his greyness reported that small amount, and whoever denied it meant that it had not become abundant, as stated in another narration: "The greyness did not intensify," i.e., it did not become plentiful, nor did his hair depart from its blackness and beauty, as stated in yet another narration: "Only a little greyness was seen." His statement: "I counted his grey hairs" — in another narration: "He had become somewhat grey" (with kasrah on the mīm). The scholars are agreed that the intended meaning of "shamaṭ" here is the beginning of greyness; one says "shamaṭa" and "ashmaṭa" from it. His statement: "Abū Bakr, ʿUmar, and ʿUthmān, may Allah be pleased with them, dyed with henna and katam" — as for "al-ḥinnāʾ," it is with madd (prolongation) and is well-known. As for "al-katam," it is with fatḥah on the kāf and the tāʾ (the second letter with two dots above) with tashdīd removed — this is the well-known pronunciation. Abū ʿUbaydah said it is with tashdīd on the tāʾ, and others have narrated this as well. It is a plant with which hair is dyed, increasing its whiteness or redness toward duskiness. His statement: "ʿUmar dyed with pure henna" — it is with the unpointed ḥāʾ, meaning pure, unmixed with anything else.

His statement: "From Anas, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: It is disliked for a man to pluck a white hair from his head or beard" — this is agreed upon (muttafaq ʿalayh). Our companions and the companions of Mālik said: It is disliked (makrūh), not forbidden (ḥarām). His statement: "And on the head were a few scattered hairs" — they transmitted it in two ways: one with ḍammah on the nūn and fatḥah on the bāʾ, and the second with fatḥah on the nūn and sukūn on the bāʾ, which is what the Qāḍī affirmed. Its meaning is: sparse, scattered hairs. His statement: "I heard Abā Iyās" — he is Muʿāwiyah ibn Qurrah. His statement: "I shape arrowheads and fletch them" — as for "ubrī," it is with fatḥah on the hamzah; as for "urīshuhā," it is also with fatḥah on the hamzah, kasrah on the rāʾ, and sukūn on the yāʾ, meaning: I attach feathers to the arrows.

| Chapter: Affirming the Seal of Prophethood, Its Description, and Its Location on His Body, May Allah Bless Him and Grant Him Peace |

His statement: "And I saw the seal at his shoulder like the egg of a pigeon, resembling his body" — and in one narration [2345]: "Between his shoulders like the button of a ḥajalah." And in another narration [2346]: "I looked at the seal of prophethood between his shoulders, near the upper part of his left shoulder, with moles gathered upon it like warts." As for "bayḍat al-ḥamāmah" (pigeon's egg), it is its well-known egg. As for "zar al-ḥajalah," it is with zāy then yāʾ, and "al-ḥajalah" is with fatḥah on the ḥāʾ and the jīm — this is the correct and well-known pronunciation stated by the majority. Some said the intended meaning of "al-ḥajalah" is one of the "ḥijāl," which is a tent like a dome, having buttons like those of a falcon's perch and loops. This is the correct and well-known view stated by the majority. Some said the intended meaning of "al-ḥajalah" is the well-known bird, and its button is its egg — al-Tirmidhī indicated this, but the scholars rejected it against him. Al-Khaṭṭābī said: It is also narrated with the rāʾ preceding the zāy, and the intended meaning would be the egg; one says "arazat al-jarādah" (with fatḥah on the rāʾ and tashdīd on the zāy) when it presses its tail into the ground and lays eggs. It came in Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī: "It was a raised piece of flesh," i.e., elevated above his body. As for "nāghiḍ katifihi" (the upper part of his shoulder), it is with nūn, ghayn, and ḍād (both pointed), with kasrah on the ghayn. The majority said: "al-naghaḍ," "al-nughḍ," and "al-nāghiḍ" mean the top of the shoulder. It was also said: It is the thin bone at its edge. And it was said: It is what appears from it upon movement. As for his statement "jamʿan" (gathered), it is with ḍammah on the jīm and sukūn on the mīm, meaning: like the gathering of the palm — which is its form after one gathers and closes the fingers. As for "al-khīlān," it is with kasrah on the pointed khāʾ and sukūn on the yāʾ, the plural of "khāl," which is a mole on the body. And Allah knows best.

The Qāḍī said: These narrations are close and agree that it was a protrusion on his body, the size of a pigeon's egg, which is approximately the egg of the ḥajalah and the button of the ḥajalah. As for the narration of "the gathering of the palm" and "raised," its apparent meaning contradicts, so it is interpreted in accordance with the numerous narrations, and its meaning would be: in the form of a gathered palm, but smaller than it, about the size of a pigeon's egg. The Qāḍī said: This seal is the trace of the two angels' incision between the shoulders. What he said is weak — rather, false — because the two angels' incision was only in his chest and belly. And Allah knows best.

| Chapter: The Duration of His Life, May Allah Bless Him and Grant Him Peace, and His Stay in Mecca and Medina |

[2348] [2349] Three narrations are mentioned in this chapter: one that he, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, died at sixty years of age; the second, sixty-five; and the third, sixty-three — which is the most authentic and most famous of them. Muslim narrated it here from ʿĀʾishah, Anas, and Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with them. The scholars are agreed that the most authentic is sixty-three, and they interpreted the others in light of it. The narration of sixty restricted itself to the decades and omitted the fraction. The narration of sixty-five is also interpreted, and confusion occurred in it. ʿUrwah objected to Ibn ʿAbbās's statement of "sixty-five," attributing it to error, and noted that he (Ibn ʿAbbās) did not witness the beginning of his life.

chapters.arabic_text:
النبوة ولا كثرت صحبته بخلاف الباقين
# [2350]
# [2351]
# [2352]
# [2353] واتفقوا أنه صلى الله عليه وسلم أقام بالمدينة بعد الهجرة عشر

سنين وبمكة قبل النبوة أربعين سنة وإنما الخلاف في قدر إقامته بمكة بعد

النبوة وقيل الهجرة والصحيح أنها ثلاث عشرة فيكون عمره ثلاثا وستين وهذا

الذي ذكرناه أنه بعث على رأس أربعين سنة هو الصواب المشهور الذي أطبق عليه

العلماء وحكى القاضي عياض عن بن عباس وسعيد بن المسيب رواية شاذة أنه صلى

الله عليه وسلم بعث على رأس ثلاث وأربعين سنة
# 
# والصواب أربعون كما سبق وولد عام الفيل على الصحيح المشهور وقيل بعد

الفيل بثلاث سنين وقيل بأربع سنين وادعى القاضي عياض الإجماع على عام الفيل

وليس كما ادعى واتفقوا أنه ولد يوم الاثنين في شهر ربيع الاول وتوفي يوم

الاثنين من شهر ربيع الأول واختلفوا في يوم الولادة هل هو ثاني الشهر أم

ثامنه أم عاشره أم ثاني عشره ويوم الوفاة ثاني عشرة ضحى والله أعلم قوله
# [2347] (ليس بالطويل البائن ولا بالقصير) المراد بالبائن زائد الطول أي

هو بين زائد الطول والقصير وهو بمعنى ما سبق أنه كان مقصدا قوله (ولا

الأبيض الأمهق ولا بالآدم) الأمهق بالميم هو شديد البياض كلون الجص وهو

كريه المنظر وربما توهمه الناظر أبرص والآدم الأسمر معناه ليس بأسمر ولا

بأبيض كريه البياض بل أبيض بياضا نيرا كما قال في الحديث السابق أنه صلى

الله عليه وسلم كان أزهر اللون وكذا قال في الرواية التي بعده كان أزهر

قوله (قلت لعروة كم لبث  النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بمكة قال عشرا قلت فان بن

عباس يقول بضع عشرة قال فغفره وقال إنما أخذه من قول الشاعر) هكذا هو في

جميع نسخ بلادنا فغفره بالغين والفاء وكذا نقله القاضي عن رواية الجلودي

ومعناه دعا له بالمغفرة فقال غفر الله له وهذه اللفظة يقولونها غالبا لمن

غلط في شئ فكأنه قال أخطأ غفر الله له قال القاضي وفي رواية بن ماهان فصغره

بصاد ثم غين أي استصغره عن معرفته هذا وإدراكه ذلك وضبطه وإنما أسند فيه

إلى قول الشاعر
# 
# وليس معه علم بذلك ويرجح القاضي هذا القول قال والشاعر هو أبو قيس صرمة

بن أبي أنس حيث يقول ثوى في قريش بضع عشرة حجة يذكر لو يلقى خليلا مواتيا
# 
# وقد وقع هذا البيت في بعض نسخ صحيح مسلم وليس هو في عامتها قلت وأبو قيس

هذا هو صرمة بن أبي أنس بن مالك بن عدي بن عامر بن غنم بن عدي بن النجار

الأنصاري هكذا نسبه بن إسحاق قال كان قد ترهب في الجاهلية ولبس المسوح

وفارق الأوثان واغتسل من الجنابة واتخذ بيتا له مسجدا لا يدخل عليه حائض

ولا جنب وقال أعبد رب إبراهيم فلما قدم النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم المدينة

أسلم فحسن إسلامه وهو شيخ كبير وكان قوالا بالحق وكان معظما لله تعالى في

الجاهلية يقول الشعر
# 
# في تعظيمه سبحانه وتعالى قوله (سمع معاوية يخطب فقال مات رسول الله صلى

الله عليه وسلم وهو بن ثلاث وستين وأبو بكر وعمر وأنا بن ثلاث وستين هكذا

هو في جميع النسخ وهو صحيح وتقديره وأبو بكر وعمر كذلك ثم استأنف فقال وأنا

بن ثلاث وستين أي وأنا متوقع موافقتهم
# 
# وإني أموت في سنتي هذه قوله (يسمع الصوت ويرى الضوء) قال القاضي أي صوت

الهاتف به من الملائكة ويرى الضوء أي نور الملائكة ونور آيات الله تعالى

حتى رأى الملك بعينه وشافهه بوحي الله تعالى

| باب في أسمائه صلى الله عليه وسلم

# ذكر هنا هذه  الأسماء وله صلى الله عليه وسلم أسماء أخر ذكر أبو بكر بن

العربي المالكي في كتابه الأحوذي في شرح الترمذي عن بعضهم أن لله تعالى ألف

اسم وللنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ألف اسم أيضا ثم ذكر منها على التفصيل بضعا

وستين قال أهل اللغة يقال رجل محمد ومحمود إذا كثرت خصاله المحمودة وقال بن

فارس وغيره وبه سمي نبينا صلى الله عليه وسلم محمدا وأحمد أي ألهم الله

تعالى أهله أن سموه به لما علم من جميل صفاته قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم
# [2354] (وأنا الماحي الذي يمحى بي الكفر) قال العلماء المراد محو الكفر

من مكة والمدينة وسائر بلاد العرب ومازوى له صلى الله عليه وسلم من الأرض

ووعد أن يبلغه ملك أمته قالوا ويحتمل أن المراد المحو العام بمعنى الظهور

بالحجة والغلبة كما قال
# 
# تعالى ليظهره على الدين كله وجاء في حديث آخر تفسير الماحي بأنه الذي

محيت به سيئات من اتبعه فقد يكون المراد بمحو الكفر هذا ويكون كقوله تعالى

قل للذين كفروا إن ينتهوا يغفر لهم ما قد سلف والحديث الصحيح الإسلام يهدم

ما كان قبله قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (وأنا الحاشر الذي يحشر الناس على

عقبي) وفي الرواية الثانية على قدمي فأما الثانية فاتفقت النسخ على أنها

على أنها على قدمي لكن ضبطوه بتخفيف الياء على الإفراد وتشديدها على

التثنية وأما الرواية الأولى فهي في معظم النسخ وفي بعضها قدمي كالثانية

قال العلماء معناهما يحشرون على أثري وزمان نبوتي ورسالتي وليس بعدي نبي
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ق-د-م (q-d-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: "Foot" or "precedence"; also "anteriority in time"
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Temporal precedence implying prophetic finality — the last to come, after whom none follows
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) = physical foot; metaphorical (majāz) = "at my time/after my era"
- Sībawayh Rule: Taqdīr (Ellipsis Restoration) — supplying omitted elements in sentences like "Abū Bakr and ʿUmar [likewise]" to complete the grammatical sense
chapters.translation:
I say: And they are agreed that he, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, remained in Medina after the emigration (hijrah) ten years, and in Mecca before prophethood forty years. The disagreement is only concerning the extent of his stay in Mecca after prophethood — and it was said: after the emigration — and the correct view is that it was thirteen years, making his age sixty-three. This which we have mentioned — that he was sent as a prophet at the age of forty — is the correct and well-known view upon which the scholars are unanimous. Al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ reported from Ibn ʿAbbās and Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib an anomalous narration (riwāyah shādhdhah) that he, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was sent as a prophet at the age of forty-three.

And the correct view is forty, as has preceded. He was born in the Year of the Elephant (ʿām al-fīl) according to the correct and well-known view; and it was said: three years after the Elephant; and it was said: four years after. Al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ claimed consensus (ijmāʿ) on the Year of the Elephant, but it is not as he claimed. And they are agreed that he was born on a Monday in the month of Rabīʿ al-Awwal, and died on a Monday in the month of Rabīʿ al-Awwal. They differed concerning the day of birth — whether it was the second of the month, or the eighth, or the tenth, or the twelfth — and the day of death was the twelfth, at mid-morning (ḍuḥā). And Allah knows best.

His saying [2347]: "(He was) not excessively tall (al-ṭawīl al-bāʾin) nor short" — the intended meaning of al-bāʾin is "exceeding in height," i.e., he was between the excessively tall and the short. This is equivalent to what has preceded: that he was of medium stature (maqṣad). His saying: "Nor white with a pallid whiteness (al-amhaq) nor brown (al-ādam)" — al-amhaq, with the letter mīm, is the intensely white like the color of plaster (jiṣṣ), and it is repulsive in appearance; the beholder might even imagine him to be leprous. Al-ādam is the brown-skinned. The meaning is: he was not brown, nor white with a repulsive whiteness, but rather white with a luminous whiteness, as he said in the preceding hadith that he, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was of radiant complexion (azhar al-lawn). Likewise he said in the narration that follows: he was azhar.

His saying: "I said to ʿUrwah: 'How long did the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, remain in Mecca?' He said: 'Ten years.' I said: 'But Ibn ʿAbbās says: "Bidʿ ʿasharah" (several more than ten).' He said: 'He erred — may Allah forgive him (fa-ghafarah). He only took it from the saying of the poet.'" Thus it appears in all the copies of our lands: fa-ghafarah, with ghayn and fāʾ. Al-Qāḍī likewise transmitted it from the narration of al-Julūdī. Its meaning is: he prayed for forgiveness for him, saying "May Allah forgive him." This expression is commonly used for one who errs in something, as if he said: "He erred — may Allah forgive him." Al-Qāḍī said: In the narration of Ibn Māhān it is fa-ṣaghgharah, with ṣād then ghayn, i.e., he deemed him too insignificant to have knowledge of this matter, to grasp it, and to master it. He only attributed it to the saying of the poet.

And he has no certain knowledge of that. Al-Qāḍī favors this latter view. He said: The poet is Abū Qays Ṣirmah ibn Abī Anas, who said:
"He dwelt among Quraysh bidʿ ʿasharah years — remembering, if he might find a loyal friend."

This verse occurs in some copies of Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim, but it is not in the majority of them. I say: This Abū Qays is Ṣirmah ibn Abī Anas ibn Mālik ibn ʿAdī ibn ʿĀmir ibn Ghanm ibn ʿAdī ibn al-Najjār al-Anṣārī. Thus Ibn Isḥāq traced his lineage. He said: He had become a monk (tarahhaba) in the Jāhiliyyah, wore woolen garments (musūḥ), forsook the idols, performed the major ablution (ghusl) from janābah, and took for himself a house as a place of prayer (masjid) — no menstruating woman nor one in a state of janābah would enter upon him — and he said: "I worship the Lord of Abraham." When the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, arrived in Medina, he embraced Islam and his Islam was excellent, though he was an old man. He was one who spoke the truth and held Allah Almighty in veneration during the Jāhiliyyah, composing poetry in His glorification, may He be exalted.

His saying: "(He heard Muʿāwiyah while he was delivering a sermon, and he said: 'The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, died when he was sixty-three, and Abū Bakr and ʿUmar [likewise], and I am sixty-three.')" Thus it appears in all the copies, and it is correct. Its estimated completion (taqdīruh) is: "And Abū Bakr and ʿUmar [died] likewise." Then he resumed, saying: "And I am sixty-three," i.e., "And I anticipate joining them, and I shall die in this my year."

His saying: "He hears the voice and sees the light" — Al-Qāḍī said: i.e., the voice of the caller (al-hātif) to him from among the angels, and "sees the light" means the light of the angels and the light of the signs of Allah Almighty, until he saw the angel with his own eye and he addressed him directly with the revelation of Allah Almighty.

| Chapter on His Names, may Allah bless him and grant him peace

These names are mentioned here. He, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, has other names as well. Abū Bakr ibn al-ʿArabī al-Mālikī mentioned in his book al-Aḥwadhī, in his commentary on al-Tirmidhī, from some of them, that Allah Almighty has one thousand names, and the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, also has one thousand names. Then he mentioned from them, in detail, sixty-some. The linguists (ahl al-lughah) say: A man is called muḥammad and maḥmūd when his praiseworthy qualities are numerous. Ibn Fāris and others said: And by this our Prophet was named Muḥammad and Aḥmad — i.e., Allah Almighty inspired his family to name him thus, for what He knew of the beauty of his attributes.

His saying, may Allah bless him and grant him peace [2354]: "(And I am al-Māḥī (the Eraser), by whom unbelief is erased)" — The scholars said: The intended meaning is the erasure of unbelief from Mecca, Medina, and the rest of the lands of the Arabs, and whatever was conquered for him, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, of the earth, with the promise that the dominion of his nation would reach it. They said: It is also possible that the intended meaning is the general erasure, in the sense of prevailing by proof and dominance, as He, exalted, said: {«ليظهره على الدين كله»} ("that He may make it prevail over all religion"). And it has come in another hadith explaining al-Māḥī as the one by whom the sins of those who follow him are erased. So it may be that the intended meaning of "erasure of unbelief" is this, and it would be like His saying, exalted: {«قل للذين كفروا إن ينتهوا يغفر لهم ما قد سلف»} ("Say to those who disbelieve: if they desist, what has passed will be forgiven them"), and the authentic hadith: "Islam demolishes what was before it."

His saying, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: "(And I am al-Ḥāshir (the Gatherer), by whom the people are gathered upon my heel (ʿaqibī))" — and in the second narration: "upon my foot (qadamī)." As for the second, the copies agree that it is "upon my foot," but they vocalize it with a lightened yāʾ for the singular, and with a doubled yāʾ for the dual. As for the first narration, it is in most copies, and in some of them it is "my foot" like the second. The scholars said: Their meaning is: they are gathered upon my trace and the time of my prophethood and my message, and there is no prophet after me.
