His saying (peace be upon him) [2373]: "(The Trumpet will be blown, and all who are in the heavens and all who are on the earth will swoon, except whom Allah wills. Then it will be blown again, and I will be the first to be raised. Then behold, Moses will be clinging to the Throne, and I do not know whether he was recompensed for the swoon of the Day of Ṭūr or was raised before me.)" In another narration: "The people will swoon, and I will be the first to recover. Then behold, Moses will be grasping the side of the Throne, and I do not know whether he was among those who swooned and recovered before me, or was among those whom Allah exempted." Al-ṣaʿq and al-ṣaʿqah mean destruction and death. From it is said: "ṣuʿiqa al-insān" (the man swooned), with the ṣād opened or dammed—though some reject the damma—and "ṣaʿaqat-hum al-ṣāʿiqah" (the thunderbolt struck them), with the ṣād and ʿayn opened, and "aṣʿaqat-hum." The Banū Tamīm say "al-ṣāqʿah" with the qāf advanced. Al-Qāḍī said: This is among the most problematic of hadiths, because Moses has died—how can the swoon overtake him? For the swoon only strikes the living. His saying "(among those whom Allah exempted)" indicates that he was alive, and it has not come that Moses returned to life, nor that he is alive as has come regarding Jesus. And he (peace be upon him) said: "Had I been there, I would have shown you his grave beside the road." Al-Qāḍī said: It is possible that this swoon is a swoon of terror (ṣaʿqat fazaʿ) after the resurrection, when the heavens and the earth split asunder, and thus the verses and hadiths become consistent. This is supported by his saying (peace be upon him): "I recovered" (afāqa), for "recovery" is only said of one emerging from a swoon (ghashy); as for death, one says "he was raised from it." And the swoon of Ṭūr was not death. As for his saying (peace be upon him): "I do not know whether he recovered before me," it is possible that he (peace be upon him) said this before he knew that he would be the first from whom the earth splits open—if this wording is taken literally—and that our Prophet (peace be upon him) is the first person from whom the earth splits open absolutely. He said: And it is permissible that its meaning is that he is among the group (zumrah) who are the first from whom the earth splits open, and Moses is from that group. And it is—Allah knows best—the group of the Prophets, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon them. This is the end of al-Qāḍī's speech.

His saying (peace be upon him): "And I do not say that anyone is better than Jonah son of Mattā." In [2376] a narration: Allah (exalted is He) said: "It is not fitting for a servant of Mine to say: 'I am better than Jonah son of Mattā.'" In [2377] a narration from the Prophet (peace be upon him): "It is not fitting for a servant to say: 'I am better than Jonah son of Mattā.'" The scholars said: These hadiths admit of two aspects. The first: He (peace be upon him) said this before he knew that he was better than Jonah; when he learned that, he said: "I am the master of the children of Adam," and he did not say here that Jonah was better than him or than other prophets (may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon them). The second: He (peace be upon him) said this as a deterrent (zajr) against any of the ignorant imagining anything that would diminish the rank of Jonah (peace be upon him) because of what is in the Mighty Quran of his story. The scholars said: What befell Jonah (peace be upon him) did not diminish from his prophethood the weight of a dust-mote (mithqāl dharratin). And Jonah was singled out for mention because of what we have mentioned of his mention in the Quran.

chapters.title_en: Section 868 — On the Prophet's Saying "No Servant Should Say 'I Am Better than Jonah'"; The Virtues of Joseph, Zachariah, and al-Khiḍr
chapters.arabic_text:
بما ذكر وأما قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم ما ينبغي لعبد أن يقول أنا خير من

يونس فالضمير في أنا قيل يعود إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وقيل يعود إلى

القائل أي لا يقول ذلك بعض الجاهلين من المجتهدين في عبادة أو علم أو غير

ذلك من الفضائل فإنه لو بلغ من الفضاء
# 
# ما بلغ لم يبلغ درجة النبوة ويؤيد هذا التأويل الرواية التي قبله وهي

قوله تعالى لا ينبغي لعبد أن يقول أنا خير من يونس بن متى والله أعلم قوله

صلى الله عليه وسلم
# [2375] (مررت على موسى وهو قائم يصلي في قبره) هذا الحديث سبق شرحه في

أواخر كتاب الايمان عند ذكر موسى وعيسى صلى الله عليه وسلم
#

| (باب من فضائل يوسف صلى الله عليه وسلم قوله
# [2378] (قيل يا
# رسول الله من أكرم الناس قال أتقاهم لله قالوا ليس عن هذا نسألك قال يوسف

نبي الله بن نبي الله بن خليل الله قالوا ليس عن هذا نسألك قال فعن معادن

العرب تسالوني خيارهم في الجاهلية خيارهم في الإسلام إذا فقهوا) هكذا وقع

في مسلم نبي الله بن نبي الله بن خليل الله وفي روايات للبخاري كذلك وفي

بعضها نبي الله بن نبي الله بن نبي الله بن خليل الله وهذه الرواية هي

الأصل وأما الأولى فمختصرة منها فإنه يوسف بن يعقوب بن إسحاق بن إبراهيم

الخليل صلى الله عليه وسلم فنسبه في الأولى إلى جده ويقال يوسف بضم السين

وكسرها وفتحها مع الهمز وتركه فهي ستة أوجه قال العلماء وأصل الكرم كثرة

الخير وقد جمع يوسف صلى الله عليه وسلم مكارم الأخلاق مع شرف النبوة مع شرف

النسب وكونه نبيا بن ثلاثة أنبياء متناسلين أحدهم خليل الله صلى الله عليه

وسلم وانضم إليه شرف علم الرؤيا وتمكنه فيه ورياسة الدنيا وملكها بالسيرة

الجميلة وحياطته للرعية وعموم نفعه إياهم وشفقته عليهم وإنقاذه إياهم من

تلك السنين  والله أعلم قال العلماء لما)
# 
# سئل صلى الله عليه وسلم أي الناس أكرم أخبر بأكمل الكرم وأعمه فقال

أتقاهم لله وقد ذكرنا أن أصل الكرم كثرة الخير ومن كان متقيا كان كثير

الخير وكثير الفائدة في الدنيا وصاحب الدرجات العلا في الآخرة فلما قالوا

ليس عن هذا نسألك قال يوسف الذي جمع خيرات الآخرة والدنيا وشرفهما فلما

قالوا ليس عن هذا نسأل فهم عنهم أن مرادهم قبائل العرب قال خيارهم في

الجاهلية خيارهم في الإسلام إذا فقهوا ومعناه أن أصحاب المروءات ومكارم

الأخلاق في الجاهلية اذا اسلموا وفقهوا فهم خيار الناس قال القاضي وقد تضمن

الحديث في الأجوبة الثلاثة أن الكرم كله عمومه وخصوصه ومجمله ومبانه إنما

هو الدين من التقوى والنبوة والإعراق فيها والإسلام مع الفقه ومعنى معادن

العرب أصولها وفقهوا بضم القاف على المشهور وحكي كسرها أي صاروا فقهاء

عالمين بالأحكام الشرعية الفقهية والله أعلم

| (باب من فضل زكريا صلى الله عليه وسلم)
# قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم
# [2379] (كان زكريا نجارا) فيه جواز الصنائع وأن النجارة لا تسقط المروءة

وأنها صنعة فاضلة وفيه فضيلة لزكرياء صلى الله عليه وسلم فإنه كان صانعا

يأكل من كسبه وقد ثبت قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم أفضل ما أكل الرجل من كسبه

وإن نبي الله داود كان يأكل من عمل يده وفي زكريا خمس لغات المد والقصر

وزكري بالتشديد والتخفيف وزكر كعلم

| (باب من فضائل الخضر صلى الله عليه وسلم)
# جمهور العلماء على أنه حي موجود بين أظهرنا وذلك متفق عليه عند الصوفية

وأهل الصلاح والمعرفة وحكاياتهم في رؤيته والاجتماع به والأخذ عنه وسؤاله

وجوابه ووجوده في المواضع
# 
# الشريفة ومواطن الخير أكثر من أن يحصر وأشهر من ان يستر وقال الشيخ ابو

عمر بن الصلاح هو حي عند جماهير العلماء والصالحين والعامة معهم في ذلك قال

وإنما شذ بإنكاره بعض المحدثين قال الحبري المفسر وأبو عمرو هو نبي

واختلفوا في كونه مرسلا وقال القشيري وكثيرون هو ولي وحكى الماوردي في

تفسيره ثلاثة  أقوال أحدها نبي والثاني ولي والثالث أنه من الملائكة وهذا

غريب باطل قال المازري اختلف العلماء في الخضر هل هو نبي أو ولي قال واحتج

من قال بنبوته بقوله وما فعلته عن امري فدل على أنه نبي أوحي إليه وبأنه

أعلم من موسى ويبعد أن يكون ولي أعلم من نبي وأجاب الآخرون بأنه يجوز أن

يكون قد أوحى الله إلى نبي في ذلك العصر أن يأمر الخضر بذلك وقال الثعلبي

المفسر الخضر نبي معمر على جميع الأقوال محجوب عن الأبصار يعني عن أبصار

أكثر الناس قال وقيل إنه لا يموت إلا في آخر الزمان حين يرفع القرآن وذكر

الثعلبي ثلاثة أقوال في أن الخضر كان من زمن إبراهيم الخليل صلى الله عليه

وسلم أم بعده بقليل أم بكثير كنية الخضر أبو العباس واسمه بليا بموحدة

مفتوحة ثم لام ساكنة ثم مثناة تحت بن ملكان بفتح الميم وإسكان اللام وقيل

كليان قال بن قتيبة في المعارف قال وهب بن منبه اسم الخضر بليا بن ملكان بن

فالغ بن عابر بن شالخ بن أرفخشد بن سام بن نوح قالوا وكان أبوه من الملوك

واختلفوا في لقبه الخضر فقال الأكثرون لأنه جلس على فروة بيضاء فصارت خضراء
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ف ض ل (faḍl)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Excess, surplus; superiority in rank or merit.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Excellence (faḍīlah) as a divinely granted distinction, not mere worldly preference.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense of abundance; metaphorically, moral and spiritual preeminence.
- Root: ك ر م (karam)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Generosity, nobility, honor; the essence of goodness.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Comprehensive virtue (karm) encompassing piety and prophetic nobility.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: abundance of good; metaphorical: noble character and lineage.
- Root: خ ض ر (khaḍr)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Greenness, verdure; freshness.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Symbolic of enduring life and divine blessing.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: green color; metaphorical: perpetual vitality and hidden sanctity.
- Sībawayh Rule: ʿAṭf al-Bayān (Appositional Clarification) — For parsing "Nabiyy Allāh ibn Nabiyy Allāh ibn Khalīl Allāh" as sequential genealogical apposition.
chapters.translation:
I say: Regarding his saying, peace and blessings be upon him, "It is not befitting for a servant to say, 'I am better than Jonah (Yūnus),'" — the pronoun in "I" (anā) is said to refer to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and it is said to refer to the speaker, meaning: no ignorant person among those who strive hard in worship, knowledge, or other virtues should say this. For even if he reached the utmost degree of virtue, he would not attain the rank of prophethood. This interpretation is supported by the narration preceding it, namely his saying, the Exalted: "It is not befitting for a servant to say, 'I am better than Jonah son of Mattā.'" And God knows best.

His saying, peace and blessings be upon him: [2375] "I passed by Moses while he was standing in prayer in his grave" — this hadith has already been explained at the end of the Book of Faith (Kitāb al-Īmān) when mentioning Moses and Jesus, peace be upon them.

(Chapter: On the Virtues of Joseph, peace be upon him)
His saying: [2378] "It was said, 'O Messenger of God, who is the most noble of people?' He said: 'The most God-fearing of them.' They said: 'It is not about this that we ask you.' He said: 'Joseph, the Prophet of God, son of the Prophet of God, son of the Friend of God (Khalīl Allāh).' They said: 'It is not about this that we ask you.' He said: 'Then you ask me about the mines of the Arabs? The best of them in the pre-Islamic era (Jāhiliyyah) are the best of them in Islam, when they acquire religious understanding (fiqh).'" Thus it occurred in Muslim: "The Prophet of God, son of the Prophet of God, son of the Friend of God." In some narrations of al-Bukhārī likewise, and in some of them: "The Prophet of God, son of the Prophet of God, son of the Prophet of God, son of the Friend of God." This latter narration is the original, while the former is abbreviated from it. For he is Joseph son of Jacob son of Isaac son of Abraham the Friend, peace be upon him. Thus in the first narration he was attributed to his grandfather. It is said "Yūsuf" with ḍammah on the sīn, kasrah, and fatḥah, with hamzah and without it — these are six forms. The scholars said: The origin of nobility (karam) is abundance of good. Joseph, peace be upon him, combined noble moral qualities with the honor of prophethood, the honor of lineage, and his being a prophet descended from three prophets in succession, one of whom was the Friend of God, peace be upon him. To this was joined the honor of knowledge of dream-interpretation and his mastery of it, the leadership of the world and its sovereignty through excellent conduct, his guardianship of his subjects, the generality of his benefit to them, his compassion toward them, and his deliverance of them from those years of famine. And God knows best.

The scholars said: When he was asked, peace and blessings be upon him, "Which people are most noble?" he informed them of the most complete and most comprehensive nobility, saying: "The most God-fearing of them." We have mentioned that the origin of nobility is abundance of good, and whoever is God-fearing possesses abundant good and abundant benefit in this world, and is the possessor of the highest ranks in the Hereafter. When they said, "It is not about this that we ask you," he said: "Joseph," who combined the goods of the Hereafter and this world and their honors. When they said, "It is not about this that we ask," he understood from them that their intent was the tribes of the Arabs. He said: "The best of them in the Jāhiliyyah are the best of them in Islam, when they acquire religious understanding." Its meaning: those who possessed manly virtues (murūʾāt) and noble moral qualities in the Jāhiliyyah, when they embraced Islam and acquired understanding, they are the best of people. Al-Qāḍī said: This hadith, in its three answers, implies that all nobility — its general and specific, its summary and detailed — is solely religion: through piety, prophethood and deep roots therein, and Islam with understanding. The meaning of "mines of the Arabs" is their origins. "Faqihū" is with ḍammah on the qāf according to the well-known reading, and it is reported with kasrah, meaning: they became jurists, knowledgeable in the legal rulings of the Sacred Law. And God knows best.

(Chapter: On the Virtue of Zachariah, peace be upon him)
His saying, peace and blessings be upon him: [2379] "Zachariah was a carpenter" — in this is the permissibility of crafts, that carpentry does not diminish manly virtue (murūʾah), and that it is a virtuous craft. In it is a virtue for Zachariah, peace be upon him, for he was a craftsman who ate from his own earnings. It is established that he said, peace and blessings be upon him: "The best of what a man eats is from his own earning, and the Prophet of God, David, used to eat from the work of his own hand." In "Zakariyyā" there are five pronunciations: with lengthening (mad) and shortening (qaṣr), "Zakarī" with tashdīd and takhfīf, and "Zakar" like "ʿalima."

(Chapter: On the Virtues of al-Khiḍr, peace be upon him)
The majority of scholars hold that he is alive and present among us. This is agreed upon among the Sufis, the people of righteousness and knowledge. Their accounts of seeing him, meeting with him, learning from him, questioning him, his answers, and his presence in noble places and sites of goodness are too numerous to be enumerated and too famous to be concealed. Shaykh Abū ʿAmr ibn al-Ṣalāḥ said: He is alive according to the majority of scholars and righteous people, and the common folk concur with them in this. He said: Only some traditionists (muḥaddithūn) deviated by denying this. Al-Ḥibarī the exegete and Abū ʿAmr said: He is a prophet. They differed as to whether he was a messenger (rasūl). Al-Qushayrī and many others said: He is a saint (walī). Al-Māwardī reported in his commentary three opinions: first, that he is a prophet; second, that he is a saint; third, that he is of the angels — and this is strange and false. Al-Māzarī said: The scholars differed concerning al-Khiḍr, whether he is a prophet or a saint. He said: Those who affirm his prophethood adduce his saying: "And I did not do it of my own accord" {«وَمَا فَعَلْتُهُ عَنْ أَمْرِي»} — this indicates that he was a prophet to whom revelation came — and that he was more knowledgeable than Moses, and it is unlikely that a saint should be more knowledgeable than a prophet. The others answered: It is possible that God revealed to a prophet of that era to command al-Khiḍr to do that. Al-Thaʿlabī the exegete said: Al-Khiḍr is a prophet, long-lived, according to all opinions, veiled from sight — meaning from the sight of most people. He said: It is said that he will not die except at the end of time, when the Qurʾān is raised up. Al-Thaʿlabī mentioned three opinions as to whether al-Khiḍr was from the time of Abraham the Friend, peace be upon him, or shortly after him, or much later. The kunyah of al-Khiḍr is Abū al-ʿAbbās, and his name is Bilyā — with an open bāʾ (single dot), then a silent lām, then a dotted yāʾ (under) — son of Malkān, with fatḥah on the mīm and sukūn on the lām. It is also said: Kalyān. Ibn Qutaybah said in al-Maʿārif: Wahb ibn Munabbih said: The name of al-Khiḍr is Bilyā ibn Malkān ibn Fālikh ibn ʿĀbir ibn Shālikh ibn Arfakhshad ibn Sām ibn Nūḥ. They said: His father was among the kings. They differed concerning his appellation "al-Khiḍr" (the Green). The majority said: Because he sat upon a white barren land (firwah), and it became green.

chapters.title_en: Section 869 — Commentary on the Hadith of Moses and al-Khiḍr: On the Meaning of "al-Farwah," the Name of Nauf al-Bikālī, and Juridical and Theological Inferences
chapters.arabic_text:
والفروة وجه الأرض وقيل لأنه كان إذا صلى اخضر ما حوله والصواب الأول فقد

صح في البخاري عن أبي هريرة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال إنما سمي

الخضر لأنه جلس على فروة فإذا هي تهتز من خلفه خضراء وبسطت أحواله في تهذيب

الأسماء واللغات والله أعلم قوله
# [2380] (إن نوفا البكالي) هكذا ضبطه الجمهور بكسر الموحدة وتخفيف الكاف

ورواه بعضهم بفتحها وتشديد الكاف قال القاضي هذا الثاني هو ضبط أكثر الشيوخ

وأصحاب الحديث قال والصواب الأول وهو قول المحققين وهو منسوب إلى بني بكال

بطن من حمير وقيل من همدان ونوف هذا هوابن فضالة كذا قاله بن دريد وغيره
# 
# وهو بن امرأة كعب الاحبار وقيل بن اخيه والمشهور الاول قاله بن أبي حاتم

وغيره قالوا  وكنيته أبو يزيد وقيل أبو رشد وكان عالما حكيما قاضيا وإماما

لأهل دمشق قوله (كذب عدو الله) قال العلماء هو على وجه الإغلاظ والزجر عن

مثل قوله لا أنه يعتقد أنه عدو الله حقيقة إنما قاله مبالغة في إنكار قوله

لمخالفته قول رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وكان ذلك في حال غضب بن عباس

لشدة إنكاره وحال الغضب تطلق الألفاظ ولا تراد بها حقائقها والله أعلم قوله

(أنا أعلم) أي في اعتقاده وإلا فكان الخضر أعلم منه كما صرح به في الحديث

قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (فعتب الله عليه إذ لم يرد العلم إليه) أي كان حقه

أن يقول الله أعلم فان مخلوقات الله تعالى لا يعلمها الاهو قال الله تعالى

وما يعلم جنود ربك الا هو واستدل العلماء بسؤال موسى السبيل إلى لقاء الخضر

صلى الله عليهما وسلم على استحباب الاستكثار منه وأنه يستحب للعالم وإن كان

من العلم بمحل عظيم أن يأخذه ممن هو أعلم منه ويسعى إليه في تحصيله وفيه

فضيلة طلب العلم وفي تزوده الحوت وغيره جواز التزود في السفر وفي هذا

الحديث الأدب مع العالم وحرمة المشايخ وترك الاعتراض عليهم وتأويل ما لا

يفهم ظاهره من أفعالهم وحركاتهم وأقوالهم والوفاء بعهودهم والاعتذار عند

مخالفة عهدهم وفيه إثبات كرامات الأولياء على قول من يقول الخضر ولي وفيه

جواز سؤال الطعام عند الحاجة وجواز إجارة السفينة وجواز ركوب السفينة

والدابة وسكنى الدار ولبس الثوب ونحو ذلك بغير أجرة برضى صاحبه لقوله

حملونا بغير نول وفيه الحكم بالظاهر حتى يتبين خلافه لإنكار موسى قال

القاضي واختلف العلماء في قول موسى لقد جئت شيئا إمرا وشيئا نكرا أيهما أشد

فقيل إمرا لأنه العظيم ولأنه في مقابلة خرق السفينة الذي يترتب عليه في

العادة هلاك الذي فيها وأموالهم وهو أعظم من قتل الغلام فإنها نفس واحد

وقيل نكرا اشد لانه قاله عند مباشرة القتل حقيقة وأما القتل في خرق السفينة

فمظنون وقد يسلمون في العادةوقد سلموا في هذه  القضية وليس
# 
# فيه ما هو محقق إلا مجرد الخرق والله أعلم قوله تعالى (إن عبدا من عبادي

بمجمع البحرين هو أعلم منك) قال قتادة هو مجمع بحري فارس والروم مما يلي

المشرق وحكى الثعلبي عن أبي بن كعب أنه بأفريقية قوله (احمل حوتا في مكتل

فحيث تفقد الحوت فهو ثم) الحوت السمكة وكانت سمكة مالحة كما صرح به في

الرواية الثانية والمكتل بكسر الميم وفتح المثناة فوق وهو القفة والزنبيل

وسبق بيانه مرات وتفقده بكسر القاف أي يذهب منك يقال فقده وافتقده وثم بفتح

الثاء أي هناك قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (وانطلق معه فتاه) وهو يوشع بن نون

معنى فتاه صاحبه ونون مصروف كنوح وهذا الحديث يرد قول من قال من المفسرين

إن فتاه عبد له وغير ذلك من الأقوال الباطلة قالوا وهو يوشع بن نون بن

إفراثيم بن يوسف صلى الله عليه وسلم (وأمسك الله عنه جرية الماء حتى كان

مثل الطاق) أما الجرية فبكسر الجيم والطاق عقد البناء وجمعه طيقان وأطواق

وهو الأزج وما عقد أعلاه من البناء وبقي ما تحته خاليا قوله صلى الله عليه

وسلم (فانطلقا بقية يومهما وليلتهما) ضبطوه بنصب ليلتهما وجرها والنصب

التعب قالوا لحقه النصب والجوع ليطلب الغذاء فيتذكر به نسيان الحوت ولهذا

قال صلى الله عليه وسلم ولم ينصب حتى جاوز المكان الذي
# 
# أمر به قوله واتخذ سبيله في البحر عجبا قيل إن لفظة عجبا يجوز أن تكون من

تمام كلام يوشع وقيل من كلام موسى أي قال موسى عجبت من هذا عجبا وقيل من

كلام الله تعالى ومعناه اتخذ موسى سبيل الحوت في البحر عجبا قوله ما كنا

نبغي أي نطلب معناه أن الذي جئنا نطلبه هو الموضع الذي نفقد فيه الحوت قوله

صلى الله عليه وسلم (فرأى رجلا مسجى عليه بثوب فسلم عليه فقال له الخضر أنى

بأرضك السلام) المسجى المغطى وأنى أي من أين السلام
# 
# في هذه الأرض التي لا يعرف فيها السلام قال العلماء أنى تأتي بمعنى  أين

ومتى وحيث وكيف وحملوهما بغير نول بفتح النون وإسكان الواو أي بغير أجر

والنول والنوال العطاء قوله لتغرق أهلها قرئ في السبع بضم التاء المثناة

فوق ونصب أهلها وبفتح المثناة تحت ورفع اهلها وجئت شيئا إمرا أي عظيما كثير

الشدة ولا ترهقني أي تغشني وتحملني قوله أقتلت نفسا زاكية بغير نفس لقد جئت
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ف-ر-و (f-r-w)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: The root denotes the outer surface of the earth, the skin, or the fur/pelt of an animal; "al-farwah" is the face of the ground.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological usage, it retains its literal sense of the earth's surface, without metaphorical extension here; the Prophet's explanation anchors it to the physical ground.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) designation of the earth's crust; the alternative claim (that the earth greened around him) is a metaphorical conjecture rejected by the sound report.
- Root: ب-ك-ل (b-k-l)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: A tribal name; "Bikāl" is a sub-tribe of Ḥimyar, and per another report, of Hamdān.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradats): Used as a proper noun (nisbah), indicating lineage; no theological nuance.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal proper-name attribution; the vocalization dispute (kasrah on bā' with takhfīf vs. fatḥah with tashdīd) affects only orthoepy, not semantics.
- Sībawayh Rule: Naṣb vs. Jarr in "laylatahumā" (نصب ليلتهما وجرها) — The accusative (naṣb) denotes that fatigue (naṣab) befell them, as the grammarians note the homonymy; the genitive (jarr) is also transmitted, both being valid readings of the transmitted text.
chapters.translation:
I say: "Al-farwah" is the face of the earth. And it was said: He was named thus because when he prayed, what surrounded him became green. But the correct view is the first, for it has been authentically established in al-Bukhārī, on the authority of Abū Hurayrah, from the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him), who said: {«إنما سمي الخضر لأنه جلس على فروة فإذا هي تهتز من خلفه خضراء»} — "He was only named al-Khiḍr because he sat upon a barren land (farwah), and behold, it was quivering green behind him." And his circumstances have been expanded upon in Tahdhīb al-Asmā' wa al-Lughāt. And Allah knows best.

His saying — [2380] (Indeed, Nauf al-Bikālī): Thus the majority have fixed it with a kasrah on the bā' (bikālī) and a takhfīf (unshaddled) kāf. And some narrated it with a fatḥah on the bā' and a tashdīd on the kāf. Al-Qāḍī said: This second is the fixation of most of the shaykhs and hadith scholars. And he said: The correct is the first, and it is the saying of the verifiers (muḥaqqiqīn). And he is attributed to the Banū Bikāl, a sub-tribe of Ḥimyar; and it was said: of Hamdān. And this Nauf is Ibn Faḍālah — thus said Ibn Durayd and others. And he is the son of the woman of Kaʿb al-Aḥbār; and it was said: the son of his brother. And the well-known is the first — thus said Ibn Abī Ḥātim and others. They said: And his kunyah was Abū Yazīd; and it was said: Abū Rushd. And he was a learned man, a sage, a judge, and an imam for the people of Damascus.

His saying (Kaʿb lied, the enemy of Allah): The scholars said: This is in the mode of severity (īghlāẓ) and deterrence (zajr) against the like of his statement — not that he (Ibn ʿAbbās) truly believed him to be an enemy of Allah in reality. He only said it as an exaggeration in rejecting his statement, because of its contradiction of the saying of the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him). And that was in a state of anger on the part of Ibn ʿAbbās, due to the intensity of his rejection. And the state of anger releases utterances whose realities are not intended. And Allah knows best.

His saying (I am more knowledgeable): That is, in his own belief — for otherwise, al-Khiḍr was more knowledgeable than him, as he explicitly stated in the hadith.

His saying, peace and blessings be upon him (And Allah reproached him for not referring the knowledge back to Him): That is, his duty was to say "Allah knows best," for the creatures of Allah Almighty are not known except by Him. Allah Almighty said: {«وما يعلم جنود ربك إلا هو»} — "And none knows the soldiers of your Lord except Him" (Qur'an 74:31).

And the scholars have adduced, from Moses' asking the way to meet al-Khiḍr (peace be upon them both), the recommendation of seeking abundance from one more knowledgeable, and that it is recommended for the scholar — even if he occupies a lofty station in knowledge — to take from one more learned than himself, and to journey to him in pursuit of it. And in this is the virtue of seeking knowledge. And in his provisioning of the fish and other things is the permissibility of taking provisions for a journey.

And in this hadith: the etiquette with the scholar, the sanctity of the shaykhs, the abandonment of objecting to them, the interpretation (ta'wīl) of what is not understood from the apparent sense of their actions, movements, and sayings, the fulfillment of their covenants, and the offering of excuses when their covenant is contravened. And in it is the affirmation of the miracles of the saints (karāmāt al-awliyā') — on the view of those who say al-Khiḍr was a saint (walī). And in it is the permissibility of asking for food when in need, the permissibility of hiring a ship, and the permissibility of riding a ship, an animal, dwelling in a house, wearing a garment, and the like, without payment, with the owner's consent — due to his saying: "They carried us without fare (bi-ghayri nawl)."

And in it is the judgment by the apparent (ḥukm bi al-ẓāhir) until its contrary becomes evident, due to Moses' rejection (of al-Khiḍr's actions).

Al-Qāḍī said: The scholars differed concerning Moses' saying "You have committed a thing unprecedented (imrā)" and "a thing detestable (nukrā)" — which of the two is more severe? It was said: "imrā" is more severe, because it denotes the great, and because it was said in response to the scuttling of the ship, which ordinarily entails the destruction of those within it and their wealth — and that is greater than the killing of the boy, for that is but a single soul. And it was said: "nukrā" is more severe, because he said it at the actual commission of the killing; as for the killing in the scuttling of the ship, it was only conjectural, and they might ordinarily be saved — and indeed they were saved in this very incident. And there is nothing in it that is certain except the mere scuttling. And Allah knows best.

His saying, Almighty (Indeed, a servant of My servants at the junction of the two seas is more knowledgeable than you): Qatādah said: It is the junction of the seas of Persia and Rome, toward the east. And al-Thaʿlabī narrated from Ubayy ibn Kaʿb that it is in Africa.

His saying (Carry a fish in a basket; wherever you lose the fish, then it is there): "Al-ḥūt" is the fish, and it was a salted fish, as explicitly stated in the second narration. And "al-miktal" — with a kasrah on the mīm and a fatḥah on the tā' (miktal) — is the basket (al-qaffah) and the wicker container (al-zambil). Its explanation has preceded multiple times. And "tafaqqadahu" — with a kasrah on the qāf — means: it goes from you. One says: faqadahu and iftaqadahu. And "thumma" — with a fatḥah on the thā' — means: there (hunāka).

His saying, peace and blessings be upon him (And he set out with him, his attendant): And he is Yūshaʿ ibn Nūn. The meaning of "fatāhu" is his companion. And "Nūn" is declined (maṣrūf), like Nūḥ. And this hadith refutes the saying of those commentators who claimed his attendant was his slave, and other such false sayings. They said: And he is Yūshaʿ ibn Nūn ibn Ifrāthīm ibn Yūsuf (peace be upon him).

(And Allah held back from him the flow of water until it was like an arch (ṭāq)): As for "al-jariyah," it is with a kasrah on the jīm. And "al-ṭāq" is the arch of a building; its plural is ṭīqān and aṭwāq. And it is the vaulted structure (al-azaj), and whatever is arched at its top from a building, while what is beneath it remains hollow.

His saying, peace and blessings be upon him (And they set out for the rest of their day and their night): They have fixed it with naṣb on "laylatahumā" and with jarr. And the naṣb is the expression of fatigue (naṣab). They said: Fatigue and hunger befell him, seeking sustenance, so that he would be reminded by it of the forgetting of the fish. And for this reason he said, peace and blessings be upon him: "And he was not fatigued until he had passed the place which he was commanded."

His saying (And he took a path in the sea, wondrously (ʿajaban)): It was said that the word "ʿajaban" might be part of Yūshaʿ's speech; and it was said: it is from Moses' speech, i.e., Moses said: "I marveled at this with wonder." And it was said: it is from the speech of Allah Almighty, and its meaning is: Moses took the path of the fish in the sea, wondrously.

His saying (We did not intend): i.e., we did not seek. Its meaning: that which we came seeking is the place where we would lose the fish.

His saying, peace and blessings be upon him (And he saw a man covered with a garment, and he greeted him; and al-Khiḍr said to him: "How (annā) is peace in your land?"): "Al-musajjā" is the covered one. And "annā" means: from where (min ayna) is peace in this land in which peace is not known? The scholars said: "annā" comes with the meaning of "ayna" (where), "matā" (when), "ḥaythu" (wherever), and "kayfa" (how).

And their saying "bi-ghayri nawl" — with a fatḥah on the nūn and a sukūn on the wāw — i.e., without payment. And "al-nawl" and "al-nawāl" are the gift.

His saying (To drown its people): It was read in the seven readings (al-sabʿ) with a ḍammah on the tā' (tughriqa) and naṣb on "ahlahā," and with a fatḥah on the tā' (taghriqu) and rafʿ on "ahluhā."

And "You have committed a thing unprecedented (imrā)": i.e., great, of much severity.

And "Do not burden me (lā turhiqnī)": i.e., do not overwhelm me and do not impose upon me.

His saying (Have you killed a pure soul without [retribution for] a soul? You have certainly committed...): [The text continues, but the provided excerpt ends here.]

chapters.title_en: Commentary on the Phrase "Zakiyyah" and Related Issues in the Story of al-Khaḍir (Section 870)
chapters.arabic_text:
شيئا نكرا قرئ في السبع زاكية وزكية قالوا ومعناه طاهرة من الذنوب وقوله

بغير نفس أي بغير قصاص لك عليها والنكر المنكر وقرئ في السبع بإسكان الكاف

وضمها والأكثرون بالإسكان قال العلماء وقوله إذا غلام يلعب فقتله دليل على

أنه كان صبيا ليس ببالغ لأنه حقيقة الغلام وهذا قول الجمهور أنه لم يكن

بالغا وزعمت طائفة أنه كان بالغا يعمل بالفساد واحتجت بقوله اقتلت نفسا

زكية بغير نفس فدل على أنه ممن يجب عليه القصاص والصبي لا قصاص عليه وبقوله

كان كافرا في قراءة بن عباس كما ذكر في آخر الحديث والجواب عن الأول من

وجهين أحدهما أن المراد التنبيه على أنه قتل بغير حق والثاني أنه يحتمل أن

شرعهم كان إيجاب القصاص على الصبي كما أنه في شرعنا يؤاخذ بغرامة المتلفات

والجواب عن الثاني من وجهين أحدهما أنه شاذ لا حجة فيه والثاني أنه سماه

بما يؤول إليه لو عاش كما جاء في الرواية الثانية قوله قد بلغت من لدني

عذرا فيه ثلاث قراآت في السبع الأكثرون بضم الدال
# 
# وتشديد النون والثانية بالضم وتخفيف النون والثالثة بإسكان الدال

وإشمامها الضم وتخفيف النون ومعناه قد بلغت إلى الغاية التي تعذر بسببها في

فراقي قوله تعالى فانطلقا حتى إذا اتيا اهل قرية قال الثعلبي قال بن عباس

هي انطاكية وقال بن سيرين الأيلة وهي أبعد الأرض من السماء قوله تعالى

فوجدا فيها جدارا يريد أن ينقض هذا من المجاز لأن الجدار لا يكون له حقيقة

إرادة ومعناه قرب من الانقضاض وهو السقوط واستدل الأصوليون بهذا على وجود

المجاز في القرآن وله نظائر معروفة قال وهب بن منبه  كان طول هذا الجدار إلى

السماء مائة ذراع قوله لو شئت لتخذت عليه اجرا قرئ بالسبع لتخذت بتخفيف

التاء وكسر الخاء ولاتخذت بالتشديد وفتح الخاء أي لأخذت عليه أجرة تأكل بها

قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (وجاء عصفور حتى وقع على حرف السفينة ثم نقر في

البحر فقال له الخضر ما نقص علمي وعلمك من علم الله تعالى إلا مثل ما نقص

هذا العصفور من البحر) قال العلماء لفظ النقص هنا ليس على ظاهره وإنما

معناه أن علمي وعلمك بالنسبة إلى علم الله تعالى كنسبة ما نقره هذا العصفور

إلى ماء البحر هذا على التقريب إلى الأفهام وإلا فنسبة علمهما أقل وأحقر

وقد جاء في رواية البخاري ما علمي وعلمك في جنب علم الله إلا كما أخذ هذا

العصفور بمنقاره أي في جنب معلوم الله وقد يطلق العلم
# 
# بمعنى المعلوم وهو من إطلاق المصدر لإرادة المفعول كقولهم رغم ضرب

السلطان أي مضروبه قال القاضي وقال بعض من أشكل عليه هذا الحديث إلا هنا

بمعنى ولا أي ولا نقص علمي وعلمك من علم الله ولا مثل ما أخذ هذا العصفور

لأن علم الله تعالى لا يدخله نقص قال القاضي ولا حاجة إلى هذا التكلف بل هو

صحيح كما بينا والله أعلم قوله (كذب نوف) هوجار على مذهب أصحابنا أن الكذب

هو الإخبار عن الشئ خلاف ما هو عمدا كان أو سهوا خلافا للمعتزلة وسبقت

المسألة في كتاب الإيمان قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (حتى انتهينا إلى الصخرة

فعمي عليه) وقع في بعض الأصول بفتح العين المهملة وكسر الميم وفي بعضها بضم

العين وتشديد الميم وفي بعضها بالغين المعجمة قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (مثل

الكوة) بفتح الكاف ويقال بضمها وهي الطاق
# 
# كما قال في الرواية الأولى قوله (مستلقيا على حلاوة القفا) هي وسط القفا

ومعناه لم يمل إلى أحد جانبيه وهي بضم الحاء وفتحها وكسرها أفصحها الضم

وممن حكى الكسر صاحب نهاية الغريب ويقال أيضا حلاوا بالفتح وحلاوى بالضم

والقصر وحلواء  بالمد قوله (مجيء ما جاء بك) قال القاضي ضبطناه مجئ مرفوع

غير منون عن بعضهم وعن بعضهم منونا قال وهو أظهر أي أمر عظيم جاء بك قوله

صلى الله عليه وسلم (انتحى عليها) أي اعتمد على السفينة وقصد
# 
# خرقها واستدل به العلماء على النظر في المصالح عند تعارض الأمور وأنه إذا

تعارضت مفسدتان دفع أعظمهما بارتكاب أخفهما كما خرق السفينة لدفع غصبها

وذهاب جملتها قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (فانطلق إلى أحدهم بادي الرأي فقتله)

بادئ بالهمز وتركه فمن همزه معناه أول الرأي وابتداؤه أي انطلق إليه مسارعا

إلى قتله من غير فكر ومن لم يهمز فمعناه ظهر له رأي في قتله من البدء وهو

ظهور رأي لم يكن قال القاضي ويمد البدء ويقصر قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم

(رحمة الله علينا وعلى موسى قال وكان إذا ذكر أحدا من الأنبياء بدأ بنفسه

رحمة الله علينا وعلى أخي كذا رحمة الله علينا) قال أصحابنا فيه استحباب

ابتداء الإنسان بنفسه في الدعاء وشبهه من أمور الآخرة وأما حظوظ الدنيا

فالأدب فيها الإيثار وتقديم غيره على نفسه واختلف العلماء في الابتداء في

عنوان الكتاب فالصحيح الذي قاله كثيرون من السلف وجاء به الصحيح أنه يبدأ

بنفسه فيقدمها على المكتوب إليه فيقال من فلان إلى فلان ومنه حديث كتاب

النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم من محمد عبد الله ورسوله إلى هرقل عظيم الروم

وقالت طائفة يبدأ بالمكتوب إليه فيقول إلى فلان من فلان قالوا إلا أن يكتب
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ز-ك-و (z-k-w)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Purity, growth, and increase; a thing free from blemish or defilement.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Moral and spiritual purity—freedom from sin and moral corruption.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense denotes physical cleanliness; metaphorical sense denotes moral innocence.
- Root: ن-ك-ر (n-k-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Disapproval, denial, and that which is unrecognized or abhorrent.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): That which the intellect or divine law deems repugnant (munkar).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: unknown/strange; metaphorical: morally odious.
- Root: ق-ص-ص (q-ṣ-ṣ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To follow a trace; retribution (qiṣāṣ) as exact equivalence in recompense.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Legal retribution—the just requital of a life for a life.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: narrating/tracing; metaphorical: legal retaliation.
- Root: غ-ل-م (gh-l-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: A boy in the state of youthful vigor, before or at the threshold of maturity.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): A male child; in legal discourse, one who has not yet attained puberty (bulūgh).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: young male; metaphorical extension to a servant or slave.
- Root: ع-ذ-ر (ʿ-dh-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Excuse, justification, and the removal of blame.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The attainment of a point where one is excused from further obligation.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: cutting off blame; metaphorical: reaching the limit of justification.
- Sībawayh Rule: Taqdīr al-Maḥdhūf (Ellipsis Reconstruction) — For interpreting "بغير نفس" as "بغير قصاص" (without retaliation), the omitted noun is supplied from context; also applied to "لتخذت" where the underlying form is "لاتخذت" (to take).
chapters.translation:
I say: The word "zakiyyah" (زكية) was recited in the Seven Readings (al-Sabʿ) both as "zākiyah" and "zakiyyah." The scholars said: Its meaning is "pure from sins." His saying {«بغير نفس»} — "without a soul" — means without retaliation (qiṣāṣ) incumbent upon you for it. The word "al-nukr" (النكر) is "al-munkar" (the abominable). It was recited in the Seven Readings with the sukūn on the kāf and with its ḍammah, though the majority read it with sukūn.

The scholars said: His saying — "when a boy was playing" — and then he killed him is evidence that he was a child not yet having reached puberty, because this is the literal sense of "ghulām" (boy). This is the position of the majority: that he had not reached puberty. A faction claimed that he was an adult who worked corruption, adducing his saying {«اقتلت نفسا زكية بغير نفس»} — "You have killed a pure soul without a soul" — as proof that he was one upon whom retaliation is obligatory, and a child incurs no retaliation. They also adduced his saying "he was a disbeliever" in the reading of Ibn ʿAbbās, as mentioned at the end of the ḥadīth.

The answer to the first proof is from two angles: First, that the intent is to draw attention to the fact that he was killed without right. Second, that it is possible their law (sharʿ) required retaliation against a child, just as in our law he is held liable for the restitution of destroyed property.

The answer to the second proof is from two angles: First, that it is an anomalous reading (shādhdh) carrying no evidential weight. Second, that he named him by what he would have become had he lived, as comes in the second narration.

His saying {«قد بلغت من لدني عذرا»} — "I have reached from me an excuse" — has three readings in the Seven: the majority read with ḍammah on the dāl and tashdīd on the nūn; the second with ḍammah and tashdīf on the nūn; the third with sukūn on the dāl and its imālah toward ḍammah, with tashdīf on the nūn. Its meaning: "I have reached the utmost limit by which I am excused in parting from me."

His saying, the Exalted: {«فانطلقا حتى إذا اتيا اهل قرية»} — "So they set out until when they came to the people of a village" — al-Thaʿlabī said: Ibn ʿAbbās said it is Antioch (Anṭākiyah). Ibn Sīrīn said it is Aylah, which is the land farthest from the heaven.

His saying, the Exalted: {«فوجدا فيها جدارا يريد أن ينقض»} — "So they found therein a wall intending to collapse" — this is metaphorical (majāz), because a wall cannot truly possess intention. Its meaning: it was near to collapsing, i.e., falling. The uṣūliyyūn (scholars of legal theory) adduced this as evidence for the existence of metaphor in the Qur'an, and it has well-known parallels.

Wahb ibn Munabbih said: The height of this wall reached one hundred cubits toward the sky.

His saying {«لو شئت لتخذت عليه اجرا»} — "If you wished, you could have taken a wage for it" — was recited in the Seven as "latakhadhta" with tashdīd on the tāʾ and kasrah on the khāʾ, and "lāttakhadhta" with tashdīd and fatḥah on the khāʾ, meaning: "You would have taken a wage to eat from."

His saying, peace and blessings be upon him: "A sparrow came until it landed on the edge of the ship, then pecked in the sea. Al-Khaḍir said to him: 'My knowledge and your knowledge have not diminished from the knowledge of God except like what this sparrow diminished from the sea.'" The scholars said: The word "diminution" (nuqṣān) here is not to be taken literally. Rather, its meaning is that my knowledge and your knowledge, relative to the knowledge of God the Exalted, is like the proportion of what this sparrow pecked to the water of the sea. This is by way of approximation to understanding; otherwise, the proportion of their knowledge is even less and more insignificant. It has come in the narration of al-Bukhārī: "My knowledge and your knowledge in relation to the knowledge of God is only like what this sparrow took with its beak" — i.e., in relation to what God knows. Knowledge (ʿilm) may be used to mean the known thing (maʿlūm), which is the application of the verbal noun to intend the object, like their saying "the striking of the Sultan" meaning "the one struck."

Al-Qāḍī said: Some who found this ḥadīth problematic said that "illā" here means "and not" (wa-lā), i.e., "and my knowledge and your knowledge do not diminish from the knowledge of God, nor even the like of what this sparrow took," because the knowledge of God the Exalted admits no diminution. Al-Qāḍī said: There is no need for this strained interpretation; rather, it is sound as we have explained. And God knows best.

His saying: "Nawf lied" — this is in accordance with the doctrine of our companions (al-Shāfiʿiyyah) that lying (kidhb) is informing about a thing contrary to what it is, whether intentionally or by mistake, contrary to the Muʿtazilah. This issue has preceded in the Book of Faith (Kitāb al-Īmān).

His saying, peace and blessings be upon him: "Until we reached the rock, and he lost consciousness over it" — occurs in some manuscripts with fatḥah on the ʿayn and kasrah on the mīm; in others with ḍammah on the ʿayn and tashdīd on the mīm; and in others with ghayn (muʿjamah).

His saying, peace and blessings be upon him: "Like the window (al-kawwah)" — with fatḥah on the kāf, and it is said with ḍammah; it is the archway (ṭāq), as stated in the first narration.

His saying: "Reclining on the sweetness of the nape (ḥalāwat al-qafā)" — it is the middle of the nape. Its meaning: he did not incline to either of its sides. It is with ḍammah on the ḥāʾ, and fatḥah, and kasrah — the most eloquent being the ḍammah. Among those who reported the kasrah is the author of Nihāyat al-Gharīb. It is also said "ḥalāwā" with fatḥah, and "ḥalāwā" with ḍammah and shortening, and "ḥalwāʾ" with elongation.

His saying: "The coming of what brought you (majīʾu mā jāʾa bika)" — Al-Qāḍī said: We recorded it as "majīʾu" raised without tanwīn from some of them, and from others with tanwīn. He said: The latter is more apparent, meaning: "A momentous matter has brought you."

His saying, peace and blessings be upon him: "He bore down upon it (in-taḥā ʿalayhā)" — i.e., he leaned upon the ship and intended to pierce it. The scholars adduced this as evidence for considering public interests (maṣāliḥ) when matters conflict, and that when two harms (mafsadatān) conflict, the greater is repelled by committing the lesser — just as he pierced the ship to repel its seizure and the loss of its entirety.

His saying, peace and blessings be upon him: "So he set out to one of them with the first opinion (bādī al-raʾy) and killed him" — with hamzah on "bādiʾ" and without it. Whoever hamzahs it, its meaning is "the first opinion and its beginning," i.e., he set out to him hastening to kill him without reflection. Whoever does not hamzah it, its meaning is: a view appeared to him for killing him from the start (badʾ), which is the emergence of an opinion that had not been. Al-Qāḍī said: "al-badʾ" may be elongated or shortened.

His saying, peace and blessings be upon him: "The mercy of God be upon us and upon Moses. He said: Whenever he mentioned any of the prophets, he would begin with himself: 'The mercy of God be upon us and upon my brother so-and-so; the mercy of God be upon us.'" Our companions said: In this is the recommendation (istiḥbāb) of a person beginning with himself in supplication and similar matters of the Hereafter. As for worldly shares, the proper conduct (adab) therein is preferring others and putting them before oneself.

The scholars differed regarding the beginning in the heading of a book (kitāb). The correct view — which many of the Salaf held and which the authentic (ṣaḥīḥ) reports affirm — is that one begins with himself, putting himself before the addressee, saying: "From so-and-so to so-and-so." From this is the ḥadīth of the letter of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him: "From Muḥammad, the servant of God and His Messenger, to Heraclius, the emperor of Rome." A faction said: One begins with the addressee, saying: "To so-and-so from so-and-so." They said: Except when one writes...

chapters.title_en: The Ruler Addressing His Inferior, the Master His Slave, and the Father His Child; The Sealing of Hearts; The Superiority of the Companions
chapters.arabic_text:
الأمير إلى من دونه أو السيد إلى عبده أو الوالد إلى ولده ونحو هذا قوله

صلى الله عليه وسلم (لكن أخذته من صاحبه ذمامة) هي بفتح الذال المعجمة
# 
# أي استحياء لتكرار مخالفته وقيل ملامة والأول هو المشهور قوله (وأما

الغلام فطبع يوم طبع كافرا) قال القاضي في هذا حجة بينة لأهل السنة لصحة

أصل مذهبهم في الطبع والرين والأكنة والأغشية والحجب والسد وأشباه هذه

الألفاظ الواردة في الشرع في أفعال الله تعالى بقلوب أهل الكفر والضلال

ومعنى ذلك عندهم خلق الله تعالى فيها ضد الإيمان وضد الهدى وهذا على أصل

أهل السنة أن العبد لا قدرة له إلا ما أراده الله تعالى ويسره له وخلقه له

خلافا للمعتزلة والقدرية القائلين بأن للعبد فعلا من قبل نفسه وقدرة على

الهدى والضلال والخير والشر والإيمان والكفر وأن معنى هذه الألفاظ نسبة

الله تعالى لأصحابها وحكمه عليهم بذلك وقالت طائفة منهم معناها خلقه علامة

لذلك في قلوبهم والحق الذي لا شك فيه أن الله تعالى يفعل ما يشاء من الخير

والشر لا يسئل عما يفعل وهم يسئلون وكما قال تعالى في الذر هؤلاء للجنة ولا

أبالي وهؤلاء للنار ولا أبالي فالذين قضى لهم بالنار طبع على قلوبهم وختم

عليها وغشاها وأكنها وجعل من بين أيديها سدا ومن خلفها سدا وحجابا مستورا

وجعل في آذانهم وقرا وفي قلوبهم مرضا لتتم سابقته فيهم وتمضي كلمته لاراد

لحكمه ولا معقب لأمره وقضائه وبالله التوفيق وقد يحتج بهذا الحديث من يقول

أطفال الكفار في النار وقد سبق بيان هذه المسألة وأن فيهم ثلاثة مذاهب

الصحيح أنهم في الجنة والثاني في النار والثالث يتوقف عن الكلام فيهم فلا

يحكم لهم بشئ وتقدمت دلائل الجميع وللقائلين بالجنة أن يقولوا في جواب هذا

الحديث معناه علم الله لو بلغ لكان كافرا قوله (وكان أبواه قد عطفا عليه

فلو أدرك أرهقهما طغيانا وكفرا) أي حملهما عليهما وألحقهما بهما والمراد

بالطغيان هنا الزيادة في الضلال وهذا الحديث من دلائل مذهب
# 
# أهل الحق في أن الله تعالى أعلم بما كان وبما يكون وبما لا يكون لو كان

كيف كان يكون ومنه قوله تعالى ولو ردوا لعادوا لما نهوا عنه وقوله تعالى

ولو نزلنا عليك كتابا في قرطاس فلمسوه بايديهم لقال الذين كفروا الآية

وقوله تعالى ولو جعلناه ملكا لجعلناه رجلا وللبسنا عليهم وغير ذلك من

الآيات قوله تعالى خيرا منه زكاة واقرب رحما قيل المراد بالزكاة الإسلام

وقيل الصلاح وأما الرحم فقيل معناه الرحمة لوالديه وبرهما وقيل المراد

يرحمانه  قيل أبدلهما الله بنتا صالحة وقيل ابنا حكاه القاضي قوله (تمارى هو

والحر بن قيس) أي تنازعا وتجادلا والحر بالحاء والراء وفي هذه القصة أنواع

من القواعد والأصول والفروع والآداب والنفائس المهمة سبق التنبيه على

معظمها سوى ما هو ظاهر منها ومما لم يسبق أنه لا بأس على العالم والفاضل أن

يخدمه المفضول ويقضي له حاجة ولا يكون هذا من أخذ العوض على تعليم العلم

والآداب بل من مروءات الأصحاب وحسن العشرة ودليله من هذه القصة حمل فتاه

غداءهما وحمل أصحاب السفينة موسى والخضر
# 
# بغير أجرة لمعرفتهم الخضر بالصلاح والله أعلم ومنها الحث على التواضع في

علمه وغيره وأنه لا يدعي أنه أعلم الناس وأنه إذا سئل عن أعلم الناس يقول

الله أعلم ومنها بيان أصل عظيم من أصول الإسلام وهو وجوب التسليم لكل ما

جاء به الشرع وإن كان بعضه لا تظهر حكمته للعقول ولا يفهمه أكثر الناس وقد

لا يفهمونه كلهم كالقدر موضع الدلالة قتل الغلام وخرق السفينة فإن صورتهما

صورة المنكر وكان صحيحا في نفس الأمر له حكم بينة لكنها لا تظهر للخلق فإذا

أعلمهم الله تعالى بها علموها ولهذا قال وما فعلته عن امري يعني بل بأمر

الله تعالى
# 
#

| كتاب فضائل الصحابة رضي الله عنهم
# قال الإمام أبو عبد الله المازري اختلف الناس في تفضيل بعض الصحابة على

بعض فقالت طائفة لا نفاضل بل نمسك عن ذلك وقال الجمهور بالتفضيل ثم اختلفوا

فقال أهل السنة أفضلهم أبو بكر الصديق وقال الخطابية أفضلهم عمر بن الخطاب

وقالت الراوندية أفضلهم العباس وقالت الشيعة علي واتفق أهل السنة على أن

أفضلهم أبو بكر ثم عمر قال جمهورهم ثم عثمان ثم علي وقال بعض أهل السنة من

أهل الكوفة بتقديم علي على عثمان والصحيح المشهور تقديم عثمان قال أبو

منصور البغدادي أصحابنا مجمعون على أن أفضلهم الخلفاء الأربعة على الترتيب

المذكور ثم تمام العشرة ثم أهل بدر ثم أحد ثم بيعة الرضوان وممن له مزية

أهل العقبتين من الأنصار وكذلك  السابقون الأولون وهم من صلى إلى القبلتين

في قول بن المسيب وطائفة وفي قول الشعبي أهل بيعة الرضوان وفي قول عطاء

ومحمد بن كعب أهل بدر قال القاضي عياض وذهبت طائفة منهم بن عبد البر إلى أن

من توفي من الصحابة في حياة النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أفضل ممن بقي بعده

وهذا الإطلاق غير مرضي ولا مقبول واختلف العلماء في أن التفضيل المذكور

قطعي أم لا وهل هو في الظاهر والباطن أم في الظاهر خاصة وممن قال بالقطع
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ذ م م (dh-m-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Blame, dispraise; the state of being blameworthy (dhammah) — here, a sense of shame or reproach that restrains one from action.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Moral censure internalized as a deterrent; in theological context, the natural human disposition toward decency.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: blame (dhamm). Metaphorical: the inner feeling of shame (istiyā') that acts as a self-reproach — a transferred sense from external censure to internal restraint.
- Sībawayh Rule: ʿAṭf al-Bayān (Appositional Clarification) — The phrase "أو السيد إلى عبده" is coordinated to clarify the scope of the initial address, each term specifying a distinct relational hierarchy.

- Root: ط ب ع (ṭ-b-ʿ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To stamp, seal, imprint; the natural constitution (ṭabʿ) of a thing.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In Qur'anic usage, the divine sealing (ṭabʿ) of hearts denotes the irreversible fixation of disbelief as a consequence of persistent rejection — an act of God's justice.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: physical stamping. Metaphorical: the complete envelopment of the heart by sin such that truth can no longer penetrate — a state of moral blindness.
- Sībawayh Rule: Ḥāl (Circumstantial Clause) — "كافرا" is a circumstantial accusative describing the state of the boy at the moment of his creation.

- Root: ف ض ل (f-ḍ-l)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Excess, surplus; superiority in rank or merit.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological discourse, tafḍīl denotes the graded hierarchy of excellence among the Companions, grounded in divine grace and prophetic testimony.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: abundance. Metaphorical: precedence in virtue and nearness to God — a relational superiority, not merely quantitative.
- Sībawayh Rule: Tamyīz (Specification) — "أفضلهم" requires a specifying accusative to delineate the domain of superiority (e.g., "in rank," "in virtue").
chapters.translation:
I say: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "But I took it from his companion out of a sense of shame (dhamāmah)." This word is pronounced with a fatḥah on the dhāl (dhamāmah), meaning: a feeling of shyness (istiyā') due to his repeated opposition. It was also said: meaning blame (malāmah). The first interpretation is the well-known one.

His saying, peace and blessings be upon him: "As for the boy, he was stamped (ṭubiʿa) on the day he was stamped as a disbeliever" — Al-Qāḍī said: In this there is a clear proof for the People of the Sunnah (Ahl al-Sunnah) regarding the soundness of their foundational doctrine concerning the stamping (al-ṭabʿ), the rust (al-rayn), the covers (al-akinnah), the veils (al-aghshiyah), the barriers (al-ḥujub), the enclosures (al-sudd), and similar expressions that occur in the Sacred Law (al-sharʿ) concerning the acts of God Almighty upon the hearts of the people of disbelief and error. The meaning of all this, according to them, is that God Almighty creates within them the opposite of faith and the opposite of guidance. This is in accordance with the foundational principle of the People of the Sunnah that the servant has no power except what God Almighty wills for him, facilitates for him, and creates for him — contrary to the Muʿtazilah and the Qadariyyah, who assert that the servant has an act originating from himself and a power over guidance and error, good and evil, faith and disbelief, and that the meaning of these expressions is merely God's attribution of these states to their possessors and His judgment upon them accordingly. A group among them said: its meaning is that He created a sign of that in their hearts.

The truth, concerning which there is no doubt, is that God Almighty does whatever He wills of good and evil; He is not questioned about what He does, but they shall be questioned. As He, exalted, said concerning the atoms (al-dharr): "These are for Paradise, and I do not care; these are for the Fire, and I do not care." Thus, those for whom He decreed the Fire — He stamped upon their hearts, sealed them, covered them, veiled them, placed before them a barrier and behind them a barrier, and cast a covering veil, and placed in their ears heaviness and in their hearts sickness, so that His prior decree might be fulfilled in them and His word might be executed. There is no repeller of His judgment, and no annuller of His command and decree. And with God is success.

One may also adduce this ḥadīth as evidence for those who say that the children of the disbelievers are in the Fire. The exposition of this question has already preceded, namely that there are three schools of thought concerning them: the sound one is that they are in Paradise; the second is that they are in the Fire; the third is that one refrains from speaking about them and passes no judgment concerning them. The evidences for all of these have already been presented. Those who hold the view of Paradise may respond to this ḥadīth by saying: its meaning is that God knew that had he reached maturity, he would have been a disbeliever.

His saying: "And his parents had already been inclined toward him, and had he reached them, he would have overwhelmed them with transgression (ṭughyān) and disbelief" — meaning: he would have compelled them to both and attached them to himself. The intended meaning of "transgression" here is increase in error.

This ḥadīth is among the proofs of the doctrine of the People of Truth (Ahl al-Ḥaqq) that God Almighty knows what was, what will be, and what would have been had it been otherwise — how it would have been. From this is His saying, exalted: "And had they been returned, they would have reverted to what they were forbidden" {«ولو ردوا لعادوا لما نهوا عنه»}, and His saying, exalted: "And had We sent down to you a Book on parchment and they touched it with their hands, those who disbelieve would have said..." {«ولو نزلنا عليك كتابا في قرطاس فلمسوه بايديهم لقال الذين كفروا»}, and His saying, exalted: "And had We made him an angel, We would have made him a man, and We would have confused them" {«ولو جعلناه ملكا لجعلناه رجلا وللبسنا عليهم»}, and other such verses.

His saying, exalted: "Better than him in purity (zakāh) and nearer in kinship (ruḥm)" {«خيرا منه زكاة واقرب رحما»} — It was said: the intended meaning of "purity" is Islam; and it was said: righteousness. As for "kinship," it was said: its meaning is mercy (raḥmah) toward his parents and dutifulness to them; and it was said: the intended meaning is that they would have shown mercy to him. It was said: God replaced them with a righteous daughter; and it was said: with a son. Al-Qāḍī narrated this.

His saying: "He disputed (tamārā) with al-Ḥurr ibn Qays" — meaning: they contended and argued. "Al-Ḥurr" is with a ḥā' and a rā'.

In this story there are various kinds of principles, foundations, subsidiary rulings, etiquettes, and important gems. The majority of these have already been noted previously, except for what is apparent from them. Among what has not been previously mentioned is that there is no harm for the scholar and the virtuous man that the one of lesser rank serves him and fulfills his need — and this is not to be considered as taking compensation for teaching knowledge and etiquettes, but rather it is from the chivalrous virtues (murū'āt) of companions and good fellowship. The evidence for this from this story is the carrying of their lunch by his young servant, and the carrying of Moses and al-Khiḍr by the ship's owners without payment, due to their knowledge of al-Khiḍr's righteousness. And God knows best.

Among them also is the encouragement of humility in one's knowledge and otherwise, and that one should not claim to be the most knowledgeable of people, and that when asked about the most knowledgeable of people, one should say: "God knows best."

Among them is the exposition of a great principle of the principles of Islam, namely the obligation of submission (taslīm) to everything that the Sacred Law has brought, even if some of its wisdom is not apparent to the intellects, and most people do not understand it — and perhaps none of them understand it — such as the decree (al-qadar) in the place of the evidence: the killing of the boy and the scuttling of the ship. For their outward forms are forms of wrongdoing, yet they were sound in reality, having clear wisdom, but it is not apparent to creation. So when God Almighty informed them of it, they came to know it. For this reason he said: "And I did not do it of my own accord" {«وما فعلته عن امري»} — meaning: rather, by the command of God Almighty.

---

BOOK: The Virtues of the Companions, may God be pleased with them

The Imām Abū ʿAbd Allāh al-Māzarī said: People have differed concerning the preference (tafḍīl) of some Companions over others. A group said: We do not prefer; rather, we refrain from that. The majority (al-jumhūr) affirmed preference. Then they differed: The People of the Sunnah said: the most excellent of them is Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq. The Khaṭṭābiyyah said: the most excellent is ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb. The Rāwandiyyah said: the most excellent is al-ʿAbbās. The Shīʿah said: ʿAlī. The People of the Sunnah agreed that the most excellent of them is Abū Bakr, then ʿUmar. The majority of them said: then ʿUthmān, then ʿAlī. Some of the People of the Sunnah from Kūfah held the precedence of ʿAlī over ʿUthmān. The sound and well-known view is the precedence of ʿUthmān.

Abū Manṣūr al-Baghdādī said: Our companions are in consensus that the most excellent of them are the four Caliphs in the aforementioned order, then the rest of the ten, then the people of Badr, then the people of Uḥud, then the people of the Pledge of Riḍwān. Among those who have a special merit are the people of the two pledges (ahl al-ʿaqabatayn) from the Anṣār, and likewise the foremost forerunners (al-sābiqūn al-awwalūn) — who, according to Ibn al-Musayyab and a group, are those who prayed toward both qiblahs; according to al-Shaʿbī, the people of the Pledge of Riḍwān; and according to ʿAṭā' and Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb, the people of Badr.

Al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ said: A group among them — including Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr — held that those Companions who died during the lifetime of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, are more excellent than those who remained after him. This absolute statement is neither satisfactory nor acceptable.

The scholars have differed as to whether the aforementioned preference is definitive (qaṭʿī) or not, and whether it pertains to the outward and the inward, or to the outward alone. Among those who affirmed its definitiveness...

chapters.title_en: On the Ranking of the Companions, the Justice of All Parties in the Civil Wars, and the Meaning of Khalīl (Intimate Friendship)
chapters.arabic_text:
أبو الحسن الأشعري قال وهم في الفضل على ترتيبهم في الإمامة وممن قال بأنه

اجتهادي ظني أبو بكر الباقلاني وذكر بن الباقلاني اختلاف العلماء في أن

التفضيل هل هو في الظاهر ام في الظاهر والباطن جميعا وكذلك اختلفوا في

عائشة وخديجة أيتهما أفضل وفي عائشة وفاطمة رضي الله عنهم أجمعين وأما

عثمان رضي الله عنه فخلافته صحيحة بالإجماع وقتل مظلوما وقتلته فسقة لأن

موجبات القتل مضبوطة ولم يجر منه رضي الله عنه ما يقتضيه ولم يشارك في قتله

أحد من الصحابة وإنما قتله همج ورعاع من غوغاء القبائل وسفلة
# 
# الأطراف والأرذال تحزبوا وقصدوه من مصر فعجزت الصحابة الحاضرون عن دفعهم

فحصروه حتى قتلوه رضي الله عنه وأما علي رضي الله عنه فخلافته صحيحة

بالإجماع وكان هو الخليفة في وقته لا خلافة لغيره وأما معاوية رضي الله عنه

فهو من العدول الفضلاء والصحابة النجباء رضي الله عنه وأما الحروب التي جرت

فكانت لكل طائفة شبهة اعتقدت تصويب أنفسها بسببها وكلهم عدول رضي الله عنهم

ومتأولون في حروبهم وغيرها ولم يخرج شئ من ذلك أحدا منهم عن العدالة لأنهم

مجتهدون اختلفوا في مسائل من محل الاجتهاد كما يختلف المجتهدون بعدهم في

مسائل من الدماء وغيرها ولا يلزم من ذلك نقص أحد منهم واعلم أن سبب تلك

الحروب أن القضايا كانت مشتبهة فلشدة اشتباهها اختلف اجتهادهم وصاروا ثلاثة

اقسام قسم ظهر لهم بالاجتهاد أن الحق في هذا الطرف وأن مخالفه باغ فوجب

عليهم نصرته  وقتال الباغي عليه فيما اعتقدوه ففعلوا ذلك ولم يكن يحل لمن

هذه صفته التأخر عن مساعدة امام العدل في قتال البغاة في اعتقاده وقسم عكس

هؤلاء ظهر لهم بالاجتهاد أن الحق في الطرف الآخر فوجب عليهم مساعدته وقتال

الباغي عليه وقسم ثالث اشتبهت عليهم القضية وتحيروا فيها ولم يظهر لهم

ترجيح أحد الطرفين فاعتزلوا الفريقين وكان هذا الاعتزال هو الواجب في حقهم

لأنه لا يحل الإقدام على قتال مسلم حتى يظهر أنه مستحق لذلك ولو ظهر لهؤلاء

رجحان أحد الطرفين وأن الحق معه لما جاز لهم التأخر عن نصرته في قتال

البغاة عليه فكلهم معذورون رضي الله عنهم ولهذا اتفق أهل الحق ومن يعتد به

في الإجماع على قبول شهاداتهم ورواياتهم وكمال عدالتهم رضي الله عنهم

اجمعين

| (باب من فضائل أبي بكر الصديق رضي الله عنه قوله صلى 
# الله عليه وسلم
# [2381] (يا أبا بكر ما ظنك باثنين الله ثالثهما) معناه ثالثهما بالنصر

والمعونة)
# 
# والحفظ والتسديد وهو داخل في قوله تعالى إن الله مع الذين اتقوا والذين

هم محسنون وفيه بيان عظيم توكل النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم حتى في هذا المقام

وفيه فضيلة لأبي بكر رضي الله عنه وهي من أجل مناقبه والفضيلة من أوجه منها

هذا اللفظ ومنها بذله نفسه ومفارقته أهله وماله ورياسته في طاعة الله تعالى

ورسوله وملازمة النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ومعاداة الناس فيه ومنها جعله

نفسه وقاية عنه وغير ذلك قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم
# [2382] (عبد خيره الله بين أن يؤتيه زهرة الدنيا وبين ما عنده فاختار ما

عنده فبكى أبو بكر وبكى وقال فديناك بآبائنا وأمهاتنا) هكذا هو في جميع

النسخ فبكى أبو بكر وبكى معناه بكى كثيرا ثم بكى والمراد بزهرة الدنيا

نعيمها وأعراضها وحدودها وشبهها بزهرة الروض وقوله فديناك دليل لجواز

التفدية وقد سبق بيانه مرات وكان أبو بكر رضي الله عنه علم أن النبي صلى

الله عليه وسلم هو العبد المخير فبكى حزنا على فراقه وانقطاع الوحي وغيره

من الخير  دائما وإنما قال صلى الله عليه وسلم إن عبدا وأبهمه لينظر فهم أهل

المعرفة ونباهة أصحاب الحذق قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (إن أمن الناس علي في

ماله وصحبته أبو بكر) قال العلماء معناه أكثرهم جودا وسماحة لنا بنفسه

وماله وليس هو من المن الذي هو الاعتداد بالصنيعة لأنه أذى مبطل للثواب

ولأن المنة لله ولرسوله صلى الله عليه وسلم في قبول ذلك وفي غيره قوله صلى

الله عليه وسلم (ولو كنت متخذا خليلا لاتخذت أبا بكر خليلا ولكن أخوة

الإسلام) وفي
# [2383] رواية لكن أخي وصاحبي وقد اتخذ الله صاحبكم خليلا قال القاضي قيل

أصل الخلة الافتقار
# 
# والانقطاع فخليل الله المنقطع إليه وقيل لقصره حاجته على الله تعالى وقيل

الخلة الاختصاص وقيل الاصطفاء وسمي إبراهيم خليلا لأنه والى في الله تعالى

وعادى فيه وقيل سمي به لأنه تخلق بخلال حسنة وأخلاق كريمة وخلة الله تعالى

له نصره وجعله إماما لمن بعده وقال بن فورك الخلة صفاء المودة بتخلل

الأسرار وقيل أصلها المحبة ومعناه الإسعاف والإلطاف وقيل الخليل من لا يتسع

قلبه لغير خليله ومعنى الحديث أن حب الله تعالى لم يبق في قلبه موضعا لغيره

قال القاضي وجاء في أحاديث أنه صلى الله عليه وسلم قال ألا وأنا حبيب الله

فاختلف المتكلمون هل المحبة أرفع من الخلة أم الخلة أرفع أم هما سواء فقالت

طائفة هما بمعنى فلا يكون الحبيب إلا خليلا ولا يكون الخليل إلا حبيبا وقيل
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ف ض ل (faḍala)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Increase, surplus, excellence; superiority in merit.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Faḍīlah as a divinely-granted excellence distinguishing rank (martabah) in the Hereafter and in communal estimation.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Used literally (ḥaqīqah) for graded superiority; metaphorically (majāz) for preference in legal judgment (ijtihād).
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional-Responsive Construction (al-sharṭ wa-l-jawāb) — "لو ظهر... لما جاز" (if it had appeared... it would not have been permissible) governs a counterfactual apodosis requiring the lām of answer in the jumlāh.
chapters.translation:
I say: Abū al-Ḥasan al-Ashʿarī (may God have mercy on him) erred in [asserting] that their superiority [i.e., of the Companions] follows their order in the imamate [i.e., the caliphate]. Among those who held that [the determination of superiority] is a matter of ijtihādī conjecture (ijtihādī ẓannī) was Abū Bakr al-Bāqillānī. Ibn al-Bāqillānī mentioned the disagreement of the scholars as to whether the preference [of one Companion over another] is in the outward [apparent merits] only, or in both the outward and the inward [hidden virtues] together. Likewise, they disagreed concerning ʿĀʾishah and Khadījah — which of the two is more excellent — and concerning ʿĀʾishah and Fāṭimah (may God be pleased with them all).

As for ʿUthmān (may God be pleased with him), his caliphate was valid by consensus (ijmāʿ), and he was killed unjustly (maẓlūman). His killers were transgressors (fussāq) because the causes warranting [his] killing were precisely circumscribed, and nothing issued from him (may God be pleased with him) that would necessitate it. None of the Companions participated in his killing; rather, only rabble and riffraff from the dregs of the tribes and the base of the factions and the worthless — partisan mobs — conspired and came against him from Egypt. The Companions present were unable to repel them, so they besieged him until they killed him (may God be pleased with him).

As for ʿAlī (may God be pleased with him), his caliphate was valid by consensus, and he was the caliph in his time — no caliphate belonged to anyone else. As for Muʿāwiyah (may God be pleased with him), he was among the upright and virtuous, and among the noble Companions (may God be pleased with him). As for the wars that occurred [between them], each party had a plausible pretext (shubhah) on account of which they believed themselves to be in the right. All of them were upright (ʿudūl) (may God be pleased with them) and exercised interpretive reasoning (mutaʾawwilūn) in their wars and otherwise. Nothing of that removed any of them from [the status of] justice (ʿadālah), because they were mujtahids who differed over matters falling within the domain of ijtihād — just as the mujtahids after them differed over matters involving bloodshed and otherwise. No deficiency attaches to any of them on account of that.

Know that the cause of those wars was that the issues were ambiguous (mushtabihah). Due to the intensity of their ambiguity, their ijtihād diverged, and they became three categories:
- A category for whom it became evident through ijtihād that the truth lay with this party and that its opponent was an aggressor (bāghī); thus it became obligatory upon them to support [the former] and fight the aggressor against him, according to what they believed. They did so, and it was not lawful for one of this description to hold back from assisting the imam of justice in fighting the aggressors, in his belief.
- A category the reverse of these: it became evident to them through ijtihād that the truth lay with the other party, so it was obligatory upon them to assist him and fight the aggressor against him.
- A third category for whom the issue remained ambiguous and they were perplexed, with no preponderance of either side appearing to them; so they withdrew from both parties. This withdrawal was the obligatory course for them, because it is not lawful to advance upon fighting a Muslim until it becomes evident that he deserves it. Had preponderance of one side appeared to these, and that the truth was with him, it would not have been permissible for them to hold back from assisting him in fighting the aggressors against him.

Thus all of them are excused (maʿdhūrūn) (may God be pleased with them). For this reason, the people of truth and those whose [opinion] counts in consensus have agreed upon accepting their testimonies and their narrations, and upon the completeness of their justice (may God be pleased with them all).

---

| (Chapter: On the Virtues of Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq (may God be pleased with him). His saying (peace and blessings of God be upon him): [2381] "O Abū Bakr, what do you think of two, of whom God is the third?" — Its meaning is: the third of them in aid (naṣr) and assistance (maʿūnah), and in protection (ḥifẓ) and guidance (tasdīd). This falls under His saying (exalted is He): {«إِنَّ اللَّهَ مَعَ الَّذِينَ اتَّقَوْا وَالَّذِينَ هُمْ مُحْسِنُونَ»} [Indeed, God is with those who fear Him and those who are doers of good]. In it is a demonstration of the immense trust (tawakkul) of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), even in such a situation. In it is a virtue for Abū Bakr (may God be pleased with him), and it is among his greatest merits (manāqib). The virtue [here] has several aspects: one is this very utterance; another is his offering of himself, his separation from his family, his wealth, and his position in obedience to God (exalted is He) and His Messenger, his constant companionship of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and his enmity toward people on account of him; and another is his making himself a shield for him. And other [aspects].

His saying (peace and blessings of God be upon him): [2382] "A servant whom God gave the choice between being granted the bloom of this world (zahrat al-dunyā) and what is with Him — and he chose what is with Him." Abū Bakr wept, and then wept again. He said: "May we ransom you with our fathers and mothers." Thus it appears in all copies: "Abū Bakr wept, and wept" — meaning: he wept much, then wept [more]. The intended meaning of "the bloom of this world" (zahrat al-dunyā) is its delight, its adornments, and its pleasures — likened to the bloom of a garden (zahrat al-rawḍ). His saying "may we ransom you" (fadīnāka) is evidence for the permissibility of ransoming (tafdiyah), and its explanation has preceded on multiple occasions. Abū Bakr (may God be pleased with him) knew that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was the servant given the choice, so he wept out of grief at his separation, the cessation of revelation, and [the loss of] other perpetual good. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) only said "a servant" and left it ambiguous in order to test the understanding of the people of knowledge and the acumen of the masters of discernment.

His saying (peace and blessings of God be upon him): "The most generous of people to me in his wealth and his companionship is Abū Bakr." The scholars said: its meaning is the most abundant of them in generosity and liberality toward us with his self and his wealth. It is not [a case of] obligation (mann) in the sense of counting favors as a reproach, for that is a harmful act that voids reward; rather, the obligation (al-minnah) belongs to God and His Messenger (peace and blessings of God be upon him) for accepting that and for other [blessings].

His saying (peace and blessings of God be upon him): "Had I been going to take an intimate friend (khalīl), I would have taken Abū Bakr as an intimate friend — but [it is] the brotherhood of Islam." And in [2383] another narration: "But [he is] my brother and my companion. And God has taken your companion as an intimate friend (khalīl)."

Al-Qāḍī said: It is said that the root of khullah (intimate friendship) is need (iftiqār) and utter dependence (inqiṭāʿ); thus the khalīl of God is the one who cuts off [everything] unto Him. And it is said [it is] because he confines his need to God (exalted is He). And it is said: khullah is special distinction (ikhtiṣāṣ); and it is said: it is selection (iṣṭifāʾ). Ibrāhīm was called khalīl because he befriended for the sake of God (exalted is He) and showed enmity for His sake. And it is said he was so named because he was characterized by excellent traits (khilāl ḥasanah) and noble morals (akhlāq karīmah). And God's khullah toward him was His aiding him and making him an imam for those after him.

Ibn Fūrak said: khullah is the purity of affection through the interpenetration of secrets (taḫallul al-asrār). And it is said its root is love (maḥabbah), and its meaning is gracious response (isʿāf) and kindness (ilṭāf). And it is said: the khalīl is one whose heart does not expand for anyone other than his khalīl. The meaning of the ḥadīth is that love of God (exalted is He) left no place in his heart for another.

Al-Qāḍī said: It has come in ḥadīths that he (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: "Indeed, I am the beloved (ḥabīb) of God." The theologians (mutakallimūn) differed: is love (maḥabbah) higher than khullah, or is khullah higher, or are they equal? A group said: they are synonymous — so the beloved (ḥabīb) is none other than a khalīl, and the khalīl is none other than a ḥabīb. And it was said...

chapters.title_en: The Superiority of the Beloved (al-Ḥabīb) over the Intimate Friend (al-Khalīl), and the Virtues of Abū Bakr and ʿUmar
chapters.arabic_text:
الحبيب أرفع لأنها صفة نبينا صلى الله عليه وسلم وقيل الخليل أرفع وقد ثبتت

خلة نبينا صلى الله عليه وسلم لله تعالى بهذا الحديث ونفى أن يكون له خليل

غيره وأثبت محبته لخديجة وعائشة وأبيها وأسامة وأبيه وفاطمة وابنيها وغيرهم

ومحبة الله تعالى لعبده تمكينه من طاعته وعصمته وتوفيقه وتيسير ألطافه

وهدايته وإفاضة رحمته عليه هذه مباديها وأما غايتها فكشف الحجب عن قلبه حتى

يراه ببصيرته فيكون كما قال في الحديث الصحيح فإذا أحببته كنت سمعه الذي

يسمع به وبصره إلى آخره  هذا كلام القاضي وأما قول أبي هريرة وغيره من

الصحابة رضي الله عنهم سمعت خليلي صلى الله عليه وسلم فلا يخالف هذا لأن

الصحابي يحسن في حقه الانقطاع إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قوله صلى الله

عليه وسلم (لا تبقين في المسجد خوخة إلا خوخة أبي بكر) الخوخة بفتح الخاء

وهي الباب الصغير بين البيتين أو الدارين ونحوه وفيه فضيلة
# 
# وخصيصة ظاهرة لأبي بكر رضي الله عنه وفيه أن المساجد تصان عن تطرق الناس

اليها
#

| 3 - 
# في خوخات ونحوها إلا من أبوابها إلا لحاجة مهمة قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم

(ألا اني أبرأالى كل خل من خله) همابكسر الخاء فأما الأول فكسره متفق عليه

وهو الخل بمعنى الخليل وأما قوله من خله فبكسر الخاء عند جميع الرواة في

جميع النسخ وكذا نقله القاضي عن جميعهم قال والصواب الأوجه فتحها قال

والخلة والخل والخلال والمخاللة والخلالة والخلوة الإخاء والصداقة أي برئت

إليه من صداقته المقتضية المخاللة هذاكلام القاضي والكسر صحيح كما جاءت به

الروايات أي أبرأ إليه من مخالتي إياه وذكر بن الأثير أنه روي بكسر الخاء

وفتحها وأنهما بمعنى الخلة بالضم التي هي الصداقة قوله
# [2384] (بعثه على جيش ذات السلاسل) هو بفتح السين الأولى وكسر الثانية

وهو ماء لبني حذام بناحية الشام ومنهم من قال هو بضم السين الاولى وكذا

ذكره بن الأثير في نهاية الغريب وأظنه استنبطه من كلام الجوهري في الصحاح

ولا دلالة فيه والمشهور والمعروف فتحها وكانت هذه الغزوة في جمادى الأخرى

سنة ثمان من الهجرة وكانت مؤتة قبلها في جمادى الأولى من سنة ثمان أيضا قال

الحافظ أبو القاسم بن عساكر كانت ذات السلاسل بعد مؤتة فيما ذكره اهل

المغازي الا بن إسحاق فقال قبلها قوله (أي الناس أحب إليك قال عائشة قلت من

الرجال قال أبوها قلت ثم من قال عمر فعد رجالا) هذا تصريح بعظيم فضائل أبي

بكر وعمر وعائشة رضي الله عنهم وفيه دلالة بينة لأهل السنة في تفضيل أبي

بكر ثم  عمر على جميع الصحابة
# 
# قوله
# [2385] (سئلت عائشة من كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم مستخلفا لو

استخلفه قالت أبو بكر فقيل لها ثم من بعد أبي بكر قالت عمر ثم قيل لها من

بعد عمر قالت أبو عبيدة بن الجراح ثم انتهت إلى هذا) يعني وقفت على أبي

عبيدة هذا دليل لأهل السنة في تقديم أبي بكر ثم عمر للخلافة مع إجماع

الصحابة وفيه دلالة لأهل السنة أن خلافة أبي بكر ليست بنص من النبي صلى

الله عليه وسلم على خلافته صريحا بل أجمعت الصحابة على عقد الخلافة له

وتقديمه لفضيلته ولوكان هناك نص عليه أو على غيره لم تقع المنازعة من

الأنصار وغيرهم أولا ولذكر حافظ النص ما معه ولرجعوا إليه لكن تنازعوا أولا

ولم يكن هناك نص ثم اتفقوا على أبي بكر واستقر الأمر
# 
# وأما ما تدعيه الشيعة من النص على علي والوصية إليه فباطل لا أصل له

باتفاق المسلمين والاتفاق على بطلان دعواهم من زمن علي وأول من كذبهم علي

رضي الله عنه بقوله ما عندنا إلا ما في هذه الصحيفة الحديث ولو كان عنده نص

لذكره ولم ينقل أنه ذكره في يوم من الأيام ولا أن أحدا ذكره له والله أعلم
# [2386] وأما قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم في الحديث الذي بعد هذا للمرأة حين

قالت يا رسول الله أرأيت إن جئت فلم أجدك قال فإن لم تجديني فأتي أبا بكر

فليس فيه نص على خلافته وأمر بها بل هو إخبار بالغيب الذي أعلمه الله تعالى

به والله أعلم قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم لعائشة
# [2387] (ادعي لي أباك أبا بكر وأخاك حتى أكتب كتابا فإني أخاف أن يتمنى

متمن ويقول قائل انا ولا يأبى الله والمؤمنون إلا أبا بكر) هكذا هو في بعض

النسخ المعتمدة انا ولا بتخفيف اما ولا أي يقول أنا أحق وليس كما يقول بل

يأبى الله والمؤمنون إلا أبا بكر وفي بعضها أنا أولى أي أنا أحق بالخلافة

قال القاضي هذه الرواية  أجودها ورواه بعضهم أنا ولي بتخفيف النون وكسر

اللام أي أنا أحق والخلافة لي وعن بعضهم أنا ولاه أي أنا الذي ولاه النبي

صلى الله عليه وسلم وبعضهم أنى ولاه بتشديد النون أي كيف ولاه في هذا

الحديث دلالة ظاهرة لفضل أبي بكر الصديق رضي الله عنه وإخبار منه صلى الله

عليه وسلم بما سيقع في المستقبل بعد وفاته وأن المسلمين يأبون عقد الخلافة

لغيره وفيه إشارة إلى أنه سيقع نزاع ووقع كل ذلك وأما طلبه لأخيها مع أبي

بكر فالمراد أنه يكتب الكتاب ووقع في رواية البخاري لقد هممت أن أوجه إلى
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ح-ب-ب (ḥ-b-b)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning of love, affection, and attachment; al-ḥabīb is the one who is loved, denoting a state of intense and continuous affection.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological terms, maḥabbah of Allah for His servant signifies His willing of good for him, His protection (ʿiṣmah), and His granting of success (tawfīq)—not a physical or emotional attribute.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage denotes human affection; metaphorical (majāz) usage for Allah denotes His beneficent will and action, as love cannot be attributed to Him in a corporeal sense.
- Root: خ-ل-ل (kh-l-l)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: The root signifies penetration, interstice, or a gap; khullah (friendship) is so named because it penetrates the heart deeply, leaving no room for anything else.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Khullah is the highest degree of intimate friendship, exclusive and all-encompassing, as in the case of Ibrāhīm (ʿalayhi al-salām) being taken as khalīl.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): The term is used literally for human intimacy; for Allah, it denotes His exclusive selection and honor of a servant, without any implication of need or reciprocity.
- Sībawayh Rule: Rule of Exception and Restriction (al-Istithnāʾ wa al-Takhṣīṣ) — The phrase "lā tabqiyanna... illā khūkhah" employs an exception particle to restrict the general negation, indicating a specific exclusion that carries legal and honorific weight.
chapters.translation:
I say: The term "beloved" (al-ḥabīb) is more elevated because it is an attribute of our Prophet ﷺ. And it was said that "intimate friend" (al-khalīl) is more elevated. The intimate friendship (khullah) of our Prophet ﷺ for Allah the Exalted has been established by this hadith, and it negated that he has any intimate friend other than Him. It also affirmed his love for Khadījah, ʿĀʾishah, her father, Usāmah, his father, Fāṭimah, her two sons, and others.

The love of Allah the Exalted for His servant is His enabling him to obey Him, His protecting him (ʿiṣmah), His granting him success (tawfīq), His facilitating His graces (alṭāf), His guidance, and His pouring forth of His mercy upon him. These are its beginnings.
