As for its ultimate end, it is the unveiling of the veils from his heart until he sees Him with his inner vision (baṣīrah), such that he becomes as stated in the authentic hadith: {«فإذا أحببته كنت سمعه الذي يسمع به وبصره»} ("When I love him, I become his hearing with which he hears, and his sight...") to the end of the hadith. This is the statement of al-Qāḍī.

As for the statement of Abū Hurayrah and others among the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, "I heard my intimate friend (khalīlī) ﷺ," this does not contradict the above, because it is fitting for a Companion to attach himself exclusively (inqiṭāʿ) to the Prophet ﷺ.

His statement ﷺ: (لا تبقين في المسجد خوخة إلا خوخة أبي بكر) — "Let there not remain in the mosque any small door (khūkhah) except the small door of Abū Bakr." The word khūkhah is with fatḥah on the khāʾ, and it is the small door between two houses or two abodes, or similar. In this hadith there is a virtue and a manifest distinction for Abū Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him. And in it [there is the ruling] that mosques are to be protected from people passing through them via small doors and the like, except through their main entrances, unless there is an important need.

His statement ﷺ: (ألا إني أبرأ إلى كل خل من خله) — "Indeed, I disavow myself to every intimate friend from his friendship." Both occurrences are with kasrah on the khāʾ. As for the first, its kasrah is agreed upon, and it is al-khull meaning al-khalīl (intimate friend). As for his statement "min khillihi," it is with kasrah on the khāʾ according to all narrators in all copies, and al-Qāḍī likewise transmitted this from all of them. He said: The correct and most appropriate [reading] is fatḥah on it. He said: And al-khullah, al-khill, al-khilāl, al-mukhāllah, al-khilālah, and al-khilwah all mean brotherhood and friendship. That is: "I disavow myself to him from my friendship with him that necessitates intimate association." This is the statement of al-Qāḍī. And the kasrah is correct as the narrations have conveyed it, meaning: "I disavow myself to him from my intimate association with him." Ibn al-Athīr mentioned that it was narrated with kasrah and fatḥah on the khāʾ, and that both mean al-khullah with ḍammah, which is friendship.

His statement [2384]: (بعثه على جيش ذات السلاسل) — "He sent him over the army of Dhāt al-Salāsil." This is with fatḥah on the first sīn and kasrah on the second. It is a watering place belonging to the tribe of Judhām in the region of al-Shām. Some said it is with ḍammah on the first sīn, and Ibn al-Athīr mentioned this in al-Nihāyah fī Gharīb al-Ḥadīth. I think he derived it from the statement of al-Jawharī in al-Ṣiḥāḥ, but there is no indication of it therein. The well-known and recognized [reading] is fatḥah on it. This expedition occurred in Jumādā al-Ākhirah of the eighth year of the Hijrah, and the expedition of Muʾtah preceded it in Jumādā al-Ūlā of the eighth year as well. Al-Ḥāfiẓ Abū al-Qāsim ibn ʿAsākir said: Dhāt al-Salāsil was after Muʾtah, according to what the scholars of military expeditions (ahl al-Maghāzī) mentioned, except for Ibn Isḥāq, who said it was before it.

His statement: (أي الناس أحب إليك قال عائشة قلت من الرجال قال أبوها قلت ثم من قال عمر فعد رجالا) — "Which people are most beloved to you?" He said: "ʿĀʾishah." I said: "Among the men?" He said: "Her father." I said: "Then who?" He said: "ʿUmar." Then he counted [several] men. This is an explicit declaration of the immense virtues of Abū Bakr, ʿUmar, and ʿĀʾishah, may Allah be pleased with them all. And in it there is clear evidence for the people of the Sunnah (Ahl al-Sunnah) regarding the preference (tafḍīl) of Abū Bakr, then ʿUmar, over all the Companions.

His statement [2385]: (سئلت عائشة من كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم مستخلفا لو استخلفه قالت أبو بكر فقيل لها ثم من بعد أبي بكر قالت عمر ثم قيل لها من بعد عمر قالت أبو عبيدة بن الجراح ثم انتهت إلى هذا) — "ʿĀʾishah was asked: 'Whom would the Messenger of Allah ﷺ have appointed as his successor (mustakhlif) had he appointed one?' She said: 'Abū Bakr.' It was said to her: 'Then who after Abū Bakr?' She said: 'ʿUmar.' Then it was said to her: 'Who after ʿUmar?' She said: 'Abū ʿUbaydah ibn al-Jarrāḥ.' Then she stopped at this." Meaning: she halted at Abū ʿUbaydah. This is evidence for the people of the Sunnah regarding the precedence of Abū Bakr, then ʿUmar, for the caliphate, along with the consensus (ijmāʿ) of the Companions. And in it there is evidence for the people of the Sunnah that the caliphate of Abū Bakr was not by an explicit text (naṣṣ) from the Prophet ﷺ designating his succession, but rather the Companions reached consensus on contracting the caliphate for him and giving him precedence due to his virtue. Had there been a text concerning him or another, the dispute from the Anṣār and others would not have occurred initially, and the one who preserved the text would have mentioned what he had, and they would have referred to it. But they disputed initially, and there was no text; then they agreed upon Abū Bakr, and the matter was settled.

As for what the Shīʿah claim of a text (naṣṣ) upon ʿAlī and the bequest (waṣiyyah) to him, it is false and has no basis, by the agreement of the Muslims. And the agreement on the falsity of their claim has been [established] since the time of ʿAlī. The first to declare them liars was ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with him, by his statement: "We have nothing with us except what is in this scroll" — the hadith. Had he possessed a text, he would have mentioned it, and it has not been transmitted that he mentioned it on any day, nor that anyone mentioned it to him. And Allah knows best.

[2386] As for his statement ﷺ in the hadith that follows this one, to the woman when she said: "O Messenger of Allah, what do you think if I come and do not find you?" He said: "If you do not find me, then go to Abū Bakr." There is no text in this concerning his caliphate, nor a command to it. Rather, it is an informing of the unseen (ghayb) which Allah the Exalted had made known to him. And Allah knows best.

His statement ﷺ to ʿĀʾishah [2387]: (ادعي لي أباك أبا بكر وأخاك حتى أكتب كتابا فإني أخاف أن يتمنى متمن ويقول قائل أنا ولا يأبى الله والمؤمنون إلا أبا بكر) — "Call for me your father Abū Bakr and your brother, so that I may write a document, for I fear that a wisher may wish and a speaker may say: 'I am [more deserving],' but Allah and the believers refuse except Abū Bakr." This is how it appears in some reliable copies: "anā wa lā" with takhfīf of the mīm and the lām, meaning: he says, "I am more deserving," but it is not as he says; rather, Allah and the believers refuse except Abū Bakr. And in some copies: "anā awlā" meaning "I am more deserving of the caliphate." Al-Qāḍī said: This narration is the best of them. And some narrated it as "anā walī" with takhfīf of the nūn and kasrah of the lām, meaning: "I am more deserving, and the caliphate is mine." And from some: "anā walāh" meaning "I am the one whom the Prophet ﷺ appointed." And some: "annā wallāh" with tashdīd of the nūn, meaning: "How could he appoint him?" In this hadith there is a manifest indication of the virtue of Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq, may Allah be pleased with him, and an informing from him ﷺ of what would occur in the future after his death, and that the Muslims would refuse the contracting of the caliphate for anyone other than him. And in it there is an indication that a dispute would occur, and all of that did occur. As for his request for her brother along with Abū Bakr, the intent is that he would write the document. And it occurs in the narration of al-Bukhārī: "I was about to send to..."

chapters.title_en: Section 874 — On the Visions of the Prophet (ﷺ) Concerning Abū Bakr and ʿUmar, and the Interpretation of Dreams
chapters.arabic_text:
أبي بكر وابنه وأعهد ولبعض رواة البخاري وآتيه بألف ممدودة ومثناة فوق

ومثناة تحت من الإتيان قال القاضي وصوبه بعضهم وليس كما صوب بل الصواب ابنه

بالباء الموحدة والنون وهو أخو عائشة وتوضحه رواية
# 
# مسلم أخاك ولأن إتيان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان متعذرا أو متعسرا وقد

عجز عن حضور الجماعة واستخلف الصديق ليصلي بالناس واستأذن أزواجه أن يمرض

في بيت عائشة والله أعلم قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم
# [1028] (من أصبح منكم اليوم صائما) قال أبو بكر أنا إلى قوله صلى الله

عليه وسلم ما اجتمعن في امرئ إلا دخل الجنة قال القاضي معناه دخل الجنة بلا

محاسبة ولا مجازاة على قبيح الأعمال وإلا فمجرد الإيمان يقتضي دخول الجنة

بفضل الله تعالى قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم في كلام البقرة وكلام الذئب وتعجب

الناس من ذلك
# [2388] (فإني أومن به وأبو بكر وعمر وما هما) ثم قال العلماء إنما قال

ذلك ثقة بهما لعلمه بصدق إيمانهما وقوة يقينهما وكمال معرفتهما لعظيم سلطان

الله وكمال قدرته ففيه فضيلة ظاهرة لأبي بكر وعمر رضي الله عنهما وفيه جواز

كرامات الأولياء وخرق العوائد وهو مذهب أهل الحق وسبقت المسألة قوله (قال

الذئب من لها يوم السبع يوم لا راعي لها غيري) روي السبع بضم الباء

وإسكانها الأكثرون على الضم قال
# 
# القاضي الرواية بالضم وقال بعض أهل اللغة هي ساكنة وجعله  اسما للموضع

الذي عنده المحشر يوم القيامة أي من لها يوم القيامة وأنكر بعض أهل اللغة

أن يكون هذا اسما ليوم القيامة وقال بعض أهل اللغة يقال سبعت الأسد إذا

دعوته فالمعنى على هذا من لها يوم الفزع ويوم القيامة يوم الفزع ويحتمل أن

يكون المراد من لها يوم الإهمال من أسبعت الرجل أهملته وقال بعضهم يوم

السبع بالإسكان عيد كان لهم في الجاهلية يشتغلون فيه بلعبهم فيأكل الذئب

غنمهم وقال الداودي يوم السبع أي يوم يطردك عنها السبع وبقيت أنا لها

لاراعي لها غيري لفرارك منه فأفعل فيها ما اشاء هذا كلام القاضي وقال بن

الأعرابي هو بالإسكان أي يوم القيامة أو يوم الذعر وأنكر عليه آخرون هذا

لقوله يوم لا راعي لها غيري ويوم القيامة لا يكون الذئب راعيها ولا له بها

تعلق والأصح ما قاله آخرون وسبقت الإشارة إليه من أنها
# 
# عند الفتن حين تتركها الناس هملا لا راعي لها نهبة للسباع فجعل السبع لها

راعيا أي منفردا بها وتكون بضم الباء والله أعلم

| (باب من فضائل عمر رضي الله عنه قوله
# [2389] (فتكنفه الناس)
# أي أحاطوا به والسرير هنا النعش قوله (فلم يرعني إلا برجل) هو بفتح الياء

وضم الراء ومعناه لم يفجأني إلا ذلك وقوله برجل هكذا هو في النسخ برجل

بالباء أي لم يفجأني الأمر أو الحال إلا برجل وفي هذا الحديث فضيلة أبي بكر

وعمر وشهادة علي لهما وحسن ثنائه عليهما وصدق ما كان يظنه بعمر قبل وفاته

رضي الله عنهم أجمعين قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم)
#

| 9 - 
# في رؤيا المنام
# [2390] (ومر عمر وعليه قميص يجره قالوا ما أولت ذلك يا رسول الله قال

الدين) وفي الرواية الأخرى
# [2391] رأيت قدحا أتيت به فيه لبن فشربت منه حتى إني لأرى الري يخرج من

أظفاري ثم أعطيت فضلي عمر بن الخطاب قالوا فما أولت ذلك يا رسول الله قال

العلم قال أهل العبارة القميص في النوم معناه الدين وجره يدل على بقاء

آثاره الجميلة وسننه الحسنة  في المسلمين بعد وفاته ليقتدى به وأما تفسير

اللبن بالعلم فلاشتراكهما في كثرة النفع وفي أنهما سبب الصلاح فاللبن غذاء

الأطفال وسبب صلاحهم وقوت للأبدان بعد ذلك والعلم سبب لصلاح الآخرة والدنيا

قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم
# [2392] (رأيتني على قليب عليها دلو فنزعت منها ما شاء الله ثم اخذها بن

أبي قحافة فنزع بها ذنوبا أو ذنوبين وفي نزعه والله يغفر له ضعف ثم استحالت

غربا فاخذها بن الخطاب فلم أر عبقريا من الناس ينزع نزع عمر بن الخطاب حتى

ضرب الناس بعطن) أما القليب فهي البئر غير المطوية والدلو يذكر ويؤنث

والذنوب بفتح الذال الدلو المملوءة والغرب بفتح الغين المعجمة وإسكان الراء

وهي الدلو العظيمة والنزع الاستقاء
# 
# والضعف بضم الضاد وفتحها لغتان مشهورتان الضم أفصح ومعنى استحالت صارت

وتحولت
# 
# من الصغر إلى الكبر وأما العبقري فهو السيد وقيل الذي ليس فوقه شئ ومعنى

ضرب الناس بعطن أي أرووا إبلهم ثم آووها إلى عطنها وهو الموضع الذي تساق

إليه بعد السقي لتستريح قال العلماء هذا المنام مثال واضح لما جرى لأبي بكر

وعمر رضي الله عنهما في خلافتهما وحسن سيرتهما وظهور آثارهما وانتفاع الناس

بهما وكل ذلك مأخوذ من النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ومن بركته وآثار صحبته

فكان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم هو صاحب الأمر فقام به أكمل قيام وقرر قواعد

الإسلام ومهد أموره وأوضح أصوله وفروعه ودخل الناس في دين الله أفواجا

وأنزل الله تعالى اليوم اكملت لكم دينكم ثم توفي صلى الله عليه وسلم فخلفه

أبو بكر رضي الله عنه سنتين وأشهرا وهو المراد بقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ق-ل-ب (q-l-b)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning of turning, overturning, or inversion; a well (qalīb) is so named for the inversion of its earth in digging.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In dream interpretation (taʿbīr), the well symbolizes the seat of authority and governance, as it is the source from which water—sustenance and knowledge—is drawn.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) refers to the physical well; metaphorical (majāz) extends to the caliphate as the source from which the community draws its guidance.
- Sībawayh Rule: Rule of ʿAṭf al-Bayān (Appositional Clarification) — The phrase "أخو عائشة" (brother of ʿĀʾishah) functions as an explicative appositive clarifying the identity of "ابنه" (his son), removing ambiguity in the reading.
chapters.translation:
I say: The correct reading is "ibnihi" (his son) with an unvowelled bāʾ (ب) and a nūn (ن) — and he is the brother of ʿĀʾishah. This is clarified by the narration of Muslim: "your brother." For the coming (ityān) of the Prophet (ﷺ) was either impossible or extremely difficult, as he was unable to attend the congregational prayer and appointed al-Ṣiddīq to lead the people in prayer, and he sought permission from his wives to be nursed during his illness in the house of ʿĀʾishah. And Allāh knows best.

His saying (ﷺ): [1028] "Who among you has fasted today?" Abū Bakr said: "I have." — up to his saying (ﷺ): "These have not gathered in a man except that he enters Paradise." Al-Qāḍī said: Its meaning is that he enters Paradise without reckoning (ḥisāb) and without requital for evil deeds. Otherwise, mere faith necessitates entry into Paradise by the grace of Allāh the Exalted.

His saying (ﷺ) regarding the speech of the cow and the speech of the wolf, and the people's amazement at that: [2388] "For I believe in it — I and Abū Bakr and ʿUmar, though they were not present." Then the scholars said: He only said this out of confidence in them, due to his knowledge of the truthfulness of their faith, the strength of their certainty (yaqīn), and the perfection of their knowledge of the magnificent dominion of Allāh and the perfection of His power. In this is a manifest virtue for Abū Bakr and ʿUmar (may Allāh be pleased with them both), and in it is the permissibility of the miracles of the saints (karāmāt al-awliyāʾ) and the breaking of customary norms (kharq al-ʿawāʾid) — and this is the doctrine of the people of truth (ahl al-ḥaqq). This matter has been discussed previously.

His saying: "The wolf said: Who will be for them on the Day of the Sabʿ (al-sabuʿ) — the day when there is no shepherd for them other than me?" It is narrated "al-sabuʿ" with ḍammah on the bāʾ and with sukūn; the majority favor ḍammah. Al-Qāḍī said: The narration is with ḍammah. Some linguists said it is with sukūn, making it a noun for the place where the gathering (al-maḥshar) will occur on the Day of Resurrection — i.e., "Who will be for them on the Day of Resurrection?" Some linguists rejected that this is a name for the Day of Resurrection. Others said: One says "sabaʿtu al-asad" (I called the lion) — so the meaning would be: "Who will be for them on the Day of Terror (yawm al-fazaʿ)?" And the Day of Resurrection is the Day of Terror. It is also possible that the intended meaning is: "Who will be for them on the Day of Neglect?" — from "asbaʿtu al-rajul" (I neglected him). Some said: "Yawm al-sabʿ" with sukūn was a festival they had in the pre-Islamic period (Jāhiliyyah) in which they occupied themselves with their games, so the wolf would eat their sheep. Al-Dāwūdī said: "Yawm al-sabʿ" means the day when the beast of prey drives you away from them, and I remain for them — "there is no shepherd for them other than me" — because of your fleeing from it, so I do with them what I wish. This is the speech of al-Qāḍī.

Ibn al-Aʿrābī said: It is with sukūn, meaning the Day of Resurrection or the Day of Terror. Others rejected this, due to his saying "the day when there is no shepherd for them other than me" — for on the Day of Resurrection, the wolf would not be its shepherd, nor would it have any connection to them. The most correct is what the latter group said, and the indication has been previously mentioned — that this occurs during tribulations (fitan) when people abandon them neglected, with no shepherd, as prey for beasts of prey. Thus the beast of prey is made its shepherd, i.e., alone with it. And it is with ḍammah on the bāʾ. And Allāh knows best.

| Chapter: On the Virtues of ʿUmar (may Allāh be pleased with him)

His saying: [2389] "Then the people encompassed him (fatakanafahu al-nās)" — i.e., they surrounded him. And "the bier (al-sarīr)" here means the funeral bier (al-naʿsh).

His saying: "Then nothing startled me (fa-lam yarʿanī) except a man" — it is with fatḥah on the yāʾ and ḍammah on the rāʾ, meaning: nothing suddenly confronted me except that. And his saying "except a man (bi-rajul)" — thus it appears in the manuscripts with a bāʾ, i.e., nothing suddenly confronted me — neither an affair nor a situation — except a man.

In this ḥadīth is a virtue for Abū Bakr and ʿUmar, and ʿAlī's testimony for them, his excellent praise of them, and the truthfulness of what he had thought of ʿUmar before his death. May Allāh be pleased with them all.

His saying (ﷺ):

| 9 — Chapter on the Vision in Sleep (Ruʾyā al-Manām)

[2390] "And ʿUmar passed by, wearing a garment (qamīṣ) that he was dragging." They said: "How did you interpret that, O Messenger of Allāh?" He said: "The religion (al-dīn)."

In the other narration: [2391] "I saw a cup (qadaḥ) brought to me containing milk, and I drank from it until I saw the satiation (al-riyy) coming out from my fingernails. Then I gave my excess to ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb." They said: "How did you interpret that, O Messenger of Allāh?" He said: "Knowledge (al-ʿilm)."

The scholars of dream interpretation (ahl al-ʿibārah) said: The garment (qamīṣ) in a dream signifies the religion. His dragging it indicates the endurance of his beautiful traces and his excellent practices (sunan) among the Muslims after his death, so that they may be followed. As for the interpretation of milk as knowledge, it is due to their shared abundance of benefit and their being a cause of righteousness — for milk is the nourishment of infants and the cause of their well-being, and a strength for bodies thereafter; and knowledge is the cause of well-being in the Hereafter and this world.

His saying (ﷺ): [2392] "I saw myself at a well (qalīb) upon which there was a bucket (dalw). I drew from it as much as Allāh willed. Then the son of Abū Qaḥāfah took it and drew with it one or two full buckets (dhanūb), and in his drawing — and Allāh forgives him — there was some weakness (ḍaʿf). Then it turned into a large bucket (gharb), and the son of al-Khaṭṭāb took it, and I have not seen a giant (ʿabqarī) among people drawing water like the drawing of ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, until the people watered their camels and brought them to their resting place (ʿaṭan)."

As for "al-qalīb" — it is the well that is not lined with stone. "Al-dalw" (bucket) is both masculine and feminine. "Al-dhanūb" (with fatḥah on the dhāl) is the filled bucket. "Al-gharb" (with fatḥah on the ghayn and sukūn on the rāʾ) is the great bucket. "Al-nazʿ" is drawing water. "Al-ḍaʿf" — with ḍammah on the ḍād and with fatḥah — are two well-known variant readings; the ḍammah is more eloquent. The meaning of "istaḥālat" is: it became and transformed from smallness to greatness.

As for "al-ʿabqarī" — it is the master (al-sayyid); and it is said: the one above whom there is nothing. The meaning of "ḍaraba al-nās bi-ʿaṭan" is: they watered their camels until satisfied, then brought them to their resting place (ʿaṭan) — which is the place to which they are driven after watering to rest.

The scholars said: This vision is a clear example (mathal) of what transpired with Abū Bakr and ʿUmar (may Allāh be pleased with them both) in their caliphates, their excellent conduct, the manifestation of their traces, and the people's benefit from them. All of that was derived from the Prophet (ﷺ), from his blessing, and from the traces of his companionship. For the Prophet (ﷺ) was the master of the affair — he undertook it with the most complete undertaking, established the foundations of Islam, ordered its affairs, clarified its principles (uṣūl) and branches (furūʿ), and the people entered into the religion of Allāh in droves. And Allāh the Exalted revealed: {«الْيَوْمَ أَكْمَلْتُ لَكُمْ دِينَكُمْ»} (This day I have perfected for you your religion) [Al-Māʾidah 5:3]. Then he (ﷺ) passed away, and Abū Bakr succeeded him for two years and some months — and this is what is meant by his saying (ﷺ)...

chapters.title_en: The Commentary on the Prophetic Vision of the Well and the Succession of Abu Bakr and Umar (Section 875)
chapters.arabic_text:
ذنوبا أو ذنوبين وهذا شك من الراوي والمراد ذنوبان كما صرح به في الرواية

الأخرى وحصل في خلافته قتال أهل الردة وقطع دابرهم واتساع الإسلام ثم توفي

فخلفه عمر رضي الله عنه فاتسع الإسلام في زمنه وتقرر لهم من احكامه مالم

يقع مثله فعبر بالقليب عن أمر المسلمين لما فيها من الماء الذي به حياتهم

وصلاحهم وشبه  أميرهم بالمستقي لهم وسقيه هو قيامه بمصالحهم وتدبير أمورهم

وأما قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم في أبي بكر رضي الله عنه وفي نزعه ضعف فليس

فيه حط من فضيلة أبي بكر ولا إثبات فضيلة لعمر عليه وإنما هو إخبار عن مدة

ولايتهما وكثرة انتفاع الناس في ولاية عمر لطولها ولاتساع الإسلام وبلاده

والأموال وغيرها من الغنائم والفتوحات ومصر الأمصار ودون الدواوين وأما

قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم والله يغفر له فليس فيه تنقيص له ولا إشارة إلى

ذنب وإنما هي كلمة كان المسلمون يدعمون بها كلامهم ونعمت الدعامة وقد سبق

في الحديث في صحيح مسلم أنها كلمة كان المسلمون يقولونها افعل كذا والله

يغفر لك قال العلماء وفي كل هذا إعلام بخلافة أبي بكر وعمر وصحة ولايتهما

وبيان صفتها وانتفاع المسلمين بها قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (فجاءني أبو بكر

فأخذ الدلو من يدي ليروحني) قال العلماء
# 
# فيه إشارة إلى نيابة أبي بكر عنه وخلافته بعده وراحته صلى الله عليه وسلم

بوفاته من نصب الدنيا ومشاقها كما قال صلى الله عليه وسلم مستريح ومستراح

منه الحديث والدنيا سجن المؤمن ولا كرب على ابيك بعداليوم قوله صلى الله

عليه وسلم
# [2393] (فلم أر عبقريا من الناس يفري فريه) أما يفري فبفتح الياء وإسكان

الفاء وكسر الراء وأما فريه فروي بوجهين أحدهما فريه بإسكان الراء وتخفيف

الياء والثانية كسر الراء وتشديد الياء وهما لغتان صحيحتان وأنكر الخليل

التشديد وقال هو غلط اتفقوا على أن معناه لم أر سيدا يعمل عمله ويقطع قطعه

وأصل الفري بالإسكان القطع يقال فريت الشئ أفريه فريا قطعته للاصلاح فهو

مفري وفري وأفريته إذا شققته على جهة الإفساد وتقول العرب تركته يفري الفري

إذا عمل العمل فاجاده ومنه حديث حسان لأفرينهم فري الأديم أي أقطعهم

بالهجاء كما يقطع الأديم قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (حتى ضرب الناس بعطن) سبق

تفسيره قال القاضي ظاهره أنه عائد إلى خلافة عمر خاصة وقيل يعود إلى خلافة

أبي بكر وعمر جميعا لأن بنظرهما  وتدبيرهما وقيامهما بمصالح المسلمين تم هذا

الأمر وضرب الناس بعطن لأن أبا بكر قمع أهل الردة وجمع شمل المسلمين وألفهم

وابتدأ الفتوح ومهد الأمور وتمت ثمرات ذلك وتكاملت في زمن عمر بن الخطاب

رضي الله عنهما قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (كأني أنزع بدلو بكرة) هي بإسكان
# 
# الكاف وفتحها قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (حتى روى الناس) هوبكسر الواو

والمخففة
# 
# أي أخذوا كفايتهم قوله
# [2396] (عن صالح عن بن شهاب قال أخبرني عبد الحميد بن عبد الرحمن بن

سيدان محمد بن سعد أبي وقاص أخبره أن أباه سعدا قال استاذن عمر) هذاالحديث

اجتمع فيه أربعة تابعيون يروي بعضهم عن بعض وهم صالح وبن شهاب وعبد الحميد

ومحمد وقد رأى عبد الحميد بن عباس
# [2396]
# [2397] قوله (وعنده نساء من قريش يكلمنه ويستكثرنه عالية أصواتهن) قال

العلماء معنى يستكثرنه يطلبن كثيرا من كلامه وجوابه بحوائجهن وفتاويهن

وقوله عالية أصواتهن قال القاضي يحتمل أن هذا قبل النهي عن رفع الصوت فوق

صوته صلى الله عليه وسلم ويحتمل أن علو أصواتهن إنما كان باجتماعها لا أن

كلام كل واحدة
# 
# بانفرادها أعلى من صوته صلى الله عليه وسلم قوله (قلن انت أغلظ وأفظ من

رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم) الفظ والغليظ بمعنى وهو عبارة عن شدة الخلق

وخشونة الجانب قال العلماء وليست لفظة أفعل هنا للمفاضلة بل هي بمعنى فظ

غليظ قال القاضي وقد يصح حملها على المفاضلة وأن القدر الذي منها في النبي

صلى الله عليه وسلم هو ما كان من إغلاظه على الكافرين والمنافقين كما قال

تعالى جاهد الكفار والمنافقين واغلظ عليهم وكان يغضب ويغلظ عند انتهاك

حرمات الله تعالى والله أعلم وفي هذا الحديث فضل لين الجانب والحلم والرفق

مالم يفوت مقصودا شرعيا قال الله تعالى واخفض جناحك للمؤمنين وقال تعالى

ولو كنت فظا غليظ القلب لانفضوا من حولك وقال تعالى بالمؤمنين رؤف رحيم

قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (والذي نفسي بيده ما لقيك الشيطان قط سالكا فجا

إلا سلك فجا غير فجك)  الفج الطريق الواسع ويطلق أيضا على المكان المنخرق

بين الجبلين وهذا الحديث محمول على ظاهره أن الشيطان متى رأى عمر سالكا فجا

هرب هيبة من عمر وفارق ذلك الفج وذهب في فج آخر لشدة خوفه من بأس عمر أن

يفعل فيه شيئا قال القاضي ويحتمل أنه ضرب مثلا لبعد الشيطان وإغوائه منه

وأن عمر في جميع أموره سالك
# 
# طريق السداد خلاف ما يأمر به الشيطان والصحيح الاول قوله
# [2398] (عن بن وهب عن إبراهيم بن سعد عن أبيه عن أبي سلمة عن عائشة عن
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ق-ل-ب (q-l-b)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning is "turning/inverting" a thing; al-qalīb (القليب) is the well before its lining is built, or the well itself, from the turning over of its earth in digging.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In prophetic discourse, the well (qalīb) symbolizes the source of communal life and sustenance; its water is the means of survival (ḥayāt) and rectitude (ṣalāḥ) for the people.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Used here as a ḥaqīqah (literal) metaphor for the polity of the Muslims—the well is the state, the water is its life-giving resources, and the drawer is the caliph who administers them.
- Sībawayh Rule: Rule of ʿAṭf al-Bayān (Appositional Clarification) — The phrase "ذنوبا أو ذنوبين" involves a doubt (shakk) from the narrator, resolved by apposition to the explicit "ذنوبان" in the other narration, requiring the dual to be understood as the intended referent.
chapters.translation:
I say: The Prophet's words "sins (dhanūban) or two sins (dhanūbayn)" contain a doubt from the narrator, and the intended meaning is "two sins," as is made explicit in the other narration. During his caliphate, the fighting against the people of apostasy (ahl al-riddah) occurred, and their traces were cut off, and Islam expanded. Then he (Abu Bakr) died, and Umar—may Allah be pleased with him—succeeded him, and Islam expanded in his time, and there were established for the people from its rulings what had never occurred like it before. Thus, the Prophet expressed the affair of the Muslims through the "well" (qalīb) because of the water it contains, through which is their life and their rectitude. He likened their leader to the one who draws water for them, and his drawing (saqy) is his undertaking of their interests and the management of their affairs.

As for the Prophet's—peace and blessings be upon him—statement concerning Abu Bakr—may Allah be pleased with him—"and in his drawing there was weakness," this contains no diminution of Abu Bakr's virtue, nor does it establish any superiority for Umar over him. Rather, it is merely an informing about the duration of their two caliphates and the abundance of the people's benefit during Umar's caliphate due to its length, the expansion of Islam and its lands, the wealth and other spoils and conquests, the founding of garrison cities (amṣār), and the registration of military registers (dawāwīn). As for the Prophet's—peace and blessings be upon him—statement "and Allah will forgive him," this contains no disparagement of him, nor any indication of a sin. Rather, it is a phrase with which the Muslims used to reinforce their speech—and excellent is that reinforcement. It has already preceded in the hadith in Sahih Muslim that it was a phrase the Muslims used to say: "Do such-and-such, and Allah will forgive you." The scholars said: In all of this is an announcement of the caliphate of Abu Bakr and Umar, the soundness of their authority, an exposition of its nature, and the benefit of the Muslims therein.

The Prophet's—peace and blessings be upon him—statement: "Then Abu Bakr came to me and took the bucket from my hand, so that I might be relieved (li-yurawwiḥanī)"—the scholars said: In this is an indication of Abu Bakr's deputyship (niyābah) on his behalf and his succession (khilāfah) after him, and the Prophet's—peace and blessings be upon him—rest (rāḥah) through his death from the toil of this world and its hardships, as he said—peace and blessings be upon him: "One who is at rest, and one from whom rest is taken" (mustarīḥ wa mustarāḥ minhu)—the hadith—and "this world is the prison of the believer," and "there is no distress upon your father after this day."

The Prophet's—peace and blessings be upon him—statement [2393]: "I have not seen a man of genius (ʿabqarī) among the people who could match his feats (yafrī faryahu)." As for "yafrī," it is with the opening of the yā', the stillness of the fā', and the kasrah of the rā'. As for "faryahu," it is transmitted in two ways: one is "faryahu" with the stillness of the rā' and the lightening (takhfīf) of the yā'; the second is with the kasrah of the rā' and the doubling (tashdīd) of the yā'. Both are correct dialects. Al-Khalīl rejected the doubling and said it is an error. They are agreed that its meaning is: "I have not seen a master (sayyid) who does his work and cuts his cut." The origin of "fary" with stillness is "cutting." One says: "faraytu al-shay'a afrīhi faryan," meaning "I cut it for the purpose of rectification," so it is "mufrin" and "farin." And "afraytuhu" is when you split it in the manner of corruption. The Arabs say: "I left him cutting the fary" (taraktuhu yafrī al-fary) when he does the work and perfects it. From this is the hadith of Hassān: "I will cut them with the fary of leather" (la-ufriyannahum farya al-adīm), i.e., "I will cut them with satire as leather is cut."

The Prophet's—peace and blessings be upon him—statement: "until the people struck at the watering-place (bi-ʿaṭan)"—its explanation has preceded. Al-Qāḍī said: Its apparent meaning is that it refers specifically to the caliphate of Umar. And it is said it refers to the caliphate of Abu Bakr and Umar together, because through their vision, their management, and their undertaking of the Muslims' interests, this affair was completed, and the people struck at the watering-place. For Abu Bakr suppressed the people of apostasy, gathered the scattered ranks of the Muslims, unified them, initiated the conquests, and paved the affairs; and the fruits of that were completed and perfected in the time of Umar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb—may Allah be pleased with them both.

The Prophet's—peace and blessings be upon him—statement: "as if I were drawing with the bucket of a young she-camel (bakrah)"—it is with the stillness of the kāf and its opening (both readings).

The Prophet's—peace and blessings be upon him—statement: "until the people were watered (rawā)"—it is with the kasrah of the wāw and the lightening (takhfīf), i.e., they took their sufficiency.

His statement [2396]: "On the authority of Ṣāliḥ, on the authority of Ibn Shihāb, who said: ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Zayd ibn al-Khaṭṭāb informed me, on the authority of Muḥammad ibn Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ, that his father Saʿd informed him, saying: ʿUmar sought permission..." This hadith brings together four Successors (tābiʿūn), each narrating from the other: they are Ṣāliḥ, Ibn Shihāb, ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd, and Muḥammad. And ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd saw ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās.

His statement [2396–2397]: "And with him were women of Quraysh speaking to him and asking him for much (yastakthirnahu), their voices raised high." The scholars said: The meaning of "yastakthirnahu" is "they sought much of his speech and his answers for their needs and their legal rulings (fatāwā)." As for his statement "their voices raised high," al-Qāḍī said: It is possible that this was before the prohibition of raising one's voice above the voice of the Prophet—peace and blessings be upon him—and it is possible that the raising of their voices was only due to their gathering together, not that the voice of each one individually was higher than his voice—peace and blessings be upon him.

His statement: "They said: 'You are harsher (aghlāẓ) and more severe (afāẓ) than the Messenger of Allah—peace and blessings be upon him.'" "Al-faẓ" and "al-ghalīẓ" are synonymous, and it is an expression of harshness of character and roughness of disposition. The scholars said: The word "afʿal" here is not for comparison (tafḍīl); rather, it is in the sense of "faẓ" and "ghalīẓ" (harsh and severe). Al-Qāḍī said: It is also possible to carry it on comparison, and that the portion of it in the Prophet—peace and blessings be upon him—is what was of his harshness against the disbelievers and the hypocrites, as Allah—Exalted is He—said: {«جاهد الكفار والمنافقين واغلظ عليهم»} ("Strive against the disbelievers and the hypocrites and be harsh with them") [Quran 9:73]. And he would become angry and harsh when the sanctities of Allah—Exalted is He—were violated. And Allah knows best. In this hadith is the virtue of gentleness of disposition, forbearance (ḥilm), and kindness (rifq), as long as it does not forfeit a legally intended purpose. Allah—Exalted is He—said: {«واخفض جناحك للمؤمنين»} ("And lower your wing to the believers") [Quran 15:88], and He said: {«ولو كنت فظا غليظ القلب لانفضوا من حولك»} ("And if you had been harsh and severe of heart, they would have dispersed from around you") [Quran 3:159], and He said: {«بالمؤمنين رؤف رحيم»} ("Kind and merciful to the believers") [Quran 9:128].

The Prophet's—peace and blessings be upon him—statement: "By Him in Whose hand is my soul, Satan never met you traversing a mountain pass (fajj) except that he took a pass other than your pass." "Al-fajj" is the wide road, and it is also applied to the place that is split open between two mountains. This hadith is carried on its apparent meaning: that Satan, whenever he saw Umar traversing a pass, fled out of awe of Umar, abandoned that pass, and went to another pass, due to the intensity of his fear of Umar's severity, lest he do something to him. Al-Qāḍī said: It is also possible that he struck a metaphor for the distance of Satan and his seduction from him, and that Umar in all his affairs traverses the path of rectitude (saḍād), contrary to what Satan commands. And the correct view is the first.

chapters.title_en: Section 876 — On the Muhaddathūn, the Virtues of ʿUmar, and the Chapter on the Virtues of ʿUthmān
chapters.arabic_text:
النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه كان يقول قد كان يكون في الأمم محدثون فإن

يكن في أمتي منهم أحد فإن عمر بن الخطاب منهم) قال بن وهب تفسير محدثون

ملهمون هذا الإسناد مما استدركه الدارقطني على مسلم وقال المشهور فيه عن

إبراهيم بن سعد عن أبيه عن أبي سلمة قال بلغني أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه

وسلم وأخرجه البخاري من هذا الطريق عن أبي سلمة عن أبي هريرة واختلف تفسير

العلماء للمراد بمحدثون فقال بن وهب ملهمون وقيل مصيبون وإذا ظنوا فكأنهم

حدثوا بشئ فظنوا وقيل تكلمهم الملائكة وجاء في رواية متكلمون وقال البخاري

يجري الصواب على ألسنتهم وفيه إثبات كرامات الأولياء قوله
# [2399] (قال عمر وافقت ربي في ثلاث في مقام إبراهيم وفي الحجاب وفي أسارى

بدر) هذا من أجل مناقب عمر وفضائله رضي الله عنه وهو مطابق للحديث قبله

ولهذا عقبه مسلم به وجاء في هذه الرواية وافقت ربي في ثلاث وفسرها بهذه

الثلاث وجاء في رواية أخرى في الصحيح اجتمع نساء رسول الله صلى الله عليه

وسلم عليه في الغيرة فقلت عسى ربه إن طلقكن أن يبدله أزواجا خيرا منكن

فنزلت الآية بذلك وجاء في الحديث الذي ذكره مسلم بعد هذا موافقته في منع

الصلاة على المنافقين ونزول الاية
# 
# بذلك وجاءت موافقته في تحريم الخمر فهذه ست وليس في لفظه ما ينفي زيادة

الموافقة والله أعلم قوله
# [2400] (لما توفي عبد الله بن ابي  بن سلول) هكذا صوابه ان يكتب بن سلول

بالألف ويعرب بإعراب عبد الله فإنه وصف ثان له لأنه عبد الله بن أبي وهو

عبد الله بن سلول أيضا فأبي أبوه وسلول أمه فنسب إلى أبويه جميعا ووصف بهما

وقد سبق بيان هذا ونظائره في كتاب الإيمان في حديث المقداد حين قتل من أظهر

الشهادة وأوضحنا هناك وجوهها قوله (إن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أعطاه

قميصه ليكفن فيه أباه المنافق) قيل إنما أعطاه قميصه وكفنه فيه تطييبا لقلب

ابنه فإنه كان صحابيا صالحا وقد سأل ذلك فأجابه إليه وقيل مكافأة لعبد الله

المنافق الميت لأنه كان ألبس العباس حين أسر يوم بدر قميصا وفي هذا الحديث

بيان عظيم مكارم أخلاق النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقد علم ما كان من هذا

المنافق من الإيذاء وقابله بالحسنى فألبسه قميصا كفنا وصلى عليه واستغفر له

قال الله تعالى إنك لعلى خلق عظيم وفيه تحريم الصلاة والدعاء له بالمغفرة

والقيام على قبره للدعاء
#

| (باب من فضائل عثمان بن عفان رضي الله عنه)
# قولها
# [2401] (كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم مضطجعا في بيته كاشفا عن فخذيه

أو ساقيه فاستأذن أبو بكر فأذن له وهو على تلك الحال إلى آخره) هذا الحديث

مما يحتج به المالكية وغيرهم ممن يقول ليست الفخذ عورة ولا حجة فيه لأنه

مشكوك في المكشوف هل هو الساقان أم الفخذان فلا يلزم منه الجزم بجواز كشف

الفخذ وفي هذا الحديث جواز تدلل العالم والفاضل بحضرة من يدل عليه من فضلاء

أصحابه واستحباب ترك ذلك إذا حضر غريب أو صاحب يستحي منه قوله (دخل أبو بكر

فلم تهتش له ولم تباله) هكذا هو في جميع نسخ بلادنا تهتش بالتاء بعد الهاء

وفي بعض النسخ الطارئة بحذفها وكذا ذكره القاضي وعلى هذا فالهاء مفتوحة

يقال هش يهش كشم يشم وأما الهش الذي هو خبط الورق من الشجر فيقال منه هش

يهش بضمها قال الله تعالى وأهش بها قال أهل اللغة الهشاشة والبشاشة  بمعنى

طلاقة الوجه وحسن اللقاء ومعنى لم تباله
# 
# لم تكترث به وتحتفل لدخوله قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (ألا أستحي ممن تستحي

منه الملائكة) هكذا هو في الرواية أستحي بياء واحدة في كل واحدة منهما قال

أهل اللغة يقال استحيى يستحيي بياءين واستحى يستحي بياء واحدة لغتان الأولى

أفصح وأشهر وبها جاء القرآن وفيه فضيلة ظاهرة لعثمان وجلالته عند الملائكة

وأن الحياء صفة جميلة من صفات الملائكة قوله
# [2402] (لابس مرط عائشة) هو بكسر الميم وهو كساء من صوف وقال الخليل كساء

من صوف أو كتان او غيره وقال بن الاعرابي وابو زيد هو الازار قولها (مالي

لم أرك فزعت لأبي بكر وعمر كما فزعت لعثمان) أي اهتممت لهما واحتفلت

بدخولهما هكذا هو في جميع نسخ بلادنا فزعت بالزاي والعين المهملة وكذا حكاه

القاضي عن رواية الأكثرين قال وضبطه بعضهم فرغت بالراء والغين المعجمة وهو

قريب من معنى الأول قوله
# [2403] (عن عثمان بن غياث) هو بالغين المعجمة والثاء
# 
# المثلثة قوله (في حائط) هو البستان قوله (يركز بعود) هو بضم الكاف أي

يضرب بأسفله ليثبته في الأرض قوله (استفتح رجل فقال افتح وبشره بالجنة) وفي

رواية أمرني أن أحفظ الباب وفي رواية لأكونن بواب رسول الله صلى الله عليه

وسلم يحتمل أنه صلى الله عليه وسلم أمره أن يكون بوابا في جميع ذلك المجلس

ليبشر هؤلاء المذكورين بالجنة رضي الله عنهم ويحتمل أنه أمره بحفظ الباب

أولا إلى أن يقضي حاجته ويتوضأ لأنها حالة يستتر فيها ثم حفظ الباب أبو

موسى من تلقاء نفسه وفيه فضيلة هؤلاء الثلاثة وأنهم من أهل الجنة وفضيلة
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ح د ث (ḥ-d-th)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Origination, occurrence of an event; a ḥadīth is speech that is newly articulated.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological usage, muḥaddathūn denotes those divinely inspired with true insight, distinct from prophets (anbiyāʾ) yet receiving illumination (ilhām).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense is "being spoken to"; metaphorically extended to inner inspiration, as the speaker is the angel or God, not a human interlocutor.
- Sībawayh Rule: ʿAṭf al-Bayān (Appositional Clarification) — In "عبد الله بن أبي بن سلول," the second genitive phrase functions as an explanatory appositive, clarifying dual lineage (father and mother) without altering the grammatical case of the head noun.
chapters.translation:
I say: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to say: "There have been among the nations before you muḥaddathūn (those spoken to by inspiration); if there is one among my community, it is ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb." Ibn Wahb said: The interpretation of muḥaddathūn is "those who are inspired (mulhamūn)." This chain of transmission is among those that al-Dāraquṭnī criticized in Muslim's collection, and he said: The well-known version is from Ibrāhīm ibn Saʿd, from his father, from Abū Salamah, who said: "It reached me that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace..." Al-Bukhārī transmitted it via this path from Abū Salamah, from Abū Hurayrah. The scholars differed over the meaning of muḥaddathūn. Ibn Wahb said: "Inspired ones." It was also said: "Those who are correct in their judgments (muṣībūn); when they form an opinion, it is as though they were spoken to concerning a matter, and so they opine correctly." Another view: "The angels speak to them." In one narration it appears as "those addressed (mutakallamūn)." Al-Bukhārī said: "Correctness flows upon their tongues." In this hadith there is affirmation of the miracles of the saints (karāmāt al-awliyāʾ).

His saying — [2399] — "ʿUmar said: I concurred with my Lord in three matters: in the Station of Ibrāhīm, in the matter of the hijāb (veiling), and in the captives of Badr." This is among the most noble of ʿUmar's merits and excellences, may God be pleased with him, and it corresponds to the preceding hadith; for this reason Muslim placed it immediately after. In this narration it appears as "I concurred with my Lord in three matters," and he specified these three. In another narration in the Ṣaḥīḥ, the wives of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, gathered against him out of jealousy, and I said: "Perhaps his Lord, if he divorces you, will give him in exchange wives better than you," and the verse was revealed accordingly. And in the hadith that Muslim mentions after this, there is his concurrence in prohibiting prayer over the hypocrites, and the revelation of the verse concerning that. And his concurrence came in the prohibition of wine. These total six, and there is nothing in his wording that negates additional concurrences. And God knows best.

His saying — [2400] — "When ʿAbdullāh ibn Ubayy ibn Salūl died." This is how it is correctly written: "ibn Salūl" with an alif, and it is declined in case exactly as ʿAbdullāh is declined, for it is a second descriptive epithet for him, because he is ʿAbdullāh ibn Ubayy, and he is also ʿAbdullāh ibn Salūl. Thus Ubayy is his father and Salūl is his mother, so he is attributed to both of his parents and described by both. We have already explained this and its parallels in the Book of Faith (Kitāb al-Īmān) in the hadith of al-Miqdād when he killed one who had declared the shahādah, and we clarified its aspects there.

His saying: "The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, gave him his shirt to shroud his father, the hypocrite, in it." It is said that he gave him his shirt and shrouded him in it to soothe the heart of his son, for he was a righteous companion and had requested this, so he granted it to him. Another view: It was a recompense for ʿAbdullāh the hypocrite, deceased, because he had clothed al-ʿAbbās with a shirt when he was captured on the day of Badr. In this hadith is a great demonstration of the noble character of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. He knew what harm had come from this hypocrite, yet he requited it with goodness: he clothed him in a shirt as a shroud, prayed over him, and sought forgiveness for him. God, exalted is He, said: {«And indeed, you are upon an immense character»} (Q 68:4). In it also is the prohibition of praying over a hypocrite, supplicating for his forgiveness, and standing at his grave to pray.

| Chapter: On the Virtues of ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān, may God be pleased with him |

Her saying — [2401] — "The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was reclining in his house, uncovering his thighs or his shanks; then Abū Bakr sought permission and he granted it to him while in that state," to the end. This hadith is used as evidence by the Mālikīs and others who hold that the thigh is not ʿawrah (a part of the body that must be covered). But there is no proof in it, because it is uncertain what was uncovered — whether it was the shanks or the thighs — so no definitive ruling on the permissibility of uncovering the thigh follows from it. In this hadith there is also the permissibility of a scholar or virtuous man being at ease in the presence of those of his virtuous companions who are familiar with him, and the recommendation to refrain from that when a stranger or someone who would feel shy arrives.

His saying: "Abū Bakr entered, and she did not stir for him nor pay him any mind." This is how it appears in all the copies of our lands: "tahattash" with a tāʾ after the hāʾ. In some variant copies it is omitted, and al-Qāḍī mentioned it thus. On this reading, the hāʾ is open; one says "hasha yahishu" like "shamma yashimmu." As for "al-hashsh" which means beating leaves off trees, one says from it "hashsha yahushshu" with a ḍammah on the hāʾ. God, exalted is He, said: {«And I beat down with it leaves for my sheep»} (Q 20:18). The linguists say: "al-hashāshah" and "al-bashāshah" both mean cheerfulness of face and excellence of reception. The meaning of "lam tubālihi" is: she did not concern herself with him nor make a fuss over his entrance.

His saying, may God bless him and grant him peace: "Shall I not feel shy before one whom the angels feel shy before?" This is how it appears in the narration: "astahī" with a single yāʾ in each instance. The linguists say: One says "istahyā yastahyī" with two yāʾs, and "istaḥā yastaḥī" with one yāʾ — two dialects; the first is more eloquent and more famous, and the Qurʾān came with it. In this hadith is a manifest virtue of ʿUthmān and his majesty before the angels, and that modesty (ḥayāʾ) is a beautiful attribute of the angels.

His saying — [2402] — "Wearing the mirṭ of ʿĀʾishah." It is with kasrah on the mīm; it is a garment of wool. Al-Khalīl said: A garment of wool, linen, or other material. Ibn al-Aʿrābī and Abū Zayd said: It is the izār (waist-wrapper).

Her saying: "Why do I not see you stirred for Abū Bakr and ʿUmar as you are stirred for ʿUthmān?" Meaning: I was concerned for them and made a fuss over their entrance. This is how it appears in all the copies of our lands: "faziʿt" with zāy and unpointed ʿayn. Al-Qāḍī likewise reported it from the majority of narrations. He said: Some of them recorded it as "faright" with rāʾ and pointed ghayn, which is close in meaning to the first.

His saying — [2403] — "From ʿUthmān ibn Ghayyāth." It is with pointed ghayn and the triple-pointed thāʾ.

His saying: "In a ḥāʾiṭ." It means the orchard (bustān).

His saying: "He was planting with a stick (yarkuz bi-ʿūd)." It is with ḍammah on the kāf, meaning he strikes with its lower end to fix it in the ground.

His saying: "A man sought permission to enter, so he said: Open, and give him glad tidings of Paradise." In another narration: "He commanded me to guard the door." In yet another: "I shall surely be the doorkeeper of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace." It is possible that he, may God bless him and grant him peace, commanded him to be the doorkeeper for that entire gathering, so that he might give glad tidings of Paradise to those mentioned, may God be pleased with them. And it is possible that he commanded him to guard the door initially until he finished his need and performed ablution, because that is a state in which one seeks concealment; then Abū Mūsā guarded the door of his own accord. In this hadith is a virtue for these three, that they are among the people of Paradise, and a virtue for Abū Mūsā as well.

chapters.title_en: Section 877 — On the Permissibility of Praising Someone to Their Face When Safe from Temptation, and Related Matters
chapters.arabic_text:
لأبي موسى وفيه جواز الثناء على الإنسان في وجهه إذا أمنت عليه فتنة

الإعجاب ونحوه وفيه معجزة
# 
# ظاهرة للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لإخباره بقصة عثمان والبلوى وأن الثلاثة

يستمرون على الإيمان والهدى قوله (والله المستعان) فيه استحبابه عند مثل

هذا الحال قوله 0فخرج وجه ها هنا) المشهور في الرواية وجه بتشديد الجيم

وضبطه بعضهم بإسكانها وحكى القاضي الوجهين  ونقل الأول عن الجمهور ورجح

الثاني لوجود خرج أي قصد هذه الجهة قوله 0 جلس على بئر أريس وتوسط قفها)

أما أريس فبفتح الهمزة مصروف وأما القف فبضم القاف وهو حافة البئر وأصله

الغليظ المرتفع من الأرض قوله (على رسلك) بكسر الراء وفتحها لغتان
# 
# الكسر أشهر ومعناه تمهل وتأن قوله (في أبي بكر وعمر رضي الله عنهما أنهما

دليا أرجلهما في البئر كما دلاهما النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فيها هذا فعلاه

للموافقة وليكون أبلغ في بقاء النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم على حالته وراحته

بخلاف ما اذا لم يفعلاه فربما استحى منهما فرفعهما وفي هذا دليل للغة

الصحيحة أنه يجوز أن يقول دليت الدلو في البئر ودليت رجلي وغيرها فيه كما

يقال أدليت قال الله تعالى فأدلى دلوه ومنهم من منع الأول وهذا الحديث يرد

عليه قوله (فجلس وجاهتهم
# 
# بكسر الواو وضمها أي قبالتهم قوله (قال سعيد بن المسيب فأولتها قبورهم)

يعني أن الثلاثة دفنوا في مكان واحد وعثمان في مكان بائن عنهم وهذا من باب

الفراسة الصادقة

| (باب من فضائل علي بن أبي طالب رضي الله عنه)
# قوله
# [2404] (عن يوسف بن الماجشون) وفي بعض النسخ يوسف الماجشون بحذف لفظة بن
# 
# وكلاهما صحيح وهو أبو سلمة يوسف بن يعقوب بن عبد الله بن أبي سلمة واسم

أبي سلمة دينار والماجشون لقب يعقوب وهو لقب جرى عليه وعلى أولاده وأولاد

أخيه وهو بكسر الجيم وضم الشين المعجمة وهو لفظ فارسي ومعناه الأحمر الأبيض

المورد سمي يعقوب بذلك لحمرة وجهه وبياضه قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم لعلي رضي

الله عنه (أنت مني بمنزلة هارون من موسى إلا أنه لا نبي بعدي) قال القاضي

هذا الحديث مما تعلقت به الروافض والإمامية وسائر فرق الشيعة في أن الخلافة

كانت حقا لعلي وأنه وصى له بها قال ثم اختلف هؤلاء فكفرت الروافض سائر

الصحابة في تقديمهم غيره وزاد بعضهم فكفر عليا لأنه لم يقم في طلب حقه

بزعمهم وهؤلاء أسخف مذهبا وأفسد عقلا من  أن يرد قولهم أو يناظر وقال القاضي

ولا شك في كفر من قال هذا لأن من كفر الأمة كلها والصدر الأول فقد أبطل نقل

الشريعة وهدم الإسلام وأما من عدا هؤلاء الغلاة فإنهم لا يسلكون هذا المسلك

فأما الإمامية وبعض المعتزلة فيقولون هم مخطئون في تقديم غيره لا كفار وبعض

المعتزلة لا يقول بالتخطئة لجواز تقديم المفضول عندهم وهذا الحديث لاحجة

فيه لأحد منهم بل فيه إثبات فضيلة لعلي ولا تعرض فيه لكونه أفضل من غيره أو

مثله وليس فيه دلالة لاستخلافه بعده لأن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إنما قال

هذا لعلي حين استخلفه في المدينة في غزوة تبوك ويؤيد هذا أن هارون المشبه

به لم يكن خليفة بعد موسى بل توفي في حياة موسى وقبل وفاة موسى بنحو أربعين

سنة على ما هو مشهور عند أهل الأخبار والقصص قالوا وإنما استخلفه حين ذهب

لميقات ربه للمناجاة والله أعلم قال العلماء وفي هذا الحديث دليل على أن

عيسى بن مريم صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا نزل في آخر الزمان نزل حكما من حكام

هذه الأمة يحكم بشريعة نبينا محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم ولا ينزل نبينا وقد

سبقت الأحاديث المصرحة بما ذكرناه في كتاب الإيمان قوله
# 
# (فوضع إصبعيه على أذنيه فقال نعم وإلا فاستكتا) هو بتشديد الكاف أي صمتا

قوله (إن معاوية قال لسعد بن أبي وقاص ما منعك أن تسب أبا تراب) قال

العلماء الأحاديث الواردة التي في ظاهرها دخل على صحابي يجب تأويلها قالوا

ولا يقع في روايات الثقات إلا ما يمكن تأويله فقول معاوية هذا ليس فيه

تصريح بأنه أمر سعدا بسبه وإنما سأله عن السبب المانع له من السب كأنه يقول

هل امتنعت تورعا أو خوفا أو غير ذلك فإن كان تورعا وإجلالا له عن السب فأنت

مصيب محسن وإن كان غير ذلك فله جواب آخر ولعل سعدا قد كان في طائفة يسبون

فلم يسب معهم وعجز عن الإنكار وأنكر عليهم فسأله هذا السؤال قالوا  ويحتمل

تأويلا آخر أن معناه
# 
# ما منعك أن تخطئه في رأيه واجتهاده وتظهر للناس حسن رأينا واجتهادنا وأنه

أخطأ قوله
# [2405] (فتساورت لها) هو بالسين المهملة وبالواو ثم الراء ومعناه تطاولت

لها كما صرح في الرواية الأخرى أي حرصت عليها أي أظهرت وجهي وتصديت لذلك

ليتذكرني قوله (فما أحببت الإمارة إلا يومئذ) إنما كانت محبته لها لما دلت

عليه الإمارة من محبته لله ورسوله صلى الله عليه وسلم
# 
# ومحبتهما له والفتح على يديه قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم
# [2405] (امش ولا تلتفت حتى يفتح الله عليك فسار علي رضي الله عنه شيئا ثم

وقف ولم يلتفت فصرخ يا رسول الله على ماذا أقاتل الناس) هذا الالتفات يحتمل
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ث ن ي (th-n-y)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Bending, folding; the second of a thing; praise (thanā') as "bending" the speech toward goodness.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Thanā' is the mention of virtues; its opposite is dhamm (blame). It is a verbal act of the tongue, distinct from inward intention.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) — to bend/repeat; metaphorical (majāz) — to repeat a person's virtues in speech, as if "folding" them back upon him.
- Sībawayh Rule: ʿAṭf al-Bayān (Appositional Clarification) — The phrase "al-thalāthah" (the three) functions as an appositive clarifying the antecedent group, requiring precise referent tracking.

- Root: د ل و (d-l-w)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: The bucket (dalw); to lower the bucket into a well (adlā); the act of drawing water.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Adlā is the act of lowering; the well (bi'r) is a locus of extraction — used metaphorically for seeking benefit.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — lowering the bucket; metaphorical — extending the leg into the well as an act of humble service.
- Sībawayh Rule: Taʿaddī bi-al-Hamzah (Causative Transitivity) — "Adlā" (IV form) governs the object directly, while "dalā" (I form) with the same meaning is debated; the ḥadīth settles the permissibility of both.

- Root: ق ف ف (q-f-f)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: The elevated, rugged edge of the earth; the rim of a well (qaff).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The qaff is the raised boundary — a natural marker of limit and containment.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — the physical rim; no metaphorical extension here, as it denotes a concrete location.
- Sībawayh Rule: Ẓarf Makān (Adverbial of Place) — "ʿalā qaffihā" (upon its rim) functions as a locative predicate requiring the preposition ʿalā for surface contact.

- Root: ر س ل (r-s-l)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To be gentle, unhurried; to send (arsala); "ʿalā rislika" — at your ease, slowly.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Risl denotes deliberate calmness; it is the opposite of haste (ʿajalah) and is commended in all affairs.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — slowness of movement; metaphorical — composure of the soul in speech and action.
- Sībawayh Rule: Ishtiqāq (Derivational Morphology) — The two readings (kasr and fatḥ of the rā') are twin dialectal variants of the same nominal pattern (fiʿl/faʿl).

- Root: و ج ه (w-j-h)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Face (wajh); direction (jihah); to face toward (tawajjaha).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Wajh is the front of a thing; "wajh al-amr" is its proper aspect. The ḥadīth's "kharaja wajh" (with shaddah) means he exited toward a direction.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — the face; metaphorical — the direction of intent, as in "wajjaha amrahu" (he directed his affair).
- Sībawayh Rule: Tashdīd vs. Taskīn (Gemination vs. Quiescence) — The variant readings (wajj with shaddah vs. wajh with sukūn) are both valid; the former is the majority reading, the latter preferred by al-Qāḍī for semantic precision.

- Root: ف ر س (f-r-s)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To lie in wait; a lion (firās); insight (farāsah) — the ability to discern hidden matters.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Farāsah is a divinely-granted perception (nūr) by which the believer sees through appearances.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — predatory stalking; metaphorical — acute discernment of truth from signs.
- Sībawayh Rule: Naʿt Sababī (Attributive Qualification) — "al-farāsah al-ṣādiqah" (truthful insight) is a qualified noun phrase where the adjective carries a verbal sense.

- Root: م ج ش (m-j-sh)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Not a classical Arabic root; a Persian loanword (mājūshūn) meaning "red-white" (al-aḥmar al-abyaḍ al-muwarrad).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Not applicable — non-Arabic proper noun; treated as a foreign name (ʿalam aʿjamī).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): The word is a nickname (laqab) — a rhetorical device of identification by physical trait.
- Sībawayh Rule: ʿAlam Aʿjamī (Foreign Proper Noun) — Non-declinable in some contexts; here it is a laqab governing its bearer's lineage.

- Root: خ ل ف (kh-l-f)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To succeed, to come after (khalafa); a successor (khalīfah); the caliphate (khilāfah).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Khilāfah is the vicegerency of authority; istikhlāf is the appointment of a deputy.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — to follow in time; metaphorical — to hold authority on behalf of another.
- Sībawayh Rule: Mafʿūl Muṭlaq (Cognate Accusative) — "Istikhlāf" in the discussion of the ḥadīth requires distinguishing the verbal noun from the act of appointment.

- Root: س و ر (s-w-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To leap upon (sāra); to assault; "tasāwara" — to rise up toward something eagerly.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Musāwarah is the eager exertion of oneself toward an object of desire.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — leaping; metaphorical — striving with one's face and attention toward a goal.
- Sībawayh Rule: Mufāʿalah (Reciprocal/Intensive Form) — "Tasāwartu lahā" (VI form) implies self-projection toward the object with intensity.

- Root: أ م ر (a-m-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To command (amara); a matter (amr); authority (imārah) — the office of command.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Imārah is the trust of leadership; its love is permissible when it serves obedience to God.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — command; metaphorical — the office of governance (wilāyah).
- Sībawayh Rule: Maṣdar Ṣināʿī (Artificial Verbal Noun) — "al-imārah" is a derived noun for the office, distinct from the act of commanding.

- Root: ل ت ف (l-t-f)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To turn around (iltafata); to look back; gentleness (lutf) is a homonym.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Iltifāt is the physical turning of the face; metaphorically, it is the shifting of attention.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — turning the head; metaphorical — diverting one's resolve.
- Sībawayh Rule: Ifʿāl (IV Form) — "Iltafata" (VIII form) is used here in its literal sense of physical turning, as the context demands.
chapters.translation:
I say: In this ḥadīth of Abū Mūsā (may Allah be pleased with him) there is the permissibility of praising a person to his face when one is secure from the temptation of self-admiration (iʿjāb) and the like upon him. And in it there is a manifest miracle (muʿjizah ẓāhirah) for the Prophet ﷺ, because of his informing of the affair of ʿUthmān and the trial (al-balawā), and that the three would continue upon faith and guidance.

His saying (and Allah is the Succor — {«وَاللَّهُ الْمُسْتَعَانُ»}): In it is the recommendation (istihbāb) of uttering this at such a state.

His saying (then he exited toward a direction — "fa-kharaja wajj"): The well-known narration is "wajj" with the tashdīd of the jīm. Some of them recorded it with its sukūn (i.e., "wajh"). Al-Qāḍī transmitted both readings. He reported the first from the majority (al-jumhūr) and preferred the second, because of the existence of "kharaja" meaning he intended that direction (qaṣada tilka al-jihah).

His saying (he sat upon the well of Arīs and took the middle of its rim — "jalsa ʿalā biʾr Arīs wa tawassaṭa qaffahā"): As for Arīs, it is with the fatḥ of the hamzah, fully declinable (maṣrūf). As for al-qaff, it is with the ḍammah of the qāf, and it is the rim of the well (ḥāfat al-biʾr). Its origin is the elevated, rugged ground (al-ghalīẓ al-murtafiʿ min al-arḍ).

His saying (at your ease — "ʿalā rislika"): With the kasr of the rā' and its fatḥ — two dialects (lughatān). The kasr is more famous. Its meaning is: be slow and deliberate (tamahhal wa taʾannā).

His saying (regarding Abū Bakr and ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with them both, that they lowered their legs into the well just as the Prophet ﷺ had lowered his): These two did this for the sake of conformity (al-muwāfaqah), and so that it would be more effective in keeping the Prophet ﷺ upon his state and his comfort — unlike the case if they had not done so, for then perhaps he would have felt shy before them and lifted his legs. And in this is evidence for the correct linguistic position that it is permissible to say "dalaytu al-dalw fī al-biʾr" (I lowered the bucket into the well) and "dalaytu rijli" (I lowered my leg) and other things into it, just as one says "adlaytu." Allah the Exalted said: {«فَأَدْلَىٰ دَلْوَهُ»} (So he lowered his bucket — Sūrat Yūsuf 12:19). And some of them forbade the first form, and this ḥadīth refutes them.

His saying (then he sat facing them — "fa-jalasa wijāhatahum"): With the kasr of the wāw and its ḍammah, meaning: opposite them (qibālatahum).

His saying (Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib said: So I interpreted them as their graves — "fa-awwaltuhā qubūrahum"): He means that the three were buried in one place, and ʿUthmān in a place separate from them. And this is of the category of truthful insight (al-farāsah al-ṣādiqah).

| (Chapter: On the Virtues of ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah be pleased with him)

His saying [2404] (from Yūsuf ibn al-Mājishūn): In some copies: "Yūsuf al-Mājishūn" with the omission of the word "ibn." Both are correct. He is Abū Salamah Yūsuf ibn Yaʿqūb ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Salamah. The name of Abū Salamah is Dīnār. Al-Mājishūn is the nickname (laqab) of Yaʿqūb — a nickname that applied to him, his children, and his brother's children. It is with the kasr of the jīm and the ḍammah of the shīn (al-muʿjamah). It is a Persian word, and its meaning is: the red-white, rosy-complexioned (al-aḥmar al-abyaḍ al-muwarrad). Yaʿqūb was so named for the redness and whiteness of his face.

His saying ﷺ to ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with him: (You are to me in the station of Hārūn from Mūsā, except that there is no prophet after me — "anta minnī bi-manzilat Hārūn min Mūsā illā annahu lā nabiyya baʿdī"): Al-Qāḍī said: This ḥadīth is among those by which the Rāfiḍah, the Imāmiyyah, and the rest of the Shīʿah sects have clung, claiming that the caliphate (al-khilāfah) was the right of ʿAlī and that he was the legatee (waṣī) designated for it. He said: Then these groups differed among themselves. The Rāfiḍah declared the rest of the Companions to be disbelievers (kufr) for giving precedence to other than him. Some of them went further and declared ʿAlī himself a disbeliever, because — in their claim — he did not rise to demand his right. These latter are too foolish in doctrine (askhaf madhhaban) and too corrupt in intellect (afsad ʿaqlan) for their statement to be refuted or to be debated. Al-Qāḍī said: There is no doubt in the disbelief of whoever says this, because whoever declares the entire ummah and the first generation (al-ṣadr al-awwal) to be disbelievers has nullified the transmission of the Sacred Law (naql al-sharīʿah) and demolished Islam. As for those other than these extremists (al-ghulāh), they do not take this path. As for the Imāmiyyah and some of the Muʿtazilah, they say: They (the Companions) erred in giving precedence to other than him — but they are not disbelievers. Some of the Muʿtazilah do not affirm the charge of error (al-takhṭiʾah), because of the permissibility — in their view — of giving precedence to the lesser (al-mafḍūl) over the greater. And this ḥadīth contains no proof (ḥujjah) for any of them. Rather, in it is the affirmation of a virtue (faḍīlah) for ʿAlī, and it does not address whether he is more virtuous than others or equal to them. Nor does it contain any indication of his succession (istikhlāf) after him, because the Prophet ﷺ only said this to ʿAlī when he appointed him as his deputy over Medina during the expedition of Tabūk. This is supported by the fact that Hārūn — the one to whom he was likened — was not a caliph after Mūsā. Rather, he died during Mūsā's lifetime, approximately forty years before Mūsā's death, according to what is well-known among the people of reports (ahl al-akhbār) and stories (al-qaṣaṣ). They said: He (Mūsā) only appointed him as deputy when he went to the appointed time of his Lord (mīqāt rabbihi) for the private communion (al-munājāh). And Allah knows best.

The scholars said: In this ḥadīth is evidence that ʿĪsā ibn Maryam ﷺ, when he descends at the end of time, will descend as a judge from among the judges of this ummah, ruling by the Sacred Law of our Prophet Muḥammad ﷺ — and he will not descend as a prophet. The ḥadīths explicitly stating what we have mentioned have already preceded in the Book of Faith (Kitāb al-Īmān).

His saying (then he placed his two fingers upon his ears and said: Yes, and if not, then both of them fell silent — "fa-waḍaʿa iṣbaʿayhi ʿalā udhunayhi fa-qāla naʿam wa illā fa-stakattā"): It is with the tashdīd of the kāf, meaning: they both became silent (ṣamatā).

His saying (Indeed Muʿāwiyah said to Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ: What prevented you from reviling Abū Turāb?): The scholars said: The ḥadīths that have come down whose apparent meaning contains reproach (dakhal) against a Companion must be interpreted (taʾwīl). They said: Nothing occurs in the narrations of reliable transmitters (al-thiqāt) except what is capable of interpretation. So this statement of Muʿāwiyah does not explicitly state that he commanded Saʿd to revile him. Rather, he asked him about the reason preventing him from reviling — as if he said: Did you abstain out of scrupulousness (tawarruʿan) or fear (khawfan) or something else? If it was scrupulousness and reverence (ijlālan) for him from reviling, then you are correct and excellent (muṣīb muḥsin). And if it was other than that, then he has another answer. Perhaps Saʿd had been among a group who were reviling, and he did not revile with them, and was unable to disapprove of them, and he disapproved of them — so he (Muʿāwiyah) asked him this question. They said: Another interpretation is possible, namely that its meaning is: What prevented you from declaring him mistaken in his opinion and his ijtihād, and from showing the people the goodness of our opinion and our ijtihād, and that he erred?

His saying [2405] (then I rose eagerly toward her — "fa-tasāwartu lahā"): It is with the unpointed sīn (al-muhmalah), then the wāw, then the rā'. Its meaning is: I stretched myself toward her (taṭāwaltu lahā), as explicitly stated in the other narration — i.e., I yearned for her (ḥaraṣtu ʿalayhā), meaning: I showed my face and presented myself (taṣaddaytu) for that, so that she might remember me.

His saying (and I never loved authority (al-imārah) except on that day): His love for it was only because of what authority indicated of his love for Allah and His Messenger ﷺ, and their love for him, and the conquest (al-fatḥ) at his hands.

His saying ﷺ [2405] (Walk and do not turn around until Allah grants you victory — "imshi wa lā taltafit ḥattā yaftaḥa Allahu ʿalayk"): So ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with him, walked a little, then stopped and did not turn around. Then he cried out: O Messenger of Allah, upon what do I fight the people? This turning (iltifāt) admits of [multiple] possibilities.

chapters.title_en: Section 878 — The Command to Fight, the Invitation to Islam Before Combat, and the Merits of ʿAlī (May Allah Be Pleased with Him)
chapters.arabic_text:
وجهين أحدهما أنه على ظاهره أي لا تلتفت بعينيك لا يمينا ولا شمالا بل امض

على جهة قصدك والثاني أن المراد الحث على الإقدام والمبادرة إلى ذلك وحمله

علي رضي الله عنه على ظاهره ولم يلتفت بعينه حين احتاج وفي هذا حمل أمره

صلى الله عليه وسلم على ظاهره وقيل يحتمل أن المراد لا تنصرف بعد لقاء عدوك

حتى يفتح الله عليك وفي هذا الحديث معجزات ظاهرات لرسول الله صلى الله عليه

وسلم قولية وفعلية فالقولية إعلامه بأن الله تعالى يفتح على يديه فكان كذلك

والفعلية بصاقه في عينه وكان أرمد فبرأ من ساعته وفيه فضائل ظاهرة لعلي رضي

الله عنه وبيان شجاعته وحسن مراعاته لأمر رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

وحبه الله ورسوله وحبهما إياه قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (فإذا فعلوا ذلك فقد

منعوا منك دماءهم وأموالهم إلا بحقها وحسابهم على الله) وفي الرواية الأخرى

ادعهم إلى الإسلام هذا الحديث فيه الدعاء إلى الإسلام قبل القتال وقد قال

بإيجابه طائفة على الإطلاق ومذهبنا ومذهب آخرين أنهم إن كانوا ممن لم

تبلغهم دعوة الإسلام وجب إنذارهم قبل القتال وإلا فلا يجب لكن يستحب وقد

سبقت المسألة مبسوطة
# 
# في أول الجهاد وليس في هذا ذكر الجزية وقبولها إذا بذلوها ولعله كان قبل

نزول آية  الجزية وفيه دليل على قبول الإسلام سواء كان في حال القتال أم في

غيره وحسابه على الله تعالى معناه أنا نكف عنه في الظاهر وأما بينه وبين

الله تعالى فإن كان صادقا مؤمنا بقلبه نفعه ذلك في الآخرة ونجا من النار

كما نفعه في الدنيا وإلا فلا ينفعه بل يكون منافقا من أهل النار وفيه أنه

يشترط في صحة الإسلام النطق بالشهادتين فإن كان أخرس أو في معناه كفته

الإشارة إليهما والله أعلم قوله
# [2406] (فبات الناس يدوكون ليلتهم أيهم يعطاها) هكذا هو في معظم النسخ

والروايات يدوكون بضم الدال المهملة وبالواو أي يخوضون ويتحدثون في ذلك وفي

بعض النسخ يذكرون بإسكان الذال المعجمة وبالراء قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم

(فوالله لأن يهدي الله بك رجلا واحدا خير لك من أن تكون لك حمر النعم) هي

الإبل الحمر وهي أنفس أموال العرب يضربون بها المثل في نفاسة الشئ وأنه ليس

هناك أعظم منه وقد سبق بيان أن تشبيه أمور الآخرة بأعراض الدنيا إنما هو

للتقريب من الأفهام وإلا فذرة من الآخرة الباقية خير من الأرض بأسرها

وأمثالها معها لو تصورت وفي هذا
#

# الحديث بيان فضيلة العلم والدعاء إلى الهدى وسن السنن الحسنة قوله
# [2408] (ماء يدعى خما بين مكة والمدينة) هو بضم الخاء المعجمة وتشديد

الميم وهو اسم لغيضة على ثلاثة أميال من الحسنة عندها غدير مشهور
# 
# يضاف إلى الغيضة فيقال غدير خم قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (وأنا تارك فيكم

ثقلين فذكر كتاب الله وأهل بيته) قال العلماء سميا ثقلين لعظمهما وكبير

شأنهما وقيل لثقل العمل بهما قوله (ولكن أهل بيته من حرم الصدقة) هو بضم

الحاء وتخفيف الراء والمراد بالصدقة الزكاة وهي حرام عندنا على بني هاشم

وبني المطلب وقال مالك بنو هاشم فقط وقيل بنو قصي وقيل قريش كلها قوله في

الرواية الأخرى فقلنا من أهل بيته نساؤه قال لا هذا دليل لإبطال قول من قال

هم قريش كلها فقد كان في نسائه قرشيات وهن عائشة وحفصة وأم سلمة  وسودة وأم

حبيبة رضي الله عنهن وأما قوله في الرواية الأخرى نساؤه من أهل بيته ولكن

أهل بيته من حرم الصدقة قال وفي الرواية الأخرى فقلنا من أهل بيته نساؤه

قال لا فهاتان الروايتان ظاهر هما التناقض والمعروف في معظم الروايات في

غير مسلم أنه قال نساؤه لسن من أهل بيته فتتأول الرواية الأولى على أن

المراد انهن من اهل بيته الذين يساكنونه ويعولهم وأمر باحترامهم وإكرامهم

وسماهم ثقلا ووعظ في حقوقهم وذكر فنساؤه داخلات في هذا كله ولا يدخلن فيمن

حرم الصدقة وقد أشار إلى هذا في الرواية الأولى بقوله نساؤه من أهل بيته

ولكن أهل بيته من حرم الصدقة
# 
# فاتفقت الروايتان قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (كتاب الله هو حبل الله) قيل

المراد بحبل الله عهده وقيل السبب الموصل إلى رضاه ورحمته وقيل هو نوره

الذي يهدي به قوله (المرأة تكون
# 
# مع الرجل العصر من الدهر) أي القطعة منه قولها
# [2409] (فخرج ولم يقل عندي) هو بفتح الياء وكسر القاف من القيلولة وهي

النوم نصف النهار وفيه جواز النوم في المسجد واستحباب ملاطفة الغضبان

وممازحته والمشي إليه لاسترضائه

| (باب في فضل سعد بن أبي وقاص رضي الله عنه)
# قولها
# [2410] (أرق رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ذات ليلة) هو بفتح الهمزة وكسر

الراء وتخفيف القاف أي سهر ولم يأته نوم والأرق السهر ويقال أرقني الأمر

بالتشديد تأريقا أي أسهرني ورجل أرق على وزن فرح قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم

(ليت رجلا صالحا يحرسني) فيه جواز
# 
# الاحتراس من العدو والأخذ بالحزم وترك الإهمال في موضع الحاجة إلى

الاحتياط قال العلماء وكان هذا الحديث قبل نزول قوله تعالى والله يعصمك من

الناس لأنه صلى الله عليه وسلم ترك الاحتراس حين نزلت هذه الآية وأمر
chapters.anchors:
- Root: و-ج-ه (w-j-h)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: The face (wajh); a direction, aspect, or mode of facing; turning one's countenance toward a goal.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological discourse, denotes the "aspect" or "interpretive facet" of a command—whether literal (ẓāhir) or figurative (maʾāl).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: physical turning of the face. Metaphorical: directing one's resolve and intention (niyyah) toward a purpose.
- Sībawayh Rule: Taqdīr al-Maḥdhūf (Ellipsis Restoration) — The phrase "على ظاهره" requires supplying an implicit referent (the command's outward sense) to parse the dual interpretive possibilities.

- Root: د-ع-و (d-ʿ-w)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To call, summon, or invoke; the act of inviting someone toward a presence or allegiance.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In legal-theological context, daʿwah is the formal summons to Islam (al-Islām) prior to hostilities—a condition of prophetic praxis.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: vocal call. Metaphorical: the comprehensive invitation to faith, encompassing both speech and evidentiary proof.
- Sībawayh Rule: ʿAṭf al-Bayān (Appositional Clarification) — "ادعهم إلى الإسلام" functions as an explicative restatement of the prior command, not a separate injunction.

- Root: ث-ق-ل (th-q-l)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Weight, heaviness; something burdensome or precious due to its magnitude.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The "Two Weighty Things" (al-Thaqalān)—the Book of Allah and the Ahl al-Bayt—signify their immense ontological and moral gravity in the cosmic order.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: physical heaviness. Metaphorical: the profound responsibility and honor of adhering to them.
- Sībawayh Rule: Taṣghīr al-Tafkhīm (Diminutive for Magnification) — Though the form suggests smallness, the context magnifies, indicating rhetorical emphasis.
chapters.translation:
I say: The Prophet's statement (peace and blessings be upon him) — "Do not turn [your face]" — has two aspects. The first is that it is upon its literal meaning, i.e., do not glance with your eyes to the right or left, but rather proceed upon the direction of your intent. The second is that the intended meaning is the urging toward advance and swiftness in that matter. And ʿAlī (may Allah be pleased with him) acted upon its literal meaning and did not turn his eye when the need arose. In this is the application of his command (peace and blessings be upon him) upon its outward sense. And it was said: it is possible that the intended meaning is "do not turn away after meeting your enemy until Allah grants you victory."

In this hadith are manifest miracles (muʿjizāt) of the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him), both verbal and actual. The verbal is his informing that Allah the Exalted would grant victory at his hands, and so it was. The actual is his spitting into ʿAlī's eye while he was afflicted with ophthalmia (ramad), and he was cured instantly. In it are also apparent virtues of ʿAlī (may Allah be pleased with him), the demonstration of his courage, his excellent observance of the command of the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him), his love for Allah and His Messenger, and their love for him.

His statement (peace and blessings be upon him): "If they do that, then they have protected from you their blood and their wealth except by their right, and their reckoning is upon Allah." In the other narration: "Call them to Islam." This hadith contains the summons to Islam before fighting. A group (of scholars) held it obligatory absolutely. Our school (al-Shāfiʿī) and the school of others is that if they are among those whom the call of Islam has not reached, then warning them before fighting is obligatory; otherwise it is not obligatory, but it is recommended (mustaḥabb). The issue has already been discussed in detail at the beginning of the chapter on Jihad. There is no mention here of the jizyah (poll tax) and its acceptance if they offer it—perhaps this was before the revelation of the verse of the jizyah.

In it is evidence for accepting Islam, whether in a state of fighting or otherwise. His statement "and their reckoning is upon Allah" means: we refrain from them outwardly, but as for what is between them and Allah the Exalted—if he is truthful, believing in his heart, that benefits him in the Hereafter and saves him from the Fire, just as it benefited him in this world. Otherwise, it does not benefit him; rather, he is a hypocrite among the people of the Fire. In it is that the validity of Islam requires the utterance of the two testimonies (al-shahādatayn). If one is mute or in its equivalent, a gesture indicating them suffices. And Allah knows best.

His statement [2406]: "The people spent the night discussing (yadūkūn) their night, as to which of them would be given it." Thus it is in most copies and narrations: yadūkūn, with a ḍammah on the dāl (unpointed) and with a wāw, meaning they were plunging into discussion and conversing about that matter. In some copies: yadhkurūn, with a sukūn on the dhāl (pointed) and with a rā'.

His statement (peace and blessings be upon him): "By Allah, that Allah guides through you a single man is better for you than possessing red camels (ḥumr al-naʿam)." These are the red camels, which are the most precious of Arab wealth; they use them as a proverb for the preciousness of a thing and that there is nothing greater than it. It has already been explained that likening matters of the Hereafter to the ephemeral goods of this world is only for bringing [the meaning] near to understanding; otherwise, a single atom of the everlasting Hereafter is better than the entire earth and its like, even if it were conceivable. In this hadith is the clarification of the virtue of knowledge, the call to guidance, and the establishment of good precedents (sunan ḥasanah).

His statement [2408]: "A water called Khumm, between Mecca and Medina." It is with a ḍammah on the khā' (pointed) and tashdīd on the mīm. It is the name of a thicket (ghayḍah) three miles from al-Juḥfah, near which is a well-known pool (ghadīr), attributed to the thicket, so it is said: Ghadīr Khumm.

His statement (peace and blessings be upon him): "I am leaving among you two weighty things (thaqalayn)" — then he mentioned the Book of Allah and his Ahl al-Bayt. The scholars said: they were called "two weighty things" due to their greatness and immense significance. And it was said: due to the weight of acting upon them.

His statement: "But my Ahl al-Bayt are those for whom charity (ṣadaqah) is forbidden." It is with a ḍammah on the ḥā' and takhfīf on the rā'. The intended meaning of "ṣadaqah" is the obligatory alms (zakāh), which is forbidden in our school upon the Banū Hāshim and Banū al-Muṭṭalib. Mālik said: only the Banū Hāshim. And it was said: Banū Quṣayy. And it was said: all of Quraysh.

His statement in the other narration: "We said: who are your Ahl al-Bayt? Are your wives [included]? He said: No." This is evidence for invalidating the view of those who said they are all of Quraysh, for among his wives were Qurashī women—namely ʿĀʾishah, Ḥafṣah, Umm Salamah, Sawdah, and Umm Ḥabībah (may Allah be pleased with them all). As for his statement in the other narration: "His wives are from his Ahl al-Bayt, but his Ahl al-Bayt are those for whom charity is forbidden"—and in yet another narration: "We said: who are your Ahl al-Bayt? Are your wives [included]? He said: No." These two narrations appear contradictory. The well-known [version] in most narrations outside of Muslim is that he said: "His wives are not from his Ahl al-Bayt." Thus the first narration is interpreted to mean that they are from his Ahl al-Bayt in the sense of those who dwell with him and whom he supports, and he commanded respect and honor for them, and called them a "weight" and exhorted regarding their rights—so his wives are included in all of this, but they are not included among those for whom charity is forbidden. He alluded to this in the first narration by his statement: "His wives are from his Ahl al-Bayt, but his Ahl al-Bayt are those for whom charity is forbidden." Thus the two narrations are reconciled.

His statement (peace and blessings be upon him): "The Book of Allah is the rope of Allah (ḥabl Allāh)." It was said: the intended meaning of "the rope of Allah" is His covenant. And it was said: the means (sabab) leading to His pleasure and mercy. And it was said: it is His light by which He guides.

His statement: "The woman who is with the man for a period (al-ʿaṣr) of time"—i.e., a portion of it.

Her statement [2409]: "He went out and did not take a midday nap (yaqīl)"—it is with a fatḥah on the yā' and kasrah on the qāf, from al-qaylūlah, which is sleeping at midday. In it is the permissibility of sleeping in the mosque, the recommendation of gentleness toward the angry person, jesting with him, and walking to him to seek his appeasement.

| Chapter on the Virtue of Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ (May Allah Be Pleased with Him)

Her statement [2410]: "The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) was sleepless (arq) one night"—it is with a fatḥah on the hamzah, kasrah on the rā', and takhfīf on the qāf, i.e., he stayed awake and sleep did not come to him.
