chapters.arabic_text:
ذكرني خاليا أثابه الله وجازاه عما عمل)
# 
# بما لا يطلع عليه أحد قوله تعالى وإن ذكرني في ملأ ذكرته في ملأ هم خير

منهم هذا مما استدلت به المعتزلة ومن وافقهم على تفضيل الملائكة على

الأنبياء صلوات الله وسلامه عليهم أجمعين واحتجوا أيضا بقوله تعالى ولقد

كرمنا بني آدم وحملناهم في البر والبحر ورزقناهم من الطيبات وفضلناهم على

كثير ممن خلقنا تفضيلا فالتقييد بالكثير احتراز من الملائكة ومذهب أصحابنا

وغيرهم أن الأنبياء أفضل من الملائكة لقوله تعالى في بني إسرائيل وفضلناهم

على العالمين والملائكةمن العالمين ويتأول هذا الحديث على أن الذاكرين

غالبا يكونون طائفة لانبى فيهم فاذا ذكره الله تعالى في خلائق من الملائكة

كانوا خيرا من تلك الطائفة قوله تعالى وإن تقرب مني شبرا تقربت إليه ذراعا

وإن تقرب إلي ذراعا تقربت منه باعا وإن أتاني يمشي أتيته هرولة هذا الحديث

من أحاديث الصفات ويستحيل إرادة ظاهره وقد سبق الكلام في أحاديث الصفات

مرات ومعناه من تقرب إلي بطاعتي تقربت إليه برحمتي والتوفيق والإعانة وإن

زاد زدت فإن أتاني يمشي وأسرع في طاعتي أتيته هرولة أي صببت عليه الرحمة

وسبقته بها ولم أحوجه إلى المشي الكثير في الوصول إلى المقصود والمراد أن

جزاءه يكون تضعيفه
# 
# على حسب تقربه قوله تعالى في رواية محمد بن جعفر وإذا تلقاني بباع جئته

أتيته هكذا هو في أكثر النسخ جئته أتيته وفي بعضها جئته بأسرع فقط وفي

بعضها أتيته وهاتان ظاهرتان والأول صحيح أيضا والجمع بينهما للتوكيد وهو

حسن لا سيما عند اختلاف اللفظ والله أعلم
# [2676] قوله جبل يقال له جمدان هو بضم الجيم وإسكان الميم قوله صلى الله

عليه وسلم سبق المفردون قالوا وما المفردون يا رسول الله قال الذاكرون الله

كثيرا والذاكرات هكذا الرواية فيه المفردون بفتح الفاء وكسر الراء المشددة

وهكذا نقله القاضي عن متقني شيوخهم وذكر غيره أنه روي بتخفيفها وإسكان

الفاء يقال فرد الرجل وفرد بالتخفيف والتشديد وأفرد وقد فسرهم رسول  الله

صلى الله عليه وسلم بالذاكرين الله كثيرا والذاكرات تقديره والذاكراته

فحذفت الهاء هنا كما حذفت فى القرآن لمناسبة رؤس الآي ولأنه مفعول يجوز

حذفه وهذا التفسير هو مراد الحديث قال بن قتيبة وغيره وأصل المفردين الذين

هلك أقرانهم وانفردوا عنهم فبقوا يذكرون الله تعالى وجاء في رواية هم الذين

اهتزوا في ذكر الله أى لهجوابه وقال بن الأعرابي يقال فرد الرجل إذا تفقه

واعتزل وخلا بمراعاة الأمر والنهى
#

| (باب فى اسماء الله تعالى وفضل من أحصاها
# [2677] قوله صلى
# الله عليه وسلم إن لله تسعة وتسعين اسما مائة إلا واحدا من أحصاها دخل

الجنة إنه وتر يحب الوتر وفي رواية من حفظها دخل الجنة قال الإمام أبو

القاسم القشيري فيه دليل على أن الاسم هو المسمى إذ لو كان غيره لكانت

الأسماء لغيره لقوله تعالى ولله الأسماءالحسنى قال الخطابي وغيره وفيه دليل

على أن أشهر أسمائه سبحانه وتعالى الله لإضافة هذه الأسماءاليه وقد روي أن

الله هو اسمه الأعظم قال أبو القاسم الطبري وإليه ينسب كل اسم له فيقال

الرؤف والكريم من أسماء الله تعالى ولا يقال من أسماء الرؤف أو الكريم الله

واتفق العلماء على أن هذا الحديث ليس فيه حصر لأسمائه سبحانه وتعالى فليس

معناه أنه ليس له أسماء غير هذه التسعة والتسعين وإنما مقصود الحديث أن هذه

التسعة والتسعين من أحصاها دخل الجنة فالمراد الإخبار عن دخول الجنة

بإحصائها لا الإخبار بحصر الأسماء ولهذا جاء في الحديث الآخر أسألك بكل اسم

سميت به نفسك أواستأثرت به في علم الغيب عندك وقد ذكر الحافظ أبو بكر بن

العربي المالكي عن بعضهم أنه قال لله تعالى ألف اسم قال بن العربي وهذا

قليل فيها والله أعلم وأما تعيين هذه الأسماء فقد جاء في الترمذي وغيره في

بعض أسمائه خلاف وقيل إنها مخفية التعيين كالاسم الأعظم وليلة القدر

ونظائرها وأما قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم من أحصاها دخل الجنة فاختلفوا في

المراد بإحصائها فقال البخاري وغيره من المحققين معناه حفظها  وهذا هو

الأظهر لأنه جاء مفسرا في الرواية الأخرى من حفظها وقيل أحصاها عدها)
# 
# في الدعاء بها وقيل أطاقها أي أحسن المراعاة لها والمحافظة على ما تقتضيه

وصدق بمعانيها وقيل معناه العمل بها والطاعة بكل اسمها والإيمان بها لا

يقتضي عملا وقال بعضهم المراد حفظ القرآن وتلاوته كله لأنه مستوف لها وهو

ضعيف والصحيح الأول قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم إن الله وتر يحب الوتر الوتر

الفرد ومعناه في حق الله تعالى الواحد الذي لا شريك له ولا نظير ومعنى يحب

الوتر تفضيل الوتر في الأعمال وكثير من الطاعات فجعل الصلاة خمسا والطهارة

ثلاثا والطواف سبعا والسعي سبعا ورمي الجمار سبعا وأيام التشريق ثلاثا

والاستنجاء ثلاثا وكذا الأكفان وفي الزكاة خمسة أوسق وخمس أواق من الورق

ونصاب الإبل وغير ذلك وجعل كثيرا من عظيم مخلوقاته وترا منها السماوات
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ذ-ك-ر (dh-k-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning is "to remember, to mention, to be mindful"; also denotes "honor" and "renown" (dhikr as the opposite of nisyān, forgetfulness).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological usage, dhikr of Allah is the heart's presence with Him and the tongue's utterance of His praise; divine dhikr of the servant denotes His mercy and commendation of him in the higher assembly (al-malaʾ al-aʿlā).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) sense is verbal mention; metaphorical (majāz) sense is divine favor and recompense, as in the ḥadīth qudsī where Allah's "drawing near" is His mercy, not spatial movement.
- Sībawayh Rule: Taqdīr al-maḥdhūf (Ellipsis Restoration) — In the phrase "wal-dhākirātu" (the women who remember much), the feminine plural ending -āt requires a restored taʾ marbūṭah (i.e., al-dhākirātuhu), elided for rhythmic concordance with Quranic verse-endings (munāsabat ruʾūs al-āy), a permissible omission of an object.
chapters.translation:
I say — may Allah reward him who recalls me in solitude with the best of recompense for what he has wrought, in a manner unseen by any:

His statement — Allah be exalted — {«وَإِنْ ذَكَرَنِي فِي مَلَإٍ ذَكَرْتُهُ فِي مَلَإٍ خَيْرٍ مِنْهُمْ»} (And if he mentions Me in a company, I mention him in a company better than they). This is among the proofs adduced by the Muʿtazilah and those who concur with them for the superiority of angels over the prophets — may Allah's prayers and peace be upon them all. They also argued with His statement — exalted be He — {«وَلَقَدْ كَرَّمْنَا بَنِي آدَمَ وَحَمَلْنَاهُمْ فِي الْبَرِّ وَالْبَحْرِ وَرَزَقْنَاهُمْ مِنَ الطَّيِّبَاتِ وَفَضَّلْنَاهُمْ عَلَى كَثِيرٍ مِمَّنْ خَلَقْنَا تَفْضِيلًا»} (And indeed We have honored the children of Adam, carried them on land and sea, provided them with good things, and preferred them above many of those We created with a marked preference). The restriction to "many" (kathīr) is a precaution excluding the angels. The doctrine of our companions (al-Ashāʿirah) and others is that the prophets are superior to the angels, due to His statement — exalted be He — in Sūrat Banī Isrāʾīl: {«وَفَضَّلْنَاهُمْ عَلَى الْعَالَمِينَ»} (And We preferred them above the worlds), and the angels are among the worlds (al-ʿālamīn). This ḥadīth is interpreted [by them] as referring to the fact that those who remember [Allah] are, in most cases, a group among whom there are no prophets; so when Allah mentions them in a multitude of angels, those angels are better than that particular group [of non-prophetic rememberers].

His statement — exalted be He: {«وَإِنْ تَقَرَّبَ مِنِّي شِبْرًا تَقَرَّبْتُ إِلَيْهِ ذِرَاعًا وَإِنْ تَقَرَّبَ إِلَيَّ ذِرَاعًا تَقَرَّبْتُ مِنْهُ بَاعًا وَإِنْ أَتَانِي يَمْشِي أَتَيْتُهُ هَرْوَلَةً»} (And if he draws near to Me by a span, I draw near to him by a cubit; and if he draws near to Me by a cubit, I draw near to him by a fathom; and if he comes to Me walking, I come to him running). This ḥadīth is among the ḥadīths of the Divine Attributes (aḥādīth al-ṣifāt), and the literal meaning (ẓāhir) is impossible [to affirm of Allah]. We have already discussed the ḥadīths of the Attributes on multiple occasions. Its meaning is: whoever draws near to Me through obedience to Me, I draw near to him through My mercy, divine success (tawfīq), and assistance; and if he increases [in obedience], I increase [in mercy]. And if he comes to Me walking — i.e., hastening in obedience — I come to him running (harwalah), meaning I pour upon him mercy and outstrip him with it, not needing him to walk much to reach the intended goal. The intended sense is that his recompense is multiplied in proportion to his drawing near.

His statement — exalted be He — in the narration of Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar: "And if he meets Me with a fathom, I come to him — I come to him (jiʾtuhu ataytuhu)." Thus it appears in most copies: "jiʾtuhu ataytuhu." In some copies: "jiʾtuhu bi-asraʿ" (I come to him faster) only; in others: "ataytuhu" only. These latter two are clear [in meaning], and the first is also sound. The combination of the two [verbs] is for emphasis (tawkīd), which is excellent — especially when the wording differs. And Allah knows best.

[2676] His statement — peace be upon him: "The mufridūn have preceded." They said: "O Messenger of Allah, who are the mufridūn?" He said: "Those who remember Allah much, male and female (al-dhākirūn Allāha kathīran wal-dhākirāt)." Thus is the narration: "al-mufridūn" with fatḥah on the fāʾ and kasrah on the shaddah'd rāʾ. Al-Qāḍī [ʿIyāḍ] transmitted it thus from the proficient scholars among their shaykhs. Others mentioned that it is also narrated with the rāʾ unshaddah (lightened) and the fāʾ unvoweled (sukūn). One says "farada al-rajul" and "farda" — with lightening and with shaddah — and "afrada." The Messenger of Allah — peace be upon him — interpreted them as those who remember Allah much, male and female. The estimation (taqdīr) is "al-dhākirātuhu" (the women who remember Him), the hāʾ being elided here just as it is elided in the Qurʾān for the sake of concordance with verse-endings, and because it is an object whose omission is permissible. This interpretation is the intended meaning of the ḥadīth. Ibn Qutaybah and others said: The origin of "al-mufridūn" is those whose peers have perished and who have become isolated from them, remaining to remember Allah — exalted be He. It also came in a narration: "They are those who are stirred (ihtazzū) in the remembrance of Allah," i.e., devoted to it. Ibn al-Aʿrābī said: One says "farada al-rajul" when he devotes himself to religious understanding (tafaqqaha), withdraws, and secludes himself in observance of the command and prohibition.

| Chapter on the Names of Allah — Exalted be He — and the Virtue of Whoever Enumerates Them

[2677] His statement — peace be upon him: "Indeed Allah has ninety-nine names — one hundred minus one. Whoever enumerates them (aḥṣāhā) enters Paradise. Indeed He is Witr (Odd) and loves the odd." In another narration: "Whoever preserves them (ḥafizahā) enters Paradise." Imām Abū al-Qāsim al-Qushayrī said: In this there is evidence that the name (al-ism) is the named (al-musammā); for were it other than it, the names would belong to something other than Him, due to His statement — exalted be He: {«وَلِلَّهِ الْأَسْمَاءُ الْحُسْنَى»} (And to Allah belong the Most Beautiful Names). Al-Khaṭṭābī and others said: In it there is evidence that His most famous name — glorified and exalted be He — is "Allah," because these names are attributed to Him. And it has been narrated that "Allah" is His Greatest Name (al-ism al-aʿẓam). Abū al-Qāsim al-Ṭabarī said: To it is attributed every name He has; thus one says "al-Raʾūf" (the Compassionate) and "al-Karīm" (the Generous) are among the names of Allah, but one does not say "Allah" is among the names of al-Raʾūf or al-Karīm. The scholars are agreed that this ḥadīth does not restrict His names — glorified and exalted be He — so its meaning is not that He has no names other than these ninety-nine. Rather, the intent of the ḥadīth is that whoever enumerates these ninety-nine enters Paradise. The purpose is to inform of entering Paradise through their enumeration, not to inform of a restriction of the names. For this reason, it came in the other ḥadīth: "I ask You by every name You have named Yourself with, or which You have kept to Yourself in the knowledge of the unseen with You." Al-Ḥāfiẓ Abū Bakr ibn al-ʿArabī al-Mālikī mentioned from some of them that he said: Allah — exalted be He — has one thousand names. Ibn al-ʿArabī said: And this is little regarding them. And Allah knows best.

As for the specific identification of these names, it has come in al-Tirmidhī and others that there is disagreement concerning some of them. It is said that their identification is hidden (khafiyyat al-taʿyīn), like the Greatest Name, the Night of Decree (laylat al-qadr), and their analogues. As for his statement — peace be upon him: "Whoever enumerates them enters Paradise," they differed over the intended meaning of "enumerating them" (iḥṣāʾ). Al-Bukhārī and others among the verifying scholars said: Its meaning is preserving them (ḥifẓ). This is the most apparent (al-aẓhar), because it is explained in the other narration: "Whoever preserves them." It is also said: "Enumerating them" means counting them in supplication by them. It is also said: "He encompasses them" (aṭāqahā), i.e., he excelled in observing them and maintaining what they necessitate, and believed in their meanings. It is also said: Its meaning is acting by them, obeying through each of their names, and faith in them — which does not necessitate action. Some said: The intended meaning is preserving the Qurʾān and reciting it entirely, because it encompasses them. This is weak. The correct view is the first.

His statement — peace be upon him: "Indeed Allah is Witr and loves the odd." Al-witr is the single (al-fard). Its meaning regarding Allah — exalted be He — is the One who has no partner and no equivalent. The meaning of "He loves the odd" is His preferring the odd in works and many acts of obedience. Thus He made the prayer five [daily prayers], the purification three [washings], the circumambulation (ṭawāf) seven, the saʿy seven, the stoning of the jamarāt seven, the days of al-Tashrīq three, the cleansing after relieving oneself three, and likewise the shrouds. And in the zakāh: five wasqs, five ounces of silver, the nisāb of camels, and other such things. And He made many of His magnificent creations odd, among them the heavens.

chapters.title_en: Section 931 — On Resoluteness in Supplication, Disliking the Wish for Death, and Loving the Encounter with Allah
chapters.arabic_text:
والأرضون والبحار وأيام الأسبوع وغير ذلك وقيل إن معناه منصرف إلى صفة من

يعبد الله بالوحدانية والتفرد مخلصا له والله أعلم

| (باب العزم فى الدعاء ولا يقل إن شئت
# [2678] قوله صلى الله
# عليه وسلم إذا دعا أحدكم فليعزم في الدعاء ولا يقل اللهم إن شئت فأعطني

فإن الله لا مستكره له وفي رواية فإن الله صانع ما شاء لا مكره له وفى

رواية ليعزم الرغب)
# 
# فان الله لايتعاظمه شيء أعطاه قال العلماء عزم المسألة الشدة فى طلبها

والحزم من غير ضعف في الطلب ولا تعليق على مشيئة ونحوها وقيل هو حسن الظن

بالله تعالى في الإجابة ومعنى الحديث استحباب الجزم في الطلب وكراهة

التعليق على المشيئة قال العلماء سبب كراهته أنه لا يتحقق استعمال المشيئة

إلا في حق من يتوجه عليه الإكراه والله تعالى منزه عن ذلك وهو معنى قوله

صلى الله عليه وسلم في آخر الحديث فإنه لا مستكره له وقيل سبب الكراهة أن

في هذا اللفظ صورة الاستعفاء على المطلوب والمطلوب منه قوله عن عطاء بن

مثنى هو بالمد والقصر باب كراهة تمني الموت لضر نزل به
# [2680] قوله صلى الله  عليه وسلم لايتمنين أحدكم الموت لضر نزل به فإن كان

لا بد متمنيا فليقل اللهم أحيني ما كانت الحياة خيرا لي وتوفني إذا كانت

الوفاة خيرا لي فيه التصريح بكراهة تمني الموت لضر نزل به من مرض أو فاقة

أو محنة من عدو أو نحو ذلك من مشاق الدنيا فأما إذا خاف ضررا فى دينه
# 
# أوفتنة فيه فلا كراهة فيه لمفهوم هذا الحديث وغيره وقد فعل هذا الثاني

خلائق من السلف عند خوف الفتنة في أديانهم وفيه أنه إن خاف ولم يصبر على

حاله في بلواه بالمرض ونحوه فليقل اللهم أحيني إن كانت الحياة خيرا لى إلخ

والأفضل الصبر والسكون للقضاء قوله حدثنا عاصم عن النضر بن أنس وأنس يومئذ

حي معناه أن النضر حدث به في حياة أبيه
# [2682] قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا مات أحدكم انقطع عمله هكذا هو في بعض

النسخ عمله وفي كثير منها أمله وكلاهما صحيح لكن الأول أجود وهو المتكرر في

الأحاديث والله أعلم
#

# باب من أحب لقاء الله أحب الله لقاءه ومن كره لقاء الله كره الله لقاءه
# [2683] قوله حدثنا هداب هذا الإسناد والذي بعده كلهم بصريون إلا عبادة بن

الصامت فشامى قوله صلىالله عليه وسلم من أحب لقاء الله أحب الله لقاءه ومن

كره لقاء الله كره الله لقاءه قالت عائشة فقلت يا نبي الله أكراهية الموت

فكلنا يكره الموت قال ليس كذلك ولكن المؤمن إذا بشر برحمة الله ورضوانه

وجنته أحب لقاء الله فأحب الله لقاءه وأن الكافر إذا بشر بعذاب الله وسخطه

كره لقاء الله وكره الله لقاءه هذا الحديث يفسر آخره أوله ويبين المراد

بباقي الأحاديث المطلقة من أحب لقاء الله ومن كره لقاء الله ومعنى الحديث

أن الكراهة المعتبرة
# 
# هي التي تكون عند النزع في حالة لا تقبل توبته ولا غيرها فحينئذ يبشر كل

إنسان بما هو صائر إليه وما أعدله ويكشف له عن ذلك فأهل السعادة يحبون

الموت ولقاء الله لينتقلوا إلى ما أعدلهم ويحب الله لقاءهم  أي فيجزل لهم

العطاء والكرامة وأهل الشقاوة يكرهون لقاءه لما علموا من سوء ما ينتقلون

إليه ويكره الله لقاءهم أي يبعدهم عن رحمته وكرامته ولا يريد ذلك بهم وهذا

معنى كراهته سبحانه لقاءهم وليس معنى الحديث أن سبب كراهة الله تعالى

لقاءهم كراهتهم ذلك ولا
# 
# أن حبه لقاء الآخرين حبهم ذلك بل هو صفة لهم
# [2685] قولها إذا شخص البصر وحشرج الصدر واقشعر الجلد وتشنجت الأصابع أما

شخص فبفتح الشين والخاء ومعناه ارتفاع الأجفان إلى فوق وتحديد النظر وأما

الحشرجة فهي تردد النفس فى الصدور وأما اقشعرار الجلد فهو قيام شعره وتشنج

الأصابع تقبضها

| باب فضل الذكر والدعاء والتقرب إلى الله تعالى وحسن
# الظن به قوله تعالى وإذا تقرب مني ذراعا تقربت إليه باعا أو بوعا الباع

والبوع بضم الباء والبوع بفتحها)
# 
# كله بمعنى وهو طول ذراعي الإنسان وعضديه وعرض صدره قال الباجي وهو قدر

أربع أذرع وهذا حقيقة اللفظ والمراد بها في هذا الحديث المجاز كما سبق في

أول كتاب الذكر في شرح هذا الحديث مع الحديثين بعده
# [2687] قوله تعالى فله عشر أمثالها أو أزيد معناه أن التضعيف بعشرة

أمثالهالا بد بفضل الله ورحمته ووعده الذى لايخلف والزيادة بعد بكثرة

التضعيف إلى سبعمائة ضعف وإلى أضعاف كثيرة يحصل لبعض الناس دون بعض على حسب

مشيئته سبحانه وتعالى قوله تعالى ومن لقيني بقراب الأرض خطيئة هو بضم القاف

على المشهور وهو ما يقارب ملأها وحكي كسر القاف نقله القاضي وغيره والله

أعلم
#
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ع ز م (ʿ-z-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning is firm resolve, determination, and binding intent — the opposite of hesitation or vacillation.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological context, ʿazm denotes unwavering certainty in one's request to Allah, untainted by doubt or conditional hedging.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Used literally here as "resoluteness" (ḥaqīqah) in the act of supplication, not metaphorically.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clause (al-Sharṭ) — The prohibition of "if You will" (in shi'ta) is analyzed as a suspended condition (taʿlīq) that weakens the performative force of the request.
chapters.translation:
I say: And the earths, the seas, the days of the week, and other such things [are included in what is meant]. And it was said that its meaning is directed toward the attribute of the one who worships Allah with absolute oneness (al-waḥdāniyyah) and exclusivity (al-tafarruf), devoting himself sincerely to Him. And Allah knows best.

| Chapter: On Resoluteness in Supplication, and That One Should Not Say "If You Will"

# [2678] His saying, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: "When one of you supplicates, let him be resolute in the supplication, and let him not say: 'O Allah, if You will, then give me.' For verily Allah is not compelled by anyone." And in another narration: "For verily Allah does what He wills; there is none who can compel Him." And in yet another narration: "Let him be resolute in the desire (al-raghbah)."

For verily nothing is too great for Allah to grant. The scholars said: Resoluteness in the request (ʿazm al-masʾalah) means intensity in seeking it, and firmness (al-ḥazm) without weakness in the request, and without suspending it upon the will [of Allah] or similar conditions. And it was said: It means having a good opinion (ḥusn al-ẓann) of Allah, the Exalted, regarding the response. The meaning of the hadith is the recommendation of decisiveness in the request and the disapproval of suspending it upon the will. The scholars said: The reason for its disapproval is that the employment of the conditional "if You will" is only truly applicable to one upon whom compulsion (al-ikrāh) may be directed, and Allah, the Exalted, is transcendent above that. This is the meaning of his saying, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, at the end of the hadith: "For verily He is not compelled by anyone." And it was said: The reason for the disapproval is that in this expression there is a semblance of seeking exemption (al-istiʿfāʾ) from the one requested and the one from whom the request is made.

His saying, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn Muthannā — it is with lengthening (al-madd) and shortening (al-qasr) [of the vowel].

Chapter: On the Disapproval of Wishing for Death Due to a Harm That Has Befallen One

# [2680] His saying, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: "Let none of you wish for death due to a harm that has befallen him. But if he must wish for it, let him say: 'O Allah, keep me alive as long as life is better for me, and cause me to die when death is better for me.'" In this is an explicit statement of the disapproval of wishing for death due to a harm that has befallen one — whether from illness, poverty, tribulation from an enemy, or similar hardships of this world. However, if one fears harm to his religion or a trial (fitnah) therein, then there is no disapproval in it, by virtue of the implication (mafhūm) of this hadith and others. Indeed, many of the Salaf (pious predecessors) did this second thing when they feared trial in their religions. And in this [hadith] is [the ruling] that if one fears [harm] and cannot bear patiently his state in his affliction of illness and the like, then let him say: "O Allah, keep me alive if life is better for me," etc. But the superior course is patience and tranquility before the divine decree (al-qaḍāʾ).

His saying: "ʿĀṣim narrated to us from al-Naḍr ibn Anas, and Anas was on that day alive" — its meaning is that al-Naḍr narrated it during the lifetime of his father.

# [2682] His saying, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: "When one of you dies, his deed (ʿamaluhu) is cut off." Thus it is in some copies: "his deed," and in many of them: "his hope" (amaluhu). Both are correct, but the first is more excellent and is the one repeated in the hadiths. And Allah knows best.

Chapter: Whoever Loves the Encounter with Allah, Allah Loves His Encounter; and Whoever Dislikes the Encounter with Allah, Allah Dislikes His Encounter

# [2683] His saying: "Haddāb narrated to us" — this chain of transmission (isnād) and the one after it are all Baṣran, except ʿUbādah ibn al-Ṣāmit, for he is Syrian (Shāmī).

His saying, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: "Whoever loves the encounter with Allah, Allah loves his encounter; and whoever dislikes the encounter with Allah, Allah dislikes his encounter." ʿĀʾishah said: "I said: 'O Prophet of Allah, is it the dislike of death? For all of us dislike death.' He said: 'It is not that. Rather, the believer, when he is given glad tidings of Allah's mercy, His good pleasure, and His Paradise, loves the encounter with Allah, so Allah loves his encounter. And the disbeliever, when he is given glad tidings of Allah's punishment and His wrath, dislikes the encounter with Allah, so Allah dislikes his encounter.'"

This hadith — its end explains its beginning and clarifies the intended meaning of the remaining absolute hadiths: "Whoever loves the encounter with Allah" and "Whoever dislikes the encounter with Allah." The meaning of the hadith is that the disapproval that is considered [valid] is that which occurs at the moment of death-agony (al-nazʿ), in a state in which repentance is no longer accepted, nor anything else. At that time, every person is given glad tidings of what he is destined for and what has been prepared for him (mā uʿidda lahu), and it is unveiled to him. Thus, the people of felicity (ahl al-saʿādah) love death and the encounter with Allah, so that they may pass on to what has been prepared for them, and Allah loves their encounter — meaning, He grants them abundantly of His giving and honor (al-karāmah). And the people of misery (ahl al-shaqāwah) dislike His encounter because of what they know of the evil of that to which they are passing, and Allah dislikes their encounter — meaning, He distances them from His mercy and His honor, and He does not will that for them. This is the meaning of His dislike, glorified be He, of their encounter. It is not the meaning of the hadith that the cause of Allah's dislike of their encounter is their dislike of it, nor that His love of the encounter of others is their love of it. Rather, it is an attribute of them [i.e., a description of their state].

# [2685] Her saying: "When the eyesight becomes fixed (shakhasa), the chest rattles (ḥashraja), the skin bristles (iqshaʿarra), and the fingers contract (tashannajat)" — As for "shakhasa," it is with the opening of the shīn and the khāʾ, and its meaning is the rising of the eyelids upward and the fixing of the gaze. As for "al-ḥashrajah," it is the repetition of breath in the chest. As for "iqshaʿrār" of the skin, it is the standing of its hair. And "tashannuj" of the fingers is their contraction.

| Chapter: On the Virtue of Remembrance (dhikr), Supplication, Drawing Near to Allah the Exalted, and Having a Good Opinion of Him

His saying, the Exalted: "And if he draws near to Me by a span, I draw near to him by a cubit (bāʿan)" — or "būʿan." The bāʿ and the būʿ — with the ḍammah on the bāʾ — and the būʿ with its opening [i.e., bāʿ], all have the same meaning: it is the length of a man's two forearms and upper arms and the width of his chest. Al-Bājī said: It is the measure of four cubits (adhruʿ). This is the literal meaning of the word, but the intended meaning in this hadith is metaphorical (majāz), as has preceded in the beginning of the Book of Remembrance in the commentary on this hadith along with the two hadiths after it.

# [2687] His saying, the Exalted: "Then for him is ten times the like of it, or more" — its meaning is that the multiplication by ten times its like is certain by the grace of Allah, His mercy, and His promise that does not fail. The increase thereafter is by the abundance of multiplication up to seven hundred fold, and up to many multiples that are attained by some people and not others, according to His will, glorified and exalted be He.

His saying, the Exalted: "And whoever meets Me with an earthful (qirāb) of sin" — it is with the ḍammah on the qāf according to the well-known [reading], and it means approximately a full measure of it. The kasrah on the qāf has also been reported; al-Qāḍī and others transmitted it. And Allah knows best.

chapters.arabic_text:
# باب كراهة الدعاء بتعجيل العقوبة في الدنيا
# [2688] قوله عاد رجلا من المسلمين قد خفت مثل الفرخ أي ضعف وفي هذا

الحديث النهي عن الدعاء بتعجيل العقوبة وفيه فضل الدعاء باللهم آتنا في

الدنيا حسنة وفي الآخرة حسنة وقنا عذاب النار وفيه جواز التعجب بقول سبحان

الله وقد سبقت نظائره وفيه استحباب عيادة المريض والدعاء له وفيه كراهة

تمني البلاء لئلا يتضجر منه ويسخطه وربما شكا وأظهر الأقوال في تفسير
# 
# الحسنة في الدنيا أنها العبادة والعافية وفي الآخرة الجنة والمغفرة  وقيل

الحسنة تعم الدنيا والآخرة

| (باب فضل مجالس الذكر
# [2689] قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم إن
# لله تبارك وتعالى ملائكة سيارة فضلا يبتغون مجالس الذكر أما السيارة

فمعناه سياحون في الأرض وأما فضلا فضبطوه على أوجه أحدها وهو أرجحها

وأشهرها في بلادنا فضلا بضم الفاء والضاد والثانية بضم الفاء وإسكان الضاد

ورجحها بعضهم وادعى أنها أكثر وأصوب والثالثة بفتح الفاء وإسكان الضاد قال

القاضي هكذا الرواية عند جمهور شيوخنا في البخاري ومسلم والرابعة فضل بضم

الفاء والضاد ورفع اللام على أنه خبر مبتدأ محذوف والخامسة فضلاء بالمد جمع

فاضل قال العلماء معناه على جميع الروايات أنهم ملائكة زائدون على الحفظة

وغيرهم من المرتبين مع الخلائق فهؤلاء السيارة لاوظيفة لهم وانما مقصودهم

حلق الذكر وأما قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم يبتغون فضبطوه على وجهين أحدهما

بالعين المهملة من التتبع وهو البحث عن الشيء والتفتيش والثاني يبتغون

بالغين المعجمة من الا بتغاء وهو الطلب وكلاهما صحيح قوله صلى الله عليه

وسلم فإذا وجدوا مجلسا فيه ذكر قعدوا معهم وحف بعضهم بعضا هكذا هو في كثير

من نسخ بلادنا حف بالفاء وفي بعضها حض بالضاد المعجمة أي حث على الحضور

والاستماع وحكى القاضي عن بعض رواتهم وحط بالطاء المهملة واختاره القاضي

قال ومعناه أشار بعضهم إلى بعض بالنزول ويؤيد هذه الرواية قوله بعده في

البخاري هلموا إلى)
# 
# حاجتكم ويؤيد الرواية الأولى وهي حف قوله في البخاري يحفونهم بأجنحتهم

ويحدقون بهم ويستديرون حولهم ويحوف بعضهم بعضا قوله ويستجيرونك من نارك أي

يطلبون الأمان منها قوله عبد خطاء أي كثير الخطايا وفي هذا الحديث فضيلة

الذكر وفضيلة مجالسه والجلوس مع أهله وان لم يشاركهم وفضل مجالسة الصالحين

وبركتهم والله أعلم قال القاضي عياض رحمه الله وذكر الله تعالى ضربان ذكر

بالقلب وذكر باللسان وذكر القلب نوعان أحدهما وهو أرفع الأذكار وأجلها

الفكر في عظمة الله تعالى وجلاله وجبروته وملكوته وآياته في سمواته وأرضه

ومنه الحديث خير الذكر الخفي والمراد به هذا والثاني ذكره بالقلب عند الأمر 

والنهي فيمتثل ما أمر به ويترك ما نهي عنه ويقف عما أشكل عليه وأما ذكر

اللسان مجردا فهو أضعف الأ ذكار ولكن فيه فضل عظيم كما جاءت به الأحاديث

قال وذكر بن جرير الطبري وغيره اختلاف السلف في ذكر القلب واللسان أيهما

أفضل قال القاضي والخلاف عندي إنما يتصور في مجرد ذكر القلب تسبيحا وتهليلا

وشبههما وعليه يدل كلامهم لا أنهم مختلفون في الذكر الخفي الذي ذكرناه والا

فذلك
# 
# لايقاربه ذكر اللسان فكيف يفاضله وانما الخلاف فى ذكر القلب بالتسبيح

المجرد ونحوه والمراد بذكر اللسان مع حضور القلب فإن كان لاهيا فلا واحتج

من رجح ذكر القلب بأن عمل السر أفضل ومن رجح ذكر اللسان قال لأن العمل فيه

أكثر فإن زاد باستعمال اللسان اقتضى زيادة أجر قال القاضي واختلفوا هل تكتب

الملائكة ذكر القلب فقيل تكتبه ويجعل الله تعالى لهم علامة يعرفونه بها

وقيل لا يكتبونه لأنه لايطلع عليه غير الله قلت الصحيح أنهم يكتبونه وأن

ذكر اللسان مع حضور القلب أفضل من القلب وحده والله أعلم

| (باب فضل الدعاء باللهم آتنا في الدنيا حسنة وفي 
# الآخرة حسنة وقنا عذاب النار
# [2690] ذكر في الحديث أنها كانت أكثر دعاءالنبى صلى الله عليه وسلم لما

جمعته من خيرات الآخرة والدنيا وقد سبق شرحه قريبا والله أعلم)
#

# باب فضل التهليل والتسبيح والدعاء
# [2691] قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم فيمن قال في يوم لا إله إلا الله وحده لا

شريك له له الملك وله الحمد وهو على كل شيء قدير مائة مرة لم يأت أحد بأفضل

مما جاء به إلا أحد عمل أكثر من ذلك هذا فيه دليل على أنه لو قال هذا

التهليل أكثر من مائة مرة في اليوم كان له هذا الأجر المذكور فى الحديث على

المائة ويكون له ثواب آخر على الزيادة وليس هذا من الحدود التى نهى عن

اعتدائها ومجاوزة أعدادها وإن زيادتها لا فضل فيها أو تبطلها كالزيادة في

عدد الطهارة وعدد ركعات الصلاة ويحتمل أن يكون المراد الزيادة  من أعمال

الخير لا من نفس التهليل ويحتمل أن يكون المراد مطلق الزيادة سواء كانت من

التهليل أو من غيره أو منه ومن غيره وهذا الاحتمال أظهر والله أعلم وظاهر

- Root: ك-ر-ه (k-r-h)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Dislike, aversion, or disapproval; the opposite of love and choice (maḥabbah).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In Sharīʿah terminology, karāhah denotes that which the Lawgiver discourages without absolute prohibition, carrying no punishment for the doer but reward for the one who abstains.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense is inner repugnance; here it is transferred (majāz) to the legal ruling of disapproval, not a description of the act itself.
- Root: ع-ج-ل (ʿ-j-l)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Haste, acceleration, seeking something before its appointed time.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In supplication, taʿjīl al-ʿuqūbah means requesting the swift arrival of trial or punishment in the worldly abode rather than the Hereafter.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Used literally here—requesting temporal acceleration—not metaphorically.
- Root: ح-س-ن (ḥ-s-n)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Beauty, goodness, excellence; that which is pleasing and praiseworthy.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Ḥasanah in the Quranic supplication {«رَبَّنَا آتِنَا فِي الدُّنْيَا حَسَنَةً»} is a comprehensive term for every praiseworthy affair—faith, health, knowledge, and virtue.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): The term is general (ʿāmm) in its literal scope, yet the scholars differed over whether it is restricted by context or remains universal.
- Root: ذ-ك-ر (dh-k-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Remembrance, mention, recollection; the opposite of forgetfulness (nisyān).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Dhikr is of two types: remembrance by the tongue (dhikr al-lisān) and remembrance by the heart (dhikr al-qalb); the highest is reflective contemplation (fikr) upon Allah's majesty.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): The literal sense is verbal mention; the metaphorical extension includes heart-based remembrance and even the state of being present with Allah.
- Sībawayh Rule: Rule of ʿAṭf al-Bayān (Appositional Clarification) — When the author states "أما السيارة فمعناه سياحون في الأرض" (As for al-sayyārah, its meaning is travelers), he employs a nominal sentence with a detached pronoun (ḍamīr al-faṣl) to clarify the predicate, a structure Sībawayh treats as emphatic specification.
chapters.translation:
I say: The author (may Allah have mercy on him) said:

**Section: On the Disapproval of Supplicating for the Hastening of Punishment in This World**

[2688] His saying (peace and blessings be upon him) concerning the man who visited a Muslim who had become weak "like a fledgling chick (al-farkh)"—meaning feeble. In this ḥadīth there is a prohibition against supplicating for the hastening of punishment. In it also is the virtue of supplicating with: {«اللَّهُمَّ آتِنَا فِي الدُّنْيَا حَسَنَةً وَفِي الْآخِرَةِ حَسَنَةً وَقِنَا عَذَابَ النَّارِ»} (O Allah, give us good in this world and good in the Hereafter, and protect us from the punishment of the Fire). In it is the permissibility of expressing wonder by saying "Subḥān Allāh" (Glory be to Allah), and its parallels have already preceded. In it is the recommendation (istiḥbāb) of visiting the sick and supplicating for him. In it is the disapproval of wishing for affliction, lest one become vexed by it and resent it, and perhaps complain. The strongest of the statements concerning the interpretation of "al-ḥasanah" (the good) in this world is that it means worship (ʿibādah) and well-being (ʿāfiyah), and in the Hereafter it means Paradise and forgiveness. And it was said: al-ḥasanah encompasses both this world and the Hereafter.

**Section: On the Virtue of Gatherings of Remembrance (Majālis al-Dhikr)**

[2689] His saying (peace and blessings be upon him): "Indeed Allah, Blessed and Exalted, has roaming angels (malāʾikah sayyārah) who go about seeking out gatherings of remembrance." As for "al-sayyārah," its meaning is: travelers upon the earth. As for "fuḍḍalan" (excelling), they transmitted it in several ways. The first—and it is the most preponderant and most famous in our lands—is "fuḍḍalan" with ḍammah on the fāʾ and the ḍād. The second is with ḍammah on the fāʾ and sukūn on the ḍād, which some scholars preponderated, claiming it is more frequent and more correct. The third is with fatḥah on the fāʾ and sukūn on the ḍād. Al-Qāḍī said: This is the transmission according to the majority of our teachers in al-Bukhārī and Muslim. The fourth is "fuḍḍal" with ḍammah on the fāʾ and ḍād and rafʿ on the lām, as the predicate of an omitted subject. The fifth is "fuḍalāʾ" with elongation, the plural of "fāḍil" (excellent one). The scholars said: The meaning according to all transmissions is that they are angels additional to the recording angels (al-ḥafaẓah) and others appointed among the creatures. These roaming ones have no fixed function; their sole purpose is the circles of remembrance. As for his saying (peace and blessings be upon him) "yabtaghūna" (they seek), they transmitted it in two ways: the first with the unpointed ʿayn (yabtaghūna) from "al-tabaghhī," which is searching and investigating for a thing; the second with the pointed ghayn (yabtaghūna) from "al-ibtighāʾ," which is seeking. Both are correct.

His saying (peace and blessings be upon him): "When they find a gathering in which there is remembrance, they sit with them and surround one another (ḥaffa baʿḍuhum baʿḍan)." Thus it is in many of the copies of our lands: "ḥaffa" with the fāʾ. In some of them it is "ḥaḍḍa" with the pointed ḍād, meaning urging one another to attend and listen. Al-Qāḍī narrated from some of their transmitters "ḥaṭṭa" with the unpointed ṭāʾ, and al-Qāḍī chose this, saying: Its meaning is that they signal to one another to descend. This transmission is supported by his subsequent saying in al-Bukhārī: "Come to your need." And the first transmission—"ḥaffa"—is supported by his saying in al-Bukhārī: "They surround them with their wings (yaḥuffūnahum bi-ajniḥatihim)" and encircle them and go around them, and they cover one another.

His saying: "And they seek refuge with You from Your Fire (yastajīrūnaka min nārik)"—meaning they request safety and protection from it. His saying: "a servant who is khaṭṭāʾ" (very sinful)—meaning one who commits many sins (khaṭāyā).

In this ḥadīth is the virtue of remembrance (dhikr), the virtue of its gatherings, and sitting with its people even if one does not participate with them. Also the virtue of sitting with the righteous and their blessing. And Allah knows best.

Al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ (may Allah have mercy on him) said: The remembrance of Allah, Exalted is He, is of two types: remembrance by the heart and remembrance by the tongue. Remembrance by the heart is of two kinds. The first—and it is the most elevated and most sublime of remembrances—is reflection (al-fikr) upon the greatness of Allah, His majesty, His omnipotence (jabarūt), His sovereignty (malakūt), and His signs in His heavens and His earth. From this is the ḥadīth: "The best of remembrance is the hidden one (khafī)," and what is meant by it is this. The second is remembrance of Him by the heart at the time of command and prohibition—so that one complies with what He has commanded, abstains from what He has prohibited, and pauses at what is ambiguous to him. As for remembrance by the tongue alone, it is the weakest of remembrances, yet it contains immense virtue, as the ḥadīths have conveyed.

He said: Ibn Jarīr al-Ṭabarī and others mentioned the disagreement of the Salaf (the pious predecessors) concerning remembrance by the heart versus remembrance by the tongue—which of the two is superior. Al-Qāḍī said: In my view, the disagreement is only conceivable regarding mere remembrance of the heart—such as tasbīḥ (glorification), tahlīl (declaration of Allah's oneness), and the like. Their statements indicate this, not that they differed over the hidden remembrance (al-dhikr al-khafī) which we have mentioned—for that is not even approached by remembrance of the tongue, so how could it be weighed against it? Rather, the disagreement is only concerning remembrance of the heart by mere tasbīḥ and similar acts. And what is meant by remembrance of the tongue is with the presence of the heart; for if one is heedless, then it is not [counted as such]. Those who preponderated remembrance of the heart argued that the secret deed (ʿamal al-sirr) is superior. Those who preponderated remembrance of the tongue said: Because the deed therein is greater in quantity—for if one increases by employing the tongue, it necessitates an increase in reward.

Al-Qāḍī said: They differed over whether the angels record the remembrance of the heart. It was said: They record it, and Allah, Exalted is He, gives them a sign by which they recognize it. And it was said: They do not record it, because none but Allah is aware of it. I say: The correct view is that they do record it, and that remembrance of the tongue with the presence of the heart is superior to remembrance of the heart alone. And Allah knows best.

**Section: On the Virtue of Supplicating with {«اللَّهُمَّ آتِنَا فِي الدُّنْيَا حَسَنَةً وَفِي الْآخِرَةِ حَسَنَةً وَقِنَا عَذَابَ النَّارِ»}**

[2690] It was mentioned in the ḥadīth that this was the most frequent supplication of the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him), because it combines the goods of the Hereafter and this world. Its explanation has already preceded recently. And Allah knows best.

**Section: On the Virtue of Tahlīl (Saying Lā Ilāha Illā Allāh), Tasbīḥ (Glorification), and Supplication**

[2691] His saying (peace and blessings be upon him) concerning the one who says in a day: "Lā ilāha illā Allāh waḥdahu lā sharīka lah, lahu al-mulku wa lahu al-ḥamdu wa huwa ʿalā kulli shayʾin qadīr" (There is no god but Allah alone, with no partner; His is the sovereignty and His is the praise, and He is over all things competent) one hundred times—"no one brings anything better than what he has brought, except one who does more than that." This contains evidence that if one were to say this tahlīl more than one hundred times in the day, he would receive this mentioned reward for the hundred, and he would have another reward for the increase. This is not among the limits (ḥudūd) whose transgression and exceeding of their numbers is prohibited—such that increasing them carries no virtue or nullifies them, like the increase in the number of ablutions (al-ṭahārah) or the number of units of prayer (rakʿāt). It is possible that what is meant by "more than that" is an increase in deeds of goodness, not from the tahlīl itself. And it is possible that what is meant is an absolute increase, whether it be from the tahlīl or from other deeds, or from both. And this latter possibility is the more apparent. And Allah knows best.

chapters.title_en: The Virtue of Tahlīl, Tasbīḥ, and Gathering for Qur'anic Recitation — Section 933
chapters.arabic_text:
إطلاق الحديث أنه يحصل هذا الأجر المذكور في هذا الحديث من قال هذا التهليل

مائة مرة في يومه سواء قاله متوالية أو متفرقة في مجالس أو بعضها أول

النهار وبعضها آخره لكن الأفضل أن يأتي بها متوالية في أول النهار ليكون

حرزا له في جميع نهاره قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم في حديث التهليل ومحيت عنه

مائة سيئة وفي حديث التسبيح حطت خطاياه وإن
# 
# كانت مثل زبد البحر ظاهره أن التسبيح أفضل وقد قال في حديث التهليل ولم

يأت أحد أفضل مما جاء به قال القاضي في الجواب عن هذا إن التهليل المذكور

أفضل ويكون ما فيه من زيادةالحسنات ومحو السيئات وما فيه من فضل عتق الرقاب

وكونه حرزا من الشيطان زائدا على فضل التسبيح وتكفير الخطايا لأنه قد ثبت

أن من أعتق رقبة أعتق الله بكل عضو منها عضوا منه من النار فقد حصل بعتق

رقبة واحدة تكفير جميع الخطايا مع ما يبقى له من زيادة عتق الرقاب الزائدة

على الواحدة ومع ما فيه من زيادة مائة درجة وكونه حرزا من الشيطان ويؤيده

ما جاء في الحديث بعد هذا إن أفضل الذكر التهليل مع الحديث الآخر أفضل ما

قلته أنا والنبيون قبلي لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له الحديث وقيل إنه

اسم الله الأعظم وهي كلمة الإخلاص والله أعلم وقد سبق أن معنى التسبيح

التنزيه عما لا يليق به سبحانه وتعالى من الشريك والولد والصاحبة والنقائص

مطلقا وسمات الحدوث مطلقا قوله في حديث التهليل عشر مرات حدثنا عبد الله بن
# 
# أبي السفر عن الشعبي عن ربيع بن خثيم عن عمرو بن ميمون عن بن أبي ليلى عن

أبي أيوب الأنصاري رضي الله عنهم هذا الحديث فيه أربعة تابعيون يروي بعضهم

عن بعض وهم الشعبي وربيع وعمرو وبن  أبى ليلى واسم بن أبى ليلى هذا عبد

الرحمن وأما بن أبي السفر فبفتح الفاء وسكنها بعض المغاربة والصواب الفتح
# [2696] قوله الله أكبر كبيرا منصوب بفعل محذوف أي
# 
# كبرت كبيرا أو ذكرت كبيرا
# [2698] قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم يسبح مائة تسبيحة فيكتب له ألف حسنة أو

يحط عنه ألف خطيئة هكذا هو في عامة نسخ صحيح مسلم أو يحط بأو وفي بعضها

ويحط بالواو وقال الحميدي في الجمع بين الصحيحين كذا هو في كتاب مسلم أو

يحط بأو وقال البرقاني ورواه شعبة وأبو عوانة ويحيى القطان عن يحيى الذي

رواه مسلم من جهته فقالوا ويحط بالواو والله أعلم
#

| (باب فضل الاجتماع على تلاوة القرآن وعلى الذكر
# [2699] فيه
# حديث أبي هريرة من نفس عن مؤمن كربة إلى آخره وهو حديث عظيم جامع لأنواع

من العلوم والقواعد والآداب وسبق شرح أفراد فصوله ومعنى نفس الكربة أزالها

وفيه فضل قضاء حوائج المسلمين ونفعهم بما تيسر من علم أو مال أو معاونة أو

إشارة بمصلحة أو نصيحة وغير ذلك وفضل الستر على المسلمين وقد سبق تفصيله

وفضل إنظار المعسر وفضل المشي في طلب العلم ويلزم من ذلك الاشتغال بالعلم

الشرعي بشرط أن يقصد به وجه الله تعالى وان كان هذا شرطا في كل عبادة لكن

عادة العلماء يقيدون هذه المسألة به لكونه قد يتساهل فيه بعض الناس ويغفل

عنه بعض المبتدئين ونحوهم قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم وما اجتمع قوم في بيت من

بيوت الله يتلون كتاب الله تعالى ويتدارسونه بينهم إلا نزلت عليهم السكينة

وغشيتهم الرحمة قيل المراد بالسكينة هنا الرحمة وهو الذي اختاره القاضي

عياض وهو ضعيف لعطف الرحمة عليه وقيل الطمأنينة والوقار هو أحسن وفي هذا

دليل لفضل الاجتماع على تلاوة القرآن في المسجد)
# 
# وهو مذهبنا ومذهب الجمهور وقال مالك يكره وتأوله بعض أصحابه ويلحق

بالمسجد في تحصيل هذه الفضيلة الاجتماع فى مدرسة ورباط ونحوهما إن شاء الله

تعالى ويدل عليه الحديث الذي بعده فإنه مطلق يتناول جميع المواضع ويكون

التقييد  في الحديث الأول خرج على الغالب لا سيما في ذلك الزمان فلا يكون له

مفهوم يعمل به قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم ومن بطأ به عمله لم يسرع به نسبه

معناه من كان عمله ناقصا لم يلحقه بمرتبة أصحاب الأعمال فينبغى أن
# 
# لايتكل على شرف النسب وفضيلة الآباء ويقصر في العمل
# [2701] قوله لم أستحلفكم تهمة لكم هي بفتح الهاء وإسكانها وهي فعلة وفعلة

من الوهم والتاء بدل من الواو واتهمته به اذا ظننت به ذلك قوله صلى الله

عليه وسلم إن الله عز وجل يباهي بكم الملائكة معناه يظهر فضلكم لهم ويريهم

حسن عملكم ويثني عليكم عندهم وأصل البهاء الحسن والجمال وفلان يباهي بماله

أي يفخر ويتجمل بهم على غيرهم ويظهر حسنهم

| (باب استحباب الاستغفار والاستكثار منه
# [2702] قوله صلى
# الله عليه وسلم إنه ليغان على قلبي وإني لأستغفر الله في اليوم مائة مرة

قال أهل اللغة الغين بالغين المعجمة والغيم بمعنى والمراد هنا ما يتغشى

القلب قال القاضي قيل المراد الفترات والغفلات عن الذكر الذي كان شأنه

الدوام عليه فإذا فتر عنه أو غفل عد ذلك ذنبا واستغفر منه قال وقيل هو همه

بسبب أمته وما اطلع عليه من أحوالها بعده فيستغفر لهم وقيل سببه)
# 
# اشتغاله بالنظر في مصالح أمته وأمورهم ومحاربة العدو ومداراته وتأليف
chapters.anchors:
- Root: هـ ل ل (h-l-l)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To raise the voice, to proclaim; the core of tahlīl (lā ilāha illā Allāh) is the vocal declaration of divine oneness.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Tahlīl is the verbal attestation of tawḥīd, the foundational theological confession that negates all partners and affirms sole divinity.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) — the utterance itself; metaphorical (majāz) — its spiritual efficacy as a shield (ḥirz) and expiation, extending beyond mere speech.
- Root: س ب ح (s-b-ḥ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To swim, to float; to be free of defect; tasbīḥ is the declaration of divine transcendence above all imperfection.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Theological nuance — absolute negation (tanzīh) of all attributes of contingency (ḥudūth), partners, offspring, and deficiency from Allah.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — verbal glorification; metaphorical — the inner state of recognizing Allah's incomparability, often paired with tahlīl for comprehensive worship.
- Root: ك ر ب (k-r-b)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Grief, distress, or a heavy burden that constricts the chest; kurbah denotes a severe affliction.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In the ḥadīth, "removing a kurbah" (nafsa kurbah) signifies the act of alleviating a believer's worldly or spiritual distress, a meritorious deed tied to divine recompense.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — physical or emotional constriction; metaphorical — any trial requiring relief, as used in the context of communal aid.
- Root: غ ي ن (gh-y-n)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: A veil, cloud, or covering that obscures; ghayn refers to what envelops the heart.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In the prophetic statement, "it is veiled over my heart" (yughān ʿalā qalbī), it denotes moments of spiritual heedlessness (ghaflah) or lapses in constant remembrance, not sin per se.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — a physical covering; metaphorical — a subtle spiritual state requiring istighfār as a remedy.
- Sībawayh Rule: Naṣb by an Omitted Verb (al-naṣb bi-fiʿl maḥdhūf) — In "Allāhu akbar kabīran" (Allah is Great, greatly), kabīran is accusative (manṣūb) due to an implied verb like kabbartu (I magnified) or dhakartu (I remembered), as parsed in the text.
chapters.translation:
I say: The ḥadīth's unrestricted wording indicates that this mentioned reward is attained by whoever utters this tahlīl (lā ilāha illā Allāh) one hundred times in his day, whether he says it consecutively or intermittently, in gatherings, or part at the beginning of the day and part at its end. However, it is superior to perform it consecutively at the start of the day, so that it may serve as a protection (ḥirz) for him throughout his entire day.

His saying, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, in the ḥadīth of tahlīl: "And one hundred sins are wiped away from him," and in the ḥadīth of tasbīḥ: "His sins are shed, even if they were like the foam of the sea" — its apparent meaning is that tasbīḥ is superior. Yet he said in the ḥadīth of tahlīl: "And no one brings anything better than what he has brought." Al-Qāḍī said in response to this: The mentioned tahlīl is superior, and what it contains of increased good deeds, erasure of sins, the merit of freeing slaves, and its being a protection from Satan is additional to the virtue of tasbīḥ and the expiation of sins. This is because it is established that whoever frees a slave, Allah frees a limb of his from the Fire for each limb of that slave. Thus, by freeing a single slave, all sins are expiated, along with what remains for him of the increased merit of freeing additional slaves, and with what it contains of the elevation of one hundred degrees and its being a protection from Satan. This is supported by what comes in the ḥadīth after this: "The best remembrance is tahlīl," along with the other ḥadīth: "The best of what I and the prophets before me have said is: lā ilāha illā Allāh waḥdahu lā sharīka lah" (There is no god but Allah alone, with no partner). And it is said that it is the Greatest Name of Allah (ism Allāh al-aʿẓam), and it is the word of sincerity (kalimat al-ikhlāṣ). And Allah knows best.

It has preceded that the meaning of tasbīḥ is the declaration of transcendence (tanzīh) above what is unbefitting of Him, Glorified and Exalted — above partners, offspring, consort, and all deficiencies absolutely, and above all attributes of origination (ḥudūth) absolutely.

His saying in the ḥadīth of tahlīl "ten times": We were narrated by ʿAbdullāh ibn Abī al-Safar, from al-Shaʿbī, from Rabīʿ ibn Khuthaym, from ʿAmr ibn Maymūn, from Ibn Abī Laylā, from Abū Ayyūb al-Anṣārī, may Allah be pleased with them all. In this ḥadīth there are four Successors (tābiʿūn) narrating from one another: al-Shaʿbī, Rabīʿ, ʿAmr, and Ibn Abī Laylā. The name of this Ibn Abī Laylā is ʿAbd al-Raḥmān. As for Ibn Abī al-Safar, the fāʾ is opened (with fatḥah); some Maghribīs pronounce it with sukūn, but the correct pronunciation is with fatḥah.

[2696] His saying, "Allāhu akbar kabīran" (Allah is Great, greatly) — kabīran is accusative (manṣūb) due to an omitted verb, i.e., "I magnified (Allah) greatly" (kabbartu kabīran) or "I remembered (Him) greatly" (dhakartu kabīran).

[2698] His saying, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: "He glorifies (Allah) with one hundred tasbīḥāt, and one thousand good deeds are written for him, or (aw) one thousand sins are shed from him" — thus it appears in most copies of Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim with "or" (aw). In some copies, it is "and" (wa) — "and one thousand sins are shed." Al-Ḥumaydī said in al-Jamʿ bayn al-Ṣaḥīḥayn: Thus it is in the book of Muslim — "or" (aw). Al-Barqānī said: Shuʿbah, Abū ʿAwānah, and Yaḥyā al-Qaṭṭān narrated it from Yaḥyā (the one from whom Muslim took it), and they said: "and" (wa). And Allah knows best.

| (Chapter: The Virtue of Gathering for Qur'anic Recitation and Remembrance)

[2699] In it is the ḥadīth of Abū Hurayrah: "Whoever relieves a believer of a distress (kurbah) of the distresses of this world..." to its end. It is a tremendous ḥadīth, comprehensive of various types of sciences, principles, and etiquettes. The explanation of its individual sections has preceded. The meaning of "relieving a distress" (nafsa kurbah) is removing it. In it is the virtue of fulfilling the needs of Muslims and benefiting them with whatever is easy — whether knowledge, wealth, assistance, indicating a benefit, advice, or otherwise. Also, the virtue of concealing the faults of Muslims has preceded in detail. Also, the virtue of granting respite to the debtor in difficulty, and the virtue of walking in pursuit of knowledge. Necessarily implied by this is engaging in sacred knowledge (al-ʿilm al-sharʿī), on the condition that one intends thereby the Face of Allah. Although this condition applies to every act of worship, the scholars customarily qualify this particular matter with it because some people may be lax regarding it, and some innovators and their like may neglect it.

His saying, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: "And no people gather in a house of the houses of Allah, reciting the Book of Allah and studying it among themselves, except that tranquility (sakīnah) descends upon them, mercy envelops them..." It is said that the intended meaning of sakīnah here is mercy (raḥmah) — this is the choice of Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ — but it is weak, because mercy is conjoined to it (in the same sentence). It is also said: it means serenity (ṭumaʾnīnah) and dignity (waqār) — and this is the best interpretation. In this is evidence for the virtue of gathering for Qur'anic recitation in the mosque — and this is our school (madhhab) and the school of the majority. Mālik said it is disliked (makrūh), and some of his companions interpreted it (as referring to a specific context). The mosque is joined by a school (madrasah), a ribāṭ (hospice), and the like in attaining this virtue, Allah willing. This is indicated by the subsequent ḥadīth, for it is unrestricted, encompassing all places. The restriction in the first ḥadīth is expressed according to the predominant circumstance, especially in that era, so it carries no operative specific implication (lā mafhūm lahu yuʿmal bihi).

His saying, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: "Whoever is slowed by his deeds will not be hastened by his lineage" — its meaning is: whoever's deeds are deficient will not be brought by his lineage to the rank of those with (excellent) deeds. Therefore, one should not rely on the nobility of lineage or the virtue of forefathers while falling short in deeds.

[2701] His saying: "I did not make you swear out of suspicion of you" (lam astaḥlifkum tuhmatan lakum) — tuhmatan is pronounced with fatḥah on the tāʾ or with sukūn, and it is a verbal noun (fiʿlah) or (fuʿlah) from wahm (suspicion), with the tāʾ substituted for the wāw. One says: ittahamtu bihi (I suspected him of it) when one holds that opinion of him. His saying, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: "Indeed, Allah, Glorified and Exalted, boasts of you before the angels" (yubāhī bikum al-malāʾikah) — its meaning is: He manifests your virtue to them, shows them the excellence of your deeds, and praises you in their presence. The origin of bahāʾ (beauty) is comeliness and handsomeness. One says: "So-and-so boasts with his wealth" (yubāhī bi-mālihi), i.e., he takes pride and adorns himself with it before others, and displays its excellence.

| (Chapter: The Recommendation of Seeking Forgiveness and Doing So Abundantly)

[2702] His saying, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: "Indeed, my heart is veiled (yughān) and I seek Allah's forgiveness one hundred times a day." The people of language said: al-ghayn (with the dotted ghayn) and al-ghaym are synonymous. What is meant here is what envelops the heart. Al-Qāḍī said: It is said that what is meant is the periods of lassitude (fatrāt) and heedlessness (ghaflāt) from the remembrance that was his constant practice — so when he lapsed from it or was heedless, he counted that as a sin and sought forgiveness for it. He said: And it is said that it was his concern due to his community (ummah) and what he was shown of their conditions after him, so he sought forgiveness for them. And it is said: its cause was his engagement in attending to the welfare of his community, their affairs, fighting the enemy, dealing diplomatically with them, and reconciling their hearts.

chapters.arabic_text:
المؤلفة ونحو ذلك فيشتغل بذلك من عظيم مقامه فيراه ذنبا بالنسبةالى عظيم

منزلته وإن كانت هذه الأمور من أعظم الطاعات وأفضل الأعمال فهي نزول عن

عالي درجته ورفيع مقامه من حضوره مع الله تعالى ومشاهدته ومراقبته وفراغه

مما سواه فيستغفر لذلك وقيل يحتمل أن هذا الغين هو السكينة التي تغشى قلبه

لقوله تعالى فانزل السكينة عليهم ويكون استغفاره إظهارا للعبودية والافتقار

وملازمة الخشوع وشكرا لما أولاه وقد قال المحاشي خوف الأنبياء والملائكة

خوف إعظام وإن كانوا آمنين عذاب الله تعالى وقيل يحتمل أن هذا الغين حال

خشية وإعظام يغشى القلب ويكون استغفاره شكرا كما سبق وقيل هو شيء يعتري

القلوب الصافية مما تتحدث به النفس  فهو شها والله أعلم

| (باب التوبة قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم يا أيها الناس 
# توبوا إلى الله فإني أتوب في اليوم مائة مرة هذا الأمر بالتوبة موافق

لقوله تعالى وتوبوا إلى الله جميعا أيها المؤمنون وقوله تعالى يا أيها

الذين آمنوا توبوا إلى الله)
# 
# توبة نصوحا وقد سبق في الباب قبله بيان سبب استغفاره وتوبته صلى الله

عليه وسلم ونحن إلى الاستغفار والتوبة أحوج قال أصحابنا وغيرهم من العلماء

للتوبة ثلاثة شروط أن يقلع عن المعصية وأن يندم على فعلها وأن يعزم عزما

جازما أن لايعود إلى مثلها أبدا فإن كانت المعصية تتعلق بآدمي فلها شرط

رابع وهو رد الظلامة إلى صاحبها أو تحصيل البراءة منه والتوبة أهم قواعد

الإسلام وهي أول مقامات سالكي طريق الآخرة
# [2703] قوله صلىالله عليه وسلم من تاب قبل أن تطلع الشمس من مغربها تاب

الله عليه قال العلماء هذا حد لقبول التوبة وقد جاء في الحديث الصحيح إن

للتوبة بابا مفتوحا فلا تزال مقبولة حتى يغلق فإذا طلعت الشمس من مغربها

أغلق وامتنعت التوبة على من لم يكن تاب قبل ذلك وهو معنى قوله تعالى يوم

يأتي بعض آيات ربك لا ينفع نفسا إيمانها لم تكن آمنت من قبل أو كسبت في

إيمانها خيرا ومعنى تاب الله عليه قبل توبته ورضي بها وللتوبة شرط آخر وهو

أن يتوب قبل الغرغرة كما جاء في الحديث الصحيح وأما في حالة الغرغرة وهي

حالة النزع فلا تقبل توبته ولا غيرها ولا تنفذ وصيته ولا غيرها

| (باب استحباب خفض الصوت بالذكر إلافى المواضع التى 
# ورد الشرع برفعه فيها كالتلبية وغيرها وإستحباب الاكثار من قول لاحول

ولاقوة إلا بالله
# [2704] قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم للناس حين جهروا بالتكبير أيها الناس

اربعوا على أنفسكم انكم ليس)
# 
# تدعون أصم ولاغائبا إنكم تدعون سميعا قريبا وهو معكم اربعوا بهمزة وصل

وبفتح الباء الموحدة معناه ارفقوا بأنفسكم واخفضوا أصواتكم فإن رفع الصوت

إنما يفعله الإنسان لبعد من يخاطبه ليسمعه وأنتم تدعون الله تعالى وليس  هو

بأصم ولاغائب بل هو سميع قريب وهو معكم بالعلم والإحاطة ففيه الندب إلى خفض

الصوت بالذكر إذا لم تدع حاجة إلى رفعه فإنه إذا خفضه كان أبلغ في توقيره

وتعظيمه فان دعت حاجةالى الرفع رفع كما جاءت به أحاديث وقوله صلى الله عليه

وسلم في هذه الرواية الأخرى الذى تدعونه أقرب إلى أحدكم من عنق راحلة أحدكم

هو بمعنى ما سبق وحاصله أنه مجاز كقوله تعالى ونحن أقرب إليه من حبل الوريد

والمراد تحقيق سماع الدعاء قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم لا حول ولا قوة إلا

بالله كنز من كنوز الجنة قال العلماء سبب ذلك أنها كلمةاستسلام وتفويض إلى

الله تعالى واعتراف بالإذعان له وأنه لاصانع غيره ولاراد لأمره وأن العبد

لايملك شيئا من الأمر ومعنى الكنز هنا أنه ثواب مدخر في الجنة وهو ثواب

نفيس كما أن الكنز أنفس أموالكم قال أهل اللغة الحول الحركة والحيلة أي لا

حركة ولا استطاعة ولا حيلة إلا بمشيئة الله تعالى وقيل معناه لا حول في دفع

شر ولا قوة في تحصيل خير إلا بالله وقيل لا حول عن معصية الله إلا بعصمته

ولاقوة على طاعته
# 
# إلا بمعونته وحكى هذا عن بن مسعود رضي الله عنه وكله متقارب قال أهل

اللغة ويعبر عن هذه الكلمة بالحوقلة والحولقة وبالأول جزم الأزهري والجمهور

وبالثاني جزم الجوهري ويقال أيضا لا حيل ولا قوة فى لغة غريبة حكاها

الجوهرى وغيره
#
chapters.anchors:
- Root: غ-ي-ن (ghayn)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: A covering or veil that envelops the heart, obscuring its clarity.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): A transient state of heedlessness or awe that overtakes the heart, distinct from permanent sin.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal in describing a physical or spiritual covering; metaphorical when applied to the heart's state of reverence.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clause (al-sharṭ wa al-jawāb) — The protasis "if he repents" governs the apodosis "God accepts," with the condition's temporal limit specified by the following clause.
chapters.translation:
I say: The author of the commentary (al-Ḥāshī) said: The fear of the prophets and angels is a fear of magnification (khawf iʿẓām), even though they are secure from the punishment of God Almighty. And it was said: It is probable that this "veil" (al-ghayn) is a state of awe and magnification that covers the heart, and his seeking forgiveness is an act of gratitude, as has preceded. And it was said: It is something that befalls pure hearts from what the soul whispers to itself — and God knows best.

Chapter on Repentance (Bāb al-Tawbah): His saying, peace be upon him: "O people, repent to God, for I repent a hundred times a day." This command to repent corresponds to His saying, the Exalted: {«And repent to God all together, O believers»} (Quran 24:31), and His saying, the Exalted: {«O you who believe, repent to God with sincere repentance»} (Quran 66:8). The explanation of the cause of his seeking forgiveness and repentance, peace be upon him, has already preceded in the previous chapter. And we are more in need of seeking forgiveness and repentance. Our companions and other scholars said: Repentance (tawbah) has three conditions: that one desists from the sin, that one regrets having committed it, and that one resolves with a firm resolve (ʿazm jāzim) never to return to the like of it ever again. If the sin involves a human right, then it has a fourth condition: restoring the due right to its owner or obtaining his absolution. Repentance is the greatest of the foundations of Islam, and it is the first station of the wayfarers on the path to the Hereafter.

[2703] His saying, peace be upon him: "Whoever repents before the sun rises from its west, God accepts his repentance." The scholars said: This is a limit for the acceptance of repentance. It has come in the authentic hadith that repentance has an open door, and it remains accepted until it is closed. When the sun rises from the west, it is closed, and repentance is prevented for whoever had not repented before that. This is the meaning of His saying, the Exalted: {«On the day when some signs of your Lord come, no soul will benefit from its faith if it had not believed before, or had earned good through its faith»} (Quran 6:158). The meaning of "God accepts his repentance" is that He turns toward him with acceptance and is pleased with it. Repentance has another condition: that one repents before the gurgling of death (al-ghargharah), as has come in the authentic hadith. As for the state of ghargharah — which is the state of death throes — his repentance is not accepted, nor anything else, and his will is not executed, nor anything else.

Chapter on the Recommendation of Lowering the Voice in Dhikr, Except in Places Where the Law Has Prescribed Raising It, Such as the Talbiyah and Others, and the Recommendation of Increasing the Saying "Lā ḥawla wa lā quwwata illā billāh" (There is no might and no power except with God).

[2704] His saying, peace be upon him, to the people when they raised their voices in the takbīr: "O people, be gentle with yourselves (arbiʿū ʿalā anfusikum), for you are not calling upon a deaf one or an absent one. You are calling upon a Hearing, Near One, and He is with you." "Arbiʿū" is with a conjunctive hamzah and with the opening of the bāʾ (i.e., arbiʿū), meaning: be gentle with yourselves and lower your voices. For raising the voice is only done by a person due to the distance of the one being addressed, so that he may hear him. But you are calling upon God Almighty, and He is not deaf nor absent. Rather, He is Hearing and Near, and He is with you by knowledge and encompassing. In this is the recommendation to lower the voice in dhikr when there is no need to raise it. For when one lowers it, it is more effective in showing reverence and veneration. If there is a need to raise it, one raises it, as has come in the hadiths. His saying, peace be upon him, in this other narration: "The One you are calling upon is nearer to one of you than the neck of his riding beast" — this is equivalent to what has preceded. Its gist is that it is metaphorical (majāz), like His saying, the Exalted: {«And We are nearer to him than his jugular vein»} (Quran 50:16). The intended meaning is the realization of His hearing of the supplication.

His saying, peace be upon him: "Lā ḥawla wa lā quwwata illā billāh is a treasure from the treasures of Paradise." The scholars said: The reason for this is that it is a word of submission (istislām) and delegation (tafwīḍ) to God Almighty, and an acknowledgment of yielding to Him, and that there is no agent other than Him, and no repeller of His command, and that the servant owns nothing of the matter. The meaning of "treasure" here is that it is a reward stored up in Paradise, and it is a precious reward, just as a treasure is the most precious of your wealth. The linguists said: "al-ḥawl" is movement (al-ḥarakah) and stratagem (al-ḥīlah), i.e., there is no movement, no ability, and no stratagem except by the will of God Almighty. And it was said: Its meaning is: there is no power to repel evil, and no strength to attain good, except through God. And it was said: There is no turning away from disobedience to God except by His protection, and no strength to obey Him except by His assistance. This was narrated from Ibn Masʿūd, may God be pleased with him, and all of it is close in meaning. The linguists said: This word is expressed as "al-ḥawqalah" and "al-ḥawlaqah." The first was affirmed by al-Azharī and the majority, and the second was affirmed by al-Jawharī. It is also said "lā ḥayla wa lā quwwah" in a rare dialect narrated by al-Jawharī and others.
