chapters.arabic_text:
أركان الإقلاع والندم على فعل تلك المعصية والعزم على أن لايعود إليها أبدا

فإن كانت المعصية لحق آدمي فلها ركن رابع وهو التحلل من صاحب ذلك الحق

وأصلها الندم وهو ركنها الأعظم واتفقوا على أن التوبة من جميع المعاصي

واجبة وأنها واجبة على الفور لايجوز تأخيرها سواء كانت المعصية صغيرة

أوكبيرة والتوبة من مهمات الإسلام وقواعده المتأكدة ووجوبها عند أهل السنة

بالشرع وعند المعتزلة بالعقل ولا يجب على الله قبولها إذا وجدت بشروطها

عقلا عند أهل السنة لكنه سبحانه وتعالى يقبلها كرما وفضلا وعرفنا قبولها

بالشرع والإجماع  خلافا لهم وإذا تاب من ذنب ثم ذكره هل يجب تجديد الندم فيه

خلاف لأصحابنا وغيرهم من أهل السنة قال بن الأنباري يجب وقال إمام الحرمين

لا يجب وتصح التوبة من ذنب وإن كان مصرا على ذنب آخر وإذا تاب توبة
# 
# صحيحة بشروطها ثم عاود ذلك الذنب كتب عليه ذلك الذنب الثاني ولم تبطل

توبته هذا مذهب أهل السنة فى المسئلتين وخالفت المعتزلة فيهما قال أصحابنا

ولو تكررت التوبة ومعاودة الذنب صحت ثم توبة الكافر من كفره مقطوع بقبولها

وما سواها من أنواع التوبة هل قبولها مقطوع به أم مظنون فيه خلاف لأهل

السنة واختار إمام الحرمين أنه مظنون وهو الأصح والله أعلم
# [2675] قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (قال الله تعالى أنا تعالى عند ظن عبدي

بي وأنا معه حيث يذكرني ومن تقرب إلي شبرا) إلخ هذا القدر من الحديث سبق

شرحه واضحا في أول كتاب الذكر ووقع في النسخ هنا حيث يذكرني بالثاء المثلثة

ووقع في الأحاديث السابقة هناك حين بالنون وكلاهما من رواية أبي هريرة

وبالنون هو المشهور وكلاهما صحيح ظاهر المعنى قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (لله

أشد فرحا بتوبة عبده من أحدكم يجد ضالته بالفلاة) قال العلماء فرح الله

تعالى هو رضاه وقال المازري الفرح ينقسم على وجوه منها السرور والسرور

يقاربه الرضا بالمسرور به قال
# 
# فالمراد هنا أن الله تعالى يرضى توبة عبده أشد مما يرضى واجد ضالته

بالفلاة فعبر عن الرضا بالفرح تأكيدا لمعنى الرضا في نفس السامع ومبالغة في

تقريره
# [2744] قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (في أرض دوية مهلكة) أما دوية فاتفق

العلماء على أنها بفتح الدال وتشديد الواو والياء جميعا وذكر مسلم في

الرواية التي بعد هذه رواية أبي بكر بن أبي شيبة أرض داوية بزيادة ألف وهي

بتشديد الياء أيضا وكلاهما صحيح قال أهل اللغة الدوية الأرض القفر والفلاة

الخالية قال الخليل هي المفازة قالوا ويقال دوية وداوية فأما الدوية فمنسوب

إلى الدو بتشديد الواو وهى البرية التى لانبات بها وأما  الداوية فهي على

إبدال إحدى الواوين ألفا كما قيل في النسب إلى طي طائي وأما المهلكة فهي

بفتح الميم وبفتح اللام وكسرها وهي موضع خوف الهلاك ويقال لها مفازة قيل

إنه من قولهم فوز الرجل إذا هلك وقيل على سبيل التفاؤل بفوزه ونجاته منها

كما يقال للديغ سليم
# [2744] قوله (دخلت على عبد الله أعوده وهو مريض فحدثنا بحديثين حديثا عن

نفسه وحديثا عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم) ثم ذكر حديث رسول الله صلى

الله عليه وسلم ولم يذكر حديث عبد الله عن نفسه وقد ذكر البخاري في صحيحه

والترمذي وغيرهما وهو قوله المؤمن يرى ذنوبه كأنه قاعد تحت جبل يخاف أن يقع

عليه والفاجر يرى
# 
# ذنوبه كذباب مر على أنفه فقال به هكذا قوله في رواية أبي بكر بن أبي شيبة

(من رجل بداوية) هكذا هو في النسخ من رجل بالنون وهو الصواب قال القاضي

ووقع في بعضها مر رجل بالراء وهو تصحيف لأن مقصود مسلم أن يبين الخلاف في

دوية وداوية وأما لفظة من فمتفق عليها في الروايتين ولا معنى للراء هنا
# [2745] قوله (حمل زاده ومزاده) هو بفتح الميم قال القاضي كأنه اسم جنس

للمزادة وهي القربة العظيمة سميت بذلك لأنه يزاد فيها من جلدآخر قوله

(وانسل بعيره) أي ذهب في خفية قوله (فسعى شرفا فلم ير شيئا) قال القاضي

يحتمل أنه أراد بالشرف هنا الطلق والغلوة كما في الحديث الآخر فاستنت شرفا

أو شرفين قال ويحتمل أن المراد هنا الشرف من الأرض لينظر منه هل يراها قال

وهذا أظهر
# [2746] قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم
# 
# (مر بجذل شجرة) هو بكسر الجيم وفتحها وبالذال المعجمة وهو أصل الشجرة

القائم قوله (قلنا شديدا) أي نراه فرحا شديدا أو يفرح فرحا شديدا قوله

(حدثنا يحيى بن يحيى وجعفر بن حميد) هكذا صوابه بن حميد وقد صحف في بعض

النسخ قال الحافظ وليس لمسلم في صحيحه عن جعفر هذا غير هذا الحديث قوله صلى

الله عليه وسلم في حديث أنس من  رواية هداب بن خالد (لله أشد فرحا بتوبة

عبده من أحدكم إذا استيقظ على بعيره قد أضله بأرض فلاة هكذا هو في جميع

النسخ إذا استيقظ على بعيره وكذا قال القاضي عياض أنه اتفقت عليه رواة صحيح

مسلم قال قال بعضهم وهو وهم وصوابه إذا سقط على بعيره أي وقع عليه وصادفه

من غير
# 
# قصد قال القاضي وقد جاء في الحديث الاخر عن بن مسعود قال فأرجع إلى
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ت-و-ب (t-w-b)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Return, turning back; the act of reverting from a state to its origin
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The soul's return from sin to obedience, entailing cessation, regret, and resolve
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense is "return"; metaphorically denotes the servant's return to God's favor through cessation of sin
- Root: ن-د-م (n-d-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Regret, remorse; the heart's pain over what has passed
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The core (rukn aʿẓam) of repentance—the affective recognition of sin's gravity
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: biting of the hand (as in Quranic idiom); metaphorical: psychological anguish over transgression
- Root: ع-ز-م (ʿ-z-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Firm resolve, determination; the knotting of intention
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The volitional commitment to non-recurrence, distinguishing sincere tawbah from mere verbal confession
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: hardening of a thing; metaphorical: the heart's firmness against relapse
- Sībawayh Rule: ʿAṭf al-Nasaq (Coordination of appositives) — The three pillars (cessation, regret, resolve) are coordinated as equal constituents of a single predicate, with the fourth (restitution) conditionally appended via fa-in kānat, indicating a conditional protasis governing an additional requirement.
chapters.translation:
I say: The pillars of repentance (tawbah) are three: cessation (iqlāʿ) from the act of disobedience, regret (nadam) over having committed that transgression, and firm resolve (ʿazm) never to return to it again.

Know that if the transgression involves a right owed to a human being (ḥaqq ādamī), then it has a fourth pillar, namely, seeking release (taḥallul) from the one who holds that right.

The foundation of repentance is regret, and it is its greatest pillar. The scholars are in agreement that repentance from all sins is obligatory (wājibah), and that it is obligatory immediately (ʿalā al-fawr); it is not permissible to delay it, whether the sin be minor (ṣaghīrah) or major (kabīrah). Repentance is among the most important matters of Islam and its firmly established principles (qawāʿiduhu al-muʾakkadah). Its obligation, according to the People of the Sunnah (Ahl al-Sunnah), is established by the Sacred Law (al-sharʿ); according to the Muʿtazilah, it is established by reason (al-ʿaql). It is not obligatory upon God—exalted is He—to accept it, when it is found with its conditions, as a matter of reason, according to the People of the Sunnah. Rather, He—glorified and exalted—accepts it as generosity (karman) and favor (faḍlan), and we have come to know its acceptance through the Sacred Law and consensus (ijmāʿ), contrary to them (the Muʿtazilah).

If a person repents from a sin and then recalls it (in memory), is it obligatory to renew regret over it? There is a difference of opinion among our companions (the Shāfiʿīs) and others of the People of the Sunnah. Ibn al-Anbārī said: It is obligatory. Imām al-Ḥaramayn (al-Juwaynī) said: It is not obligatory.

Repentance from one sin is valid even if the person persists in another sin. And if one repents a sound repentance with its conditions, then returns to that same sin, that second sin is recorded against him, and his (prior) repentance is not nullified. This is the doctrine of the People of the Sunnah on both questions, and the Muʿtazilah opposed them on both.

Our companions said: Even if repentance and the recurrence of sin are repeated multiple times, the repentance remains valid.

Then, the repentance of the disbeliever (kāfir) from his disbelief is definitively known to be accepted (maqṭūʿ bi-qabūlihā). As for other types of repentance—whether their acceptance is definitively known or merely conjectured (maẓnūn fīhi)—there is a difference of opinion among the People of the Sunnah. Imām al-Ḥaramayn chose the view that it is conjectured, and this is the more correct (al-aṣaḥḥ) opinion. And God knows best.

[2675] His saying—peace and blessings be upon him: (God—exalted is He—said: "I am as My servant thinks of Me, and I am with him wherever he remembers Me. Whoever draws near to Me by a handspan...") — this portion of the hadith has already been explained clearly at the beginning of the Book of Remembrance (Kitāb al-Dhikr). In the copies (of Muslim) here, it occurs as "ḥaythu yadhkurunī" with the dotted thāʾ (thāʾ muthallathah). In the earlier hadiths there, it occurred as "ḥīna" with the nūn. Both are narrated on the authority of Abū Hurayrah. The version with the nūn is the well-known one (al-mashhūr), and both are sound (ṣaḥīḥ) with clear meaning.

His saying—peace and blessings be upon him: (God is more intensely joyful at the repentance of His servant than one of you who finds his lost camel in a desolate wilderness (al-falāh)). The scholars said: The joy (faraḥ) of God—exalted is He—is His good pleasure (riḍā). Al-Māzarī said: Joy is divided into various kinds, among them delight (surūr), and delight is accompanied by pleasure (riḍā) with that which delights. He said: So the intended meaning here is that God—exalted is He—is pleased with His servant's repentance more intensely than the one who finds his lost camel in the wilderness is pleased. He expressed pleasure by the term "joy" (faraḥ) to emphasize the meaning of pleasure in the soul of the listener and to exaggerate in establishing it.

[2744] His saying—peace and blessings be upon him: (in a desolate, destructive land (arḍ dawiyyah muhlikah)). As for "dawiyyah," the scholars are agreed that it is with the fatḥah on the dāl and the tashdīd on both the wāw and the yāʾ. Muslim mentioned in the narration that follows this one—the narration of Abū Bakr ibn Abī Shaybah—"arḍ dāwiyyah" with an increased alif, and it is also with tashdīd on the yāʾ. Both are sound. The people of language (ahl al-lughah) said: "al-dawiyyah" is the barren land (al-qafr) and the empty wilderness (al-falāh al-khāliyah). Al-Khalīl said: It is the waterless desert (al-mafāzah). They said: One says "dawiyyah" and "dāwiyyah." As for "dawiyyah," it is a relative adjective (mansūb) to "daww" with tashdīd on the wāw, which is the barren land in which there is no vegetation. As for "dāwiyyah," it is formed by substituting one of the two wāws with an alif, just as one says, in the relative adjective to Ṭayy, "ṭāʾī." As for "muhlikah," it is with fatḥah on the mīm and with fatḥah or kasrah on the lām, and it is a place where destruction (halāk) is feared. It is also called "mafāzah." It is said that this is from their saying "fāza al-rajul" when he perishes, and it is said (that it is named thus) by way of optimistic augury (tafāʾul) of his success (fawz) and deliverance from it, just as one says of the one stung by a scorpion, "salīm" (safe).

[2744] His saying: (I entered upon ʿAbd Allāh to visit him while he was sick, and he narrated to us two hadiths—a hadith from himself and a hadith from the Messenger of God—peace and blessings be upon him). Then he mentioned the hadith of the Messenger of God—peace and blessings be upon him—but did not mention the hadith of ʿAbd Allāh from himself. Al-Bukhārī has mentioned it in his Ṣaḥīḥ, as have al-Tirmidhī and others, and it is his saying: "The believer sees his sins as if he were sitting beneath a mountain, fearing that it might fall upon him, while the wicked one sees his sins as a fly that passed over his nose—and he waves it away like this."

His saying in the narration of Abū Bakr ibn Abī Shaybah: (from a man in a desolate land (min rajulin bidāwiyyah)). Thus it is in the copies: "min rajulin" with the nūn, and this is correct. Al-Qāḍī said: In some of them it occurs as "marra rajulun" with the rāʾ, and this is a corruption (taṣḥīf), because Muslim's intent is to clarify the difference between "dawiyyah" and "dāwiyyah." As for the word "min," it is agreed upon in both narrations, and there is no meaning for the rāʾ here.

[2745] His saying: (he carried his provision (zādahu) and his waterskin (mizādahu)). It is with fatḥah on the mīm. Al-Qāḍī said: It is as if it is a generic noun (ism jins) for "mizādah," which is the great water-skin (al-qirbah al-ʿaẓīmah). It is so named because additional leather (zīdah) is added to it from another hide.

His saying: (and his camel slipped away (insalla baʿīruhu))—that is, it went away secretly (dhahaba fī khufyah).

His saying: (so he climbed to a high place (sharaf) and saw nothing). Al-Qāḍī said: It is possible that he meant by "al-sharaf" here the elevated tract of land (al-ṭalaq) and the distance of a bowshot (al-ghulwah), as in the other hadith: "so I raced to a high place (sharaf) or two." He said: And it is possible that the intended meaning here is the elevated ground (al-sharaf min al-arḍ) from which one looks to see whether he can see it. He said: And this latter is more apparent (aẓhar).

[2746] His saying—peace and blessings be upon him: (he passed by the stump of a tree (jidhl shajarah)). It is with kasrah on the jīm and also with fatḥah, and with the dotted dhāl (al-dhāl al-muʿjamah), and it is the standing base of the tree (aṣl al-shajarah al-qāʾim).

His saying: (we said: intense (shadīdan))—that is, we see him rejoicing intensely, or he rejoices with intense joy.

His saying: (Yaḥyā ibn Yaḥyā and Jaʿfar ibn Ḥumayd narrated to us). Thus is its correct form: "ibn Ḥumayd." It has been corrupted (ṣuḥḥifa) in some copies. Al-Ḥāfiẓ said: Muslim does not have, in his Ṣaḥīḥ, from this Jaʿfar anything other than this single hadith.

His saying—peace and blessings be upon him—in the hadith of Anas, from the narration of Haddāb ibn Khālid: (God is more intensely joyful at the repentance of His servant than one of you when he wakes up upon his camel, having lost it in a desolate land). Thus it is in all the copies: "when he wakes up upon his camel (idhā istayqaẓa ʿalā baʿīrihi)." Likewise, al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ said that the narrators of Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim are agreed upon it. He said: Some of them said: It is an error (wahm), and the correct form is "when he falls upon his camel (idhā saqaṭa ʿalā baʿīrihi)"—that is, he falls upon it and encounters it without intending to. Al-Qāḍī said: And it has come in the other hadith, on the authority of Ibn Masʿūd: "So I returned to..."

chapters.title_en: Section 941 — On the Falling Away of Sins through Seeking Forgiveness (Tawbah), the Virtue of Constant Remembrance and Reflection, and the Vastness of Allah's Mercy
chapters.arabic_text:
المكان الذي كنت فيه فأنام حتى أموت فوضع رأسه على ساعده ليموت فاستيقظ

وعنده راحلته وفي كتاب البخاري فنام نومة فرفع رأسه فإذا راحلته عنده قال

القاضي وهذا يصحح رواية استيقظ قال ولكن وجه الكلام وسياقه يدل على سقط كما

رواه البخاري قوله (أضله بأرض فلاة) أي فقده

| (باب سقوط الذنوب بالا ستغفار توبة
# [2748] قوله (عن محمد بن
# قيس قاص عمر بن عبد العزيز) هكذا هو في جميع نسخ بلادنا قاص بالصاد

المهملة المشددة من القصص قال القاضي عياض ورواه بعضهم قاضي بالضاد المعجمة

والياء والوجهان مذكوران فيه ممن ذكرهما البخاري في التاريخ وروي عنه قال

كنت قاصا لعمر بن عبد العزيز وهو أمير بالمدينة قوله (عن أبي أيوب أنه قال

حين حضرته الوفاة كنت كتمت عنكم شيئا) إنما كتمه أولا مخافة اتكالهم على

سعة رحمة الله تعالى وانهما كهم في المعاصي وإنما)
# 
# حدث به عند وفاته لئلا يكون كاتما للعلم وربما لم يكن أحد يحفظه غيره

فتعين عليه أداؤه وهو نحو قوله في الحديث الآ خر فأخبر بها معاذ عند موته

تأثما أي خشية الإثم بكتمان العلم وقد سبق شرحه فى كتاب الايمان والله أعلم

| باب فضل دوام الذكر والفكر فى أمور الآخرة
# والمراقبة وجواز ترك ذلك فى بعض الأوقات والاشتغال بالدنيا
# [2750] قوله (قطن بن نسير) بضم النون وفتح السين قوله (عن حنظلة الأسيدي)

ضبطوه بوجهين أصحهما وأشهرهما ضم الهمزة وفتح السين وكسر الباء المشددة

والثاني كذلك إلا أنه بإسكان الياء ولم يذكر القاضي إلا هذا الثاني وهو

منسوب إلى بني  أسيد بطن من بني تميم قوله (وكان من كتاب رسول الله صلى الله

عليه وسلم) هكذا هو في جميع نسخ بلادنا وذكره القاضي)
# 
# عن بعض شيوخهم كذلك وعن أكثرهم وكان من أصحاب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

وكلاهما صحيح لكن الأول أشهر في الرواية وأظهر في المعنى وقد قال في

الرواية التي بعد هذه عن حنظلة الكاتب قوله (يذكرنا بالنار والجنة كأنا رأي

عين) قال القاضي ضبطناه رأي عين بالرفع أي كأنا بحال من يراها بعينه قال

ويصح النصب على المصدر أي نراها رأي عين قوله (عافسنا الأزواج والأولاد

والضيعات) هو بالفاء والسين المهملة قال الهروي وغيره معناه حاولنا ذلك

ومارسناه واشتغلنا به أي عالجنا معايشنا وحظوظنا والضيعات جمع ضيعة بالضاد

المعجمة وهي معاش الرجل من مال أو حرفة أو صناعة وروى الخطابي هذا الحرف

عانسنا بالنون قال ومعناه لاعبنا ورواه بن قتيبة بالشين المعجمة قال ومعناه

عانقنا والأول هو المعروف وهو أعم قوله (نافق حنظلة) معناه أنه خاف أنه

منافق حيث كان يحصل له الخوف في مجلس النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ويظهر عليه

ذلك مع المراقبة والفكر والإقبال على الآخرة فإذا خرج اشتغل
# 
# بالزوجة والأولاد ومعاش الدنيا وأصل النفاق إظهار ما يكتم خلافه من الشر

فخاف أن يكون ذلك نفاقا فأعلمهم النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه ليس بنفاق

وأنهم لا يكلفون الدوام على ذلك ساعة وساعة أي ساعة كذا وساعة كذا قوله

(فقلت يا رسول الله نافق حنظلة فقال مه) قال القاضي معناه الاستفهام أي ما

تقول والهاء هنا هي هاء السكت قال ويحتمل أنها للكف والزجر والتعظيم لذلك
#

| باب سعة رحمة الله تعالى وأنها تغلب غضبه
# ))
# [2751] قوله تعالى (إن رحمتي تغلب غضبي) وفي رواية سبقت رحمتي غضبي قال

العلماء غضب الله تعالى ورضاه يرجعان إلى معنى الإرادة فإرادته الإثابة

للمطيع ومنفعة العبد تسمى رضا ورحمة وإرادته عقاب العاصي وخذلانه تسمى غضبا

وإرادته سبحانه وتعالى صفة له قديمة يريد بها جميع المرادات قالوا والمراد

بالسبق والغلبة هنا  كثرة الرحمة وشمولها كما يقال غلب على فلان الكرم

والشجاعة إذا كثرا منه
# [2752] قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (جعل الله الرحمة مائة جزء إلى آخره) هذه

الأحاديث من أحاديث الرجاء والبشارة للمسلمين قال العلماء لأنه إذا حصل

للإنسان من رحمة واحدة في هذه الدار المبنية على الأكدار الإسلام والقرآن

والصلاة والرحمة في قلبه وغير ذلك مما أنعم الله تعالى به فكيف الظن بمائة
# 
# رحمة في الدار الآخرة وهي دار القرار ودار الجزاء والله أعلم هكذا وقع في

نسخ بلادنا جميعا جعل الله الرحمة مائة جزء وذكر القاضي جعل الله الرحم

بحذف الهاء وبضم الراء قال ورويناه بضم الراء
# 
# ويجوز فتحها ومعناه الرحمة
# [2754] قوله (فإذا امرأة من السبي تبتغي) هكذا هو في جميع نسخ صحيح مسلم

تبتغي من الابتغاء وهو الطلب قال القاضي عياض وهذا وهم والصواب ما في رواية

البخاري تسعى بالسين من السعى قلت كلاهما صواب لاوهم فيه فهي ساعية وطالبة

مبتغية لابنها والله أعلم
# [2756] قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (في الرجل الذي لم يعمل حسنة أوصى بنيه

أن يحرقوه ويذروه في البحر والبر وقال فوالله لئن قدر علي ربي ليعذبني

عذابا ما عذبه أحدا ثم قال في آخره لم فعلت هذا قال
# 
# من خشيتك يا رب وأنت أعلم فغفر له) اختلف العلماء في تأويل هذا الحديث
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ق-ص-ص (qa-ṣād-ṣād)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To follow a trace, to narrate a story (qaṣaṣ); one who recounts tales or narratives.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological usage, qaṣaṣ refers to the recounting of prophetic narratives and moral exhortations, distinct from mere entertainment.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense is "to trace footsteps" (taqaṣṣī al-athar); metaphorically extended to "narrating" as one follows the sequence of events.
- Sībawayh Rule: Naṣb on the Maṣdar (المصدر المنصوب) — When "ra'y al-ʿayn" is read in the accusative, it functions as an absolute object (mafʿūl muṭlaq) indicating the manner of seeing, i.e., "we see it with the seeing of the eye."
chapters.translation:
I say: The place where he had been, he slept until he died — so he placed his head on his forearm to die, then he awoke. And his riding beast was with him. In al-Bukhārī's book: "He slept a sleep, then raised his head, and behold his riding beast was with him."

Al-Qāḍī said: This confirms the narration "he awoke." But he said: The wording and its context indicate an omission (saqaṭ), as al-Bukhārī narrated it. His saying "I lost it in an empty land" (aḍallahu bi-arḍi falāh) means: he could not find it.

| Chapter: The Falling Away of Sins through Seeking Forgiveness (Tawbah)

# [2748] His saying (on the authority of Muḥammad ibn Qays, the storyteller (qāṣṣ) of ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz): Thus it is in all copies of our lands — qāṣṣ with the unpointed ṣād, doubled, from al-qaṣaṣ (storytelling). Al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ said: Some narrated it as qāḍī with the pointed ḍād and yā'. Both readings are mentioned by those who cited them, including al-Bukhārī in al-Tārīkh. It is narrated from him that he said: I was a storyteller for ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz while he was governor of Medina.

His saying (on the authority of Abū Ayyūb that he said when death approached him: "I concealed something from you"): He concealed it initially only out of fear that they would rely upon the vastness of Allah's mercy and become lax in committing sins. He only narrated it at his death so that he would not be one who conceals knowledge — and perhaps no one else preserved it besides him, so its transmission became incumbent upon him. This resembles his saying in the subsequent hadith, where Muʿādh informed them of it at his death, "tā'aththuman" — i.e., fearing sin (ithm) in concealing knowledge. Its explanation has already preceded in the Book of Faith (Kitāb al-Īmān). And Allah knows best.

| Chapter: The Virtue of Constant Remembrance (dhikr) and Reflection (fikr) upon Matters of the Hereafter, and Vigilance (murāqabah), and the Permissibility of Abandoning That at Certain Times and Occupying Oneself with the World

# [2750] His saying (Qaṭan ibn Nusayr): With ḍamma on the nūn and fatḥa on the sīn. His saying (on the authority of Ḥanẓalah al-Usayyidī): They fixed it with two readings — the more correct and more famous being ḍamma on the hamza, fatḥa on the sīn, and kasra on the doubled bā'; the second is the same except with sukūn on the yā'. Al-Qāḍī mentioned only this second one. He is attributed to Banū Usayyid, a sub-tribe of Banū Tamīm.

His saying ("and he was among the scribes of the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him"): Thus it is in all copies of our lands, and al-Qāḍī mentioned it from some of his shaykhs likewise, and from most of them: "and he was among the companions of the Prophet, peace be upon him." Both are correct, but the first is more famous in transmission and more apparent in meaning. He said in the narration that follows this one, concerning Ḥanẓalah the scribe.

His saying ("he reminds us of the Fire and the Garden as if we see them with the seeing of the eye" (ka'annā ra'y al-ʿayn)): Al-Qāḍī said: We fixed it as ra'y al-ʿayn in the nominative — i.e., as if we are in the state of one who sees them with his own eye. He said: The accusative is also valid, as an absolute object (maṣdar), i.e., we see them with the seeing of the eye.

His saying ("we frolicked with our spouses, children, and properties" (ʿāfasnā al-azwāj wa-al-awlād wa-al-ḍayʿāt)): It is with fā' and unpointed sīn. Al-Harawī and others said: Its meaning is we pursued that, practiced it, and occupied ourselves with it — i.e., we attended to our livelihoods and our shares. Al-ḍayʿāt is the plural of ḍayʿah, with the pointed ḍād — the means of a man's subsistence, whether from wealth, a craft, or a trade. Al-Khaṭṭābī narrated this word as ʿānasnā with nūn, saying its meaning is "we played." Ibn Qutaybah narrated it with pointed shīn, saying its meaning is "we embraced." The first is the well-known reading and is more comprehensive.

His saying ("Ḥanẓalah has become a hypocrite" (nāfaqa Ḥanẓalah)): Its meaning is that he feared he was a hypocrite (munāfiq), because fear would overcome him in the assembly of the Prophet, peace be upon him, and that would appear upon him along with vigilance, reflection, and turning toward the Hereafter. But when he went out, he occupied himself with his wife, children, and worldly livelihood. The origin of hypocrisy (nifāq) is displaying what conceals its opposite of evil. So he feared that this might be hypocrisy. The Prophet, peace be upon him, informed them that it was not hypocrisy, and that they are not obligated to persist in that state continuously — "hour and hour" (sāʿatan wa-sāʿatan), i.e., at one time thus and at another time thus.

His saying ("I said: O Messenger of Allah, Ḥanẓalah has become a hypocrite. He said: 'Mah!'"): Al-Qāḍī said: Its meaning is interrogative — i.e., "What are you saying?" The hā' here is the hā' of pausing (hā' al-sakt). He said: It may also be for restraint, rebuke, and magnifying that matter.

| Chapter: The Vastness of Allah's Mercy and That It Overwhelms His Wrath

# [2751] His saying, exalted is He: {«Inna raḥmatī taghlibu ghaḍabī»} ("Indeed My mercy overwhelms My wrath"). In another narration: "My mercy has preceded My wrath." The scholars said: The wrath (ghaḍab) of Allah and His good pleasure (riḍā) both revert to the meaning of will (irādah). His willing reward for the obedient and benefit for the servant is called good pleasure and mercy; His willing punishment for the disobedient and His abandonment (khidhlān) of him is called wrath. His will, glorified and exalted is He, is an eternal attribute of His by which He wills all things that are willed. They said: The intended meaning of "precedence" and "overwhelming" here is the abundance of mercy and its comprehensiveness — just as one says "generosity and courage overwhelmed so-and-so" when they are abundant from him.

# [2752] His saying, peace be upon him ("Allah has made mercy into one hundred parts... to the end"): These hadiths are among the hadiths of hope (rajā') and glad tidings for the Muslims. The scholars said: For when a person obtains from a single mercy in this abode — which is built upon tribulations — Islam, the Qur'an, prayer, and the mercy in his heart, and other things with which Allah has favored him, then what must one expect from one hundred mercies in the Hereafter, which is the abode of permanence and the abode of recompense? And Allah knows best. Thus it occurred in all copies of our lands: "Allah has made mercy into one hundred parts." Al-Qāḍī mentioned "Allah has made al-raḥm" (with the hā' elided and ḍamma on the rā'), and he said: We narrated it with ḍamma on the rā', and fatḥa is also permissible — its meaning being mercy (al-raḥmah).

# [2754] His saying ("then behold, a woman from the captives was seeking" (tabtaghī)): Thus it is in all copies of Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim — tabtaghī from ibtighā', which is seeking. Al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ said: This is an error (wahm), and the correct version is what is in al-Bukhārī's narration: tasʿā with sīn, from al-saʿy (striving). I say: Both are correct — there is no error in it — for she is both striving (sāʿiyah) and seeking (ṭālibah), searching for her son. And Allah knows best.

# [2756] His saying, peace be upon him (concerning the man who had not done any good deed, who instructed his sons to burn him and scatter him over the sea and the land, and said: "By Allah, if my Lord has power over me, He will punish me with a punishment He has not inflicted upon anyone" — then he said at its end: "He said: Why did you do this? He said: Out of fear of You, O Lord, and You know best. So He forgave him"): The scholars differed concerning the interpretation of this hadith.

chapters.title_en: Section 942 — On the Interpretations of the Saying "If Allah Has Decreed Punishment Upon Me" and Related Matters
chapters.arabic_text:
فقالت طائفة لايصح حمل هذا على أنه أراد نفي قدرة الله فإن الشاك في قدرة

الله تعالى كافر وقد قال في آخر الحديث إنه إنما فعل هذا من خشية الله

تعالى والكافر لا يخشى الله تعالى ولا يغفر له قال هؤلاء فيكون له تأويلان

أحدهما أن معناه لئن قدر علي العذاب أي قضاه يقال منه قدر بالتخفيف وقدر

بالتشديد بمعنى واحد والثاني إن قدر هنا بمعنى ضيق علي قال الله تعالى فقدر

عليه رزقه وهوأحد الأقوال في قوله تعالى فظن أن لن نقدر عليه وقالت طائفة

اللفظ على ظاهره ولكن قاله هذا الرجل وهو غير ضابط لكلامه ولاقاصد لحقيقة

معناه ومعتقد لها  بل قاله في حالة غلب عليه فيها الدهش والخوف وشدة الجزع

بحيث ذهب تيقظه وتدبر ما يقوله فصار في معنى الغافل والناسي وهذه الحالة

لايؤاخذ فيها وهو نحو قول القائل الآخر الذي غلب عليه الفرح حين وجد راحلته

أنت عبدي وأنا ربك فلم يكفر بذلك الدهش والغلبة والسهو وقد جاء في هذا

الحديث في غير مسلم فلعلي أضل الله أي أغيب عنه وهذا يدل على أن قوله لئن

قدر الله على ظاهره وقالت طائفة هذا من مجاز كلام العرب وبديع استعمالها

يسمونه مزج الشك باليقين كقوله تعالى وإنا أواياكم لعلى هدى فصورته صورة شك

والمراد به اليقين وقالت طائفة هذا الرجل جهل صفة من صفات الله تعالى وقد

اختلف العلماء في تكفير جاهل الصفة قال القاضي وممن كفره بذلك بن جرير

الطبرى وقاله أبوالحسن الأشعري أولا وقال آخرون لا يكفر بجهل الصفة ولا

يخرج به عن اسم الإيمان بخلاف حجدها وإليه رجع أبو الحسن الأشعري وعليه

استقر قوله لأنه لم يعتقد ذلك اعتقادا يقطع بصوابه ويراه دينا وشرعا وإنما

يكفر من اعتقد أن
# 
# مقالته حق قال هؤلاء ولو سئل الناس عن الصفات لوجد العالم بها قليلاوقالت

طائفة كان هذا الرجل في زمن فترة حين ينفع مجرد التوحيد ولا تكليف قبل ورود

الشرع على المذهب الصحيح لقوله تعالى وما كنا معذبين حتى نبعث رسولا وقالت

طائفة يجوز أنه كان في زمن شرعهم فيه جواز العفو عن الكافر بخلاف شرعنا

وذلك من مجوزات العقول عند أهل السنة وإنما منعناه في شرعنا بالشرع وهو

قوله تعالى (إن الله لا يغفر أن يشرك به) وغير ذلك من الأدلة والله أعلم

وقيل إنما وصى بذلك تحقيرا لنفسه وعقوبة لها لعصيانها وإسرافها رجاء أن

يرحمه الله تعالى قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (أسرف رجل على نفسه) أي بالغ

وعلا في المعاصي والسرف مجاوزة الحد قوله ان بن شهاب ذكر هذا الحديث ثم ذكر

حديث المرأة التي دخلت النار وعذبت بسبب هرة حبستها حتى ماتت جوعا ثم  قال

بن شهاب لئلا يتكل رجل ولا ييأس رجل معناه أن
# 
# بن شهاب لما ذكر الحديث الأول خاف أن سامعه يتكل على ما فيه من سعة

الرحمة وعظم الرجاء فضم إليه حديث الهرة الذي فيه من التخويف ضد ذلك ليجتمع

الخوف والرجاء وهذا معنى قوله لئلا يتكل ولاييأس وهكذا معظم آيات القرآن

العزيز يجتمع فيها الخوف والرجاء وكذا قال العلماء يستحب للواعظ أن يجمع في

موعظته بين الخوف والرجاء لئلا يقنط أحد ولايتكل قالوا وليكن التخويف أكثر

لأن النفوس إليه أحوج لميلها إلى الرجاء والراحة والاتكال وإهمال بعض

الأعمال وأما حديث الهرة فسبق شرحه في موضعه
# [2757] قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (إن رجلا فيمن كان قبلكم راشه الله مالا

وولدا) هذه اللفظة رويت بوجهين في صحيح مسلم أحدهما راشه بألف ساكنة غير

مهموزة وبشين معجمة والثاني رأسه بهمزة وسين مهملة قال القاضي والأول هو

الصواب وهو رواية الجمهور ومعناه أعطاه الله مالا وولدا قال ولا وجه

للمهملة هنا وكذا قال غيره ولا وجه له هنا قوله (فإني لم أبتهر عند الله

خيرا) هكذا هو في بعض النسخ ولبعض الرواة أبتئر بهمزة بعدالتاء وفي أكثرها

لم أبتهر بالهاء وكلاهما صحيح والهاء مبدلة من الهمزة ومعناهما لم أقدم

خيرا ولم أدخره وقد فسرها قتادة في الكتاب وفي رواية لم يبتئر هكذا هو فى

جميع النسخ وفى رواية ماامتأر بالميم مهموز أيضا والميم مبدلة من الباء

الموحدة قوله (وإن الله يقدر على أن يعذبني) هكذا هو في معظم النسخ ببلادنا

ونقل اتفاق الرواة
# 
# والنسخ عليه هكذا بتكرير إن وسقطت لفظة أن الثانية في بعض النسخ المعتمدة

فعلى هذا تكون إن الأولى شرطية وتقديره إن قدر الله علي عذبني وهو موافق

للرواية السابقة وأما على رواية الجمهور وهي إثبات أن الثانية مع الأولى

فاختلف في تقديره فقال القاضي هذا الكلام فيه تلفيق قال فإن أخذ على ظاهره

ونصب اسم الله وجعل تقدير في موضع خبر إن استقام اللفظ وصح المعنى لكنه

يصير مخالفا لما  سبق من كلامه الذي ظاهره الشك في القدرة قال وقال بعضهم

صوابه حذف أن الثانية وتخفيف الأولى ورفع اسم الله تعالى قال وكذا ضبطناه

عن بعضهم هذا كلام القاضي وقيل هو على ظاهره بإثبات إن في الموضعين والأولى

مشددة ومعناه إن الله قادر على أن يعذبني ويكون هذا على قول من تأول

الرواية الأولى على أنه أراد بقدر ضيق أو غيره مما ليس فيه نفي حقيقة
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ق د ر (q-d-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning is measure, decree, power, and capacity; the root denotes determining something with precision and also the ability to do a thing.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological usage, it signifies divine decree (qadar) and omnipotence; the nuance of "straitening" (taḍyīq) is a recognized secondary sense.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense is "to measure/decree"; metaphorically it extends to "straitening" as in {«فَقَدَرَ عَلَيْهِ رِزْقَهُ»} (He straitened his provision), distinguishing ḥaqīqah from majāz.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Construction (al-Sharṭ wa al-Jazā') — The particle "in" (إن) governs a protasis and apodosis; when "in" is repeated, the second may be either an emphasized confirmation or a separate conditional, affecting the syntactic parsing of the sentence.
chapters.translation:
I say: A group (of scholars) said: It is not sound to interpret this (saying) as intending a negation of Allah's power, for one who doubts Allah's power is an unbeliever. And he (the Prophet, peace be upon him) said at the end of the hadith that this man only did this act out of fear of Allah the Exalted; and the unbeliever does not fear Allah the Exalted, nor is he forgiven. These scholars said: Thus it (the saying) has two interpretations. One of them is that its meaning is: "If Allah has decreed punishment upon me," i.e., ordained it. One says from this: "qadara" with tashdīd (intensification) and "qadara" with takhfīf (lightening) with a single meaning. The second (interpretation) is that "qadara" here means "He straitened upon me," as Allah the Exalted said: {«فَقَدَرَ عَلَيْهِ رِزْقَهُ»} (But He straitened his provision for him). And this is one of the sayings concerning His statement the Exalted: {«فَظَنَّ أَن لَّن نَّقْدِرَ عَلَيْهِ»} (And he thought that We would not straiten him). And another group said: The wording is upon its apparent (literal) meaning, but this man uttered it while he was not precise in his speech, nor intending the reality of its meaning, nor believing in it. Rather, he said it in a state in which bewilderment, fear, and intense distress overwhelmed him, to the extent that his alertness and his reflection upon what he was saying departed from him, so he became in the category of the heedless and the forgetful. And a person is not held to account in such a state. This is similar to the saying of that other man who was overcome by joy when he found his riding beast: "You are my servant and I am your Lord." He did not become an unbeliever due to that bewilderment, overwhelming emotion, and forgetfulness. And it has come in this hadith, in (the narration of) other than Muslim: "Perhaps I strayed from Allah," i.e., I was absent from Him. And this indicates that his saying "If Allah has decreed (qadara)" is upon its apparent (literal) meaning. And another group said: This is from the figurative speech (majāz) of the Arabs and their exquisite usage; they call it "blending doubt with certainty," like His saying the Exalted: {«وَإِنَّا أَوْ إِيَّاكُمْ لَعَلَى هُدًى»} (And indeed, we or you are upon guidance). Its form is the form of doubt, but the intended meaning is certainty. And another group said: This man was ignorant of one of Allah's attributes, and the scholars have differed concerning declaring the one ignorant of an attribute an unbeliever. Al-Qāḍī said: Among those who declared him an unbeliever on that account was Ibn Jarīr al-Ṭabarī, and Abū al-Ḥasan al-Ashʿarī said it initially. And others said: He is not declared an unbeliever for ignorance of an attribute, nor does it remove him from the name of faith, unlike its denial (juhūd). And to this Abū al-Ḥasan al-Ashʿarī returned, and upon it his final position settled, because he (the ignorant one) did not believe that (false notion) with a belief that he is certain of its correctness, nor does he regard it as religion and law. Rather, only the one who believes that his statement is true is declared an unbeliever. These scholars said: And if the people were asked about the attributes, one would find few among them who are knowledgeable of them. And another group said: This man was in a period of intermission (fatrah) when mere monotheism (tawḥīd) sufficed, and there is no obligation (taklīf) before the arrival of the revealed law (sharʿ) according to the correct school, due to His saying the Exalted: {«وَمَا كُنَّا مُعَذِّبِينَ حَتَّى نَبْعَثَ رَسُولًا»} (And We were not to punish until We sent a messenger). And another group said: It is permissible that he was in a period in which their law allowed the forgiveness of the unbeliever, unlike our law. And that (forgiveness of the unbeliever) is among the things that the intellect deems permissible according to the People of the Sunnah; we only prohibit it in our law by (virtue of) the revealed law, which is His saying the Exalted: {«إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يَغْفِرُ أَن يُشْرَكَ بِهِ»} (Indeed, Allah does not forgive that partners be associated with Him), and other evidences. And Allah knows best. And it was said: He only enjoined that (the burning of himself) as a belittlement of his soul and a punishment for it due to its disobedience and excess, hoping that Allah the Exalted would have mercy upon him.

His saying, peace be upon him: "A man exceeded (asrafa) against himself" — i.e., he went to extremes and rose high in sins; and "excess" (sarf) is transgressing the limit.

His saying: Ibn Shihāb mentioned this hadith, then mentioned the hadith of the woman who entered the Fire and was punished because of a cat that she confined until it died of hunger. Then Ibn Shihāb said: "So that no man may rely (upon mercy) and no man may despair." Its meaning is that Ibn Shihāb, when he mentioned the first hadith, feared that the listener might rely upon what it contains of the vastness of mercy and the greatness of hope; so he appended to it the hadith of the cat, which contains deterrence (takhwīf) against that, so that fear and hope might be combined. And this is the meaning of his saying: "So that he may not rely and may not despair." And thus most of the verses of the Mighty Qur'an combine fear and hope. And likewise the scholars said: It is recommended for the preacher to combine in his sermon both fear and hope, so that no one may despair and no one may rely (excessively). They said: And the deterrence should be more (emphasized), because souls are more in need of it, due to their inclination toward hope, ease, and reliance, and their neglect of some deeds. As for the hadith of the cat, its explanation has already preceded in its proper place.

[2757] His saying, peace be upon him: "Indeed, a man among those before you — Allah enriched him (rāshahu) with wealth and children." This word has been narrated in two ways in Sahih Muslim. One of them is "rāshahu" with a silent alif, unhamzated, and with a pointed shīn. The second is "ra'sahu" with a hamzah and an unpointed sīn. Al-Qāḍī said: The first is the correct one, and it is the narration of the majority, and its meaning is: Allah gave him wealth and children. He said: And there is no justification for the unpointed (sīn) here. And others likewise said: There is no justification for it here.

His saying: "For I have not stored up (abtahhiru) good with Allah" — thus it is in some copies, and with some narrators "abta'iru" with a hamzah after the tā'. And in most of them it is "lam abtahir" with a hā'. And both are correct, the hā' being a substitute for the hamzah. And their meaning is: I have not sent forward good nor stored it up. Qatādah has interpreted it in the Book. And in one narration: "lam yabta'ir" — thus it is in all copies. And in one narration: "mā'mtāra" with a mīm, hamzated, and the mīm is a substitute for the unpointed bā'.

His saying: "And indeed Allah is able (yaqdiru) to punish me" — thus it is in most copies in our lands, and the agreement of the narrators and copies has been transmitted upon it, thus with the repetition of "inna." And the second "inna" is dropped in some reliable copies. Upon this (latter reading), the first "in" is conditional, and its estimation is: "If Allah decrees (qadara) punishment upon me, He punishes me." And this agrees with the previous narration. As for the narration of the majority, which is the affirmation of the second "in" along with the first, there is disagreement concerning its estimation. Al-Qāḍī said: This speech contains a patchwork (talfīq). For if it is taken upon its apparent (literal) meaning, with the name of Allah in the accusative and "yaqdiru" placed in the position of the predicate of "inna," the wording becomes sound and the meaning correct — but it then becomes contrary to what preceded of his speech, which apparently suggests doubt concerning (divine) power. He said: And some said: The correct (reading) is the deletion of the second "in" and the lightening (takhfīf) of the first, with the name of Allah the Exalted in the nominative. He said: And thus we recorded it from some of them. This is the speech of al-Qāḍī. And it was said: It is upon its apparent (literal) meaning, with the affirmation of "in" in both places, the first being emphasized (mushaddadah), and its meaning is: "Indeed, Allah is able to punish me." And this is upon the view of those who interpreted the first narration as intending by "qadara" the meaning of "straitening" or other than that which does not involve a negation of the reality (of divine power).
