Al-Qāḍī said: our transmission from the group (of narrators) has it with an unpointed ṣād. Some said: "al-rafṣ" with unpointed ṣād means striking with the foot, like "al-rafas" with sīn. He said: if this is correct, then that is its meaning. He said: however, I have not found this word in the foundational lexicons. He said: in the narration of al-Qāḍī al-Tamīmī, it occurs as "rafaḍahu" with a pointed ḍād, and that is an error. He said: in al-Bukhārī, from the narration of al-Marwazī, it occurs as "rafaṣahu" with qāf and unpointed ṣād, and there is no basis for it. In al-Bukhārī, in the Book of Etiquette (Kitāb al-Adab), it occurs as "rafaḍahu" with a pointed ḍād. He said: al-Khaṭṭābī narrated it in his Gharīb as "rafaṣahu" with unpointed ṣād, i.e., he pressed him until he compressed some parts of him against others — from which is the statement of Allah the Exalted: {«بنيان مرصوص»} (a structure firmly compacted) [Quran 61:4]. I say: it is also possible that the meaning of "rafaḍahu" with the pointed letter is that he abandoned asking him about Islam, out of despair of his acceptance at that time, and then proceeded to ask him about what he saw. And Allah knows best.

[2931] His statement "wa-huwa yakhtilu an yasmaʿa min Ibn Sayyād shayʾan" — it is with kasrah on the tāʾ, i.e., he was deceiving Ibn Sayyād and exploiting his heedlessness to hear something of his speech, so that he and the Companions could ascertain his condition — whether he was a soothsayer (kāhin) or a sorcerer (sāḥir) or similar. In this is the permissibility of uncovering the states of one whose corruption is feared, and in this is the Imam's personal investigation of important matters.

His statement "innahu fī qaṭīfatin lahu fīhā zamzamah" — "al-qaṭīfah" is a velvet cloak, previously explained multiple times. This word "zamzamah" occurs in most copies of Muslim with two pointed zāʾs, and in some with two unpointed rāʾs. It occurs in al-Bukhārī with both forms. Al-Qāḍī transmitted from the majority of Muslim's narrators that it is with the two pointed letters, and that in some copies it is "ramzah" — with rāʾ first and zāy last, omitting the second mīm — meaning a faint sound that is barely understood or not understood at all.

His statement "fa-thāra Ibn Sayyād" — i.e., he rose from his resting place and stood up.

[169] His statement ﷺ: "There was no prophet except that he warned his people — indeed, Noah warned his people" — this warning was due to the greatness of his trial and the severity of his affair.

His statement ﷺ: "taʿallamū annahu aʿwar" (know that he is one-eyed) — the narrators are agreed on its vocalization as "taʿallamū" with fatḥah on the ʿayn and the shaddah on the lām, and likewise al-Qāḍī and others transmitted this from them. They said: its meaning is "know and be certain." It is said "taʿallama" with fatḥah and tashdīd, meaning "know."

His statement ﷺ: "Know that none of you will see his Lord until he dies" — al-Māzarī said: This ḥadīth contains a notification affirming the vision of Allah the Exalted in the afterlife, which is the doctrine of the people of truth (ahl al-ḥaqq). Had it been impossible, as the Muʿtazilah claim, then restricting it to death would have no meaning. The ḥadīths with this meaning are numerous, and a group of them were previously mentioned in the Book of Faith (Kitāb al-Īmān) along with verses from the Quran, and the discussion of the issue was established there. Al-Qāḍī said: The doctrine of the people of truth is that it is not impossible in this world, but rather possible; then they differed regarding its actual occurrence. Those who denied it clung to this ḥadīth along with the statement of Allah the Exalted: {«لا تدركه الأبصار»} (Vision comprehends Him not) [Quran 6:103], on the interpretation of those who applied it to this world. Likewise, they differed regarding the Prophet's ﷺ vision of his Lord on the night of the Ascension (al-Isrāʾ). Among the Salaf of the Companions, the Followers, and those after them — then the imams of jurisprudence, ḥadīth, and theoretical theologians — there is a well-known disagreement on this. Most of those who denied it in this world said: the reason for the prohibition is the weakness of human faculties in this world to bear it, just as Moses ﷺ could not bear it in this world.

chapters.title_en: The Dajjāl's Trial, His Marks, and the Proofs of His Falsehood
chapters.arabic_text:
والله أعلم
# [2930] قوله (ناهز الحلم) أي قارب
# 
# البلوغ
# [2932] قوله (فانتفخ حتى ملأ السكة) السكة بكسر السين الطريق وجمعها سكك

قال أبو عبيد أصل السكة الطريق المصطفة من النخل قال وسميت الأزقة سككا

لاصطفاف الدور فيها قوله (فلقيته لقية أخرى) قال القاضي في المشارق رويناه

لقية بضم اللام قال ثعلب وغيره يقولونه بفتحها هذا كلام القاضي والمعروف في

اللغة والرواية ببلادنا الفتح قوله (وقد نفرت عينه) بفتح النون والفاء أي

ورمت ونتأت وذكر القاضي أنه روى على أوجه آخر والظاهر أنها تصحيف
#

| (باب ذكر الدجال قد سبق في شرح خطبة الكتاب بيان 
# اشتقاقه وغيره وسبق في كتاب الصلاة بيان تسميته المسيح واشتقاقه والخلاف

في ضبطه قال القاضي هذه الأحاديث التي ذكرها مسلم وغيره في قصة الدجال حجة

لمذهب أهل الحق في صحة وجوده وأنه شخص بعينه ابتلى الله به عباده وأقدره

على أشياء من مقدورات الله تعالى من إحياء الميت الذي يقتله ومن ظهور زهرة

الدنيا والخصب معه وجنته وناره ونهريه واتباع كنوز الأرض له وأمره السماء

أن تمطر فتمطر والأرض أن تنبت فتنبت فيقع كل ذلك بقدرة الله تعالى ومشيئته

ثم يعجزه الله تعالى بعد ذلك فلايقدر على قتل ذلك الرجل ولاغيره ويبطل أمره

ويقتله عيسى صلى الله عليه وسلم ويثبت الله الذين آمنوا هذا مذهب أهل السنة

وجميع المحدثين والفقهاء والنظار خلافا لمن أنكره وأبطل أمره من الخوارج

والجهمية وبعض المعتزلة وخلافا للبخاري المعتزلي وموافقيه من الجهمية

وغيرهم في أنه صحيح الوجود ولكن الذى يدعى مخارف وخيالات لاحقائق لها

وزعموا أنه لو كان حقا  لم يوثق بمعجزات الأنبياء صلوات الله وسلامه عليهم

وهذا غلط من جميعهم لأنه لم يدع النبوة)
# 
# فيكون ما معه كالتصديق له وإنما يدعي الإلهية وهو في نفس دعواه مكذب لها

بصورة حاله ووجود دلائل الحدوث فيه ونقص صورته وعجزه عن إزالة العور الذي

في عينيه وعن إزالة الشاهد بكفره المكتوب بين عينيه ولهذه الدلائل وغيرها

لايغتر به الارعاع من الناس لسد الحاجة والفاقة رغبة في سد الرمق أو تقية

وخوفا من أذاه لأن فتنته عظيمة جدا تدهش العقول وتحير الألباب مع سرعة

مروره فى الأمر فلايمكث بحيث يتأمل الضعفاء حاله ودلائل الحدوث فيه والنقص

فيصدقه من صدقه في هذه الحالة ولهذا حذرت الأنبياء صلوات الله وسلامه عليهم

أجمعين من فتنته ونبهوا على نقصه ودلائل إبطاله وأما أهل التوفيق فلا

يغترون به ولايخدعون لما معه لما ذكرناه من الدلائل المكذبة له مع ما سبق

لهم من العلم بحاله ولهذا يقول له الذي يقتله ثم يحييه ما ازددت فيك

الابصيرة هذا آخر كلام القاضي رحمه الله
# [169] قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (إن الله تبارك وتعالى ليس بأعور ألاوإن

المسيح الدجال أعور العين اليمنى كأن عينه عنبة طافئة) أما طافئة
# 
# فرويت بالهمز وتركه وكلاهما صحيح فالمهموزة هي التي ذهب نورها وغير

المهموزة التي نتأت وطفت مرتفعة وفيها ضوء وقد سبق في كتاب الإيمان بيان

هذا كله وبيان الجمع بين الروايتين وأنه جاء في رواية أعور العين اليمنى

وفي رواية اليسرى وكلاهما صحيح والعور في اللغة العيب وعيناه معيبتان عورا

وأن احداهما طافئة بالهمز لاضوء فيها والأخرى طافية بلا همزة ظاهرة ناتئة

وأما قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم إن الله تعالى ليس بأعور والدجال أعور فبيان

لعلامة بينة تدل على كذب الدجال دلائل قطعية بديهية يدركها كل أحد ولم

يقتصر على كونه جسما أو غير ذلك من الدلائل القطعية لكون بعض العوام

لايهتدى إليها والله أعلم
# [2933] قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (مكتوب بين عينيه كافر ثم تهجاها فقال ك

ف ر يقرأه كل مسلم)  وفي رواية يقرأه كل مؤمن كاتب وغير كاتب الصحيح الذي

عليه المحققون أن هذه الكتابة على ظاهرها وأنها كتابة حقيقة جعلها الله آية

وعلامة من جملة العلامات القاطعة بكفره وكذبه وإبطاله ويظهرها الله تعالى

لكل مسلم كاتب وغير كاتب ويخفيها عمن أراد شقاوته وفتنتة ولاامتناع في ذلك

وذكر القاضي فيه خلافا
# 
# منهم من قال هي كتابة حقيقة كما ذكرنا ومنهم من قال هي مجاز وإشارة إلى

سمات الحدوث عليه واحتج بقوله يقرأه كل مؤمن كاتب وغير كاتب وهذا مذهب ضعيف
# [2934] قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (معه جنة ونار فجنته نار وناره جنة) وفي

رواية نهران وفي رواية ماء ونار قال العلماء هذا من جملة فتنته امتحن الله

تعالى به عباده ليحق الحق ويبطل الباطل ثم يفضحه ويظهر للناس عجزه قوله صلى

الله عليه وسلم (فإما أدركن أحد فليأت النهر الذي يراه نارا) هكذا هو في

أكثر النسخ أدركن وفي بعضها أدركه وهذا الثاني ظاهر وأما الأول فغريب من

حيث العربية لأن هذه النون لاتدخل على الفعل قال القاضي ولعله يدركن يعني

فعبره بعض الرواة وقوله يراه بفتح الياء وضمها قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم

(ممسوح العين عليها ظفرة غليظة) هي بفتح الظاء المعجمة والفاء وهي جلدة
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ن-ه-ز (n-h-z)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To draw near, approach, or be at the point of reaching something; proximity in time or degree.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Used for approaching a threshold or boundary, here the verge of puberty (bulūgh).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal proximity; no metaphorical extension here.
- Root: س-ك-ك (s-k-k)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: A straight, aligned row; a path or road; from the notion of things set in orderly array.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Technical term for a lane or alley; extended to rows of palm trees.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for a road; metaphorical for alleys due to houses aligned in rows.
- Root: ط-ف-أ (t-f-') / ط-ف-ي (t-f-y)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: طافئة (with hamzah): extinguished, light gone; طافية (without hamzah): floating, protruding, elevated.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Distinguishes loss of sight (hamzah) vs. protrusion with retained light (yā').
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal physical descriptions; no metaphor.
- Root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To cover, conceal; ingratitude; unbelief.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Theological term for rejection of divine truth; the written mark as a sign of kufr.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal inscription vs. metaphorical interpretation debated; the author affirms literal.
- Sībawayh Rule: The Conditional Particle (in) with the Apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) — governing the subjunctive or jussive; also the rule of the nūn of emphasis (nūn al-tawkīd) not entering upon the past tense verb, as discussed regarding "adrakan."
chapters.translation:
And Allah knows best.

[2930] His saying (he approached puberty (nāhaza al-ḥulum)) — meaning he drew near to reaching maturity (bulūgh).

[2932] His saying (and he swelled until he filled the street (al-sikkah)) — al-sikkah, with kasrah on the sīn, is the road; its plural is sikak. Abū ʿUbayd said: The origin of al-sikkah is the aligned row of palm trees. He said: And the alleys were called sikak due to the alignment of the houses therein. His saying (and I met him another meeting (laqiyah ukhrā)) — al-Qāḍī said in al-Mashāriq: We narrated it as laqiyah with ḍammah on the lām. Thaʿlab and others said they pronounce it with fatḥah. This is the speech of al-Qāḍī, but the well-known in the language and in the narration in our lands is the fatḥah. His saying (and his eye had become swollen (wa qad nafarat ʿaynahu)) — with fatḥah on the nūn and the fā', meaning it had become inflamed and protruding. Al-Qāḍī mentioned that it was narrated on other faces, and the apparent is that they are corruptions (taṣḥīf).

| (Chapter: Mention of the Dajjāl. There has already preceded in the commentary on the introduction of the Book the explanation of its derivation and other matters, and there has preceded in the Book of Prayer the explanation of his being named the Messiah (al-Masīḥ), its derivation, and the disagreement over its precise form. Al-Qāḍī said: These ḥadīths which Muslim and others mentioned concerning the story of the Dajjāl are a proof for the doctrine of the people of truth (ahl al-ḥaqq) regarding the soundness of his existence, and that he is a specific person whom Allah tested His servants with, and empowered him over certain things from among the capabilities of Allah the Exalted — such as reviving the dead man whom he kills, the appearance of the bloom of the world and abundance with him, his paradise and his fire, his two rivers, the treasures of the earth following him, and his commanding the sky to rain so it rains, and the earth to sprout so it sprouts. All of that occurs by the power of Allah the Exalted and His will. Then Allah the Exalted incapacitates him after that, so he is unable to kill that man or anyone else, and his affair is nullified, and ʿĪsā (peace be upon him) kills him, and Allah establishes those who believed. This is the doctrine of the people of the Sunnah and all the ḥadīth scholars, jurists, and speculative theologians — contrary to those who denied him and nullified his affair from among the Khawārij, the Jahmiyyah, and some of the Muʿtazilah; and contrary to al-Bukhārī the Muʿtazilī and his supporters from the Jahmiyyah and others in that his existence is sound, but what he claims is delusions and fantasies with no realities to them. They claimed that if he were real, one could not trust the miracles of the prophets (may Allah's prayers and peace be upon them). This is an error on all their parts, because he does not claim prophethood — such that what is with him would be like a confirmation of him. Rather, he claims divinity (ilāhiyyah), and in the very claim itself he is contradicted by the form of his state, the existence of evidences of origination (ḥudūth) in him, the deficiency of his form, his inability to remove the one-eyed defect in his eyes, and his inability to remove the witness of his disbelief written between his eyes. And due to these evidences and others, none is deceived by him except the rabble of people, due to dire need and poverty, desiring to sustain their last breath, or out of dissimulation (taqiyyah) and fear of his harm — because his trial is very great, stunning the intellects and confounding the minds, along with the swiftness of his passage in the matter, so he does not remain in a place such that the weak could ponder his state and the evidences of origination and deficiency in him. So whoever believes him does so in this state. For this reason, the prophets (may Allah's prayers and peace be upon them all) warned against his trial and drew attention to his deficiency and the evidences of his nullification. As for the people of divine success (ahl al-tawfīq), they are not deceived by him nor deluded by what is with him, due to what we have mentioned of the evidences that give him the lie, along with what has preceded for them of knowledge of his state. For this reason, the one whom he kills then revives says to him: "I have not increased in you except insight." This is the end of the speech of al-Qāḍī (may Allah have mercy on him).

[169] His saying, peace be upon him: (Indeed Allah, Blessed and Exalted, is not one-eyed. Indeed, the Messiah the Dajjāl is one-eyed of the right eye, as if his eye is a protruding grape (ṭāfi'ah)) — As for ṭāfi'ah, it is narrated with hamzah and without it, and both are sound. The one with hamzah is that whose light has gone, and the one without hamzah is that which protrudes and floats elevated, and in it there is light. There has already preceded in the Book of Faith the explanation of all of this, and the explanation of the reconciliation between the two narrations — that it came in one narration "one-eyed of the right eye" and in another "the left," and both are sound. And al-ʿawar (one-eyedness) in the language is a defect, and his two eyes are defective with one-eyedness — one of them is ṭāfi'ah with hamzah, no light in it, and the other is ṭāfiyah without hamzah, apparent and protruding. As for his saying, peace be upon him: (Indeed Allah the Exalted is not one-eyed, and the Dajjāl is one-eyed) — it is an explanation of a clear sign indicating the lie of the Dajjāl by decisive, self-evident proofs that everyone perceives. And He did not restrict to his being a body or other such decisive proofs, because some of the common folk do not attain to them. And Allah knows best.

[2933] His saying, peace be upon him: (Written between his two eyes: Kāfir. Then he spelled it out and said: K, F, R. Every Muslim reads it.) And in another narration: (Every believer reads it, literate and illiterate.) The sound view, upon which the verifiers (muḥaqqiqūn) are agreed, is that this writing is upon its apparent meaning, and that it is a real writing (kitābah ḥaqīqah) which Allah made a sign and mark from among the decisive signs of his disbelief, his lying, and his nullification. Allah the Exalted manifests it to every Muslim, literate and illiterate, and conceals it from whom He wills of wretchedness and trial. And there is no impossibility in that. Al-Qāḍī mentioned a disagreement concerning it: among them are those who said it is a real writing as we have mentioned, and among them are those who said it is metaphorical (majāz) and an indication of the marks of origination upon him, and they argued by his saying "every believer reads it, literate and illiterate." And this is a weak doctrine.

[2934] His saying, peace be upon him: (With him is a paradise and a fire; his paradise is a fire and his fire is a paradise.) And in another narration: (Two rivers), and in another narration: (Water and fire). The scholars said: This is from among his trials; Allah the Exalted tests His servants by him, to establish the truth and nullify falsehood, then He exposes him and shows the people his incapacity. His saying, peace be upon him: (So if any of you reaches him, let him come to the river which he sees as fire) — thus it is in most copies: adrakan (with nūn). And in some of them: adrakahu (with hā'). This second is apparent, and as for the first, it is strange from the perspective of Arabic grammar, because this nūn does not enter upon the verb. Al-Qāḍī said: Perhaps it is "adraka" (i.e., without the nūn), and some narrators transmitted it with the nūn. And his saying "yarāhu" — with fatḥah on the yā' and with ḍammah on it (two readings). His saying, peace be upon him: (With a wiped eye upon which is a thick membrane (ẓafarah)) — it is with fatḥah on the ẓā' (the pointed letter) and the fā', and it is a piece of skin.

chapters.title_en: The Dajjāl's Description, the Length of His Days, and the Linguistic Analysis of "Akhawf" (Most Frightening)
chapters.arabic_text:
تغشي البصر وقال
# 
# الأصمعي لحمة تنبت عند المآقي
# [2937] قوله (سمع النواس بن سمعان) بفتح السين وكسرها قوله (ذكر رسول

الله صلى الله عليه وسلم الدجال ذات غداة فخفض فيه ورفع حتى ظنناه في طائفة

النخل) هو بتشديد الفاء فيهما وفي معناه قولان أحدهما أن خفض بمعنى حقر

وقوله رفع أي عظمه وفخمه فمن تحقيره وهو أنه على الله تعالى عوره ومنه قوله

صلى الله عليه وسلم هو أهون على الله من ذلك وأنه لايقدر على قتل أحد إلا

ذلك الرجل ثم يعجز عنه وأنه يضمحل أمره ويقتل بعد ذلك هو وأتباعه ومن

تفخيمه وتعظيم فتنته والمحنة به هذه الأمور الخارقة للعادة وأنه ما من نبى

الاوقد أنذره قومه والوجه الثاني أنه خفض من صوته  في حال الكثرة فيما تكلم

فيه فخفض بعد طول الكلام والتعب ليستريح ثم رفع ليبلغ صوته كل أحد قوله
# 
# صلى الله عليه وسلم (غير الدجال أخوفني عليكم) هكذا هو في جميع نسخ

بلادنا أخوفني بنون بعد الفاء وكذا نقله القاضي عن رواية الأكثرين قال

ورواه بعضهم بحذف النون وهما لغتان صحيحتان ومعناهما واحد قال شيخنا الإمام

أبو عبد الله بن مالك رحمه الله تعالى الحاجة داعية إلى الكلام في لفظ

الحديث ومعناه فأما لفظه لكونه تضمن ما لا يعتاد من إضافة أخوف إلى ياء

المتكلم مقرونة بنون الوقاية وهذا الاستعمال إنما يكون مع الأفعال المتعدية

والجواب أنه كان الأصل إثباتها ولكنه أصل متروك فنبه عليه في قليل من

كلامهم وأنشد فيه أبياتا منها ما أنشده الفراء ... فما أدري فظني كل ظن ...

أمسلمتي إلى قومي شراحي ...

$ (يعني شراحيل فرخمه في غير الندا للضرورة وأنشد غيره ... وليس الموافيني ليرفد خائبا ... فإن له أضعاف ما كان أملا)
# ولأفعل التفضيل أيضا شبه بالفعل وخصوصا بفعل التعجب فجاز أن تلحقه النون

المذكورة في الحديث كما لحقت في الأبيات المذكورة هذا هو الأظهر في هذه

النون هنا ويحتمل أن يكون معناه أخوف لي فأبدلت النون من اللام كما أبدلت

في لعن وعن بمعنى لعل وعل وأما معنى الحديث ففيه أوجه أظهرها أنه من أفعل

التفضيل وتقديره غير الدجال أخوف مخوفاتي عليكم ثم حذف المضاف إلى الياء

ومنه أخوف ما أخاف على أمتي الأئمة المضلون معناه أن الأشياء التي أخافها

على أمتي أحقها بأن تخاف الأئمة المضلون والثاني بأن يكون أخوف من أخاف

بمعنى خوف ومعناه غير الدجال أشد موجبات خوفي عليكم والثالث أن يكون من باب

وصف المعاني بما يوصف به الأعيان على سبيل المبالغة كقولهم في الشعر الفصيح

شعر شاعر وخوف فلان أخوف من خوفك وتقديره خوف غير الدجال أخوف خوفي عليكم

ثم حذف المضاف الأول
# 
# ثم الثاني هذا آخر كلام الشيخ رحمه الله قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (إنه

شاب قطط) هو بفتح القاف  والطاء أي شديد جعودة الشعر مباعد للجعودة المحبوبة

قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (إنه خارج خلة بين الشام والعراق) هكذا في نسخ

بلادنا خلة بفتح الخاء المعجمة واللام وتنوين الهاء وقال القاضي المشهور

فيه حلة بالحاء المهملة ونصب التاء يعني غير منونة قيل معناه سمت ذلك

وقبالته وفي كتاب العين الحلة موضع حزن وصخور قال ورواه بعضهم حله بضم

اللام وبهاء الضمير أي نزوله وحلوله قال وكذا ذكره الحميدي في الجمع بين

الصحيحين قال وذكره الهروي خلة بالخاء المعجمة وتشديد اللام المفتوحتين

وفسره بأنه ما بين البلدين هذا آخر ماذكره القاضي وهذا الذي ذكره عن الهروي

هو الموجود في نسخ بلادنا وفي الجمع بين الصحيحين أيضا ببلادنا وهو الذي

رجحه صاحب نهاية الغريب وفسره بالطريق بينهما قوله (فعاث يمينا وعاث شمالا)

هو بعين مهملة وثاء مثلثة مفتوحة وهو فعل ماض والعيث الفساد أو أشد الفساد

والإسراع فيه يقال منه عاث يعيث وحكى القاضي أنه رواه بعضهم فعاث بكسر

الثاء منونة اسم فاعل وهو بمعنى الأول قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (يوم كسنة

ويوم كشهر ويوم كجمعة وسائر أيامه كأيامكم) قال العلماء هذا الحديث على

ظاهره وهذه الأيام الثلاثة طويلة على هذا القدر المذكور في الحديث يدل عليه

قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم وسائر أيامه كأيامكم
# 
# وأما قولهم يا رسول الله فذلك اليوم الذي كسنة أتكفينا فيه صلاة يوم قال

لا اقدروا له قدره فقال القاضي وغيره هذا حكم مخصوص بذلك اليوم شرعه لنا

صاحب الشرع قالوا ولولا هذا الحديث ووكلنا إلى اجتهادنا لاقتصرنا فيه على

الصلوات الخمس عند الأوقات المعروفة في غيره من الأيام ومعنى أقدروا له

قدره أنه إذا مضى بعد طلوع الفجر قدر ما يكون بينه وبين الظهر كل يوم فصلوا

الظهر ثم إذا مضى بعده قدر ما يكون بينها وبين العصر فصلوا العصر وإذا مضى

بعد هذا قدر ما يكون بينها وبين المغرب فصلوا المغرب وكذا العشاء والصبح ثم

الظهر ثم العصر ثم المغرب وهكذا حتى ينقضي  ذلك اليوم وقد وقع فيه صلوات سنة

فرائض كلها مؤداة في وقتها وأما الثاني الذي كشهر والثالث الذي كجمعة فقياس

اليوم الأول أن يقدر لهما كاليوم الأول على ما ذكرناه والله أعلم قوله صلى
chapters.anchors:
- Root: خ-و-ف (kh-w-f)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning of fear, dread, and apprehension; the verbal noun (khawf) denotes a state of alarm or terror.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological discourse, khawf is the pious fear of Allah's punishment or displeasure, but here it is applied to worldly tribulation (fitnah) — a graded, relative fear.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage denotes actual fear; metaphorical (majāz) usage extends to "that which causes fear" (mukhīf), as in the hyperbolic construction "akhawf" (most fear-inducing).
- Root: ع-ي-ث (ʿ-y-th)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: ʿayth signifies corruption, mischief, or the most severe form of devastation, often with rapid, destructive movement.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Used for moral and physical corruption, particularly the Dajjāl's spreading of evil across the earth.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for physical ravaging; metaphorical for spreading ideological or spiritual corruption.
- Root: خ-ل-ل (kh-l-l)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: khallah denotes a gap, interval, or road between two places; also a rugged, rocky terrain.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In prophetic reports, it signifies a spatial passage or boundary zone.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for a physical path; distinguished from ḥillah (a dwelling place) and ḥullah (a garment or valley).
- Sībawayh Rule: Rule of Nūn al-Wiqāyah (Protective Nūn) — The nūn appended to the first-person singular object pronoun (yāʾ al-mutakallim) is normally restricted to transitive verbs; its attachment to the elative (ism al-tafḍīl) "akhawf" is an anomalous but attested usage, paralleled in poetic license, where the elative is treated as a verb due to its semantic affinity with the verb of wonder (fiʿl al-taʿajjub).
chapters.translation:
I say: The phrase "he was overcome in his sight" (tughashshā al-baṣar) — and he said: Al-Aṣmaʿī said: It is a piece of flesh that grows at the corners of the eye.

[2937] His saying — may Allah bless him and grant him peace — "I heard al-Nawwās ibn Samʿān" — with the fatḥah (a) on the sīn and also with the kasrah (i) on it. His saying — may Allah bless him and grant him peace — "The Messenger of Allah mentioned the Dajjāl one morning, and he lowered his voice and then raised it, until we thought he was in a cluster of palm trees" — this is with the tashdīd (doubling) of the fāʾ in both verbs. Regarding its meaning, there are two opinions. The first is that "lowered" (khaffaḍa) means "belittled," and his saying "raised" (rafaʿa) means "magnified and aggrandized." So from his belittling him is that he is, relative to Allah the Exalted, insignificant — and from this is his saying — may Allah bless him and grant him peace — "He is more insignificant to Allah than that," and that he has no power to kill anyone except that man, and then he becomes incapable against him, and that his affair will collapse and he will be killed thereafter, he and his followers. And from his magnifying and aggrandizing his tribulation and the trial through him are these matters that break the customary course of things, and that there is no prophet except that he warned his people of him. The second opinion is that he lowered his voice in the state of abundance in what he was speaking about, so he lowered it after lengthy speech and fatigue to rest, then he raised it so that his voice would reach everyone.

His saying — may Allah bless him and grant him peace — "Other than the Dajjāl, I fear most for you" (ghayr al-Dajjāl akhawfunī ʿalaykum) — thus it is in all the copies of our lands: "akhawfunī" with a nūn after the fāʾ. Likewise, al-Qāḍī transmitted it from the narration of the majority. He said: And some narrated it with the deletion of the nūn, and both are correct dialects with a single meaning. Our teacher, the Imām Abū ʿAbd Allāh ibn Mālik — may Allah have mercy on him — said: The need calls for discussion of the wording of the ḥadīth and its meaning. As for its wording, because it contains what is not customary: the annexation of "akhawf" (more frightening) to the yāʾ of the speaker joined with the protective nūn. This usage occurs only with transitive verbs. The answer is that the nūn's affirmation was the original rule, but it is an abandoned principle, so attention was drawn to it in a small portion of their speech. He cited verses for this, among them what al-Farrāʾ recited: "So I do not know — and my conjecture is all conjecture — / whether my safe-conduct to my people is Sharāḥī" — meaning Sharāḥīl, truncated outside vocative usage due to poetic necessity. And another recited: "And the one who comes to me (al-muwāfīnī) is not to be denied aid, / for he has multiples of what he had hoped for."

And the elative (ism al-tafḍīl) also resembles the verb, especially with the verb of wonder (fiʿl al-taʿajjub), so it is permissible that the aforementioned nūn attach to it in the ḥadīth, just as it attached in the aforementioned verses. This is the most apparent [explanation] for this nūn here. And it is possible that its meaning is "more frightening to me" (akhawf lī), so the nūn was substituted for the lām, just as substitution occurred in "luʿan" and "ʿan" meaning "laʿalla" (perhaps) and "ʿalla." As for the meaning of the ḥadīth, there are several aspects. The most apparent is that it is from the elative, and its estimation is: "Other than the Dajjāl is the most frightening of my fears for you" (ghayr al-Dajjāl akhawfu makhāwātī ʿalaykum), then the annexed noun was deleted before the yāʾ. From this is his saying — may Allah bless him and grant him peace — "The most frightening thing I fear for my community is the misguiding leaders" (akhawfu mā akhāfu ʿalā ummatī al-aʾimmatu al-muḍillūn), meaning: the things I fear for my community, the most deserving of them to be feared are the misguiding leaders. The second aspect is that it is from "akhawfu min akhāfa" meaning "made afraid" (khawwafa), and its meaning is: other than the Dajjāl is the most severe cause of my fear for you. The third is that it belongs to the category of describing abstract meanings with what describes concrete entities, by way of hyperbole (mubālaghah), as they say in eloquent poetry: "poetry that is poetic" (shiʿr shāʿir) and "the fear of so-and-so is more frightening than your fear" (khawfu fulān akhawfu min khawfik). Its estimation is: "The fear of other than the Dajjāl is the most frightening of my fears for you" (khawfu ghayr al-Dajjāl akhawfu khawfī ʿalaykum), then the first annexed noun was deleted, then the second. This is the end of the Shaykh's speech — may Allah have mercy on him.

His saying — may Allah bless him and grant him peace — "He is a young man with very curly hair" (innahu shābbun qaṭaṭ) — it is with fatḥah on the qāf and the ṭāʾ, meaning: intensely curly-haired, removed from the beloved curl.

His saying — may Allah bless him and grant him peace — "He will emerge from a gap (khallah) between Syria and Iraq" (innahu khārijun khallatan bayna al-Shām wa al-ʿIrāq) — thus in the copies of our lands: "khallah" with fatḥah on the khāʾ (unpointed) and the lām, with tanwīn on the hāʾ. Al-Qāḍī said: The well-known [narration] is "ḥillah" with the unpointed ḥāʾ and naṣb on the tāʾ, meaning un-nunated. It is said its meaning is its direction and its opposite. In Kitāb al-ʿAyn, "al-ḥillah" is a place of rugged stones and rocks. He said: And some narrated it as "ḥillahu" with ḍammah on the lām and the hāʾ of the pronoun, meaning his descent and his alighting. He said: Likewise, al-Ḥumaydī mentioned it in al-Jamʿ bayn al-Ṣaḥīḥayn. He said: And al-Harawī mentioned it as "khallah" with the unpointed khāʾ and tashdīd on the lām, both with fatḥah, and he interpreted it as what lies between the two lands. This is the end of what al-Qāḍī mentioned. And this which he mentioned from al-Harawī is what is found in the copies of our lands, and in al-Jamʿ bayn al-Ṣaḥīḥayn in our lands as well, and it is what the author of Nihāyat al-Gharīb favored, interpreting it as the road between them.

His saying — may Allah bless him and grant him peace — "He will ravage to the right and ravage to the left" (fa-ʿātha yamīnan wa ʿātha shimālan) — it is with an unpointed ʿayn and an unpointed thāʾ with fatḥah, and it is a past-tense verb. Al-ʿayth is corruption, or the most severe corruption, and haste in it. One says from it: ʿātha yaʿīthu. Al-Qāḍī reported that some narrated it as "fa-ʿāthin" with kasrah on the thāʾ, nunated, as an active participle, and it has the same meaning as the first.

His saying — may Allah bless him and grant him peace — "A day like a year, and a day like a month, and a day like a week, and the rest of his days are like your days" — the scholars said: This ḥadīth is upon its apparent meaning, and these three days are long to this extent mentioned in the ḥadīth. This is indicated by his saying — may Allah bless him and grant him peace — "and the rest of his days are like your days."

As for their saying: "O Messenger of Allah, that day which is like a year — will the prayer of one day suffice us in it?" He said: "No, estimate its measure for it" (lā, qaddirū lahu qadarahu). Al-Qāḍī and others said: This is a ruling specific to that day, legislated for us by the Master of the Law. They said: Were it not for this ḥadīth, and we were left to our own reasoning, we would have limited ourselves in it to the five prayers at the known times of other days. The meaning of "estimate its measure for it" (aqdirū lahu qadarahu) is that when, after the dawn (fajr), there passes an amount [of time] equivalent to what is between it and the noon prayer (ẓuhr) on every [normal] day, then pray the noon prayer. Then if there passes after it an amount equivalent to what is between it and the afternoon prayer (ʿaṣr), then pray the afternoon prayer. Then if there passes after this an amount equivalent to what is between it and the sunset prayer (maghrib), then pray the sunset prayer. Likewise the night prayer (ʿishāʾ), then the dawn prayer, then the noon prayer, then the afternoon prayer, then the sunset prayer, and so on until that day concludes. And there will have occurred in it the prayers of a full year, all of them obligatory, performed within their [estimated] times. As for the second day, which is like a month, and the third, which is like a week, they are analogous to the first day: one estimates for them as for the first day, according to what we have mentioned. And Allah knows best.

chapters.title_en: Section 978 — Commentary on the Hadith of the Descent of Jesus (ʿAlayhi al-Salām) and the Signs of the Hour
chapters.arabic_text:
الله عليه وسلم (فتروح عليهم سارحتهم أطول ما كانت ذرا وأسبغه ضروعا وأمده

خواصر) أما تروح فمعناه ترجع آخر النهار والسارحة هي الماشية التي تسرح أي

تذهب أول النهار إلى المرعى وأما الذرى فبضم الذال المعجمة وهى الأعالى

والأسنمة جمع ذروة بضم الذال وكسرها وقوله (وأسبغه) بالسين المهملة والغين

المعجمة أي أطوله لكثرة اللبن وكذا أمده خواصر لكثرة امتلائها من الشبع

قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (فتتبعه كنوزها كيعاسيب النحل) هي ذكور النحل هكذا

فسره بن قتيبة وآخرون قال القاضي المراد جماعة النحل لاذكورها خاصة لكنه

كنى
# 
# عن الجماعة باليعسوب وهو أميرها لأنه متى طار تبعته جماعته والله أعلم

قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (فيقطعه جزلتين رمية الغرض) بفتح الجيم على

المشهور وحكى بن دريد كسرها أي قطعتين ومعنى رمية الغرض أنه يجعل بين

الجزلتين مقدار رميته هذا هو الظاهر المشهور وحكى القاضي هذا ثم قال وعندي

أن فيه تقديما وتأخيرا وتقديره فيصيبه إصابة رمية الغرض فيقطعه جزلتين

والصحيح الأول قوله (فينزل عند المنارة البيضاء شرقي دمشق بين مهرودتين)

أما المنارة فبفتح الميم وهذه المنارة موجودة اليوم شرقي دمشق ودمشق بكسر

الدال وفتح الميم وهذا هو المشهور وحكى صاحب المطالع كسر الميم وهذا الحديث

من فضائل دمشق وفي عند ثلاث لغات كسر العين وضمها وفتحها والمشهور الكسر

وأما المهروذتان فروي بالدال المهملة والذال المعجمة والمهملة أكثر

والوجهان مشهوران للمتقدمين والمتأخرين من أهل اللغة والغريب وغيرهم وأكثر

ما يقع في النسخ بالمهملة كما هو المشهور ومعناه لابس مهروذتين أي ثوبين

مصبوغين بورس ثم بزعفران وقيل هما شقتان والشقة نصف الملاءة قوله صلى الله

عليه وسلم (تحدر منه جمان كاللؤلؤ) الجمان بضم الجيم وتخفيف الميم هي حبات

من الفضة تصنع على هيئة اللؤلؤ الكبار والمراد يتحدر منه الماء  على هيئة

اللولؤ فى صفاته فسمي الماء جمانا لشبهه به في الصفاء قوله صلى الله عليه

وسلم (فلايحل لكافر يجد ريح نفسه الامات) هكذا الرواية فلا يحل بكسر الحاء

ونفسه بفتح الفاء ومعنى لا يحل لا يمكن ولا يقع وقال القاضي معناه عندي حق

وواجب قال ورواه بعضهم بضم الحاء
# 
# وهو وهم وغلط قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (يدركه بباب لد) هو بضم اللام

وتشديد الدال مصروف وهو بلدة قريبة من بيت المقدس قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم

(ثم يأتي عيسى صلى الله عليه وسلم قوما قد عصمهم الله منه فيمسح عن وجوههم)

قال القاضي يحتمل أن هذا المسح حقيقة على ظاهره فيمسح على وجوههم تبركا

وبرا ويحتمل أنه إشارة إلى كشف ما هم فيه من الشدة والخوف قوله تعالى

(أخرجت عبادا لى لايدان لأحد بقتالهم فحرز عبادي إلى الطور) فقوله لايدان

بكسر النون تثنية يد قال العلماء معناه لا قدرة ولا طاقة يقال مالى بهذا

الأمر يد ومالى به يدان لأن المباشرة والدفع إنما يكون باليد وكأن يديه

معدومتان لعجزه عن دفعه ومعنى حرزهم إلى الطور أي ضمهم واجعله لهم حرزا

يقال أحرزت الشيء أحرزه إحرازا إذا حفظته وضممته إليك وصنته عن الأخذ ووقع

في بعض النسخ حزب بالحاء والزاي والباء أي اجمعهم قال القاضي وروي حوز

بالواو والزاي ومعناه نحهم وأزلهم عن طريقهم إلى الطور قوله (وهم من كل حدب

ينسلون) الحدب النشز وينسلون يمشون مسرعين قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (فيرسل

الله تعالى
# 
# عليهم النغف في رقابهم فيصبحون فرسى) النغف بنون وغين معجمة مفتوحتين ثم

فاء وهو دود يكون في أنوف الإبل والغنم الواحدة نغفة والفرسى بفتح الفاء

مقصور أي قتلى واحدهم فريس قوله (ملأه زهمهم ونتنهم) هو بفتح الهاء أي

دسمهم ورائحتهم الكريهة قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (لايكن منه بيت مدر) أى

لايمنع من نزول الماء بيت المدر بفتح الميم والدال وهو الطين الصلب قوله

صلى الله عليه وسلم (فيغسل الأرض حتى يتركها كالزلفة) روي  بفتح الزاي

واللام والقاف وروي الزلفة بضم الزاى وإسكان اللام وبالفاء وروي الزلفة

بفتح الزاي واللام وبالفاء وقال القاضي روي بالفاء والقاف وبفتح اللام

وبإسكانها وكلها صحيحة قال في المشارق والزاي مفتوحة واختلفوا في معناه

فقال ثعلب وأبو زيد وآخرون معناه كالمرآة وحكى صاحب المشارق هذا عن بن عباس

أيضا شبهها بالمرآة في صفائها ونظافتها وقيل كمصانع الماء أي إن الماء

يستنقع فيها حتى تصير كالمصنع الذي يجتمع فيه الماء وقال أبو عبيد معناه

كالإجانة الخضراء وقيل كالصحفة وقيل كالروضة قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (تأكل

العصابة من الرمانة ويستظلون بقحفها) العصابة الجماعة وقحفها بكسر القاف هو

مقعر قشرها شبهها بقحف الرأس وهو الذي فوق الدماغ وقيل ما انفلق من جمجمته

وانفصل قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (ويبارك في الرسل حتى إن اللقحة من الإبل

لتكفي الفئام من الناس) الرسل بكسر الراء وإسكان السين هو اللبن واللقحة
# 
# بكسر اللام وفتحها لغتان مشهورتان والكسر أشهر وهي القريبة العهد
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ر-و-ح (r-w-ḥ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: "To return, to go back; the spirit (rūḥ) as that which animates; al-rāʾiḥah is the evening return of livestock from pasture."
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): "In theological usage, denotes the return of a state or being to its origin; here, the temporal return of cattle at day's end."
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): "Literal (ḥaqīqah) for physical return; metaphorical (majāz) for spiritual restoration or divine re-ordering."
- Sībawayh Rule: "Rule of Ẓarf and Fiʿl (Adverbial Accusative) — The verb 'tarūḥu' governs an implicit time adverb (ākhira al-nahār), requiring the accusative of specification (tamyīz) for 'aṭwalu mā kānat dharā'."

- Root: س-ر-ح (s-r-ḥ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: "To go out early, to depart; al-sāriḥah is livestock that grazes freely by day."
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): "In Quranic usage (e.g., {«وَمِنَ الْإِبِلِ اثْنَيْنِ»}), it signifies the natural, unconstrained movement of creatures, here applied to cattle."
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): "Literal for physical grazing; majāz for the soul's unhindered pursuit of sustenance."
- Sībawayh Rule: "Rule of Ism al-Fāʿil (Active Participle) — 'al-sāriḥah' functions as a substantive adjective with an implied verbal force, governing the genitive of purpose (li-l-marʿā)."

- Root: ذ-ر-و (dh-r-w)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: "The upper part, summit; dhurwah (pl. dharā) is the highest point of a thing, especially a camel's hump."
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): "Metaphysically, the apex of excellence; in this hadith, the fullness of livestock's physical prime."
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): "Literal for anatomical height; majāz for superiority in abundance and quality."
- Sībawayh Rule: "Rule of Jamʿ al-Kathrah (Plural of Multitude) — 'dharā' is a broken plural indicating multiplicity, requiring the adjective 'aṭwalu' to agree in the feminine singular due to non-human plural treatment."
chapters.translation:
I say: The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: "Their livestock will return to them in the evening, the tallest in humps, the most copious in udders, and the fullest in flanks." As for "tarūḥu" (returns in the evening), its meaning is "to come back at the end of the day." "Al-sāriḥah" (the grazing livestock) is the cattle that go out (yasraḥu), i.e., that depart at the beginning of the day to the pasture. As for "al-dharā" (the humps), it is with a ḍammah on the dhāl (dh-dhāl al-muʿjamah), and they are the upper parts and the humps; it is the plural of "dhurwah," with a ḍammah or a kasrah on the dhāl. His saying "wa-asbaghuhā" (most copious) — with an unpointed sīn and a pointed ghayn — means "the most abundant in milk." Likewise, "amaddahā khawāṣir" (fullest in flanks) is due to their great fullness from satiety.

His saying (peace and blessings of God be upon him): "Then its treasures will follow it like the male bees (yaʿāsīb) of the honeybees" — these are the male bees. This is how Ibn Qutaybah and others interpreted it. Al-Qāḍī said: The intended meaning is the entire group of bees, not specifically the males; but he used the metaphor of the group by "al-yaʿsūb," which is their leader, because when it flies, its group follows it. And God knows best.

His saying (peace and blessings of God be upon him): "Then he will cut it into two pieces (jizlatayn), the throw of a target (ramyat al-gharaḍ)" — with a fatḥah on the jīm, according to the well-known reading; Ibn Durayd reported a kasrah on it, meaning "two cut portions." The meaning of "ramyat al-gharaḍ" is that he places between the two pieces the distance of his throw. This is the apparent and well-known interpretation. Al-Qāḍī reported this, then said: In my view, there is a forward and backward arrangement (taqdīm wa-taʾkhīr) in it, and its estimation is: "He will strike it with the strike of a target-throw, then cut it into two pieces." The correct view is the first.

His saying: "Then he will descend at the white minaret (al-manārah al-bayḍāʾ) east of Damascus, between two Mahrūdatayn (garments dyed with wars and saffron)" — As for "al-manārah," it is with a fatḥah on the mīm. This minaret exists today east of Damascus. "Dimashq" (Damascus) is with a kasrah on the dāl and a fatḥah on the mīm; this is the well-known pronunciation. The author of al-Maṭāliʿ reported a kasrah on the mīm. This hadith is among the virtues of Damascus. As for "al-Mahrūdatān," it has three pronunciations: kasrah on the ʿayn, ḍammah, and fatḥah; the well-known is the kasrah. As for "al-Mahrūdhatān," it is narrated with an unpointed dāl and a pointed dhāl; the unpointed dāl is more frequent. Both forms are well-known among the early and later scholars of language, strange narrations (gharīb), and others. Most occurrences in the manuscripts use the unpointed dāl, as is the well-known form. Its meaning is "one wearing two Mahrūdahs," i.e., two garments dyed with wars (a yellow dye) and then with saffron. It is also said they are two cloths (shuqqatān), and a shuqqah is half of a large wrap (milāʾah).

His saying (peace and blessings of God be upon him): "Pearls like large pearls (jumān) will stream down from him" — "Al-jumān," with a ḍammah on the jīm and a lightening (takhfīf) of the mīm, are beads of silver made in the form of large pearls. The intended meaning is that water will stream down from him in the form of pearls, in their qualities; thus the water is called "jumān" due to its resemblance to it in clarity.

His saying (peace and blessings of God be upon him): "It will not be lawful (fa-lā yaḥillu) for any disbeliever who finds the scent of his breath (nafasihi) but that he dies" — This is the narration: "fa-lā yaḥillu" with a kasrah on the ḥāʾ, and "nafasihi" with a fatḥah on the fāʾ. The meaning of "lā yaḥillu" is "it is not possible and does not occur." Al-Qāḍī said: In my view, its meaning is "true and obligatory (ḥaqq wa-wājib)." He said: Some narrated it with a ḍammah on the ḥāʾ, and that is an error and a mistake.

His saying (peace and blessings of God be upon him): "He will overtake him at the gate of Lud (Bāb Ludd)" — It is with a ḍammah on the lām and a shaddah on the dāl, and it is declinable (maṣrūf); it is a town near Jerusalem (Bayt al-Maqdis).

His saying (peace and blessings of God be upon him): "Then Jesus (peace be upon him) will come to a people whom God has protected from him, and he will wipe (yamsaḥu) their faces" — Al-Qāḍī said: It is possible that this wiping is literal (ḥaqīqah) on its apparent meaning, so he wipes their faces as a blessing and an act of goodness. It is also possible that it is an indication of removing (kashf) the hardship and fear they are in.

His saying (God Almighty): "I have brought forth servants of Mine over whom none has power to fight (lā yadāni), so gather My servants to the Mount (al-Ṭūr)" — As for "lā yadāni," it is with a kasrah on the nūn, a dual of "yad" (hand). The scholars said: Its meaning is "no power and no ability." It is said: "I have no hand (yad) in this matter" and "I have no two hands (yadāni) for it," because direct action and repulsion are only by the hand; it is as if his two hands are non-existent due to his inability to repel it. The meaning of "ḥurrizuhum ilā al-Ṭūr" (gather them to the Mount) is "gather them and make it a refuge (ḥirz) for them." It is said: "Aḥraztu al-shayʾa uḥrizuhu iḥrāzan" when you preserve it, gather it to yourself, and protect it from being taken. In some manuscripts, it occurs as "ḥuzb" with a ḥāʾ, zāy, and bāʾ, meaning "gather them." Al-Qāḍī said: It is also narrated as "ḥawz" with a wāw and zāy, and its meaning is "remove them and turn them away from their path to the Mount."

His saying: "And they will hasten forth from every elevated place (ḥadab)" — "Al-ḥadab" is the high ground (al-nashaz), and "yansilūn" means "they walk quickly."

His saying (peace and blessings of God be upon him): "Then God Almighty will send upon them the maggots (al-naghaf) in their necks, and they will become corpses (farsā)" — "Al-naghaf" is with a nūn and a pointed ghayn, both fatḥah, then a fāʾ; it is a worm that occurs in the noses of camels and sheep, its singular being "naghafah." "Al-farsā" is with a fatḥah on the fāʾ, and it is a shortened form (maqṣūr), meaning "slain ones"; its singular is "farīs."

His saying: "The earth will be filled with their grease (zahamuhum) and their stench (natunuhum)" — It is with a fatḥah on the hāʾ, meaning "their fat and their foul odor."

His saying (peace and blessings of God be upon him): "No house of clay (bayt madar) will prevent it" — i.e., no house of clay will prevent the descent of water. "Al-madar" is with a fatḥah on the mīm and dāl, and it is hardened clay (al-ṭīn al-ṣulb).

His saying (peace and blessings of God be upon him): "Then he will wash the earth until he leaves it like a mirror (al-zulfah)" — It is narrated with a fatḥah on the zāy, lām, and qāf; also narrated as "al-zulfah" with a ḍammah on the zāy, sukūn on the lām, and with a fāʾ; and also "al-zulfah" with a fatḥah on the zāy and lām and with a fāʾ. Al-Qāḍī said: It is narrated with a fāʾ and a qāf, with a fatḥah or sukūn on the lām, and all are correct. He said in al-Mashāriq: The zāy is fatḥah, and they differed on its meaning. Thaʿlab, Abū Zayd, and others said: Its meaning is "like a mirror." The author of al-Mashāriq reported this from Ibn ʿAbbās as well, likening it to a mirror in its clarity and cleanliness. It is also said: "Like water reservoirs (maṣāniʿ)," i.e., the water will pool in it until it becomes like a reservoir in which water collects. Abū ʿUbayd said: Its meaning is "like a green basin (ijānah khaḍrāʾ)." It is also said: "Like a dish (ṣaḥfah)," and it is said: "Like a meadow (rawḍah)."

His saying (peace and blessings of God be upon him): "A group (al-ʿiṣābah) will eat from a single pomegranate and seek shade under its skin (qilfuhā)" — "Al-ʿiṣābah" is the group (al-jamāʿah). "Qilfuhā" is with a kasrah on the qāf; it is the concave part of its peel, likened to the skull (qilf al-raʾs), which is what is above the brain. It is also said: It is what splits off from the cranium and separates.

His saying (peace and blessings of God be upon him): "And blessing will be placed in the milk (al-risl) until a single she-camel (al-laqūḥah) from the camels will suffice a large multitude (al-fīʾām) of people" — "Al-risl" is with a kasrah on the rāʾ and sukūn on the sīn; it is milk. "Al-laqūḥah" is with a kasrah or fatḥah on the lām, both being well-known pronunciations, with the kasrah being more famous; it is the she-camel that has recently given birth (al-qarībah al-ʿahd).

chapters.title_en: Section 979 — Lexical Clarifications on the Dajjāl Narrations and the Descent of Jesus (ʿAlayhi al-Salām)
chapters.arabic_text:
بالولادة وجمعها لقح بكسر اللام وفتح القاف كبركة وبرك واللقوح ذات اللبن

وجمعها لقاح والفئام بكسر الفاء وبعدها همزة ممدودة وهي الجماعة الكثيرة

هذا هو المشهور والمعروف في اللغة وكتب الغريب ورواية الحديث أنه بكسر

الفاء وبالهمز قال القاضي ومنهم من لايجيز الهمز بل يقوله بالياء وقال في

المشارق وحكاه الخليل بفتح الفاء وهي رواية القابسي قال وذكره صاحب العين

غير مهموز فأدخله في حرف الياء وحكى الخطابي أن بعضهم ذكره بفتح الفاء

وتشديد الياء وهو غلط فاحش قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (لتكفي الفخذ من الناس)

قال أهل اللغة الفخذ الجماعة من الأقارب وهم دون البطن والبطن دون القبيلة

قال القاضي قال بن فارس الفخذ هنا بإسكان الخاء لا غير فلا يقال إلا

بإسكانها بخلاف الفخذ التي هي العضو فإنها تكسر وتسكن قوله صلى الله عليه

وسلم (فتقبض روح كل مؤمن وكل مسلم) هكذا هو في جميع نسخ مسلم وكل مسلم

بالواو قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (يتهارجون تهارج الحمير) أي يجامع  الرجال

النساء بحضرة الناس كما يفعل الحمير ولا يكترثون لذلك والهرج بإسكان الراء

الجماع يقال هرج زوجته أي جامعها يهرجها بفتح الراء وضمها وكسرها قوله صلى

الله عليه وسلم (يسيرون حتى
# 
# ينتهوا إلى جبل الخمر) هو بخاء معجمة وميم مفتوحتين والخمر الشجر الملتف

الذي يستر من فيه وقد فسره في الحديث بأنه جبل بيت المقدس
# [2938] قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (محرم عليه أن يدخل نقاب المدينة) هو

بكسر النون أي طرقها وفجاجها وهو جمع نقب وهو الطريق بين جبلين قوله صلى

الله عليه وسلم (فيقتله ثم يحييه) قال المازري إن قيل إظهار المعجزة على يد

الكذاب ليس بممكن وكيف ظهرت هذه الخوارق للعادة على يده فالجواب أنه إنما

يدعي
# 
# الربوبية وأدلة الحدوث تخل ما ادعاه وتكذبه وأما النبي فإنما يدعي النبوة

وليست مستحيلة في البشر فإذا أتى بدليل لم يعارضه شيء صدق وأما قول الدجال

أرأيتم إن قتلت هذا ثم أحييته أتشكون في الأمر فيقولون لافقد يستشكل لأن ما

أظهره الدجال لادلالة فيه لربوبيته لظهور النقص عليه ودلائل الحدوث وتشويه

الذات وشهادة كذبه وكفره المكتوبة بين عينيه وغير ذلك ويجاب بنحو ما سبق في

أول الباب هو أنهم لعلهم قالوا خوفا منه وتقية لاتصديقا ويحتمل أنهم قصدوا

لانشك في كذبك وكفرك فإن من شك في كذبه وكفره كفر وخادعوه بهذه التورية

خوفا منه ويحتمل أن الذين قالوا لانشك هم مصدقوه من اليهود وغيرهم ممن قدر

الله تعالى شقاوته قوله (قال أبو إسحاق يقال ان هذا الرجل هو الخضر عليه

السلام) أبو إسحاق هذا هو إبراهيم بن سفيان راوي الكتاب عن مسلم وكذا قال

معمر في جامعه فى أثر هذا الحديث كما ذكره بن سفيان وهذا تصريح منه بحياة

الخضر عليه السلام وهو الصحيح وقد سبق في بابه من كتاب المناقب والمسالح

قوم معهم سلاح يرتبون فى المراكز كالخفر أسموا
# 
# بذلك لحملهم السلاح قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (فيأمر الدجال به فيشبح

فيقول خذوه وشجوه) فالأول بشين معجمة ثم باء موحدة  ثم حاء مهملة أي مدوه

على بطنه والثاني شجوه بالجيم المشددة من الشج وهو الجرح في الرأس والوجه

الثاني فيشج كالأول فيقول خذوه وشبحوه بالباء والحاء والثالث فيشج وشجوه

كلاهما بالجيم وصحح القاضي الوجه الثاني وهو الذي ذكره الحميدي في الجمع

بين الصحيحين والأصح عندنا الأول وأما قوله (فيوسع ظهره) فبإسكان الواو

وفتح السين قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (فيؤشر بالمئشار من مفرقه) هكذا

الرواية
# 
# يؤشر بالهمز والمئشار بهمزة بعد الميم وهو الأفصح ويجوز تخفيف الهمزة

فيهما فيجعل في الأول واوا وفي الثاني ياء ويجوز المنشار بالنون وعلى هذا

يقال نشرت الخشبة وعلى الأول يقال أشرتها ومفرق الرأس بكسر الراء وسطه

والترقوة بفتح التاء وضم القاف وهي العظم الذي بين ثغرة النحر والعاتق
# [2939] قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (وما ينصبك) هو بضم الياء على اللغة

المشهورة أي ما يتعبك من أمره قال بن دريد يقال أنصبه المرض وغيره ونصبه

والأولى أفصح قال وهو تغير الحال من مرض أو تعب قوله (قلت يارسول الله إنهم

يقولون إن معه الطعام والأنهار وقال هو أهون على الله من ذلك) قال القاضي

معناه هو أهون على الله من أن يجعل ما خلقه الله تعالى على يده مضلا

للمؤمنين ومشككا لقلوبهم بل إنما جعله له ليزداد الذين آمنوا إيمانا ويثبت

الحجة على الكافرين والمنافقين
# 
# ونحوهم وليس معناه أنه ليس معه شيء من ذلك
# [2940] قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (فيبعث الله عيسى بن مريم) أى ينزله من

السماء حاكما بشر عنا وقد سبق بيان هذا في كتاب الإيمان قال القاضي رحمه

الله تعالى نزول عيسى عليه السلام وقتله الدجال حق وصحيح عند أهل السنة

للأحاديث الصحيحة في ذلك وليس فى العقل ولافى الشرع ما يبطله فوجب إثباته

وأنكر ذلك بعض المعتزلة والجهيمة ومن وافقهم وزعموا أن هذه الأحاديث مردودة

بقوله تعالى وخاتم النبيين وبقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم لا نبي بعدى وباجماع
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ل-ق-ح (L-Q-Ḥ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning is "to impregnate" or "to fertilize"; for she-camels, "to conceive." The plural forms cited (لِقْحٌ, لِقَاحٌ) denote a lactating she-camel (ذَاتُ لَبَنٍ).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological usage, the term is literal (ḥaqīqah) for animal lactation, with no metaphorical extension in this context.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): The distinction here is purely phonetic/orthographic—whether the initial consonant is kasrah (لِقْح) or fatḥah (لَقْح)—not rhetorical.
- Root: ف-ئ-م (F-ʾ-M)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: The root denotes "a large multitude" or "a great company" (الْجَمَاعَةُ الْكَثِيرَةُ).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Used literally for a crowd; no theological nuance.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): The debate is whether the hamzah is retained (فِئَام) or replaced with yāʾ (فِيَام), and whether the fāʾ takes kasrah or fatḥah—a purely morphological variance.
- Root: ف-خ-ذ (F-KH-DH)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: The thigh (body part); also a "clan" or "sub-tribe" (الْجَمَاعَةُ مِنَ الْأَقَارِبِ), smaller than the بَطْن (belly/sub-tribe) and larger than the قَبِيلَة (tribe).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In kinship terminology, it is a technical social category, not metaphorical.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): The distinction is vocalic—إِسْكَانُ الْخَاءِ (sukūn on khāʾ) is obligatory for the kinship meaning, whereas the body part allows both kasrah and sukūn.
- Root: ه-ر-ج (H-R-J)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: The root means "sexual intercourse" (الْجِمَاع); also "slaughter" or "confusion" in other contexts.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Here it is literal for copulation, used in the ḥadīth to describe shameless public fornication.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): The verb هَرَجَ زَوْجَتَهُ is literal (ḥaqīqah) for intercourse; the simile "like donkeys" (تَهَارُجُ الْحُمُرِ) is a comparative majāz for lack of shame.
- Root: خ-م-ر (KH-M-R)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: The root means "to cover" or "conceal"; الْخَمْرُ (wine) is so named for covering the intellect. Here, الْخَمَرُ (with fatḥah) is "dense, intertwined trees that conceal those within."
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In the ḥadīth, it is literal for a thicket, identified as the mountain of Jerusalem.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): The term is used literally for vegetation, not metaphorically for wine.
- Root: ن-ق-ب (N-Q-B)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: The root means "to pierce" or "bore through"; النَّقْبُ is a mountain pass or road between two mountains.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Literal for a geographical passage; no theological sense.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): The plural نِقَابٌ (with kasrah on nūn) refers to the roads and passes of Medina—literal usage.
- Root: ش-ج-ج (SH-J-J)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: The root means "to wound the head or face" (الْجُرْحُ فِي الرَّأْسِ وَالْوَجْهِ).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Literal for physical injury; no metaphorical extension.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): The verb شَجَّ is literal for head wounds; the passive form يُشَجُّ is used in the ḥadīth for the Dajjāl's punishment.
- Root: ن-ص-ب (N-S-B)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: The root means "to erect" or "set up"; also "to tire" or "exhaust" (أَنْصَبَهُ الْمَرَضُ).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In the ḥadīth, it is literal for fatigue caused by another's affair.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): The verb أَنْصَبَ (with ḍammah on yāʾ) is the more eloquent (أَفْصَح) form for "to weary," versus نَصَبَ.
- Root: خ-ل-ق (KH-L-Q)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: The root means "to create" or "measure"; also "to smooth" or "polish."
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In kalām, الْخَلْقُ is origination (ḥudūth) of beings; the ḥadīth's phrase "أَهْوَنُ عَلَى اللهِ مِنْ ذَلِكَ" (easier for God than that) refers to divine power over creation.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): The phrase is literal—God's ability to create is not constrained; the Dajjāl's miracles are not true creation but tests.
- Sībawayh Rule: Nominal Sentence with Predicate Emphasis (الْجُمْلَةُ الِاسْمِيَّةُ وَتَقْدِيمُ الْخَبَرِ) — In "هُوَ أَهْوَنُ عَلَى اللهِ مِنْ ذَلِكَ," the pronoun هُوَ is the subject (mubtadaʾ) and أَهْوَنُ is the predicate (khabar), with the comparative form (afʿal al-tafḍīl) governing the preposition عَلَى and the source of comparison (مِنْ ذَلِكَ). The construction emphasizes the ease of the matter relative to God's power, not its impossibility.
chapters.translation:
I say: Know that the word "لِقْح" (with kasrah on the lām and fatḥah on the qāf) is the singular, and its plural is "لِقَاحٌ" — like "بَرَكَة" and "بِرَك" — and it means a she-camel that has milk. Its plural is "لِقَاحٌ." The word "فِئَام" (with kasrah on the fāʾ and a lengthened hamzah after it) means a large multitude. This is the well-known and established form in the language, in the books of gharīb (rare expressions), and in the narration of the ḥadīth — that it is with kasrah on the fāʾ and with hamzah. Al-Qāḍī said: Among them are those who do not permit the hamzah but rather pronounce it with yāʾ. He said in al-Mashāriq: Al-Khalīl reported it with fatḥah on the fāʾ, and that is the narration of al-Qābisī. He said: The author of al-ʿAyn mentioned it without hamzah, so he placed it in the chapter of yāʾ. Al-Khaṭṭābī reported that some mentioned it with fatḥah on the fāʾ and tashdīd on the yāʾ, and that is a gross error.

His saying, may God's peace and blessings be upon him: «لَتَكْفِيَنَّ الْفَخِذَ مِنَ النَّاسِ» (The clan of people will suffice). The people of language said: "الْفَخِذُ" is a group of relatives, and they are below the "بَطْن" (sub-tribe), and the "بَطْن" is below the "قَبِيلَة" (tribe). Al-Qāḍī said: Ibn Fāris said: "الْفَخِذ" here is with sukūn on the khāʾ, and nothing else — it is not said except with sukūn, unlike "الْفَخِذ" which is the body part (thigh), for it may take kasrah or sukūn.

His saying, may God's peace and blessings be upon him: «فَتُقْبَضُ رُوحُ كُلِّ مُؤْمِنٍ وَكُلِّ مُسْلِمٍ» (Then the soul of every believer and every Muslim will be taken). Thus it is in all copies of Muslim: "وَكُلِّ مُسْلِمٍ" with the wāw.

His saying, may God's peace and blessings be upon him: «يَتَهَارَجُونَ تَهَارُجَ الْحُمُرِ» (They will fornicate publicly like donkeys fornicate) — meaning men will have intercourse with women in the presence of people, just as donkeys do, and they will not care about that. "الْهَرْج" (with sukūn on the rāʾ) is intercourse. It is said: "هَرَجَ زَوْجَتَهُ" meaning he had intercourse with her; "يَهْرِجُهَا" with fatḥah, ḍammah, or kasrah on the rāʾ.

His saying, may God's peace and blessings be upon him: «يَسِيرُونَ حَتَّى يَنْتَهُوا إِلَى جَبَلِ الْخَمَرِ» (They will travel until they reach the mountain of al-Khamar). It is with a muʿjamah khāʾ and fatḥah on both the khāʾ and the mīm. "الْخَمَرُ" is dense, intertwined trees that conceal those within. It has been explained in the ḥadīth that it is the mountain of Jerusalem.

[2938] His saying, may God's peace and blessings be upon him: «مُحَرَّمٌ عَلَيْهِ أَنْ يَدْخُلَ نِقَابَ الْمَدِينَةِ» (It is forbidden for him to enter the passes of Medina). It is with kasrah on the nūn, meaning its roads and mountain passes. It is the plural of "نَقْب," which is the road between two mountains.

His saying, may God's peace and blessings be upon him: «فَيَقْتُلُهُ ثُمَّ يُحْيِيهِ» (Then he will kill him, then bring him back to life). Al-Māzarī said: If it is said, "The manifestation of a miracle at the hand of a liar is not possible — how then did these violations of custom (kharq al-ʿādah) appear at his hand?" The answer is that he (the Dajjāl) only claims divinity (rubūbiyyah), and the proofs of origination (ḥudūth) invalidate what he claims and belie him. As for the Prophet, he only claims prophethood (nubuwwah), which is not impossible for a human being. So when he brings a proof that nothing contradicts, he is believed. As for the Dajjāl's saying, "Do you see — if I kill this one and then revive him, do you doubt the matter?" and they say, "No" — this is problematic, because what the Dajjāl displays has no evidence for his divinity, due to the appearance of deficiency upon him, the proofs of origination, the ugliness of his form, the testimony of his lying and disbelief written between his eyes, and other things. The answer is similar to what preceded at the beginning of the chapter: perhaps they said that out of fear of him and as dissimulation (taqiyyah), not as affirmation. And it is possible that they intended, "We do not doubt your lying and your disbelief" — for whoever doubts his lying and disbelief commits disbelief — and they deceived him with this equivocation (tawriyah) out of fear of him. And it is possible that those who said "We do not doubt" were his believers among the Jews and others whom God Almighty decreed for wretchedness.

His saying: «قَالَ أَبُو إِسْحَاقَ: يُقَالُ إِنَّ هَذَا الرَّجُلَ هُوَ الْخَضِرُ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ» (Abū Isḥāq said: It is said that this man is al-Khiḍr, peace be upon him). This Abū Isḥāq is Ibrāhīm ibn Sufyān, the transmitter of the book from Muslim. Likewise, Maʿmar said in his Jāmiʿ, following this ḥadīth, as Ibn Sufyān mentioned. This is an explicit statement from him affirming the life of al-Khiḍr, peace be upon him — and that is the correct view. It has already preceded in its chapter in the Book of Virtues (Kitāb al-Manāqib).

"الْمَسَالِح" — a people with weapons stationed in outposts, like guards; they were named thus for carrying weapons.

His saying, may God's peace and blessings be upon him: «فَيَأْمُرُ الدَّجَّالُ بِهِ فَيُشَجُّ، فَيَقُولُ: خُذُوهُ وَشُجُّوهُ» (Then the Dajjāl will command regarding him, and he will be wounded, and he will say: Take him and wound him). The first is with a muʿjamah shīn, then a muwahḥadah bāʾ, then a muhmalah ḥāʾ — meaning "stretch him on his belly." The second, "شُجُّوهُ" with a mushaddadah jīm, is from "الشَّجّ," which is the wounding of the head and face. The second narration is "فَيُشَجُّ" like the first, and he says "خُذُوهُ وَشَبِّحُوهُ" with bāʾ and ḥāʾ. The third is "فَيُشَجُّ وَشُجُّوهُ" — both with jīm. Al-Qāḍī authenticated the second version, which is what al-Ḥumaydī mentioned in al-Jamʿ bayn al-Ṣaḥīḥayn. The most correct view with us is the first. As for his saying «فَيُوسِعُ ظَهْرَهُ» (and he will widen his back), it is with sukūn on the wāw and fatḥah on the sīn.

His saying, may God's peace and blessings be upon him: «فَيُؤْشِرُ بِالْمِئْشَارِ مِنْ مَفْرِقِهِ» (Then he will saw him with a saw from the crown of his head). Thus is the narration: "يُؤْشِرُ" with hamzah, and "الْمِئْشَار" with hamzah after the mīm — and this is the most eloquent (afṣaḥ). It is permissible to lighten the hamzah in both, making it a wāw in the first and a yāʾ in the second. It is also permissible to say "الْمِنْشَار" with nūn, and on this basis one says "نَشَرْتُ الْخَشَبَةَ" (I sawed the wood), while on the first basis one says "أَشَرْتُهَا." "مَفْرِقُ الرَّأْسِ" (with kasrah on the rāʾ) is the middle of the head. "التَّرْقُوَة" (with fatḥah on the tāʾ and ḍammah on the qāf) is the bone between the hollow of the collarbone and the shoulder.

[2939] His saying, may God's peace and blessings be upon him: «وَمَا يُنْصِبُكَ» (And what will weary you) — it is with ḍammah on the yāʾ, according to the well-known language, meaning "what will tire you from his affair." Ibn Durayd said: One says "أَنْصَبَهُ الْمَرَضُ وَغَيْرُهُ" (illness or other things wearied him) and "نَصَبَهُ" — and the first is more eloquent. He said: It is the alteration of one's state due to illness or fatigue.

His saying: «قُلْتُ: يَا رَسُولَ اللهِ، إِنَّهُمْ يَقُولُونَ: إِنَّ مَعَهُ الطَّعَامَ وَالْأَنْهَارَ. قَالَ: هُوَ أَهْوَنُ عَلَى اللهِ مِنْ ذَلِكَ» (I said: O Messenger of God, they say that with him are food and rivers. He said: That is easier for God than that). Al-Qāḍī said: Its meaning is that it is easier for God than to make what God Almighty created at his hand a means of misleading the believers and causing doubt in their hearts. Rather, He only made it for him so that those who believe would increase in faith and so that the proof would be established against the disbelievers, the hypocrites, and those like them. It does not mean that he has none of that with him.

[2940] His saying, may God's peace and blessings be upon him: «فَيَبْعَثُ اللهُ عِيسَى ابْنَ مَرْيَمَ» (Then God will send Jesus son of Mary) — meaning He will descend him from heaven as a just judge from among us. The explanation of this has already preceded in the Book of Faith (Kitāb al-Īmān). Al-Qāḍī, may God Almighty have mercy on him, said: The descent of Jesus, peace be upon him, and his killing of the Dajjāl is true and correct according to the People of the Sunnah (Ahl al-Sunnah), due to the authentic ḥadīths on that. There is nothing in reason (al-ʿaql) or in the Sacred Law (al-sharʿ) that invalidates it, so affirming it is obligatory. Some of the Muʿtazilah, the Jahmiyyah, and those who agree with them denied this, claiming that these ḥadīths are rejected by His saying, the Most High: {وَخَاتَمَ النَّبِيِّينَ} (and the Seal of the Prophets) [al-Aḥzāb 33:40], and by his saying, may God's peace and blessings be upon him: «لَا نَبِيَّ بَعْدِي» (No prophet after me), and by the consensus (ijmāʿ).

chapters.title_en: Section 980 — The Descent of Jesus, the Dajjāl's Narrative, and the Story of Jassāsah
chapters.arabic_text:
المسلمين أنه لانبى بعد نبينا صلى الله عليه وسلم وأن شريعته مؤبدة إلى يوم

القيامة لاتنسخ وهذا استدلال فاسد لأنه ليس المراد بنزول عيسى عليه السلام

أنه ينزل نبيا بشرع ينسخ شرعنا ولا فى هذه الأحاديث ولافى غيرها شيء من هذا
# 
# بل صحت هذه الأحاديث هنا وما سبق في كتاب الإيمان وغيرها أنه ينزل حكما

مقسطا بحكم شرعنا ويحيي من أمور شرعنا ما هجره الناس قوله (في كبد جبل) أي

وسطه وداخله وكبد كل شيء وسطه قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (فيبقى شرار الناس

في خفة الطير وأحلام السباع) قال العلماء معناه يكونون في سرعتهم إلى

الشرور وقضاء الشهوات والفساد كطيران الطير وفي العدوان وظلم بعضهم بعضا في

أخلاق السباع العادية قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (أصغى ليتا ورفع ليتا) الليت

بكسر اللام وآخره مثناة فوق وهى صفحة العنق وهى جانبه وأصغى أمال قوله صلى

الله عليه وسلم (وأول من يسمعه رجل يلوط حوض إبله) أي يطينه ويصلحه قوله

(كأنه الطل أو
# 
# الظل) قال العلماء الأصح الطل بالمهملة وهو الموافق للحديث الآخر أنه

كمني الرجال قوله (فذلك يوم يكشف عن ساق) قال العلماء معناه ومعنى ما في

القرآن يوم يكشف عن ساق يوم يكشف عن شدة وهول عظيم أي يظهر ذلك يقال كشفت

الحرب عن ساقها إذا اشتدت وأصله أن من جد في أمره كشف عن ساقه مستمرا في

الخفة والنشاط له
#

| (باب قصة الجساسة
# [2942] هي بفتح الجيم وتشديد السين
# المهملة الأولى قيل سميت بذلك لتجسسها الأخبار للدجال وجاء عن عبد الرحمن

بن عمرو بن العاص أنها دابة الأرض المذكورة في القرآن قوله (عن فاطمة بنت

قيس قالت نكحت بن المغيرة وهو من خيار شباب قريش يومئذ فأصيب في أول الجهاد

مع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فلما تأيمت خطبني عبد الرحمن) معنى تأيمت

صرت أيما وهي التى لازوج لها قال العلماء قولها فأصيب ليس معناه أنه قتل في

الجهاد مع النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم)
# 
# وتأيمت بذلك إنما تأيمت بطلاقه البائن كما ذكره مسلم في الطريق الذي بعد

هذا وكذا ذكره في  كتاب الطلاق وكذا ذكره المصنفون في جميع كتبهم وقد

اختلفوا في وقت وفاته فقيل توفي مع علي بن أبي طالب رضي الله عنه عقب

طلاقها باليمن حكاه بن عبد البر وقيل بل عاش إلى خلافة عمر رضي الله عنه

حكاه البخاري في التاريخ وإنما معنى قولها فأصيب أي بجراحة أوأصيب فى ماله

أونحو ذلك هكذا تأوله العلماء قال القاضي إنما أرادت بذلك عد فضائله

فابتدأت بكونه خير شباب قريش ثم ذكرت الباقي وقد سبق شرح حديث فاطمة هذا في

كتاب الطلاق وبيان ما اشتمل عليه قوله (وأم شريك من الأنصار) هذا قد أنكره

بعض العلماء وقال إنما هي قرشية من بني عامر بن لؤي واسمها غربة
# 
# وقيل غربلة وقال آخرون هما اثنتان قرشية وأنصارية قوله (ولكن انتقلى إلى

بن عمك عبد الله بن عمرو بن أم مكتوم وهو رجل من بني فهر فهر قريش وهو من

البطن الذي هي منه) هكذا هو في جميع النسخ وقوله بن أم مكتوم يكتب بألف

لأنه صفة لعبد الله لا لعمرو فنسبه إلى أبيه عمرو وإلى أمه أم مكتوم فجمع

نسبه إلى أبويه كما في عبد الله بن مالك بن بحينة وعبد الله بن أبى بن سلول

ونظائر ذلك وقد سبق بيان هؤلاء كلهم في كتاب الإيمان في حديث المقداد حين

قتل من قال لا إله إلا الله قال القاضي المعروف أنه ليس بابن عمها ولامن

البطن الذي هي منه بل من بني محارب بن فهر وهو من بني عامر بن لؤي هذا كلام

القاضي والصواب أن ما جاءت به الرواية صحيح والمراد بالبطن هنا القبيلة لا

البطن الذي هو أخص منها والمراد أنه بن عمها مجازا لكونه من قبيلتها

فالرواية صحيحة ولله الحمد قوله (الصلاة جامعة) هو بنصب الصلاة وجامعة

الأول على الإغراء والثاني على الحال قولها (فلما تأيمت خطبني عبد الرحمن)

إلى آخره ظاهره أن الخطبة كانت في نفس العدة وليس كذلك إنما كانت بعد

انقضائها كما صرح به في الأحاديث السابقة 
# 
# في كتاب الطلاق فيتأول هذا اللفظ الواقع هنا على ذلك ويكون قوله انتقلي

إلى أم شريك والى بن أم مكتوم مقدما على الخطبة وعطف جملة على جملة من غير

ترتيب قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (عن تميم الداري حدثني أنه ركب سفينة) هذا

معدود في مناقب تميم لأن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم روى عنه هذه القصة وفيه

رواية الفاضل عن المفضول ورواية المتبوع عن تابعه وفيه قبول خبر الواحد

قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (ثم أرفؤ إلى جزيرة) هو بالهمز أى التجؤا إليها

قوله (فجلسوا في أقرب السفينة) هو بضم الراء وهي سفينة صغيرة تكون مع

الكبيرة كالجنيبة يتصرف فيها ركاب السفينة لقضاء حوائجهم الجمع قوارب

والواحد قارب بكسر الراء وفتحها وجاء هنا أقرب وهو صحيح لكنه خلاف القياس

وقيل المراد بأقرب السفينة أخرياتها وما قرب منها للنزول قوله (دابة أهلب)

كثير الشعر الأهلب غليظ الشعر كثيره قوله (فإنه إلى خبركم بالأشواق) أي

شديد الأشواق إليه وقوله (فرقنا) أي خفنا قوله
# 
# صادفنا البحر حين اغتلم) أي هاج وجاوز حده المعتاد وقال الكسائي الاغتلام
chapters.anchors:
- Root: أ-ب-د (abada)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Perpetuity, endless duration; something that remains without termination.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Theological term for the eternal abrogation-proof nature of the Sharīʿah — its perpetual binding force until the Hour.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense of unending time; here used ḥaqīqah for the unalterable continuity of the divine law.
- Sībawayh Rule: Naṣb on ʾighrāʾ (الإغراء) — The accusative in exhortation/urging, where the verb is omitted and the object is set in naṣb to command attention (e.g., «الصلاة جامعة»).
chapters.translation:
I say: The Muslims are unanimously agreed that there is no prophet after our Prophet — may Allah bless him and grant him peace — and that his Sacred Law is perpetually binding until the Day of Resurrection, never to be abrogated. This [claim of those who allege abrogation] is a corrupt inference, because the intended meaning of the descent of Jesus — peace be upon him — is not that he descends as a prophet bringing a law that abrogates our law. Neither in these hadiths nor in others is there anything of this sort.

Rather, these hadiths are authentically established — here and in what preceded in the Book of Faith (Kitāb al-Īmān) and elsewhere — that he descends as a just judge (ḥakaman muqsiṭan) ruling according to our law, and he revives from the matters of our law what the people have abandoned.

His saying — peace be upon him — (in the flank of a mountain, fī kabad jabal): i.e., its middle and its interior; the kabad of everything is its middle.

His saying — peace be upon him — (there will remain the worst of people, in the lightness of birds and the intellects of beasts, fī khiffat al-ṭayr wa aḥlām al-sibāʿ): The scholars said: Its meaning is that they will be, in their swiftness toward evils, the fulfillment of lusts, and corruption, like the flight of birds; and in aggression and mutual wrongdoing, in the morals of predatory beasts.

His saying — peace be upon him — (he inclined his neck (aṣghā laytan) and raised his neck (rafaʿa laytan)): al-layt — with kasrah on the lām and its final letter is tāʾ marbūṭah (here: tāʾ muthannāh, i.e., tāʾ) — is the side of the neck, its flank. Aṣghā means he inclined.

His saying — peace be upon him — (and the first to hear him is a man who is plastering (yalūṭ) the cistern of his camels): i.e., coating it with clay and repairing it.

His saying — (as if it were the dew (al-ṭall) or the shade (al-ẓill)): The scholars said: The more correct [reading] is al-ṭall with the unpointed ṭāʾ, and this is consistent with the other hadith that it is like the semen of men (ka-maniyy al-rijāl).

His saying — (that is the Day when the shin shall be uncovered, yawm yukshaf ʿan sāq): The scholars said: Its meaning — and the meaning of what is in the Qurʾān, {«yawma yukshafu ʿan sāq»} — is the Day when a severe terror and great horror is uncovered, i.e., it becomes manifest. One says: "The war uncovered its shin" (kashafat al-ḥarb ʿan sāqihā) when it intensifies. Its origin is that whoever is earnest in his affair uncovers his shin, persisting in lightness and vigor for it.

---

| (Chapter: The Story of al-Jassāsah)

[2942] It is with fatḥah on the jīm and tashdīd on the first sīn (the unpointed one). It is said that it was so named because of its spying out (tajassus) of news for the Dajjāl. It is reported from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ that it is the beast of the earth (dābbat al-arḍ) mentioned in the Qurʾān.

His saying — (from Fāṭimah bint Qays, who said: "I married Ibn al-Mughīrah, who was among the best of the youth of Quraysh at that time, and he was afflicted (fa-uṣība) in the first jihad with the Messenger of Allah — may Allah bless him and grant him peace. When I became a widow (tāʾayyamt), ʿAbd al-Raḥmān proposed to me"): The meaning of tāʾayyamt is "I became a widow (ayyim)" — she who has no husband.

The scholars said: Her saying "he was afflicted" does not mean that he was killed in the jihad with the Prophet — peace be upon him — and that she became a widow thereby. Rather, she became a widow only through his irrevocable divorce (ṭalāq bāʾin), as Muslim mentioned in the transmission that follows this one, and likewise in the Book of Divorce (Kitāb al-Ṭalāq), and likewise the compilers mentioned in all their books. They differed over the time of his death: it was said he died with ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib — may Allah be pleased with him — in Yemen right after her divorce; this was related by Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr. And it was said rather that he lived until the caliphate of ʿUmar — may Allah be pleased with him — related by al-Bukhārī in al-Tārīkh. The meaning of her saying "he was afflicted" is only that he was afflicted with a wound, or his wealth was afflicted, or something of that sort — thus the scholars interpreted it.

Al-Qāḍī said: She only intended by this to enumerate his virtues, so she began with his being the best of Quraysh's youth, then mentioned the rest.

The explanation of this hadith of Fāṭimah has already preceded in the Book of Divorce, along with the clarification of what it contains.

His saying — (and Umm Sharīk, from the Anṣār): Some scholars have rejected this, saying: She was rather a Qurashiyyah from the Banū ʿĀmir ibn Luʾayy, and her name was Ghurbah — and it was said Ghurbalah. Others said: They are two women, one Qurashiyyah and one Anṣāriyyah.

His saying — (but move to the house of your paternal uncle ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr ibn Umm Maktūm, a man from Banū Fihr — Fihr of Quraysh — and he is from the clan (al-baṭn) from which she comes): Thus it is in all copies. His saying "ibn Umm Maktūm" is written with an alif because it is an attribute of ʿAbd Allāh, not of ʿAmr — for he is attributed to his father ʿAmr and to his mother Umm Maktūm, combining his lineage to both parents, as in ʿAbd Allāh ibn Mālik ibn Buḥaynah, and ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ubayy ibn Salūl, and similar cases. The explanation of all these has already preceded in the Book of Faith, in the hadith of al-Miqdād when he killed the one who said "There is no god but Allah."

Al-Qāḍī said: The well-known [view] is that he was not her paternal cousin, nor from the clan from which she comes; rather, he was from Banū Muḥārib ibn Fihr, and he is from Banū ʿĀmir ibn Luʾayy. This is al-Qāḍī's statement. The correct view is that what the narration brought is sound, and the intended meaning of "clan" (al-baṭn) here is the tribe (al-qabīlah), not the clan that is more specific than it. The intended meaning of "her paternal cousin" is metaphorical (majāzan), because he is from her tribe. Thus the narration is sound — and praise be to Allah.

Her saying — (the prayer is gathering, al-ṣalātu jāmiʿah): al-ṣalāh is in the accusative (naṣb) and jāmiʿah — the first [word] is on the pattern of exhortation (al-ʾighrāʾ), and the second is on the pattern of the circumstantial accusative (al-ḥāl).

Her saying — (when I became a widow, ʿAbd al-Raḥmān proposed to me) to the end: Its apparent sense is that the proposal occurred during the waiting period itself (al-ʿiddah), but it is not so; rather, it was after its completion, as explicitly stated in the preceding hadiths in the Book of Divorce. Thus this wording occurring here is interpreted accordingly, and his saying "move to Umm Sharīk and to Ibn Umm Maktūm" is placed before the proposal, with one sentence conjoined to another without chronological ordering.

His saying — peace be upon him — (from Tamīm al-Dārī, who told me that he boarded a ship): This is counted among the virtues (manāqib) of Tamīm, because the Prophet — peace be upon him — narrated this story from him. In it is the narration of the virtuous one from the less virtuous, and the narration of the followed one from his follower. And in it is the acceptance of the solitary report (khabar al-wāḥid).

His saying — peace be upon him — (then they sought refuge (arfaʾū) on an island): It is with hamzah, i.e., they took refuge on it.

His saying — (they sat in the nearest of the ship (aqrab al-safīnah)): It is with ḍammah on the rāʾ — a small boat that accompanies the large one, like a companion vessel (al-junaybah), in which the ship's passengers move about to fulfill their needs. Its plural is qawārib, and the singular is qārib — with kasrah or fatḥah on the rāʾ. It occurs here as aqrab, which is correct but contrary to the analogical pattern (qiyās). It is also said that the intended meaning of "aqrab al-safīnah" is its rear parts and what is near it for disembarking.

His saying — (a beast, shaggy (ahlab)): Abundant in hair; al-ahlab is thick-haired and abundant in it.

His saying — (for it is intensely yearning (ashwāq) for your news): i.e., intensely desiring it.

His saying — (we were terrified (fariqnā)): i.e., we feared.

His saying — (we encountered the sea when it was in fury (ightalam)): i.e., it raged and exceeded its usual limit. Al-Kisāʾī said: al-ightilām is [the sea's] agitation.

chapters.title_en: Section 981 – Commentary on Hadiths Concerning the Dajjāl, Tribulation, and Asceticism
chapters.arabic_text:
أن يتجاوز الإنسان ما حد له من الخير والمباح قوله (عين زغر) بزاي معجمة

مضمومة ثم غين معجمة مفتوحة ثم راء وهي بلدة معروفة في الجانب القبلي من

الشام وأما طيبة فهي المدينة ويقال
# 
# لها أيضا طابة وسبق في كتاب الحج اشتقاقها مع باقي أسمائها قوله (بيده

السيف صلتا) بفتح الصاد وضمها أي مسلولا قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (من قبل

المشرق ما هو) قال القاضي لفظة ما هو زائدة صلة للكلام ليست بنافية والمراد

إثبات أنه في جهات المشرق قوله (فأتحفتنا برطب يقال له رطب بن طاب وسقتنا

سويق سلت) أي ضيفتنا بنوع من الرطب وقد سبق بيانه وسبق
# 
# أن تمر المدينة مائة وعشرون نوعا وسلت بضم السين وإسكان اللام وبتاء

مثناة فوق وهو حب يشبه الحنطة ويشبه الشعير قوله (تاهت به سفينته) أي سلكت

عن الطريق قوله
# 
# (فيضرب رواقه) أي ينزل هناك ويضع ثقله

| (باب في بقية من أحاديث الدجال
# [2944] قوله صلى الله عليه
# وسلم (يتبع الدجال من يهود أصبهان سبعون ألفا) هكذا هو في جميع النسخ)
# 
# ببلادنا سبعون بسين ثم باء موحدة وكذا نقله القاضي عن رواية الأكثرين قال

وفي رواية بن ماهان تسعون ألفا بالتاء المثناة قبل السين والصحيح المشهور

الأول وأصبهان بفتح الهمزة وكسرها وبالياء والفاء
# [2946] قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (ما بين خلق آدم إلى قيام الساعة خلق

أكبر
# 
# من الدجال) المراد أكبر فتنة وأعظم شوكة
# [2947] قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم (بادروا بالأعمال ستا طلوع الشمس من

مغربها أو الدجال أو الدخان أو الدابة أو خاصة أحدكم أوأمر العامة) وفي

الرواية الثانية الدجال والدخان إلى قوله وخويصة أحدكم فذكر الستة في

الرواية الأولى معطوفة بأوالتى هي للتقسيم وفي الثانية بالواو قال هشام

خاصة أحدكم الموت وخويصة تصغير خاصة وقال قتادة أمر العامة القيامة كذا

ذكره عنهما عبد بن حميد قوله (أمية بن بسطام العيشي) هو بالشين المعجمة قال

القاضي قال بعضهم صوابه العاشي بالألف منسوب إلى بني عاش بن تيم الله بن

عكابة ولكن الذى ذكره عبد الغنى وبن ماكولا وسائر الحفاظ وهو الموجود في
