- Root: و ق ف (waqafa)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To stand still, to halt; a standing position (wuqūf) in place.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In ritual context, denotes the physical stance of the worshipper in prayer (qiyām), distinct from movement.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) for physical standing; metaphorical (majāz) for steadfastness in obedience.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clause Structure (al-sharṭ wa al-jawāb) – The phrase "إذا كان ضيقا" introduces a conditional protasis, with the apodosis "فاشدده" governing the imperative, requiring precise parsing of the verb's object.
chapters.translation:
I say: And if he stands to his left, the Imam turns around him. And among these (matters) is that the followers should form a single row behind the Imam, as when they are three or more. This is the doctrine of all scholars (al-ʿulamāʾ) universally, except Ibn Masʿūd and his two companions, for they said: "The two (followers) stand at his two sides."

His saying (may Allah bless him and grant him peace): «يرمقني» (he glances at me) – meaning: he looks at me with a continuous, successive gaze.

His saying (may Allah bless him and grant him peace): «وإذا كان ضيقا فاشدده على حقوك» (and if it is narrow, then tighten it upon your waist-wrapper) – "ḥaqw" is with the opening (fatḥ) and the breaking (kasr) of the ḥāʾ, and it is the knot of the waist-wrapper (izār). The intended meaning here is that it should reach the navel. In this (hadith) there is the permissibility of praying in a single garment, and that if one tightens the waist-wrapper (miʾzar) and prays in it, while it covers what is between his navel and his knee, his prayer is valid. Even if his nakedness (ʿawrah) could be seen from beneath it, were he on a rooftop or the like, this does not harm him.

[3011] His saying: «وكان قوت كل رجل منا كل يوم تمرة فكان يمصها» (and the sustenance of each man among us was, every day, a single date, and he would suck it) – "qūt" is with the opening of the mīm, according to the well-known language, and it has been narrated with its ḍammah (i.e., "qūt" with ḍammah on qāf), and its explanation has preceded. In this (hadith) is (evidence of) what they were upon of the straitness of livelihood and patience upon it in the path of Allah and His obedience.

His saying: «وكنا نختبط بقسينا» (and we would beat with our bows) – "al-qisiyy" is the plural of "qaws" (bow). The meaning of "nakhbiṭ" is: we strike the trees so that their leaves fall, and we eat them. And «وقرحت أشداقنا» (and our mouths' corners became sore) – meaning: they became lacerated from the roughness of the leaves and their heat.

His saying: «فأقسم أخطئها رجل منا يوما فانطلقنا به ننعشه فشهدنا له أنه لم يعطها فأعطيها» (and a man among us swore, "He missed it one day," so we went off with him, reviving him, and we bore witness for him that he was not given it, so he was given it) – the meaning of "aqsama" is: he swore an oath. His saying «أخطئها» means: it eluded him. Its meaning is that there was a distributor (qāsim) for the dates who divided them among them, giving each person one date every day. He divided (them) on some days and forgot a man, so he did not give him his date, and he (the distributor) thought that he had given it to him. So they disputed over that, and we bore witness for him that he was not given it, so he was given it after the testimony. The meaning of «ننعشه» is: we raise him up and set him upright from the severity of weakness and exhaustion. Al-Qāḍī said: "What seems most correct to me is that its meaning is: we strengthened his side in his claim and bore witness for him." In this (hadith) is evidence of what they were upon of patience, and in it is the permissibility of bearing witness to a negation (al-shahādah ʿalā al-nafy) in a limited matter (al-maḥṣūr) that can be encompassed.

[3012] His saying: «نزلنا واديا أفيح» (we descended into a wide valley) – "afyaḥ" is with the fāʾ, meaning: spacious. And "shāṭiʾ al-wādī" is its side.

His saying: «فانقادت معه كالبعير المخشوش» (and it led along with him like a camel with a nose-ring) – "makhshūsh" is with the khāʾ and the shīn, both unpointed (i.e., muʿjamah), and it is (the camel) into whose nose is placed a "khishāsh" – with the kasr of the khāʾ – which is a piece of wood placed in the camel's nose when it is stubborn, and a rope is tied to it to subdue it and make it lead. And it (the camel) may resist due to its stubbornness, but when it (the ring) becomes severe upon it and pains it, it leads somewhat. For this reason, he (the narrator) said: "one who placates his leader." In this (hadith) are these manifest miracles (muʿjizāt) of the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace).

His saying: «حتى إذا كان بالمنصف مما بينهما لأم بينهما» (until when he was at the midpoint between the two, he joined them together) – as for "al-munṣif," it is with the opening of the mīm and the ṣād, and it is half the distance. Among those who explicitly stated its opening is al-Jawharī and others. His saying «لأم» is with a shortened hamzah and a lengthened one, and both are correct, meaning: he brought them together. And in some copies (it occurs as) "alām" with an alif without a hamzah. Al-Qāḍī and others said: it is a corruption (taṣḥīf).

His saying: «فخرجت أحضر» (and I went out hastening) – it is with the ḍammah of the hamzah, the sukūn of the ḥāʾ, and the kasr of the ḍād (i.e., "uḥḍir"), meaning: I run and strive with severe effort.

His saying: «فحانت مني لفتة» (and there occurred from me a glance) – "al-laftah" is a look to the side, and it is with the opening of the lām. And it occurs in some narrations as «فحالت» with the lām, and the well-known (version) is with the nūn (i.e., "ḥāna"), and both have the same meaning, for "al-ḥīn" and "al-ḥāl" both mean time, i.e., it occurred and coincided.

And his saying: «وأشار أبو إسماعيل» (and Abū Ismāʿīl gestured) – and in some copies (it is) "ibn Ismāʿīl," and both are correct. He is Ḥātim ibn Ismāʿīl, and his kunyah is Abū Ismāʿīl.

His saying: «فأخذت حجرا فكسرته وحسرته فانذلق فأتيت الشجرتين فقطعت من كل واحدة منهما غصنا» (and I took a stone, and I broke it and sharpened it, and it became sharp, then I came to the two trees and cut from each one of them a branch) – his saying «فحسرته» is with a ḥāʾ and a sīn, both unpointed (i.e., muhmalah), and the sīn is ungeminated (mukhaffafah), meaning: I sharpened it and removed from it what prevented its sharpness, such that it became possible for me to cut the branches with it. And that is the meaning of his saying «فانذلق» with the pointed dhāl (i.e., muʿjamah), meaning: it became sharp. Al-Harawī and those who followed him said: "The pronoun in «حسرته» refers back to the branch, i.e., I stripped a branch from the branches of the tree, meaning: I peeled it with the stone." Al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ rejected this against al-Harawī and his followers and said: "The flow of the speech (siyāq al-kalām) precludes this, because he sharpened it (the stone), then came to the tree and cut the two branches, and this is explicit in its wording. And because he said: «فحسرته فانذلق» – and that which is described as becoming sharp (al-indhilaq) is the stone, not the branch. The correct view is that he only sharpened the stone." And al-Khaṭṭābī said the same. Know that his saying «فحسرته» with the unpointed sīn – thus it is in all the copies, and thus it is in "al-Jamʿ bayn al-Ṣaḥīḥayn" and in the book of al-Khaṭṭābī and al-Harawī and all the books of gharīb (rare expressions). Al-Qāḍī claimed its narration from all their shaykhs with the pointed shīn (i.e., "ḥashartuhu"), and he claimed it was more correct – but it is not as he said. And Allah knows best.

His saying (may Allah bless him and grant him peace): «يرفه عنهما» (he lightens from them) – meaning: he alleviates.

[3013] His saying: «وكان رجل من الأنصار يبرد الماء لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في أشجاب له على حمارة من جريد» (and a man from the Anṣār used to cool water for the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) in his old waterskins (ashjāb) upon a wooden frame (ḥimārah) made of palm-branches) – as for "al-ashjāb" here, it is the plural of "shajb" with the sukūn of the jīm, and it is the waterskin (siqāʾ) that has become worn out and tattered, becoming an old skin (shann). One says "shājib," meaning: dry. And it is from "al-shujūb," which is destruction (halāk). From it is the hadith of Ibn ʿAbbās (may Allah be pleased with them both): "He stood up to a shajb and poured from it water and performed ablution." And similar to it is his saying (may Allah bless him and grant him peace): «فانظر هل في أشجابه من شيء» (then look – is there anything in his old waterskins?).

As for the saying of al-Māzarī and others that the intended meaning of "al-ashjāb" here is the sticks upon which the water-skin is hung – it is an error, because of his saying: "he cooled (water) in them upon a ḥimārah of palm-branches."

As for "al-ḥimārah," it is with the kasr of the ḥāʾ and the takhfīf (un gemination) of the mīm and the rāʾ, and they are sticks upon which water-skins are hung. Al-Qāḍī said: "In some narrations, it occurs as 'ḥimār' with the deletion of the tāʾ (i.e., the feminine ending), and the narration of the majority is 'ḥimārah' with the tāʾ, and both are correct, and their meaning is what we have mentioned."

His saying: «فلم أجد فيها إلا قطرة في عزلاء شجب منها لو أني أفرغه شربه يابسه» (and I found in it nothing but a drop in the mouth of an old waterskin of them – were I to pour it out, its dryness would drink it) – his saying «قطرة» means: a small amount. And "al-ʿazlāʾ" is with the opening of the unpointed ʿayn, the sukūn of the zāy, and with lengthening (madd), and it is the mouth (fam) of the waterskin. His saying «شربه يابسه» means: it is very little, for due to its scantiness combined with the severity of the dryness of the rest of the shajb – which is the waterskin – were I to pour it out, its dry part would suck it up and nothing would descend from it.

chapters.title_en: Section 990 — Commentary on the Prophet's Sayings Regarding the Journey, the Camel-Saddle Cloth, and Related Matters
chapters.arabic_text:
شيء قوله (ويغمزه بيديه) وفي بعض النسخ بيده أي يعصره قوله صلى الله عليه

وسلم (ناد بجفنة فقلت يا جفنة الركب فأتيت بها) أى ياصاحب جفنة الركب فحذف

المضاف للعلم بأنه المراد وأن الجفنة لاتنادى ومعناه ياصاحب جفنة الركب

التي تشبعهم أحضرها أي من كان عنده جفنة بهذه الصفة فليحضرها والجفنة بفتح

الجيم
# [3014] قوله (فأتينا سيف البحر فزخر البحر زخرة فألقى دابة فأورينا على

شقها النار) سيف البحر بكسر السين وإسكان المثناة تحت هو ساحله وزخر بالخاء

المعجمة
# 
# أي علا موجه وأورينا أوقدنا قوله (حجاج عينها) هو بكسر الحاء وفتحها وهو

عظمها المستدير بها قوله (ثم دعونا بأعظم رجل في الركب وأعظم جمل في الركب

وأعظم كفل فى الركب فدخل تحته ما يطأطىء رأسه) الكفل هنا بكسر الكاف وإسكان

الفاء قال الجمهور والمراد بالكفل هنا الكساء الذي يحويه راكب البعير على

سنامه لئلا يسقط فيحفظ الكفل الراكب قال الهروي قال الأزهري ومنه اشتقاق

قوله تعالى يؤتكم كفلين من رحمته أي نصيبين يحفظانكم من الهلكة كما يحفظ

الكفل الراكب يقال منه تكفلت البعير وأكفلته إذا أدرت ذلك  الكساء حول سنامه

ثم ركبته وهذا الكساء كفل بكسر الكاف وسكون الفاء وقال القاضي عياض وضبطه

بعض الرواة بفتح الكاف والفاء والصحيح الأول وأما قوله بأعظم رجل فهو

بالجيم في رواية الأكثرين وهو الأصح ورواه بعضهم بالحاء وكذا وقع لرواة

البخاري بالوجهين وفي هذا الحديث معجزات ظاهرات لرسول الله صلى الله عليه

وسلم والله أعلم
#

# باب في حديث الهجرة ويقال له حديث الرحل الحاء
# [2009] قوله (ينتقد ثمنه) أي يستوفيه ويقال سرى وأسرى لغتان بمعنى وقائم

الظهيرة نصف النهار وهو حال استواء الشمس سمي قائما لأن الظل لا يظهر فكأنه

واقف قائم ووقع في أكثر النسخ قائم الظهر بضم الظاء وحذف الياء قوله (رفعت

لنا صخرة) أي ظهرت لأبصارنا قوله (فبسطت عليه فروة) المراد الفروة المعروفة

التي تلبس هذا هو الصواب وذكر القاضي أن بعضهم قال المراد بالفروة هنا

الحشيش فإنه يقال له فروة وهذا قول باطل ومما يرده قوله في رواية البخاري

فروة معي ويقال لها فروة بالهاء وفرو بحذفها وهو الأشهر في اللغة وإن كانتا

صحيحتين قوله (أنفض لك ما حولك) أي أفتش لئلا يكون هناك عدو وقوله (لمن أنت

يا غلام فقال لرجل من أهل المدينة) المراد بالمدينة هنا مكة ولم تكن مدينة

النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم سميت بالمدينة إنما كان اسمها يثرب هذا هو الجواب

الصحيح وأما قول القاضي إن ذكر المدينة هنا وهم فليس كما قال بل هو صحيح

والمراد بها مكة قوله (أفي غنمك لبن) هو
# 
# بفتح اللام والباء يعني اللبن المعروف هذه الرواية مشهورة وروى بعضهم لبن

بضم اللام وإسكان الباء أي شياه وذوات ألبان قوله (فحلب لى فى قعب معه

كثيبة من لبن قال ومعي إداوة أرتوي فيها) القعب قدح من خشب معروف والكثبة

بضم الكاف وإسكان المثلثة وهي قدر الحلبة قاله بن السكيت وقيل هي القليل

منه والادواة كالركوة وأرتوي أستقي وهذا الحديث مما يسأل عنه فيقال كيف

شربوا اللبن من الغلام وليس هو مالكه وجوابه من أوجه أحدها أنه محمول  على

عادة العرب أنهم يأذنون للرعاة إذا مر بهم ضيف أو عابر سبيل أن يسقوه اللبن

ونحوه والثاني أنه كان لصديق لهم يدلون عليه وهذا جائز والثالث أنه مال

حربى لاأمان له ومثل هذا جائز والرابع لعلهم كانوا مضطرين والجوابان

الأولان أجود قوله (برد أسفله) هو بفتح الراء على المشهور وقال الجوهري

بضمها قوله (ونحن في جلد من الأرض) هو بفتح الجيم واللام أي أرض صلبة
# 
# وروي جدد بدالين وهو المستوي وكانت الأرض مستوية صلبة قوله (فارتطمت فرسه

إلى بطنها) أي غاصت قوائمها في تلك الأرض الجلد قوله (ووفى لنا) بتخفيف

الفاء قوله (فساخ فرسه في الأرض) هو بمعنى ارتطمت قوله (لأعمين على من

ورائي) يعني لأخفين أمركم عمن ورائي ممن يطلبكم وألبسه عليهم حتى لايعلم

أحد وفي هذا الحديث فوائد منها هذه المعجزة الظاهرة لرسول الله صلى الله

عليه وسلم وفضيلة ظاهرة لأبي بكر رضي الله عنه من وجوه وفيه خدمة التابع

للمتبوع وفيه استصحاب الركوة والإبريق ونحوهما في السفر للطهارة والشرب

وفيه فضل التوكل
# 
# على الله سبحانه وتعالى وحسن عاقبته وفيه فضائل للأنصار لفرحهم بقدوم

رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وظهور سرورهم به وفيه فضيلة صلة الأرحام سواء

قربت القرابة والرحم أم بعدت وأن الرجل الجليل إذا قدم بلدا له فيه أقارب

ينزل عندهم يكرمهم بذلك والله أعلم
# 
#

| كتاب التفسير
# [3015] قوله تعالى (وقولوا حطة) أى مسئلتنا حطة وهي أن يحط عنا خطايانا

وقوله (يزحفون على أساههم) جمع است وهي الدبر
# [3017] قوله في قوله تعالى اليوم أكملت لكم دينكم (انها نزلت
# 
# ليلة جمع ونحن مع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بعرفات) هكذا هو فى النسخ

الرواية ليلة جمع وفى نسخة بن ماهان ليلة جمعة وكلاهما صحيح فمن روى ليلة
chapters.anchors:
- Root: غ م ز (gh-m-z)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To press, squeeze, or pinch with the hand; physical compression.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Physical action denoting tactile pressure, used literally here for the Prophet's gesture.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage—no metaphorical extension; the hand's action on the animal.
- Sībawayh Rule: Ellipsis of the Muḍāf (حذف المضاف) — The genitive construct's head noun is omitted when context makes the referent unambiguous, as in "O Jafnah of the caravan" meaning "O owner of the Jafnah of the caravan."

- Root: ز خ ر (z-kh-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To swell, rise, or surge—said of the sea's waves mounting high.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Natural phenomenon described literally; the sea's agitation as a divine act.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal description of physical elevation; no metaphorical sense intended.
- Sībawayh Rule: Verbal sentence structure (جملة فعلية) — "Zakharat al-baḥru" with the subject following the verb, standard word order for intransitive verbs of natural phenomena.

- Root: ك ف ل (k-f-l)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: A cloth wrapped around a camel's hump to secure the rider; also a portion, share, or guaranty.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In the Quranic verse {«يؤتكم كفلين من رحمته»} (57:28), it denotes a double portion of mercy that preserves one from destruction, metaphorically extending from the physical cloth that guards the rider.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): The literal sense is the camel-cloth; the Quranic usage is metaphorical (majāz) — protection as a share of divine mercy.
- Sībawayh Rule: Derivation (اشتقاق) — The verb "takaffaltu al-baʿīr" (I wrapped the cloth around the camel) is formed from the noun "kifl," showing nominal-to-verbal derivation.
chapters.translation:
I say: Regarding his statement (and he pressed it with his hands) — and in some manuscripts "with his hand" — meaning he squeezed it. His statement, peace and blessings be upon him, (Call out for a Jafnah, and I said, "O Jafnah of the caravan," and I brought it) — meaning "O owner of the Jafnah of the caravan," with the genitive head noun omitted due to the certainty that this was intended, for the Jafnah itself cannot be called out to. The meaning is: "O owner of the Jafnah of the caravan that suffices them — bring it," i.e., whoever possesses a Jafnah of this description, let him bring it. The Jafnah (جفنة) is with a fatḥah on the jīm.

# [3014] His statement (We came to Sayf al-Baḥr, and the sea surged a surge, casting forth a creature, and we kindled a fire upon its flank) — Sayf al-Baḥr, with kasrah on the sīn and sukūn on the tāʾ (under it), is its shore. "Zakhar" is with the dotted khāʾ, meaning its wave rose high. "Awraynā" means we kindled. His statement (the ḥijāj of its eye) — it is with kasrah and fatḥah on the ḥāʾ, meaning its encircling bone. His statement (Then we called for the greatest man in the caravan, the greatest camel in the caravan, and the greatest kifl in the caravan, and he entered beneath it without bowing his head) — the kifl here is with kasrah on the kāf and sukūn on the fāʾ. The majority (al-jumhūr) said: The intended meaning of kifl here is the cloth that the camel-rider wraps around the camel's hump so as not to fall, for the kifl protects the rider. Al-Harawī said: Al-Azharī said, and from it is derived the saying of the Exalted {«يؤتكم كفلين من رحمته»} — i.e., two portions that preserve you from destruction, just as the kifl preserves the rider. One says from it: "takaffaltu al-baʿīr" and "akfaltuhu" when one wraps that cloth around its hump and then mounts it. This cloth is called kifl, with kasrah on the kāf and sukūn on the fāʾ. Al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ said: Some transmitters recorded it with fatḥah on both the kāf and the fāʾ, but the correct is the first. As for his statement (the greatest man), it is with jīm in the narration of the majority, and it is the most correct; some narrated it with ḥāʾ, and likewise it occurred in the narrations of al-Bukhārī with both forms. In this ḥadīth there are manifest miracles of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him. And Allah knows best.

# Chapter on the Ḥadīth of the Hijrah — also called the Ḥadīth of the Raḥl (the saddle) — with ḥāʾ.

# [2009] His statement (he would collect its price) — i.e., receive it in full. It is said "sarā" and "asrā" are two dialects with the same meaning. "Qāʾim al-ẓahīrah" is midday, when the sun is at its zenith; it is called "standing" because the shadow does not appear, as if it were stationary and upright. In most manuscripts it occurs as "qāʾim al-ẓuhr" with ḍammah on the ẓāʾ and the yāʾ omitted. His statement (a rock was raised up for us) — i.e., it appeared to our sight. His statement (I spread a farwah upon it) — the intended meaning is the well-known fur garment that is worn; this is the correct view. Al-Qāḍī mentioned that some said the intended meaning of farwah here is grass, for it is called farwah — but this is a false opinion. What refutes it is his statement in the narration of al-Bukhārī: "a farwah with me." It is called farwah with the tāʾ marbūṭah, and farw with its omission, which is the more famous in the language, though both are correct. His statement (I will search around you) — i.e., I will investigate lest there be an enemy. His statement (To whom do you belong, O boy? He said: To a man from the people of the city) — the intended meaning of "the city" (al-madīnah) here is Mecca, for the Prophet's city, peace and blessings be upon him, was not yet named al-Madīnah; its name was only Yathrib. This is the correct answer. As for al-Qāḍī's statement that the mention of "the city" here is an error — it is not as he said; rather, it is correct, and the intended meaning is Mecca. His statement (Is there milk in your sheep?) — it is with fatḥah on the lām and the bāʾ, meaning the well-known milk. This narration is famous. Some narrated "laban" with ḍammah on the lām and sukūn on the bāʾ, meaning sheep and milk-producing animals. His statement (He milked for me into a qaʿb that was with him, a kathībah of milk. He said: And with me was an idāwah from which I would drink) — the qaʿb is a well-known wooden cup. The kathbah, with ḍammah on the kāf and sukūn on the thāʾ, is the amount of one milking; Ibn al-Sikkīt said this. It is also said it is a small amount of it. The idāwah is like a small water-skin (rakwah), and "artawī" means I draw water. This ḥadīth is among those asked about, and it is said: How did they drink milk from the boy when he was not its owner? The answer is from several aspects: First, it is carried on the custom of the Arabs that they permit shepherds, when a guest or passerby comes to them, to give him milk and the like. Second, he was a friend of theirs whom they would direct to, and this is permissible. Third, it was war booty (māl ḥarbī) with no guarantee of safety, and such is permissible. Fourth, perhaps they were in dire need. The first two answers are the best. His statement (its lower part was cold) — it is with fatḥah on the rāʾ according to the famous view, and al-Jawharī said with ḍammah. His statement (We were on a jald of the earth) — it is with fatḥah on the jīm and the lām, meaning hard ground. It is also narrated "jadad" with two dāls, meaning level ground, and the ground was level and hard. His statement (his horse sank into it up to its belly) — i.e., its legs plunged into that hard ground. His statement (and he sufficed us) — with takhfīf on the fāʾ. His statement (his horse sank into the ground) — it has the same meaning as "irtatamat" (plunged). His statement (I will blind those behind me) — meaning I will conceal your affair from those behind me who seek you, and I will confuse them so that no one knows. In this ḥadīth there are benefits, among them: this manifest miracle of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him; a manifest virtue of Abū Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, from several aspects; the service of the follower to the followed; the carrying of the water-skin (rakwah) and the ewer and the like on a journey for purification and drinking; and the virtue of reliance upon Allah, Glorified and Exalted, and the goodness of its outcome. In it are virtues of the Anṣār for their joy at the arrival of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, and the manifestation of their happiness with him. In it is the virtue of maintaining family ties, whether the kinship and relation is near or distant, and that a venerable man, when he arrives in a land where he has relatives, should lodge with them, honoring them by that. And Allah knows best.

# The Book of Tafsīr (Quranic Exegesis)

# [3015] His statement, the Exalted (And say: "Ḥiṭṭah" — forgiveness) — i.e., our request is ḥiṭṭah, which is that our sins be lifted from us. His statement (they crawl on their astāh) — the plural of "ist" (anus), meaning the posterior.

# [3017] His statement regarding the saying of the Exalted {«اليوم أكملت لكم دينكم»} (This day I have perfected for you your religion — 5:3): (It was revealed on the night of Jamʿ (Muzdalifah), and we were with the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, at ʿArafāt) — thus it is in the manuscripts: "the night of Jamʿ." In the copy of Ibn Māhān: "the night of Jumuʿah (Friday)." Both are correct, for whoever narrated "the night of..."

chapters.title_en: The Night of Muzdalifah, Polygamy Limits, Guardian's Right to Orphan's Wealth, Slandering the Companions, The Unforgivable Murderer, and Related Rulings
chapters.arabic_text:
جمع فهي ليلة المزدلفة وهو المراد بقوله ونحن بعرفات في يوم جمعة لأن ليلة

جمع هي عشية يوم عرفات ويكون المراد بقوله ليلة جمعة يوم جمعة ومراد عمر

رضي الله عنه إنا قد اتخذنا ذلك اليوم عيدامن وجهين  فإنه يوم عرفة
# 
# ويوم جمعة وكل واحد منهما عيد لأهل الإسلام
# [3018] قوله (تعالى فانكحوا ما طاب لكم من النساء مثنى وثلاث ورباع) أي

ثنتين ثنتين أو ثلاثا ثلاثا أو أربعا أربعا وليس فيه جواز جمع أكثر من أربع

قولها (يقسط في صداقها) أي يعدل قولها (أعلى سننهن) أي أعلى عادتهن في
# 
# مهورهن ومهور أمثالهن يقال ضره وأضر به فالثلاثي بحذف الباء والرباعي

بإثباتها قولها
# 
# (فيعضلها) أي يمنعها الزواج قولها (شركته في ماله حتى في العذق) شركته

بكسر
# 
# الراء أي شاركته والعذق بفتح العين وهو النخلة قولها في
# [3019] قوله تعالى (ومن كان فقيرا فليأكل بالمعروف) أنه يجوز للولي أن

يأكل من مال اليتيم بالمعروف إذا كان محتاجا هو أيضا مذهب الشافعى والجمهور

وقالت طائفة لايجوز وحكى عن بن عباس وزيد بن أسلم قالا وهذه الآية منسوخة

بقوله تعالى إن الذين يأكلون أموال اليتامى ظلما الآية وقيل بقوله تعالى

ولاتأكلوا اموالكم بينكم بالباطل واختلف الجمهور فيما إذا أكل هل يلزمه رد

بدله وهما وجهان لأصحابنا أصحهما لايلزمه وقال فقهاء
# 
# العراق إنما يجوز له الأكل إذا سافر في مال اليتيم والله أعلم
# [3022] قولها (أمروا أن يستغفروا لأصحاب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

فسبوهم) قال القاضي الظاهر أنها قالت هذا عندما سمعت أهل مصر يقولون في

عثمان ما قالوا وأهل الشام في علي ما قالوا والحرورية في الجميع ما قالوا

وأما الأمر بالاستغفار الذي أشارت إليه فهو قوله تعالى والذين جاؤا من

بعدهم يقولون ربنا اغفر لنا ولإخواننا الذين سبقونا بالايمان وبهذا احتج

مالك فى انه لاحق في الفيء لمن سب الصحابة
# 
# رضي الله عنهم لأن الله تعالى إنما جعله لمن جاء بعدهم ممن يستغفر لهم

والله أعلم قوله (عن بن عباس رضي الله عنهما أن القاتل متعمدا لا توبة له)

واحتج بقوله تعالى ومن يقتل مؤمنا متعمدا فجزاؤه جهنم خالدا فيها هذا هو

المشهور عن بن عباس رضي الله عنهما وروي عنه أن له توبة وجواز المغفرة له

لقوله تعالى ومن يعمل سوءا  أو يظلم نفسه ثم يستغفر الله يجد الله

غفورارحيما وهذه الرواية الثانية هي مذهب جميع أهل السنة والصحابة

والتابعين ومن بعدهم وما روي عن بعض السلف مما يخالف هذا محمول على التغليظ

والتحذير من القتل والتورية في المنع منه وليس في هذه الآية التي احتج بها

بن عباس تصريح بأنه يخلد وإنما فيها أنه جزاؤه ولايلزم منه أنه يجازى وقد

سبق تقرير هذه المسألة وبيان معنى الآية في كتاب التوبة والله أعلم
# [3023] قوله (فرحلت إلى بن عباس) هو بالراء والحاء المهملة هذا هو الصحيح

المشهور فى الروايات وفى نسخة بن ماهان فدخلت بالدال والخاء المعجمة ويمكن

تصحيحه بأن يكون معناه دخلت بعد رحلتي إليه
# 
# قوله (فأما من دخل في الإسلام وعقله) هو بفتح القاف أي علم أحكام الإسلام

وتحريم القتل قوله (نسختها آية المدينة) يعني بالناسخة آية النساء ومن يقتل

مؤمنا متعمدا قوله (عن سعيد بن جبير قال أمرني عبد الرحمن بن أبزى أن أسأل

بن عباس عن هاتين الآيتين) هكذا هو في جميع النسخ قال القاضي قال بعضهم

لعله أمرنى بن عبد الرحمن قال القاضي لايمتنع أن عبد الرحمن أمر سعيد أيسأل

له بن عباس عمالا يعلمه عبد الرحمن فقد سأل بن عباس أكبر منه وأقدم صحبة

وهذا الذي قاله القاضي هو الصواب
# [3024] قوله (اخبرنا ابوعميس عن عبد المجيد بن سهيل) هكذا هو هو في جميع

النسخ عبد المجيد بالميم ثم الجيم الانسخة بن ماهان ففيها عبد الحميد
# 
# بحاء ثم ميم قال أبو علي الغساني الصواب الأول قال القاضي قد اختلفوا في

اسمه فذكره مالك في الموطأ من رواية يحيى بن يحيى الأندلسي وغيره فسماه عبد

الحميد بالحاء ثم بالميم وكذا قاله
# 
# سفيان بن عيينة وسماه البخاري عبد المجيد بالميم ثم بالجيم وكذا رواه بن

القاسم والقعنبي وجماعة في الموطأ عن مالك وقال بن عبد البر يقال بالوجهين

قال والأكثر بالميم ثم بالجيم قال القاضي فإذا ثبت الخلاف فيه لم يحكم على

أحد الوجهين بالخطأ
# [3028] قوله (فتقول من يعيرني  تطوافا) هو بكسر التاء المثناة فوق وهو ثوب

تلبسه المرأة تطوف به وكان أهل الجاهلية يطوفون عراة ويرمون ثيابهم

ويتركونها ملقاة على الأرض ولايأخذونها أبدا ويتركونها تداس بالأرجل
# 
# حتى تبلى ويسمى اللقاء حتى جاء الإسلام فأمر الله تعالى بستر العورة فقال

تعالى خذوا زينتكم عند كل مسجد وقال النبى صلى الله عليه وسلم لايطوف

بالبيت عريان
# [3029] قوله (فأنزل الله تعالى ولاتكرهوا فتياتكم على البغاء ان أردن

تحصنا إلى قوله ومن يكرههن فإن الله من بعد إكراههن لهن غفور رحيم) هكذا

وقع في النسخ كلها لهن غفور رحيم وهذا تفسير ولم يرد به أن لفظة لهن منزلة
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ج-م-ع (j-m-ʿ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To gather, assemble, bring together; the place of gathering (Muzdalifah) derives from this root as the site where pilgrims congregate.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In ritual context, denotes the collective assembly for worship at the appointed sacred site, emphasizing communal devotion.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal gathering of bodies in a place; metaphorically extended to the convergence of hearts in unified worship.
- Sībawayh Rule: Nominal sentence with implicit predicate (al-mubtadaʾ wa-l-khabar) — "ليلة جمع هي عشية يوم عرفات" (The night of Muzdalifah is the eve of the Day of ʿArafah), where the predicate is explicit for clarity.
chapters.translation:
I say: The gathering — it is the night of Muzdalifah, and this is the intended meaning of his statement, "while we were at ʿArafāt on a Friday," because the night of Muzdalifah is the evening of the Day of ʿArafah. The intended meaning of his statement "the night of Friday" is the day of Friday. The intent of ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, is that we have taken that day as a festival (ʿīd) from two aspects: for it is the Day of ʿArafah and it is a Friday, and each one of them is a festival for the people of Islam.

[3018] His statement (the Exalted): {«فَانكِحُوا مَا طَابَ لَكُم مِّنَ النِّسَاءِ مَثْنَىٰ وَثُلَاثَ وَرُبَاعَ»} ("So marry what is pleasing to you of women, two, three, or four") — meaning two by two, or three by three, or four by four. There is no permission in this for marrying more than four.

Her statement, "he is equitable in her dowry (yuqsiṭ fī ṣadāqihā)" — meaning he is just. Her statement, "upon their customs (aʿlā sunanihinna)" — meaning upon their customary practice regarding their dowries and the dowries of their peers. It is said: ḍāra and aḍarra bihi — the triliteral form with the elision of the preposition (bāʾ), and the quadriliteral form with its affirmation.

Her statement, "he prevents her (fa-yaʿḍiluhā)" — meaning he prevents her from marriage. Her statement, "he shared with her in his wealth, even in the date-palm (ʿidhq)" — "shārakatuhu" with kasrah on the rāʾ, meaning she participated with him; and "al-ʿidhq" with fatḥah on the ʿayn, which is the palm tree.

Her statement in [3019] regarding the saying of the Exalted: {«وَمَن كَانَ فَقِيرًا فَلْيَأْكُلْ بِالْمَعْرُوفِ»} ("And whoever is poor, let him eat in a reasonable manner") — that it is permissible for the guardian to eat from the orphan's wealth in a reasonable manner if he himself is in need. This is the school of al-Shāfiʿī and the majority. A group said it is not permissible, and it is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās and Zayd ibn Aslam that they said: This verse is abrogated by the saying of the Exalted: {«إِنَّ الَّذِينَ يَأْكُلُونَ أَمْوَالَ الْيَتَامَىٰ ظُلْمًا»} ("Indeed, those who devour the wealth of orphans unjustly...") — the verse. And it was said: abrogated by the saying of the Exalted: {«وَلَا تَأْكُلُوا أَمْوَالَكُم بَيْنَكُم بِالْبَاطِلِ»} ("And do not consume your wealth among yourselves in falsehood"). The majority differed regarding whether, if he eats, he is obligated to repay its equivalent — and these are two aspects (wajhān) among our companions, the sounder of which is that he is not obligated. The jurists of Iraq said: He is only permitted to eat if he travels in the orphan's wealth. And Allah knows best.

[3022] Her statement, "They were commanded to seek forgiveness for the Companions of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, so they reviled them." Al-Qāḍī said: The apparent meaning is that she said this when she heard the people of Egypt saying about ʿUthmān what they said, and the people of Syria saying about ʿAlī what they said, and the Khawārij saying about all of them what they said. As for the command to seek forgiveness to which she alluded, it is the saying of the Exalted: {«وَالَّذِينَ جَاءُوا مِن بَعْدِهِمْ يَقُولُونَ رَبَّنَا اغْفِرْ لَنَا وَلِإِخْوَانِنَا الَّذِينَ سَبَقُونَا بِالْإِيمَانِ»} ("And those who came after them say: Our Lord, forgive us and our brothers who preceded us in faith"). With this, Mālik argued that there is no right in the spoils (fayʾ) for one who reviles the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, because Allah the Exalted only made it for those who came after them among those who seek forgiveness for them. And Allah knows best.

His statement, "from Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with them both, that the intentional killer has no repentance" — and he argued with the saying of the Exalted: {«وَمَن يَقْتُلْ مُؤْمِنًا مُّتَعَمِّدًا فَجَزَاؤُهُ جَهَنَّمُ خَالِدًا فِيهَا»} ("And whoever kills a believer intentionally, his recompense is Hell, abiding therein forever"). This is the well-known view from Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with them both. And it is narrated from him that he has repentance and the permissibility of forgiveness for him, due to the saying of the Exalted: {«وَمَن يَعْمَلْ سُوءًا أَوْ يَظْلِمْ نَفْسَهُ ثُمَّ يَسْتَغْفِرِ اللَّهَ يَجِدِ اللَّهَ غَفُورًا رَّحِيمًا»} ("And whoever does evil or wrongs himself, then seeks forgiveness from Allah, will find Allah Forgiving, Merciful"). This second narration is the school of all the people of the Sunnah, the Companions, the Followers, and those after them. What is narrated from some of the Salaf contradicting this is interpreted as severity and warning against killing, and as dissuasion from it. There is no explicit statement in this verse with which Ibn ʿAbbās argued that he abides forever; rather, it only states that it is his recompense, and it does not necessarily follow that he will be recompensed. The establishment of this matter and the clarification of the meaning of the verse have already preceded in the Book of Repentance. And Allah knows best.

[3023] His statement, "So I traveled (fa-raḥaltu) to Ibn ʿAbbās" — it is with rāʾ and unpointed ḥāʾ; this is the correct and well-known form in the narrations. In the copy of Ibn Māhān, it is "fa-dakhaltu" with dāl and pointed khāʾ, and it can be validated such that its meaning is "I entered after my journey to him."

His statement, "As for the one who entered into Islam with his intellect (ʿaqluhu)" — it is with fatḥah on the qāf, meaning he knew the rulings of Islam and the prohibition of killing. His statement, "the verse of Medina abrogated it (nasakhat-hā āyat al-Madīnah)" — meaning the abrogating verse is the verse of al-Nisāʾ: {«وَمَن يَقْتُلْ مُؤْمِنًا مُّتَعَمِّدًا»} ("And whoever kills a believer intentionally").

His statement, "from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, who said: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abzā commanded me to ask Ibn ʿAbbās about these two verses" — thus it is in all copies. Al-Qāḍī said: Some said, "Perhaps he meant: Ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān commanded me." Al-Qāḍī said: It is not improbable that ʿAbd al-Raḥmān commanded Saʿīd to ask Ibn ʿAbbās on his behalf about what ʿAbd al-Raḥmān did not know, for Ibn ʿAbbās was asked by those greater than him and more advanced in companionship. What al-Qāḍī said is the correct view.

[3024] His statement, "Abū ʿUmayyis informed us, from ʿAbd al-Majīd ibn Suhayl" — thus it is in all copies: ʿAbd al-Majīd with mīm then jīm. As for the copy of Ibn Māhān, in it is ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd with ḥāʾ then mīm. Abū ʿAlī al-Ghassānī said: The first is correct. Al-Qāḍī said: They have differed regarding his name. Mālik mentioned him in the Muwaṭṭaʾ in the narration of Yaḥyā ibn Yaḥyā al-Andalusī and others, naming him ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd with ḥāʾ then mīm, and Sufyān ibn ʿUyaynah said likewise. Al-Bukhārī named him ʿAbd al-Majīd with mīm then jīm, and likewise Ibn al-Qāsim, al-Qaʿnabī, and a group narrated it in the Muwaṭṭaʾ from Mālik. Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr said: It is said both ways, and he said: The more frequent is with mīm then jīm. Al-Qāḍī said: When the disagreement regarding it is established, neither of the two forms is judged as erroneous.

[3028] His statement, "She says: Who will lend me a garment for circumambulation (ṭawāf)?" — it is with kasrah on the tāʾ (the doubled letter above), and it is a garment that a woman wears to circumambulate in it. The people of the Jāhiliyyah used to circumambulate naked, throwing off their clothes and leaving them cast upon the ground, never taking them again, leaving them to be trampled under feet until they wore out — and it was called "al-liqāʾ." Then Islam came, and Allah the Exalted commanded the covering of the private parts, saying: {«خُذُوا زِينَتَكُمْ عِندَ كُلِّ مَسْجِدٍ»} ("Take your adornment at every mosque"), and the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "No one naked shall circumambulate the House."

[3029] His statement, "Then Allah the Exalted revealed: {«وَلَا تُكْرِهُوا فَتَيَاتِكُمْ عَلَى الْبِغَاءِ إِنْ أَرَدْنَ تَحَصُّنًا»} ("And do not compel your slave girls to prostitution if they desire chastity") — up to His saying: {«وَمَن يُكْرِههُّنَّ فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ مِن بَعْدِ إِكْرَاهِهِنَّ لَهُنَّ غَفُورٌ رَّحِيمٌ»} ("And whoever compels them, then indeed Allah, after their compulsion, is Forgiving, Merciful")" — thus it occurred in all copies: "lahunna ghafūrun raḥīm" ("for them, Forgiving, Merciful"). This is an interpretation (tafsīr), and it was not intended that the word "lahunna" is part of the revealed text.

chapters.title_en: Section 992 — On the Coercion of Slave Women to Fornication, and the Commentary on the Hadith of Abū Dharr Regarding the Two Contending Parties
chapters.arabic_text:
فإنه لم يقرأ بها أحد وإنما هي تفسير وبيان يردان المغفرة والرحمة لهن

لكونهن مكرهات لا لمن أكرههن وأما قوله تعالى إن أردن تحصنا فخرج على

الغالب إذ الإكراه إنما هو لمريدة التحصن أما غيرها فهي تسارع إلى البغاء

من غير حاجة إلى الإكراه والمقصود أن الاكراه على الزنى حرام سواء أردن

تحصنا أم لاوصورة الاكراه مع أنها لاتريد التحصن أن تكون هي مريدة الزنى

بانسان فيكرهها على الزنى بغيره وكله حرام قوله (إن جارية لعبد الله بن أبي

يقال لها مسيكة وأخرى يقال لها أميمة) أما مسيكة فبضم الميم وقيل إنهما

معاذة وزينب وقيل نزلت في ست جوار له كان يكرههن على الزنى معاذة ومسيكة

وأميمة وعمرة وأروى وقتيلة والله
# 
# أعلم قوله (عن عبد الله بن معبد الزماني) بكسر الزاى وتشديد الميم قوله

في تحريم الخمر
# 
# [3032] (وإنها من خمسة أشياء وذكر الكلالة وغيرها) هذا كله سبق بيانه في

أبوابه قوله
# 
# [3033] (عن أبي مجلز عن قيس بن عباد قال سمعت أبا ذر يقسم قسما أن هذان

خصمان اختصموا فى ربهم أنها نزلت في الذين برزوا يوم بدر) أما مجلز فبكسر

الميم على المشهور وحكي فتحها وإسكان الجيم وفتح اللام واسمه لاحق بن حميد

سبق بيانه مرات وقيس بن عباد بضم العين وتخفيف الباء وهذا الحديث مما

استدركه الدارقطني فقال أخرجه البخاري عن أبي مجلز  عن قيس عن علي رضي الله

عنه أنا أول من يجثو للخصومة قال قيس وفيهم نزلت الآية ولم يجاوز به قيسا

ثم قال البخاري وقال عثمان عن جرير عن منصور عن أبي هاشم عن أبي مجلز قوله

(قال الدارقطني فاضطرب الحديث) هذا كله كلامه قلت فلا يلزم من هذا ضعف

الحديث واضطرابه لأن قيسا سمعه من أبى ذركما رواه مسلم هنا فرواه عنه وسمع

من علي بعضه وأضاف إليه قيس ما سمعه من أبي ذر وأفتى به أبو مجلز تارة ولم

يقل إنه من كلام نفسه ورأيه وقد عملت الصحابة رضوان الله عليهم ومن بعدهم

بمثل هذا فيفتي الإنسان منهم بمعنى الحديث عند الحاجة إلى الفتوى
# 
# دون الرواية ولا يرفعه فإذا كان وقت آخر وقصد الرواية رفعه وذكر لفظه

وليس فى هذا اضطراب والله أعلم
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ك-ر-ه (k-r-h)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning is compulsion or forcing someone against their will; the passive participle (mukrahah) denotes one subjected to duress.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological context, ikrāh negates moral culpability for the coerced act, as the agent's intent (irādah) is overridden by external constraint.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage refers to physical or psychological coercion; metaphorical (majāz) extension applies to legal rulings where duress nullifies punishment for the victim.
- Root: ب-غ-ي (b-gh-y)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning is seeking or desiring; baghā' (fornication) is a technical term for illicit sexual intercourse, specifically prostitution.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Denotes transgression against divine boundaries; in Quranic usage, it carries moral and legal prohibition.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense is 'seeking'; metaphorical sense is the act of seeking unlawful gratification, hence fornication.
- Root: خ-ص-م (kh-s-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning is dispute or contention; khaṣm refers to two parties in a legal or theological argument.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In Quranic context (e.g., {«هذان خصمان اختصموا في ربهم»}), it signifies opposing factions in a matter of faith.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal is verbal altercation; metaphorical is the eschatological confrontation before God.
- Sībawayh Rule: Rule of 'Aṭf al-Bayān (Appositional Clarification) — When multiple names are cited (e.g., the slave girls), each is in apposition to the preceding, requiring precise grammatical case matching; also, the rule of Ḥikāyah (Quotation) for transmitting variant readings without altering the narrator's wording.
chapters.translation:
I say: Know that his statement (concerning the verse {«ولا تكرهوا فتياتكم على البغاء»} — 'And do not compel your slave girls to prostitution') — for no one has recited it in this manner; rather, it is an exegesis and clarification that repels forgiveness and mercy upon them (the coerced women), because they are the ones coerced, not upon those who coerced them. As for His statement, the Exalted, {«إن أردن تحصنا»} — 'if they desire chastity' — it is expressed according to the predominant case, for coercion only occurs against one who desires chastity. As for one who does not, she hastens to prostitution without any need for coercion. The intended meaning is that coercion to fornication is unlawful, whether they desire chastity or not. The form of coercion, even when she does not desire chastity, is that she desires fornication with a man, and he coerces her to fornicate with another — all of this is unlawful.

His statement (in the narration): (A slave girl of ʿAbdullāh ibn Ubayy, called Musaykah, and another called Umaymah) — as for Musaykah, it is with a ḍammah on the mīm. And it is said that they were Muʿādhah and Zaynab. And it is said that it was revealed concerning six slave girls of his whom he used to coerce to fornication: Muʿādhah, Musaykah, Umaymah, ʿAmrah, Arwā, and Qutaylah. And God knows best.

Know that his statement (concerning the chain): (From ʿAbdullāh ibn Maʿbad al-Zamānī) — with a kasrah on the zāy and a tashdīd on the mīm. His statement: (On the prohibition of wine).

[3032] (And it is from five things, and he mentioned al-kalālah and others) — all of this has been previously explained in its respective chapters. His statement:

[3033] (From Abū Mijlaz, from Qays ibn ʿUbād, who said: I heard Abū Dharr swearing an oath that {«هذان خصمان اختصموا في ربهم»} — 'These two opponents dispute concerning their Lord' — was revealed concerning those who came forth on the Day of Badr.) As for Mijlaz, it is with a kasrah on the mīm according to the well-known pronunciation, and it has been reported with a fatḥah on it, with a sukūn on the jīm and a fatḥah on the lām. His name is Lāḥiq ibn Ḥumayd, and its explanation has preceded multiple times. And Qays ibn ʿUbād — with a ḍammah on the ʿayn and a takhfīf on the bā'. This hadith is among those that al-Dāraquṭnī deemed defective, for he said: Al-Bukhārī narrated it from Abū Mijlaz, from Qays, from ʿAlī, may God be pleased with him, who said: 'I will be the first to kneel for the dispute.' Qays said: 'Concerning them the verse was revealed,' and he did not go beyond Qays with it. Then al-Bukhārī said: And ʿUthmān said, from Jarīr, from Manṣūr, from Abū Hāshim, from Abū Mijlaz, his statement (i.e., as a saying of Abū Mijlaz, not raised to the Prophet).

He said — al-Dāraquṭnī: 'The hadith has become disordered.' All of this is his speech. I say: This does not necessitate weakness or disorder in the hadith, because Qays heard it from Abū Dharr, as Muslim narrated it here, and he narrated it from him. And he heard part of it from ʿAlī, and Qays added to it what he heard from Abū Dharr. And Abū Mijlaz gave a legal opinion based on it at one time, and he did not claim it was from his own speech or opinion. The Companions, may God be pleased with them, and those after them acted upon similar matters: one of them would give a legal opinion based on the meaning of a hadith when needed for a ruling, without raising it (to the Prophet); then at another time, when intending to narrate, he would raise it and mention its exact wording. There is no disorder in this. And God knows best.
